metadata.school_name: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

reviews.comment: RELI 101 ended up being one of my favorite classes I've ever taken at UNC. Professor Tsoulouhas gives amazing lectures and makes complicated ideas easy to understand with real-world case studies. I would definitely take a class with her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Tsoulouhas is very organized with her Canvas being extremely accessible and all of her rubrics/deadlines being very clear. This class has a lot of group work and class discussions.

I took RELI-101 with professor Tsoulouhas this semester and it ended up being by far my favorite course I took. Prof. Tsoulouhas is very kind and displays a good knowledge of subject matters present in the course. She is not difficult to reach outside of class and you can tell student success is a priority. I would take class again with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: An interesting course. I learned a lot while investing a reasonable amount of time. Discussions were also worthwhile. Quick aside: Students at a school as prestigious as this one shouldn't lash out because the professor prohibits plagiarism, or because they assign college-level amounts of reading. It makes us all look bad and devalues our degrees.
Be prepared to read.. Make sure you cite every quote. Not a fun class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The best physics teacher I've ever had.

Dr. Erickcek is knowledgeable and does a good job covering the material. The material is difficult though, and your grade comes down to how well you do on the midterms so study accordingly! Still, they are fairly graded and often were curved slightly (including the final) if she saw the majority of the class struggled on certain sections.
She is really nice, gave good feedback on all assignments, but the material is vast and she doesn't give exam practice problems. So it is difficult to study for those exams.

Dr. Erickcek is amazing, this class made me switch my major to astrophysics! Fantastic class, lectures, and professor. The homework can be difficult but is totally manageable if you start on time. Having python experience can be helpful.

She is an exceptional teacher, her lectures are so thorough and well-planned. She is so helpful if you make it obvious that you're trying to understand. The content of the classes are super challenging. she doesn't downplay the difficulty. She delivers excellence in her teaching and expects excellence from her students. It's intense, but worth it

Like all physics courses, this is a difficult class, but Dr. Erickcek does everything she can to make material understandable and engaging. She's clearly interested both in the material and teaching as a whole. Office hours are great. She very obviously wants students to succeed, so if you do struggle, don't be afraid to reach out.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Erickcek is a fantastic lecturer, and makes ASTR 202 exciting and fun. She is great at breaking down difficult concepts, extremely helpful in office hours. Homework is difficult (it's astrophysics) but she encourages and allows you to work in groups and gives help. Tests are difficult but not at all unfair. She's caring and nice, take her!

Dr. Erickcek knows what she's talking about and she's a good communicator. PHYS 118 is a hard class no matter how smart you are. If you are dedicated about going to her office hours she will do her best to help save you in this course.
The course as a whole is rather difficult, but Dr. Erickcek is a phenomenal lecturer. It's clear that she's passionate about the subject, and she answers questions well.
The course isn't easy, but she is a great lecturer. There are lot of assignments and three midterms, but it helps with learning the material. Would recommend for this course.

Dr. Erickcek is very enthusiastic about physics, and it showed in both lecture and studio. The class is very well structured, so it was always clear what the expectations for the students were. Even if you bomb a midterm (like I did), there are enough homework and studio assignments to boost your grade to an A if you put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you don't have to take Physics, do not under any circumstances. The class structure is flawed and really alienates any non-Physics major taking the class. The lectures are entirely concept based and were so dull, but Erickcek did the most with what she had. She wasn't the best professor, but was much more enjoyable than Dr. Lu.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: An absolutely wonderful lecturer. Her lectures were engaging and she gracefully fielded questions from even the most obnoxious students. She was accessible outside of class and made everything make sense during her office hours. She taught in tandem with Dr. Jianping Lu, but the class had a clear preference for her.

Erickcek taught the majority of Dr. Lu's class;She seems nice, but fakes sympathy. Not readily available,send emails or ask TA questions;All content department made;Tests only similar to some lab sheets and ponderables;use chegg,A's possible if took AP or taking one STEM class,work with peers for HW,WU, labreport;Skim reading and study formulas.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Erickcek definitely knows a lot about physics and seems to enjoy teaching, but her excitement at how difficult and confusing the material (especially relativity) could be, paired with lectures that focused on concepts and left out a lot of the more complex underlying math, was a little disheartening.

PHYS118 is hard regardless of who you take it with. The class covers lots of material quickly and you have to put in effort outside of class to do well. That said, Dr. Erickcek is caring and works hard to help students understand difficult concepts. She's a great lecturer and is passionate about the material, great at answering student questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: 118 is a big class that goes fast (intro physics is chock-full of material no matter what you do), but Dr. Erickcek is a wonderful lecturer and she is willing to take the time to work with you individually if you're having issues. Definitely attend office hours, even if you're not sure you need it - I learned quite a bit from there.

PHYS118 is a very difficult class. To be honest, I would have failed if I didn't take high school physics. Erickcek is nice for the most part, but her explanations for certain concepts are a little confusing (kinematics, rotational motion, etc). Just try and do good in Studio to make up for the exam grades, because they're going to be rough.

For the ones who hate physics but have to take it for their major (shout out CS), this class can be very difficult. Without putting in the effort outside of class, a C is a feat. The exams are mostly free response, and there is no curve. I wouldn't recommend Erickcek as your studio TA since she grades much harsher than other sections. Good luck.

Exams are the same level of difficulty as Mastering Physics. Textbook was confusing. Lectures are not helpful for homeworks or exams because you just learn the concept from the warm up. Office hours are for learning how to do problems.
stellar
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Erickcek is a wonderful professor- she knows exactly what she's going to say in each of her lectures and explains things really well. Her problem sets are hard (don't leave them until the night before) but she was always really helpful in her office hours. If you have any interest in astronomy or astrophysics, definitely take 301 with her!

Ava was caring and accommodated for everyone's needs in terms of feedback and giving extensions. Lots of tough reading but she explained it well in class. Lecture and participation heavy, you will be expected to speak at least 2x a class for a good participation grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This course was fairly difficult for an introductory class and contained a lot of reading and lectures. Professor Geenen was always willing to help outside of class and had some interesting lectures. The material was pretty comprehensive as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ava is a great professor. She understands the material extremely well and, more importantly, can explain it well. Her readings were thoughtfully chosen and refreshingly contemporary compared to many introductory-level philosophy courses at UNC. Additionally, her unit quizzes required meaningful engagement with the texts, which helped learning.

PHIL 140: Very nice prof. but class can get dull. Worksheets give good overview of papers but the subject matter is really confusing, especially for your first philosophy class. Half of class stopped attending. Papers are hard but if you go to office hours and the writing center you can totally do well. If you love philosophy, you will 100% enjoy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: PHIL140 was an awful experience. The class material felt like a giant circle leading back to the same discussion and topic we had on the first day of class. Paper grading was harsh for the class, and the lectures were very discussion-based, yet dull. Half the class stopped showing up throughout the semester, if that says anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Overall okay professor. Wasn't the biggest fan of the way the class was graded/assessed. The grading was not at the level of an introductory philosophy class. 2 essays worth 65% of your grade. The class content was interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Took this class for a gen-ed and was disappointed. She takes lateness into account and if you arrive a minute past class start time, poof! your participation goes down. She grades harshly- even after meeting with her several times about a paper she gave me a B+ on it and her critiques are absolute nonsense. Will not give you the grade you deserve.

This class was so enjoyable and fulfilling; I learned so much. The lectures were a bit rough at first but got better as the semester went on. We had anywhere from 10–40-page readings due every class period and classes were discussion based. Expectations for assignments were clear, and Ava is very accessible.  I would recommend this class!

She is very reachable and caring to give extensions when needed. Her grading for papers is fair, with a clear rubric, and she gives line notes feedback. She incorporates different views, and grades based on the quality of arguments rather than her personal likeness. Reply emails very quick.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I think I would have enjoyed this course if it wasn't at 8 am. Ava is a very caring professor & is clear about what's required. Graded on outside reading annotations before each class, attendance/participation in class, 2 papers, and a final group project. Missing a class will make your grade plummet, otherwise the course content is doable.

The UNC chem department is tough, but Dr. Curtis does a great job teaching students the content needed to pass exams, and she does so in a way that is easier to understand than the textbook. Dr. Curtis is also a friendly person, and it is clear that she wants her students to succeed. Definitely take with Curtis if you can!

If you are a pre-med and thought this course was difficult, you should take a step back and reconsider your long-term goals. This class is by far one of the easiest STEM classes you will take. If you got anything below a B+ and are not 100% sure if becoming a doctor is what you want to do, drop medicine now. It is easier to pivot early on.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is wonderful and very accessible.  However, exams are 85% of your grade (20% per midterm, 25% final) and they were tough.  The rest of your grade is homework which is graded very leniently.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had her class in Spring 2025. She was a fine chemistry teacher, and she is definitely passionate about her job. I didn't really find her inspiring, and some days she could go from being the sweetest lady to quite snarky. The chemistry department is also just tough. Self study and practice is super necessary, but take with her if you can!

101/102 get a bad wrap, but they're some of UNC's best-designed courses regarding evidence-based learning and avid practice problem exposure. PAY ATTENTION AND BUY INTO THE SYSTEM. I learned so much + Curtis was clear + qualified. Take accountability for your learning, and trust that 102 provides everything you need to succeed. TLDR: loved Curtis!!

The UNC Chemistry department is extremely difficult; however, I found her teaching to be extremely helpful. She really emphasized understanding the underlying principles of chemistry - the “why” - which, once you actually learn, is crucial and helps with your chemistry intuition. If you take 102, definitely take it with her!!

Chem is hard no matter which professor you have for 102, as it is the same slides and the same exams for everyone. I think Curtis was a great professor, especially outside of the lecture. In GPSS she was very sweet and helpful, and she was great help for study habits in office hours. She's a little corny and had a few laughs in class too.

UNC gen chem is definitely not perfect but Curtis is super caring and approachable and explains examples/topics well in class. Class is designed for you to learn from the textbook and lectures just reinforce the topics from readings. If you read the textbook carefully her lectures are helpful and you will be fine.

The way gen chem is structured at UNC tend to be more dependent on how well you prepare yourself and less about the actual professor you have in my opinion. Curtis was clearly passionate about chem and was kinda entertaining and quirky, but because of the nature chem here I simply can not give her above a 3. chem here sucks but it is what it is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Anna Curtis is a great professor, chemistry here is just difficult. She is a little quirky but is genuinely excited about chemistry and helping students learn. She really emphasizes knowing the reason why behind concepts and equations, which does make exams harder, but she does a good job explaining things.
If you're not religious, pick a religion and pray. I have never been in such a difficult and unnecessarily confusing course like this. Truly good luck to everyone who has to take this. Godspeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's very passionate for sure but only teaches surface level, and on the midterm, they expect you to be Antoine Lavoisier (the father of chemistry). The class is 84% midterms and finals together. The lectures felt pointless but you have to go because attendance is graded. Go to GPSS if you want to pass. GPA killer for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have to take chem 102, I would take it with her. It's a super hard class and the tests are awful, but she as a teacher is very nice and enthusiastic about her subject.

Professor Curtis is not a good professor by any means. She is very bad at explaining basic chemistry concepts and prepares her students in a poor manner for every midterm. The averages in her classes are incredibly low because it requires students to self study to the fullest to perform well. Do not take chemistry with her by any means.

She is incompetent. I would rather watch paint dry than sit in her class. She does an awful job of keeping students engaged. She goes over what 2+2 is like we are in first grade and doesn't prepare us for the exams.
Doesn't do a good job of explaining anything. Very incompetent
She is a very sweet lady but tends to repeat herself. Also, her pacing varies: one day she moves through the slides very slowly, then the next class time she rushes. Wouldn't recommend her :p

I am not joking when I say she is likely the worst professor in the chemistry department. During her lectures, she repeats the same idea numerous times and takes forever to finish simple problems that anyone in the class would understand. If you are taking Chem102, take it with any other professor who doesn't waste their students' time.
She was a good teacher, but chem 101 will be hard no matter who you take it with. Ask questions and go to GPSS if you are having trouble.

Prof Curtis is a great lecturer! She is engaging and kind. When she explains things she shows her thought process so you get a better idea of how to approach the problems. An A is achievable if you put in the effort.
My advice:
1) Read chapters to understand, and put what you're learning in the context of what you already know
2) Go to CHEMPossible

Standardized class but her lectures were by far the best. She explained concepts and thought processes instead of step by step instructions which aligned perfectly with the challenging tests. People with all deferent grades in the class respect her greatly and would take again.

Curtis was a great lecturer overall. Only issue I had was that she would often be very behind on lessons so it was a bit frustrating at times. Class was pretty difficult but you will be okay if you focus on understanding concepts and doing LOTS of practice.

I would say Anna Curtis is one of the best Chem 101 lecturers. She seems to really care about the subject matter and is enthusiastic while teaching, without being too overboard. Although chem 101 is a flipped classroom format which can be somewhat difficult, I feel like she addresses all difficult content and allows time for questions always.

CHEM 101 is standardized, so the formatting of the class and its assignments are the same no matter which professor one has, but I really enjoyed Dr. Curtis as a lecturer.  She was very kind and always full of energy while teaching.  She made difficult concepts easier to understand, which was great because I hadn't taken a chem course in a while.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly, it doesn't matter what professor you get Chem because it is standardized and you will teach yourself most of the content, but Anna curtis is absolutely the best professor that you can get for chem 101. She explains concepts in a way that is digestible to anyone. You will have to put in the work though because Chem at UNC is hard.

Dr. Curtis is a great lecturer and teaches concepts in a digestible way. The formatting of Chem101 is mostly textbook heavy, so the professor you have won't impact your grade nearly as much as how much you read. To get a good grade in the class I recommend staying on top of your pre-class assignments and attending ChemPossible.

Dr. Curtis is a pretty good lecturer, however the content is difficult. Chem 101 really shows you what studying is and you are going to have to learn it on your own as well. Just attend GPSS sessions, watch youtube videos, and study the concepts rather than just memorizing the formulas.

If you're taking 101, take it with Dr. Curtis! This is a tough class no matter what, but Dr. Curtis is thorough in her explanations and goes really in-depth on concepts she knows students struggle with. Collaboration and participation is heavily encouraged in her class.
Dr. Curtis is a caring professor, but Chem 101 is a tough class overall. Attend office hours, use the free textbook, and try Unstuckstudy for extra prep - it really helps.

Dr. Curtis is probably the best professor in the UNC Chem department. If you have to take chem 101 DO IT WITH HER. Her lectures are clear and she explains things well with examples and applications. She also great at getting a feel for that the class doesn't understand.

She was good in her quirky way. She genuinely loves chem and wanted us to see the beauty in it, unfortunately I just could not. Remember to redirect your anger from chem teachers to the chem department, they are the real enemies. She held really informative GPSS and would take thorough time in class to explain concepts and exam-type questions.
Chem101 is hard, but she's nice and always had so much energy. Don't take chem if you don't have to.

CHEM 101 is hard no matter which professor you take. Professor Curtis is a really sweet person and very approachable and I appreciated how she took things slow until she was sure we understood basic concepts before moving on. I felt like we did a lot of easy stuff in class and were expected to do challenging problems alone, which I struggled with.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Curtis is fine but Chem is really tough and takes getting used to. Make sure you work outside of class to understand everything
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis cares about chemistry and her students. I just wish that she would've spent more time in class going over exam-type questions rather than explaining the basic concepts to us (that we were already expected to know before class). The chem department here can be frustrating so I honestly don't think it matters who you take the class with.

Dr. Curtis is kind and attentive to students. Chemistry is a hard class regardless of professor and your grade will rest heavily on exams. However, Curtis is easy to reach and available to help students. Lectures are pretty standard between professors (use the same slides). If you have to take chem, Curtis is a great option!

Anna Curtis was very sweet and an engaging lecturer. Chem 101 at UNC is just extremely hard and requires extensive practice (recitation, Chem Possible, GPSS, etc). I think she moves at the perfect pace for students who are just learning these chemistry concepts for the first time.

Chem here is annoying, but Dr. Curtis made it better. She's very sweet and quirky and cares a lot about her students understanding the content. Her lectures can run slow/long, but it's because she takes the time to explain the concepts. GPSS is a must for 101 though; lecture and homework will not be enough to understand the content fully.

Offers good explanations especially in GPSS, but moves extremely slow during lecture. Ultimately, the course is not a reflection of her, the chem department is just terrible in itself. You will end up teaching yourself most of the content in chem, but that is not because of Dr. Curtis. She has clear enthusiasm for the subject.

Whoever you take chem-101 with, it's gonna be hard and you're not gonna like the professor. Go to GPSS, and find a study group if you can, and you'll do fine. Overall, she was good though, and if you have to take chem-101, I'd recommend.

Chem is hard, but Dr Curtis is a good teacher and truly cares about all of her students. She is accessible outside of class and gives plenty of opportunities to attend group problem-solving or other forms of tutoring. Her instructions are clear and her canvas page is detailed. I do not recommend the class, but if you have to then take it with her.

Chem 101 in general is a tough class but she made it extremely digestible. She thoroughly explains the concepts and is available for problem solving sessions outside of class. Many people don't do well and blame it on the professor but as long as you practice outside of class and re-write the lecture notes you will do fine.
Do. Not. Take.

The way Dr. Curtis lays out her train of thought when approaching problems is incredible. She emphasizes application over memorization. The grade I received isn't a reflection of her abilities. This was my first semester at UNC, and I also had bad study habits. One major downside is that there were no office hours where you could meet one-on-one.

Curtis's lectures are engaging and she explains the material well. This class is tough because the exams dictate the grade. Instead of going to GPSS or UL sessions, I did the UL practice problems they posted on Canvas. One bad move that Curtis made was that I proved that I was right on an exam question I got wrong, and she kinda blew me off.

If you don't have to take chem at UNC, don't. She was a boring lecturer, made mistakes frequently and we never finished lessons the day of. Only available for meetings 6 min. long. Use TA resources but know the tests will be way harder. It feels we are set up to fail and they don't realize these grades impact our future. Major GPA tanker.

Pros: 
- Very animated / fun to talk to
- Helpful resources outside of class
- The coolest classroom on the planet

Cons:
- Could not stand group discussions
- Exams were tougher than 101
- Gatekeep answers on practice exams

How to Study: Go to ULA sessions and do their practice problems!

Dr. Curtis was a great professor. I found this class to be a little difficult but going to office hours was extremely helpful. She always answered my questions there and really cared about getting to know me which was so sweet. Tests do make up a majority of your grade but go to class and do the homework so that you don't miss easy points.

Chem at UNC is hard no matter who your professor is. This class is a major time commitment. Curtis is OK but I felt like she left out some important things in the lecture. Make sure to attend GPSS and get extra help before falling too far behind.

Dr. Curtis is awesome! Although the class itself is very challenging (but that's just Chem at UNC in a nutshell), she explains very well during lecture and includes plenty of practice problems to help you prepare for exams. That being said, do not skip class or let content pile up and make sure to take advantage of CHEMPossible, GPSS and PMs/SIs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's up to you to read the textbook; you'll understand much more if you do. Exams are 84% of grade - do practice problems. I went to one peer mentor's session every week. I sat in the same seat next to a peer mentor I liked each lecture. Prof Curtis is engaging with lots of energy. When I met with her, I found her to be willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was lucky to have Curtis for both CHEM 101 and 102. Both semesters, her lectures focused on the lesson objectives for that day and included time to address student questions and plenty of exam-type practice questions. The 102 peer mentors are generally unhelpful; ChemPossible and GPSS are good resources! Also, read the textbook before each class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Curtis. She's incredibly knowledgeable and super nice. Definitely read the textbook and go to GPSS and her 6-minute meetings. Always has a positive attitude and is supportive. Take her for any class you can!

The chem department is not great- if you do bad on one exam it can screw you over and the final is worth a lot. However, Anna Curtis is a kind queen and I enjoyed her lectures. She's very sweet and loves chemistry and is overall just an enjoyable professor.

Ms. Curtis is probably the best chem 102 professor at UNC. She was sweet and cared about the success of her students. The material can be challenging but if you go to GPSS and actively do practice questions you'll be fine. I think 102 is easier than 101 because it's just utilizing equations, and is less focused on conceptual information like 101.
The chem department at UNC is awful, but professor Curtis is a good teacher. The exams are much harder than anything taught in class and basically dictate your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very bubbly, which is good for keeping you awake in chemistry! Study the slides to do well on the exams and take notes during lectures. The PMs are very helpful for answering questions in class. Chem 102 isn't terrible, and she's the best professor for this class.

Dr. Curtis is probably the best 102 professor. She is engaging and decent at explaining concepts, though not particularly available outside of class. But the Chem department is a mess. Communication between the professors and the review session leaders is severely lacking. Tests are tough and account for a huge portion of your grade and are long.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There is a lot of out of class work but it is worth it to do, the readings are helpful but not always necessary i just guessed my way through the warmups and (since its for completion not correctness) and things got explained during class pretty well, other than that just making you understand the concepts and the class is manageable

The professor herself is great! she is very upbeat and excited about the class, but I found her hard to reach throughout the semester as when you have a question about something in class, you have to go to GPSS or find other outside the class resources to find the answer. Exams are harder than taught but that's just how the chemistry department is

Curtis is a good teacher, but I feel like there isn't enough practice especially with questions that are similar to the difficulty and wording of the exam. I find class problems to be a lot easier than test questions but that's more of an issue with the chem department in general. Overall, Curtis is a good choice just wish there was more practice
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Explains concepts clearly. Flipped classroom as you are expected to read the textbook and learn the concept before class. Tests are fair but overall difficult. No curves or incentives for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, chem here is terrible and this was my worst class, but none of that is because of Dr. Curtis. She's a pretty good lecturer but I found that reviewing the slides posted by other profs could help with certain topics. Exams are worth 75% but they're really lax with participation and you can miss like 15 classes without affecting your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: CHEM 102 is a super hard class, but Dr. Curtis did her best to tailor lectures to students' understandings of different topics. The structure of the class makes it hard to focus on harder practice questions during lecture, but she encouraged students to go to Group Problem Solving Sessions, and I personally got a tutor, which was super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Every professor in this department has some issue w them, but Curtis is the exception. She is very nice and a good lecturer. However, the tests are standardized across all 102 sections and graded harshly by TAs. I think that grading would be far easier if she was the one making/grading the tests. Chem sucks, but if you have to take 102, take her.

Curtis is hands-down the best option for CHEM 101! She tailors the lectures to the needs of her students and takes extra time in-class to answer questions/re-explain a topic if needed. Didn't always post lecture slides on time but you can look at the other profs' slides or go to GPSS/ChemPossible to make up for this. Kind and wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: TAKE CHEM 101 WITH CURTIS!!!! Any chem at UNC is going to be hard but Curtis makes the lectures very tolerable. She is very consistent.

Chemistry is unnecessarily hard at this school and the chem department seems to want everyone to fail. Curtis was good at explaining some hard concepts, but always seemed to brush over somethings. She never posted her lecture slides on time. I really liked her, but chem 101 is HARD FOR NO REASON.

She's super sweet and I really like her as a person- her enthusiasm about teaching chemistry is admirable! UNC Chem Department is terrible in general and will make your life hell, but Curtis is one of the best options. Just make sure you pay attention during lectures and attend review sessions

I really like prof Curtis. The TA's grade everything and UNC's chem department is very hard in general so this class is not easy. But Curtis always knew what she was doing in lectures and was always excited to teach us chem at 9am. She has a great attitude.

Professor Curtis is great. I think CHEM101 is just a stupid hard class and since the pace of the class is fast, you might get left in the dust trying to understand one topic (i did). I would say just study way before midterms and exams as they are a big chunk of your grade. Other parts of the grade are easy like homework, participation, etc.

Chem 102 is a difficult class but Curtis is a good professor. Tests are sometimes unreasonable but that has to do with the department more than the professor. GO TO PEER MENTOR SESSIONS, Isabella is amazing and will help you do well in the class. Stay on top of reading the chapter and seek extra support outside of class to do well.

The chem department at UNC is always tough. Dr. Curtis is definitely knowledgable, but her lectures were too slow and we were always behind. Wish she spent more time explaining rather than giving us excess time to solve practice problems. She's definitely a kind and caring person - just not the best style for me.

If you have to take chem, 1000% take it with Dr. Curtis!!! She is an amazing lecturer and she helps make the material feel doable. I didn't actually have her as my professor but I skipped my own chem class every day to attend her lectures instead and it made all the difference. I love her as a person and as a prof even though chem is hard.

Dr. Curtis is your best choice for CHEM 102! You can tell she's really into what she's teaching, and I thought that the tests were fair as long as you attended lectures & read the textbook pages she gives you. Gave our class full participation points since she thought we earned it, no graded pop quizzes, easy to talk to with her 6-minute meetings

Very nice professor!

At least in the online format, all CHEM 101 classes have the same asynchronous lectures, assignments, tests, and quizzes. That being said, they should all be the same difficulty level. Professor Curtis is a great choice for CHEM 101 because she is sweet and understanding when you ask questions in class.

Dr. Curtis kinda sucks. Her teaching style is subpar, she never sounds confident in her explanations, and she honestly just confused me more. Once, she explained an entire problem for 15 minutes just for a student to call her out for getting the wrong answer and she never went back to explain the right way. She seems like a good person but.

There is a lot of material in Chem 101 and it can be overwhelming for any student. There's little instruction and lots of group work. This sounds great until the entire group doesn't know what to do and we teach ourselves wrong. Curtis is a great person, but her online style of teaching isn't good for students well-being.

I had Dr. Curtis for Summer Session 1 and would definitely recommend taking her. She really puts in time for her students and does tons of exam like practice questions throughout lecture. She does grade on participation in lecture and recitation. She also puts you into groups with other students for projects and practice problems.

Dr. Curtis is a wonderful professor IF you are willing to commit to daily readings and homework. If you are not prepared to work for at least an hour a day then I would not recommend this class. The tests are challenging but fair. If you are applying yourself and using all the resources, there is no reason you shouldn't earn a stellar grade. READ!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis has a spunky personality which makes her class a little more entertaining. She does a good job at thoroughly explaining concepts and will work though problems until she feels the majority of the class understands it! She definitely made this class better than I expected it to be.

Dr. Curtis tries her hardest to be a fun lecturer but it just doesn't happen. If you have any sort of high school chemistry background then you wont have any trouble in chem 101 w/ Dr. Curtis, but this class is not a fun experience. Be sure to know how to do all the problems on the practice tests. If you can take this w/ another prof. you should.

Dr. Curtis was a great professor for Chem 101. It is a hard class regardless of who teaches it, but I think she does a great job of giving everyone the opportunity to succeed as long as you work for it. I read the textbook and took notes before class and then studied her slideshows for exams as well. If you do that it will be easy to get an A.

Professor Curtis is a good gen chem professor! Despite what some of the reviews say she has a ton of information to cover and has not much time to finish it. Her exams are very fair but beware test 2 as it is very difficult material and the test is difficult too. She is very accessible with Q&A sessions and her 6 minute meetings. I would recommend.
Dr Curtis was a fun professor to have! Her classes were very easy, and her exams were mostly based off of notes given in the class. Definite recommendation for an intro level Chem class!

Chemistry at UNC is hard regardless of who you take it with. You will have to put in the extra work to understand chemistry. Dr. Curtis is a very understanding and approchable professor, and the best professor you could have for a chemistry class. Taking her class will make your overall chemisty experience better at UNC.

Dr. Curtis was pretty alright until the pandemic hit. She is very enthusiastic, which helps not get bored during lecture, but I fear this class is pretty fast if you don't have a background in chem and you'd need to put in a lot of work outside class. Watch out on Mastering for last minute homework due date changes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is a good professor! CHEM101 is a difficult course no matter what professor you have, but Dr. Curtis provides many opportunities to succeed in her class. I took her class during the pandemic and she was very great when it came to helping us perform our best. She always has Q&A's which I recommend attending!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is a good professor. CHEM at UNC is hard, but I did not think Dr. Curtis' class was hard to understand. If you go to class and study for exams, it shouldn't be hard to get an A or B. Tests are not that hard and reflect what is learned in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis was not my favorite. There was little to no application of the topics we were learning to real life or even broader chemistry topics. The "purpose" behind everything we were learning was just to get us to chem 102, but after how dull this class was I don't even wanna take 102. Not a terrible class but so boring and dull.

CHEM 101 is a hard topic at UNC overall, but she was very enthusiastic about teaching it despite it being 8 in the morning. She's a nice person but not the best lecturer, but the class is standardized so it doesn't really matter. If you want to actually learn the material, I would advise taking another professor if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Despite what most of these reviews say, Dr. Curtis is a pretty good professor. Her notes are helpful and tests are similar to practice problems. Chem 101 has a lot of material so she has to go quickly which just means you have to put in a little extra work yourself.

Nice person but doesn't respect the fact that students have other places to be outside of her class. She often continues teaching two to three minutes after class is supposed to be over which isn't very accommodating to those who have class directly after hers. We end up missing explanations because she refuses to stop teaching after class is over.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis was new when I had her, but you can see her enthusiasm for chemistry. In the beginning of the semester they will tell you to not rely on the textbook. Ignore that completely, to succeed I would suggest to read the part of the book before the lecture or you will be completely lost. I highly regret not doing that and thats why I did so bad
The professor is very quirky but sweet. You're graded mainly on tests, so studying is very important. Most of the work you do HAS to be done outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis has a good attitude and is enthusiastic about the subject matter she teaches. She places a lot of emphasis on students showing her they know what to do, so during lectures students have to complete examples of concepts they're working on. Chem 101 is a standard weed-out class, but study the slides and you'll be just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Curtis was fine. At times, I was confused by the way she explained things. The CHEM101 department works together, so all the sections have the same homework and tests. She wasn't my favorite, but I got through most of the material okay. Your grade really depends on your test grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is fairly average when it comes to other professors at UNC in terms of the structure of the class, but don't bother asking her questions. She will try her best to come up with some form of response, but in doing so she just ends up confusing the entire class. Also, MC test questions are meant to trip you up, not to gauge knowledge.

Dr. Curtis is super enthusiastic about chemistry but it is really necessary that you read the textbook in order to do well. Lectures are basically the textbook on slides. Overall chem 101 is hard across the board. I don't really think that professor really matters that much for this level of chemistry. She's quirky and it makes 8am classes better.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is alright, but I tend to get so bored during lectures that I fall asleep. It got to a point during the year in which I was only showing up to lecture for the iclicker points. If you read the book on your own, you'll probably learn just as much, if not more than at lecture.

For chem 101 it really does not matter what professor you have, but out of the ones at UNC I'll say Anna is average. Don't expect to learn everything during lectures, chem 101 is a flip classroom and the bulk of your understanding will come from outside of class practice. Quizzes like every other Wednesday

Chem101 is hard regardless of the professor. You'll have to read the textbook, NOT fall behind, and practice often to get a good grade. Professor Curtis is bubbly and gives alright lectures, but most of the class you have to take initiative and learn outside of class. If you have specific questions, she's always SUPER approachable and helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is a young and super enthusiastic professor who really loves chemistry, but some of the concepts are just over-complicated. Can get side-tracked and start rushing in lecture. Really helpful during office hours. You will basically teach yourself but she helps a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Anna Curtis is such a goofball! She is a pretty good professor overall. Honestly, Chem 101 wasn't as hard as it was made out to be. I didn't even read the textbook. Make sure you study hard before each exam, do a lot of practice problems, and read each slide! You've got this.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Ariel is fantastic! His classes can be hard to follow and he interrupts presentations. BUT! He is a wealth of knowledge and I have never had a professor be more complimentary and supportive of my passion. He can take a joke, is willing to be (respectfully) challenged by students, and brought food to share at the beginning of class. He is great!
Great professor, gets to know his students, very personable. Would recommend him to anyone.

Great professor. Provided clear expectations for exams and opportunities to help prepare the class. Would highly recommend any class with Dr. Ariel. Honestly, a gem of a human. 

The topic of 242 (New Religious Movements) was unlike anything else I've ever learned and broadened my understanding of other faith communities.

I LOVED this class. Favorite professor and favorite class and i'm about to graduate. I would take any class he teaches. It's not hard if you try and are thoughtful. I really enjoyed the topics and Dr. Ariel always brought snacks, which was super kind. For the class, we got to visit churches and write about our experiences visiting them.

Dr. Ariel was the best professor of the three. He kept the class engaged through clips, texts, and slides. His essays were the easiest of the three, if you listened to him for 5 mins you could easily score an A. Plus, he gave you hints ahead of time. Great professor, especially if you are a history buff.
Professor Ariel is not engaging. The slides were all over the place and very boring class overall. Would not recommend.
horrible class. ariel is mid.

Yaakov was a bit eccentric, but always kind and caring. The class isn't difficult at all as long as you show up and participate in lecture. Grading criteria can be unclear at times, but contacting him via email/outside of class is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ariel is an extremely genuine and passionate teacher. There were just a few church observation papers due throughout the semester that he graded pretty easily, and you could observe online. He brought snacks to every class, which always made my day. Readings were assigned but never mattered for class.

Semester consisted of four written assignments plus a comparative midterm assignment. Classes were very lecture heavy and at times a bit boring. Professor Ariel's feedback was not always super clear but he does offer regrades and wants everyone to succeed. Be prepared to put in a moderate effort to secure the grade you want.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't think he was a bad professor. The class just sucks and the location was not helping me learn. The microphones in the Stone Center were always hard to listen to and honestly I never could understand what either of the professors were saying. Yaakov definetely was the funniest one and liked to make a spectacle of students.

You can sit in the back row and avoid eye contact and he will still make you stand up in front of the class and say something. He's really funny and definitely a great personality but he doesn't really teach as much as he tries to facilitate discussion. This is a terrible class (mostly the TAs and UNCs faults) but Dr. Ariel is a great teacher

His assignments are broad, but he expects specific criteria in writing. It gets frustrating when trying to do assignments since his instruction is so broad and is usually only discussed in class rather than posting guidelines. Nice guy and occasionally gives second chances.

This class requires a lot of writing: there are four reflections on online church videos, at least two reviews, and an essay midterm, all of which are graded somewhat toughly. He let us write the midterm in advance and gave us all the terms that were going to be on the final, though. There's also a lot of reading, but you can get by not doing it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I recommend both this class and Professor Ariel. He is an understanding professor that gives clear, precise feedback. You are graded on multiple papers (at least 6), but he offers extra credit in the form of redoing your papers for a better grade. Attend class! Lectures were slow and boring at times, but this class is an easy Gen-ed to knock out!

This class was super interesting to me, but often the lectures were hard to follow. Papers were graded harshly, but many opportunities were available to improve upon your work. Professor Ariel and his TA were easy to work with and wanted us to do well.
Prof. Ariel is personable and understanding. If you're a self-starter and remain engaged, the courseload is pretty manageable.
the guy is a jerk and the material is so boring and hard. worst class i have EVER taken (I am a senior)

Do not take a class with him. The most unorganized professor I've had. Syllabus was so confusing which caused problems for everyone in the class. Lectures hardly made sense because he went off on so many tangents. I feel liked I barely learned anything because I was confused the whole time. I'm a RELI major but I dreaded this class.

Professor Ariel is kind, but classes with him feel like they cover 20 minutes of content in a 70 minute session. He doesn't teach to the textbook. The only graded assignments are digital church visits and film/book reviews. He asks questions on the material before he teaches it, so if you have no background knowledge, you won't have answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not understand other comments complaining about a Christian bias. Professor is Jewish, and REL242 discussed other religious groups besides Christian offshoots. Prof. Ariel made a solid attempt to bring the class together as a group. Granted, knowing something about the subject beforehand was beneficial.
Prof Ariel was great. He is the sweetest teacher and is clearly very knowledgeable. I learned a lot in his class, and you're graded on only a few assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far the worst professor I've ever had! So rude....
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: dont take if you don't have any knowledge ab Christianity. Prof Ariel is the sweetest but the lectures were SO BORING and so hard to follow especially bc he teaches the class as if everyone there is christian--I AM NOT, so I never knew what was going on. TA didn't grade above a 90 all semester but he pulled thru w an easy final and no other tests

Dr. Ariel is a very knowledgeable man who gives solid lectures and structures his class well. He is also funny and caring, which makes him a good professor to get to know. This class wasn't totally inspirational or one of my top few, but it was very good and taught me a lot of relevant history.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Ariel is confusing in his lectures, doesn't stick to the syllabus, doesn't tell you how assignments are graded (if he even remembers to tell you what the assignments are), and is just generally rude. Regularly makes you watch movies that have nothing to do with the class and penalizes you if you're not there to watch them.

Professor Ariel gives lots of opportunities for extra credit and replies to emails very quickly. His lectures can be dull at times as he can get lost in his thoughts and go off on tangents, but you can tell he is very knowledgable and passionate about the subject. 3 short papers plus a couple more for extra credit.

Definitely the most boring professor I've ever had. He gets off topic almost every sentence and is just too dry to even follow. But watch out he does like to strip if you if he sees people falling asleep. Just don't sign up, you'll be happier without him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Ariel! He was lowkey a savage but was great. His lectures can be dry at times, but they were pretty informational. There were lots of interesting guest lecturers (and some not interesting ones) too. His tests were easy and readings didn't really matter. Basically, go to lecture and listen/take notes and you'll get an A

Dr. Ariel veered away from the syllabus to say the least. There was a required reading of at least one novel, usually more per class.  The readings were dense, the videos were boring, he was confusing, not to mention the 12 pg term paper. I would not recommend. He was also HATEFUL if you ever had to miss a class, even if you were sick.
Amazing!!
Very enthusiastic and knowledgeable.

Attendance is mandatory, but you really don't have to pay much attention as long as you look at the study guide before tests. Requires a lot of outside commitment - visiting synagogues and outside lectures. Ariel is funny and the TAs were helpful this semester.

Professor Ariel's class is a lot of work, but not overly hard. His lectures are somewhat unclear, but he tries. My issue is with the TAs. Don't expect to get anything graded back until a month after you submitted it. They are some of the laziest people on the planet.

Professor Ariel is very passionate about the subject. The workload isn't too bad. I learned a lot in RELI 72. If you are looking for an easy first-year seminar, do not take RELI 72. It's not that hard, but it is harder than most first-year seminars. I will say that Prof Ariel tends to interrupt people - even the guest lecturers. Don't take offense.
Boring lectures and exams are really difficult.

Dr. Hussong is one of the most genuine professors at this university. She provides a level of flexibility for her students that shows she really cares about what is going on outside of class. Most assignments are easy, the lectures are repeating the textbook chapter so just read at some point. Exams were a bit hard so be sure to do the study guides
I absolutely adore her. She's wickedly smart, loves her work, and is dedicated to making sure her students understand the "why" rather than the "what" of psychological research.
Really helpful professor and very nice person.
Prof. Andrews-Lee is by far one of the best professors at UNC! She is so smart and really cares about her students. The work is 100% manageable, the final and the midterm are very achievable.

Best polisci professor! So passionate about her work and super engaging. Almost too smart for us, so sometimes we leave her hanging when she asks us questions in class. Overall, highly recommend her class! 2 exams, 3 in-class writing assignments, and a final policy simulation. Meet with her in office hours if you want her to explain/help review.

Professor Andrews-Lee clearly cares for her students and their wellbeing both inside and outside of class. Lenient on attendance if you are sick, but make sure to show up as much as you can, as the exams are directly based on lecture slides and conversations held in class. Exams were easy if you studied the way she said. Lots of reading.

Prof Andrews-Lee is such a knowledgable professor on comparative politics and one of the nicest professors I've ever had. She truly wants her students to succeed and the assignments she chose for class are interesting. The midterms and finals are not too difficult and she makes her lectures really engaging! I would definitely recommend her class.

This course deals with Latin American politics, and it is clear that Professor Andrews-Lee is extremely knowledgeable about this topic. I also found it highly beneficial to speak with her during her office hours when I needed clarification on the course. She will suggest scheduling appointments so keep that in mind if you plan on speaking with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Andrews-Lee is one of the most kind and caring professors I've had. She is so great at making the material easily digestible. If I had any questions I found she was more than willing to answer them during office hours and over email, and often went the extra mile to help. If you review the slides before exams you should easily ace them.

Professor Andrews-Lee genuinely cares about her students and the topics she teaches. She's passionate and encourages students to participate regularly in discussions. No textbook, but there's still quite a bit of reading outside class. I learned so much, 10/10 would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Andrews-Lee is genuinely passionate about what she teaches, and she teaches in a way that's very easy to understand and relate to politics around the world. She's always open to answer questions and takes care to make sure everyone understands the material. Homework was very manageable.

French 105 is a VERY difficult class, especially if you have only taken HS French. Aubrey was very caring and gave great feedback. I learned a lot about French in this class, but again, French is hard. If you are interested in French, Aubrey is great, but if this is for credit, take it at community college.
This is a hard class, but Professor Lewis grades fairly. She's very sweet and doesn't cold call.

Aubrey was great! She really made an effort to teach us to speak the language, but didn't make us feel bad when we messed up. Was very accessible for office hours, and prepared us well for the tests. Would definitely take again!

The problem is really mainly just the structure of FREN105, Aubrey is really nice but the structure of the class means there isn't much opportunity for her to teach, its very self-taught and the textbook was kind of weird. There are a lot of different grades though so it's not only based on tests/quizzes.

tbh I think the problem with fren105 is the class itself, not the professor, but the model just felt a lot like she wasn't doing much teaching, and we had to just figure everything out on our own outside of class bc that's how fren105 is set up. the online textbook is not very helpful, either. duolingo was my best friend. she's very nice, though.

Aubrey is first and foremost a sweetheart. She does her best to make class engaging, but overall this course sucks. It's not her fault though, she's a TA who is stuck doing what UNC has decided Fren105 should do. The textbook sucks too. It's not unreasonable in terms of what you're expected to know, so while you have to self-teach, it's not awful

She's awesome! She bring real world experience as a planner, and always keeps the class engaged. This was a really fun class to understand various aspects of urban planning. There are two big projects though
Wonderful professor and great class content! Very thoughtful and understanding!

Really enjoyed this class and this professor. Class was not very challenging but graded by a few things. Would recommend for anyone interested in city planning and no experience alike. I was not familiar at all with anything about city planning and was really struggling to find a class for freshman but stumbled across this one and loved it.
Defended him until the final. Great lecturer and professor, and his midterms are very fair. Final dropped my grade two letter points. Avoid at all costs for analytical.
He makes the content so much harder than it needs to be

DO NOT be fooled by Austell's first-day friendliness. His lectures are disorganized, concepts are rushed, and he expects huge jumps without clear explanation. From his teaching the exams don't match lectures, leaving students confused. His reputation exists for a reason. LET THIS BE A SIGN TO TAKE ORGO ANYWHERE ELSE!!!

Took the honors section, loved Dr Austell but did bad in this class because in-class lectures are conceptual with NO problem solving. He directs you to weekly problem sets and textbook problems, I didn't find them helpful but I probably didn't work hard enough. He is kind and will replace your lowest midterm with the final, but the final is HARD.

Had Austell for 241H and it was a great experience!! He was super caring and always asking for ways that he could help us more.  Midterms weren't too difficult but the final was horrendous; he was generous with rounding final grades at the end of the semester (for honors section at least). This section also had 10 mandatory seminars to attend

DO NOT take this class with him! The material itself is not difficult, but when his students do well on one exam he deliberately makes the next exams infinitely harder and impossible. I had an A throughout the course and it already dropped multiple letter grades after my final. He clearly favors male students too and disrespects female students.
This man is evil, and he deletes RMP reviews do not take analytical with him!
Leaving hate

Todd is a great professor. His midterms are significantly easier than his extremely challenging finals. You have to take advantage of the midterms being easier or you won't succeed. Great professor, better person.

Worst professor ever! Lectures would not include any math practice, and the entire exam would be math problems. Was incredibly distracting during exams by talking and giving time updates. TOOK ROLL CALL MID FINAL!!! Has no respect for his students or desire for them to succeed. He created the final with the intention of the average being a 60.

Todd is an amazing guy and a better professor. Took Chem261 with him over the summer and he puts in tremendous amounts of effort to making sure his students succeed by hosting Q&A sessions and providing students with handouts similar to exam content. Exams were overall fair and manageable, especially the final. Would highly recommend Orgo with him.

DO NOT LET THE NAYSAYERS DISSUADE YOU FROM ORGO WITH AUSTELL!!!! Guy's a teachersaurus maturity-wise but you can't deny he knows the in's and out of the 261 curriculum. Put in the time, and I mean real time into the content, and you'll find Austell is not what the critics make of him. Expect Todd to make shared review sheets because he loves you.

AVOID!!! This professor intentionally makes the class as hard as it can be with NO mercy. I highly regret taking it. Literally made me think about dropping out. save yourself. tests are insanely hard, every question is a trick question, hard grader, I am convinced he hates students and wants us to fail. final average was 60 this year.

I withdrew from his class after he told me I was going to fail it. Orgo doesn't need to be as hard as he is making it the way he teaches makes no sense and confuses students. I was going to barely pass the class so I withdrew for my own mental health because he made me feel so bad about myself. Finishing at ncsu with an A, he wants you to suffer.

Todd is GOATED. Y'all give him too much hate. This class is low-key overhyped in its difficulty. He tells exactly what you will be tested on it so if you put in the work and study, you can make an A. Do all the handouts and practice problems. Find past exams, he pulls a lot of questions from those as well. In todd we trust

AVOID AT ALL COSTS!! While the content is interesting , Austell makes it so much more difficult than it would ever need to be. Half the class is filled with personal anecdotes and the content and exam matter is largely based around his own area of studies. Had a high B+ after midterms and final took me to C+ after weeks of all day studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Austell is an okay lecturer given the very dry course material. Midterms were very fair and reflected the content well, but the final was the most unfair test I've ever taken and was worth 33% (or 50% if using exam replacement) of overall grade. The average of the final was in the 60s with no curve and brought me from a high A to a C+.

Austell  requires you to buy a $70 note packet w/ no electronics in class and access a $100 online textbook/warm-up software that he says isn't even good for teaching. The lecture style is ok but can be hard to review sine lectures aren't recorded. Preparation for the midterms is fair with resources but the final was EXTREMELY hard w/ little prep
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Midterms were very fair. FINAL WAS PURE HELL. Got 2 A+s , 1 B on the midterms, got a D on the final. Actually insanely difficult and nothing like midterms (EChem especially). Absolutely ridiculous he didn't curve the final at all (even though he admitted he was dissatisfied with our performance).

Got an A on all the midterms, bombed the final and ended with a B+. Final was EXTREMELY hard compared to the midterms, but likely doable if you did all the practice problems. Really nice guy and makes it very clear what you will be tested on (with the exception of the final). His teaching style isn't for everybody, but he tries to be helpful.
todd is a nice person but some things he does is annoying. chem 241 is a very boring class and the midterms are
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: bro oh my god don't take this class dude makes you buy a $100 online program for a e-textbook (which he says teaches you wrong) and to do pre class assignments. then makes you buy ~$70 of notes from student stores and then on top of that you have to buy an iclicker for participation. Taught final unit in four days and made the final super hard

This class is hard. The midterms are actually pretty fair, but the final was genuinely absurd. It is doable though, if you take the time to do the practice problems and truly understand the concepts, you will be fine. The lectures could be improved upon, I wish Austell would actually go over problems in class. Better to take directly after CHEM 102
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grades on exams were 98, 100, and 100, AQI was 100 too. Made a 65 on the final. Emailed him about it and turns out I just bombed it so if you see the other reviews around the time of this one then they bombed it too according to Austell. Final was rough and possibly the hardest exam I have taken my entire educational career. Cool guy otherwise tho.

One of the worst professors I've had at UNC. He makes lectures seem easy, but barely teaches anything that is on the exam. He doesn't post the answers to any practice problems. I went into the final with an A- and finished with a C+. He acts extremely friendly in class but is very condescending in person. I would avoid Austell if you can.
Had a 98 going into the final and ended with a B+. Final was nothing like the midterms. No curve no empathy…

241 is not the most interesting class but Todd makes the lectures interesting and digestable. He's a great lecturer who explains concepts very well. The midterms were not to difficult and given a generous buffer, however the final was pretty difficult but doable. Watch out, no partial credit. If you do a lot of practice problems you'll do fine

Extremely unorganized and it made the class so much harder than it needed to be. Nice guy, bad lecturer and didn't explain content well at all. Midterms weren't bad if you studied but the final was genuinely terrible. I wish I listened when everyone said not to take this professor. Made the class so much harder than it needed to be

Austell is a great professor who receives a lot of hate because his course is difficult. Be ready to do A LOT of work. This work isn't necessarily required but if you want to do well you need to read the textbook on your own and do practice problems on your own. Austell makes this very clear and encourages students regularly to do this.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: dont bother going to lectures. dude talks about swamp water
Great lecturer but that's about it. I loved going to his lectures but his exams are very difficult and they require a lot of out of class preperation. The online textbook is also pretty expensive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Todd is a pretty engaging lecturer, but that's it. He makes you buy >$100 worth of his own course notes. He doesn't release any ANSWER KEYS which made exams very hard to study for. The midterms weren't bad but the final was ungodly hard. One time a student fell asleep and he stomped on his desk which is insane to me.

There is no doubt that Todd is a great guy. I enjoyed his lectures and he is very clear about his expectations and what content you'll be tested on. However, he does not give ANY partial credit on exams which feels harsh for the complex titrations he will give you. I would avoid if you aren't a chem major/aren't interested in analytical chem.

Dr. Austell is a wonderful, hilarious man who clearly likes teaching. Analytical is a dull subject if you're not really into chemistry, but it was certainly manageable and his expectations are very clear. Having taken 5 UNC chem classes before this one, it didn't phase me as much as it might have had I taken it earlier. Lock in and you'll do fine.

Todd receives a lot of criticism. This is from people who shouldn't be chem majors. If you aren't willing to put in the work you will not like Todd. Todd is a genius and he is so dedicated to the department and every one of his students. Thank you for sharing my love for chemistry and being the weed out prof that UNC needs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Exams are tough, but Austell is the GOAT. I feel like he's the best STEM teacher I've had at UNC so far. Explains complex topics very and is very fair. Also had him for 241. If you are planning on taking the MCAT/DAT, I would recommend taking Austell. Make sure to read the textbook before class.

Todd is a great professor. In Chem 102H, he understands that everyone in the class has credit for 101 and 102. Because of this, he makes sure that everyone will get an A or B in the class. There was a good amount of homework in the class, but it is feasible especially if you read the textbook. He is a good teacher and cares for his students.
His class was my favorite of the semester, he made Chemistry interesting and cared a lot about us inside and out of the classroom

Orgo is a tough class. If you want to do well YOU need to do the work. Practice, practice, practice. Austell is a wonderful lecturer, very passionate about chem and really wants you to succeed. Lots of Q&A sessions to answer questions, but you have to choose to go to them. There is only so much he can do to help if you dont put in the work yourself

Analytical is actually a pretty interesting class, but I would honestly recommend taking it with any other professor if possible. Midterms are pretty doable if you have access to previous exams, however, can seem pretty hard if not. The textbook used also isn't the greatest.

I love Todd! He was always so sweet to us and made sure we understood all the topics he was teaching. Lectures were great and always had us well-prepared for exams. The final was a bit hard, but the class was curved really nice and the lowest you could get was a B-. The class does have quite a bit of homework, but it helps you out in the long run!

I thought Professor Austell did a decent job explaining content in the lecture slides and keeping the lecture engaging. The exams most closely reflected the problems in the workbook so do all the possible assigned practice problems in both the workbook and textbook.

The UNC Chemistry GOAT. Todd is an institution and you either love him or hate him and I can absolutely say I love him. So engaging and caring. Made me excited for 8AM Orgo! Not easy! I'm upset I probably won't get the pleasure of taking another class with him. Orgo is his teaching specialty and if you get a chance to take it with him, do it.

I absolutely loved taking orgo with Austell this semester. Incredibly engaging for an 8am, hilarious, and taught the course content incredibly well. Textbook is very helpful for understanding content. Exams are very fair if you take the time to understand the "why" behind it all instead of strict memorization. Cannot recommend him enough.

Being my first semester, CHEM 102H was a great launchpad into what the school has to offer, especially in the chemistry department. We got to interview a chemistry professor, tour various facilities on campus, and had multiple guest speakers visit our class. I didn't find the content that difficult and we were guaranteed a B- or above. Fun class!

Austell gives ok lectures but is very unhelpful outside class. Expect to spend all your free time on practice if you want to survive this course.
Professors try to grade 500+ tests all in one day which results in grade errors more often than not, and the way regrade process is set up getting a correction is hard even for obvious answer key matches.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: AVOID taking CHEM 261 with Todd as he makes the tests extremely hard and not reflective of class content. He is not helpful in office hours and makes you feel dumb instead of helping you to understand the material. Organic is hard enough as it is and Todd goes out of his way to make sure to set you up for failure.

This class was honestly relatively doable if you have access to previous notes/exams and understand the format. However, the final is considerably more challenging and I don't think Austell does a great job of setting up students for success on it. If possible, I would advise taking this class with someone else!

Todd is a very caring & knowledgeable man. No laptops, only notebooks/flat tablets. iClickers. If you prefer active writing and talking, this is the professor for you. Handouts & practice exams are EXCELLENT exam prep, MANY Q&As. Final much harder than midterms. He tries very hard to be accessible to everyone. My fav chem course I've taken here.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Austell is super communicative, friendly, and wants us to succeed! Such a kind professor. He sometimes goes on tangents, but that makes class enjoyable lol. Fair amount of work for a Chem 102 class! Would reccomend!

Professor Austell has a unique teaching style that works if you're willing to put in the effort. Exams can be tough, but he prepares you well. For study prep, I found unstuckstudy AI and the textbook really helpful.

DO NOT TAKE AT ALL COSTS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Dr. Austell acts like he is your friend but will turn around and send the meanest emails known to man. His tests are ridiculously difficult and not curved (a few extra point opportunities that barely help your overall score on the exam). He is rude to ARS students and not accommodating.
Austell is a great teacher who really cares about his students. His assignments and exams were hard, which is expected in any orgo class, but fair.
Austell has a unique style of teaching without technology, but it works if you are willing to work with it. His exams are fair and he prepares you pretty well not really many surprises.

Todd is a great lecturer and cares for his students. However, this goes out the window when you consider his lack of partial credit on extremely long titration problems.Sig figs will cause you to lose full credit. I literally just lost 2 points on my test for forgetting a zero. The final was the hardest exam ive taken in my entire life

Austell's exams were notoriously more difficult than Lockett's exams, and students in Austell's class suffered A LOT more than Lockett's class, so I definitely suggest taking it with Lockett if possible. However, Austell is super nice and hilarious - caring about his students, just don't take Analytical Chem with him if possible.

Fast pace in lectures. Expects you to know gen chem stuff well. Tests are hard. Wrong sig fig = wrong answer. Offers extra credit but quite minimal compared to the overall grades. Offers lots of practice problems but doesn't release keys. You must go to Q&A sessions for uncertain questions.
In Todd We Trust

Todd is a pretty solid lecturer. As someone who hates notetaking, I also found the note packets useful. However, the difficulty of exams was all over the place. I did poorly on exam 1, aced exams 2 and 3, and got my worst grade ever on the final. STUDY HARD. I should've received a lower grade, but he must've curved the final without telling us.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Todd isn't a bad prof and I thought that the first 90% of this class was actually pretty great-I was getting A's and B's on the midterms, but the final was insanely difficult and dropped my grade by an entire letter.  He also didn't teach sensors until the last day of class (but they were on the lab final which we had taken the week prior???)
The midterms were not too bad and were reasonable but the final was awful. I got As and B on the midterms but the final dropped my grade to a C+
Good for 102H, only gives B- though A grades for this class. No curves on exams but tests out of over 100pts so you can get Qs wrong and still do well. Funny guy, recommended!

Analytical Chem is not Todd's strong suit and he openly admits it if you take orgo with him. You have to practice the computations in class A LOT if you want to be ready for his exams where the questions can range from doable to a question forged in the depths of hell. Personally, I liked his lectures but he focuses a lot on theory instead of math.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Makes you buy notes pack that you have to use to have any shot at succeeding and does not allow any devices. Offers no partial credit on extremely arduous exams, but has a curve and grade replacement where exam portion can replace midterm score. Inconsistent grading between TAs creates exam score discrepancies that he refuses to fix.
