Participation does matter, but he curates a very low-stakes environment and is very kind and patient with students.

This prof is awesome! I had him for 203, and he is simply the nicest professor I've ever had. Extremely understanding of circumstances and is always there to help. The class structure is very standardized due to the nature of beginner level Spanish courses. But overall I would very much recommend taking 203 with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really great guy. His first semester here at UNC and rocked it. He was so nice but 203 is tough. Pop quizzes (that he warned you about) and then just the conjugations are hard. Only Spanish talking in class for all 203 courses. But Prof. was awesome, highly recommend

Benjamin Romero-Salado was an incredible professor. He was hilarious in class and taught the spanish language clearly with fun and applicable practice. He gets to know you as a student, and it is very clear that he wants each student to succeed. Just pull your weight! Participation really helps you and your grade!!

This guy is the GOAT. As to both his first and my first experience at UNC Chapel Hill, Dr. Salado did an amazing job teaching Span 203. He genuinely cares about each of his students and wants them to excel in not only the class, but the language as a whole. Participation does matter, and Dr. Salado notices and appreciates each time that you do.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Salado is very kind and truly cares about your education. There's a lot of homework, but it's fairly manageable, and the assignments are really simple. We did a lot of group activities in class but it helps you with better speaking. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He was a fantastic and charismatic lecturer. He was very patient with everyone's Spanish ability. Fun class overall and it was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I had a really good time in his class! He had an engaging way of approaching the material and his class is very well-structured. Very reliable with grading/getting our assignments back to us and assigned us interesting projects throughout the semester. A challenging class, but one of the most unique and cool ones I've taken at UNC!

The best Spanish teacher I have ever had. The course itself is pretty easy if you took Spanish in high school, but there are some new concepts that Benjamín thoroughly reviewed and created fun and interactive lessons. The class is pretty small and he does a lot of partner work (sometimes random partners sometimes you get to choose). Participate!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: CLAS241*. He does NOT give you the full time to take written exams. Also, it seems he wants students to give 120%, but in terms of being helpful and accommodating for students, it feels he only gives 70%. if he likes you, yay! if he doesn't, go ahead and drop.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Baroud is an amazing storyteller and professor. I got a B and still would take the class again because of how well he taught the course.

Prof. Baroud is easily one of my favorite professors. His class was immensely difficult (300 pages of dry, dense reading each week; could not bullshit your way through exams), but his grading was fair and he forces you to grow as a thinker/reader. He's scary (and maybe a bit snarky) at first, but he is super approachable in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if you want to sit by, skip the readings, and hope you'll get a good grade. Professor Baroud is an amazing professor, extremely intelligent, and loves the Roman Empire. Highly recommend going to office hours, as he wants to know every student personally. If you are willing to go a little crazy, then this is the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Quite literally the most engaging and thought provoking lectures I've ever heard. He's an incredibly knowledgable and charismatic professor. Main downside of the class are the reading assignments, almost too lengthy to handle. If you show up to all the lectures, do the readings, and ask questions, you'll do well. I wish I could take CLAS122 again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof is very passionate, intelligent and gives good lectures. I wouldn't recommend this class as a gen ed unless you actually like the Romans and classics. Readings are long and confusing ~150-200 pages a week but he explains the readings in class. Tests were graded kinda harsh but office hours helped me improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Maintaining a GPA of 4.0 for four years and screwed up in this class. Thank you Prof.
DO NOT take this class for gen ed. If you are a stem dude like me, your GPA will plummet pretty soon.

***THIS REVIEW IS FOR CLAS-122***

Dr. Baroud is one of the most intelligent and insightful professors I have had here at UNC. While the readings can be long, and the exams difficult, his amazing lectures make it all worth it. He is a passionate and charismatic professor who is never terribly unreasonable, and he knows his stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: **this review is for WGST/CLAS 241** Prof Baroud was truly one of my favorite professors I've ever had. I was nervous about taking a women's studies class with a male teacher but he exceeded all my expectations. He is so ntelligent and cares about the material. He values students' questions/opinions. His exams were not too difficult if you studied.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment:
Read his other reviews at NYC -> they are aptly complimentary. 
Baroud has been my favourite prof in nearly 3 years of university. His lecturing/teaching is incredibly good, he clearly has a natural interest in the work. My Ancient Roman Empire class with him was incredibly enjoyable. Check out his office hours; interesting in conversation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Her lectures are often a bit monotonous, her tests are incredibly difficult, and large portions of your grade rely on group projects. Arguably the most engaging and easy to understand class of the semester was the day our TA taught the lesson. Also 2 points are taken off your semester grade for every class you miss starting day one. Good otherwise.

2 tests, 4 individual assignments, and 4 group assignments ending with the final research project. Tests were moderately difficult; use flashcards for vocab and practice quizzes for question style. Focused mostly on application. No final, just comment on other projects. Great instructor, super experienced and friendly if you showed you cared.

Prof. Entwisle is nice, but she will get mad if ur on ur phone. The class is okay, basically one big group project the whole semester and the grading criteria for it is unclear, and if u miss a class its 2 pts off ur overall grade. It was not hard to get a B+ or an A, but only take this if ur interested in the subject, or ur gonna be really bored.

Barbara is VERY knowledgeable, but she occasionally was condescending when speaking to students. Her feedback was great and fair, but sometimes grading was harsh. Overall not bad, but I wouldn't choose to take her again.

Barbara is amazing and clearly knows what she's talking about. The class was pretty easy, there were clear rubrics for everything, and you learn a lot about research processes. Exams were a bit tricky with vague study guides, but its fine cause you can ace everything else. Lots of group work, so depending on your group you may have more work.

Prof Entwisle can be a good prof at times but sometimes it feels like she has 0 humanity. There were several times people expressed concerns and she seemed like she couldn't care less. We had two tests that were less than 10% of our grade and I failed both and still got out with a B. Easy B to pass but no one felt great about tests.

Professor Entwisle was very knowledgeable about the subject. The individual assignments were easy and graded fairly, but the semester-long group project was somewhat difficult and graded harshly. Also, the multiple choice questions on the tests were unnecessary difficult.

It is evident that Dr. Entwisle knows her stuff and is passionate about the course. TA gave very vague feedback which was frustrating. Odd grade scale (ex. a test is 8 points). Tests are difficult. She is very understanding about attendance as long as you communicate. The course is tough but Barbara really cares.

Assignments were generally easy to complete and the material wasn't hard but the exams felt like you were set up to fail. There wasn't any one I spoke to who felt confident about the exams so no matter how much you study, its not going to work out. Also the group projects felt repetitive.

Prof Entwisle makes class easy enough, but the big project we worked on all semester was broken into small assignments that felt repetitive. No tests or quizzes though, just open-note in-class assessments, which was great.

Prof. Entwisle entirely re-structured the class once COVID started. There were no exams, quizzes, etc - only small individual assignments and a large group project that spanned over about half the semester. Participation is important. Overall I really liked the way the class was designed for online learning and would highly rec this course.

Her classes are very structured and you can tell she has done this for many years. She is clear about what we are learning and explains concepts well. The vocab quizzes are really easy and straightforward, but you will need to study well for tests. She is a very kind and competent teacher - not sure what others are saying.

She doesn't give tell you much about what's on exams. Exams cover things not always covered in class. Exams have test corrections, but you need them because typically people make in the 70s for her exams without test corrections. Class is a little boring, but just show up.
Professor Entwisle is very knowledgeable, but the class got a little boring at times. This seminar on American universities definitely didn't feel like a sociology class.
Go to a fortune teller to figure out what reasons she'll take off points for because it won't be stated on the rubric. Oh, also a billion points off for grammar. Take with someone else.

never hated myself more in this class. she assigns a lot of work each week and disregards the fact that we are students with other classes. she changes assignments halfway through the deadline, takes off loads of points for minor errors. I highly recommend taking a different professor if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Took her a different semester and still haunts me. Busy work every week, very condescending, has favorites, seems like one to date a student ngl
Literally don't take her if you want to stay sane. And if you take her, be ready to lose 50 points without her giving any feedback on why
I had her in a past semester--she's just not very inviting or engaging. Lots of busy work, curses, and a really strict grader. Overall, my least favorite class at UNC

So many projects and short deadlines. Super strict grader (you WILL get loads of points off for grammar), makes you go into random communities to do a walk audit (almost attacked by homeless people), gets annoyed when you ask questions, and has a fetish for the baseball dudes.
Very spiteful person.

Dr. Courtney was great! She really values participation and a good relationship with her will only benefit you. She wants you to succeed and is always eager to answer questions and give feedback. The class itself is heavily centered around group work but it's not too terrible. She gave extra credit and saved my grade even after I bombed the final.

Very confusing professor, gets aggravated with students when they ask questions. She is quick to judge her students and will hold grudges against an individual when she feels they ask annoying questions or takes offense when a student tries to explain why they are struggling and seeks help. She takes it as an attack on her teaching. She also curses

I hate group projects but that's not on her. This class is an easy A and she wants you to learn a lot. There are occasional homeworks but can be pretty tedious. I feel like some people may find her confusing but thats on them for messing around during class. She's a great prof

Love love love Dr. Chanon, she is the best!! I enjoyed her class so much, and it's genuinely been one of my favorite classes I've taken. She puts in a lot of effort into making it such a great experience.

I would love to say this is an awful class to get off her waitlists lol, but Dr. Chanon is an amazing professor. She's incredibly kind and personable and learns everyone's name, and her lectures are fun to attend. This class was mainly group project focused with that taking the place of the final, which I really enjoyed. 20/10 reccomend Dr. Chanon.
Dr. Chanon's lectures were really engaging, and she had a lot of demos that made class more fun. She also made the content easy to understand.

I love Vicki down! Super kind and cracked me up all semester. She learns everyone's names and her in-class participation is engaging and solidifies concepts. Exams are pretty straightforward, 2 homework drops, and quizzes that you can take until you get a 100. You can also miss 6 classes which is nice. Very easy class and an excellent prof.

Dr. Chanon is just a great professor. Super kind and enjoyable to be in class with. She has a weird attendance policy with the use of flashcards to answer in class questions and then you turn in the flashcard the same day so you will have to be ok with that. She'll learn everyone's names so that's nice.

One of my favorite professors I've had at UNC! Her lectures are very engaging including fun activities to understand the content. Her exams are very straightforward and she also offers a few extra credit opportunities. Also, one exam is dropped, and you can take the quizzes as many times as you want. I genuinely enjoyed going to her class :)

Dr. Chanon genuinely cares about her students, making an effort to know everyone's name, and she also makes class enjoyable to attend. There are a ton of interesting demonstrations that make lectures fun, and her grading scale is super chill. 3 exams, 1 dropped, weekly homework that will get full credit if completed, and the final.

I absolutely adore Dr. Chanon! She's hilarious and gets to know every student in her class (and our lecture was definitely more than 50 people)! She's really great about posting slideshows and recordings! Number one tip is to fill out the outlines for learning checks! The lowest learning check is dropped! Homeworks are pretty easy too!
Nice professor but the learning checks were hard for me and there was a lot of content on each one

LOVE HER super nice she learned everyone's name in a 100+ lecture, exams were super easy, attendance is mandatory via notecards you write on during class but for completion, lets you review exams in office hours, lectures recorded, hw one a week but rly easy, take her!!

AVOID AT ALL COST! Her teaching style was so confusing and inconsistent and never align with the textbook content order.  I spent most of my time just figuring out where the content she taught on the textbook. Her learning checks were one of the hardest STEM exam I have at UNC without any practice problem sets. DO NOT TAKE. SAVE YOUR GPA.

I loved going to this class because of Dr. Chanon. She is absolutely hilarious and so much fun to listen to. I really enjoyed the activities we did in class, they made the lectures engaging even when the content could be dull. Dr. Chanon, on the other hand, is never, ever dull. Also you get four absences, two homeworks, and one midterm dropped!

The class is super chill—graded based on weekly homework, a few quizzes, and a group project (you get to pick your group). Chanon is awesome. This is my third class with her and I honestly have nothing bad to say. She even says everyone should get an A.

Dr. Chanon was an amazing professor, probably one of the best I've had at UNC. She makes an effort to learn every students name (even in a class of over 100 students), is very understanding, and makes lectures fun. Homework and quizzes are guaranteed 100s, and the midterms and finals are easy. As long as you pay attention and try, you'll be fine.

dr chanon is so sweet, yes this class is kinda difficult, but as long as you put the work into it, you'll def do good, if you study hard for the final, you'll get an A, weekly hws, take home quizzes, 21/25 lectures need to be attended, 1 quiz and learning check is dropped, 2 hws are also dropped, def take it w her.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Chanon is so funny and upbeat! Attendance matters a lot and is mostly done by using notecards and answering questions. She is super knowledgable and honestly this class is very easy and straight forward especially if you prior knowledge of the nervous system and actually come to class.

Dr. Chanon is the Gold-Standard. Her lectures are engaging, grading criteria is clear & fair, & she gives you every opportunity to succeed. She cares about her students & will learn your name in a class of 200 students. I plan to take every class I can with her, and I recommend you do, too! She's the type of professor that changes students' lives.

Chanon is amazing, take her if you can! She genuinely cares about students understanding the material, not just memorizing it. Lots of opportunities to get your grade up and clear grading criteria. Really interesting lectures that are interactive and get you invested in the material.

Dr. Chanon was AMAZING. I was nervous for the class since I didn't think it'd be my strong suit, but she made it easy to learn and ask questions. Lectures are great and she also does a lot of helpful review. Attendance is technically mandatory but you get like 6 free absences. Tests are low-stakes and all multiple choice. Plus she's funny and nice!

Dr. Chanon is amazing. She structures grading so that you have wiggle room. Her lectures are incredibly entertaining with lots of activities. Her review for exams are very helpful. As long as you show up and put in effort you will do great. She's also super nice and hilarious.

Chanon is one of the best professors I have had at UNC. She learned everyone's names in an over 100 person class and made an effort to connect. She gave us countless opportunities to up our grade and class was so engaging. I could not recommend a class more!!!!

Dr. Chanon is an awesome professor! She really cares about you and made an effort to learn my name in a classroom of hundreds of students. Her classes were really engaging and helped you learn the material. The learning checks (midterms) and final were easy. Homework and quizzes are a guaranteed 100.

the content is medium/difficult and the exams are tricky, but she is easy to talk to and is more than willing to meet to help you understand the content. Even though the exams are tricky, there is a lot of flexibility in the grading and many opportunities to improve your grade! She's really engaging and overall a fun person!

Easily one of my favorite professors and classes! She makes an effort to learn your name, even among so many students, and she does a lot of in class activities to keep you engaged. She gives cumulative quizzes in between unit exams that you can take as many times as you want to get a 100, so getting a good grade is really attainable.

This was my third class with Dr. Chanon, and it was the easiest class I have taken of hers.  She made it easy for everyone to get an A (she literally said everyone should get an A in this class).  Half of your grade can easily be a 100 with HW and attendance.  Quizzes have simple questions, and she allows retakes.  Group project was fun too.

Dr. Chanon is the absolute best professor! She is so organized and considerate of students, making it really easy to manage her class. This 490 was on Animal Sensation/Perception which is a new class and it was super interesting. Highly recommend!

Dr. Chanon was one of my favorite professors this semester! The class structure involves attending class, taking notes, weekly quizzes, and 3 exams. You can drop your lowest scores in attendance, quizzes, and exams! She is super engaging and made cognitive psychology fun. The exams were super straightforward and reasonable.
Dr. Chanon is amazing!! I genuinely learned so much and enjoyed doing it. She's pretty lenient in terms of attendance/exam grades so it's not difficult to get a good grade with minimal effort.

This was my 2nd class with Dr. Chanon, but first online class with her over the summer.  Class was organized well, and there was plenty of wiggle room for participation.  Assignments and LCs were same difficulty, maybe a bit easier than her in-person class.  Would recommend any class with Chanon

Dr. Chanon is AMAZING. She tries very hard to make her lectures interactive so that students can relate to the information that she is teaching. Despite the lecture hall being massive, she makes an effort to put a face to every name, and is there for her students to help them. All tests are based entirely on lectures, which are recorded.

Awesome, Awesome, Awesome! This class has a lot of content but she makes learning easier and fun (she is so funny)! There is HW, 2 online quizzes (can retake many times), 3 tests (one dropped), and a final! The exams were not terrible, as long as you take good notes and do the learning objectives/outlines. The final was easier than her tests! DO IT

Awesome Professor! Truly cares about her students. She learned all the names for a 100 or so person class. There are 3 exams and one is dropped! As well, as a final that was somewhat easier than the other exams! This has been one of my favorite classes at UNC, and I feel like I learned a lot!

Dr. Chanon is amazing! Her grading is based off HW assignments, 2 cumulative quizzes (which you can retake to get a 100!), exams, and a final! Her exams were pretty straightforward as long as you took note of important things she says in class and look over the learning objectives. She is also really funny and learned all of our names! Not a hard A

The absolute best professor I've had at UNC! Dr. Chanon is so caring and very accessible, definitely a teacher to the core. She and the TAs provide plenty of review materials, and the homework assignments aren't too demanding. Her grading criteria are also very clear and there's a lot of flexibility. Very funny, highly respected, overall 10/10!

Love Vicki! She is so kind and hilarious in class. The homework and tests are pretty easy. I would recommend buying the book (if you really want it), taking pictures of all the pages, and then returning it for all your money back at the UNC Student Store. Textbook pretty much goes over everything in class - so maybe I'm just extra.

Dr. Chanon is amazing! She's so sweet, and she tries her best to get to know everyone in the class.  Content was fun, and all assignments were chill.  She has a nice grading system; you can drop lowest midterm and 2 HWs.  HW was graded nicely.  The final was easier compared to midterms/LCs.  Make sure to study a bit. We got 1 point EC for final.

I thought it was a tough class content-wise, especially compared to her PSYC 230 class. But, Dr. Chanon still has teaching down to a science and is an engaging lecturer. Her grading system is incredibly reasonable too, just make sure you really put in the work for the exams. The final is easy compared to them!
Every lecture was incredibly engaging and she taught the material really well. They were also recorded and posted if you missed a day. Really fair tests too.

She was such a caring professor and I rly want to take another class with her before I graduate! She learned everyone's names (and our class is over 100 people)!! It's a lot of material, but she makes it manageable for sure!

Dr. Chanon is my favorite professor so far at UNC. She cares so much about her students and responds to emails very quickly. Her grading system is very forgiving. Her exams are very straight forward. Plus, she practically does reviews every day. She also makes the lectures interesting by making what we learned relatable. Highly recommend!!!

Professor Chanon is one of the best professors ever. She learned all her ~100 students' names within the first few weeks of class. Her lectures are well-organized, engaging, and fun. Cognitive Psychology requires lots of memorization, but she makes it durable for her students. I have so many good things to say about her. Highly recommend!

I loved this course! The content was interesting and Dr. Chanon is an amazing lecturer! She really wants all her students to succeed. She was more than fair with all assignments. The workload was manageable. I recommend this class to anybody.

Dr. Chanon is one of the best professors at UNC. She is positive and encouraging toward her students and clearly wants to see everyone succeed. Her tests are pretty straightforward and the posted recorded lectures are great for studying. She was super understanding and flexible with attendance and assignment grading.

Professor Chanon is really kind and caring. The material wasn't that bad, but she teaches it very well. There are 3 exams but 1 is dropped, and they are pretty easy. As long as you pay attention in class and do the assignments, you will get an A.

Dr. Chanon is super sweet and she teaches the material very well. I felt like I actually learned a lot from her class. You have easy homework due every Friday, 3 exams (1 is dropped), and a few quizzes but you can use your notes. The material is a little hard, but she explains in very well. Tests are fair.

I loved Dr. Chanon! She's super passionate about neuroscience and she was always ready to answer our questions. The workload was very manageable and the tests were fair. She cares a lot about her students and consistently updates us about the class. Make sure to keep up with the content! Definitely take this class with Dr. Chanon, she's the best!

One of the best at UNC! The way she set up her class was perfect. I feel like I genuinely learnt a lot from the class- the material stuck all semester. Content is cool and she gives great lectures. The 3 tests are kinda challenging but you drop one and the final is easy in comparison. You can miss up to 6 classes without penalty but should catch up

Professor Chanon is a great professor. Textbook was not required for the course and lectures covered all the material that we were tested on. Chanon made this course very stress free and her learning checks were great preparation for the final. She sets this class up for your success and it is easy to pass if you put in the effort!

Dr. Chanon is so incredible it makes me emotional. In a way, I literally felt like her office was a safe space for me because of how caring and helpful she was. She has kids which I think helps her have even more of a heart for college students & their well-being. Her lectures are amazing, the class is very organized, and she is so accessible!

Dr. Chanon is super sweet. The class was not super difficult so long as you study (especially for the learning checks!) The unique part of this class is the UX BeAM project, which while tedious at times was pretty cool to do. There is pretty regular homework, but you don't necessarily have to read the book. Be sure to study the learning goals!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She was great! It was online and asynchronous, but I still felt very engaged with the class. She also made the material super easy to understand. I have no complaints about her or this class!

Professor Chanon is funny and so relatable. She is also very caring. Her exams are easy and she accommodates her students well. I would without a doubt take more classes with her, she makes the content very interesting and has her students engage in a way that actually helps.The class content is hard at times but her exams are easy and minimal work

Dr. Chanon truly gives students all the guidance and materials we need to succeed in her class. Her class is well organized, you have decent cushioning for your grades, and most importantly, she's a great lecturer and is really good at breaking down concepts in easy to understand language.

I love Dr. Chanon so much I would give her my first born child. The material is not easy but she makes it so understandable and her exams are a direct reflection of what is taught. Amazing professor and incredibly helpful to anyone wanting to get into research. Take her for a class if you can!

Dr. Chanon is an amazing professor. She gives you exactly what information you need to know for the exams. If you miss class, you can still get participation credit and lectures are posted online, so that was very accommodating. She genuinely wants you to learn and has everything structured very well. You will definitely get an A if you study well!
Vicki Chanon is wonderful. This class was a bit of work (studying, the usual) but she is very flexible with having online lectures posted and participation credit.

Fantastic prof. I highly recommend her for Learning. She is a veteran and has teaching down to a science. She is also fun, pleasant, and makes lectures highly interactive. The class was also not challenging, if that's your thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Most organized class I have ever taken. 100% take this class if you can and if not take it the semester after. Dr. Chanon is an amazing lecturer and is SO understanding and genuinely cares. Anybody can take this class and do well, she has it structured so amazingly. I always knew my grades and always felt supported.

Dr. Chanon's a fantastic instructor. This course specifically is laid out well and all of the assignments are presented on a very easy-to-grasp schedule. Dr. Chanon teaches with an enthusiasm and clear interest in the material that makes it easy to be interested yourself. Highly recommend taking a class or two with her!

The absolute epitome of what a professor should be! The entire class is structured so that you know exactly what to expect, when assignments are due, how assignments need to be done, what you REALLY need to know for the exams, and all of that is laid out in the least stressful way possible! Dr. Chanon actually cares unlike most professors at UNC.

Dr. Chanon is absolutely amazing! Not only was the content and the demos so interesting but also very accommodating as well. She is very supportive and pushes you to do your very best! If you are stem, consider majoring in neuroscience and take her!!!

Professor Chanon's NSCI 225 class is an example of a remote async class done right. She was accessible all semester, was great with feedback, never blindsided us with exam questions, and had forgiving grading policies. Considering that this is a demo-heavy class, it's probably the toughest type of class to do remotely, but she did incredibly well.

Ive had Dr. Chanon for nsci 222,225 and now 330. I LOVED this class. Well made asynchronous lessons, fair quizzes/learning checks, extra credit and test corrections, and a super fun human centered design project with the makerspaces. Dr. Chanon is a phenomenal teacher and PSYC 330 was an awesome class

I normally don't like async courses but this one (cog sci) was outstanding. Dr. Chanon builds in so many opportunities for active learning into class and was very organized with course content, even making a due date list on Sakai. Really enjoyed the diverse guest speakers, makerspace UX project, group activities and cool readings. Take Dr. Chanon!

Dr. Chanon is awesome! Her lectures are very engaging, and she is an incredibly reasonable grader. The textbook is optional, and you are graded on attendance, weekly homework assignment, non-cumulative quizzes, cumulative quizzes (can take more than once), and the cumulative final. Her class is designed to really help you learn the material!

Knows how to teach in a pandemic and is intentional about assigning easy work that supplements core concepts. Open note tests/quizzes with lax time limits. Easy participation questions and homework assignments. Allows flexibility by letting your drop a certain number of assignments. Very effective teacher who is passionate about her work.

Dr. Channon was the only professor I had who truly understood and respected the fact that we are in a pandemic. Her lectures were all recorded and to get participation credit you had to answer a couple of questions throughout the lectures. Her quizzes and exams were open-note and you could take her quizzes many times to get 100.

Chanon is a GEM! I absolutely love her. She has such a nice personality and she really cares about her students. I wish we weren't online this semester because I would've really enjoyed having her in person. Exams/quizzes are open-note so that takes the pressure off, but the info you learn is very interesting and she makes it easy to understand!
She's simply the most fantastic online instructor I've had at UNC yet, and I'm sure her in person class would be much of the same. Absolutely recommended, take NSCI225 with her!

Dr. Chanon is amazing! She is knowledgable and incredibly caring. Her tests, and her class overall, are incredibly fair. Her online class flows really well and is super easy to keep up with. All assignments build off of each other and are meant to help you solidify the material. 10/10 recommend any class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had her before in psyc 330. both classes are super easy and interesting. Her classes do overlap somewhat but that is to be expected with the content. Great lecturer and super engaging. Study a little bit and you'll do great. 10/10

Dr. Chanon is a great professor especially given the circumstances. However, the online class felt like a lot of busy work. Homework was often barely related to the content or seemed silly. The due dates for homework were also a little inconsistent, so make sure you double check due dates. Overall she was super nice and the class was fine.

Dr. Channon is an AMAZING professor and person! She has a kind heart and made my first semester at UNC the best it could be considering COVID. Her online lectures is structured beautifully and I cannot stress how fair of professor she is. I wish I had her for in person to know her more since she is my favorite prof at UNC. I will miss her def :(

I adore Professor Chanon, and I'm trying so hard to get another class with her, but they're all full. Her lectures are really interesting and interactive. She has a very forgiving grading and attendance policy. She also responds quickly to emails, and makes a good effort to get to know students -- even in large lecture halls. Would def recommend.

This was online, but her Sakai site was beautifully done and her lectures were clear, interactive, and accessible. It was obvious that she put a ton of care into making sure that we still got a great learning experience. This is a nerdy thing to say, but the class was... can I even say that it was too easy? I felt like I could have learned more.

Dr. Channon is amazing! Her tests are very fair (+1 is dropped) and her lectures are enjoyable. She was very understanding and organized when we moved to online learning, as she was in the classroom. She makes an effort to know everyones name and encourages participation. 222/225/230 are great classes and I recommend Dr. Channon for them!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Chanon is amazing as a person and a professor. She is very accessible outside of class too, but honestly if you pay attention in lectures and take good notes and study, you should be fine. She never tries to trick you on exams and while there is some homework, they're usually easy while also helping you learn. 10/10 would recommend.
Chanon is an absolute gem!! One of the sweetest professors I've had at UNC. PSYC 230 was an easy A and is so so interesting. 10/10 recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Chanon is amazing!! I had her for NSCI 225 and PSYC 230. Very clear in what is going to be on the exam and easy to follow during lecture with all the demos. She gave homework once a week and does PollEv in class for participation.. As long as you study from the guides she makes and your notes, you should be good for the exams!

Super fun and easy professor! Her PSYC 230 class is super engaging. There are homework assignments every week but theyre easy and it helpful to know for the exam. Participation is required so as long as youre good with that, you can get an A in the class! Exams were fair, just use her study guide that she makes and you will get an A!
Dr. Chanon is amazing. She is very clear with her class and is always helpful with any questions you may. I cannot recommend her enough and she always makes class as enjoyable as possible!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr Chanon was such a great professor. She made the class really fun and enjoyable with her demos throughout the semester. She also gives you all the tools you need to be successful. Highly recommend!

This is the best class I have taken at UNC. Dr. Chanon is an incredible professor who connects concepts from psychology to your daily life, making the class super interesting. I would take as many classes as I could with Dr. Chanon. For tests, studying your notes from class is more than enough. You won't regret taking this class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Chanon is a really great professor. She is very helpful, and really cares about your success in her class. She is always accessible and holds office hours every weak which are helpful if you dont understand the material. Her tests can be hard, so be prepared to study, but overall I really enjoyed the class.

Dr. Chanon is amazing! I will say if you dont pay attention in class, take notes, & don't study this class can be hard. It may be easier for those people who have a strong neuroscience background (I didnt) I have gone to her office hours & she was always so helpful & caring. Exams can be easy when you study and she is never trying to trick you.

Prof Chanon goes through lectures SO FAST AND IS HORRIBLE AT EXPLAINING CONCEPTS. Then when you go to read through the slides to understand the material better, she has no explanation on the slides. Her tests are way too hard considering there is no explanation anywhere online to learn from. I wish I could put her at half speed during lectures.

Dr. Chanon is the best instructor that I had at UNC I took two of her classes, and she is an excellent instructor. She includes plenty of spaced practice so you don't forget earlier material. Her exams make up a large portion of the grade, but if you pay attention and try you will do well. Her lectures are interesting and she does fun demos.

Easy class if you pay attention in lecture. Dr. Chanon is so sweet and cute! She is kind of shy but warms up after the first few weeks and tries really hard to make the material fun. She's good for 222 and 225!

Dr. Chanon is a GREAT prof. I took learning psychology with her last semester, and now I have her for sensation and perception. She sets up the class to be very lenient towards absences and drops one exam grade plus three homework grades at the end of the year. She is also cute and engaging and seems to really match the mood of her students!

I lOVE Dr. Chanon. The material in the class was somewhat hard to understand at first but I always understood it after she lectured on it. As long as you read most of the assigned textbook readings and pay attention, this class is super interesting and easy to do well in.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I had Sensation and Perception psychology with her. She was a good teacher, but I think the material just happened to be a little dry. She did her best to spice it up though, and there were many interesting activities sprinkled throughout the semester.
I took Dr. Chanon for 225 as well. She's really nice, funny, and helpful, but her exams are pretty difficult. Be ready to study for those.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Kyle is the GOAT. Its lowkey hard to get a bad grade in his class unless you just don't do any assignment. Just do the work and you'll be fine. Super chill with extensions too. His lectures can be a bit boring sometimes but overall he's a great teacher for an easy A.
This is genuinely the easiest 105 course you could take. Such an easy grader and there is barely any work
Great guy, very accommodating, doesn't make his class stressful.

Choose Kyle as your 105 teacher. 30 mins of work PER WEEK, easiest class you will ever take, 1 assignemnt a week, asnychronus classes, at the end he lets you argue for an A if you somehow dont already have one. He's also super super chill.
Kyle might be the best 105 teacher. Allows late submissions, easy assignments that take 1-2 hours a week max. Also you can call him Kyle and not professor Cunningham

kyle was amazing! he is very kind, down to earth, and funny. he cares about his students and is very flexible with due dates and assignments. he also gives very good feedback and grades fairly. very chill and easy class, good for people who don't want much work to do for their 105 class.
best professor you could ask for, finished the class with a 100% (even though english wasn't my first language), very flexible with dates and assignments and care about his students

Professor Cunningham is incredibly kind and genuinely cares about his students' success. While the textbook is required, he doesn't use it. His assignments are manageable, effective, and well-structured, and he provides excellent feedback. Though attendance isn't mandatory, attending class occasionally is beneficial.
Dr. Claytor is great! He's just a chill guy. Beware if you're hard of hearing though because he does mumble and can be hard to hear.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Claytor is awesome! BIOL104 isn't a hard class but I think a lot of people also underestimate it. When you're studying for the exams focus on the slides and don't worry about the GRQs.

Jordan Claytor is the GOAT! He is so nice and office hours are super helpful. Sometimes the grqs didnt align but I'd still recommend them. Tests werent too bad, pretty straightforward with a 1-2 difficult questions. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's seems very chill when it comes to teaching, he will expect you to be able to use what you learned in class and apply it to different scenarios so practice that.

I don't understand why so many people are complaining but I think he was a really good prof! His lectures were helpful and reading the textbook was also helpful. My grade was ultimately nerfed because I didn't know how to study and the exams were made up of application questions. As long as you fully understood the concepts, you will do well!
He's an amazing professor and so funny. Explains concepts very well. I didn't do great on the first exam but it's dropped at the end of the semester which is amazing.
so fun and kawaii Claytor is so funny. class is fun make sure to yell trixxi for fun stickers. exams are hard so be prepared to study!

Dr. Claytor is such a fun professor to have. However, his exam questions were often worded confusingly and would sometimes "trick" you. But overall, he is amazing and funny and kind. Definitely try to take at least one class with him.
There was a lot of work for this class, and the exams made up most of the grade. For it being an intro class, he makes difficult topics easy to understand and was available outside of class for help.

There are 3 test, and the final. With the lowest test grade dropped! You read the chapter, do your GRQ, and mastering homework before the lecture. He records lectures and post presentations! For a biology class I did not feel like there was a lot of work, just make sure to study for exams!

I absolutely loved Dr. Claytor. He is such a wonderful professor and I learned so much in his class. His lectures are very well structured and easy to learn from, especially doing the GRQs before hand. Exams are very reasonable and follow exactly what has been covered. I can not recommend Dr. Claytor more!

Exams were unnecessarily tricky, and the hard questions were all weighted more. GRQs are long and a waste of time- not helpful for lecture. He is a nice guy, but not a fan of the way he writes tests. Still a pretty easy class- lots of common sense.
An engaging professor with good lectures. A lot of homework, though. The lowest midterm is droped and the final is pretty easy comparatively. Would recommend.

Good and chill professor, lecture content is pretty easy but the tests are lowkey ridiculous, questions are unnecessarily tricky and I still don't understand the logic behind his answers a whole semester in.
Made exams tricky, grqs are not helpful and take time

Lectured all class; all slides and class videos up on canvas. He drops 1/3 midterms, 1 quiz, and 2 GRQs/ masterys. Grades are fair, and you'll do well if you're actively studying and not just cramming before exams.

This professor is AMAZING! I loved his class the most, and he actually made biology fun. The tests can be hard, but manageable. If you're struggling, def go to office hours as he is extremely helpful one on one. Overall, amazing professor and person!

Professor Claytor is great, teaches things in a way that is understandable and fun, and truly cares about students. BIO 101 is just a very difficult weed out class. Tests are weighted super heavy. Claytor made it enjoyable, but it is a lot of work and difficult to get an A.

very understanding and entertaining! he doesnt take himself or the class too seriously and he finds ways to make the content more engaging. GRQs lowk take forever and for the most part all of the test content is from lecture, so hw can be time consuming but never hard. midterms had some specific questions that were kinda hard but final felt easier

Claytor is an engaging instructor, and his lectures are pretty clear. Either him or the peer instructors have office hours multiple times a week, so it's always possible to get help. As long as you listen to his studying tips and focus on the learning objectives, it's easy to obtain an A.

Dr. Claytor is a super kind and funny professor. Tests are pretty tricky but he does drop a midterm. GRQs are SUPER time consuming and a lot of the stuff that you read isn't even covered on tests. Tests also have material that we talk about in class but isn't included on the slides so I had to rewatch the lectures to study for midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Claytor was great, exams are very difficult with trick questions so make sure you know how to study. There is lots of homework but in the long run if you do all the homework it will boost your grade in the end and it will help your studying.

Claytor is a really cool guy and a good lecturer. In terms of BIOL101, he's probably the easiest professor. That being said there is A LOT of homework. Attendance is technically mandatory but it's only 6% of the grade so it doesn't matter much if you miss a few lectures. Tests can be confusing and are weighted pretty heavily.

Content is easy, but midterms feel much trickier so don't underestimate them. Often take questions in class and somehow make them weirder? Tests are weighted 77% so big part of the grade. Really cool person, often gives Trixie stickers and wears costumes. Final felt easier than the midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The content of this course is not difficult. However, the exams are weirdly worded and confusing. He definitely does this on purpose to confuse you. He is a nice guy, though, but if you don't do well on the exams, you're cooked.

As long as you attend class, actually do homework instead of using AI, and study hard for tests, then you will do well in the class. Dr. Claytor is very caring and understanding and wants you to succeed in this class.
He makes the lectures very fun by making it interactive and responding well to his students. He is extremely caring and accessible outside of class. Amazing teacher overall.

He was a good prof but the exam questions were designed to trip you up and some of the questions were very poorly worded. The exams make up 70% of your grade so you're out of luck if you get lower grades on two of them. The written responses were easily misinterpreted and worth a lot of points, so I would say to make sure you read carefully!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Love Professor Claytor, lectures aren't boring and are very helpful. Midterms are tricky sometimes, but one is dropped. The first midterm is supposed to be the hardest, so make sure to really study for that one. Other than that he's the best possible bio professor you could have!

A nice professor and accessible outside of class. You need to apply yourself to succeed, so attend lectures and ask for help when needed. STEM classes don't really require an extraordinary professor, and it's more about what you put in to do well.

This was my first stem class in college and although it was a lot of work, I never felt overwhelmed and he only tested us on the material and the exams weren't too hard. There are 3 and the lowest one gets dropped but they are worth a lot of your grade but as long as you put in work outside of class you'll do fine

This class was not very difficult if you put in the right amount of time to study. There are three exams and the lowest one gets dropped. There are GRQ's and Mastering assignments that are fairly easy, they just take a bit of time. His lectures are helpful and he does Learning Objectives in class which is what he also uses to take attendance.

Although Claytor is nice as a person, this can be easily overlooked when the exams are worth so so so much of your grade. From someone who is OOS and always had an A in high school bio/chem this is super difficult esp if you have other hard classes. The tests are there to stump you and really are tricky even if you know material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely ELITE Bio 101 teacher. If you have the chance to take him I would highly recommend. Yes the material and work load can be hard, but thats just Bio 101 at UNC. Dr. Claytor makes this as seamless and easy as it can be.

Most of the material in this course is learned through the textbook readings and homework. The lectures are mostly review of the homework. I felt very prepared for exams after doing the homework because half of the homework is multiple choice questions that served as exam practice. The exams were decently short, usually less than a class period.
Good professor, questions can be tricky, definitely conceptual

Prof Claytor is one of the best in the bio department at UNC. His lectures are clear and concise. Exams are difficult but nothing ridiculous if you studied and do the practice exams. GRQs can be long and take a lot of time but do really help you understand content. Would recommend that people jump at the opportunity to take a class with Claytor.
super sweet but god did those tests make me question my sanity.

Overall great lectures, If you pay attention and do the homework you should be able to do pretty good. Test content is gone over in class, no curves though. A little homework heavy, quizzes are online on your own. Drops 2 lowest quiz and HW grades and your lowest exam grade. Probably the best Bio 101 teacher though.
He's a great guy, and gives great lectures. The tests feel kind of unfair at times, but that's to be expected in Biology classes.

I really enjoyed Dr. Claytor's teaching style and his ability to keep the class engaged. It was a massive lecture hall but I still felt like I was participating in the class through the active learning breaks he adds into his lectures. I would highly recommend trying to take a class with him at some point during your time at UNC.

Very good professor. Lectures everyday and homework due before class. I do not think he does a great job at preparing you for the exams, he will only give typical test questions every once in awhile in lecture. He will also talk about things in class that are not on the lecture outlines. Bio is hard but he is very nice and explains concepts well.

Dr. Claytor is a great professor. He is very hilarious and his lectures are EASY to pay attention to. I would highly recommend him, but the tests are much harder compared to the hw in class. Definitely go to BioCell or office hours to get extra help. Make sure to look out for Trixxy on his slides.

Good professor, pretty engaging. Young and personable, makes jokes, and has lots of tools to help you succeed. Drops one exam grade. Material isn't that challenging if you follow along in class and do the reading questions outside of class.

I loved his sense of humor and the energy that he brought to every lecture. His slides and teaching was engaging and he was always welcome to meeting after class or helping in any way that he could. I had a difficult time in my life at the time of taking this class, otherwise I would've likely gotten a high A, but even through it, he was very kind.

Dr. Claytor is phenomenal. He is a young professor which makes him able to relate to students a lot more. His lectures are engaging, but I have noticed in both BIOL101 and 104 that his tests are so tricky. Even when you really know material the wording/answer choices can seriously trip you up. Wish he would make his exams more clarifying.
Never take this professor's class, When you doing the GRQ and Master quiz at 2:00 AM, and its only calculate for 10percent of your grade, you will know what I said.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Have quiz each week and homework everyday for up to 2 hours! I just got depression from taking this class. He never teach in lecture. This class is 101 and shouldn't be that hard. IS FOR PEOPLE WHO JUST START THEIR BIOLOGY JOURNEY BUT NOT A PHD STUDENT! The quiz is extremely hard and the exam calculate for 70% percent of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I LOVE Claytor. He was such a good Professor. Bio 101 is pretty easy in itself, but Claytor made it fun. He's funny, keeps you engaged, and teaches the content well. He really cares about his students! Anyone I know who has had him has loved him.

Tons of Homework, GRQ and lecture that do nothing with the exam. YOU WILL BE COOKED SO BAD BY ATTENDING THIS COURSE. Impossible to get A since do one question wrong will dropped to B immediately. SAVE YOUR GPA

course is entertaining but the lectures are almost useless and everything relies on self-study. Each question is 3 points out of 20, and one mistake means losing all 3—dropping to a B. It counts heavily toward the grade. Covering 150 pages in three weeks all on our own makes the setup unreasonable, with a grading system that feels truly unfair.
Super chill and nice professor! He actually wants to interact with students! Simply do the readings, ask questions, do the work and you should get a good grade.

All my homies love Dr Claytor. BIOL 101 is not an easy class, but Prof Claytor is a great professor, and he tries to be understanding of students with the course content, assignments, and grading. Would DEFINITELY recommend for a good bio professor.
Just paying attention and taking notes during lectures and on the homework was enough for me to do good. I feel like some test questions were a bit tricky so make sure to read questions twice.

Class is easy if you're intentional about doing the readings when you're supposed to. If you read, GRQs are not only easy, but helpful in making studying for tests super easy. (Started studying the day before midterms and did well, but ONLY BECAUSE I LEARNED OVER THE COURSE OF THE SEMESTER). 

Claytor is super sweet, and lectures are lighthearted.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super nice, chill guy and very good lecturer. You can really tell he cares about his students and wants us to do well. As long as you pay attention to the readings and lectures you will do fine. Only complaint is that GRQs were time-consuming and a few times felt like a waste of time, but all bio 101 sections have to deal with that.

Dr. Claytor was amazing, I would definitely recommend him for any intro course. The class itself was fairly difficult, and just know if you want an A it takes a good bit of work. Go into this course knowing that they will try to "trick" you on tests, and lean into it by working hard to figure out how to see through the deception. You've got this!

Goated BIOL professor, his lectures were never too difficult and I thought his exams were pretty fair. As long as you do all the required homework and readings, you'll be fine. GRQs were sometimes annoying but the homework overall wasn't too demanding. Claytor has a super chill vibe which gives the class a very comfortable environment!

Dr. Claytor has a really calm air about him. He's not stressed out about bio, so you're not stressed out about bio. His midterms are very reflective of the lectures and readings. Sometimes he even straight up tells you what some of the questions will be. Great prof.

Dr. Claytor is an amazing lecturer! He's a super cool and funny guy, and you can tell he cares for his students. The tests are somewhat challenging, but if you participate and focus on the Learning Objectives, then it's not too bad.

He is such a kind and funny professor although his exams could be considered challenging. I felt like there was trick questions often but he was a very good lecturer and always kept them interesting. Homework is very helpful, especially the GRQs, and I also found the textbook very helpful!

I loved 101 with Dr. Claytor, and he is very engaging in class, and encourages participation. The class content is definitely hard, so it's important to get help with the tricky content (there are so many resources for this class!! use them!).

Dr. Claytor is an AMAZING professor. He makes the lectures engaging and there is a lot of partner activities. The content can be tough, but as long as you complete the GRQ's, mastering, and go through the learning objectives it shouldn't be too bad! I highly recommend taking this class with him!!

I hated biology before taking Bio 101 with Dr. Claytor. He is very passionate, and even though there was a lot of work, he made me start to love biology. He gave a lot of opportunities to get help outside of class and just really wants his students to do well! Definitely take his class!!

I LOVED professor Claytor. I loved his lectures and teaching style. He makes sure to keep you engaged. If you pay attention in the lectures and pay attention to the readings/the GRQ's, you are set. Claytor is also super nice and funny. TAKE BIO 101 WITH HIM
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: It's clear that Claytor is super knowledgeable about subject matter and he breaks down content in ways that make it much more understandable. Homework and quizzes are straightforward but you need a really good understanding to do good on exams, especially because exams are weighted really heavily.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great teacher, kind of reads off slides but def makes lectures as interesting as possible for bio 101.

Claytor is an interesting lecturer and a really cool guy. The lectures apply concepts you are expected to have a basic understanding of from the reading before class. I would strongly recommend actually doing the readings. The material is not difficult but the tests are worded in ways that feel like they're made to trick you, so be careful.

Dr. Claytor is a little dry and kind of just speaks off the slides. However, I do think he is a pretty good lecturer and definitely knows what he is talking about. For the class, you do GRQs before almost every single class, a few quizzes, and then 3 exams and a final. The exams are fairly difficult, but nowhere near as difficult as Chem 101.
Dr. Claytor is funny and a good lecturer. His exams aren't too bad in my opinion if you study the learning objectives.

I really enjoyed this class! BIOL 101 is definitely difficult but Dr. Claytor does a really good job at providing adequete review and going over questions. The class itself is going to be difficult because it is a weeder but he does a good job.
Super fun and conversational, wears fun costumes, exams were harder than rest of material

Dr. Claytor is really good at explaining hard material. He is also super fun and is accessible outside of class. However, this class is hard! Test are super hard and are meant to trick you. Claytor is a really good lecturer but the class is hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Bio 101 is very content heavy so it's pretty difficult no matter what. There is weekly homework in the form of guided reading questions that are hit or  miss on how long they take. Tests are heavily weighted so you HAVE to study. Claytor provides students with lots of resources and I found him to be kind and entertaining. I would choose him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is awesome! While Bio 101 is difficult, Dr. Claytor provides a ton of resources to help succeed and is very accessible outside of class. Tests make up a large part of your grade but are not too hard if you pay attention in class and study the material. Take Claytor!

Dr. Claytor is incredibly kind and a great professor. I wish I had listened to his advice at the beginning of the semester to be consistently studying for the final exam throughout the course. He was a pretty perfect teacher.

BIOL 101 is tough in general. There's a decent amount of homework (GRQs and Mastering) assignments outside of class that are hit or miss on how long they take. The class is very exam heavy and questions can be tricky so take advantage of your resources and STUDY! I found Claytor himself caring and entertaining; I'd definitely choose him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Claytor did a great job of engaging the class despite it being a very large lecture (more than 300 people). He was very funny and his fits were always fire. Tests were fine, but sometimes had confusing wording. The lowest midterm is dropped, and there is no curve. Participation is required, but a certain amount are dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Claytor was an amazing professor. He is an inclusive and encouraging professor, and he never failed to keep me engaged. His tests are a bit harder due to them being application-based, but the course overall wasn't too bad. There aren't many busy-work assignments, and everything was informational. I'd definitely recommend Claytor!

I LOVE Dr. Claytor, he is such an amazing person and his lectures cover the material comprehensively. Homework consists of guided reading which is due before the lectures, but shouldn't take longer than 1h. There are also take-home quizzes and in-class tests which are difficult but as long as you do the GRQs (pay attention to them) you'll do great!

This was my first STEM class at UNC and having Dr. Claytor as my professor has raised the bar high! Absolutely loved him as a professor and he brought great energy every lecture; he kept the classes engaging and all material was interesting. As expected though, this class is very exam heavy, so be ready to study consistently to get a good grade

I took this class as a non-bio major expecting to not like it and struggle, but I actually really enjoyed it. The exams were definitely stressful, but him dropping the lowest one provided some flexibility. Dr. Claytor is an awesome lecturer. I wish I had a reason to take another class with him!!

Dr. Claytor is so kind and wants you to succeed. Although the content may seem straight forward, don't underestimate it and study for the tests. There are online textbook readings with online quizzes twice a week, but they are fine if you do the readings. Lowest exam is dropped and so are lowest 2 reading quizzes.

Dr. Claytor is honestly a great professor and cares for his students. He drops your lowest exam score which was nice. I recommend coming to class, doing GRQs and Masterings, and the quizzes. Take advantage of his office hours because that was very helpful. This course is exam heavy which sucks, but is expected. Y'all please take him he's funny.

i love prof. claytor (hes so bonita). even though bio 101 is a huge class he's super chill. tests are very heavily weighed though, which was a pain. lectures got boring sometimes because the class is structured to where we teach ourselves the concepts before going to class by reading through the textbook.

The syllabus is very clear. Do your GRQs, go to lecture, and do practice exams and you'll be fine. This course is really easy but for some reason I got worst exam grades than my other chem/bio tests. Almost didn't get an A, but I think I underestimated the class, the exams were kinda tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was very boring, but ecology isn't really my thing. Just study lectures, practice exams, and peer mentor review slides and you'll do fine.

Dr. Claytor explained things well for what the class was, the worst unit was the phylogeny unit but honestly that wasn't his fault it is genuinely just a confusing unit.  Class grade is majority midterms and the midterms contain A LOT of stuff from lecture so you really have to show up to class.

Dr. Claytor was great, but nothing special. Honestly, the class could be completely learnt on your own, he was less of an instructor and more of a facilitator - but I guess that is just how a lot of the STEM classes at UNC are. The exams make up most of your grade, but are quite similar in difficulty to the practice exams, assignments and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: its obvious he cares about the subject and his students.

Biology is in itself a very difficult course, especially for freshmen. However, Dr. Claytor did a great job at making the class friendly. His lectures are sometimes boring, and your grade is very test-reliant. Be prepared to struggle on exams, but that isn't directly his fault. Dr. Claytor is a great professor and is passionate about his subject.

If you do the homework and read the textbook on your own, it is easy to excel in the course. However, this course is extremely test reliant and the lectures alone are not really enough to understand the material so it is crucial to put in maximum effort on the homework.
He is honestly great and the tests were not too hard. I didn't put enough time into this class because I was focused on other classes but could of gotten an A if I had worked just a little harder.

Professor Claytor is a great professor, this is just a hard class. The GRQs tend to take a while and then you have mastering on top of it and the exams are extremely difficult for no reason. It's a weed out class, so get the credit before if your grade really matters unless you're willing to spend your life in the library before any test/exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do not take this class if you have the choice. He is a good person, but his lecture style is weird and you have to learn everything on your own. There is also limited resources for studying for exams which are also much harder compared to the content covered in class. GRQs take way too long and don't help either.

As long as you understand the answers to the TA review session slides and the practice exams, ur set for an A on the exams. It isn't hard, just show up because everything you need to know is said in the lectures and he breaks it down pretty easily; reading takes long but most of the info in readings is used for a quiz you take when ur done reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Claytor's lectures are always fun and engaging. BIOL 101 does a good job of balancing content between homework (textbook reading) and lecture. There is about 2 hours of homework per week. Participation and completion grades make up a decent portion of your course grade; only quizzes (at home), exams (easy if studied for), and masterings graded.

For me it is difficult to do very well in this class, but I don't think this is due to Claytor's teaching. He is very accessible and provides many resources for the students and wants them to succeed. He's outfits slay and if you're lucky he will run around the class singing HOT to go. Not the biggest BIO 101 fan but I would take Slaytor again.

This class isn't too bad, there is a good amount of work before and after class but it's pretty easily managable. The exams are pretty difficult, but one gets dropped and there is a bunch of resources to help get you ready. In general, Dr. Claytor is really caring about his students and he's very engaging.

Don't take Dr. Claytor, he makes the course and exams very difficult and there are MANY exams/tests. You have to learn basically everything on your own, his "practice exams" are nothing like the actual exam, so you fool yourself by thinking you're ready, then bomb the exam. Every practice he posts he doesn't check and the content is very outdated.

I feel like people are being harsh because it's a Bio course, but then again, it's a biology course; it's not meant to be easy. He does good during office hours and is easily available. The homework is reading heavy, but the textbook is helpful. I got a 50% on my first exam. Got a 88% on the second with his help. I'm a freshman and I love him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Reading through his reviews and I feel as if everyones being a bit harsh. Does he give a lot of HW? Yes. Are tests a cakewalk? No. But its a bio course, its not going to be insanely easy. Going to class and actually doing the readings brought my exam scores from a D in the 1st to an A in the 2nd. Claytor is a fantastic guy, highly recommend

In this class you are going to have to teach yourself everything because the quizzes based on readings are due before lectures. Yet, you still have to go to lectures for attendance. This along with the lab is arguably one of the worst intro classes at UNC.

Dr. Claytor himself is a decent lecturer. However, the way he structured his course could use a lot of work. The textbook readings/reading quizzes were due BEFORE he gave his lecture on the topic, and most were not even on his exams or discussed during lectures. I recommend using his powerpoint slides to study for midterms/final.

Dr. Claytor is awesome! BIOL 104 is a pretty structured, big lecture style class, but he does his best to make the material interesting. He's super funny and passionate about ecology, and we do cool case studies in class. He's really clear about assignments, and the exams aren't necessarily easy, but the class is super manageable.

His 1st year here & he slayed it. If you take time to understand the material the class is good. Many readings/GRQs outside class (common for any bio course @ UNC) but easy A's; DO them. He makes silly jokes in lectures which is nice. He/TAs are easy to reach & provide many resources to help if you are struggling. Tests are 70% of the grade; STUDY.

I love Dr. Claytor! He is one of the professors that I feel as though I had the opportunity to connect with outside of the classroom. BIOL101 at UNC in general is tough just due to the nature of it being one of the 1st you take, but Dr. Claytor made it fun. Take notes, do homework, form study groups and you'll be set. Go to office hours frequently.

I absolutely loved BIO104 with professor Claytor. He's an all around really nice guy and really cares about his students. The grading criteria is very clear and all of the homework answers come from the readings. There is a project that is done in parts throughout the semester, but it isn't challenging and I actually found it enjoyable.

104 is easy; dont underestimate it. Youll get an A if you read & go to class. Sometimes readings are extra so skim. Def take it with Claytor; the other prof is harder. Doing just hw & projects, you'll get at least a B. Premeds take this class seriously! Claytor's lectures are boring sometimes, but he's really cool 1:1 so set up a meeting fs.

LOTS of reading that turned out to be not very helpful (better off just skimming and reading the chapter summary). His lectures are fine--the content is not super interesting itself, but he tries his best to make it enjoyable. Cheat sheets are allowed on the tests, so it's not too hard to do well on them. In class questions are counted for accuracy

One of the worst lecturers at UNC. He tries to be funny but his jokes are often cringe. During the entire lecture, he basically has his back towards the audience and reads from the big projector, which is only helpful to the people in the back who can't see. But for the others in class, it's basically a waste of time since those notes are posted.

One of the hardest classes I've ever taken at UNC. The exams are nothing like the content we cover in class so I'm not sure how I was supposed to prepare for them. He gives no partial credits and grades very harshly. When I went to his office hours, he just talks about how students need to relax and that grades do not define you.
We had a lot of textbook reading that barely related to what we learned in class. But Dr. Claytor was really nice and seemed to really enjoy teaching us, which made class more interesting.

Dr. Claytor was a very caring professor and always provided resources for his students. I'm not a BIO major so I didn't enjoy the content, but he did his best to make class engaging. The tests are really hard, though, so it's important to do all homework and Poll EVs to get as much credit as possible outside of tests.
I like Professor Claytor, I didnt really get to know him at all, but this was the only bio class I have taken that hasnt made me want to switch my major (Im switching my major).

Love Dr. Claytor. 104 is not a difficult class by any means and his exams are fair (one-sided cheat sheet). Additionally, he gave us an extra credit opportunity for learning catalytic when 20% of them were already dropped. I enjoyed the course content but the simutext has got to go.

BIOL104 is not a challenging class. 3 exams, one is dropped, and a final exam, a few quizzes a week from readings, a project split into 3 parts spaced in the semester, and attendance is an important part of the class. The only downside is that lectures can be quite boring and mundane, but overall pretty easy class with clear guidelines.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: No completion grades. No extra credit or curves. Exams are weirdly hard to do well on. The more I studied the worse I did. The final exam's graded questions aren't released. He does not care and reads off the slides word for word. Sounds bored; only offers one office hour a week. This semester many people said they did better in chem than this.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the most boring biology classes at UNC. Be prepared to self-study because the lectures are absolutely worthless. To add to this, I was never able to reach out to him outside of class. I had to get help from a senior who already took the class to barely pass in Claytor's class.

Overall, Dr. Claytor was a good guy and actually cared a lot about his teachings. The problem with this class was the lack of material outside of lectures. Few topics were covered during lecture, making it very boring. The assigned textbook readings were a huge waste of time because we were only tested on 20% of the material from the textbook.
I loved this class. Not the easiest but definitely not the hardest and I love Dr. Claytor.

He was nice but I did not like how he lectured. There is a lot of self studying because the lectures assume that you know what things mean. The tests weren't that hard if you study based off of the learning objectives. He is dry and not really exciting. Attendance and participation grade was based off of learning catalytics.

GRQs are the worst, and take forever to complete. Essentially, how his class is structured is that unless you do your GRQs, you aren't going to learn anything from the class because all he does during lecture is go over the GRQ content. He is also not the best at communication, and is almost impossible to reach out outside of lecture.

So much tedious homeworks from billion dollar education companies. Also his exam questions are awful and unclear. When you try to submit a regrade response he'll deny it even if his question is confusing and your logic makes sense. The material isn't difficult, the exam questions just make it harder than it needs to be.

DO NOT TAKE! You basically have to self-study, since all he does in lecture is read off the Powerpoint with no emotions. As boring as the lectures are, he makes you show up to class because he takes attendance. Not to mention that with BIOL 101, you have to take BIOL 101L which is a story for another day.
