Dr. Claytor is a super chill guy. As long as you complete the pre-class assignments and study for the exams, passing this class isn't difficult. In-class participation is required and that's how attendance is taken (Learning Catalytics), so just make sure to show up prepared. He's a bit dry but can be funny when he tries, but personally I'm a fan!

Dr. Claytor is a good professor, however this class is a bit difficult in general. 70% of your overall grade is exams   
(with one dropped) so if you aren't great with understanding in depth content and then applying it to test questions then you will most likely struggle. His tests are not the greatest, but it is manageable if you need a credit.

Do NOT take this class with him!! He is a horrible professor who says grades don't define you, but then every little thing we do in class/out of class is graded for accuracy, even participation. He purposely will try to drag your grade down. He does not care about teaching and he does not want to even be there, so avoid him.

Do not take 104 with Claytor. Lectures are pointless and so boring, and he seems like he doesn't even want to be there. Doesn't accept late work, tests don't align with what we learned in class, and reading the book is pointless because it doesn't align with the curriculum/tests at all. All tests were the same day as chem, and they knew it.

Boring and useless lectures, basically reading the powerpoint. A ton of readings on SimuText and reading quizzes. Quizzes and exams have very few questions, so no room for mistakes. Final grade is largely based on tests. A one-sided cheat sheet is allowed but useless as the exam questions are mostly application-based.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of reading outside of class and attendance is recommended because it contributes to your grade. Cheat sheets allowed on tests and he drops lowest grades. Very caring and easy going- would recommend! Just really study for the tests!
Genuinely a great professor. He was engaging and fun in lectures. The way the class was set up made it super manageable, even if the content was tricky at times. 14/10 would recommend.
Claytor was very easy to reach outside of class and tried to make the lectures fun. You get to drop your lowest test grade and have a front and back cheat sheet.

Dr. Claytor is AMAZING. Interesting lectures, very easy to access via email, and I go to his office hours fairly regularly, and he's always prepared to answer questions or to just talk about anything.

You will do good in the class if you do the GRQs (which aren't that difficult) and show up to the lectures. His lectures use cool, real-life examples with helpful diagrams/flowcharts and your lowest exam grade gets dropped.  He also posts recordings on Canvas and drops 20% of missed LC points. Obviously he cares about his students' success.

What's the point of taking bio with him, if he makes you learn the material by yourself? Lectures are useless but attendance is mandatory. GRQs take forever to complete but they contribute to nothing for your final grade. All he does is talk about how his students are capable of teaching themselves the material.

Is a flipped classroom so you definitely need to learn how to learn by yourself (although all of the information you need is in the textbooks and from GRQs). Claytor is a great professor, super concise! I recommend taking the course with them!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I felt like the lectures were great. Dr Claytor breaks down concepts and even relates them to current events which was nice. The exams make up 70% of the grade but one gets dropped and there are other grades that get dropped if needed. The workload is to be excepted for a UNC bio courses. An A felt impossible but a B was manageable. Studying is key

Tests dominate your grade, leaving no room for error, with their inflated point values. GRQs and mastering, though mandatory, contribute next to nothing. Succeeding hinges solely on acing tests, as the professor's idea of teaching is essentially making you self-tutor. At least he's a stand-up comedian and decent cheerleader. Best of luck.

All the ratings say that you have to teach yourself. I don't understand why people are giving him 4's and 5's when they are admitting that he just reads off his slides in lecture. Isn't the point of a professor to teach not to read?

This was one of the first bio classes I had ever taken other than Bio 1 in high school, so I pretty much had to learn everything from scratch. He does an okay job explaining, but the GRQs and mastering do the majority of teaching for you. It's important to know the concepts before class because he just talks more about them during his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: flipped class so know the material before. often asks you to interact w peers. in class participation marks your attendance. 3 midterms, one dropped. hella homework. funny guy tho and young. you get a full page front back cheat sheet for exams. not the best teacher and mainly read off slides but that's just because you should know material before.

All I learned from this class is that you have to rely on your peers to pass BIOL 101. Whenever I had a question he would say "talk to your peers" and not give a definitive answer. This man is clearly new, does not know how to answer questions, and often gets uncomfortable when asked questions he doesn't know the answer to.

Claytor is a new professor who clearly does not know how to teach an intro-level biology course. Tests make up most of your grade and the homeworks are clearly not the same difficulty as the exams. Do not take.

Claytor was an amazing professor who genuinely cares about his class. He offers several opportunities to make up missed assignments. Several people have rough grades because exams make up 70% of the class but he dropped the lowest midterm. He's a great guy and you'll do fine if you study. He makes things clear and easy to comprehend.

I had a nightmare taking the lecture with Jordan Claytor and the lab with Barbara Stegenga and her TA. Absolute worst combination possible at UNC because they make nothing clear, and you are expected to learn on your own. I wish I could at least go to one of them to ask questions, but they never answer emails and have minimal office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: great guy, outstanding fits. feel like he wouldve be mean to me if we had gone to the same high school but i don't even blame him. yes you are expected to know content before lecture, but that's just the structure of the course. he goes at a very reasonable pace. exams are tough with 1-2 missed causing like 10 points off. to be expected in 101.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is Jordan Claytor's first year teaching at UNC Chapel-Hill. He attended Elon University for his undergraduate degree and studied dinosaurs at the University of Washington. He may be a better fit to teach an upper-level course, because he made topics more difficult than it needed to be.

Be ready to teach yourself the material by reading the textbook because lectures are pointless. His homeworks are tedious too but I guess that's the only way you learn the content. Tests make up your entire grade and if you do bad on 2, you are pretty much screwed.

I highly recommend that you take Dr. Claytor, as he was a great professor. His exams are heavily weighted, with the midterms being 25% of your grade each, but 1 out of the 3 midterms are dropped. The readings can take a while, but they aren't that bad and they do help you understand the material if you put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There is no point in going to class because this person will just read off his slides. The bad news is that he takes attendance through the stupid Pearson website. His office hours were useless and I had to spend hours learning the material on my own. Claytor encourages peer teaching, but I'm convinced he says that because he doesn't know how.

no way everybody is giving him 5s. he literally had a panic attack during his first lecture and would almost never face the students. simply reading off his boring white powerpoint turned the other way
Honestly, he doesn't know how to teach. Take with another professor if you want to learn.

He's new. That was glaringly obvious. He tried to connect with us, but was often very condescending. His style of reading off slides and relying on learning catalytics was not a favorite, and everything I learned from this class I taught myself. YOU HAVE TO STUDY FOR EXAMS!! the three midterms and completion of the homework will determine success.
Very very good professor especially for his first year here. Writes hard quizzes and exams though. Very caring and willing to help. Fosters a very good environment

Dr. Claytor seems like a nice person, but honestly his homeworks were not very helpful in regards to the content covered on the exam. He also holds office hours, but with 400+ students, you are lucky if you have one question answered. He also did not answer many of my emails, although I understand this is a large course.
He is a first year professor and is not very confident in his teaching abilities. His powerpoints are very poorly structured and unengaging.

Dr. Claytor is AMAZING!!! He is very knowledgeable about the class topics and cares about his students. He connected with the class and created a fun and comfortable learning environment. There is a decent amount of work outside of class, but it is beneficial for mastering the information. I would definitely recommend Dr. Claytor for BIOL 101!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Claytor deserves every 5.0 he gets. You can tell he is passionate about his students and work. There is a good bit of homework but it isn't hard, just time consuming. The HW makes the lectures easier to follow, and there is a lot of wiggle room if you happen to miss an assignment. We got a cheat sheet for our exams this semester, which was great.

Dr. Claytor was an amazing professor. He really cares about all of his students, and really takes the time to assure that everyone is confident in themselves and the material. Do all of the GRQs and mastering because they are great notes/study materials. Overall Dr. Claytor is an excellent professor and you can definitely succeed in his course!

Professor Claytor is great. He is super caring, always reminds you that a test grade does not define you (which allows you to feel better about it and do better next time). He typically ask how everyone is doing by a show of thumbs. I definitely recommend you take Biol101 with him.

This was Dr. Claytor's first year teaching at UNC and he was awesome. He is knowledgable and passionate about the material. He helps class be relatable through modern examples and humor. There is frequent homework, but it is reasonable, helps you learn, and isn't busy work. Exams are a heavy weight, but are reasonable and related to the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Claytor is AWESOME!!!!! He cares about every single student in his lecture. It is not easy, but he does a really awesome job of teaching the material and clarifying for understanding. You have to study very hard and do your homework (2 GRQS per week), but he drops your lowest exam grade and you get a cheat sheet for every test!

Dr. Claytor is an amazing professor! I had him for Bio 101 freshman year. He assigns about 2-4 hours of homework every week (not busy work). Read the syllabus! It explains his expectations, methodology, and essentially step-by-step instructions of how to succeed in his class. Very funny; lectures are helpful; he is accessible outside of class.

If you are looking for a Biol 101 professor, he should be one of your top choices. There will be a little bit of homework before each class that you need to stay up to date on(little room for late work). Our year got a cheat sheet(front and back page) before each class which made tests a lot easier(and we allowed to drop 1/3 midterms).

This was his first year teaching and I was in his Biol 101 FY Launch class and he did a great job. Was very accessible outside of class, gave plenty of opportunities to look for help, and was enjoyable to listen to even at 8 am. Class is only hard if you don't prepare, if you do the homework beforehand, the class is very easy.
gave low final grades, we complained and he changed them, dont bother writing about your true beliefs, youll only get a good grade if you write about what he agrees with

Papers shouldn't be hard but turning them in and then receiving harsh rubric afterwards. Grading not based on the quality of arguments, but simply how close we got to his."here's a 100 if you say exactly what I want, 0 if you miss anything" Made fun of me for stuttering in class and rolled his eyes. Horrible experience.

Reeve is brilliant. His lectures are incredibly insightful. The papers are sometimes difficult but he gives you plenty of opportunities to correct them and improve your grade. One thing to watch for, if you show up with a lot of enthusiasm or confidence, he'll give you more of a hard time than the other students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: Easy as long as you are willing to rewrite papers, he lets you rewrite as many times as needed to get a better grade. Very easy A. However, he's a specific personality and interrupts students after begging for involvement. The class itself was fairly easy, but I was frustrated with his inability to accept other ideas & students to fully conversate.

This class was an amazing, in-depth dive into Plato's "Republic" by one of its foremost scholars. Reeve is very passionate, and while getting good grades on the papers is tough, he gives excellent feedback and allows corrections. It's clearly his goal for you to gain a deep understanding, and he'll help you work toward the grade that you want!

Professor Reeve is an interesting person, but his class lacks structure and clear feedback. Grade is based on best 5 of 6 papers, but the texts are rarely discussed in lecture (focuses more on tangential discussion than paper topics). Heavily focused on your ability to dissect old literature and isolate factual evidence.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Reeve is quite possibly one of the most intelligent men alive. He is just bursting with information. He doesn't really care if you speak or not because he loves to be able to just share what he thinks and why. Do your readings, it'll help immensely. He only gives 2 grades a semester & no exams, so you'll need to do well but he wont let you fail.
Reeve is brilliant. Like super smart. He can teach you everything there is to know about Aristotle if you read and pay attention. He grades harshly and the papers are monstrous

Reeve thinks that he knows everything about everything. He tells some funny and intellectual jokes and I enjoyed his profanity, but as far as actually teaching things you need to know for the papers, he is super unproductive.

Reeve is a great, clear professor who really knows what he's talking about. He is pretty intimidating though, so if you don't have a good TA, your questions may not get answered. He very clearly outlines the readings so you don't really have to read the books, but the exams are not easy at all, unless you're pretty good at philosophy already.

Reeve is a joy to listen to and he really knows his stuff (and is quite aware that he knows it). Readings can generally be skipped if you attend lecture, but they can help to understand the material. This class can be a challenge if you don't think the way Reeve does, but if you do you're golden
This man radiates wisdom! And his lectures are laced with wit!
Best class and professor ever. It's tough if you aren't philosophically-minded. This class changed my minor to philosophy.

Reeve is a great professor and a captivating lecturer. Lots of reading is assigned, but it is not essential as long as you attend the lectures. Your grade is based off 3 five page papers which are graded by TAs, so try to select a good one.

Great at simply laying out major problems. Enjoyable lectures that were well delivered. Many mostly well-chosen assigned readings in this course. I am sure his other classes are more difficult--PHIL 112 (sometimes taught by others) is an introductory/overview course. He knows his Greek! And he can rattle off extensive quotes from various texts!

If you think it's fun or entertaining to mock religion (especially Christianity), take the class. I could barely get through many of the lectures and some of the readings because they were so derisive. I'm able to think critically about my beliefs in an academic way, but the tone of this class felt snarky and childish to me.
reeve is a genius
AWESOME PROFESSOR! always enthusiastic! He's not easy, but he's not trying to fail you. He honestly wants everyone to do well. Participate in class and you'll do fine.

Honestly, THE BEST professors I've had here.  If you don't like reading or are closed minded you probably won't enjoy the class.  If you are willing to challenge yourself some then you will GAIN SO MUCH.  I could sit and listen to him lecture all day. Don't go into the class looking for a grade, look for an experience and the grade will come.
He is awesome. Reeve brings in humour, and at the same time makes the students understand the coursework. The ease of the class varies greatly by your TA, so be careful there!

Reeve is a genius. Given the choice, I would spend every waking moment of my life in this man's shadow. He's completely off in his own world and if you can't handle that, you'll hate him. Don't expect to have a relationship with him other than basking in his presence from afar. This is definitely  my favorite class this semester.
This course is awesome, but the papers are tough. TA's can be a pain, but they make your grade. Go to them for paper help, and you will be fine.

easy class- the reading is good but if you don't want to do it just go to class and recitation. lecture is funny and interesting. papers can be frustrating because there's not much room for your own ideas/interpretation. if you listen in lecture and write what reeve said or what your ta thinks then your grade will be fine. overall an easy A

class is good, lectures are pretty interesting. a LOT of reading that can be avoided for the most part if you listen in lecture and recitation. if you have any views contrary to the professor/TA be prepared to change them or get a poor grade. papers were graded very harshly, some TAs dont even give As, final was easy.
Very interesting and funny.  Requires a lot of reading, usually not very interesting but the lectures clarify everything.
Prof Reeve had great energy and made lectures interesting.
Great, interesting lecturer. Would definately recommend!

GREAT CLASS and GREAT PROFESSOR. I had very little interest in Philosophy, yet Reeve's lectures are so engaging that it became my favorite class. Although I didn't undestand everything, Reeve's lectures and the materials are interesting and I definately would recommend this class.
Reeve is spectacular.
Awesome professor. Best lecturer so far! Very interesting and insightful. A++ would definately take another class taught by him.
This was a small seminar with reeve and a whole lot of fun.  he's a funny guy and the stuff we talked about was extremely interesting and he is very smart.
this guy ****in rules
The best class/teacher i have ever had at this school.  Ignoring the fact that he is brilliant, the man is f-ing hilarious in lecture.  Very interesting anf griping lecturer.
It's all Prof. Reeve. Said to be brilliant. I'd say self-absorbed..

First time teaching this class, but very poorly done. Not all of the material went together well, the tests were not a good test of performance, and the TAs were out to lunch all semester. Take small classes with this guy, not big ones.

Brilliant man, but that's about it. He sexualizes all lectures, does not prepare you for tests, and once compared himself to GOD. the worst class i have ever taken at this school. but if you are a phil major, the man is brilliant.

Brilliant and incredibly interesting lecturer.  Most personal contact involved a TA, but his lectures are awesome and the tests, while hard, are strongly curved.  The papers were a little confusing but graded very fairly.  Take any class you can with him.
Excellent philosopher and lecturer.  Does not coddle students.
No Comments
Other professors claim he doesn't read students work and thus assigns grades randomly.  Witnessed him belittling students in every course I had with him.  He is brilliant, for what its worth.
McLaughlin was a fair teacher who helped out on grades for the most part. Lectures weren't amazing but if you do all the homework you will do fine on tests.
do not trust her, she wont give any partial credit EVEN when you deserve it! i self studied everything for the final and ended up doing well ONLY because of that

People do hate on her too much, but she is not great at teaching. She does not explain things very well, nor are her lectures engaging or well-paced, making it very difficult to follow. This class is definitely still doable, but due to the poor quality of her lectures and teaching style it is largely self-taught.

Professor McLaughlin is extremely sweet and gives quite good advice in office hours. She will give you good, truthful answers to anything you ask her. That being said, this class is pretty test heavy, so I recommend going to office hours as much as you possibly can, staying on top of homework, and beginning to study for each exam a few weeks out

She was mostly fine, the math department is awful, though. Anything after exam 2 had no official notes, and a stupidly heavy weighting on the final that went beyond the level of difficulty we covered in class. The first 2 exams were challenging but fair, the final was awful, but she didnt make it so. Shes nice though, and does want you to succeed.

Tests are pretty easy; they cover only the content she covered in class. A pretty light class for those good at math and can do the problems in class and recitation. Uninspiring and kinda monotone, but people hate on her too much. She also did some magic and raised my grade from an A- to an A. Some homework is way harder than test questions.

- Teaches very well, very nice professor, but tough grading criteria
- Three midterms and final worth about 70 percent of grade, very difficult, one replaced with final
- If you study the textbook, you can essentially skip the lectures
- Recitation weekly, quizzes in recitation and some are very hard
- Our class gpa average was high, around a B

I hope God blesses her for rounding my grade up. i didn't go to lectures after october because it was easier to self teach. she is not a good teacher but her tests are fair and you can manage with lots of studying.

She is a good professor, the attendance not required for her lecture. She usually uses well-written notes as class materials and there are recorded videos on Canvas for us to review. Midterms and final are not difficult and they aligns with the homework contents and class materials.

She teaches content pretty quickly and you definitely need some calc background if you're taking her class. She doesn't curve tests and that makes up the majority of your grade. But, overall, not terrible and if you just pay attention during her lectures, you should be fine.

Worst professor I have had a UNC by far. She is very old and seems to be losing it, lectures are unorganized and she does not explain content well. She does all the work very quick and sucks at teaching the material, you might as well just skip the lectures and go on khan academy. I had friends in 152 with Grey and Corbin who had better experiences
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She hardly checks her email and is not accessible virtually.Posted notes aren't bad,assuming she posts them.Material past midterm 2 was only recorded videos,and still lacked some of the required info.Promised to post written(nope),even after 3 follow-up emails that she ignored.Often uses fading ink in class,so goodluck translating her scratch work.

She's a great professor but she goes through the content relatively quickly, but as long as you look through the notes before hand, its easy to understand the content. The homework is very difficult and unnecessary, but the exams are easy as long as you understand the problems she gives you in class. Overall, she was wonderful.

Lectures move fast, and there's little time to be behind on course content, so expect to teach yourself a good bit. Other than that, her tests are very fair and practice exams cover most of the expected material.

Only reason why I didn't get an A+ is because I didn't put in any effort. Tests are fair and she makes the final as well, so if you do well in her midterms you'll ace the final.

ATTEND THE MIDTERM REVIEWS BY THE TAs!!! Everything they cover is word-for-word the same on the tests, and they single handedly prevented me from failing.

Self-studyable
Solid class. Algebra heavy. Make sure you attend class and do the homework. Nice lady.

This teacher did not explain material clearly.  She would not give partial credit on tests.  Friends who took same class with different teachers were given the opportunity to correct wrong answers on tests.  This was not the case with this teacher.  Do not recommend.

Solid professor. She doesn't speak very loudly and is a little hard to understand. No major complaints. Be sure to go to recitation with the TAs and the review sessions before the tests- they will help enourmously.
Well taught class.

If you do not have a calc background would not recommend her. She speaks very quietly so sit in the front of the class. She gets confused with her other calc classes a lot. Do not email her to change a grade you will get a bad email response. She is normally late. I did feel like I understood the material with the way she taught it.

For the first 2 months of class she didn't seem to grasp which class she was in and what time our class ended. That's all you need to know. Crazy disorganized. Puts in little effort. Take anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm honestly surprised the ratings aren't lower. She's the absolute worst for Calc 1- lectures make no sense, she jumps from topic to topic, she doesn't post guided notes or slide shows you can follow. Tests are hard with impossible algebra; doesn't curve anything; doesn't drop anything. It's clear she doesn't care for Calc 1 students.

prof mclaughin is able to complete all content and have 2 weeks left for revision. Homework is optional and is due right before the exams, it was not of much help. She does have a policy if you get 80% on the assignment you will get 100% on the homework grade. all of her exams came from her notes that she publishes.

Midterms were extremely fair, except that mcq were worth 10% each w/ no partial credit. Her lectures tend to be disorganized, but are usually helpful. Understand the problems in the notes inside out, and you'll do well on the exams. Lecture is optional and recorded, but make sure you watch them b/c that is key to doing well.

Professor McLaughlin is overall the best professor that taught calc 3 when I was taking it. She can get boring sometimes in lecture, but if you focus she does do a fair job explaining the concepts, and does offer extra help if needed. Additionally, her tests are fair and are very representative of the example problems that we did in class.

I have the utmost respect for Professor McLaughlin. She is a great lecturer and managed to explain abstract concepts really well to people just getting introduced to them. Midterms were very fair, and the final (which she wrote) was even more fair. She got me to understand what calculus actually is, not just how to solve problems. Highly recommend.

Very nice lady to talk to, but she doesn't seem to care about this class. I'm not sure if she thinks it's just light work and only focuses on higher-level classes, but it felt like teaching this course was a chore for her. I bombed one test, and it ruined my grade for the semester—she doesn't drop any exams. Take it with Miranda Thomas instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Failed one exam and literally ruined

Her teaching style isn't as bad as people say it is, the only problem is that she jumps content and that confuses the class. Her exams are fair and cover everything learned in class. Thankfully attendance isn't required so go ahead and learn it yourself if that works better for you. Final was weird with tedious derivatives and infinite limits.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All over the place.  She missed 3 classes due to surgery.   Gives practice problems and never explained how to do them.  Doesn't give clear feedback.  Don't take this teacher.

I think McLaughlin is an okay professor, but not as great as everyone says she is. The fact that all of her notes are posted before class was really helpful, but she's very monotone during lectures and doesn't answer questions clearly. As others have said, exams pretty much make up your entire grade, so you need to do well on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: My GOAT. The class is super chill tbh and she is nonchalant. But the homework is much harder than exams so as long as you do the homework on your own you're good, just dont let it pile up. People hate on McLaughlin but she's great in my opinion.
This class was a good experience for me since I had trouble with calc 2. The presentation of material was clear and she's funny and friendly. Good choice for calc 3.

I had to teach the content to myself because her lectures made very little sense. Tests make up pretty much the entire grade (each free response question on the final turned out to be 2% of the overall class grade...ridiculous). I know some of the issues are unavoidable, but if you have to take calc 3, try to get a different teacher.
Test heavy, harsh grader
Lectures are awful you have to watch another professors lectures just to understand
By far my favorite class this semester. The lectures are intuitive and engaging. Definitely recommend.

While very knowledgeable and willing to answer questions, the professor's teaching style was rushed and felt unfit for students learning brand new content. The homework was very hard and not useful for tests. However, the TAs and ULA were super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought this class would be fine because I took Calc 1 in HS. Nope. The tests are hard, TAs are told to grade harshly on certain questions, and if you do poorly on one test, your grade will be ruined. McLaughlin is funny and seems like a nice person, but if you are new to calc, take it with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. McLaughlin doesn't follow lesson plans or the syllabus schedule. She puts little effort into teaching, but has intentionally harder exams than other professors and refuses leniency (i.e. dropping the lowest midterm) unlike other professors. She is passive-aggressive about people not coming to class, even though she knows her lectures are bad.
I was worried about taking calc 1 but Prof Mclaughlin made it doable and interesting. I'm definitely taking her calc 2 class.

Heard shes great for Math-232+ but do not. DO NOT take her for math-231. Shes horrible at teaching the material and KNOWS it and makes the exams insanely hard that even TAs have trouble explaining the material. Told TAs to "grade harshly" to spite students that didn't come to class. Go to another profs lectures to learn. Take exams when needed.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS I've had a mil. bad teachers and struggled, but this professor was the worst. The TA told me to watch YT videos to learn, and the only reason I stayed was because of her and she left. take it with Linda Green or at a community college instead. if you take this class get on antidepressents cuz you'll need them
Do not value lecture at all. She bounces around topics which only confuses students. I supplemented class by going to math plus and the math help center but I wouldn't even bother going to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Anything on our exams is clearly discussed in class (attendance not required), all lectures are filmed and uploaded online, and she teaches you an intuitive approach to math. The only difficulty was that she relied heavily on everyone in the room having taken calculus before, which wasn't true, but watch some videos and you'll be okay.

Great class. She tells you what will be on the exams during class. The homework is long but we get full credit with 80% score. I need to take two more calculus classes so I appreciate learning concepts she says will be covered in those classes. Easy recitations. the TA is super helpful.

Worst professor I've had. Lectures are disorganized, rushed, and unhelpful. No study guides, unclear expectations, and tests include unseen material. Homework is overly hard but barely affects your grade. Recitation adds no value and feels pointless. Took 20+ hours of studying per exam just to pass. Avoid if possible.

Attendance not being mandatory was nice cause you could show up whenever. Homework was annoying cause some problems were hard, but u only needed 80% for full credit. Fair exams, her online notes are great, a pretty approachable lecturer, would def recommend! Be warned exams are ~85% of the grade (but they're easy if u just review practice exams)

After taking AP Calc and MATH130, I had a fair understanding of the topics, but after Mclaughlin, I have never been more confused about calc. After having near-perfect attendance for the first two midterms, I decided it was a waste of time to continue attending. She makes new notes for each class period and has not followed her posted curriculum.
She does test corrections. The exams are medium difficulty. Maths is hard for me and the professor is patient.
The homework is hard but the class notes are good.

This is a good class. Great prof. If you go to class and do the homework it's an easy A. Lots of complaining on this site. Must be students who can't do math because it's an interesting class and well taught. I have As on both exams so far.

She is the worst math teacher I ever had. Although she gives partial credit on tests (which is super helpful), the only way I understand the material is doing 2x more work outside of lectures (such as watching YT videos, AI explanaitons, and getting help from others) to even begin to understand the topic.

DO NOT TAKE CLASSES WITH HER UNLESS YOU ABSOLUTELY HAVE TO….if you can take a class with Miranda Thomas instead do that 100%. McLaughlin teaches as if it is a flipped classroom but with no outside resources. I skipped all of her lectures and just taught myself calc because her lectures made no sense and had no structure. tests were pretty easy tho

Take Mclaughlin. She does test corrections!  I had to take this class over and she is better than the TA I had before. The exams are like the class notes. I reworked the problems a few times before the tests and got As on both. The class can be boring at times because some students slow it down with ridiculous questions. But she's nice about it.
This is not a hard class. The prof is nice and explains the topics really well. The homework is long and difficult but she gives us full credit if we finish 70% of it.

McLaughlin is very confusing and very bad at answering questions. I would avoid taking her if this is your first time taking calculus, as she has a very harsh grading style. Be ready to put in a lot of hours of homework and studying to pass.

Do not take this class if you have not taken calc before. A lot of the material was taught very half-heartedly, and the only way to learn it fully was to learn it outside of class. Tests are challenging and each question is worth a lot of points, but other than that, she is a very kind woman.

If you have not taken calc in high school, do not take this class. She moves very fast and does an OK job explaining concepts. Her exams are harder than there sections and she does not curve or drop a midterm. Overall a nice lady but I wouldn't recommend unless you've taken calc.

I do not recommend taking Calc 1 with her. Her lectures are a waste of time. Her notes are very disorganized. She often makes mistakes during class and the students have to correct her. She does not know how to do the homework that she assigns. She does not follow the syllabus and does not inform students of what units are on the exams. Not a fan.
take stor113. if you are a business major, do not take this class. she rushes through lectures and does not answer questions effectively.
This is my second time taking this class. Prof Mclaughlin has made it a lot easier than the first time. It's a good class with good notes.

Awful, awful, awful class with an even worse teacher. By FAR the worst experience I've had here at UNC. Do not take this class! Do NOT take this class! If you absolutely have to, take it with someone else.
Probably my favorite professor, while this class is difficult, if you want to actually learn the material, read the notes and ask questions in class. Exams are just like the notes and homework.

I absolutely love having Professor Mclaughlin. She's such a kind and understanding person. I also took her for algebra, and she was always incredibly helpful. Her explanations are clear and easy to grasp!
Mclaughlin explains the homework in each class. Exams are like homework. Easy class. I like that the second exam is multiple classes after spring break.

Don't take this professor if you have no calculus experience. She teaches very fast-paced like she's reviewing the topics instead of teaching them. People who have taken calculus in high school do well. However, if this is not you, take a different professor who can actually teach you the topics like you're learning them for the first time.
Easier than my high school calc class. Good prof. Nice person.
Easy first exam. Questions are like the class notes and homework.

Nice lady who knows what she's talking about but can't teach it to save her life. Lectures are fast-paced, the notes she gives you are horrible, homework takes hours and is much more difficult than the material taught, and the exams are graded by nitpicky TAs who take a million points off for minor inaccuracies. Avoid at all costs, seriously!
She's very monotone, doesn't have much class resources, but is pretty nice.
Awful class, awful teaching style. Nobody takes this class for fun. Avoid at all costs.
Too much homework but overall a good prof and class.
No study guides. No extra credit or curves. All the other calc teachers gave their students review guides for tests and optional quizzes for extra credit. This teacher did not.

I had an ok experience, her lectures weren't that helpful so I had to put in a lot of work outside of class like reading the textbook and going through her notes on my own. I would recommend spending less time on the edfinity and more on other rsources such as the textbook or crambetter, which is a site with rly good resources for this class!

i took my first math class at unc with her and had a pretty good experience. the grading is scary (final is >40% of the class) but her tests/quizzes are very straightforward. as long as you go over her notes thoroughly and understand how to solve those types of problems, you will be fine. she wrote the final last sem so it was also pretty easy

Professor Mclaughlin's instruction is alright, not great.  She expects you to understand the material ahead of time, and that her class time is "review" and practice.  Hard to get a hold of outside of class, office hours times jumped around, not great at responding to emails. Homework is harder, but tests are extremely fair. Must work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mclaughlin was a great professor. Calc 3 introduces a lot of new things but she was able to teach it in a way that wasn't overwhelming. The class is very test heavy, like 90%, but the tests were very manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not an interactive or interesting lecturer. Hard to follow in class at times, but mostly fine. IMPOSSIBLE homework but VERY fair tests. Overall positive because homework was 4% of the grade and tests were 92%. Take if you can self motivate, self teach some concepts, or are a good test taker. Go to ULA sessions and pray for a good recitation TA.
Excellent class. Great notes. Tests are straightforward.

One of my best decisions was taking the course Pass/Fail. The classes were difficult to understand. Her explanations felt more like summaries than detailed instructions, and her notes were erased within 10 minutes. The homework was difficult and lengthy, with little relevance to the exams. I studied on YouTube for the final and got a better score.

MATH233 is tough no matter how you slice it. McLaughlin was a good professor and made all lectures available after the fact via recordings, as attendance isn't required. Tests were worth 90% and some HW on edfinity is very different from lecture so use ChatGPT and you'll be fine. Tests were fair and she's prob the best you'll get with 233.

She's not the best at explaining concepts, but her class structure is good enough. The homework is way too difficult to be useful (use the MHC! and TAs are helpful), but as long as you practice her drill problems from the notes and watch Prof. Leonard on Youtube, her tests are very doable. She will round up to the nearest whole # for letter grades.

She is a smart professor who understands calculus; however, intro-level calc is not her specialty. She teaches the course as if everyone has already taken it. Homework was about 10% of my grade, the rest being tests. The only people who succeeded in this course were those taking it again after high school AP. Be ready to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Okay experience taking MATH-233 with Prof. McLaughlin. Daunting grading criteria (final was like 41% of grade) and heavy amounts of material did set the bar early on. Interesting material, alot of self-studying (lectures were usually her reiterating notes written years ago). 

Expect this to be more difficult than 232 and a continuation of 231.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests are heavy, but easier than homework (less than 5% of grade). Do all homework and you should be fine. Lectures are extremely useful IF you review the notes before going to class. Content is easier than Calculus 1 or 2 in my opinion, much more straightforward. Partial credit is very forgiving.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Inflexible. Uncaring. No empathy. Professor does not have respect for you and does not give any partial credit or respond to emails! Avoid.
No empathy. Tough grader. Inflexible with deadlines and does not give partial credit. Avoid this professor please if you want to feel valued and respected.

Let me warn you. No Calc 3 prof at UNC will be “easy”. The math department holds no kindness in its soul. If you are worried about this class, do not take it with her. Take it at Wake Tech/Durham Tech and protect yourself from this horror. Everyone I knew who did well learned from another professor (YouTube) and didn't even do the HW. Just don't.
Her lecture style was monotone and enthusiasm nil.
To do well on this course, you should find a good YouTube channel.
She seems to be a nice person on the outside, but the way she treats students is customer service.
She is the most boring professor I had at UNC.
Do not take this professor for calc 3. She doesn't know how to explain concepts in an intuitive way.

She is a kind professor and seems to really care for her students. I found her lectures easy to understand. The homework can be very frustrating, but as long as you get 80%, you'll get full credit. Exams are WORLDS easier than the homework. If you're a math major, know that she doesn't go over proofs during lecture. I would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very very easy class. Too much time was spent on the people who couldn't do algebra. McLaughlin was a good teacher, but the class was slow.
Easy class. Edfinity homework had hard problems that were difficult to follow..

This is my favorite class this semester!!!! Prof Mclaughlin is an awesome teacher. The notes are helpful, well written and the exams arent hard if you do the work. The homework is long and not always helpful.

Clearly, she is a smart woman who knows her stuff and cares about her students... that being said, she cannot teach an intro-level, basic class. She was confusing and patronizing, and overall, it was a negative experience. The math here sucks no matter what, and this is NOT an exception. I would recommend taking this course with anyone else.

She isn't a super interesting, but she explains concepts clearly the first time. She doesn't answers question well, but she available to answer them outside of class. The homework is stupidly hard, just get through it and then use the notes and example problems to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Please dont take her. Please!
Please dont be deceievd. Her tests are not at all similar to her class content. Struggled a lot even though I practised and studied a lot for this class.

I'm retaking this course and have never been more confused. The professor projects the notes she took with almost illegible handwriting and presents them in a disinterested way which makes it hard to follow. I tried to meet with her many times outside of the office hours which didn't work with my schedule and she was ALWAYS "unavailable".
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The prof's lectures can be confusing, but she's helpful if you actively seek help. Homework is standard for all Calc 3 classes and may not always align with her lectures, so her notes that she posts are better study tools for tests than the homework. You can definitely get by in McLaughlin's class if you put in the work.

Dr. McLaughlin is extremely kind and caring and will always go out of her way to make sure students understand concepts. Her exams are very straightforward and she explains concepts well in class. She posts all of her notes in Canvas and does a good job going over them in lectures. Homework was more difficult than exam questions. Highly recommend!!
Amazing teacher! I was sooo scared to take math and Prof Mclaughlin has helped me.. 45 on the first exam and 76 on the second. Definitely take her.
The exams are straight forward and from the notes and homework. The lectures are interesting. It will be an easy A. She answers all questions in a patient way. Nice person.

Her lectures are all over the place and the homework is wildly hard. There are no practice materials for the exam so you don't know what to expect and they just continue to get harder each time (they are the majority of your grade). Lastly, she is simply just a very rude professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although Calc 2 is tough, Professor McLaughlin's detailed notes and practice-focused approach made it doable. Unstuckstudy AI was a lifesaver for study prep. Challenging but rewarding class.

She was absolutely amazing. Although lectures could often be a bit confusing, she was happy to answer questions and give feedback which made all the difference for my understanding. The tests are super straightforward and many questions have a similar format to those in the lecture notes. DO NOT fall behind, especially, if you do this over summer.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the easiest classes I have ever taken. Her homework is brutal, but you only need a 40% to get full-credit. Her tests are an absolute cakewalk. I barely studied and got a 100% on the final. She never makes you feel stupid when asking questions. She's so kind; I nominated her for a teaching award. Take this class!

Taking Math 231 at UNC went well and the material was accessible, however, taking Math 232 was a completely different ball game. Specifically with Dr. Mclaughlin, she goes through lectures extremely quickly, is not very concise, confuses herself, uses old notes and writes in disappearing ink. Any youtube video will do better at explaining material.

I was concerned about taking calc 2 as it has a reputation at UNC for being very difficult, but her lectures and notes helped me succeed in the class. I scored a 94 on the final. It was a good experience.

Although Calc 2 is regarded as being challenging, taking it with Professor McLaughlin made it even harder. She has an unorthodox method of teaching, and would give sarcastic responses to students who asked questions. This made me uncomfortable to ask questions when I didn't understand something and my grade kept going down.

This class was an absolute nightmare. She did not use textbooks and her notes written during covid was used instead. The problem was that her handwriting was awful and hard to follow. During lectures, she just underlined the same notes with her red disappearing pen on her iPad. The final screwed me over, as I got a 43. I know many people failed.
Great notes. The exams are straightforward and not hard. The homework is ok.

Used prewritten notes during lectures. Lectures material very quickly. Homework is so much harder than it needs to be and is not great practice. Easy exams. TA recitations are very helpful. I recommend watching a video on the material or reading through her notes before class. Her notes are a fantastic study tool.

She does not have the best lectures, but she posts her notes, which are clear and easy to understand. If you skip the lectures, read her notes, and do the assigned homework you can get an A in this class quite easily because the tests are extremely easy.

A very passive aggressive professor. Made things seem straightforward when they weren't. You will have no idea what your final grade is until the very end or how curves or test corrections will help you. Barely responded to my emails. You will have a lot of homework only for it to have no positive impact. If you do bad on her exams, you're doomed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not an easy class but prof Mclaughlin makes it doable. The structure works for me. You read detailed notes before class. Like a textbook. Then she goes over the notes and we do examples in class. It's hard when i don't have time to read the notes before class. The homework is harder than her examples sometimes. The exams aren't too hard.
My favorite class by far. Love the way she teaches. The examples are intuitive and interesting. Definitely take her. It's hard to get in the class. Waitlist was messed up.

Mostly used a laser/disappearing pen to talk about previously written notes. Didn't actively work through many problems. Made math so difficult, and even the ULA joked about this habit of hers. Used too much terminology and "interesting" references and offshoots that I found lecture pointless. Attendance didn't matter in lec but did for recitation.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Mclaughlin's class is my favorite class this semester. I didn't like my prof last semester but she has a way of explaining that makes sense to me.
Take her class. Very interesting lectures. The class isn't hard if you go to class and do the homework.

A nice person but not a good lecturer. Scattered and teaches in a way as if you already have a high level of understanding on the material. Taught myself the entire class using Professor Leonard Utube Vids. The exams were not extremely hard and were similar to the practice material she provided so that is great. Also there is tons of homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the better calculus professors for sure. Two midterms and a final. Only other thing that's graded is the homework, worth 10%. Let us have test corrections on midterms, but is a slow grader and disorganized. Wouldn't get exam grades back until weeks later. Homework has example vids tho which were very helpful for studying and exams were fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Did not enjoy her lectures and ended up teaching myself the material from the Pearson videos. Both TAs were better lecturers than her. However, her midterms are very similar to the example questions in her notes, and seemed easier than the other professors'. A good choice if you just need the credit, as long as you practice her examples

As far as calc 3 goes, she is your best pick if you can take notes in class and practice the material on your own time, she has very straightforward tests, but be warned the final is 38% of your grade. She is very lecture heavy and doesn't do many practice problems, so I would suggest asking your TA for help if you have questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I did not like her teaching style, which was just reading notes off the board. She didn't do math problems with the class like all my other calc profs have done. So I just taught myself everything. But her tests were manageable if you studied hard and memorized how to do different problems. Overall, she isn't your worst pick for calc 3
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super detailed notes and interesting clarification in class. We worked a lot of in class practice problems that were helpful, especially right before the final.

Professor Mclaughlin is nice and her notes are very detailed, but her teaching style is odd because she is explaining notes that are already written down. Tests are also around 87% of the grade. You can still study and end with a good grade though.

Calc 3 isn't easy with anyone, but Prof. Mclaughlin is a great teacher who cares about her students. The lectures are fast, but they are recorded. The class is very exam heavy and the final is worth 40% of your grade. There were a lot of resources to succeed with a ULA and the help center, and her tests were manageable.

Calc 3 is hard no matter who or where you take it just because of the amount of material covered. Her lectures are great but fast, so if you're able to go over the notes before class (as she recommends) you'll be good. Plus all lectures are recorded. Only fault is having a majority of your grade come from 2 exams plus a final worth 38%.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very interesting class. Especially the way lectures involve an intuitive understanding of the material and how all the material connects. Nice prof too.

yawn. I don't blame her. She clearly doesn't care about calculus, but she cares about the class. She'll hold up the hoops for you to jump through, so for all you CS and physics majors who need calc iii, this is a really easy way to get through it all. Not a lot of actual "mathematics" so if you like proofs or the "art" of math, this ain't it.

Typical bad UNC math professor. My main problem with Mclaughlin is how fast she went through material, and the way she set up her lectures. She would go so quickly, and write important things down in the I-pad laser pointer so it disappeared in 30 seconds. Never explained things. People must just like her as a professor bc you can skip lecture.

Lecture is kind of boring/she goes very fast, but for a calculus professor she is great. Accessible outside of class, ULA's make a big difference, majority of grade is based on two midterms and a final (final is worth 38% of grade), but the tests are very straightforward and almost identical to class notes. probably one of the better clac 3 profs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Calc III has a lot of material and is inherently difficult. Prof. McLaughlin is a good at teaching it and communicates what will be on each test. The homework is harder than what is in class but each problem can be done three times; the tests are a lot easier than the homework. If you show up/watch the lectures and study, you'll get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
She is not easily accessed after classes or outside of classes. 
She doesn't take other student's personal situations into account.

Took her online over the summer. Class was very quick, but that was the nature of it. Professor was good at being understanding of the fact that we were drinking out of a fire hydrant. Very good about telling us what to expect on her tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I have ever seen at UNC. The lecture style is insane, you have to preread notes for every class which isnt that bad but she explains the concepts so fast that it is impossible to take notes during the class. She goes through the example problems even faster. There is no room to breath so do not fall behind during SS.

Dr. McLaughlin was really nice, but not great at actually explaining the material. I really recommend going to ULA sessions and for tests, just do all the problems on her posted slides. As long as you can do those problems, you should do pretty well on tests, which count for most of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Try to get into Dr. McLaughlin's section at all costs. She is great at explaining and the class was enjoyable and more passive. Do the homework problems to get used to the math, but the test problems will be much easier. It seems that the final exam has changed from previous years; it was very much easier than how previous students portrayed it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of homework but do it to understand. Lectures are clear with good notes. McLaughlin is a good teacher. Strange reviews below. Not logical thinking. Maybe that's why they didn't do well in the class. I heard 30% of the class scored A- and higher.

The average on her second midterm was a 65. On the final exam, which was standardized for all the calc classes, our class had the highest average. Apparently the other teachers let the final replace a midterm grade, and even had midterm averages in the 90's. She did not, and no curve. We knew the most, best score on the final, worst class grade.
Definitely take this professor. She genuinely cared how I did in the class. The class was easy and there wasn't much homework. She gives test corrections worth a full grade.

Calc 3 is a tough class no matter how you slice it. For this class, you always know what is expected of you, especially since the practice problems during lecture are like what you'll see on the exams. Also, she coordinates writing the final, so the class sets you up well for it. However, the lectures can be pretty dry and there's alot of hw.
My favorite class this semester. The practice problems in class helped with the exams. The homework is long.

Most mid professor ever. So boring, if you don't have an iPad just don't go to lecture because she moves at the speed of light with the most monotone voice to ever exist. the homeworks are ridiculously and unnecessarily long, the test averages are in the 60s. class overall not good, recitation garbage as well.

She teaches this class as if everyone has already taken calc, and she moves very fast. However, she is very very patient when it comes to explaining things as long as you ask questions. She is very straightforward and calm. The exams were much harder than the homework in my opinion. Your entire grade is graded by three exams and like 5% homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took both MATH232 and 233 with McLaughlin and I found her to be a great teacher. Her lectures can be a drag, but if you read the material beforehand and come with questions, it makes it way better. Keep up with the homework as there's a lot, but exams were straightforward and all from lecture. She's also super caring!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Calculus 1 with her. Calculus is a hard class but from what I heard from other students with different teachers, I could tell Mclaughlin was the best. Her tests also seemed to be the easiest (each professor made their own test except for the final). Her lectures are pretty clear and she is very approachable.

Professor McLaughlin was a very good lecturer and she did a great job at answering questions both in class and in office hours. Her lectures are a little dry and monotone, so I guess that's something to consider if that's an issue for you. Overall, highly recommend for your required calc classes.

Easily the best math class I've ever taken. I normally struggle with math courses but her lectures are just so clear and she really makes it easy to understand what you should be taking away from each practice problem.  Types of problems on tests are also just like the examples. Most of the grade is from tests though and there was no curve.

The way she taught concepts was hit or miss; either clearly explained it in a way that made sense with what we had already learned, or completely breezed through ideas without much elaboration. Grades are almost entirely made up of just 3 tests, which is frustrating considering partial credit was fairly hard to receive. Neither terrible nor great.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: easy professor if you go to class and do the homework. Doesn't curve tests but the averages are usually high
Solid class, make sure to study enough for tests since there are so few that affect your grade that one bad test can ruin the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's an average professor. Most of the class had already taken calculus, and she taught the class like everyone had already taken it. Not helpful for my first calculus class. There is weekly homework, two midterms, and a final. She did curve the final by a lot and expanded the C range for the final class grade.
Too much homework but lectures are good. The exams are similar to the notes.
I learned a lot in this class. Mclaughlin is a nice person who spent a lot of time helping me. Thanks to her!

I improved so much from the second midterm to the final and it seems like every other math professor take in consideration of that except for her. Her course material are hard to understand if you never took calculus before as she doesn't go much in depth into the materials she teaches and breeze through the examples she give in class.
Good class. Too much homework but the exams are not hard.

Good, caring professor. Wants you to have read notes beforehand, but you can get by just going to class and doing homework. Tests are most of the grade. Both midterms are fair and much easier than the homework questions. It's hard because it's math, but if you have to take calc, McLaughlin is not a bad choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As everyone else has already stated, 80% of grade is tests and 36% on a final that she has prepared us poorly for. She has shown on multiple occasions that she doesn't know exactly what's on the final, which I anticipate to be much harder than other exams. One screw up on a test and your grade is done for
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So overall, she is not that bad. But, the final grade is basically just your two midterms and the final. I was doing great and then the second final completely screwed me and now I have to make a 94 on the final to end with a B-. She definitely expects that most of the students took calc in high school when that is just not the case.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wasn't a fan of my calculus teacher last semester. But this class is very interesting and well taught. I'm a physics major and feel prepared for my next class.
MvLaughlin's class is my favorite class this semester. I didn't like calculus in high school but she has a way of explaining that makes sense to me. Definitely take her.

I didn't really like the way this class was formatted; Prof. McLaughlin utilized a "read my notes first, then I'll teach off of them" system, which just didn't work for me. She goes super quickly through subjects, explaining things very vaguely, and then expects you to have questions so she could answer them. I'd recommend someone else for 233.

McLaughlin is a good teacher. I didn't have calculus in high school and am following her instructions on hw and study plans for exams. Some of the people around me watch videos in class and don't pay attention. It's distracting when they ask questions that have already been answered. My only complaint is that she spends time on these people.

Ok so as a person, Professor Mclaughlin is very nice and lowkey kind of funny. However, the structure of her class is horrendous. There are three exams total (2 midterms, and 1 final) that are worth about 82% of your grade. The homework is also extremely time-consuming but it is only worth 9% of your grade.She expects everyone to know calc already.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No study guides, 80% of your grade is tests/final exam (Last exam average was a 60 btw), Homework is so unhelpful, Do not take this class

Professor McLaughlin is perhaps the worst professor I have had, she is unclear, monotone, and a tough grader on her tests, which are worth around 80% of the overall class grade. I would not recommend this class, especially for anyone who has not taken Calc before.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely DO NOT take this class, she doesn't reply to emails at all, her tests averages are a 60 and tests/final exam are worth 450/550 points for the class. This class has absolutely DEMOLISHED my gpa. Homework is on a website that doesn't reflect problems in class. It baffles me how there are so many good reviews
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are horribly boring. The exams are so hard and are worth a significant part of your grade. The homework is time consuming and doesn't align with the exams. She is not responsive to emails and expects you to already have a significant understanding of calculus. Do not recommend takign her at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Mclaughlin's 231 class after never taking calc before. She tries to make it sound like this class is open to student's who haven't taken calc before but it's not, you're expected to already know some things and she skips over some details when explaining processes. Her tests are often harder than the examples reviewed in class.
very nice person. easy class

McLaughlin is a good teacher. She's covering the text examples and adding her own notes which makes reading the book easier. The exams are fair and she's a nice person. The homework is long but not very hard. Definitely take her class.

Do NOT take this class if you haven't taken calc, you will be confused since she kinda jumps from a to b without an explanation, like i've taken calc and she confused things I was sure I knew. The tests are really broad which is good bc it's easier than the hw but the hw is very hard and doesn't represent what we actually have to know on tests
Easy A on the first exam. Not a hard class.

Prof McLaughlin's lectures do not help in the slightest and I have NO idea why she has so many 5 star ratings. If you don't already know some Calc you're screwed. Never explains things all the way/will assume you have prior knowledge even when she KNEW many of us hadn't taken calc before. You have to teach yourself!! DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

wow Was just talking with my friends in the same 231 class about what a great teacher she is, super patient. She's traveling to her mom's funeral in October and is trying to not get covid. Sorry to see entitled bs posted here.
Her tone stays the same, making me wanna sleep. I basically learn through self-learning and recitation. btw, she's rly rly scared of COVID...

Honestly, I was super hesitant to take calc 2 over the summer cause of all the stories but its the best decision I made with this professor. Shes super nice and if you know the content she shows in class, the tests are virtually the same. Just do the homework she wants you to do well !!

McLaughlin is lenient and very caring: 70% on homework is full credit; and tests are similar to homework questions, with a lot of partial credit. She works hard to clarify difficult concepts and is direct with test expectations. Summer Session final exam was easy. Be sure to do homework every night, and you'll have no problems getting an A or B.
I took this class in summer. Really good class. It goes fast but if you read the notes ahead of class then it's not very hard. A lot of homework. Loved the lectures. She's really clear and detailed.

Her lectures did not help at all. She never explained how to fully do a problem, just spent all class going over highlights of her notes pages. I could've spent that time actually teaching myself the material. It is worth your time to understand homework problems because they will help with exams (the class is exam heavy when it comes to grading).

Hardest class I've taken at UNC. Took this during the summer so the already challenge course got even harder with 6 my math lab due each week. So much work and so much harder in the summer. Had to put so much work into this class. With that being said, McLaughlin is a good professor and is adaptable and accessible. Hard professor but is very caring

I took her class during a summer session and wasn't impressed. Her lectures via zoom were mandatory, though they weren't helpful in the slightest. She gave the option of video lectures which were much more helpful, but stopped posting them midway through the course. She also grades the exams fairly hard with very little partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: McLaughlin explained things very well and her midterms were really not too hard. Be aware that the final exam for MATH233 is written by all the professors and not just McLaughlin, so it was insanely difficult. The homework for this class is tough but I couldn't have asked for a better professor.
Math is hard for me and Professor McLaughlin was patient and helpful. I appreciate everything she did. I got a B+

The exams are much harder than material she goes over in class. It is a difficult class and she is not very accessible, I emailed her once trying to see if she could do appointment office hours since I had a class during hers and never got an answer. She is kind and funny but goes over things very quickly with little explination.

McLaughlin is a fair prof. Nice lady. Solid, well organized class. The homework is tough but necessary to get a decent grade because the exams look a lot like the homework. She has prerecorded videos of all of the topics which is helpful.
My final grade is 89.5 and she gave me an A- !!!!!!! I LOVE HER.
Very easy class. Some of my friends in the class were struggling and she was patient.
Shes extremely nice, however the exams are harder than what we do in class. There was no study material for the final and practice that was done in class did not look like final questions at all.

She really does love what she does and she is always down to help but I wish there was more that the class was not so test heavy. Mclaughlin is def the best 233 prof out there but if you are not a good test taker i do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Fair exams. Nice prof. Homework is hard.
Wrong! I loved this class. The notes are detailed and helped me get through this class. It's a tough class with a lot of homework.

Terrible. Do not take this class. The rating does not reflect the professor at all. Her lecture problems were all pre-solved and weren't solved in class. Her lectures did not reflect the homework or the tests at all and left you completely unprepared.
Awful professor. Her notes were terrible and she did not prepare her students well for the exams. She's a nice person and all, but not a good choice if you actually want to learn.
Just finished this class. The lectures were solid and the notes were very detailed. Really good lectures. I recommend taking her.

Not sure why Professor McLaughlin has such a good rating. Her lectures were rushed and difficult to follow - it was as if she expected us to have a good understanding of the material before coming to class. I had to do a lot of work outside of class to be comfortable with the level of difficulty in lecture and on tests. Pick a different prof.

Don't take this class with her if you don't have to. Bad professor that wasn't there to lecture for half of the class (her husband came in and lectured). Tests were way too hard and final average was really low for the class. Said she would curve but did not.
By far the best math prof I've had. She's detailed in her explanations. The notes are good.
Great notes and lectures.
Solid class. Excellent lectures. Was really into it because it helped me with physics.

She's not the most exciting lecturer on the planet, and she moves a little quickly, but she provides a lot of resources to help you out if you're stuck. Recordings from past years, very thorough notes, etc. Especially for a class as difficult as multi-variable calculus, I think she's the best you can get at UNC.

Prof. McLaughlin is a great calculus teacher, and with her fantastic note documents will give you the tools and knowledge to do well on the exams and get better at math. There is a good bit of homework, but it's acceptable and often helpful given the difficult content, which requires a lot of practice. I would certainly recommend her!

McLaughlin has a complete set of notes. We're asked to read them before class and watch a video explanation for clarification. Then she goes over them again in class. I like her intuitive approach to explaining the concepts. Interesting to understand why we are solving problems the way we are. It's been vey helpful for my physics class.

Professor McLaughlin is a solid choice for Math 110. The content isn't hard at all as it is mostly review from high school with a little new material. She was a good lecturer but can get confusing at times but is quick to respond to emails and very helpful in office hours.

Honestly, I'm surprised at how high these ratings are. Prof. McLaughlin was approachable, nice, and passionate about calc. I also know college calc is significantly more difficult than high school. However, the lectures were way over-complicated and didn't follow a clear format. Class made me more confused, but not attending made me fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My issue w McLaughlin is that she can't dumb material down enough when teaching. She provides notes, but instead of going through the problems step by step, she shows it to you already done and hits the highlights, which made a lot of concepts unnecessarily hard. Tests aren't bad compared to other profs, but her teaching style isn't for me
Best math instructor I've had.

This Professor was very average, which can make things difficult if you need really good explanations for math. She recorded lectures which was helpful. Homework could be significantly different approach from the lesson at times. I think that she just has a lot of stress to follow certain standardizations.
Very clear lectures and a fair professor. Lots of homework and the subject is difficult. I did well because I completed most of it.

DO the practice tests she offers and you'll ace the class. Her exams are not hard if you use the resources she provides. Not the best lecturer but a solid choice for math 110. Pretty fair person and easy to ask questions.
This is not an easy class but Professor McLaughlin explains the ideas clearly and the homework isn't too bad. Reading the notes before class is important if you want to keep up.

Sometimes lectures can be difficult to follow if you haven't been keeping up. She responds to emails quickly and is very accommodating. She posts notes for every lecture on sakai which are very helpful. I recommend reading those before lecture to get the most out of it.
Best class I've taken! Clear and interesting lectures. Do the work and you'll do well.
If you have to take Math 231, TAKE HER!!! Her exams were 10x easier than other sections, and very very similar to the final. She usually gave out a study guide which was super helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Mclaughlin is a really nice person. She was very understanding when I had issues when I was sick and she worked around them. However, I didn't really like her teaching style and I had to learn a lot by myself. The class is very test heavy so make sure you prepare well for them.

Took freshman year bc I liked math and got a 5 on the calc ABBC exam. Struggled so much. First 2 exams got Fs, the homework doesn't help w/tests. I finally learned how to study for her then got 100s on second two tests. Practice and rewrite her notes! Recitation is req but lecture isn't (I didn't go a lot). Try to take a diff prof
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Fair professor. Easy class. Prepare for the tests and you'll be good.
