She was a fair teacher. The exams were easy enough and the lectures were good. She's a nice person, too.

Was no point in going to class, as she lectured straight from the textbook. None of the hw assignments matched with those on the test. The one time she did give study material was the one time in which I did well on a test. However, she only gave review material once.

Prof McLaughlin is not a good teacher in my opinion, be prepared to teach yourself the material. The tests define how you will do in this course, and some of which I thought were unfair. Not understanding of people who struggle/need extra help. Do not recommend.

Professor McLaughlin was really good. Her teaching style came off as a bit new. She will have all her notes already written and uploaded on the website, as well as videos going over the notes. However, don't skip the lectures. The tests are straight from the lectures and homework. Her tests are very fair, including the final. Amazing professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great teacher! Very clear lectures and is nice.
I had calculus in high school and placed back into this class. Prof McLaughlin is the best math teacher I've ever had. She's patient and explains the ideas in a clear way.

Lectures do not help at all. She moves quickly and expects you to understand from a Calc perspective when it's only algebra. This could be a challenging math course for those who even considered themselves good at math. Please choose another professor if you can, if not make group chats and actively study with explanations from other professors.
Professor McLaughlin's lectures are clear. Her exams are fair if you follow her study suggestions.
Calc 231 can be difficult for some people but Professor McLaughlin will make supplementary videos of certain lecture topics if you ask. The three tests are a large part of your grade, just beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best class of my semester.

Professor McLaughlin cares about her students, has fair tests that reflect the material covered in class, and is clear on what will show up on a test beforehand. However, her lectures are not very effective. Be prepared to teach yourself the material in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: McLaughlin makes clear what concepts and types of problems are going to be on the tests, so its pretty easy to study and make sure you know how to do those. Her lectures do go somewhat fast, but if you print out notes that she posts on Sakai, it's easier to keep up. I also haven't opened the textbook since the first week and am doing well still.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: queen period! bestie! i love calculus with her!

Professor Mclaughlin isn't a rude or strict person, but her grading is pretty tough. I would always get points off my tests because I didn't solve the math problems exactly how she said to do it. However she does take the time to teach the material but the homework usually tends to be harder than the examples she does.

Her lectures are pretty fast, but she is really patient with questions, so don't be afraid to ask them. Her notes are super good and mostly easy to read, and are very similar to the exams. Exams are weighted pretty heavy, and you definitely need to study quite a bit to do well, but overall one of the better MATH 233 profs.

She's very nice and approachable. Calculus isn't exactly my strong suit, but she clearly knows what she's talking about, and doesn't look down on students for asking "dumb" questions. Tests are worth a very large portion of the grade, so make sure you're prepared. You will need to study for them, and don't procrastinate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a hard class and Prof McLaughlin is very patient. I appreciate all the effort she puts in.

This teacher has made algebra far more difficult than it needs to be. Class time is spent swiftly going over a few examples of the unit, which forces the student to teach themselves the rest of the content. The teacher does not respond to direct emails about math problems. We are supposed to receive help from Piazza, but many are left ignored.
Great professor, knows the course content really well. Is very nice and approachable IMO. Would take with her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She 's about the best that you could ask for in terms of teaching math. Her patience really impressed me, and every day she was prepared to enthusiastically discuss the material. Her exams were straight forward and the material on them was clearly covered in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor McLaughlin is an amazing instructor who really seeks to ensure each student has a full understanding of the material. Although online, she was able to make this class feel as if it were a traditional, engaging in-class experience. She deals out a lot of homework but my class only had to do 75% of it. Lecture-heavy with lots of time for Qs

I took this class during the summer and it definitely took a lot of time each day just to complete the homework and understand the material. 80% of our grade was calculated from two midterms (20% each and final as 40%), but McLaughlin always directly told us what would be on the tests. Solid choice for MATH233 and explains concepts pretty well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Your grade consists mostly of the three tests but I found them to be pretty fair. The lectures weren't always clear to me so I ended up having to use YouTube video lectures to help and that made a huge difference. Overall, I think she's a kind professor but depending of the kind of learner you are, you might need to outsource some assistance.

Prof. McLaughlin was super understanding and was an amazing lecturer. Calc 3 is hard in general but her teaching style was very helpful. Her exams aren't bad at all and resemble the questions in her notes very closely. There is a good amount of homework and it is hard but very helpful to understand topics conceptually. Overall a great class!
This was a well organized class. I don't do well in math and appreciated all her help.

I had to drop the class. I am not good at math and found that taking it over Zoom with this professor was not the easiest. She was patient and nice, but I struggled too much to stay in the course. If you are already decent at math, you would be fine with this professor, but if not, you've got your work cut out for you.

I think she tried her hardest to teaching through zoom this semester, but often times I felt there was a miscommunication between her and the class. A large part of the grade is determined by tests and quizzes. I was not a fan of her style, I felt as if she only reviewed content than teaching it. However, she was helpful to any questions asked!
Very patient. Detailed class. She make calculus interesting.
Take this prof if you want to understand the material in depth. Very good so far.
She works hard to make sure each person gets their questions answered. She is very patient.
My favorite class this semester. She's an excellent teacher. Not hard if you do the work.
Although Ms. McLaughlin was kind, she was not the best at teaching. Her explanations were confusing and she made lots of mistakes, but if we did the same, we were given no partial credit on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Calc 3 is def not easy, especially online, regardless of what prof you take it with. You will have to study super hard to get an A, but she always takes time to help. She has the most straightforward exams (all questions from HW and notes), which is great but also screws you over for the final since other profs write harder questions.
Its a hard class but her tests tend to be more straightforward. Can be time-consuming but doable to do well. Final may be curved a little, but not the midterms.
Exams are fair. A lot of homework. Class notes are clear and cover everything. Nice prof.
So good!

Professor McLaughlin's notes are usually really helpful and if you go to office hours, she can be really helpful. Your grade is almost entirely dependent on two tests and the final but the questions are almost exact copies of the examples she gives in class. Calc is going to hard regardless but I this definitely wasn't bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Midterms will not try and trick you. Most all problems will come directly from lecture and recitations. However, there is a boatload of homework that is only intended to further your conceptual knowledge, not help for exams. Just tedious work to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: We have the least amount of work among all 233 sessions (only hw, no participation) and Prof McLaughlin posts her notes online, which summarize the topics clearly and are much easier to read than the textbook. Tests could be a bit difficult but this is calc 3 after all. She is a very kind person and encourages you to go to her office hour.

Overall, the class isn't insanely difficult, but it definitely requires a good bit of work. Her teaching style isn't very good (in my opinion), so be prepared to teach yourself the material. With access to practice exams, progress checks, and past exams, doing well on exams is very possible.

I honestly didn't have a problem with her teaching style-- I think it could've turned out better for me if Fall 2020 semester wasn't so chaotic. I think the grading system is a bit harsh: only three tests w/ minimal partial credit, and the final is close to 40% of your grade. The homework inflation helps. Slightly disorganized but nothing too bad:)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Good class. Not too hard. In depth explanations.
I put a lot of time into this class using her notes and videos. It was not an easy A, I definitely worked for it but everything is well organized and she's a good teacher.

We only had 2 tests for the semester and then the final, so if you did poorly on the tests, you better get a great score on the final. I, personally, had a hard time understanding the material during the lectures so I stuck to reading the textbook. Overall its an ok class, just put a lot of effort into the tests and homework and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It's an ok class. Homework takes awhile but is easy to get a 100 on cause you get 3 tries to answer it. Exams are ok, if you study and do a lot of practice questions. I liked her class but that was just because I was ok with the lecture style of her teaching. I also like rewatching lectures to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Online format: posts lecture video/notes before class; goes over same notes during class; homework due on Sundays; two tests and final exam; suggests textbook reading. Overall, the class wasn't impossible, the homework is WAY more difficult than the exams, but she's approachable with questions.

I didn't have a lot of trouble in her class (took bc in hs), but I could see how learning from her would be hard. Read the textbook & watch videos of her going over notes before class. She stopped posting the videos halfway through the semester so that made it trickier. Do the practice problems! The practice problems are way harder than tests.
No partial credit was given on tests which make up the majority of the class grade
Interesting class. Nice prof.
Detailed class and good lectures. Definitely recommend this instructor.
Solid class.
lectures were not super in depth and the homework was very different than the class notes

I appreciate the amount of time she put into our class. The course notes are helpful and her explanations are clear. The exams are not too difficult but the homework is. This is a very hard class but I'll be getting an A- because of the extra help she provided.

I really like this course. McLaughlin provides detailed notes and corresponding videos. The lectures are clear. Very solid class. She's approachable and works with you if you miss assignments. Definitely take her if you want to understand concepts.

I am taking this class fully remote atm. Class is very lecture heavy and she isn't very good at lecturing. The homework is not relevant and often covers material outside the course and is auto graded. Most of the grade is from tests and have no partial credit. Class averages for tests are in the 60s with no curve until the end of course.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took this class in the summer online due to COVID. I thought she was a pretty solid instructor. She was nice and would answer specific questions about what exactly we needed to know for tests. The online hw had unlimited attempts so was a completion grade. I barely passed the class but test averages were in the 80s so I would recommend!
The class was well organized and the videos helpful. She is a very detailed and quality prof. Definitely take her if you want to understand concepts.

Dr Mcluaghlin is a very good professor! I had heard some not-so nice things before taking her but she was actually a very good professor. She was easy to understand and was always helpful outside of class.

Not sure about the last review since she wasn't live lectures. It was all recorded lectures and was excellent. A very clear and organized class. She grades the exams with the other instructors. I'd definitely take another class from her.

Her TA's grade tests. When you're in class and she says that she would give you credit if you answered a math problem a certain way, don't trust it because she won't be grading your tests. Also, the problems you do in class are way easier than the ones on the tests. She can be demeaning and I think she cares more about her higher level math classes

Easy A if you read the text, go to class and do the homework. Her lecture style is detailed and informative. She really knows the material and doesn't dumb it down. I liked that about her teaching style. I feel prepared for the class I'm in this semester. Definitely take her if your priority is understanding the material.

Prof McLaughlin's class prepared me for calc 3 this semester. She is a thorough and detailed teacher. One of the smartest teachers I've had. If you take good notes and pay attention in class, getting a good grade shouldn't be a problem.

McLaughlin is caring but not great at teaching. You may fall asleep during lectures. The material taught was not difficult but wasn't taught well. Felt like the homework wasn't helpful. The recitations were more helpful than the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The best teacher I've had in math. Prof McLaughlin was awesome! Lectures were clear and she cared about how well we did. Definitely take her class.

I have never made below an A+ in a math class until now. She's hands down the worst professor I've had thus far and I went to just about every class. She sped through lectures, does not write out all of the steps/work in class and does not teach down to people without a calculus background and the average for the final (that she wrote) was a 65.
Tests are very reasonable if you show up to class and pay attention. Make sure to stay on top of work and ask questions if you are ever stuck.

Tests make up the good majority of your grade in this class, but McLaughlin makes her tests really easy. She gives really hard examples in the homework and in class, but the problems on the test are the most basic and simplified versions of what was taught, making it easy to do well on the tests.

The class was taught clearly and paced well. Lectures are a little dull, and the graded recitation worksheets and long homework assignments were a bit of a drudgery, but overall, the class is designed to teach the material thoroughly, and the tests are a pretty fair evaluation of how much you've learned.

I really liked being in Dr. McLaughlin's class. She was very clear about what kinds of questions we should expect on the exams (she also usually writes the math 231 final). I went to every lecture, took notes, and did many practice problems from the textbook and I was able to do well on her midterms. She is also really helpful in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: McLaughlin was my favorite teacher this semester. She was super helpful in office hours. Very funny and smart.
Good class. Exams are easy. Go to class and review her class problems. Pretty much the same test questions.

Thanks to Prof Mclaughlin I passed calculus. She's an awesome teacher! She really cares about her students. She answers emails on the weekends and will work with you until you understand. I was afraid to take this class, but she was kind to me, which helped. She's also very patient so if you are freaked about taking this class, go see her in office

I enjoyed the course. The objectives were clear and her lectures and the homework prepared me for the exams. The final exam was fair. I worked for my A- and feel that it reflected my performance. I've never had calculus and I'm pleased with my grade. The homework is long and crashes, but that happened in my other classes too.

I enjoyed Professor McLaughlin's class; however, her teaching style is heavily centered around what students should have already learned from the textbook. She does not track attendance; however, it's hard to pass if you don't come to class. Sadly, our final exam grade was extremely low and although she promised a curve, it wasn't applied to A & Bs
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: McLaughlin spent a majority of the class solving problems incorrectly and then students would be forced to help her correct her errors. The final exam had no similarity to the midterms and midterms were graded in a manner so that one incorrect question would be deducted 14 pts. Seemingly simple material was taught in a complex manner.
Awesome class!

McLaughlin for MATH 232 was the hardest class that I have taken at UNC, and I'm usually a great math student. You have to teach yourself all the material because she is so bad at teaching the class. The tests are completely unfair, but she doesn't write the final, so that's the only way to save your grade. DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Definitely take this prof. She teaches beyond the text. More like a concept style class. Very interesting. Don't take her if you are looking for a teach and regurgitation type lecture. It makes getting an A harder, but will be useful for the next calc class I'm taking.
This was a very good class. She was helpful and provided examples in class that were useful for studying for the exams. She's nice and pretty funny if you get to know her in office hours.

Good class. Prof McLaughlin uses a lot of examples to explain the topics. It was helpful to hear what to expect in the next calculus class up. Homework is long. The recitations have worksheets which are helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I LOVED this class. She explains beyond the textbook. Really interesting class.

If you're premed avoid this class like the plague. I screwed my GPA so bad by taking this class and it's only my first semester of college which means I'm only one semester in and I've already ruined my shot at med school. This class is absolutely impossible and McLaughlin doesn't explain anything. She's very smart/kind but a terrible professor.
Her class is not that hard. Don't slack off. The homework is long but not bad.
Easy class if you do the homework and not miss class. Lectures are clear and helpful. She's very nice and approachable. It would have been useful if she had office hours later in the day.

Lectures are all over the place and tough to follow. But if you go to class and pay attention, exams are pretty straightforward. She did not write her own final when I took the class and it was ridiculously hard and nothing like the midterms. If you are good at math, take her, but if you struggle please take with another professor
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was a difficult class but Prof Mclaughlin explained ideas well and answered all of my questions in class. The homework is painful but if you do it all the exams aren't too bad.

Really excellent teacher. She makes difficult material easy to understand if you go to class and ask questions. She knows the math. I'm surprised how much I ended up liking calculus. Didn't in high school.

If you go to class and do the homework, getting an A isn't hard. Prof McLaughlin is very good at explaining the material and providing feedback via email if you need it. She's helpful in office hours and cares if you understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If I hadn't taken calc in high school I would be beat. Try to find another professor if this is your first time learning it. She does not explain concepts very well and gets confused when doing practice problems. Tests are quite difficult and they count for like all of the grade. Recitation and TAs were very helpful though.
awesome class! show up, do the homework. easy grade

McLaughlin's class is interesting. Not very difficult if you attend the lectures. Exams are more or less the problems she works in class. She was very kind to me during office hours. I was sick a lot and she helped me to get back on track. I highly recommend taking her class.

Going to class confuses you rather than helps you. If you ask a question she never knows the answer and just tells you she'll get back to you and never does. If you get her for math and have to take her for some reason wait another semester for another teacher because you will struggle so hard.

Dr. Mclaughlin is nice but awful at conveying the material during lectures. She says she can slow down but will just speed back up 5 minutes later. 3 exams written by the TA's and not her. Funny thing is that TA's do not even show up to class to see the difficulty of problems we do during class. Overall, it is a stressful class. Don't recommend.
good class

If you listen actively during the lectures, you'll feel prepared by the time of the exams. Professor McLaughlin explains things at a good pace and has great explanations! Personable and open to answering questions or slowing down during lecture. The homework is usually harder than the exams, which actually helps in the long-run.

reviews.comment: I was scared to take calculus but Prof McLaughlin made this class easy to understand. She's very patient. I recommend taking her !

reviews.comment: I'm in math 232 and I think it's an awesome class. Mclaughlin is very clear and interesting! Not sure why people review and speak for an entire class. if you go to class and do the homework you will pass.

Calc is hard in general, she is a very intelligent professor but she isn't the best at dumbing thing down which could make things very confusing to understand during lecture. reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She clearly knows her stuff, but can't explain it simply during lecture. You're going to get a headache trying to understand her during class, and then get another headache later when you try to teach yourself the material at home. There's nothing more unifying than a room full of people that have no idea what is going... at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I won't pretend that Ms. McLaughlin is the best teacher ever, but she knows her stuff and she's not half bad. She has a relaxed personality which doesn't necessarily serve the enunciation of math concepts. Self study is definitely needed, but she's also very approachable in office hours. In the end, I sought her help and got an A in Calculus 2.

I personally loved prof McLaughlin. I highly recommend not skipping classes because she teaches concepts well and teaches from the book so you can use that as a resource as well. You have to work for your grade but it's not unfair or unreasonable. The tests are derived from hw and class exercises and are regular enough to reinforce the material.
Really good summer class. It went fast but McLaughlin explained all the topics very well. She gave plenty of review materials for the final exam during the last week of classes.

At first I really didn't like her disorganization. She didn't write her own syllabus. For some reason she had someone else write it so she was always a little confused on where we were and why we were doing what we were doing. After a while I kinda got use to her sporadic teaching. The only reason I did so well was that I had a calculus background.

I took Math 232 and 233 from Prof. McLaughlin. She's a detailed oriented teacher and very smart. Class lectures go quickly so if you keep up with the homework you will follow. Lectures connected key concepts throughout the semester so by the time we made it to the end the ideas came together in an interesting way. I highly recommend her.

Really good class. She gives problems for us to work in class and then walks around the room giving individual feedback. Super helpful. The homework is long and keeps crashing, but is necessary for getting a decent grade on her tests.

Monotonous and excruciatingly boring lecture style. It's hard enough to keep a 100 person class interested normally, and her style really doesn't help in that regard. Nice curve on the final grade, but I gained more from my weekly recitation with the TA than in any of the actual lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor McLaughlin does go fast, but she does care if you understand the material. It is imperative you practice outside of class, because she expects that you're ready to move on by the next lecture. She always seemed ready to answer questions and always used relevant examples in class. Graded by 4 midterms, a cumulative hw grade, and a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: While it may take a little getting used to her style, she's a really great teacher. While she does not provide many worksheets, she often gives extra problems at the end of lecture or emails them out after class and provides the answers too.
I love this class! Ms McLaughlin has an interesting teaching style. Her examples are visual based which makes this class easier to understand.
Class is just a regurgitation of the textbook, and the professor doesnt help you much if you have questions of your own. If you want to do well in this class read ahead in the textbook.

reviews.comment: I took Professor McLaughlin for all three calculuses (231, 232, 233) and I did this because I loved her teaching style. reviews.comment: Very clear objectives. Excellent class. Easy A if you attend class, do the homework, and review class notes.

She has quick hand writings but a clear introduction to the things she would like to convey. To succeed in class, you can read the relevant chapters before head. She teaches the chapters based on textbook. If you do homework and the examples given during the class well, you will get good grades for it.
Only take her if you have to, the textbook saved me in my class.
Really awesome teacher!

I had an amazing AP Calculus teacher in highschool and so I was nervous coming into Math 232 with Mclaughlin after reading her reviews. Don't believe the lies! reviews.comment: LOVED the class! She made calculus interesting with cool visual explanations.
Elizabeth is a clear lecturer. The exams are fair. I did well in the class. I dont usually like math but I liked this class.
Easy class if you do the homework. She curves the final grade so it didnt matter if the tests were curved. Clear explanations and easy exams if you take notes. Tests are like the notes.

This is the worst class I have ever take, the teacher is unclear about what she is teaching and require you to learn by yourself most of the time. Hard exam and hard homework, regret taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. McLaughlin is a clear lecturer who gives great visual explanations where possible. The WebAssign homework is good practice (and usually more difficult than the exams), but also the most time-consuming part of the class.

reviews.comment: Loved this class! I'm taking her for 233 next semester.

Elizabeth is very nice & not intimidating. She teaches straight out of the book & the class is lecture heavy. She may seem a little unprepared/scattered, but she has a passion for math. If you work hard in recitation and do the hw you should not struggle too much. When she makes her own tests they are always fair and on stuff we have covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The final exam was difficult but McLaughlin prepared us adequately. We were given review sheets in class. I appreciated that. Overall it was an interesting class and well taught.
Good class.
Ms. McLaughlin always explained topics in a methodical manner. Step by step. This gave me a solid foundation for continuing on to Math 233.
A lot of homework, but all of my math classes had the same. Very good teacher. Definitely take her.

Really excellent class. Ms. McLaughlin was a very patient teacher and always available. When I couldn't make office hours she would let me email screenshots of my work, grade and return to me. She answered questions with respect during class. I don't understand why some of these reviews say otherwise. I guess math can be frustrating for some peopl.

I absolutely despised this class. I have always loved math, but Ms. McLaughlin truly ruined that for me. She speeds through everything, and acts annoyed if someone would have a question. I also found it more helpful to go to other teacher's office hours because when I went to her she made me feel like I was an idiot for not knowing the answer.

Calc 3 was an interesting class. I really love math and wasn't disappointed in Ms McLaughlin's teaching style. The homework was overwhelming at times, but necessary, I guess. I wish she was teaching diff eq next semester.

I took her for 152 and had to take an incomplete. Finally finished. She was so patient and worked with my constant delaying of due dates and exam dates. When I sent screenshots of work, she corrected and returned them. She went out of her way to help me and I'm very grateful!

I liked this class. McLaughlin went very fast but there was so much to cover. Reading ahead helps. The material was interesting and she had a clear presentation of the concepts. The class problems were helpful.
This is a very good class! It's a lot of work but if you go to class and do the homork it's not so bad.

McLauglin has a very complicated teaching style. For the0 tests she did not give us any exam review material or old practice tests. reviews.comment: She was disorganized and basically taught straight out of the book. She never gave us practice tests or study guides so we were on our own for tests. Was very unclear about what would be on tests. Her teaching style is basically rushing through a few concepts, and then doing a ton of complicated examples. Advice if you take her: read ahead!

Unless you already know how to do calc 3 dont take it with her. Youll spend hours studying just to find out the test is half on material youve barely gone over. Bad lecturer. Does things old school when that obviously doesnt work. Fair warning dont do it

Nice person, but not great instructor. Lectures quickly and straight from the book- big lecture hall class so if you prep and read book well, don't need to go to lecture. reviews.comment: Lot's of work. Don't miss lectures and read ahead. Good teacher.

reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Consensus was she has no idea what she's doing. I really hope that she just spends more time focusing on her other classes because multiple times she said, "I know this is Business Calculus, but I frankly know nothing about Business, so you can figure that out for yourself." I tried multiple times to talk after class and she said "I have no time."

One of the worst lecturers I've ever had. I went to every single class and took notes and almost failed. She gives horrible examples and doesn't even finish them sometimes. It's impossible to talk to her as there are so many students in the class and her TAs do their best but she doesn't communicate with them either.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Teaches by walking the class through an example problem, which I found helpful. Webassigns don't always completely line up with class material but tests are fair to what's taught in class. Is extremely patient (had to deal with so many first-semester freshmen attitudes so I really feel for her). Tests can be very short though (like 12 mc questions)

I love McLaughlin! My Calc teacher in high school had a similar style to hers, so learning was not that difficult. DO THE WEBASSIGNS and make sure you understand the problems. They are definitely harder than the problems she asks on the tests, so if you can master those, you'll be prepared. A lot of self-teaching, but nothing too bad. PRACTICE!!!

There are only 9-15 multiple choice questions on every test which makes it super easy to lose points. She also doesn't curve at all. Professor McLaughlin is available for assistance if you go to office hours, but this class is super hard! Definitely only take it if you absolutely have to.

Very poor teacher. Doesn't teach topics clearly. Must teach everything to yourself. Not very helpful when asked questions. Very rude when asked for assistance. Condescending and doesn't curve grades no matter how many people fail tests.

If you don't vibe with her teaching style, talk to her and then decide whether you should go to a different section. She's a great professor and truly made my freshman and sophomore years great, I actually wanted to go to class over the summer when I had her!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: You can tell that she relatively enjoys the material she's teaching. The homework is pretty tricky but once you get the hang of it, it's not so bad. Her tests are very straightforward if you understand the material. However, her tests are multiple choice with only 10-15 questions, so every point counts. She doesn't tend to curve tests.

Class is spent entirely going over problems from the book, not actually teaching. Students who do well are those who clearly are already great math students. The material wouldn't be that bad if she would actually teach it. I asked for help,, she said "read the book". Wouldnt recommend, take this class with someone else if you have to have it.

McLaughlin is not a great teacher. You can tell she knows what she's talking about, but she doesn't do well in conveying it to the class. She basically writes on the board exactly what is from the textbook and only elaborates if someone asks specific questions. The tests aren't too bad, but they're very short so it's easy to lose points quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Lecture is really fast paced but she still explains the material very well. She takes time in class to do practice problems and is very willing to answer questions during that time. Tests are only a few questions but they are not that difficult and all multiple choice. Go to office hours if you need help! She's always there.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took BC Calculus before retaking it at UNC, and Math232 with her was not hard at all. She basically just goes over the different "types" of problems that you'll encounter and then you do the rest on your own outside of class. Pro tip: don't retake MATH232 unless you got a 3 or lower on the AP exam, it's useless for MATH233 and a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: McLaughlin isn't as horrible as people make her out to be. MATH 232 isn't that hard either. Just study. She follows the flipped model, so you'll have to read the book and watch YouTube. However, her tests are easy and she puts test questions on the board when she has a review day for tests. She writes fast, so make sure you read before class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher
Never take this prof ever
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was my first experience with a flipped class. I struggled very much in the beginning but Professor Mclaughlin was still very encouraging to all of us. She would help us during class when we struggled with the homework and believed that we could do it. At the end of the class I actually liked math because of her and how she pushed me.

This is the hardest class I've ever taken. Pretty much every grade is based on 3 midterms and the final (she replaces a midterm grade). I think Mclaughlin is good but there is not enough time for the material so she has to go super super fast. If you get behind it's really tough to catch up, I would only take this class if you absolutely must

The exams she writes consist of 10 multiple choice questions, each covering a different complex topic with applications barely touched on in class. She does not understand what students ask of her half the time. As a student who attended every class, completed every homework, and studied hard for every exam, this was my least favorite math professo
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She was not a great instructor. I stopped going to class after the first exam because I could learn better teaching myself the material. She mostly does examples in class so I would read the text book before each class and get ahead so you know the material before she starts doing examples. Exams and the final are straight forward but study hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Math 231 was difficult, but definitely doable. Professor McLaughlin does go fast, but she does a good job of explaining concepts in detail when asked. Having a prior knowledge of calc from high school will definitely help. Her tests are difficult, but doing tons of practice problems out of the textbook will prepare you best for them.

Be sure to take this class somewhere else, especially if you're not a math major.  Her test averages (she makes the tests literally so impossible that she has trouble answering the questions) are literally around the 50-60%.  The A's are people who already know calculus from high school.  Her tests are usually unrelated to the questions in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She goes through topics very quickly and makes mistakes way too regularly making her class confusing and hard to follow. Doesn't really seem to care about students learning anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I had Mclaughlin for Calc 1 and 2, and she is definitely much better for Calc 2. She has much more enthusiasm for higher level topics, so she teaches Calc 2 more effectively. She is very fast paced, but does care about students and will go over certain topics if you ask for clarification. She will also personally go over your tests in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Everyone complains about how hard math 232 is, but as long as you study and go over the webassign problems before the tests you will be fine. If you think you can skip class or cheat on the homework and pass, you are wrong. Speak up if you do not understand something because sometimes she assumes you know something/the steps & no one says anything
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you skip class you are going to fail, so seriously do not skip. Sometimes she assumes you know something and keeps going, so don't be afraid to speak up if you need explanation. Her 3 exams are not too hard, and if you go over webassign and notes you will know how to do the problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I enjoyed and made an A in my high school Calc class. McLaughlin made me hate math. She taught advanced concepts (which were not complicated but she made them so) abstractly with few  concrete examples. TAs and my recitation leader taught me everything and I got an A but put in tons of hours outside of class. I will not take anymore math at UNC.

Professor McLaughlin is far from the worst Calculus professor you could have. She really knows the material and is capable of explaining things in clear detail - if she wants to. However, she speeds ahead during each lecture leaving many questions unanswered as she assumes you'll already know what to do by reading the textbook.

She mostly spends time proving things and does not really go through how to solve problems. After a while I stopped paying attention in class and caught up in recitation. However, I found her exams very straightforward and easy, so I recommend taking her class.

Professor Mclaughlin is a very good professor, even though I did not do as well as I wanted to in the class. Math 233 is a difficult class and i recommend reading before class and doing many practice problems. I believe that is where i slacked and if i had a regime then i would've done much better in the class. Prepared me well for the final.

Professor McLaughlin clearly is passionate about math/calculus but is not a gifted teacher. She does not go out of her way to help students. The material is very difficult, and McLaughlin does not make it much easier. Avoid taking this course, take MATH 231 or STOR 113 if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Do not take her. I'm sorry, she may be very knowledgeable of calculus, and it showed during some points of the semester. However, she DOES NOT know how to convey ideas very clearly, and often times forgets what class she is teaching, and expects you to know higher level concepts that you haven't learned yet (she also teaches 232 and 233)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Goes through material very quickly and with not much explanation.  Very nice woman but a difficult professor if you aren't math-oriented.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A straightforward teacher who worked closely to the textbook. Her tests are almost all based on questions shown in class or homework. She was always willing to take her time to explain something to any one student even if it took the whole class block. Overall, caring and rather straightforward tests. Webassigns took a fair amount of time though.

McLaughlin takes her time in lectures and provides plenty of examples to make sure you understand the material. The examples are much harder than the tests, so if you can do those then the tests won't be bad. There is homework twice a week, but aside from that its not a terribly demanding class. I feel like a learned a lot from McLaughlin.

She keeps it real and tries to put you in the best position to get good scores in the exam. She could be better with explaining sometimes. Take good notes in class because the problems she works on the board are likely to show up in one of the three midterms. Shes say it as it is and will usually give obvious hints for pop quizes.

Professor McLaughlin was oddly lax every time I reached out for help after receiving a not-so-great grade and just told me not to worry about it which was pretty frustrating. Unless you REALLY go out of your way to make yourself known to her (i.e. going to office hours, going up to the board, etc.) don't expect much help from the professor.

McLaughlin is a nice woman. However, she moves really fast and she doesn't clarify very well. It is extremely hard if you've never been exposed to Calculus concepts before. Tons of Webassign homework. Three hard midterms. Final can replace one of them. The important thing is to have a good recitation leader; they can really help you understand.

Lectures are her explaining and working out problems. Sometimes quizzes are given in recitation but its just more working out problems. Doesn't give partial credit. Claims you need to read the book in order to pass the test. Personally, not true. Read it once and it wasn't much help. Web Assign takes a very long time to finish. Tests are a bit hard
Terrible writing on the blackboard. She teaches really fast sometimes makes me confused.
she expects you to know a lot of stuff  prior to taking her class

I took calculus in high school and came in with a pretty good understanding. Somehow, through the course of the semester, I actually became more confused than I have ever been before. McLaughlin took the material I thought I knew, and explaining it in the worst way possible, managed to un-teach me all of it.

WebAssign is easy and helpful if you put in the time. She is willing to help if you come to class. Tests are very fair--more so than other calculus professors. Taking her for 232 next semester and would recommend. Class is a breeze if you had Calculus in high school.

While she is probably the easiest Math 231 professor, she's also the worst professor. Do not take McLaughlin if you have no calc background because she won't help much. She's confusing and does random example problems without explaining the concepts. This is the only class where my recitation actually helped because I had no idea what was going on.

Do not take math 231 with this professor.  She is very scatterbrained and her class is impossible. I got an A in AP Calc in high school and math was my strongest subject before now. I didn't get above a 54 on any test, including the final this year.

One of those math professors that, when doing practice problems, does not know how to explain what she is doing and why she is doing it.  Likes to skip steps when solving.  test avg has never been over 53. If you like math, don't take her because she can't teach you anything; if you don't like math, don't take her because you will fail her class.

I don't know if I am missing something with all of these previous ratings, but I am currently failing calculus and I have attended every class and have lived in office hours, relying on my TA to teach me the stuff she never taught us yet tests us on. She goes way too fast and expects us to already know everything, and her tests are HARSHY graded!

She is terrible. Very scatterbrained and flaky, and not good at explaining anything. The only good thing about my class is that I have an excellent TA, but it sucks that he's basically teaching us everything because she's so bad at her job. I don't know how I will pass this class. Avoid her at all costs unless you like being confused.

Not really a math person but I absolutely loved  McLaughlin. She was incredibly clear during lectures and made the material very easy to understand. The WebAssign is usually hard, but the answers can be found online and in the book. The problems on the exam are much easier and if you know the class examples and homework, its easy to make an A or A-

She goes pretty fast. Although very intelligent, not prepared for class at times. She did a whole problem on the board and never solved it. She changes homework dates a few times which sometimes doesn't help.

She is pretty clear in explaining her expectations, helpful and inspirational. Homework is lot more harder than test themselves but if you attend lectures and do homework properly than you should be fine with all her tests. I would definitely recommend taking her!
Excellent teacher. If you have to take calc I definitely recommend her.

McLaughlin is one of my favorite professors: she is extremely clear and is quite nice. Her tests are 'easy', but she gives no partial credit for your answers even if you make the smallest mistake, so averages are in the 60s. Also, the bottom third of the class drops, so the curves go away after the first midterm which is annoying.

She is nice and knows what she is talking about. Calculus is gonna be hard no matter what, but she is head of the math department and writes the exams so when you take it with her you know the types of questions that will be on there. Overall, I fairly enjoyed her class.
Horrible

Professor McLaughlin is what I would consider ok.  She explains concepts fairly well, but tends to do so rather quickly.  She does lots of practice problems in class, but SHE does them... and tends to do them pretty fast too.  She is fairly helpful in class, and very helpful during office hours, but her office hours are set in stone.

The lectures are fast paced, she doesnt appreciate being slowed down. She is inflexible with her office hours. If you can't make it, she will not make another time for you. Her tests are hard. The average right now is a 45. She comes to class and asks if there are any questions, then she tells people to see her after class instead of answering them
Very very hard class.  She is straightforward and not personal, but I really liked her.  I learned calculus completely and it challenged me.

Straightforward, no nonsense math. Class moves at a good pace, slow enough to digest a new theorem, fast enough to lessen redundant calculations. She doesn't assign too much homework and her tests are very reasonable. For once, your grade actually depends on whether you understand the material or not.
She is a pretty good teacher.  She tends to ramble on about the same concepts and she has a droning voice.  Tests are pretty tough, but the final is pretty easy if you study.

Professor McLaughlin is pretty nice and helpful.  Her teaching methods are pretty clear.  I would suggest trying to get into her class if you are ok at math but are willing to do some independent studying.

Great Professor.  I had her this semester for Calculus 3 and I like the pace of the course and she gives fair tests unlike most.  If you study you should pass.  I'm going to take her again for Calc4 or differential.  Thanks.
I hated this class. She never slows down in class, and her office hours are set in stone.  If you can manage to make it to her office, she'll usually help, but good luck if you aren't a math whiz.

She is a great teacher, and has obviously taught this subject before, because she is simple, straightforward, and to the point. No unneccesary material, and all tests/quizzes come directly from notes. Go to every lecture, and do the optional homework, and its an easy A/B.
No curve when the class average was a 60, students with 100 averages got 80's and not flexible during office hours.

Liked her so much for math31 that i took her for 32 Tries to make the material as straightforward as possible Has experience teaching these courses so they are structured & coherent. If you do the homework (optional) the tests are familiar Fair & understanding. Considering the options for math profs (not speaking clear english, etc) shes a goldmine
some confusing lectures, but no due homework, no absent policy, and extremely helpful with clarifying problems and is very open to questions

I fell in love with Calc after taking her course.  She has very reasonable quizzes and exams and is such a clear, straightforward lecturer.  She always made sure people understood the material.  I would recommend her to anyone.
good lectures, straight-forward quizzes, no due hw, no absent policy, good teacher
lectures were unclear and unhelpful

Hard class, but it's not her fault. She tries to make it as clear as possible and is very straitforward in her explanations. The material is a bit hard just because it is one of the hardest classes at Carolina, but very good teacher. I would recommend her.
No Comments
No Comments

Super interesting class, especially if you're interested in art history! I definitely wouldn't take it if you're looking for a gen ed to skip out on and still get a good grade, as concepts will be very hard to find/grasp outside of lecture. But I learned so much! Go to class!!!

Great professor. Very lecture heavy class, going to class helps. Everything was graded by TAs, I had a great TA so as long as you followed the rubric clearly and used what you learned in class lectures it's fine. Final and midterm criteria was posted so you know what you're in for, as long as you study the material from class, you'll get an A.

I find that she made an already boring course more difficult by slow lectures and few assignments that determined your final grade. Although she was accessible outside of class and kind, she was very harsh on grading, giving unhelpful feedback. An absolute bore to sit through with long readings and pointless in class assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Cao's lectures were very interesting. Attendance was only mandatory for recitations, but I don't see how you could get in-class content without actually going, since her slides only had images. The TAs didn't grade harshly at all, but there was no way to know what they were looking for, and they seemed mildly disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love art but still this is a frustrating class, super picky graders on midterms but then don't care about other assignments. You can still do well, just expect vague feedback, unclear expectations, and the confusing lectures. I was taking an 200 art and it was easier than this. also the ta judged me a little and did not care to help much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you show up to the lectures, take notes, and pay attention you will be fine in the class. For me, the lectures were interesting and fun to learn about. No textbook, but posted readings which I always did before class (some are longer than others). Not many assignments throughout the semester, but they aren't difficult to complete.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super frusterating class. Lectures are insanely boring and their is a certain social narratives that run as an undertone in the class that Cao seems to perpetuate. Aside from that the TA's are sporadic graders with some assignments getting 100% stamped on and others being scrutinized to the T, but you never know which is which.

It's a pretty easy class if you attend the lectures consistently, there are not much assignments to do. Though it would be better if the TAs provided rubrics for the assignments and projects as they're the ones that grade everything.

The TAs grade everything and they are usually pretty tough graders. What sucks most is that they don't give you a rubric yet will take off random points. With that being said it is not a hard day-to-day class, it is just frustrating at times and I would not recommend it if this is not in your major. Choose another class for focus capacities.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is extremely knowledgable in the topics she teaches, but is not very engaging. We were graded on a few things---a paper, a project, and maybe two assignments. She graded extremely harshly, taking points off for small things. She is accessible after class, but I wouldn't say it is any more enjoyable than hearing her lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Reviewing for ARTH557-- The best class I have ever taken at UNC! She is so smart. Small group, very discussion based and I learned so much. Not a harsh grader, and assignments never felt like busy work. Lots of readings, which had to be printed out, but the material was always so interesting.

Professor Cao is super knowledgeable and engaging, but the TAs in this class make everything way harder than it needs to be. They are unhelpful, slow to respond to emails, and grade inconsistently. It feels like they don't even understand the material sometimes, and when you ask for clarification they are bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
I cannot wait to take another class with her, it was an incredible semester and I loved every lecture. I will day that while attendance was technically not mandatory, I don't see how people could succeed without attending them because there are no recordings and the slides don't have any of the important information on them. 
\
just don't
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Maggie Cao is a really good and inspiring professor. Every lecture, she expands on the reading materials she gives during the weekends. You can always learn more perspectives of America and art history through her course. T I do have three Ras this semester, but overall I get good grades. You do need to respond to the prompt precisely.

Recommend avoiding this class unless you're passionate about art history and happen to satisfy the preferences of three different TAs (for one recitation section) throughout the course of the semester. Professor Cao is sweet but her grading should be for more advanced classes or actual art history majors. I liked the most of the material, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quite easily the worst professor at UNC. Tests were next to impossible, treated us as Art major students even though its just an elective class, and lied to us about a curve. Lectures were terrible, wouldn't excuse my absence even though I was in critical condition, and had a terrible personality (hated when asking questions). AVOID THIS CLASS!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor isn't bad, but genuily one of the worst classes I've taken. Don't take this class if you want an easy gen ed. The TAs give awful feedback, and don't even explain in depth what you got wrong. Do not take this class if you think it will be an easy gen ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable and passionate, with engaging lectures. Great survey class, with diverse artists and contemporary debates included. Homework readings weren't too difficult. The midterm and final suck, and I thought the midterm was graded excessively harshly (having taken multiple ARTH classes), but assignments were otherwise pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Cao's passion for her subject is very clear; however this does tend to most of the salient information (i.e. stuff on the tests) to be said by her and not really on slides. The TAs grade tough even though most ARTH 100 level courses are meant to fufill focus capacities. Overall if you are looking for an easy A it might not be here.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Maggie is a good professor, very caring and knowledgable. This class really depends on the TAs though, as they do most of the grading. Not a ton of assignments, but the ones you do have are pretty big and a large part of your grade. Some TAs grade pretty harshly so this class is not really an easy A if you just want an easy gen ed.

ARTH 150 is a unique, relevant and interesting class. many guest lecturers and various topics, but prof. cao brings them together well. i would 100% recommend her and this class, but beware; maybe don't take it just for funzies like I did. Still, so glad I took this class. lecture attendance is "optional" but you MUST go if you want to do well.
Interesting lectures from multiple different professors, enjoyable and easy to consume. I really enjoyed this class

This was an amazing class, but the classes were guest lecturers for every lecture. I surprisingly loved this class, and the TAs were great as well. Very few assignments, but it was easy to prepare for as long as you paid attention during class and read most of the material. Some guest lecturers were hit or miss, but that's the only downfall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The professor is good, BUT THE TAs??? THEY CAN HONESTLY SHOVE THEIR PHD DOWN THEIR THROATS! They are harsh graders for an introductory level. If you are a STEM major and want an easy GEN-ED, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

I took ARTH 150. Lectures are interesting because there are guest speakers every week however, the assignments are all graded by the TAs. I would advise choosing your TA wisely because some are tough graders. The feedback I received wasn't so helpful so if you are not used to writing for an Art class don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I actually took ARTH 150, but that wasn't an option listed. This class consisted of a variety of different topics and different professors lecturing throughout the semester, which I enjoyed. Your grade is based off of a midterm and a total of 3 papers + a final, leaving not much room for error. Readings get lengthy and lectures are not recorded.

Prof Cao is super knowledgeable and her research is sick, but her lecture style is geared toward a non-art history major. I was bored because we didnt dive into the ideas more. Maybe Im a nerd, but I was bummed & felt babied. Her research seminar felt more like a survey course, which is a shame because the readings she selected were really cool.

Professor Cao is honestly amazing. If you like art history, take this course or any other course she teaches. Her lectures are super interesting and I always walked away feeling like I genuinely learned something new. All of the readings are brilliant articles that work well with the lectures. There's a mix of papers and creative group projects!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: For an intro level class, this was pretty difficult. I would not recommend unless you're really passionate about art history or are a major/minor. The TA grading is pretty harsh, and had a hard time communicating with both my TA and Dr. Cao in a timely manner. It's pretty lecture heavy; we have readings for every class, though they're not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Fantastic and passionate professor, loved this first year seminar. Relatively easy so long as you know how to write a paper. Readings are interesting and insightful but not always absolutely necessary.
Fun and intriguing first-year seminar. Visit Prof Cao during office hours: she's incredibly insightful and wise beyond her years.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Only did pop quizzes the first month then didnt do any more, midterm is super easy you study off a jeopardy, class seems so intimidating at first but it gets so easy so quickly, final is not too difficult, final project is super easy you get a 100 as long as you put in minimal effort, be ready to ask classmates for missed notes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof is huzz

Professor Cushman if you're reading this I'm so sorry. I almost hit you with my car the other day on campus. I don't want you to know it was me because you're my favorite professor and I don't want you to hate me but I want to say I'm so sorry it was me who almost hit you. I'll be more careful I'm so sorry. I hope you have a great break!
I took this class a year ago and another class with him last semester. He is very kind and knows a lot about the subject matter. Not too much writing, which is nice for a freshman seminar.

I don't understand why all the comments are good. Dr. Cushman is a nice person and can be flexible, also knowledgeable about his field. But the syllabus is super disorganized and looking back, I learned zero stuff in the class and really thought it was a waste of time. To do the final project you really need background knowledge outside or prior.
This class is so special. It's unlike anything I've ever taken before. Just take it and you'll see.

Seriously one of the best Professors at UNC. This class was so amazing, and I would totally recommend taking it. Its easy to read when you know you get to go discuss and understand further! 10/10 class

i loved this class and really enjoyed the book. it felt like one large book club! if you are even considering this class, take it. in fact, even if you don't enjoy reading, take it. it was so fun getting to hear everyone's different perspectives and takeaways from the novel—that's what reading is all about, after all!
Great class, fair grader, interesting discussions. If you read the book and go to class you'll be fine.

I loved this class so much! He is such a great teacher, and he really helped us think about the text deeply. It wasn't very hard at all. I looked forward to the discussions because everyone in the class was so into it. He is a pretty relaxed grader and very nice person.

This is a life-changing class. I'm a STEM major and this was my favorite class I've taken at UNC (and it's not close). Take it if you're not an English major or anything like that. I learned to like reading again after falling off after graduation. Don't miss this one!

Really solid class and even better instructor. The book was good, but even better were the discussions. Perfect for a first year seminar. Met some awesome people, read something hard, and got to know a good prof.
The most amazing professor ever! Super accessible and helpful. Lots of reading but it was so worth it with the meaningful discussions he led. Truly loved this class, take it if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Such an amazing professor and class! The best first-year seminar I probably could have taken & I wish I could take it every semester on a new book. The class was mainly discussion based and Professor Cushman created an open, accepting environment for all answers and opinions. We did two interesting presentations on topics we cared about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great class. Did not think I would enjoy reading this book but I absolutely loved it. Prof. Cushman did a great job helping us through slowly and encouraging us to stick with it. I feel like I climbed a mountain. Would take again for sure!

There are so many amazing things about Dr. Cushman! There's definitely a good amount of reading, but his lectures help simplify any questions. Class is discussion heavy but is well-guided. Papers were graded with really good feedback and he would always make time outside of class to talk. The best though was him sometimes bringing his dog to class!

H.M Cushman is a very nice professor. He is accessible to students, funny, open to talk, and just a great guy all around. The reading can be a lot at times, but if you really pace yourself you'll be fine. Just try to participate, read what's required, and take notes on the class slides and you will be fine. He is also very passionate!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Cushman is a very funny and passionate teacher who really enjoys what he teaches. Although the reading can be quite heavy on some nights it was well worth taking the class. The homework mainly consists of reading while the class is heavily focused on the context and analysis of the tales. Overall great class and an even better teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof Cushman is accommodating, friendly and very knowledgable about Chaucer. I took this course on a whim to satisfy the depth english requirement and I am so glad I did. I enjoy class a ton! The reading is a bit dense sometimes, but it's interesting. She wants you to succeed & tests have extra credit! Super funny as well :)

Had her for ENGL320 (Chaucer/Canterbury Tales) and ENGL120 (Early English Lit.). Definitely one of the best professors at Chapel Hill. She gives great feedback, is personable, truly cares about her students, etc. As with any class, office hours are an even better way to connect and get your ideas out to her. Don't be afraid to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Cares about each of her students. She is funny, cusses a little bit, and is receptiveerested when students have thoughts/ideas. Her tests are simple to the ones who read, hard if you don't. Some pop quizzes. Attendance is not mandatory, but she does not release powerpoints until a few days before the exam. She never releases her lecture notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He's fine but try to get another 121 teacher if you can. He has no clear grading criteria at all and will take off points differently for each student depending on how he's feeling...I tried to talk to him about a grading concern I had and he responded with very rude emails. Definitely have to teach yourself all the coding and video editing too.

Peter can be hard to reach outside of class sometimes. While other times he is quick to respond. I guess it depends on his mood. Extremely easy grader, but the instructions are very unclear and confusing. Doesn't really teach. But honestly, as long as u put in a little bit of effort on the assignments, you'll get an A.
Take MEJO 121 with Doyle! He is so kind and helpful. This class is a lot of hard material to learn, but he does a great job teaching it and helping each individual student.

Take this class with Peter Doyle! He was so kind and approachable, as well as very accessible outside of class. He is always willing to help if you have any questions. I wish I was able to take more classes with him, he is the sweetest guy ever and has very interesting experience!

Professor Doyle is very approachable and knows his material very well! Be sure to pay attention in class and put time into doing your work well — the quality of your work will clearly show in your grade. Some of the material (especially HTML) is hard, but Professor Doyle is happy to give you help if you need it. Take MEJO-121 with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Doyle is the kindest guy ever! There were points where it felt like we had a lot of projects due at once, but he gives them out far in advance. He's very accessible and understanding of literally everything. This class really touches on every type of digital media and he gives great feedback without hurting your grade. Take his class!!

If you are interested in anything related to editing, filming, and MEJO, take this class with Professor Doyle! He is incredibly sweet, understanding, and helpful. I seriously have no complaints about him. If you are feeling unwell or away, he lets you join the class via Zoom. He is also a rather understanding grader.

Easy class, but Prof. Doyle teaches very fast and not always clearly, so would not recommend him if you aren't able to teach yourself the programs. Very nice, typically let out class early. Cares about his students and wants them to learn. Doesn't give an exact rubric, but follow the instructions and what he says in class and you will succeed.

He was a pretty good professor and let us join class on zoom, which was lovely. He sometimes didn't give us great lessons and class got boring. He also graded a little harshly and inconsistently, which frustrated me. Had to ask for a few regrades (but usually got them). Grading scale is a 95 for an A, but he doesn't give above a 95 super easily.

Professor Doyle is so nice and one of my favorite at UNC!! He is so caring and will give you extensions if you need them. He also lets you join on zoom if you need to. All project based, and they are not too hard if you try on them!! Love him

Doyle made taught the programs well and set realistic expectations for an intro class. He goes over everything you need to know how to do in class and posts videos to rewatch. Took attendance, but I don't think it was factored into grade, just the couple straightforward assignments. You do have to buy kinda a lot of equipment. Peter's a great guy

This is an introductory class so don't stress about the new, different programs. The coding with html and css was easily the most difficult aspect of the class, varying teacher to teacher. Be aware - classes are lecture heavy with little hands-on practice during class. Professor Doyle is a very experienced teacher and excited to teach y'all.
Professor Doyle is friendly, considerate, and helpful!

I liked this class and Professor Doyle. He talks very fast during lectures but records them so you can watch them after class. It is a project-heavy class, but Professor Doyle tries to make it as fun as possible. If you are not comfortable with Premier Pro or Word Press, he is very helpful.
Professor Doyle wasn't super clear with the rubric for assignments and not a very engaging lecturer. Overall I gained lots of skills from this class but wish my grade reflected it.

Professor Doyle is extremely kind and he is very professional and  experienced. I strongly recommend students who majors in mejo to take this course. Although 95 is A, he will give you some curve. All the projects are interesting and not heavy.

Professor Doyle is so kind, easily accessible, and VERY experienced. The class is project-based (5 + the final) with no rubrics, but he is not a tough grader by any means. He's also super open to discussing project errors. The only complaint is that he doesn't explain HTML/CSS very well, but a few youtube videos filled in the blanks. Easy A.

Peter Doyle is very kind and was flexible with office hours. His grading criteria is not always clear which isn't ideal for a project based class but he is not a harsh grader. I learned a lot of digital skills in this class. This is a fun and enjoyable class especially if you are interested in video, coding, or photoshop.

Professor Doyle is one of the kindest professors I've had while at UNC.  Classes are tutorials on how to use various media applications. Lectures are fast-paced but recorded for future reference. Professor Doyle provides good feedback and help on assignments. He's definitely a good professor for first-years still getting used to college academics!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy but gives very little instruction to assignments.

Professor Doyle is extremely caring and is always accessible outside of class. The assignments were super interesting and I learned a lot about Adobe software. He can be a little nit-picky with grading, so make sure you are submitting your best work. Overall, wonderful class!

Prof Doyle is a very nice, helpful teacher. I learned a lot from his video/coding class, and he always took the time to show us how to do things/give examples instead of outsourcing material. He also talked to us about the journalism/video industry, where he is very experienced. Overall, super useful class and an interesting professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: While it can be a bit hard to understand him at points with the mask and his British accent, he knows a lot about the field and is a pretty relaxed grader. He is also very caring and is always willing to talk about your work if you need help. However, he does go fast during lectures, but he also records them so you can just rewatch them later.

Doyle was one of my favorite professors this semester. His grading system is clear and easy to understand, and his lectures and instructional sessions are very informative. I feel that my editing skills, both web and video, have improved greatly.

Prof. Doyle's class was my favorite this semester. Assignments every other week and you get to learn video editing/shooting. Very low stress and honestly just a good time. Final is a documentary on anything you want and it's lots of fun to make. Take MEJO 121 with him! I've heard its unnecessarily hard with others. I did half in person half online.

Extremely boring if you already know anything at all about visual media. For MEJO majors, I would suggest making an appeal to not take the class if you've already taken COMM 130 and MEJO 187 like I had. It seemed to me like he hardly knew how to do the things he was teaching. I would have struggled if I hadn't already known the material.

Genuinely my favorite professor this semester. He takes the time to listen and engage with his class. He really made me feel seen and noticed, which is hard to come by with online classes. Everything was clearly explained and grading criteria was straight forward. Definitely would take again!
Peter is so kind and helpful. I loved 121 and how simple he made everything. He will give good feed back but make sure you know your work is good. Highly recommend!!!

Peter is genuinely the kindest professor I have had at UNC. He gives you the opportunity to re-submit assignments, move deadlines, and loves to celebrate student successes. He probs wouldn't be a great choice if you are *really* interested in learning the material, but he is lovely if you only want to grasp the basics of editing/coding (and an A!)
