Peter Doyle is the best professor to take MEJO 121 with! He explains how to do things with editing so well, and he lets you resubmit assignments because he understands that you're learning!

You could tell Purifoy was a knowledgeable professor, but she spent too much time trying to force group discussions in a big lecture hall. I wish she would have just lectured and used recitations for group discussions. She generally picked interesting readings to assign for homework.

This class is just not structured well. Very lecture heavy and no activities, yet prof was confused at the lack of participation and discussion. Topics were somewhat interesting but were repetitive and I never felt engaged. On the bright side there were only a few assignments. Prof just needs to find ways to make class more engaging and interesting

DP is knowledgeable and inclusive of all thoughts, but their class is so dry sometimes. I think the class covers some really interesting topics, but between the extensive reading for class and conversations that are dragged out, it can be hard to stay engaged. Grading is pretty lax- online midterm and no final.

DP was okay. They pretty much only lectured for all of the classes and never left appropriate time for discussion. You are graded on four assignments, two of which are group assignments, and the other two are papers/midterm. DP is a great person with lots of experience but they made an interesting class so dull with endless and redundant lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is super easy. We were only graded on 4 things (a reading presentation, an art project/paper, a midterm, and a final group project). Participation is not required. A ton of reading assigned, I only did the readings a few times, and skimmed them before the midterm. Lectures were tedious. An easy A, but I wasn't interested in the material.

I enjoyed the content of the lectures, but after a few weeks it became extremely repetitive. They are very knowledgable, but I found my engagement decreasing as the weeks went on due to repeated topics and 'nuances'. Overall great class topics but a little boring! She's super understanding and great professor to have despite all.

DP is an awesome person and super passionate about EJ but the class can be pretty dull even with cool topics. They lecture at you for the whole class, easy to zone out. It's not required to attend class, but I went to most anyway. Only a few assignments, but easily graded if you know what's going on & put in work. Go to the field trip, it's fun!

I really wanted to like this class, but it is just so boring. Dr. Purifoy is super nice and super accommodating, but this class can seem very repetitive, especially if people don't participate. You're only graded on 2 forums, a midterm, a project, and a final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Some people adored this class, and I understand why. It just wasn't my favorite. I'm not a huge fan of the way they lectured, and the forums felt kind of redundant with a load of groupwork (sucks cause no one wants to respond) and your grade is heavily dependent on that. If you go with friends and can do work that way I could see myself liking it.

Although Professor Purifoy is really smart and respect, the class was honestly a little boring though really easy. The class consisted of constant lectures where the students didn't really discuss any of the topics, meaning that I didn't learn that much.

Dr. Purifoy was an amazing professor. The class was heavy on reading, but Dr. P broke it up with documentaries, class discussion, and a novel at the end of the semester. This class was great for learning more about EJ, environmentalism, abolition, colonization and a lot more.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Purifoy was by far the most understanding prof I had during COVID. They were flexible, empathetic, and honest. The class itself was easy, interesting, and digestable and the TA was great. If you're interested in learning more about colonization, the environment, abolition, this class is for you!

She was understanding about deadlines & class content was really interesting. Extremely dense readings though, and lectures were often a straight 75 minutes of her talking about the readings but in less detail. There is a final group project but she lets you choose whatever format you want. Midterm was a lot of writing. Uses single-spacing though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Sweet professor who cares about his students. Only a couple of homework assignments throughout the semester that you can do in groups. Exams are heavily weighted but he curves a ton. Manageable if you can do practice problems and in-lecture practice. Confused by low ratings, he is such a nice guy who wants everyone in his classes to do well!

He is a nice guy but has no backbone. He made the exams but didn't grade anything (all grading done by his poor TA), so it took forever to get stuff back. Cheating was rampant on the final exam. You can tell he wants his students to like him, but he is an inefficient lecturer and bad with technology. He does allow cheat sheets and curves heavily.

Professor Shin really cares about his students' education. 408 has difficult material, but he does a great job explaining concepts. If you pay attention during lectures, you will do well and have a strong understanding of corporate finance outside of just the exams.

The class is just hard but he's cool and loves FRED. I don't know what type of voodoo witchcraft insane formula he curved the final using, but I thought I would finish with maybe a C if I was lucky and I got a B+. I am not like that. He maybe just didn't want us to hate him. One day he will buy that house!

I loved Professor Shin. Busi 408 is a difficult class, but he made the information digestible and less intimidating. All homework is done in groups, and there are plenty of practice problems for the midterm and final. Overall such a nice guy who clearly cares deeply about his students and the course topics.

I loved Professor Shin. Busi 408 is a challenging class, especially for me with no prior finance knowledge, but he made information digestible and less intimidating. Homework is group-based and there's lots of practice for midterm and final. Such a nice guy who obviously cares so much about the subject and his students.

I LOVE Dongwha. I was scared for this class because I'm not a fan of finance, but he really wants you to do well. Lectures are a little hard to follow and he can sometimes go on tangents. However, the expectations are very clear and he gives you all the materials you need to succeed. I highly recommend.

Not hard to earn good grade but class is disorganized. Little practice for concepts that need more than 2 problems to understand. Professor is sweet but if you want to deeply learn the material consider other instructor. Class is focused on applying concepts instead of learning equations, but if you want to take more advanced courses you need both.

Very weird class. Prof is chill but disorganized and prone to digressing, esp when the fratty finance bros ask random questions to flex their niche finance knowledge. Very unclear class and you basically self-study the whole thing, because lectures are not super relevant to exams. Still, very accomodating prof and overall a neutral experience.

Prof. Shin is super chill, obviously super passionate about crypto. He can get off-topic sometimes and can go on tangents on complex concepts that lose a number of ppl in the class. Class was interesting though and I enjoyed the final research project.

Professor Shin is the best!! 408 is hard, but I would 1000% recommend taking it with him. The final is hard and weighted heavy, but he curves a lot. Few long homeworks done in groups, but it's not too hard to do well on them. Real world examples make the content relevant and I always looked forward to class. His energy makes lectures fun!

Professor Shim is such a sweet professor. Those who are giving him bad reviews didn't put in enough time for this class. He even prefaced that he will push you more than other sections, so you can gain practical skills, representing yourself and Kenan in the workplace. As someone not going into finance, I was excited every day to go to class.
Confusing and unnecessarily difficult class. 45% of grade is final and spends the lecture before the final teaching new material. Surprised his rating is 4.5.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Shin is a nice guy, BUT I wouldn't recommend! Although he assigns little homework, this means the class is EXTREMELY test-heavy. You also have to teach yourself everything because the lectures are so confusing. Also, from what I heard from other 408 students and tutors, he teaches different, more complex material than other classes.

He's a nice guy and in theory makes Corporate Finance interesting by bringing in current events. However, he puts practice problems on the board with the solutions on the same slide and many of his answer keys have basic arithmetic mistakes. Not the worst teacher by any means, but lacks basic diligence. Final average is 60 - would take someone else

408 is a hard class in general, but I recommend taking with Shin. He genuinely cares for students, is funny, and will help you out and provide additional resources if needed. Very test heavy but are graded or curved as needed. Not many HWs but they take a long time, but you can work with group. Most of work was studying before midterm and final
phenomenal prof, really vested in students. took him for two classes absolutely love the guy. if you have the opportunity to take a class with shin take him!!!!!
Excellent professor; goated

Prof Shin is the best 408 professor. He provides everyone with resources to succeed and is transparent about his expectations. He teaches challenging concepts in a way that everyone can understand. I highly recommend taking 408 with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is THE BEST for 408, hands down. The content is hard and there is nothing you can do to change that, but he really listens to students feedback and will slow down if you ask him. Literally only half of the class shows up, but going is so worth it because the lectures are easier to follow in person. I love him! Wish I could stay in this class tbh
Dongwha is the man and I really hope he can buy a house soon. 408 sucks tho and investment banking is for try-hards.

Professor Shin was one of the best professors I've had at unc. He explained often abstract topics beautifully and used plenty of examples to make sure that we all understood. Plenty of opportunities to ask questions. My favorite part of the course is his frequent inclusion of real world examples to show how what we are learning is actually useful.

Professor Shin was by far the best option for taking 408. He has 6 homeworks that are worked on in groups. Midterm is very easy. He said the final is really the only thing he cares about, so it is very hard but he curves. You wont get less than a B if you do basically anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved 408 with Professor Shin. He was very down-to-earth and incorporated current events into his teaching (Evergrande, cryptocurrency, etc.). Lectures were easy to follow. The final was particularly difficult, but it was curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely cool guy. Class is hard but not a lot of work. You'd have to be super lazy to get less than a B. Would recommend.

He said I knew my lecture is much harder than other professors', but you guys deserve harder courses. Spent a week preparing for the final and doesn't help at all. DON'T believe that he said two days for the final is enough! It is super difficult! Even though he curved, I still feel that there's no need to make simple things complicated.
Super cool professor and extremely nice guy. The final is super hard but he curves so definitely would recommend. Not much work at all

Professor Shin is an awesome professor- my favorite at UNC. He made a difficult concept like corporate finance fun to learn. The class is still challenging but he lets you use a cheat sheet on the midterm and final, which helps alot. If you work hard and show up, Professor Shin will take notice and help you out. He is also hilarious.

Professor Shin seriously cares about his students! He was so helpful during these crazy COVID times. He regularly checked in on us and modified the course to ensure that we could learn at a good, healthy pace. He is a great instructor and genuinely wants you to succeed! I could not recommend him enough.

Professor Reid is very kind and encouraging. Although the class has a lot of reading (80-100 pages of reading due per class), I found the material fascinating. Classes are almost all discussion, so participation matters!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If I have one piece of advice, take HIST398 with Dr. Reid. He's so awesome at giving feedback, always checking in on us as people, built good community in class, and easy to reach outside of class. He made the paper feel less daunting. 1000/10 recommend one of my favorite professors at UNC!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The lectures aren't very engaging and you really have to pay attention to what he is saying because not all the material is on the slides. That being said, there aren't too many assignments. As long as you read the assigned material and participate in recitation you will be fine. It does mainly depend on the TA that you get and how hard they grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Reid is very knowledgeable, and is passionate about teaching students. Which TA you get can heavily influence your grade. I got a hard one, but was fortunate enough because they liked me.

Lectures aren't too engaging, but some content (eg Israel/Palestine, the environment, Apartheid) is very relevant, & the readings/films are interesting. You need to love history to enjoy the class, though, and 3-page essay limits can make it tough to say everything I want to (one required us to use 4 sources!). Worthwhile class for some but not all

We have 4 papers to write. The recitation was required, but the lecture was not. It was easy to learn if you didn't go to the lecture. Participation in the recitation was also required to count as present. We had 3 books we had to read, and would strongly suggest actually reading because you will write a paper on it in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Professor Reid and his course!! The material was heavy but extremely engaging nonetheless. There were two 6 page papers and a 6-8 pages final, all which were graded and returned extremely quickly. Dr. Reid gave incredible feedback and was extremely encouraging! I highly reccomend going to his office hours/talking to him 1 on 1!

291H: To succeed in his class, talk to him, do your readings, and PROOFREAD EVERYTHING. No tests or exams, but he's very into class participation and writing compositions as an alternative. I really enjoyed this class, it felt like just the right amount of challenging without being totally overwhelming. Very flexible about accommodations.
Nice guy. Decent amount of reading and movies you have to look at for recitations. Overall, solid professor.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I liked Professor Reid but my TA was awful. The TAs grade everything and mine was way too tough and gave mostly Bs (only 3 As total) for participation in the lecture even if you attend all classes and participate every time. There were 4 essays and the prompts were unclear and incredibly long.

This was a relatively easy, interesting class. Be aware Reid is often challenging to hear and rambles some. Attending lectures isn't mandatory, but attending the weekly recitation section is. These are NOT study sessions but seminars you need to prep for. Four three-page papers, recitation attendance, and the final paper are the only grades.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: With one 2 1/2 hour class per week, you will be spending a lot of time reading novels for the class. In total we read 7 novels which sometimes necessitated us to read a full novel in one week. The assignments are not too bad, each week you'll submit a brief reflection on the assigned reading and there were 3 6-page essays (including the final.)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Unfortunately for me, attendance was not mandatory (so obviously I did not go). This led to me struggling immensely on the final because it was entirely based on lecture content. All papers/assignments are based on readings and films not covered in lecture so technically you could never go to class and do fine (until the final).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are interested in history, you will love Dr. Reid! He assigns really interesting readings and films that deepen your understanding of world history. Theres only 4 papers but they allowed for a lot of creativity and intepretation. His lectures can be long and a little dull to those not into history.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Reid's lectures are boring, but the class isn't hard at all. Be prepared to read, write, and watch films often though. There is a recitation, but you just talk about what you read/watched. The final consists of writing an essay over a certain time period, but he doesn't tell you which time period you'll get before. TAs grade everything.

65% of his class are based on 4 essays. The essays are hard, boring, and they do not have a clear structure. The essays are graded by the TA's - they are graded very unfairly as they do not have a clear structure or requirements checklist and the grade only depends on the TA (better hope that u get a good one). Lot of reading and film watching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Reid is absolutely amazing! He is extremely caring, compassionate, & kind. He really cares about his students and wants us to succeed. He was very understanding with some extenuating circumstances I was dealing with & showed me so much kindness throughout. Truly a gem. Hes also very accessible! Take this class you will learn so much!
Personally love Reid. Taken 2 classes with him because of how much I liked him. All paper-based but relatively easy and as long as you study the slightest bit, you'll pass. Would recommend! Love!

Really smart guy. He's understanding and accessible outside class. The lectures are a bit dry sometimes but the events he focuses on are interesting and he really gets you to think about history in new ways. I'm about 80% sure everyone complaining about how hard the class is didn't actually read the material, because it's not that bad if you do.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I was a little nervous going into my class based on the reviews on here, however, I absolutely adored Professor Reid. I really enjoyed his class and his discussion. I do not know if maybe it was just because it was a seminar class and he is different in other classes but he was not a harsh grader for us. Really recommend!

The workload at times was a lot with readings and lectures but the class overall was good. Professor Reid is willing to work with you if you simply ask. Our grades were based on papers and participation. We mostly interacted with TA, but he cares about his students and wants to get to know them. He also tweaked the final grading scale to help us.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor offers tons of lecture to watch and they can be long and boring. His voice can be tricky since it's too hoarse. Grades depends heavily on your TA (avoid tough grader!) Three papers per semester and each for 5 pages. A 9 pages essay for final. Books and films every week. Do not take this class if you only want GenEds. Heavy workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: In the online portion, lectures were asynchronous and often unrelated to recitations, which focused on readings and films. The 3 5-page papers and part of the final were all based on recitations, so make sure you prepare and participate for those. As far as I could tell, all grades (including the final) were done by the TA's.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You have to read a novel or watch a movie every week, and the recitation is on that work. The lectures are very boring and don't really tie into the novels or movies watched. You're graded on three 5 page papers and a final 2 part 9 page paper. This isn't the worst class I've taken, but I would probably choose a different class for the gen ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Took HIST140 as a Gen Ed and I think it was worth it. Lots of reading (read about 4 whole novels the whole semester) plus other assigned online readings. Lectures were pretty lengthy and not the most interesting. Total of three 5-page essays plus the final which was a 3 page essay and a 6 page essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I used rate my professor to decide if I was going to take this class and honestly the good reviews let me down, this class was my toughest and I seriously considered pass/fail. The TAs grade the essays harshly and the final was the most stressful thing I've done in awhile. I somehow did well, but the stress isn't worth the 3 gen eds I promise.

I really enjoyed Dr. Reid's first-year seminar. It was based around a TV show you had to watch, and where you'd a few episodes a week, write a weekly journal on it, and have occasional papers. If you come to class, participate enough, and show that you are actually interested then it's a pretty easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Reid was a good professor to work with but his grading does not make any sense. He does not give 100s and even if you do everything he asks you will probably not receive an A
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Reid's class is a bit of a hard one, there's a lot of reading and if you aren't the type to participate in lectures then be prepared to fail because he will try to get you to speak. The Professor is very knowledgeable about the topic, and has proven to be good at lectures although at times it is slow. Can be hard but it is manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Quizzes save your grade, he gives them about every other week with no warning and they are usually based on the book/film that was assigned that week. Everything else depends on the TA, Reid is obviously very smart but his lectures are dry as dirt.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Reid is very knowledgeable, however, when asked a question in lecture, he would usually never fully answer. Lectures were sometimes boring. There is sometimes a lot of reading and the pop quizzes are very in-depth. The three topics for the papers were very vague mostly because you had to write a paper about a single word.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Reid is very lecture heavy and the lectures can sometimes be boring, but this class is otherwise easy. The course does not require a textbook, but you are required to read 3 books over the semester and watch around 10 movies which will have pop quizzes. There are also 3 papers throughout the semester which are graded by TA's.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: hands down the WORST professor I have ever had. He cannot finish a single sentence! The only reason I took this was because of the three gen-eds but honestly not at all worth it. There's three papers with extremely vague topics and a final paper to be written in the final time. He has "pop" quizzes on the assigned texts and sometimes the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Awful class. His lectures are incredibly boring. You have to watch movies every week to discuss in recitation. Would not recommend this class for gen ed.

Don Reid is not a good professor at all. He treats the class as if he is your only professor for the entire semester. You have to read and watch videos before sectionals on Thursdays and Fridays, but he will give a quiz on Wednesday. This becomes an issue for students like me who have a busy beginning to the week. Paper prompts are too vague.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class for a GenEd and I don't know how people can complain. His lectures are heavy but he posts the full powerpoints and does not take attendance. You have to read the books and go to recitation but there isn't any other homework. There are three papers and a final exam and your worst paper grade is worth a low percentage of your grade.

Professor Reid is an extremely nice guy, but the lectures were almost pointless. Attendance is not mandatory and attending lectures doesn't effect your grade much at all. TA's grade the 3 papers and reading quizzes, so be sure to attend recitations. Grade based on 3 papers, 5-6 quizzes on books and films, and the final exam.

Took for the gen eds and totally regret it. nice guy but horrible at lecturing - uses powerpoints with no clear points and raises questions about the subject of the lecture without answering them. quized on 5 or 6 obscure books and a few films. learned more studying for the final than all his lectures combined. graded on quizes, 3 papers, final
Nice guy but drones on in lectures, his mic doesn't work 75% of the time so beware of sitting in the back.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Reid is super passionate about his class and makes a lot of modern references, which is cool. The books he makes you read are actually kind of interesting - take the recitation with Donald Santacaterina!! But there is literally SO MUCH information because you learn about so many eras. Also the fact that our final exam is ONE ESSAY question.....
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: God bless him but well I learned nothing from the lectures. Didn't really need to come to class at all because Prof Reid posted the slides online. The papers were actually not that bad (usually based on movies) and a lot of people in my class didn't actually read the book. I skimmed it, so the class wasn't bad at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Reviews are accurate. Very tough grading; I only know of a couple As. Nice guy, I think he cares about his students, but teaching is not his gift. Prompts were very confusing. Lectures were unnecessary because they don't relate the assignments. Only really have to watch the films for grades because you can prepare for the final with good Googling.

I took this class because it fills 3 gen-eds, and I have regretted every minute of it. Professor Reid's lectures are incredibly boring, dense, and LONG. He makes minimalistic powerpoints for each lecture, and half of the time, I'm not sure how the lecture relates to anything we're reading about. Also, you watch a film every week. And write A LOT
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Horrible speaker. His lectures made little to no sense and he made the same hand motion for the entire lecture. He didn't teach chronologically and the "thematic" learning style didn't make sense. There is a reading every week and two extensive papers.

Don't take this class. Even though the content is interesting, many students often get more confused by going to the lectures than by researching the content themselves. You must read a novel every week and complete two 7 page papers. Guidelines and expectations for tests and papers are very vague yet they are graded very specifically.

Donald Reid is a very smart guy, but has trouble getting his points across. He will pose very dynamic questions at the beginning of class and seldom arrive on an answer. The T.A.'s are your best resource. They will explain anything that you are confused about because they understand how jumbled Prof. Reid's lectures really are.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Reid isn't very clear when he asks questions on exams and many times his lectures are both boring and confusing. He's very smart and sort of funny but he talks very fast and gets off track easily.
Draws the A line at 95, be very cautious about taking a class from him.

Reid is a nice guy in person but his class is pretty tough.  The paper assignments are difficult and expectations are a bit unclear.  The grading on papers is also tough but the tests aren't too bad and he gives the questions before hand.  You also have to read cause half the exams come from the textbook.  Also I had a bad TA so that made it worse.

Professor Reid is very enthusiastic and helpful in person. His lectures are convoluted, but he cracks jokes and they seem to go by pretty quickly. The recitations are *amazing*. Essays are tough but the tests are simple enough, and he gives a generous curve. I would recommend for anyone who wants a better understanding of current events.

Professor Reid is quirky person and is passionate about history. He may not be the best public speaker but he really tries to get students interested. He ended up being my favorite professor this semester. The content the class covers is eye opening and interesting. The class wasn't too hard but it also wasn't easy.

Super boring lectures, then the tests are hardly based on anything he talked about. Memorize a whole bunch of pointless facts (not from the book).  Tough paper assignment in the beginning. Harsh on grading - 5 assessments make up a total of 100 points, so every point missed is a point off your final grade.

EXTREMELY boring lecturer. Has the longest and most convoluted essay prompts I've ever seen. Hard class not because the material is difficult but because he is a bad lecturer and his tests are difficult.

I had Professor Reid for a upper level research and writing seminar and I wouldn't have wanted anyone else. He worked with me to explore a topic that was somewhat unusual, but he encouraged me to pursue it. He is very articulate and I found him very helpful and supportive whenever I asked him about something. Great professor!

His lectures weren't clearly organized and he isn't the best speaker on campus.  Overall, the class isn't that difficult and uses fairly interesting books and films to teach.  If you interested in history or are looking for a class to fill, this isn't a bad option
His lectures are nearly impossible to follow.
choose another professor if u want coherent lectures. If not youll get his stream of conscious which is filled with tangents that dont relate to the topic at hand. He is not a good speaker
A wonderful, helpful professor.
I like the guy a lot, but found his class to be mediocre. Teaches off of books and movies, but still lost my interest.
Awesome professor. There's a good amount of work, but the class is a real learning experience.

Worst lecturer i've ever had. His lectures are disjointed and it feels like you're in a different class every time you go. Weekly quizzes require attendance, often had to read a book  or see a 3 hour film every week. Too much work required for this class for the level it is and none of it is enjoyable. Grading was harsh, multiple long papers.

His fuzzy head (and chest mind you) can distract you from his digressions. He finds it impossible to focus on one topic and follow it through in a logical coherent manner. Instead he meanders through vague themes "stepping back" every other sentence to re-clarify an already simple topic. prepared to do a ton of reading and sleeping in this class.
The class is kinda hard, and a B is to be expected.

Professor Reid definately knows what he's talking about. His lectures are a little jumpy and you have to read and write alot, but you learn so much. The sections are great because of the engaged TA's.
No Comments

Brillant professor, finally a challenge after breezing through high school. Many of my friends in the class thought it was vague or difficult, but that's just because they failed the quizzes on the assigned readings. You have to read things a couple of times to actually absorb the information, not just once the morning of.
Would not recommend.

Lectures were boring and hard to follow.  The reading was interesting, and the TA section with a great TA made up for the short comings of the class.  The class was not hard, but that was mostly thanks to being a good writer and having a great TA.
rambling, ineffective lectures, LOTS of reading on a few specific questions on quizzes. 3 massive 10 page papers on obscure questions

BEST MEJO 340 PROF EVER!!!! You can tell she genuinely cares about her students and the topic. Lots of reading, but exams were easy, and she offered extra credit. Grade is based on midterms, participation, a couple of engaging case brief assignments, and reading quizzes. If you need to take 340, take it with her. You will absolutely not regret it.

This class with Professor Dancy was the easiest class I've taken at UNC. Don't get me wrong though, it was very helpful. I learned a lot about how to speak more clearly. She doesn't necessarily teach you how to have a standard reporter voice, but she helps you polish it. She gives a normal number of assignments and they're all super easy.

Professor Dancy is one of the kindest professors at UNC. She is passionate and a seasoned reporter and really knows what she's teaching. The assignments are time consuming, but she is just trying to prepare you for the real world. As long as you put in the work and ask questions, you'll do fine. Interesting lectures, too!

Professor Dancy, so far, has been one of the best teachers I have had in the Hussman School. I had her for MEJO340, and she was very clear and responsive with questions, well aligned with her rubric, and extremely knowledgeable in the content she teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best class ever, best professor ever! There is such a stigma going into this class, but it genuinely couldn't have been more interesting and easy. Professor dancy breaks it down so clearly, and her tests replicate word-for-word what she tells you to study in class. Her lecture keeps me engaged the entire time, and she offers a ton of extra credit!

MEJO 421 can be hard but entirely manageable. Reporting isn't an easy job, but if you give it the time and effort it deserves it's very easy to succeed in this course!  Professor Dancy is such a great tool and mentor, who is accessible to breakdown any aspect of the class. She is one of the best at UNC, and I recommend taking time to work with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Dancy was one of my favorite professors I have had at UNC so far! She went to law school, making learning even more interesting. The discussion posts and quizzes helped summarize information, and she gave great feedback on all assignments. The class consists of readings, discussion posts, quizzes, a midterm, case briefs, and a final.

This is an easy class, but Prof. Dancy does a lot to make sure it isn't boring, even if you don't want to go into broadcast which this class is aimed towards. Her lectures are engaging, the textbook readings are extremely manageable, and you will definitely learn something new about your voice!

425 is an extremely easy class, but I still felt like I learned a lot about my voice! Professor Dancy is incredibly kind and encourages you to put your own spin on your projects. Her expectations of classroom conduct are high but perfectly reasonable. She readily encourages participation, and being in the front row of her class is so fun!

The ONLY negative thing I could ever say about Professor Dancy is that she is a really textbook-heavy professor. Besides that, this woman is an angel. She really cares about everyone, will give you time and effort if you put it back in to her, and will do anything to ensure your success. I thought Media Law would be terrible, it was the opposite.

Professor Dancy is a kindhearted person who wants to see her students succeed. While MEJO 421 is difficult and she expects quality, deadline-meeting work, she will meet you more than halfway if you put in the effort. Go to office hours with a shell of an idea, and you will leave with a story. I really love Professor Dancy and she is one of my favs.

I really like Professor Dancy, but I am not sure I like this class. The class is super easy but its not super interesting. I think other reviewers are mistaking her when they say she is difficult. Professor Dancy can be stern and upfront which could turn away some students but she is actually very kind and enjoys talking to her students.

At a high level school like UNC this class seemed like a waste of my time. All we did was practice saying letters and breathing. Just a free social period. The "lectures" were just what was in the book. Half of the information made no sense at all and I really learned nothing from this class. Easy, but a total waste of time.

Ms. Dancy was not the professor for me. In a hands on, learn as you do the work class, her expectations were SO high. She expects perfection as we are learning and has no grace. She is rude and not willing to work with students. It is impossible to ask questions unless you go to office hours, no matter what the question is. Do NOT take this class.

Simply put she makes your life 10x harder than it has to be. Her criteria for what she accepts as news for this class is extremely narrow: It must take place less than 4 days before the due date, you must be able to find info not reported on by news orgs, and she has to think its news. How does she tell you to find stuff? LOOK ON MAJOR NEWS ORGS!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For a class I heard so many scary things about, Media Law w/ Prof Dancy was actually enjoyable. Prof Dancy was excellent at explaining law concepts, and you could tell it's something she's passionate about. She's a pretty light grader, and gives many hints as to what will be on the midterm and final. If you study what she mentions, you're golden.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dancy offered literally, and I do mean literally, no outside resources, no study guides, and her lectures were all ripped straight from the textbook. In class "exercises" were, again, just what's in the book. None of the assignments came back with any real substantive feedback, good or bad. A passive-aggressive communicator, slow grader.

Took Arab 407 with Prof. Doria and currently in Arab 408. The topics are interesting and the class is easy. She's very caring and lenient but gives a lot of work. The work amount is justified since the class is just a conversation. You must do the reading or watch the movie in order to participate. If you speak Arabic, give it a try.

Doria is very sweet and caring and is always willing to take additional time to explain the language and Arab history and culture; she also has easy tests. That being said, the class isn't too enjoyable because of the heaps of HW (1-2 hours/night) and unclear class calendar. Just make sure you show up and don't fall behind on HW or it'll be tough.

Doria means well, but it's hard to do well in her class. She constantly talks about how she's sad students are stressed, but grades on unclear guidelines & doesn't teach grammar. I did corrections AND extra credit, and she told me she wouldn't give me the points back because I already had a "good enough" grade. I wish someone else was teaching 204.

Professor Doria is the sweetest person. She gives a good amount of homework that is crucial to learning the material, so it is for good cause. She is very lenient with due dates if you speak with her about it and she is not at all a tough grader. If you want to learn Arabic and are excited about doing so, you should have no trouble in her class.

Ustaaza Doria really emphasizes language immersion and speaks only in Arabic for nearly the entire class period. She also has a lot of cultural knowledge and is eager to share it with students. The homework was excessive, usually amounting to 3-4 hours of homework a day, but she tried to be flexible with everyone and sometimes accepted late work.
Doria is very enthusiastic about Arabic which is wonderful to have in a teacher, however she gives heaping amounts of homework and does not always explain what is reviewed in the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Doria is very sweet, but homewrk load was awful, especially during a pandemic. There was some sort of a project due along w/ usual 2-3 wrth of homewrk every single weekend toward the end of this class, hw was worth more than tests and almost every hw was graded on accuracy. Too much work and disappointed that there was virtually no accomodation

Doria is tough, but also very caring. She wants you to do your best and puts in a lot of effort to give you helpful feedback. If you go in knowing its going to be a lot of work she will be your biggest cheerleader. I have had a friend who had a breakdown in her office and she made them tea. Make sure you stay up on hw and go to office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed my time with Prof. El Kerdany. She is very patient with her students and gives a lot of feedback on hw assignments for you to improve on. Participation in class is rly important to understanding the language and the rules associated with it. She also introduces you to Arab culture around the middle east which is really interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Favorite class, and favorite professor - really cares for her students and wants you to do well. Makes language learning challenging, but I'm leaving this semester actually speaking/writing Arabic independently. If you want to learn the language, are happy to put some work in, and don't mind learning the Egyptian dialect, TAKE THIS CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is the kindest professor I have ever had. I struggled a lot in class, but she always took time to help me when I showed that I cared. She goes the extra mile to ensure students understand what is going on. The class is so much work, but I learned so much.

ARAB 101 is designed as a "weed-out" class for non-native speakers. If you have taken Arabic before or speak it at home, you will pass with flying colors. If you have never done anything with Arabic before, you will not pass. This class is HARD. This class is TIME-CONSUMING.

Professor El Kerdany is a very good Arabic teacher. She is deeply knowledgeable about Arabic, being a native speaker, and tries to help students, although she can be a bit confusing sometimes. I found her very nice, but I have heard she can be harsh if you're struggling in the class. Overall, ARAB 102 is a lot of work, but manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I was scared to take her at first but once I started going to office hours you get to know how sweet she is. Also, was willing to work with my schedule which I could not make most office hours. She makes you work for your grade. You will learn a lot about Arab culture from her and she will usually invite you to events on campus.
Dr. D is honestly one of my favorite GEOG professors! He explains concepts super well and actually seems to care and want to connect with his students. His class is pretty laid back and fun.

Comes off as a pleasant and understanding person but your first conversation with him outside of class will make you change your mind immediately. He's so incredibly condescending and rude when you ask questions in office hours and doesn't actually care about helping you -- instead he just belittles. The TAs were the only redeemable part of him.

This was my first time really working with R, and Dr. D made it super approachable. Everything we did on a "major" grade assignment (hw or project) came straight from an in-class assignment or demo that we had access to. Very easy to do well if you take the time to pay attention to the coding. I thought the class was fun, and Dr. D is a good prof.

I love Dr. D and this class! I learned so much (you learn R) & he was really helpful with feedback & responding to emails & discussion posts. There's a semester-long final project, many coding assignments, demos, and in-class exercises. It's a lot but if you pay attention to his (sometimes boring) lectures and do everything on time you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is INCREDIBLY organized and you learn R which is great but the lectures are beyond boring and Dr. D is honestly rly condescending which can create barriers when you need to ask for help. There are in class assignments for "attendance" but on canvas and you can do them from home. Exams are easy and its rly easy to do well in his class

My biggest problem with this class is that he waited till last minute to tell us problems he had with a semester long project. His class is not too hard and very organized which I appreciated. Attendance was not mandatory but there are in class activities (you can do these outside of class). You do learn R by the end though!

This isn't an easy A, but manageable. The class has a ton of assignments and two midterms, no final though. You definitely learn to code R and there's a class website which details all of the content and assignments. However, this guy is condescending and rude. Not a huge problem, but be aware. Overall decent class but I did not like the professor.

While there is nothing wrong with the course content, Delameter is very disrespectful and condescending in his feedback and when students ask questions. Never have felt scared to talk in a class before. For a class about technology, no question is a dumb question. Consider a student might be struggling with serious issues before you berate them.
GEOG 215 might be the most organized class I've ever taken. Everything was very clear and there were several examples given before we were expected to do stuff on our own.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I really connected with Dr. Delamater, and he ended up being my favorite professor. I had no coding experience coming into GEOG215, but picked it up really quickly. The TAs are super helpful too if you get confused. Material is easy to learn, just pay attention and do your work and you'll get an A.
Easy class. Straightforward directions. Can be condescending and assigns a lot of busy work.

Mostly graded by tasks that have very detailed instructions so its easy to do well but the lectures were super boring and frankly unnecessary. I skipped half the classes and got an A. Don't mistake this for an easy class though. Even tho the assignments were handed to you, they took several hours to complete. Learned R but did not enjoy the class
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class was so unnecessarily stressful and Dr. D is the most condescending person ever, he's so mean and degrades you if you ask questions, don't go to his office hours. Lectures are so painfully boring and participation in this class is so obscure. This class would have been more enjoyable if he wasn't teaching it. You do learn R though!

Dr. D is a great lecturer. He is very structured, organized, and transparent about what can be expected in assignments and exams. You will learn a lot about data science and R. My only complaint is that he has the tendency to be condescending and harsh toward students. If you have extenuating circumstances, please don't rely on his understanding.

Cool class. Great professor. Definitely recommend it.  Class is made up of many assignments that are easy to complete with the detailed instructions given. The final Project is a little difficult for me but that was only because my topic was weird. Just pick something simple. The participation grade is weird too, but it's only 5%. Awesome class!

We had 7 assignments, a (pretty simple) semester-long project, & 2 tests. Super easy to get a high grade if you follow the assnmt instructions & study a bit for the tests. He also provides many resources for success with writing the code. The lectures could get boring, but having an easy & semi-fun workload made up for it imo. Take this!

I honestly had no idea what I was signing up for when I registered for this class, I mostly used it to fill hours, but I ended up loving it so much! Dr. D was seriously great in every aspect. The lectures could get slightly boring from time to time, but you could tell just how passionate he was about the content. No coding experience required!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He's such a cool dude. I love watching him lecture. I have had some family issues this semester and he was beyond accommodating even with the arrival of his baby. I really enjoyed the class, it's fun and easy if you like coding. But, even if you never coded before, it is beyond doable. Take it!

Professor Delamater is a really nice guy and also very passionate about what he teaches. He's a great professor that genuinely cares about his students and making sure they understand the course material. Personally, I thought the course content was a bit difficult, but if you pay attention, take notes, and do the exercises you will be fine.

This was my first class with Dr. D and I hope it won't be my last! We used R for every assignment and test (so beware if you didn't know) however, I had never used R and still managed to get an A in the class. He is EXTREMELY helpful and always makes time to sit down and talk you through the coding until you get it. Hard work in this class pays off

Dr. D is very organized and clear, both with expectations and learning material. He is willing to help anyone with any level of programming experience get through this class. I especially loved the ability to pick a topic of interest to me and research it all the way through. Though easy-going, he provided opportunities to challenge ourselves.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: 215 is a fun class if you want to learn data science or R in a unique and cool way! Assignments are very easy to follow thanks to Dr. D's instructions and the tests are very fair. I'd definitely recommend taking 215 if you're a comp sci student and need an extra class. It's a nice breather from the usual stuff but also extremely helpful!

215 was a good course, it helped me gain experience with data science and coding in R. The assignments were worth 30% of the grade and were easy, exams were also not bad, and the final project was interesting and fairly graded. Participation is part of the grade so if u want an A you need to go to most classes, however.

Dr Delamater is a really great guy and very easy to get on with. His lectures are engaging, interactive and clearly structured. He references his own work to explain aspects of the course (446 and 541) and is genuinely enthusiastic about his research and the education of students. I would thoroughly recommend you take his classes.
amazing professor-kind, funny, engaging-and the material he teaches is super useful! highly recommend his GEOG491 and GEOG215 classes
He's a really dynamic lecturer that keeps the class engaged. Definitely a great guy to take a class with. As long as you show up to class and ask for help if you need it, you'll do fine in the class.

Only reason I wouldn't take again is becuase no one really seems that interested, so he lectures for a long time. Otherwise, easy exams, short writing assignments, and he is very accessible outside of class. I think he should just teach higher level classes and not a 100-level class, maybe he would get more engagement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor, I loved his LTAM 101 class. Expect to have 20-45 page readings per class, but the lectures broke down all of the denser, more complex concepts into something that anyone can understand, so it truly wasn't bad at all. Definitely would recommend taking his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He gives students opportunities to come to their own conclusions, help them learn how to work collaboratively, would recommend this class and teacher to anyone interested in the subject

Dr. Walker is an incredibly nice guy and cares a lot about his students. He is newer as a prof but has his stuff together way more than any other prof I had this sem. He makes learning fun and approachable. Don't hesitate to take one of his classes
The class is a super easy A if you sit through the lectures, midterm and final were both open book. Monje is a nice guy but has a tendency to ramble.

Very kind and knowledgeable, yet I don't feel like I've learned anything in this class which is weird as its a pre-req for many COMM courses. The few things that have been discussed more in-depth I've already learned in other COMM courses at UNC, making me wonder what I'm supposed to get out of this class as someone who is interested in the major.
Poorly prepared, regurgitated msnbc talking points. You can learn way more from just reading any book basically on media studies
Prof Monje the goat. He's so nice and is super understanding.

There were barely any assignments so most of the weight went on the exams, but the exams were open books and open notes, so it's really not a big deal. He tends to rant a lot, but he's really entertaining, and it kept me engaged.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: incredibly easy A as long as you're willing to show up to and sit through the required lectures. midterm and final are both open-book. he has a tendency to ramble but he's a nice guy.
Class was easy but attendance is taken every day. The actual class isn't too hard but the lectures are kind of boring.
Nice guy. Lectures can be boring, but he's not a stickler about paying attention. The midterm and final are open-note take-home. No homework. Take this class for some easy hours.

Lecture based - somewhat interesting but can be boring sometimes. Tends to get sidetracked. Loses track of time a lot of the time. Class is graded by attendance (randomly taken), two forums post, a midterm, and a final. The midterm and final were take-home and open-note. Textbook was boring but the new readings he pivoted to were more interesting.

Dr. Monje was very knowledgable for the subject but he often went on long tangents during lecture, they were interesting but often he lost track of time. Grade comes from attendance, forum posts, and tests. Generally an easy grader, but if he detects and AI used you will get a 0.

COMM690: He lectures for the vast majority of class periods unless we are watching something. He does frequently go a bit over class time while he is talking so beware of that. He is not strict on attendance and participation, but by showing up to a good amount of the classes, you can get a 100 for that. Not many grades or clear rubrics-hard grader
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: David is a super caring guy, and very knowledgeable. The class is a bit lecture heavy but totally worth it, as there are rarely any assignments. Good, easy class for anyone interested in the topic or just needs the credit.
He's nice and makes the material in the textbook easier to understand in his lectures. Not much homework other than a couple assignments a semester, one quiz, and one final.

Dr. Monje is the best! The textbook was verbose but interesting, and the lectures were all about real-world application. Incredibly engaging and applicable to the modern world in nearly every respect. Dr. Monje is so kind and accessible; I found myself chatting with him for half an hour after every lecture. Lenient grader, too. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

Monje does a great job at making his lectures relatable and easy to digest. There isn't much work, a few writing assignments and a couple reading checks, but as long as you can explain yourself and use applicable vocab you should be fine!
Certified yapper.

Dr. Monje is a very smart man with lots of fun facts up his sleeves. This class is very interesting and low stress. The two midterms and final are open book, open note, multiple choice exams on Canvas that you do from home on your own time. That being said it is a very easy A and a great GPA booster or gen-ed for COMM majors.

Dr, Monje is an amazing professor. He cares about his students and can work with you on any problem that you have. The class is very easy, but you do have to do work with a random partner. His lectures can be a bit boring, but he is very informative. I would take another class with him. Recitation is required and attendance is mandatory.

One of my favorite professors at UNC. he seems like he loves his job and this institution, unlike most professors at unc that act like someone forced them to be here. I 10000% recommend this professor. And for a class I was not actually interested in, he definitely did a good job making the material enjoyable to learn. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Super easy, attendance not mandatory, chill class to add to your schedule. Midterm and final were super easy as well, highly recommend!

COMM140 was very easy because exams were open book and note. But, lectures were boring and it did not seem like he prepared before class. The lectures review the readings and do not provide any additional information. Attendance is not mandatory so if you are looking for an easy A or GPA booster this is a great class to take.

Monje is a very nice person, and he clearly cares a lot about his students Class was ridiculously easy; attendance wasn't required, and we were graded off of 1 essay, 5 forum posts, a midterm and a final. He's not very structured though, and lectures are kinda pointless to attend, so if that bothers you it's prob not for u. material is interesting

My favorite professor so far. He is so caring for his students. His class is extremely easy but it's because he understands the stress we are under most of the time as college students. Everyone needs to take at least one class with Monje.

He is a very chill professor, but if I didn't show up at all, I still would've gotten an A. The final project was a group project of 5 pages per group member due at the end of the semester, a book review, and a response paper. There was no telling what your grade was, until the very end of the semester.
This class was easy and stress free. Prof. Monje was really nice and chill. He didn't require attendance which was nice and we were graded on very few things. Easy A type of class

This class involves a group project which lasts all semester long, and you don't get to pick who you work with. My experience with this has been awful, I dread coming to every class, and I have learned absolutely nothing this whole time. Plus, he takes over a month to produce grades and is inconsistent with due dates. Would not recommend at all.

Dr. Monje's lectures are kind of boring, but the reading content is interesting. He doesn't take attendance, and you don't really have to do anything in class, which he cancels often anyway. All exams are online and open note. He's very nice and you don't have a lot of homework. Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: COMM majors take 140 with him for an easy A. You need to write 10 forums and 10 assignments throughout the semester. No need to study for midterm or final. Lectures are kind of boring, same with the recitations. Overall is a good class to take if you have a heavy semester and need that COMM requirement.

I loved professor Monje! His class was great and I feel like I learned a lot about global warming and the environment. He is so nice and is always willing to give extensions. If you write good and thoughtful essays you are sure to get a great grade. Overall, I would take him again, take him for your FYS if you get the chance!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took comm 140 because I thought it was easy. I was also expecting Dr. Monje to grade my work, but NO! It was graded by the TA. We had to do a weekly forum post and an assignment (250 words essay). My TA was a hard grader, and even though I tried my best, she thought I lacked specificity. BE AWARE! The TAs grade everything! It was super annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great, easy-A class. Read the textbook and participate every once in a while and you'll be fine. I kinda feel bad cuz he didn't get much interaction during class, just staring at names with maybe two people with cams on. Communication got mixed up multiple times though which was frustrating but overall good class if you need it.

Professor Monje is an awesome teacher, I would take a class with him again! He is so kind and always there to help when we have questions about the readings/lectures/. The tests are fair, based off the textbook, while the lectures are more discussion-based but still very interesting. Monje has so much knowledge to share and is the nicest prof.

Tough luck if you have to take COMM 140, as far as I am aware, he is the only prof for this class. Don't get me wrong he's a good guy, but is an awful communicator, getting assignments returned, and isn't engaging. His class is pointless. He doesn't understand the concepts that he talks about; you likely know more than he does & won't learn a thing

Most of the class relied on the textbook and his in class lectures really were just some common sense and stuff from the book. Really nice and the class is an easy A if you show up to class and talk two times the whole semester and read the book's specific chapters before exams. Book was interesting, the class was a bore though.

Easiest class I've ever taken at UNC. The class itself is not engaging at all. As long as you read the textbook, you should get an A. Monje is a decent professor but he goes on tangents about random things that are unrelated to the subject matter. If you need a GPA boost and want to learn about something relatively interesting, it's fine for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is very well-versed on COMM, but unfortunately this class is not very conducive to deep conversations. You MUST do the readings to get above a C on the exams. He encourages engagement in lecture. This class is pretty much what you make of it - attendance is not mandatory but definitely worth going.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Monje is a great guy and a great professor. The class was an easy A but also had interesting discussions that I really enjoyed. Also watched a few disaster movies (always a plus)! There was one paper and one final project, basically completion grades. He is super passionate about climate change so talking/ participating in class helps.

Hes a great guy and is entertaining to listen to when you can tell he cares about what hes saying, but in COMM140 at least, that feels like a rare occasion.  Learned way more in recitation than in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Monje is nice and his class isn't that difficult but he is a terrible communicator and very poorly organized. The day before an exam none of his TAs knew what was going to be on it and his lectures were completely offbase from the textbook we had to read. Unfortunately the exam drew from both his rambling lectures and the book.

Okay, you will get an A in this class if you literally just exist as a person. However, it is so boring I would not take this a class with Monje again. He is very kind and very knowledgeable, but I have learned just about nothing from this class. The whole class was one open book quiz, an in-class midterm, one paper, and a take-home final.

Professor Monje is full of interesting facts and I learned so much from his class! Grading consisted of one paper, some article summaries and participation/attendance (aka small work load). I highly recommend taking him and getting to know him! He has some great advice on subjects both of the class and of success in school/life in general.

Prof Monje is the most kindhearted professor I've had in college so far. He was very flexible with deadlines and gave good feedback, sometimes even "soft" grades so you had a chance to resubmit and improve if needed. He is a very interesting dude to talk to outside of class, which is easy to do because he's very accessible. Also makes class great.

Professor Monje made what was supposed to be a relatively easy class, even easier. And I still learned a lot! We had one essay and one group project, both of which were quite doable and interesting. However, he was a little unclear at times with his grading criteria/expectations. Other than that, he's very knowledgeable and approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Monje is a very likeable person, but not great professor. This class was equivalent in difficulty to my high school freshman English class: just two short papers, neither of which he grades harshly at all. Would recommend if you're looking for an easy class to fulfill hours, but if you actually want to learn something, take someone else.
Great professor. ENG 105 is aggravating for most, but he made it a fun class. A's are very attainable, and he isn't too harsh with attendance or late wok.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: I would 100% take any class taught by Professor Monje. He made what is usually a boring, pointless class into a fun and engaging one, and you can tell that he genuinely cares about his students' success. One of the nicest teachers I've ever had for sure, and grades really fairly. If you have to take ENGL 105, take it with him!

He is an amazing teacher and really takes the time to make sure you know exactly what you should be writing about. Usually I don't enjoy English classes but he did an amazing job of keeping me interested and used different methods to get us to write papers. It was a really enjoyable class.

Dr. Monje is really interesting and is a terrific professor. He was one of the first professors I had at Carolina and reaffirmed by love of English. The class isn't terribly difficult, but it is informative and does teach you how to write.

I LOVE Dr. Monje. He is one of my most favorite professors, not only because he gives an easy/informative class, but because he is such an amazing supporter for his students. B/c he does not follow a strict schedule for assignments, students are allowed to voice when they fell comfortable turning them in (b/c of other class assignments) Great guy.

My favorite professor at UNC by far. As a person he is caring, understanding, and passionate.  It's an easy A, but at the same time I learned a lot. You learn a lot of practical stuff like writing a resume, obituary, business plan, etc.  This is the only class I genuinely looked forward to going to.

Monje is super chill. He has experience in a lot of different fields, and that shows in his lectures and assignments. Very few assignments, and very easy. I never stressed about this class. Not the best at getting the schedule organized and sticking to it, but that doesn't make the class harder.
While, the instructor was helpful and it was not hardto get an A

Literally the chillest guy ever. I thought he was hilarious and super entertaining for a class that could have been really boring. While we did some technical stuff, he let us write about basically whatever we wanted every unit, unlike most other english 105 professors. I would definitely recommend it, easy A and awesome dude!
Outstanding professor!

David is awesome! He made English 105 enjoyable and I never stressed about this class. You just discuss in class and have occasional quizzes (which are super easy). You write all of the assignments outside of class and do peer edits before they are due. He is open to any writing style and a really relaxed, awesome guy. TAKE 105 WITH DAVID!

Super nice guy!!! He is so nice and passionate about just about any topic you can think of. Definitely would recommend him for English 105. He helps you get the assignments done ahead of time and gives lots of extensions if you have a busy week.
He is the best english professor you can ask for. Hes understanding and interesting and accessible in office hours. You will not regret taking this class with David.
Good professor. Easy grader on papers.

Monje is a super cool guy who is totally devoted to his students. His assignments are easy and broken down into smaller parts to ensure a great grade (not to mention he's an easy grader). Couldn't have been more happy in my ENGL105 class than with Monje

Suuuuper chill guy. Very understanding of the fact that students are humans and not robots, and he is all around an understanding guy. As long as you do the work, you'll get an A. Take with him if you can!!! 10/10 recommend.

He is very passionate about course content which made lectures insightful. 1 group project, a few easy assignments, but lots of reading that you have to discuss. Had a pop quiz when people stopped reading. He never gave feedback on stuff or responded to emails unless you asked him in person. Caring in class & office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very chill dude. He is a very slow to grade but I'm sure that's normal. Super easy in class sessions and easy to get an A.

i did not appreciate a lot that he had to say on my work, acted like it was a 400 level writing class. but class time was easy, never put in grades, i dont know im not really a fan even though it was easy.

Super cool. Accommodating and lenient grader, but attendance is important. The class is very conversation-based, so the more you speak up, the smoother it goes. Pretty great, especially for a required class.

Bro is a D1 chiller. He doesn't take attendance. Very lenient on deadlines and was just nice. You can't ask for much more in a professor. For ENGL 105, having him as my professor was such a blessing. Love you Emilio

Emilio is a great teacher. There are about 3 relatively easy major assignments for the entire semester. Overall, the class was super easy and manageable. If you go to class and complete the work, you will get an A. If you can't make it to class, email him, he is super flexible about attendance.I HIGHLY recommend taking this class with Emilio.

Emilio is super nice and really chill. Attendance is not mandatory as long as you email him. The class is composed of three unit projects that each consist of a couple feeder assignments, annotated bibliography, and a paper. He always asks for feedback on assignments and how we are feeling about them. I definitely recommend ENGL 105 with him.

Class is only graded by 2 exams and a participation grade, but Bruno makes it as easy as possible. He is very passionate about linguistics and wants us to talk to him in class (will cold call). No course schedule, just occasional reading homework to keep us engaged. Attendance is important, and he is sure to explain concepts clearly in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very passionate teacher but very strict. Make sure you go to office hours. No computers/phones/ipads allowed in class-- all hand written. The class was also quite difficult for being an introductory course.
Lit teacher played Roblox all class and leveled up in adopt me hella take his class for an easy A
great class took it with the fellas and day traded the whole time I put bruno onto forex

Forensic linguistics, new course. Bruno is scary, but honestly the sweetest. Mad respect he's so smart. The homework is hard but if you start early and ask he'll help you. There's hw every class but he only requires 5 graded, you can ask for an excuse if you ask ahead of time no questions asked. My 1st class with him, dunno what he's like in person

Estigarribia was the worst professor to have during a pandemic and civil unrest. For some reason, he decided to grade even more assignments than he usually does this semester. All homework was graded for accuracy and he will lower your grade if you don't understand the topic or don't use italics. I do not recommend taking his class during covid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Bruno is hands down the best Spanish professor I have EVER had. He's hard, don't take any of his classes expecting an easy A, but he's such a good professor he justifies his challenging grading. He randomly grades homework and he grades it on a curve so you have to do it. His lectures are very though so take notes and ask questions if you're lost.

Bruno was one of the hardest professors I've ever had. We had no guidance for the exams (other than study everything- literally), would get locked out of the room if you left to use the restroom, and would have incredibly hard to follow lectures. In his office hours he wasn't much help either, and assumed you should know everything. Rough class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Estigarribia was one of the most unapproachable, and difficult professors I have ever had. Class was always just lecturing, usually no powerpoint. For the 2 midterms and final, there was no review, and only our notes and the daily homework to look over. After the class average for the first midterm was failing the students were blamed. AVOID!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Phonetics was my favourite course this semester, and not only because it's a fascinating field for me, but also because professor Bruno exceeded my expectations by far: knowledgeable, approachable, organized and enthusiastic. He's an amazing researcher but he also is passionate about what he teaches, and he does it extremely well. 10/10.

Dr. Estigarribia is a very good professor and he did an excellent job bringing in new research in the field of Guarani Linguistics to our class. I definitely try to take courses with this professor, because he can be depended on to help you get a solid foundation in the major. This was one of my favorite courses in my undergraduate career.

Very fair prof. You have to do the work (sometimes there's a lot of it) and know the material, but his exams are very straight-forward and his expectations are generally very clear. He offers extra credit throughout the semester and he is enthusiastic about his subject.

Dr. Sahle is methodical and thorough, and expects her students to be the same. She has a deep knowledge of Africa. There are a lot of readings, but they are very interesting. I learned a lot in this class and really appreciate her perspective.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Avoid like the plague... Sahle is the worst professor I have had at UNC. I literally went to her office hours to try to understand the material and she was not helpful at all, it actually was a very uncomfortable experience as I felt like I was being judged the whole time. Please do yourself a favor and sign up with the other professor or avoid.
