I will say that she doesn't have a clear form of grading or deciding the final grade, which can confuse some, but you can argue your case for a higher grade. Easy final project too.

She's a nice person, like a grandma but she's one of the worst teachers I've ever had. Absolutely no form of grading criteria and she has a "grading contract" instead of normal grades. She makes a bunch of convoluted rules surrounding each assignment. Never knew my grade, and she hated giving feedback. Class was really slight, just annoying.
Professor Ficke was lowk evil. She is not scared to fail people and is so unengaging. She's definitely a nice person, but as a teacher I would not want to have her again.

Dr. Ficke is very nice, but I found this class to be extremely boring and un-engaging. It was very easy to just tune out and do work for other classes. Which is a shame, because I was very excited for this class. Not a lot of work though, easy A. I thought that the projects were kind of fun, especially the meme project and the final project.

Professor Ficke's class is not as easy as the other 105 classes, but as long as you put in the effort for your assignments and participate a decent amount in class, you should be fine. She gives good feedback and is lenient on deadlines. The only downside is that she only lets you know your grade twice: mid-semester and at the end of the semester.

Dr. Ficke is one of the sweetest professors I have had! The assignments were pretty easy, and I love that she gave so many opportunities for us to receive feedback on drafts. She uses a grading contract and when we had big projects coming up, she would host individual conferences to give us feedback on our work so far.

prof helps you lots with english/writing, gives much feedback, wants u to succeed. compared to other eng105, class is harder. contract grading where grades based on ability to meet standards(each assignment given grade of meets, exceeds, doesn't meet expectations. final grade is numerical so this confuse u abt where you are/difficult to get A
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ficke was a great professor! She was helpful with providing feedback and was often accessible if you needed any help. The grading is a little bit weird in the class, as you don't know what you have in the class till the very end of the course. There is a decent amount of work for a 105 class, but not bad at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved taking her class! She is a great professor and is really willing to work with students to ensure they do well. There is a decent amount of work for this class, but she gives plenty of time for students to complete their work and provides tons of feedback. Overall would take again.

Professor Ficke is so kind and clearly loves her class. The assignments are easy to complete with high grades, just don't procrastinate on your essays. We had an easy 5 minute presentation and she explained exactly what she was looking for in class. Just please answer her questions because she gets sad if no one responds. :)

She was very kind and lenient as long as you communicate. She is quick to take off points for small errors on presentations or papers. Definitely recommend for Engl 105 if its the only english requirement you need, pretty easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Ficke was the best!

This class was pretty enjoyable and the content was quite diverse. Dr. Ficke had a clear outline for how the class was going to run and she didn't step outside that outline. This class doesn't have a big time commitment as you do most of your work during class. Highly recommend!

She is super nice, super caring, and considerate. There is a grace period available if needed, you just have to reach out ahead of time. Expect homework after almost every class, but it is not always a lot. As long as you put in effort, you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She's a caring professor and has the perfect outline for her class where you come out learning a lot. She checks in on her students just enough and has solid lectures. The one downside is only a 96.00+ is an A which is RIDICULOUS considering the means on essays are around 91's so don't expect an easy A, maybe an easy B+ and likely A-.

Prof Ficke is a new teacher to UNC and is very kind. She cares about her students and gives grace periods to students, and takes student feedback into consideration because she understands her role is to strengthen students' writing skills, not to make us work too hard on things that do not matter. She gives clear feedback, very helpful

Do not take a class with her. She is so boring, and has no idea how to lead discussions on the literature. I love English, and was extremely disappointed with this class, to put it lightly. Avoid her at all costs!
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
Dr. Fokina is so nice and funny. She likes for students to participate, so don't be afraid to! She is a super fair grader, so just show up and pay attention to lectures, and you'll be golden!
She wants you to succeed. Great lecture and course material. Attend lecture and you'll be good.

I honestly don't know why other people dislike her, she is truly such a good professor, who when you ask for clarification will help you understand complex concepts better. She is really funny and always made attending class enjoyable. Definetly would take her for 225, HW is not that bad and exams are pretty fair.

She was fine and a funny lecturer, a lot of the material/hw/slides did seem written by chat gpt which is a little disheartening but the class was pretty easy and exams weren't too hard if you practiced with the poll everywhere questions. HW load is light and attendance policy is forgiving

Dr. Fokina is truly the kindest professor I've had the pleasure of learning from. I know so many people who can say the same about her kindness and genius. She understands time constraints and the under load of an undergraduate, which not many professors do. Above all though, she teaches with compassion and intention. I highly recommend taking her.

Only reason why I got a good grade in this class because I studied on my own. Her slides are not clear and very hard to study from, especially if you miss a class. She also just does not teach effectively and is bad at explaining so it's not really of use to go to class anyway. Would not recommend taking it with Fokina

Professor Fokina is not a good teacher. She does not explain things well and everything I learned in this class was taught on my own. She made a topic that could've been really interesting incredibly difficult and hard to understand. Don't take this class if you want to learn everything yourself.

I personally really enjoyed this class. All assignments were pretty easy and the only thing you have to study for are two midterms and a final, which weren't that hard. The class was also interesting and we often did demos in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Figueroa is clearly knowledgeable, but the class focused almost entirely on musical ethnographies rather than music theory or history. Most classes involved discussing readings in a lecture of about 100 students. There were only four graded items (midterm, final, and two projects). The class is easy overall, but I found it very boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class and professor were extremely easy, and earning an A required minimal effort. However, the material itself was very boring, which made attending class feel unnecessary and frustrating, but attendance was mandatory and graded. The readings were not required to succeed, and I did not feel that I learned anything meaningful from the course.

easiest class ever, but since it isn't fulfilling any requirements for me and it wasn't that engaging it really felt tedious to show up. Focuses on readings during lectures, but doesn't go that far in depth to ever feel obligated to read them. There were a few interesting lectures, but those were a minority for sure.

Like many of the other musicology classes, this class was loosely defined as a concept. Dr. Figueroa didn't seem particularly interested in reading our work or giving us feedback, and a lot of our time was wasted with him trying to figure out what to do. I'm almost sure that he didn't read our final papers before grading them.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor. Didn't take attendance but syllabus mentions participation so still go to class. Very supportive during the research process and wants you to succeed. I wish he would have given more feedback throughout the semester since his feedback was super helpful. The final paper is super manageable if you make steady progress on it.

Dr. Figueroa is wonderful and very smart. If you genuinely care about music, this class is great. However, if you are taking this for the requirement, you must show up. Attendance is the biggest thing in the course. I loved it, but I can see how someone who doesn't have good attendance would not be able to pass the course.

Figueroa is caring and knows a lot, however he made attendance mandatory for a class where nothing in class actually contributed. Whole class is based around writing one paper, and yet I barely got feedback through the drafting process. Easy A if you complete assignments, not a whole lot of work on a day to day.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Figueroa is very nice and caring, but the class time itself was often wasted in "writing workshops" or empty discussions on how to write or edit a paper. Late & minimal feedback & no clear assignment instructions. I enjoyed researching a unique topic, and I did learn, but mostly from my own research rather than from the professor. Easy grader.

Overall a kind and respectful professor. However the course was a learning void: empty Canvas modules or a single link, vague paper instructions with no rubric, and an absent professor during "writing workshops". Feedback arrived at least a month late, assignment extensions were frequent, and learning was nonexistent. Wouldn't recommend this course

Prof. Figueroa is a super kind and encouraging professor. The content of this class is kind of difficult, but he grades very easily as long as you are willing to try. Very participation heavy, but not like you have to volunteer every class. Great professor and class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Figueroa is the best professor I have had at UNC. He is so obviously passionate about what he teaches and he really instills that passion in his students. The assignments are relatively easy but are relevant to the material and are truly engaging. Absolute BEST choice for VP credit (or just for fun and learning).

Professor Figueroa is one of the best professors I have had. Lectures are interesting with cool music being played and just 5 projects for the class that basically everyone did well in. There is no better option for a VP credit at all.

Great professor and TAs; Very easy class and interesting; there are low stakes quizzes each week in recitation and 5 projects; people often don't participate in class which makes me feel bad since Prof Fig is awesome and clearly excited about the topics so pls participate if you can!

Probably one of the easiest classes you could take. Super nice guy and the TA I had graded extremely easily and was also super nice. Main assignments are 5 projects (1 per unit) which take no almost time and 3 out of 5 are group projects.
Take this for an Easy A/Gen eds. lots of group projects, attendance and readings aren't necessary. grade based upon five projects and a final paper which are graded by TA's.

Figueroa is an outstanding professor! There is a lot of reading; however, it's both manageable and engaging. Assignments were relatively easy, and he offered a few extra credit opportunities. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Figueroa is super understanding and just cares about you participating. Doesn't grade hard, you just need to show that you're giving effort. Great guy!! Took his class for a VP credit, I'd definitely recommend.

So far Prof Figueroa has been the most genuine and caring professor I've had at this school. His lectures are really interesting and he really tries to make sure the whole class understands. Our class consisted of 1 mid-term group project, 5 in-class writing assignments, and the final exam so the work is quite light. Overall great class
An amazing professor! Genuinely cares so much about students and his lectures were extremely interesting.

Prof Figueroa is one of the kindest, most caring professors I've ever had. He is uniquely in-tune with student needs in a way that's unlike any professor I've had before. He is very honest with his classes and is open to feedback. He's also a good instructor-- he leads very stimulating conversation-based classes and is all around a nice guy. 10/10

Professor Figueroa is a really caring person. The material wasn't interesting to me, but the class was easy to get an A in as long as you did well in the recitation and attended lectures because he takes attendance.

The class wasa joke, we showed up to lectures because of the UNC Check-in app but everyone just did other homework. Figueroa is a really nice guy tho and even if you take this class for the VP wants you to get something out of it. No tests, just projects but the TAs are pretty chill graders if you put some effort in. Ez VP credit.

Loved this class. Perfect way to get BN credit. Finds a way to make a 200 person lecture seem fun and engaging, which I've found to be a very rare skill. 75% of the course is group work though so I'd be wary of that if that's not your thing.

Prof. Figueroa is the best! The class is the easiest/least work I have taken at UNC by simply going to lecture and doing the projects (didn't do readings). He is so caring and understanding and passionate about music. He gives good lectures that you don't have to follow closely and do not need the material at all for the weekly group projects.

Professor Figueroa is hands down the best professor I have ever encountered at unc. Class consist of lectures mostly covering assigned readings, which you don't need to read if you go to class. Recitations is where most work is done and in groups for projects. Prof Figueroa truly cares about his students and wants nothing for them to succeed.
He is a good guy and can be funny sometimes. The class is really easy if you show up and do well on the group projects. Pretty easy for the VP, BN gen eds

Prof. Figueroa is a great instructor! His lectures were interesting and funny. Grades for the class came from 6 group projects in recitation that were not very hard and were graded super leniently. I would recommend taking this class as it is easy and the topics can be interesting. Great way to get VP and BN gen eds.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Pretty easy A, only gave papers and no midterm or final. I wish he had given us more opportunities to use the info he gave us in lectures, which is why no one really showed up to class. Otherwise, easy BN credit.

Knows his stuff but you don't have to know it all. Did not do readings, went to 60% of lectures, all recitations and got an A. Class was interesting at times, but was taking for BN & VP so it usually put me to sleep. Assignments graded by TAs so honestly your grade hangs in the balance of their kindness, but the lowest I've heard was a B+.

Good choice for the BN gen ed! There were 6 projects/papers (3 were group) that TAs grade, & they were all relatively easy. The final was essay-based & wasn't too bad if you did the readings & attended lectures. Prof. Figueroa is super passionate about the subject & really wants you to learn! Go to lecture/recitation and you should do well!

This was a good, easy class that teaches about global concepts. Lecture is interesting! Professor Figueroa is very nice and most of your grade comes from group projects in recitation that your TA grades. Attendance and participation in recitation matters! Read readings + go to performances + go to recitation/class + study a little   achievable A.
Figueroa is so boring. The class is easy, and I basically never went to lecture. Never did the reading. The assignments are juvenile. If that sounds like your kind of thing, go for it.

Overall, Figueroa was a great professor. The only thing is the class was only offered early in the mornings and sometimes it's hard to stay awake. His lectures can be a little dry but it's easy to get engaged when familiar music samples are played. Figueroa also doesn't grade tough at all and is really easy to talk to. Definitely loves what he does
Awesome teacher and awesome class! All you really need to do is go to class, stay awake, and participate every now and then. Lectures are fascinating and you can really learn a lot.
Chem 101 is very hard, but she does her best to make the content seem less daunting and lectures as interesting as possible!

Hands down my favorite chem professor so far (junior chem major). I love Dr Fostvedt so much. She cares about your learning, is kind, and is very accessible. She also wants you to succeed and do your best. Dr. Fostvedt will meet you where you are and try to help you every step of the way. Truly a wonderful human being--her kindness is contagious.
Take her. Favorite class ever

Dr. Fostvedt is awesome! Super sweet and takes all the time needed to answer questions. Since CHEM101 is 90% freshman, she validates us by acknowledging that chemistry is hard. Most of the TAs are great too

Fostvedt is literally amazing, she always has fun ways to teach you content (dances, yoga, models, etc.) and is sooo caring. She will slow down to answer questions and makes jokes inbetween. I only need to take chem101 for my major, but she also teaches 251 and her personality is tempting me to take 251

Her office hours are extremely helpful. ULAs are very helpful too. She has extra credit opportunities. I would take her again. I have never had a more understanding and kind professor, which is rare in UNC's CHEM department. She had helpful practice sheets. On the downside, multiple-choice questions on tests were difficult, in my opinion.

Would give 6/5 if it was an option. Fostvedt is incredible at explaining difficult concepts in ways that are understandable to students. She is also extremely caring and wants all of her students to succeed. She has options for 10 minute meeting every week — strongly recommend. Side note: If you're taking 251, don't read the textbook, it's useless
Dr. Fostvedt is a great profesor and makes sure her students succeed in class

Dr. Fostvedt is by far one of if not the kindest and most down to Earth professor I've ever had. She makes chem 251 and absolute joy, and is one of the most accommodating professors ever. Her exams are always fair, and her lectures are really interesting and taught extremely well. Additionally, she gives a lot of practice.
Leaving love

One of, if not the best professor I've had in college. I learned a ton in this class and had fun doing so. This course was also not overly-demanding at all and I enjoyed it even though synthetic chemistry is not my field of interest within chemistry. Definitely take a class with Dr. Fostvedt if you can.

Dr Fostvedt is the best professor i have had at UNC! The textbook for this class is DENSE but in class her explanations make it so clear. So many opportunities for practice (TONS of practice exams) and her exams are so fair! Hard material but if you go to class it makes so much more sense.

Dr. Fostvedt is incredible--truly a gem among an otherwise heinous Chemistry department. No rating below a 5 here has anything to do with her, or is at all under her control. She is inviting and engaging--I enjoyed chem because I looked forward to learning from her. One of the best and sweetest professors I've ever had the privilege to learn from.

Professor Fostvedt is so sweet and caring! She tries to make CHEM 101 as engaging as it can be. The class is definitely very difficult but that's because of the department, not her, since all the professors follow the same format and use the same exams. As for the class, practice is very important and what helped my study best for the exams.

The best professor in the UNC chem department. Amazing lecturer, tried to make how boring chemistry was into something great. She was always caring for EVERY student. Chem is very hard because of the terrible department, but not Dr. Fostvedt. I love her!

Dr. Fostvedt is a QUEEN in all aspects. She's super fun, caring, and conducts very engaging lectures. She also plans fun activities like bingo and jeopardy where you get the chance to win fun chemistry stickers. Exams are fair and straightforward if you pay attention and do the problem sets. Every exam also has an extra credit question.

Best wet lab I've taken at UNC. To my knowledge, Dr. Fostvedt is the only lab instructor that actually releases the grading criteria used for evaluating each assignment. This course is 100x better than it used to be, and the pigment synthesis is actually pretty fun. Group research project at the end of the course with a poster presentation & paper.

Fostvedt is hands down the best chemistry professor at UNC. Shes so kind, good at teaching, and approachable. So reasonable with grades and classwork and takes feedback from students fullheartedly. An angel sent down to bring a little light to the hell that is the UNC chem department. If youre a chem major or need to take a chem class PLZ TAKE HER

FY-Launch section. Hands down best professor ever. So sweet, knowledgeable, and flexible. Outfits consistently eat and her explanations make you laugh. She gets us to enjoy chemistry, which is a talent. Class itself is not hard, especially if you do the recommended textbook and recitation practice problems. Nightly reading and completion hw grade.

Fostvedt is AMAZING. I loved inorganic chemistry with her, loved the content of the course, loved going to lecture, loved being taught by her. Could not recommend her enough. She is so caring, she is so smart, and she is so good at teaching. If I could take 251 again, I would :)

She is such a great person and great lecturer. She is open to feedback and is very passionate about her subject. By far the best chem prof I've had so far (chem major). She writes very fair exams and gives an extra credit question at the end of the midterms and final. There is also an opportunity to memorize the periodic table for a grade boost.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's nice but this class was not it for me. Content feels very hand-wavey at times and not very interesting to be honest. Exams are difficult, final was marginally easier. Extra credit of +1% to course grade is available for memorizing periodic table!

Dr. Fostvedt is the most caring chem professor I've ever had. She wants you to succeed and is always available outside of class to help. She even asked the class halfway through the semester how she could improve. Lectures are great and exams are fair. I hate the class but love her as a professor.
Not her fault, but the class is designed to hand-wave a lot of physical principles, which results in the need to memorize seemingly random facts for the exam.
Amazing professor who explains concepts very well. Slows down when needed and will give additional examples in class. Great at her job fr and passionate about chem which made the class more engaging

Couldn't recommend Fostvedt enough! Caring, great at explaining hard concepts, and sets very clear expectations. Learning Assistants are truly the best in the Chem Dept as well. There's one bonus question on each exam, and she gives one extra credit opportunity for overall grade. Not an easy class, but not impossible. Study from the slides!!

I had Dr. Fostvedt for 102 and she was an awesome teacher. The lectures were amazing and engaging, and the class was always fun and informative. The class is even more test heavy and harder than 101, but none of that is Dr. Fostvedt's fault. An amazing class overall, absolutely get Dr. Fostvedt for this class.

I look CHEM 101 With Dr. Fostvedt, and she was absolutely amazing. She is very caring, her lectures are phenomenal, and she is always willing to help. The class is slightly difficult and test heavy, but that is due to the chemistry department and not her fault. 10/10, definitely try and get this class with her.

Fostvedt is amazing but 102 w/ her wont make it much better bc all 102s use the same teaching+slides. Def take her; dont get stressed if you cant. To pass, go to 2 LA/TA sessions weekly & re-do all class slide problems plus the practice exams (sometimes theyre exam questions). Plz do hw, dont stress over text readings, & go to class its important!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fostvedt is great but this class is very difficult.  Exams make up the majority of your grade and they are not easy, although the final was significantly easier than the midterms in my opinion.

As any chem, this was test heavy. But her tests are fair based on lectures and participation. Be sure to go to every class and have a good understanding of content. She has a lot of resources outside of class as well and is very understanding.

Dr. Fostvedt is the literal only good professor in the CHEM department here. Her tests are fair to the point where you could earn up to 5 points back on the last test because she thought it was "too long." She has a lot of opportunities to practice exam-type problems, and is very willing to help you improve if you seek it out. BEST CHEM PROFESSOR

Professor fostvedt is the best of the unc chem professors. This department is rough but professor fostvedt explains the material really well, great depth, and actually cares that we understand the material. only note is that she does frequently spend so much teaching a topic that we then fall behind on notes and material.

I LOVE FOSTVEDT. She responds to emails very fast, is VERY thorough, and genuinely cares about her students. She is just so sweet, really tries to learn everyones name(even in a HUGE lecture hall), and is very involved. She is amazing.
She is really passionate about chemistry and takes time to get to know her students. The UNC chem department is a BEAST but she tries to help us out the best that she can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is hard but take it with Fostvedt if you can. She is super engaging and enthusiastic during lecture and really approachable. Be prepared to attend outside sessions, get a tutor, and/or do a lot of practice problems. The midterms varied in difficulty but overall very challenging.

Dr. Fostvedt is the most kind, respectable, humble, and best lecturer I have ever had! She genuinely cares for her students which shows as she learns the names of half of her students when they ask questions! Any chem class is hard at UNC and you will have to work diligently, but if you have the chance take a class with Dr. Fostvedt!

Dr. Fostvedt completely changed chemistry for me. She makes complicated concepts simple and approachable. Chem102 is not easy, but she made it great. That being said, I sometimes felt like I lacked the nuanced understanding of concepts needed to succeed in difficult exams. You should attend the sessions outside of class! Take her if you can!!!

Dr. Fostvedt is incredible! She always brings joy to the classroom and provides lots of extra practice through PSS, PS, and LA worksheets, and practice exams. The exams aren't too bad and any other work is collaborative.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is amazing! Clearly cares about her students. I literally switched my major to chemistry because she made it seem so interesting. Very available outside of class. As long as you do the abundant practice problems she provides, you will be fine.

Dr. Fostvedt is an incredible professor! She goes over the material thoroughly, and goes the extra mile to make her lectures engaging. She cares a lot about her students, and provides useful feedback in class, GPSS, and six-minute meetings. Still study well outside of class, as the course material is objectively challenging.
Dr. Fostvedt is such a kind, caring professor! She makes the lectures so fun, and really makes an effort to get to know her students. I'd definitely recommend going to her 6-minute meetings.

Dr Fostvedt is an amazing professor who cares for her students success. This class is very manageable especially if you go to the office hours she offers throughout the semester. Not a lot of homework and gives extra credit opportunities.

Prof. Fostvedt is incredible. She takes the time to explain everything in a concise manner and often uses analogies that we can relate to to make the concepts more accessible. Chem is a tough subject, but she tried to make it as straightforward as possible and provide us with all of the resources we could possibly need. Would 3,000% take again.

Great professor who tried her best to make the class as easy as possible, unfortunately the class is too hard cause we have to be up to standard with our "top 10 chemistry school" so in the end it technically doesn't matter who you take either get the concepts or you don't but probably best to go with fostvedt.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have never enjoyed nor understood chemistry until I took 101 with Dr. Fostvedt. She is extremely caring towards her students and very responsive to any questions asked. She makes her lectures easy to follow and straightforward. It is a flipped classroom, but I think it helps in the end as long as you put in the work to understand the content.

Fostvedt is by far the best professor, she made a very difficult course like CHEM101 very understandable and simple as possible. She is super encouraging and actually learned names in a big lecture (if you are in the first couple rows). Her GPSS sessions are the best and I wish everyone could take 101 with her! Put in the work to succeed though.
she's a good teacher it's just the chem department is so hard, there's almost nothing she can do but try and teach. Sometimes her age and how new she is to teaching can show

Prof. Fostvedt is an amazing teacher. While she is confined to the standards/exams of the chem dept, she makes lectures easily understandable and engaging. She is always willing to answer questions and wants everyone to do well. CHEM101 is difficult no matter what, but she is a fantastic professor to take it with. Also a very kind and cool person!!

Dr. Fostvedt is definitely one of, if not THE best chemistry professors at UNC. Her lectures are extremely easy to understand, and she's always willing to answer questions. She's extremely kind and friendly, and genuinely cares about her students. I'd definitely recommend taking advantage of the "Six-minute meetings" as well.

She is so sweet and she is an amazing teacher. There were very few lectures where I came out confused. I also went to her GPSS sessions which were also awesome. She carefully went through everything we asked and made sure we understood what wwe were doing. She also learned so many peoples names for such a giant lecture hall.

Prof. Fostvedt is an amazing lecturer who I felt like really cares about her students. I would recommend her GPSS if possible. Chem 101 has the same tests department wide so if you are worried about hard tests taking it with a different prof will not affect this!

She is the nicest professor ever. I think she is probably the best out of the chem department. She is very understanding and always willing to help. Now with that said, Chem 101 is very hard at unc. But if you have to take it I would try to get her.

Professor Fostvedt keeps our attention in class effectively transmits concepts.  We thought we were well prepared with materials to succeed on the first exam we took recently.  She even gave us last years exams, but when we took this exam it was much more difficult.  The guidance we were given was far from parallel to what we were presented with.

Professor Fostvedt=great lecturer. We were provided with last year's exams in preparation for our first exam last week. We got slammed because it was tremendously more difficult.  We feel like we were misled.  Perhaps she was told to make the exams harder this year because last years exams were too easy?  New professor to the school=easier exam?

I LOVED Prof. Fostvedt! The class itself isn't an easy A, but she was able to make the material very interesting to learn and I thought her tests/grading were extremely fair. The few assignments she assigns aren't just busy work, but actually help you learn which was much appreciated.

She was hands down my favorite chem professor. She taught the class really well. By no means was the class easy but with the problem sessions and office hours the challenging concepts I didn't understand in class became so much easier. Anyway, take the course with her if you need to she's great!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Fostvedt was such a great 101 professor!! The chem101 curriculum is tough no matter what professor you take it with, but she did such a great job explaining the new topics and realizing when the class needed more time on something. She gave time for us to practice in class, communicated any schedule changes, and really cared for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The best professor I have had at UNC, bar none. Dr. Fostvedt is incredibly passionate about her material, and it shows. She explains difficult concepts in a simple way, and is very accessible outside of class if you need anything. Could not recommend taking a class with her enough.

Dr. Fostvedt was great and made learning fun. Her tests were fairly difficult, but the other assignments weren't too bad. The class gets easier as it goes on and the final was extremely fair. Dr. Fostvedt is very approachable and fun to talk to about chemistry and non-chemistry topics. Overall I think she's a professor every chem major should take.

Basically no homework, so unfortunately I fell behind and thought the tests would be very easy. I did not do well in the beginning at all. Inorganic was a tough subject for me but then the final I aced it after finally understanding so don't fall behind! She is very nice tho. Textbook is useless. Personally, orgo 2 was easier.

Dr. Fostvedt is easily my favorite professor at chapel hill. She actually cares about her student's success, and willingly helps you. Regardless if you have her for chem 101 or not I HIGHLY recommend going to her GPSS on fridays at 12 (this time might be changed though). This is easily the best way to stay on top of her class and to study as well.

I though Professor Fostvedt was alright. We ended up behind in lectures often, she starts every lecture with like a 5-10 minute talk about a fun fact or person that she wanted to share with us which really took away important time from class. This made it feel like we had to rush through some of the later material.

I honestly don't understand the Fostvedt hype. In my opinion, students were taught to memorize rather than understand the material. This was evident when taking the midterm exams in which virtually every question included some niche exception to the more common physical principles. The final exam was much more straightforward.

Dr. Fostvedt has been my favorite Professor at UNC so far! She is so sweet and really wants to see her students succeed. When she goes through problems she walks through every single step no matter how simple which is really helpful. I always felt prepared for the tests if I did the homework and payed attention in class. Absolutely loved her!!

Dr. Fostvedt is hands down the best professor I've had at UNC as of yet. She's super sweet, so passionate about chemistry that even lectures on boring mathy stuff become engaging and fun, and she's a lenient grader even on exams. There's extra credit on exams as well as an additional extra credit opportunity, and there was virtually no homework!

Pls take any class u can with her- shes super nice and approachable, and shes really a great lecturer! You can tell she genuinely loves teaching and wants to help you learn, and is super smart and good at teaching. 11/10 one of my best instructors ever

The tests for this class are hard, so do lots of practice, but they're pretty reflective of the practice problems and lectures. The class was hard, but I I LOVE Professor Fostvedt. She's makes it all worth it and just brightens the day of everyone around her.

Dr. Fostvedt is the best Chem professor you will get at this school. The Chem department is overall like a 4/10 here, so do yourself a favor and take fostvedt. Makes topic simple and is very accessible outside of class. The effort you put in is basically the grade you get out. She made my 9am chem bearable because she was so good.

Just take her, it's a no brainer. I'm convinced that she is the best professor you can get for a general chem class. She's incredibly patient and practically defines how a good professor acts and teaches like. Hard to believe that I found myself enjoying this class at times... something that wouldn't have happened if I wasn't in her section.

Jade Fostvedt is amazing, chemistry is not. She didn't control the material that was on the test, but believe me they were extremely difficult. She is a passionate and interesting lecturer. If you have to take this class I can't recommend her enough.

Dr. Fostvedt is a great professor! She's very passionate about chemistry and is frequently accessible outside of class. The practice you do in class and for homework very accurately reflects the tests. The material isn't easy, but if you come to lecture and practice you'll do well. Wouldn't recommend taking this class before orgo though
Honestly, Dr. Fostvedt was an amazing professor. The reason my grade isn't super good is because I did not try anywhere near as good as I should have. My grade does not reflect her she was the best.

I took CHEM 101 last semester with Dr. Fostvedt, I just forgot to do a review for her. I found her to be incredibly nice and caring about her students, as well as a great professor. She also made chemistry very interesting, despite it being a hard subject. Chem at UNC is difficult, but it is not impossible to get an A.

She is one of the nicest people ever. She's so understanding if you're ever sick or out of class, and tries to explain the material so everyone understands it. She is one of those people who would genuinely never hurt a fly

Very chill and likable person. Whole chemistry department is very organized, I would recommend using all of the resources offered. Clearly shows how to do problems. Answers everyones questions. Only trouble was with running out of time towards the end of class because she answers so many questions.

I can't express my love for Dr. Fostvedt enough. Super caring, listens to students, excellent lecturer, super knowledgable, but has no problem admitting when she's unusure of something or if she's made a mistake. If I could take all my chemistry classes with her I would. Could've done better in her class but that was simply me being lazy.

Fostvedt is great for 101. Her teaching style shows that she really cares about her students gaining a true understanding of the material. Learning chemistry for the first time is hard work, but she approaches questions + concerns with respect. I felt engaged in her lectures; I totally recommend taking her class!

Dr. Fostvedt is amazing! She is so great during lecture and you can really tell how passionate she is about the subject matter. If I could take every class with her I would. Her class made me remember the reasons why I became a Chemistry major in the first place and I am incredibly grateful for that. Take her class if you can, you won't regret it!
i only got a d because i am stupid. dr. fostvedt is a queen and my grade doesnt reflect her amazingness

Her lectures are great, she makes the material easy to understand and is always willing to answer questions. Would recommend her office hours for practice problems and more clarity as needed, I found them super helpful. Exams are tough but totally fair and from lecture (I didn't open the textbook once).

Dr. Fostvedt has a great personality and is enthusiastic about the content. She answers any questions in class, although this can cause her to not completely go through the slides in class. 

Make sure you pay attention to the in-class slides, even if you did not entirely go through them. Chances are it's on your exam. Also, attend chem-possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: While this was her first semester, she was an amazing chemistry professor and really cared about learning. She knew the material really well and explained all the concepts succinctly. Go to office hours and review session as those are great ways to ask questions and get a lot of practice! Exams are difficult but extremely fair!

Was extremely sweet and understanding and went out of her way to help students who asked for it. Was her first semester teaching here and she did an awesome job, was so down to earth and transparent. Only thing I'd say is that there was more material than there was class time, so I would advise going to office hours/ review sessions. 11/10.

Though this was her first semester, she taught like she's been a professor for many years. Clearly knows the material, and she's always willing to explain content. Attend office hours and ask questions. Exams are difficult but always reflect the material taught in lecture. One of the best profs in the chem department. Take inorganic with her.

great professor in a disorganized department. Easy-to-understand lectures, answers questions, kind person.  Go to GPSS, work out practice problems, read chapters, watch "The Organic Chemistry Tutor" on YouTube (my saving grace), and make a study guide for each chapter, this allows you to have your notes summarized for exams.

Dr. Fostvedt is an amazing professor. Chemistry was difficult for me but she went above and beyond to answer everyone's questions. I do recommend going to class to get participation points and to ask questions about the material!

Prof. Fostvedt is a very sweet first-year instructor! Made coming to class at 8am worth it, very enthusiastic about the material, + never failed to put a smile on my face. She is also so stylish and humorous :) Participation based on responding to questions using an iclicker throughout lecture, incorrect answers do not affect participation grade.
She's a fine Gen Chem professor. She didn't always get through the material in class, but that was usually because she was answering people's questions.

Took her lecture in freshman year for CHEM 101. She was really enthusiastic about learning and helping students understand things that puzzle them. Helped me to find opportunities for chemistry teaching within department, outside of class. Super receptive to feedback, like when making a mistake in class.

Professor Fostvedt was an amazing professor who really cared about her students. You can tell that she worked really hard to make everyone understand the material and wanted everyone to do well. I loved her lectures and felt like she was really easy to understand. I would definitely take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Fostvedt is an amazing lecturer. She explains each and every concept very well and concisely. She wants everyone to succeed and is very caring, especially during her office hours. She also tries to understand and personally know her students. I 100% recommend taking her!
She's awesome!! I love the fact that she can relate to us, since she went to UNC.

She was a wonderful teacher and support system at UNC. She makes it very clear that she cares about every one of her students, inside and outside of the classroom. If you have the opportunity to take a class with her, do it!

kind, genuine, and supportive person who understands the struggle of students. super open about her own experiences and listens if you need help with anything/deadlines. she will sit and wait for someone to speak if no one is responding to her questions but she gives good feedback for any answer. would recommend again and again!
absolutely love toni f. goat.
Sweet guy, genuinely wants you to do as well as possible. Also we had 2 home exams! Would recommend, especially for a second semester senior

Greg is a hilarious professor and his jokes made lectures entertaining. His teaching style wasn't for me (he tried to cover as many examples as possible rather than explaining what he was doing). This class is extremely test heavy, but he gives decent review sheets. At the end he changed the syllabus so everyone got the highest grade possible!

Dr. Forest is very funny and an open book. I think he truly wants his students to do well. His style was often rather chaotic, and this was sometimes frustrating. He releases a practice exam before any exam that he promises looks exactly like the test, and this is true sometimes even to the question.

One of my best classes ever. Although I had taken calc in hs this was a  much harder and required studying. He made sure to explain each concept and for our final exam he went through each students grades to adjust scores to make sure we got the highest grade we could also also rounded many people. Would 100% recommend taking calc 1 with him.
Really kind proferssor and I can tell how much he wants the students to get an A in this course, would love to take again!!!

Very nice person but very bad teacher. He uses no technology in class, and writes everything in chalk with not so great handwriting. He is better for those who are comfortable with their calculus skills, but if you are learning calculus for the very first time I DO NOT RECOMMEND. He does not curve his hard tests which sets us up for failure.

Very sweet man.. very hard class. I could definitely tell he was not used to teaching 231 because a lot of things did not make sense and he did a poor job explaining. Course moves very fast and it is quite easy to fall behind due to old school teaching style. Don't purchase textbook, it's free online. He does not have office hours-relies on TAs.
Bro let me take my final in his office for an extra 3 hours after I missed the first 2 purely because of my mistake. Absolute goat of a person. lectures are somewhat difficult to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very great professor for calc, would tell what's on exam, didn't try to stump and a great guy.

He seems like he knows what he's talking about, but I don't think he should be teaching introductory classes. I wish he would use technology more instead of scribbling on a chalkboard (with not the best handwriting i fear). It feels hard to keep up with him in his lectures. The only reason I've done well in this class is because I took calc in hs.

*This was for MATH 231*
Greg is the most caring professor I've had. He genuinely cares about the success of his students, and will work with you to make sure you succeed! You will probably have to put in effort outside of lectures to be successful, but he doesn't try to stump you. Take Calc with Greg!!!

TOOK MATH 231
Super sweet guy, lectures were pretty confusing, most people lacked understanding when tests came around. confusing test review materials.

Great professor and interesting classes, though sometimes hard to follow. Leaving this review because he changed the syllabus with three weeks left, requiring everyone to take the final—even though it previously stated the lowest exam out of all the midterms and the final exam would be dropped. Disappointing to see such a major change so late.

Great lecturer and a kind, funny person who genuinely cares about his students' success. His exams closely match the practice materials, so putting in the effort to complete them and check answers pays off.
This review is for 528. Just had one class with this guy. Giving 20/10 without hesitation. Best prof I've ever seen in UNC.

This review is actually for Math 528. Greg was wonderful, he genuinely cares about his students and wants everyone to do well. Exams are just like the practice but with different numbers. Our second midterm and 4/5 of the final was take-home. Do the work and you'll be fine. He's super approachable and accommodating! Overall great person and prof.

I've taken two classes with Greg. He is the most caring prof ive had, super accessible outside of class, and easy to talk to (about math or just to chat!). he wants his students to succeed. whatever he says is on the exam, will be on it, nothing more nothing less. his study guides very similar to the exam. very smart, great mentor. hes the best.

Good professor for an easy A but I felt like I was lacking more concrete knowledge of diff eq. Often learned shortcuts instead of how to actually do things which is good for those who don't need diff eq for other courses. Wish I was taught a bit more formally but I appreciate his approach to the course. Nice guy.

Greg Forest is the GOAT! His lectures were very straightforward, and his study guides were essentially the midterms. He would also walk you through the study guide before the test, so his test average was around an A. Also funny and was very approachable. If you need to take a class and he is teaching it, definitely take it with him!

Dr. Fish is one of the most impressive and inspirational professors I've had. She cares deeply about each of her students and all of her assignments and exams are written to cause the least amount of confusion possible. Her exams are very fair and the few assignments we have are also not bad. She brings in cool guests lecturers sometimes too.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Fish is the reason why I decided to do the focus area in healthcare comms! Her lectures were SO interesting and tests were fair. She truly cares about her students learning what they need in class and in post grad. You actually learn content you'll use in life instead of doing meaningless busy work. I couldn't recommend her enough!!

Professor Fish is hands-down one of the best professors I've had at UNC. I took her for Healthcare Communications, and she made the class super engaging and actually taught skills that are super useful for getting a job. She really knows her stuff and genuinely cares about her students.

Prof. Fish is so caring and she really wants you to succeed! I recommend going to her Office Hours.
The tests go beyond her test review and you will be tested on some specific examples in her slide so make sure to go to class and pay attention to the details.

My favorite professor at UNC!!! I wish I knew about her sooner to take more classes with her. If you come to class and pay attention and study, the class will be easy. You can tell she cares about her students and what she teachers

Prof. Fish is a great teacher and has tons of experience in the healthcare sector. Her lectures are interesting and she really cares about her students and wants them to succeed post grad. Her exams  only covered big topics which were on the slides and readings. If you listen in class and study a little for the exams, its an easy A!
Most impactful professor I have had here at UNC! I highly suggest meeting with her outside of class as she is very interested in each of her students and helping them succeed school/career wise.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was actually the best class I've ever taken at UNC. I feel like you learn SO many important things that you can really see how you'd use outside of the classroom. Her exams are very fair and always focus on big picture ideas, barely any homework, the most entertaining lectures I've ever had. Take her if you get the chance she's amazing!!!
I love Professor Fish so much. She is a fantastic lecturer and teacher. She cares about her students, and the class is exciting. I wish I could take this class again.

Flaxman is a straightfoward lecturer and professor and his passion for film is evident. Engl142 is an great class if you do your readings/viewings and follow essay instructions. Everything was graded by TAs. Beware his dog.

His soft, slow voice doesn't engage or excite the room about movies, so skip class and use his online slides. Started with film theory, but this class is really all about basic terminology. He grades papers "harshly" (unclear guidelines), but he also sent us last year's identical exams. Encouraged AI use for an art project :(

He's a funny and nice guy, but I personally didn't mesh with the lectures. I thought a class about movies would be fun but more often then not felt like a chore. A lot of the papers are a pain to write and I felt as if most times I was just jabbering on to met the word count because there wasn't enough content to write about in the scenes/shots.

I just finished his ENGL680 (wasn't an option here) class and still have yet to receive a single grade. We had a midterm, paper abstract, and final paper, and I have no idea what my grade could possibly be because I've gotten close to no feedback. The classes are long and 95% him talking with no slides. He's very knowledgeable, just super difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Flaxman is an extremely knowledgeable professor. The class was lecture heavy but he did ask questions and encouraged class discussions. My biggest qualm with the class was the hap-hazard organization. There were only 2 writing assignments for undergrads but he did not communicate prompts and guidelines well. Still a chill class and Flaxman is nice.

His lectures are amazing, he is an eloquent and engaging speaker; as a film lover I learned so many cool facts from him. The class isn't very demanding and if you are interested in film at all is definitely worth taking! The papers are graded harshly, but you have plenty of time. Professor Flaxman is who I want to be when I grow up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy who really knows his stuff, really interesting lectures that are mostly just watching clips. Expectations are quite reasonable if you spend any time at all studying and thinking about the content on your own. Decent workload, but it's mostly films and readings. The TA sections can be less useful, but in general a very interesting class.

Professor Flaxman is clearly passionate about the subject that he teaches, which helps make his lectures a bit more engaging. Your success in the class is pretty much solely determined by your performance on the essays in the first half of the semester, which can be graded pretty harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Greg is so kind if you get to know him! Go up and talk to him after class and he will give you great feedback and help (yoi will need it, this class is HARD). Don't be fooled by the level 100 this class is a ton of work

(INTRO) to film analysis is not expected by Greg. He requires great effort in understanding the material he gives. You have to live and breathe film in order to succeed in this class. Beware that its not easy unless you know how to BS ur papers and write about nonsense in regard to film elements. You will not just watch and talk about films here.

While lectures were interesting, very few of them stayed on topic and then we were expected to write essays and questions related to the reading or movie that we barely discussed. It was possible to get by with a lot of work outside of class and good reading and writing skills.

While the title "Intro to Film Analysis" alludes to an easy class - it is not. Professor Flaxman grades very toughly, but you will certainly learn from his critiques. He is very knowledgeable about the content and provides very good lecture slides and notes. Attendance to lectures is not mandatory, and you do not have to participate much.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved Flaxman's class! His knowledge of both history and production of cinema is unmatched! Professor Flaxman is passionate about teaching film and his lectures are insightful. Definitely a good beginner film class to take. Grading is collaborative with the REC teachers and they are typically not too harsh, but will leave lots of comments.

Two less than 1500 word essays, take home mid-term, and final essay on three prompts with greater than 700 words each. Lectures were philosophical at times and on many topics surrounding art in different medias. Grading's tough but great feedback and took a while to get back.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took this class as a gen ed and it ended up being way more work that I thought. Papers were graded harshly and they made up most of the final grade. Despite listing a clear grading on the syllabus, the final grade you get in the class is changed based on a curve that can bring final grades down.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is a lot more effort than just watching movies, but I really learned a lot. Though the content was interesting and the accompanying assignments helped me learn, Professor Flaxman is extremely lecture-heavy and didn't speak very loudly, so you have to really pay attention. However, you could tell he cared alot about what he was teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really knowledgeable prof, but I did think that he graded a bit harshly on the few assignments we did have. Takes a while for grades/feedback to come back but it is helpful for other writing intensive classes. I wish he gave more guidelines for what he wanted to see but if you talk to him during office hours he can give you a lot of insight!
Flaxman is a horrible lecturer but the exams are easy, the study guides are very helpful. I never went to the class and am looking at an A. If you're a good writer you'll get an A.
An incredible professor. His lectures are always engaging. Seriously recommend.

What Flaxman seems to value most of all is sincere engagement with the material in the class and with the projects/papers. If you're a bad writer or even a good writer and you want to get better, he's one of the best. Take advantage of how much he knows and ask as many questions as you can

Flaxman knows his stuff, but isn't great at teaching it. Discussions fall flat since he fishes for the answer he's looking for until he hears it, discouraging people from participating. Lectures are often unrelated to the films for the week, it seems like he just talks about whatever he wants to and his analysis of films is often head-scratching.

Class was very enjoyable. Used ton of examples of films in lecture to help better get concepts across. Only reason why it's tough grading is because of TA's who aren't very consistent. Experience in the class is more based on who your TA is vs Flaxman. Not very accessible out of class. Very knowledgable on the material.

I enjoyed this class right up until I received (or didn't) my final grade. Grading in this class is done entirely by the TAs and is extremely ambiguous for no reason. I never got back the grades for my final/final project. + Don't take this class if you aren't interested in the technical aspects of filmmaking; that's literally what the class is.

I took this English 142 class with the intent of finding an interesting, but not too difficult class. What came from this class was nothing of substance and just a general waste of time. Greg assigns too many movies and grades papers not for grammatical accuracy, but rather based on faithfulness to the in-class formal elements. Stay away from this.

Definition of dgaf. Could be pretty rude, but laidback and easy. 3 papers total with midterm and final. Papers were more work than I was anticipating, but exams were not hard. Most of the films were incredibly boring, though

Dr. Flaxman is very knowledgable in his field and the class is lecture heavy. I recommend this only if you find film interesting to read and write about. Not necessarily an easy A, but if you put in the work and have a decent TA, you will do fine.

This class was a lot of work, but easy to get a good grade if you put in the work. Very dependent on your TA because they grade everything and basically teach you everything. Lectures weren't necessary to attend, just read the online lectures and go to recitation. Important to watch the movies but the readings don't matter as much.

Professor Flaxman was okay. I was zoned out during his lectures most of the time, but the material is not difficult to understand. Your TAs do everything from reviewing the info to you, to explaining projects/papers, and grading. Your grade ultimately depends on your TA. I've never taken a film class and I got an A+

This class is lecture heavy! There are so many videos and lots of wordy power-points. I had to email my prof several times just to get a response and even then my questions werent answered. Hopefully you get a good TA. Mine did not follow the syllabus grading outline so I was unfairly graded several times and the prof didnt address the issues.

If you want to improve your writing, take Greg's classes. His feedback is harsh, but that's how he makes you improve so much. It's completely worth it. Greg is an absolute genius. His world knowledge is astounding, and he connects different themes and historical events throughout his lectures in an amazing way.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: greg was a fine professor - kind of lost me often in class but the grade is truly dependent on your TA. lots of papers and all very subjectively graded. not an easy A by any standard because he doesn't determine the grading scale until he sees the final grades and makes it so the average grade automatically gets a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Do you like watching French films from the 1950s? Do like to learn abstract concepts that the professor has difficulty communicating? Do want to rewatch boring old movies 3 times? If you answered no to any of these, don't take him. The class sounds easy, but he sucks as a teacher. It is even worse if you have bad TAs. Avoid him and the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Greg really knows what he is talking about. There are weekly screenings (two/week) and readings, but if you show up to class, you can just skim the readings. The midterm and the final are fair and he tries to work with you to make sure it's not difficult. The rest is quizzes which are two question movie/concept checks and 5 papers (2-5 pages).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a very funny person and a great lecturer. He seems to care about his students. However, he gives very, very harsh paper feedback, to the point where his feedback on one of my papers made me cry. I don't think I've become much of a better writer, either. Sometimes he can be unclear about what he wants and is slightly disorganized. Good overall.

I took this class for a VP credit and was blown away about how little I knew. Greg knows his stuff and is great, but take this class if you are really into art/ film culture. I am not and found myself trying to comprehend things I felt my peers found really easy. If you want a super easy VP class this is not for you

I have taken two classes with this professor and I will happily take more. He is a tough grader when it comes to papers, but that is really because he wants to make sure that you are writing to the best of your ability. So, if he feels you're selling yourself short, he'll call you out on it. Mostly, he just cares about honest effort.

DISCLAIMER: This class is not an excuse to watch a bunch of movies! Professor Flaxman knows a lot about the history of the cinema, and during his lectures he shows a lot of examples taken from films- monotonous . You watch 2 films/week. 2/month you have a 2 question quiz (your TA makes them). 4 papers based off analyzing a scene- graded tough.
Had him ten years ago or so for an advanced literary theory class focusing on semiotics. By far the smartest person in the English/Comp Lit Department and one of the best professors I've ever had.

Greg is probably the smartest professor I have ever had here at UNC. He is so knowledgeable about a vast array of topics, I sometimes forget to participate in class because I am listening to his stories. The films he selected for viewing were all relevant and entertaining. Overall, this was a highly enjoyable class that I recommend to anyone

He's funny and engaging, for the most part. The lectures can be very boring when going over technical stuff like lens types and the history of film, but otherwise interesting. Don't let the three hour class intimidate you, you'll watch a movie in almost every single one. For the final exam: make sure you understand Auteur theory!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Flaxman is generally a good professor, but he's also part of the problematic elitist mentality in academia.  The way he demeans opinions that run contrary to his own makes this pretty clear, though he'll try, mostly successfully (depending on your level of perception) to bury his elitist snobbery underneath a pile of "i don't care what you think".

This is a great class. It's tough and it's time consuming, but I loved it. Flaxman is kind of a hardass, but in the best possible way. He's really entertaining, unapologetically himself, and he takes the class really seriously without being obnoxious. Smart guy, fantastic professor, fascinating class. Highly recommended.
I loved Professor Flaxman and Film Analysis. He puts on a hard front but he's a pretty great guy that knows his stuff. The TA's are another story. I loathed my recitation.

Great professor.  Super knowledgeable and very enthusiastic about the subject.  Started off the semester with this whole "I'm an arrogant jerk" shtick, but he mostly dropped that after a few weeks.  Rather a lot of work and classroom time for just a 100 level course, but a great class if you're seriously into film.
Really interesting lectures, overall a great professor. No idea what the curve is gonna be but there is a lot of points to gain (four papers, quizzes, discussion and exams). The ta's are boring.
Very smart, explains things well,  cute, overall a great prof
Very cool guy and definitely loves his subject. Work is graded hard at first. Tests are crazy long...
No Comments
Great class, great lectures, very knowledgable and amiable.
I've got no real complaints, some of the material was dull (especially for a film class) but he knows his stuff.  The "I'm an ****" pretense got a little old, though.
Super nice and funny guy. 3/10 lecturer. Makes content more confusing that it needs to be. Exams are extremely difficult and poorly written. Tests on content that he covered for

Dr. Matera is a great professor! Definitely one of the best research professors to take in the bio department. His exams are fair and he's really engaged with the lectures. The more you engage with his lectures the more you will learn. Not a lot of study resources like other sections but not bad for anyone experienced in bio classes at UNC.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Basically your entire grade is comprised of exams. You can study for weeks for the exams and it is absolutely pointless because nothing covered in class is going to be on the exam. He writes the exams very very poorly and they cover topics you will have never heard of.

Do not take BIOL220 with Dr. Matera if you want to ensure a high grade in this course. The exams are written extremely poorly and it genuinely does not matter how much you study as you will be tested on things that were not covered whatsoever. I promise that it would be easier to obtain an A in Organic Chemistry.

Professor Matera is an expert on molecular biology, and he is great at explaining the details. The class focuses solely on analyzing research papers, but background is provided and Dr. Matera is happy to help. Tests focus on interpreting scientific figures and applying mechanisms. Video project was a nice break and spaced out well.

Professor Matera structures his class around research papers relevant to advancements and discovery in molecular biology. While this may be overwhelming at first, he does a wonderful job explaining the papers and the science. He has a clear passion for the topic which made lectures extremely engaging and learning easy.

Professor Matera is super knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches. He knows a LOT about molecular biology and it can be kind of intimidating. However, he really cares about his students and whether or not they are learning the material. There was a lot of reading primary scientific articles, but he clears things up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Matera can come off as intimidating but only because clearly cares about his students and pushes them to engage with the material at a high level. He is extremely knowledgeable about his field and always eager to discuss material in more depth. I learned the most in this course than possibly any other biology course I have taken at UNC.

Professor Matera is clearly very passionate and knowledgeable about genetics. He may seem a bit intense at first but it helps you actually engage with the material and participate in class. He's quite funny as well. Material requires effort but you will learn a lot. Give it your best shot, he answers questions and is willing to help.

Dr. Matera really cares about his students. He cares that you know the material and will take the time to really answer your questions. He gives partial credit on exams. Exams are heavy on assigned scientific papers and methods, which you cover in depth in class. A lot is based on application of the material, not just regurgitation from the papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His "create your own experiment" questions are slightly ambiguous but I think it depends on how the TA grades them,and if everybody does poorly, the class is curved at the end of the semester. He's not very clear and gives you way too much unnecessary information about his lab. Also, a NIGHTMARE to get in contact with for emergency situations.

The material isn't difficult. The grading, however, is very annoying. Test questions will ask something like "List 2 ways that...." Although there may be a dozen different technically correct things you can list, only 3 of them will be in his answer key. Also, the two specific things you list might only be counted as one very broad thing.

This is the first science class I've really struggled in during my college years...Though I didn't feel that the material was extremely difficult, the tests were challenging due to the fact that some of the questions were unclear in what they were asking and it was hard to determine what info was really important.
He obviously knows the material, but he fails to convey that knowledge to the class in any kind of useful way. His lectures lack clarity, comprehensiveness, and organization.

Straightforward class, one big group project that allowed us to apply what we learned, and we got to pick our groups or join a random one. 100 point quiz, 150 point project, 200 point final, 25 for research (filling out surveys), and 25 for attendance. These numbers get put together with the advertising section as well for the total grade.
Just an OK professor.
Professor Fields was kind and funny. Slideshow presentations were a bit difficult to read. We had a group project with plenty of time in class to get it done.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Easy Mejo class with a quiz, exam, and one final PR portfolio project with same groups as AD section. Lectures were required and not that engaging, mainly based off posted slides. Quiz and final were similar and on Quizlet. Final project had clear rubric and she posted an example outline to follow. Didn't read the textbook at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've had VK 3 times over the course of my time at Carolina and has been the most rewarding professor i've had. Her 137 course is completely different from her other two in where she grades in a tougher manner and expects a lot more from you, but it is 100% worth it. Provides strong portfolio materials and takes you out of your comfort zone.

Valerie knows what she is talking about, but the lectures are not that interesting. The creative assignment is done with the same groups are the advertising section, so just keep that in mind. Study for the quiz and final on quizlet. Reading the textbook isn't necessary.
Shes okay but the quiz and test was lowkey hard

VK is definitely an expert in her field! Her lectures are a bit dry but I also don't have much interest in PR so it might be that. The exam & quiz were easy, just straight from her notes. There's a pretty heavy group project, but as long as you're with a good group, it should be a breeze (also get to choose your own group).

V.K. is well respected in her field and very knowledgeable. The lectures could be boring at times, but taking detailed notes wasn't necessary. The best way to study for the midterm and final is Quizlet. Lots of people have made practice tests already.

She is a great person and the class is very easy. The lectures were very bland, powerpoint oriented, and just a big change of pace from Gary. I tried to take notes but could not keep up with how much unnecessary stuff was incorporated in the slides.
Easy class!

VK seems like a nice person, but her lectures are quite boring, and I didn't feel like I learned a lot during her section of the class. Take her class if you want an easy A, but don't expect to gain deep knowledge about PR.
Valerie kept class fun and interesting, and I enjoyed her lectures. I didn't love the criteria of the final project but it wasn't difficult.

Valerie is an angel! She is so kind and so smart. Her lectures are really interesting and she is just an overall awesome person. Very little work and tests. I hope to take more classes with her in the future. One of my favorite professors at UNC.

VK is very knowledgeable! The quiz & final exam were pretty easy it takes 15 min max. Tries to keep the lectures engaging with the room with case studies & PR activities. don't buy the textbook. The content you need is on the slides so pay attention to those. Group project where you work on a campaign but pretty easy, just follow the rubric!

Prof. VK was a wonderful professor. You can tell she knows exactly what she's talking about and that she knows a lot about her field. There was a quiz and a 'PR final' which were similar, easy, and from the lectures. Group project was not hard either. You have to pay attention to slides because there is a lot of content on them.

No papers or anything. 1 project you have over a month to complete, & it took us 1 day for a 93%. Seems knowledgeable in PR but incredibly boring compared to Gary. I stopped going after the 2nd week of her lectures & still got an A because the final was common sense & posted on quizlet (I looked ahead of time). Plan for 137 to be your easy class.

VK is nice and the class is easy but her lectures were very boring compared to Gary's. However, she read through my group's entire final project and fixed any errors before final submission which was the nicest thing ever.
Very easy class but SO boring. She's very low-energy and reads right off the slides. Going from Gary to VK in 137 was a huge difference.
VK is very respected in her field, and you will learn a lot from her. A lot of her lectures are backed up by her career experiences. one big project and 2 exams.

Professor VK was a very nice lady, her lectures are a little boring but you are squeezing a ton of information into a small period. +she had some classes where she let us experience real pr moments so that helped a ton!

a nice person but class was painfully boring. Most of class consisted of her reading out of the textbook and then going over some slides that she posts to canvas. Had a quiz and final exam for her portion of the class that were both easy if you used notes, and she didn't take attendance to see who was in class ever so you don't have to go.

VK knows her stuff, and you'll leave this class having learned a LOT. Expect timed writing assignments nearly every week. These can have a very steep learning curve, so don't worry if the first few don't go the way you want them to! Do the rewrites, and you'll be okay. Also, depending on your client, the APPLES project could be a burden.

VK is great and sets you up to be a PR pro; it won't be easy but it also won't be the hardest thing ever. She makes you better and gave us materials I've used in my job and gotten great feedback from. She sticks to the strict Hussman writing rubric as that is her job. Her teachings were the highlight while the client work was the irritating part.
I learned so much in her class but the first part of the semester was difficult! She holds her student to a professional standard. I would highly recommend this class.

Professor Fields was my favorite professor I have had at UNC. She prepares you for real world public relations. The course load can be a lot at times, but she is always ready to listen for feedback if things get too hard. She is very understanding and cares about student success.

I took two courses from VK and I learned more in those two courses than any other class in the J school. VK will prepare you well for the real world, but she does not mess around.
