In summary, to A in her classes you'll have to be really hard working and organized-- but if you aren't before, you definitely will be after.

VK is the toughest yet most helpful and inspirational professor I have ever met! The course was never easy, but she helped everyone all along the way with actual practices and her real-life experiences. Might not practice in Crisis Comm in the future, but the skills we learned from the class are adaptable to all other fields in Communications.

This is my second class with VK. I love VK as a person; she is also a great lecturer, as well as very knowledgeable about PR. Her classes definitely push you, but they make you so much better as a PR writer and crisis communicator.

Professor Fields is incredibly unforgiving and will take off 50 points for the smallest error on assignments. She does not try to get to know her students and does not care about them. She didn't even respond to me when I told her I had a psychiatric emergency and needed to miss class for a day.

Loved VK's crisis communication class. It really pushes you to work on your public speaking. Expect to be challenged, but also expect to be grateful for it. Mostly participation-based, group work as well. We don't really discuss the textbook in class, but it matters for the midterm and final - so make sure you read it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: VK is one of my favorite professors at the Hussman School and made PR writing very fun and interesting. She is very harsh on typos, understandably, but otherwise, if you spell everything right and have it formatted the way she tells you, there is no reason you should get less than a 95. However, she made a 96 the cutoff for an A, so that was beat.

I really liked VK's class - she's a tough grader and makes you work for it, but an overall great experience! If you're interested in PR writing definitely take it with her, she covers all the important PR documents like news releases, media advisories, etc., and gives great feedback. It's also a good portfolio-building class.

V.K.'s Crisis Comm class is no joke! Our end of semester project was to take on crises faced by companies like Facebook and host a press conference with real journalists and reporters. V.K. is also a PR writing professor so all written assignments are graded hard. She's very experienced in the field but sometimes lacks empathy and character.

This class is a wild ride! Prof. Fields is amazing and a true inspiration. Class is a lecture, or you have to do a timed writing assignment. SO much is covered in this class! At first, I was failing things but then my grade got better. Midterm and final were not bad, and you work with a non-profit client all semester. Solid class, but no joke!

Really enjoyed this class. VK is very entertaining and its a lot of work but I learned a lot. I didn't think the workload was too bad but probably depends on your group for the project. VK is strict and no-nonsense but you will leave the class feeling confident when applying for jobs and internships . Exams are not hard if you take good notes.

Professor VK is one of the top three professors Ive had in my seven semesters at UNC. This class is very difficult and will stress you out but I learned more from it than any other class I have taken. I feel prepared to enter the field of PR after taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Although her class is very challenging, VK is amazing and wants her students to succeed. The class is stressful and pushes you, but I learned more about writing and PR from this class than any other class I have taken. Be ready to work though.

VK is an absolute goddess and an inspiration. She's easily my favorite professor I've ever had. Granted, crisis comm is scary. Its a lot of public speaking, but its so rewarding. But the homework is nonexistent, so getting in front of the class and doing it is the hardest part and your class always has your back. Trial by fire but totally worth it.

Prof VK was extremely strict and no-nonsense, but I learned a lot of really useful information. She has a lot of experience in the real world and lots of fun stories to share. Definitely a class you have to work hard for - pretty much every class session involved a deadline-written piece that was graded very harshly. Expect to be stressed out.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Gemayel's asynchronous course was one of the best I've taken. She was organized and clearly cared about student success. The course was easy to follow, the workload was fair, and the materials were helpful. I'd highly recommend her. She made an online class feel engaging and supportive throughout and gave thoughtful feedback throughout!

Professor Gemayel was a wonderful teacher, i really enjoyed taking her class and learned a lot from her. The grading was extremely fair. If you study and work hard, you'll get a good grade. I went to office hours for additional support with some of the assignments, and she was very nice and encouraging.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Do not take this professor for an easy A gen ed. She is a very tough and harsh grader for a 100 level GEOG course. She takes off lots of unnecessary points on discussion boards and is hypercritical if she doesn't like what you wrote. Presented an extra credit opportunity, but wouldn't give it to me when asked for it over office hours and email.
So Free. Literally Take notes and do ur work for a guaranteed A. ZERO flexibility on missing assignments or turning in late tho, so if you do that even once you might be cooked.

She is one of the best professors I have had at UNC. Her lectures are very information heavy but it you pay attention and take notes then everything is easy for her exams. She knows how to keep people engaged and is very funny. Def recommend her for everyone!!!

Dr. Guzzo is such an amazing woman and professor. Genuinely hilarious, cares about the subject, and tests are very straightforward and easy if you go to class. If you need to take Soci 101, take it with her for sure. Hardest part of the class is remembering to do the reading responses.

Allow me the honor of telling you how AMAZING Professor Guzzo was. Funny, intriguing, and passionate, Professor Guzzo was always available and open during class. Her slideshows were easy to follow and informative, the readings were chill, and the hardest parts were the reading response papers, which you could easily forget about.

Scott Geier, oh Scott Geier. I love this class and given the opportunity I would take it over again. His assignments are fun and interesting and he genuinely cares for his students outside of class. I've gone to his office hours to just discuss career options and random things. He very rarely gives 100s though, but he is open to working with you.

Scott is very smart in regards to MEJO, has passion,and cares about student success beyond class.121 is not a difficult course within itself, if you were to take him I would just be wary of his grading. I essentially only got an A because I went to office hours for every assignments. His grading is harsh, but atleast he's open to working with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: TAKE SCOTT. As a student who hates coding and digital media creation more than anything, this was my favorite class of the semester. He goes a little fast, but the skills I developed with AI in this class that he taught us are incomparable, and he's super amazing in office hours! TAKE HIM TAKE HIM
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Scott is hands down one of the best professors I've ever had at UNC! His lectures are engaging and his personality was bomb. As someone with zero prior coding experience, he made coding non-intimidating and genuinely something I now love doing. 100% would recommend to any design or interface-interested student.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TAKE HIS CLASS! He is a 100/10. Such an interesting course, and I learned so much. Really accessible outside of class, clear grading criteria, and minimal homework outside your actual project. His lectures are funny and engaging. Takes time to get to know you and actually helped me figure out a career path I'm very interested in! Love Uncle Scott!

Amazing person, amazing professor. I left the course feeling like an entirely different individual from how much I learned. He isn't an easy A, and I had to work really hard all semester, but he pushed me to become better and I'm so glad I took 121 with him. He is so knowledgeable on everything and really cares about his students. My favorite prof!

If you're not a mejo major don't take this class. Scott is really cool and nice but doesn't have clear grading criteria. A lot of course is based on creativity which is great for some and not others. He deeply cares a lot about the material and wants students to succeed, but this is by no means an easy course.

Scott is the most caring professor I have ever had. From day one, you can tell he loves teaching. He made coding fun, which is rare, and he gives great feedback on assignments. Best of all, he is always available for office hours if you get stuck on a line of code.

Uncle Scott is a wonderful professor. I would even go as far to say my favorite professor at the Hussman School. I credit him with the reason why I want to do Ui/Ux development as a future career. He was so willing to teach us the basics and class lessons were very helpful. I strongly encourage you to take a class with him.

Probably the coolest professor I've had at UNC. If you have the chance to take Uncle Scott please do so. I didn't know much about coding and UI design but learned a lot from this course. Some websites were difficult to create but schedule office hours and you'll be just fine. It's a 1:45-minute class but it just feels like a friend teaching you.

Scott is so funny; he makes a lot of funny dad jokes. The class is not hard, but you need to be creative and put in effort, he has his own standards when it comes to how things are being graded. Scott always pushes his students to produce excellent work rather than just completing the assignments. Good preparation class for MEJO students.

This is a really great class. Coding was definitely the toughest part, but Professor Geier was super helpful and takes you through it step-by-step in class. No one in my class had coded before but we got through it lol. You'll learn a ton about user experience and interactivity. You definitely need to attend class to learn and do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed the class with Scott. Was not excited to take MEJO 121 but Scott makes it really enjoyable and works individual with students with as many questions as they have. I didn't find that he was a harsh grader and was pretty fair. I am by no means an expert in anything Digital Storytelling related but I never received lower than a B.

Dr.Geier made MEJO 121 very enjoyable. Since there are so many new applications and programs introduced, it would be easy to get lost in this class. However, Dr.Geier walks through assignments slowly and posted grading criteria online. He gives very helpful feedback and homework is assigned well in advance so it never felt like things were rushed.

Scott Geier is a straight up awesome guy. He gives great feedback, and honestly inspired me to take video more seriously. He's very laid back, and he also very clearly knows what he's talking about. If you have to take 121, definitely take it with him. If you've never made a video or a website before, he will make sure you can succeed.

Professor Geier is a pretty tough grader. You have to read his mind to receive an A. He is interesting and a good lecturer. Although, he expects a lot for an entry level class. He wouldn't round my final grade of an 89.6 to a 90.

Has high expectations but I couldn't say enough good things about this professor! If you put in the work you will get the grade deserved.  Truly CARES and wants what is best for his students.  I wouldn't say i'm tech savvy but this class made me so much more confident and comfortable in my abilities.  This dude rocks.

Scott was a great Prof. He gives good feedback, is available for questions out of class, & creates a good classroom energy. He has clear notes and guidelines to refer to & clearly knows what he's talking about. Definitely would recommend for 121.
Scott made the class interesting and easy to follow. He was super accommodating for us and provided decent feedback. Genuinely enjoyed going to class. Definitely one of the better MEJO 121 profs.

Scott is great! He's chill, a pretty lenient grader, and always willing to help on assignments. I got the impression that he had a bit of a difficult semester, but he didn't let that affect his teaching. The class is mostly projects, but as long as you stay on top of it, you'll be fine. Definitely a great professor all around!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: great prof

Scott is an awesome professor and made an almost 2-hour class enjoyable. Coming into this class I had zero coding or web design experience but he always made sure everyone understood and went out of his way to help you. It is a hard class so don't take it if you're not willing to put in extra work to really learn the material!

Scott is great. Coding is difficult, but he truly walks through everything. Engagement is key in this class and it's really up to the student to pay attention and ask questions. He's easily accessible outside of class and has a very charismatic personality. Great dude.

Very tough grader. I feel like he's one of those professors where you kind of have to read their mind to get an A. He's a good lecturer and he's knows a lot, he just expects too much out of intro level students in my opinion.

Scott was an extremely harsh grader and expected students in an intro class to produce professional quality work while giving virtually no instruction or guidelines. Would not recommend his class if you are easily offended or can't handle his sometimes questionable remarks and uncomfortable comments.
Honestly one of the worst professors Ive had at UNC. Expected students in an intro course to turn out professional quality work almost immediately. Barely taught us. Made me hate this topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Scott is great! He makes the class really interesting and funny, but the class is a lot of work. You should be prepared to spend lots of hours coding
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Scott is an amazing professor, one of the best I've had so far at my time at UNC. He really cares about the success of his students and is willing to put extra time and effort to helping his students understand the material of the course and to improve upon themselves. Loved the course and had a lot of fun with the assignments. Highly recommend!

Scott has been one of my favorite professors at UNC. He is a great instructor, provides clear expectations of the course, and is willing to go above and beyond when helping students. His lectures are clear and he posts them online, so it's easy to follow up if you miss. The class is project based with a few quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Hope he doesn't teach this class in the future. Poor students.

Not the greatest teacher. Not accomodating at all. Just finished midterm 2 that had no correlation to what we learned in class. Designs questions to trick you before you even understand what concept it is testing. Would not take for this course.

Greg isn't bad but his lectures are disorganized i.e he doesn't provide notes but its bc he teaches from the textbook so j look at that. The key to being successful in this class is going to office hours. His lectures are theoretical so it is really helpful to go to office hours to get help applying concepts from lecture. Hard, but def manageable!

On the midterm I used the correct formula to get the correct answer, wrote everything out step by step and still got 11/14 points on two questions because I didnt write a sentence in english explaining it at the end. I simply didn't have time to focus on this, but he requires it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are very confusing and hard to follow but the homeworks and exams are manageable

while the homework is manageable most of the time, it doesn't really feel like the lecture material applies to it. his lectures are a bit unorganized because he often jumps in without telling us what section of the text he's working from. no example numbers from text. he does all of his notes in chalk, so write fast and never be absent.

His lectures don't really make sense as he tends to go on tangents about random things. When asked what he refers to in the textbook, he says to pay attention in class. This class is already hard as it is and other than offering office hours which don't really help imo, he doesn't do anything outside of that. Would not take :(

Even if math isn't your strength, a good grade is achievable. Greg genuinely cares and gives generous curves to balance harsh grading. Lectures can be hard to follow, but he is very accessible outside of class. Be wary of bad reviews as most people just skipped. I definitely recommend him, especially if you have prior knowledge.

Greg is a super nice professor but for an intro course the class is difficult, especially if you are not good at math. He gives past exams for you to study but he make mistakes on the answer key which makes it hard if you are already confused. Tests are a big portion of grade and are graded very strictly, he does give extra credit and curves exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Didn't show up to class once and got an A. If you know your derivative rules it is a super straight forward class, so having no required attendance was very nice.

The lecture was useless and very hard to follow. The exams and midterms are graded much more strictly than the answer key. Not to mention he even makes mistakes on the answer key. There are no helpful files or a summary for exam reviews. Textbooks are super expensive.

If you're bad at math and you have a busy course schedule dont take this class. Lectures are useless and hard to follow. Grading is very specific. He posts study guides for the exams but the tests are so much harder than what he gives us. Textbook is over $100. Final exam is 35% of your grade. Tests average in the 40's he gives a curve though.

His lectures are hard to follow & he doesn't interact well with students in class. He makes mistakes in his own work that students have to correct & is very inconsistent in grading tests. This does cause massive curves on the tests which is a redeeming factor. Attendance isn't mandatory and often it is easier to learn concepts outside of class.

Class materials/concepts were not too complex until multivariable calculus. Sometimes talks/goes through problems very fast and asks for any questions but doesn't look for any raised hands. I recommend going to his office hours as he is very approachable and wants you to succeed in his class. Very easy to get an a if you go to the lectures.

I thought Greg was going to be easier due to these comments however he does not explain anything at all. The class content isn't that difficult but he can't teach, I'd recommend using a different teacher if possible.

Greg was the helpful math teacher I've had. He cared a lot about math & his students. He explained concepts well enough and provided resources. I've never been a math person but found this class to be pretty easy & straightforward. Very decent curves on all the exams & final grades. He even drops your lowest exam score completely. 10/10 recommend.

Im just gonna start with saying im not a math guy. Ironic because i am an econ major, but regardless, i thought greg was great. He gives you the previous semester midterms as study material, and it was very similar to the test he gave me in the class. I worked really hard in this class, but it was nothing unattainable. I would recommend him 100%

Professor Grigory is nice guy, however the class is very test heavy. You have 3 midterms (one is dropped) and a final that comprise your grade. Lectures are sometimes hard to follow and I wouldn't recommend taking the class without some sort of calculus experience. Extra credit was offered at the end and he curved every test (including the final).
Test heavy course and crazy exams. Practice exam will have apples and oranges while exam will have you calculating the percentage chance of nuclear fission in south african soil. Chill guy however.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor who cares about his students. Grades consisted of a weekly HW assignment, 3 midterms (2 which were curved) and a final. He even curves final grades but not by much. This class builds off calculus concepts and there are lots of word problems involved. Don't love the subject but Prof. Terlov is awesome.

Very solid lectures, tests were pretty easy other than a few questions. Very helpful, thorough explanations. Overall pretty easy class, if you are at all mathematically inclined this is a very slight class. Test heavy grading scale.

Professor Terlov is very understanding and truly loves the subject he teaches. Exams were a little tough, but all except for one was curved. Definitely need to put some time into the material outside of the class to make sure you understand, but overall he provided us with many resources that made it easier to succeed on exams.

Great class and professor wants his students to succeed! Lots of review if you've already taken calculus in the past. If you attend class and utilize the resources (office hours, tutoring) it's very easy to attain a good grade. Highly recommend!

You spend most of the class looking at the back of his head as he is writing on the chalkboard the whole time, but it is a small enough class where you can interrupt to ask questions. He is very understanding and clearly loves math. Exams are tough though. So make sure to take time and study.

Prof. Terlov is kind and patient and it is clear that he wants students to succeed in his class. My section was held at 8am MWF and I attended maybe 10 classes total. The material is just basic calculus and the whole course builds from the basics up. All the resources are there if you need them (TA tutoring, office hours, etc).

Got a 100 for everything, she is super sweet and understanding, put in a little bit of effort and you will be fine, you dont have to talk if you dont want to, very easy class, if you miss class you are literally more than okay, pls be nice to her, gives a lot of no classes bc of holidays so thats a W
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Grayson is one of the nicest professors you can have! She was very knowledgeable about a wide variety of subjects in the time frame (Middle Ages). The mapping project in the middle of the class was a little all over the place, but as long as you tried you got a good grade. She always made herself available for help outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Grayson has been an amazing professor. She grades extremely easy and does not assign much reading for a history class. She makes you write a couple sentences about a reading before class, but it can be about anything and the readings aren't long. Exam questions given ahead of time. Lectures were reading off the slides, so sometimes boring

Dr Grayson is hands-down the easiest processor I've had at UNC. No textbook, just very light (a page or two) readings after every class. Aside from the midterm and final (study guide shows exactly what will be on the exam), there are 2 5-pg papers and she gives outlines of exactly what she wants. Incredibly, incredibly easy. Take for an easy A!

Prof Prairie has been absolutely review-bombed. She is a very good professor - the subject material is hard. There is a ton of content that this class covers, and she does her absolute best to make it engaging. Homework is long but manageable, just start early. Exams have good practice material and are reasonable.

A course difficult to teach and a confused professor together make a disastrous course. Java and programming design pattern can easily been taught and tested as memorization heavy things, you remember all contents you get A, which is not the case of computer science course, not to say she provides cheatsheets but not allowed to use for exams.
The practice she gave us (from last semester) made me feel like she's somewhat. I'd like to second the reviews on her from last semester......

Because this is a foundational CS course, the material is challenging but incredibly important. Professor Prairie has thoughtfully structured the course to help students grasp and use these concepts effectively. The workload is heavy, but the learning payoff makes it well worth it. I genuinely loved this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Genuinely the worst professor I have had at UNC. Tried her best to mess up literaly everyone's grade and made the class a lot harder than it should've been considering the material wasn't too hard.

The first midterm was harder than it needed to be given that she tested us on a topic we had not been taught formally and then proceeded to give a lecture on the topic post-exam. Additionally, we had NO additional study materials and thus the first exam average was a D. That seemed to open her eyes and she gave us a lot more review materials after.
When you interact with her, especially if you're a member of any marginalized community, keep in mind her voting history. She's a republican.

She's the goat. Yeah, the class is harder than before, but it's not impossible. The assignments were long but were helpful, and the lectures were interesting, and she put her own spin on things to make it more engaging. I probably learned more from this one CS class than I have in the past two semesters.

Prairie is easily one of the best professors I've had at UNC and within the comp sci department. She cares a lot about her students, and her lectures were easily my favorite part of the class and always really interesting. Like others have said though here her exams are long but fair, and assignments were pretty difficult at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's a professor who is genuinely good at teaching. Her exams are fair despite what others might claim. She provides great resources to help you prepare for exams. As long as you understand the design patterns conceptually and remember how to set up your code, you'll be successful in her class. However, some assignments can be time consuming.

She's very passionate! Her lectures can be boring, but that's just the inherent manner of the material. Her tests are harder than class material, but there are bonus points and she gives lots of resources to prepare. But, her assignment schedule is frustrating since we were assigned the most difficult assignments over fall and thanksgiving break.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DONT LISTEN TO THE GOODWIN HATERS HERE. She's one of best professors I've had a UNC. Her lectures are amazing and she even approved final grade to replace midterm 2 grade. Yes, the test are hard but they are definitely doable if you put the time in. The projects were definitely crammable in a day other than the final project and few of other ones.

What bothers me about the class in fall 2025 was that it was inexplicably way harder than previous versions of the same class for no apparent reason. She's really nice, and I get the sense that she's passionate, but the exams are much more difficult than previous semesters, homework takes forever, and overall the class is just harshly graded.

Professor Prairie is a very understanding professor who lectures well. I will say, however, that her exams are difficult, especially if you do not have much prior experience coding in Java. There are lots of opportunities to get bonus points and she does round the class average to an 80. Some of the assignments are a lot of work, but worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: genuinely hell experience. awaiting final grade and likely to finish anywhere from B to A- but just an absolutely horrible class that was 100x harder than previous iterations of it for no apparent reasons.

I heard the class was easy, but I struggled in this class. Could be that I was a poor coder coming into the class, but I personally felt the tests were somewhat fair, maybe a tiny bit too in-depth. Be careful about using AI in this class, she is very picky about it and will honor code you. I think I finished w/ a B/B+ but awaiting final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was extremely difficult based on the given content. Exams didn't match the difficulty of practices given and had limited study resources. While the midterms seemed to improve after the first, where she blindsided everyone, they still were not good. Anyone saying they got an A did not take it this semester b/c grades are not finalized yet

Prof. Goodwin is a good lecturer who really understands the content. lectures are important for doing good and she goes in depth about each concept, but sometimes too much. The exams are fair for the content but were harder than the practices given. Assignments were interesting but took 1+ hours and extra credit was only awarded if you got a 100.

As of December 10th, none of us have received our final exam grades. I'm not sure how some people here claim they already “got an A,” and there's been no announcement about "many people" getting over 100s. If you're one of her TAs, please stop posing as students in the comments.

Prairie is a hopeful professor in the sea of careless ones. Unfortunately, she has not mastered the correct mediums for her vision of the course. This course falls flat on that promise because it COVERS TOO MUCH DEPTH AND BREADTH. Her enthusiasm is refreshing and fun, but it has inflated her expectations for this class beyond comprehension.

Initially felt she was rude, but after going to see her in OH, she became MUCH more helpful, remembered my name, personally spent hours helping me on assignments, and was gracious with regrade requests. Only got an A on one midterm and still ended with an A. Double check for grading errors and do all the extra credit possible.

My opinion of her initially was poor since the MT1 had a bunch of topics we barely covered. HOWEVER, she improved in outlining what would be covered on MT2 along with adding tons of resources for the final. Overall, 301 was tough and time consuming, but very fair if you studied for the easier final (though the project should've been weighted more).

Hard class no doubt, but don't trust the anti-Prairie mob on here. If the class was so impossible there wouldn't be so many people getting over 100s on tests. Assignments are very time consuming but are good practice for the exams, you will want to be very comfortable with the content before you take the midterms/final.

Very caring professor, but the class itself was extremely difficult. It feels that you spin the lottery every semester, as looking at some in the past exams before us some had it easier while others just as hard. Lots of homework, super difficult tests. HW extra credit is capped at 100, and the grading weights change every semester.

Literally the worst professor i've ever had. The campus closed for weather but she refused to reschedule the in-person final at 8 am and made everyone walk in 20 degree weather since transportation is down. She makes the assignments with poor planning, challenging for no reason, and struggles to help the students and says “you should know this.”

I think Prairie cares about students, but her tests are VERY difficult. Exams are 70% of the grade, so it becomes hard to do well, especially for bad test takers. Sounds like she significantly changes the grading scale every semester. Even though I understand and do all assignments, this class has been my hardest, and I'm worried about passing.

I was initially worried about this class, but ended up being pleasantly surprised. Homeworks are assigned every week, but they have clear instructions and TAs available who understand the content. Midterms are on the harder side, BUT the practice problems given were very helpful. Don't understand the hate! I thought this class was fair and useful.

HORRIBLE. Her weekly coding projects take hours upon hours, and you have to live in office hours to pass them. Her exams are unfair, her lectures are boring but very necessary, and every week, she sends out multiple announcements about errors she made in the projects that make your life ten times harder because she is reckless and does not care.

Gave an assignment over fall break and assigned the second part of the final project over Thanksgiving break, and on top of that, we have to study for the final. Terrible scheduling and no regard for the fact that students can't dedicate all 24 hours to one class.

Overall a very caring professor but the HWs are very tedious and time-consuming. The class is well-structured and I believe the content is really useful in a real-world sense, but I don't know... some things just aren't that great. Do with that what you will.
PRAIREE IS THE GOATTTTTTT.

As much as everyone likes to hate on this class as of fall 2025, there were some useful things taught in it. Homework did take a long time though and tests were generally harder than the practice material. The TA review sessions also were not that good. Just a class you have to get through, but there's some good info taught in the class, mostly.

Quite literally said at the beginning of the semester, "This will be the class you complain about the most." Tells you about everything you need to know, since all she wants is to make this the bane of your existence.

My friends who took this class last semester all got A's and spoke very highly of her, which is why I enrolled. I can tell she can be a kind person. If the class had always been graded this strictly, I could accept that. But it feels unfair that I'm facing such a different and much harsher standard only because I took the course one semester later.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You need to know a lot of Java beforehand to succeed in this class. The assignments are long and heavy, the tests are hard to understand, and the grading is extremely harsh. The course content changed a lot from last semester for no clear reason. Worst class ever.

Practice material is often very different from the actual test, answer keys are revised the day of the exam, random questions and parts of questions get thrown out and added in that end up making the difference between a 70 and a 90 a dice roll, lots of very long assignments, grading rubrics oddly specific while directions are ironically vague.

She is really nice but I wish she could teach java better. I know she is great but I really don't want to approach her. She seems scary when I try to walk in her direction. I don't feel comfortable going up to her and talking and getting help. I am struggling because I am not smart. I wish her teaching style was detailed for slow people like me.

She is a nice professor and I really don't think she's maliciously doing anything, but the class this semester has been a disaster. She is a poor lecturer and if you don't already know some java you probably will really struggle. But the biggest issue is her midterms, extremely unfair and ungenerous with points. She won't even release the averages.

I put my heart into studying for this last test for two weeks and still got the worst grade I've ever had. I attended every class, reviewed all the slides, and practiced nonstop, yet still felt unprepared. With little Java experience, the fast pace and dense content make it feel nearly impossible to succeed. I'm genuinely worried I wont pass

As someone who scored poorly on the past two midterms, it feels mostly like a result of your own work, rather than her teaching/work. If you have little experience with Java, it makes the class considerably harder, so there is a large spread in the class between the people who already know what they are doing and the people who are lost.
Worst professor oat made the class a lot harder this semester

The ratings speak for themselves. Don't come here rating her 5.0 just because you take 1-2 comp classes and a bunch of gen-eds, and have tons of time to go to office hours. The class isn't inclusive of people with really heavy schedules. Oh, and don't get confused by ratings from past semesters. Find a friend and compare how midterms have changed.

I've seen people rate her 5.0, and don't get me wrong, she really does seem like a kind person. The issue is that the class has changed significantly, so it's not fair for people to rely on older experiences when rating it. This semester, the course is much harder, and honestly, it feels nearly impossible to get an A if you're double-majoring.

This class is NOT homework heavy. You have an entire week for each assignment as well as office hours.  The homework assignments took me at most 4 hours each to complete. If you struggle with Java, I suggest going to office hours or attending the dedicated session. Finally, the tests aren't that bad, just go over study guide/slides.

Professor Prairie is one of the best and sweetest professors in the CS department. I have learned so much from her class and was able to apply my knowledge at my internship this past summer. The tests were on the harder side but were definitely doable if you put the time in and actually do the assignments yourself (i.e., didn't just use ChatGPT).

Honestly, I think the reviews speak for themselves. She is a nice person though and does care. Unfortunately, the class is structured in a way that is unlike the sentiment from previous semesters. Either the entire class population got dumber for this class, or she made your 2nd ever java class at UNC unnecessarily hard and not beginner friendly.

I've spent hours every day on this class for weeks, even over fall break when an assignment was due and a test was right after. She expects this to be our only priority, ignoring that most of us take 3-4 other classes. Assignments take endless time yet count for only 20%, and the tests are long, stressful, and completely unlike the given material.
She makes the class absurdly difficult. Tests are 70% of your grade, and I feel like she is out to fail students. I have never felt so discouraged and stressed about a class before.

The professor doesn't teach how to write Java, making the class nearly impossible without prior experience, so you end up teaching it all to yourself. Exams are unlike reviews and worth 70% of the grade. Despite hours of studying, I feel set up to fail. I've always loved CS, but the lack of support and empathy makes this class deeply discouraging.

Key takeaways so far:
1. answer keys frequently wrong
2. tests on content that is not taught during lecture
3. TA's are frequently incorrect during review sessions. Personally, I think its difficult to study when resources given are so obviously and drastically incorrect. Difficulty doesn't come from rigor of material, but rather these aspects.
tests are extremely stressful and graded harshly. some of the reviews seem artificial. she's not a good prof by any stretch of the imagination.

I personally dont understand why you have a midterm that takes the whole class period. I feel like we should have some extra time at the end to look at our answers. Also I am slow so I need extra time to even understand the questions.

The TAs don't know what they're doing but have large egos. Office hours are often a waste of time because most of the TAs are just as confused if not more confused than we are. The professor isn't receptive to feedback and lacks empathy. Tests are long and impossible to study for. Tests are also graded harshly. 

TLDR: Horrible in every aspect

No matter how much I study, I will never feel like i am ready for her midterm because she is unpredictable. My hands are cramping from writing code for over a week. I am so stressed that I have forgotten about my other classes and I stopped going to them so I could study for this midterm. I will still probably fail at the end. Pray for me.

The professor seems to treat student confusion as proof of “rigor” rather than a signal to clarify. It literally drains motivation. Even when you put in the work, there is minimal feedback. The TAs were the only reason I survived, thx to them for doing what the professor should've done. Be prepared to teach urself everything if u take this class.

First midterm had topics we talked about once. The grading scale is very unfair, especially for those who are bad at test. Midterm one is 15%, Midterm 2 is 25%, and out final is 30%. She doesn't teach enough to make you feel confident. Also, once you learn a new topic in class, you immediately have a goevalute coding assignment due that day :(

This was the most discouraging class I've taken at Carolina. I felt completely unsupported and often left class feeling demoralized. The environment was unnecessarily harsh, and it seemed like the professor valued making things difficult over helping students learn. This experience made me seriously question pursuing this field.

I've never had a professor at Carolina who actively wanted to watch their students fail. Never felt so unsupported. Made me rethink my whole career because I refuse to go into a field with people like her. Instead of building respect between herself and students, she tries to build strife and intends to make everybody's life harder.

Her lectures are boring but she is a really good teacher. Somehow it's a lot easier to pay attention when you're actually studying for the exams. don't llm the homeworks, she can tell (or if you do at least do it early in the week when there are office hours). first midterm was brutal, nothing like practice resources

Prarie can seem tough/uncaring at first, and 301 isn't an easy class. However, once you get to know her, she's really sweet. The lectures can be cheesy, but you'll pick up a ton of practical SWE tips that will stick with you. The exams are tough but very fair, though be ready to write a lot of code by hand and quickly, since they're pretty long.

Prof Prairie is an amazing instructor for 301. Her slides are beautifully made and extremely helpful to help study the night before an exam. The exams were honeslty fun to take and were extremely studyable if you just put in a couple of hours. I also want to give props to the TA team doing the review sessions this sem cause they were AMAZING.

Her lectures are excellent with helpful and often entertaining analogies. There were a lot of assignments—more then in other COMP classes—but they are LLM-able and have straightforward autograding. The tests aren't particularly difficult, but they are long and can be a time crunch. She had terrible TAs which led to grading issues, but not her fault

Prof Praire is a solid instructor, and the class was a good experience overall. But if you already know Java (with some experience), prepare to be bored out of your mind. The exams are long, but also incredibly easy. There's so much extra credit that it barely feels like a test. Honestly, it was easier than my ENG 105.

Prof Prairie was a great prof who clearly knew the expectations of industry level code. There was an emphasis on writing clear and maintainable code. Tests are long but if you knew how to code in Java it was more an exercise of cobbling together concepts than it was to sit down and think about what to write ie you have to know your stuff coming in.

If you actually try, you will learn a ton in this class. She teaches very practical skills. If you talk to her, she cares about her students a lot and will make sure you have what you need to succeed.  

But you can't walk all over her if you don't do the work.  Due dates are not suggestions, and she can tell if you aren't  trying.

I have really enjoyed this class as we got a perspective on real-world software development. I do not agree with the some of the other reviews here since the lectures are quite clear and concepts are taught very well. Tests are very coding heavy and on paper, so it is important to be comfortable with programming in Java.

A lot of people get thrown off because she doesn't seem as "nice" as other professors, but Priaire knows her stuff. Attendance isn't mandatory, but she does class activities. Coding assignments aren't always that clear, but she responds to emails fairly quickly and is ready to help. Also does some extra credit.

One of the best classes I've ever taken at UNC. The slides included cute characters and memes, making potentially boring concepts enjoyable. Gradescope assignment instructions were sometimes unclear but still doable. She may seem self-centered, but she actually cares about her students. If you find this difficult, you should probably give up on CS.

Extremely boring lectures, the only good parts are the video game references. Homework assignments are not difficult but are tedious and teach you little to nothing about the class. Exams are easy as long as you review the slides. She spent a lot of time teaching things not relevant to the course such as threading and JavaFX.

Favorite CS prof at UNC! Clearly passionate about the material, taught in applicable ways rather than just theoretical concepts. Labs were fun. Tests were majority code writing, but broken down and very well guided. She was open to feedback (posting slides, curving mid2) from the class. TAs weren't great but that was truly the only negative!

Prairie is a great professor. She takes accountability and feedback very well. Her second exam had a lot of negative feedback and a low average, so she gave a big curve and extra credit. Her exams were straightforward, and each question had a few lines of code to write. 
Con: exams are paper and pencil writing code, so you need to know the syntax

This was Prof. Prairie's first semester, so some things understandably didn't go smoothly. Her optional lectures are very well-organized, and I highly recommend attending them. The second exam was too long, but she acknowledged it and took accountability. Put in the effort, and you'll do well—she genuinely cares about her students' success.

Prof Prairie's first semester teaching at UNC so it definitely wasn't perfect. I will admit the exams were frustrating at times, but getting over the grade, it's all a learning experience. There was a lot of code writing on the tests. Lectures were interesting and relatively organized. Prof Prairie is responsible and owns up to her mistakes.

She was sweet, my biggest issue with her were the tests. They were all code-writing which is fine, but it got to a point where it felt like straight memorization. She gives lots of extra credit, though, just getting an A can be hard because it is a 95+ to get one. Not hard to do well in the class, though and she takes feedback, so she'll get better
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Prof. Prairie is the most relatable CS instructor I had so far, and it's been a blast taking her course. Although it's her first time lecturing @ UNC, I'm sure the complaints you see from other posts will get ironed out in the upcoming semesters. 

Overall, course was interesting and helpful (moreover necessary) if you aspire to be in the industry.

She does treat us like high schoolers but her lectures are decent. I thought the tests had too much code writing for no cheat sheet (she gave a notecard but took it away for the final), and very poorly written questions, but they weren't bad and had EC. I really enjoy the content but the class could be taught and tested in better ways.

Seriously not that bad. There are a lot of negative reviews because of a midterm that was made too long by accident, but she acknowledged this mistake and applied a hefty curve to account for it, which shows more integrity than most professors. Preparing for the midterms is not difficult, there are many resources (posts slides, practice test).

Come to class. Take notes on lectures. Actually do the practice she assigns. Tests are fair. Lengthy but fair. I think she's getting rated lower than she should because she gives highschool teacher vibes...but honestly thats a good thing. She actually cares about her students being good programmers. If you took APCS, this is a good follow up course

she was ok for her first semester at unc i guess, but the material was just so hard to follow the way she taught it. she took our feedback into consideration though, so that's a plus for future semesters.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures were made well, she listened to students feedback about testing, and genuinely wants to see her students succeed. We had to hand-write code for tests but she provided plenty of practice. If you go to lecture and put in the effort you'll be fine.

I personally found her to be a good teacher. Her slides included in depth coding examples for the concepts she teaches which helps a lot. Her second midterm was hard but she curved it and gave opportunities to earn back points. She took our feedback which some professors don't do and said she'd revise the midterms going forward. Brings energy too.

made simple concepts overly complicated. Exams felt intentionally difficult, with 90% coding on paper, not reflecting a full understanding of the course. another review mention its first sem teaching- she was literally gaining experience at the cost of our grades. Overall, it felt like she was testing us more than teaching the concepts.

Does not do a very good job explaining important concepts in the class. From my experience, office hours were often not available. The final had a lot of typos and errors. This is her first time teaching here so maybe it will get better in the future. Lectures are not recorded and at the start of the class she did not post slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Acts way more like a teacher than a professor - which has its perks but also downsides. Felt like I was back in high school - lots of little assignments which amount to a LOT of the grade. (9 labs = 50% of grade) Very accessible outside of class but also definitely doesn't feel like a college class. Yawn like high school too sometimes.
In my nightmare blunt rotation, but she taught well and had engaging lectures. She obviously put a lot of work into this semester. 95 A is brutal though, dunno if its the same for other instructors
very long exams, and does not teach content very well. she's a nice person at least. tas were rude.

she does not teach the content well at all. not even a good simple example to give u an idea of whats going on. this class could have been so fun and the content is interesting too but the way she taught it was a nightmare.

went to every class. payed attention. went to OH. and still i dont like her. she DOES NOT teach the material. she just talks and talks. does not explain in simple detail about how to actually do anything. TAs are so rude. someone said this but the only thing that was good was the review day on LDOC. she actually showed us how to do stuff that day.

midterms r long. why on earth is it the same length as our final. not exaggerating. did not teach the material well. just clicked through slides and went on tangents. did not give good SIMPLE examples so that we had some basis of understanding for the hw. review at the end was good tho (only time she explained stuff well). she is kinda snarky too.

She was very receptive to feedback. The tests are fair and made to weed out students who ChatGPT all of their assignments. She's always happy to discuss with students and takes time to break down a concept if you ask her. She did a lot of practice with content directly on the midterm. Low ratings either cheated on assignments or didn't go to class.

Honestly disagree with the bad ratings here. If you utilize all the resources she puts out, you'll do fine. I also loved her teaching style and found myself really enjoying the content.
The tests are mostly coding and the questions build on each other, so make sure you learn syntax and logic. Loved her asides and emphasis on industry knowledge.

Great professor overall - encourages understanding and implementation rather than memorization. Tests can be challenging but they're very fair in terms of what's discussed in class, especially since you're allowed a notecard for each midterm. You'll be more than prepared if you go to the lectures and review in-class coding examples.

This was her first semester at UNC and it wasn't flawless but she was very responsive to feedback and adjusted her approach. The midterms were long and challenging, but the assignments helped. She is funny, kind, and experienced. Every complaint I've heard about her has reeked of misogyny and comp sci bro nonsense. Don't let them scare you off.
Not the greatest, but she did her best with teaching her first semester at UNC
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As someone who has struggled in COMP classes (I struggled in COMP 110 for reference), Professor Prairies has made this class one of the most engaging at my time at Carolina. An amazing professor that explains complicated concepts in a way that is easy to understand. GO TO CLASS! Low ratings did not go to class, or didn't actually do the assignments
Content isn't taught in the best way, but she's a nice person

I don't really get the hate to be honest. As long as you showed up and tried to do the assignments yourself without ChatGPT (TAs were pretty helpful), the material was not too difficult. The second midterm was definitely more difficult, but she did apply a generous curve, and partial credit was given out. Overall, show up to class and pay attention
take with someone else

Honestly pretty good lecturer and (although very Millennial type humor) lectures were entertaining and informative. She does have a bit of a problem with treating us like we're high schoolers and lowkey it seems like she might crash out at all times but shes still better than other cs professors currently.
Very difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Prairie is an amazing professor with industry knowledge and knows how to make lectures interesting. You should be fine for the tests if you attend lecture and review the in class assignments and slides. This was her first semester teaching the class and there were definitely some growing pains, but not the nightmare some made it out to be.

Not sure why there are so many bad reviews but she is a decent professor. She runs the class in a way where you can't just memorize everything but must understand what you're doing. The tests are mainly handwritten code, and each question builds on the others. If you want to do well in this class, attend the live coding lectures and read slides.
Content not taught well. Exams are horrible. No resources whatsoever to help us learn outside class or prepare for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Shes nice, lectures are boring as any CS lecture tends to be. Assignments where usefull in understanding concepts. Tests where hard. TA's where not helpful during review sessions (or anything tbh). Prairie is a great prof, but her tests are difficult to prepare for given the lac of resources she provides and her janky slides.

there is literally no way to prepare for exams. no recorded lectures, slides are difficult to understand, unrelated (and lack of) practice exams, exams much more difficult than what we're taught, and so much content taught poorly at the same time that i constantly feel behind. she's nice though and at least assignments are worth half your grade.

Worst professor ever. Slides are confusing and filled with pointless memes she uses to "make class fun" but fails. No study resources, no recorded lectures, and no poll answers. Syllabus claimed exams would have MC, code tracing, and T/F, but they're all code writing. Practice exams don't match actual exams, leaving us unprepared.

falls short on all accounts, horrible exams(don't line up w practice tests), poor lectures w awful slides & even if u go to class hard to understand what shes talking abt (no lecture recordings!), wastes lecture time on history/memes rather than giving us more content/review,  lil flexibility in course structure, no study resources, DONT TAKE HER
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Literally no study resources: no lecture recordings, bad slides, no poll everywhere solutions, no midterm solutions, barely any feedback on Gradescope. Claimed she can't record lectures when almost every CS prof does. Claimed she can't post poll solutions even after a student told her how to. Test questions are way harder than what we're taught.
Do not take her. Exams are hard and lectures are boring. Take this class with someone else.
Exams are very very hard. Very bad professor. Slides do no make sense.

midterms are unpredictable in content, the first and second varied widely and the second was only code writing. didn't give us a practice exam for the second one, and the practice exam for the first one was useless. great person, but i'd recommend taking 301 with someone else
gave us one hell of a midterm but applied such a legendary curve it didn't even matter, mashallah love prof prairie 🙏🙏

Prof Prairie indeed knows how to make the lecture fun and full of laughters. If you're looking for a good lecturer, Prof Prairie would be the choice. But for the test, it's kind of deviate from the real course concept. It's only about coding, and there's only one setting. All codes are linked together. So if you missed one part you'd miss other.

Professor Prairie is a professor who tries her hardest to appeal to the audience with her lectures, with her slides including somewhat humorous memes and her coding appealing to the gen z audience. For the tests, make sure that you spend a lot of the time learning the implementation of what is taught in class. Coding

Nice lady makes the class engaging and shows how concepts are useful in the modern workforce. Her tests are just pages and pages and pages of code writing. Which in essence isnt bad, but coupled with the fact that the wordying is really funny and the stresses of being in a test make the exams very annoying. Id recomend taking 301 with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Prairie is an incredible professor. She's very down-to-earth and human: she can stumble and make mistakes, but this doesn't take away from her skill as a teacher and only adds to the comfort of attending her lectures and having conversations with her. Class is of very average difficulty if you pay attention. Live Laugh Love Prairie!

I 100% stand behind Dr. Goodwin. She is actually the GOAT for 301. she has industry knowledge as well so thats a plus and shes a really fun lecturer. she's new but shes doing a fantastic job so far and I'm really excited whenever I go to her class. fav class this semester!
She is super sweet and knows what she is doing. I always wanted to go to class because she made it so fun. The homework is fine and the tests are fair. Big big fan of her teaching

Teaching is very straightforward and the first midterm was very similar to tasks assigned in coding labs as well as things taught during lectures. This professor knows what they are doing, at least so far!

Dr. Goldsmith selects good readings and has interesting topics to lecture on but he relies too much on audience participation. He uses class time to get student opinions, and often doesn't even adress the questions he poses. I found it hard to study for tests because he rarley provides definitions for terms, yet he grades in a very specific manor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Course was way too hard for a first year intro course, homework and test were obnoxiously hard for no reason.

Such an understanding and knowledgeable professor. Probably the smartest and most well-informed professor I've had at UNC thus far. Semester long paper, wasn't too bad. Before and after class assignments as attendance. Reading heavy but it wasn't too strenuous. Take him, if you have a slight interest in public policy or PPE you won't regret it.

There's nothing wrong with this professor, but I wasn't a fan. This class was at 8 am, and I had enough trouble staying awake without his lectures lulling me to sleep. He graded fairly, but we just didn't click.

Dr. Goldsmith is the goat. He assigned a lot of readings, but I didn't do any and did fine in the class. He really cared about his students and public policy. As long as you put a little bit of effort into the class and study for the midterm/final you'll be fine. He's an awesome professor.

Very knowledgeable about policy, and it definitely shows in this class. He clearly puts a lot of effort into each lecture, but there is also a lot of reading before each class. Very kind, nice to speak with in and outside of class, and gives so many opportunities to improve your grade. You will need to put effort in, but you will get a lot out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Goldsmith is a really caring person, but this class itself should not have been so hard for a first year requirement. The grading criteria is extremely vague and frustrating. Homework takes hours nearly every week and you are expected to do a lot of pre-class reading. Great professor, but disorganized and unnecessarily difficult class.

Dr. Goldsmith is one of the most passionate and caring professors I have met on this campus. Although he is strict in his syllabus, he is open to listening about problems you see with it, allowing for compromise. However, even with that being said, I feel that he gives too much pre-class work, assigning more than he should for a first year class.

Goldsmith is AMAZING! However, he did not have the grade calculator on for the entire semester. The class focuses on your final brief, so pick a topic you are interested in, most of your grade will depend on it (even part of your final). You get a cheat sheet for exams! I learned a lot and always wanted to attend classes. Take this class!
Kind of boring, but nice guy.

Dr. Goldsmith had no respect for students in IDST 131 and brushed off concerns about unfair grading in the class. His lectures were dry and disorganized. He was not helpful when asked questions about course content. IDST 131, more broadly, is a difficult, unorganized class with lots of work, unclear grading, and unhelpful TAs.

I loved this class! Very smart guy and you can tell he really cares. The main assignment is a 10 page final policy brief with assignments before that help you write it. If you do the work and go to office hours (he's very accessible for help) you can get the grade you want. Would recommend to anyone who is interested in learning about public policy
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great intro course for public policy. A little dry at times but rlly interesting to take during an election year. You learn applicable content I've alr used as a pub pol major. Final and midterm (you get cheat sheets) that are writing intense with a long policy brief assignment and presentation at the end, but useful for the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He was a good professor, just don't EVER take this class if you wish to maintain your mental health. You are given so much homework that is worth a big portion of your grade but after they grade it…they don't tell you the correct answers so in the class you'll never really know what the exact answer should have been. Spare yourself and don't do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was very difficult for a first year foundation course, I would not recommend it to anyone. 3 tests and a final presentation with a paper. Professor Goldsmith is an amazing person on his own, but I would not take a class from him again. Does not matter how much time you spend, the TAs grade homework extremely harsh with vague questions.

Though this Triple-I is not a fun time, Dr. Goldsmith is an awesome lecturer and does make me more interested in public policy. You have to actually pay attention though when he lectures because his slides don't contain much information. Though I would never wish this triple-I on my worst enemy, I would definitely take Goldsmith again

Dr. Goldsmith lectures the most in this class. Public policy is dry, but he does a very good job of giving detail. Take this class only if you're actually interested! The homework and tests are a bit intense, but the subject matter is fascinating and detailed. Dr. Goldsmith can feel challenging, but he genuinely wants his students to thrive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Loved Dr. Goldmith! He's passionate about what he teaches, and he's very accessible outside of class. He's very understanding and doesn't want anyone to stress about grades, but he still gives good feedback on the policy brief. He's a little funky, but also funny and kind. Classes were interesting, despite the decent amount of readings.

Dr. Goldsmith was my favorite amongst the professors that taught this triple I, but man, this triple I is ridiculous, it might as well be a 300-level course due to the kind of material you are expected to digest. Dr. Goldsmith is a very caring man, and he's very straightforward. Wouldn't recommend this triple I, but I would recommend Goldsmith.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are good, but this is a very tough Triple-I. Homework was often quite long, with some unclear questions that were graded harshly by TAs. The concepts were interesting, and you will like the course if you like poli sci/public policy. Definitely hard for a first-year course though. Goldsmith is a great lecturer, would take again.

This class might be the worst I have taken so far. This class is INSANELY hard for a first year required class. This is the first semester they have tough it, and it better be the last. Do not take this class. Trust me. Homework is graded so intensely, as everyone I know gets a C average on the homework. This class is ridiculous for freshmen.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I have taken at UNC so far and it is a Triple I of all things. It is harder than any of the classes I have taken for my STEM major and the grading is harsh for no reason. On top of that they do not care if you are literally on your deathbed, attendance still matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Goldsmith cares about getting to know his students and exposing them to all types of policy. This class really is a sampler platter. However, For a 101 class, this is a lot of work (heavy reading). Your grade relies on a a end-of-term 10-page policy brief (in addition to a final), but it's managable.

This class made me question if I want to still be a policy major. Class consisted of way too much reading, boring lectures, and huge assignments that made up most of the grade. I worked my butt off and still could not get an A. Goldsmith comes off really condescending and the way he teaches is not helpful at all, most of the content is theoretical.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Goldsmith is an excellent professor; his lectures are interesting (and well-written), everything he does is designed carefully and intentionally, and he is intent on meeting his students and helping them succeed. He can be a bit paternalistic (he used to be a high school teacher), but I think it's helpful in the end, especially for an intro course.

Idk why he has such good ratings on here. I thought the class was boring. There was way too much reading for a 100-level class, and Goldsmith is extremely rude and condescending. I went into policy 101 hoping I would want to add policy as a minor, and he made me hate the entire subject. You WILL be bored. He is genuinely annoying and unpredictable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was borderline disrespectful. Almost no graded feedback all semester, expectations were constantly vague, and the syllabus was meaningless. I worked like crazy in a class that felt like an afterthought, with due dates for major assignments sprung on us right before the deadline. Dropped 2,000+ words of writing on us on LDOC. Run away.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Take this class if you have any interest in policy!!! A true sampling platter class that will either confirm or deny your interest in policy. Great lectures, interesting readings, and a great opportunity to write a policy brief on a topic of your choice. Exams were overall easy with a few nitpicky questions. Recommend to all freshmen and sophomores
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the best teachers here at Carolina. You can tell how much he cares and tries to get you to care. I would 110% take this class again. The work you put in is the grade you get out of it!

Took him because I loved him in 101. This class is harder in that you're expected to have a more in depth understanding, but also assignments are less heavy. You will be discussing with classmates every day. Very easy to reach for office hours and also very approachable. Can sometimes be a tough grader, but not unfair. Lots of reading.

Professor Goldsmith was one of the best teachers I've ever had. He is so caring and makes sure his students can communicate with him in and outside of class. He uses science/research to achieve the most efficient teaching and learning. He is just a very nice and personable person and I would absolutely take another class with him given the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Goldsmith was the best policy professor I could ask for. He is understanding, clearly passionate about the material, and easily accessible. Although his lectures were sometimes confusingly theoretical, the discussion-based classroom setup and recitation provided clarity. Overall, I thoroughly enjoyed this class and Professor Goldsmith.

Goldsmith is a nice guy who really cares about his students. PLCY 101 is a TON of reading and homework, but if you put in the effort, your grade will reflect it. His lectures do not directly tell you what you need to know and are typically philosophical and discussion-based. The papers and final policy brief are A LOT of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I highly recommend Professor Goldsmith and his honors section. He is accessible outside class and demonstrates a consistent interest in helping his students succeed. Note that the course is fairly reading-heavy, but given what he calls his "sample-platter" approach to public policy you will come to appreciate a background prior to class discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: getting an A in this class is definitely attainable if you do the readings and take notes during class. that being said, it was a lot of work. there was about an hour of reading to do to be prepared for each class. we also had to write a policy memo, outline, and brief, which was about 10 pages when finished. overall amazing prof though!!!

Professor Goldsmith shows a true desire to get to know his students and does his best to inspire them to make changes through policy. While I found some lectures to be too philosophical or lacking focus, I did learn a great deal from this class. This was the most assignments I've ever had in a class, but if you put the work in, you'll get an A.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! I have taken 300- 400 level PLCY courses and this class was by far the hardest class with the MOST amount of work. There is so much reading every night and every detail matters. The final was 10 pages front and back of writing. Participation is a huge chunk of your grade and if you miss one class your grade is jeopardized.

Although Goldsmith's lectures could be confusing, he is truly passionate about policymaking! I learned a great deal in this class. The grading criteria was incredibly detailed so you always knew exactly what to do, he was accessible outside of class, and offered lots of extra credit! Despite bombing the midterm, I still ended with an A :)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Goldsmith, a brilliant individual, stays culturally attuned and brings a crucial philosophical perspective to his public policy lectures. While the class workload isn't overwhelming, the assignments are meticulously graded, so don't underestimate the attention to detail needed to succeed.

Professor Goldsmith's teaching style class made class material interesting, and he cares about his students as well. Also, there is a good mix of lecture and small group discussion in the class. However, it was a work-heavy class for the 100 level. This being said, I learned so much and I'm glad I took the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Everybody who complains about Goldsmith being too philosophical is misunderstanding his teaching style. He uses theoreticals to get you to think about material so you're not just copying the notes from slides. I took this class as a throwaway, but because of Goldsmith I'm now pursuing a minor in policy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Goldsmith is an amazing professor. Those saying he's not simply didn't take the time to put in the work to learn and understand. You can tell he truly cares about what he is teaching and his students. The work and readings are a bit challenging, but going to his or your TA's office hours will help with that. This was the best class I took at UNC.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Seems like a good guy but lectures aren't straightforward & very philosophical. So much reading and I think this class would be particularly challenging if taken as a freshman. Assignments aren't hard, but a lot of work (esp for a 101). The final brief isn't bad but make sure you like the topic, semester long. Exams open note but a lot to cover.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lectures not straight forward and a little too philosophical for an intro course. Multiple extra credit opportunities offered. Midterm and final open note. Grade can depend on your TA. Pick a good, specific policy problem at beginning of semester to use for your memo and 10 page policy brief. Goldsmith's nice but too much work for a 101.

Goldsmith is a very tough professor. This class really depends on who your TA is because they will be grading all of your assignments. Mid Term was open note but incredibly hard. There is a lot of reading and you need to stay on top of things to get an A. He doesn't round up grades. He talks down to students a lot. The class is very broad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Goldsmith is the worst lecturer I have ever had to listen to. He's a nice guy and its not that the assignments are too difficult, but everything he says is so philosophical and not straightforward. Way more work than any other 100 level class. Overall, I do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, was always inspirational in and out of class, kept up with students with a gateway entrance to public policy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Goldsmith truly cared about his students, but his lectures were too philosophical. He never really answered topic questios in class, so you learn everything from the readings. If you are willing to do the readings and participate, you will be successful. He cares a lot about the students, but is not very straight forward.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Although the topic was sometimes dull, Professor Goldsmith made lectures engaging. He was always available outside of class, and he seemed to want to get to know his students. The assignments were not exceptionally difficult and had many extra credit opportunities. I enjoyed this class and would really recommend taking it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Goldsmith is a great professor. This is my second class with him and he did not disappoint! Goldsmith is super passionate about public policy and it shows throughout the class. If you're interested in state and local politics definitely take this class. Policy brief at the end and lots of readings but nothing unmanageable!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class
