reviews.comment: I liked Goldsmith. Mostly interesting lectures and clear outline of class and expectations. I would take his class again. TA's do the grading and there are a lot of easy grades that count for a large % of overall grade

Great guy and passionate about the material but DO NOT take this class as a throwaway class. If you want an A/A- you'll need to work for it. TA's were entirely responsible for your grade but mine was really chill and graded very easily. Midterm and Final were HARD. Recommend to PLCY majors or if you're planning on making it pass/fail.
I absolutely loved Dr. Goldsmith, you will not regret taking a class with him.

I liked Goldsmith as a person, most of the time as a professor. His lectures were kinda philosophical? I couldn't really tell what we needed to know or the point of his lecture. A lot of reading, but I barely did it and still did well. A couple big assignments and weekly forum posts (super easy). Nice, caring, sometimes weird guy. Overall not bad.

Quite a bit of reading for an intro level class, but Goldsmith is such a kind and flexible professor! He obviously really cares about his students and the content he is teaching. Very attainable A if you put in a reasonable amount of effort.

I never paid attention in lectures and just did the readings at the end of the semester before the final and got a solid A in the class. The major assignments are graded really easy across the board and a majority of students get As or A- in the class. Pretty interesting material, but make sure you do the readings as that's what you're tested on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall pretty decent class that was not very difficult. TA's do all of the grading for the papers and the final policy brief, which often means it is easier to do well. Lectures can be very boring and there is lots of reading for homework.

Professor Goldsmith's policy 101 course is a great introduction to public policy, for both policy majors and those curious about policy. His lectures are great, and the longer paper for the class lets you explore a topic that interests you. Even as somebody very involved in politics, I learned a great deal from this class. Highly recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Goldsmith is a great professor and really cares for his students and the material, which can be hard to find. There is a lot of reading in this class but you don't need to read all of it to get the general idea. I would recommend it whether you are a policy major or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was a lot of work for a 101 and entry-level course. It was tough to get clear feedback on assignments as well as clear definitions of topics during lectures. Goldsmith seems like a good, fun person, but the lectures strayed off-topic and did not address what was later tested. Start policy brief early.

Goldsmith provides good sources and examples of the concepts, however, he does not give clear definitions of the concepts we are learning during class. Moreover, the lectures can be boring at times and he tends to spend too much time on specific examples rather than the idea itself. He seems like a good/funny person, but he does not teach well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Goldsmith was one of my favorite professors this semester. He was funny and wanted to hear what students had to say in class. The assignments weren't easy but they helped me learn a lot. The final grade is a 10 page paper which is difficult, but the assignments leading up to it help you prepare to write it. Overall I loved this class and the prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Goldsmith is a great person and is incredibly smart. I would say this class is WAY better if you actually care about public policy/are a public policy major. It's a lot of boring work if you don't care about the subject. TON of reading. For the most part, they're interesting but dense. The main assignment is a 10-page policy brief.

This is definitely an easy A, but if you want to understand the material you need to do the readings, as Prof. Goldsmith doesn't really explain concepts from the readings in his lectures. His lectures can be engaging, but they don't really help in terms of understanding the actual material. Beware of the semester long policy brief project
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Goldsmith is a very good lecturer who explains the material thoroughly. He cares about his students and is accessible outside of class. The course is somewhat paper-heavy but he and the TAs give advice to improve your final paper. Exams are not too challenging but require at least a rudimentary understanding of the readings. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great! This is best course you can get at UNC!!!!!!!!

Goldsmith is a caring and eloquent professor who cares about the mental health of students and seeks to instill an appreciation of learning in students. That said, the class is reading-heavy. The readings are interesting though. PLCY 101 had exponentially more reading than PLCY 210. The exams are open note but will pull on reading content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is super discussion-based, and you have to do the readings. He doesn't do tests (at least not for this class), but you are expected to participate and know your stuff. The assignments aren't too bad, but his expectations are kind of nebulous and you don't get most of your grades back until the end of the semester. He's a nice guy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Goldsmith is a nice guy. He provides many opportunities for extra credit, is generous with extensions, and always makes time to meet with students: I disliked the format of this course the entire semester, but reflecting at the end, I think that as long as you're ready for the reading and pacing (20-40 pages per class), you'll succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: Goldsmith is amazing! 360 is very discussion and reading heavy but most if not all the readings were very interesting. I will say the final policy brief I'm procrastinating writing right now didnt have very clear guidelines which made it a little hard to navigate so maybe avoid if that, not something you want to deal with.

I loved Professor Goldsmith! His class is super easy to do well in. His class is super organized (there is an 8-10 page paper on a topic of your choosing). I would recommend taking a few notes on the readings for the midterm. The midterm and final was open note. There is a mandatory presentation you have to do at the end of the semester!

I took professor Goldsmith's class last semester and I do not regret it at all. If you are any chance thinking of becoming a policy major or even poli sci it is a great class to take. There was one 8-10 page policy brief and another short paper. Yet, it was not too difficult with his feedback. Easy grader and great professor overall.
Alright professor, I found the class boring at times but if you follow the lectures and study you'll get an A

Goldsmith had an online and in person option. I did the online option. Participation is important. Make sure to check everything off the checklist or you wont get credit. A midterm/final exam study guide is crucial for passing. Use lesson takeaways. Several papers off one topic so pick interesting topic. Several opportunities for extra credit.

Great lectures, and thats coming from a non-policy major. The class is hard but definitely fair since the grading is so split up. Glance into the readings, spend time on the papers, and take notes on the lesson takeaways in class and you will be fine.
I definitely learned a lot but it was SO MUCH writing for a 101 class, definitely improved my writing skills though.

Professor Goldsmith was a really good professor, he made lectures pretty enjoyable and included a song of the day with each one that related to the topic. The class is extremely reading-heavy, and the midterm was pretty difficult since we had no prior experience on what tests were like in his class. Despite the amount of work, I enjoyed this class!

The class was pretty easy. Readings typically aren't super long. There's a big paper due at the end of the semester but the smaller papers you turn in leading up to it help write that for you. Participation grades are easy and he gives good lectures. He was also very flexible with students given COVID and other extenuating circumstances.

Professor Goldsmith's PLCY 101 class had a lot of lecturing, and a good amount of reading for each class. Most of your grade is split between tests and writing a public policy brief. The grading can be a little tougher so you'll need to put in a bit more effort if you want to guarantee an A in the class.

Goldsmith reads off of a script for the entire class. He is a fantastic writer, but it is so boring when he is just looking down reading something he wrote. The readings are fascinating, but time-consuming. You can get an A if you know stuff about policy and politics without putting in the work. If you don't and do put in the work, you'll get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Goldsmith really cares about his students. He always made time for office hours, and would check up on me whenever I attended them. If you are deciding between 101 and 101H, I would recommend 101H. The work is identical, but in 101H he offered essay corrections and more one-on-one meetings. We had a textbook but only read 2-4 chapters :/
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Goldsmith puts so much time and effort into this course. He really cares about the students and provides more feedback on assignments than he probably needs to. He completely changed the way I write and allowed me to explore a different side of public policy than I had previously thought about. Participation is a must!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Goldsmith is a great person, he's fun to talk to and is one of the most intelligent people I've ever met. His class didn't really go in-depth on anything (he did call it a sampler platter numerous times), and sometimes the lectures didn't really go anywhere. Overall though, I learned a lot from the class and enjoyed him as a person.

lots of smaller grades including projects and papers, which I liked way better than just big exams. lot of assigned reading, but very structured and it's easy to keep up. great lectures and very understanding on extensions

Although he was very accommodating when it came to extensions, the workload for this class was almost impossible to manage, even at only 14 credit hours. He is a sweet person but his class is very stressful and the midterm was very ambiguous, as it was the first "test" so you dont know what to expect. Don't recommend this class as it's not required
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Goldsmith is an absolute legend. He is a great lecturer and is lenient with extensions, and he is a very down to earth person. If you do the assigned reading and pay attention during class, you should do well. I would highly recommend him for Public Policy 101.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Goldsmith stated at the beginning of the semester that he didn't think this class would be too much work. He lied. I've never had so much assigned reading for a class before. We wouldn't even spend that much time discussing it. If you're interested in pursuing public policy, I suggest you skip over this class as it is not required.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I enjoyed his in-class discussions. His class is very discussion-based, so it made a lot of us nervous for the midterm as we were not sure what to expect. Overall a good choice, but the class is a bit of work. He's a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I have now taken Dr. Goldsmith twice - once before COVID, & one since. When I say Dr. Goldsmith is a real gem, I mean it. He is incredibly kind, understanding, and interesting. He keeps the class engaged during lectures, knows what he's talking about, and gives you clear expectations for assignments and tests. Don't hesitate to take a class w/ him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Goldsmith was a really engaging professor to have. He clearly cares a lot about public policy and especially local and state politics. This class was a lot of reading but the actual tests and assignments weren't too bad. He also had a bunch of speakers come talk to us which was cool.

Goldsmith is truly one of the best professors I have had at UNC. His lectures are extremely captivating, and you can really tell that he is passionate about teaching Public Policy. Be ready to do a good amount of writing, reading, and research in PLCY101, but don't be scared to go to office hours, Professor Goldsmith is very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is the 2nd class I took with Goldsmith and I still love him. He's friendly, nerdy, and approachable. His lectures are very engaging with students. He will work with you throughout the semester to help you succeed. He makes you think hard about class topics in the best way. He makes me glad I'm a PLCY major. 10/10 would recommend.
I love Professor Goldsmith and his classes. He's an insanely smart guy and is a great teacher. He does grade more on the tougher side, but he's still a great guy and he just wants to see you succeed.

Dr. Goldsmith is such an amazing professor especially during COVID. He's said many times that he doesn't like teachers that make things ridiculously hard, so he tries not to do that. He has really good outlines and examples for papers, but he doesn't tell you what kind or how many questions will be on exams which was not the best for me.

Professor Goldsmith was awesome. He was really caring and provided accommodations for me when I had an accident and broke my clavicle a week before finals. This classes were great. I had the privilege of taking him online, so I sped his lectures up by 2X. His lecture questions are easy to answer. He really wants you to understand the material.

Goldsmith was a wonderful teacher even online. He never gave unnecessary work and lectures were short but engaging. It is not hard to get an A with effort. He is pretty nerdy but in the best way, he is informative, funny, and very easy to talk to. I always attended all his zooms even though they weren't required because he was just that good.

PLCY 101 with Professor Goldsmith wasn't hard, but it was quite a heavy course load (I took this online). Over the semester, you work on one long policy brief, but there are "mini" essays that build up to it. Grading is spread out over A LOT of different categories, so one bad one won't hurt you. Definitely recommend him for 101!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Easily the best professor I've had at UNC. His lectures are so engaging that you won't want to skip them. You can approach him during office hours to ask for help with papers. If you do poorly on a test, that won't sink your grade because there's a lot of assignments and tests in this course. Only con: this is a reading heavy course.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof Goldsmith is an awesome lecturer. I took this class to become a better citizen in this world. It was fascinating to dig deeper into the vast variety of interesting and relevant topics. I definitely finished the class feeling like a more well-rounded individual with a better understanding of the countrys institutions. You must do the readings!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Professor Goldsmith! It was more reading than I expected but if you go to class and recitation you will get all of the information you need. Also, the TA's and Professor Goldsmith are so accessible outside of class. Plus there is so many grades one mistake wont mess you up!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was a lot more work than I expected. There were a lot of outside readings assigned and pop quizzes. The exams were a little rough and require you to know the material well (from readings and lecture), but there were a lot of other grades that went in to help balance it out. Very caring/organized professor with clear grading standards.

Dr. Goldsmith is such a great professor. He really cares about engaging with his students! The class can be a lot though if you are not that interested in Public Policy. You are graded on a lot of things so if you don't do as well as you would have liked it won't tank your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Will was a great lecturer and an amiable personality. He was funny and easily approachable as well. He structures his class to be very discussion heavy, which I enjoyed as everyone in our class was pretty engaged. Group projects and presentations also occurred throughout the semester, but were fairly low-stakes. Would definitely recommend.

Doesn't teach anything from the textbook that he wrote, but still tests all vocabulary from it. Exams are way too difficult and harshly graded for an introductory level class. Spent more time studying for this class than for any of my biology or math classes, it was unnecessarily time consuming and difficult
I loved this class. I learned a lot and Dr. Mendez was passionate about what he taught. The tests however were graded hard, so I didn't do as well as I wanted to.

If you get the opportunity to take a class with Dr. Mendez, take it! He made going to a 9am easy. His lectures are entertaining. He is also an incredibly kind professor and wants to see his students succeed. Now, the class is quite test heavy with three exams making up 68% of your grade. However, he gives a detailed study guide that is cumulative.

Prof. Mendez was one of my favorite professors I have ever had at UNC. He kept lectures engaging, attendance was mandatory but he made them fun. Workload was one 6-8 sentence reflection from each class and one 8-10 sentence paragraph from a prompt a week. Exams were very fair and study guide was super helpful. LOVED this class and this professor!

Wonderful professor, great lectures, and such a nice guy. Midterms count for a good amount of your grade, but they are pretty easy and you can do well if you use his study guides. Overall really enjoyed this class and would definitely recommend him as a professor.

Great professor and cares a lot about the material! Unbiased, and easily accessible. Definitions on tests can be oddly specific and meant to trick you, but everything is in the slides from class. Made attendance required halfway through the semester because everyone stopped showing up. Hard to bring your grade back up if you do bad on a midterm.

He is one of the best professors I've ever had! He truly cares about each and every student. For each test, he gives a detailed study guide with all the possible questions he could give. Have multiple assignments that also help your grade, as they are basically just a completion grade. Lectures are very interesting.
the absolute goat. if you can take his class do it. easy A. gives you the test questions to study. so nice and very knowledgable.

I loved Dr. Mendez. I took him for 416 cult of the Saints (not an option), he is a sweetheart and cares so much. Class was a few discussion posts, in-class talks, a martyrs feast, and one big paper broken up to keep you on track 100/10 recommend

Amazing class. Took online during maymester. Second class with Mendez. Super flexible. Low effort. Gives 100s for almost everything. Open book quizzes and exams. Don't buy the textbook, you can find it online for free. I wouldn't even read it honestly, just use it to find answers for the quizzes.

Took this class over maymester for a gen ed and recommend to anyone who needs it for a gen ed or even as an elective. The ideal workload for what you'd expect from a gen ed. Discussion posts and daily quizzes to do everyday with a midterm and final. Professor Mendez is easily accessible outside of class, very caring, and responds to emails quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hugo was a great teacher, gave study guides, and attendance wasnt necessarily mandatory. however, my TA was very unreasonable and kind of screwed me over.

Dr. Mendez is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. Down to Earth, kind, and comprehensible/interesting lectures. Teaches Christianity from an unbiased, academic perspective; very respectful of all beliefs. Such a fabulous professor, could not recommend him more.

Dr. Mendez has been my favorite professor at UNC. He's funny and is responsible. He made an error in one recitation's exam and gave everyone a 100% to make it fair. His lectures are very interesting and you can tell he knows what he's talking about. Study guides are clear and exams are easy if you know the vocab and study the free response answers.

I took 2 RELI classes with prof Mendez and both were awesome. He is kind, funny, and loves what he does. Exams are very straightforward and memorization heavy, which I enjoyed. Daily reflections are helpful for keeping up with the information and lecture material in the class. Definitely take one of his classes!!

Professor Mendez has been one of my favorite professors at UNC. He's obviously very knowledgable about what he's teaching and cares about his students. He is understanding when things come up and will take responsibility if he makes a mistake, which happened with one of our exams. I would definitely take him if given the chance.

Take every single RELI class you possibly can by Hugo Mendez. His smaller classes specifically are the best. The class consisted of weekly readings, prompt posts, reflection posts, 2 big essays, and a presentation. Professor Mendez is incredibly lively and cares a lot about his students as well as his lectures.

Dr. Mendez is the best! He is genuinely such a nice guy who seems to really care about his students. The class consisted of three easy exams and biweekly discussion posts. Dr. Mendez is an entertaining speaker, and even though class was at 9AM, I enjoyed attending each lecture. I would recommend RELI 114 to anyone looking for an easy gen ed.

Dr. Mendez is my favorite professor I have had at UNC. It is so clear he cares about his students and wants them to succeed. It is very easy to do well in this class as long as you do the discussion posts and put in effort on the final paper. I would absolutely recommend taking this class!

Take this class. Prof Mendez is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. Best lecturer on campus. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you have to write a reflection for every class that's easy to make up. All exams have a clear study guide that, if you follow, guarantees at least a B. He posts all slides and tests only on them.

Amazing, engaging professor! Required daily reflections and recitations are easy 100. DO NOT BUY THE TEXTBOOK- you only need the slides from class to study for exams (exact definitions and info). 2 midterms (20% each) plus the final (30%), graded harshly, but if you memorize definitions you will be fine. Very particular about grades being final.
hes literally so nice and caring and this class was so easy

This is my second class I've taken with Hugo, and I would take all of his courses if I could. He is engaging and makes it super easy to learn and get a good grade. Daily lecture reflections make up your attendance; otherwise, you attend recitations and participate in discussions. Exams have clear, helpful study guides and he wants you to succeed.
Awesome professor!

Good lecturer and a nice guy, but the weighting of assignments is tough. Exams require extensive memorization so get ready to study. It is hard to get your overall grade back up after one mistake. TAs all seem really sweet, mine is such a cool and approachable dude.

Mr. Mendez has been my favorite professor so far! You can tell he genuinely cares about what he's teaching, and he makes the 9 AM lectures surprisingly engaging. I really enjoy it! It's an easy gen ed class with discussion posts (easy 100s) and 2/3 exams(provides study guides). There is a textbook but I never used it. Definitely take this class!

Such an easy class. Take this to fulfill a gen ed req. Prof is extremely caring and kind, and is always available by email or OH to chat. Lectures are kinda mandatory because you have to submit a reflection after every lecture. But, they are interesting because Mendez cares so much. Exams are so easy, if you're looking for an easy class, here it is

Nice and chill Maymester class that I took for geneds. The workload was very reasonable with just a discussion post and a couple reading quizzes due every day. As long as you put in a decent amount of effort, you'll do well. Dr. Mendez is also very accessible and understanding. Highly recommended for geneds or even just credits.

Pretty good lecturer! Attend class so you don't fall behind and take notes from his slides. Make sure you go to recitation and do the daily reflection/weekly papers (the TA you choose MATTERS!). Exams have a vocab section (quizlet!) and free response-- he will provide the prompts so you can practice beforehand.

Dr. Mendez is a very caring and intelligent professor. He makes this class interesting, engaging, and fosters an environment that facilitates tough discussions. Anybody who is interested in frauds, conspiracies, or Christianity should consider this class. It's graded on reflections and reading prompts, a book review, and a final paper.
Goat, easy and cool class. Take it with him

He is an engaging lecturer. Outside of attending recitation and lecture, completing pass/fail assignment, and studying the vocab, there is really not much else to do for the class. This prepared me for the tests which are based on questions they tell you about beforehand.

Hugo Mendez was amazing! We had a 1 page position paper due weekly, as well as a discussion after every lecture. We only had two exams, the midterm and final. He gives you the prompts but STUDY THE VOCAB as it is worth 50% of the midterm and final exam grade. If possible get Jerry Grimes as your TA, he truly cares about you and is great!
Best professor I've ever had

Honestly one of the best professors I've ever had, he makes the material so interesting and engaging. There are 3 cumulative tests which were very difficult but other than that the class was fairly easy and you will learn a lot!
I took this course online over the summer and it was pretty nice/easy. Mendez set class up to be easily understood and I genuinely learned a lot of interesting things.

The class was lecture-heavy, & all the information on exam was from the lectures. (not textbook readings). Weekly 1-page reflections (graded P/F), a discussion post after each class (P/F), a participation grade for recitation, and midterm/final. The midterm and final were easy, we had all of the vocab in class & were given the prompts before.

Dr. Mendez is one of the most engaging lecturers I have ever taken a class from. He is super interested in the material which shows even in a room of 100+ students. The exams were a little bit on the more difficult side however he gives you the prompts before hand so you can prepare well. Overall would recommend!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Interesting course. Only thing I was ever worried about was exams. There was a midterm and final. Both contained a vocab section and a short writing portion. The only hard part of the exams was studying the vocab. Wasn't a clear list of words that we needed to study, so most people just studied a large number of words. Besides that it was chill!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the best classes I have taken at UNC. I highly recommend. Everything besides the midterm and participation is pass/fail.

Incredible. His lectures are easy to digest and very entertaining. I went in with low expectations and now this is my favorite class to go to. Mendez is understanding and cares about his students. I would 100% take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Mendez was truly upfront about his class and what he expected from us. His class overall was easy to get an A in as long as you did the work and tried. He offered a remote option for our class which was very helpful with the struggles of this semester. He truly cared about his students and wanted us to do our best.

I can't say enough good things about Dr. Mendez! I loved this course. Some of the work can feel a bit tedious at times, but it's very manageable. He truly is an amazing professor who cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He was funny, accommodating, and receptive. If I needed another gen-ed, I would absolutely take it with Dr. Mendez!

Professor Mendez was amazing! He's very passionate about the subject which makes lectures interesting. His class is very easy, however, you have to stay on top of your stuff. It's easy to get an A but if you fall behind it's hard to catch up. I definitely recommend him though, one of the best profs I've had at UNC.

Prof. Mendez is amazing! He is so knowledgable and caring, you do not have to be religious to succeed in this class. Seriously, if you need a gen-ed, take this class, he is such a sweet person and a really good lecturer. He also attempts to sneak jokes in which I find amusing. Take this class!!!

One of the best lecturers at UNC. He's personable and intelligent. As someone not initially interested in religious studies, he made each class engaging. If you're at all considering taking his class, I absolutely recommend it.

Lowkey disappointed with my grade in this class. Basically a fourth of our final grade is based on peer reviews, which I wasnt able to do, and there was no makeup opportunity. Hes a really nice guy, but you gotta be ON TOP of your work; if you fall behind, theres very little grace periods with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Good dude, went abovve and beyond for his students.
Hes the man! Good guy and a fun class

It was an asynchronous class with all take home exams. Amazing amazing guy, truly knows his stuff but is so cool. The grading was done very nicely, I got 98s on all of the take home exams just by doing them. If you do everything asked, guaranteed A. Plus, he's literally such a gem, I would take ANY class with this man. Highly recommend him.

He is SUUUPER caring an a great professor. The class is a breeze EXCEPT for when we have exams due. There are three exams due throughout the semester, and not only are they exceptionally long, but each one has an essay at the end. Each exam took me around 8-10 hours to complete. There's also a final project, but that was chill.

I took this class for a gen ed credit but honestly loved this professor. The topics were interesting, and you can tell that he is passionate about what he teaches which makes for amazing lectures. He also is very understanding and the class is well organized!

Dr. Mendez's RELI 104 is very clearly structured. You'll have weekly readings and response essays. Participation matters in recitations and in lectures (in the form of lecture responses on Sakai). Weekly response essays are graded for completion. The tests were graded very fairly.

Hugo is a dramatic (good) lecturer. The course was taught w/ the premise that all students know abt Christianity to begin w/. Only a limited # of ppl can get 100 for participation, so ur at a disadvantage if u haven't been going to church for 18 yrs & ur classmates have. Did 14 2pg P/F papers but only got a grade back for 1. Never got midterm grade
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Only need to attend lectures to submit the post-lecture forum post, otherwise no need to listen in class. Homework is one two-page paper a week for recitation but theyre graded P/F so theyre so easy. Midterm/final have a study guide with everything on it. Mendez is so kind and really understanding of his students so dont be scared to reach out!

Professor Mendez is hilarious. I learned a ton from this class. Arguably one of the best professors at UNC. The TAs can make this class make or break, however, they prepare you very well for his exams. Phenomenal class, attendance to lectures is not required but is important.

This class was great. I learned a lot. There are readings which I almost never did, the weekly papers take an hour at most but usually less (2 pages is nothing), the forum posts take 2 secs and are graded for completion, there is extra credit and detailed study guides. Show up for all recit./classes and do all of the assignments and you'll get an A

Not recommended. If you are a Christian, be prepared to hear lecture after lecture attempting to disprove much of the Bible. Forums due after each lecture and a pt is deducted for each one missed.. 2-3 pg papers are due weekly; 2 pts deducted for each not completed. Unreasonable grading of midterm and final. Waste of time. TA was awesome!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hugo was awesome, very welcoming of all sorts of religious views, and never forced his own personal beliefs on anyone. He gave great lectures and I learned a ton. Take him if you need a gen ed, you won't regret it.

Hugo was a solid Professor, and his class is a solid choice to get the PH requirement out of the way. Graded on participation in recitation, forum posts, papers (due weekly and are graded pass/fail), and a midterm and final. Lots of memorization for the two exams, but this is still an easy class to do well in.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I will give Professor Mendez credit for making the subject material interesting. The reason I didn't like this class was because of the busy work. I found the 2 page response papers each week to be a waste of time. This is one of those classes where you learn the material to pass the test, not to actually learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: TAKE A CLASS WITH HUGO!! reli 104 was super interesting. even though it was for a gen ed, i enjoyed the class a lot! Hugo is super nice and funny at times during the lectures. there is a recitation but all of the TAs are cool. there is a 2 page, double spaced paper due every week but theyre graded pass/fail. gives exact study guides of tests.

Although the subject matter of this class isn't the most interesting, it is a solid choice for a PH credit. Mendez is really likable and funny. Short responses due every week, but they are mostly opinion based. One midterm and a final. Really easy class to manage.

Dr. Mendez is truly passionate about Religious Studies, and though he personally is Catholic, he takes an extreme amount of care in not applying actual religious beliefs to his lectures. Attendance is checked through a forum response to every lecture, but it is worth it because he reads every single one of them and responds in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Mendez's passion for religious studies and the historical approach. Analyzing ancient texts can get boring or confusing, but he makes it relatable and approachable. He is always willing to listen to students and honest-to-God reads each forum post in order to make sure we understand the concept. Very funny and relatable, easy to follow.

Really great Professor. Does speak a little fast but he's very interesting. Really cares about his students and wants to make sure everyone understands. Not condescending about your religious beliefs and jokes a lot during class. Overall 10/10.

Professor Mendez is my favorite professor that I have ever had! He is the most genuine person and he cares about each and every one of his students. He's also very open-minded, contrary to other RELI professors that I have taken.

The lectures aren't very helpful, so I just went to class for participation. You're going to have to self study a lot, but the topics covered on the tests are VERY clear, he tells us exactly what kind of questions to know how to do. I basically taught myself everything with the textbook, but the class is really easy to get a good grade in.

MATH 528: This guy is nice, but sometimes he will go off on tangents talking about his research or loosely related topics.. like please just get back to the lesson. Also, that second midterm was extremely difficult since it involved proofs, computer output, and sum/difference trig identities.

Never understood any of his lectures. Rambles a lot, and his class notes are not useful for tests only the homeworks are which he doesn't teach us how to do. Has in-class worksheets so attendence is mandatory but chooses the easiest questions for them. Midterms are strange and not what we do in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The syllabus of his 235 is unreasonable. Too many concepts he wants to cover, and there's even not one main textbook but only his OneNote, which is sometimes super confusing. He always wants to focus on something comprehensive, but it IS the instructor's job to lead students to dive into details all the time. Y'all should take 233 with another Prof

For M528. There are two sections for this course this semester. I was on the waitlist of another section for two months, from November until the waitlist was purged in January. So he was the only option left for me to take 528 with. He couldn't rephrase the concepts taught in 383 clearly. Thankfully this course has a tb, otherwise you'll get lost.
I am very surprised he is allowed to be a professor. The two lectures I went to were agony. Disorganized, confusing, and not at all conductive to learning. Swapped to a different section.

I dropped this class on the first day to switch to a different section. I had a very hard time understanding him. I was confused the entire class period. It took me an hour to realize he was trying to explain how to multiply vectors, a relatively easy concept. He also danced around questions when asked, instead of just giving a straight answer.

His class is super disorganized and boring. Though he makes the exams reasonable and easy, the contents of 235 are still heavy. He always emphasized on 'big picture', which sometimes confusing and useless. Overall, good teacher but not fitting to teach.

Professor Huang is caring and kind, however, the class was extremely disorganized. Attendance isn't mandatory, but all the answers to the worksheets are in the lecture. I think we spent barely a week on the last few topics, and it made up a good amount of the final. Be ready to learn things on your own and go to tutoring/office hours.
Nice professor and very willing to provide help.

Advantages: fast grading, cheat sheets, extra credit, and quick responses on Piazza. The instructor offered insights into the practical application of concepts in research or hints about future advanced courses. While the class was disorganized, keeping up with lectures made the exams manageable. The concepts were challenging but explained easily.

Caring and intelligent man. But I'm not sure, with his level of intelligence, that he quite grasps what an undergrad is capable of. First exam average was ~95, next two and the final average were around 50-70. There were topics that were on the final that we never discussed in class. Prepare to self-teach (though office hours can also be helpful).
I LOVE THIS PROFESSOR HE IS AWESOME AND SUCH A COOOL DUDE LOVE THE PIAZZA. THE GOAT OF THE MATH DEPARTMENT.
He is so sweet and caring. Highly recommended.

He's a kind, smart guy. However this class is pretty difficult, and very exam heavy. He graded the final really kindly, but there were also questions that didn't resemble anything we did in class. Not the most organized class, and you may have no clue what is going on. Fantastic dude, difficult class. Achievable for a 500 level math, but hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super nice teacher! Though his lecture might be somewhat disorganised, he gave us many chance to improve our grades (i.e. replace the lowest midterm and 2 extra credits). Math235 is mixed by Math232/233/347/383, therefore it is not easy to catch up everything at first. But if you put some effort you should get at least an A- (this semester >40%)

Professor Huang is extremely knowledgeable and willing to help. However, his lectures are disorganized and hard to follow. He often assumed prior knowledge of material from courses that were not formal prerequisites. The difficulty of the final exam did not reflect that of the Midterm and HW's (which he told us would adequately prepare us).

Professor Huang is one of the nicest and smartest people I've met. However, he does not know how to teach. His lectures are disorganized and impossible to follow. You can get a good grade since homework, lab, and attendance combine for 40%. If you want to learn anything though do not take this class. You will have to teach yourself everything.

SUPER SWEET!! Really kind professor who cares about his students and wants to ensure they understand the material. His lectures are slightly unorganized but going to office hours and tutoring helps a bunch. Replaces the lowest midterm with final and drops lowest worksheet/lab/hw grade!!

You have to review heavily outside of class and hope for the best going into exams since his lectures and notes make absolutely no sense. But, he is a very kind professor and is accessible and willing to help.

Very very nice guy. cares about his student. unfortunately a bad teacher. his intellect is too high to dumb down his steps down for us undergrads. Doesn't write down all the steps and does all problems in general terms. no concrete examples done with numbers (aside from some worksheet/HW problems) until the midterm.

Best professor ever! lecture is a bit unorganized but just go to his oh, large curve and easy homework, drop the lowest midterm replaced by final, he will explain questions patiently after class, choose him without doubt

Although attendance isn't mandatory you kinda have to go to every lecture to understand what was going on. The lecture notes are not very helpful and often make no sense. The lab is basically a jupyter notebook introductory class, which I recommend attending even though you can do the lab assignment without.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: best professor, just take his class

Extremely disorganized. Lectures were confusing and unhelpful in learning course content--he spent a lot of time going over course topics at a high level but didn't know how to explain many concepts. He made simple concepts more complex than they should've been. Tests were pretty fair. There's definitely worse out there in the math department.

Take Linear with Jingfang. TRUST. Adeslsteinson is so hard and everyone in know in that class is struggling. jinfang exams are really fair and he is overall a sweet dude. he also curved the second exam. TAKE IT WITH HIM

Huang was a decent enough professor. It was the first time this class was offered so it was a little bit disjointed, but the class in and of itself was not too bad, and office hours were very helpful especially before exams. Generous curve and opportuninities to get free points/extra credit. Most of the content can be studies using online resources

Professor Huang is one of the nicest professors I've had at UNC. He really wants you to do well. He was always available outside class (his average piazza response time for the whole semester was under an hour). MATH235 was unorganized and confusing at times, because he wasn't following a set curriculum, and it was new. Overall good experience.

First time this course was offered at UNC and was very disorganized. Professor Huang is very caring and accessible outside of class, fast grader, but uses a lot of technical language off the bat and it could be difficult at times to understand him in lecture. Allowed students to have 10 hand-written cheat sheets per midterm and 30 on final.

I didn't think he was the best at teaching things and it lead me to teach myself almost all the concepts outside of class through online videos. His tests were hard IMO and I've heard from friends and people around me the other linear professor is better, adalstein or something.

Professor Huang is one of nicest professor that I've had at UNC. He was always available outside of class though the piazza and office hours, and is very quick to reply. He is however, incredibly unorganized. It might be because the class was new this semester, but the lectures and notes were almost impossible to follow. Tests hard.

Prof. Huang is a very nice guy and he really cares about his students' success; his exams had generous curves and all of his grading was very fair. However, he was extremely unorganized, both logistically and in the classroom. It was near impossible to understand what was going on in his lectures and assignment deadlines were changed constantly.
Best of the best, the only thing is the lectures are either 8 or 9 AM and that's TOOOOOO early!

Very good prof, give alot of help, reply to email and piazza really fast!!!!! Super fast grader!!!!!(our finals finish at 7pm, he gave the exam back to us at 3am the next day, which is like 8hrs later) really care about his student. Alot of curves on exams as well!

Dr. Huang does his best to make sure every student succeeds. 2 of the 3 midterms were "curved" (more like test corrections), and he would do his best to answer every question. Responsive on Piazza. Recitation focused on Python application of concepts. Learn how to "drive the car" and apply mathematical concepts, as he says.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The best, kindest, and most accessible math professor you can ever have at UNC. The course is an easy A and super inspirational. Office Hour is brilliant. Take him!

He is very nice, but he is extremely unorganized. No one ever knows what's going on and his lectures make no sense. One of our midterms average was a 50 and he barely curved it. The homework is very difficult and his lectures don't prepare you at all for the homework or tests.

Professor Huang is a kind-hearted person more than willing to assist you when you have questions. The exams are not horrible. In fact, a majority of the exam questions are related to the homework assignments. There are also 3 group projects that may or may not be time-consuming depending on your previous programming experience. Take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Kindest professor at UNC in terms of attitude, responsiveness to Piazza questions, test difficulty, and grading. Helpful and patient in OH. Fastest grader at UNC (final released in 9 hours). Homework questions feel different from other classes' but you do learn a lot. Highly recommend Prof. Huang for any class.
Very smart professor, office hours can help a lot. Getting the big picture idea is very important in class.

Professor Huang is really a great guy. He is friendly and caring. His tests are not hard, and he didn't give us too much homework to do. But make sure to understand the worksheets and check if there is anything you don't understand. The only thing is that he didn't explain things well enough. However, his office hour is useful.

Had a virtual option but clearly did not want students to actually use it. Recorded his (often blank) computer screen instead of the board. Messy work during lecture, which are impossible to refer back to when studying because of the disorganization. Took off a lot of points for stupid stuff on exams.

He didn't round up my 92.73 after my mom had a stroke and it was my 21st birthday. Horrible professor, you have to learn everything by yourself. Class isn't hard but he doesn't care about his students

Prof Huang was super sweet, but a disorganized lecturer. I went to every class and then watched the Gilbert Strang MIT videos which were super helpful. I ended up learning a lot, the exams were very fair and homework was not too excessive. Just go to class, understand worksheet problems, ask questions if you are confused, and you will do fine!

Prof Huang is really nice guy and always ready to help. Unfortunately, his lectures are unclear, so you'll need to learn to solve problems on your own. A big advantage of taking 347 with him is that his exams after midterm 1 are open book/note and allow computer tools, so you can easily prepare and don't need to worry about computations.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I swear this guy was one of the worst lecturers I've ever had. He's a nice person but is not made for teaching. I had to self study a lot, but at least the recitations were helpful.

Take Professor Huang for Math 566! He is one of the most caring professors I ever had in the math department. Understand the "big picture" he gives in class and do the homework, then you are ready for an A.

Prof. Huang is 100% the nicest and most caring professor you'll encounter. He is willing to share his time with students outside official hours despite being busy, and he is the fastest grader at UNC (released final grades within 15 hrs). He grades leniently, has an insane work ethic and is insanely smart.
nice professor! drop 4 homework instead of 2!
Really nice professor
Not a lot of new material covered in lecture, the recitations were much more helpful.
Professor Huang was very kind and really cared about his students. His lectures aren't super clear so you have to basically teach yourself.

Prof Huang is nice & wants you to succeed; his teaching style just didn't work for me. I ended up learning the material from Youtube & Khan Academy. Thankfully, he's a forgiving grader--curves tests & drops lowest quiz grades.
Wonderful man. Hard class. A lot of it was concept-based so be prepared to teach yourself most of the material prior to the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Huang is a very genuine and caring professor however this man was not made to lecture. I learned all the material through youtube videos or through the textbook. I would only take this class with Huang if math comes easily to you or if you prefer learning the material in your own time. He is a lenient grader and responds to emails quickly.

The textbook CARRIES; seriously have never relied on it more for any other class. I really did try to get something out of Professor Huang's lectures but eventually gave up. He's a real nice guy-- very lenient in terms of extensions and grading --but is more of a big-picture lecturer and I learned the hard way that that's not for me.

I ended up teaching myself most of content from the textbook. With that being said, Professor Huang is a genuine person, and he cares about his students. As others have said, his lectures are somewhat difficult to follow, but it's still possible to learn from them if you stay focused. Ask questions in office hours. Solid choice.

The class can be self-taught with the textbook, homework, and before class videos. That's what I ended up doing. His lectures are very difficult to follow so I would recommend a different prof but you will live if you have to take him. He is also a really nice and genuine guy. Tests were reasonable. 3 tests  33% of grade and the final exam 36%.

So kind and genuinely cares his students. However, lectures are hard to follow (he is more a research guy), so plz attend office hours (ironically he explains things better in office hours than in classes) and teach yourself before each class. Easy grader as he curves grades and gives extra points. Not so bad choice for 233 but stay highly prepared

He seems like a nice guy but the lectures are kinda useless. He clearly knows & understands everything and is passionate, but his lessons are hard to follow. Learning the topics by doing the homeworks and taking notes on the methods there worked better for me than trying to learn from the lectures.
Very nice guy and always willing to help. Exams straightforward if you understand the homework. Went through a lot of material but only the main ideas were necessary to do well.

Jingfang is very helpful and wants us to succeed. Pay attention in class and focus on what he says are the most important "big picture ideas" and you'll be fine. He is super accessible through email and has office hours frequently. Honestly, he was really great and this class was interesting.

Very sweet guy and very accessible. However, not a very good lecturer. He does have an accent that is sometimes difficult to understand but the way he teaches just does not make much sense. I recommend just watching Gilbert Strang lectures and reading the textbook. A lot of your grade is homework so getting a good grade isn't that hard.

Dr. Huang's teaching style did not vibe with me at all. I had to do most of my learning outside of the classroom. But, I will say he is possibly the most wholesome profesor I've ever had. He genuinely cares about the material and making sure you enjoy and learn it too. I wish I had appreicated his lectures but I just didn't.

As others have said here, Dr. Huang is an incredibly nice man and wants his students to do as well as possible. However, his lectures are scattered and he often taught the material assuming the students had watched other (better) lectures on the same material. I hope this is just a symptom of online teaching but I can't say he taught very much.

Prof. Huang is a very kind professor but is exceptionally poor at actually teaching material. The entire structure of the class is extremely disorganized, from the overall structure of the class all the way down to the organization of each individual lecture. Going to the lectures doesn't really aid learning; I ended up teaching myself everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is horrible. I have not completed the course but literally. worst lecturer I have ever had. We have had eight lectures and I can positively say I have not learned a single thing. We did review basic algebra. SO frustrating. He is very nice but should not be teaching.

Professer Huang is very caring and wants to help you learn. His lectures can be pretty hard to follow, but he makes up for that with his willingness to discuss questions and assignments in office hours. He is very transparent about his desire for you to succeed.
A bad professor with heavy work and involved exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Huang is really a good professor. MATH 566 is a tough class but he made it very accessible for everyone to understand the concepts. The homework is very challenging and the workload is pretty heavy. But if you just follow his instructions in class and you can make it. The test is heavily related to the homework and the final is bit challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He gives a lots of homework assignments and group projects. Heavy workload and tough grader. He holds office hours which is kind of helpful.

His lectures run too fast and he gives way too much homework and group projects. His office hours are helpful but the lectures contain just too much content. Quizzes and exams are tricky but not very difficult. He is a nice person though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: He had all his notes and sample codes uploaded to SAKAI before class. In each class, he just spoke to his notes and assigned lots of homework. His homework is really struggling because you may not have a clear direction to start with. He always likes to play tricks on tests or quizzes. If you are not a fan of programming, do not take this.

Jingfang is a very caring man. He is very accommodating, but his lectures are awful. His tests are really easy, but he does not prepare you for the common final. The final is ridiculously hard for MATH231 and counts for 40%. Jingfang usually curves the grades at the end and bumps half a letter grade. Good guy, eh teacher.
Tests are easy, but the common final is hard.

I very much enjoyed this class and Jingfang. This may be credited to the fact I already took AP Calc in high school. However, if you stay on top of homework and teaching yourself what you don't understand, you'll do excellent. Class attendance is optional, highly recommend attending recitation tho! Only major downfall to the class was the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Huang, although not the best lecturer, is extremely fair in terms of grading, amount of homework, number of quizzes etc. There isn't much homework and you have to do it. He often gave us practice exams with really similar questions to the tests. Would recommend him! Must be willing to teach some material to yourself!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is the one of the best professors I have ever met. He provides many chance to help you get A. He provides a lot of examples both in the class and online. The tricks for A is to do the online Pearson questions. His exams are much easier than his sample exam questions. I want to study with him for all my math courses but I know it is impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Sweet guy, lenient grader. However, he was not meant to teach. His lectures are hard to follow as he goes on frequent tangents. Explains lots of topics that end with "you don't need to know this for this class". I received a good grade but I learned nothing from lectures, rather it was self teaching and visiting TA office hours that helped most.

Jingfang is truely a kind man. He is probably one of the only professors who cares about your grade at UNC. However, It is very hard to understand when Jingfang speaks, his accent is so heavy. Jingfang really wants your GPA to be good and curves tests when the whole class bombs. Jingfang occasionally puts smiley faces in his emails.

This was a pretty average class. It's easy to get 100s on homework, but if you don't understand it, it'll probably be on the test. The good thing is that he did a test redo, dropped lowest grades, and gives multiple attempts on some quizzes. However, you will rely mostly on textbooks and videos to figure it out if you haven't learned calc before.

Overall he is a very nice man who is willing to work with you on anything you need. He answers emails fast and in many cases is willing to let you redo assignment if you misunderstood the criteria. His lectures are extremely boring because he is so smart. Make sure you have the discipline to do your work and learn the concepts yourself. (I didn't)

Prof. Huang is a very smart and nice man, but is a mediocre instructor. He constantly jumps around trying to cover multiple sections in a day, and gives very awkward answers to questions. However, he is VERY lenient. He let us redo our 2nd exam over fall break and dropped our 4 lowest hw grades which is nearly unheard of at UNC. Overall, he's ok.

Jingfang is one of the smartest people I have ever met but he was not destined to be a professor. He cares about his students, puts in a lot of effort and adds curves to keep our GPAs up but he is just awful at being a professor. Overall, if you do the homework and try hard on the tests, you'll do about as good as you expect you will in calculus.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: He is hard to understand in class but sometimes gives us two attempts on tests and warns us about what exactly will be on the quizzes. I only go to class about once a week and I'm doing okay.

Math 547. Horrible lecturer. Can't even understand what he is trying to say. He is not so-called "open book, notes, computer". Rather, he allows unlimited numbers of cheat sheets. So I end up with copying every single page of my textbook when I prepare for the exam. But if you don't mind wasting your time copying the textbook, you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He is a decent lecturer. It's a hard class, and he only wants to focus on the big picture-- this is evident on his exams, that are open laptop/open notes. Go to class, do the readings/homework, and you'll be fine. Extra credit up to 5% on final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Pretty good professor, really passionate about history and engages class in interesting discussions about the dark(er) history of Warren County. Lectures were boring at the beginning, but they've been getting more interesting, and class can get super interactive. Lots of group projects, but he provides a lot of help. Overall, chill class!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Glenn is very articulate, and expresses his thoughts elegantly. However, the lectures in class dragged a lot, leaving the class disengaged. There is not much homework in this class, but it wasn't easy to get an A. To be successful in this course, you need to attend class, participate, and put a lot of effort into the few papers that you have.

Very nice guy and cares a lot about his students, but it's difficult to get through his lectures. He was not very organized with the class, and in our group projects we never knew what we were supposed to be doing. Do not recommend the class for someone with a short attention span.

really nice guy. Lectures can be boring. Class is chill. Though it was called roots of rap and hip hop, hip hop wasnt really mentioned. Learned about black vernacular poetry which was still cool. Grades easily if you try and you can persuade grade if its not your ideal if he likes you.

Dr. Hofweber is a spectacular lecturer. He does a great job of getting you to think about things in a really abstract way, yet maintains your attention. His class is very lecture heavy, but it is easy to follow along.
I originally thought the lectures would have been a lot more interesting than they actually were. The recitations were fun; basically just talking with a group about various topics.

This class was enjoyable to attend, but if you are looking for an easy A, this may not be the class for you. Your final grade depends on your TA, which may hurt you in the end. As someone who studies a lot and dedicated a lot of energy to the class, my grade wasn't reflective of my effort.
Incredible lectures if you are interested in the topic. Essays and tests are graded by TA's, so you just have to hope you get a lenient one. Great class and I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took the class originally just for the FC credit but ended up really enjoying Dr. Hofweber's lectures. The difficulty of the class really depends on your TA but mine (Mattesich) did an excellent job in recitations and was also really kind to give us study guides for the midterm and final which is all you need to do a good job on them both.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Phil 143 was a pretty interesting class. The midterm and final were pretty easy if you just go to class and take some notes. I didn't do any of the readings and still did well on both since he brings up any important points from the readings in class. Go to your TA's office hours to ask about your main argument on your paper and you will do fine.

The class is easy if you have a good TA. Attendance wasn't mandatory in lectures but recitations was. I didn't go to class after midterm and was still able to do well afterwards (review powerpoints and readings). You're only graded on 4 things (two 5-page papers, midterm, and final). Make sure to follow what your TA wants and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture was boring, but you need to attend to understand the obscure slides he posted. Your grades are composed of two 5-page papers, a midterm, and a final, so your grades depend pretty much on your TAs. Just do your readings and participate in recitation discussion, and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not think the professor was very fair overall. I had a 100% all semester and received positive feedback on all 5 reading responses, but then got a 7/10 on our final paper which brought my grade down to a B+. It seems unfair to not have received constructive feedback throughout the class to help me with my final paper.

the professor was great overall but the structure of the class was not good, we were graded on very few things but the work load was easy. it has no final but there is a final paper that is very hard and is 40 % of ur grade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great teacher who encourages lots of in class discussion. Doesn't take attendance but participation definitely aids in comprehension of the readings. 5 one page papers, one final paper, and one partner presentation all pretty evenly spread out. Overall just a great teacher and cool guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Interesting lectures. Hofweber is a stickler for attendance and only gives recorded lectures to those with an official excused absence. Do the readings and attend class and you'll get an A.

This class was a pretty easy A. The class was graded by only two papers and the final, but the papers were pretty easy if you followed the format the TAs asked for or got feedback, and the first one had a rewrite option. I didn't go to lectures for the second half and the final was still easy, I just reread the readings. Lectures were boring though

The class is so interesting and taught really well. Prof. Hofweber is such a great lecturer and the readings never felt like "too much". The papers were great and the TA's really helped structure them. The class isn't hard at all, but it does have readings, papers, and weekly recitation discussions. I would highly recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Your grade is completely on 3 assignments. The TAs all grade these assignments differently. People can get very different grades dependent on your TA. And the class has so many readings.

Dr. Hofweber was an amazing professor. It is clear that he is passionate about what he teaches and he makes the lectures extremely interesting. He's also really funny. Your TA will determine your grade in the class, so make sure to reach out and show them that you care about your grades on the 2 papers and ask them ANY questions you might have.

This class was not hard at all and lectures were at 8 am, so not everyone always showed up. However, your entire grade is based off three assignments that are graded by one of his TA's and it is very clear that some TA's graded assignments with much higher expectations than others. Feedback took forever and wasn't very helpful.

Prof. Hofweber is great! If the class wasnt at 8 I definitely would have gone to every lecture. Even still the final was very easy despite only doing the readings and going to recitation. The lectures were interesting and his accent is very fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kind professor who makes changes in order to be more lenient to students. Took off stressful lectures from final exam content in light of mental health awareness issues. Lectures can be somewhat stale. If you go to office hours and speak with TAs, you will get a great paper grade. You can rewrite 1st paper. Put in the effort and you'll get an A/A-.

No homework/quizzes, however, grade is based only on two papers and a final. Hofweber was awesome and uploaded his lectures on Sakai so missing wasn't that bad. The papers were not bad imo but I like writing. You have to understand the reading pretty well to do them though. Ask him about his chickens
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Hofweber did a very good job teaching the material. Some topics were more dull than others, but he tried his best during the lectures to make it interesting. The class had very few grades, just two 5 page essays and a final exam. Overall a very good professor, I'd recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are dull but the overall course is easy. Only 3 grades all semester so make sure you take his papers seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Hofweber is really passionate about his topics, which makes the class super interesting. He's always very thorough and a good explainer. This class only required two papers, which were moderately difficult to write if you don't know the material really well (5 pages though!) and a final exam. A good GenEd to take.

Awesome class on an interesting topic, I took it to get my Philosophy credit. Hofweber is very knowledgeable on the subject and his TAs are fantastic too. Only two 5-page essays plus an open notes exam, easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really fascinating lectures! There is no textbook and the readings arent too difficult. The entire class is 2 papers and a final exam so you have to perform well on the papers to do well. Attending the lectures is really important for writing the papers. The TAs are extremely helpful for this class.

There are only 2 papers and a final for the grades in the class. The lectures are interesting and the reading is manageable. I really enjoyed the lectures and recitations. He is veryyy nice, changed our final to accommodate for students!! Def recommend for a phil credit

No textbook but there are weekly readings that are very manageable. Grade is based upon 2 papers and final exam, but you get a rewrite for 1st paper and the TA's are very accessible. Lectures are interesting, recitations are helpful. I highly recommend this class for a PH gen ed.

The lectures are really interesting but the entire class is graded on 2 5-page papers and one final exam. The TAs are amazing and give really good feedback for the papers. They are also very reasonable and understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Seem to be a nice person but...I did not feel students' opinions and feedback are respected by him. Ineffective teaching method. Repeat readings in lectures. Meaningless group discussion. One of the worst professors I have ever met. Ruined the topic. Super regret about taking this uncomfortable class.
A really awesome professor, very caring and enthusiastic. He is definitely one of my favorite professors at UNC! His lectures are very interesting and he is super nice!

My favorite professor by far. His lectures are smart. First, he would introduced new topics broadly and encouraged thought. Then, he would explain the papers in depth using the new vocabulary. His class focused mainly on the material and not on ANY busy work. If you like philosophy and thinking for yourself, then he's the best.

Seemed like a fun guy and engaging teacher, but it was just impossible for that to get across in a 200 person lecture. Only 3 grades all semester, and I would zone out in the lectures I didn't skip. Learned way more in the weekly recitation. Only recommend if its a smaller class where it can be more personable and one on one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I appreciate that Thomas lectured on different philosophical topics than ancient philosophy, it was more modern and applicable. His lectures had flashes of excellence, but were often dull. It would be impossible not to zone out a little. Overall he is very personable, but beware of the grading criteria with the 2 essays and final (straight forward)

Prof Hofweber is a highly charismatic and passionate guy. For PHIL 101 there two 5 page papers and final (each 33% of your grade). I was one of a few students that actually attended lectures, and it was probably a waste of time. Everything is in the readings, several of which were taken from modern philosophical works (1900s on).

I was excited about philosophy before, but this kind of put a damper on that. The readings were somewhat interesting, but I found lectures and recitations pretty dull as much as I wanted to stay engaged. The grading criteria (2 difficult papers and a final) seems a bit extreme for an intro course. I really wanted to like this class.

Don't take this for the PH credit. Only 3 grades: 2 papers, 1 final. First paper you can re-do b/c most students don't do well. Attendance/participation do not count. Professor talks a lot in lecture, but doesn't really say much. My TA was slightly stronger at explaining, but hard to listen to at 8 am on a Friday. Don't really need to attend.

Discussions were basically student lead, by a student presentation every week; He did not follow the regular teacher to student lecture style. For some this could be confusing, because half of the time students don't know what they're talking about either. 50% of the grade is determined by peer evaluations, so be careful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Take this if u need a PH credit. Super easy class as long as u do the reading and put in some effort on the weekly responses. Don't need to show up to class as he doesn't take attendance and its not really necessary. Pretty much a guaranteed A.

Professor Hofweber is an amazing dude. If you put in the effort, you will get a good grade. His class is not an easy A, but if you do the homework just like he shows you in class, you'll do good. He is a great professor, very funny, and cannot recommend enough!

Thomas is very knowledgeable in Philosophy, and does a decent job of conveying complicated ideas to his students. I had him for a FYS so my experience with him would probs be a little different. Easy class that was easy to do badly in because there were only 2 grades and they were moderately difficult papers.

He's not awful but he's not all that great either. The main problem is that the material can be very confusing and the TA's aren't too helpful and neither is the prof, partially that's just because the class is so big though.

He was a horrible explainer and the subject was complicated to begin with. When you asked him for help, he answered you with a question, which was not helpful. Definately not an easy topic and he makes it even harder to understand.

Being German, there are rare occasions where you have to ask him to explain himself, and it can also be difficult sometimes when he explains concepts. Nonetheless, he is a fun, young guy, perfect for teaching this sort of intro course.

She's an amazing professor and is so sweet! She's full of wisdom and really cares about her students! I took the class last year but still have coffee chats with her! Would totally recommend this course--I learned a lot!
Very caring! No exams, just a longer course paper and final paper and other things. Super nice and accommodating. Lots of lectures
She is the best!! I recommend this class to anyone, it was so interesting and she is very flexible with deadlines.

She genuinely loves what she teaches and is very accommodating if you ever need an extension or have to miss a class. All we had to do was write a discussion post each week and create one final paper. There was also a short presentation, but it was only graded by whether you did it or not.

Super manageable class! The only assignments we had were 250 word discussions due at the end of each week, and one 10 page paper due near the end of the semester. There were also 2 quizzes, but as long as you read, you would be fine. Prof. Hudani is super understanding, and wants her students to pass and do well in her class. 100% recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Hudani was great! Very nice! The class covers interesting topics I wouldn't have learned as a biology major. But she allows one unexcused absence, then penalty for further absences. Lots of reading and class is a lecture about the reading and then discussion. She loves to hear from EVERYONE so will have to share something. But recommend!

Hudani is very passionate about her class and is a great lecturer. Her classes are always engaging, and she takes time to know every student. She gives great feedback and fosters a lot of intriguing conversation in class. There is a lot of reading, so be prepared to at least skim the texts before class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Hudani for AAAD as a freshman fall semester of my freshman year, and at first I was intimidated by the class. There are a lot of readings that are unrealistically lengthy but she does a great job at breaking them down in the lectures, so it's okay to skim.
