She is also by far the most caring professor I've had at UNC, especially for MH.

This is the sweetest lady ever, and you can tell that she really wants you to do well. She loves when people ask questions and engage with the content. There is a fair amount of reading each week, but the quizzes on the readings are always open note and open text. Her lectures are interesting, and it feels like a seminar style class.

Prof. Hudani is the sweetest! She is very understanding, gives high quality feedback on every single thing we submit, and is not a difficult grader. She's super accessible and really wants people to succeed - the assignments are not difficult although there can be some dense readings. I would absolutely take another one of her classes!! 10/10
Sweetest and kindest teacher

THIS IS A REVIEW FOR PLAN 576: Her wealth of knowledge seems almost limitless. If you read and engage with the texts and answer her equally interesting discussion questions, you will learn something new every class. She is an incredibly sweet person and will always go the extra mile when you ask a question.

Dr. Hudani was wonderful. I learned so much in her class, it was pretty engaging! The readings could sometimes be dense, but she was understandable. She also receives criticism and feedback very well. All it takes is a meeting or quick conversation with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I learned a great deal from this class! There was a lot of reading, but she did her best to be understanding and responded to our feedback, including about the quizzes. Would definitely recommend.

At one point she assigned over 80 pages of reading for one class period. Quizzes entirely based on the readings (not classes) and focused on specific details rather than main ideas. She ended up dropping the lower quiz grade when we complained, but it soured me on her class. She seems nice otherwise and class was ultimately easy, but be aware.

Caring teacher that is seriously invested in student wellbeing. Won't cold call and if no one raises their hands to answer a question, moves on. Kind of a pushover in that way? No huge penalty to not doing the readings; I would have gotten more out of the class if weekly forum posts required me to skim readings and not just answer from lecture.

This class was mainly discussion based, so it was interesting to hear differing opinions on certain topics. She did not hush anyone and wanted everyone to participate well. I think if you just do the forums, talk in class, and work on the final paper (which is not graded harshly at all), you should get an easy A.

She cares about her students in and outside the classroom. She constantly checks in on us and our mental health. The class consists of a lot of long readings, but they are not too hard to understand. The class is very discussion heavy and there is a weekly forum post about a reading. We did not have a midterm and our final was a 10 page paper.

Weekly readings and sometimes videos that you read and then discuss in class. I have bad anxiety and don't like to talk unless I'm spoken to. She seems very understanding and doesn't force me to share my thoughts which I appreciate. She checks up on students, and sends great feedback on homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I love Prof. Harry, his class was fun and engaging. He grades kind of strictly, where you have to go above and beyond in discussion and reading posts to get an A, so maybe ask what he expects for that. Other than that, learned a lot in the class.
He's a really great professor. He's pretty funny which makes the class enjoyable. He's obviously really knowledgeable and skilled at what he does, but still very modest and approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Phenomenal professor, take his class if you get a chance

Professor Harry is new to the United States, but he is a kind, funny, and passionate instructor. He is understanding with his students, perhaps due to being a younger professor, and he tries hard to be friendly and engaging. There's a lot of reading, but you can get through it. Make sure to participate in class. He is a hard grader, but not unfair
My GOATT!!!!!!

Dr. Hansen was great! He made physics easier to understand for such a hard and standardized class. He co-taught my section and did an amazing job. He was accessible, caring, and took questions well. Highly recommend taking physics with him

Physics is co taught and pretty standardized, but Dr Hansen is very fair and understanding. He is also easy to talk to and get to know and seems like he cares about his students. If you truly understand the material his tests are socreable, especially in comparison to tests written mainly under other professors.

Professor Cherednik was a nice and funny professor. He has an extremely thick Russian accent that can take a while to understand. He is too smart to teach a class such as MATH231. Had a weird grading scale that ended up making a lot of people have their final exam as 80% of the final grade. Overall, I would recommend with someone else if possible!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cherednik was kind and good with email, but was difficult. His accent was thick and hard to understand since he didn't wear a mic. The homework was easy, had multiple attempts, but the exams did not reflect his lectures. If you take it, use CramBetter; it helped me out a ton! Overall, really really nice guy but really hard to keep-up-with :(

He has a very heavy accent but you will get used to it. He is a funny guy and he kind of goes all over the place while teaching. In my opinion he is too smart to be teaching 231 to the point where he glosses over the importance of certain subjects.

Dr. Cherednik is a kind and caring professor. Unfortunately, he has a super thick Russian accent, so learning discrete mathematics from him is a challenge. He is very clear about what to prepare for the exams and is very understanding. The class, especially the homework, is complex, but he makes himself accessible and his notes are helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It was a very difficult class but Professor Cherednik provided comprehensive preparation for each exam, which helped tremendously.

Do not take this course unless it is required. The professor has a very strong Russian accent, which makes lectures difficult to understand. On the first day, I was completely lost and could not follow what he said. However, he reviews material for the midterms except the first take-home exam. Later midterms usually have about four questions total.

Friendly personality, but is hard to learn from. Our first to in-class tests were very fair, but the final was very intense. If this professor is your only choice don't completely despair, but get ready to put in a little work.
Professor Cherednik is a very nice guy and definitely wants his students to succeed, but his lectures are very hard to follow, so be ready to teach yourself a lot of content.

If I wasn't paying really close attention to lectures, it was very hard for me to understand what he was saying ( thick russian accent). He does seem like a nice and caring person. The final was so much harder than any prep material we were given, and everyone seemed to agree.

Guy has a heavy Russian accent, so if you're bad with accents, I wouldn't recommend. Took about half the semester, but I understand him now. He's alright at explaining things, but I spent all class looking at his slideshow and following the explanations on there, not him actually doing it.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU DON'T HAVE TO!!!  Extremely smart, but thinks you should be on the same level as him. He WILL test you on things not covered in class. He 's extremely inequitable, never listening to my remarks about how I was one of few people in class that never cheated. No duh the students that use chatgpt are doing better than me.

Lectures are often confusing, but he breaks down the problems that will be on each exam the class before. One of the easier 500 electives for math. Lots of extra credit on the exams, so as long as you come to class it is very straightforward to get an A. The homeworks (worth 10%) are much harder than anything you see on an exam and can be daunting.

He's not a great instructor, and he's bad at answering questions, but he's nice and wants you to succeed. He has extra credit built into all of his assignments (e.g., there are 28 points available on a test, but it's only graded out of 20). The material is also interesting when it makes sense, but there are weird difficulty spikes here and there.

Super smart and nice professor. Ridiculously hard content. I'm a calc tutor and still struggled with the concepts. If you're going to take this course, you're going to need a good grasp of math - it's not for the lighthearted, but it's not that hard to get an A. Gives hints on HW, fast email response time, take home final. GO TO THE FINAL REVIEW.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ivan is a genius but impossible to understand in lectures. Every time I went to class or asked a question, I came out feeling more confused. Thankfully, the final grade only counted the last exam (take-home) and final group project, and the final had bonus credit which was very helpful. Homework takes forever, don't take if you don't know math.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TERRIBLE PROFESSOR! Incoherent lectures with random thoughts. Course prerequisites were high school algebra but the class was harder than Calc 3 and Differential Equations, which I took at UNC. Despite a grade of a 90, I received B+. Homework was impossible with little support. Only those who devoted their lives to this class got As. Please avoid!

TERRIBLE PROFESSOR! Incoherent lectures with random thoughts. Course prerequisites were high but the class was harder than Calc 3 and Differential Equations. Despite a 90 score, received B+. Homework was impossible with little support. Only those who devoted their lives got As. Avoid this class!

Great mathematician, ok lecturer. For a class that only requires high school algebra, it is significantly harder than one would initially expect. His lectures are fast paced if no one tells him to slow down, and he talks with a heavy accent. Lots of extra credit on a final that's worth half your grade makes it pretty easy to get an A.

Professor Cherednik is sweet and caring, but this class was nearly impossible. This class should not be a first-year seminar, much less one without prerequisites. The class required calculus, statistics, and physics knowledge. It's doable with hours of research spent on homework, but it will not be an easy A. Prof. Cherednik has a thick accent.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ivan is very nice, but the content was not explained well. Spent hours trying to comprehend what was in the textbook so I could get the homework problems correct. He responds to emails very quick and there is extra credit on the final, but this math was far too advanced for a first-year seminar. Not as easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was a very tough grader. There was extra credit options on tests, but that was for a reason. Tests were so difficult that he had to give us the built in curve or else everyone in the class would have failed. The positive reviews are from the .1% of students who spend hours upon hours just studying for this one class. DO NOT TAKE!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ivan is an amazing and great person, however, as someone who went into this course thinking they could skate by with the prerequisite, which was high school algebra, I STRUGGLED with this course. If you are a fan of computer science and discreet math, you will probably love this course, but beware that Ivan does have a THICK accent. Love him tho :)

Many opportunities to get extra points (quiz 14/10, midterm 28/20, final 70/60). It is very hard to understand him not just the accent but also his logic. Content is self teachable but WILL take time, his notes is more like a guide use textbook. He provides study guides for each test that includes ALL type of question that will be on the test.

Easiest MATH elective, many opportunities to get extra points (grades 28/20 for midterms, 70/60 on final). I never went to class because it was so hard to understand him, but the content isn't that difficult and most of the questions he asked you can teach to yourself. If you need an A, take his class.

If you need a math elective, take this course. Exams are 80% of your grade. He will tell you the exact problem type for each exam and solve examples. Grading wise, he put 28 points on a midterm, scored it out of 20, and put the remaining 8 points towards your final grade. Same with the final (70pts scored out of 60, i.e 10pts extra credit).

Prof Cherednik is a wonderful human being who is a math wizard! But I'm ngl it was really hard to follow him in lecture. He is really approachable though so do not hesitate to reach out to him for help. Promise it will be worth it, this man has his grading criteria set so that everyone who tries can pass with an A. Hw due every other week.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Cherednik is the sweetest man ever. He's very passionate about math, and cares about his students. That said, taking his class was scary. There were few homework assignments, a project, and an exam. He gives as much credit as possible, but the material is very difficult to comprehend.

Professor Cherednik is a very caring and smart professor. Although he introduces topics as if students have previous experience in the subject, if you simply ask, he will try his hardest to break down the concept to make it easier to understand. He has a rather strong accent, but he allows you to ask questions about HW and the take-home final.

Final is 60% (tests are 2x15%), but he tells you the exact topics that will be on the tests during review days, so attend those. Class attendance is severely lacking because it's hard to follow along, but he's super smart (check his Wikipedia), kind, and quirky. 548 is the easiest math elective at UNC but it's nontrivial. Lot of opportunity for EC.

Ivan is one of the most caring professors you will ever have at UNC. The math was incredibly complicated, but Ivan made it simple and allowed us to see some very interesting math concepts. Combinatorics involves difficult math, but this first-year seminar was very fun. He reviews right before the final and basically tells you what is on it!

Other reviews of this course are no joke. The material often feels absolutely impossible to understand. Despite this, Ivan is an amazing person that is always willing to go out of his way to help make sure you have enough knowledge to complete assignments. The work is typically a few questions due every other week, so it is definitely manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: In this class, there is one homework assignment every two weeks but they each take a good bit of time. There is a final exam and group project that are more important, and you are set up to do well. However, the professor can be hard to understand at times. He answers all emails quickly whenever help on home assignments are needed.

Cherednik is here for a good time. Being a seminar, he wants you to try something new and wants you to do well. Lectures are hard to understand, homework is every other week, but don't expect to understand it all. Keep up with the work and you'll be fine. He'll give you homework help if needed, but this class is not for the weak.

Cherednik is a super cool guy and 548 is the easiest math class at UNC. He really wants you to succeed and makes you feel so welcome to ask questions during lecture. His class is a bit too easy; he gives you similar questions to the exams so its very easy to not learn as much and just study for the test. Talks fast so ask him to slow down!

Ivan is the only math professor that wants you to do well. He is very smart, often hard to follow; the content is very hard, but he genuinely tries to set you up for success. You can do well if you put in effort. His accent is thick but understandable. Heavy final (60% or more), but he reviews everything. HW is biweekly, pretty reasonable for math.

Ivan is one of my favorite math professors at UNC (and I've seen a lot). He cares about student comprehension, teaches in a practical and non high-brow way, and clearly understands the material. This isn't to say it's an easy class, but if you try and participate then you won't get a bad grade.

Professor Cherednik is a really awesome person, clearly super smart, and cares about his students. The material can be tough and hard to follow, but he provides reviews before the midterm and final that will save you. He is also helpful in office hours
Combinatorics with Cherednik is the easiest math class at Carolina. Great class for an easy A but not a great class for learning.

Math62H is ridiculously easy to get an A. Material is impossible to understand, but the final is take home and the projects are easy after help from the GRC. Homework is graded but not factored into final grade unless it helps your grade. Ivan is so smart it is mind boggling, however his accent and random trains of thought make it tough to learn in

Thought I was doomed because the class is broken up into a 30% midterm and 60% final. However, there's a lot of extra credit, and Cherednik  gives "progress points." You'll get a much better grade than you think you deserve. Class was typically useless because of the incomprehensible Russian accent, but the reviews are basically the test answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Cherednik flies through each lecture and uses every bit of the 75 minutes going over the material. I felt as if he jumped into each subject as if the students already had some knowledge of it, which for me was not the case. The homework is biweekly and very manageable, and the final is take home. Cherednik is a nice guy always eager to help out.

He is clearly a genius and expects you to be on his level. His class is unconventional but totally worth it. A good course will leave you with a new perspective on the world, and I can assure you he will have that effect on you if you can work past the comprehension barrier.

Comprehension is an issue (accent + flies through content), very cordial. Material is tough but the bi-weekly homework is manageable, Final (50% of grade) is take-home w/ a bonus question. Final research group project (30% of grade) takes a bit of work but will boost your grade. Doesn't take attendance, but skipping class means missing material

His accent takes a bit of getting used to, and he tends to fly past materials if nobody stops him. He is very passionate about his subject and will not stop to clarify if nobody asks him to. The final is a take home test

Couldn't even understand what he was teaching, so I never really learned the material. However, he goes over what will be on each test exactly, and test/hw aren't too difficult. Get someone else though if you want to learn

Ivan is very hard to understand, but he is very friendly. he can be very helpful if you know how to ask the right questions. I have seen him give answers to exams during the exam time. he also makes it almost impossible to fail the course: many tries on h, 2 tries on exam questions, and the process for how to solve exam question before the exam.

Ivan is a very kind person, and he genuinely wants you to understand the material, but he won't force you to. I had Calc 3 (multi var), and the day before each exam, he showed you an example of each problem on the test as well as exactly how to find the answer. I haven't learned anything from him this year but will ace the final grade easily.
Ivan is a sweet Russian guy who loves Rabbits, History, Sweaters and Ivan's Game.  His endearing personality makes combinatorics a memorable class.

His accent is very thick and normally difficult to understand. He speaks through sayings and odd stories, which sometimes helps but sometimes just compounds the difficulty. I am good at math (scored an 800 on the math SAT), yet this class kicked my butt because I couldn't understand him and therefore couldn't understand the material.
Had him for FYS Combinatorics.  The class wasn't hard but his accent takes some getting used to.  He knows what he's talking about but sometimes it's hard for him to make you understand.

The lectures are very informative and she explains things very well especially if you are new to the topic. At first I did very poorly on the quizzes but after I went to tutoring with the TAs I did way better on the quizzes. I recommend going to tutoring right when you see yourself struggling and recommend it a bit more the office hours.

She is a wonderful professor and explains things very clearly. This class is hard so once you start to see yourself struggling on quizzes take advantage of the tutoring (this is what I did and it truly helped me). At first, I got 60s on the quizzes and after going to the tutoring with the TAs my scores went up to 80s/90s!
Nice and caring professor. I got a 40s in one of the quizzes and still managed to get a B+. However, slides and homework weren't really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: really great person and a pretty great lecturer. highly recommend.

Dr. Hinks is so nice and breaks information down really nicely so that students can actually understand the reasoning behind the code. She doesn't rush through lectures and is generous with grading. All quizzes and the final have roughly the same difficulty level.
Very great professor. Class can feel repetitive at times but she tries to keep everyone engaged.

Very clear lecturer; the content takes into account that not everyone has prior programming experience. Values student feedback. The course is already pretty generously structured, and she still gave additional grace with quiz and participation grades at the end.

Great teacher for Comp 110. If you don't have any coding experience I can see how this class could be a little challenging, but she teaches really well and is extremely sweet and kind during lectures. She records and posts lectures as well as review sessions, and there are ample opportunities to get your grade up. If u try, u can get an A.

Dr. Hinks is very nice and the class is super easy! Lectures are honestly pretty boring and you can skip them if you already have coding experience. Quizzes are easy, just make sure you know memory diagrams and do the study guide. Exercises can be tedious but are helpful in making sure you know how to code.

Big lecture hall class, but very manageable. She goes through all the slides with explanations. Study guides are very accurate for quizzes and the final. Lecture notes are online to relearn topics. Grading also has generous partial credit. Knowing how to code beforehand helps a lot(less studying), but not required. Memory diagrams are hard.

Dr. Hinks is the best! She is extremely kind and teaches foundational programming concepts well. She gives extra credit on exercises turned in early and loves to answer questions. There are a good amount of quizzes in the comp110 class (around every other week), but, overall, the class is an easy A.

I have previous coding experience so my opinion is flawed, but I thought the class was super easy. Lecture was clear but dry. If you don't feel like coming to class then def skip. Most lenient grading imaginable. Dr. Hinks is clearly a kind person and wants you to succeed. There is tons of support from the TAs.
Great professor, easy class, just make sure you can do python.

SO AMAZING Literally holds your hand the entire time, thoroughly explains concepts (I've never coded a day in my life before), is SUCH a fair grader, and overall clearly cares a ton about students' understanding of the material and their personal wellbeing. Exercises take time, but there aren't many and tons of resources are provided.

she clearly wants everyone to do well in this class. turning EXs in before due date gets extra credit at the end of the semester, most missed quiz Qs often dropped, takes the time to explain things well. lectures can be a bit boring if you already know the content, but she is so nice and helpful! this class is so easy if you just put the time in

Awesome professor! Cares about her students and is passionate about the material. I've never coded before and this class was a great introduction. Honestly moved too slowly sometimes for me. Class has a decent amount of work, coding exercises are cool and helpful but time consuming. Highly recommend!
Great professor. Quizzes were very fair, and she ended up adjusting grading to help us out at the end.

Although some lectures can tend to be slow and longer than needed, COMP 110 with Dr.Hinks is super easy and enjoyable. She offers office hours everyday and all the TA's are super helpful! The quizzes are super fair content wise and she gives practice quizzes that prepare you for them.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best comp teacher ever

I don't know if it was just that I already had some coding experience, but I found this class VERY easy. Lectures generally were slow and if you already understood the topic they would not be interesting. the quizzes and final were like the lectures but a little harder. Honestly its just a boring class and the homework isn't bad.

I came into this class with 0 coding experience and struggled to grasp the content often. However, the resources provided by the CS department are crazy. There is tutoring and office hours almost every single day (Sundays too!). 

Dr. Hinks is great, and she truly did everything (including omitting the late submission penalties) to help our grades.

Coming into this class with no coding background, I really had no idea what was going on. Professor Hinks is accessible outside class and going to office hours/tutoring is helpful. I did horrible on the final exam and still made a B+ so make sure you do all the homework/classwork assignments. Overall a good class but compsci just isn't for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is well organized. But, if you've never coded, I think Dr Hinks is not the best teacher. Lecture slides are very high level w/ few examples covered in class. Quizzes are short so if you miss 1 section, its tough to do well. I found other resources to learn the content. She did adjust the final quiz/exam weights, which helped grades a lot.

If you need to take COMP110 you should fight for her sections. It is literally imposable to get lost in this class she breaks everything down and if she runs out of time she will add a video thoroughly explaining the problem. Professor Hinks is also incredibly kind and helpful. The best professor that I've had at this school without contest.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took the class for my Stats major. Going to class is a key part of the class although attendance isn't mandatory. If you actually lock in for each quiz, you'll be fine. Homework also is a good chunk of your grade, so take it seriously and don't use obvious AI (my friend got caught).

Literally the sweetest professor! I came in with 0 programming experience and I think is is impossible to do poorly in this class if you do the assignments and study for the quizzes. There are SO MANY resources (tutoring and office hours) and the final was super easy. if u have a choice between this and stats for bio major - Take this!

Professor Hinks is so sweet and she really tries her best to make it easy for everyone. Exercises were easy. The quizzes are very similar to what she posted for the review. The final was lowkey easier than the quizzes. In the end, she changed the rubric to benefit everyone which shot my grade up by like 3%.

This class is very simple (especially if you come in with some experience) and she's very clear about what she wants. The only thing was that some lectures were pretty slow-paced, which made it a difficult class for me to stay awake for

I had a great time in this course! I had never programmed before, but the comp 110 curriculum was perfect for beginners. It does require a lot of logical / mathematical intuition. Professor Hinks is very sweet and a good lecturer. I skipped class more than I'd like to admit, but the online material and TA office hours helped me get caught up.

Professor Hinks was super sweet. She merely lectures so if you have coded before with python, attendance is not mandatory. I struggled slightly on quizzes (there are five total) because everything was new, but many of my friends who had coded before found the class exceptionally easy. COMP 110 department is also super helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Hinks is the best person to have for a college level intro to coding + CS class. IF, and only if, you attend lectures you are set. She explains things with tons of depth + memory diagrams help so much in developing logic. Quizzes are straightforward & TA's know what they are doing! The class structure and people are amazing! Take this class!

Honestly COMP 110 comes down to if you can follow the logic or not. If you can't, the course will be hard. If you can, a night of studying can get you an A. I fell into the latter, even with VERY little coding experience. Dr. Hinks herself is very kind and approachable. She doesn't take attendance.
Go to class, bro, don't fade, and it's an easy A. 5 quizzes and a final, just lock in and don't take it early in the morning because you will fade

Hinks is nice, but this course is awful. It is the opposite of beginner-friendly; in fact, you are likely going to do poorly if you do not have prior experience coding. This class assesses on code-writing without ever teaching the concept. One of my worst class experiences at UNC. Would not recommend.

I actually found this class very difficult. Extremely tedious, very boring, overall an experience that left me wishing I'd taken something else. TAs are nitpicky graders for the quizzes, and Izzi will drone on and on about memory diagrams for probably 1/4 of the lectures total. Take something else if you're not a computer person.

she's really nice and the course is structured very well. they have a ton of resources for u to get help. u just have to accept that coding can be difficult. she sometimes does not word things correctly but if u connect with tutoring u will be fine.

This class is hard especially coming into it with zero experience. It is fairly fast paced, but the workload is SUPER manageable. Hinks is nice but I don't love her. The TA's though are AMAZING and so helpful. I went to tutoring and office hours for every assignment and learned it all. Quizzes are every 2-3 weeks and lowk hard.
really nice, brings good energy to class

Great professor, but the lecture hall is huge, so if you have questions, it's best to ask them outside of class during office hours. As someone with ZERO computer science experience, I'm kind of struggling in the class, but if you need to take it, professor hinks is great.

As someone with 0 computer science experience and doesn't enjoy coding, this class was hard and concepts were difficult to grasp. To do well, I'd 100% recommend going to office hours or tutoring (happens every day). Professor Hinks is super duper sweet and her lectures are quite fun to attend! Use the resources provided to you!
Best comp110 professor

I LOVE PROFESSOR HINKS. She is literally the GOAT of CS and she explains everything in detail and makes sure the whole class understands everything before we move on. Really kind in person and always willing to assist students. Tons of office hour time and quizzes and final are extremely fair and lots of opportunity for extra credit.

Dr. Hinks was a good professor to have for this course, she made everything easy and straightforward and there were lots of opportunities to get outside help. Attendance was optional and the lectures were recorded and posted afterwards.

She is so caring and does a great job making sure all concepts are understood. TAs are always available and quizzes are very similar to practice. Attendance is not mandatory and lectures are posted. Overall the class is not too difficult and is definitely doable for those with no experience!

The quizzes are what made this class somewhat difficult, not the teaching. Izzi is respectful and tries to keep people engaged during the lecture. There's a good amount of work outside of class, but the TAs host reviews often and tutoring everyday.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As someone who had 0 coding and experience, I was really worried about whether I was able to survive. But the course in organized to make most of the people to get A if you study the material seriously. Make sure to submit long-writing project 2 days earlier than ddl to get extra credit.

Prof. Hinks is a passionate and organized lecturer. Attendance is not mandatory, but conducive if u have no prior Python experience. Reasonable workload, and she really seriously reviewed our regrade request  to improve grading fairness. A robust UTA team that can solve general issues in time. The only choice for Comp 110, but a great one!

I would recommend this class to anyone! I got a 76 on one quiz and still ended the class with a 99. I can tell Prof. Hinks tries to make it as easy as possible, with the exception of some longer exercises. Things can seem complicated but are actually pretty straightforward. So glad I got to learn from her!
queen! forgiving grader and clear lecturer. test questions very similar to practice tests. I learned a lot!

Genuinely the most pure and kind soul ever. The course is hard without previous coding experience and a lot of people dont show up to class, but if you apply yourself you'll do fine. She really cares about her students and is passionate about what she teaches. Nice to have a prof who really enjoys their subject. Great prof!!!

Prof. Hinks was a pretty good lecturer, and always answered students' questions carefully and respectfully. She was pretty forgiving in terms of late work and the quizzes were doable. Be aware that this class is very project heavy, so it would be unwise to take it with a heavy course load.

Dr. Hinks was a really good professor for this course. I had zero experience in Python, and had only taken AP CSP in high school, but she made it easy to follow along. Her quizzes were very similar to the practices, which made studying minimal. Highly recommend!

Dr. Hinks always urged people to voice questions they had and never made anyone feel as though their question was trivial. She worked slowly and was thorough with examples to ensure we understood the underlying process. She & ULAs were always available for OH and additional help. Overall, she made this class as beginner friendly as possible!

Professor Hinks is great! She really tries to explain the topics we learn, making them easy to understand and provides a good amount of resources that really help with the quizzes. Quizzes aren't bad at all, especially if you do the practice quizzes. Really easy class for beginners and a great professor!

Really enjoyed Professor Hinks and this class. People are right that it can be hard/frustrating at times, but Izzi makes it pretty easy to get good grades by offering corrections, dropping lowest scores, extra credit, etc. The final was easier than expected, too, and made up for some tough quizzes and exercises. Highly recommend her!!

Dr. Hinks is so kind and a good teacher, and as long as you pay attention in lecture (or watch the recordings), you'll do great. The practice questions were always a lot harder than the quizzes, so if you could do those, the quizzes will be a breeze. Definitely recommend!

If you want to do well in this class, I would attend lecture as much as possible. The class is weighted through monthly coding assignments and 5 quizzes (basically exams). If you don't have experience with python, you will be fine! It is mostly logistics based and everything is explained in depth. Overall, a great class

Professor Hinks is great! You can really tell she cares for her students and wants the best for them. There are practice quizzes given to help prep, and the format of the actual quiz is very similar to those practice quizzes she gives. Honestly she makes the course not as bad and easy to understand if you are willing to learn. Would recommend!

This class, and professor Hinks, are really not bad at all. Put in the work and the studying and you'll be fine, I can tell a lot of work has gone into improving the student experience in this class. I feel like the easy things balance out the tough things. It's so cool to go from zero knowledge to being code literate, and Izzi is a nice teacher!
Professor Hinks is one of the best professors I have ever had. I was so scared for this class, but she has made it so fun! Take her!!!!!!

COMP 110 in general is a hard class, but if you actually show up to her lectures and pay attention the class is actually pretty easy to get an A in. She explains things really easy and simply and the practice quizzes are just like the actual ones.

you probably will not receive practice material until the start of the week of the quiz. once she said the practice material would be uploaded over the weekend. it wasn't uploaded until tuesday noon. our quiz was friday. poor communication and timeliness, just sorta unreliable. she does just read off the slides.
Dr. Hinks is a very dry instructor and will literally just read from lecture slides.

This class is not as bad as I expected. Izzi is very sweet, I like that she's straight to the point and moves slowly through concepts. The only HW outside class are the exercises, which are hard but you get plenty of time fir them. The quizzes require a lot of prep - use ChatGPT to help you study, it's a lifesaver! Don't let this class scare you!
the other comments tell the tale, she is ok-ish i guess. she just reads off the slides. haven't received a lot of practice material.
uhm, she's ok. kind of just reads off the slides, has a lot to say.

Kinda stated the obvious and didn't really explain anything too in depth during lectures. i went to every class but lectures were not very valuable. especially for diagramming, she did not really explain much. i was in the 8 am so maybe she was just tired but my friends said the same in the later sections too.
Lectures recorded attendance was not mandatory, honestly, I never showed up to class.
Very easy course, made the quizzes easy and had a huge curve at the end with the final replacing 2 quiz grades. Lot of opportunities to do well in other assignments and not test heavy.
this class is much easier than it used to be, but the help infrastructure around it is robust.

Dr. Hinks was very kind and clearly loves comp sci, and I thought she explained things well. The COMP 110 grading policy is very nice - dropping the lowest grades for certain assignments, infinite attempts for exercises, and the final exam isn't worth an insane amount of your overall grade. I definitely recommend this class with Dr. Hinks!
Dr. Hinks is the kindest professor and loves computer science. This class might be difficult to understand sometimes but she is motivated to help students as much as possible.
shes ok. communication could be better. doesnt really explain stuff in detail. i went to alyssa's lectures a couple times and she explained things in more detail. overall, fine.

Love Professor Hinks!! Super kind and caring. Grading policy is very generous (lowest of multiple homework and assignments and quizzes dropped). Quizzes are straightforward with tons of practice problems. Lectures are clear and recorded. Final only worth 10%. Very easy class even with 0 coding/programming experience!

It is 24 hours before my final and I still have yet to receive my grade for quiz 04 (a unit midterm essentially). The TA's are not always helpful. I went to office hours with them to code my assignment, got a clear from them for 100 for them to change my grade from 100 to 70 3 days before the finals. It is unfair to those with finals today.

Dr. Hinks was nice but I went to Alyssa's lectures in the beginning of the semester instead because she explained things better. If you have to option between Alyssa and Dr. Hinks, I would recommend Alyssa. Grades were kinda a nightmare. We didn't get back quizzes until almost the next time we had to take another quiz which was stressful.

I like Professor Hinks. The only downside was when the TA's put the wrong hyperlinks for the practice for one of the quizzes (worth 10%) of the final grade and kind of screwed the whole class over. Luckily, there's a replacement policy for your lowest quiz with your final grade if it's higher so I still have hope. The professor explains clearly.
good professor
She's so sweet and good at explaining! Her class is very fair and she helped me really learn foundational concepts in comp sci while making it enjoyable.
Great professor. Lectures are interesting and content is taught in a speed that ensures even complex things are easy. Would take again.

If you are a stem major and don't have the mindset for creative thinking, unfortunately this is not the professor for you. Dr. I is very abstract and creative with her thought processes. To others, her guidelines appear to be vague and complex, but she wants to give you ideas and creative freedom. She is very caring and passionate.

Dr. I appears to be very caring and kind. However, I was very confused by her lectures. There are 3 major performances, but your TA gives good feedback on how to improve. This class was a nice brain break for me as a STEM major. I still didn't mind the class and would recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gave multiple assignments over university mandated holidays, unclear assignment guidelines, excessive homework for a 100 level course. Currently have an A but not worth the effort. Professor is difficult to reach. TAs were the only saving grace for this course

her speech is very difficult to understand, and on top of the fact that the concepts are all very abstract makes her lectures very confusing. jumps between topics too quickly. the details of the performance requirements are usually incredibly vague and not fully explained until very close to the due date. take this class with literally anyone else.
Very strict on attendance
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Way to much homework, think assignments class period everyday, mandatory attendance, and makes the class way harder than it needs to be. DO NOT TAKE

Her lectures can be very boring and convoluted, and she also has a thick accent which can make understanding her a bit difficult, especially in the mornings. Otherwise, you can tell she's very into performance and analysis and if you are too she'd be a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easy A. I recommend Irina and Comm160. All TAs are great. Irina does talk quite a bit during lectures and expects student response. Very imaginative and gives feedback on our performances, but occasionally is vague on expectations. Very kind and laid back.
She's a very good teacher and explains tough spanish concepts very well. Her in class activities were always fun, and I've always felt prepared for the tests.

Spanish at UNC is hard, but I would definitely recommend taking 105 with Iris! She's super accessible outside of class and genuinely wants her students to succeed! Be prepared to learn A LOT of content, but as long as you start studying for exams early, you can succeed in this class!

Profe is amazing! Class is interesting, and she always engages with students. There is a LOT of homework and vocabulary in class, but the Spanish department assigns that, not her. Midterms and finals are difficult due to the amount of material covered, but profe always helped us with what to study. Go to her office hours as well!

Dr. Brodey was very kind, and invited the class over to her house for dinner a couple times. She was nice to talk to, and I enjoyed the class a lot. She offered good feedback on essays when asked. However, the workload was definitely overwhelming at times. We consistently read 150 pages of dense reading for each class, or watched long movies.
She is a really tough grader and rarely provides grading guidelines for rubrics. She also expects a ridiculous amount of effort for a freshman seminar.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: professor brodey is knowlegeable, kind, and accessible. lots of reading, but to be expected for an english seminar, and definitely manageable. her grading criteria could be a bit unclear at times but she's always open to explaining! she even invited us over to her house for dinner, she's super sweet.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Brodey is very kind and knowledgeable about Jane Austen. However, the course has an unreasonably heavy workload and her Canvas is both difficult to navigate and frequently wrong.

I would rather retake Gen Chem, pull out my anterior cerebral artery, and lasso a bear with it than take this class again. Expected full-length novels in a week and acted like we only had her class. Gives zero feedback on assignments but continues to grade extremely harshly.

Professor Brodey is very kind and passionate, but the workload is overwhelming. Full novels in under a week and long films in one night made the class feel unrealistic with other commitments. Creative final project, but I wouldn't recommend unless you have lots of free time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: As a Jane Austen fanatic, I was very disappointed. I feel like we did 85% of the teaching. We had group presentations where we taught parts of adaptations or extra readings. Also, lots of group discussion. We read 8 books, so you had 150+ pages due every class, which was impossible. No rubrics for anything. Brodey was very sweet, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was cool. Lots of reading that corresponds to journal entries, you do not have to read everything. Just get a general understanding of what its about. Essays that are easy, but she never gives a grade on anything. Had no idea where my grade was at the end of the semester, but it felt like I was easily getting an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Get ready to read a ton of Jane Austen! However, assignments are very easy and straight-forward (mostly just weekly short forum posts on the reading). The teacher is incredibly kind and understanding, and there are typically chill class discussions every day on the reading.

I took CMPL 130 which I think is listed as 134 on here, but I thoroughly enjoyed this class, however, it was very reading heavy, at times we had to read 300 pages a week. Doesn't give much feedback on essays but is willing to discuss further if you schedule office hours. I enjoyed the diverse selected readings and felt that I learned a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ms. Brodey is by far my best and favorite teacher this semester. You can tell she cares about each one of her students. The course is heavy on reading but if you don't have time to complete the readings before class, you can choose to simply listen to discussions rather than adding to them. There are no tests or quizzes.

Dr. Brodey is a great & smart professor and I enjoyed her class - BUT you better get ready to read (like 6 hours per reading assignment) I don't suggest taking this class unless you're super interested in Jane Austen and dedicated to reading all 6 of her novels PLUS supplementary reading. Participation is also very important. Overall, good class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the sweetest and most caring teachers I've had during my time at UNC. That being said, she certainly doesn't hand out easy A's. The class was not very difficult, but she wants to see that your engaging with the material. Stay on top of the films and you'll be fine. Bring an interesting comment or observation to each class.

You're going to read a lot in this class, but that is to be expected since it is an English class. Professor Brodey is amazingly intelligent - she speaks six languages - but she doesn't make you feel inferior to her. Her English class is mainly discussion-based; she cares what her students have to say. She invited our class to her house for dinner.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I had her for my first semester of my freshman year and I don't think I will ever have another professor as great as her in my next three years at UNC. She has the most fascinating insight and despite the heavy workload, is extremely understanding if something goes wrong. She really cares about her students being successful

You better like Jane Austen. A terrific class and professor, however, and we got to meet her family and go to her house on multiple occasions. The class was more work than most first year seminars, but she has so much passion and such a sweet personality.

Massive amounts of reading - I wasn't prepared.  Tests came out of nowhere and were very difficult to do well on.  Brodey is the nicest, calmest, most chill professor I have ever had though, and actual class time is extremely low-key.  Honestly would not take again though because Jane Austen does not interest me.  NEED to love Austen to take!

Dr. Brodey is an excellent professor, who integrates literature and art in variety of mediums into her classes. While she produces cutting-edge research, I always found her approachable, and she helped me improve my writing a great deal. A fair bit of reading, but very interesting. Looking forward to my third class with her!

I loved this class so much. I didn't even really know what it was all going to be about when I first signed up but I really enjoyed her as a teacher. There is a lot of reading and it is difficult but I think it is worth it. She is very helpful and let us come over to her house for a movie for the class! Would recommend her as a teacher.
This class was awesome. One of the best classes ever.

This has been my favorite class thus far. She taught the class with James Thompson, and they both enjoyed what they were teaching so much and had such a rapport with one another that I looked forward to coming each day. She was incredibly caring and really developed a relationship with each of the students. Basically, she was wonderful!

I had her for ASIA/CMPL 379: Cowboys, Samurai and Rebels. The topic is absolutely fascinating, but she is completely boring. There are approx 10 required books ($$$) and almost a movie a week required to watch. WAY TOO TIME CONSUMING! however, the grades are controlled by TA's and mine is fair...
Dr. Harrison is so kind and a great lecturer! He genuinely cares about his students and does all he can to see them succeed. Would definitely recommend taking any of his classes.
Such an amazing professor and overall nice guy. You should definitely take a class with him if you have the chance to.
Amazing professor and genuinely kind man. Take class with him!

Awesome guy who takes you through how to do a study and write a research paper. He made it all very doable and was always there to help. Quizzes are online and open notes. Final is also open notes, but in person. The major part of the grade is the paper.

Professor Harrison is kind and accomodating, and this course is super helpful for writing. The course involves a semester-long research paper which is broken up into sections, and there are clear rubrics to follow for each. Take notes during class to make studying for the final easier, as the final is open note!  Attendance is through PollEv.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Believe these reviews, Professor Harrison is amazing. I am not a psych major, but I was still able to gain a lot from this course. It strongly helped that Professor Harrison always cared about his students and their comprehension of the material. If you're like me and simply in need of a research and discovery class, I highly recommend this course.

🐐

There is groupwork but it's manageable and he is always happy to help you out
I took him for PSYC 210 online, and he's very nice and helpful! He's also pretty chill and understanding.

Very kind and accessible professor who responds fast to emails about any questions. He is there for you so utilize those office hours. Grade is mainly made up of project papers which is just sections of one big paper you compile at the end for the final project.

This is my second semester with Dr. Harrison after 210. He remembered me and is still so kind and understanding. Amazing lectures, funny, helpful, and fun to talk to. It's clear he cares a lot about his students and loves what he teaches. Highly recommend taking any classes with him if you can.

Dr. Harrison is a great guy and wants everyone to succeed. No question is stupid to him. The course involves a semester-long research paper, but it's broken up into manageable sections. You are given everything you need to do well (examples, outlines, rubric, data, etc). Attendance was only counted for the first week or so.

Phenomenal professor! Very passionate about the topics in class! The class itself is very draining in the sense of the semester is spent writing a research paper. Don't procrastinate and you'll do great! If you do, you'll be fine! To me, the content of the class was kind of dull, but it's centered on research, so it's expected. Definitely take it!
Trust the RMP reviews and take him he is so great!

Dr. Harrison is one of the best professors I have had at UNC. You can tell how much he truly cares about his students and wants all of them to succeed. Relatively easy work in the class as long as you show up and pay attention.

Dr. Harrison is genuinely one of the best professors I have ever taken a class with. He is so kind and truly cares about what he is teaching and how well his students are doing. It is clear that he wants the best for his students and will do what he can to make the class easier/more accessible. If you have the opportunity to take his class, DO IT!!

This class is great. Most of the grade is one big research project. Pick a good group and put effort in up front on the Lit Review and you'll be fine. Lots of extra credit, but also I ended up at >100%. Super kind and caring guy.

Dr. Harrison is an amazing professor that truly cares about his students. He is always understanding and doesn't expect you to know everything. He'll work with you and teaches in a way that's digestible and interesting. One of my favorite professors ever!!!

Dr. Harrison is a great guy, but psych 270 with him was horrible. Extremely unclear instructions, every student confused, very few grades, and just simply weird projects. I never knew what was going on, but he is a really nice and fun guy.

One of the best professors I have ever had. He genuinely cares about both the course content and his students. He is also very understanding—when I got sick, he made sure that my recovery was the top priority, not his deadlines. I would highly recommend taking his class. The midterm was take-home, and the final was in-person but open everything.

Dr. Harrison is a very nice professor and seems to truly enjoy what he does. All of the assignments are fairly easy and don't take long to complete, and the exams are not too dificult either and open note. He doesn't track attendance besides pollev's, but following the lectures asynchronously can be hard at times - probably worth going in-person.

Harrison is absolutely amazing. You can tell straight off the bat that he cares for each and every student. He always triple-checks to see if everyone understands each topic. The midterm is take-home and the final is in-person but open-internet.
Dr. Harrison was so sweet and funny! he clearly loves teaching and is passionate about psych. Homework was super easy and gives plenty of extra credit.

He is super helpful and really wants students to learn. He was lenient on the grading for exams and assignments. He also offers extra credit a lot. I would 100% recommend taking this class, it was very beneficial.

Prof Harrison is very caring and competent. The course material is easy enough, but I found that the TA's grade the weekly assignments very harshly and I was consistently getting B's and C's on them. Despite this, I recommend the class as an easy intro to stats.

Dr. Harrison gives take home exams and lots of extra credit. He understands that as a statistician you would be using your notes to complete tasks so he lets you do that on the exam. His lectures are a lot of talking and little interaction, you need to take notes. He works with you on all HW and prepares you for the quizzes.

Dr Harrison wants to teach and loves it! His class is so easy, with take home exams and quizzes, and the assignments genuinely take me 10 minutes. He is funny and tries to engage in class, and is very open outside of class. His lectures go smoothly, and while I find them boring, he tries so hard to make them fun. Take him! Easy, fun, and caring!

he is my favorite professor here so far. i hated the topic of his class (research methods), but by the time i finished, i loved the topic. he is an amazing teacher, so kind, funny, and helpful outside of class. you can tell even by the first day of class that he actually likes teaching and helping people. he is there to help with whatever you have.

Harrison is a very kind and you can tell he cares about psych. At times instructions were VERY unclear and was left wondering what I should be working on outside of class. The whole class is a big group project and it is working on one huge paper that you submit at the end. It was interesting, but you have to but in effort for a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. H is an amazing professor, and this class is super cool! It's based on replicating a research paper, and it is a lot of group work, but you can change groups if you want. Your papers are graded by grad students, but the guidelines are pretty clear. Many parts of the final grade are easy 100s, so a bad grade won't kill you. Def recommend him!

I love Dr. Harrison. You can tell he genuinely care about all of his students and wants you to succeed. The main component of the class, the group paper, has very clear guidelines to follow. He made it easier than he could've which is awesome. He has a good bit of extra credit and seems very flexible with deadlines. He's an awesome person!

Dr. Harrison has been one of my favorite professors at UNC so far! He is funny, heavily interested in the material, and his enthusiasm alone can keep the class engaged. PSYC-270 with him was relatively easy. Just try to do well on both project papers and the final paper! Learning checks and final were open note. Take this class with Dr. Harrison!

Dr. Harrison is very clear in his class structure and makes things as simple as they can be for students. While his class is very writing-heavy (with a huge APA paper), he breaks it into manageable portions. He cares a lot about his students doing well and will be there if you need his support. The grade you get will largely depend on the TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Harrison is a great professor who truly cares about his students' learning. The class has a good amount of work, but with tools like Unstuck ai and the open-note exams, it's manageable. Definitely worth taking if you're interested in psychology.

An amazing professor and a great class. I took AP Stats in high school so this class felt more like an extension of that. Professor Harrison does a wonderful job at making the content understandable and clear.

very nice guy. Mid term was tough, final not so bad. Make sure you do the participiation polls and packbacks. If you took Stats in highschool it should be light. Very nice guy, but the lectures were sometimes a snooze fest. Overall 10/10

Dr. Harrison was the most caring professor I've had so far. Assignments and quizzes were doable, exams were tough but everything was online. Tons of extra credit. Could've easily gotten an A if I put in more effort. I did find it difficult to listen and stay engaged in his lectures; make sure to focus more on what he's saying rather than slides.

Dr. Harrison is a gem of a professor. He offers extra credit and will answer every question you have no matter how stupid it is. If you pay any sort of attention in class, you should be able to get an A. The workload is more than you might want, but at least it is consistent, so you know what you're getting into each week of classes.

I loved this class, I definitely could've gotten a better grade I just did not try hard enough but Dr. Harrison is the kindest professor out there, really wants to make sure we know the material, and is super understanding. If you go to class and stay on top of assignments you will be set for an A in this class.
Dr. Harrison is so incredibly kind and truly wants the best for his student. He gave us so many opportunities to learn and to improve our grades in that class and his kindness really shone through.

This class will go down as the easiest I'll ever take at UNC. Grades are 10 assignments, 5 quizzes, 2 midterms, and a final, with participation polls being posted on Canvas, so I never really needed to go to lecture, I just had to do the poll. Also, Harrison is one of the sweetest and most caring professors ever. I can't believe he works at UNC.

There isn't much here I can say that hasn't already been said - he is one of the best professors at UNC. If you review the TA's materials and pay attention in class you will be set. The material sucks but he is fantastic, seriously.

Love Dr. Harrison! You can tell he really cares about his students and this class. The powerpoints don't have much detail in them so make sure you pay attention to lectures to get the big picture of the lesson. Although assignments were a bit tedious, the open note midterm and final exam made this class a breeze.

Dr. Harrison is the nicest professor I've had during my time at Carolina. He genuinely cares about each of his students and wants you to succeed. I would suggest taking the class seriously though and taking good notes, so you can do well on the quizzes and tests.

Professor Harrison is a great professor and is very passionate about statistics! He is funny and does a good job presenting the information. He will always accept questions and spends time answering them until he knows the student has a better understanding. Tests are a little difficult but open note. I recommend him!!
Very good professor! Everything was graded fairly. Tests were a little harder than I expected but still manageable.

Dr. Harrison is truly one of the kindest professors at UNC. Although it was a course with over 200 students, he made the effort to meet each student's needs to ensure a great learning experience for all. He is very understanding and most, if not all of our course work are open note which is extremely helpful! Take his class!

This class is very manageable. Dr. Harrison is a nice professor and makes you feel very comfortable. Some of the assignments are a little confusing, but I felt as though everything was fine. I'd recommend the class if only to get to meet Dr. Harrison!

I can not say enough good things about Dr. Harrison. He is so compassionate and truly wants you to succeed. He offers a lot of extra credit and is always wanting to help you understand everything in the course. Assignments are super easy, quizzes and exams are a little difficult, but they are all open note. Easily the best professor&person at UNC.

Knows what he is talking about and teaches it very well. Responds very quickly and clearly. It's obvious he actually cares about his students. Chances for extra credit. Easy to talk to and funny. Assignments have clear instructions and rubrics. Excellent teacher and person.

I absolutely loved Dr.Harrison and would recommend this class to anyone. Tests and quizzes are all take home and open note. Weekly homework assignments are pretty easy and not time consuming. Plus there's a ton of extra credit. Even if you hate statistics, you can succeed in this class if you put effort in.

Not much to say that hasn't been said but genuinely one of the best people ever. So nice and caring and made me look forward to his class even though it was so long. He really makes sure you understand the content and I would love to take another class with him. GOAT.

This class was a bit more difficult than I expected, but Dr. Harrison did a great job explaining things. His grading criteria is clear and the assignments are easy. The midterm and final were slightly challenging, but Dr. Harrison was transparent with the structure and content for both exams.

Very good lecturer. You can tell he cares a lot about the material he teaches. For the class work there were not too many assignments but it's very easy to lose minor points on them due to certain missing parts. For PSYC 210, he focuses mainly on theory and understanding of the statistical analyses instead of performing the calculations.

There's not much I could say about him that hasn't already been said, but he's truly the best professor I've had at UNC. On top of being extremely caring and funny (you get extra credit for making stats memes!), he's such an amazing teacher. If you get a chance to take him for a class, do it. Stats can be naturally confusing but he makes it okay!

Best professor I had this semester. The work is easy as long as you show up to classes and ask questions when needed. I had some complications at the beginning of this semester with my grades, and he was incredibly helpful and quick in helping me solve said issue. If you're a psych major take this professor.
I loved Dr. Harrison. He was by far one of the best professors I've had so far! He is so so kind and caring and you can tell he really cares about his students and the class content.

There is no doubt that Patrick Harrison has changed a student's life. He so obviously cares about his students and the best thing I did was take him freshman year (because it is a big adjustment, taking a great professor made a difference). I know psyc 270 has a huge paper, I promise it is doable hundreds of students do it every year, you can too.

Harrison is just an amazing human. He is funny and super smart. As someone who did not know or care about stats, he made the class both enjoyable & understandable. The class is not easy, but he makes it manageable! Plus he loves memes, and will give you extra credit for submitting them! I 100% recommend!!!
very good professor

Actually such an amazing teacher. Very friendly and patient, invites questions and explains the answers super well! Probably the best professor I've ever had, and you can tell he has such a love for this class. He's super helpful and there were grace periods for each assignment, which we nearly always go over in class before submission.

Dr. Harrison was one of the best professors I've ever had. He taught the material in such a way where you could feel comfortable asking questions, which I really appreciated. His office hours were an amazing resource because they were online, and he never made you feel dumb for any question you ask. You can tell he enjoys teaching.

Dr. Harrison is an outstanding professor who truly cares about all of his students. I took this class during Summer Session I and even though the class was fast paced, he made all of the lessons accessible and easy to comprehend. He is also great at dedicating time to prepare us for exams and to review content/assignments.

Loved Professor Harrison as a human -- super caring and understands most students are just there for psyc major credit. Makes content as interesting as possible, but his slides are very hard to understand if you don't pay attention to every second of lecture... Exams are hard but fair, and assignments help reinforce what's taught in lecture.

Highly recommend taking Professor Harrison for PSYC 210. The assignments & quizzes are straightforward and he provides clear rubrics for how he grades. A caring professor that wants his students to learn and succeed! Took this class online over the summer but definitely a class that you can do well in by showing up and completing assignments.

Work is fairly easy if you go to class and listen in class. All the answers for the assignments are mentioned in class and he has a tutorial video for each assignment. I got a B because I barely went to class and got average grades on the assignments.

Dr. Harrison is very caring and wants the best for you to succeed in his class. You need to pay for an website called packback for the class but the assignments on it are very easy and can be completed in 15 min or less. Dr. Harrison is very helpful and allowed me to gain partial credit when I missed an assignment.

This was my first class with Dr. Harrison (online Summer) and I will definitely be recommending him to others and taking his classes again! He wants his students to succeed, and is passionate about his work. He responds quickly to emails, and is always willing to answers questions. He is by far the best professor I have had at UNC thus far.

Dr. Harrison is the best professor I've ever had the pleasure of taking a class with. He genuinely wants his students to succeed and he gives great lectures. Everything was open note so if you take good notes in class, the tests are not too difficult. He always responds to emails, even at midnight.
Midterm and final were kind of hard. Try to get old midterms from a friend to practice. Otherwise, moderate work load. Not the easiest class by any means, but take Harrison. Good guy.
Patrick Harrison is the most caring, kind, and warmhearted professor I have had a chance to encounter at UNC.  He is also an amazing lecturer :)

Dr. Harrison is an amazing professor who made the course paper manageable! He actually cares about students' mental health and well-being. Plenty of extra credit opportunities were provided, and deadlines were extended for students to make his class more convenient. Lectures were funny and inspiring, which was needed for the late afternoon.

Dr. Harrison is the nicest and most caring professor I've ever met. He is accessible outside of class. The class is based on one research paper (~20-30pgs); The paper has separate deadlines throughout the year, so it's bearable. Come to class! Participation is the only factor that could've made my A- to an A. I had a B+, and he rounded me to an A-!
A very caring teacher than knowledges the stresses of college students so he is super considerate
Amazing professor and overall person! Super kind, funny, and passionate about what he teaches. We need more like him at UNC. Very responsive to emails and flexible.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Truly one of a kind. UNC has a gem by having him teach here. He is so caring and truly respects and worried about all his students. He is funny and understand that you are not only a student, but a person as well. 10/10 recommend! Favorite professor at UNC!

This is hands down the best professor at UNC. He truly cares about his students and allows flexibility with deadlines in an effort to allow his students to actually learn things. He will help you in any way he can! Take as many of his classes as you can.

Nicest professor I have ever seen. Tries to present statistics in a very digestible way. However, class can be extremely slow. Additionally concepts are presented in such a general way that it causes it to mush with all of the other concepts we learned previously. This leads to things being more confusing than it needs to be. But overall easy class

I could not recommend Dr. Harrison enough. If I could take any class with him again, I would 100% would. He is so kind and he really cares about his students and their well-being.  Dr. Harrison is genuinely such a caring person and he keeps lectures interesting.  You can make memes for extra credit in his class.  Take him if you can!!

Harrison is an awesome person, but I just want to warn that, at least in his Psych 210 class, you will succeed mostly if you are an auditory learner. Slides don't really contain any information that is helpful when it's exam time. He tries to assist outside of class, but if you can't process lots of information auditory, get ready for a battle.
one of the best professors at UNC! I had him for both psyc210 and psyc270 and still use what he taught me. I highly recommend a class with Patrick, it's an easy A as long as you participate

I took Harrison for PSYC210 last fall and my choice to take him again for PSYC270 this fall was one of the best choices I have made at UNC. Dr. Harrison is kind, caring, and one of the best professors I've ever had at UNC. The material in this class is difficult but with Dr. Harrison it's manageable

Professor Harrison is one of my favorites at UNC. He tries to make the class as easy to understand as possible. The assignments are relatively easy, but the midterm and final were challenging. He is super easy to work with and flexible with deadlines to meet student feedback.
Dr. Harrison is the best! I was lucky enough to have him for both 210 and 270 and he is amazing. Truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed both inside and outside the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: best professor I've had at UNC. genuinely cares about his students and their success.

Dr. Harrison is great, and any pre-health should take this class if they need statistics. He is caring and doesn't pull dumb stunts or make things too difficult. He is one of the few professors who cares for the mental well-being of his students. The main components of the course are assignments, quizzes, participation, and the midterm and final.

I took 210 and 270 with Dr. Harrison. He is the kindest professor I have ever had. The class itself is research-heavy. You will have to conduct and write a research paper (25-30 pages). But Dr. Harrison made it durable. He always writes kind words to us and tells us how much he appreciates our efforts and energy. Dr. Harrison is the best.

Having Dr. Harrison as a professor was a breath of fresh air. If you can take one of his classes as a UNC student, DO IT!!! I can't recommend him enough. He is accommodating, cares about the well-being of his students, and wants his students to succeed!!! The material is easily digestible when learning through him.

Dr. Harrison is indeed so very kind. I found the course design to be challenging - with it being so large and so writing-intensive, it was challenging to know what was going on. I'd suggest taking a smaller section if it is offered.
Dr. Harrison is the most caring professor I have ever had. I recommend taking him 1000000% Stats is not my favorite subject, but Dr. Harrison made it easy to understand.

THE BEST PROFESSOR AT UNC!! I love him to bits. If you have to take a stats class, take this one!! I had to take it for a pre-med requirement and I had taken AP Stats before and didn't love it, but I loved this class. He makes everything so easy to understand and he really wants everyone to succeed. TAKE ANY CLASS WITH HIM.

Patrick is potentially the nicest professor I have had here. I strongly recommend taking a class with him if at all possible. He really tried to make sure everyone gets an A and is incredibly kind to students. Every assignment has a 24 hour deadline buffer to help students.

Dr. Harrison is AMAZING!!! He is so caring and really empathizes with his students. Class is an easy A, so don't worry about it at all; you will have 1 big paper due at the end that you get to work on throughout the semester.

Amazing professor!!! Stats can be really intimidating but he made them very approachable. He is a great lecturer and a really caring professor. Even if u hate stats, this is one of the best classes Ive taken so id definitly recommend.

Dr. Harrison is one of the best professors I have had at UNC. He is so kind and understanding. He acknowledges that we are people with lives, not just students. Psych 210 with him was very doable, and he went very slowly. The final was tough but fair. He prepared us well with in-class reviews and many resources! Take any class with him!

Just amazing!! Dr. Harrison is one of my favorite professors I've ever had. He genuinely wants all of his students to succeed inside and outside of the classroom. Definitely recommend taking a class with him!
Literally the best and most sincere professor I've ever had at UNC. All Neuro majors should take research methods with him.

Dr. Harrison is AMAZING. I literally don't have enough room to describe it all. He livestreams class on Zoom, gives grace periods for assignments, quizzes and exams are open-note, there are extra credit opportunities, slides are posted online, etc. etc. etc. He is also SUCH a nice person and a hilarious lecturer. Easy A if you put in effort.
He is genuinely the sweetest person and this class was so a breeze to get through thanks to him and the great IA team.

Genuinely one of the best if not the best professor I have had in the psych dept. He is so caring for his students and he made a subject a definitely would've struggled with extremely easy. He is very flexible with deadlines if you need it, and is always willing to work with you. Make sure to take his class if you get the chance, he is amazing!

Wonderful man. I would go to his lectures and just online shop on my computer with my roommate. He is so funny and caring, he makes the weirdest jokes but he is adorable so it is fine. If you make memes about statistics, he gives you extra credit. Pretty easy class
