I have zero interest in the subject but enjoyed the lectures because of her love for it. The lectures could be a little confusing with no prior knowledge but it is easy to pick up. I definitely recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A truly knowledgeable and caring professor.

Taking this class online was not great because it's asynchronous and I had a hard time motivating myself to watch the lectures. Short papers and quizzes every week to make sure you know your stuff. I wish I could have taken this in person because Magness seems to be really nice and a fun professor.

Jodi is an awesome lecturer! This class is asynch during the pandemic so it's kinda rough, and with the same workload each week, it gets kinda boring. Material is super easy, just a lot of work. Tests were 70% total and are open notes. Textbook is a waste of money.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While Prof. Magness likely won't be the one to grade your work, she is a really incredible teacher. I honestly looked forward to going to her lectures. She is super knowledgable and experienced with the material, plus some classes will just be watching documentaries (which she was a part of)

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! For it being a 100 level class you would think it wouldnt be too bad. Nope! You have to study so much for this class because you basically have to memorize almost all of the material to earn a mediocre grade. You could take one of her exams and think you got an A but youll really earn a C or D. One of the worst classes.

Worst class I have ever taken. The professor's lectures are dull and the TAs grade VERY harshly. When I tell you, please do yourself a favor and take something else. I regret taking this class. You can spend days preparing and the TAs will tear apart your test. The grading is very unfair. They were also very inconsiderate during the pandemic.

This class is the worst and if you're looking for a sign to drop it and take something else this is it. The content is easy and should be interesting, but it is graded so it is impossible to get a good grade. This is coming from someone who tried! NOT an easy gen-ed. The lectures are the worst but if you don't go she takes points off your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Jodi Magness is a very egotistical professor. First, the textbook is a book that she wrote herself and the lecture is just us students sitting and listening to her speak for an hour and fifteen minutes. Yes, she is very passionate about archaeology, but she didn't make it exciting for us. Tbh I slept during most of the classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Definitely the worst class i've ever taken at UNC. Do not listen to anyone when they tell you to take this course for "easy" gen eds. Professor Magness has been incredibly inconsiderate given the COVID-19 pandemic. The TAs will literally perform surgery with your test responses to the broadest of questions. Also, the term paper was terribly graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT take RELI 110 if you are just looking for your gen ed credits. PLEASE listen to me. I took this for the WB and BN credit. Whenever we thought we aced an exam, we got C's and D's because the TAs take off random, unnecessary points. The exams are very hard no matter how much you study. If you're only looking for gen eds, TAKE SOMETHING ELSE.

While this class was extremely easy, it was miserable. Prof. Magness enforces a strict no electronics policy in the classroom, so all notes have to be hand-written, despite every class just being a PowerPoint lecture. A large portion of the grade comes from the recitation, which required an unnecessary amount of work and weekly quizzes/papers.
I wish all my classes were taught by Jodi Magness. She is adorable and funny and I loved her lectures, she made Biblical Jerusalem seem like the most interesting thing on the planet
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Do not do it!!! The TAs are absolutely crazy and the exams are completely unfair in that you have to guess what answers they are looking for. Magness just lectures- she wont look at any of your work and doesnt even show up to exams. It doesnt matter how much you know, the TAs will find something to take off for.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Jodi is an amazing professor and is world renowned in her field. She is passionate and can be funny. The topic is genuinely interesting. However... the exams are a total guessing game and the TAs are insane. This ended up being my hardest class and the only grades you get are exams and a monsterous paper. Don't expect to get an easy A.
This class is hard. The professor has lots of passion for the subject, which I like. Injecting the bit about the Talpiyot tomb and the term paper were nice additions to the class.

I hate the guessing game exams. Even if you memorize the textbook, your notes, and Quizlet, you get points taken off for the randomest stuff. It's a misery studying for and taking the tests because 1) you get all the test questions beforehand 2) it's a boatload to memorize and 3) you know your prepped answer is not good enough no matter what.

Do not do it. You can write out all correct facts and completely answer questions on the exams and still lose points because you did not mention something specific that they were grading for. The TAs are ridiculous, but you have to go to them if you want help, because magness will not help you. If you get 'Zara' as your TA drop....

Look Im going to be honest, the professor lectures are fine even great sometimes. Regardless you are going to struggle on the test, you must describe everything you can on those study slides and hope that you will get credit for them. You may have written legit facts but at the end of the day they may not be the facts that they were grading for.

This teacher is one you just do not want to take. Save yourself the effort to deal with her. For real. She is not out to help you unless you are one of her favorites. Tied for worst teacher I have had.

Dr. Magness covers a lot of information in lecture so taking detailed notes is important for this class. She is receptive to student feedback, as she made the tests multiple choice due to previous complaints about test format. She is passionate about this topic and it made the lectures interesting, even for someone with no religious background.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Jodi Magness does a great job lecturing however study for her tests are extremely hard because her test questions, even though they are multiple choice, are on random small things instead of big topic questions. I did all the reading and still was unprepared for the test just because the tests are set up in a poor unclear way. Dont take her class

She's obviously passionate about the topic, which makes the class so much more interesting. Only tip is that her tests can get pretty detail-oriented but if you show up to class and take thorough notes, you'll be fine.
She is so nice and makes the class enjoyable! This was one of my favorite classes at UNC!

This was the worst class I have taken at UNC. Jodi spit out so much information in her lectures that it was impossible to get it all written down. Not to mention, my TA, Annie O'brien, made my grade plummet in this class. My recitation grade was worse than my midterms, and I did all assignments and attended weekly. Do NOT take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Jodi is very knowledgable and passionate about what she teaches. The lectures can be boring, but you must attend to learn the material. The tests are not too bad, and I think they are easier than last year. Recitation is also required, and it is dependent on your TA. A good TA will make the class easier and better!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Jodi is amazing! She is very passionate and knowledgable about the subject matter. The class is not a lot of homework, but it graded difficultly. There are some weird assignments like dressing up and artwork, but it is only Jodi trying to make the class fun.
I absolutely loved this class! She is really passionate about helping her students, but it is a class that you have to work for an A!

RELI106 has been my favorite class this semester. You aren't allowed to even touch an electronic in class, but her lectures are AMAZING. You can tell how passionate she is about the topic, you can't help but be interested. Exams are very reasonable, and she recently switched to a multiple choice format on exams instead of short answer.

I talked to my TA. He said Jodi told them they could only give credit for certain facts on tests. So, you might write all true facts but not get full credit bc they weren't allowed to give points for stuff Jodi didn't predetermine. TAs can't help it/ don't have a choice in the matter. In any case, it's annoying. Just memorize as much as you can!

Everything is graded by TAs and they take their job WAYYYY too seriously. Jodi is super nice and her lectures are interesting. All test material is given beforehand but you never know what the TAs want. The class would be better if the TAs werent power happy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very well respected/famous in field, so that's neat. 3 midterms, 1 paper, 1 final. Attendance checks. Tests frustrating bc you are asked for 2-3 facts about each object, but TAs are only allowed to give you credit for facts Jodi has predetermined as the ones she's looking for. (My TA described guessing which facts Jodi's looking for as a crapshoot)

Dr. Magness really knows her stuff! Coming into this class I was sure I was going to hate it, but because she was so passionate about the material, the class was not bad at all. Your grade come from 4 exams and a term paper (kinda a pain), but I would highly recommend it considering it knocks out 3 get-eds!

The lectures can sometimes be really dense, Professor Magness is really a master of the material and is super excited about teaching it. She's accessible outside of class and is always willing to help clear up difficult concepts, but your grade is ultimately determined by how easy/hard your TA grades. Her lectures are based exactly on her book.

Not an easy A. There is not a lot of work associated with the class but even if you pay deep attention to the lectures and prepare for the tests early, you are bound to do only alright. They look for such specific information and don't allow room for creativity. Grade depends entirely on which TA you have.

Anyone complaining about this class simply didn't try bc they thought it be an easy A. Jodi is an amazing & passionate lecturer and literally gives you what will be on the exams. TAs may grade differently, but if you put the right info they will give you credit. As for the term paper, it was simple as long as you spent time reading it. EASY CLASS!

lectures literally put me to sleep they were so boring. so much information to memorize for tests and they don't tell you what information is relevant so you end up having to memorize the entire textbook and still get a B. 10/10 would NOT recommend. save yourself before its too late

this class is entirely based on your TA you get which is unfair. expected to memorize absurd amounts of dates and get counted off for the stupidest things. I memorized every slide and essay word for word and still got Bs on the exams. the final exam is the most unfair exam ive ever had. memorizing 41 slides and 10 essays to be tested on 5 of them.

literally worst class I have ever taken. so boring. tests are impossible and graded so harshly by TAs. jodi really knows what she's talking about and is very passionate but is actually the most boring lecturer of all time. i literally can not stress enough how much the tests suck.

Jodi is the beeest - she is so passionate about what she does. Class can get long and feel like a lot of writing but the information is interesting if you put in the work. My TA was helpful but a hard grader. Hard to get an A in this class. I definitely recommend it - especially because it gets three gen eds !!

Graded completely by TAs and it's pretty harsh. A few times my TA told me what I put on my exam was correct but she had to count it wrong because it wasn't exactly what was on the grading key. Get your BN credit somewhere else. Easy to get a B, pretty hard to get an A. Term paper is beyond the scope of the class/undergrad ability.

She is hilarious! The class is all lectures and though many reviews say it's 'so boring', this has been one of my favorite courses. If you're interested in Biblical times it's cool to see the archaeology. If you study really hard for the exams you can get an A- (even if you know everything you won't get a 100 because UNC doesn't work that way).

Dr. Magness clearly knows her stuff. However, class is so so so boring. There is no point in going as she gives you test questions ahead of time and you can get all info from the textbook. You have no interaction with her, it is all through your TA. The TA ultimately determines your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved her class. So worth it. Lectures can get long, but she does try to make them interesting. Your grade does depends on the TA you get, but they will be fair for the most part. The exams are directly from her notes and powerpoints, so you should be fine if you try a little! By the way, I got away with not using the textbook at all.
Absolutely loved Jodi!  Her lectures are long but very interesting, and all the material you need for the test and more is described in lecture.  Go to class and take notes and you'll do well!

The only reason I took this class was bc I heard it was an easy A, but they had to CURVE the first exam. I think she got hard after the scandal. Was harder than my Bio 202 class No help at all-- she won't even acknowledge someone who has their hand raised in the front row Doesn't allow technology but talks fast and doesn't post ppts or outlines

Magness is cool, but your grade depends on your TA, and if you need help, you go to them. Magness just lectures and makes the assignments. 3 midterms with 6 identifications and an essay. All given ahead of time. Term paper is tough because the lectures and tests cover different material. NOT AN EASY A. Lectures are mostly about history.

TAs are very inconsistent with grading. There is A LOT of memorization but you're only tested on a couple terms so you still have to study everything. It is clear she is passionate about her subject. To me, she made this boring subject as interesting as it possibly could. GO TO CLASS and take DETAILED notes, including DATESNAMES.

Jodi Magness is the most boring lecturer I've ever had.  She is an elitist who will not tolerate opinions that go against hers.  Her TA's were very inconsistent and they decide your grade as they grade your exams and papers and make your quizzes.  This class was as miserable as it gets.  NEVER TAKE THIS CLASS

A complete waste of a first year seminar- this class was incredibly boring and the daily essays made students feel as though they were imbeciles for not knowing about toilets in 30BC. Do not recommend.

This is a terrible class. Do not be swindled into being convinced that this is an easy A. Worst class I've taken at Carolina, period. Boring and entirely lecture-based, with extreme variations on grades that are entirely dependent on the TA you get. Don't take this class, it's not worth whatever gen ed credits you're trying to get.
This class in NOT an easy A.  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS if you aren't good at essay writing or history.

Jodi is brilliant. Her class was one of the most interesting classes I have ever taken. Her lectures are well planned and you will learn a lot. She is an expert in her field and talks about her own experiences. She does talk fast, so you have to write down things quickly. Her tests were short ID's and essays, which she gives in advance. Great Prof.

Amazing professor, she does a great job of making all of the lectures interesting. Very experienced in her field of work, so she knows what she's talking about. She doesn't put the notes online so you can't skip lecture without having a friend to get them from. The TAs vary in difficulty but they're fine- I had the hardest one and managed an A-.

This class was supposed to be an easy A.  It wasn't for me.  She is great!  Her lectures were interesting and she gave us the pictures for the ids and the essays before the tests.  Your grade depends on your TA.  I got a B-...

She was probably the best professor I had this semester. She kept the class entertaining. The exams were not to bad, the TAs didnt grade too harshly, and she even offered extra credit opportunities. The hardest part of her class was the 7-8 page term paper due before the thanksgiving break, so if you dont procrastinate on this then youll do fine.

This was a grad/undergrad course, and my major is far outside of the religious studies department. That being said, i found the seminar style class to be interesting and Jodi is very bright and well rehearsed in the subject matter. We did presentations which I did really well on, and then had a 10 pg paper-DONT SCREW UP CITATIONS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
fun

I. Love. Jodi. Magness. She is by far one of the most interesting professors I've had at Carolina. Her test questions come straight from class, so you can't miss it, but it makes them easy (you get the essay ?'s ahead of time). The books basically reiterate class lecture so you don't really have to read. Recitation attendance is mandatory.

Great class, better teacher. She goes incredibly fast but makes ancient religious study very interesting. Tests are ID's and essays given in advance. Normally gives oppertunity for extra credit and a large portion of the final grade is easy recitation attendance.
Great class Great Professor. Incredibly interesting!  Im looking forward to having her again next semester!
As long as you can keep up, this class is great
One of my favorite professors!

Lecture was boring and she packs a lot of info into each lecture. I had to study a bit to keep all the names and dates straight, but I never had to do any of the reading except for what was assigned for recitation. The tests came straight from lecture and with or without the GENEROUS extra credit, I easily got an A!

I had this professor while she was still at Tufts.  As a lecturer, she's brilliant.  As an advisor, she's rude, arrogant, and clearly selects favorites.  What's worse is her attitude to new ideas -- if they don't conform to her narrow view of history, they're of no use to her and summarily discarded.  Not an enjoyable experience.
Lecture was very in depth but was also very boring.  The lecture gives you a billion names and dates and you have to know all of them just to have like 5 appear on the test.

Jodi is a GREAT professor, in fact she is THE BEST professor I've had at UNC so far.  She's very easy to approach and talk to, and her lecture style is not only clear and understandable, but can be entertaining as well.
Great prof; teaches what's on the tests and well.

He is very passionate about teaching; however, his methods are not for everyone. He is very dramatic and at times a bit disorganized. He has a poor work-life balance, and talks a lot about it. While his train of thought is often heading to an insightful and interesting place, it sometimes gets lost on the way there.  Super easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had so much fun this semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved his class!

Joe was an amazing professor and I would love to take his class again. You can tell he loves rhetorical analysis. He does bring up the TV show Succession quite a bit, as well as Kanye West, Taylor Swift, and Elon Musk. He is very accessible outside of class time, and he makes sure you know where and how to find him.
If you aren't a super confident writer but need ENG 105 credit, Joe is perfect. Genuinely cares about everybody in class and lets you revise any assignment unlimited times.

By far the easiest A I got all semester. He goes on a lot of tangents, but I tended to find them pretty interesting. If you're an English major or particularly care about learning about the field, maybe choose a different professor, since there were some days we straight up just watched TV shows in class that vaguely related to course content

Joe is really nice, and very accessible outside of class if you need help. This class is great if you want an easy A and enjoy talking about pop culture. He does go on a lot of tangents and I didn't really leave the class feeling like I'd learned much about writing though.

Joe is a nice guy, but rambles about unrelated stuff for most of class and frequently goes off track so I didn't get much out of his lectures. He is very friendly and tries to connect to students, but goes over the top sometimes. Almost all in-class work is group work, but rarely is it productive. He is a lenient grader and is very accessible.
Take him! I would 100% take him again. Hoping to have another class with him in the future.
Professor Telegen (Joe) was a great 105 instructor and made the course super easy!

Honestly loved Joe.  He is a very easier grader but lowk bipolar.  He rambles in class but you don't have to listen.  Ended with a 100 in the class.  You can submit assignments as many times as you want.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really recommend to anyone. Great professor.
Good GPA booster. Very caring and is always there to help you. Do the work and you will have a good grade.
Easiest teacher ever. Very accessible outside of the classroom. Overall, an easy A

This professor is quite odd. If you want an easy 100 I would recommend but beware because he goes on random tangents and you will not learn anything about English. He is obsessed with Succession and he makes us watch it both in class and for homework. Have fun!

Joe is probably one of the EASIEST Engl105 teachers you'll find. If you want an easy A take this class cause there are unlimited revisions on everything. If you actually want to learn something, then that's debatable cause he tends to go on a tangent often. Extremely accessible outside of class and very accomodating however.
A huge waste of time. Joe doesn't give a lot of clear instructions on homework so you may need to revise a couple of times before getting an A. But overall an easy class.

McClean is a good professor, but the course is ridiculously hard. The course description did not mention the endless amounts of coding. I went to tutoring for 2 hours a week, spent upwards of 12 hours a week on homework and studying, just to get a B-. Attendance is mandatory, but it only makes up 2% of your final grade. He is super nice tho.

Professor McLean seems like a pretty nice guy, but his lectures can be pretty boring. His midterms are also super difficult and he had said the class averages were very low, but doesn't curve the grades. It's doable if you actually put in the work.

Lectures are good and the readings are very helpful if you get confused. The hw and labs are a lot of work, but they're also the only way to prepare for the exams. I wish that there were practice questions to study, but he is good at answering questions in office hours. He is a little awkward, but very nice if you make the effort to be friendly.

Very code-heavy class. Lectures focus on syntax and go through stats quickly. About 2 HW assignments a week that are graded strictly, but aren't too hard. Attendance is lenient, but the final was difficult. He makes lectures interesting, but isn't very accessible outside of class. I'd recommend it, but prior stats knowledge is really helpful.

Decent prof. Awkward to talk to but nice & willing to explain things. Barely a stats class, basically only coding outputs that most of our tests were based on. No practice beforehand but tests only weighted 30% total and 20% final, so HW/labs brought up my grade. Not sure why this class needs a lab, but decent class overall.

his lectures are organized well, but he moves too slowly through the python snytax and too fast through the stats equation. I alr knew most of both, so it was fine for me, but he didn't fully explain how each stats equation worked, but did explain every word in the python syntax

I don't think this is Mclean's fault, but the class is structured to be an "intro" for people without stats or CS experience, but boils down to a very stats-heavy class (conceptually) and mostly simple code. If you've taken stats, the class is easy despite in-class midterms being somewhat tricky. Mclean does a good job of explaining and being fair.

Even as a pre-med, I think learning how to code statistical concepts in Python is useful, and Dr. McLean is a good teacher. The textbook is free, and the day-to-day assignments and even midterms are easy. The final was a bit difficult. Lectures are him coding stuff and you following along.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: McLean is a very cold unapproachable guy who rarely answers his email. Even if everyone fails a test, he will proudly put the grades in- no curve/ rounding. I got a fine grade in this class, but it was such a nightmare as he genuinely tried his best to make everyone fail. Not sure why he's so intent on everyone doing poorly? but here we are

McLean is extremely knowledgeable about the subject but is also super kind and caring. He did his best to make the class as easy as possible for those of us who are new to coding and/or stats, and is very understanding and generous. 3 midterms and a Final (cumulative because concepts build on each other throughout the semester). Best prof for 120!

I'm not good at coding and but I think that Prof. McLean explained all the concepts in class pretty well and explains how to do the code by going through it all in class. I think the midterms were a little hard, but not impossible, and the homework/lab assignments will pick your grade up.

Also, the textbook is free, so don't worry about that.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor McLean's organized style and teaching style were very good. Watching him go through code, and then using the code in a weekly lab helps drill the concepts in. Tests were not very difficult if you go to class and pay attention and study the textbook/previous assignments. Made me want to take another data science class.

McLean overall is a great professor! Ignore all the reviews about the insane workload, there's a lab and hw due every week and it really does not take that long. Exams are difficult, there's no curve and they're on paper which can be a little frustrating. Overall I learned a lot in this class, I would recommend if you're willing to put the work in!

McLean is the best professor I have had here at UNC so far. His lectures are so well structured and he is very caring and passionate about the subject he teaches. STOR 120 is NOT the easiest introduction course but if you pay attention and do the work you will be fine. I would ONLY recommend McLean if you need to take STOR 120.

This class was a nightmare. I P/F the class, because there was no way I was going to get out unscathed. I put in 10 hours a week and ended with a B- (i.e., a pass). Ultimately, don't take the class unless necessary. If you take it, go to the TAs and ULAs every week; they will give you the answers. In my experience, boosting HW and Lab grade helps.

The class content is relatively chill, but the exams can be unfairly difficult. Lectures focus too much on coding with little exam prep. Definitely use unstuck study and the textbook to study - they were super helpful.

this class is labeled as an introduction to datascience, but even the tutors i went to said it is absolutely not an introductory course. i think this shouldnt be labeled as a stat class, it should be labeled as comsci, there is little to no actual math happening-all coding. as a freshman just trying to fill focus capacities, do not take this class.

I don't think Dr. McLean is intentionally difficult, but our past semester was rough. New paper coding exam format, no practice materials, incredibly late homework grading, rarely answered forum questions, poor slide decks, robotic lecture coding sessions. Course content is relatively chill and will hopefully be ironed out. Disappointing.

Professor McLean lectured well overall. He always answered my questions with detailed explanations of concepts. The first exam felt unfairly difficult with no past exams posted, but the rest were good, including the final. However, exams are more conceptual compared to lectures. Midterms were closed note and written, involving some written code.

This was his first semester with exams for this class and it is evident that he himself wasn't prepared for them by not grading homeworks in time, by not covering the statistics content that would be on the test (emphasized too much coding during class), and by not providing correct answers after the exams so that students know what they got wrong.

If you are a good test taker you will have success. I deeply understood this material, but dont work well under time constraint, and my grade suffered because of it. 68% is test, which is normal, but the tests covered irrelevant material that is not useful in real life. Got nearly a 100% in homework, but did bad on tests even tho I study well.

Professor McLean is engaging during lectures. Homework and labs take a few hours to complete, 3 exams were really hard for me, but the take-home portions were better + weighed more for grade, weekly quizzes and lab, final exam is the easiest exam in the course, overall a great course and I learned a great deal!
4 midterms 12% each, they were not super hard but READ THE QUESTIONS CAREFULLY. The final was not bad at all and in all it was a cool class and McLean does a good job explaining the material.
Explains concepts well and this course is not terrible for conceptual difficulty. But my word the amount of homework was so unnecessary.

Only take if you are a statistics major. Material is fast, but useful. Takes a lot of studying and effort, even with previous coding experience. However, if you are hardworking, study, and take good notes, you can do well in this class. But it definitely is not an easy grade, you have to work for it. He doesn't release exam or homework solutions.

This class was super difficult. Exams were all written and about equations yet we only played in R during class. He goes super fast and his approach to teaching the material is not the best. He'll spend the whole class in R just for the exams to have 10% coding questions. Would not recommend especially for a data science elective.

The class content is not too bad, but there are four midterms, one of which was during the second to last week of class. There is plenty of study material, but homeworks are not graded in time for the exams, so you don't know if you made any mistakes. He doesn't also release answers for homeworks or solutions for the midterms.

I wouldn't take this class if you don't already have a strong background statistics/coding. The whole lecture consists of coding practice problems from templates he creates. The whole class seems very robotic. The midterms and and final were pretty difficult and the majority of the class didn't score great. For a 120 level class this class was hard
Great professor, solid tests. Only issue is the homework, it would be a lifesaver if we got 4 drops instead of 3.

Dr. Mclean is a pretty good lecturer. The homework is using methods of data analysis in R, while the 4 tests are mostly conceptual data analysis questions. The final is then similar to the homeworks. The one complaint I have is that that he really does not give guidance on what to expect on the exams beyond "what we covered on the slides."
This professor would be amazing if he dropped the lowest HW assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a statistics major, this class is honestly not that difficult, but it does take some getting used to. Don't worry about memorizing large chunks of code for exams (you will learn what to prioritize after the first exam). Lots of homework and annoying group projects though.

Not sure why all the hate-He is a good lecturer, and the material is useful. Do not recommend without R experience. The tests are hard, but if you study they are doable. Homework is doable by going to lecture and taking good notes. Overall, it is a 400-level class and the material reflects that, but if you are a hardworking student, you'll be fine.

Class would be doable with previous R experience. Material is good and Professor McLean is accessible outside of class. I wish he was responsive on Piazza though. Have not gotten HWs back before the midterm. It's not the code, it's the analyses. Knowing if our thought processes are correct is vital to learning, or post an example of HW problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jeff is a very nice guy, but this class was all over the place. The exams were very conceptual despite focusing on mostly application in lecture. The homework was fair and I thought that they reflected what was taught in lecture. Lectures were also all over the place and sometimes it was hard to follow what he was trying to get at.
Dr. Mclean is a very strict professor for no absolute reason and he has unnecessarily tough standards. He needs to drop the students lowest homework assignment from their grade.
Awful group projects, awful grading system and awful teaching. The materials are not difficult but lectures are difficult to understand and too complicated.

This class is all python coding and you use it for data analysis, which I wasn't expecting and makes the class more difficult than it should be. The labs and textbook are helpful to learn the actual coding aspect of the class. The in-class midterms are a lost cause, the class average is normally a 50/60 percent. Difficult for being an intro.

Jeff is a good guy but the midterms were horrendous you should definitely take STOR 155 and COMP 110 before this class. I dont hate the class but i literally dread the midterms and Im a cs student who took comp 283 with jack. I borderline consider the in class midterms a lost cause. Big man also assigns 2 assignments to be due the day of midterms

This class is 4 midterms; however it is a class clearly for statistics major. If you're not interested in statistics in any way avoid this class. The exams were purely conceptual which I think is a very good way of preparing for the data science world. The professor tries his best to accommodate everyone.

This class by far is one of the most difficult classes I have had. The material being taught is not bad, but the assignments that he expects you to complete and the closed-note exams make the class difficult. Does not respond in the Piazza, so not point in joining it, and takes relatively long to give back the HW grade and leaves no comments.

He wants the students to fail. The clas average for the first midterm was a D and he's not curving it. The homework is very hard and time consuming. He doesn't teach he just codes on his laptop during class.
never ever ever EVER in your life take 455 or any class with McLean. TERRIBLE

Terrible professor. Tests have absolutely nothing to do with homework. Assigns a group project that is impossible to coordinate within the due date. Test averages in the 60s and claims he won't be curving.

Not sure why he's being review bombed. It's true that the tests switched to closed-book (unfortunately), but he's genuinely a good lecturer. Apart from one bad question, the first test was fair if you actually did the readings and completed the HWs thoughtfully. I do wish he would utilize all of class instead of finishing 5 minutes early though!

This professor is unorganized and lazy because before the first exam which was a couple of days away, he had not made the exam yet so it was a poorly written exam. Moreover, he doesn't provide any study resources and the homeworks before the exam were not graded until after the first exam so there was no way to know if we did the homeworks right.

He just plays in R studio during class with no explanation at all. Only our first homework has been graded and there is no explanation for any grades. The average for the first midterm was a D and he didn't care. My discrete math class is easier than this class. Do not take this class with him.

The class format was changed this semester. Exams are no longer open-note, which makes them extremely difficult. The average for the first exam was a 60, and all that he said was that the exam grades are not going to be curved. The homeworks are graded very slowly and there are no study guides, so studying is nearly impossible for the exams.

He changed everything about the way this class works. No more open note tests. He doesn't teach and expects us to understand new material automatically. I have all A's, and now I'm afraid I won't even pass. Grades way too harshly.

Exams are no longer open note. He is a very harsh grader overall, and grades very slowly. For grade feedback, all you see is what you got wrong with no explanation as to why it's wrong. There are also no study guides for his exams. Attendance is required, but all he does is code in R with no explanation as to what he's actually doing.

Took this class because the tests were supposed to be open note. He changed his policies this semester. Lectures are hard to follow, all he does is open an r notebook and code whatever he is feeling that day. Provides no materials for exams and grades homework slowly and harshly. Also had nothing to say about the first exam average being a 60.

His lectures are not helpful as he just codes and uses random R functions with little to no explanation or context. As a CS major I'm used to reading documentation, but you aren't given enough time in class to read about the function. Attendance is mandatory, but useless. Expect to learn the entire class on your own with a poorly written textbook.

The midterms are no longer open note like people said below. This class kept me up at night stressing because he didn't teach us how to do anything well at all. Thank you for inspiring to switch out of the statistics major lol.

His powerpoints are not helpful and the work does not feel like the only preq needed is stor 155. The homework is so hard and so was the first midterm. The midterm average was literally a 67. He doesn't teach he just writes code and expects you to learn everything on your own.

Out of all the comsci courses I've taken hes got to be the most usless. He doesn't answer the piazza questions students have, his lectures are pointless (he just does the code and doesn't explain it), has weird trust issues during exams (and then tries to one-up you by saying hes recording you). Just overall, not very good.

McLean has insane trust issues. He wants to report students for breaking the honor code. He records the room while you take exams. Obviously, you'll be fine, just do your work yourself, but his obsession with finding cheaters makes the course stressful. The entire semester I was worried about accidentally breaking honor code, even though I wasn't.

Mclean is a very kind professor and really cares about his students, but is still very serious about his work. He does give a lab every week for the lab portion, but there is time to work on it during the lab time. The class was project heavy since there are no tests/midterms but there were quizzes and analyses which worked as assessments.

Absolutely don't take STOR 120 with McLean. He makes all labs and homeworks due before each midterm. His in class midterms are difficult but his take home midterms are all right. The final was the only reason why my grade boosted, but he never curves each midterm or final, so beware. Even on the last midterm, the average was low but he didn't care.

Nice and smart professor, very organized, a lot of homework that was sometimes difficult, occasionally dull lectures that were more because of the material than him, a group final project that maybe could have been structured a little better. Quizzes had a bit confusing layout but they're all common sense so they were often pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: he's a nice guy but work load went insane. it was extremely fast paced. quiz, lab, homework due every week. midterms were hard but thank GOD for the take home tests and that cushioning. oh lord study for that final, prepare for it as much as you can, I AM WARNING YOU! girl next to me started crying during it (not even being dramatic).

He is an amazing guy. The third midterm was brutal but if you read and understood the concepts you will do very well. The workload is massive, but it is a 4-credit course for a reason. I will take him a zillion times. Nice guy.

Jeff McLean is a nice person outside of class. In class, however, the lectures are organized but difficult to follow. He does NOT record lectures anymore and unless you are typing notes for every aspect, it will be tough to go back and follow. Homework and weekly labs are graded on correctness. Take this class with friends and a peer tutor.

Amazing! He was very understanding and genuine in wanting each student to succeed. He took the time to answer all questions clearly and was very approachable. If you try your best, come prepared, and get clarification on anything you are confused about, you will do well.

McLean is great. The complaints about too much work aren't quite fair; the class is 4 credit hours after all. And it is definitely NOT more work than the average stem class. Good lectures and fair exams. Cheating is rampant so I understand why McLean is vigilant about it.

Edit: Lowered to 4 because of no curve. The tests absolutely need a curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Mclean is serious about the Honor Code Violations and WILL give them out easily. he recorded class during an exam to check later if we were cheating or not on in person exams. there are 6 midterms and get ready to dedicate most of your study time to this class. this class is more work than your average stem class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There is an unreasonable amount of work for this class. Mclean has 6 midterms + a final. Labs+HW take up at least 10+ hours a week. I have no time to do other work or study. I was up til 4am working on a take-home exam due the next morning instead of studying for my other midterms and I ended up failing everything due of it. DO NOT ever miss class.

An outrageous amount of work. Im a junior, so I understand a workload, but Prof McLean thinks this is our only class. Next week, we have a take home exam on Mon., due Wed. Also on Wed. We have an in class midterm. We just got assigned a homework and lab due the day of the midterm (takes hours) that is graded for accuracy. Im drowning in work :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class over the summer, and it was manageable. You do have to pay attention during lecture and keep up with the constant homework and labs (which were all graded for accuracy). Do not fall behind. Dr. McLean and the TAs were helpful in answering questions on assignments. The class structure is straightforward and organized.

Prof McLean assigned a TON of assignments. Do not take this class alongside other difficult classes, it will be difficult to manage. Very difficult class if you do not attend every.single.lecture. and pay 100% attention the whole, also very easy to fall behind quickly.

Overall a nice guy and decent professor. A ton of homework and assignments, but drop grades make it very doable. Only complaint is that the final was pretty substantially harder than the in-class and hw content. Definitely better at explaining the code than the underlying statistics, but recorded lectures are always nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was a super hard and slow grader. The final felt designed for ppl to fail. Decent class but very mid from the final

Very organized, the class was nothing special but was very straightforward. McLean gives clear lectures and is happy to help students outside of class. If you can, take this class with a friend or make friends. Coding is easier with more people's input!
Good professor, lots of homework/lab assignments. Midterms were open note but still kinda hard. If you work hard, you can easily get an A!

Dr. McLean is definitely the most organized professor I've had during my time at UNC. You can always find what you should know and what you should be doing. Some of the exams were a bit tricky, in terms of asking for niche concepts that were either briefly covered or require an amount of intuition that might seem random. Great content to learn tho!

The lectures were a little boring, but if you went to lecture, it made the homework super manageable. All tests and quizzes were open note and open book so nothing was ever super difficult. He recorded and posted most, if not all of is his lectures which was really helpful when doing some of the homework assignments in case you missed anything.

Professor Mclean does assign a lot of hw but if you do the hw you do not need to study for the exams since the hw covers everything you need to know.The exams are manageable if you put in the work (unfortunately I slacked off for this class don't be like me!)Overall, great prof,managable class if you are ready to put in a bit of effort !
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. McLean was very knowledgeable and passed on the concepts really well, but the class structure was definitely an issue. We never had enough time on the tests and quizzes, and it felt like he was testing our R skills instead of understanding of class material. He forces you to apply your learning at a deep level, which is helpful. Good luck!

Not too difficult, great intro to R. Mclean is great, very helpful. Class is not too bad, homeworks take time but not too much. Middle of the road STEM class in time it takes up. Overall one of easier STOR courses.

Dr. McClean is really knowledgable and makes the content very digestible.  Open book quizzes/tests but you really need to understand the material to do well because you only have 50 minutes on them. Also helps to read the textbook before class and do the suggested exercises.
Probably one of the best stats profs I've had!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I didn't HATE this class, but I dreaded lectures because he literally just talks at you for the full block. The lectures drag, and he doesn't always explain what he's doing or why he's doing it so it can be easy to get lost. BEWARE of the in class midterms, they're only worth 5% of your grade each but everyone bombs them.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor McLean is great. He makes STOR120 really easy to pass and do well on as exams are open note/internet and much of your grade is homework and lab assignments that are easy if you pay attention in class. He also posts lecture recordings so you can easily catch up if you miss class. If you can take STOR120 with McLean, DO IT!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very clear lectures, and the homework, group projects, quizzes, midterms, and the final were all understandable and easy as long as you come to class and pay attention.

Professor McLean was the best professor I have encountered in UNC's statistics department. Attendance in lectures is optional as professional Mclean uploads live recordings following class, however, I have found that frequent attendance significantly helps on the exams, as it can be difficult playing catch up. Overall a very manageable course

Prof McLean is extremely organized and records every single lecture while also posting all necessary materials used in class. As someone who gets caught in the cycle of skipping class, this was a bit dangerous. However, as long as you attend class/watch lectures later and complete homework assignments this class is very manageable.

This class is really hard for someone with no coding experience; wish I had taken COMP 110 first. Pay attention to homework and go to office hours for help. Everything is graded for accuracy so try your hardest on homework and labs! They help a lot with the exams. Just follow lectures and understand the content as best as you can as you'll be fine.

McLean is very knowledgeable about the material and it is very applicable to anything. The midterm and quiz questions were sometimes worded weirdly and became confusing compared to the hw and lectures. His lectures are rly detailed and you need to pay attention in class so that you don't miss important details. Overall a good class to take.

Dont know where those good rating came from. taken 120 and 455 from him, basically doing nothing but copy and paste pre written codes for 50 minutes. 3 quiz and 2 mt, quiz 2 result in a hilarious distribution where the curve is overall flat and downward sloping lol, hate this website for not allowing picture upload, really want you guys to see.

Professor's lectures are very straightforward and he makes things very clear. There are a lot of things to do assignment wise but they aren't too time consuming and help you keep a good grade so a few mishaps don't bring you down. If you don't understand things, he directly uses the textbook so just take time to read and understand it.

extremely useful and applicable course material. take time to listen in lectures/read and there is clear reason behind the things he does; he always explains intuitively the purpose/logic behind code. lectures can be a little dull but they make sense. fair exams and grading (everything in previous lecs/hws). great choice for 455 and any others/120

He stands at the front of the room and copy-pastes pre-written code. Moves pretty fast and doesn't give a good explanation as to why he does anything in R. Grading rubrics are often unclear; tests are long and have difficult questions. Hard for people who are new to R. Has Piazza but never replies and is slow to release answer keys.
Super Chill guy. Makes data analytics easy to digest.

This guy taught nothing during lectures but copying and pasting code. He just told the class what he is doing rn but not the reason behind those codes. hw is not too heavy, but there are so many exams. quizzes and exams are given the same time limit but the exams are having much more and harder questions than those on quizzes.  hws are just fine.

Lab attendance is required every week. The class was very interesting, although he can be a bit monotone at times. His entire class is scripted (like he actually reads a script). Tests are very similar to HW and lab work. Overall a very good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof McLean is very organized and straightforward, however it seems a misjudgment to say this class is for beginners. If you have background in coding, you will be absolutley fine. However if you don't have basic stat knowledge prior to taking this class it would be very difficult. Homework is constant, weekly labs and hw graded for accuracy.
Professor McLean was a great professor who was very caring. Midterms are only worth 5%, so he doesn't want exams to sink your grade. Overall, great experience.

The class was basically come in, write code for 50 minutes then leave. Professor Mclean doesn't really do any teaching. This class does have a lot of work as you are assigned a Lab and an HW each week to complete.  Midterm 1, easy. Midterm 2, extremely hard, got a 61. But, lots of assignments and percentages make up for bad grades. Be ready to work

Dr. McLean was a great lecturer and the course content is very interesting. While this is a beginner-level course, he covers a lot of useful advanced material in a fairly intuitive and easy-to-understand way. The coding portions of the class are actually much easier to understand than the actual statistics.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Mclean is amazing with lecture material, his slides are very helpful and he helps you practice your knowledge of the class by doing code in class with him every lecture. Midterms were two parts, one being take home and the other being in class which was slightly more difficult but worth less than the take home portion.

Not for beginners. McLean says that you should be able to take the class without coding experience, but you will definitely need to have some sort of coding background to follow along in this class. He made lessons accessible, but they are hard to follow along because they aren't labeled. So much homework and labs to do in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I loved Jeff!! His lectures were so interesting as he used fun examples for us to apply our data analysis skills.
Ridiculous amount of assignments, stacked together, with concepts you have to apply while never seeing an example like it
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Though it was challenging, I learned so much in this class. He expected us to have no coding background so he taught us from square one then taught us how to apply it to statistics. Class consists of coding along with him on a template similar to the homework and lab where you will apply the knowledge. Find people to do homework with and TAs help.

Jeff was a great professor and was accommodating and flexible during the semester. You learn a lot of things and he is very fair about grading. As long as you watch the lectures / show up and focus on learning, the course will be fine for you
Pretty easy but you learn a lot which is awesome. Great guy, let me reschedule a midterm when I got sick asf

Professor McLean is great, his office hours are super helpful and he is pretty clear about what you need to know. All the tests and quizzes are open note, but they are far easier if you actually study/practice beforehand. While they are slow to grade the homeworks, if you ask he will always put up an answer key.

Wonderful class and introduction to data science! Jeff McLean is a great professor who is very lenient with grading. I missed many lab quizzes and still ended up with an A. I learned so much from this class, and I am glad I took it. I am looking into a career in data science now.

Professor McLean is a solid teacher as he knows very well what exactly he is teaching. However, the amount of homework given is almost brutal. There is rarely a break from the homework you are given. And he didn't curve one of the midterms even though over half the class failed the in class portion so be warned.

Be ready to pay attention in lectures and take side-notes. Professor McLean is very quick to respond to emails outside of class and is willing to answer questions. Don't leave the work to the last minute.

Professor McLean is overall a great person and professor but this class is essentially a computer science course and I struggled to take this course online without having any previous knowledge of coding. Just be ready to put in a lot of work and know that this is not a traditional statistics course.

Overall the class isn't hard, topics on tests and quizzes are gone over in class. You just have to pay attention and not blindly write down whatever code Prof. McLean is writing down. Homework is graded after you take your assessments which sucks. I really liked that he recorded class sessions and was very kind to students asking for help.

Overall I liked Professor Mclean. His lectures consist of copying code that he types in front of you as he explains it. While this may not work for some people, I didn't mind it. You have 1 lab assignment, 1 hw assignment, and 1 lab quiz per week. Overall the workload isn't too bad compared to other stem courses. All work/exams are open notes/web.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is based entirely on your TA and their grading, so it is a risk. Homework was often graded after the exam or quiz, which was hard when you needed interpretation of things. The class is a lot of homework that is usually pretty manageable, but you definitely have to be prepared for it to take up a lot of your time.

Prof McLean is a great teacher and so helpful outside of class. However be warned that it is A LOT of work. I never felt like I could take a breath with the course load of this class which led to me burning out at the end of the semester. He has very detailed lectures and lab examples, so don't be scared, but you definitely have to put in the work.

Prof. McLean is a helpful, considerate professor. Seems to be a cool guy & has a nice beard. There is a good amount of work to do & midterm 2 was rough. The final exam was much better than the midterms. I feel like I learned a lot from this class & am now considering the new data science minor.

McLean was very helpful and kind the entire semester. Near finals he even made class asynchronous to give us more fluidity. Understanding some concepts (p-value, confidence intervals) was confusing, but he tried to help as much as possible. He wants you to do good, and unless you put in no effort, you should do just fine. Majoring in comp sci now!

McLean is competent, organized and helpful in office hours. I like McLean. But I hate STOR 120. Heavy heavy workload (3 projects, 12 hws, 10+ labs, 14 quizzes), doing stats calculations "the long way" in python, half the class getting 70 or below on in-class midterm 2, work over wellness breaks. Run!! If you do take 120 use data8 midterms to study.

Prof McLean is a star!! He taught python so well and made the class very engaging even though it was asynchronous. Some of the coding was hard but he is accessible and so are the TAs. McLean is the only reason I am surviving my current stats class I couldnt do it without him. He gave a strong foundation in 120. This class with McLean is a must!

Prof has assigned loads of work for "Wellness Weekends," and has previously poked fun at the fact that he's assigned too much. Just found out that he pulls most of his assignments from the internet. Weekly homework and labs that take long times, projects and midterms every few weeks. I feel like I never get to breathe in this class.

The course content is easy. Great lecture. You don't need to know the underlying reason behind the computation, just following the examples, which is both a good and a bad thing. The exams and hws only test your knowledge on the surface level, but you may struggle once you enroll in advanced statistic classes without fully understanding the theory.

Very understanding about covid. Made the last test, quiz, and final 24 hours and did not change the difficulty. All tests and quizzes are open notes, he always responded to my emails quickly, understanding of tech issues, posted lectures on time. The group assignments were a little confusing, but he was always easy to contact for any questions

Your grade in this class is determined by labs, projects, homework, and exams. These assignments are not difficult if you watch the class lectures and fill in the notebooks that go along with those lectures. Overall I really loved this class (and I came in with ZERO coding experience).

If you take him for an introductory course like STOR 120, he understands and assumes that you may have no programming experience and takes the perfect amount of time teaching you the basics without making you feel like you're stupid. He does a review before each of his tests which really helps and he makes himself easily available.

Professor McLean was a great professor overall. His lecture videos were great. If I were to give some criticism, it would be that homework and lab questions could be vague sometimes. Usually the questions were pretty clear. The workload is very manageable and the pacing is great.

Despite being an asynchronous online class, I thought Prof. McLean did a great job teaching this class. The homework assignments are reasonable but are graded moderately harshly. The designs of the group projects were pretty confusing at times. Exams and quizzes were often timed, which made them very hard to complete in the set amount of time.

The character limit doesn't do enough justice to how great Prof. McLean's been this semester. 455 can be intimidating to those who haven't programmed in R, but the class is VERY straightforward, he is VERY accessible and understanding. Homeworks vary in length, exams a bit rushed, but he makes everything VERY feasible to do. (TAKE THIS CLASS)

Professor McLean is incredibly skilled and teaches Data Science in such an accessible, understandable, and inspiring way. The topics, the way they're taught, the Jupyter Notebooks - I love everything! This is one of the best decisions I've EVER made in my life to take this class and I don't think there's anyone anywhere who can teach this better.

McLean is a great 455 professor. He posts videos with course content, which is a shame bc he seems like a great guy to know. Regardless, his HW is doable as long as you give yourself more than a day, and the exams are extremely rushed but not that hard. I feel like I've learned 3 semesters worth of material in 2 months with McLean.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: easy to follow, even as a non-stem major. his lectures are clear and detailed, and as long as you pay attention you'll be fine. exams are open note and internet, but a little lengthy so don't get too comfy. coding is needed, but i've never coded before and it was super easy to do  it's not scary.

Don't treat this class like an easy A - put in the work from the beginning and you'll thank yourself. Do not take those open-book open-note exams likely - you need to know the material really well if you want to finish on time. I really appreciate what I learned from this class - it'll definitely be useful in the future!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. McLean is pretty solid. All of the exams are open note and he is very clear with his rubrics and what he expects out of homework assignments. Sometimes I found him going a little too fast and having the expectation that we had some knowledge about R already. However, he is very helpful in office hours and before/after class if you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor McLean is a great professor. The class is fairly easy, all tests and quizzes are open note. A coding system is used in the class, make sure to keep up with all codes. Highly recommend.

Dr. McLean is an awesome professor! I highly recommend taking STOR151 with him if you can. The class is super easy and goes by quickly. He is always available after class for questions. Also, everything is open note so tests are a breeze. We used a coding system in his class so I recommend keeping a section in a notebook just for codes. 10/10!!!!!

mclean is great. he taught me linear reg and logistic reg, both of which are important and interesting. would recommend try harding mclean's 455, its worth it. learned how to use R effectively, though i wish mclean would use tidyverse, because it makes using R a lot cleaner and more satisfying. also, he has pretty great datasets and fair tests
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: McLean is a great lecturer and very helpful in office hours. His homework assignments may be tedious at times but they are great ways to prep for his exams. Make sure to go to class though because his slides are purposefully ambiguous to ensure students show up to class and pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The exams are very much like the homework and are open note. However, lecture slides are extremely unclear, and paying attention in class doesn't help much either since most of it is watching him code.

Easy class. Show up to class, complete the homework which doesn't take long, and organize all of your code in your R notebook so you can just plug things in on the exams. Exams were open note/internet and required little studying if you showed up to class and kept all of your R code organized. Only bad thing: very easy to lose a lot of points.

He's an amazing person. Sometimes you don't want to go to class, but it is needed so that you can get the codes to do everything. Super easy to understand. Stay organized in your code notebook, and just plug and chug on the exam (which are open note). He is an amazing person, and regrades test when TAs graded unfairly!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was the easiest class I took at Carolina. Tests were open everything except each other and they were just like the homework so you can get an A without even studying. Attendance isn't mandatory and he puts everything up on Sakai. Prof. McLean is also just a nice and caring guy so highly recommend his class.

A bit unclear during lectures, switching the class to be more code-heavy. Mainly just shows examples, so if that's how you learn. Weekly online assignments with multiple attempts, rare written hw. Attendance isn't mandatory but if you show up, you'll do better hearing him talk than just looking at slides. Ready to answer dumb questions
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: McLean is a wonderful professor. It's almost all lecturing, but he is good at it. When a student had a question, he would answer thoroughly and make sure they understood. Biggest of all, he cares about YOU. He raised my grade significantly on an exam a TA had graded and gave us answers to a homework that was poorly phrased. Great guy.

stor151 with mclean is a MUST. it is so so easy, practically got 100s on all my exams without studying and he lets you all the resources you want on the exams. He is always helpful during office hours and his exams were just like the homework. No curveballs and overall an amazing professor. Attendance in his class was not mandatory and no one came.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: The tests were just like the homework. You can use all notes and powerpoints during the tests. Three written homework assignments, and then 2 weekly easy online assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I am a star major student, and he is one of the worst lecturers I've ever seen. He just reads the slides which are unorganized and useless. The only thing we do in class is typing or copying the codes that we don't understand since he never explain how they work. The grading criteria are very unclear and confused, he does not give homework answers

This dude just stands in front of the class and rambles on about his terribly unorganized powerpoints. This class was so difficult that I decided to withdrawal from University and go work on the coal mines. Steady pay and I don't have to deal with R-studio. No regrets on my end.

He's a great lecturer and overall the class is very manageable. His homework is pretty straightforward and he'll do his best to help out. Tests are like the homework so not very much theory based. Easy to miss points if you don't actually understand the course material though. Was able to skip half his classes and keep up with online class notes

Prof McLean is a great professor as he explains the concept very well and the workload over the course is manageable. Also, he will teach how to use software to do all the calculate stuff which is more helpful than other STOR 155 class. However, you should attend the class regularly as the tests will have many question explained in class.

McLean is great at explaining concepts and a really nice guy. I've never liked statistics before, but I found this class pretty interesting and useful. He focuses on software rather than doing anything tedious by hand. Homework is easy, group projects are a bit vague but not too hard, and tests are straightforward if you come to class.

Dr. McLean, in my opinion, is a great professor. The class made me want to take more statistic courses. However, his tests are difficult, but you can have note sheets with you during the tests. For the final exam, you can have up to four note sheets. The group projects' criteria are vague, but they are not too difficult.

Homework seemed easy, but the exams were completely different and very complicated. Gave no extra credit, office hours were pointless. He gave projects with no criteria and then just threw out random grades. He teaches units and uses software that is completely different from the other STOR 155 classes so don't expect to get help from friends.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Look I'm going to it real with y'all! The homework is so so easy, but the exams ARE SO DIFFICULT FOR NO APPARENT REASON! He contradicts him self frequently and when given projects he does not have a clear, concise concrete idea in mind on what he wanted. Gave no extra credit at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Jeff is a great lecturer and a very solid choice for 455. Lectures were clear and concise, something not too common in the STOR department. Assignments emphasized coding in R and applying concepts to do real data analysis, which felt useful. Exams aren't too tricky, but require clear knowledge of concepts since there is a definite time crunch.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The homework and tests make up your entire grade. Homework is fairly easy as he will help you go through it during office hours if you need help. Tests are essentially what was on the homework with different data sets. He doesn't focus too heavily on the theory, preferring to help you understand the output from your R code.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really like Professor McClean and his class! The class moves at a nice pace, and the workload is very manageable. Most people in the class had never used R before; however, he does a very good job at teaching the basics. If you want to get really good at regression and R (which is important for anyone STEM), I would definitely take 455 with him!
Be aware that the tests are not always like homework.
Bro it was so haed to underrstand the writing bro
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took in Spring 2025, and I believe it was his first time teaching. He was not very confident at the front of the room, and he could be somewhat condescending at times. He was late to his own office hours and at times wouldn't show up. He grades the homework strict but drops the lowest 2, and the class was curved. I would avoid taking it with him.

Nice guy but harsh grader. He took off points easily by a few things, and homework were harshly graded. Final was not easy as agreed. It's hard to get decent grade in his class although he curved the boundary.

Nice guy, horrible teacher. Unorganized lectures, unclear expectations of students, no resources for success. HARSH grader - doesn't accept certain proofs even if they're correct in the textbook. Was late multiple times to his own office hours. DO NOT TAKE DISCRETE WITH HIM. but he is willing to work with students.

He was an okay professor for discrete, but sometimes seemed confused on what he was teaching or by simple questions students asked. A very tough grader and doesn't accept methods other than what was taught in class (even if its in the textbook/still correct). Office hours are slightly helpful for explanations.

Lectures can be a little dry sometimes, and the time would be better spent going over textbook yourself at certain points in the class. The class can be pretty hard but eventually becomes pretty easy. It was also pretty hard to do well on the homework assignments. He's a genuine guy despite that, and made sure we know how to write good proofs.

He was not super great at communicating what we NEEDED to learn during lectures and seemed to focus more on what he felt like teaching versus what would be on the overall (professor determined) final exam
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a really good professor, but half of the semester it felt like we were learning the same thing over and over again. Overall, lots of assignments and only 1 midterm and a final, which were really easy, so def recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. King is passionate and wants to share her knowledge, if you are taking ANTH270 after the spring 2026 semester the exams are in person and the classroom is interactive, with groups of four. Attendance is not mandatory but random attendance checks are done during the semester. Overall I would recommend this class and professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures are long, and she tends to repeat the same idea multiple times. There are at least 2 readings per week. There are asynchronous quizzes based on the reading, and there are 6 essays you need to write, and 1 can be dropped. Attendance isn't mandatory, but she includes pop-up participation grades that cannot be dropped.

Dr. King is very lenient about attendance, but there are in person assignments for part of the grade so it's still important to show up. Very easy class and 1-2 assignments a week. Lectures aren't super content heavy or interesting. Attending recitations is super important for your grade.

Dr. King is great! She is very knowledgeable and a good lecturer. The readings for this class were super interesting, and the discussion elements made class engaging—certainly an achievable A, but maybe not super easy. The final was discussion-based and creative, albeit a little odd. I would definitely recommend if you're interested in med anth!

Dr. King is a miserable person. She is not friendly, kind, or approachable. Her classes are also completely tailored to her woke agenda. ANTH 448 is supposed to be Medicine in the American South. 99% of the class was talking about one race, Black, and racism, specifically in the 18-1900s. There is a lot more to the American South than one race.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: lots of readings. every week there was either a reading quiz (online) or an essay due. midterm and final are online. class was only monday and wednesday with one recitation. there are random attendence checks. overall, very interesting topics and not too time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Interesting med anth class, only 6 reading responses every other week and some annotation assignments. Grading criteria is unclear and grading is harsh sometimes so make sure to check over work. Lots of surprise in-class assignments so you have to attend every class as they do not drop any assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class is nice, and the readings are time-consuming, but so interesting! I found the lectures less engaging with Dr. King, since she (although passionate) can be redundant, but the most important points are in the slideshows. The content is great for someone looking for an intro to medical anthropology. Weekly readings + async assessments

she is def passionate about the subject and the class Is usually interesting. reading the articles is really annoying though but its really easy and there are no tests except for the final. super easy class. I like her

Find another gen ed to take because she acts like this class is a priority and is extremely rude and condescending. Provides a rubric for assignments that she doesn't actually use.
