reviews.comment: Content was interesting but lectures were boring and assignments were a drag to complete. Not hard, do your work and you will pass. You can get away with skimming the readings as they're only really brought up in recitation. Wasn't my favorite class but could float your boat

Dr. King was very arrogant/pompous. She liked to make smug comments to the class about our participation and discussion posts/responses. She was pretty rude. Most lectures involved her going on tangents or spewing her opinions to the class. She liked to talk about herself as well. Did not get a whole lot out of the lectures. Very reading heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Knowledgeable about the course material, but monotonous lectures made the class extremely boring. She is unwilling to accommodate students who have to miss class for any reason and is not compassionate. Additionally, she refused to round up grades, even by 0.1% to the next letter grade, which discouraged me from ever taking a class with her again.

This class is interesting intersection of health and social issues but the lectures got very boring at times along with the out of class readings.  Assignments every week are either a short 10-15 question online quiz or short reading response which are super easy to complete so long as you do the readings/listen to the lecture.

Loved Dr. King but her lectures were so boring. You will be doing two-page write-ups so be ready based on weekly readings. The content is really interesting and makes you question your views on biomedicine as a system. Your recitation TA matters as they grade your write-ups which make up majority of your grade. Really easy gen ed and med anth class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: ANTH 270 was not a difficult class, just a lot of reading that could catch up with you if you were not careful. There is either a take home quiz that you can attempt twice or a writing assignment due every week on Thursday night, but you can skip two of the assignments. There are also random attendance activities during lecture, so don't skip class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easiest A yet! Professor was not as approachable, however, she was a great lecturer and very passionate about med anth. Participation was important, she did polls and canvas assignments. Only 4 useless recitations but the TA's were nice and graded lightly. Its easy to get an A as long as you do the work and attend class. Would take again!

Dr. King is definitely passive aggressive, but is so straightforward and I really enjoyed her passion about what we learned in 270. If you do as she says, you'll get an A. The layout this past spring was mandatory lecture (because of in class polls) and 4 recitations the whole semester. Would take her again!

Dr. King does not answer emails and is not very approachable. She does not share her lecture slides so you need to take your own notes word for word. But, everything in the class is broken down very clearly and if you take great notes, you'll get an A in the class because the quizzes/exams are open note. All you need to do is try and you're good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Workload was extremely light for this course. Respectfully though, Dr. King took this class way too seriously. reviews.comment: This class was very exam/reading heavy. The professor does not hold class on recitation days. If you are good at reading quickly and writing then you will be good. I did not find the lectures particularly helpful, but the class was easy overall. The professor ranted a lot of political ideology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lectures were incredibly boring (covered a weeks worth of material over the entire semester). Required very little work. Had a few random attendance quizzes throughout the semester. Recitation only met every other week. Assignments and readings were easy and straightforward.

Professor King is a great professor, and is very knowledgeable about her field and shares a lot of her personal research experience. ANTH 326 is set up like a graduate seminar, so it's mostly just participation grades up until the midterm and final, which were seminar discussions! Overall, just show up and do the readings, and it'll be a fun class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures were often pretty boring but lecture attendance is never graded, only recitation is and recitation only meets 4 times over the semester. A lot of reading but the readings were always interesting. There are assignments due at the end of every week but they are not difficult as long as you read most of the material required.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. King explains course material clearly and thoroughly. Lectures could get boring, but group activities were a time for the students to really connect with the material and regain focus. Reading responses & quizzes make up majority of the grade, but are fairly easy to complete. Would recommend to pre-med and med anth students.

Lectures can be boring sometimes but she required a lot of group activities. Weekly quizzes or papers that were online and pretty easy, and you were allowed to skip two of each. Recitation only meets 4 times. No midterm and take home final.

Dr. King is very knowledgable. Lectures can be repetitive sometimes, but this makes it possible to miss a couple classes/skip readings and you'll be just fine. No midterm; take-home final; everything else is reading responses/quizzes, and you don't have to do all of them. Overall a great course for beginner or veteran med anth students alike :)

She was a little boring, but it was overall an easy class. There were a lot of readings (including 2 full books), but I only read about 5 pages of each, and I was fine. A lot of it is intuitive. Weekly papers or quizzes, but only test is the final.

Dr. King is amazing! This is my second class with her, and I hope to take more. She's so caring and passionate about her classes. Skimming the assigned readings is necessary, but the readings are pretty interesting. There's a lot of group work (which went great), and the assignment prompts weren't terribly hard to answer. Great class!

class was manageable. TA was harsh grader, but can't control that since you  can't pick. Class was interesting. Feedback on work took too long which was frustrating. Honestly, it bothers me that the class itself is good but the way they grade you makes it less enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: not sure what happened this sem. heard good things about this class, but experience: horrible. Feedback on papers took forever, literally the last week of class! reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This is probably the easiest class I have taken here. The lecture material is very interesting and so are the readings. That being said Professor King is a pretty dry lecturer, I found myself having a hard time paying attention in most classes.

Dr. King is one of the best professors I've had at UNC and I want to take every class with her. The assignments are straightforward, and the exam isn't too difficult if you pay attention in lecture and do the readings.

reviews.comment:
Matha King is the best ever!

reviews.comment: If you show up to recitation and do the weekly assignments, you are guaranteed an A. Lectures can be monotonous, but taking digital notes will help with the Final (take-home).

I enjoyed Dr. King as a professor! She was very accommodating to our class this semester, you can tell she really cared about the student's mental health and performance. The workload was manageable, short quizzes, reading responses, recitation participation, plus a final. I enjoyed the readings and discussions we had in class. Overall good choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. King refused to grant me my accommodations, even though I have a 504 plan. She is the single worst professor Ive had at UNC. I found Dr. Kings recorded lectures to be kind of dry and boring and I disliked recitation. But I liked the books we read for this class. Overall an easy A

Meh. The class is at least interesting, but I had heard a lot of good stuff about this class and I don't think it's really been that life-changing or mind-blowingly good. It's an easy A, the material is fine. It's just fine.

Dr. King wasn't a particularly inspirational or caring professor, but the content of her course was interesting. The readings were very interesting and manageable, and I found that everything was graded pretty easily.

I was disappointed because since the class was asynch I never really interacted with her and she never really had sessions besides office hours and we mainly worked with our assigned TA but she seemed really nice during the lecture videos. Class was mainly readings and reading responses with a final exam that was only 10% of the overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: I loved professor King! This class is all participation so make sure you show up to class and read the readings! Most of the readings were interesting and I got a lot of of this class. I recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: The lecture was asynchronous, but they were posted and short, sweet and to the point. Recitation was mandatory and synchronous and participation matters. Lots of reading and posed as a Wednesday-Wednesday class rather than Mon-Fri. Interesting class taught well. All emphasis on short papers due every week. She knows her stuff though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I love Dr. King! I have taken 3 different courses taught by Dr. King and I really enjoyed them all and did fairly well. She splits up the writing assignments into a few short ones over the semester instead of having super long papers. Content is very interesting. She was very understanding and flexible throughout the pandemic!

Dr. King is a great choice for ANTH 470. The class was very interesting, and she was very understanding during the transition to online learning. She gives engaging and interesting lectures and assigns readings that are very doable. Would highly recommend.

I really enjoyed this class with Dr. King. She is so knowledgeable and passionate about the content, her lectures are almost like TED talks. I learned so much in this class! Everything is graded by a TA (I loved mine), and if you do the readings and take notes in class you can get an easy A.

Lots of readings and a short response due every week. Not a bad lecturer but can get boring. If you enjoy medical anthropology then you should really enjoy this class. Pick a good TA because they grade everything.

TAs grade everything. During the lecture, my friend always fell asleep. Taking good notes are necessary. If you are very interested in the topic (medical anthropology), you'll enjoy the reading assignments every week. There's short reading response every week that you should be aware of.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She lets us out of class about 15 minutes early every lecture. All grading is determined by the TA, so keep that in mind. You have a short essay writing assignment just about every week, but you don't have any long papers which is nice. Recitation occurs almost every week, too, and attendance to that is mandatory. Fair amount of reading each week.

Professor King made this class both interesting and educational. This was my favorite class I have taken this semester! Dr. King is incredibly knowledgeable and aims to make the class interesting and informative. She is a great professor and I would highly recommend taking a course with her. Her small classes are better!

Dr. King splits up the writing requirement for a 400-level course over the semester, so there are no papers greater than 600 words. Such an interesting class and she lets us out early every class! Would definitely take Dr. King again
Seriously the GOAT- and my fav class at UNC. No other words- he had engaging lectures, passionate and serious discourse at times, but kept it light and a great time.
Best Professor at Kenan-Flagler hands down. Most engaging and inspirational dude ever. If you get the chance, definitely take 404 with him.

Wow -- what a great class and such a caring professor. Class is graded on a curve so its hard to earn an A but such great lectures and fun material. Really loved every lecture and each project. Very caring and inspirational when talking about how ethics interplay with business. Highly reccomend taking 404 with Kundro.

Great teacher! He really goes above and beyond to make class engaging and makes sure everyone is having a good time during lectures. He's super kind and genuinely cares about the topics he teaches.  Would definitely recommend taking 404 with him.
Tim is one of the best professors i've had at KF. If you participate and study for the quiz you'll be set. Class is unplugged which I actually liked. Wish he taught more undergrad classes.
The best. Super engaging. Best class/prof at KF.

Amazing professor, definitely take 404 with him. Unplugged classes with lots of fun participation activities makes the time fly by and helps you learn. Reading and homework is pretty minimal, but he's not a pushover. He's the funniest professor I've had so far and clearly makes an effort to make class entertaining. One of my favorite professors!
really nice prof, his projects are fun compared to other classes, quiz isn't bad and it reflects the lectures, class is unplugged which is really nice, the readings are also interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: what can i say about tim, hes the man! i looked forward to each class of his, he made learning fun. and its a plus that hes easy on the eyes. tim gets an A+ from me!!

Amazing class. Tim is super fun and I enjoyed his class everyday. Beware of one incredibly hard midterm that is a huge chunk of your grade. I got A's on every assignment and then did bad on the quiz and ended the class with a B. Other than he is a great teacher and deserves the world!

Tim is the boy. Best class I have taken at the B-school so far. Looked forward to each class because of how engaging Tim made them. He has your sanity in mind and does a great job of conveying concepts and teaching students without swamping you in unnecessary work. GOATED

Tim is the best professor I've had so far. He really cares about students and his grading is extremely fair. He made lectures really enjoyable and easy to pay attention. Group project heavy but he balances the class to evaluate in a variety of methods.
Her Engl105 is focused around environmental studies, which usually bores me to death, but she kept things interesting. If you're a competent writer you'll be absolutely find with her.

Krysten was awesome. Her class is environmentally focused, which is not usually something I would enjoy focusing on, but she ran it so well that I ended up liking it a lot. She encourages discussions/debate in class (especially materialism vs. idealism). If you are a reasonably strong writer, you will have zero issues and appreciate the discussions

She was great, very approachable, an excellent choice for ENGL105. The class will be environmentally focused, even if you're taking a specific concentration of the class like humanities. I found her grading to be very lenient, everything I turned in was an easy A.

Krysten is such a unique and interesting professor to have. She really just cares about you becoming a better writer, without making you jump through hoops. She is very clear on what she is looking for and will let you resubmit papers for a regrade if you are not happy. I think most people in this class will end with an A.

I loved Krysten and I'm not even an English person in general. She's funny, I will say her classes are pretty much lectures but they're very engaging and she's super understanding about missing class.

She is great. She's super down-to-earth, gives no tests, and pretty much grades all projections/essays on completion(I ended with a 100.0), as long as you put effort and follow her instructions. She focuses a lot on plants from various perspectives to teach class, so if you find that boring, she may not be for you, but definitely extremely easy A.
Krysten is great, really funny and passionate about plants. Super chill with grading, and I'm really grateful she was my ENGL 105 professor!!

Given that you put effort into assignments, it is very likely that you will end the class with a 100. This is one of the best professors you can take for ENGL105, and she is very caring to her students. There is an attendance/participation grade, but she is very lenient with grading it.

I loved this class, and the teacher was very passionate, making each class interesting! There was a lot of writing, but she graded easily and helped whenever needed. I love her, she is hilarious, definitely take her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: She is literally amazing! She is super into plants and coloniality so be prepared to talk about that for the entire class. She is very kind with her grading and attendance policy as well. I was really glad to have her as my ENGL105 teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Easy A, just go to class and write the papers and you'll get a 100, definitely sounds easier than what I've heard from friends about other professors.
Easiest A ever. She is also very kind and understanding. She gets that we're just there to fulfill the requirement. I didn't go to half the classes... She is really cool definitely take this class!
She's great, easy A for 105
She is a really nice professor, and grades the assignments very easily. I've only not gotten a 100 0nce.

Great teacher. Gives in depth feedback and cares about your success. There are a lot of readings but she doesn't expect you to comprehend all of them in depth. Moderately easy assignments and opportunities for regrade and revisions on papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Krysten is a great english teacher. You have 3 main units; the first two are essays and the final one was a group podcast. As long as you revise your work and keep improving, you will get an A in this class. Definitely try to take it

Krysten is such a chill professor that balances her class better than I've seen any other professor thus far. I came out of her class feeling like I learned a lot but also never felt overwhelmed. Do whatever you can to take this class, you will not regret it.

Prof Voelkner has been my favorite instructor thus far at UNC. Her course material is SO engaging and interesting. She is super chill and I always looked forward to attending her class. She is also super accessible outside of class and understanding of personal conflicts. Take her for 105 if you have the chance!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Krysten is a really great instructor for regular 105. You don't follow the normal 105 structure, so you're able to write about things that actually interest you. I highly recommend signing up for her section of 105. There are some extra readings as well, but you can just look up summaries online.

Krysten was so accommodating and genuinely cares about her students. There were 2 projects: 1 literary analysis and another which you could choose between a creative/art project and an autoethnography

I was automatically put into her class for the required freshman English. Very easy. Had three papers over the semester, no final exam. Most everybody got 100s on all of the assignments. She is very nice and cool. A little boring during class but I am not a fan of English at all. Good choice, easy A, and some interesting topics.

I LOVED this class. I took this class my freshman year, terrified because there was a lot of upperclassmen but the professor was very welcoming and the class environment was definitely stress free. The readings aren't hard, the class definitely helps explore oneself. I would take this class again without a doubt.

krysten is so nice, understanding, & very passionate about what she does . The topics she chooses for us to right about were very niche and weren't always the most interesting which made them kinda hard plus she did grade a bit harshly. she lets you resubmit but i resubmitted using her comments and didnt improve a ton. solid pick for 105 though

Loved her class. Fully conversation based and you only have 2 papers and a final presentation based on the last paper. She cares about her students and the material is also super interesting. She also lets you re-submit the midterm paper if you want a better grade. Super cool, definitely recommend

Great choice for ENGL105! She has 3 units, with each unit having 1-5 page papers due at the end of them. She's a very lenient grader and doesn't expect too much out of you. She's also super personable and understands if you need extensions or anything like that. If you need to take ENGL105, she's a very good choice for an easy A.

Professor Voelkner was so kind and caring! She was always available for questions outside of class and gave great feedback. She was willing to understand our situations, which was really helpful in an online class. While I did not enjoy waking up for class at 8 a.m., this class was pretty manageable and helpful as an intro to writing assignments.

Krysten is really chill and nice and a good teacher. We had mandatory zoom once a week and could keep our cameras off. There are weekly writing assignments and a presentation at the end. Sometimes it was stressful but other times easy.

Voelkner is kind and funny and is a lenient grader. She wants you to do well so she gives good feedback but isn't too harsh when grading papers. This class was three papers (one of which required a visual presentation and 3 minute speech) and the final was just a portfolio highlighting these papers. Loved having her class!
I took 418. She's super funny, lectures are engaging, exams are fair and not many other assignments. Her grading is good, nothing to complain, I would definitely take her again

Reissner is the sweetest person and amazing teacher. However, her tests are tricky because there is so much information and little guidance. Same goes with her papers-you never get a score back and have no idea how you did.

reviews.comment:
She really enjoys what she's teaching! Very approachable. 
She was quite accommodating and seemed like she cared about how we were doing.

Tests were not bad. Doesn't give a rubric for papers, kinda vague.

Dr. Reissner was one of my favorite professors at UNC. You could tell how passionate she was about the content of the class and it made lectures so exciting. reviews.comment: Dr. Reissner is one of the kindest professors I've ever had at UNC, esp. with COVID. Willing to extend guidelines and work with the class if everyone agrees that something doesn't feel fair. She does grade pretty strictly for the tests, and they're really difficult if you don't take good notes. Two small papers, one longer research paper.

Dr. Reissner cares so much about the topic and that everyone is stress-free while learning it. A super interesting first-year seminar that everyone can relate to while Dr. Reissner being super nice about grading. She cares a ton and is always available. 3 papers graded nicely and a few fairly easy quizzes made this class super enjoyable

Professor Reissner is wonderful!! She cares deeply about her students success both in and outside of the classroom. Her lectures were very interesting. I would be excited going to her class. The quizzes and papers are not hard because she outlines the necessary information clearly. This is such an eye-opening first year seminar. I loved it!

Dr. Reissner was the best professor I ever had at UNC. Her lectures are extremely straightforward and in-depth. She's extremely efficient at preparing you for the four quizzes and four papers. She genuinely cares about her students and always puts their interests first.

Dr. Reissner is absolutely amazing! Her depth of knowledge in the subject makes her lectures very dense and informative. She is very good at explaining the material and always answers questions! Although the material is difficult, she really wants her students to do well! My favorite class ever at UNC- it inspired me to be pre-pharm! Amazing class!

Dr. Reissner's FYS was awesome. You could tell she really cared about the material and tried to get the class interested in it as well. Class was a super easy A- only homework is 3 short papers throughout semester graded basically for completion. Course material was engaging and relevant. Highly recommend taking this course.

Dr. Booth is truly an amazing professor and human. You get out of her course exactly what you put into it. She is a lecturer who challenges you to think and especially encourages discussion, so get ready to talk.This is a collaborative learning class, so group and individual participation is ESSENTIAL. She is also WONDERFUL in office hours.

This was an amazing class! Prof B did a great job at explaining the main components of reproductive justice and she created a good environment for meaningful discussion. There is a semester long project but it was broken down into check points with feedback along the way.

Prof B. is a great professor! She is very knowledgeable and is able to teach a wide variety of topics. This is a survey course so there is a lot of material to go over but Professor Booth does a great job at explaining the nuances of all of them. There is a semester long research project but it broken up into manageable segments with feedback.

The class has assigned reading assignments followed up by in class discussion and pop quizzes. Talking with other students definitely helps with better understanding different experiences in the community. Overall I think this class is definitely worthwhile!

I was worried to take a class with Prof B due to her poor rating but I found her class pleasant. She can be a bit old school but I feel her class is accessible to disabled students and she's incredibly understanding. I also felt the class material and assignments were understandable/doable. Prof Booth is also a good resource for WGST majors.

I've taken and enjoyed two classes with Booth. This class emphasizes participation b/c it is a discussion-based class. Yes, Prof. Booth talks a lot, but I think she is insightful. reviews.comment: Idk why there are so many bad ratings. Everyone who actually tried/cared about the class seemed to do really well. There were some that just didn't put effort in and I'm assuming they're the ones rating her. She's genuinely the sweetest professor I've ever had. She's so understanding and will work with you if you go to office hours.

IGNORE THE POOR RATINGS. They were in my class and literally didn't put effort into it/care abt it at all. They're just offended their grade actually reflected the quality of their work lol. Prof B is the sweetest. If you actually care abt social justice and you try in class, you'll be golden. Unfortunately those who liked the class didn't rate her

I highly recommend taking this class with professor booth. She is so knowledgeable of reproductive care around the world and you will learn a great amount in this class. This is the second class I have taken with her, and I will be looking for more classes to take with her in the future.

Professor booth is an amazing professor and I loved having multiple classes with her. I have taken 2 classes with her now and loved both of them. She is extremely caring for every student in her class and is very knowledgeable of every topic she teaches. She is an amazing person and I will be looking for classes to take with her in the future.

I was hesitant to enroll because of the ratings, but I'm so so glad I took her class. Professor Booth is kind, knowledgeable, and truly cares about her students. Discussions are open and respectful, and different opinions are welcomed. I would absolutely take another class with this amazing professor!!!

Do not let the other reviews lie to you. Professor Booth is extremely knowledgeable, down-to-earth, open-minded, and caring. Grading rubrics are somewhat tedious, but mundane compared to what college students should realistically be expected of. The class is quite elementary. Readings are simple and straightforward, as are class assignments. 10/10.

This was the first time that she taught the class. For the final, it is a research project and presentation, and the rubric was very unclear of what she wants and when you ask questions she doesn't give a solid answer. There were a lot of pre-class readings that were being discussed about during class, which participation mattered a lot.

unclear grading criteria and was late/disorganized with many assignments and their rubrics, cared about the class as a whole but made some portions unnecessarily difficult. research project was main part of grade

Solid class, but instruction was just plain boring sometimes. Dr. Booth has a very interesting collection of  personal research and ideas that reflects in this class, but she is not very engaging. Would take again tho. Maybe WGST388 is better since it directly relates to her field? All my papers and exams were graded fairly by the TA.

She only calls on a few students that she knows will agree with her even if others have their hands up.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

- Extremely tough grader. If you don't say exactly what she wants, how you want, as if she wrote it herself, you will not get a good grade

Really interesting readings though, I did learn a lot from them.

STEM senior here. okay yes, she is probably the worst professor I have ever had at UNC. yes, she is probably the worst grader I have ever had. yes, she's probably the worst lecturer I have ever had. however, if you don't really care about your GPA, she's alright. she's also nice in office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I did do well in this course, but unfortunately I would not recommend it with Prof. Booth. Grading criteria was not specifically stated, feedback was harsh, and the assignments were not necessarily clear.

This teacher will only respond to your emails when she wants to and will wait several days to only state you need to discuss the concerns in person. Additionally, she does not follow her syllabus to the detriment of your grade. I was given an 85 on a completion graded assignment: complete (95), partially complete (75), and incomplete (0)

DON'T TAKE A CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR!! I cannot express how AWFUL she is; there is no clear rubric for anything, she gives extremely harsh and unhelpful feedback, and changes her mind on how she is grading papers with no warning, explanation, or rationale. As a WGST major, she has made me rethink that given I will inevitably have her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She eats college student's dreams for breakfast. Would have changed major/minor if i knew it would be this bad. Cant understand most of what she says. Subjective grading. Forces her ideas onto you. passive aggressive. Cried more times than I can count. Left all important work for last 3wks. Adds new/graded assignments w/10days left in semester. RUN

This teacher is such a harsh grader and I swear that I can never do anything right. I am trying to take her feedback but it is so convoluted, confusing, and unhelpful. I am exhausted and near tears often over how frustrating it is to try and do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: We're 6 weeks into class and I've already cried about this class more than once. She's worse than I expected, so unreasonable, and the class is absolutely useless.

I normally lend caution to RMP ratings- but don't take Prof Booth if you don't have to for your major/minor. She's exclusionary, isn't' clear on grading criteria, announces large syllabus shifts at random, and is not flexible or understanding to student's experiences. Listen to the previous RMP posts, they're right.

Do not take this class or any class with Professor Booth. She has an insane attendance policy. I missed a few classes due to illness and mental health. When I emailed her to explain she never responded or even acknowledged that she received my email. She tends to ramble and will take points off if your response isn't exactly what she's looking for.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Most of the material covered solely focused on the experiences of women. MSM, men of color, and even nonbinary individuals faced sexual and reproductive injustices yet weren't discussed in this class. To me, this class was focused on the white feminist movement. There should've been more discussion on all who suffered from these injustices.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Do not take a class with her if you can avoid it. Has an insane attendance policy. Is a very harsh grader on writing assignments (most assignments are writing assignments) and isn't clear on what she wants from your writing to begin with. Doesn't want to hear any opinion that is different than her own. Bad at using technology. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Participation is pretty much the entire class, there are few lectures and everything is discussion based. She is very picky about terms/phrasing when you speak and it can get grating. Tends to assume you mean the worst instead of the best when you explain something. No rubrics for anything and inconsistent instructions for assignments and papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: If you are a man, do not choose Booth. It is nearly impossible for Booth to consider you a feminist if you are a man. I will admit that her feedback to students is extensive and that is a really great quality of any professor. However, I feel I have regressed in my gender studies major since having her as a professor. Simply do not take her, ever.

Karen Booth is awful at explaining things. We had an assignment with three different syllabi, all of which had different instructions. She'll give you a zero on an assignment if it isn't done exactly the way she wants it. She makes up assignments and tells us about them the day before they're due. Do yourself a favor and never take this class.
DON'T TAKE HER CLASS

don't take this class or anything by this professor. she never gave any clear instruction, changed the type of instruction constantly, and expected doctoral-level contribution to the discussion. she also always expected one type of answer and was disrespectful to anyone who said anything else, even if it was positive. her grading scale was wack.

Very unclear instructions when assigning work yet grades very harshly. Makes comments like "I bet none of you want to be here" when people don't answer her discussion questions. Extremely outdated course material. Classroom environment really does not feel like a safe place to answer questions incorrectly and that's why no one talks. DONT RECOMMEND
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: asynchronous lecture and synchronous recitation didn't really give us a chance to absorb any information. no preparation for what was required on the midterm and final. Participation was graded in recitation, one group project a semester and weekly quizzes. if you didn't agree with her opinion you were wrong, avoid her if you can

Honestly while I found WGST 101 informative and not hard, it felt very white-feminist and a little too #girlboss, but that might just be the department as a whole. Go take a class that focuses on women in another department, like the African American Studies department or Religious Studies - you'll get a lot more out of it!

Honestly didn't interact with Prof. Booth since my class was asynchronous. The material was interesting and the work was pretty easy. Show up to and participate in recitation and do the reading quizzes and lecture assignments and you'll be fine.
Midterm and final exam were incredibly complicated for a simple 101 class.

Prof. Booth is kind, but she definitely sometimes fishes for answers (in class and on papers), which can make it difficult to get things right. The class isnt always super organized, but we have some good discussions. If youre just interested in WGST in general, I would recommend a different course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her standards are very high and the course is difficult. She has very specific criteria and expectations, but if you pay close attention to her feedback and use her critiques she'll notice!

I liked WGST 101. I did not like Prof Booth, super unclear and unorganized. Made it super frustrating to try to get things done on time because she would never post lectures until hours after they were due. Weekly quizes were due before "class" even started (even though she posted things late.) Bad with technology and frequently blamed students.

Professor Booth is very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. She does have very specific standards for assignments which can be challenging, but if you do the readings and assignments you should do well in the course. She also seemed pretty understanding of students' needs and wanted people to do well and learn in the course.

Prof Booth is very knowledgeable about the material in this class, but is not open-minded enough when it comes to others responses. If you don't respond to a prompt exactly how she thinks it should be answered you will not do well. I did great on the mc quizzes, but the exams DESTROYED my grade. She's very nice but this class is not an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The worst professor I have ever had at UNC. This class in so difficult for no reason. The course material is interesting but the grading is so subjective and assignments have no clear grading outline. Also, every assignment has the most vague instructions. Overall, it seems as though she didn't want to teach this class.

In a glass about sexuality, she only mentioned trans people once, she refused to take any criticism from students and would constantly change deadlines. There was no consistency with almost any assignments, and grading is too subjective without clear guidelines. Refused to acknowledge students' analysis that varies from her own.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do not take a class with Karen. She has impossibly high standards for participation, and her grading is incredibly subjective. She WILL give you a bad grade if she doesn't like you. These "subjective" grades make up 80% of your total grade. You can participate everyday and still get an 80% for participation for no reason. Such a subjective grader!

Do not take a class with Dr. Booth. She is unorganized, has very inconsistent and random deadlines ex. 4:15, and unclear grading policies. She randomly canceled class and added assignments at the last minute. This would not be such an issue but she was inconsiderate of student's needs, even if there were issues with tech or health (in a pandemic).

DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH KAREN BOOTH!!!! I have taken a class previously with her and thought I could manage another one but boy was I wrong. She is so disorganized and her lectures do not make sense. All we do is read and go into breakout groups, The material is interesting but she ruins the class for me. I dread going to this class every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It was my least favorite class I took at UNC, mainly because of her teaching style. I agree with the comments here that she has a very subjective tone, and I'm afraid her grading of the essay-based final exams weren't much different. Makes one wonder whether it is possible to ever be properly prepared for this class. Try taking another prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I can't explain how much I disliked this class in 300 characters. Professor Booth lectures on her opinions and acts like they're fact. The readings are unnecessary and the recitations are boring. I am a feminist, but I'm also a Christian and some of the things Ms. Booth said felt like attacks (traditional marriage is stupid). Don't take this class.

If you aren't super passionate about feminism, do not take this class. Half of the subject matter is common sense, or it is so stupid that it will straight up ignore you. The lectures are extremely boring, she is so repetitive, and kind of scatterbrained. She is also technologically inept, which is annoying. She's nice though.

Karen is a good teacher, and the readings are interesting. You have to write either a 500 or 800 word response before every class, but if you do them, you should get a good grade. The midterm was a take-home online exam. If you write your responses/essays to agree with her point of view, you'll do well. Speak once per class.

Do not take this class. Dr. Booth uses lectures not to challenge students, but to find students who validate her own world view. The course does have very interesting readings, but you can do them in your free time. She is also incredibly trans-exclusive and has disorganized lectures. She is not willing to explain confusing course assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Booth is very passionate. She is a great teacher, as she puts a lot of effort into making class time engaging and worthwhile. The books we read for class were fascinating and not too difficult; the class's workload as a whole is very manageable. However, Dr. Booth does not give very clear assignment guidelines and can be a bit disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She does search for the right answer out of students and is looking for a specific wording on exams. I felt like I had a clear understanding of all work and assignments but still received lower than par grades. You must put things in her words or you won't receive the grades you are looking for.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I would seriously recommend you do not take this class. Ms. Booth spent a lot of time silencing students who challenged her in lecture, and then subsequently denied doing it. The class requires far too much reading for an introductory course, and does not attempt to teach or inform, but rather to indoctrinate. The recitations were also too long.

You can tell that Dr. Booth really cares about the material she is teaching. The class isn't designed to be challenging as much as it is getting you to think about things in a different way. Lectures aren't mandatory but recitations are. I would definitely recommend taking WMST101 with Dr. Booth.

I really enjoyed Karen's class, and by the end I felt as if I had learned a lot. She starts off by letting students know she has biases which made me respect her even more. Classes were very discussion based and she'd challenge our statements often. I believe she just wanted to think outside the box. I'd def recommend taking this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: It feels like everything we get back is based subjectively- not even on the criteria she gave us in the first place. This class is supposed to be a capstone culminating in an entire semesters worth of work on a 20ish page paper. She piled on all of the relevant paper work in the last 3 weeks, creating an undue burden for most if not all of us.

Not impressed at all. Class "discussions" entailed her calling on different people until she got the answer she wanted. She is very self-righteous & actively shut me down when I tried to bring up trans health issues in a sexual health class. Reading materials were interesting but I would suggest reading them on your own time.

Karen is the best professor ever. Don't expect an easy class though; she makes you read, do assignments, and actually work for it. However, it's totally worth it. She cares about the material and teaches it very effectively. She keeps class interesting, and facilitates discussion really well. This is my favorite class I've taken at UNC.
She is AMAZING. One of the best professors I have had at UNC.
Karen is hilarious and very down to Earth. I love the lecture and the TAs are pretty awesome as well!

It's a relatively interesting class and it is obvious professor Booth has a passion for what she is teaching. The class has made me think a good deal. Exams are easy if you've been to class and look over the study guide. Not much outside work either. Recitation is hit or miss depending on the TA. I personally love mine with Kim.
One of the best professors at UNC.

OHMYGOSH, karen booth is by far the best teacher i have had at unc thus far. after taking her 388 class (which i highly recommend if you can manage to get into it), i decided to double major with wmst. she is phenomenal. literally, every class discussion blowed my mind and it was the one class i had this semester that i actually looked forward to a

She was an interesting teacher who really cared about Feminism and educating the students (majority of them taking this class as gen. ed.) about feminism.  Recitation felt a little monotonous at times. As long as you read the required readings and look at the study guide, it's a good class to attend.

Such an interesting lecturer. I was initially taking the class to fulfill a curriculum requirement, but found a passion for the subject.  She really opens your eyes to feminist ideas and shooting down the myths.  I'm taking a smaller class with her next semester as well because I enjoyed her so much.  Highly recommended!
Excellent Professor! Interesting concepts about sexuality!

I did not enjoy this class, though I do have a developed interest in the subject. Although I learned a lot, I found the class unnecessarily difficult and I dreaded class time.  I found class to be formal, serious, and monotonous.  It was not a good learning environment and diverse opinions were not encouraged.

This class turned me off of women's studies altogether. She was extremely biased, and it showed in her comments on student's papers. There were meaningless daily papers that only served as busy work. Her lectures were scattered and pointless. Her pop quizzes were impossible regardless of whether you did the reading.

Literally changed my life. What an amazing professor. She's always ready for discussion and always made time for me. There were times when I did not agree with things she said - b/c they didn't fit into my life - and she was always courteous. It was a phenomenal experience for me.

Her wmst 50 class was the most amazing class I've ever taken. She was an interesting lecturer and was truly interested in getting her students to know the material, even if they don't agree with some of her ideas. She does an excellent job of bringing in movie clips, etc to make lecture interactive.

The problem with Prof Booth's class is that she treats her lectures as a way to advance an agenda.  That wouldn't be as problematic, but instead of allowing students to search, explore, and discover the issues that face women, she forces her class to adopt her views on the subject of women and specifically genderism and discrimination (hostility, etc).  Because I, at the time, didn't buy into what she and the TA wanted, I was graded harshly compared to other classes.  A joke of a class - b/c of above probs.
No Comments
AWFUL.

Her teaching focused more on gay/lesbian, and anti-war activism than anything having to do with globalization. Her schedule was never clear, her assignments were inappropriate, and her grading was personal and not professional.
ignore the above bad rating, i got her confused with karen ruffle
I have never had a teacher grade my papers so harshly, even in English classes.

Friendly and approachable with clear-cut expectations and tons of extra credit. I had to be very self-directed and mature but as long as you do the basics like understand + rework the hw/quizzes/worksheets, come to class, follow expectations, and ask questions early, you will be more than fine. Easier than gen chem and other 241 profs for sure.

The content and lectures can get pretty boring but he is pretty entertaining and funny. Can go on unrelated tangents. You have grade and extra credit quizzes after every class but are graded on participation. He gives a lot of partial credit on exams and the grade can be replaced by the grade on your final pertaining to that unit.

Dr. Lockett was a very good teacher and was very precise and understandable during lectures. He focuses more on the content than grading, so if you get the final math answer incorrect, but the process correct, he will give you credit. I loved taking his class so much, and he was a great friend overall.

Horribly disorganized lectures, would go on strange tangents and convolute simple topics with vaguely related metaphors. It was difficult to follow with notes as he didn't really use the empty slides he posted. Didn't post notes or recordings and answer keys were often inaccurate. I did not learn a single thing about chemistry from this class.
Basically whatever you get on the final is your grade in the class based on the exam replacement strategy. Kinda hate that but its fine. At least I passed

Don't get me wrong Lockett seems like a great guy and his humor made lectures enjoyable but I cannot recall a single thing I learned this semester. Tests seemed impossible because of the sheer amount of questions/ work needed. Everything was curved and extra credit was generous but I regret not taking Tiani and actually learning instead.

I generally liked Lockett except for his exams. He is a hilarious guy and his lectures I didn't think were too boring for an analytical chem class. However, his exams were difficult especially the final exam(brutal!). I finished in on the last second thinking I failed it for sure. There was a nice curve though at the end so I guess it worked out.

He was nice and funny. His tests were very difficult though. Open note exams, but they were much harder than the practice provided. Final was open note but extremely hard and most of the class took the whole 3 hours. Probably still the better 241 option but it was very hard.

Pretty funny professor and cool topics. Go to class, he literally tells you the exam questions! The final is very lengthy and has harder questions than the midterms. However, there was an excessive amount of extra credit and a final grade curve too! Probably the easiest chem/prof combo at UNC. Don't look at any other option if you see this!

Hilarious guy, very to-the-point lectures in terms of what you needed to know for the exams, very generous grading policy. The Canvas materials were pretty unorganized. Skipped over a bunch of content during lecture, making it hard to use previous exams for practice. Ultimately don't feel like I really learned anything despite making an A.
Best Teacher!

I struggled in this class until I followed Dr. Lockett's advice to use flashcards. At first, I ignored it, but before the final, I made flashcards from quizzes and past exams. It changed everything—I scored high on the final and got an A+. Trust the process and start using flashcards early—they truly work!

Was so excited that I got into his class because of his 5.0 ratings but wish I took a different professor. Did not like this class, tests were hard and much different from the in class practice. He would say the test was going to be easier than practice exams and then it would be much harder.

Worst class ever!!! Everyone told me that he was a good professor, however he did not live up to my expectations. I genuinely don't understand how so many students like Lockett. Lectures were disorganized and didn't help with understanding the content. Half of his answer keys are incorrect. Tests are extremely difficult!!

I waited a semester to take this course with Lockett because of his amazing reviews but I was incredibly disappointed. Expect to go over the easiest question in class 4 times only to open the HW to the most impossible unrelated questions. All the tests, including the final, are open note but he makes them very difficult.

Dr. Lockett is an amazing professor. He cares about his students and is very accessible outside of class. He offers extra credit and a curve on the final exam. Definitely make sure to practice outside of class so you can have a better understanding of what was covered in lecture. He can be mean sometimes but just be respectful and you will be fine.

Lockett was an absolutely amazing professor, he taught the class in a traditional format. The class also has 20 points extra credit if you just complete the EC quizzes. He also curves the final which is one of the hardest finals I've ever taken but still ended the class with an A cuz of the curve. The final is open note and open internet.

I genuinely don't understand how so many students like Lockett. He would teach something completely different in class and test us on something else entirely. This made the class incredibly difficult. Maybe it is because of the pacing of summer session but I have never done worse in a class despite my consistent study habits. Disappointed.
Lockett was a truly amazing professor! "Big 'D'" was the highlight of the class by far.

Dr. Lockett is nice, hilarious, a little quirky, and actually cares about his students. Quizzes are graded for completion. The midterms are the fairest that you'll get from UNC Chem, and there is so much extra credit in the class that you can bomb all exams and still have a decent shot at an A. The final was awful, but curved.

I took 241 with Todd and found that he taught his class with the assumption that people had taken/understood orgo, causing me to get a D. With Matt, I confidently got a B+/A-. He also cares more than Todd ever did. I know some think our final was unfair but I disagree, nothing on it was new. Unlike Todd, all material is relevant, highly recommend.
i dont love chem but this was definitely best case scenario for chem 241

Matt is a wonderful person and a kindhearted professor. I felt safe in his classroom from the first day of class. It is so easy to see that he cares deeply about his students. I will say I feel like this class lacked organization, and the final was significantly longer and harder than the midterms. 241 is a rough class, but Matt is great.

LOVED taking 241 with Dr. Lockett! He made the class and lectures so engaging and was so accomodating with us this semester. I think people read through these and expect the exams to be easy but it's like any other STEM class and you have to put in the effort for the grade. Couldn't recommend a better prof for 241, take it with him!!!!

Dr. Lockett is a great professor, although attendance is not mandatory everything you need to learn comes straight from lectures, readings are optional and aren't very helpful. All exams were very fair but the final was extremely difficult so be sure to overstudy for that. I recommend going to his office hours they are very helpful.
Don't take 241 with him. Take it with Todd Austell. There are open seats in his course.

Matthew is a great professor that is really good at expressing the ideas of the material in a way that makes sense. He gives so many opportunities to practice and learn the material and is really good about understanding that life happens. 100% recommend taking this class with him.
SUCH A GREAT TEACHER
He makes it very easy for everyone in the class to succeed. Provides lots of great resources, office hours, and is always ready to help us. If you have to take analytical, this is the way to go.

Dr. Lockett is one of the best professors at UNC. He truly cares about his students- and shows it! Extremely fair grading (so much respect for this), EC opportunities, engaging lectures, encourages & helps students get involved with research. I've never felt more comfortable in a STEM class at UNC. I only wish he taught more courses here.

Dr.Lockett is the world's most ideal professor. He teaches a very complex topic in an accessible way, he is hilarious and his grading guidelines could not be more fair. His final is extremely difficult, I under-studied, but otherwise, keep up with the lectures and concepts and you'll be good. He is just phenomenal and uses online readings (free).
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I absolutely LOVED 241H with Dr. Lockett!!! He has a great way of making any lesson engaging and entertaining, has great final exam replacement and extra credit policies, and cares a lot about his students, I think he's your best option for analytical chem. His midterms were pretty fair, but warning: the final exam was TOUGH in comparison!

Analytical has the potential to be super dry, but Matt used super interesting examples and found ways to make the material more engaging (and the examples helped me grasp concepts so much more easily). Plenty of practice problems and practice exams, and he will let you know problem types to expect so you study the right stuff. 10/10.

Dr. Lockett is the best chem professor I've had at UNC. He's super organized, explains difficult concepts in an easy-to-understand way, and gives you tons of resources and practice problems to master the material. Analytical chemistry is a pretty dry topic but he makes it fairly digestible.
The best 241 professor. Very willing to answer any questions and a fair grader. Wants you to learn and succeed in chemistry. Lectures are good too.

One of the best profs in the chem department. He makes difficulty concepts very easy to understand, and he has an answer to any question you might have. He's hilarious, and he makes the class more interesting by tying concepts back to real-world applications. Take 241 with him if you have the chance; you won't regret it.
I love Professor Lockett! Take this class if you can. He makes Chemistry understanding!

If you have the option to take him do it. As a non-hnrs student in CHEM 241H, I thought I would feel behind, but Matt makes sure everyone knows exactly how to succeed. Extra Credit quizzes each week, review sesh that gives u exact test question prep, and NO hw. I don't do much except study at the review  & EC quizzes, and I have an A. BEST PROF!

It's not hard to see why Dr. Lockett is one of the most loved Chem professors at UNC-- I actually looked forward to lectures because of how entertaining he was. That being said, analytical chemistry is a really hard class, so don't let the laid back lectures make you think the tests aren't killer.

Lockett is by far the best chem professor at UNC. Truly cares about his students and is an amazing person all around. Tests are hard but he does test replacement and has extra credit quizzes. He really just wants all his students to succeed.

Professor Lockett is one of the kindest and most caring professors at UNC! He was so accommodating this semester with the pandemic, providing us with extra time for exams and many extra credit opportunities! His lectures are super helpful but make sure to do the practice problems! Exams are difficult but if you don't cram (like me), you'll be fine!

Dr. Lockett was the best professor I have ever had at UNC. He was very accomodating during this semester and truly cared about his students. His class was challenging, but the exams were very fair. Overall I would recommend Dr. Lockett to everyone!!!!!!!!

Dr. Lockett cares a lot about his students and made learning chemistry manageable and bearable online. Although the quizzes were difficult, they were great practice for the exams. Very inspirational and funny. Gives a lot of opportunities to do very well in the class whether its the extra credit quizzes or the final exam replacement policy.

Lockett was so amazing! Actually gave me hope in getting a good grade for a chemistry class and being able to understand the material. You can tell hes super passionate about chemistry! 11000/10 professor

Lockett is the best teacher known to man. If you can get him please do yourself a favor and get him. He truly cares about his students and wants us to get As. Best professor by far and is an overall amazing person

Dr. Lockett is an AMAZING person and professor, he definitely has made an impact on me as a student. I usually struggle heavily with chemistry, and although this was a tough course I excelled because of him. He gives so many opportunities to improve your grade and writes his own free textbook. EASILY the best professor at UNC !!
Professor Lockett is the best chemist professor at UNC by far. The most caring man on the planet, especially during the pandemic with online classes. Absolutely love this man

Chemistry is a rough subject, but Prof. Lockett really tries his best to help you through it. He breaks down how to study in each unit and gives LOTS of opportunity to do better on exams. He's extremely understanding to circumstances and honestly just wants his students to learn. Couldn't recommend a prof. more.

By far the most impactful and best profs. He is very clear and engaging so if you take good notes you dont have to open the textbook. His exams are fair and his review sessions are helpful. His final and replacement policy REALLY came in clutch. I liked the class but I loved him. He is a great person, hes very funny, and really inspiring!

Lockett is an amazing person, but as a professor he lacks a little. His exams are incredibly hard and don't seem to match his lectures which are a lot easier. He gives you a million practice problems but his keys aren't always correct or detailed enough. His extra credit quizzes are impossible and make you feel like you'll fail the whole class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Lockett is the best chem professor that I've had at UNC. He explains the material thoroughly and gives students all the resources they need to do well on his exams. Not only is he a great professor, but he is an extremely kind person. Definitely take 241 with Dr. Lockett if you have the chance!

Lockett explains the material very well and he is a super funny guy who really cares about his students. His tests are HARD even if you know the material well. He does offer grade replacement and a ton of extra credit which is really helpful. He is a great person and lecturer, but I definitely feel some of the tests were unfair

Matt really is a caring professor. He does a good job explaining things and he really does do his best to make sure you do your best. Best CHEM professor at unc, super relatable. This man is also funny, he'll have you sitting there like bruh.

Dr. Lockett is the kindest professor that I have met at Carolina. He genuinely cares so much for each of students, believes in their potential, and wants them to succeed... And he will remind you of this throughout the semester if you ever struggle or doubt yourself. He is the best chemistry prof. in the department, and one of the best at Carolina.

He gives you all the tools you need to succeed, on top of some amazingly inspirational speeches at the beginning and throughout the course. Quite literally he has made me cry from how much he cares for his students. Absolute best chemistry teacher at UNC.

Dr. Lockett is by far one of the most talented professionals at UNC. He was extremely encouraging throughout the semester and helped me overcome roadblocks. The course is not easy by any means, but he makes it possible. I would definitely take another class with him. He is the total package- brilliant and kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Best professor I've ever had. His exams are hard, but he prepares you for them by giving you tons of practice exams. I could have failed every exam of his and would still rate him like this. Funny lecturer, understanding teacher, and overall great person. If you do bad on an exam DON'T PANIC because you always have the chance to replace it

Never realized how bad my gen chem profs were until I had Matt. He explains the content using super relevant examples which make it easier to understand. Your entire grade is based on tests, but the test replacement policy and extra credit points help your grade. Seriously Matt was the best prof I've had at UNC and I couldn't recommend him enough!!

Matt is the best professor I have ever had. I came out of chem 101 and 102 pretty discouraged (gen chem kinda sucks), but this guy really encouraged me to be my best. I went from despising chemistry to loving it. He's the best there is, period. TAKE HIM. PLEASE. His class will be the best you ever have at Carolina. Love this guy. You will too.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Matt is undoubtedly my fav professor after taking this course. He makes lectures interesting and explains everything really well. Going to office hours and doing the practice problems/exams will help out a lot. Wouldn't recommend anyone else for this course.

One of the best professors I have ever had at UNC and probably will ever have. Sympathetic, organized, and an amazing lecturer. I had lots of respect for this man, but towards the end he let me down quite a bit. It was petty and he disappointed me. But he is outstanding nonetheless and I still highly recommend him.
PHENOMONAL

Lockett is a very clear lecturer, and he is super funny and approachable, both during and outside of class. Lots of extra credit points via poll everywhere, so be sure to come to class. However, your course grade is solely dependent on your exam grades. The final was harder than I expected it to be, so my grade dropped at the very end.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lockett is great at explaining the conceptual stuff in lecture. However, the class is very math based so prepare to do a lot of formula work on your own. I'd still totally recommend him though bc his lectures kept me engaged.  Be aware he does work at a quick pace and you need to take your own notes bc the outlines he posts on sakai are worthless.

During an exam, a person's calculator broke. They didn't have a backup, and I could seriously feel the dread overcoming that person. However, Matt sat down with them to help fix their calculator in a super calm and easy going manner. I feel this exemplifies Matt as a person -  he's a super caring person, and he will give you help if you ask for it.

Dr. Lockett is my favorite professor at UNC. He genuinely cares about his students and he wants them to succeed. He teaches in a way that is thoughtful and that makes you truly learn. I would take another class with him in a heartbeat.

His lectures are amazing and well thought out. I genuinely learned chemistry through these lectures, but make sure to do all practice problems and tests before each exam. Go to the review sessions, they help a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: TAKE DR. LOCKETT'S CLASS! He gives so many opportunities to pull your grade up. Even if you're not a chemistry whiz, if you're willing to put in the work, you'll do well. He gives you a lot of resources to study from, and you will go into tests with a good idea of what you are expected to know. Additionally, Dr. Lockett gives great pep talks.
Great professor with good and funny lectures. Goes fairly fast, but has to so that all of the material can be covered. Gives many opportunities to pull up your grade. Study the old tests!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Not my favorite professor. You can tell he's smart; I just don't think he's organized enough to communicate the information at our level. Often seemed distracted and was also often moody. He is pretty funny so that made his lectures a little better.
Dr. Lockett always does his best to help his students to succeed in his class. He gives a lot of chances to get extra credits and raise scores.

A lot of people are intimidated by taking analytical chemistry because of rumors about it. This was my favorite chemistry course so far and I loved Professor Lockett. He kept lectures interesting, provided real world applications, and has fair grading where you can replace exams with final if you improve

The class is hard. That's the sad truth, but Lockett is a legend. He keeps the class interesting and he is hilarious. There is very little homework, and your final can replace your previous test scores (which is really good because you will probably bomb the tests). He really wants students to get a good grade, but the material and exams are hard.

I love Prof. Lockett. I hate chemistry most of the time (which sucks when you're premed) and he made every single class enjoyable. I had him for a summer session, which is difficult enough for 241, and he did what he could to help our grades and ensure our success. He's super nice, gives great examples in class, and is just a great professor.

I had Professor Lockett for Analytical during summer school, and he was amazing! He's someone who, above all, cares that students understand the big concepts in the class. Rather than having to provide a steep curve, he gives poll everywhere problems in class for extra credit. Lockett is a very calm and kind person--a true legend!
A great seminar for science major transfer students. Which helps you to know some faculties in the departments and teach you skills to find an undergraduate research.

simply put, this guy is a legend. He truly cares about if you understand the material.  gives extra credit because he wants people to learn and not feel down in a very difficult class.  Do everything you can to take his class.

I'm a big fan of Professor Lockett because he cares for his students (inside and outside of academics), and it really shows. Exams are hard, but really what would you expect from analytical chemistry? He definitely wants to challenge you, but in a passionate, pedantic, and ego-free way. Highly recommend him!

Dr. Lockett is honestly one of the best chemistry professors at UNC. He really wants each and every one of his students to be successful. He gives out a ton of extra credit points that'll help buffer your grade. His tests may be challenging, but if you work hard and do the practice problems (of which there are many), you'll be fine. He's also funny

Dr. Lockett is the best Chem professor I've taken at UNC. He is fair, really funny, and more than willing to help. You get extra credit for poll everywhere and it makes a huge difference in your final grade. I highly suggest going to his office hours when you can. It's a tough class, but if you put the work in you'll be ok!

Dr. Lockett is the most fair professor I've had at UNC. He genuinely wants his students to do well and gives them ample opportunities to do so. His tests are all fair and he curves the exams. I highly recommend going to lectures because he grants extra credit for poll everywhere. I had 35 extra points at the end of the semester because of this.

Professor Lockett was one of the most fair professors I have ever had at Carolina. Yes, his tests were difficult, but they were definitely doable if you studied. He is also BIG on poll-everywhere, awarding as much as 40 extra credit points, so be sure to attend lecture. Overall a great class.

Professor Kable is genuinely interested in his students (he learned everyone's name in my 40-person class). I enjoyed his selection of plays, and most reading was done in class. He is funny, invested, and very professional.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Kable is very respectable. I love his choice of drama and play, as they are representative and thought-provoking.
Attendance matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was probably the easiest I've ever taken, and Dr. Kable is so funny, caring, and supportive. Literally 75% of your grade comes from three journal entries that he grades super leniently on. The rest is participation and one "scene panel" that is a really simple acting project.

Class was very straight forward and very fun! I enjoyed his class a lot during this semester, as it is basically watching musicals based on the era we were learning about! I highly recommend taking this course as it is an easy A.

IF YOU ARE A FIRST YEAR HONORS STUDENT TAKE THIS CLASS!! super duper easy to get an A - literally just show up, submit the 3 assignments (only 3.), and give an ounce of effort when you do your scene panel. in class we just watched movies and read aloud scenes and chatted, but most ppl were just doing homework from other classes. highly recommend!

Kable is such an amazing professor! You'll read a lot of plays, but as long as you show up to class, occasionally participate, and think about the material, it's an easy A. He's a generous grader and clearly knows a ton about the subject material. Take any and all of his classes!!
He's just the best. I've taken him twice now and he's so smart and cares so much about his classes. I hear rumors he's retiring soon so take a class with him while you still can.
I am taking as many classes as I can with him.  He is absolutely amazing and one of my favorite professors.

Took this class fully asynchronous over the summer. 
Take it! I learned a lot about American musicals. Kable is a very fast and lenient grader.

DRAM120 was the perfect AES focus capacity. The whole class is graded on two exams, an 8-page paper, and 10% participation. As long as you show up to class and read parts/answer questions occasionally, you'll be good. He chose really interesting plays, and I got good scores on the tests without doing much reading outside of class time. Loved Kable!

While participation isn't required its so much easier to comprehend if you go to class. There are two exams and one 8-page paper total with no other homework. Be careful to look out for smaller details before exams, but overall the class is wonderful and I would take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Favorite professor ever! He was so kind, caring, and passionate about the subject. As long as you participate, the class is very easy, and you will get a good grade -- it helps if you actually enjoy theatre. His class was a delight every day and I would love to take another class by him in the future.
I would die for this man.

I will ALWAYS recommend prof Kable. Ample opportunities for participation, and tries to make lectures as engaging as possible, even though it may be difficult for some because of content. Easy grader and passionate about the subject.

Kable is an amazing professor who only wants his students to succeed and learn about Drama. The class is based on 3 assignments, each worth 30%, and participation is 10%. Get ready to read a lot of plays but he makes it fun and grades pretty easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor!! Read lots of plays but if you stay on top of the work then you're fine. Only had three journal entries to write and they were just diary style on your opinions of the play. No midterm, no final! For group project you act out a scene from a play - but it's low stakes and as long as you commit, you'll get a good grade. Take this!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Okay, so I skipped class three weeks in a row and got 66 on my first exam but I managed to bounce back and get straight 100's and extra credit. The professor is a little boring but DRAM 115 is totally a GPA buffer if you actually have the willpower to show up to class.

This is the most wonderful man alive. He is so sweet and such an easy grader. There's barely any work at all, and almost everything assigned outside of class is fully covered inside class as well. If you are taking this class as a drama student or just for gen ed, Kable is the best way for you to go.
Kable's class is fun, with plenty of extra credit opportunities. Just show up, participate, and use tools like Unstuck ai to ace the exams. The workload is manageable if you put in the effort.

I took this asynchronous class over the summer. It included five Voicethread clips, two papers, and a final paper. Professor Kable grades very leniently! The Voicethreads involved recording short videos answering questions about musical clips. The final paper was more like a list with short descriptions. Follow the prompts for an easy 100.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Probably the least intensive class I've taken at UNC and it was pretty interesting! The course (took it async during summer) is online and there are multiple video assignments that are reflections, along with a few 3-4 pg papers. As long as you answer the prompt and do the video reflections, you get 100s. Prof. Kable is kind, passionate & lenient!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took this class over the summer asynch.  It was so easy.  Class consisted of five voicethread clips that were easy to complete, 2 short papers that were fun, and a final "mixtape" paper.  Prof Kable grades VERY EASY (literally got 100s on everything).  Just follow the prompts and meet the requirements.

Kable is an absolute sweetheart. His class is great, but few people show up to his lectures. There are 3 tests and one mid-term project that each makes up 25% of your overall grade.
