If you show up and try your best, he makes sure you get the grade you deserve. He even rounded up my 87 (B+)  to a 91 (A-) at the end of the semester! :)

He is such a fun professor, I really very truly enjoyed this class! If you participate, he gives so much extra credit. So many people would ignore him when he asked for volunteers so I volunteered a ton, and I ended up having 32 points of extra credit on one exam lol. Only graded by four things, 2 exams, course journal, and a final but not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love Kable so much! He is very passionate about what he teaches and is a kind grader. We watched clips from musicals every single class period which was super fun. There are 3 regular papers and a final paper. Make sure to participate in class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would die for this man. He is the nicest professor I have ever had. If you slightly pay attention in class and know the general plot of the plays and vocab you will get an A on the exams. Participants have many opportunities for extra credit through reading and answering mundane questions. Course journal is a free 100! He is very accommodating.

Great professor, it's just tests are hard af. Unless you're a drama major or super interested in the topic and are willing to read and memorize all the plays, I say brother ya gotta chill out. Nonetheless, the 10-page long journal is basically a free A.
Really nice professor but the exams are HARD!

This is the easiest class I have ever taken at UNC and Professor Kable is so nice. There is 3 essays and a essay-style final. You are graded on participation, so you have to participate and go to class if you want an A. I found the class interesting and somewhat of a "brain break" from my other classes because we just watch clips from musicals.

I just want to remind all of you this is NOT an easy class!!! 10 plays in a semester and 3 exams each worths 25% make this class difficult. You have to READ and look really carefully to remember his every PowerPoint to get an A. But I would say it's easy to get above B in this class because of the extra credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Grade in the course is determined by participation, two non-cumulative tests, and a 10 page course project. He provides free pdfs for all readings and all assignments are fair. Overall, a great teacher that provides an engaging introduction to the drama department's offerings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kable is incredible! Not only is he passionate about what he teaches, but he also cares about his students. Get ready to participate in class discussions and read lots of plays! There are only 4 grades in the class(participation, midterm, 10-page analysis paper, and final exam) so pay attention and participate!

the only grades are participation, midterm, final, and one project. he is a very kind man who is clearly very passionate about the subject matter. also, when students answer questions incorrectly, he doesn't try to embarrass them or anything like that. lots of reading, but he provides pdfs, and class is mostly re-reading the plays aloud&discussing

Gregory Kable is the funniest man ever. The exams and singular journal assignment make up your entire curse grade. Just study for the exams and everyone gets a 100 on the journal as long as you do it. Plus, he gives out so much extra credit. Sit in the front of the class, Kable is friendly and will soon know you by name.

Professor Kable is the sweetest guy ever. He offers so much extra credit, all you have to do is read a play for at most 5 minutes once per unit. There's two midterms, a 10 page journal, and the final exam. Since it's graded on four things, it's definitely harder to bring your grade up from one bad grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have taken 3 courses with Kable and I love having him as my professor. He is an amazing person whose passion permeates into his lectures and care for students. It is important to read the plays and pay attention to lectures; while the courses are extremely easy, some stuff will appear on the final!

This class was super easy, you read 8 plays but I never read any of them outside of class and I did fine because all the class time is devoted to students reading the script. The class is based on a midterm, course project, final, and participation. He won't cold call so ss long as you show up occasionally and pay attention you'll be fine. Love him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: He was a great professor. Understanding about students not always reading the plays in time for lecture, and gave lots of opportunities for extra credit. If you actually just read the plays and come to lecture its a very easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT take this class. Three exams each worth 25% and they are difficult. YOU NEED TO READ 10 PLAYS. There are too many people raising hands for extra credits and you will NOT likely get any.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy, I really like prof. Kable. There are 3 tests throughout the semester, study the tests for real or you're not gonna get a good grade. Don't listen to those guys whoever says it's easy. Tests are pretty detailed, if you don't pay attention and study hard for the tests, you're gonna mess up your GPA fr.

Kable is a great professor, and this class is a fun way to be introduced to a variety of plays. The course journal is a pretty long assignment, but the writing is easy as long as you start early. Would definitely recommend for FC-AESTH.

Gregory Kable was so fun and very passionate about what he teaches. I enjoyed going to this class every meeting. The class was not hard at all, with 4 reflections being spread throughout the semester. As long as you do the work and show you're interested in class, I think it's an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kable's class was engaging and so fun! The class was set up sort of as a dialogue; most days we would read plays or watch clips and both the class and Prof Kable would make comments about the material. His comments were always so insightful and he always reacted very positively to students' ideas. I never felt afraid to raise my hand.

Kable is really sweet and kind and always brought a relaxed energy to the class. The exams were ridiculously easy and the paper was a lot of work, but graded leniently. I thought his lectures were interesting and provided a different viewpoint on understanding story. Classroom atmosphere was chill too. Great class for any level of experience.

I adore Prof Kable! He is so kind and makes every student feel valued, welcome, and comfortable in class. His passion for the subject material shines and makes the class engaging. This class was never stressful, but I was introduced to a lot of plays  and learned a lot. The class was graded on 3 papers, but they were interesting and not difficult.

One of the best classes I have taken at UNC. The plays are interesting and Prof Kable's explanations are great. The class is graded on one midterm, one final, and one course project. Participation in class makes a huge difference so make sure you show up and interact a few times per class and you should be good. A really easy and fun class overall!

The class had 1 midterm and 1 final that were structured the same. Also, the ten-page paper is graded very generously. There are assigned readings but as long as you go to class and pay attention, the midterms are really easy. The readings are pretty interesting but lectures can be boring. Overall great professor and highly recommend taking it.

Final grade is based on a 10-page course journal, 2 exams, and the final. exams were mainly memorization based, and the course journal wasn't particularly hard, just tedious -- keep up with it and it's fine. Greg gives a COPIOUS amount of extra credit, so if you show up with the play skimmed and participate once per unit, you're set. I adore him

Only four grades in the class and each are 25% (2 midterms, final, and a course journal) so you need to do well on everything to get a decent grade. TONS OF EXTRA CREDIT, make sure to read in front of the class for extra points on the exam it helps a lot. Exams are mostly memorization and making sure you read the plays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I liked professor Kables class. I took this Gen Ed for my LA credit and also NA credit. Only graded on 4 things. Test 1 and 2, a course journal paper on which he was super lenient. Study for the tests but he gives so many opportunities for extra credit. This is a super easy class. he is super sweet and cares a lot. Take this class if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you read the plays and show up to class, you will do just fine. He will randomly give out extra credit for just showing up to class, so make sure you go. Greg is funny, caring, and helpful. There is a long paper, 9-10 pages single spaced, but it is not bad if you space it out.

Professor Kable is amazing! His lectures were engaging and he is very charismatic. He is understanding and easy to access outside of class. Attendance is not fully mandatory but definitely go to class because things he says in lectures are what's on the quiz. The class is an easy A if you pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Kable is so passionate about this class, and that definitely shines through in the lectures. We got to watch so many musical numbers, so this was such a fun class. Graded by participation and 3 papers. Although heavily weighted, are graded fairly easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An easy, yet eye opening class. Make sure to participate as much as you can, as that and 3 papers are your only grades. Papers are weighted heavily, but graded fairly easily. You will be reading a lot of plays. Ultimately a caring, funny, and nice, lovely prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors. I've taken two classes with him, and always find him passionate about the material and kind to his students. Your attendance might affect your grade if it's really bad, but it isn't a huge concern. I've never gotten below an A on one of his papers. Definitely recommend!

Best professor I've had at UNC. Kable is the GOAT. The class is 3 tests and one 10 page paper, but it's really not that bad, you have the entire semester to do it. Raise your hand to read in front of the class when he asks because he will add 6 points of extra credit to your next test. He even rounded up my A- to an A.

His tests were pretty specific, so heavily based on memorization, but he gave lots of extra credit opportunities, and he ended up rounding my grade up to an A even though I was a few points off. I read all the plays and wouldn't have gotten an A without the rounding, but if you put in some memory work, it's not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
The KINDEST professor I have ever had in my entire life. He is such a sweet, entertaining prof. The class is entertaining and not too bad.
The class is based on 3 exams and 1 10 page paper (which is not as bad as it seems as long as you start it early). Each grade is worth 25%.
Raise your hand to speak to earn 6 points added to your exam grades!

His powerpoints are KEY... there are only 3 tests and a course paper so you must do well on the tests. The tests are straight memorization of his PowerPoint with a few basic elements of the plots. ALWAYS RAISE YOUR HAND for reading in front of the class for extra credit, the legend gives 6 (sometimes double) whole points to your test grade

Professor Kable is truly a joy to be around!  While I am not a fine arts major, I still greatly enjoyed his class.  He is so enthusiastic about the material and makes lectures fun and interesting in every way he can.  I cannot stress enough that this class is such a great choice for gen ed requirements.  Study powerpoints and you will do fine.

Prof. Kable was great!  I took this course as a non major and thoroughly enjoyed it - most of class time was spent watching and discussing numbers from various musicals.  It was clear that he has extensive knowledge of the subject and the course is very well organized.  The only assignments are a few 3-4 page papers that are graded pretty easily

Professor Kable is so sweet and obviously passionate about what he is teaching! His classes are typically graded by few things but he's a fair grader. Definitely recommend, his classes are a lot of fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fun class! We just watch musical clips Kable explains them through different points of view. It doesn't make very much sense but you only need a gist to do well in the class. there are only 3 essays and one final essay for assignments, so not a lot of room for error, but they're not graded harshly. I highly recommend the class!

Dr. Kable is a respectable professor. He gives good lectures. You will get a lot of extra credits. However, exams are super hard. To get good grades on them, you have to take notes as much as you can during lectures since his slides are not helpful. So, if you want to enjoy taking drama, don't take his class.

Kable is very nice and caring. not the easiest gen ed course, but attendance isn't mandatory. grade based upon three tests and one large paper. 10 plays you need to read or at least know what they're about. generous with extra credit.

Kable is a great professor and this class is fun. Basically just watching clips from musicals. Class was just 3 reflections and final. Reflections are graded super easy. Took forever to get grades back tho.
Such a fun class! Watch multiple musicals during class which you use to write 3 reflections throughout the semester and a final paper.S uper nice and understanding guy

Dr Kable is a great prof u can tell loves to teach. Funny and engaging. The tests can be specific but it's an easy A bc he gives SO MUCH extra credit. Some u have to earn but most is free. Barely need to study. Only grades are 3 tests + a final paper that is graded by TAs (grade is highly dependent on who grades your paper which is unfair but eh.)

Greg is a great, passionate guy. His lectures are very enjoyable. The whole class is graded on 3 exams and a 9 page paper. You really have to study for the exams and work hard on the paper, but it's not too bad. He gave us full credit for one of our exams if we turned the paper in on time. Lots plays to read. There's many chances for extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I love this man. Hes adorable and obviously very intelligent, has an amazing memory. He always incorporated relevant videos into his lectures. Every day he gave extra credit if you read in front of the class. Gave lots of 100s on essays. The tests were pretty hard (we took 2) but extra credit helped a ton! Definitely recommend this class.

Professor Kable was incredible! He knew so much about theatre but delivered his lectures in ways that were very digestible. The class is based on only 4 grades, but he gives very generous extra credit. However, don't think you can just sleep through this class. Many people were caught off guard by the content on the tests, so pay attention.

Dr. Kable is a wonderful professor and really knows his stuff. We read all the plays out loud in class, so it's totally fine if you miss a reading or two. I thought a "Staging America" class would be all white male focused, but he does a great job of incorporating diverse plays. Three papers, but he's a generous grader. Loved this class!
grade is made up of 3 papers and a project, but he is very helpful and not that tough of a grader. his lectures are great and class was always entertaining
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class content was fairly easy with a lot of reading for the plays and the tests contained a lot of questions about specifics. Lectures were not recorded which made it hard to be flexible for this class. Extra credit is given if you read in front of the class or attended lectures (esp LDOC). He was very generous with our assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was my fun class for the semester and I really enjoyed it. The professor made class fun by showing videos and making us read plays(which was extra credit). He understands that students have a tough time in school so he gives a lot of extra credit. The tests can be a lil specific but if you pay attention and take good notes you will be fine! :)

I LOVED my class with Professor Kable and I'm definitely taking a class with him again. He's very easy to take a class with and while it was very easy to skip, I did get a lot out of it. Be prepared to watch scenes from High School Musical and Glee in class, because he will GET you to participate. Highly suggest.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: tests are in person and HARD. take 115 ONLINE ONLY. DO NOT TAKE THIS FOR EASY A bc it is not

Only grades are 3 multiple choice tests and a 10 page (single-spaced) paper. You are not well-prepared for the tests and they tend to be pretty difficult. The paper grade was mainly based on if you were lucky enough to get a TA that just gave 100's if you had at least 10 pages written.

Grade is based on 3 tests and a 10 page paper. The tests are super specific and includes things he said wouldn't be included. He's a nice guy, tries to keep class interesting with movie clips and songs, and you can tell he's passionate about drama.
Love Mr. Kable!! Hes so kind and gives so much extra credit. You can tell hes super passionate about what he teaches.

Professor Kable is so kind and passionate about the material. Lectures were entertaining and included movie clips related to the plays. There are only 4 grades. The 10 page course paper is graded leniently as long as you follow the rubric. The exams were very specific, but an A is doable if you are willing to take detailed notes and study hard.
Love Kable, the class is graded by three tests and a final, due to the suicides on campus he gave us all 100s 0n the second test and the paper is not graded harshly. God amongst men.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: A perfect choice for GenEd! Grade mainly depends on three tests and one paper (he actually gave all of us 100 in one test). Bunch of extra credit (5 points in one test if reading the paper, and 6 points in each test if showing up).The 10-page paper is long but doable in two months. Only thing to notice: read the scripts before each class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Kable is so so sweet. He was so passionate and excited about the plays that we analyzed. The class is a lot of reading and graded by two tests, a course project, and participation. He's a pretty generous grader though.

Professor Kable is a really great professor - he's very passionate about the arts. However, if you aren't, this is not the class for you. You are assigned hundreds of pages of plays per week, and aren't well-prepared for his exams. If this is something you enjoy; go for it. Really great guy and professor. Manageable but difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Literally such a great guy, very understanding and cares about his students. Will say the paper was a bit taxing, but that is one of the only assignments you get all semester along with 2 tests and the final. If you're going to take dram 115, TAKE IT WITH HIM!!!! Can't stress this enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Kable is amazing! His class is interesting and the expectations are clear and not confusing at all. I took his class during summer session and his caring personality will never be forgotten. Take a class with him!
Kable makes DRAM a DREAM. He is truly the kindest professor I've had at UNC. Great and prompt feedback make this class a job. Thanks, Professor!

Love Professor Kable. He was a really nice guy and really loved the material he was teaching. Just keep up with the plays so you can write a few solid essays because that is all you're graded on basically.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Love Kable. Kable is a God amongst men. Participate and be generally aware and he'll love you and you'll love him.

I took this class virtually during fall freshman year. Professor Kable was extremely accommodating and very willing to give extensions. The readings were fun (you read most of it in class) and you didn't have to participate a lot to get full participation scores. I think everyone got instant A's on the essays too. Take this class!

Kable is an amazing professor! I took this class to satisfy my VP credit with no background in theatre and I found the class easy! All midterms and the final was a paper that were all super clear with the expectations. He is understanding if you can not make lecture one day and posts recordings.

Professor Kable is a really nice guy with engaging lectures. He made drama for non-theater students really entertaining. His class was also super easy with only 3 papers and a multiple choice final. Overall would definitely recommend him and his class for someone who wants an easy and interesting GenEd course!

I've never been exposed to much theatre, but I took this credit for a gen ed. I learned a lot in this class, and Prof Kable has a great sense of humor, is extremely knowledgeable, and can always put a smile on my face. The class itself was just clip viewing and conversing about it. 3 short papers and a final paper. All graded easily and timely.

I loved this professor. I had never taken a drama course before, but enrolled in this one to fulfill a general education requirement and I loved it. If I had a reason to take another class from him, I would in a heartbeat. He is nice, understanding, and if you understand what he is teaching, you should do just fine in this course.

Kable is just a nice guy! Class is super fun even for non-theater kids, you just watch musical numbers and chat. Show up, write the 3 reflections (3 pages each, practically graded for completion), and get an A. Kable knows a lot and just wants to have some meaningful conversation. I recommend this class but it does get boring after a while!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Kable is the definition of delightful. In Covid classes, he has made me feel like an actual student with fun lectures that foster a great environment. He is incredibly receptive to students, often flexible with deadlines without even asking. He has such a love of dramatic arts that is hard not to feel in his classes.

Took this at 8am and was very boring. Requires a lot of reading, but grades are based on 3 papers and final. Mostly a very chill class. However, a lot of students emailed him about grading and he never responded to most of us. That was really frustrating because there wasn't really any set rubric for the papers and TA grading seemed to vary.

Prof. Kable was really understanding of the COVID circumstances and was there to help everyone out. Final grade was based upon three papers and one final, which were easy to do well on if you read the material. If you're a dramatic arts major, you will probably take many classes with him. Thankfully, he is a great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Despite it being honors, this was my easiest class this semester. He is very passionate about what he does and was always considerate of our individual situations in response to COVID. This class had very little work or reading, and was actually really fun

Prof. Kable was a very fun guy to listen to during his lectures. The three papers we did during the semester were graded very leniently but I did hear about a few of my friends who got screwed over on one or two of the papers. Overall, pretty easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I LOVE PROFESSOR KABLE!! He's a very easy grader. He's also a real gem, so caring and nice. I highly recommend him and would take him again.

Professor Kable is such a nice guy! I was hesitant to take this class because it said drama majors only, however, the class was fairly straight forward. If anything, keep track of the terms used during class because you will see them or need them again either in papers or in the final. You will not regret taking a class with him!

He is a very nice guy. You read a lot for homework, but the plays are normally pretty interesting so it isn't horrible. Classes are kind of boring because you just read through different scenes that you already read for homework for the majority of the class. 3 papers and participation grade.
Dude really knows his stuff! Although I took it at 8am it was still enjoyable. Be sure to participate!

I took this class to fulfill a gen-ed, but ended up getting a lot out of it. As someone who was involved with theater in high school, I enjoyed reading plays and discussing them in a different context. Easy A. A textbook is listed for the class, but is not needed because Professor Kable posts all plays as PDFs. Interesting lectures and discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Kable is gem. A ray of sunshine IMO. I had his 8am class this semester. I *hate* waking up early in general but if you have to take a 8am class this class is a good pick. Be sure to participate when reading plays, it will make the time go faster. When it comes to papers just meet the guidelines and pray you get a TA who grades fairly.
I wish I liked this class, but it was SO boring. The plays we read in class were often monotonous and for an 8 am, I was constantly on the verge of falling asleep.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: He's such a nice human being. Such a chill 8 am class. You just gotta show up and listen to the book. You read for homework. It's chill, light and an escape from the other classes. The only problem I have is that TA's usually grade the work, so you can get unlucky with a tough grader. Prof. Kable is a great prof however

Prof. Kable is my favorite professor at UNC. If you love musicals, TAKE THIS CLASS. He is so kind and caring about his students and the course material. If you show up and participate, you'll do great in this class. Just 2 papers and a final, plus participation grade. Best class I've taken at UNC. Kable is amazing. 10/10 recommend.

This class is best for people that like to talk in front of others because that's how you get all of the extra credit. Attendance is mandatory. I hated this class, but I'm not into plays. There is an 8 page paper, but I somehow managed to get an A on it. I did not do well on the exams because they are specific. If you're into drama its probably ok.

Kable's really neurotic, but in a good way. Really nice guy who ties in a lot of modern culture to ancient works. Has a lot of funny quips and is generally engaging. You can get an ungodly amount of extra credit on exams if you read in class, so DO THAT. The eight page paper admittedly isn't that fun, but it was graded very leniently. Easy A imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Super caring professor! Drama is really not my thing but I found the class fairly interesting. You can get away with not doing the readings, and the projects are fairly easy but still interesting and creative. A great class for a first year looking for a breather class amongst a heavy schedule.

You really need to go to class, pay attention, AND READ ALL THE PLAYS if you want to get an A. He will give extra credit opportunities, information and show clips in class that will be on the exams. You also really need to do good on the paper but he is really nice and gives great lectures in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thoroughly enjoyed having Kable as a professor. He is clearly passionate about what he teaches. I suggest anyone interested in the fine arts take at least one of his courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kable is an interesting guy, and definitely knows his stuff. I wasn't that into drama, but he kept my attention throughout the entire semester. Also, he wants you to learn the material (especially what he teaches), and you'll do fine if you pay attention. There was a 10 page paper (not fun to write), but other than that, not much work.

Professor Kable is extremely caring and wants you to participate and pass his class. The paper you have to write is not bad at all because it is in dialogue style and he gives PLENTY of extra credit. Keep up with your readings and you should be able to make an A in the class.

Overall pretty good! Kable teaches almost all of the Analytical, High School-style drama courses at UNC, but he has it down to a real formula and he's a very effective prof! Project was a bit long, but overall worth taking I believe!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: DRAM292 was a ton of fun. It was a breezy class but I learned a lot. Dr. Kable is awesome and a hilarious person.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Kable is one of my favorite professors at UNC! He gives awesome lectures and makes it really fun to discuss plays! We watch a ton of videos in class, and the assigned readings were all really great plays and most of them were super easy to read! Absolutely loved this class and the professor! 10/10 recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Greg is awesome! You can see how passionate he is when he lectures, and his selection of plays for the class is amazing. I've loved them all. If you have any background with reading drama, definitely take Kable for 120. The reading lists of other professors have a lot of repeats from my high school English classes, so I'm glad I took Kable instead.

Super sweet and approachable. He cares about his students and gives great lectures, that although sliiiggghhhtttlllllyyy scatter brained, he gives clear information, entertaining plays to read, and makes class really fun and interesting with his insight, activities (such as scene panels and acting exercises), and funny videos.
Read a few plays which we reread in class. He really makes sure you understand what he wants you to put on papers etc. which makes it easy to get a good score. Just watched movies in class.

Your whole grade comes from four things: weekly forum posts, a paper, a final, and attendance. Kable posted our grades for the forum posts publicly on Sakai every person who wrote one always got a 100. I figured the papers would be graded similarly, but he was extremely harsh and didn't give us our grades until LDOC and had no more office hours.

Kable is very passionate about this topic. However, the 3 tests (your only grades+a ten page paper) were difficult to study for. Take notes on everything in the class and study them, and you can do well. Maybe consider taking it with someone else so that the tests aren't so frustrating. Also, I read all of the plays, and it didn't help me at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's super sweet, is usually accessible out of class. There's only four grades and the class is more relaxing rather than a burden. You don't need the book, but make sure to sparknote it before class. He also rounded my grade up a letter grade so make sure to go to office hours and be familiar with him. Final paper was a breeze as long as you try.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class seemed like it would be easy until the first test. I felt very prepared but still had to struggle all year to barely pull out a B. Unfair grading on the 10 page single spaced paper by a TA that did not know basic grammar rules and Kable was unwilling to meet to discuss the paper after. Take this class with someone else
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Kable is my absolute favorite professor at UNC. Specifically for this class, he used little clips from so many modern films to relate the material, and all exams were multiple choice. There was a huge paper toward the end of the semester, but I wrote it in two sittings and got a B on it. If you study effectively, you'll do well.

Professor Kable was not the best professor I've had. Lectures were very monotonous and unexciting. He was barely accessible out of class and wasn't available during office hours numerous times. Also the 10 page, single-spaced paper didn't really sell me on the class either.

Kable is a nice and knowledgable guy. But he rambles on and on in his lectures and it doesn't feel like he is actually saying anything. His PowerPoints are also just random words slapped on a slide that provide no insight whatsoever.
Super nice guy! Read the material and go to class, that's it. But he is worth taking just for the relaxed feel of the class.

Kable is a good guy, but his class is so much more than what it should be. The exams are pretty difficult for an "easy A" class. I wish I would have taken drama with another professor, as it's a good way to get the LA credit. 10 page dialog paper sucked, especially with only 4 grades.

Kable is sweet, but take DRAM115 w a different professor (easy A with anyone else). Tests are too specific/tricky. Don't buy the textbook & sparknote all the plays instead (you won't read them anyways). Actual play content isn't that important, just what he says during class. Class is just 3 tests and a 10 page paper. Gives out extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Kable is the classic drama teacher. He is very kind, and although it is a large class, he will get to know you if you want. You don't have to attend class, but almost everything on the tests come from his lectures and the reading. There is a lot of reading but it is mostly interesting and he divides it up so it isn't overwhelming.

Kable is one of my favorite professors at UNC. He gives lots of extra credit and makes the class interesting with modern references. As long as you take notes, this class is an easy A. Tests are multiple choice and based on lectures or plays you have to watch. One long 8 page paper dialogue style, although it is very doable. Highly recommend!!!!

He's a nice guy. His lectures involve the showing of lots of movie scenes and in-class readings of plays.  His slides are creative too.  He gives lots of extra credit - especially on the last class day before a holiday weekend or break.  You don't have to read every play or go to every class to make an A. The class paper isn't so bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Kable was a decent choice for DRAM 115. While the class workload was nearly nothing, our entire grade was based off 2 midterms, a final and a paper. If I had known how to study I wouldn't have got a 62 on the first midterm. Take notes on the powerpoints from Sakai and you'll be fine. Glad to have my LA credit out of the way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: One of my favorite teachers here at UNC-CH. I've taken his classes before, and I'm excited to take another of his classes next semester.
Super nice guy. Tests are long, but classes are interesting. We read through the plays a lot which is helpful.

Stands in the front and lectures, take notes on your computer because he doesn't put words on the slides. Learning old literature, but he tries to make it better by showing videos of modern examples (like Taylor Swift music videos). But he gives LOTS of extra credit, sit up front bc you are more likely to be chosen for reading script, he is sweet.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Kable's lectures are fantastic! I never thought I would enjoy a drama class but we read so many different plays I had never heard of that I thoroughly loved. He's funny and tries really hard to make everything relatable. I really like his interpretation and analysis of each and every play and how he connects it to contemporary culture. Take him!

Kable is quite a character (in a good way)! Never thought I would enjoy a drama class, but the plays we read actually aren't bad at all. If you go to lecture and actually jot down what he's saying (and do other crap the entire time) you'll ace the tests. It's all pretty straightforward and Kable is a fun guy.

Okay so Drama 115 should be an easy A right? Not with this professor. I made a B- with a lot of effort as compared to friends with no work and A's with another professor. The tests are half true and false, which are extremely easy to confuse so don't think of true and false as something easy. He talks the entire hour with slides with literally pics

Loved Greg! He's hilarious in an eccentric way. The assignment descriptions are not entirely clear, but as long as you put in a visible amount of work, he'll appreciate your effort. Definitely recommend for anyone, not just people interested in drama!
very eccentric, love him to death. took DRAM81H, was super fun and an easy A! highly recommend

Passionate professor who loves his subject. HOWEVER, Dr. Kable is a confusing lecturer and gives tests with unclear prompts. He is also unwilling to help; I had trouble all year asking him questions and he even refused to see me for office hours. I would not recommend taking his class unless drama is your strong suit.

Greg Kable is honestly the not-so-hidden gem of UNC. Ask any Drama student and they will most likely tell you that you should probably take at least one of his classes while you're at UNC. If you wanna watch Lady Gaga and Birdman to illustrate drama history concepts, then this is your class. Hilarious, fun, and you'll learn a lot.

Prof. Kable makes his lectures fun.  I had him for DRAM 292: The American Musical.  His lectures are full of comedy and videos that explain exactly what he is talking about.  While his grading rubrics are always the clearest, if you need help, it's definitely there.  Attendance policy is very strict.  GO TO CLASS!!!

Professor Kable clearly loves Drama, and this drama class is really fun and gets rid of a lot of GENEDS.  Its not too hard at all, and his grading criteria for essays is always very specific so you know what to do to get a good grade.  Definitely recommend this seminar.
My 2nd class with Kable. I love him- favorite professor here. Makes my day bright with clips from Lady Gaga concert footage, Mean Girls, Glee, and Pitch Perfect.

This class is completely doable.  Kable makes the subject interesting and when I took this class last spring it was easy to do well if you did the assigned readings and came to class.  The paper is daunting at first, but it really isn't that bad once you get started.  Would definitely recommend!

Take this class with this professor! He is absolutely great! Makes a dull non-major subject very interesting. I was dreading this course when I enrolled but it is definitely one of my favorite classes that I have taken. Kable is the man!

His personality will strike you, he's funny and witty although he won't look like it at first glance. Very passionate about theatre and is enthused with class participation. Test we multiple choice and true/false so they could be tricky, but they were generally easy if you pay attention to lecture

Great professor! No homework outside of a few papers/group project. Not a lot of work and an easy grader. Class is mandatory (with the exception of a few absences he'll excuse) but reading is not mandatory. As long as you read up on sparknotes before class you can generally be fine in the class discussions which are voluntary to speak in.
Funny and clever but lectures are often monotonous, tests are confusing.
A really fascinating lecturer but his tests are confusing and difficult.
He was one of my favorite teachers. such a great class to go to.
This class was pretty easy. Kable's lectures aren't that boring, considering that it's drama. If you take good notes and are good at memorization, you'll be fine.

Prof. Kable is great! He's a really nice guy, and is very passionate about theatre.  He relates all of the plays to today by comparing them with movies and TV shows today.  There are four essays a semester, including the final exam.  There is almost never any homework besides reading plays.
Professor Kable is passionate about what he teaches and makes classes interesting. Makes drama enjoyable even to those who are not interested in the arts

I love Greg. He's interesting and knowledgeable and it's obvious that he cares about teaching. Make sure you know the information on the study sheets and you'll be golden on tests. Attendance isn't mandatory, but class is always interesting; he shows film clips every day and often gives extra credit.

The A was much harder to get than it should've been with my prior knowledge because TAs arbitrarily grade papers (mine had only a 3 word comment) and test questions can be ambiguous even with studying. Still, it's a fun class with an entertaining professor. Start the paper early and come every day in case he gives EC (esp days right after tests).

I thought I was going to fail this class after the first test but that was because I literally didn't pay attention. After that, I started taking notes and paying attention in class. I got A's on both the second test and the 8 page paper. You don't have to know drama to do well. He's funny and gives lots of extra credit but there are NO CURVES.

Kable is very funny and friendly, he works hard to create a fun, comfortable learning environment.  He shows videos pretty much everyday and is a very passionate lecturer.  Tests are easy as long as you read and you will get an A on the 8-page paper if you put any modicum  of effort into it.  He made me look forward to coming to class, take him.
Entertaining, a bit tough at times, but not too unfair.

Definitely an entertaining guy.  He doesn't take attendance, but if you want to pass his exams, you should definitely go to class.  His exams are multiple choice and true false, and they basically come straight from his lectures.  Some questions are about things that he never really talked about, but you really only need to sparknote the plays.

Great class! Not too challenging, but you definitely need to have a general sense of what is going on in the plays. Okay to miss class occasionally. Tests can be tricky, but as long as you study the night before you'll be fine. Kable is a very entertaining professor!

Greg is so fun! Very enthusiastic and he likes to show multi media stuff like music videos and fun stuff!!  Grading was very easy, just read the plays and do the assignments.  Also participation is key... he will ask a question and let there be an awkward silence until someone raises their hand!!!

Took this class to fulfill a requirement. I don't like drama, but Kable was alright. He's an interesting fellow. Def need to read the plays. Papers aren't hard. Attendance mandatory and he demands participation. But no tests! Not a bad drama class to take care of that requirement.

Greg is awesome! He's quirky but in a good way.  His class is fun.  There were three essays, including the final and they were creative and fun to write.  If you need a performing arts credit, take one of his classes!
Way too hard for a drama class. 8 page paper isn't as bad as it first seems. Mandatory to read plays and attend lecture or else your exam grade will suffer

I liked Kable.  Very funny at times, make sure you read the plays-& not just scan through them either..he takes somewhat minute details from plays for questions.  Not a hard class, just read the plays and go to lecture (notes are pretty straightforward, he just explains things as they relate to different "movements" in the drama world).  Take him!

loved him! attendance is not mandatory, but definately rewarded. he occasionally gives extra credit and about 90% of his tests are based DIRECTLY off of his notes/lectures. he likes to make little jokes and video/movie days are always enjoyable. overall, a great professor who is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches!
he was funny, but the class was too hard for a freaking drama class
love it!! he makes awesome use of multi media and he loves to joke around... its also kinda easy to convince him to delay deadlines for assignments! :)

I would recommend this class because it is fairly easy and Professor Kable is knowledgeable. However, the 8 page paper you have to write is very tedious. Go to class and take notes because exam questions can be specific. If you go to class on days where a fair amount of students are missing he will give 5-6 points extra credit on the next exam!!

Don't let his joke and lighthearted nature fool you, this class is no walk in the park. Exams require that you read and know minute details from the plays. In addition to this, the eight page paper is tiresome and your grade depends completely on your TA and are FINAL!!!! And if you ever email him, don't expect a response.

Prof Kable is very knowledgeable on the plays that we read and offered interesting insight. The two papers and final paper are graded easily & class is mainly discussion based. Movie clips and often used.
True & false questions suck. Half the final was T&F. He's really funny and nice. Paper's pretty annoying because it really long. Exams aren't too bad. Interesting class. Some notes in class.

Relatively easy. True or false questions are kind of annoying on his tests. Try to go to class as much as possible, but it doesn't kill you if you miss a class or two. Video clips are fun and he's a pretty funny guy. The only real problem I had was how drastically different his TAs graded our papers, but that's not his fault.
Kable is eccentric and you can tell he's a nutty artsy genius guy. He shows lots of video clips in class, so coming to class is something you look forward to!

It's a good idea to go to class since he sometimes gives in-class assignments, but otherwise it's a pretty easy going course as long as you try to write papers beforehand. He watches a lot of interesting clips in class and is pretty cool for a professor.

Knows his stuff and is very fun.  Though attendance is mandatory, you really only need to pay attention one of the days (out of 2-3) a play is discussed--the information is repeated often and the lectures can be circular.  Not bad at all.
I liked the class and the test were extremely easy. Prof. Kable is an extremely nice person but is often not very clear about what he wants esp. on the course paper. All in all not a bad class.

lots of reading involved in the class and lots of pop quizzes so attendance is a must.  he makes examples interesting by using movies, music videos, etc.  he is a character; very entertaining.  however, he is very unclear and the tests are harder than the lectures, which seem like they were thrown together right before the class.

I absolutely hated this class.  It was boring and useless.  I only liked one of the plays and it was hard not to fall asleep.  He speaks very softly which makes u fall asleep.  He doesn't give back papers, so you never know how you did.  The tests aren't that bad...I never payed attention and did alright but there was really no point to this class.

Greg is amazing. I really don't know why these ppl have been givin him a bad rep.  Funny as hell which makes class interesting. Pop quizzes for attendance so be there.  Tests aren't that bad just make sure you've read the plays.  His true or false can be tricky so you need to study a little bit.  Seriously take his class!!!!!
makes class fun, tests aren't bad if you go to class, does attendance checks so make sure to be there for those, very approachable, nice professor-take his class!
i hated this class
Classes are extremely easy, professor is very engaged in the material and understanding of students' concerns

this teacher is def. strange, I do not know what's up with him but he tries to make stupid statements. Plus the class i very boring, probably the least interesting class I ever took, nothing helpfull in this class just waste of time, plus the exams are pretty confusing, I would never take this class if I knew who he was. good luck~
Just write a creative paper. Like...really creative. Hell, tape yourself doing a bad modern dance and justify it. I promise it will work.

Random weird guy.  Goes around the subject and makes up each class. The plays read were somewhat interesting but the lectures were almost unbearable. Random test questions come from lectures so you have to go.

Weird guy. I hated his class, but I can see how somebody would like him. He tries hard to be funny and makes a lot of references to pop culture. He has an obnoxious voice, and he makes up class as he goes along. I thought it was really boring, and it's hard to study for it. He messed up my grade and wouldn't help me with it. Easy class though.
He just talks and talks and does not give clear definitions, and this class is mostly definitions. The paper is not clear and have to attend to 3 plays during the semester which is very inconvenient.
No Comments
A fun teacher who makes class interesting rather than a bore.  Tests aren't that hard but you need to study.  Watch lots of movie clips.  A great class
Greg rocks my face off. He's such a riot.
Obnoxious lecture delivery style.  Paper requirements and grading are unclear.
Usually easy class but interesting.
class is a breeze and he is very animated and good for a laugh
No Comments
take this class!

Exams are worth 85% of your grade in this class, so be ready to study outside of class. However, Dr. Lassiter was very straight-forward in his lectures and got straight to the point. Honestly such a chill guy and is very open to giving feedback during office hours. Definitely recommend.

In his class currently and really enjoy it. Attendance is not mandatory. The tests are lengthy but doable if you study. You also get a two sided cheat sheet for each exam that you can use your ipad to make. He is very accessible and always willing to help you go through a few practice problems in office hours which has helped me a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Lassiter was an engaging professor. Homework was weekly (sometimes he extended deadlines) and manageable. The exams were a bit long so it will be hard to finish in time if you get stuck, but most if not all of it is addressed in lectures or practice exams, so I would say they are fair! Although I didn't go to office hours he encourages us to.
It was a chill class, you get cheat sheets, extra credit, and some easy bonus points from watching his Mini Lectures. Some homeworks do take some time. Overall good class for stats major!

Very fair class with opportunities for extra credit. You get a cheat sheet for exams however they are somewhat difficult, particularly the final. Lassiter really knows what he is doing and takes time to ensure everyone understands.

It was shocking to see bad reviews. He cares for the material, being a teacher, and seeing his students succeed. He has very dry humor but it works for a stats class. The lectures and homework build effectively for midterms and final, and he allows cheat sheets. Attend and do the work on time, the material will stay fresh. I can't recommend enough.

AMAZING. He holds 3-hour office hours twice a week and is always accessible to answer questions. Attendance isn't mandatory, but to know what you're doing, you have to go since he doesn't post his lectures. The exams are close to the practice given, but can get tricky. Overall, he truly cares and is easily the best professor I've had at UNC.

He's truly an excellent professor. He's kind, consistently responsive, and always willing to help when the material gets tough. One of the top instructors in the STOR department. If you get the chance to take a class with him, don't hesitate.

It's his first time to teach STOR 415 but he did a great job on it. The lecture notes are clear and the homework questions are similar to the exam questions. Have 2% extra credit if you go to class every time and finish the bonus quizzes. He is also really caring as he holds 6-hour office hours per week and is always ready to offer help.

Lassiter was a very engaging lecturer, and I enjoyed coming to class. Gave 4 extra credit "pop" quizzes which each added .5% to total grade. OH were helpful especially for homework. Exams were fair and similar to HW, make sure to study the examples he gives in class.

Lassiter is tough but fair. His tests are very challenging, but they are material he covered in the lecture. You get one cheat sheet on midterms (2) and two for the final. reviews.comment: I took his STOR 415 class—he's the best professor I've had. He's kind, patient, and truly cares about students. His slides are clear and well-organized, making hard topics easy to follow. I highly recommend him if you're starting STOR 415. A great teacher for this course!

Prof Lassiter is a great choice for stats. Tests were extremely fair and only covered what was discussed in class. He's very helpful in office hours, I went every week to stay caught up. Homework is straightforward and cheat sheets are allowed on both the midterms and the final. Highly recommend, I was terrified of stats and he made it great.

take this class with lassiter!!! he was so nice and his lectures were super engaging as he posts fill in the blank notes which i enjoyed. he allows cheat sheets for all midterms and the final, as well as access to calculators. would take again!

He's a fine professor. The lectures and in-class examples are fairly straightforward. Homework and exams pretty much make up the entirety of the course grade, but both are pretty easy. We didn't get through all of the material, so he ended up cutting stuff from the exams.
Good professor for STOR 155, very helpful office hours if you go, exams weighted a lot, use cheat sheets
He genuinely cares about his students and is always willing to help clarify the material. The exams are challenging, but he curves the final grades to be fair. Highly recommend!

He is so great! The midterms and final weren't that hard, he will curve the grades if necessary. There are also some chances for extra credit, he is super organized and approachable. I would recommend taking his class!

Professor Lassiter is a pretty good teacher, this class moves fast but is manageable to keep up with. It's very test heavcy but you get cheat sheets so make sure to use them. His lectures move pretty quickly, so pay attention to everything he says. Overall, he is pretty good and also helpful during office hours.

I've never taken a statistics class before, but Lassiter's lectures were clear and exams were fair - you also get cheat sheets. Pay a fair amount of attention in lectures - the content jumps from easy to difficult quickly. Sometimes he was standoffish or annoyed during office hours, which was tough since new material lectures were dense/confusing.

If you have to take stats here take it with prof Lassiter! His exams were very fair and he wanted you to succeed. Traditional lecture style and homework was weighted as much as an exam. Best stor 155 teacher by far.

If math/stats doesn't come easy to you, prepare to study a lot for this class. If you do all the homework and study a good amount before exams, you can deff get an A. Info goes from easy to hard pretty quickly. You get a cheat sheet for all the finals, PACK them with info from the lectures. Lassiter does a great job going through the material.
Very hard class for me, as someone who hasn't taken statistics before. Very test heavy around 70% of your grade. Final was curved.

reviews.comment: Professor Lassiter is such a great teacher! His lectures are clear and organized, and the mini lectures definitely aid the understanding of the course materials. HW every week, but they prepare you for the exams. You def need to put in effort to earn a A, but it is a very fun course to take!

Just go to class for 2 points to your final grade thru random bonus quizzes(completion). The hardest problem of the HW was usually gone over in class so those were pretty chill too. Exams are super fair, and there were points back for a hard problem. Office hours were really good as well. Overall, nice professor and an interesting class.

Amazing clear lectures. Opportunities for extra credit for showing up to class (bonus "quizzes"). Homework is manageable and we usually go over a problem the class votes on. - Weekly Homework (about 3h per)

- Super helpful and gives lots of time to ask questions

- Responsive on Piazza if you have questions outside of class hours
Professor Lassiter makes this class very manageable. Just watch the mini lecture videos and go to class and you will be fine.

reviews.comment: He has very solid lectures and his homework was exactly what we practiced in class. He was always super positive in class and happy to answer questions. So long as you show up for lecture and do/review the homework, you should be able to get an easy A.
Lassiter is dope—he got Brandwein's for us during final project presentations

reviews.comment: Worst class I have taken at UNC. Lectures are difficult to understand. I studied the most for this class than I did for any of my other classes that semester and still barely passed. Professor Lassiter is so nice. His lectures are clear and easy to understand. And he gives us extra points through bonus quiz. If you put in some effort, you will get a good grade. Take his class!

Prof. Lassiter made the material easy to understand and was very accessible outside of class. He's a nice person, but the class sucks. Would not recommend 515 with any professor. Lassiter did alright, but I think his lectures can be a bit bland at times. He is very very helpful outside of class, and was a lenient grader. He wants you to succeed, but the class does not.

easy but annoying. Very inflexible about teaching style. One of those profs who only sort of answers your questions.

Was my favorite class all semester. He takes his time to prepare lesson plans to teach the class and make sure everyone understands it. He is a very nice guy and wants his students to succeed. Would definitely recommend taking Professor Lassiter's STOR 155 section.

Prof Lassiter is a good guy, and he does lots of helpful examples in class. He is extremely accessible, holding office hours for 6 hours a week. reviews.comment: Lee is very kind and a great professor! He really encourages participation (20% of grade) and grades the rest on 3 papers, midterm, and final. Exams are kinda tricky, but papers are easily graded. The topics are really interesting, and learning about leadership is great for any major, not just journalism. Highly recommend!!

Prof Meredith is pretty solid. Very approachable. 424 has 2 short papers about a selected reading and then 1 longer research paper. HW is mostly book/textbook reading. Overall, not a hard class and Meredith makes it pretty flexible and adaptable to the changes in media management.

Prof. Meredith is so sweet and caring! His classes were lecture heavy, but the grading criteria is clear and he is very accessible outside of class. Readings are light and easy to follow!! Would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He cares about his students, but grading guidelines are unclear, making it hard to write essays. The lectures do not add much to helping you understand course material, so make sure to read the textbook. Class grade is based on 3 essays, participation, midterm, and final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Meredith is a wonderful professor even under the circumstances of being online. His class was my favorite class I took this semester. The lectures are easy to understand and the assignments are clearly outlined. You really can't fail unless you're trying to. He is very kind and cares about his students greatly. I 1000% recommend him.

They had so many awesome guest lectures and had an awesome format. Were very understanding and extended deadlines. Weekly quizzes with two papers. The papers were laid out exactly the way they wanted. Easy A. Just do the work. Midterm and final based off of weekly quizzes. Highlighted material on the midterm and final for easy study guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was almost always guest speakers, so it was more like Prof Meredith was a moderator and grader, rather than a teacher. This class feels easy until you get to papers/exams, and then all of a sudden you have to remember seemingly irrelevant details from random guest speakers.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: MEJO101 is a carousel of different lecturers each class discussing different attributes of journalism, but Prof. Meredith fills in the gaps nicely. He cares for his students and professionally facilitates group discussions on usually touchy subjects. Class is weighed way too heavily by random fact memorization exams but mixed with two big papers.

Professor Meredith truly wants all of his students to succeed. He we always available to help me review material outside of class and to also help me clarify my career path. Can take him a while to put things in the grade book so make sure you're proactive and meet with him in office hours to ensure a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lee is a really nice guy and wants you to be successful. He is a pretty easy grader on the research paper as long as he knows you put in the effort. Tests and assignments are pretty straightforward and I definitely learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such an interesting guy and class! Lee was really funny, and him and Deb do a great job together in class. Lee was the one who graded all my papers and was a little harsh sometimes, but overall very helpful. I loved Mejo 101 and all the lectures were so interesting. You can tell how they are all experts. Loved this class.

Professor Meredith is incredible. He is so inspirational and really cares about his students. He expects a lot from students so you have to put in the effort to do well in his class but he is very helpful and knowledgable. Definitely recommend taking a course with Professor Meredith.

Every student should be able to come out of this class with extensive knowledge of media management. Prof. Meredith's class was reliant on a research paper, two small book reports, midterm, and final. Current events was a nice touch to spice up the class and get everyone involved. Meredith is a kind-hearted individual and grades fair. Solid choice!

I took this class online no homework and you just have to attend class and participate once in a while. Two tests and three papers (one of which was 8 pages). They are extremely informal papers and he is an easy A type of grader. Super nice guy and always available to help!

No tests in this class, just two papers that determine nearly all of your grade. But, Prof. Meredith is a pretty easy grader and he's so willing to help his students. Don't be afraid to ask for clarification or guidance. He's one of the friendliest professors I've had at UNC and I look forward to his classes. Heavy reading, but it's interesting.

Lee is a nice guy BUT his lectures are incredibly boring and I feel like I wasted my time taking this class. For the entire semester he gave the impression that this would be an "easy A" course and didn't grade but a single assignment until the week of finals. When he did release grades, they were harsh and were hardly constructive.

Very light on work (reflecting on discussions, 3 short essays, readings, 2 presentations) which was basically all completion grades, but deadlines and instructions are often unclear, hard to find, or only mentioned verbally. Attendance is a huge part of your grade so do not skip. She is very kind and approachable, just a bit disorganised.

It is a philosophical course based on art than a studio art course. Work: responses to readings (short), hands-on activities, documentaries, or field trips. Half of the assignments are "complete" grades on Canvas, so they are not actually counted towards your grade. Midterms and the Final are presentations (easy). Do not skip it impacts your grade.

Professor Lawrence is down to earth and understanding with each of her students. You will never have a problem with her as the professor. The class is seminar based to be prepared to read texts and discuss them. There are activities we do throughout the semester that are easy and fun. Class is smaller so connecting with the professor is easy. 10/10

She is a super sweet professor. She is easy to have a conversation with. My only complaint is it is nearly impossible to make anything higher than 90. I have gotten maybe 2 grades over 90, and heard this is common for other students. We don't do much in class, but from what we do it is an interesting and engaging class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: great professor, like actually amazing, take a class with her

Dr. Boynton is so sweet and funny! The content can be a little boring at times, but she always managed to make us smile during class. Daily in-class group assignments were pretty easy and useful. Sometimes, she can be a tough grader, but she genuinely cares about her students and loves her job.
She clearly cares about her students and makes each class discussion interesting. Also good at giving feedback on accuracy graded assignments

Lois is so funny and gives entertaining lectures. Cares about her students and is accessible outside of class! Can be a tough grader at times but she cares about her students succeeding, especially in a 100 level class.

Dr. B was a great professor who truly cared for her students. I thoroughly enjoyed her course and learned a great deal about the world of public relations. I would recommend this course for anyone who is interested in doing the same.
Dr. Boynton was amazing! She is funny and gives great feedback on assignments. She is willing to work with you and has clear grading criteria.

She is such a sweetie and so funny! She makes the lectures so fun and teaches the content well. There are a lot of small assignments, but I like that because it balances grades. Most are usually just short discussions. Take this class with her!!

I loved her as a professor and I wish I could've taken more classes with her. Truly caring and gives clear instructions and useful feedback. She is always there to help, she even sent me resources for my papers on random days when I didn't even ask for it, shows you how much she thinks of her students and is cheering for their success.

I love Lois. She is my favorite professor I've taken at UNC (141 & 531) and I consider her a friend. She is a tough grader and I tend to hover around an A- in her classes as a result, but 531 is my favorite class of the semester. I always feel welcomed by her and look forward to learning from her. I highly recommend taking her before you graduate.

I absolutely love Dr. B. I had her for 141 and again for 531. I think she is an amazing professor who truly cares about her students and wants them engaged, however, she is a super tough grader. It's really hard to get higher than an A- on any assignment just through the nature of her grading. I love Dr. B and can't recommend her enough!

Professor Boynton is nice, but her lectures are so dry and the homework feels tedious a lot of the time. I was less than a tenth of a point away from an A- in the class but she did not round up, which is incredibly frustrating. If you want to avoid a situation like that, don't take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Nice lady. BUT class feels so long and she is a tough grader. you cant miss a single class or discussion post or it will ruin ur grade. It is a required class, so you have to take it but honestly not bad,, just is a lot of work. Lots of homework, like 5 quizzes, a midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class is very lecture heavy and you HAVE to attend. It seems like a lot of busy work.

Professor B is great and really cares about her students. I learned a lot in this class and would take another class with her. The only negative is that sometimes she is a hard grader when you aren't expecting it, so be careful. About 6 reading quizzes, 1 big project and 3 exams total. Extra credit available and she made the final open-book.

Dr. Boynton made this class interesting. She is very relatable and loves to talk about random things. She is the sweetest and even gives out candy when we have tests. She really does want you to succeed and she is amazing.
Professor Boynton really cares about her students and tries to make her lectures fun and engaging

Some of my friends were in other sections of this class with other professors, and I definitely had the best deal in this class. Dr. B made it so easy and fun to learn about ethics, and she was one of the most caring professors I've ever had. Would recommend literally any class you can take with her.

Dr. B is a Gem! She's such a kind and caring professor and really wants to build relationships with her students. She made ethics as interesting as she could given how mundane the material can be. Tests were not hard as long as you paid attention in class and the quizzes were straight out of the book! FYI: dont bother buying the newest textbook...

I love Lois, she's such a kind professor and she's super accomodating to her students. I enjoyed her class so much. She can grade a little bit hard sometimes but always within reason. I really recommend taking her class.

Dr. Boynton is possibly my favorite professor at UNC. She really cares about the course material and, more importantly, her students and their mental health. If you want to take MEJO 141, please try to take it with Dr. B. You will not regret it. I love her.

Dr. B is such a funny person and she made class really engaging for her students. The class is definitely not an "easy A" as there are frequent quizzes, a group assignment every single class, and tests are weighted heavily, but TBH it is worth it. I learned a lot and she made a super dry subject interesting. I'd totally take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. B was my favorite prof this semester. She is hysterical and frequently has her cat, Sophie, show up to class. She explains content really well and makes it really engaging. I was thoroughly impressed by how engaging it was especially given we were on Zoom! I'm going to try to take any and all other courses she teaches bc I loved her that much.

Dr. B is awesome  so nice and caring! We had a lot of group work during classes, so coming to class is important, but it is such an enjoyable class anyway! Graded on 3 exams, 1 group project, reading quizzes, participation, and in-class/homework assignments. If you want to take MEJO 141, take it with Dr. B! An interesting class with a great prof!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Caring

reviews.comment: Loved MEJO 141 with Professor Boynton. She was funny and the classes were pretty interesting. Lectures definitely took up the full class period but the examples she used were relevant and really helped with understanding the material.

Professor Boynton is such a fun professor. Media Ethics isn't the most fun topic, but she really makes it so enjoyable. Her tests are kind of difficult, but if you pay attention in class they aren't too bad. Also, if you decide to take her class, be prepared to laugh a lot.

I LOVE Lois. She made some pretty dry subject matter enjoyable and she was hilarious. When I didn't do well on a test she was available to go over what I got wrong and made me feel so much more confident. If you need to take 141, for sure take it with Lois!

Dr. B is a great professor and tries to make it as interesting as she can but it still is ethics and the material can get dry. Pay attention in class and do the readings or its a little tough to understand the cases. Great professor for this class but can grade harshly on small assignments sometimes. Participation is v important in the class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Yall, take her class. I'm only a few weeks in, but she is so caring, makes a constant effort to make us laugh/enjoy class, and she just rocks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Boynton's class. She is a caring, enthusiastic professor who really just wants her students to succeed. Her class definitely isn't an easy A, but if you show up, do the readings, and participate, you'll be fine. The exams are pretty tough, some multiple choice, t/f, but mostly essay questions.

Lois is awesome! Her teaching style is very relaxed, and she is very comedic. Her test material comes directly from info/application methods explained in lectures. Participation definitely matters in this class. She grades semi-harshly, especially before anything is really taught (first few weeks of class), which I wish I would have known earlier.

I really enjoyed Dr. B's Media Ethics class! The tests are straightforward and relatively easy, from my experience. She grades homework a little more harshly, but there are also a few freebie assignments to boost your grade. She's pretty funny, and she plays music (SZA, Kendrick, etc) before every class which seems irrelevant but it's nice

I want to love Dr. B, but I am not happy with the experience I had this past semester. She uses her lecture time as a standup comedy hour. She is hilarious, but I learned approximately 25 percent of what I wanted to learn. My classmates and I agreed that we were teaching ourselves by the end of the semester. Take 141 with someone else.

One of the most genuine and talented professors in the J school. I've never met someone who cares more about their students and wants them to succeed. Grading policies are strict, but you'll be a better writer because of it and will be thanking Lois when you're out in the real world. Super understanding & opportunities for extra credit.
She doesn't teach the class then expects you to know material from the lectures... there are only guest lectures
An awesome professor. Great personality. Highly recommend her courses.

Prof Boynton had a great personality, but she honestly doesn't teach much in her JOMC 101 class. The class really lacks any sort of cohesiveness, which I think made it more difficult for me. Definitely don't write this off as an easy A and fall behind. You really do have to attend the lectures, take notes, and do the reading to do well.

Dr. B seems like a great professor, but the problem with JOMC 101 is that she doesn't really teach it. There is a different guest lecturer every class, which helps explore multiple topics but makes for an awkward class. The tests can be a little tricky, especially the truefalse section. Overall the class was okay.
Baller.

Definitely tried to make the class interesting, but it was a bunch of guest lecturers that didn't really add up to a cohesive class. Homework and exams were very easy and straightforward. Pretty easy A class
Dr. B is great! Not only does she try to give us information we'll use in the real world, she's helpful and wants us to succeed.  I'd take another class with her in a heartbeat.

Dr. B is awesome. She makes class enjoyable by employing a variety of different professors from the J school. There's not a ridiculous amount of work, and the material, while subject, is not at all difficult. She's a very fun person and if you're at all interested in journalism, I recommend this class.

I loved Lois! For a 5:00 class, she made it more enjoyable than I could've have asked for! She's so nice and always willing to help, plus her emails are always encouraging unlike some daunting professors.  Some of the info is not crystal clear, but that's how must every subject is.  I would ABSOLUTELY recommend this class in a heartbeat!

Great, great professor. She's funny, discussions are interesting, and the readings are minimal (and interesting). I don't know why people say this class is so hard, it's really not as long as you put in the same amount of effort you would any other class. (It's easy not to because it seems like such easy material, but she's a tough grader).

By far the best professor in the J-School and probably the best professor I have had. She is very helpful and cares a lot for the students. She is really easy to talk to and always tries to make class fun. It's definitely not easy; she is a very tough grader but if you make an effort to go to class and work hard then an A is possible.
bottom line to taking intro to pr with lois, you're going to get a b, no matter how much work you put into the class.  if you're okay with that, she's not a bad prof to have.
Hey now! I thought she was funny. Really cares about the kids.
