dare i say the best professor ever at UNC. extremely organized, very helpful in OH, basically gives you the answers to homeworks if you go. homeworks are super similar to exams, just practice those. so much practice probelms and there are review sessions every week if you need it. the best professor fr, so easy to interact with as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice professor and fair gradings. Materials are not hard if you are good at algebra and calculus. You only need to understand the concepts and apply mathematical way to solve problems. All 3 exams have an average of ~78% (she even curved the final exam by 3 points to make that). This semester 28% got an A and another 8% got an A-. MSA is the GOAT!

GET READY TO MAKE THIS CLASS YOUR LIFE OTHERWISE YOU WILL HAVE TO RETAKE IT…this class will LITERALLY BECOME YOUR LIFE. IF YOU THOUGHT ECON101 WAS HARD GET READY FOR DOUBLE THE STUDYING AND DOUBLE THE STRESS. Make sure to STAY ON TOP OF HW/go to EconAid, if you check out for even a week you're SCREWED because new things build off previous concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the most organized professors I've had, and she seems passionate about what she's teaching! She provides a lot of resources to help out. This class required a lot of work, though, so be ready to put in the time. I just don't like how the midterms/final determine almost your entire grade.

ECON 410 is difficult, but MSA does a great job making the material make sense. Plenty of resources/practice problems to study for exams as well, which is nice. While attendance in lecture/recitation is technically mandatory, she offers an alternate grade scale that gives extra weight to tests to replace attendance grade. Overall great experience

MSA is one of the best professors I have had at UNC. She's an incredibly good lecturer that makes difficult content easy to understand. She had pre-recorded videos and a lot of resources to help students. She's always available for questions and her tests are very fair. The exams are not easy, but if you pay attention and study, you will be fine.

MSA provides a lot of resources however the amount of resources she provides is overwhelming. In addition, I've found the pre-recorded lecture videos to be unhelpful as later on in the semester what she teaches in class doesn't align with the lecture video and it can be confusing. 75% of your grade is two midterms and final with no curve.

You need to be good at calculus and algebra, I struggled at first and I'm pretty good at math. MSA is super nice and very passionate. She gives tons of resources/ practice problems, but the class structure is annoying. She expects a lot of time outside of class, which is fair but if you don't watch pre-class videos you will be lost during lectures.

Class is not that bad you should be fine as long as you are decent at basic calc. Tests are actually way easier than she makes them seem. Like she will hype up how hard they are and say you will need to apply concepts in new ways we have not seen. This is not true, practice problems were for sure harder than exam.
MSA is the goat. Not only does she make 410 understandable, but it provides a great foundation for a lot of the stuff you use throughout the econ major. She's hilarious and charismatic too.

Do not take this class with her. Just had our first exam and she purposely tries to trick you. She is an awful teacher, I've had to teach myself everything on my own. Studied more than I ever have and still did bad on the exam.

I don't understand how her reviews are so high. Everyone I know in upper level econ courses says her class is taught very poorly for learning the basics that are needed later on. Do not take this class with her.

I took this course with MSA because of her reviews on here, but I strongly advise to not take this class with her. While there are a lot of resources available, they are not beneficial and are overwhelming. Her lectures are all over the place and have no structure. Everyone I know in this course with her is extremely confused.

MSC is good at explaining concepts and providing resources. My complaint is that 78-83% of the grade comes from timed exercises and exams. Only 17-22% of grades will be determined by things that students can take their time on. This class feels like taking the ACT and is a neurotypical-focused class where testing alone judges your capability.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: GOAT status in the economics department. Networking with other students and engaging with genuinely enticing class content. No exams. Procrastinating the portfolio is not advisable, but you'll survive...probably. Best of luck to any future ULAs.

She really knows her stuff. Try to go to class as most of my notes are from class. I didn't really use the textbook at all. Everything builds off of each other so make sure to know the beginning units very well. I took this 2nd semester freshmen year and thought it was doable- used all the resources she gave. Def go to her help sessions with TAs.

MSA gave us many resources to succeed in this class including lecture videos, help sheets, etc. Exams and homeworks were somewhat difficult but the amount of practice and guidelines she gave make it possible to do well if you put effort. In general she and the TAs were very helpful as far as answering questions if there was confusion.

MSA is easily the best prof I've ever had at UNC. If you do the pre-class videos and pay attention during lecture you will be fine. The midterms were not too bad, and I thought the final was a little easier. Your grade in this class will reflect how much work you put in. If you are willing to work, I would definitely recommend taking 410 with MSA.

MSA is a fantastic professor and if you have to take this class at all, take it with her. She provides so so so many resources, and those are the key to doing good in the class. Truly understand the content to a deep level, and know how to apply concepts in conjunction with when to use them! Exams are SO fair & class felt easier than ECON 101 tbh.

MSA made ECON410 so much easier than I thought it would be. She's a great lecturer and truly cares about her students. The exams aren't too hard as long as you pay attention in class, watch the lecture videos, and study practice materials.

She is the best professor at UNC. This class wasn't the hardest but definitely not easy, however she is super accessible and gives tons of resources. Study hard, do the practice problems and an A is definitely attainable
She is an amazing professor, but the course might be one of the hardest at UNC. Take 410 with her if you need it, but prepare to lock in like never before.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: I wish that there was a way to rate her as more than a 5. MSA is the sole reason that I am interested in economics now. She's worth the wait to take her if she isn't teaching 410 at the moment. The only reason that I rate her as a 3 in difficulty is just because the material is more difficult than average.

MSA is the absolute best. She is super sweet and cares so much about each student. She's amazing at explaining concepts in a way that makes sense. She also told so many funny stories in class that related to the material which made it memorable. I never struggled to pay attention during her lectures because they were so interesting.

MSA once again is unmatched in her ability to teach complex concepts in a clear, concise way. Her teaching style and quizzes were set up well for us to succeed in the class. Overall, relatively easy class but very enjoyable and interesting.

This is my second class with MSA and she's an amazing professor (probably one of the best in the department). The content is an extension of 410 so a lot of the lectures are familiar which is nice. She was really accessible outside of class and a 10/10 class!

MSA is a true gift to the ECON department. After having her for both 410 & 415, she is my favorite professor by a mile. She is kind and takes time to get to know her students individually. For a professor to teach such difficult classes and consistently be rated amongst the highest, you know she is worth it! When I think UNC, I also think MSA!

MSA is one of the best econ lecturer I ever had. She is funny and obviously passionate about what she teaches. She has very clear grading criteria and wants you to succeed. If you just keep up with her class, attend lectures, do the homework, and use the resources she gives you, you will get an A. I was sick for three weeks so I fell behind.

MSA is the best teacher you will ever have. Pre-class assignments and problem sets are short, but useful. She creates study guides for every quiz that are super helpful for studying. Very responsive to students ideas and questions, via campuswire, email, and office hours.
Dropping the lowest quiz grade???? Praise the goddess that is MSA.

MSA was my favorite professor at Carolina. She was fair, encouraging, and willing to spend time out of class helping students understand the material. I got a C+ in her class (totally fair), so be ready to study. Her 410 class was tough, but I enjoyed learning from her so much I took another class with her - would do it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Humble and kind energy in the classroom. Expectations are clear and concise. Resources are organized and bountiful. She did her part, the course is on you.
Hands down the best professor at UNC. Passionate, caring and extremely knowledgable. I fought tooth and nail to get into her summer class and did not regret it.

If you find yourself in the unfortunate situation of having to take ECON410, you must choose MSA. She is the best at getting you through this weed-out class. She is highly organized and provides you with every resource you could possibly need. Make sure to attend ALL lectures and you'll be fine.

ECON410 is a difficult course but MSA offers a lot of resources, is very organized, and is genuinely good at teaching. As long as you stay on top of your stuff in this class and put in effort to understand the material as you go, you'll be fine.

Great professor that provides numerous resources, practice problems, and help sessions to help students succeed. Content is challenging, but exams are fair and not designed to trick you. Her lectures are very engaging and help you master the material. I definitely recommend taking ECON 410 with MSA!

MSA is my absolute favorite professor at UNC. She has so many resources available to help you succeed and explains things very clearly. Her lesson videos are great and while she is not willing to bend deadlines, she has enough built in drops in the syllabus that you will be fine.

MSA is the professor to take for 410. Do not try to take someone else because it is a challenging class and MSA is the best one at making the information clear and understandable. Wants each student to succeed but will not give any particular student extra advantages over others.
MSA is the person to take for Econ, it is a challenging class, but she makes it straightforward and genuinely wants success for her students.

410 is definitely doable and you are given all the resources you need to succeed. If you haven't taken calc in a while, you'll struggle at first but you'll catch on as you do practice problems. Don't buy the textbook, you won't need it. Also, MSA is an amazing person and teacher. Love her and honestly love 410, it's not that bad if you put in work!

Econ 410 is a very difficult class but MSA gives you plenty of resources to be successful if you put the work in. I really wound up enjoying the class as time went on and would 100% recommend taking 410 with her.

MSA is the best choice for 410. Definitely the hardest class I've taken at UNC, but if you put in the work you can do decently. I wasn't the best at math but there's SO many resources (aid center, help sessions) you can use. Only thing is that they're usually really crowded during midterms szn. The exams are super hard tho but grading is fair.
Super super dense class but do the practice problems a TON and it'll help. Shes very nice and caring but this class is tough. Watch lectures again if confused about conceptual stuff.
A very hard course. She gives you everything you need to succeed but do not get behind. I would advise doing literally every practice problem she gives to study. Econ is strange...

MSA is a literal goddess. She is engaging and kind and organized. Econ410 is a hard class, but she explains the concepts well and is very generous with partial credit on exams. It is obvious that MSA truly cares about her students. I would give my left kidney and my appendix to have MSA teach me all the Econ courses I need for graduation.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super kind and super helpful. ECON 410 is naturally a tough course, but MSA does everything she can to ensure everyone succeeds. Using your LAs and online resources are key to getting a good grade.

MSA is easily the best choice for ECON 410. A lot of people hate because it's naturally a hard class, but she puts in a lot of effort outside the classroom and provides you with resources to succeed. She also drops one of three midterms and two of nine homeworks. Recitations not mandatory but helpful. Would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: MSA is an absolute gem of UNC! She is accessible outside of class, offers countless resources to succeed, explains things thoroughly, and takes time out of class to address students' (often unnecessary) concerns after exams. 410 is a hard class, but it's totally doable if you do the work. I had a 94 until the final, but it was my fault. Take MSA!

This is a difficult class, but MSA provides soo many resources to help you learn the material and prepare for exams. She also drops the lowest midterm and 2 lowest homework grades. The lectures were mainly practice problems but she explained them very in-depth which was very helpful, and she also answered every question people asked in class.

Her lectures are engaging and she provides resources. Thats where the positives end. She cannot be reasoned with when it comes to grading and provides practice questions she says are similar to the exams and then proceeds to make the exams completely different while claiming, "trust me, i'm not trying to trick you." She always has an attitude.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams are fairly difficult, but MSA gives you all the resources to comprehensively prepare for them. Seriously... I've never experienced a more organized professor in my academic career. For every single chapter, MSA provides videos, help sheets, guided worksheets, a powerpoint, and close to 50 practice problems. Also, she drops the lowest midterm!

MSA is a great professor. Her lectures are engaging and funny and she ties in current events. The math wasn't too bad for me, with the hardest being simple partial derivatives (that she teaches if you haven't taken calc 3). She drops the lowest hw or 2 and the lowest midterm. Attending recitations is optional but can help if you need the practice.

MSA is awesome! She really cares about her students and gives you a lot of resources to do well. Beware though, 410 is super hard and you have to dedicate a lot of time to this class to do well. If you can do that, take 410 another semester because you can't do well by cramming.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course material is difficult, but MSA provides so many resources and practice problems that if you put in the work you'll be fine. Tests are exactly like homeworks and practice problems so once again, just don't put the class off and do your work and it's not that bad. MSA herself is a gem, so kind and always willing to help out.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I wouldn't hesitate to give MSA a 5 if it weren't for the tight time constraints on midterms. The exams were long and the 50 min time limit resulted in people rushing over things and making small mistakes; I made mostly average scores on the midterms but killed the final since there was significantly more time. Otherwise, she's a fantastic teacher

The class is difficult just because of the amount of content. MSA prepares you extremely well for every exam, giving you more than enough resources to get an A on every assessment. From practice problems to office hours & Piazza, any question you have will be answered within 24 hours. Amazing professor despite having to teach such difficult content

This professor the GOAT. Her resources are abundant and clearly organized on her sakai site. The class contains difficult material but she does give so many ways to learn it that you will do well if you put in effort.

MSA is an amazing professor! I 100% recommend her to anyone taking ECON 410 or an econ class! She really cares about her students and was really accommodating to all of us so we could succeed in the class. She also provided lots of resources and practice problems that were very helpful for exam studying!

MSA is the best teacher I have had at UNC by far. She is very clear about what is on exams & what you need to know. exams are fair & similar to homework in content and difficulty. provides so many helpful resources and office hours. You can really tell she cares about her students and their learning, she is passionate about teaching and it shows.

MSA truly is an amazing teacher and cares about her students. The students who criticize her often don't put in the time outside of class to understand the subject matter themselves. ECON 410 is a hard class, but she is constantly available for questions and help, as are the ULAs. Best professor I've had at UNC--take MSA for any Econ class you can!

MSA is great with lectures and answering questions in class. She really wants us to do well and provides countless resources for reviews and practice problems for the exams. The class is not easy and does take a lot of studying, but if you stay on top of your work, you can be successful.

People who criticize MSA are often at fault themselves. Her lectures are clear, and she provides the most resources to help out of any professor I've had. The material is very straightforward and just takes practice. If you have good math skills and understand the content, the tests are definitely doable, and the questions are very fair.
Very challenging course but she did her absolute best in making everything easier.

This class is extremely difficult if you do not have a very solid calculus background. It is extremely easy to get lost in this class if you do not ask for help early. MSA is very very organized and tries her best to help students out. However, this is one of the hardest classes I've taken at UNC. She is a gem, the class is hell.
I LOVED MSA!! She was incredibly fair. If you do the work consistently and ask for help (especially at ECON Aid Center), you will do well.

Econ 410 was the hardest class I've ever taken. That said, if you must take it, do it with MSA. The material, tests, and homework are incredibly difficult. Personally, I worked hard but it was hard for me to connect topics critically, other students did well though. MSA did everything she could to help us despite that, she's brilliant and caring.

Econ 410 is a difficult class no question, but MSA does her best to help you succeed. If you do the practice problems and take the homework seriously, getting an A is manageable. She is very kind and caring and will work with you to help you understand the material and your mistakes.

LOVE MSA! After doing well in 410, took her Seminar class for ULAs. This is where you see her learning method and pedagogy SHINE. Her methods to make us better teachers combined with AWESOME TA MEGAN and good "psychology"-like readings so that we can all be better ULAS to assist in ECON, in addition to LEARNING HOW TO LEARN and be better students.

It's not an easy class because of the course content but she is an amazing professor. Pay attention in class and do all the practice problems and it is manageable to get an A, but you will have to work for it.

MSA is an absolute gem, she's a super dedicated professor. The class is more on the difficult side in terms of the material, but if you take the time to understand the material, the class isn't too bad. I would recommend taking the class with people you know and staying on top of the material. If you fall behind, it is really difficult to catch up.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: MSA is amazing, extremely accommodating by allowing notecards during the exam to transition into in-person testing and reweighting midterms. She provides all of the resources you need to succeed, do the practice problems, homework to prepare for the exams. It does require lots of calculus, partial derivatives. She also provided zooms as an option.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: MSA is a nice person and is also a great instructor. She was very considerate towards her students during tough times. The only criticism I have of her is that she could've provided more practice resources for her exams, which were difficult and a big part of your grade.

ECON410 is a very difficult class, and that is because the material is very dense. Her homework assignments really do make you think, but they help on the exams. Exams are definitely not easy and you need good prior math skills like derivatives to succeed. She is a nice professor but with a big classroom of 500 kids, most due dates are firm.

Lectures weren't boring & she was always in a great mood. Once you learn how to study for this class it gets easy. Only downside is that she is very against giving extra credit. Rewatch lesson videos before exams and do all practice problems! Practice problems are very similar to the exams.

MSA is awesome, she does everything in her power to help you succeed, and she is great at explaining everything. If you come in with knowing how to take a partial derivative and are good at math, this class is pretty easy (and super fun if you love derivatives). The ULA office hours are super helpful as well.

I wish I could've given her a 0/5. Flipped classroom & in-class examples were extremely easier than the homework&exams. no longer offering an index card so the exams will become extremely harder. When the tragedies occurred on campus she failed to accommodate the students who felt they needed to go home and refused to make it online.

During an incredibly difficult semester for UNC students, it was nice to know that we had a professor who cared for us in MSA. Many professors of large classes in popular majors can be cold towards their students, but this was not the case. MSA would stop lectures to make jokes when students seemed down, and she was always willing to help.

MSA is an amazing teacher and truly cares about her students. I found this class to be much easier than 101. When studying for tests, do the practice problems & HW's as many times as it takes to understand the material (going back over videos didn't help me). I did average on the first two midterms but when I realized how to study, killed the class

MSA made me want to switch to an economics major after taking her course just from her kindness and obvious love she has for teaching and economics. Initially, the class will be very overwhelming (math prerequisite knowledge, long syllabus, 12-16 hours of recommended studying/week). Once you settle in, though, it is very doable. Amazing professor!

This class is VERY hard (especially if you're not strong in math/calc). I have never worked harder in a class, yet done so poorly. MSA's exams are so challenging I had to plan a backup major at one point. On a positive note, even though she had 500 students, she met with me 1:1 after doing poorly on a test to help me review study strategies.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: MSA could be a case study in why bad RMP reviews should be taken with a grain of salt... Econ 410 IS an extremely difficult course, with frustrating content and tests. However, MSA gives her students every opportunity to succeed. I got off to a rough start but recovered well thanks to MSA's help and grading policies. Honestly learned a lot.

MSA is truly a gem, but the exams are considerably more difficult than you would think. The only issue is that there is not a lot of time to really process a question on the exam since its only 50 minutes, but she is really generous on giving bonus points on the exams and is truly an amazing lecturer.

I'm very confused why people say she's a good professor. Absolute worst I've ever had. On day 1, she said "You will never apply anything from this class to the real world." The structure of the course makes it nearly impossible to do well. She's also not accommodating. I had to study for 3-4 hours a day for 14 days to do well on the final.
An extremely difficult class. Would not recommend. The other prof had open note/take home exams.

ECON 410 is definitely a hard class but MSA is the best there is. You definitely need to put the work in to do well but she really cares about all her students and there are so many resources to help you understand the material. If you have to take 410 100% take it with MSA

From my experience, MSA makes this class more challenging than it needs to be. The material is arranged in an intentionally confusing manner. Rather than presenting steps to solve the toughest problems, it is on the student and whatever groups they work with to figure them out.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: MSA is a lovely professor and person. I have had the privilege of developing a relationship with her in 410 and outside of lectures. She loves teaching micro, and she is extremely open to helping students. She gives you all the resources you need, and overall, she is wonderful to talk to about econ and life outside class.

MSA is the best! We watch videos before class that are short and very clear. Then in class we mostly do practice problems. MSA does a really good job of building content so learning comes easily. The Sakai page and Syllabus are really clear. The tests are hard but you are given a lot of study resources so you are well prepared.

MSA has an incredibly structured, organized course. She is so knowledgeable about micro and has taught this class forever. Be prepared to do a lot of calc! There are so many resources if you need help however. You'll never run out of practice problems and there are so many people that can answer any questions you have. She's great at what she does.
This was a teaching course. The professor is an inspiration, I'd take any course she teaches.

I am currently taking Econ 410 with MSA, and honestly the best teacher I have had in a WHILE. The class itself can be very complex but I promise if you ask questions you will understand and pass the class. MSA as a professor rejuvenated my love for Econ and is probably one of the best professors at Chapel, she is very sympathetic and caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: MSA is one of the best professors I've had at Carolina. The material is difficult and does take a good amount of effort to learn; however, MSA does a great job teaching in a way that makes the content easier to understand. Additionally, she is always willing to stay after class and answer questions. Highly Recommended for ECON 410.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: MSA is amazing! Great choice for ECON410. Midterms will be graded leniently/harshly depending on TA but you can submit regrade requests. 3 midterms but she drops the lowest 1. Midterms are only difficult due to the time limit. Overall, a good class.

This rating is more of a reflection on 410 than MSA. I thought she was a pretty good professor and I'm pretty sure there aren't any better options. There are a few assignments each week but midterms and the final determine 80% of your grade. ECON 410 is the hardest business pre-requisite, don't let anyone say different. Your TA matters a lot.

She is super nice, makes the material as simple as possible (it's def not an easy A), and overall great prof. However, midterms and finals are graded harshly. It is kind of necessary to really understand every aspect of the material to make a decent grade. Also I didn't use the textbook at all so make sure you need it before you buy.

MSA was THE BEST professor I had as a 1st year! MUST TAKE! She is so sweet & kind, willing to understand as us students via "brags and drags" and plenty of office hours and resources like help sheets (USE THEM!). Class is not too hard but a GRIND! w/ study buddies with a small group to get the A! Content is great/interesting! 100% REC & RESPECTED!

TAKE MSA FOR 410! Like any higher level ECON class, this isn't going to be an easy A, but MSA cares about her students and will do everything she can to help you succeed. Listens to feedback and adjusts exams accordingly. Mandatory attendance, but you want to be in class anyway since some exam Q's are taken from lectures. Definitely read the book!

WHAT AN AMAZING PROFESSOR!!!!!! I have soo much respect for her! She works over time to make sure students understand the material. The class is not that difficult. The material is very doable and MSA does a great job taking complicated topics and really simplifying them. Its not that bad!!! Arguably the best Professor I ever had PERIODT.
So difficult, shes a very good professor, but I feel really stupid in the class. Ive got a 3.7 GPA, and this was the first class ive felt like a complete idiot in.

Im a first-year, and if every professor I have for the rest of my time here was like her, I would be living in a dream. I never really paid too much attention in lectures, but most of the time you spend actually learning the material is before/after class time. 410 is not easy course material, but MSA does a great job. Would recommend.
A kind person and great at teaching. My only concern is with the tests she gives. Not nearly enough time to complete them in their entirety and extremely difficult.

MSA is easily one of the best professors I have had at UNC. The material that ECON 410 consists of can sometimes be challenging, but MSA works overtime to ensure that she makes it as easy to understand as possible. She supplies an amazing amount of material to ensure you grasp the class concepts and cares very much about her students' well-being.

Dr. Sheran-Andrews is very kind, funny, and down-to-earth. Her class, while interesting, is difficult due to the heavy-weighted tests that aren't easy. However, overall, these tests are based heavily on the homework, classwork, and class problem sets also assigned. Participation is for a grade. Overall, she definitely cares about your learning.

MSA is an amazing teacher especially for econ410. She goes beyond her limits to accommodate every student. Her lectures are interesting and she solves all your doubts in the class. There are 3 midterms (she chooses best 2) and a final. Recitation and participation also count towards your final grade. Highly recommend yall to take MSA.

Really sweet and funny. 3 midterms but u can drop 1. Grind before the exams and you'll be fine. Exams are very similar to problem sets and practice problems so do those over and over again. Polls during class for attendance. Calculus is all partial derivatives so not too complex. A lot of simplifying. Lowkey easier than ECON101.

Undeniably the best professor I've had at UNC. If you enjoyed 410 and think highly of MSA this is a must-take. She teaches it each fall and the material is far easier than 410 and is applicable to real life. Simply fascinating if you love econ. Best professor in the UNC system in my mind.

ECON410 is hard but Dr. MSA made it enjoyable even online. She's nice, helpful, funny, and is willing to help us to understand difficult concepts during class and office hours. Her class is flipped but she always explains topics we learned from pre-class videos in class to ensure we fully understood it before moving on. She's always happy to help!

MSA is a fantastic professor. I had heard that ECON 410 was an awful course but she delivered it in a way that made the class a breeze. I found it really easy to ask her questions both in class and her lecture videos were concise and helpful. There is a fair bit of math-intensive work in the class but it really prepares you for the exams

I took her for 410 and liked her enough to take 415 with her. I would say it's about as challenging as 410, but if I had to pick, I'd say 415 is a little bit easier. MSA is probably my favorite professor at UNC, but certainly my favorite in the Econ department. If 410 wasn't too bad for you, I'd recommend taking 415 with her. It's less math-heavy.

MSA is a great lecturer and communicator. However, the material of this course is naturally hard to begin with, and I don't think the structure of this class made it any simpler to comprehend. With that said, she's very likeable and accessible, and will do her best to answer any questions you may have. I'd recommend her for 410, but get ready.

I spent 6-7 hours per day working on this class during summer because of how much work it was, but having MSA definitely eased the pain. She was always accessible via email and held office hours every day, which were basically small group Q&A sessions and they helped a ton. She puts up a ton of resources and keys and adapted to online really well.

MSA was the best ECON professor I have had at UNC. She is not only a great person but an even better teacher. The class is hard, but she gives you so many resources and so much attention that the class is manageable and it is completely possible to get an A. MSA is the only professor anyone should take 410 with. She is the absolute best!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: An amazing professor that clearly cares about her students. If you've done well in Math/Chem/Comp classes, then 410 is actually really easy in comparison. However, anyone can do well if they put the appropriate level of effort forward. Even if you're not a STEM person, just pay attention to MSA's awesome teaching and you will be more than fine!

It may seem daunting but she is truly an amazing professor and don't you dare take this with anyone else. She KNOWS HER STUFF and is very accommodating. Study a lot for the tests, but it's not impossible. It's very repetitive material as well so once you learn the first unit, that's the main hurdle, it's smooth sailing really. LOVE HER.

Econ 410 is not an easy class, but can be made so much easier because of how good of a teacher MSA is and more importantly, how many resources she gives to you. If you just study the practice problems and homeworks before her tests, they are very fair and you'll do very well.

MSA is truly the best professor that I've had in my time at UNC. Econ 410 is a difficult class, but if you put in the time it takes to learn the material then you can do very well in this class. Be sure to go to office hours/EconAid center in the days before homework is due though! (tests come from hw problems!)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: MSA was a great professor and is extremely clear in her teaching of Econ410. Go to class, utilize the Econ Aid center, and study the practice problems and you can get an A in this class. Econ 410 is a class that is not necessarily hard but can be very confusing, and MSA will guide you through this confusion if you put in the time. Great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I was nervous about taking econ410, but MSA proved me wrong. This was overall my easiest A so far, and she structures the class so it is like that. I barely went to class, but used resources she provided to learn and study and they proved effective. The exams are essentially the HW questions, just slightly different. It is clear what to expect.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: What you see is what you get. You do the work you get the grade. Exams are difficult but fair. If you study the material you will do well, and MSA will certainly help you if you need it.

MSA is very straightforward in the things you need to do well in her class. There are no secrets. You WILL have to grind for exams to do well in them, and go through all the practice problems and the homework questions to give yourself a solid chance. Her teaching is flawless and she is the best professor I have had at Carolina. It's 100% up to you
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I'll give her 5 stars because shes a good professor, but I do not like her. She is very strict. Anyway, for spring 2020, 43% of the class made an A.

MSA is absolutely phenomenal and one of the best professors at UNC. She's so kind and caring and always willing to work with you as long as you put in the effort. Make sure you understand the homework problems and do the practice problems and you're golden for all of her exams. They're pretty straightforward once you understand the formulas.

MSA is an OUTSTANDING professor! Needless to say this class was very difficult and thankfully I was able to take it pass/fail and still receive credit. I would recommend MSA as your professor if you're needing to take Econ 410. Just be prepared to work!

So far, MSA is my favorite professor. Econ 410 is given a really bad reputation by advisors. Good news, they are wrong. Her grading is clear, she is very helpful, and gives the all the tips she can think of so you can get an A. If you listen to half of them, and do the work, you will do great.
Abandon All Hope, Ye Who Enter Here
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: MSA is a great communicator who comes across as very caring. However, the homework and tests can be especially tricky. Make sure you really understand the first few units WELL, because its extremely difficult to get caught back up later on. I barely scraped by in this class because I didnt work hard enough at the beginning, so stay on top of it.

MSA is the best teacher I've had so far at UNC. If you're confused about anything in the course, definitely go to office hours. Get started on homework and study for tests as early as possible. If you understand the homeworks and practice problems, you should be fine on the tests. She is a very fair teacher and doesn't try to trick students.

Very nice teacher and wants you to do good. You must be willing to work really hard to succeed in this class or you just will not pass. The resources are there to help you succeed. I would not recommend getting the book for the class. Graded off few things as well, 10 Homeworks and 4 tests. Also, recitation is not required which is the best part.

ECON410 is possibly one of the worst classes at UNC, but MSA makes it bearable. Her lectures are all great and the tests are fair as long as you do the homework. I would recommend that you print out the lecture notes online to follow along with in class. MSA has a radiant personality and loves her students/the class. Great ECON professor to have.

MSA is a sweet person and great lecturer, literally the best economics teacher I've had. She provides a lot of resources to her students which makes the fairly difficult content digestible. Attend class, do the practice problems, look at the help sheets, and go to the ECON Aid Center if you need help and you'll probably do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you want a good grade in this class, be sure to put in the work needed! MSA is a wonderful professor and her lectures are clear and concise. Her exams are fair as well, final is simple if you know your material. Just do the homeworks and you will be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: MSA is easily the best professor I have ever had during my time at Carolina. If you get the chance to take 415 with her, you won't regret it. Taking a small class with her has been amazing, she really makes an effort to get to know you individually. The class itself was difficult but she really wants all her students to succeed!
Best Econ professor ever. She clearly knows what she is talking about, she knows how to let students understand her. I am planning to take every class she teaches.

MSA is awesome. She truly wants her students to succeed and gives them the resources to do so. The class is difficult at times, but if you attend lectures and put in the hours for all problem sets and other practice you should be find. Use the ECON AID CENTER! Take advantage of the resources available to you, and it will certainly help you.

I loved MSA! She is one of the best professors at UNC. She knows the material and does a good job at explaining it. I don't think the material is difficult, but I thought the midterms were a bit tough because of time. Final is easier because you have 3 hours. If I prepared more ahead of time, I would've gotten an A in the course. MSA is the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Overall, this class was difficult but not impossible. I'm no math genius but I was able to understand most of the content if I studied well. My advice would be to do problem sets as soon as you can instead of waiting. Also, I thought there was not enough time for the midterms. I did better on the final than any of them because I had more time.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: MSA gives you all the tools to succeed along with clear grading expectations. However, when you take this course, know yourself. If you are good at calc and can easily understand economic concepts, you will excel. If you struggle with derivatives, good study habits, etc..., this class will be hard, and you will have to put in extra work.

MSA is the best. Homework is easy to do with the help sheets. Midterms are exactly as the homework, just beware of the time constraint. I would take another class with her without a doubt just to be her student again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I love love love MSA! We often joke that she is too nice to be an ECON prof at UNC. The material is challenging, but MSA made it so easy and understandable. Before the tests, do the homework and practice problems again, and you should be fine!

Despite receiving a poor grade in the course, I recognize that MSA is an excellent lecturer and empathetic person. Kindhearted, helpful, and knowledgeable on the course material, Professor Sheran-Andrews does an excellent job of teaching microeconomic theory
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I think MSA is a bit overrated. Her lectures are okay, but not amazing or particularly engaging. Main issue is the exams are so short. A plus is that the exams are in the exact format of the homeworks, but a bit easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ECON410 is not easy. You have to work hard to get good grades. It is possible and with her help it's more than doable. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. She is so helpful and will work through any problem you don't understand. She remembers your name and believe me the difference between my first midterm and the midterm after I talked to her was significant.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: MSA is the best! She is super kind to her students, and her lectures are clear, engaging, and insightful. She is really good at breaking things down and allowing students to understand real-world applications. Office hours are also really helpful! Just an incredible person and professor.

MSA is one of the best professors at UNC. You'll definitely need to do the hw and keep up with the material to do well in the class, but it's not impossible. Midterms aren't difficult but they are short so each question is worth a lot of points. Utilize the help sheets, extra practice problems, and office hours. Study for final well in advance.
she is absolutely fabulous. tests are incredibly hard though so beware. as long as you study hard and try your best you should be fine.

MSA is probably the single best professor I've ever had. She explained concepts super well and provided us with practice problems and 'help sheets' that were extremely useful. The exams were the same difficulty, maybe even a little easier, than the homeworks. It's very possible to succeed if you put effort in, and you'll learn a ton!

he key to a good grade in this class - do the practice problems and do the homeworks over again to prep for the test. On top of being a phenomenal teacher, she gives you the resources you need to succeed. If you keep up with the workload throughout the semester, there's no reason you shouldn't make an A. Better than Econ 101 by a longshot.

I didn't think the material was fundamentally challenging, there's just a lot of it to keep up with. Tests and homework seemed like they were designed to trick you on certain questions, but overall this is a very doable/fair class. Just read her online materials religiously and you'll be fine. No need for the textbook

Don't buy the textbook - never opened it once. Midterms are exactly like homework and homework practice problems. Study those problems and hw until you understand everything and you will do fine on the midterms. Final is cumulative multiple choice. The difficulty is in how much material is covered and keeping up with all of it. MSA is kind though.

MSA gives you everything you need to succeed in her class, it's just a matter of you using those resources. No need for the textbook, do the practice problems in advance so you have time to ask questions in office hours &look at help sheets! She is a great professor that truly cares for you to do well and wants to know how she can improve as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Andrews put together the best organized class I've ever taken. She posts an abundance of resources online that are essential to doing well in the class, and reading the textbook is helpful for consolidating understanding of material. If you work hard and are diligent, you will do well.

Not the best teacher for getting some subjects across, but will answer any questions she is asked so blame that on the students who obviously arent ready for the class. Huge class sizes and fast paced. Very fair and open to communication though. She tries hard and I loved her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Sheran-Andrews is very fair and straight-forward with her grading criteria but I didn't like her teaching style. She's very heavy on memorization (though she constantly claims otherwise) and often covers concepts in a convoluted way. Class is somewhat easy if you have a good grip on basic economic principles and calculus but very hard if not.

Sheran-Andrews started the semester off with a great start by showing all the resources available and laid the class out really well. However, as the semester continues, the class slowly gets more confusing in terms of what the reacher expects from you on tests. Take advantage of office hours and keep up with the material in order to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: MSA really cares about her students and tries to make the class as understandable as possible. Do all of the practice problems, and skip on the textbook!

MSA has been the best teacher that I have had since I began my education at UNC. She is by no means an easy teacher, but she provides you with all the material necessary for you to succeed in her class. You get out of this class what you put into it. She is always available for office hours and super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: 410 is notoriously tough. No getting around it. But MSA is the best possible prof for it. TONS of extra material: practice Qs, outlines, study guides, (actually good) PP's, exam-relevant HW . PLUS: recitations, 3x/week help sessions, genius-level office hrs. MSA takes pedagogy seriously. Use her resources or don't whine about the class!

Such a rough class but MSA is a really good professor. Meet with her out of class - shes nice and she seems to care about her students. Shes SUPER fair (but also SUPER tough). I would definitely agree that this is very math based. She does a great job of answering questions and using lecture time to do questions. Interesting class too but TOUGH!
Class is extremely hard. does not spend enough time going over who to do problems in class. be prepared to each yourself all the material

This class is perhaps the only fair class I've ever taken. She's clear with everything she does, and her lectures explain things extremely well to her students. She'll try to explain things in different ways if you don't understand. Her tests are exactly the same style as her homework, so if you practice homework problems you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Michelle-Sheran Andrews really cares about her students and is so kind at office hours. Her class is obviously inherently hard, however she goes out of her way to provide extra resources and help for her students. Doing homeworks over and over and over again is the only way to continually nail down the material and hopefully recognize patterns.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: MSA knows her stuff and is a good communicator. However, where she falls short is the fact that you could rewrite Dante's Inferno with her playing the role of Lucifer and the story wouldn't change. Her tests are made to trick you (yet aren't too difficult) and she is mostly mean-spirited. She gets a 5 for being good, but that doesnt mean I like her
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I love MSA- By far the best professor I've had at UNC! This class is definitely tough, but she does a great job of explaining things in lecture, providing supplemental resources and practice problems, and being accessible outside of class. If you have a solid foundation in math, engage in class, and do the assignments you can do well in this class.
I really liked MSA and I dont think this class was too hard. It's easy to mess up on tests though, and look out because some people really struggle. I messed up on the final so study a bunch for that

MSA is the best professor I've had at UNC. She is so nice and such a great instructor. Bottom line-- this is a math class. If you're good at math, you'll be just fine. If not, you're going to need to put in lots of time studying. Test problems very similar to weekly HW assignments. Graded polls in class, and optional TA recitations.

Econ 410 is a hard class, with that being said, Dr. Sheran-Andrews does an amazing job at teaching this course. She's very accessible outside of class and her office hours/15 minute appointments are extremely helpful. The textbook (WHICH YOU CAN FIND ONLINE) was not that great, I would focus on HW and Besanko problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Sheran-Andrews is a solid choice for Econ 410. This class is really difficult. So far the worst grade I've got in college, but Sheran-Andrews does a decent job of getting the material across. I wouldn't recommend copying too many of the homework assignments, there's about one a week. They'll help on the 2 midterms and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Extremely difficult class. I don't blame the prof as much as the course itself. The exam averages are in the mid 70's and you'll definitely have to put in a lot of time to study. Exams are most of your grade and HW/polls make up almost none of it. It isn't enough to know the material, you have to be able to solve questions quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Sheran-Andrews is a great professor who really cares about the subject and takes time to make sure everyone in the class understands the material. All though the class is difficult, put in the work for the homework and go to the help sessions and you will do well! I would definitely recommend this class!!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Homeworks and tests are difficult so study groups will be your bestfriends. Super math oriented so if calc is your thing you probably won't have a tough time. Lot's of material, but an A is very attainable if you work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: It shows when professors are really focused on teaching & not just their own research, and MSA is the perfect example. Everything she does is so carefully thought through to keep students accountable while also encouraging maximum learning. If you take advantage of the resources she provides, you will do well AND you'll learn a lot about micro!

MSA is an awesome professor and actually cares about her students. If you go to her office hours she will get to know you and start engaging with you one-on-one despite the enormous size of the class. Econ 410 is tough and there's no way around it, but if you put in the time it's definitely manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: She is LITERALLY the most awesome professor I have ever met. Super passionate about economics, very easily approachable even though it's a huge class. Very well organized courses, even though the class is slightly hard and you will have to work for it. I definitely think this was my favorite class at Carolina.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: MSA is a great professor, but class will make you work. Some tips: 1) Come to class- good way to learn concepts/poll everywhere questions in class count for grades. 2) Do hw diligently- actually learn concepts, not just answers. 3) Learn to do basic calculus quickly. 4) Prepare for exams by redoing hw problems over and over. 5) Go to help sessions
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was the bane of my existence while in it, and if economic theory doesn't come easily to you, or you got below a B in 101, my best advice is take with friends and ride the struggle bus together, and don't take a chance on any other class known to be time consuming like BUSI 101 or you'll hate every Sunday and Monday of that semester
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class has three parts: Consumer Theory, Firm Theory, and Market Organization.  She is amazing at teaching consumer but speeds through firm, so it can be confusing.  Overall, her lectures are clear and spell out what you need to know for the exams (so don't skip).  Weekly homework (six total); they help prepare you for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tough class, no way around it. Put in the time and you'll be ok. 6 homeworks, 1 will be dropped. 2 midterms and a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof. Sheran-Andrews was very good. She is clearly passionate about the material and gives good lectures. The midterms are pretty difficult, especially due to time, so it is important to know the material inside and out. The best way to do this is to work the homework problems (from current and previous semesters) ad nauseum. Final was much easier.

Michelle Sheran-Andrews really cares about her students. When she gets feedback, she really takes it into consideration and she really wants her students to do well. The material is tough but if you do the Besanko problems and the homework problems as practice then the tests won't trip you up.

Great teacher and definitely passionate about economics. Class is pretty challenging and so consistently practicing the material, going to office hours, and seeking out help when needed is the way to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great Professor. Helps you understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great Professor. Does a good job explaining material that can get very confusing very fast. Pay attention in class and make sure you understand things conceptually, not just on the surface. The tests are pretty short so each problem ways a lot which was kind of intimidating.
Nice person, not the best teacher

MSA is by far my favorite professor this semester. Her lectures are extremely engaging and she very clearly shows that she wants us to learn the material. The homework/midterms are tough because of the format (10 MC + long form), but I feel that I have learned a lot from her class, beyond just memorization and regurgitation, but actual application.

Dr. Sheran-Andrews is extremely organized and passionate about Economics. She makes the class more difficult than it needs to be (the homeworks) but rewards you later with relatively easy tests and midterms. The recitations are optional and helpful about 50% of the time. The Besanko problems are very helpful for the homeworks and the tests.

Excellent teacher. Knows her stuff and cares about it, along with her students.  But beware: if econ does not come naturally to you, you will have to work. A lot. Multiple choice questions are hard and account for half of each test (missing two brings you down a full letter grade). But overall she's an effective teacher despite harsh grading.

This is one of my favorite classes I've taken because the professor is great at teaching. Every word she says is important, so pay attention in class. She's strict and intimidating, but gives you the tools to be successful. She is very knowledgable and is great at breaking down concepts. The exams and homework are tough, but I've learned so much!

Dr. Sheran-Andrews is one of the best professors I've ever had.  She makes what could be dry material interesting and is always willing to explain a concept further if it doesn't make sense. Lectures are interesting and crystal clear. Tests are tough but not impossible.  She's also really funny! Take her class and you won't regret it!

Econ 410 with Sheran-Andrews was okay. She's decent at explaining material and her exams aren't impossible, but I wouldn't take a class with her again. Her office hours are very unhelpful and she doesn't provide much individual feedback. I wouldn't recommend her, but it's not the end of the world if you end up in her class.

Hardest class I've ever taken so far. She is a very effective teacher, but her tests are very challenging. Tests are very tricky and sometimes ridiculous. They are way harder than the homework. Avoid this teacher if you do not enjoy math.

Dr. Andrews is a clear, engaging, and fun lecturer. She broke down tough material into digestible bits  and did a great job of relating it all to the everyday world. I have no doubt she will be a favorite prof here for years. Tough class (it's econ): 3 midterms and a final. She really wants to see her students succeed and is always there to help.
Exams are tough, but the overall class grade is determined by a lot of different things.  RA projects help to boost the grade as long as you put effort into them. Textbook reading is long
Great guy, great professor, and so interesting.
This dude is amazing. Fantastic professor. Ethnography can be a bit time consuming.

This was one of my most favorite classes I've taken at UNC. While you do have to put work in in reading, getting to know your character, and writing and memorizing speeches, this class truly helps you become a better public speaker. There is no judgement and the more you engage with the material and design of the class, the more fun it is.

Professor Caren is an amazing professor with such a welcoming personality. I took this course to fulfill my minor, and it was a great class with wonderful people in it as well. We have speeches to give, but the process leading up to the speeches is structured so well that you truly shouldn't feel scared. Take his class, you'll love it!

He is so funny and I would retake his class. Although my friends who had other professors for Soci 101 said their exams were easy, which is the downside to taking his, I found his exams to be challenging after spending days studying to prepare. However, if you follow the criteria for the homework, you get a 100, so it's a pretty easy course.
One of the best professors at UNC. Take Soci 101 with Professor Caren, you won't regret it.
Great guy -- gave everyone a free 100% on a midterm!

This is the goat of Sociology 101. We all got 100s on our last mideterm since more than 60% of the class didn't take it(He stated if more than 60% of students get a question wrong it will be given full points). Not much work other than Research Apllications and Inquizzitives. Pollev is used for attendance. Overall show up and it's an easy A.

Neal Caren is THE SWEETEST prof you will ever take at UNC. Everyday, he arrives so excited to teach and engage with students. He is extremely knowledgeable and makes his course engaging with online polls and halftime quiz games (i got to play soci family feud on LDOC). Easy homework, bi weekly assignments, 1 midterm exam, 1 final exam.

Wow. One of the funniest and nicest professors of all time. Tons of easy extra credit. The only downside is having to write about 3600 words of "research applications" throughout the semester. But even as someone who hates writing, take this class.The exams are easy and he made a custom quiz website so you can study for the exams in no time at all.

I love Prof. Caren.  His lectures are sometimes boring but more often than not fun.  The assignments are very easy, and you don't have to read the textbook.  There are 2 midterms and a final but he'll replace your midterm with the final if you do better.  I would highly recommend him to everyone!
The BEST professor. He's amazing, I love his class.
G.O.A.T Professor. Definitely for the memory books!

Just dont consider any other options, he is GOAT!!! His assignments and class both are fun. For someone who really struggles to go to class I have been going every class!! I just love being in this class
About as easy as a gen ed you can take. Exams can be aced simply by spending 30min on the cover quilt. The textbook very clearly tries to influence you to think like a Marxist though

This guy goes out of his way to make studying for exams as easy as possible and hands out extra credit. Really a nice and hardworking professor. The research applications (8 per class, lowest score dropped) are kind of a lot of work but not difficult or heavily graded.
Such an easy class and I learned so much. He was super interesting in lectures, would recommend to anyone. Tests weren't very hard either.

This is by far the BEST class I've ever taken. It was so interactive and engaging and everyone in my class got so close. I never missed this class because it was that fun to go to. Prof. Caren is hilarious and super chill. If you try a little bit you'll get an A. There is a public speaking component but Caren creates a really safe environment.

Dr. Caren was fine. He was funny and witty. This class, for me, was kinda difficult. The papers were easy, but its veryyy participation heavy. I'm sure it was easier for people more extroverted and social, but for introverts, I think it can be anxiety inducing and exhausting. Just understand what you are signing up for; its almost an acting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: SOCI 274 is the best class I have ever taken!!! The way the course is designed is very interactive and really really fun. Dr. Caren is interesting, knowledgeable, easy to talk to, and very reasonable. There can feel like a lot of reading at times, but honestly if you're engaged in the class you'll do great.
Highly recommend. Class was chill.

Caren is hilarious! I loved coming to class everyday and reading the textbook for his class. The material was so interesting, and we watched movies pretty often in class. Great professor, I already signed up for his other class because I loved him so much. He curves every test and will drop lots of things at the end of class, hard to not get an A

Professor Caren is great! You have to do a little bit of work for this course, but it isn't terrible. For exams, make a Quizlet with the terms and do the practice exams, and you will do fine. Honestly just try your best in the course and do the extra credit, and you can get an A easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was very easy yet very interesting! If you are looking for an easy elective, I definitely recommend this class. As long as you take the practice exams, study keywords, and memorize the vocabulary, you will do well in this class. The documentaries that were sprinkled throughout the semester were also a nice break from lectures.

Lectures were pretty boring and they didn't really connect that well with textbook readings or exam material. I never paid attention during lecture, didn't do a single textbook reading, and my exam average was a 96. This is SOCI101 so it isn't hard, but if you want to actually learn the material, maybe take a different professor.

Profesor Caren loves what he teaches and it shows in his lectures. He makes class engaging especially when we watch movies and genuinely wants his students to succeed. At first, the class may seem like it has lots of work but it is very spaced out and doesn't take long to complete the assignments. I would totally recommend taking a class with him.

Gonna keep this short and simple. Prof Caren is the best teacher possible for SOCI101 and if he teaches it, take him. Projects are basically graded for completion and exams are pretty straightforward and if they weren't he gives us points back. Barely studied and got near-100.

Prof. Caren is great. Lectures were sometimes boring but he tried to make them fun and interactive. He gives tons of opportunities to get a good grade and all assignments were pretty easy. Short quizzes & papers. He posts possible midterm/final questions and gives plenty of study resources. Would highly recommend this course for an easy credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The coursework (textbook quizzes and research applications) set you up really nicely for the tests. He drops at least one assignment from each category and gave back points on each exam so your grade will be really boosted by the end of the semester. Utilizes PollEverywhere throughout the lecture for attendance credit.

Professor Caren is super nice and easy to talk to when you have issues. The homework and projects are super easy and interesting you just have to make sure to plan ahead for them. Participation is very important in this class because it counts for your attendance.
Dr. Caren is a really nice guy, however how he runs this class is a bit boring and he can make some weird comments that could be perceived as hateful towards certain groups of people.

Extremely passive aggressive professor, but overall a very easy class. I took SOCI100 and it was rather interesting, but the way he lectured was terribly boring. On-time submission will typically lead to an 100% on the assignment, except the final and midterm were significantly more difficult. Staying on top of reading the textbook definitely helps

Dr. Caren is great! The exams are the hardest part of the class, so definitely take the practice tests many times. However, there are a lot of other assignments to balance out exam grades. The final exam included questions from the midterms, so definitely go back and review those questions when the final comes along. Very knowledgeable guy.

Lectures are not helpful, just read the books. Hard to get good grades. The class has tons of assignments. However, the exams largely determined the grade (so even if you got 100 on every other assignment you might still mess the grades up) and it test literally everything. Never got exam scores higher than 85 and ends up with an A-.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures and readings for this class can be pretty long. The class consists of applications, case studies, film discussions, inquizitive, midterms, and the final. TA's are great and allow you to resubmit applications if necessary. You need to thoroughly study all of the vocabulary in the textbook. Take practice tests MULTIPLE TIMES.

Grading criteria is super clear. You can get a decent grade without putting in much effort. Lecture can be interesting and Neal is knowledgeable. The exams are likely the worst part of the class but even then, the reviews and Quizlet help with studying. Overall, not a bad course if you're looking for an interesting elective that isn't too rigorous.

Neal Caren, I love you so much. Best professor I've ever had hands down. I took this for PH credit and had so much fun. Truly got to be me in this class and have never had a better time. Neal literally catered IP3 for our final... king. Easy A if you put in a little bit of effort and honestly such a rewarding class... gonna miss this class so much

I was super nervous about Caren's 274 section because the teaching method was so unusual (you have to take on the perspective of historical figures) but I learned so much and this class was something I looked forward to. Dr. Caren is super chill and we had a pizza party during our final if that says anything. Take this class!!!

Dude is hilarious and clearly knows a lot about sociology. Assignments are fairly easy to complete and have very clear grading criteria. Has offered extra credit opportunities throughout the semester as well. Tests are pretty difficult so I recommend actually studying for a couple days in advance. Very helpful and has interesting classes as well.

Prof Caren is funny and his lectures always have something that make me laugh. Multiple extra credit opportunities. Know the key terms/do the practice exams before exams and you should do well. Not a hard class to succeed in if you put in some effort and understand the material, was never stressed about this class.

Super knowledgeable and great at facilitating a hands-off experience where students can truly immerse themselves in the simulation. Will help when you're stuck. A lot of reading is required to truly understand the material, and you have to put in a lot of effort, but it's worth it. Grading not bad. Class is different, but my favorite one I've taken
Assignments have clear grading criteria and are relatively easy although time consuming. Tests are pretty hard, definitely need to put a good amount of time into studying.
pretty easy as long as you do the work and study, many movie days and few papers and case studys but nothing too difficult

I really loved Professor Caren. He was engaging in class and had very clear expectations. His tests are not hard if you take the practice exams he posts a couple of times (there are infinite questions). The applications every week are not hard ... I don't think they are actually graded for content, got 100 on all of them.

Professor Caren is an AMAZING guy. His classes are fun, entertaining and thought provoking. However, the tests are disproportionately hard compared to his lectures, so be prepared to not do well on those versus other assignments. Overall, highly suggest his course.

He's a chill guy and a nice person but there's way too much work he makes you do for a stupid intro to sociology class. Every other teacher gives less work - he's so extra and for no reason. Would have never taken this class if I knew that he made you work like a donkey for even a B.

The lectures and readings for this class are so boring. There isn't enough engagement in class to keep you focused it's just him talking for 1 hour and 15 minutes straight. The applications also take you a long time and the due dates are too short for a project of that manner. Midterms are okay it's just memorizing like 100+ terms.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: SUCH a great professor. Super easy class if you just do the PRACTICE EXAMS MULTIPLE TIMES. Some of the exam answers are on Quizlet if you know where to look; hint use practice exam problems to search. Great and engaging professor. DON'T READ TEXTBOOK. Complete waste of time, j skim for answers and study vocabulary.

Prof Caren is an extremely nice professor. He chooses interesting documentaries to watch and is funny with the lectures. He is well respected by the class and there is no way you can get less than a B in this class unless you genuinely do not do anything. Love him!

Professor Caren is a delightful professor. He's kind, funny, and does his best to keep students engaged during lecture. However, much of what is required to succeed in this course comes from the textbook, not the lectures. As long as you do the required readings, the class shouldn't be too difficult.

Massive lecture, interesting content but midterms are tricky if you don't study the right things. Hard to have a connection with your Professor if you're with 350+ other students. Read the bolded terms in the textbook if you're short on time, do the Inquizitives, and always shoot for a high pass on the projects. Definitely show up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Caren is a super nice guy and quite funny. I didn't enjoy the class though, as it relied heavily on textbook readings. The lectures were a bit useless since most of the material came from the textbook. The projects seemed to be busy-work, as well as most of the other homework.

SOCI 101 was an amazing class to take with neal. as long as you met the requirements for the assignments, did well on the quizzes on sakai, and participated in the discussions; you'll get a good grade. 10/10

This class was interesting and assignments were easy, although some were time-consuming. Class was watching a movie and tying it to course concepts every Thursday (if taken on a Tuesday/Thursday schedule). He makes the material extremely interesting, only downside is that grading depends on which TA you get assigned.

Neal is awesome. Best class I took this semester. His ability to make it interesting with documentaries each week is something I have yet to see in other classes. Is very clear about what to do for each assignment. Super Easy A. Good lecturer too and can be funny. Very easy to get in touch with. I really suggest taking this class!

I loved this class. Very easy A. Consisted of one lecture per week and an interesting documentary each Thursday. Very laid back and easy material. Basically just show up, do the few and easy assignments, and you'll do well. Caren is good at lecturing and seems like a really chill guy. This class fulfills a gen-ed so I 100% recommend.

This class was my favorite this semester! Prof Caren is super accommodating and makes class interesting with a film every week. You get to drop assignments and some are graded P/F so you really never stress about your grade. Tests are easy; some assignments are more time consuming but still not hard. Definitely got me interested in sociology!
worst professor i've had in my entire life. not personable at all and hardly paid attention to his students. took forever to grade anything.

Super easy class. Made one lecture async and we watched a movie for the other every week. Just get all the assignments done and the midterm/final will be a breeze. He's super accommodating and flexible--I took this class during the pandemic. Awesome guy too.

Drops lowest quizzes/assignments in all categories. Very understanding during pandemic. Actually cares that students engage with/learn material. Great online class. Options for students who cannot attend class due to work or other obligations. 11/10. Easy A if you do what is expected most of the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Neal Caren is the best choice for Soci 101. He did an amazing job with online classes and we were connected without too much lecture. We had lots of projects and opportunities to apply sociology in movie discussions and case studies. Super interesting and easy and Prof. Caren is a funny, caring, understanding guy! Great class.

Professor Caren is the most disengaged professor I have ever had. He took forever to grade assignments and did not release many grades until right before finals. He was also not accommodating nor understanding in regard to circumstances surrounding COVID. The class website was unorganized and the communication of his expectations was horrible.

Dr. Caren was extremely accommodating with assignments and work due to COVID. The Tuesday lectures were recorded and usually pretty enjoyable. We also watched a documentary every week which always ended up being pretty good. The homework didn't take too long and the assignments were a pass/fail type.

Kept class interesting during online instruction with having us watch a film on Netflix each week that pertained to that week's concept. Normal amount of assignments and an easy A! Zooms once a week but were optional and were posted online if you wanted to watch later. Has his own website for the course keeping it separate from Sakai which I liked!
