Loved this class. Optional Tuesday lectures that I attended in the beginning and stopped going to at the end but still did well. Netflix Documentaries on Thursdays! Multiple assignments could be dropped, with clear grading. We didn't have to read books like past classes since he switched to docu's. Very easy class.

I absolutely loved taking this class with Professor Caren. The assignments were all self-explanatory and easy to do well on. I also really liked the way the class was structered. We had an optional lecture on Tuesday and watched a film on Thursday. I definitely recommend taking a class with him!!

Dr. Caren was very easily contacted, as well as the TA's. His grading criteria was very clear and the assignments were mostly busy work but were still very interesting. Caren gave the option to skip certain assignments and dropped the lowest two grades for each assignment type. He was very caring and understanding of the stress of this semester!

Literally the easiest into class to exist. Caren was so accommodating for our COVID semester and allowed multiple drops for each type of assignment. Homework can be corrected until you get a 100. Everything else is graded pass/fail. If you put in effort it's easy to make 100's on the assignments. Interesting class with fun films, too!
Took his class for a PH credit and am so happy I did. He handled the COVID 19 shift to online learning so well. He really cares about his students.

Definitely lots of busy work, but overall I found the course interesting enough that it made it bearable. The lectures are generally interesting, I really liked the books we read, and lots of extra credit opportunities. Overall a solid class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Not really sure how I got a B in this class because there are SO many extra credit opportunities. Caren is an awesome professor and I would probably take him again if I get the chance. He is very accessible and willing to help! However, there is a lot of extra/busy work done in this course and some of his lectures can be kind of boring.

Professor Caren was great! The workload could be a lot sometimes but it really furthers your understanding of the topic. Book groups were a thing in this class but I enjoyed the books assigned for the most part. Overall a great class to take!

LOTS of busy work/ reading but as long as you just do it, you'll do great. graded on a lot of different things & he gives curves/drops lowest grades. doesn't take a lot of effort, just a lot of time. Caren is funny & keeps lectures interesting. I only read 1 of the 3 books & still made an A. A lot of the stuff on quizzes/test are common sense
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Caren is a boring lecturer but he's funny and makes the class easy. This class has weekly readings, a couple bigger assignments, a few online quizzes, book clubs and he monitors attendance through the check in app. Overall, it is a super easy class if you do your work and briefly skim the textbook and the three books! There's also extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: no saying his class is hard. its just way too much unnecessary busy work that doesnt rly prepare you for anything. hes funny and interesting but i dont like how some extra credits are given based on huge groups. Also, most of his assignments are graded by his TAs, one of the TA is very nice but the other one isnt that nice. Soooo good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Literally one of the easiest classes I've took so far. Why are the reviews so bad? literally his class is sooooooo easy. Yes, there is a lot of work but the grading is so lenient it's impossible to fail. Out of all the 101 classes I've took so far. This is by FAR the best choice you can ever make. Maybe another teacher is better? but he's chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The workload for this SOCI101 class is actually ridiculous compared to every other 101 course. You will read at least 3 books completely and be expected to have at least 10 pages of notes for each. The quizzes aren't the worst thing but they are definitely not easy; you will need to study a lot. I took this class thinking it would be easy, it's not
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof Caren is really nice, but this class was a little ridiculous. The lectures are useless, there is an exorbitant amount of homework for an introductory class, and attendance is mandatory 100% of the time. The tests are pretty easy, so it isn't hard to do well in the class, but the amount of useless busy work and useless lectures make it a chore.

Homework seems extensive for an introductory course, but is generally an easy grade. Best reading list I've had for a class. As a professor, Caren is fairly inefficient. Being entertaining and empathetic does not make up for a lack of substance in every lecture. A straightforward course with disappointingly little content in the classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Neal Caren is the one of the nicest professors I've had at UNC. He genuinely cares and even though his class has a lot of assignments he makes sure not to heavily weigh your grade on one exam which allows for plenty of forgiveness. As long as you go to class and do the work you will do well.

Neal Caren is the worst Professor that I've had at UNC. His focus seems to be more on brainwashing young adults with an agenda than with teaching and runs much of his class with strict, ridiculous guidelines. Class activities are awful. His "book groups" are bad as well and seem to be used to get him out of actually teaching a class hald the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's a great professor and for SOCI 101 being a big lecture class, he makes the class seem king of small because of the many group activities. I would definitely take another one of his classes.

If you want an easy class, pick a different professor. Disproportional homework amount for introductory class, required attendance, weekly graded quizzes and assignments where in order to get 100% you need to include an extra paragraph explaining why you deserve it. Gives huge extra credit based on luck, making it unfair to most of the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Caren definitely makes a large lecture class interesting. I was surprised by how much I enjoyed this class, and it was definitely not as difficult as the rating might make you believe. There's a lot of busy work, which is fair, but it's easy, and usually not time consuming. Exams are basically the study guide, so if you study, you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: It felt as if the professor thought that we didn't have any classes other than his. 3 tests, 3 novels to read(with reading notes, reading questions, and a book review on one), and online book quizzes before every class. Also 4 other "applications" to complete. Unless you love homework do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Great guy. He's a little dorky but very sweet. His class is not hard, but there is a good amount of work to do. Reading the textbook is how you learn the information. The class is just small group activities but it counts for participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Neal is adorable & such a sweetheart. Even though there are a lot of assignments to do like reading due every class etc, it was not that hard. He assigns book clubs that meet a few times throughout the semester which is a fun way to meet other people in the class which you do not normally get to do in a large lecture class.

Professor Caren is a very sweet and caring teacher. He requires us to attend book clubs but the books were pretty interesting. Also he provides us with study guides so if you do them, you will be fine on the exams.
This class was so boring that it made learning tough. We had to learn everything ourselves and lectures were a waste of time. It was an easy A tho.

I took this class because Sociology was a recommended course for my track; I took SOCI 101 because I thought it was the easiest option. The class isn't extremely difficult, but Professor Caren is big on busy work. If you're wanting to take a class where you show up and take notes, this isn't it, expect a lot of unnecessary group work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Was a bit unorganized throughout the semester... I would have done things differently. However, he was really nice and was good at taking into account our requests for due-dates, projects, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He is a funny but slightly weird professor. The class, in the beginning, is fairly confusing but as the semester goes on it becomes extremely easy. This is not your typical lecture class, it is very hands-on and interactive. There is a few quizzes that he won't grade, 4 short papers, and a take-home final which was a 600-900 word paper.

He's a funny professor, BUT you will be swamped with work. So many things are going on at the same time in this class (assignment wise) that it's overwhelming. You have a lot of reading to do, a lot of acting out to do, and a lot of group projects. This class is NOT an easy "A."
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She's perfect I love her take any class she ever offers
Second time I've had her as my professor!! One of my favorite teachers here at unc
I'm not convinced IDST is much different between professors but she was nice enough and an easy grader
She was a good Data Literacy Lab instructor. If you turn in your work, you will do very well. There are only a few in person meetings of the class but she made those as engaging as possible.
Natashas amazing, no work, everything so slight, and shes so sweet
AMAZING! A wonderful class with a wonderful professor, who gave great, informative, and USEFUL lectures that all of the quizzes/exams were based off of. Take this class if you have the opportunity!

Amazing Professor! She made retaking stats an enjoyable experience. The one downside I had with her is that she often would respond to emails very late, and many times she wouldn't even respond. But, it was not an issue as she was very welcoming and always had time before or after class to speak. I would recommend taking a class with her!
The best professor ever. She is so understanding and welcoming to everyone. Work is not difficult because she posts in-depth explanations of content.
Genuinely easiest class if you just submit the assignments and do the pollev. She is super sweet and understanding so no worries taking this course with her.

She was wonderful. The course was structured where you watch lectures before class and do some compression questions (but that should take about an hour at most). In class we do review, poll everywhere, and work on assignments, which is really nice because you can get a lot of help from both Dr Parikh and the ULAs/IAs. Overall a great course!!!

Prof Parikh is a wonderful teacher! All assignments are online and take a short amount of time to complete, can finish in class with time to spare. Quizzes and exams are online, open note. She is very good at answering questions and will go out of her way to help your grade.

Prof. Parikh is a great professor! 210 content was a bit dull just because it's statistics focused, but she made it as interesting as it can be. Easy A! Labs are automatic 100s as long as you try, and assignments are pretty easy. I liked how detailed instructions were provided. Overall, take it with Prof. Parikh.

Professor Parikh is really caring and sweet. In the class, there is weekly assignments and labs which are not hard at all to complete. And all the exams will be taken online. Easy class and the lecture could be a little be hard to concentrate.

take this class! pollev in class, so attendence is required but u get 2 missed days. tests and quizzes are online at home. labs and assignments are once a week for accuracy. prof. parikh is a great instructor! i am taking another class with her next semester :)

Fantastic professor that truly cares, the work she assigns is very simple and can usually get done during class time. She provides so many sources to help, if you even need it because she is a fantastic teacher in the first place.
She is so great! You have an online midterm, and some assignments but they are very easy and straightforward. I would 100% recommend taking this class with her.

Prof Parikh is a great professor! Her lectures are easy to understand, and the structure of the overall class is very organized. Quizzes and exams are take-home on Canvas, she gives us a lot of time in class to work on assignments, and is very accessible through Piazza. Take this class!!

super nice, class was rly easy, poll everywhere everyday, labs every week for completion, assignments every week for accuracy but super easy and using jamovi. take home quizzes, midterm and final. uses piazza for participation

She is a great person! But on top of that this is the best class I have taken. The lectures are actually interesting and all test are take home and open note including the midterm and final. The only thing that you are not guaranteed to get an 100 on is the in class assignment but those don't really impact your grade. Take this easiest A.

Great class overall to get the Research credit, but make sure you pair yourself with a good group. Collaboration and communication is key to doing well on research project. The exams are super easy and asynchronous. Assignments could be graded a little harshly, but in general if you follow the guidelines for the paper you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was my second time taking Parikh. Both times, she was an amazing professor. She made information very accessible and easy to understand. Most of the work is a semester long group project so make sure you have a good group. Exams were fairly easy. I never had a good grasp on research until this class. Would for sure take again.
Professor Parikh was very kind and always happy to help!

The group project was very easy if you have good group members that actually do there part. Lectures were pretty boring and very redundant if you have already taken 210. She was super sweet and understanding. Also I  wouldn't say participation matters a lot but she will have random assignments due that are completed in class.

Dr. Parikh is an incredibly kind professor. I had her for both 210 & 270, and I had a good experience in both. She recognizes that students are people, too, and is willing to work with you. Content, expectations & grading are clear & fair. Grading issues (slow; subjective) were due to the IAs, & Dr. Parikh was willing to talk through any concerns.
Amazing professor who clearly wants you to succeed. Class was structured around a semester long group research project. Online assessments and occasional worksheets were very manageable.

I love Dr. Parikh's teaching style and lectures. Her assignments are pretty straightforward and easy to get an A in. She is also very helpful outside of class. Tests are online and the only assignment that really matters is the research paper due at the end of the semester. 10/10 recommend her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I LOVE Prof. Parikh, she is easily my favorite professor at UNC. This class focused on an overarching research paper, and every Friday was a work day without a lecture. I met with her multiple times to discuss the project in office hours, and she always seemed super excited to chat. Can't recommend her enough!!!

Parikh is amazing! Over the semester, you will be writing/conducting a research paper. She breaks it down and gives good deadlines, but the UA's grade VERY tough. Grades do take a minute to get back, and you often get feedback for your ideas after you've already had to write/conduct it. Learning checks along the way are application based.

Ever since I took 210 with her, I've looked to take other classes she teaches. She is amazing! She is so caring and her class is overall pretty easy! She cares about effort, not getting everything perfect! Take home exams, mostly homework and projects for grading.

Dr. Parikh was by far my favorite professor for Fall semester! She was very considerate in terms of helping with practice problems, questions on Jamovi Labs, and preparing you for the main exams! In addition, she offers a little bit of EC plus drops many of your lowest assignment grades, so getting an A is extremely doable. Highly Recommend!

For PSYC 535!
Dr. Parikh is incredibly kind. First 1/2 semester is Python, then midterm, then second 1/2 in PsychoPy and R. Big partner project makes up a lot of your grade, but graded generously. Weekly homework assignments and attendance taken on "lab" days. She starts from the very basics and is very approachable + reachable in office hours.

I love Prof P! She is the sweetest professor I've ever had and she makes class so enjoyable. The class structure consists of watching lectures online before class and then during class she reviews the more difficult concepts and does examples. All assessments are done outside of class, including the final. I could not recommend a professor more!!

Typically has a video/quiz before each class, then in class reviews the material. She spends the last part of class as a work period for the lab/assignments. She and the TA's circle answering any questions. You have to do no math! It is an easy class with a caring professor. Final exam was application based and by far the hardest thing in the class

Dr. Parikh was a very caring professor. Every first class of the week she asked if anyone had anything good to share. The assignments were completed in class and could be completed with peers. The lectures were videos that we watched before class. The exams were asynchronous. Overall, great course!

Super chill and sweet professor! I was scared about taking this class initially because I thought it would be super math heavy but it wasn't at all! The math was more conceptual and often didn't require many calculations! There were also a few extra credit opportunities throughout the semester!!!

Super interesting course structure, the lectures are recorded and you do outside of class, and you complete the homework in class, so that help is readily available. I loved her class because I learned a great deal from it without being constantly stressed. She is very sweet and I highly recommend her 210 course!

I'm convinced Dr. Parikh is the kindest person to ever grace the Earth with their presence. She begins every class by asking if anyone has good news to share, which is always a morale booster. She explains everything very well, and made what was seemingly a dry subject pretty interesting. The quizzes are easy, but make sure to study for the final!

Great professor and great class! The class was mainly flipped, watching lecture videos at home and doing assignments in class which worked great for me. Professor Parikh is amazing at explaining concepts and clearly cares about her students and wants them to succeed. I definitely recommend her!

Dr. Parikh is absolutely amazing. She is incredibly warm and encouraging, and made statistics fun! The class itself was very reasonable. All tests and quizzes were take home and open note, which helped me focus on actually applying/understanding the material. As someone who dislikes math, this class was great and convinced me to pursue research!
great professor, teaches well, quizzes are online, take home, open note. learned a lot, and grading is very fair. as a premed love the A in an intermediate psyc class for my gpa

The TAs were a saving grace. The class is online and maybe because math is not required, it's hard to figure out what you're doing half the time. It felt very hand-holdy the entire time. Also the Piazza requirement was pretty annoying. Not my favorite way to take a class.
I loved Dr. Parikh! She is just the absolute sweetest and cares deeply about her students and their success. The class content was incredibly fair and applicable.

Prof Parikh is the best! She is so kind and always available to chat about course material during office hours. The class content is fairly digestible and there is time to ask questions and work on assignments during class. If you have taken stats before, this class will be easy! If not, you should still be just fine as long as you pay attention!

Dr. Parikh is literally an angel on earth. She's the nicest human and her lectures are very clear and concise. She gives A LOT of extra credit opportunities, her quizzes are two attempts online, midterm and final are online, and she finishes the lecture early if she's done teaching. Her TAs' feedback is also very helpful for assignments.

Dr. Parikh has got to be the kindest soul on Earth. Her lectures are very straight forward and easy to understand, and she is also always willing to explain concepts that students may struggle with or answer questions. Please take her class, you won't regret it!

Prof Parikh is the sweetest and she genuinely cares about her students! She is always willing to answer any questions on the material and is super knowledgeable. All coursework is online and attendance is taken through in-class polls. Easy material if you've taken a statistics class and she provides plenty of resources to succeed.

Prof. Parikh is amazing at explaining concepts and incredibly kind. Quizzes and tests are online, and the coursework is pretty light. However, keep in mind that this class is just an introductory statistics class, basically none of it has to do with psych.

Material is very digestible, and tests are take-home. Prof. Parikh does a great job at breaking the concepts down and she's very kind. Assignments are easy. If you've taken any sort of introductory stats clas before, this class will be a breeze.
She's so nice, the tests are take home, and you learn a lot.

Pretty easy class especially if you put in effort. Assignments get trickier over time but quizzes and midterm are easy and straightforward. Final isn't super hard. Although attendance itself isn't taken, there are in class polleverywhere that count for part of the grade and using the piazza site. Extra credit is offered for the midterm and final.

This class was very easy, but you could also learn a lot about statistics. There is one midterm and a final that are both straightforward and very easy, all alone. The weekly homeworks do get hard overtime, but two of them are dropped along with extra credit at the end on the final. very easy class, best professor to take it with.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This is a great class and Dr. Parikh made it very easy to get a good grade. There are weekly homework assignments that can be tricky, but there are plenty of opportunities to receive help. There is one midterm and a final exam that are both very straightforward.

Dr. Parikh was an awesome professor. There are online lectures to watch before class so the class itself never lasted longer than 30 minutes. Assignments were tricky and graded meticulously but nothing too hard. Probably the easiest class I've taken at UNC so far. Dr. Parikh was very knowledgable and passionate. Take her class!

TAKE 210 W/ HER!!!!!!!! PLENTY of dropped grades, open note quizzes/tests (take home), and easy weekly assignments. I'm not a big stats person and I killed it. I adore her and she does this thing at the beginning of every class "does anyone have anything good to share" and it makes a big lecture hall feel a lot smaller! Love her! Take it!

Super clear grading and very supportive. All tests and quizzes are taken online and are open note. There are weekly assignments and she gives you time in class to do it with the help of her/TAs if you need it. Take 210 with her if you can!!

Prof Parikh is excellent. All tests are open-book, open-note, and take-home. Class never goes the full time. The problem is her IA's: a different one grades all your assignments so you never know what you're going to get.

Parikh is genuinely one of the sweetest and smartest professors I know. She is very passionate about promoting equality. I have a ton of respect for her teaching style as well. The class is easy yet informative. She helps you learn the necessary information without making things unnecessarily difficult. Very understanding and empathetic

Nicest person I've ever met. Easy material and well explained. Midterm, quizzes, and final were online and open note with 2 attempts and your scores averaged. She's accessible and an engaging lecturer. She gives SO much extra credit. You could have a B and bring your grade to an A solely from extra credit. I can't recommend her enough! Easy A.

Parikh's teaching style didn't come naturally to me, but I still enjoyed the class. She genuinely cares about her students and wants to get to know them. Sometimes I think she made things more complicated than they needed to be, and there are a lot of lectures (two 30-min videos a week along with the in-person class), but it was still pretty easy.

Parikh is great & cares about her students! The class is a lot of writing over the course of the semester, and you do your research in groups. As long as you pay attention & stay on top of things, you will love her!

Overall a good mostly async class. We had a zoom call once a week, but attendance was not required, could be made up by watching and answering questions. Quizzes and tests were fairly easy, although final was a little more difficult than I thought it would be.

Dr. Parikh is great. She teaches about the things that matter. It wasn't that hard of a class considering it was a stat class. I wouldn't say it should really be a psychology class, though. Either a stats or maybe ethics class, but it wasn't psych heavy at all. The software was super easy to use.

I loved having Professor Parikh for this course!  She is super understanding and gives the perfect amount of work that isn't too overwhelming.  Attendance isn't mandatory and is done on PollEv, and there is a midterm and a final that are both open-note and moderate.  Overall, I really enjoyed this class and loved having Parikh as my professor!!

Dr. Parikh is a great professor, and she really wants her students to do well. This is not a difficult class as long as you attend class and watch the video lectures she posts online. She gives you time to work on the assignments in class and ask questions if you have any. Great class, but beware the final was extremely difficult for no reason.

Really easy class if you are decently ok at stats. The assignments are written out step by step. She is extremely flexible and caring! The two lowest grades of everything were dropped (minus the exams), but we only had a midterm and final so it was worth it for sure. Recommend!

Assignments in this class are kinda hard and the TA's grade very harshly depending on which one grades yours.  Final exam was nearly impossible and brought a lot of people's grades down, did not match the energy of other quizzes or midterms in the class, the final was just unnecessarily hard

Dr. Parikh is an amazing professor. She cares about her students and allows them to work on extra credit. In my opinion, the hardest item in her class is the final. Attendance is not mandatory, but if you do not go you might miss something very important. She also has review sessions that are very helpful. I would definitely take her class again.

Loved this class, she is very kind and truly cares about her students. She is always offering help and making sure you are graded fairly. You get to select your group for the final paper and although it is really long it is split up throughout the semester so it doesn't feel too bad at the end.

Does PollEV for attendance. Quizzes and Midterm are super easy, everything is online. Makes sure you never fail and can never get lower than 75 on the comprehension Q's. Some of the assignments can be hard but you are allowed to work in groups. Great professor and wants you to pass with an A and you will understand the material, if not you'll be ok

Take this class with Prof P! There are online video lectures before each class so you learn at your own pace. She ended class early on Thursdays to give us time to work on the assignments. There are weekly assignments, a few quizzes, and a take-home midterm and final. All quizzes and exams are open-note and online. Super easy and not a lot of work!

There is a reason Professor Parikh has 5/5. She is awesome! There is one semester-long GROUP paper that you submit parts of along the way, so submitting at the end isn't too difficult or overwhelming, and you get feedback. All of her classes were zoomed and did poll ev, and every Friday the whole class was given to work with your group.

Prof P is a gem at UNC. Her classes are insanely easy and I didn't go to class except for FDOC. She zooms her classes and does poll ev, so I just did them from home. Fridays also don't have poll ev's. 1 weekly assignment that took about 1 hour and with the slides were easy. Exams are also take home. If you need a PSYC class, take Prof P!!!!!

parikh is very caring and easily accessible! she really just wants everyone to understand the material and succeed. she gives notice of upcoming assignments, quizzes, etc. way ahead of time and it is easy to fit the amount of work she gives into a weekly schedule. it is not exhaustive and adds to your understanding. also extra credit things too!

Professor Parikh is amazing. I recommend taking any of her classes. There are 10 assignments and 5 quizzes, I  believe, which are easy. The midterm was tough, and the Final was harder, but not impossible. She also allows for extra credit and she is always there in class or in office hours to be able to help if you are confused. Use your resources.

I can't say enough good things about Dr. Parikh, she is such a great professor and person! Her lectures are very engaging and she is very kind about deadlines. Her class was also super accessible, as she had a Zoom link up for every class in case anyone had to miss it in person. If you have the chance to take any psyc. class with Dr. Parikh, DO IT!

I loved Prof Parikh! Her class was very accessible (offered zoom) and she was such an amazing person overall. Very understanding of personal situations, passionate about the work, caring towards her students. Definitely recommend taking a class with her.
One assignment due a week, very manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Love Prof Parikh!! She really cares about her students learning the material and actually getting something from the class. Just do poll ev's and she has zoom options. Pick a good group and you'll be set. Lots of good feedback and easy to get help. Take classes with Prof Parikh. (Also had her for 220 and she was equally amazing)
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class was fairly easy, and prof P's very kind and cool!  Make sure to keep up with assignments and poll ev participation!  Grading may seem a bit rough at fist, but just incorporate feedback into the final project! Provided example assignments help too! Learning checks were not bad as long as you study the notes! Extra credit was given at end!

Her lectures are can be boring/redundant but she is always there if you need extra help on the material/research paper. Class is easy as most of your grade is a semester-long project divided into small due dates throughout the semester, the learning checks/final exams are open-note, and 1/3 class are project workdays. Highly recommend taking her!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Certainly not one of the most interesting courses at UNC, but Dr. Parikh made it great. This class focused on a semester-long group project with 2 quizzes throughout. Extremely manageable. This was my second class with her and she was still an amazing professor. I recommend her courses to anyone.

Dr. Parikh is an amazing professor! If you have the opportunity to take her class, do it! Our class consisted of either an assignment each week or a quiz (although there were only 5 quizzes throughout the semester). The midterm was fairly simple, but the final was a bit more challenging than anything we did in the class.

Dr. P is one of the best psych professors out here! Take atleast one of her classes if you can! This class was doing a research project + paper and it was fairly easy as long as you had a good group, if you don't have a good group please speak to her about it because some assignments are submitted as a group and she always answers your questions!
if ur studying psych and have the option to take a class with dr. p, DO IT! this woman is literally an angel like
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, I really enjoyed her class. Even though Friday classes are optional, you pretty much HAVE to attend if you want to do well on the assignments. The quizzes, assignments, and midterm are fair and honestly pretty easy. But the final is very challenging. Luckily, she offers extra credit periodically.

Also had her for 210. There's an online option for this class, just make sure to answer pollev questions 
(they don't have to be correct). Can be flexible about assignment deadlines, offers extra credit at the end of the semester. Just make sure you don't get stuck with a bad group for the project (and communicate with her if you do)

Parikh made the class well structured with informational lectures, concise/shorter classes, lots of practice (PollEv and homework assignments), and extra credit towards the end of the semester. Def recommend!
She was great but paul sucks

Professor Parikh is one of the best professors I've had this semester. She is the best lecturer. We basically have no work- one assignment per week at 5 quizzes throughout the semester. Classes can be joined in person or on zoom, and friday class is optional!! TAs are pretty tough graders though
She offers optional online

Prof. Parikh is fantastic, each week we have a short video to watch before class (20-40 mins) then review what we watched during our in-person lecture. All tests and quizzes, including the midterm and final, are administered through Canvas and are open note. She explains topics super well, I highly recommend her class!

Professor Parikh is hands down the BEST professor I've had at UNC. Attendance is mandatory for participation credit, but there's always a zoom option. She is so sweet and caring and is always accessible outside of class. All quizzes and the final are asynchronous and open-note and Fridays are optional assignment workdays. Definitely take her class!

Dr. Parikh is a incredibly kind and understanding person. She is good at explaining topics during her lectures and is very knowledgeable. PSYCH 270 is a lot of work, but she gives plenty of time to work on each part of the research paper. The class is available on Zoom as well, in case you can't make it to the lecture.

Professor P is super sweet and caring, and will never make you feel dumb. Before every class, there is a 20-30 minute online lecture due, and her lectures are usually reviews (there is a zoom option too). There are 5 quizzes, three exams, and a weekly assignment (all online). Participation = pollev. Psyc210 is essentially an easy AP Stats class.

I love professor P! She is super sweet and caring and the class is pretty straightforward: two M/W lectures and a Friday project workday where you meet with your group during class time (on zoom or in class) to work on your semester-long research project. The TA's can be a little tough at grading, but overall great class structure person!
Professor Parikh is one of my favorite professors I have had at UNC. She was super easy to work with and clear on expectations. Grading was fair and opportunities for extra credit were available.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: common parikh W

Probably one of the nicest professors I've seen at UNC. Basically AP Stats all over again (didn't know that bc it's listed as a psyc course) so it was pretty straightforward, and even if you don't have a stats background, it was much easier than AP Stats. Graded fairly and tried to make it as interesting as possible.

Statistics isn't my strong suit but Professor Parikh made it so incredibly easy to do well in this class. Not only is she super accomodating, but she's so knowledgable and easy to feel comfortable around. I would recommend her to anyone fearful of stats because she'll make it a manageable experience :)

The content of this course was interesting and presented in a clear, engaging, and multifaceted way. There were plenty of opportunities to balance out lower grades, and the tests were very fair. Dr. Parikh is very knowledgeable, approachable, and clearly cares a lot about her students and the material she teaches.
This was a great class. Dr. Parikh does her best to make the class fun, welcoming, and engaging. The readings were sometimes long, but the tests were fair and clear.

The goal of the class is creating decent research papers, so she doesnt try to trick you or make quizzes/tests unfair. The pacing of the research project was  good in terms of workload. Shes also genuinely one of the sweetest professors ive ever had, and was super accommodating with any students personal/deadline issues!

Great professor. Caring and understanding. The class grades come from weekly assignments alongside quizzes and 2 exams. She understands that you have a life outside of school and tries her best to make it easier. Fridays are workdays for assignments or quizzes. Great lecturer
One of the few professors ive had who genuinely cares about her students and their well-beings. Very kind and helpful.

Professor Parikh is extremely kind and caring. She assigned a reasonable amount of work and was very lenient with things like deadlines and grades. Learned a lot from her as well. Would definitely recommend to anyone.

Prof. P is super sweet and understanding. 10 assignments, 5 quizzes, a midterm, final, and participation. TAs could grade a little harshly but overall an awesome class with clear expectations and pretty quick grading. Also offers extra credit and a small curve on the final.
Dr. Parikh is absolutely amazing!! She responds so fast to emails, explains content in a simple and concise yet effective manner, and is just such a sweet person!

I have to leave an obligatory 5 stars because of how nice she is and how much she cares about her students. I wouldn't recommend taking her classes unless your interested in them, otherwise they might be kind of boring. She is good professor, a beautiful person, and a pretty good teacher.
Psych 220 has a lot of material, but she broke it down and all of the exam material was covered in the lectures. I was not a fan of the writing assignments but she gave extra credit opportunities.

Prof. Parikh is nice and her lectures were pretty good. She gave an option to join and receive participation credit through Zoom. The weekly assignments had clear instructions and were not difficult to complete.

Prof Parikh was a good professor! I didn't necessarily think the class content was easy but thought it was taught well. Prof Parikh was flexible and understanding, offered zoom options, recorded lectures, and time to do assignments in class throughout the whole semester.

Best prof I have this semester! Prof P is kind and her lectures were amazing as well. Lots of great resources, and she replies to emails quickly. 
You can also retake quiz and she will average the two quiz grades if you scored higher on your second take.

She is so nice, super accessible and always understanding and willing to help or move deadlines if you're struggling. She really shows that she cares for her students, offers extra credit and does not give a ton of busy work. Also offered a zoom option the whole semester and recorded lectures. Overall wonderful prof that truly wants you to succeed!

Dr. Parikh is very nice! She lectures two days of the week and Fridays are project workdays. The whole class is designed to get you to write a research paper, but it is broken down into manageable parts throughout the semester. She gives detailed instructions for assignments. Overall, it wasn't too much work.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No textbook to buy, allowed zoom option whole semester, two classes of lecture a week and third class would be to work on our weekly assignment. All quizzes online open note, participation through PollEv, and she was super super nice! The class overall is also very easy (basic stats info). Not too much effort needed.

I loved Natasha Parikh and really look forward to taking her again. This class was decently easy as long as you watched her video lectures. She explains the material very well and is honestly a great teacher. She's very sweet and encouraging and always tries to help if you're struggling with something. Her assignments are relatively easy.

Dr. P is literally the sweetest professor ever, this is my second semester at UNC and I've had her both semesters and loved each. She understands you are human, and you have a life outside of school, and things happen. Very accommodating with COVID related preferences. Do your work, read the textbook, and you'll do great.
Dr. P is an amazing professor and I would definitely recommend taking any of her classes if you can. I loved her so much from PSYC210 that I decided to take her 220 and 270 the next semester!

Prof. Parikh is EXTREMELY amazing, not just as a professor but person as well! She is very caring and wants all of her students to succeed and know the material. The grading criteria is clear, with most assignments due on the weekend for which she also gives you class time to work on them. Again, such an amazing professor, I highly recommend!

Prof Parikh is truly the most wholesome and caring professor at UNC. She is incredibly understanding and just a good person (which is hard to find with most professors at UNC). She is the professor you will recommend to all of your other friends, and she gives you every opportunity possible to succeed in her class (including extra credit!)
necessary class for PSYC majors. Show up, pay attention and you'll get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved PSYC210, because of how great professor Parikh is! Shes very easy to communicate with, gives a clear list on how your assignments will be graded. She always starts lectures off asking if anyone has good news they would love to share. Shes gives many extra credit opportunities and overall you can tell she truly cares about her students.

Please take her class. I have never had a better, more caring professor. She is so sweet and funny. The format of this class was really helpful--watched online lectures then came to class to review and work on assignments. She is truly the best. Assignments were not too hard and really well made to prepare for exam. Quizzes were pretty easy too

She starts off every lecture asking for positive things that happened and you could tell people appreciated this and liked her because they actually answered. I loved that she gave us a hybrid option due to COVID. She gives extra credit and retakes.( I recommend doing all the assignments on time even if you don't know how to do them!)

She truly cares about everyone in her class. There are no stupid questions, and she is one of the only professors that has never been intimidating and never judges! Dr. Parikh is a breath of fresh air, and she values mental health. Her TAs are great too--Nick and Eric! I hope she has a wonderful life and both sides of her pillow are always cold!!!!

she's amazing and so sweet! you're going to have to actually put in the work, but if you do, it is an easy A. watch the video lectures she posts and study them-- they will help with the quizzes and midterm! it is a big lecture but she adores every single one of her students.

Prof Parikh is an amazing professor! She is super nice and available, explains concepts well and posts lecture videos to watch before class. She also records class lectures so attendance is not always required (she does have zoom options for class too). Easy A, offers extra credit and cancelled class because it was a no bones day. best prof

I really enjoyed her PSYC 210 course and she was extremely nice and accommodating. I would definitely recommend her for others who need to fulfill a PSYC 210 requirement. I had no stats background and this class was still easy to understand and the lectures were very informative.

I LOVE Prof. Parikh so much. She's so caring and her video lectures are amazing. She does an incredible job of explaining herself and everything online so I'm assuming the in person version of this class will be even more amazing. She genuinely cares about your grade and well-being. Her tests/quizzes/assignments are not difficult, just study a bit.

She's very caring and starts every class by asking us to share good news. She wants class to be fun and a safe environment and is good at explaining material. She understands stress and tries to give more time on weekly assignments on weeks we have quizzes. She cares about your feedback and if you follow rubrics you will get good grades.

Prof. Nester is very nice and enthusiastic about what she teaches. She really cares about students understanding the materials. The lectures were very informative and engaging and the class discussions were interesting. Homework assignments were straightforward and most of the time she gave the answers already in class before we had to submit.

I really enjoyed Dr. Nester's class! The lectures were very engaging and the assignments were manageable. She was very clear about what is expected in the assignments and exams and gave very detailed and helpful feedback.

The class was very interesting and the lectures were well-organized with really helpful slides that made studying for the exams much more manageable. Prof. Nester is very nice and accommodating. She encouraged participation in class and gave a lot of helpful feedback on the homework assignments.
She was very attentive to students' needs and was flexible with assignments. The lectures were super interesting and you could see Dr. Nester is passionate about the subject.

Dr. Nester was a very kind and understanding professor. She assigned lots of extremely lengthy readings which were the only things covered in lecture. Her exams were what you make of them, she is very clear with what will be on the exam, you just have to make sure to prepare for them well because she is a tough grader in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Nester's class was wonderful. We read engaging texts from diverse perspectives, creating a rich and meaningful learning experience. Discussions were consistently thoughtful and in-depth. Exams were fair, and she clearly reviewed key material and how to prepare. Highly recommended.

I enjoyed this class! You can tell Nester is very passionate about the subjects, which sometimes led to going over time with lectures and getting off schedule. She really wants to help her students, she gave plenty of feedback on assignments and offered extra credit. She can be a little bit of a tough grader, but is clear with her expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is very kind but grades extremely harsh. Make sure you go to her office hours before the analytic paper. The group project was very annoying. In the assignments you need to be as specific as possible to her questions. Midterm and final are doable they require a ton of studying
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She was vague about her expectations and did not teach much- she just expected you to know how to analyze texts in the way she wanted you to. The class was mostly just open-ended discussions. Graded harshly considering she gave so little guidance. I would steer clear of taking this class with her if you have the choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Nester is a great professor. The class had a ton of readings, and sometimes her lectures were slightly difficult to follow. But she is very approachable and always ready to answer any questions you have. Very passionate about the course topics. Not a very tough grader but you will have to work hard to get an A. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class itself was of reasonable difficulty since it is a 300-level class. The grammar wasn't that hard but had to write a few essays that were challenging. No warning about graphic content for the films we had to watch. The final consists of the usual quiz questions but also an ESSAY! Took me the entire 3h to finish, still shaky.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Nester is very nice and is passionate about the topic of antisemitism. I felt this class is very lackluster, it drags on slowly. The texts we read are somewhat confusing but philosophical. Maybe my class is just a dull group of students but don't take this course if you don't like to read. I like her as a person and she is very caring.
Super disorganized and terrible teacher. Felt my German got worse after taking this class.

This class was super unorganized and Professor Nester assigned some questionable material. Many of the mandatory films contained scenes with graphic sexual violence that I was not prepared for because she attached no trigger warnings. Aside from this, the readings are boring, and "lecture" is just her rambling about random stuff. Fell asleep daily
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: GSLL 56 was an extremely interesting first year seminar. Grading was fair, and the lectures were highly interactive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took GERM/GSLL 56 in spring semester of 2021 and it was a very interesting class. Dr. Nester was very nice and understanding and was always interested in her students' wellbeing, good professor and taught the class well

Dr. Nester is very funny, knowledgeable, and understanding of the difficulties surrounding online class and the pandemic. I was a bit intimidated by her at first, but that was largely due to freshman jitters. I loved this class, and even though it dealt with a lot of hard issues, I was never bored, and I learned a lot about antisemitic nuances.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Because of COVID-19, Fall 2020 was not easy, but Dr. Nester was very caring and accommodating. This content of this course really helps one improve in German, especially spoken German.

He is super nice and so interested in CRISPR! There is 1 midterm and you get a cheat sheet. The average was a B+ and he gave us 2 questions back that people missed. Otherwise, the only other grades are a semester long group project and the "final exam" which is a prompt that you get ahead of time and can prepare. Definitely recommend this class.

Dr. Nimchuk has been by far the best biology professor I've ever had at UNC. This course was my absolute favorite this semester and I always looked forward to sitting in lecture. He is very knowledgable with the CRISPR-CAS9 system and has so much insight to provide. Everyone should take this class and witness how marvelous Dr. Nimchuk is!

The best professor I've had at UNC. Very clear on his expectations and willing to explain difficult concepts. The class material was interesting for people interested in genetics and molecular biology. If you read and understand the papers, you will do well.

Loved Dr. Z! His lectures were engaging and entertaining to learn from. He sent out a weekly email that outlined the class we had that week and showed how much he cared about us. This was a 1-credit seminar, but he's teaching a full course on CRISPR next semester which I would highly recommend!

Great professor and person. Very knowledgeable on the subject matter and cares about the students. Seems as though he wants students to succeed and learn from his class. I highly recommend his course on CRISPR if you're a science major and interested in genetics. Final project was a lot of fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Proffesor Yaqub put together interesting readings, but was not a great lecturer. She often goes off topic and doesn't get into the meat of her lecture. She also will try and keep you after class is over to continue her lecture if she got off topic. I wish she was a better lecturer because what she has to say is often very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: These classes are not easy, it is very reading heavy and she is a harsh grader. But she really cares about students and is very understanding of any outside circumstances you might have, which can't always be said for other proffessors at UNC. I was very grateful that she was so understanding.

I really enjoyed the class. Dr. Yaqub is very knowledgeable and approaches the subject very well. She is a little disorganized, and the class is reading heavy, especially for the first two exams. Other than that, I enjoyed the class and learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super interesting and intelligent professor! I loved the Palestinian literature and films that we read/watched during this class. I gained a lot of important knowledge. She probably would be better in a smaller class though.
Not recommended. she is always unprepared to class which makes it hard to follow

Lectures can be pretty hard to follow. The test relies too much on lectures and ppt slides. If you find lost with study guides or how to prepare for the test, just approach the TAs. Some might be unwelcoming or not very enthusiastic but the one I usually had the review sessions was superb.

20% of your grade for the class is the test. She harshly shuts down people's opinions if they don't match her own. Big classes are not her forte, maybe she would be better in a small class. The content is interesting but she rarely stays on topic. Test is class attendance heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is really not that bad. It's interesting and I learned a lot. That being said, Nadia was not a good lecturer. She's clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches, but she just doesn't do a good job teaching to such a large body of students. Students should know that her unit focuses on the Israel-Palestine conflict.

She seems to not be open to students perspectives. She quickly shuts down peoples opinons and judges people harshly. She does not stick to her PowerPoints, and instead will go off on tangents that do not relate to the test material. She is hard to follow and does not seem like a genuine, caring, person. I would not take another class with her.

Her lectures and exam were centered around multiple readings and videos during the weeks she taught so as long you do those, you will be perfectly fine. She cares a lot about her content which is very apparent during her lectures. Overall good lecturer.
interesting readings, lectures can be confusing. the tests are not bad if you pay attention in lecture and review the slides

I had Nadia for Borders and Boundaries and she honestly just could not lead a clear lecture well. Everything felt very frazzled and the way that she presented her content was a bit unclear. Overall I would probably not take this class if I had another option, the tests were graded very harshly and randomly by TAs.
She's a caring teacher she's just all over the dang place and it seems like she can't control her own thoughts, not the best lecturer

Lots of reading and movie-watching, with boring lectures. Is not a good lecturer, but tries her best and is very nice. She was hampered by the other 2 professors, overall not awful, but would be better in a smaller class.

I took my first-year seminar with Dr. Yaqub and absolutely loved it. She was a very caring teacher and really encouraged the class to participate. Expect daily homework in this class, but nothing over the top.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class had a homework assignment every day but none were graded until the end of the semester when they were looped into one cumulative grade. The final project is a group project, and all the groups have very different prompts. There are a lot of readings and films to watch. However, I could tell she was really passionate about the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: average. wasn't a good lecturer for a big class, but wasn't the hardest prof for the course.

Professor Yaqub is a great person and is passionate about her work. However, in the new course setting she was often hard to hear during lectures. She assigned lots of reading but reading quizzes were moderate difficulty. Even though she's great, don't sign up for this class, it will be too much on your work load for a gen ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Generally a fine instructor, she was helpful in office hours and helped me understand what I needed to study for the midterm. She assigned SO MANY MOVIES. And books. This class has a quiz for every class meeting and the questions are very specific. I wouldn't take a class with her again but she's not the worst B&B professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures were somewhat boring and often more about artistic interpretation than borders, etc. When she isn't talking about a book or a movie she is actually pretty interesting. This class isn't hard at all if you just put in the base amount of effort, but Yaqub could have been better. She also has a notable bias towards Palestine.

She really struggled to control a large class ("Borders and Boundaries") and lacked assertion/authority. The biggest problem was I couldn't hear/understand her: she spoke very quietly, she mumbled, she had an accent, and she always wore a mask. She also never presented the other side of arguments which I thought "analysis" was supposed to be about.

Seemed like a sweet person, but clearly wasn't used to handling such a large class. Her classes were very slow and dragged on, and it almost seemed like she wasn't prepared for each lecture. Mostly just assigned long documentaries for homework. I'm so serious, don't take Borders & Boundaries. The difficulty and frustration just about killed me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Seems like a very nice person, but she clearly didn't know how to lecture to such a big class. A lot of her portion was just assigned movies and then we'd just go over the movies in class; it really dragged. It was okay for me bc I'm interested in the subject, but it was hard to get through her lectures. Sure she's better w smaller classes.

Professor Yaqub was not very good at lecturing to a large class. She assigned a ton of movies and then would spend the next class basically recapping the movie we already watched. Her portions of class were probably my least favorite but she seems very nice and knowledgeable. I think if you're interested in the topic she would be great.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: With this being a 300 person and 3 professor class, it was often choppy and disorganized. It felt as though Professor Yaqub could not control the class, and often rambled. She seemed like a really nice professor who cared, but was not used to handling 300 students.

She is very passionate about her work and teaching and that allows the students to become passionate. She is willing to help you if you put in the work. During her lectures, you just need to pay attention and you will get all the information needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: This class was so. boring. Do not recommend. There are 50-100 pages of reading/2 hour documentaries before every class along with a reading quiz that asks the most obscure questions that are often written poorly. The exams were too hard. The professors are not funny and slow with tech. A Gen-Ed should not be this extraneous.  Save yourself the time

Literally the most boring lecturer I have ever had the pain of listening to. Nobody pays attention or cares about the class and she is droning on continually for the entire class. Class is not hard and she is not a hard grader, just a ton of reading and a soul-suckingly boring class.

A real gem. I took her FYS 'Imagining Palestine.' Lots of reading for an FYS but all very interesting (and lots of variety). As a teacher, she cares so much. I once fell asleep during a class and when I woke up she had emailed me asking if everything was ok (not mad at all)! She is the least intimidating teacher, 10/10 would take her class again :)

Dr. Yaqub was really interesting to listen to and she was very educated. It is a lot of reading and a lot of films to watch. It takes a lot of critical thinking, but I loved the class. It's just difficult because you have to really work and think to be able to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Took this first year seminar for 2 gen-ed fulfillments, but would not recommend it for incoming freshmen. I had to work for an A-. There were at least 4 papers, you have to go to class, and you have to participate in lectures. There are lots of FYS that are easy A's & the profs don't care about attendance. This FYS was not one of them
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is very willing to give outside help and loves it when it visit her office hours to discuss the material. A very good communicator and wonderful, knowledgable professor

She is so inspiring, one of the most wonderful professors I've had. She is so invested and knowledgable about the material, and is really interested in our thoughts and opinions. She works are to help us formulate ideas and gain a thorough understanding.
Very challenging class but if you do your work and she knows you're trying hard you'll be fine. You'll finish al-Kitaab 2.

A generally decent teacher. A good amount of reading and short written responses, but covers everything thoroughly in class and encourages a lot of discussion. Midterm and final are both take-home essays.
His lectures were insanely boring but he is a good lecturer. Im sure he is good in other classes, bio105 was just extremely boring with a lot of busy work.

In my opinion, this class needs to be entirely restructured. Very odd grading system, tons of group work, and zero real learning. Also, zero accountability for group members not helping. Basically, a high school science class. Despite Bio 101 being a pre-rec, we spend time in 105L learning 101L skills. Could be useful, just needs to be rethought.
Insane amounts of homework and everything is graded for accuracy!!! Attendance not optional

Dr. Nevil is kind, but the lectures are a waste of time. No exams, just a bunch of projects/assignments. Peer Reviews, discussion boards, and easy online video quizzes. Every week, there's a group lab report assignment. Annoying but easy once you get the hang of it. This class had so many assignments, but easy A. Good GPA boost

Idk why Bio105L gets the bad rep. This class was super easy GPA booster. It's the easiest bio class I've ever took. The assignments didn't even take that long either. The only things that took time were the papers. But then again, they were group assignments and u r only responsible for one or two sections. Easy class. No final exam, just a paper.

Nevil seems great, but this class is the worst. Unsure if he set it up or was assigned to teach it, but it's the most nonsense class you'll ever take. Assignments take forever, are pointless, and have insanely confusing rubrics; it's a busy work highschool class. I don't get how this is considered a prereq because holy yap and time/energy wasted.

Dr. Nevil is super nice and does an amazing job lecturing. Just beware that the assignments in the beginning don't count for much of your grade, but in the later half each assignment you submit is like 10% which adds up super fast. Overall though I enjoyed the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Nevil was great in 105. There was a lot of work to do every week but there were a lot of interesting topics. Due dates were clear and easy to keep track of. The rubrics for the projects were helpful and you can resubmit if you dont do well on the first try. Dr. Nevil was the the professor who did the lectures and I thought they were interesting

DO NOT TAKE 105L with him or Hastie. SO MUCH BUSYWORK, I spent more time doing assignments for this course than my high-level bio and chem classes. Also most assignments you get MAYBE a two-day heads up before the due date. Insanely tough grading for no reason, I follow the instructions and rubric PRECISELY and still get 6/10 with no explanations.

Such a good professor!! You can tell he cares and prepares well for lectures and material. Is VERY clear on grading criteria and challenges you in good ways. Is very helpful in giving feedback, and approachable! Highly recommend Dr. Nevil

Dr. Nevil is great! He was very accommodating, made grading criteria clear, was always nice, and was quick to respond to emails. If you put in the effort, you will do well. I would definitely take Biol 290 and 290 Lab with him!

Dr. Nevil is awesome! He has very clear expectations but is laid back and is a very fair grader. HIGHLY recommend taking 227+L as opposed to other 200 level bio electives. While there are plenty of assignments, if you stay on top of it, it's very manageable. If you put in effort, you will succeed in this class. Super interesting material as well!
Really nice and a funny guy, but he tends to speed through the course. He is caring and if you keep going to his office hours you will be all good, but don't expect his lectures to be helpful.

Dr. Noonan was a very funny and nice guy, but was not a good professor. Our tests/exams made up 90% of our grade, and I never felt prepared for them. He is a very smart guy, but expected us to be on the same level as him. If you take him, prepare to spend hours outside of class studying and preparing for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Noonan is a very fun guy to be around. He did his best to make the atmosphere of the classroom positive and engaging, but he seemed to expect everyone to know the material very easily, as he has been doing it for decades. He's new to UNC, so he's still figuring things out, but he has potential to be amazing.

If you have already taken AP AB or BC, you'll be fine. If you haven't, strap in, because he goes SUPER quick. It's clear he knows the material super well, which means he kinda expects it to click for you super quickly too, but obv that's not always the case. But he's SUCH a nice person, and is always willing to meet and review.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Noonan is a great example of great person, somewhat lackluster teacher imo. He is lively and brings good energy to his classroom. However, his teaching is not my cup of tea. The material that is on exams is very different from what's practiced on homework/class. It was often "figure it out" with not much else for help. I felt unprepared.

Noonan is a really nice guy and definitely cares for his students, but his lectures were difficult to follow and things got off topic quite often. His midterms were also pretty difficult, as well as the Edfinity homework. Would only recommend if you have a good foundation with Calc.

Professor Noonan was such a great person and I enjoyed having him but the class itself was not the best. He was very all over the place and felt like we didn't have enough time to do anything. He is new though, so I think he's just getting the hang of thing and hopefully future classes will be more organized. I had to teach myself most material :(

I'm retaking calc from high school, so ik that calc is generally a hard subject. His lectures are pretty engaging and he's a funny guy. Doesn't go into as much detail as I would prefer. Offers a lot of help (had a video tutorial request form, and loved office hrs--but I never used either tbh). Edfinity homework sucks tho. 

Shoutout to my TA tho

Professor Noonan is caring but I would not recommend him for 231. He is nice, but lectures were hard to follow and he always jumped straight to the answer instead of actually walking through any steps to solve a problem. He blurred the lines between what steps were actually needed and what was extra "fun" stuff that you could do if you wanted.

Noonan is a truly a kind person, making an effort to remember your name and make 231 really entertaining than most sections. But most of us agree that he tends to ramble about things that aren't important to the curriculum at hand. the ULAs in recitation were def better at teaching than he was in general. also poll everywhere is used for attendance

Math 210 feels like a math class for people who don't like math, and Noonan does a great job teaching to that crowd despite being a math guy himself. I found him very entertaining. The lectures and due dates were a bit disorganized. But it's his first semester here and I'm sure he'll get into a groove.

I really like Noonan as a person and he wants the best for his students, his only down fall is the lectures. He gives a worksheet to work through and just gives the answers at the end of class. This was his first semester teaching here, so he was figuring out what worked along the way, so hopefully future classes will have more productive lectures.

Dr. Noonan is lots of fun! Teaching style could definitely be improved, but he's engaging and silly, and answers specific questions pretty well. I leaned HEAVILY on the ULAs in the class to actual learn material and prepare for tests... probably would've failed without them. Overall fun, but you're left to learn a lot of material on your own.

Professor Noonan is a funny and caring guy in lectures, but he did not really teach us anything. From what I have experienced and heard from my classmates, we all ended up teaching ourselves the course. Some lectures were good, but he didn't find ways to improve after people did terribly in the midterms. Class felt like a waste of my time

He's super nice, but his midterms were a lot longer than the other sections' midterms were. He also tends to do the math problems that he has fun doing in class, rather than focusing on what's on the exam. He loves math and he's passionate about what he's teaching, but he focuses a lot on what's he thinks is fun rather than on the curriculum

Notes are easy to follow, labs are mostly unrelated but easy. Her exams are quite difficult, sometimes with questions distant or only tangential to reviewed material, beware of trick questions and don't run overtime on exams, they don't account for class time well. Take MATH 347 with or before this class for some overlap. Decent curve

Katherine is nice but she isn't a very good teacher. Easy and hard content were taught at the same pace, the tests had few questions and sometimes had questions barely covered in class if at all. The labs were graded randomly with little feedback and there are daily worksheets, both of which provided little to pad your grade from the harsh tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Struggled a lot due to the unconventional nature of this class. She is a nice person, but never explains or teaches in a way that most understand and instead talks longer about concepts/motivations not in the tests. Labs were nonsensical and my TA had no idea what he was talking about. I'm great at Calc but this class made me feel stupid. Take 233.
pretty good, just do the hw urself and you'll be fine

Makes the content seem far more difficult than it actually is. Most labs were ChatGPT generated and none of the content on them was taught, so it was just extra unnecessary work. Often seemed unfamiliar with the slides (which she didn't make) and didn't have worksheet answers ready. Asking questions usually resulted in more confusion than clarity.

Made the material unnecessarily difficult and came to class without working out some problems on the slides/worksheets. When asking her questions, she often made the concept more confusing. The labs in this class were also ChatGPT generated, and the TAs were unsure how to do the lab. Take Math 233 instead.

Just take 233 instead. Not enough time to take notes in class (let alone understand). Tests are either normal/not too bad or obscenely difficult. It is very unclear what to expect from tests. There is no instruction at all on the coding in recitation (had to be 99% AI for me) and it has nothing to do with the content. Very nice person though!

Math 235 isn't an easy A and lectures can be hard to follow, but Professor Newhall is very responsive and gives a generous curve. The class is test-heavy, yet the exams are fair and one midterm can be replaced by the final. She also offers grade boosters like lab attendance and worksheets, though labs aren't very helpful, and grading varies by TA.

This class feels hard if only listening to lecture, but if you keep track of the homework and try to really understand the material getting at least a B+ is def doable. Professor Newhall might not be the best lecturer but she's a really nice person, and she gave out curve at the end which makes 92.9 an A and 89 and A-.

Prof Newhall listened and attempted to make exam 2 (mean 50) + final simpler in order to match the concerns of the class (which was appreciated) it's frustrating because the structure is confusing & she teaches so abstractly there's no connect to the material. Wish there was more depth & clarity, without so much difficulty in getting a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE, never have I struggled in math as hard as in MATH-235. Never taught the class before so she could not do half of the problems in lectures. The tests are hard. They usually do not include the material given in the review sheets. The final had no review material, topic lists, etc. The labs aren't helpful.

Honestly maybe not her fault since this is her first time teaching this course but awful. Did not teach half of exam 2 and has not curved it. Very disorganized, not responsive, overall just a difficult class. Self taught most of the material bc lectures were insufficient leading to poor grades. Avoid!!

Nice person, horrible professor. Can't lecture/teach for the life of her, tests have material that were never covered during lectures. Doesn't know what she's doing (didn't create class material, didn't create homework, lectures like she went over the slides the night before) and is only available two days of the week.

Course content was challenging but grading was generous. It was her first time teaching the course so things may change. Worst parts were the weekly homeworks (took me around 8 hours), the VERY hard exams, and the lectures (felt like she was just reading the textbook). Best part was the amount I learned (a lot of very interesting stuff).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Newhall is a overall a great teacher and lectures well. She is clear and open to questions, making sure students understand and follow the content, if not in lectures, in OH. She is also open to feedback when it comes to exams and workload. However, the subject matter itself was challenging, and we often felt overwhelmed by the material.

Exams are 80% of your grade and graded harshly, while homework is essentially completion. With a TA who couldn't answer basic questions in office hours, this was tough. It was also odd that the professor couldn't work through an exam problem in a full lecture, while holding the answer key, right after we were expected to solve several on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures come across as esoteric and move at a pace that is much too fast to follow. She does follow the textbook closely, but I find that the textbook explanations are MUCH easier to follow than those given in class, even after already having read the same explanations from the textbook.

The lectures are informative and engaging, but they sometimes move too quickly to follow. Also, I enjoyed the textbook by Strogatz which was used. My main issue is that the homework is MUCH too long. Given the time required for assignments each week, it's tough to also balance studying for exams (four in total) alongside other courses.

Dr. Newhall is a great prof. Splits her class into half lecture half worksheet, so even though there's no recitation she can answer questions and gives lots of practice. Super helpful in office hours. Tests are totally reasonable compared to homework. Take her for diff eq!!
Fair Tests, good worksheets, proper homework. I self learned but thats more due to my inability to focus in class rather than any problems with her lecture.
