Overall a good lecturer, but she missed a week in the middle of the semester and then tested the class on concepts that we had not learned yet. She also moves through examples a bit too fast, essentially copying from the textbook with little extra explanation unless questions are asked.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor. Lectures were straight out of the book, but she answers questions well and attempts to help people understand. Regardless of the professor, the class is extremely difficult. Two midterms: 1st easy and 2nd very hard, final tough, and homeworks are weekly. If you have to take 435, try to take it with her, but be ready to struggle.

Professor Olvera is a genius and she is extremely well spoken when it comes to statistics; however, that does not take away from how difficult this material is. If you fall behind, it is almost impossible to catch up. I respect her so much as a professor and it is clear that she wants her students to learn, but be prepared to fight for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very hard! the tests are way easier than hw (so much hw) but still hard. the first test was easy and the second was hard. avoid taking her for 435!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Didn't enjoy 305 (stor minor). Really wanted more active learning opportunities in class. She gave us a 2-part HW due 2 days before the final. The HWs require excel and on average took me 10+ hours each but exams don't even use excel. Stingy exam partial credit; 1st exam median was 77. 2nd midterm and final pretty easy though.

Dr. Olvera-Cravioto is a pretty good lecturer but it was very clear during the semester she had other priorities. She legit left during our final for a "very important meeting." There are weekly homeworks that will take you about 3-5 hours and its not worth nearly enough of your grade. I will say the class is very useful and still worth the hassle.
Really good professor and was super caring and flexible throughout the semester. Grading was a bit tight, however, on the second midterm and final. Would reccomend!

Professor Mariana Olvera-Cravioto is the best teacher that I have had in the Statistics department so far. She definitely knows what she is teaching. Her grading criteria is very straight-forward. If you attend all the lectures and do the homework, the class should be a breeze. Compared to STOR435, this class felt like heaven.

Easy A if you've taken 415/435 and want to strengthen your Excel skills, good introductory class to those topics if you haven't. She explains topics well and her exams are very similar to in-class examples and homeworks. She's accessible and communicates with students often. I wish more STOR profs were as structured and straight-forward as her
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Olvera is one of the nicest, most fair professors I've had. Tests are open note just like her 445 class. In hindsight, I shouldn't have taken 305 as a stats major. You can do zero work and do well (that's why I signed up), but it's far too elementary for anyone who's taken, say, past 435. She's still a great professor regardless

using chegg for the HW problems is essential: you won't survive the acute boringness of 305 unless you dodge the HWs. the lectures are necessary only insofar as learning the excel commands for the HWs. using clunky, boring excel, when you could learn python or R, is an enormous waste of time. take another STOR course if you can, you wont regret it

Mariana is one of the best prof's I've had at UNC. I had her for stor 305 and 445. Her ability to explain difficult concepts is amazing. She is willing to meet w/ students outside of her office hours and emphasizes that she wants to help us. Exams are fair, she is not trying to confuse her students. Take a class with her.

Attendance played a big role in grading. Students were often asked to upload photos, which were then used to track attendance. The class felt quite boring, relied heavily on cold calling, and the slides were very amateur and could be much better. Overall, grades seemed to be based more on attendance than on actual learning or engagement.

Long cases and a quiz required for every lecture, were just a large amount of time and super exhausting. Ott is a good lecturer, however, the final project (which is a presentation) is a large amount of time and the average for the final project was a 75. I felt like it was hard to know what he was looking for since the TA graded our quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I personally like Prof Ott, but know others who didn't. He's a tough grader, good lecturer and a nice guy. This course is based on 9 case studies with quizzes on each and a final group project. Grade-wise, it's 30% - Participation, 40% - Quizzes, 30% - Group Project. This class has a lot of reading, and if you do it, you'll do well.

He sent me this email without knowing I am mentally ill and have been struggling with school. "I noticed that you were absent on the first day. Please drop as soon as you can. As policy, I do not over-enroll and the waitlist is 18 people deep and I am sure others would love to join this class." I dropped because of this. I found this to be rude.

I took this online/asynch over the summer and it was just okay for if you want to actually improve your writing. Not much work, easy for a quick credit or A. His videos were short, simple, & a bit awkward. He gave basically no feedback (it all came from our group mates) and the canvas was a mess. Decent bit of reading followed by peer discussions

Prof Owain is amazing, super enthusiastic and cares a lot about students. He fosters a safe environment in class and makes students feel comfortable sharing their thoughts. The assignments are really enjoyable and you edit them as a small group with peers. Pro Owain gives incredibly thoughtful feedback and is all around great, cannot recommend more

Very chill professor, highly recommend taking a class with him. Participation matters a lot, but it is easy to talk in class. Three papers and one final group project. He cares a lot and wants to see you succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just a chill guy. Fun and easy class to take, attendance matters a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take Professor O'wain! In ENGL 138, there were 3 easy papers, 1 final group project, and participation (30% of grade but just talk once or twice a class you will be fine). I enjoyed coming to class everyday and highly recommend taking any class you can with Professor O'wain!

Take ENGL 138 with Matt if you can! He's amazing; hilarious, gives great feedback, and creates a fun atmosphere. The class consists of three creative essays throughout the semester and a group project, but they're all interesting topics. Lots of workshopping in small groups.
Very caring and knowledgeable professor. Will take the time and work with you to improve your writing and ideas. Class time could be repetitive, but we always had fun conversations.

O'Wain is a great professor! Overall, the class is very easy. There were four major assignments: a memoir, fragmented essay, feature story, and a final project. No textbook but there are generally 1-3 PDF readings required before class. Read and understand the pdfs, participate in class, and you will do well. I'd 100% take him again!

Prof O'wain is an incredibly caring English professor. He did a great job explaining the writing styles necessary for our papers (3x 5 page papers for this class) and then providing excellent feedback on our writing. The readings he provides are for support and just give some background information about the writing style he's looking for.

Professor Owain is very engaging and makes all the readings accessible online and does not require a textbook. The class expectations are straightforward and although the Papers can get confusing or troublesome, he is available and more than willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I am someone who loves all of my history classes. However, this was unlike any course I have taken prior (of which there are many). Grand total of 2 assignments graded by LDOC, insanely tough grader (free write exams - 45 min only), and unclear grading criteria. I literally had nightmares about these exams and almost didn't make it out alive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really hard to understand. Heavy on tests, papers and hard grading.  Curious about his actual qualifications to teach.
Don't do it. Super TA dependent, lectures can get boring and tangential but if you skip them, you'll pay for it later with a bad grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Owre is your standard, yet excellent history professor. The main class is a lecture and isn't too engaging, but the weekly recitation in which you discuss the homework assignment and that period of history is great. I do wish his class wasn't completely lectures and had more in class participation opportunities. Hope you get a good TA.

Weekly assignments, not to bad but are graded harshly. Good TAs. Lectures were engaging but hard to keep notes in. Overall it was awesome and I would take again. The assignments are graded harshly and give low A's on almost everything, but it was fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fave prof at UNC. Caring, engaged. Super thoughtful lectures. I learned a vastly more complex and nuanced way of understanding history and current events. Only complaint is that if you want to learn the content, you have to be in lectures, and you have to be taking notes.

Professor Owre was definitely very nice but the damage that I think is about to occur to my GPA is a major thorn in my side. Although that is mostly due to me TA (who pains me even more), the way the class was structured didn't help much either. Essentially, unless you're purely interested in the topic, I wouldn't take this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had to take other history classes the semester after to figure this out - Owre's courses are some of the most difficult you will probably take for 200-300 level history. Heavy reading, unclear slides, and very difficult handwritten essay exams. He's a nice guy but this class was far too difficult for a gen ed credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Owre is a kind, caring and engaged professor. Now, do not take this class if you are looking for a GPA boost or an easy one. Yes, it was interesting and I did learn a lot, but he is definitely a tough grader and you will have to work hard for a good grade. I recommend, but just be aware.
He had interesting lectures and was a cool dude. TA's are important though, as essays were an important part of the grade and my TA was extremely nitpicky.

This class was enjoyable for me and I looked forward to lectures and group discussions. He does grade slowly, though. If you're unsure about anything, definitely go to his office hours as he's very accessible. We had a variety of readings including memoirs and essays. The narrow focus on this class' topic made it dense but it was still interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Owre is a nice guy but as a history major I cannot recommend his class to anyone. I've taken difficult history courses but this one was completely unclear in its expectations and standards. The topic was interesting but the lecture was incredibly unfocused the entire semester. I unfortunately wish I had taken another course.

Genuinely one of the most frustrating classes I have ever been in. Changing deadlines, nothing posted on time, and unfocused lecturing. Also, grading criteria were super unclear for every assignment except one, and this guy has the harshest grading of anyone I've experienced in the history department. He's nice, but his class is so stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am so frustrated with this course and Professor Owre. This course was ten times more difficult and confusing than my other history courses during the semester. Owre is a nice person, but a terribly slow grader (we only had 3 grades out of 10+ assignments going into the final exam). Has the strangest methods for organizing/grading papers. 0/10.

This course was super confusing and not organized at all, plus the exams were really hard. It for sure isn't worth the GPA damage. Owre is nice, but as a teacher, I would never recommend him or take classes with him again.

Very nice professor, but the class is all over the place and not worth the hit to your GPA. Tons of readings, unclear criteria on assignments, very harsh grading on exams. If you aren't familiar with the content, would not recommend. Took thorough notes on every lecture, still none of it makes sense. Grades SO SLOWLY. One assignment graded by LDOC.

He is probably the nicest professor i've ever had. At the same time, I cannot give a good review. Lectures were boring, exams were extremely difficult, class was so unfocused. He never exactly explains what he wants on papers. As a history major, this class is not worth it. If one word could describe this class it's: CONFUSION.

Unless you have extensive background knowledge of Algeria, this class is super hard. Unclear grading and crazy difficult tests. Don't take unless you've already taken classes about Middle East. Not non-major friendly. Lots of books and discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: His classes are really tough. Homework tends to be pretty all over the place, and tests are weighted heavy and graded hard considering the time the class got to write them. Blue book, handwritten tests. IYKYK at this school. Lectures were okay but tended to be kind of unfocused on some days. I wouldn't take again, too tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely difficult tests with too little time to complete. Lectures were rambling and often off-topic, tests graded very harshly, rubrics and prompts rarely posted on time. Everything felt unorganized and chaotic. One of the most stressful classes I have ever taken at this college.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's super nice, but honestly I've never been more stressed or confused. I, like most people, have no idea what he wants. Every time he opens his mouth I get more confused. There's no clear criteria, he takes forever to grade stuff, I have no clue where I stand, and the exams are awful. The class is interesting but not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although Dr. Owre is very nice, the grading criteria for the class is extremely unclear. I have no idea what this man wants. I go into his office hours for clarification and I walk out more confused than I was before I went in. The lectures are extremely disorganized, and my notes are a total mess because of it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Incredibly disorganized, a grand total of two assignments graded by LDOC, incredibly difficult and overcomplicated tests where students were given far too high of a bar for a 45-minute freewrite essay exam. Grading criteria were vague, and assignment rubrics and prompts, if provided, were often posted one to two days before the actual due date.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His grading criteria are awful. When writing papers for him, I am so confused because the topic and what exactly he is looking for is so incredibly vague. The class was fun until grades started coming back because I felt like I was doing a lot better than I was and it was very difficult to figure out exactly what I was doing wrong.

Hist 312: Very kind, good lecturer, take good class notes, tests are ID/Essay blue books so entail a lot of prep studying. The course had multiple books which needed to be bought or rented from library. Graded by a few things and he takes a really long time to grade. Personality wise he is very nice and cracks jokes from time to time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Owre is amazing and I would 100% recommend taking anything he teaches. He is very passionate about his classes and is very available to his students. His lectures are very interesting and very entertaining. The workload was very manageable and fairly easy to do. One of the best professors I have had here at unc.
He is genuinely a kind, hardworking, and respectful professor that is passionate about his subject. I recommend 100000% percent

Professor Owre taught extremely boring material, but his personality makes the class bearable. He brings energy and a clear passion for the subject matter every day, it's just hard to connect that advanced material with students just looking to knock out a gen ed. I'd look for other options unless you're passionate the middle east since 1945.

Oh, Prof Owre. I wanted so badly to love this class, but if you don't have solid prior knowledge of history you probably won't be a fan. He's a really nice guy, but the TAs are brutal & he goes on tangents that make things confusing. Also there's weekly doc analyses that are HARD & stressed me out. Again, he is a sweetheart but this course sucks
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: This class was awful. The professor was incredibly dry and gave long lectures that were hard to follow. The professor and the TA both had high expectations of students' prior knowledge, when it was only an entry level class. I had to put way more work into this class than any others, and I still struggled greatly.

Professor Owre was one of the best professors I've had here so far. His lectures were engaging even though they were long and he is very charismatic. He's also very caring and genuinely wants students to succeed. I really liked his teaching style and personality! Class is reading heavy, but not too bad.

Professor Owre is a such a caring and funny professor, but the structure of the class was not the best. The lectures had too much information, and I didn't know what to focus on. Your whole grade depends on your TA. They say they don't expect you to be a historian, but the grading was so critical. Better hope you get a less strict TA.

Max gets so disorganized that it's hard to understand the point of the lectures. He gives no context for a lot of it, ultimately making it hard to understand for a beginning history class. All of the grades are based on the TA's, so you better hope you get a good one. I felt like getting an 'A' was practically impossible, even while going to hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Owre is an amazing professor. He took the time to learn my name in a large lecture class which I loved. His lectures are easy to follow and pretty interesting. All assignments are graded by a TA but the TA's are pretty fair. This class surprisingly barely had any reading which is amazing. Overall, He is 100% one of the nicest humans I have met.

You really can't miss with this guy. He is incredibly engaging, and when he isn't, he realizes and promptly takes a break. The course material is super interesting and the TAs are probably one of the best groups at the uni. He makes it really easy for the student to excel in his course and actually remember his material. Definitely recommend!
One of the best professors I have ever seen!

Max is truly one of UNC's best. I took this class for the gen ed's and honestly enjoyed it. Lecture was honestly interesting and Max takes breaks when it gets dry. Recitation and the homework sheets was not the same (so boring) but I liked lecture. Max cares you about as person, even having office hours outside when the weather is nice. Take this!

HIST is not easy. You have to work hard to get good grades. It is possible and with his help it's more than doable. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. He is so helpful and will work through any problem you don't understand.
Mr Owre is one of the best history teacher I've ever met, his courses are well-organized and his lectures are interesting. You will regret not choosing his classes!
GOOD PROFESSOR
BEST!!
Best professor I've ever met!!!

Dr. Owre is a bit disorganized, but overall a really great professor. His lectures are interesting and he's very passionate about his material and students. The course portfolio is a lot of time and work, but you really will learn a lot. History 140 is a good way to satisfy three gen ed requirements.

I wanted to like Max and this class but I just couldn't. His lectures are overly verbose and since he slacks on posting the readings, I was constantly confused about the material. It is obvious that his other job, exec. director of Carolina Public Humanities, is his priority and he doesn't make enough time to be an organized/effective professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Owre is a glorified high school teacher. Lecture is usually boring but class is easiest I've taken. Im a B+ student that will probably make an easy A. Busy work for recitation, but TA's were great. 2 easy take home midterms (only time I used the white textbook). Requires out of class activities for "course portfolio" (most of grade). Easy 3 geneds.

I feel set up for failure in this class. I want to stay on top of the readings, but he doesn't post them for class ahead of time or even for weeks after the fact. Also, engaged activity reports  dumb. I go to every class and recitation, but still think the best possible grade I can get is a B. I feel like I work so hard but it doesn't even matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: LOVED MAX! Not only does he have an awesome & funny personality, he's also an amazing & caring professor. He genuinely wants students to come to his office hours & ask him questions about the material-I went and he eagerly helped me write & outline a research paper for a DIFFERENT class. Reading isnt totally necessary but go to class & u'll do well

Max is such an energetic and upbeat guy. He really is passionate about history and cares about his students. You can tell he is here at Chapel Hill to connect with students and teach them about life. His lectures are very interesting, however they are random and jump all over the place. Overall, I really enjoyed Max.

one of the best professors I've had here at UNC, took three classes with him and would take them all over again. He is very enthusiastic about history and making sure you know the material. Does require lots of reading every week. Overall his lectures were interesting and his choice in music as well. Definitely  worth taking a class with.

Seriously he's incredible. I think the most important thing to consider is how much he somehow makes you want to know more about the subject. It's a LOT of reading, but his enthusiasm is really inspiring and he's always there to help when you need it. He expects a lot, but he gives so much in return.

Max is a exceptional teacher whose genuine enthusiasm about the topic makes often long/content-dense lectures entertaining and enjoyable. He knows most students in this 125 class by face and name. The class entails a lot of reading (textbook and novels) and is essay-based. Would highly recommend both this class and teacher.

AWESOME PROFESSOR. Class was always fun. He's really funny and enthusiastic and genuinely excited about history. Not an easy A... BUT even without an aptitude for history, if you go to class and read the text you'll probably atleast get a B.

I loved Max's class! This was the second class that I had taken with him and it was even better than the first. It was smaller in size and there was a greater level of discussion. He expects a lot from his students, but you also get a lot out of the class, so it's a fair trade.

Max's lectures are entertaining and packed full of information.  He is smart and passionate about both history and teaching.  Reading is very long and dense.  Be prepared to read a new book every week, in addition to daily readings in the text book.  Takes attendance in class.  Good class to learn, not a good class for an easy A.

Awesome professor. He clearly loves what he does and does it very well. His lectures are very entertaining and he is just a very likable guy. Always very helpful and understanding. Seems like he genuinely cares about his students. Very highly recommended.

Very hard grader.  Barely touches on the book but speeds through pertinent information in the lectures so he can sing/talk in French/discuss hippies. Kind and helpful, but grading system is very unclear.

Very hard grader.  Barely touches on the book but speeds through pertinent information in the lectures so he can entertain the sing/talk in French/discuss hippies. Kind and helpful, but grading system is very unclear.

Max (he is very informal) is a great teacher. He cracks a lot of jokes...he reminds me of Conan O'Brien. He is a hard grader but I didn't try very hard. When I went to see him, he was very helpful. I wouldn't say he is "hot" but he grows on you. He is definitely not ugly.

Owre is a really great professor. You can tell he likes what he teaches and knows his stuff. His lectures are dense, packed with information so taking notes is a must. He can be a harsh grader, but he's also really helpful if you go to his office hours. Talking one on one with can clear up any confusion on grading and how to make your papers better

Max was awesome. He clearly has a good time teaching. His lectures are just pure entertainment but there is also tons of information. He wraps things up and has really helpful reviews. Not an easy grader but very explicit with instructions and available to help. He's smart and nice.

Professor Owre was AWESOME. He is very funny and yet his lectures are serious and really packed full of information. He is the most helpful teacher I have ever had for writing. I went several times to his office and he took all the time in the world to help me. He looks and acts a lot younger than he is. Did I mention he is hot!
No Comments

He is funny, smart, and cute. Cracks a lot of jokes and doesn't take himself too seriously. He is a HARD grader, very demanding with writing but fair. He is also the most helpful teacher I have ever had when it comes to learning to improve. His lectures are very entertaining.

This class and Professor Abayomi's teaching was not very intuitive for someone who doesn't have any coding/limited stats experience. It isn't necessarily extremely challenging, but I would recommend taking this class when you have a lot of time to rewatch Abayomi's lectures and dedicate to the labs. He is funny and friendly, but pretty strict
Very strict professor, not care for or support students. Only create difficulties for our group project. DO NOT RECOMMEND.

I loved this class. Dr. Abayomi makes sure no one is left behind when teaching new content. He is very nice and didn't make it feel like an 8 AM. SQL is a straightforward language and has some cool nuances. Not that much work outside of class so can't complain. Exams aren't too bad and you have a cheat sheet too.

Very fun, approchable professor. Passionate about teaching and patient at explaning stuff to you. I feel he is too lax in this course. There are only 4 homeworks over the semester (each takes 0.5-1h to do) and there are not enough exercises provided to master the class.
Does not respond to emails.

Dr. Remi is a very funny and good teacher. He has a no nonsense mindset though, so don't be suprised when he doesn't give any leeway around late work. The course content is not that hard, but you need to actually put in work learning it yourself if you want to crush this class. Got by doing sort of the bare minimum and got an A-

Dr. Remi's personality made it worth it to take an 8am statistics class. He is a charming guy, and likes joking with his students. He taught pretty slowly- but only because he wanted to give everyone a chance to understand the material in this course. The workload for this class is very managable, and we had cheat sheets on the midterms/final.

Dr. Remi is an amazing lecturer; he explains concepts very well & repeats important ones we should know. However, he is a ghost outside of lectures. Never responds to emails & is not accommodating. I was one correct question away from getting an A- but he didn't even respond to my email about bumping me up. Make sure you have friends in this class.
Very mid lecture. Easy content, but the harsh grading makes the class harder than it needs to be.

The worst professor i meet in unc. The lectures were unclear, yet we were overloaded with assignments . The professor made no effort to support students, making the course feel unfair and needlessly difficult.
He is a good teacher and explains things clearly. However, he assigns a lot of work, sometimes not in a timely manner. You might have homework and midterms due in the same week.

The class itself is useful, but the grading was unnecessarily nit-picky. The professor was egotistical and unwilling to answer any questions or provide any sort of help. They spoke with an air of superiority and disrespect that I've never received from any other human being. I've never cried so much over a class. Do not take this class.

Overall, Dr. Remi was a good professor. Although this class has a lot of homework, it was relatively manageable. If you didn't take AP Stats in high school then this may be a difficult class. It is taught in python but you are expected to understand basic statistical concepts. I would recommend taking the class with him.

Old review got removed because I did not speak graciously enough about our lord and savior Dr. Remi. This class was not fun and he barely taught stats yet all the exams are about statistics. Take 155 instead. Also, if you ask a question in class he responds very condescendingly.

Extremely unaccommodating professor. Offers no extensions or drops on homework assignments, regardless of the circumstances, which makes the course unnecessarily stressful. Communication is a major issue—they rarely respond to emails, and when they do, the tone often comes off as rude or dismissive.

If you put in the work and time to really learn the course material, you'll do fine (think a few hours each week). However, the grading criteria isn't very specific, so there are many loopholes he can (and will) use to deduct points. Also, when going to office hours, he doesn't try to answer questions but makes you find out the problem on your own.

Take STOR 155 instead if you can, it is much easier. Got the worst grade of my entire UNC career, and I've taken chem and calc ll. In-class MC never reflects what we're learning and awards no drops for HWs, even though there are over 25 assignments. Also, emailed him more than two weeks ago and still haven't gotten a response. This guy is bad news.
The class isn't too hard, but the grading can be ridiculously meticulous at times. However, this is a great course for learning python and statistics.

We took our final exam on Friday but we still haven't received our grades. He was extremely rude to people who asked questions and he frames his final coding section with things we aren't familiar with and expects you to be able to complete it in 3 hours along with the multiple-choice section

Be prepared to hear, ‘Are you following the story?' and ‘This is very, very crucial,' along with gems like, ‘I'm already making my money; I don't care if you learn or not,' and, ‘In my side of the world, we did it this way...' all shouted at 8 a.m. on a Monday. If you don't need it, don't take it.

He says he's accessible, but he'll shame you for asking for help and make you think you're asking dumb questions. He argues that ‘it's 4 credits, so it's hard,' as if we signed up for boot camp. In his mind, students are the enemy, I guess we declared war by enrolling. Good luck surviving his battlefield of homework and take-home exams!

Beware of this class! It is insanely challenging for an intro-level course. There are no HW/lab drops or curves. You could be on your deathbed and Dr Remi still would not give you an extension. Never answers emails and talks down to you during office hours and when asking questions in class. Goes indepth on easy concepts, but breezes by hard ones.

Hardest 4-credit class I've taken at UNC (even compared w/ chemistry + physics). Workload and expectations are disproportionate for an intro level. He spends significant time overexplaining/ complicating straightforward concepts, while breezing through the difficult coding. No grades are dropped and no curves.

This class is just a cheap knockoff of UC Berkeley's Data8—he's stealing their work word by word and claims it as his own. At times he would switch the states from CA to NC to not make it as obvious. If you want to get a feel of how the class would be I encourage you to look it up, and practice. You'll pass the class with flying colors!

He presents himself as accessible but isn't. He shames students for asking questions, making them feel inadequate, and seems to view students as haters. The workload is excessive, because is 4 credit course you'll be finishing a take-home exam and multiple homework assignments at once. It feels like he prioritizes his ego over student success.

Dr. Remi is very smart, but he is not good at teaching the things he knows to others. As a student with no coding background, this class is very hard and Dr. Remi does not provide sufficient support to help you succeed. He does not respond to emails and is not approachable to ask questions, saying we would know had we paid attention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall I  think Dr. Remi is a good professor and I  believe the exams are fairly easy. However, when it comes to asking questions about the content or meeting with him during office hours he is very discouraging and almost looks down at you for asking a simple question. On top of that some weeks we would be piled with so much work and assignments.

His teaching style is very engaging so time flies by in class. The content he teaches is interesting and he often draws illustrations on the board to help you visualize and better understand the material. He is clear with what he expects from you, reviewing outside of class, submitting labs/homework on time, etc. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Remi is really nice and makes this class easy to understand. The material gets more difficult once the statistics part starts, but it is not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Hard to understand. Accent is so thick that I was left wondering what he was trying to say. It was online which made it that much harder to understand. He's extremely cocky. Felt like he was mansplaining everything with an attitude that he was better than the class. Math is not easy and he didn't help this. I suggest finding a different teacher.

He doesn't care if you fail or pass. He won't take extra time with you outside the classroom because “he's busy”. Not a very good professor if you have to get any extra help. I did this all on my own because he wouldn't help me in any way.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: not a good teacher for STOR320; didn't grade final project EDA part as stated on the requirements/rubric(ie. rubric said to use table or graph for each question; deducted points on putting only a table or only a graph and said in class that it is because only one table or graph is not enough; argued but didn't work); TA too strict for hw/analysis

Professor Remi is a great professor who really seems like he enjoys what he teaches. Took his class in the summer but the work didn't seem like too much. Very reasonable and the tests were manageable. Very respectful of student's times. He made statistics understandable and provided many examples with opportunities to ask questions!

Dr. Remi is the sweetest. He made lectures engaging and easier to understand. The homework didn't seem like a lot, but towards the second half of the semester, it piled up. It was also very time consuming. There is no extra credit!

Dr. Remi is always respectful and fair to all his students. I was originally scared as someone who had never taken a stats class before, but his lectures made it so easy and he is willing to meet with you outside of class to answer questions. Although his homework deadlines are strict, he is very understanding and wants to help you succeed!
His written portion of the exams are easy, but the multiple choice make it to where its so easy to miss a few but they count for a lot. He makes class fun which is important!

The class is demanding and time-consuming, but Dr. Remi makes expectations clear at the beginning and provides helpful resources (lectures/notes posted online, accessible outside of class). There are 12 homework assignments, 11 labs, 2 in-class and 2 take-home midterms, and a 3-hour final. Pay attention and it will work out.

STOR120 is an easy class, especially if you have prior statistics/python experience. Most lectures consisted of him re-explaining the same things over and over, which got pretty boring after a while. He seems nice enough, but I will say he does come off as a bit condescending when answering questions from students. Just an okay professor IMO.

Love remi! he is great and is very clear about grading and what he expects of you. not a difficult course if you stay on top of your work. only 8 hw assignments for whole year, 2 midterms, final exam. gives a lot of study resources that will prepare you VERY well for the exams if you do them(DO THEM).
Take this with him!!! He is so nice and cares for his students. Tests are just like the study guides and quizzes

I learned so much in this class and it definitely challenged me. Professor Remi is a wonderful professor and cares about all of his students. He challenges his students, but his class is do-able with a lot of practice. I would not recommend taking this class with a lot of other demanding classes.

Easiest class I have ever taken. The homework is pretty much the exact same as the exams. I always struggled with paying attention during lectures but still managed to get a 100% on one of the midterms. The attendance grade is incredibly generous.

Dr. Remi uses lots of examples, which helps bring some life into the material and make lecture interesting. He's careful to clearly explain difficult concepts to avoid confusion. His guided notes and study guides are great when you have to study for exams. Dr. Remi is also a friendly guy and seems to always be in a good mood for class.

Dr. Remi was a great professor and lecturer! His exams were 60% multiple choice, 40% written. He gives a study guide before each exam that is helpful. He also allows a 1 sided cheat sheet for each exam, and both sides for the final. Definitely recommend.

Remi is the goat. He is an amazing teacher and an even better human. Despite having big classes, he cares about every student and is easy to reach outside of class. I'm not a stats major, but I hope to take another class with him one day. He definitely knows how to teach the content in an easy-to-learn way. Take any class with him.

I think the class has helped me learn a lot. However, the class meets four times a week, with only 2 unexcused absences, which is kind of insane. It is also A TON OF WORK. Like kind of a crazy amount. He assigns take home midterms and in class misters, so if you have any other homework or exams, balancing them will be difficult.
Remi was a good professor. Be prepared to study and review lectures! He was very accessible outside of class.
If you make a mistake he will not allow you to correct it and has no grade space.

I took Remi for STOR 155 and STOR 120 and he was great in both! He really cares about his students and is knowledgable about data science. Remi makes sure you understand basic concepts rather than focusing on the small details. He is strict about deadlines, but if you stick to them there shouldn't be any issues.

Dr. Remi is quite caring for his students, though he could be stubborn sometimes. Most learning are through his lectures which is quite fast paced, so pay close attention during class. The exams have 2 parts, in-class multiple choice and after-class coding. I would say the coding parts are easier than the statistic-focused in-class parts.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good teacher and super easy class. Very easy and low effort homework, midterms, and final. Got an A+ on everything with minimal effort. This class gives me breathing room for more demanding classes. Good lectures too if you're genuinely interested in statistics.

Had great lecture notes that made homework fairly easy. Offers plenty of office hours if you are confused. Posts completed notes so missing a lecture isn't the end of the world. Would definitely recommend for STOR120.
He does not remove two of the lowest grades in our grade books.

Dr. Remi is a hilarious guy and makes this class fun. Strongly recommend his STOR-113 class to those applying to the b-school over MATH152, especially those who are not the best at math/calc. He reviews algebra at the beginning and takes all material very slowly. His main priority is that the students understand. I suck at math and got an A-.

Dr. Remi has been the best professor Ive taken a class with at UNC. His lectures are clear, interesting and fun. He wants the best for his students, is easy to contact and is by the book when it comes to grading and exams. He makes the work easy to understand and links it to real world examples. I will most definitely take another class with him.

Dr. Remi was amazing! Dr. Remi gave amazing lectures and provided plenty of examples that made the concepts so much easier. He also had very clear grading criteria and exams were straightforward. He was obviously passionate about what he was teaching and wanted his students to succeed. Highly recommend him for STOR-155!

Remi is easily one of the best professors at UNC! He is routinely disciplined, intelligent, and very caring. Strict with deadlines, but with good intentions. I had Remi as a professor during his first semester at UNC (he was great)--he has grown significantly! He is organized & communicative while retaining his kind heart and sense of humor.
Dr. Remi made me care about statistics and I am not a math person, nor am I a statistics lover. It is clear he cares about his students and his work.

prob one of the best teachers I've had as a freshman. He explains EVERYTHING so students are able to follow his classes and makes sure students really know what they're doing by going back to old material while teaching new material. Tests were very fair. Many laughs in this class, a non stressful course, gonna miss this class next semester!

Dr. Remi is an excellent professor and was very thorough in ensuring that we understood the lesson materials. He would make sure that we understood a concept before moving on and encouraged questions and concerns. I could tell that he cared about students' wellbeing and took his role as an educator seriously.

He makes jokes in class, and actually cares and answers questions in multiple ways to make sure you understand the material. 8 homework assignments total, throughout the entire course, about 20 questions each- very doable and understandable to what we are learning. Tests are worth abt 75%, but he preps you well (do study guides!). Def take him!!!

Dr. Remi is an amazing professor who truly wants you to get your money's worth out of the course. Even though this class is a lot of material, he tries his best to condense the information for anyone to understand. Can be a bit hard to follow sometimes, but overall is the best option for stor 120.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Probably only has such a high rating because his homework and tests are so easy. But the lectures are hard to follow and have no clear learning path

Professor Abayomi is one of the best Professors I have had. He is a great lecturer and the problems provided prepare you well for his exams. Some say he is repetitive, but he repeats topics that are important to your foundation in statistics. In STEM classes this is a luxury, most professors would cover a topic once (or not at all).

I appreciate how he takes his lectures slowly as that is unlike many other math or statistics classes. This makes it easy to understand the material and I don't have to spend much time outside of class teaching myself. His tests are also fair if you study and pay attention in class. He is also engaging in lectures and makes class more enjoyable.

While his lectures are slow-paced and often slightly repetitive, his class overall is very easy to follow and does a good job at teaching the basics of statistics. Homework assignments are clearly communicated and not overbearing. I would absolutely recommend Dr. Remi for this class, I feel as though he has taught very well.

Remi doesn't explain things well. He always makes mistakes unconsciously in lectures; you will be extremely frustrated if you don't figure it out yourself. Assignments are also confusing, which is even worse if he is not a good lecturer. Be prepared to self-teach if you choose a class with him. NOT going to take any class with him.
Not too much outside work and he is a super energetic and thorough lecturer. Would highly recommend.
Dr. Remi was a great professor really new how to make STOR 155 really fun. Made the class really interesting and made me more interested in statistics.

Dr. Remi is a great professor that was extremely clear on what he expects fro, his students. He always tries to make his lectures entertaining and push students to participate and to ask questions. He is very understanding and eager to improve. His well-rounded knowledge of soccer is a huge plus (he supports Chelsea). Definitely recommend!

Tests and quizzes are not an unfair percentage of the final grade. Participation and homework still mean a lot which helps cushion your grade. Remi is incredibly passionate and knowledgeable about the subject matter and he explains every topic in depth. Tests and quizzes are easier than the homework so you feel extra prepared.

I see negative reviews for stor 120 so it must be a lot different than stor 155 because the class was so manageable and easy. His exams were completely fair and he taught everything well. Definitely recommend for stor 155

I loved Dr. Remi's class! He is super passionate about what he teaches. His classes were very straight forward and his study guides are extremely helpful for the exams. If you know how to do the study guide questions, you will be prepared for his exams. The homework can be time consuming so I would recommend doing a portion each day.
Remi is a really good professor he explains so clearly the concepts and will help you out of class if you still have some doubts.

Excellent professor, and makes introductory statistics fun and comprehensible. We got behind in lecture but this was always accommodated for, rather than leaving us to self-study foreign material. Exams are very fair and have study guides; however, don't ever become complacent or it will reflect in your grade.

I'm not the best at statistics so I was very cautious to find a good professor before a stats class on. Dr. Remi is the best professor for this, he's straight up, extremely intelligent, has guided notes, and more. He made this class a (somehow) enjoyable 8am class. If you are questioning if you should take his class this is your sign you should!

Professor Remi is great! He makes sure to stop if anyone has questions during the lecture or if he senses the class is not understanding. He uses great real-world examples to help the class remember concepts. My grade could have been better if I studied differently for the first midterm. USE THE STUDY GUIDE/PRACTICE PROBLEMS!

Dr. Remi was an amazing professor! He teaches passionately, and has a sense of humor. He explained topics with clear and concise real-life examples that made it easier to understand opposed to other stat professors who just throw you the complicated looking formula straight from the text book. He makes stat easy you will not regret taking his class

Dr.Remi is a great professor who takes pride in his ability to help his students be successful in their coursework. He makes difficult concepts easier to understand and is very considerate of students circumstances outside of the classroom.

Dr. Remi was a very thorough teacher but was very condescending as a professor. He had very little patience and was rude to students on occasion. While his lectures were thorough, he spent a lot of time explaining simple concepts that everyone already knew.

He is the best choice for Stor 155. He reuses so many in class/study guide questions on tests that really reward you if you show up and pay attention. You also get a cheat sheet. I never had to worry about my grade in this class because I showed up and did the study guide before tests

Dr. Remi was a great choice for STOR 120. The midterm exams DO reflect what he lectures about in class for the most part. He explains most things more than once and will almost always ensure the class follows before moving on to the next topic. He is a really caring and passionate guy, and I would 100% take another class with him.

Professor Abayomi is awesome. He is very organized and provides many resources to prepare for exams. 2 midterms and 1 final. Midterms are fair and very similar to the study guide. You will do well if you pay attention in class, watch the recordings (if necessary), review guided module notes, and complete the study guide he provides.

Professor Remi is such an amazing professor and his class is so well organized. The exams are exactly like the study guides so it was not difficult to study. We were also allowed a one-sided 'cheat sheet' for every exam. His notes are so helpful! I definitely recommend taking STOR 155 with him!!!

Dr. Remi was not clear with lectures or material. Half of the time we would not finish the lectures in class and our homework and labs were graded incorrectly. Midterms were graded very harshly and were not very correlated with material learned. He seems like a nice and very knowledgeable guy but I would not recommend taking STOR 120 with him.

Dr. Remi seemed to randomly grade the homework and lab assignments which made it difficult to get feedback on how you are actually doing in the class. He doesn't convey the material well and puts concepts on the exams that were not clearly talked about. You'll have to teach yourself if you take 120 with him.

This was my first time using Python, and I think Dr. Remi did a good job teaching first time users how to code and then apply that to stats. He takes his time in lectures to repeat key things, which some people feel is repetitive but I thought it was helpful as someone that struggled in the class at first.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Remi is great!! The material is not easy, but he explains concepts well. The study guides are very similar to the exams and you get a cheat sheet. He is lenient on HW due dates and not a tough grader. Gives fill-in-the blank notes. The exams are hard to complete in 50 mins, but he does give some credit even if you haven't completed it.

Dr. Remi is awesome! His lectures are great, engaging, and fun. The material isn't super easy to understand but Dr. Remi makes it enjoyable to learn. Great professor and would 100% take his classes again.

Remi is the best for stor 155. Tests are fair and just like the study guides and homework, he doesn't try to trick you. You also get a cheat sheet. Requires barely any time out of class just 1 homework every ~2-3 weeks and then complete study guide/review notes a day or two before exam.

Dr. Remi is a nice guy but doesn't get through the information we need in lectures. The in-class exams test on something entirely different too. I would not recommend taking 120 with him unless you're prepared to teach yourself a lot of the material.

Professor Remi is a nice man, but is unfortunately disorganized at times. However, it was his first semester teaching at UNC so it's understandable. Exams were difficult to complete within 50 minutes while other classes had open note take-home exams. Sometimes, he was slightly condescending during class when questions were asked and through email.

I can't recommend Dr. Remi enough, he makes concepts so simple and the exams are literally exactly like the study guide he doesn't try to trick you and you get a full page for a cheat sheet. 4 free unexcused absences, the hw give you 5 tries per question and he drops the lowest 2 hw. Couldn't have picked a better prof for this class
Super clear guidelines. Review guides pre-exam were very helpful. He wants you to succeed. Very funny guy as well! Made the concepts seem simple.

Very friendly, but lectures were not very beneficial and our class fell behind the others. It was Dr. Remi's first semester at UNC, so I hope this problem doesn't happen in future classes. Work isn't too difficult, especially if you have some coding experience.

Dr. Remi's lectures were very long and tedious. He taught the material good but it would be very hard to keep concentrated with him. He has a strong accent, which at times was very entertaining. Tests were just like the in class problems. Homework is insanely long and takes forever. Overall an ok professor.

Probably the easiest class I've taken at UNC, and with an uplifting professor! It had middle school style fill-in-the-blank notes and 4 free unexcused absences before grade was affected. Exams were never surprising b/c Remi followed his own notes/study guides. Grading was lenient; HW was minimal. You're able to get a 100 on almost every assignment.

Absolutely unprofessional. Made this class much more difficult that it needed to be. Constantly spoke about how important respect is but failed to show any to his students through his actions in handling this class.

Remi is great. He provides fill-in-the-blank notes which he fills out along with you and while he talks fast and does have an accent, he literally posts every single class lecture online where you can access whenever. Always pushed back hw and web-assign gives 5 tries per Q. My friends in other stor 155 had to use my notes for their exams.

Remi is enthusiastic about data science. But he failed to return work, update the syllabus, and upload assignments when he said he would, preventing students from completing assignments on time. Even though he blamed his disorganization on his own poor time management, he was not accommodating of student latenesses due to his inconsistencies.
Remi is a good stats teacher and his passion really showed. We did get behind because he does over explain. Test were just like the review sheets.

Remi is the kindest person ever, but bad prof. Only had 6 HWs the whole semester, so was always unprepared for exams. Homework difficult and irrelevant. He explains things incredibly slowly but it is still confusing. Entire grade is pretty much based on 2 midterms and a final. If you do bad on one, your grade is done for.

The class is pretty straightforward if you know python already and honestly don't even need to show up to class because the material is pretty self-explanatory. Professor Remi is super caring as a professor but as it was his first semester, he was very unorganized with the schedule but it didn't impact my learning that much.

Prof Remi is super friendly during office hours. If it's your first data science class with no coding experience - it's not easy. The class and syllabus were super disorganized. We had to watch the videos on our own to catch up with the material. Exams are open-book. I hope he changes his time management in the future.

Pretty easy class if you know python. This class was EXTREMELY disorganized. No clear due dates. He overexplains, which led lectures to be kind of pointless and we ended up being behind the entire semester. While he is a nice man, I felt him to be somewhat condescending in class when students asked questions. Took forever to get my grades back.

Easy class if you know python already. Nice guy but wildly disorganized. We were behind the whole semester despite him constantly saying not to worry and that we would catch up. Eventually he just created videos and made us watch them by ourselves at the end of the semeseter to make up for the disorganization.
Pretty easy class if you already know Python beforehand. Tends to overexplain everything making lectures pretty useless IMO. The class is basically the exact same as the textbook

The class was very straightforward. 3 exams and homework assignments are due every other week. The exams were exactly like the lecture notes from class. Homework was annoying because it was always much more difficult than the tests themselves. As long as you attend lectures and study the notes given, the class is pretty easy!

Prof. Remi over-explains everything to the point where we had to complete learning the final material on our own time over Thanksgiving break because we ran out of time. His "review" of previous material takes over half the class every time and is extremely counterproductive. He does know the material and is passionate about data science.

He's such a nice guy who really knows the material, but his exams are extremely difficult and long. Cheat sheets are permitted tho, which is great. Lectures based on guided notes make things easy to follow. Homework felt like busy work a lot of the time and often wasn't helpful for learning the material better.

I loved Remi! First teacher at Unc to care about students. Didn't rush through material just to stick to a schedule, made sure we knew what we were doing and why. Study guides and homework matched exams! I actually learned with him despite hating math. great person overall, and an amazing professor. Take his class for stor 155!!

Prof Remi was awesome! He was very friendly which made it really easy to ask him questions. He will over explain (which makes him much better than other stat 155 profs) but he will stop if given confirmation that the class understands. The only complaint was that I wish we had slightly shorter/less test questions, but it is still easy to do well.

Dr. Remi is incredible and everything about the way his class is organized is perfect. No textbook readings, 1 homework for each unit, and 3 exams. The exams were easy and most of the problems were very similar to the examples we covered in class. Goes slowly to make sure we're understanding (this resulted in us not finishing all the units though).

He is a very great professor and really loves what he does. However, his tests are very long and you must really know what you are doing to finish on time. He spends a lot of time on one topic and tends to over explain things causing the class to fall behind. Thus, we did not finish every section that was written on the syllabus.

Dr. Remi is extremely kind and accommodating. His lectures are easy to understand and he goes through tough material several times to ensure everyone is on track--this is his downfall. We're very far behind the other class and the exams are falling out of the scope of what he's gone over. I'm worried for the final. Subject is easy if caught up.

Although the professor is kind, the exams are very challenging and account for 80% of the final grade. The PowerPoints are bland, making it difficult to learn the material without rewriting and reviewing notes outside of class. Homework is graded very specifically. Challenging for students without a physics background.

She is a great professor, while the material is hard, she did a great job communicating how to work through the problems. The first exam was a bit of a shock though as to how much was conceptual over mathematical.
Great professor that is always willing to meet with you! Very nice and a good sense of humor.

Unapproachable professor. Had to teach myself everything. Textbook homeworks + in-class quizzes you can't make up + 4 exams + 1 (easy) project. Always misgraded exams & hw. Would recommend taking pass/fail if you're not a physics buff.

I came into this class not having any physics background so I was super nervous, but both Dr. P & the ULAs were super helpful in office hours & class. Dr. P always made lectures relatable and super interesting. She does tend to overcomplicate concepts at times, so I recommend going to ULA office hours to uncomplicate things. I loved this class!

I enjoyed having Petschauer as a prof, shes hilarious and makes lecture less boring. The material for this class was very hard and I found it very difficult to study for the exams. Office hours were key but almost every exam, I felt like I was going into it blind. most of the class relies on exam and there was 1 or 2 quizzes & easy group project.

I loved taking this class with Dr. P! The class content was really hard at times, but Dr. P was very accessible outside of class and was always willing to provide explanations. This class had 3 paper exams, 2 open-note quizzes, a video project, and weekly homework problems. The exams are based on the slides, so if you study those you will be fine!

Very easy required class with Professor Petschauer. Lectures were sometimes long and drawn out, but that's expected. You do have to participate and complete some group work, but all required assignments are easy. If you do not get an A, you are not trying.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was by far my favorite class this semester. Dr. P is so passionate and knowledgeable you can't help but be completely fascinated during every lecture. The workload was very manageable and she is a fair grader. She cares about her students and is there to help if you need it. I would 100% recommend this class and taking anything with Dr. P.

The most fun professor. She made class so much fun and really cares about her students. It was only a first year seminar so nothing too hard, but she encourages class participation and cares about what everyone has to say. 10/10 would totally take any class she teaches

We basically had to teach ourselves the problems in class. We came to class and she just gave us problems to do on the board in groups, we would do them and she would just go over them. It also took up the whole class period. As far as my group, one person knew how to do the work and the rest of us just sat there in confusion.

Professor P is a very sweet lady but this class is hard, esp if u have never taken physics before. GO TO CLASS... but also she will go through a whole lecture and give one example and you will be very lost on the homework. DO THE HOMEWORK.. it's graded and helps! STUDY THE SLIDES FOR THE TEST. There are problems on the exam but also definitions!!
Syllabus doesn't say dates of homeworks or pop quizzes, so you have to go to class. She doesn't send emails out. She doesn't communicate. Harsh grader. Makes the class harder than it needs to be.

I took this class with Dr. Petschauer as a Maymester course and I highly recommend! She kept things moving and I was amazed at how much I learned in that short time frame. She was clear with her expectations and really wanted the students to do good.

Dr. Petschauer is one of the best professors I've had. She really cares about her students and understands that we are people. She treats us like adults and really wants us to understand the material. She uses examples and questions in class that are the same format as the questions on the tests. I highly recommend taking a class with her.
Best professor there is! Must take her class!
She is a great professor. Knows her stuff. Makes the information easy to understand, but studying is a good idea. I also recommend this course as a Maymester course.
Very good teacher.  Class was easy for the most part.  Tests not hard...just have to know your stuff.
Pablo is absolutely the best professor! Super awesome and so gifted!

The classes were not organized very well. His feedback on assignments was often limited to only 2 words. Assignments should have been more hands on instead of watching him read off a doc for an hour. Obvious this is just a paycheck for him, but an easy grader.

Pablo is an incredible teacher. I took this class fall of 2024, and he canceled class a lot - this has since changed in later classes. For the final project, we recorded and mixed a live performance, and we only had 2 analysis papers and 2 music projects, plus 2 quizzes. He takes a while to return grades but pushing back our due dates as a 'sorry'.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Vega is extremely knowledgable. can't really teach. I could have learned so much from him except that we barely got through any material. Cancelled class all the time, didn't grade anything till the last week, but did give feedback on assignments.

Pablo was super nice and the class work was not super hard. There was an online quiz that i missed as I had work and it brought my grade down to a B- from and A. I was not allowed to take it with a penalty or anything, just lost the points. This was frustrating as the class was not supposed to hurt my gpa and inevitably did.

Pablo is awesome. He is a great teacher and will work with you personally on anything you have trouble with. He is incredibly expereienced in the field of mixing and is great at passing that knoweldge on to others. There are two projects you have to work on and some quizzes that he gives you a study guide for.

Hands down the best professor at UNC. He is incredibly knowledgeable and passionate. He's super accessible if you need help and he truly cares about his students and their well-being. Best professor I've ever had, and the best in the music department. If you want to learn the ins and outs of music and production, the best possible way is thru Vega!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Vega was an awesome resource in further developing my skills in music production. His class was mainly project focused which was perfect for a class of this type. Professor Vega was always willing to help give advice on personal projects and class projects and has tremendous industry experience himself. Field trip was my favorite part!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I'm not a music major, I just decided to take Music Production cuz I needed a class to fill my schedule. This class is an EASY A and actually quite interesting. This was a class I actually wanted to go to each time, just cuz it was fun to learn about! But even if you missed class EVERY DAY, you'd still get 100 on the exams if you memorize the terms
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is actually for Phys 115. I cannot hear Qiu, he just reads off the slides and WHISPERS. He doesnt explain anything or write anything to solve it he just talks. Please avoid him, you will not learn.

Prof. Qiu does not explain concepts in class: he reads straight from the PowerPoints. He doesn't even try, even if students ask him to write out explanations in class. Stay away, if possible. I do not know why he is teaching intro physics as he does not seem to care whatsoever.

Professor Qiu struggled to read the slideshows, which made understanding difficult physics topics even harder. In fact, I got a better grade in 118 than 114 just because of how bad professor Qiu was. He also never answers questions, always seems nervous to lecture, and seems so out of touch with his students. if you have a class with him, DROP IT.
He's an awful lecturer, and reads off the PowerPoint word by word. He also just doesn't explain things even if someone asks him to.
He is awful

He needs to take a public speaking seminar before teaching again. Also he needs better awareness instead of staring down, as I saw a girl with her hand up for over 3 minutes without him so much as looking at her.

Just don't. It's clear he's very nervous up there and I feel bad for the guy, but you literally can't hear a word of what he says. And I sit near the front of the lecture hall. He's someone who may be too smart for his own good. It's much more productive to watch the YouTube lectures from 2020 during class and follow along with poll everywhere.
Writing this review as I'm sitting in class. Awful lecturer, reads off the PowerPoint word by word,  sounds sleepy a bored doing it.
Jesus christ, this guy is an absolutely HORRIBLE lecturer. Thank god that he's not the only professor for this course

Professor Gong was a great professor because she actually put effort into teaching rather than the flipped classroom style of some other econ classes. Problems challenged us and really tested our understanding of the material without being "trick questions." I loved this class and thought it was relevant to contemporary policy problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Gong is one of the best econ professors I've had. You can clearly tell that she is passionate about the subject, and mentions real life applications. If you're confused on anything, Dr. Gong will clarify everything during office hours. The class isn't as easy as some claim, and you do have to put in effort.
Easiest Econ elective, very few homeworks. Fair exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Gong is a really great professor and lenient grader. She really wants you to do well which is uncommon in UNC Econ. Best professor I have had in UNC Econ not because I did well but she is so passionate about teaching. This is good to see and something that UNC Econ needs more of.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Excellent econ professor, wants you to learn and that's it. This was the easiest 500-level econ class ever; great choice for an easy semester but still worth taking seriously because the material/skills are important and Dr. Gong really cares a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I LOVED her. She doesn't try to trick you at all and gives you everything you need to succeed. Exams are extremely similar to problem sets and hw. She is always there to help if anything is needed and such a nice person. Can't speak highly enough about her!! 100% take this as an Econ elective.

Professor Gong was one of the kindest professors I have ever had. She is very accessible outside of class and she genuinely wants to help you succeed. The class consists of short homework assignments and one group project that you work on throughout the semester. I cannot recommend this class and Professor Gong enough. Take this class if you can!!

Only thing that I found slightly annoying is she does not take any questions during exams at all, not even clarifying ones. However, overall this class was one of the best econ ones I have taken. She is not trying to trick you at all where it feels like a lot of econ professors try.
Makes it very easy for you to succeed, if you go to class do the 3 problem sets and do the practice exams this class is barbecue chicken
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The nicest econ professor I've ever had. She told us on the first day she wants us all to get As and she makes it very manageable to do so. The problem sets are for completion except one randomly selected question for correctness. The tests are never cumulative and exactly like practice and old tests. So funny and nice!

Super nice lady, she really takes the time to explain everything clearly in case you ever forget the basics from Econ 101 or Econ 410. You have the option to take the class form zoom instead of showing up in person.

Agree with others - best ECON prof at UNC. 552 is a readings/policy-based class, doesn't really involve typical econ math, just understand and apply data analysis. No tests or exams, assignments are reasonable and build towards a final paper that is a decent amount of work but Dr. Gong is super accessible and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best ECON professor at UNC. She explains concepts clearly and throughly, is always willing to answer questions (in and outside of class), is very fair and understanding, and her assignments always reflect what we learned in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Qing is by far the best Economics professor I have had at UNC. She explains material clearly and is very helpful outside of class. My 590 was on Healthcare and it was super interesting. No tests, just a research paper. If you put in the time and effort, it is a great class for your 500-level. Definitely ask for help if you need it. Qing is the best

Dr. Gong is a great professor. She explained concepts clearly, gave good feedback, and overall seemed to care about our success. I would definitely recommend that anyone take her for any econ course. I wish I could've taken more of her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Honestly, Qing is the best economics professor I've had at Carolina. She explains the concepts very well and the problem sets/exams were always what we went over in class. I found reading the textbook helped a lot as well; if you do what is asked of you, there's no reason you shouldn't get a good grade.
Can't emphasize previous comments enough, Qing is awesome! The material isn't the easiest, but she is a very generous grader. Attendance isn't mandatory, but I wouldn't skip too much.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Great class! All you have to do is read the texbook/slides and do the homework. Clear grading criteria and a very generous grader. Would take a class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There are only 3 problem sets, 2 midterms and a final. Her problems sets and exams are EASY, and she gives clear instruction for what will be on the exam. It's ok if you don't go to class, because her slides give everything. The most important, she is such a generous grader, and I get nearly 100% on 3 problem sets and 90%+ on exams!

I enrolled in PLAN363 for a free A, and I wish I hadn't abused this class as much as I did (attendance-wise). He is genuinely so kind and clearly cares about what he is presenting. Please make sure to go to his classes, he teaches very valuable information that I wish I didn't take for granted. Highly recommend!
Very easy class if you want an A, The lectures can get a tad boring but again, it's easy and you could get an A just zoning out in lectures and reading the slides later.

He is very unclear in his lectures about the topics that we actually need to know. Also..what a snooze fest., and he doesn't know how to work technology AT ALL. If you want the class for somewhat easy credit then sure, take the class, but don't expect to come out of it knowing anything useful about personal finance that you can't find online.

TA's did majority of grading and gave good feedback, class was not hard at all, although the lectures could be boring at times.  Quizzes came straight from the slides as well as the final, which was online.  Pretty useful class and information.  Final questions were pulled from quizzes

Very easy class, good easy A. There is a financial plan that TAs grade, my year the TA's were very nice. There are 2 "true/false" questions every class to make sure you're present. Those were kind of annoying but you can find the answer pretty easily. The quizzes were 10 questions (there were 3) those were also pretty easy. Final was online.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Super easy A - participation polls everyday for attendance but you don't really need to be there, you can just take them on Sakai during class time. He is a very sweet professor and willing to help - all the test and quizzes come from slides - an a financial plan project.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The class isn't hard but it is not interesting at all. It is hard to stay engaged in class but you have to be there to get participation points. You could learn the information by reading his slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Quercia is a wonderful professor. He wants to help you learn life skills regarding your finances. I maintained nearly a 97 in the class because the quiz questions come straight from the slides. The large project of the class is up for interpretation and easy to do well on (since it focuses on your finances). Really informative class.

This is a really good class and the things you learn are very practical. There are one or two attendance questions on Sakai every class but they are easy. There are 2 quizzes in this class which are easy. Low workload. One of my favorite classes at UNC.

super understanding and flexible prof that listened to students' feedback. course material is very easy, his lectures and quiz/test questions are very straightforward and directly from the class slides. just go to class for the attendance quizzes and review the slides before exams and you'll get an A.
