It seems the other comments are fake. The professor expects students to master material that is barely or never covered in class. The exams and assignments include topics unrelated to lectures, making it frustrating and unfair for students trying to keep up.

I really enjoy Prof Qi's course. The best class ever taken. Qi is very responsive and always ready to answer questions, usually by offering helpful hints rather than direct solutions, so solving problems feels rewarding. The coding is challenging, but the puzzle game makes it fun. Plenty of group activities and collaborations, which are engaging.

Taking Geog 567 with Dr Qi was a honor. I left this class with more knowledge, super cool projects, and the desire to learn more. Dr Qi went out of his way to make sure I was learning and understanding the material. He would encourage me and I never felt stupid. I wish I could take all my classes with him.
Qi is a great dude and loves himself some Geography. This is a great class for the research credit. DO THE CODING PUZZLE :). He gives every opportunity to learn and the labs teach you about GEE well.

I enjoyed this class & Qi's teaching; it was one of my top 3 at UNC. He often gave extensions and was great with partial credit for late work. There were times in class where he didn't give us answers, but after he hinted that the question was on the midterm! Attendance & group work are important, but I'd def take another class with Qi

Professor Qi is a passionate teacher regarding Google Earth Engine (and the research of such in many different papers) and it's obvious in his lectures. He is a fair grader and gives lots of opportunities to make up work and to work in groups if you're falling behind. Although the content is initially intimidating, Qi Zhang makes it engaging.

Nice and genuine person, but everything he said was way over my head. When I would ask questions, he would make it a point not to give an answer or even point me in a direction. I can appreciate the value of learning on your own, but this class was just a professor who presented the students with problems and refused to help us understand them.

Class consisted of weeklyish lab assignments, midterm exam, a presentation, and a final group project. Lots of collaboration in this class. Lectures were a little dry but super nice and helpful professor, always answers questions promptly and gave extensions frequently. Do the coding puzzle!!! Class content is almost exactly the same as GEOG477 tho
Easily one of the most respected professors at UNC, take Prof. Zhang!

I absolutely loved Prof. Zhang! He is such a nice, caring, and considerate guy. Definitely one of the best professors I had at UNC, and I will for sure take his class again. He gives really good lectures. Do not hesitate to take his class, it's an easy A, I promise.

Probably the best professor I ever had. Dr. Zhang is super knowledgeable in his field and a great lecturer. Really cares about his students and their progress. And he is so passionate about the subject that you can't help but love it too. Would take this class again!

Dr. Qi is an amazing professor, who offers great and enjoyable experience to students in class. He does excellent jobs to help students understand the concepts and develop programming skills with hands-on exercises. He is ready to give feedback and cares about your performance. I would definitely take his other classes if any.

He is a sweet person who cares about students and someone who likes to see you truly understand and learn from class content. This is the most diverse class I have every took with people coming from all kinds of backgrounds and ages. 10/10 would recommend!

The worst professor I have ever had. In addition to everything else that has been said, he simply doesn't care about teaching. I went to his OH 30 minutes before they ended, and right after I knocked on his door, he proceeded to pack up his things and leave while ignoring me. Impossible to reach over email. Didn't curve midterms. Don't take!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst professor I have ever had at UNC. Exams were strictly based on textbook proofs, homework questions, or proofs in lecture. Lecture notes not given and textbook gave computational algorithms while our exams were by hand. Mostly a kind person to talk to but can be rather condescending when trying to learn and ask questions. Never take.

The worst math professor I've had. His lectures are extremely difficult to understand and follow. It's much easier to understand the course by just reading the textbook, but since he does some proofs in lecture only and won't publish those notes, you still have to go to class. He did not curve any midterms despite a plurality of students failing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took MATH566 with him. HARDEST B- OF MY LIFE. I did all the homework, read through the textbook multiple times, and took great notes, and still ended up with a 70 avg on the midterms (he doesn't curve btw). I missed ONE CLASS the whole semester, and missed one proof (not in the textbook) that he then made 20% of a whole exam grade. DO NOT TAKE
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a great lecturer, hard to understand and kinda just teaches from the textbook but these reviews are unnecessarily harsh. Sun is a bro. Nice guy, pretty chill dude, helps students as much as he can while preserving reasonable course standards. Small quizzes instead of HW, easy exams with no trick questions (usually just copies of book problems).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy but he just reads from the (already not great) textbook and somehow makes it make less sense. The grade for the class was based on the final, two midterms, and quizzes. No homework or participation grades or projects.

Nice guy. Just reads off the textbook. Somehow makes the material even more confusing. Greatest waste of time in my career in carolina. take ANY OTHER prof. Focuses too much on proofs for a introductory class. At least he smiles at you.
He's very bad. He's always asking us to prove some formula.

Professor Sun was a really nice guy and accessible during office hours. His lectures were not the best, and were very theory heavy, especially for only a first course in differential equations. I have a feeling he is probably one of the more difficult 383 professors and applications were not discussed. One test was all proofs.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: DON"T TAKE WITH HIM!! Read str8 from the textbook and made us memorize proofs. Lectures were so confusing. Other classes had equations/cheat sheets, we didn't. There was no extra practice/practice tests and when asked for extra, he said redo your textbook problems, which didn't help at all. Take any other professor. An extremely frustrating class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Sun is a cool guy. Lecture can be hard to follow, but the content for this class is relatively easy compared to other 300 level math classes. The workload is pretty reasonable and there is a homework quiz almost every week. These are usually easy and are worth 40% of your grade. Tests were generally fair (for a math class) and one was curved.
It is a hard class, and his lectures are not the best, but you can get away with a good grade because of the curves and extra credit points.

Very kind and genuinely cares. Gives copious materials to be able to succeed during the exams. Curves the exams and grades very fairly. Highly recommend taking 415 with him, he's the best professor to teach it!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is extremely boring. Not hard to get a good grade because there is a heavy curve and bonus for in-class quizzes. Homework takes a lot of time
Class itself is very boring, but he gives extra credit opportunities and curves a lot
Easy exams with large curves. Prof. Quoc is also very friendly at office hours. HWs are tough but graded fair

415 is a very boring class compared to others in the statistics major. Quoc is an okay professor, but implements strange curves and refuses to give back points when his TAs make grading mistakes. Lots of tedious homework that isn't always relevant to what is tested. But overall, relatively fair class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy who is obviously very smart. Tests weren't bad and were curved. Homeworks could be tricky but he helps a ton in office hours. Gave good study materials for the tests and offered optional quizzes in class for 3% extra credit. If you just go to class, do the homeworks, and stay on pace, you should definitely be fine in his class.

Quoc is an incredibly nice guy who tries to improve his class with feedback. His office hours are very useful for HWs. His lectures may be hard to follow, but he posts all his organized notes. Tests are somewhat challenging, but he curves and shares what the FRQs will be on and important topics ahead of time. Offers 3% extra credit with quizzes.

While obviously a smart guy, absolutely horrific as a professor. Lectures were almost useless to even attend because they were nonsensical and his accent was difficult to interpret. Replies to requests for help were met with unhelpful and sometimes unreadable responses. Do NOT take this class with him if you can in any way avoid it.
A lot of homework, the exam is difficult, the class is not clear, not recommended
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A clearly well meaning and smart guy, but lectures weren't particularly engaging. Some homeworks were fairly annoying. Still offers bonus quizzes and cheatsheet on exams and uploads all lectures/notes/examples so its easy to follow along and do well in the course. Exams can have some more abstract linear algebra type questions so be ready for that
Good teacher.

This class straight up sucks.
1. too much homework
2. lectures were confusing all over the place
3. tests were way harder than the work that was given
4. genuinely had a hard time understanding what bro was saying sometimes bc of his accent
5. horrendous pacing

if you value your sanity and/or your health DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS.

Do not take this class with Quoc Dinh unless the subject is very easy for you. Very judgmental when we asked questions and his replies never made sense, or were helpful. Impossible to learn in this class- I spent 30 hours outside of class teaching myself the content. However, there was a good curve. But he means well and is intelligent.

Very nice but very bad at teaching. I learned almost nothing and had to teach myself everything. He was very judgemental if you asked a question. The final was extremely hard but he added a good curve which is the only reason I got an A- in the class. If you have not taken calculus before, do not take this class with him.

Quoc is the sweetest person, and I really enjoyed taking his class. Attendance is optional, there are weekly homework assignments that are not very difficult, two midterms, a midterm quiz, and a final exam. He also offers extra credit for completing easy quizzes in class which he gives time for. Highly recommend taking this class with Quoc!!

He is a very sweet professor but does not always explain concepts very well. You can definitely survive in this class if you attend every class but beware that he can be confusing about certain things on slides so if you aren't there to hear his explanations, you will be confused. Final was worth 40%, but extra credit and curve was available.

Where to start...Quoc is clearly out of his element teaching college students about exponents and logarithms when he clearly prefers to do his advanced research. He is out of touch with the level of mathematical understanding that students in the class have, which makes for a frustrating learning experience. Every practice test had wrong answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: nice guy but not a great prof. Study resources do not offer clear explanations to questions and there were errors on study guides way too often. Exams often seemed unreasonably difficult in comparison to the study guides we were given. Class should be easy but is annoyingly not.

Professor Quoc treats being a professor like a second job. He does an extremely bad job at teaching the concepts in class which leads to a lot of extra time spent learning the same concepts that were taught in class. There are always typos in the in-class quizzes and practice questions which leads to wrong answers and unsolvable problems.

Professor Quoc takes teaching like it's his second job. There are constant typos on the in-class quizzes and practice tests, which lead to completely different answers or unsolvable equations. He does not explain the concepts clearly which leads to more time outside of the class learning the same concepts that he taught in class.
Does not explain material well during lectures. Exams tend to be much harder than practice problems.
Lectures are very difficult to comprehend, doesn't explain concepts very well

He is not very clear or organized in his lectures, and the textbook used (which he wrote) is also not very helpful. The homework was also always pretty long, but this is consistent across all 415 classes. He was very helpful and accommodating during office hours, I just wish his lectures were better.
The course material is extremely interesting and Quoc taught it well. He's very approachable and welcomes questions during the lectures.

Dr. Tran-Dinh is nice, but I found his lectures to be difficult to follow and his tests were much more difficult than homeworks, quizzes, or anything we covered in depth in lectures. He would often use the chalk board for sections of the lecture even though it isn't visible to everyone in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Quoc taught a new course and, considering the difficulty in balancing a new course, did a great job designing it. He adjusted the pace of the course when he realized we were struggling and provided sufficient feedback on assignments. The tests and quizzes were very difficult, but he curved appropriately. Reasonably understanding if you reach out.
Took over halfway through the semester. Work got twice as hard but he was so much better at explaining concepts. Good professor. Not the best in the stats department but definitely not the worst.

Quoc is a fine professor. I liked that he uploaded his slides ahead of time so that we could follow along during his lectures, as they could be quite boring. I also felt like he spent too much time reviewing basic concepts so that he would run out of time going through the examples. The homeworks were challenging, but the tests were fair.

Quoc is a mediocre at best professor. He definitely puts effort into his course, but it seems like it's effort in the wrong places. His tests are theoretical and hard, and his posted solutions often literally say "solve this as we would in class", as if that is helpful.

he took over halfway for another teacher, and his tests were harder but his teaching was better. he follows along w the textbook, so everything you need is literally in there. the last few assignments were kind of difficult because it's on GAMS, but he gives pretty helpful examples to aid you through them. he's very understanding and accommodating!

Quoc is a solid professor. He took over for the class halfway through, and definitely improved the course. Tests did become harder (more proof/theory) when he took over, but he curved his first test by 16 points to an 86. Overall, he is a pretty boring lecturer, but if you just want to skip class, read the book and have an easy B+, he'll do.

I loved this class and professor! He was really understanding, and everything in the class was manageable. Pay attention in class, go to office hours, and keep up with the weekly homework assignments and you should do very well!

Professor Tran-Dinh is incredible! So caring, and genuinely wanted to offer a good learning experience, despite the online nature of the class. Lectures were straightforward and informative. The workload for STOR 215 (weekly homework, 2 quizzes, a midterm, and a final) isn't too difficult, as long as you pay attention in class and put in the work.

Professor Tran-Dinh was wonderful to have! Truly caring throughout the semester and you could tell he wanted to foster collaboration although we were online. STOR215 isn't bad just make sure you actually go to the classes and do the homework. Very much a "you get out what you put in" type of class but not at all unreasonable.

The WORST professor i've ever had at UNC. His lectures are dull and useless as the HW is on material that is much harder. Quoc is a great guy with good intentions but is simply not a good professor and fails in delivering the content. Wait to take STOR215 with a different professor.

He's a nice guy and it's very evident he tries to teach and wants everyone to do well in the class. His lecture slides and textbook are very detailed and useful. Also helpful in office hours. The class is tedious but not too hard conceptually. Homework usually takes awhile. Exams are similar to old exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: While Quoc isn't the best lecturer, if you pay attention and devote time to learning the material, this class isn't too hard. His slides are actually pretty detailed and well-made. He is a very nice guy and willing to meet with students whenever they need help. Brush up on your Linear Algebra before taking this, and you should be fine.

The lectures are quite heavy and you need to be good at linear algebra to understand all the concepts. He is fully prepared for his lectures, slides, and lecture notes, so you can learn and review a lot after class as well. His office hours are definitely helpful and he is willing to help on any questions. (Homework is a headache.)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Quoc clearly cares about his students and does everything to make our lives easier. But if youve never had calculus before it might be hard because he can be confusing and only reviews the subject. If you have to take STOR 113, than choose his class because your chances of having easier homework assignments and tests are bigger.

Quoc is a great guy. His english is really not that bad and it's actually super easy to understand him if you give him a chance. His class, however, is kind of all over the place. I didn't get much from lectures, but that's mainly because it was very, very boring. There's a lot of homework (good way to learn). Only take this class if you have to.

I made a 4 on the ap calculus exam and this class was still a struggle for me. He made it much harder than it should have been. Tests were much more difficult than homework and class examples. Homework graded based on accuracy. I usually regretted going to class because  lectures were confusing.  Do not take him.

While Quoc means well he is not the best teacher. If you have taken calculus before you will do fine in his class, but if you haven't then stay away from this class. The homework is graded very closely and the midterms (three of them) are only out of 35 points, so tiny mistakes cost you. The final was really tough but the grades were curved.

Prof. Tran-Dinh is a good lecturer so far I have had. He taught everything in detail and had reasonable homework load. His lectures was posted online. The exams were fine and the grades were reasonable for ones who studied hard for this course.

Quoc is a good teacher. He made a lot of effort to help students in order to let them study better. I got a lot of help from him. The final exam was a little hard, but questions were that in the HW and practical sheets he gave. The final grade was curved.

While he is a nice man, he is not qualified to be teaching. He speaks english very poorly which makes his lectures difficult to understand. His lectures are very dry and confusing, and oftentimes I would have to go to Youtube to learn material. His exams were almost always much harder than the material warrants. Don't take his class.

Quoc is a good teacher. He really cares about his students and is very responsive. Every time I have question, he really helps to solve it in detail and re-explain it until I get it. He is not a native speaker, sometimes it is a little hard to follow him, but he teaches everything very details and tries to engage students with coupons and questions

This class is essentially applied calculus. I never took calc in high school so I found this class to be extremely difficult (If you're familiar with calc you should be fine). Quoc is a nice man but it can be difficult to understand his lectures, and I usually regretted attending them because I'd have to teach myself the material at home anyways.

Quoc is a very nice man and means well, but DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS.  Lectures are very difficult to follow even though the material is not terribly difficult.  He assigns homework pretty much every class and then never goes over them in class.  Also he grades very strictly and will take off a lot of points for a small mistake with no feedback.

Quoc means well but he is not a clear teacher. The material is easy enough, especially if you took calc ab in high school. Have to go to class to turn in homework. one midterm and a quiz besides the final, and the final counts for most of your grade. If you end up with him it's not end of the world, but try to take another teacher.

If you have taken Calculus, this class is a breeze. Sometimes I skipped class and will still be fully aware of what was going on, and most of the time, I regretted showing up. He was hard to communicate with at times and I think the class was a little more difficult for people who didn't have a strong background in calc.

Prof. Tran-Dinh, in both his first year of teaching and first year in the country, graded strictly, and rapport with students was nonexistent. He seems like a very nice man, but lectures were confusing, and office hours confused concepts further. Definitely the hardest professor for STOR 113. Hopefully his teaching will improve with experience.

I took the German summer course online, and unfortunately, I found the experience quite frustrating. While I understand the challenges of teaching virtually, I felt that the instructor was not well-prepared for the online format. The instructions were often unclear, and communication lacked consistency.
Terrible professor, doesnt care about his student at all, do not take his class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Good from xhs
Wei needs to improve his  expression skills, probably because his mother tongue is not English, and sometimes I can't fully understand what Wei wants to express in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very bad attitude and arrogant
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: overwhelming emphasis on research, neglect teaching responsibilities. The pressure to publish papers and secure funding often overshadows commitment to delivering engaging and high-quality lessons.  Adopt a dismissive or authoritarian attitude towards students, which discourages open dialogue and critical thinking in the classroom.
A fair grader I would say
Amazing  guy
Won't recommend this course for beginners

Wei was a great TA! There are a lot of assignments throughout the semester (6 units with essays, written and oral exams), but as long as you pay attention and participate in every class then you will be fine. He is super understanding and is a very easy grader. Would recommend to anyone and would definitely take again!

Wei is a great professor. Given that we are learning a new language, he explains the information very well. While I was lost in the new grammar being taught at many points, he was more than willing to meet outside of class to explain it to me. Very happy to have had him!

Incredibly friendly and easy to approach. The slightest language barrier made some conversations confusing but I learned a lot. Lots of homework but I felt prepared for every test without much extra studying.

Wei was great! Super kind and very knowledgable. Even though I'm quite an anxious person, I was never afraid to participate in his class because mistakes were welcomed and used as a learning opportunity. Clear lectures and feedback. If you pay attention in class and do the homework, tests are easy. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Wei was an EXTREMELY sweet and caring guy who made me want to come to class. However, he just is not the best teacher and I often felt extremely confused or just downright lost when he tried to teach us, and I know many other students felt the same way. Very easy grader, but when it came time to take a test I often was completely lost.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: I like this prof
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Quist is pretty chill for M130 He knows his stuff but sometimes he speeds through it. If you don't get smth,hit him up during office hours.He gives good feedback if you actually ask for it. His lectures can get kinda dry, like my skin (i have eczema), but if you stay focused, you'll be good. Hes a prof who cares & knows what he's talking about

Professor Andreas isn't the best professor for math 130. He does have very good "teaching" skills and doesn't know how to explain the content well. However if you are able to go to office hours and have one on one time he does go into more depth about a concept. To do well on the exams just go over study guides prior to. He repeats questions.

Andreas was honestly a pretty straightforward teacher. Though he missed some classes, he tried his best to make the ones he couldn't attend into zoom lectures. The people complaining 1) haven't been to class all semester 2) haven't paid attention and 3) haven't done the my lab assignments. His tests were much easier in comparison to other 130 profs
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Andreas is not a very good teacher. He goes through the information way too fast. He shows it and does not explain methods. If you ask a question during lecture you will end up more confused. Andreas also missed and canceled many lectures in the middle of fall. Our class asked for him to postpone the test or review more and he said no.

He missed a lot of classes during the middle of the semester which made it really hard to understand the material and do well. The tests are very hard but he gives a ton of partial credit. He is never available outside of class and doesn't respond to emails, ever, no matter what. I would definitely take another teacher for the course.

Professor Quist wasn't a great teacher; he would miss classes and he was new to teaching so most lectures were confusing. I didn't even really pay attention during lectures, I just did the pre-class work and studied well before the exams. But he did offer extra credit on tests and made good study guides for the exams.

Professor Quist is not a very good professor (MATH 130). He goes through material way too fast and if you ask questions it only makes you more confused. My class asked for extra help, preparation, or even a curve on our test and he said no. I ended up teaching the material to myself the whole class.

Dr. Quinones-Ayala was an absolute joy to have as a professor. So caring, enthusiastic, and engaging with her students. Spanish 203 is a hard class, but she was very encouraging if you ever made mistakes and would explain them in a very understandable way. Some of her grading took a long time but I can't even care because of how amazing she was.

Genuinely one of the best professors I have encountered during my time at UNC. Take her class if you can, while SPAN203 can be difficult, she will do anything to support you and make learning Spanish fun and accessible.

Dr. QA was extremely kind, caring, enthusiastic, understanding, and accommodating. I am not the best Spanish speaker but was able to get through this class because I made an effort. If you care, you will do fine because she cares! A great option (if not one of the best) for 203.

Professor Quinones-Ayala was my favorite spanish teacher of all time! She was hilarious and generally cared about her students. I felt seen and competent, even when I completely messed stuff up as is bound to happen in a language class. She did the absolute best she possibly could with the freedom she was given, and I am so grateful.

Professor Quinones-Ayala was a very kind and generous person. Her grading was very favorable and she always encouraged participation. She's good at explaining all the grammatical concepts and always made sure we knew what would be on the tests/quizzes. Very nice person and a great choice to have for 203, although she does talk fast in Spanish.
I love Senora Quinones-Ayala. I haven't had this much fun learning Spanish in a long time. Highly recommend!

Participation grade is based solely on whether you can answer pop questions correctly during zooms. You are expected to answer 2 or more times per zoom. Personally, this made me terrified to attend class. Luckily, the end of semester culture project is worth a big chunk of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. QA is one of the most caring and enthusiastic Professors I've had at UNC. She genuinely wants students to succeed and pushes students to use the target language as much as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Quinones-Ayala is an amazing professor. She was always super upbeat and encouraging during class. You have to show up to class or your participation grade will take a hit, this is for all 203 classes. She was always extremely helpful during office hours and truly wants her students to succeed.

Professor Quinones-Ayala is so passionate and energetic! She is also super accessible outside of class. The class has a lot of assignments and homework, but she makes class pretty fun and explains the material well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: There is a lot of pressure to be conversationally perfect, and if you aren't you will pay for it. Professor QA can be very nitpicky about some grammar topics and completely lenient in others. The textbook is mostly useless, easy assignments rather than content. Don't take this class to learn, take this class if you know Spanish and want the credit.

Oh gosh Brenda is great. I came into SPAN 204 not super confident in my Spanish but her kind direction and interesting activities left me much more sure in my skills. You don't go over grammar a ton but she is always willing to help. There is a decent amount of work but it's all easy and straightforward. She never makes anyone feel uncomfortable!

Funny and bubbly- Brenda is my favorite out of all instructors I've had thus far at UNC.  She's caring, passionate, personable, and truly understands the Spanish language (as she is a native Puerto Rican.)   I went to office hours for help on a paper & she not only worked through my paper with me, but also asked about my interests and future plans.

You can tell that she's passionate about the subject and that she genuinely cares about her students. In 105, we covered a lot of material, so there were definitely a couple topics that I struggled with, but she wants each and every one of her students to be successful so don't hesitate to visit her office hours. Study the material before class!

Brenda is a great professor and truly cares about her students and how they are doing in the class. There is homework due every other day, but it is easy and helps prepare you for the next class. Grading is fair, and the class is fast-paced but organized well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He is very friendly and the class can be dry but is straightforward. Gives very helpful practice materials for midterms. Very accommodating on deadlines and changed the class based on our math backgrounds. Daily quiz for attendance. 1 HW each week that takes < 2hours
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Probably one of the best options for the required 500 level class in the statistics major. Exams are all open book/open note and align very well with practice exams. Difficult but reasonable given the course level. Homework takes about 2-3 hours per week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith tries to enable students to understand the intrinsically difficult material for the Advanced Methods of Data Analysis class. Since this class is both heavily theoretical and applicational, the class is hard to teach by nature. But Dr. Smith did really well communicating the content. Tests are fair but require attention to detail.

Grade comes mostly from tests. Prof Smith is obviously very knowledgable about the subject. Lectures can be pretty boring though. Tests involved many questions in a little too short of a time so you had to rush during the two midterms. Not too hard to get a good grade if you take good notes though.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor smith has been one of the best professors I've had at Carolina. He cares about his students and helps his students succeed. He gives extra credit and can be lenient on the exams when needed. One homework per week and class can be long and boring but in my opinion it is one of the easiest statistics classes. I would recommend taking him.
Professor Smith is a great choice for STOR 455. Very lenient with grading during covid. Homeworks prepare you well for exams and getting an A-/A is not difficult if you understand basic statistics

Professor Smith was a great STOR professor! Lectures could be a little boring but he is very knowledgable and relates the math to the real world. He grades very fairly and allows you to use notes and textbook on all exams.
Nice guy. Good teacher. Lets you use your textbook and notes on tests!

Richard is an extensive lecturer and taking notes in and out of class is important. All the tests were open note and open textbook, but the concepts on tests are more complicated than the basic problems you receive in the test book. He is very available outside of class so if you have questions ask them anytime!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Smith is quite the dull lecturer. You have to double-check your understanding outside of class because you will zone out while he's talking. However, he is very knowledgeable and available outside of class. Don't be afraid to ask him questions or meet with him if you're struggling or falling behind! He is always nice and understanding.
Really great professor who was helpful in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best 500-level Econ elective. The course is very manageable if you keep up with homework and understand the lecture slides.

Stan is such a great professor. Lectures were very clear, and he is very funny. All the topics are grounded in real-world applications, and the models are pretty similar to those in classes like 410 or 420. Exam heavy, but exams are very similar to practice problems so study those and you will be good. Might be the best 500-level elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really recommend taking a class with Mr. Rabinovich. His class is engaging and the material is interesting. He is helpful during office hours and checked in with me to make sure I was preparing well for the second midterm as I couldnt take the first one!!! 522 is based on three exams and a final theory paper.

Professor Stan is one of the best econ professors I have taken a class with. If you pay attention in lectures and work on the problem sets you won't have much trouble with the exams. Very funny guy and highly recommend for an econ 500 class. Minimal math, and ties a lot of previous econ concepts together.
Boring lectures and weird curving of the class. Your whole grade is based on exams. Not my favorite teacher.
Honestly, this class is not easy but Stan makes it so much better! His lectures are never boring and he always gives real world examples to help the material stick better! I LOVED this class!!
Stan is really nice, and the class is exciting, but the grading scale is based on distribution, need to prepare well for the exam.

So intelligent and funny. He makes macro easy to understand and his lectures are awesome. Tests can be tough but if you do the practice problems you will be fine. 522 is a good option for a 500-level econ course.
The best macro prof I ever met. So humorous, smart and crystal clear.
One of the best teachers I've had (this means a lot). Very professional, respectful, and funny. His lectures are enjoyable. PS and tests are very hard but fair. I totally recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Rabinovich is a great professor. He doesn't require a textbook so all you need to do is pay attention to the lectures and do the practice problems. The practice problems accurately mimic the exams he gives so I never had trouble with the exams. He really makes sure you are properly prepared and he emails back super fast too.

would only really take this class if you are a political science major. i took this for the gen-ed credit and had a hard time. lectures are boring, Roberts moves through material super quick, and tests are relatively hard. you def can do well, but it requires A LOT of studying/work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class average on the first exam was a 63 and blamed it on us for not memorizing extremely obscure details. Class lectures are boring and unengaging and he often stops lectures to call people out for small talk.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I honestly learned more in recitation than in lecture. He is not very engaging and can sometimes come off rude. First exam had a 63% average in the class and did not suggest any changes on his end to help our performance. There is definitely a way to do well in this class, but it requires a lot of effort outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For a first year seminar, class was difficult for no reason. Graded by a few things, so messing up on the exams doesn't help your grade. You never really know what to expect on the exams, so they were difficult. Not reading heavy but lectures are boring. Professor is nice but any other first year seminar would be easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 2 papers and 2 exams. For a 100 level class you genuinely have to lock in, and the papers are graded strictly and if you do bad on one exam then your grade is predetermined.

Overall, Roberts is a good/engaging teacher. He was very knowledgeable and kept class moving at a good rate. The exams were fairly hard but not cumulative and the papers were pretty easy if you utilize resources (TA and teacher). Do the reading to understand what he goes over in class and not have to worry as much about notes while he is talking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was fine and uninteresting but not very hard if you read the textbook. Going to class was completely useless as he just repeats parts of the textbook you already read, but he takes attendance through quizzes. My TA was fantastic though and graded papers fairly. I just wish class time was more productive as I taught myself everything.

I was disappointed in this class because I was so excited to take it and knew it was going to be an easy A. Roberts was very all over the place during his lectures and got distracted most of the time. Most of the info on the exams was not talked about or just briefly skimmed over in the lecture. There's no way I should get a B- in a 100 level

Class is incredibly easy if you review the lecture slides and skim the textbook. The biggest issue would be the professor. Dr. Roberts, at times, had this aura of "I'm better than you" during his lectures. He would also use most of the class to just answer questions, without getting to the content. Overall, take it if you need an easy A.

This class is very lecture heavy so please please please pay attention during his lecture. Hie class his weighted on 3 exams, 2 papers, and participation in his class. READ THE TEXTBOOK! The most beneficial thing to do in his class is to read the textbook.
This class was based on 3 tests, which was unfair and not based on what we learned what so ever. He isn't a bad lecturer but they were not helpful. Would not recommend unless you want have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Roberts is very easy to listen to and led very interesting lectures. However, his class is oriented around 3 exams and 2 papers. The exams are pretty tough, with a lot of trick questions. You have to read the textbook thoroughly and keep up with the lectures completely. The papers are slight. He does not curve exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests are hard for no reason. The second test (out of 3) had a 68 average. There are extra credit opportunities (to which I personally went to almost all of them) but not enough to come back from how bad the tests are. Normally an interesting lecture, but would not recommend.

For a 100-level class, this class is unnecessarily hard. The tests are hard to pass because it is based on the lecture slides and he words the exams so tricky. The average test scores were 70s and he does not curve them. Essays are easy but the exams will bring your grade down.
Definitely do not recommend.

Prof Roberts is very knowledgable, fair, and organized. He's not very flexible or accomodating, but the class is not too hard and the workload is reasonable. Totally fine professor and interesting class. Do the readings and you will be fine.

Class only consisted of three tests including final, two paper, recitation, and poll ev (had so many issues with poll ev technology).  Pretty chill class and getting a good grade is possible.  Keep up with readings and definitely study lecture slides for test.  Try to get Michael Greenberger for your TA; fair grader for papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: roberts was very nice and a good professor, but he did pollev for attendance. the papers were graded easily, but the tests revolved around the lectures and sometimes included irrelevant and hard-to-remember information. for a 100 level class, however, it was easy and relatively laid back.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, I enjoyed professor Roberts' course. The class grade revolves solely around tests and papers but the more you studied and listened to lectures, the better off you'll be. I would recommend him as he is clearly knowledgeable and engaged in politics, making it easier to not get bored.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Roberts had fairly interesting lectures, but the entire course is 3 tests and 2 papers, with participation taken through PollEv. Tests were extremely difficult and had many trick questions. Averages were in the 70s for all exams and he does not curve. TA's grade the papers, 3 and 7 pages in length.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Even if you knew all the material, the tests had badly worded questions. He didn't curve the exams even tho our 2nd exam average was low. Pollev was used for attendance but he used it halfway through the semester and many people had problems with it including me. He did not listen to problems and would not curve anything. Would not recommend.

Professor Roberts graded participation through Poll Everywhere, with accuracy counting towards full participation credit. The class consists of lectures, with a few in person multiple choice tests that most people will need to study for. There are two papers for the class that are not very research heavy and not very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While I really enjoyed Professor Roberts's lectures, his exams are unfair. Specifically, I would do all of the readings and feel as if I had a great grasp on the material, and then receive a 70 on the exams. You are basically graded off of two papers and 3 exams. If it wasn't for his trick questions on tests, I would be giving him 5/5 stars.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Roberts is very accomplished and intellectual in his field making him a good lecturer and easy to listen to. Readings are assigned but don't stress over them, they are there mainly for context. Grade is based on two papers and two exams so beware. Class was not stressful as long as you put forth effort. Would take again.

Professor Roberts is extremely smart and intellectual about Political Science, so lectures are not boring. Only bad thing about the class is that you are graded on only 4 things, 2 papers and 2 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He taught with another professor for 384, so it's hard to distinguish who graded what, etc. However, his lectures were interesting considering the content. And to respond to the reviews that said he was rude, I don't think he is whatsoever. Solid professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class for it being my first POLI SCI course at UNC. The lectures were long but Professor Roberts did try to gauge discussion throughout the classroom. The readings were very important and were applicable to discussions. Paper was long but attainable, final exam was a little off putting but relevant to current events and class topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. The content isn't difficult and he makes the class interesting with lots of open discussions. Super nice and interesting guy, try and do the readings before class so that you know certain details before class. Would highly recommend

Dr. Roberts & his class were a very enjoyable experience for my first POLI course. He is well-versed in politics, and class discussions were great. He was always willing to spend more class time to explain topics if needed. Only complaint is that readings were a bit superfluous (do them to succeed), but he's a solid professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Roberts is an interesting guy. The lectures are of decent quality and address current events but the readings are extensive. Grading varies between TAs but the tests are very straightforward and you will be fine if you read. If you get Kevin Roach as your TA, I would recommend trying to get a different one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Book is very long winded but you have to know parts of it for reading quizzes and the test. Sometimes the lectures were dry but overall the class was very straightforward and a solid teacher for an intro course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: tests are somewhat confusing and challenging. but he is funny and the material is not very hard
Rude, inappropriate and very neglectful of his teaching duties. Worst professor at UNC

Very unclear expectations, very rude. He always has to be right. You have to write a 20-25 page research paper for this class without any instruction whatsoever and then he grades you like a PhD student. His humor is raunchy and he is extremely dismissive. Don't take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I learned more from my recitation than I did from the lecture. The readings weren't very difficult, but the textbook was long-winded, so what could have been a 20-page chapter was usually 40+ pages. Professor Roberts made the tests himself, and I felt like they didn't go with the reading or the lectures very well. No more poli sci for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Roberts is a solid choice for an introduction class. His lectures are large discussions about politics and currents events to keep the class interesting. Attendance is essentially mandatory because he gives reading quizzes using poll everywhere, but he tells you when he's having a quiz. If you read the book, you should be fine on his exams.

Solid teacher, talks a lot about elections and current event, not just the material. Tests questions are all multiple choice but very ambiguous question wording. If you read and understand core concepts you shouldn't have trouble getting a B or an A
Class was pretty standard, but the tests were not very content based. Hypothetical, ambiguous questions leave you guessing, usually wrong.

TAKE HIM FOR POLI 100!!! He is awesome and has the best lecture, I actually look forward to going to his class. He uses poll everywhere for quizzes and always tells you when there will be a quiz. there are 2 exams which aren't bad. The TA's are great also. Would for sure recommend.

Roberts is a great Professor. Had him for POLI 100- Intro to US Gov't and Politics. My class was pretty unique since I took this class in a semester with the 2016 presidential elections. Lots of discussion and opinions. He uses a lot of polling and survey data taken in class. Hilarious guy and made the class fun.

I liked Professor Talpaz as a professor. Lots of interesting discussions and interesting material. The only problem wasn't super organized, she frequently went off the syllabus and took a long time to put grades in. Would have appreciated a little more feedback on essays. That being said she's very understanding if you submit something late.

She was a good professor/lecturer and facilitated interesting discussions. However, she never graded anything the entire semester and never gave feedback on any assignment, so we never knew how to improve. She didn't put in grades until after the next semester started, and we had no explanation for said grade since there was 0 feedback.
She's very kind, but doesn't give advice on major assignments or put in any grades so you never know how you're doing in the class.
She's smart and can be critical but is supportive - if you try she'll support you
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The class was fine and she presents the material well but isn't great at the administrative requirements of being a professor. She never responds to emails. Says she'll post the assignments and never does until very late. I haven't received a single grade all semester including my final grade that should've been done days ago.

Dr. Talpaz is my favorite professor here! Assignments were clear & each discussion/reading question was thought-provoking & useful for the weekly posts. She fostered an open, inclusive learning environment & this was evident in the high level of participation from each student. She's a passionate professor & truly cares about her students' success.

Never held consistent class, never graded anything and reported grades 10 days late (with no feedback), went over class everyday, never responded to a single email, AND held class over zoom during condition 2. Also the class wasn't even about monsters or monstrosity it was basically the usual comp lit literary criticism that any other class has.
Incredibly easy class and he was very understanding and nice throughout the entire semester!
THE GOATTTTTTTFT. Super nice. Good teacher. TAKE HIS CLASSROOM

easiest. class. ever. He's pretty good at teaching, but the assignments and midterms were so easy it wouldn't matter if this guy only spoke Martian. Lectures recorded, class work is trivial, and the final is weighted lightly. Easiest A I've ever gotten.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Very great professor. Super understanding, entertaining lectures. Highly recommend. :)

Professor Stenz was a great professor and very helpful during office hours. I was worried about the workload since I had a heavy semester, but the class was manageable. There were four fair quizzes based on lecture material. Attend class, participate, and use office hours and you'll do well.

Connor is a great, welcoming teacher! He was always available to answer any questions inside and outside the classroom. He started and ended lectures with a song and honestly, that was such a highlight. I always looked forward to going to this class. He also is very knowledgeable about study abroad! His lectures were easy to follow and informative.

Professor Stenz is an incredibly caring and fair professor who will make your language course the best class of your semester. He goes out of his way to make class interesting with extra vocab or relatable jokes about the material. He keeps his had on the pulse of the class and makes sure that everyone is on the same page.

Mr. Stenz in an amazing teacher! He makes class engaging, and he is very encouraging/supportive. French is difficult to learn, but he is always willing to help you succeed. There is a lot of homework due before every class, but that is standard across the department. I highly recommend taking his class if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mr. Stenz is a great instructor! French is a very difficult language to learn, and he truly tries his hardest to explain difficult topics in an effective way. He is very caring about his students and wants to see them succeed. When asking some clarification questions, he can get a little off topic, but overall he was great instructor to learn from!

Professor Stenz is a very kind person who cares about his students very much. He is also very knowledgeable about linguistics. However, this can be difficult because when students ask him a question about content, he goes very in-depth, which can be hard to follow along with. Overall, he is very good at explaining French in a way that makes sense.
Very Charismatic and flexible teacher
Had Mr. Stenz for FREN 101 and 102. He makes class fun and is a very fair grader. He's also super helpful and is forgiving if you miss an assignment or need an extension. 100% recommend!
Teaches very well.

Professor Stenz was super sweet and funny. He cared about his students and wanted us to succeed. Homework was given after every class and wasn't horribly difficult. Tests and quizzes were ok! If I had studied more I probably would have had an A!

Mr. Stenz is an excellent teacher. His class follows the schedule, and homework is assigned before every session, as is standard for all 101 courses in the department. He is encouraging and supportive. Grading is easy as long as you do it. Yet, the listening of his tests is close to the natural speed of native speakers. It was a great semester.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Stenz was an amazing teacher for this course! He truly cares for his students and their success. He responds to emails in a very timely manner and always offered to go over certain material more if the class needed. French can be a pretty difficult language to learn, but he is a great teacher to learn from.

Mr. Stenz always made his classes engaging and really fun! He always makes sure that you are understanding the content and gives good feedback quizzes and papers. Overall he teaches this class very well and makes it a fun class to go to in the morning!

I am so lucky I got Mr. Stenz as my professor this semester! I think if I had a different professor, I would be failing the class. He is super caring and accommodating, and his feedback is incredibly helpful.
He is a great teacher. While the content might be tough for some, he is by far the best Prof to teach it. He is very understanding and overall wants his students to succeed. 10/10 recommend.

Mr. Stenz was awesome! Very understanding of first time french speakers and was able to help with lots of feedback and help inside of class. The class is challenging but him and prof demsey try their best to make it easier!

Professor Salm is very passionate about her work, however her lecturing style is hard to follow, unclear, and very messy. Personally, I would not take any other courses as she is unclear with her assignment instructions as well, however she is an overall easy grader and wants students to have a passing grade.

I love Dr. Salm as a person and a Professor. This class wasn't for me, and that's ok; the content is very dense and hard to digest. Sometimes it does seem overintellectualizing and pretentious, but I think that's the nature of critical anthropology and being exposed to new ways of thinking, not her personally. Overall, an amazing professor :)

ANTH 390: Dr. Salm is hands down the most charismatic and personable prof I've had here. She always meets her students needs and works WITH us, instead of just throwing us work. Her intellect is inspiring, she has an extensive background in super interesting topics and encourages students to explore things that they otherwise would overlook.

a LOT of reading (as is the case with any anth class) but a wonderful lecturer and makes hard concepts easy to understand. i don't think ill ever forget this class, it honestly shifted how i view the world (in the most neutral way possible)

The last 2 comments seem unfair. Professor Salm clearly knows what she's talking about and expects us to engage at a high level. She doesn't dumb things down.. so yeah, that might make the lectures feel dense. it's also what makes the class interesting. It's definitely pushing me to think differently and at a higher standard than my other courses.

Professor Salm is certainly passionate about her work and I like how you can clearly see that during lectures. However, she is not the best lecturer regardless of her knowledge and everything feels like it is inflated with unnecessary flowery language. Concepts are not that hard in theory but they are made out to be by the way they are taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took 390 skepticism in science, with her but I wasn't able rate that class. I enjoyed this class, if you are going into pre-med it is definitely worth taking as it gives you a whole new perspective. There are several readings per week, few small assignments every week,1 presentation and 1 final paper. She is very caring and wants you to succeed

Dr. Salm truly listens to her students (what they find interesting, what we didn't like, etc.). There is a lot of reading to complete for class, but the response requirements (perusal comments) allows students to comment on what they find interesting. I found the class to be slightly disorganized with instructions often being given last minute.

Dr Salm is AMAZING! She really got us interested in the realm of science and anti-science. Hard but SO WORTH IT. Most of the topics in this class were to me and a different perspective than any other course at UNC. I would highly recommend Dr. Salm if you have any interest in policy making, research, admin, global health, ethnography, and more!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Salm usually has pretty short lectures creating a lot of room for group discussion - so to get the most out of her class do the readings and come to class ready to discuss. No quizzes, or tests, just two essays (10-page final), and annotations for readings. Super interesting class, and Salm is very approachable, smart, and relaxed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Loved this class! I'm a med anth minor and this class was refreshingly different than others I've taken in the past. Grades were mostly dependent on participation, in class and through the Perusal readings, and our midterm and final paper/projects. readings were sometimes long but even then still interesting. 10/10 would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: EXCEPTIONAL!! Dr. Salm is genuine of the most amazing professors I've ever had at UNC. She is inspirational and motivating in every aspect of the course. Lots of readings (~60 pages a week) with graded annotations but very manageable and interesting content. 2 papers that build off each other. Overall, 1000000% recommend if you want a great prof!!

Inspirational, enlightening course relevant to everyday life! 2 heavy, but interesting free readings per week(annotations=30% of grade), EC available. Grade reflects effort! Everything a professor should be & more! Attendance/participation=30%, flexibility if you communicate (caring). Papers (midterm 20%, final 25%) worked on progressively+feedback

Loved her and the class was cool. Definitely a lot of reading for hw but most of it was interesting. If you do the reading and give the essays your best effort you'll do well. Be prepared to spend a good amount of time each week on the class if you want to get something out it. She's also so interesting to talk to outside of class, would recommend

Great teacher new teacher here at UNC. - Lots of reading (around 30pgs per hw). The beginning assigned were boring but then the readings got very interesting.
gives extensions when u ask and is very understanding. - 2 major essays that gave alot of time to complete - very awesome, a girls girl, easy to talk too outside. Take her class wont regret.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment:
participation and attendance matters, large part of grade. 
lectures can be boring but she just trying to get us to understand and discuss what we feel towards the reading.
lot of readings that she doesn't assign for hw is extra credit which can be used anywhere
Would take her again in a heart beat
hw is mostly reading n giving 4 comments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Melissa's class! While there was a lot of readings, they were really interesting, especially when we got into the anti-science aspects of the course. There was a nice balance of lectures and discussions, and there were plenty of opportunities to ask questions. Overall, I would absolutely take another class with Melissa!

Great lecturer, class material is clear. Linear algebra is normally difficult, as is this class. The main concern comes in the exams. The exams have proof questions which are very difficult, demanding abstract thinking of newly learned concepts. Memorize definitions to death and practice how they can be used to answer different questions. Big curve

Best math professor! His lecture is pretty good, although I missed some of his class because of the first class in the morning. You can still learn it by yourself.  He explains the concept easily. I did not know how to solve a question in the final, but I still got an A grade. Many similar questions to homework and written homework. A huge curve!
Exams were really hard and didn't accurately represent material learned in the course. Be warned
It was a difficult class but I felt that I learned a great deal. Professor Rimanyi is very knowledgeable but can be slightly terse on occasion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This dude is so knowledgeable! I should have went to his office hours (he is active on Piazza as well), but AI is getting so good at clearing up computational/theory questions. Prof. Rimanyi is great at explaining the theory (I highly recommend watching 3Blue1Brown alongside his lectures!) behind linear algebra. He's a tough love kind of guy.

Rimanyi is no-nonsense & 347 is hard. However, he also tries his best to ensure students thoroughly understand the material & is an extremely fair grader. You'll have to work for your grade, but will appreciate lin-alg a lot more. If you like math, this is a VERY rewarding class & the curve is massive. Tons of respect for Prof. Rimanyi.

The professor is not kind to students! He responds with attitude and his lectures are soooo boring. He graded my midterms extremely harshly. Luckily, the homework was incredibly easy, and he curves grades at the end. For reference, I got 60s on both midterms and ended up with a B in the class.

Awesome professor, great teaching style, very caring
- Exams were tough and 80% of grade, I got a 48% and 68% on midterms and likely bombed final but received a C+ (never got final score back)
- Generous, generous curve
- Content is interesting and useful
- Take 347 with him

Very lecture heavy and he doesn't post class recordings nor any sort of slides (except his class notes which are often illegible). You will be fine if you attend lectures and do the textbook problems. Entire grade is dependent on 2 midterms (both of which I failed) and the final, yet I still passed the class thanks to his curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rimanyi is just amazing. He explains concepts of all difficulties clearly and teaches real-life applications of linear algebra which is really cool. Not very lenient with partial credit and tests are proof-heavy but the curve makes up for it. Definitely the most rewarding class I've taken so far at UNC. If you have the option, take him!

Really intelligent guy, kind of intimidating but not unkind and sometimes drops a rare unexpected joke. More "proofs"/theory than others. MTs avgd 66, 71 but the curve was phenomenal. If u have any inclination/intuition for math and do the textbook problems you'll pass. I recommend taking it in a lighter sem so u can get the most out of it!

One of the best professors I have ever had. He genuinely cares for his students and will take time to answer any questions. Exams are no joke, you will need to really study to do well, but he is not trying to trick you. The curve at the end of the class goes crazy, it was at least 10 points. If you have to take 347, take it with Rimanyi.

Crazy curve-- had a 50% average on midterms, ended up with a B. Very good lecturer, but can be a little condescending when answering questions about grades/tests-- if you ask how to prepare he'll just say read the textbook, but you have to trust him on that because that is genuinely all you have to do

A lot more conceptual than other linear sections. If you wanna do well on the exams you have to really study the theory/proofs imo. Awesome lectures. Definitely take Rimanyi if you're a math major or just very interested in the subject!
Good prof and lecturer, but his tests are awful. He does curve a LOT though. If you like math you will probably appreciate this class.

Great honestly clearcut professor. Class characterized by "give it respect and respect will be returned" format. Lectures are at times proof heavy, but greatly contribute to understanding. Useful if you are a math major/someone with genuine interest to learn Linear all around (if so you will be GREATLY rewarded) but if not you will have to study
Was condescending in office hours and on Piazza
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of, if not the best teacher in the math department

He is an incredible professor. This is a hard class, especially over the summer session, but he made it so interesting and even though I almost failed it I would take another class with him because he teaches in such a way that it forces you to have an incredibly deep understanding of the material which is incredibly valuable

Rimanyi is the best math lecturer I've had at UNC. He teaches the material in an extremely approachable way without sacrificing any rigor. You can tell by the way he explains proofs and guides you through the course content that he wants you to understand. Very tough class, but was by far the best math class I have taken here.

I usually don't rate professors but i need to get this out of my chest. He is the best teacher I've ever had. MATH521 is a challenging class but he made it truly enjoyable. He made everything so intuitive and was so helpful in office hours. He truly cares about teaching and makes us appreciate the BEAUTY of theoretical math. Make sure to study HWs.

Rimanyi is probably the best professor that you can have for a course like MATH 521. His lectures are very well organized and I really think he cares that the students learn the concepts. The tests were also fair, just make sure to study all the homework problems that he assigns before the exams. I would highly recommend him for MATH 521!

Professor Rimanyi is a knowledgeable professor. He will give you the main ingredients you to need to be aware of (i.e. definitions and theorems) for the types of proof questions you will encounter on homework assignments and tests. Do not assume lectures will give you all the answers. You will have to put in the work and effort outside of class.

Prof. Rimanyi is a great instructor who never hesitates to answer any student questions or confusions. However, although I enjoyed his class, even given the short time frame of the summer semester, expect fairly difficult exams that may or may not cover weekly material. Don't get me wrong, Prof. Rimanyi's class was great, but be aware of his exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Rimanyi was solid as a math major but if you're not into pure math and want pure computational linear algebra take it with someone else. Big curve, fair homework, but lots of proofs that can be tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a math major, I would 10/10 recommend another math major to take linear algebra with Professor Rimanyi. He taught the course the right way by including the theory behind the computation. Professor Rimanyi teaches in a way that respects the beauty of mathematics, and his lectures were great. The exams are tough, but there is a fair curve.

Rimanyi is the best lecturer Ive ever had at UNC. He is accessible and extremely intelligent. You understand his material well. His section is very much proof based compared to others. The exams are rough tbh. But he's fair because he curved us A LOT. For reference I had a 94 hw avg, 55 mid1, 76 mid2, (didnt release final grade), and got a B.
Such a nice guy but can get too into theory. The tests were so hard. Thought I failed the final but I guess so did everyone else. Other profs had easier tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Rimanyi is a unique linear instructor on campus in that he emphasizes the importance of understanding concepts rather than simply computing problems. He does a very good job of explaining concepts in lecture, and has supplemental videos uploaded to Canvas for personal review. Tests are proof-heavy, but not bad if you do problem practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures are great, and I learned a lot. I am awful at proofs, and did no better in this class at them than in others. They make up large majority of test and homework problems. He also never released our final exam grades so idk what I got. But he must have placed a large curve because I ended up with a B. Hes a nice guy, but tests are hard.

If you are reading this, and if your not a math major, please do not take this class with this guy. He's not a bad person, he's lectures are not bad, however, the midterms are really hard. There is only 5 questions in midterms, and 9 in the final. Almost all of the questions are proof based. Really hard class. I got better in my discrete class.

Great professor. First of his lectures were great. He would connect the math to the real world which was cool. His first exam was hard, but I would say the second exam and the final were definitely better. I would say really study the textbook! The proofs are not bad, the textbook is really helpful to solve them.

Dr. Rimanyi was amazing. This class is very proof/concept heavy (more so than other linear sections). But he does a great job relating theory to computation.
Tests are pretty difficult imo; combination of proofs/computation/TF.
He's a really nice guy and made linear algebra so interesting.
Good curve at the end that makes up for hard tests.

Very smart guy but this course covers more theory than other sections. Linear algebra is very easy computationally but this class requires computations done by hand on exams and are also a lot of proofs / theory based questions as well. You'll learn a lot but a less in depth course would still have been adequate for most majors

Absolute GOAT, best prof I've had at UNC. Great lecturer, explains concepts clearly, entertaining guy, tells jokes and funny stories in class. Cares a lot about student learning and very helpful in office hours. Has reasonable expectations for this course and is fair to students in terms of grades. Char limit is too short to say enough good things.

Very nice person and is extremely intelligent, delivering very interesting and in depth lectures. You are certain to learn a lot in his class. That being said, his exams are extremely difficult and the final was horrendous. He gives proofs and really vague true or false on the exam that are very hard and just not fair at all.
I have scarcely felt melancholy after the conclusion of a course.

Rimanyi is definitely a great professor and explains concepts very clearly. However, tests are HARD and the proof-based homework problems are tricky as well. It is a more difficult math 347 section, especially if you have never had exposure to the topic or this is your first college math class. Rimanyi is great though and pretty accessible.

Any reviews negative towards Rimanyi are reviewing the class, not the professor. Rimanyi is an understanding, funny, and clearly intelligent professor. He explains difficult concepts in great depth and tries his best not to leave any student behind. He is VERY strict on test grades, but our period constantly outscores others. Take 233 with Rimanyi.

Very good in comparison to all math professors at UNC. Did lots of practice problems in class and his lectures were very clear. Midterms were very short and can be easy if you study. Would highly recommend.

He cares a lot about his students and wants them to succeed. He tries his best to ensure students understand the material and gives everyone extensions on homework. This class was hard for me since I'm not used to lecture-based classes and I got a D on the first exam. I ended up mostly teaching myself with Khan Academy but his lectures were helpful

It's calc, so the class sucks, but he was a nice lecturer. Not sure why other reviews say he didn't do practice problems in class because a lot of the midterm/final questions directly mirror class examples. Recitation topics don't always line up, which is annoying, but if you review those problems as well, you should be prepared for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Amazing lectures. Explain concepts well and provide great examples. Respect students and answer questions clearly. Tests are pretty easy, no hard calculations and memorization. Just go to class and do the homework. Two midterms each worth 20% and final worth 35%. Homework might take some time but not too bad, take at most two hours.

Rimanyi is an excellent professor who explains concepts very clearly and also cracks a few jokes here and there. Every homework is due one week later than you should actually be doing it to account for extenuating circumstances and essentially give students an extension on every homework should they need it. His exams are very easy as well.

Rimanyi is a great professor. He records his lectures and posts them online. He also assigns homework weeks before they are due (the due date is much later than you should be doing them) so you don't have to ask for extensions if you get sick or are really busy in other classes. Midterms are really easy if you study and do lots of practice.

The homework assigned was the worst part just because of how long it took.  Could easily get a 100 though.  Rimanyi explained everything very clearly and was helpful staying after class to clarify concepts and interacted with the class well.  Midterms and final were not hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had. Great lectures, clear guidelines, accessible in office hours. The class is hard and the midterms/final were hard, but he curves a little bit at the end I think.

Pros: Great lecturer. HE LIVESTREAMS AND POSTS EVERY LECTURE, which was sooooo helpful if you don't want to go to class. He curves the final grades to make the average a B.

Cons: Half of each midterm was fill in the blank questions with NO PARTIAL CREDIT. This can obliterate your midterm grades. His midterms are also harder than other profs imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rimanyi is THE BEST! Calc 3 is objectively a tough course but he makes concepts seem intuitive and digestible.
