Professor Valladres has been one of the best professors I have had at UNC. She doesn't so much care about grades but only that we are growing as learners. Her lectures are interesting and the assignments aren't too difficult but require you to do a little bit of research and use your thinking skills. Ultimately learned a lot from her.

10/10 take this class! Dr. Valladares is so sweet and caring and a very easy grader. Class time is primarily a powerpoint lecture on a topic. Don't really have to show up or do the readings to get an A since short, easy essays make up most of the grade. My final average was a 100! She offers extra credit opportunities too. WB and BN credits!

Professor Valladares is absolutely wonderful. Her lectures are very informative and interesting and she is a very lenient grader. She is also a very sweet woman, which only adds to how great of a teacher she is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: I took Hellenistic Art and Archaeology with Professor Valladares. The class itself was fantastic and Professor Valladares did an amazing job making the class interesting and thought provoking through her lectures. Definitely would recommend to anyone who is interested in art history or Greek art.

Herica is such an amazing woman. She really cares about getting to know her students and figuring out what we are passionate about. She's somewhat disorganized, but owns up to it and then makes the class easier for the students because she feels bad. I highly recommend getting to know her if you're interested in Classics or Art History.

Herica really cares about her students and she herself interesting. The lectures are kind of dry, but look engaged and you'll be fine. It's a small class and she will care if you miss a bunch. There are readings for every class, but I stopped doing them and it was fine. Short reflection essays and in-class essays, but I never got below a 90.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Herica was a great professor. Honestly the topic of the class is kind of dry, but she was able to make it more interesting because of her personal connection to the class and her history with the topic. There are several short essays and a couple of decent essays to write in this class, but it is totally worth your time!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Life in Ancient Pompeii: interesting to some; boring to others.  Regardless, Valladares is one of the best people to learn about it from as she is very knowledgeable.  The course isn't hard and she is a very easy grader (I got a 90 and above on every assignment).  Put in a decent amount of effort on the assignments and you'll get an A.

Dr Snider is really caring, his lectures are great, and provides good slides. WA helped me understand the content though they can be time consuming. I wouldn't take the class if I didn't have the time to study for it, but the content is super interesting. He likes questions at the end of class, feedback from students and is open to improvements.

Probably my favorite prof ive ever had. Easily the most knowledgeable. I didn't apply myself to the fullest extent and got the grade I deserved because of that. You can get an A if you try hard for an A. Very very smart and cares about his students a lot! Love him
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Snider is very knowledgeable and covers many aspects of the systems neuroscience field in an up-to-date way which I loved. The exams were fairly written. He often speeds through lecture slides so be prepared to review after class. I would recommend taking this class if you're looking for a challenging but rewarding class.

Dr. Snider is great - he genuinely cares about getting to know his students. The course material is super relevant to emerging research in neuroscience but is challenging. The tests are most
of the grade and are detailed, but are very fair and if you study the powerpoints you'll do fine. Attendance isn't scored but participation in discussions is

Currently as a research tech in neurobiology, I think this class was the most useful class in undergrad. If you want to do any type of wet lab neuroscience research such a great course to do so. Yes the class is hard, but it's by far the most relevant and up to date class I've taken that teaches you about systems neuroscience.

If you want to continue to pursue the field of neuroscience or psychology, do NOT take this professor. He only gives you lecture slides to study, nothing else, and he doesn't let you see review past exams at all. The class is supposed to be PRINCIPLES of brain circuits and he expects you to know every intricacy of every circuit. I despise this man.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This prof is not accommodating to people with ARS. Other than that, he really isn't that bad. His exams are very detailed and you need to know almost everything that's in the slides. But if you study well the tests are very doable. He curves every exam so that the average is ~85%, so some people end up with over 100. Papers are straightforward too.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Baffled by the good reviews. Most of my interactions with him were nice, but for 1/3 tests he printed off the wrong one, noticed before class, lectures instead, and did NOT tell students at ARS. We took the test 2 days before the main class with no notice or effort to make up for the non-accommodation students getting the benefit of more study time
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cannot imagine taking this course with any other professor - Dr. Snider is the GOAT!  Dr. Snider is extremely knowledgeable about his field and truly makes an effort to get to know every student well! Be ready to work really hard to get a good grade in this course though, as LOTS of very challenging concepts are covered throughout the semester.

I'd describe him as the Neuroscience department's Tiani. Not the friendliest, but you accept it because easier tests. Beware of papers: read a recent publication, then make a 900-word (max) essay about it, due 30 hours after it is assigned. Lightly read the textbook, don't cram, and you'll be fine. Other reviews exaggerate his difficulty.

Dr. Snider is a very caring professor, & he will go out of his way to personally ask how to support and help you succeed. But the course material is TOUGH & requires a lot of time. I don't recommend if you already have heavy STEM course load for the semester. Dr. Snider is great and knows the material in and out, but not a light class by any means.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He makes a real effort to get to know his students (learns everyone's name) and wants you to come to office hours. The class isn't easy, but definitely doable if you put in the work. His tests aren't too bad if you study and he curves them normally. He also loves class discussions, so be prepared to ask questions at the end of class.

Dr. Snider was one of the best NSCI profs I've had at UNC. Definitely knows every nook and cranny of the course he's teaching and can teach it to you regardless of your background. Recommend having taken Genetics and Cell Bio to help you get up to speed with all of the experimental techniques he teaches. Go to lectures and ask questions immediately
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Snider is very passionate about the material and enjoys getting to know his students on a personal level. He wants your participation and for the class to ask questions. He definitely knows his stuff, and his slideshows have everything you need to succeed. Lots of material, but it's legitimately 'cutting-edge' stuff that's just been discovered
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Snider is an amazingly intelligent person in his field. Sometimes the material could get super complicated, but he was usually able to speak to everyone's level. It would be best to have a genetics background for this class, but it isn't required to be successful. Tests were simple (but long) and never tricky if you studied for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Liu is a GREAT prof. He rescheduled two exams to fit classes needs, includes extra credit, and has great lectures. He is hilarious, and very good at explaining concepts. Highly recommend taking. If you pay attention, you will get an A.

Professor Liu is very caring and understanding. I struggled a bit for the exams but if you show up to class, pay attention, and start studying early you'll be fine. 
His lectures are great and really clear, and you can tell he cares about the subject and the class. Great professor, choose him!

Excellent professor. He explains things so well and he is very patient with his students. He is willing to repeat his explanations until everyone gets it. The only complaint I have is that he didn't let us struggle through the examples in class enough.

Dr. Liu is a very great lecturer who explains thing pretty well. His midterms and individual part for the final exam are easy. The common part of final exam is kinda challenging... but Dr. Liu's easy individual part really makes up for my bad grade in the common part. He is very accessible and really cares for the students. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!
GOAT, choose him
iconic guy. loved xinyun and his class. enthusiastic and caring

Amazing professor who does not rush through certain difficult topics of DE and actually spent time on the non-covered pre-requisite topics. Homework and test are pretty much identical---just go to lectures and write down notes and you will basically be guaranteed an A. Great professor overall and wish him the best! ^_^

Good choice for 383. Explains computational strategies well but theory isn't as good. Tests generally reflected homework and review assignments well with some challenging theory questiosn thrown in. Recommend taking 347 before or with this class.

Dr. Liu is a very understanding professor, and I really enjoyed his class. It wasn't my main focus this semester because I was also taking organic chemistry, but it had a manageable workload and the content on tests was extremely fair. He is an engaging lecturer and really wants his students to succeed!

Material was not overly difficult and his lectures were very clear and organized. He cares about how students are doing in class and will continue to help until you fully understand the material. Liu was an incredibly nice teacher and I would absolutely take him for another class again.
Great professor. He is very excited about the material and makes sure that everyone understands.
Great Guy. Easy A

Xinyun was a good professor. He was always accessible outside of class and was always willing to help you understand the content better. The exams were more than fair difficulty and the homeworks were at a good difficulty to understand the content better. Sometimes, he inserts an unexpected joke that always lands. Overall, highly recommend.

Professor Liu was great. I loved watching him get progressively covered in chalk throughout the lectures. 

Seriously though, Professor Liu is a great guy and his lectures cover enough content so reading the textbook is unnecessary. My only note is that there can sometimes be a slight language barrier when asking questions.

Xinyun is a good time! Never read the textbook and was able to get all necessary content from lecture which typically ended early for time to ask questions about HW (or eat lunch early lol). He's funny in class and cares a lot. I can't recommend him more.
She's just professional and cares about students. She made things more flexible for students even during a hard time. I got more feedback than I expected as a junior. I will say take her class again!

She's the nicest professor I've ever met at UNC! She hopes students can learn from the course and makes the course as easy as possible. The topic is interesting and we have lots of case study about different worldwide cities, such as Chicago, Beijing, etc. She is very reachable after class. I will definitely take her class again.

She cared about her students and was very enthusiastic about teaching. Attendance was not taken and the class was graded by 7 short open-note quizzes, a presentation, two papers, and a final. All were very easy.
She's very kind and sweet, and always willing to help her students with anything.

She was always available to help and had the best, most welcoming attitude. She tried to make learning the material fun and enjoyable, and I believe she succeeded. One of the best professors I have ever had. She cares so much about her students and her field.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It was clear that he had not taught for long, as he struggled a lot early on. His teaching got better over time, and he has office hours sections where he will sit and explain material to you. The first midterm was incredibly easy. The second midterm was a lot harder, but still chill if you study hard. Final is demonic, but he curves accordingly.

Tiger is a really funny and patient professor! He is very approachable and wants all students to do well in his class, but sometimes his explanations were hard to follow. Reading the textbook is optional, but I would highly recommend reading it + doing the practice problems if you want to do well in the class!

I left this class most days understanding the material! He starts with easier content and then builds on it so we have the foundation to understand harder concepts. Some proofs can be a little abstract, but lots of practice can help you be prepared for tests. His study guides were helpful but looking up other practices can be helpful.

Office hours and in-class questions were available and very helpful. The second midterm and final were more challenging than the first test, but he curved generously at the end. The textbook aligns well with the course material and is a useful reference

At the begining of this class he did not really know how to teach well, but as the class went on he got better. There are 3 exams, homework due usually every Wednesday and a final. On exam 2 and exam 3  we got opportunities for extra credit which are the harder exams that really helped my grade. If you pay attention to lectures you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher don't take if u want to learn

He's so passionate about chem and has a molecule of the day, that said the chem department is evil so you probably won't do too well on exams. Lecture can get boring but I think that's honestly any chem lecture. Use your resources.
Professor Warren is decent at explaining concepts, textbook is easy enough to understand to fill in the necessary gaps. Exams are reasonable, no trick questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. He is out of tough and doesn't relate the reading, lectures and homework. He will test you on material that was never discussed. Test are impossible and he gives almost no credit for work. Doesn't respond to emails and out right rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He does not know how to teach. His exams are insane. I had him over a covid semester and he didn't even record his lectures for students that could quite literally not make it to class. He makes you hate chemistry even if you loved it going in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Literally hands down the worst professor for chemistry. I am now in OCHEM and came here to say how much i hate this man. He deserves to be fired for the way he treats his students. He explains everything poorly, doesn't help in office hours and his tests are pulled out of nowhere. I am telling you please avoid him and you may be happy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: To be frank, online chem102 with Dr. Warren was the worst class I've ever taken. The tests were EXTREMELY difficult and covered content that wasn't discussed in class or the assigned readings. However, Dr. Warren is a very nice guy himself and tried to help students. I think he was more limited by chem department mandates.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: As an otherwise straight-A student, this class butchered my mental health. The tests didn't reflect the class content, which I thought I understood; I did well on daily quizzes but not on tests. Warren was best choice of 3 profs, but department is bad, no curves or EC. I hope no one ever has to take it online again. Ended w/ a 79.3... so annoying!

Thought Chem 101 was a breeze and expected 102 to be slightly more difficult but I was wrong. Warren made the class 10x harder than necessary. The material covered during lecture only covered the surface, while the exams required in depth knowledge and problem solving skills that hardly anyone was prepared for. Any other prof will be better.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I appreciate that Dr. Warren allowed students to ask questions whenever we were confused about anything. He truly loves chemistry and that was well reflected in so many ways.

Scott Warren is one of those professors who only teaches because it's a requirement of doing research at the university. With such poor quality lectures and lazily written exams with an incredibly short amount of time to take them, it's no wonder the class exam averages are always in the low 60s. If you take him, you're basically on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: i didn't do great in the class, but that's on me. after bombing the first exam, i met with dr. warren and he gave me tips to improve my studying. my grades improved on the remaining exams. so glad i had dr. warren.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He messed up our final grades and stressed an entire class of student out telling us our grades were wrong. To add, the test average was terrible and the class in general is a risk to take. Its not even a hit or miss with this professor, it is simply a miss. You will do poorly and that is a promise. Good luck :)
I passed and I would still advise any students to not take this class at this university. if you think you're different good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He was very involved with the class and did all that he could in order to make himself available to students and get questions answered. His problemsolving sessions every Friday via Zoom were very helpful and helped me understand loopholes within the information. Overall, he has been the best professor I have had at UNC.

Chemistry is pretty hard to learn online, but Dr. Warren is a hero. He stayed online after every class until each student got their questions answered. Sometimes that was 30 minutes or more. Because of him, I came to understand chemistry so much better than I would otherwise.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Ok this class was so hard for no reason. They told us to study the textbook, and when it was time for the test the questions were 10x harder than I ever studied. I heard that the peer mentors make the tests (which may be wrong), but they were unnecessarily hard. Overall, the online nature of the class might have made it harder, so don't be alarmed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Like mostly everyone has said, this is the worst professor you can possibly have. I literally would ask a question in class and he would never know the answers. The people who say he is great are the students that are local Einstein's. If you are the average Joe or a little smarter, RUN! If you know everything by the time you walk in this is it!
worst professor in the university, the tests are the hardest ever, RUN
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Warren is one of my favorite professors I have had at UNC! I go to his problem solving sessions and his office hours. He is always so positive and willing to answer questions. The two times I have gone to his office hours, he does not just answer your questions but asks about you as an individual and your interests. So glad I took his class.
amazing!! a great teacher, clearly cares, and shows kindness and enthusiasm to everyone.

Professor Warren was a great instructor and he was very approachable about anything. His teaching was better than other chemistry teachers I have had and he was very helpful in explaining a concept, and in fixing anything wrong with exam grading.
Learning chemistry remotely was challenging for me, but Dr. Warren's enthusiasm and dedication to normalcy made the situation as good as it could have been.

While I never met with Dr. Warren outside of class, when I asked questions in class he was extremely helpful and enthusiastic to help. In addition, his general positive attitude and love of chemistry made it worth coming to class to learn.

Chem 102 is a hard class no matter what. In an online format, Warren showed little sympathy and made the tests obviously harder from previous years. I felt the lectures did not prepare me for the difficulty of the tests. Although he seems like a very nice guy who is passionate about chemistry, This class was impossible.

While prof. Warren was one of the better options available, he was not lenient at all and was often unable to answer administrative questions (and would even tell us the wrong due dates for items at times). Exams were incredibly difficult compared to lectures, and the hw took forever and was often unnecessarily hard. Definitely a weed-out class.

I don't post on RMP much, but Professor Warren is one of the worst professors I've had at UNC. Granted, the CHEM department is notoriously difficult and CHEM102 is no different, but Professor Warren's lectures are dry and often times not clear about the course material. Exams are extremely difficult, coupled with difficult homework and worksheets
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This Professor does not explain anything and continues to lecture. The tests are literally impossible and completely unfair. This class online was made to make you fail. I studied for weeks before each exam just to receive a 50 on each one. I am a straight A student and this class was beyond impossible. The test a averages were 50-60. Run!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I don't post on RMP often, but I think Dr. Warren deserves it because he is a professor who will listen to you and readily answers your questions even outside of class. He once stayed on for a whole hour after class to explain chemistry concepts to me and a few other students. Therefore, I think you will have a better chance of succeeding with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would take the negative comments about Dr. Warren for a grain of salt as online teaching during COVID made classes harder. This is a hard course that covers broad content and requires practice every day. Dr. Warren is nice and open to helping his students succeed if you truly work for it (attend office hr, practice sessions, ask Q's).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Did a great job breaking down some of the more difficult concepts (like redox rxns) into simple steps. Very approachable and open to questions. The course was hard and I had to do a lot of work outside of class to get a good grade, but Warren helped set a good foundation for most of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: A solid choice for CHEM 102. CHEM 102 is hard no matter who you have, but Dr. Warren is great.

Unless you can completely teach yourself and you dont rely on professors youll be fine. This sucks for students who actually need professors to teach because Warren isnt a very gifted one (which isnt fair since were all paying a lot for tuition and professors who can teach should be a part of it).

Let me tell you something "I've been hoodwinked, bamboozled, lead astray, run amok and flat out deceived" by Warren's past year reviews. He make online class so much harder and most of the time I would have to go to Kochar's slide just to study for the midterms. And the funniest thing is that his blue or white shirt been to more class than I have
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I greatly enjoyed Dr. Warren's teaching and feel like I learned a lot. He even made online lectures interesting by doing chemistry demos.

Dr. Warren is very caring towards students: accessible outside class, responsive to e-mails, MORE than willing to answer questions. He helps those who help themselves by asking questions, going to office hours, and problem-solving sessions, but the class was hard as midterms count for essentially everything. Do practice problems & pre-readings.

I wanted to like Dr. Warren more than I did. He seems like a really nice person, but I don't think his teaching style is the best. I was frustrated because the 102 teachers took turns making the tests, and I felt like his lectures didn't go over what was on the exams written by the other profs. Problems done in class are very surface level.

He cares way too much about his battery research than his students. And it felt like he would just talk and talk, but none of it would make sense. By the end of this class, nobody was actually really paying attention because he wasn't very helpful and the exams were super tough. Just make sure to read the textbook and keep up the notes.

He definitely was a solid choice for 102. The only thing that sucked was that the professors all took turns making the exams, so when the others made them, some of the questions could be difficult to answer. However, I was still able to make As on the exams, but you 100% should do the assigned book problems and attend office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is just terrible and there's not much the professor can do to help that. But he did a good job explaining chem concepts and he's a real nerdy guy. Just study for the tests. Those are impossible.

He types the solutions for the practice problems on his notes, this can be helpful when reviewing his lecture notes later because the work is shown. However, in class he just verbally walks through the work shown which can be very confusing. He tends to skip important steps needed to understand baseline concepts, I recommend Kochar's notes.
He's an amazing professor. I thought he was great at explaining the topics and was open to answering all questions. I would definitely recommend taking a chem class with Dr. Warren!

I seldom post on RateMyProfessor. But Prof. Warren deserves this. He is inspirational. Period. Does an exemplary job of breaking down those tough acid-base questions. He's also very friendly. After all, it's a Chem class at UNC, so be ready to read. But Dr. Warren is always there for you. To me, he's a Chem god. Reason why I'm now a Chem major.

Excellent professor for CHEM 102! He is so positive, lectures clearly, and explains material thoroughly. I felt that he prepared us well for the exams, and his exam review lectures were very helpful in tying concepts together. He made the concepts relatable and class enjoyable by tying examples from his research and the world in general.

Warren's lectures made the relatively dry subject of general ed chemistry more interesting, but the class as a whole was very hard. Would highly recommend his class for CHEM102 - it's a difficult class to do well in but he's a great professor and makes it enjoyable. Sense of humor 10/10.

Warren is a really cool guy. I heard he was young and kinda new so I chose him over Bliem and Tiani and I don't regret it. Very good lecturer, very smart and pretty funny. Connected lectures to the work he was doing in the UNC labs. He made this otherwise tough class fun to attend. Highly recommend.

Prof. Warren was a great teacher. He was clearly passionate about the material, and stayed after every class to answer questions if you had them. Prof. Warren was always helpful during office hours too. Definitely recommend taking him for this course.
Dr. Warren is really cool and he really cares about his students. He gives a lot of good feedback and handles regrade requests quickly. I enjoyed his class and found him to be extremely knowledgeable
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Warren really cares about teaching the class in a clear way and uses lots of interesting examples. I attended his office hours often and he's very helpful and kind.
Scott is such a sweet guy! He's really quiet, but super passionate about the course material. He truly cares about his students well being and success in the course. Overall a wonderful professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Warren is new to teaching, which is clear in the way he talks, but he is really helpful and almost always available for questions, which, in gen chem, you'll have tons of. He explains concepts well, though he tends to go off on tangents sometimes if it's a topic he's really passionate about. Be sure to read and practice outside of class.

Clicker quizzes are based on accuracy (usually 2 questions). I love how he sometimes tries to make chemistry jokes after a spectacular event or something interesting has happened! However, he does not look directly at the class when he teaches. Extremely patient. I will give him credit for teaching CHEM 102 for the first time.

Professor Warren is super helpful and really tries to be open and receptive to questions. He actually answers what is asked. He is a good teacher and does a good job explaining difficult question. It is chem it is gonna be hard no matter what
Everything is extremely fair, give feedback real quick. I am not a math person, but I did better than I thought in this class. My favorite professor!
She is definitely the best professor I have ever met at Kenan Flagler! Would love to take her class again!

She's a really good prof, the material is fairly easy and up until the final its pretty fair. The final was painful also she puts in grades extremely fast (same day we took the final) the final was really hard so just prep for that. I did not hence the grade (had an A all sem)

Dr. Xu truly cares about her students! She teaches at a very fast pace so we always get out of class early. She's very eager to answer questions and make sure students are successful. She also is open to helping students in non-class related things

Professor Xu is a fun and engaging professor. Her class covers all the content you need to know and I felt I had everything I needed to thrive. Class consists of problem sets, 2 midterms, a final, and a group project. the final was the hardest part of the class, but overall, I enjoyed this course and would take Professor Xu again.

Great teacher that clearly cares about her students. Class was pretty straightforward until the final which felt like it was trying to hurt our grades. Dropped a fair amount of people a full letter grade. Just be well prepared for an entirely different final and you're good

I'm so glad I took this class with Professor Xu! I've learned so much over the semester. She's super smart, but what really stands out is how inspiring and encouraging she is. She has this amazing way of making you feel confident and excited to learn, which makes the class even better!
Professor Xu is fantastic! Explains concepts super clearly, is always accessible for questions, and has very fair exams! Genuinely the sweetest professor!
Easy to understand everything. Awesome class.
Great class, take it if you can!
I love this class!

Professor Xu is the best professor I have ever had at KFBS. Materials and exams are hard, but still manageable if you spend a reasonable amount of time studying. She even replied to my question at 1 am!!! Would take any other courses that Xu teaches at KFBS!

Class was extremely misleading. HWs and midterm was quite easy but for some reason, she decided to make the final very difficult with no practice material being nearly as rigorous as the final. Would recommend taking with another professor. There are definitely other sections that are much easier.

Final was brutal given that both midterms were easy and that problem sets were also easy. Xu is really sweet and is a lovely person, but the final really felt like she was out to get us/bring down the class average.
Final absolutely screwed me over by a whole letter grade. Lectures I will say were very understandable, but holy cow, brace yourself for the final to see things beyond the scope of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yuqian is a great teacher and person, but I disagree with other reviews. Class is extremely test-heavy and the final was surprisingly difficult compared to other exams and course sections. Final dropped my final grade 3 thirds of a letter grade.

Professor Xu is attentive to student's needs and is genuinely just such a sweet professor. She's very fair with midterms and really cares about the wellbeing of students. Please take her class, it is worth your time, and I wished I did more to connect with her.
Xu was probably the best teacher I've had at KFBS. Such a positive person who would always smile and answer any questions I had. PLEASE take her if you have a chance
unbelievably easy class. the content is literally for middle schoolers. Xu is nice and cares a lot about teaching but the fact the class content is so easy makes it hard to rate her low

Professor Xu is an outstanding professor at KFBS. She is clear about her expectations and what she wants you to do to succeed in this course. I learned a lot from this class and her. She is also very understanding and caring. She doesn't make you stay for an entire lecture if it's not necessary. Review all slides and homeworks before exams

Professor Xu definitely made this class very understandable and easy to succeed in. She is clearly very intelligent and has a very impressive background. Despite that, she is not arrogant or short with students but is always willing to answer questions and make the material as simple and applicable as possible. Definitely would recommend.
Super nice professor. Easy material and clear explanation. She even replied to my email within 1 minute at 1 AM.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Xiaoming is a kind professor who is very passionate about what she teaches. She is slightly disorganized, and slow with grading, but she makes it relatively easy for students to succeed. She doesn't take attendance, and it's not necessary to come to every class.
She is very passionate about the topics!
She is super passionate about the topic and willing to help you to understand it!

Xiaoming as a person is a really nice lady but as a teacher, leaves much to be desired. Attendance isn't mandatory so only about 40% of the class shows up on a regular basis. I attended every class but didn't get much out of it. I wondered "why am I here?" The slides are boring and can be accessed online. Not a terrible class but needs improvement.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Xiaoming Liu is a good professor. The class only consist only of three exams and attendance isn't mandatory. Make sure that if you aren't going to attend class you keep up with the powerpoints which are all uploaded. If you can't hold yourself accountable avoid this class.

I would steer away from taking a class with Xiaoming. Her class this semester was solely based on exams. There were no attendance checks, quizzes, or projects to motivate you throughout the semester. Many people did not show up to class and didn't do so great on exams because attendance is not checked.

Xiaoming was an excellent professor! The only grades were attendance (Poll Everywhere in class) and tests. She did a fantastic job making this class a really fun introduction to geology, and covered the entertaining topics like earthquakes and volcanoes heavily.

Xiaoming is extremely sweet and approachable. She understands that it is an intro level class that most people are taking for gen ed credit and even tells you that reading the textbook is not necessary. Her only grades are two midterms, the finals, and participation so it is essential you study for tests, but overall not a hard class.

Xiaoming is a sweetheart. She is really kind and you can tell she wants her students to understand and love geology the way that she does. With that being said, I found it difficult to pay attention in this class, for whatever reason. The material is not terribly difficult to understand, so take some notes and you should be fine.

Very structured and clear-cut class. Xiaoming is a wonderful person and she teaches the material very well. I'd highly recommend for students to take this class whether they are interested in geology or just trying to fulfill a Gen-Ed. Take caution though- you will have to study the lecture slides hard to get an A.
Extremely sweet and helpful woman! I took the class for the mandatory science credit and was dreading it and she has made the class enjoyable and bearable. Wonderful lady!

I really like her as a person, she was very approachable and you can tell she knows what she is talking about. However, lectures were pretty uninspiring and the tests were horrendously written. Good news is about half of the questions on her exams are free points, but the others were often very ambiguous and did not focus on core concepts.

Dr. Bustamante-Marin is a GENIUS in the field and is very knowledgeable. She's the sweetest person if you take the time to actually talk to her. That said, she is a tough grader with exams with tricky wording (which she will not give points back on), and omg the lectures are so fast with sometimes 100s of slides. you learn a lot! DONT CRAM!!

Though Dr. Marin may seem strict, she is genuinely really nice! Class content is difficult and requires a lot of memorization to be prepared on tests, so definitely do not study last min! But it is really interesting to learn if you are interested in nutrition. Her office hours were pretty helpful to go over exams or any content related questions!

unclear guest lectures. exams questions not released for review. course flow doesn't make sense. homework doesn't impact class grade. often quizzed before lecture on the topic. bar for an a is too high (94). overall her lectures were unclear. difficult to anticipate exam qs. she is somewhat nice but i wish she would've cared more.

Dr. Marin a little more on the serious side and she goes through slideshows fast. There's LOADS of information and cramming will not do you any good. BUT Dr. Marin DOES care about you. If you're not doing well, she will personally reach out to you to chat. She's understanding and wants you to do well. But don't take this class unless you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think Professor Bustamante-Marin. While the class was difficult, it was not as bad as it sounds. If you make sure to review the lecture slides and take notes on the textbook, you should do fine on exams. This class is not as hard as others at UNC, but I would not recommend taking if not required for your major.

Dr. Marin is overhated. Just study the slides thoroughly and they align pretty well with the exams, tho some questions on the exams were pretty tricky + I didn't find the textbook to really be of use. Dr. Marin was very helpful and accessible to me in and out of class and really did want the best for me. She comes off blunt but is truly caring

Horrible class. Lectures make no sense, she reads off the slides word for word with no explanation. Test style is horrible. Practice exam answer key was wrong ALL the time, so do not even waste your time. Practice exams looked nothing like the real exam. This class is straight memorization and is very content heavy. She is also very rude.

This is the hardest class I've ever taken, mostly self-study. The professor is smart but just reads off the slides. Exams are entirely based on the slides, so skip the textbook—just memorize the slides, including wordless images. Her exams are extremely tough. You have no option tho she the only profressor and her accent does not help.

This professor is very knowledgable about the subject but fails to transfer that knowledge to her students. She is very blunt and if you don't know the information inside and out she gets frustrated with you which makes it difficult to ask questions. I dedicated so much time and effort to this course and was barely scraping by with a B.

very few grades were put in the grade book (2 midterms, 20ish quizzes, recitation, & final). average for the midterms (worth 40% of our grade) was a c. the midterms were incredibly hard and very detail heavy & based on like 5 30-40 slide ppt so lots of memorization. also, lectures were just her reading of the slides (so hard to learn based on that)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Marin is a sweetheart, but at times her lectures seemed very rushed and lack luster as she read word-for-word from slideshows. She is very knowledgeable though! I wish she were able to translate that knowledge better for us. Very caring lady and funny. This course overall was challenging for me, even though I've taken upper level chem and biol.

Dr. Marin is caring, but exams are difficult, and you need to memorize EVERYTHING from slides. She read off the slides and moved SUPER fast in lecture, so I needed to spend lots of time outside class. Make sure to do the EC. Only 1 section, so don't take it if you don't need to, but also don't let it stop you from applying to the Nutrition major.

Nice person but genuinly the hardest grader at UNC. When I took this class, I was surprised at the fact that it easily surpassed the horrors of the chem department. 
The class, hard as is, tests on biochemical metabolic reactions without us given background information how they work. Also, get ready to be tested on the most minute details possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Seems like a nice person, and very knowledgable at the subject, but for your own sake take with another professor! Genuinely one of the most difficult classes I've taken at UNC, and I've taken a good amount of chem and bio.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TAKE NUTR 240 WITH SOMEONE ELSE. Dr. Marin seems incredibly smart, but intelligence does not equal good at teaching. Her exams are insanely difficult, and when the class average was a C for BOTH midterms, she placed the blame on the students. Her expectations of us were far too high for the quality of teaching she provided. 0/10

Her expectations of us were far too high for the quality of teaching she provided. 0/10

reviews.comment: Her teaching style involves reading off the slides. She expected her students to know everything in the PowerPoint and the textbook. She would not give hints about what we were expected to know. This class is a big time commitment, and homework is not a part of your grade. Her exam questions are sometimes confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are boring. They only go over a small part of the assigned readings, so you are basically teaching yourself. If you read the chapters you could skip the lectures. Exams are hard. Multiple select questions. For example, the choices would be A; B; C; A & B; or A , B, & C. Over half of the test consist of question in this format.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Genuinely worst course I've taken at this university. I am in orgo at the same time and am even doing better in that class. She reads off the slides, tests are unbearably hard, and I have had a medical emergency, and she refuses to even take that into consideration or even respond to emails regarding the situation in terms of points.
Awful experience!

So much to say, so little words. Lectures were a waste of time, she reads directly off the slides and still finds a way to tell us inaccurate information (takes a true genius to do that). Dont bother asking questions because she wont answer them. Pros - she's funny and sarcastic, really appeals to my sense of humor. My advice, dont take this class.

Professor Marin reads directly off of the slides. The class purely based on memorization and the tests are built to trick you. I am a nutrition major and am interested in the subject, but she made this class miserable.

Dr. B-M reads directly off her slides. You are expected to teach yourself many of the learning objectives outside of class, as well as memorize nearly slide she presents (usually upwards of 30-40 per class). Unengaging and entirely depends on your ability to memorize as much information as possible before tests. Do not take unless you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only reads the slides in lecture and expects you to memorize 400 slides for exams. Exams were mostly multi-select questions with no partial credit! She doesn't take feedback well, when a question directly from the practice exam was on our exam we all got it marked wrong because her practice exam key was wrong but she refused to give us points back.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is an unorganized lecturer who just reads off the slides. There is almost no clarity about what content will be on exams. This is her first time teaching the course so it could improve but given her response to feedback I wouldn't expect it. The exams are very large parts of your grade and have lots of content along with unclear questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I do not understand why this class so hard! The material is interesting, but the exams are legit impossible! She makes her exams in a way that trick you up!!!!!!!!!! The dumb A, B, C and AB are correct and that format just did not work with me! Take this class only if you wanna fail.
One of the best professors I've ever had!! He is so incredibly kind, really cares about his students, and makes a point of getting to know you. If you have the option, TAKE IT WITH HIM!
Dr. Yackulic was great at keeping us in the loop with Honors Carolina events and resources and has some super interesting anecdotes of his own.
This is a very easy pass/fail class and Dr. Yackulic is a very kind and understanding professor.

Professor Yackulic is amazing! He really cares for his students and gives great advice for freshman to use for their future college careers. Easy class, only five assignments total and a very easy final exam but class is pass or fail. Kayden Hunt is also an amazing TA!
Dr. Yackulic is a great guy who cares about his students. HNRS 101 is Pass/Fail with few assignments, so very easy to do well.
Great guy who cares, Honors 101 is super easy with almost no assignments
Extremely easy class. Dr.Yackulic is extremely easygoing and the class is very laidback.
Super nice and a great class. You learn lots of good skills for job searching and building your resume. Pass/Fail so just turn things in on time.

Dr. Y is a walking W. He's interesting, funny, caring, & inspirational. HNRS 101 is EXTREMELY easy: it has 6 simple assignments total & is graded on a P/F basis. There are a lot of resources you get exposed to, and the material can really help orient yourself at UNC. Just attend class, do your small, easy assignments, and you're done!
Great professor. Hopefully you are lucky enough to be stuck with him!
If you have to take HNRS 201 definitely take it with Dr. Y. Class was fun and he made some boring material interesting

This class was great. It was an introductory course to get familiar with the university and what resources we have access to. Some of the material isn’t the most exciting but he makes it fun and really cares about the students. Would definitely recommend!!

Dr. Huang teaches and links concepts well, but she overestimates students' computation skills, so the lecture can be hard to follow. Lectures can be better paced to increase attendance. Contents are pretty hard, but her tests are fair and much easier than hw in terms of high-level thinking. Providing more basic prob and calc practices should help.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hard class, have some exposure to probability/stats or this is going to suck. Gives really hard tests (all MCQ) but makes up for it by offering 4% of EC to your overall grade. Must do more problems beyond homework/classwork for practice, since there are so many topics covered we do not go over all relevant examples in assigned work.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Generous weighting and extra credit are blessings. She honestly provided good explanations and solidly attempted to engage our uninterested class. Your experience will likely be determined by previous exposure to the material. I'd imagine Zoe is the best option for 435 and would be excited if she was the average teacher in the STOR department.

Exams are worth 75% of your grade, so do not mess up. She gives 4% extra credit at the end, which was a little bit helpful. Lectures are pretty difficult to follow, so I recommend reading the textbook. Do not leave studying to the last minute and do a bunch of practice problems. Exams are all MC.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very difficult. practice every day. tons of stats majors and they bring up the average bc they have done stats before. i have no stats experience. this class was so difficult for me bc i did not have the time to sit down and practice. take this class with max 2 chill classes bc this one will be your priority. exams are all mcq (cries)

Very sweet.class is really hard. She explains stuff well but if you have never had any stats experience, it is really hard to keep up in class and it will probably take you hours longer to understand a problem than someone who has done stats before. its a completely new way of thinking that requires a TON of practice. read the textbook b4 lecture

1st midterm, 18 questions MCQ. Not difficult but if you have never taken a stats class, you NEED TO PRACTICE A TON. I am a math person and got a 56. It wasn't hard but it was just too much for the time. Practice, practice, and practice every waking moment you have. The hw is not enough, open the textbook and do everything. Find more probs online.

Clear schedule, clear lecture notes. U don't need to go to the lecture if u understand all the homework and lecture notes. There's also extra credit added to the final grade on midterms like 0.5%. I didn't get any grade yet but bro rescheduled the midterm to next week, which is huge for me bc otherwise I will have 3 midterms this week on 2 days lol

HWs were manageable, and tests were not too bad. The final is worth 45% of your grade, so make sure you don't mess up. Don't know if she even curved it towards the end, but the 3% EC she offered definitely helped. If you practice from the textbook you'll be absolutely fine, and the MCQ format for the tests help as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She tends to give about one homework assignment a week, which is very manageable. Her exams are multiple choice and are in many ways easier than the homeworks, so as long as you pay attention in class and go over the content in the homeworks and lecture slides you'll be fine. Be aware that difficulty ramps up significantly after the first exam.

this class isn't that bad... i would recommend not going to class and just doing reading from the textbook and doing the practice problems. i got a B+ but couldve pulled off an A if I didnt sell on the final

I went to a few classes before realizing she lectured pretty much directly from the textbook. However, this is not a bad thing -- it gives you the full freedom of whether you would rather read the textbook or go to lecture (I never went to lecture). She is very nice and the exams were quite easy (you can't really make a super hard MCQ stor exam).
She's super nice, but RUN. Midterms and final are hell.

Really nice professor. Homework is easy (takes like an hour to do each week). Exam are tough but fair. Study hard and you will at least get a B. If you put in the work, A range is definitely attainable.

Taking class 24F. If you are good/talented in math, take it. If not, consider others. Her class is full of proof with had nothing to do with exam. Exam based on textbook, so BUY IT and go over textbook before exam. Her practice exam is JOKE, no connection with exam. If you are not good with math, RUN. Did give 3% free EC. not sure with curve yet

Lectures were focused on proofs/theorems, but tests (which made up 75% of the grade) were entirely based on applications. To succeed, you have to do textbook practice problems on your own. She provided several extra-credit opportunities and was very accessible during office hours to explain HW (which was the main workload on a weekly basis).

Painfully boring lectures that aren't super helpful with completing the assignments. HW answers are pretty available online, and the exam questions are relatively fair. Final Exam was 45% (crazy) but there are some extra credit opportunities and the curve at the end hit like a truck.

cannot stress enough that you need to READ THE TEXTBOOK FOR PRACTICAL EXAMPLES. the lectures are proof-heavy so that you understand why the formulas are what they are. homeworks are short and simple, midterms are MC and directly lifted from the textbook/lecture examples. the textbook is very detailed and follows directly with the lecture proofs.

Don't bother with lectures. They are just 50 minutes of proofs and overcomplicated explanations of theorems and definitions while skipping most of the examples. Midterm 2 is cumulative. Gives subpar practice material that doesn't map onto the exams so just do examples from notes. Will curve if the average is low. She is pretty nice.

Great Professor for STOR 435! Go to the lectures and do homework carefully, you will succeed in this course. I don't know why others complained lectures were useless. Actually, it helped a lot. Also, go to the OH, it's really helpful! Professor Huang is sooo caring and gave 3% extra credits after final.

One of the best professors in STOR department! I learned lots of useful content from this course. Although I needed to spend some time to learn the proofs(not included in exam), it helps me in other higher-level stats and math courses. If you are interested in stats and want to learn something, take Professor Huang's course without any doubts!

Professor Huang's teaching is exceptional. The course content was extremely useful and well-structured. She proved a lot in class but all contents were useful. If you can understand in-class notes well, it's easy to complete homework and exams. There was a BIG curve here after final. So don't worry about your grade if you spend time in this course.

I am having a hard time understanding all of the negative press. Professor Huang is very clear during her lectures and thoroughly answered student questions. She also offered 3% extra credit on top of the final grade in addition to a generous curve. Just read the textbook, ask questions, and go to office hours and you will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A good grade and even a small social life are mutually exclusive in this course

Worst class I've taken at UNC. So much homework and the lectures will put you to sleep. She refuses to give practice problems because she doesn't want to put anything similar on the exams. Each midterm is 20% and has 12 multiple choice questions. Huge curve on the class thankfully, but this class will be the most painful 50 minutes of your day.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's her first semester here so people should cut her some slack. Exams were all mcq, but all 435 are like that, and the content was fair. Lectures were ok. Read the textbook, you don't even have to go to class. Do the HWs, she reuses them on her exams. I do wish we had more problems. Extra credit and great curve, raw grade was a B+
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was based almost entirely on 3 multiple choice exams. The lectures were majority proofs, with very few examples, making the exams overly difficult.

She spends most of the class time doing proofs rather than providing examples to explain the concepts. She moves extremely fast and barely explains difficult concepts.Two tests that are 12 question MC, which make up a significant portion (40%) of the overall grade. The final (40% of your grade) is a a MC test w/ no partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I don't understand people complaining about Zoe doing proofs/abstract concepts - I found that was most helpful/the best use of class rather than practice problems that you should do on your own time. I actually felt like I was learning what a distribution represents rather than a generic cookbook of formulas. Overall a great professor

She's an okay lecturer and her tests are hard, but not unfair. One issue, though, is that she does not provide enough practice material for the tests. If you want to do well, make sure to do the textbook problems and review the homework before the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although friendly, professor Huang's lectures are impossible to keep up with. One week she says she is uploading her notes and the next she says she has stopped. Exams are multiple choice but extremely difficult to understand. Her lectures include maybe 1 or 2 examples while the rest is just her doing proofs that aren't helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are not helpful when it comes to homework and exams. Exams are multiple choice and do not properly test knowledge of the course (almost impossible to adequately study for). She talks more about the philosophy of statistics and goes through difficult proofs during class rather than covering necessary material that is tested on.

Goes through the material as if everyone in the class has already seen it and just needs a quick glance to understand the topics. Does complicated proofs in class; homework and exams are unrelated and difficult. Unless you have already taken STOR 435 and know all the material, this is a terrible professor to have to start learning it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Huang moves very quickly and has had me lost in confusion since day 1 of the class. Her homework assignments often cover nothing done in class and as such I cannot practice what I learned. The class is graded 80% on multiple choice tests, but with no practice questions, I'm often lost on what to study. She is nice, but her class is very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Shemer's lectures are interesting. If you don't know a lot about Jerusalem, sometimes it can be difficult to follow some of the concepts he talks about, but he's always willing to answer questions and clarify when needed. Great person!

If you're taking it for the Gen-Ed, be aware that it's a decent amount of work, & unless you're really interested in film, you probably won't enjoy it. Dr. Shemer is very caring and a generous grader, but lectures can be mind-numbing. If you do the readings, watch the films, and participate, you WILL get an A, but don't expect a fun class.

Seems like a nice guy but I dreaded going to class. Drones on and on and I had a hard time following. On tests and essays he wanted me to parrot back what he taught, didn't appreciate me putting in my own perspective on things. A deep dive into Middle Eastern Cinema, but I came out of it still not understanding why that was important.

Highly recommend Professor Shemer. A lot of readings but interesting content, especially if you are interested in film studies. Class is almost entirely discussion, he values people who are vocal & do the readings. He is kind and invested in his student's success.

Professor Shemer was obviously deeply knowledgeable and passionate about the subject matter. While I personally do not even remotely care about Israeli cinema and psychoanalysis, his sheer enthusiasm was enough to get me through the lectures. He offers generous extra credit opportunities, so you should be able to succeed by virtue of showing up.

He gave me an 86.99 on purpose and wouldn't round to an 87, even though I was deserving of an A in the class by his own grading. The whole semester he was giving me A's until I said in class I disagree with him. The entire class is pro-Palestinian propaganda under the disguise of an Israeli class, and an absolute shame to the Israeli community.

Prof Shemer is a great professor who is able to convey information about the complexity of culture by analyzing several facets of the lived experience. He sometimes goes on tangents but overall I really enjoy the class discussions we have and the media we get to watch. Overall, I think he is a really great professor.

I love Prof Shemer. ASIA 425 (Beyond Hostilities: Collaborations in Culture between Israelis and Palestinians) was an incredible course. There are a lot of readings but he is a fair grader. Sometimes, he can go on tangents but the material was really fascinating and I could not recommend this class more.

The professor is great! He really made me think of Israeli cinema on a deeper level and the films watched were very interesting. There is not too much work to be done outside of class; as long as you at least scan the reading for the lecture/discussion you will be fine. He grades work very fairly and he wants you to succeed. Wonderful course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I found the class not having enough of the Palestinian perspective or very diluted. He also took away the Zoom option and was not flexible with problem going through circumstances.
Yaron Shemer is a horrendous professor.

This class is pretty easy, although there are a lot of outside readings and films that you are expected to watch/read and fully absorb. There aren't many graded assignments, but Shemer is not a very tough grader, so it shouldn't be too much of an issue. There are also extra credit assignments throughout the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Shemer is very passionate about Israeli film and that shows through in his lectures. The content can be confusing at times and there are not very many assignments, but with some work you can do well in the class. Would recommend to anyone who needs to satisfy their art credit, but it's not an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class started off fine and got really boring. Dreaded going to class by the end of the semester. Easy grader, but grade is drawn from participation, 3 short papers, 1 presentation, 1 term paper, and a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Shemer is extremely kind, understanding, and intelligent. His discussions are always very intriguing and full of laughter. However, each class came with 2-3 assigned readings. Every class is composed of lengthy discussions of the readings, so if you come unprepared, it is very rough. Grades papers very fairly.

Prof Shemer is a great guy. I definitely recommend taking his Israeli cinema class (it takes care of a lot of pre-reqs). There is a lot of readings and since class participation is important, I'd recommend doing them. I would say he is a very easier-going grader. If you like the subject, I'd recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: A very fair grader who also offered extra credit. If you actually watch the films and put effort into your writing, you should be fine.

Boring class, he tends to ramble on and on and on and on. He's very knowledgable about Israeli Cinema and even though there is no prerequisite he does expect you to know some things about cinema and film.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Smart guy, good professor. His area of expertise is Israeli Cinema so taking that class with him was a cool experience. Class is mostly a lecture with some discussion. You'll write papers, he's a fair grader.

Yaron is a great guy and is clearly passionate about the subject matter. Attendance is mandatory and participation is recommended since lectures are discussion based. Reading for every class that is a bit dry but I would recommend doing it since he asks for opinions. 4-5 papers graded fairly easily. Straight-forward final. Some extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: his teaching style is a bit difficult to get used to but it's definitely manageable. there's a lot of reading that should be done for homework and it's important to not get behind. very interesting class and content. you definitely can't miss class (he's pretty strict about attendance).

Assigns ridiculous amounts of reading, especially for a 100 level class. I've been in college for years and have never had to do this much reading. He is a very good lecturer and encourages his students to think and discuss the themes found in the reading, though you will mostly be discussing that at recitation if you're in a large lecture class.

There are quizzes for every unit (every 1-2 weeks) but she does review right beforehand and touches on everything that will be on the quiz so PAY ATTENTION! She canceled/moved class online a few times. Notes came from slides and from things she would show on the board like BLS statistics. Current events discussions involve some participation.

Jordan's very laid back, gives lots of remote quizzes and class off days. There was some frustration with varying quiz difficulty and varying harshness of grading on assignments. Not work-heavy, but quiz-heavy with questions pulled from niche things she said like one time in class. She's a bit of a lazy professor but it was a chill class overall.

Unpredictable and unorganized. She seems very chill, but she's a harsh grader and never really has a schedule. Thankfully it's not work heavy, but it's all about memorization of random stats for short quizzes, which is tough. Also it's week 13 and we haven't been given any information about the final project.

She was an amazing professor. She was very knowledgeable about the information, but also paired everything with detailed slides that would represent what was on the weekly quizzes. The quizzes were easy if you looked over the notes from the class before and she is very chill.

This class was an easy A for me, but I think that's because I sat in the front row and Professor Young knew my name and we talked a good bit. If you participate and she knows you, this class is a breeze. Not hard content, but some of my friends that never showed up were in danger of B's. lots of online (easy) quizzes, group project, final.
Easy class to do well in.
This is my second class with Professor Young. Super low-maintenance class, content is interesting, and she's really understanding. Ended with a high A in both classes I've taken with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is kind but be sure to see her outside of class for the best understanding of things because her lectures can be confusing

Having exams worth 70% of your grade is unreasonable when lectures are unclear, the slides are filled with AI and memes, and the textbook offers little support. The exams don't reflect what's taught.

She is kind and accessible outside of class, but I don't think that makes up for what you'd get out of it.

she probably isnt bad for Econ 101 b/c the content is straightforward, but she is not equipped to be teaching Econ 420 at all. she seems nice but she cannot answer questions clearly and her lectures rarely stay on topic. the exams are not bad if you use outside resources, but in general her lectures offer little help with understanding the content.

She is the sweetest lady, don't get me wrong. But she can't teach. Most of her slides are AI memes and she deviates so much from the content. She doesn't grade the homeworks till more than a month after it is submitted.
What you are taught in class is NOT what you are presented with in the exam. And you're not allowed to ask questions on the exam..

The majority of the slides were AI generated pictures of herself or random AI pictures/memes. The lectures were not very helpful and most of the learning is done outside of class. I think she's really nice and knowledgeable about economics, but it didn't really feel like a whole lot of teaching was going on.

Truly such an amazing teacher. I would take many more classes with her. The material was not necessarily easy, but her lectures and demeanor helped deliver it clearly. The class never felt like a struggle to follow. She is so welcoming for office hours and coffee chats.

Econ 101 at UNC is not the easiest but professor Chao most definitely made it really easy to learn. Her slide shows are posted and are easy to learn from, her lectures are pretty funny and engaging with the effort that she puts into teaching the class. Make sure you work hard on the first and second midterms because the final is pretty difficult.
Dr. Chao is the sweetest! She really cares about her students and made economics interesting. If you can, take ECON 101 with her she is AMAZING.

Dr. Chao is my favorite professor I have had so far at UNC. While the tests were definitely hard, the problem sets, review exams, help sessions, and care she put into the class made them manageable. She made lectures engaging with the images in her slideshows and really tried to see what students were not understanding in order to help. Great prof!

Ying is super caring and a great person; however, she isn't the greatest lecturer and I learned most of the material on my own time from class slides. If you want to do well, you have to commit time outside of class to really understand the material and come to office hours with good questions. Generous grader, but exams were still very difficult.

Dr. Chao is amazing, and such a kind professor. That being said, this class is HARD. Exams are much harder than content learned in class and the final exam was almost impossible, even after days of studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Chao is the sweetest instructor I have ever had. She makes sure to remember your name, brings snacks and candy to class, and gives genuine feedback on any questions or concerns. Lectures can sometimes be a little messy, but if you are able to follow along, you will learn! Econ is a hard class, but Chao makes it very possible to succeed.

Dr. Chao is an amazing professor who cares for her students deeply. She actively sends messages of support if we seemed down in class, was engaging through the lectures, and had snacks in class if we were hungry. Rare to see a professor like this, definitely sign up for her class!

As a person, Dr. Chao is extremely nice. However, her teaching style is not for everyone. She tends be disorganized with her lectures and tends to do things in a more complicated sense. The final was pretty rough but I think that econ 101 is just a tough class. Probably the best out of the 101 teachers.

Dr. Chao is literally the sweetest professor ever! She tries to make lectures enjoyable and is super accessible outside of class for extra help. She genuinely cares about her students and wants each one of them to succeed. Econ 101 is challenging but she breaks down hard concepts really well. There isn't too much busy work outside of class either.

Chao was lovely for Econ, truly cared about her students and their success. Much less work outside class than Staub but still had to work hard and study lots. Sometimes was kind of confusing while teaching but is mostly due to the speed at which econ 101 needs to be taught.
shes genuinely so sweet and caring- econ101 was lowkey tough but she makes it easy to learn if u put in the work

The best Econ professor you can get. The lectures are very clear and Chao is very caring, breaking down concepts that are difficult. The tests are very manageable as long as you complete the practice. If you are taking Econ101, I highly recommend Chao as a professor.

Take Econ with her! She is the BEST Econ 101 professor. She is so caring and even provides snacks in class! Dr. Chao offers to meet with students individually because she genuinely wants you to succeed.

Hands down the best ECON prof. at UNC. Super sweet and wants her students to do well. Super responsive to emails (fixed a problem with my grade in 5 mins on the last day). Homework is very manageable, midterms and final are definitely tough but not impossible (multiple choice only). Grading is very fair, midterm 1: 15%; midterm 2 and final: 20%

I LOVE DR. CHAO! If you have to take Econ take it with her I am begging you. She is extremely sweet and actually cares about her students. She knows that we care about our grades and gave us bonus points on our final. I feel like the difficulty of Econ 101 is exaggerated; If you read the textbook chapters and do all the practice, you will be good.
Genuinely one of the most caring professors ever!

Chao is genuinely the sweetest person I have ever met and she wants to get to know you. I didn't love her teaching style- I struggled focusing. 2 midterms worth 15% and 20% and a final worth 20%. Content is very hard- exams are very challenging but she is the best option to take it with. Does only multiple choice and is so accessible anytime.
Amazing person. She is incredibly caring about her students and truly wants what best for you. Econ 101 is a hard class, but she is definitely the person to take it with.

Her teaching methods are not the best but she is understanding and the lecture is small enough you can ask her to explain or go back. There is a solid amount of work in this class that's always due Sundays at midnight (no late work accepted) but is completion grade. Do not leave it til the last minute. Definitely the best of the 3 ECON 101 teachers

Professor Chao is amazing. ECON 101 is a tough course, but she's 100% the teacher you should want to take it with. She has note outlines for the lectures and has set weekly office hours that make her very accessible. She's very willing/enthusiastic about getting to know you on a personal level. Go to class and PAY ATTENTION!

Chao is the goat. Econ 101 is a hard class conceptually, but she makes it enjoyable enough to want to come to class. She is very personable and is very accessible outside of class and really cares for her students as people. This class is legit though so you will have to put effort into it to do well, but she is definitely the best choice

She's such an amazing teacher and is very passionate about what she does. I highly recommend her class. Although ECON 101 can be pretty tough because of the material itself, she does an amazing job of providing time outside of class to study it and explains things very clearly.

she is so amazing and makes me econ fun. Her tests are not super easy, but also not hard if you study. She gives you handouts to do every day that will help you study, and I would say that attendance is kind of important. She cares so much about her students and I don't know anyone who doesn't like her
Quite a bit of work, but she is very flexible and understanding as a teacher.

Fei is a very passionate teacher. She was always communicative and understanding, so long as you communicate first. The class was organized as one major group-project with various smaller projects and quizzes sprinkled throughout. I would've liked to see shake-ups in team composition so you could interact with more students.

I have never rated a professor before but I felt like it had to be done for Professor Fei Yu. She is one of the most unorganized teachers I have ever had. She assigns a lot of little projects that have quick turn around so we never really have time to understand the material. I feel like I waste my time in her class and wish I had a different teach

I didn't learn much from 718 as the flipped classroom & virtual format puts the full burden of learning on the student. Class time was not utilized well. We'd sometimes use 45+ mins to talk logistics/rubrics & skim over actual content. I will say that Yu responds to emails/feedback readily, isn't a harsh grader, and does games on Zoom though.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: DON'T TAKE 718 W/ YU! I have taken other UX classes and was very excited to learn more in this class. Instead, I felt like each week hours were wasted of my life. Class was so DULL! She was never helpful at office hours and she didn't give clear instructions on the HW. Also didn't hesitate to call ppl out in class. MEJO 581 with Ruel was better!
