Dr. Zwemer is a great professor, and my favourite professor at UNC so far. This class is known for being challenging, however, she made very fun and easy to follow. You have to stay on top of your work to do well, as is expected. The group office hours that she holds were very helpful and she is very clear with what she expects us to learn.

Zwemer is a solid lecturer and explains tough concepts well, however this does not make up for the difficulty of exams. Exam questions were often difficult to understand and misleading and definitely nothing like the sample exam questions she posts. I liked Dr. Zwemer but personally I felt like her tests were unfair, especially the final
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Zwemer was a phenomenal professor. She took the course curriculum and related it to real life examples which kept students very captivated while simultaneously making difficult topics easier to understand. Her tests are a little difficult given that UNC likes application based exams, but this is expected from any BIOL 202 course. 10/10

I have mixed feelings after this semester. Zwemer is very understanding and thoughtful regarding the Covid circumstances, but her test questions were confusing and my grade dropped a letter after Exam 3. Based off of her fairly clear expectations outside of class, I would take her again.

Dr. Zwemer is a very polite and passionate professor. Overall, she made the course content digestible and her lectures were engaging. For the most part, her exams were fair and she did her best to accommodate for her students. Dr. Zwemer is a solid choice for this class!!

Dr. Zwemer is a caring person, however, she may go onto tangents which has nothing to do with the class. Never opened the book once, but if you watch her lectures then you will be set. Recitation is very straightforward. Tests are fair. Make sure to get those participation points (by attending OH and posting on piazza). Overall, not a bad professor

She is incredible. Her lectures albeit recorded were wonderful. She is very flexible and the course is designed to cater to various learning styles. She encourages participation. 100% would take again.

Most of your grade is determined by tests, yet the tests are more about understanding the professor's state of mind more than understanding and stitching together biology concepts. When the goal is to train scientists to be creative and diverse, this format is problematic to say the least.

Dr. Zwemer is passionate about what she teaches. I thought the class structure was fine. Her exams were fair at first. However, she made the last exam and final purposefully more difficult than the other exams, since the averages were high on the first two. This made me feel like she cares more about her reputation than the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Zwemer made the class disorganized which ultimately confused me on requirements. Participation required posting to several different websites, and anything labeled "optional" would affect your grade if you did not attend. The test questions were misleading also.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Zwemer is one of the best bio professors I've had at UNC. She's caring, accessible, kind, and extremely passionate about the subject. Lectures are interesting, tests are easy if you prepare for them, and grading is fair. Pay attention to her lectures and you'll do great.

Super convoluted class structure, the lectures were boring and incredibly topical. Professor seems excited about material but managed to make the class incredibly unengaging and downright off-putting at times.

Dr. Zwemer did a great job breaking down our lectures into smaller portions so that it was not so long of a video. The class was completely async besides group office hours held once a week on zoom. Participation points were able to be earned in many ways, and the exams were super fair. I loved the course material and Dr. Z.

Zwemer is probably one of the better bio professors, but she still isn't the greatest. Her exams are extremely random and poorly put together. For my class she two pretty decent exams and then made one of them WAAYY harder than the others with no warning. She's someone who MAKES her classes average to be around 70%, so beware.

Take her class! She is so caring and thoughtful and adapted to online class very well. She coveys biology super well! Her 3rd test kinda messed me up but thats on me so be warned. Her lectures were pre-recorded and recitation is truly not that much work compared to a lab which is worth the same 1 credit. TAKE ZWEMER! Love her so much!

Dr. Zwemer was amazing in this switch to the online format. All of her lectures are recorded and easy to follow, and there are ample practice problems to work off of. It's really easy to do well if you pay attention and focus on what she tells you to focus on. Great human being and teacher.

Dr. Zwemer is the one of the kindest professors I've ever had. She genuinely cares about student success, is very accessible, and will give her all to help you. One of the best professors I've ever had the pleasure of learning from. Lectures are engaging and exciting, she's organized, and she isn't out to get you on exams. Genuinely loved her class

Dr. Zwemer is the best! She's so warm, caring, open, and definitely knows what she's talking about. She makes great effort to work with her students and makes assignments/tests fair. Would definitely take again.
Very enthusiastic about teaching and genetics. Makes class fun. Would definitely take a class from her again
Great professor. Wish I could take her for all my bio classes!
Awesome professor who cares about students. Shes a tough grader, but makes sure she does all she can for her students.

Dr Zwemer is the best professor Ive had. She genuinely cares about her students, and does everything she can to help them succeed. She makes class fun, engaging, and makes time for individual academic needs for each student. She resparked my love for genetics. Im so grateful to have had her!
She was amazing- so kind and really cares about her students. It was a pretty hard class but she does as much as she can to help you out.

Honestly, I didnt do as well as I expected in her class, but it was because I wasn't putting in the work. Luckily I got to bring up my grade by the third test. The test are very dificult and you wont pass by studying the night before. However, shes very organized and test questions only come from what we talked about in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Z's homework, lectures and sample exam questions are much different from her actual exams. Many people study so hard in her class but still can't save our grades. No extra credits, no sample exams. Everyone is clear about the concepts but still not able to answer questions correctly. I was discouraged and it's just not impossible to do well

She was a really great teacher in class and explained things well. Only complaint is tests were unnecessarily hard and did not reflect how we learned in class. No study guides and nothing can prepare you for Type of questions on the exam

A lot of people studied very hard and had a good grasp of the material but still performed poorly in this class. I love genetics and am a Biology major, but this class really put me through it. Sample exam questions are not like the real exam questions at all. Dr. Z is a nice person, but I am personally disappointed in the grading system.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Zwemer is great person and knows Genetics well. However, the level of thinking used in lectures, homework, + sample exam questions are much different from her actual exams. There were typos in all 3 midterms and the final which caused confusion when taking the exam. Some of her questions are worded poorly. It's not impossible to do well though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Zwemer is obviously enthusiastic about biology and enjoys teaching. My only complaint is that it became very obvious she did not proof-read her exams prior to administering them & during midterms she would have to correct the wording on at least 3 questions (which leads to confusion & poor performance by the class with midterms averaging 70s).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Zwemer is certainly an enthusiastic professor and loves the subject, which was really awesome! She has a great personality and really cares about students. However, I did think many of her test questions were poorly designed/unnecessarily confusing, which was reflected in students' performance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the worst MEJO professors. She gave NO FEEDBACK. Doesn't believe in giving 100s. She told us we did great but the max she gave someone was a 94. This isn't supposed to be a difficult class, but is when she doesn't give any feedback other than a good job, and quickly goes through the slides. We have only done group work all year. DO NOT TAKE!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take this class with this professor if you want to feel terrible about yourself and want to have your work picked apart to shreds. AKA don't take it.

Very sweet lady, but she simply can't teach. Her lectures were always disorganized and she has so much trouble communicating the main points. Exams are so specific it's insane. Very unclear grading criteria. Assigns a mountain of work every week while you still have other outstanding projects. Please do yourself a favor and find another class.
Disorganized lectures and often went overtime.

Eva is clearly very smart, but she has a hard time communicating her ideas and knowledge to the class. She constantly contradicted herself in class and had to second-guess herself on many things. I don't know if this was her first time teaching MEJO 379 and she just needed a semester under her belt, but I will just say she did not make it easy.

Eva's a great professor and very skilled in digital marketing, but the structure of the class is unorganized. Most times she would stretch lectures longer than they need to be leaving us with 10-15 minutes at the end of class to work on a group activity that requires more time to complete. Also, check to see who the client is before enrolling.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is sweet and cares about learning, but definitely made this class much more stressful than it needed to be. Was not super clear on assignment and grading guidelines and graded them very harshly. Assigned a lot of work week to week and gave a final presentation in addition to a very challenging final. I'd find another professor for this course.

Eva is very sweet. She worked really hard to provide a good experience during Covid, and she was very understanding. This class was a little slowly paced, though, which was maybe good because of Covid, but I found it hard to pay attention most days. I would recommend Eva because of her obvious smartness and kind heart, but maybe not this class.
Dope professor, easy lectures, amazing materials :)

Amazing person!! I loved Dr. Fisher. He is the nicest person ever, and extremely helpful. Everyone in our class which was small loved him. He is a great professor, and if I had someone as a PI or something, he would be it. The class is whatever you want to make of it, and I think I watched some classmates truly learn and show amazing growth.

Dr. Fisher is an exceptional instructor—clear, engaging, and always accessible outside of class. He sets fair, transparent expectations and genuinely wants students to understand and succeed. He's incredibly kind and understanding when life happens. His teaching style makes the material more enjoyable and keeps the course accessible and manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Karma will come for her

Dr. Zurcher is nice but all the chem 101 professors use the same slides and have the same tests. No matter who you have you'll have to self teach for the most part. You also don't know your grade unless you calculate it yourself. Would recommend her but be aware its mostly going over practice problems, she doesn't truly teach most of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Zurcher is great. Explains topics well BUT UNC Chem department sucks. This class will humble you. You'd think you understood the topic well until you get your exam back. The slides cover everything, but even if a topic was only mentioned once with no practice questions, it's fair game. There is so much content. Practice problems are a must!
Wish I had her for the entire semester, super engaging and clear lecturer and the one exam she wrote was extremely fair.

Professor Zurcher's lectures are engaging and easy to understand, reading textbook helps a little but paying attention in class and going over the slides are more important. The course is designed to be very test heavy, but the chem department provides a lot of practice materials. The chem department requires an iClicker.
The class content is very clear, but there is too much of it. The exam covers a wide range of topics.

Chem 101 without taking AP Chem is difficult. READ the textbook assigned readings before class. Use active recall, take practice tests for midterms and finals. Do all homework until you get a 100. If you do not understand a concept, PLEASE UNDERSTAND IT before you move on to the next lesson. ALWAYS review your midterms, bc graders make mistakes.

Professor Zurcher was awesome and made the material clear and easy to understand. Unfortunately, Chem 101 at Carolina is a weed out class so there was a LOT of material thrown at you over the course of the semester. The class was difficult, and the tests were 75% of our grade, but that's the fault of the chemsitry department, not professor Zurcher.
I thought Professor Zurcher was awesome for 101. She was great at explaining concepts and you can tell she is passionate about the subject and her students.
Good professor with many opportunities to meet outside of class, explains content clearly and wants students to succeed but teaches a very hard topic so deserves a little slack for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: UNC chemistry is difficult as a whole, but I always really enjoyed Dr. Zurcher's lectures. She is a very caring a sweet woman with a clear passion for chemistry, and she tries her best to make the subject approachable. While you do have to buy the textbook to access the homework, most test questions are pulled from the daily slides.
although unc chem is hard by default as its all standardized, zurcher is definitely one of the best profs. her lectures are very helpful, and she's frequently present at after-school review things.

I love Dr. Zurcher! She is genuinely so sweet, caring, and just wants to see her students succeed. She does have high expectations, but she makes her expectations clear and holds every student to the same standard. Chem 101 is a difficult class, but she was great at explaining concepts and providing resources! She is my favorite professor so far :)

My problem is with the Chemistry Department as a whole, and since things are standardized here, there isn't anything bad that I could pinpoint on her specifically. 

Zurcher is incredibly friendly and will answer questions in class. This class requires a lot of effort outside of class. I regret not using a lot of the resources that were available.

Professor Zurcher is a great lecturer. Overall, the class is really difficult, but not unique to Zurcher because chem is just notoriously hard at UNC. Homework isn't anything crazy but make sure to study for those midterms.
Chem 101 is standardized, but she was a great professor! Very clear lectures and would actually come talk to her students.

Chem 101 is a difficult weed out class, but Zurcher is definitely the best professor to take it with. She knows her stuff, is nice, and is a good lecturer. I also appreciated how much in-class practice we got for the concepts. I wish she could teach 102 next semester lol

Because if the standardized and group taught structure of CHEM 101, there's only so much the professor can do. All exams and content is the same for each section. But regardless Dr. Zurcher's lectures were engaging, and she consistently showed that she cares about her students and their learning and success.
Zurcher is engaging, usually gets through the slides, and explains complex concepts in simple terms. She drops important hints for exams during lecture.
Chem101 is rough and you definitely need to put in a good amount of work outside of class, but Zurcher was a great lecturer and super kind. Explained concepts clearly and wants you to succeed.
I returned to zurcher after dealing with whatever the hell orgo 2 was with beaver, and i realized she is lowkey the goat. He sucks. Shes great. Preciate u mama

I absolutely loved Zurcher for this class! I was really nervous because chem has a reputation, but she was a really engaging teacher, and she explained things in a way that really made sense to me! I love her. That said, I think she is pretty inaccessible outside of class (because chem is a teaching team, not a single teacher responding to you) .
101 is extremely hard but its standardized in the chemistry department so it has little to do with Zurcher herself. she was a great teacher nevertheless. just a hard ass class.

Prof Zurcher does a solid job of presenting material and making content clear in class. Note that UNC's chem department as a whole is notoriously challenging and demanding, so the difficulty isn't unique to Zurcher. Success depends on if you keep up with assignments, avoid falling behind, and not waiting until the last minute to prepare for exams.

prof zurcher is great. her lectures are straight-forward and organized; she gets right to the point, which made the clarity of the content 100x better. she's my favorite STEM professor at UNC thus far simply because of her teaching. final grades in this class rely heavily on midterms, but zurcher prepares students for exams well. 10/10 recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I only had Dr. Zurcher for half the semester while she stood in for Dr. Eskew but her lectures were incredible. Her explanations were extremely clear and gave me confidence on exam-level questions. She is very energetic and it is clear that she cares deeply about our success.

Explained concepts well (99% of the time). Exams were extremely fair imo. Felt like the final was harder than the midterms but the grade ended up better than expected. Definitely attend lectures and GPSS (professor led sessions), and do practice. Orgo can be tough but she does not try to make it harder.

Explains concepts thoroughly if asked, GPSS & LA sessions very helpful. Expect exit tickets (low stakes pop quizzes) & lecture moves fast- if you handwrite, be prepared to spend time after class catching up w/ annotated slides. No curve/EC, liked putting a few tricky questions on midterm that built on topics students didn't grasp in class well.

Great professor. Attend LA sessions or GPSS if you have any confusion. Exams are intense, and I figured out how to do good on them too late. Time yourself doing the workbook exam to replicate the actual one. Redo the end of week problems too! Attend class for the required participation and read the textbook everyday for easy exit ticket points.
Probably one of tbe best people who can explain orgo. The practice problems from la sessions were the most representative of exams and the in class slides are very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She tells you exactly what to do to succeed - do all those things and you will. Her tests were fair, and I felt that they did not deviate from what we were taught. Orgo is a hard class, but she made it bearable. I could see that she really cared about us as students. She genuinely wants you to succeed.
Honestly, don't recommend. Class is super tough and exams were awful. She was nice, but her lectures didn't correspond with the exams. Have never done worse in a class!!!

Great professor. Attend LA sessions or GPSS if you have any confusion. Exams are intense, and I figured out how to do good on them too late. Time yourself doing the workbook exam to replicate the actual one. Redo the end of week problems too. Attend class for the required participation and read the textbook everyday for easy exit ticket points.
She's an awesome professor who is very accessible outside of class. Take orgo with her if you get a chance and ask questions!

Dr. Zurcher was passionate about the content she taught and did a good job lecturing the new content. No matter what, orgo is a hard class and you need to dedicate the time outside of class doing the readings, extra practice, and studying for exams. Grades are very test heavy but you have a lot of resources (and ULA team) to help you too.

Dr Zurcher was down to earth and definitely cared about every student's success. She made an awful class somewhat bearable. If you are taking chemistry and Zurcher is teaching, please take her. Definitely the best chem professor I have had at UNC.

Good teacher overall just sometimes skims some stuff & very loud. Gave lots of pep talks bc she could tell when we were falling behind LOL. Exams will have stuff you've never seen before but that's every chem exam. Look out for exit tickets, don't count for much but graded for accuracy. NEED to read textbook. very exam heavy. Content builds fast!!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Orgo is a hard subject, but Dr. Zurcher didn't make it any easier. She can explain concepts well but her tests were so incredibly hard, it was nothing like any of the practice problems. I never felt prepped for the exams, for all 3 midterms medians were in the 60s. Curves participation grades by dropping some points which helps.

She is a good lecturer and explains the concepts pretty clearly, this coming from a chem major who has had way worse in this department. She is a tough grader tho and I felt like she didn't give much partial credit on the exams. There's definitely a curve for the End of Week assignments, I failed most of them and got a 100 for them at the end.

Obviously orgo is one of the hardest classes at UNC so you pretty much get what you expect with this class. Dr. Zurcher did an amazing job of explaining really complicated topics and preparing you for the way material builds upon itself in this class. Lots of practice problems available and lots of review sessions (which are helpful!)

Orgo is a hard class in general but it is especially hard at UNC. Dr. Zurcher is not a bad teacher but the problems completed in class are nothing like the problems on the exam. Do not take this class if you are taking another hard stem class. Also the mean grades are never revealed, only the median which speaks for itself. All in the 60s

Dr. Zurcher is great. She is a straightforward teacher, she does not waste any time, in a good way, you feel like going to class is productive. Furthermore you WILL NOT SUCCEED if you skip classes. Everything builds off of the last lecture. Don't skip

ORGO II is just generally a hellish class, but of your options Zurcher is probably one of the better ones. Our second exam was HARD, though-- over half the class failed. There is partial credit, but partial credit for an impossible problem is still 0 points. Take with Eskew if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: CHEM 262 is a hard course, but Professor Zurcher does an amazing job at making it comprehensible. She is caring to students and makes it clear that she is proud of our efforts! I think her test questions are reasonable - going through the slides helps you to focus on content that she finds important and practicing those will set you up for success!

*Screams in agony*

Organic chem is tough but Dr. Zurcher is probably the best professor for it at UNC.  Her lectures are great but the exams are so incredibly difficult.  You really have to be prepared to dedicate 3+ hours a week just to doing extra practice problems (beyond the ones in the homework) if you want to succeed. 

*Begins sobbing*

Dr. Zurcher is a kind woman both inside & outside of lecture. She's accommodating to students who are experiencing difficulties. However, her tests are difficult & there are questions on there that will take you aback. She also gives weekly quizzes in lecture so attend. she is good at explaining concepts, but moves through the material quickly.

Zurcher's tests are hard and sometimes have wack questions that don't line up with the level of difficulty taught in class. However, she is good at teaching and answering questions. She is also very approachable and nice. I can say her hard tests helped prepare me well but sometimes were hard for no reason which is frustrating.
Random weekly quizzes were terrible
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Orgo with Professor Zurcher is tough, but she's an effective teacher. The workbook problems are really helpful, and using Unstuckstudy alongside the free textbook can make studying more efficient. Attendance is mandatory, so engage in class to get the most out of it.

Midterm 1 median = 80, midterm 2 median = 69. The exams have questions that can be so much more complex than any practice or lecture questions that they seem nearly impossible. Shes alright at teaching during lecture, but either way DO NOT skip class there is graded exit problems, iclicker, and you do not want to fall behind. Make flashcards

Orgo is always a hard class regardless of who teaches it, but Zurcher was no help. The other section consistently got better exam grades and her explanations of content were always overcomplicated. She also told me the reason the atmosphere was so stressful/competitive was because the students were "diagnosing eachother with testing anxiety"

Honestly, orgo is a very hard class, regardless of who teaches it. I think Zurcher is one of the best professors in terms of explaining concepts from ground up. Her GPSS is SUPER helpful and she is very patient and friendly. Attendance is MANDATORY since you get daily points and its such a hard class. Workbook problems are the biggest help.

Dr. Zurcher is kind, but this class is so hard. Lecture is doable, but the problems are MUCH easier than those on the exams. Workbook problems are amazing and exam-level, but they don't provide answer keys to all the problems, which is frustrating. Mid 60s medians on midterms, but the final was much easier. Course was identical to Beaver's section.

The class content itself is pretty hard, but Dr. Zurcher would sometimes fail to explain things clearly in class or assume that we understood content. Overall, the chem department loves to do a flipped classroom which everyone hates. She would move super fast even if it was clear everyone was confused.
dude. wtf. that's all i can say. the medians for our three midterms have been 68, 68, 66. that's all i'm gonna say.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The best orgo chem prof in UNC. Cares about her students, very easy-going and feel comfortable of providing support. The course design is vague and ambiguous, so your grade will largely depend on your TA, but Dr. Zurcher is nice. The office hour is helpful, don't miss it.

Didn't really have much contact with Dr. Zurcher during this class, since TAs were the primary point of contact, but the structure wasn't the best. Extremely vague grading criteria on major reports, leaving us in the dark. Workload was manageable, which was nice. Grade entirely dependent on TA.
One of my favorite professors at Carolina so far. Very caring about her students and their grades.

My initial rating of Zurcher for CHEM 261 was too harsh, given that 262 is a disaster right now. The class is insanely difficult, and I don't like how Zurcher likes to weed people out. However, she did teach the course in an effective and organized way. Her classes were not a waste of time, and had critical problem-solving opportunities.

Dr. Zurcher is nice, but orgo is incredibly hard at UNC. I was a chemistry major before this class and now can't bear to think about chemistry. If you have to take orgo, take it with Dr. Zurcher because she explains things well, but the class will still be insanely difficult. Its worse than every other chem class at unc; exams are superr difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Zurcher really cares about her students and is great at teaching. Orgo is a tough class, but Dr. Zurcher made the material manageable for sure. It's a lot of work, but if you go to class and practice outside of class, you'll be alright. Definitely recommend this class.

Orgo is hard but it's not impossible. Do not miss class because Dr. Zurcher goes through a lot of dense material during lectures and it's crucial to succeeding. Use the workbook!! It was so helpful in my opinion and it provides similar practice to exam-style questions. Do not fall behind because things will pile up. Orgo demands a lot of time
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Zurcher was amazing! You could tell that she really cared about getting you to understand the material.

She does a great job thoroughly explaining topics even as the pace of the class picks up toward the end of the semester. The exams are tough, but workbook problems are super helpful to prepare. You can tell Dr. Zurcher cares about her students; in office hours she's good at guiding you to the right answer so you understand processes yourself.

Do not skip the textbook reading. They really pile it on but don't skip if you can, or else you'll get a lot less out of lectures. She gives you everything you need for exams; the material on tests always stayed within lesson objectives, they just put in a lot of tricky questions. Go to her office hours, she's great at answering questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is difficult, as are all chem classes at UNC. To pass, you need to put in a lot of work. It is not Dr. Zurcher's fault the orgo curriculum is grueling. She is kind, caring, and willing to explain everything to you outside of class. She will remember your name if you ask her questions and wants you to succeed if you put in the effort.

She's alright - just alright though. She does her job, however I often thought she made things more confusing than needed. Tests are tricky, but not impossible, and the textbook is useless. This class is not about sitting with your best friends -- it's about finding the smart people and learning from them. At least that's how I got an A.

Zurcher is a great teacher who explains things very well. Orgo is a hard class you need to put in work in order to succeed. The test were pretty fair for the most part, but it is clear that they are trying to trick you on some of the questions. Make sure you understand the material. You have all you need to succeed.

Throughout lecture, you can tell she is caring! Explains details topic nicely and gives foundation that you can apply for other orgo questions. However, make sure to READ the textbook! And practice! Can't stress the textbook enough. Textbook let's you go into class knowing what to do, and Zurcher builds on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Worst class I have ever taken. She comes off sweet but I really do think the chem department makes students suffer more than they should. Yes organic chemistry is hard, however Dr. Zurcher makes it harder than it needs to be by not going over all the concepts that are tested. Def take at a community college to save your sanity!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have both taken this course from Dr. Zurcher and been a peer mentor.  Seeing her teach from both sides has showed me that she really cares about her students and their learning.  The material covered in the course is difficult and requires a lot of work to keep up with, but she teaches it in about as straightforward of a way as anyone could!

Yes, organic chemistry is hard but Dr. Zurcher really sets you up for success. She starts building a good base early in the course and provides so many practice resources to become familiar with content. Her office hours and problem solving sessions also cleared up many questions from lecture.

I only wanted to take Orgo 1 with Zurcher. She is the best option for lecturers. Orgo is a very difficult subject and requires a lot of work so take it during an easier semester. Same exams as Beaver, the averages are Cs and Ds.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Orgo is hard regardless of who you take it with but I definitely did waaaay better than I thought I would because she explains the material very well. I usually went to her office hours and problem solve sessions and she takes the time to properly explain the material, no matter how dumb my questions were. I wish she taught orgo 2 next semester.

Organic chem is already hard but Zurcher understands that its hard. During class, she tries to help talk through problems and the topic is literally so hard but she makes it bearable. Saying that, I dont think she has a say in the exams, I think they're fair but difficult so definitely have to do a lot of outside studying. office hours are helpful

This class takes so much time and brain power but Dr. Zurcher makes it the least miserable possible. I can ask dumb questions and she will help. She realizes that the class is hard and that students don't have every waking moment to study for her class alone. She's approachable and does a great job explaining things to prepare us for the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked Dr. Zurcher's style of lecture - definitely a lot more helpful than some of the other 101 or 102 teachers.

Professor Zurcher is by far the best professor in the chemistry department at UNC! Though the class is still very difficult, Professor Zurcher has never once made me feel inadequate for not knowing something. She is kind and teaches the material very well. She knows that the course is difficult, but is ready to help you succeed.
Very confusing and unclear. Does not know the material very well, makes many mistakes which causes even more confusion. Tests are impossible

My problems were with the setup of CHEM101, not with Zurcher. She teaches the material well and makes the lectures interesting, but if you missed a class or struggled with a concept, you are at a major disadvantage. Attendance is counted with the iclickers for participation, and tests are challenging but mostly fair. Go to problem-solving sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Chem at chapel hill is what it is. You have to know going into it that it's not going to be easy. I liked Prof. Zurcher but I was just 1/300 students. Grade primarily comes from 2 midterms and a final, but attendance to class and recitations as well as warmups and weekly homework assignments also weigh in. Stay on top of concepts. Ask questions.

I don't think the flaw in this class was Dr. Zurcher, but instead the horrible class structure. She explained things fairly well, but if you miss class, you're pretty much on your own. I understood concepts a lot better than my test scores reflected, but it's still doable if you have to take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Z is certainly not preparing students for any future graduate program. With a "C", there is no way that people can apply to graduate school due to the effect on gpa. Therefore, a C is not okay for med school or any type of school. Also, we can deduce from the very positive reviews, that Dr. Z is responding to the unfavorable reviews.

Dr. Zurcher is the most difficult professor I've had at UNC as a junior in Bio and Chem, but she is preparing her students for the academia in medical school and for those pursuing PhDs and for that I am very thankful. She is honest with the students and shares her weaknesses when she took chemistry and due to this, she can make hard yet fair exams

I swear, my test scores got better when I just did did the practice problems on the slides, that's it. She did not really have any impact on my learning and I just had to do it myself. As a freshman, it was new to me and I did not know how to adapt quick. Honestly, I don't remember much of her lectures except that she skips information a lot.
Acts nice but has condescending attitude towards students. CHEM department tries to act like they care about students but ends up saying insulting things.

I had her for Orgo 1 & 2 and I'm unbelievably grateful that I did. She has been my favorite UNC Chem professor. She's great at concisely explaining the content and organizing her course. She's fair on her exams and generous with partial credit. Loved her!! 1000% would take again!

I had Dr. Z for CHEM261 and CHEM262 and taking it with her was the best decision I've ever made. UNC chemistry can be nightmarish but Dr. Z is hands-down the best chem professor I've ever had. She seems to really care about students, explains things in a way I can understand, and has very useful problem-solving sessions.

After taking many chem classes at UNC, this was the most ridiculous class I have ever taken (the exams are unlike any of the material). The material is not taught, but somehow she expects you to learn the material by yourself (not even similar to the textbook, questions given, supplemental material). Would never recommend taking orgo 2 with her.

Dr. Zurcher knows the material, but her teaching style did not help me. I felt she went extremely fast and did not explain, but rather expected us to rely more on the readings and warm-ups. I would recommend taking with Curtis instead, it seems that she explains the material in a way that is simpler to understand. Tests were very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The exams were way too complicated than needed. Didnt teach enough and the textbook was not enough to do well on the exams.

Professor Zurcher is very good at teaching and is very knowledgable. She explains topics thoroughly and is open to answer any questions in class. Class attendance is a requirement since there are a certain amount of clicker points needed for 100% participation. I recommend sitting on the outside seats in her lecture since TA's answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Chemistry 101 is a difficult class no matter who you take it with, but Dr. Zurcher is a solid choice for professors. Definitely recommend her for Chem 101! I wouldn't say chem is the easiest, but Dr. Zurcher does a great job explaining concepts and always gave us enough time to work through class problems. Dr. Z was really great this semester. I missed some classes due to outside circumstances, and I feel like my grade reflects that. Chem 101 shouldn't be this hard anywhere.

reviews.comment: The chem department is terrible and orgo is rough. However, Zurcher does the best she can with how the department is set up and is the best chem prof I've had. She does a good job keeping the exam averages around a 70 (which is what the chem department demands), and unlike other profs, will give partial credit.

Chemistry is hard at UNC but Dr. Zurcher made the class fun. She is so passionate about chemistry and you can see that in the way she teaches. If you love chemistry, you will love her. Although chemistry is not my favorite subject, she made me want to major in chemistry because of how excited she is about the subject! Would definitely recommend!

CHEM 101 is hard no matter who you take it with, but Dr. Zurcher made the class more manageable. Her lectures were easy to understand and I felt like I walked out of each class learning something. The course is the same work load no matter what teacher you have, but Dr. Zurcher's teaching got me through this class.

The chem dept is just exhausting. They make sure to weed out as many people as possible and it certainly works. I heard Zurcher was actually disappointed when the class did well on the first exam and wanted us to do poorly. This showed when our second exam was nearly impossible and did not reflect even the hard practice problems given to us.
She makes concepts more difficult than they need to be. Not hard to get at least an A-.
The exams are impossible and lectures are not useful.

The class teaching materials and textbook are not enough to do well on the tests. The test questions are unlike anything Ive every seen (have taken many classes at UNC). The exams for chem 262 are very unlike the textbook/lectures and are unnecessarily difficult. Also, the flipped classroom is not very effective. I took this course as a prerequisite for my major and by the end, I switched my major out of STEM. It is evident that she is more accustomed to teaching at a higher level.

reviews.comment: The last test had a failing average. While you can study more from the textbook, lecture slides, or peer mentor worksheets it does not help. The worst professor I have ever had at this university. The entire class will fail a test and she will say its our fault instead of her own. She teaches one subject and tests on another. Avoid her at all costs.

reviews.comment: Dr. Zurcher is one of my favorite professors at UNC! She's great at explaining difficult concepts and she always made sure that her students were on track. Dr. Zurcher is the best chem professor I've had at UNC. Orgo is a hard class but she does a very good job at explaining the material. Most prominent thing I remembered from the semester was her saying during a class poll question: "Only 9% got this right... you guys really need to study this!" and moving on. reviews.comment: I think Professor Zurcher is the best professor anyone could ever hope for from a chem professor. The exams/quizzes were challenging but doable, and you always knew what to expect from her. Yes, you had to put in a lot of effort but that's a given in any Chemistry class. She has very forgiving grading policies as well.

If you have to endure organic chemistry, save yourself and take it with literally any other professor. Zurcher is unclear about how she would like problems solved, does not provide notes during class, only practice problems, and overall asks students to teach themselves. The textbook is the only source of info and it's not enough for her exams.

Orgo is hard regardless, but Zurcher explains everything very well. She assigns practice problems that are relevant to what you'll see on exams and her lectures are also extremely helpful. Content is taught pretty fast, so this class does require a lot of time, but Zurcher will make sure everything she assigns is helpful for exams.

I have taken many chem classes from various profs and Dr. Zurcher is easily the best. She explains concepts very clearly and in a way that is easy to understand (My favorite chem professor at UNC for sure). Tests & quizzes are fairly written. The homework is very helpful and not at all busy work. She has made me love chemistry. TAKE HER CLASS!!

Organic chemistry is hard, but it doesn't need to be this hard. The way Zurcher teaches this course leads to confusion and absolute failure to grasp the material because she does not teach. She expects you to read the textbook, understand, and be able to do practice problems instantly. Don't take this with her. Don't take it at all if you can.

She is a great teacher and the slides were very informative, but her exams were impossible!! They require a lot of critical thinking and are extensiveIy long. Knowing the basics is not enough, the application and execution on the midterms were on a whole other level!

I would say pre online classes, Zurcher did an excellent job explaining the material and she really cares about her students. Her style is typical of other UNC Chem classes, so be ready for a flipped classroom. I wish the department made more accommodations for students after transitioning to online learning, however.

Truly does her job, which is more than you can say about other chem profs. Awesome at teaching complex topics and gives more than enough practice worksheets. I will say, I think her exams are a bit excessive and she wasn't very accommodating during this past online semester. Overall, she has high expectations but teaches you what you need to know.

Zurcher is a good lecturer. I definitely recommend looking over her slides for studying for exams. Would also recommend doing all of the optional worksheets and doing lots of practice problems. Not a bad class if you stay on top of it and take good notes.

Dr. Zurcher is a great professor. She explains complex topics in a way that's easy to understand. You just need to know what's presented on the slides, do the worksheets she sends out, and memorize the mechanisms, and you should be fine!

I enjoyed CHEM 262 more than CHEM 261. Although there are many mechanisms and reactions to learn in this class, it is manageable if you put in the time. Dr. Zurcher is a very compassionate teacher. This was her first semester at UNC and it started a little rough, but it improved throughout the year. This course is difficult, but I think Dr. Zurcher is a really good teacher. She provides a lot of outside practice problems and wants you to succeed

Dr. Zurcher is super nice and is open to having students in office hours at all times. She is new to teaching and that is very evident. She dumbs down problems in class and doesn't write her own exams so we're not prepared for the level of difficulty of the problems on the exams.

reviews.comment: Knowledgeable, energetic, efficient, accessible, stays on top of her email, inspirational, patient, caring. reviews.comment: Dr. Zurcher is pretty good for Orgo 1. She knows her stuff, she explains well, and she's nice and approachable. I don't mean to roast but it is very apparent that she is new to lecturing. The problems we do in class are very simple and easy to understand. She does not write her own tests, so the prep we do beforehand is tough but doable. The tests, however, create too large of a gap between the study problems and test problems. Take Crimmins!!

It's obvious that Zurcher is new to teaching. Her class is a HEAVILY flipped classroom. If you don't read the many sections and watch the multiple videos that she assigns before every class period, you won't understand anything she's saying. "Class" is basically answering a million clicker questions with the people around you, not the professor.

Shes new to teaching so Im sure thats why shes not that great. This is great for those who thrive on flipped classes, but the majority do not. I would not recommend this prof.

I had Prof Zhang for my Physics 118 studio and she was amazing. The class was very difficult but she explained everything in a clear and engaging way so it all made sense. The canvas was very helpful and she was always willing to walk you though any problems both in class and in office hours.

Muxin was a very good professor; I had her for studio as well. She is super kind and always available outside of class if you need her. Her grading is very lenient for in-class work and gives a lot of partial credit on exams.

You will learn a lot if you keep up with the contents, while the curve won't make your grade too bad after all, since hw and projects are graded leniently.
Not a very good lecturer, but she is super nice, the final project was graded insanely easily, and homework makes up 45% of your grade, which is an absurd level for a 500-level course.

Seeing a lot of negative reviews after the first midterm but she clearly realized it was too difficult and made the second midterm easier - class avg went from 65 to 80. 

a lot of homework but no final and shes a really generous grader. will give you full credit on the final project if you put a good faith effort in.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If a professor sees the class average sitting at 60, that's usually a sign to look in the mirror. A genuinely kind one would probably throw in a nice curve or tweak the course a bit—but Professor Zhong doesn't really seem to notice there's an issue.

Not really any practice in class. Wish there was more homework to provide grade padding and practice, especially after a brutal midterm. She is clearly smart and kind, but lecture slides are posted last minute and lectures are hard to follow. I'm teaching myself the content with Google and YouTube videos. Don't stack many hard classes with this one
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhong is honestly pretty nice and not even bad at lecturing. The class is super theory heavy and homeworks do take a long time and have a good amount of coding. What makes this class so bad is the super high expectations. Midterm was on things either barely talked about or out of our scope, and average literally was failing. Good luck...
I need therapy after the midterm. Take the class with anyone else
Brutal and exhausting...

The professor seems nice, but wasn't understanding of the students.The practice exam she gave was different from the real midterm,  much harder and way more complicated. It was discouraging because it didn't feel like she wanted us to truly learn the material. I tried my best, but it felt more like being set up to fail than being guided to learn.

Can't believe how the grading changed this much from last semester. It used to be project-based, now it's all super hard exams. Totally killing my GPA.  I honestly don't know how I'm supposed to graduate if the professor doesn't make adjustments to the grading policy.

Lectures are highly theoretical and often difficult to grasp, despite the professor describing the material as easy and intuitive. You'll need independent study to try understanding the content. I wish slides were consistently posted early to read ahead of class. The first midterm was brutal and different from assignments and the practice exam.

The professor is very smart, but the lectures are mostly pure theory and really hard to follow. I spend a lot of extra time studying on my own. The practice exam for the midterm wasn't very helpful, since the actual exam was way, way harder.
horrible midterm

Dr. Kerr is one of the rare professors on campus who considers the fact that his students are people with lives outside of his class. He is very willing to be flexible as long as you are willing to demonstrate you are putting in effort to the class. Makes an otherwise really boring topic and 8 am class really enjoyable. I would highly recommend.
Data literacy is a very annoying class, but Dr. Kerr is awesome. He made a boring class as fun and easy as it could be. Could not recommend him more!
Zach is such a chill guy. He didn't make this (bs) class harder than it needed to be and understood the importance of it to students. If you still need to take IDST111L, take it with him.
Kerr's great. One of the best professors I've had up until this point. Super understanding of students lives but also does a fantastic job teaching and challenging students.

Zach is such a great professor. He seemed to really understand the point of Data Lit Lab and didn't make it more demanding than it needed to be. He was extremely engaging, understanding, and flexible with the class. Overall great guy.

Honest and understanding of students lives outside of classes, especially for a one credit course. Take this class with him if you can, it seemed he was able to be more flexible with the material than other professors because he helped create the course. Met six times throughout the semester, with biweekly online work and a final group project

Zack understood that the class was only a single credit hour, and only had us do what was necessary to learn the content. I had to meet with him for help with my final project, and I mentioned that I was looking for some good study spots on campus. He took the time after our meeting to send me a list of his favorite places to get work done.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kerr is a great professor. He actually cares about his students and wants them to succeed. We had 2-3 assignments each week, but we didn't have any tests. Best professor I've had at UNC.
I wish every teacher were like him; he actually understands that we are college students.
Take this class with Professor Kerr!

Professor Kerr was one of the best professors I have ever had. He makes class entertaining and truly cares for his students. He is one of the most energetic and fun professors I have had at UNC, especially with his endless jokes and memes. His workload is VERY manageable, and he is very passionate about research. I would 100000% recommend!!

Dr. Kerr has been one of my favorite professors at UNC so far. I genuinely felt that he cared about his students and their success and well-being. No exams but 85% group work. He does grade assignments a little harder, but usually you can submit revisions and get points back. He's also extremely funny and entertaining. Worth taking 273 with Kerr.

Professor Kerr made class entertaining and fun. You can expect to have 2-3 assignments per week, but a lot of the assignments are group work. He doesn't give exams, which means he grades take-home quizzes and writing assignments more critically. Overall, he really cares about you and wants you to succeed! Highly recommend taking EXSS 273 with him!

Great professor and person all around. I am in my 4th semester here and this is the first professor I've had that truly cares about student well-being. He is very open and the way he speaks about himself shows that we are all human and it's okay not to have everything together all the time. No exams but learned so much about the research process.

Zach is the best professor that I have had in my college career. Zach truly cares about the success of everyone in his class and his students feeling validated, understood, and cared for. His lectures can be lengthy, but he adds memes and funny aspects to them to keep you engaged. Could not recommend taking his class enough!

I've never taken a class with him, but had to rate him. He called out names during graduation. He ensured everyone's name was pronounces correctly, which means a ton to me. My name isn't easy to pronounce which caused me stress, but he MADE SURE he said it right. This is a testament to who he is.

The most entertaining and engaging professor I've had at UNC. He really cares about how you are doing and what's going on in your life. Dr. Kerr repeatedly followed up with me about what I wrote in weekly reflections, which I thought was really thoughtful and showed genuine concern. SUCH A GOOD CLASS. 10/10 recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Kerr is great!

Amazing professor all around. Cares about students, grades fairly, gives opportunities for revision. The course content itself is pretty dry and it's amazing how he makes it come to life. Often focuses on bigger picture ideas that I felt really contributed to my development as a student outside of just my grade in this class.

Dr. Kerr is hands down the best professor I have ever had! He does not give any exams, most of the work in this course is completed in a group that you will be assigned to on day one, but you learn to love the people you are working with. The material covered is informative, but Dr. Kerr does not expect you to understand everything immediately.

Dr. Kerr is a super energetic and caring professor- you'll have a fun time in his class. The whole semester is group work, but it's actually manageable and I enjoyed my group a lot. He's lenient on deadlines and always checks in to make sure you're doing okay. He gives personal feedback on every assignment and really wants you to succeed. No exams!

The best professor I've had at UNC. Genuinely cares for his students and constantly makes sure theyre doing good. Class is mostly group work but you get good feedback on assignments and can submit revisions to improve your grade. Some weekly quizzes, not too hard. Lectures are so fun so make sure to go or you get a makeup assignment that isnt fun.

Best professor I have had at UNC so far. He is hilarious and is one of the only teachers I know that checks in on students and puts them first. Class is all group work but he gives a lot of time to complete it. If 273 satisfies a Gen-Ed or you are looking for another class, take it. Goat teacher.
Amazing professor with a great intro to research topics. His lectures are hilarious and made me never want to miss a day. Best professor for EXSS 273 hands down and would take any class he teaches.

Dr. Kerr is an exceptional professor who genuinely cares about his students' success. He's super chill and creates a relaxed atmosphere in the classroom. Group work in his class is surprisingly manageable. He's understanding of life circumstances and always available as a helpful resource. Highly recommend taking a class with him!

He is the best professor at UNC. He genuinely cares about his students mental health and lives outside of school. He does everything in his power to help us and gives incredible lectures that made me love going to his class at 8am. Highly, highly recommend.

Do yourself a favor and take 273 with Zach. No exams in this class (unlike other sections), only graded by a group project and some easy mini quizzes that you have unlimited attempts. He's so funny and friendly. He genuinely cares and checks in with students to make sure they are okay. Really values course feedback and tries to improve the course.
One of the few tenured professors that actually gives a crap about teaching. Also really funny.

When I tell you that Professor Kerr is how I wish all professors at UNC were, it's the truth. Professor Kerr cares about you as a person before a student & is always very interested in how you're doing outside of class. He understands that college is hard & will help you in any way he can to meet deadlines & answer your questions. HE IS THE BEST!!!

Dr. Kerr is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. He is SO funny, which makes class enjoyable, and he cares about students' success more than any professor I've had.  He was always quick to answer questions via email, and despite being an online class, I got to build a relationship with him. I wish I could take another class with Dr. Kerr!

Zack is one of the best professors at UNC. He really does care for students and their well-being and allowed extensions. His lectures are funny and interesting to watch. There are a lot of assignments, but they are super low-stress and easy to complete and mainly graded on effort. No final. He truly is a gem, couldn't recommend him enough!

truly the best professor i've had at UNC. he is genuinely one of the most caring and understanding professors you can ask for. there's two lectures due a week and usually an assignment in between, but everything is super easy and rubrics (and extensions!!!!) are provided. cannot recommend him enough!!!

Dr. Kerr is SUPER funny and cares a lot about his students!! This course wasn't super hard aside from that statistics portion, but he helps in that unit to make things not as bad as it could be. No exams when I took it, but quizzes after each lecture (mostly completion) to make sure we were on track and no questions. Great professor and course!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. He really cares that you learn the material and cares about his students as people. He is incredibly knowledgable about research and is great with explanations. This class is labor-intensive, but there is no busy work. Everything is intentional and designed to ensure you learn the material.

Zack is one of the best professors Ive had at UNC! His class requires a lot of work on your end, but every assignment has a purpose and he gives great feedback. The class is not easy, but he sets you up for success. Zack is hilarious, understanding, knowledgeable, and very organized. Be prepared to think critically. I recommend Zack 10/10 for 273!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Kerr is one of the most phenomenal and understanding professors I've had in college! He wants you to excel and will make you work for your grade. It's one of those classes where you get out what you put in. Although asynchronous, he put forth his best effort to make the class enjoyable. He's truly deserving of tenure.

TAKE KERR... everything is pretty much just graded for completion and not accuracy and if not he lets you redo it for full credit. HE IS THE GOAT. always willing to give an extension on assignment... can be somewhat of a boring class towards the end but makes it tolerable. 10/10 take 273 with Kerr

First, its Zack, not Dr. Kerr. Provided daily memes and even brought coffee one day. Most understanding and accommodating professor at UNC. Opened every assignment early during the pandemic so I could finish the class on April 1. If he does not meet tenure, then UNC aint doing something right. Dont pass this opportunity up.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Zack is an awesome, kind professor. He truly wants you to exceed and is more than willing to answer questions. There are 3 exams (questions come from PPTs) , 10 HWs and a group research project. Attendance is mandatory and after 1 unexcused absence you will lose 1% off your overall grade for a maximum of 5% off, so definitely don't skip class.

Amazing professor & person, genuinely cares so much for his students. Very group project based and attendance is mandatory. Such an awesome & funny professor, very accessible for help & a reasonable guy. Would take this class again just to have him as a professor if I could
Zack was a great professor for 273! Really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. There is a group project instead of a final!

This class was... awkward. The rating that said "twists history to make Hindus look like the main and only aggressors in South Asia, which is extremely inaccurate and problematic" was true in my experience, and I'm not even Hindu. It was also a bit odd how Mughal conquest was never mentioned as conquest and was only painted in a positive light.

He was extremely hard to access. Thank the gods that I have a bunch of prior knowledge in this class because of my background, or else I would have failed. He doesn't give any meaningful feedback. Like seriously some comments on my essays were "????????????". He also only uses WhatsApp to communicate, which felt kind of unprofessional.

Funny professor, but spends a lot of time in class going on tangents. Participation and attendance matter a lot, and his assignment rubrics are often unclear or nonexistent. He grades relatively easily, but he has a TA who grades very difficultly, so hope you get Taj. Also grades late, as of finals week, I only had one assignment graded out of ~15.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Taj is a really funny guy. He emphasizes participation. His course content is not strictly slide-driven, so you will have to do some more implying/rely on background knowledge. Overall, the class is fairly easy and enjoyable. If you pay attention and participate, you will be fine.

He is very enthusiastic and seems like a nice guy, but could not understand anything he said. Slides are all over the place and had to self teach. The final exam was difficult and practically only his portion of the course. Would not recommend.

The worst of the three professors. This class is awful but his lectures were incoherent and did not make any sense. His questions on the final were ridiculously hard like he was trying to make us fail. Do not take this triple I and if you do- study the most insignificant parts of his lectures because that will be on the exam!
The class was just terrible. I'm sure in a smaller setting he would be a better professor but I had to self-teach most of the unit because it was hard to hear.

He was the most enthusiastic prof I've worked with. He's clearly passionate about the material and seems like a really caring nice guy, however, I couldn't understand most of what he had to say. This could have been a combo of the big lecture hall, bad mic, and his accent, but I really struggled because of it. Great prof...as for the class, RUN.

Not very accessible outside class, took a lot of time to answer. Very unclear guidelines for homework and projects. Lecture heavy but many do not relate to direct topics. Participation is required. Does not grade anything until last minute.

Afroz Ji was a great professor! The class is lecture and conversation-heavy, but I enjoyed that. We had homework weekly but it wasn't difficult and he is flexible on due dates. Be aware there are 2 group presentations and a skit. He states that he never fails students and while they are a good amount of assignments, it isn't difficult.

SUCH A SWEET PROF. available for questions at literally 1am. Funny and engaging lecture. Homework 63% literally can't fail. Super flexible deadlines. Helps out students with everything! participation = A

Best prof I've ever taken@UNC. His Homeworks are super easy and worth 63% so you can't fail even if you want to lol, final is worth 20% and easy if you speak Hindi/Urdu and did the homeworks on time. Deadlines are super flexible and lectures were super easy to follow. He is also super accessible outside class(on WhatsApp not email) I'd say take it.

Professor Taj was interesting, but it was very hard to hear/understand him in such a large lecture hall. He was definitely the better of the 3 IDST 129 professors, but it isn't a class I would recommend. He did perform an original song and dance on the last day which was very cool, and he seems to be very passionate. Good teacher, bad class.

Prof. Taj is very engaging and wants students to have fun and learn. He gave us lots of readings/films and the ones I watched were super interesting. On the last day of class he performed a song he wrote for us which was great. Awesome guy, would definitely recommend him!

He cares a lot about what he's teaching and who he's teaching. Definitely not something I was interested in (took as a gen ed) but he's the GOAT. Readings were concise but he did expect us to watch a lot of movies which I personally didn't do (wasn't gonna put in 3 hours between classes for a gen ed). Don't take the class but take Afroz' classes
GOAT

I saw the complaints that there aren't clear grading criteria. The grading is quite simple tho, engage and have fun. That's it. Other than that, the prof is super sweet, caring, and funny. It's been a tough semester, and this class was the only class that I could breathe. You're not going to get a better professor than him.

No formal lectures, everything depends on class discussions. Lot of films to watch outside of class. You write a few papers, forum posts, quizzes, student presentations. Be engaged and keep up with discussions and you'll have a blast. Prof Taj is very entertaining!

This course was supposed to be taught during study abroad but it was taught online this summer. I took it for gen ed requirements but actually enjoyed the class and Afrozji was a pretty good professor. He gave good feedback on essays and graded fairly. Although, the prompts were a little vague, they were still thought-provoking.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Taj was a nice guy and was very knowledgeable about Hindi-Urdu poetry. He was encouraging and gave very good feedback for papers. However, he often condescendingly mocks Hinduism and twists history to make Hindus look like the main and only aggressors in South Asia, which is extremely inaccurate and problematic.

Professor Taj made this course really enjoyable. He's very understanding of student needs which was especially nice during the pandemic. The class was not very hard; class participation is a must but there's plenty of opportunity for it. Lots of reading. Taj is a very sweet and funny person, I highly recommend taking any course with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Super fun class! He says participation matters a lot but I did the bare minimum and he still gave me an A. The papers seem a bit tough but if you write anything logical and reference the surface stuff from the readings, he'll give you a good grade. You don't watch a lot of movies for a VP class on film, but he's a really nice guy!

Awesome instructor! He's funny, approachable, and understanding. Grading criteria is not clear, but don't be alarmed by any terrible grades - he provides plenty of opportunity to raise them. Attendance and participation does matter A LOT, but again, it is not difficult to maintain this, especially with him as a teacher. Best class ever.

this fys is great for the ever-elusive vp credit. there's group movie project, a presentation, and a final paper that make up most of your grade. he has NO CLEAR GRADING CRITERIA and doesn't put any grades in until the very last day.

This was my second class with Afrozji, and his teaching style seems to be consistent throughout all his courses. He doesn't lecture much, if at all, and most of the classes are made up of student presentations. Not everybody likes this class setup, but I didn't have a problem with it!

(THIS IS FOR HNUR 305, not ASIA 150). Content is interesting. He makes it unenjoyable. Did the homework, grading criteria is VERY unclear. Everything seems to be subjective, so if you don't suck up to him, then chances are he won't care about you. Loves to go on rants. If you like hindi, then this class is impt, but he makes it unbearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Doesn't always give clear grading criteria, but does it matter? A legend.

Afroz is a really funny professor, and I admire his humor. He does not directly teach all of the lectures, but his class does provide lectures from multiple colleagues with information on other countries in modern Asia. Do not procrastinate on journal entries, and always attend recitation sections! Makes you answer three questions for attendance.

Not a very fine professor. Never gives clear guidelines and always assures you doing great when asked about your grades. Never posts grades until the very end and then doesn't leave you with much room for improving your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The class was a first year seminar, so participation and discussions are highly encouraged. However, with assignments there were no clear guidelines given, the grading seemed ambiguous and subjective without any explanation. Grades are not posted/made available until the end of the semester.

If you have the chance to take this class, please do it. This is one of my favorite classes and I learned so much new material in so many different ways. Each professor provided insight into some specific topic and opened up my perspectives to a much larger scale. Loved trips to shows and art museums as well. Take this class if you can!
This class consisted of different guess lectures, some were good and some weren't. He is a really good professor and cool guy. Gives extra credit and is willing to help you.

I was disappointed that the whole semester was taught by guest speakers; I wanted to listen on Dr. Taj's lectures. But if you have basic knowledge of Asia, this class will be a breeze. Assignments consist of journal entries and one (6pg) paper. Recommend seeing the movies, I really enjoyed them.
He doesn't lecture. He gets other people to do it for him. He has the best gig of any professor.
A bit disorganized; knowledgable feller
Great teacher. Take Indian film and novel if you can, it fulfills lots of requirements and is a very interesting/easy class.
They were super sweet when I took them last semester. Grading was kind of unclear, but also typically pretty easy. Really kind, was fun to have recitation with them!

I took EURO 159 when she was the teaching assistant. She is an extremely tough grader, and the rubric and expectations were often unclear. A lot of classmates ended up receiving lower grades than they thought they would. She's knowledgeable, but the grading felt inconsistent and it was hard to know what she was looking for.

Taken Abbey's classes for two semesters: TA in History 140(A-) and lecturer in History 130(A). Genuine about her interest in African History. Attend every lecture and actively participate. Helpful after class to review essay prior to submission. Grade is based on essays, participation, and a final group presentation. I am a STEM kid and did well.

Abbey was a great professor! She is very caring and did well with lectures. The class content was interesting and the discussions were engaging. 1 class per week was dedicated to student discussions which helped us better grasp the material. The course was graded based off participation, 2 papers, and 1 final group presentation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So nice!!!!!! Sweetest professor ever and a very easy A. Don't have to even show up. I'm a senior and haven't had such an easy A at UNC here.

Loved this class. Abelardo is such a great professor and he cares so much about what he teaches. I took this for a Gen Ed credit but honestly found this to be a super interesting class. He is very lenient with grading, he just wants you to learn. HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

Nicest professor and one of the easiest classes I've taken. Each class has a reading assignment with a summary, but he grades very leniently. There's one midterm, a group presentation, and a final 10-page partner essay. Overall, it's a very easy class, and he genuinely cares about his students and is passionate about the material.

Professor De La Cruz is so kind and caring, he tries his best to remember student names even in such a large lecture hall. There are a lot of readings for this class but very little assignments, the biggest ones being a group project and 10-page final essay. He is an easy and fair grader, and I found the class material very interesting.
Literally the nicest professor ever. So knowledgeable and such a great class.

He's extremely nice and I am very glad I took his class. He was caring and careful in his discussions, speaking from his personal studies and experience in the field. One of the few teachers that actually loves doing what he does.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Abelardo is by far one of the best professors I have gotten to experience at this school. He is excited about teaching and his enthusiasm makes the course interesting and insightful. In addition to this, he offers lots of insight on first hand experiences, allowing students to get a more comprehensive idea of Indigenous communities.

Abelardo is very passionate about what he teaches and a very lenient grader. I learned a lot from his RELI 138 class and can genuinely say I enjoyed writing the very few papers and assignments he gave us.

I was actually in Reli89 (Wasn't an option?), but Prof Abelardo was so funny, caring, and the class was super easy. He cares about his students and wants them to just succeed and be passionate about what he is teaching. I'd take him again, super easy class and great prof.
Nicest Professor Ive had at UNC. Very easy A if you do all the work. Would recommend him to anyone.

Dr. P is amazing and one of the best teachers I had this semester. She is always available during office hours and always checks in on students. The classwork is useful and not too difficult, with only a few hours of work outside of class each week. No exams.
You can tell that Dr. Panter actually cares about her students and she makes her classes enjoyable. She wants students to succeed and if you put effort in and participate you will do well.

Dr. P is really awesome. She cares very deeply about her students and her class is not hard at all. I had no tests. She is an easy grader and wants you to do well (very flexible with deadlines). However, her lectures can be very long and all over the place. It's fine because no tests means you don't need to be fully attentive and can space off.

Dr. P is great. She is completely bonkers, but so kind and sweet. She really cares about her students and makes you want to do your best. The class itself was very interesting and didn't have too much work associated with it. I would highly recommend her!
Dr. Panter is awesome!  She really cares about her students and is really easy to talk to.  She super enthusiastic about stats.  I would definitely recommende her :)

Dr. Panter is the most caring professor I've ever had. She really cares about each individual student and always takes the time to ask you how you're doing. She is SUPER enthusiastic about statistics. She's kind of a perfectionist, but always has a positive attitude. I'm definitely going to keep in touch with her after this class!

Dr. Panter is a wonderful woman and professor. She is so sweet and is always concerned with how people are doing as individuals, not just their performance as students. She is not always clear and doesn't always answer e-mails but she is brilliant and more than willing to help you with anything you could ask for.
Amazing!!! She is THE Prof. to take. Any class that she is teaching....TAKE IT! You will not be disappointed.
