Running wall-to-wall, arms flapping around like a coked up muppet is fun to watch, but it only taught me that Keynes is demand side, classicalists are supply side. Are the test and homework questions that simple? No way

Dr. Aguilar is the best professor I have had during my time at UNC. He genuinely cares about the learning experience. However, expect to work incredibly hard. His classes are not easy whatsoever. Despite the challenging subject matter he is more than willing to help outside of class time. I highly recommend Dr. Aguilar.

Worst professor I have ever had at any academic institution. He just can't teach. He walks from one side of the classroom then to the other (as if they were Keynesian & Classical) with his arms flapping around (not joking) telling you to use excel. I had to teach myself everything using YouTube

Dr. Aguilar is hands-down the best professor I have taken at UNC. The class may be one of the most challenging, but never have I learned so much and taken away so much value from 3 credit hours. I would highly recommend taking, but note that it is an extremely rigorous commitment.
Awesome professor that really cares and teaches very well but the class itself is very challenging. Be prepared to work hard and be confused all the time.

Aguilar's lectures, in the brief moments he would be lecturing, were fun and insightful. He's direct about what you need to know. He stops lecturing for group discussion too often though. His homework is brutal. Go to the LAs' hours. The multiple choice on his exams are similarly tough and worth too much. Negative curve makes getting an A hard.

He's a super nice, charismatic guy, which makes a lot of students (including myself) willing to overlook some of the flaws in the class. It is challenging material, but Aguilar could do more to make the class less painful. He posts very few materials online (in contrast to MSA in 410) and the textbook is quite poor.

Brilliant and nice guy, but the absolute worst professor I have ever had at any academic institution. He just can't teach. He was teaching the MAC Finance class, and it was basically him walking around the room with his arms flapping around (not joking) telling you to use excel. I had to teach myself everything using YouTube.

This class is very challenging. That being said, Aguilar does a great job teaching it. Compared to Micro (410), you will end up spending more time on homeworks and such because of the macrojournals. The material is very challenging and hard to grasp without textbook use. Take advantages of all the resources on the Sakai site.

Aguilar is a really likable guy and I think he's mostly popular because of that. This class is not easy, and it does not care if you succeed. That being said, it's very possible to succeed. Do the homeworks and understand the material and then attend help sessions for them, exams are very like the homeworks.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I am a computer science and econ double major, and this is the hardest class I have taken at UNC so far. Mike is an excellent teacher, the material is just extremely challenging, and the structure of the lectures and powerpoint are very disorganized. Get ready to work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Great teacher, very hard exams though but marks very fairly. Lots of connections high up as well, be prepared to work hard and reading the textbook helps too.  I came very unprepared to the midterm and failed it because the material seemed so much easier when he explained it in class. picked it up for the final though

Aguilar is a great lecturer and keeps you engaged. However, the material is extremely challenging. Homework assignments require great effort, but if you do these, use the resources provided on Sakai, & read the textbook for clarification, you will be prepared going into each exam. Also, do the group extra credit. It upped my final grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He's obviously very passionate which makes the class more enjoyable, but the class isn't really set up to make A's very achievable.  Concepts seem simple in class but tests and homeworks are very different.  I don't think it would be possible to pass if you skip class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Does a good job connecting material to RL. Lectures give a general sense of the concepts, but you have to apply them to questions you've never seen on the HW/exams. He curves until the avg is a 75. Hard to get an A due to the grading scale, but hard to fail (generous with Cs/Bs). This is a class that's really hard to do alone. Find study buddies.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There are times in your life when you just know a professor teaches for the right reasons. In those moments, you pause to look up and realize you are witnessing just that. Mike Aguilar is a fantastic professor. I had taken 3 courses with him at UNC and have now gone far into a PhD elsewhere. Without him, I would have never made it off the ground.

First of all he is an amazing teacher. No doubt about that.  However, the emphasis in his lectures can be misleading. He tries to give students a general sense, but his hws and exams are 90%  math. He would casually mention some points and you would likely think those are not important; they are. Don't let his economist charm fool you.
Great lectures, but difficult tests. Overall a really interested and engaging person, even if the class is really tough.

This is no easy class. Do every extra credit opportunity. Go to the help sessions and I don't just mean the one that's the night before the homework is due. Do practice questions. Ask questions. I recommend office hours for concepts/theory and help sessions for homework. Tests are doable with practice.

Very hard class but Mike is the man. Super 90's Wall Street. You will have to put in a lot of your own time if you want to do well, but it is worth it for future econ classes. The tests are very hard but not impossible. Homework is difficult but the TAs offer lots of review sessions to go through them before they are due.

Very poor quality of instruction. Class topic is complex and broad, but the professor barely explains the materialhe'll brush over it in a few seconds, and only uses about a third (literally) of total class time actually teaching. He almost never does examples, though difficult math is on tests. Expect to struggle unless you're a math genius.

420 is the bane of every econ major's existence. Aguilar makes it interesting, although the exams are impossible and the homework takes time. However, he curves well and gives opportunities for extra credit.

Professor Aguilar is clearly very smart and enthusiastic about what he teaches, which is good, except that he assumes everyone else is equally as smart and enthusiastic about the subject. I looked forward to his class every day because lectures were interesting, but the class moves very fast and the material is extremely difficult. Lots of hw.

Professor Aguilar is a great professor with extensive and interesting knowledge about the economy and its various nuances. While his lectures were fascinating and relatively easy to follow, the homework and tests were very difficult. You will not do well in this class if you don't go to lectures and TA sessions. Optional extra credit debates.

Professor Aguilar is very smart, although probably too smart for his own good. His homework and exams are very difficult and asks questions about material that hasn't always been covered.  He isn't the clearest professor, but his inclusion of current events makes the class fairly interesting. You should read the book, but you will learn a lot.

One of the toughest courses I have taken at UNC, but definitely worth it. Honestly, in this one class I feel like I've learned more about the economy than all of my other econ courses combined. AMAZING teacher. He is very difficult in terms of content and grading, but Aguilar is incredibly helpful and wants you to succeed in his class and beyond.

I got 100 on the midterm and became really lazy, so I did poorly on the final and got a B+. There are only a few multiple choice questions on the tests, which makes grades a little arbitrary. People who you know are a lot worse at the class than you can end up doing a lot better if they are lucky when guessing. If math is hard for you, good luck.

Aguilar is the best economics professor at UNC, hands down. He is not only a good researcher (which is how many professors are rated by the school), he gets really high marks on pedagogy. He just knows how to teach. We were learning some of the most difficult material I've ever seen, and he made it feel easy (sort of). Take if you like challenge.

By far the most difficult class I have taken at UNC, but even as  an intern in a totally different field, I use information learned in his class on a daily basis. If your GPA can afford to take the class, do it. Oh, and make sure you know Excel.
Tough class, but you will learn a ton through the work he requires. Any econ major should definitely take his class, otherwise you might want to save your GPA.

The class is really tough but if you put the effort in, you will be rewarded. There is no recitation section but the review sessions are all but mandatory if you want to get a good grade. Tests and homework are insane in difficulty compared to the depth of lecture, however, Aguilar is a great teacher who really cares about helping his students.
Really hard class the only midterm was an essay and 6 hard multiple choice question which count for 50% percent of the grade.

Homeworks are helpful, he's a pretty good communicator, but his tests are totally unreasonable. They're very difficult and too long so you're essentially being graded on how fast you can take the test.  I don't mind professors who make a class difficult, but this was ridiculous.

Amazing Professor! Great lecturer! VERY knowledgeable and will never misrepresent students and tries to be as helpful as possible. His tests require you to REALLY understand econ concepts and theories. Not the easiest class, but you learn a lot if you pay attention and really try.

Excellent lecturer on macroeconomics.  Aguilar will give you a solid grounding in macro theory.  I learned a lot in this class about both the theory and the math.  Only problem is that he has too much confidence in the TAs, who are absolutely clueless.  Macro Journal is a great assignment that teach you how to interpret economic news.

Though I came in with no interest in Econ, I found Aguilar to be a pretty good prof- surprisingly engaging, and good at explaining concepts and answering questions.  My problem in this class is with the tests: at least for me, the time given was never sufficient to work the problems.  I question the applicability of speed in economic analysis.
his homework and tests have nothing to do with his lecture notes. just do above the curve, which can be relatively high, and you'll do fine.
Tests are multiple choice. He tests only on key information. Previous tests are made available. Strikes a good balance between math and theory.
the material and his grading are not easy but he tries to make it salient to current events and things students are interested in.

Aguilar is a great guy. The problem with this class is the TAs. They do not come to class but they write the HW and tests which means we're tested on things that weren't taught. The questions are made as tricky as possible. TAs assume we understand everything so they don't teach what they are supposed to. Only TA worth anything is Justin Contat.

He is soooo helpful. Since it's just Macro Theory he makes sure not to use too much math,or else he makes sure to really dumb it down for those math impaired (like me). 2 midterms, HW each Fri., MacroJournals each Thurs, 1 final. And he loves what he's teaching and has real experience using macroeconomics so he is smart! and hot!!...in a geeky way

Great Professor, will never misrepresent anyone.  Doing the course compass practice problems are extremely helpful. Quizzes and HW boost your grade and its collaborative.  Curves, but it helps most and grading scale is all on 5 point increments, making a B- a 75-80.
No Comments

Mike Acosta is an incredible teacher. Class is never boring and he actually cares about each student. He has a wealth of knowledge and shares it in an understandable way. He emphasizes that the class is to grow, and you don't have to stress about turning in perfect work. You can genuinely learn. If you can take a class with Mike, do it.

He was by far the best professor I have EVER had at this school. I am a premed stem student and I took this class as my sanity class and it was the best decision. I enjoyed this class so much because of Dr. Acosta. The content and the class were enjoyable but it was Dr. Acosta who brought the class to life.

What a guy. Easily the best professor I've had at UNC. Acosta cares so much about his students. The man has lived three different lives and has countless hilarious stories he loves to share. He is so knowledgeable and inspirational, and he feels more like a friend than a professor. Cannot recommend him enough. Amazing final lecture too.

One of the best teachers I've had at UNC! Acosta tells hilarious stories that connect back to screenwriting and gives very good advice for life in general. He's very knowledgeable and truly cares for students and their education. Take this class if you can!!

Dr. Acosta has been the best professor I've had at UNC thus far. He is so funny and actually cares about us as students, which you don't see from the other professors at UNC. The lectures were so funny and he related it to screenwriting, which allowed me to learn in a way that I haven't in any other class in my life.

He has some of the most engaging lectures and every class he'll tell an incredible story. Assignments are graded for completion so as long as you submit them on time you'll get an A. He makes the group projects fun and I learned a lot over the course of the semester. Left the class with a new outlook on life.

Acosta rocks. He has lived a thousand lives and has the best anecdotes. As long as you really try in his class, it will pay off. If you're even slightly interested in screenwriting or movie production, take a class with him! He has a lot of valuable knowledge and advice about the industry, great guy!

Mike is and will probably continue to be the best professor I have had at UNC. While I am really bad at regularly attending my classes, this course is one I made sure to always go to. Not necessarily because I have to, but because I wanted to and looked forward to it. He is genuinely caring and pays attention. I could write so much more about him.
Professor Acosta is the best professor I have ever had. He is entertaining, funny, and knows what he is talking about. You must take his class if you get the chance!!
BEST PROFESSOR AT UNC!!!

Professor Acosta is one of the most influential and memorable professors at UNC. He has a plethora of knowledge about screenwriting and tells incredible stories in class. If you attend class and apply his notes/feedback, you will do good. I only hope I can take him again.

I truly believe Professor Acosta's classes have taught me more applicable knowledge than any of my others combined. Between learning how to screenwrite from scratch, to all the life skills he tries to instill in his students, I am thankful to have been a part of WSS and to have learned from him the past two years.
Mike is awesome. It's clear he cares greatly about his students. He is here because he actually loves teaching. He knows so much about screenwriting. Take this class.

Laid-back, witty, smart, cares deeply about film and his students. Some may dislike his blunt, old-school attitude but I appreciate that he always says exactly what he thinks. Cultivates a genuine connection with students and turns lectures into a conversation, making every class engaging and fun. Easily the best professor I've had at UNC.

Mike is the best professor I've had at UNC. He's hilarious, and his bluntness is never insensitive. He really cares about his students and treats them like the young adults they are. He's been a hugely influential mentor. He's not an Ivory Tower professor - he's pragmatic, no-BS, and empathetic. Take as many classes with him as you can.

One of my favorite professors I've ever had. That said, there's not much middle ground with Mike, I find that people either really vibe with him or they don't. He's got a really refreshing perspective on teaching and the industry as a whole and you'll learn a ton from him. He loves his students and wants them to succeed. Take a class with him!

Super hilarious and very knowledgable about the industry, I recommend this class for anyone who is interested in screenwriting, even if you don't plan on applying to the minor. Mike also makes it a point to give the class opportunities outside of school to gain industry experience. Class is not hard as long as you put in effort.

Professor Acosta is hilarious. Constantly made me enjoy my time in his classroom and was very caring when it came to students learning. He gave great feedback that helped me improve in screenwriting and even tried to give opportunities outside of class for students to expand their portfolios.

Professor Acosta is my favorite professor I've had at UNC so far! He was hilarious, encouraging, gave very applicable and useful lessons, and got the whole class excited about screenwriting. Assignments were very doable and graded for completion. I highly recommend taking a class with him if you get the chance.

(This rating is for 330 but still applies) Acosta is an amazing teacher!  Take a class with him if you have any interest in writing or media.  He is a very engaging speaker and you will enjoy going to class.  The workload is not heavy and he says that you can get an A as long as you put effort in.

Acosta can be a little irreverent so i might avoid him if you know you've got a thinner skin, but as a writer and teacher, he is amazing. Great feedback, great handle on storytelling and art direction, and underneath all the rowdy exterior he's a big softy who cries at well-written scripts. Class is super entertaining and it's easy to do well.
This class was atrocious. Take another professor.

Not sure why the MATH186 ratings are so bad, I guess you guys didn't study. Class is super hard, but Andy's a great professor and really accessible outside class. Doesn't give much material for exam prep, but class problems and reviews outside of class are very representative of what the exam looks like. Work is hard but doable, very fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Does not care for your grade. The hardest professor to take for stats at Lafayette.

Professor Ackerman is nice, though his class is extremely difficult. His review sheets are no where close to what an actual exam looks like. His grading is harsh and he does not like to give out good grades. Look to take another statistics professor because he is not caring of your grade, though says he is. Dislike him a lot..

Concepts are hard but Andy was helpful in OH. Virtually no material to help you study for exams and HW questions did not always relate to class / exams. Great lecturer and educator in general. Looked forward to class.
Horrible. Grading is harsh. Does not drop lowest midterm. Grading unclear. Don't take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: WOW, andy is one of the best teachers I've had at UNC, he is the sweetest guy who cares about his students. He is very open to meeting outside of class and tests are very similar to practice problems

The goat. Awesome guy who loves to teach. He genuinely cares for his students, their well-being, and their performance in class. He talks to the students often and wants to know them well. He's super chill and loves to help also. 5/5 Great guy and would so take his class again!

Super cool chill guy and good lecturer, very passionate about his job and statistics. 2 or 3 easy homeworks a week, drops lowest midterm(if final is higher) can overexplain things but sometimes that is appreciated. Best Stor 155 professor based on those I know who have had different ones. Straightforward and approachable. Take his class!

*ANTHRO 364*
I loved this class. Dr. Dorsey teaches us about professional development as an Anthropologist, and I still use the notes I took in her class to this day.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Love her! One of the best professors at UMass. Her classes and lectures are interesting and easy to follow. Provides slides before class. She does have a lot of readings but only a few of them are compulsory reads. Fairly easy midterm and final. One final project, 2 other projects and a few Course Reflections.
Dr. Dorsey is a great lecturer and a very kind professor. I would highly recommend her classes, especially Anthropology 313 (Nutritional Anthropology).

Professor Dorsey was one of the best professors I had at UMass. She makes learning content fun and super interesting. I have a lot of respect for her. Take a class with her! You'll learn so much without being overwhelmed, and she's always willing to help if you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: amazing 10/10 recommend her

Achsah was my TA for this class, and it was a pretty TA heavy class (meaning they did all the grading and that's who you actually interacted with in recitation). I enjoyed her a lot! She's really nice and has a pleasant personality, and she got to know us all by name. She isn't an easy grader, but it's nothing insane. Solid choice overall

I really loved this class! It was probably my favorite that I've taken for my minor! Professor Dorsey is super nice and accessible and I loved the content and assignments. The group project and paper are also not bad at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I enjoyed SPAN344 (not 373 344 wasn't an option). This course was chill & insightful. Sometimes it was hard do all readings. Professor wasn't perfect (a bit unorganized... FYI to ppl who get stressed over that lol) BUT he was really flexible and understanding throughout the class which is rare in the ROML department. 8.5/10 class would take again!

This was probably my favorite class at UNC. I usually struggle with participating but the prof is so knowledgeable and funny I felt really comfortable! He is also very kind and willing to work with the class on due dates. Iffy about Canvas, but everything was clear in the syllabus. 11/10, unique experience!

It is clear that this is Rafael's first semester teaching here, which can excuse his unstructured and uninspired way of teaching. Class always felt incredibly dull which is surprising considering the class was about fiction writing (one of the most entertaining forms of writing). Excited to see how he structures future classes, he has the passion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Absurdly easy. Lectures aren't mandatory and all material comes from slides, which he posts online. No point attending class if you don't want to. HW can be done as a group. Tests are really easy (my ECON 101 class was 3 times as hard!) He's pretty funny and a good lecturer.  Microeconomics need not be daunting with Ackermann. Recommended!19940

Jeff is a super nice guy and his lectures (that you definitely don't have to attend) are funny. However, his tests are not written by him so they don't relate well to what he lectures on in class. It should all be super easy, but I was definitely caught off guard with a horrible final that ruined my grade. Glad it's over.

His class seems easy until you have a test. He doesn't writes his own homework or tests so they don't correspond to his lectures very well. Also, a lot of times he doesn't really know what he's talking about. He's funny so his lectures aren't too boring and there's not much work outside of class but the tests took me off guard.
This is a tough class mostly because the professor doesn't know what he's talking about. He is good at teaching the specific material, but he lacks basic knowledge of topics taught in ECON 101.

Professor Shapiro is one of the few professors that doesn't require a purchased textbook, but instead provides us with PDFs of the material. He's very thorough and lectures are genuinely engaging. Attendance is mandatory for recitations, not for the lecture. He was very accommodating when I had to reschedule my midterm due to travel conflict.
Nicest professor I've ever had. Take his class for an easy A and interesting material. Super nice about late submissions and missing class.
** Correction to my last review, difficulty is NOT a 5.

Aaron was a gem!! I am a senior and took his Algorithms & Society class with little to no experience with interpreting data and he made sure that even the hardest readings were made understandable. He is so kind, understanding, and I genuinely learned so much in his class. 100% take this class you wont regret it
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took Comm 455: He genuinely cares about students and has an amazing response time to emails. You really don't have to go to class until you get to the end when everyone is giving presentations. There were 3 really easy assignments, a scavenger hunt, a short paper/video about a soundscape, and an essay on any sound topic for the final. 100% take him

Overall, I really liked prof. Shapiro, however if you don't have a background in algorithms/data science I think this class may be hard as just a comm major. It's not horrible and I'm looking to finish with an A or A- but a lot of the information we learned went over my head. I do like prof. Shapiro a lot and he is very knowledgeable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Such a great guy and his classes were pretty organized. The reading responses were somewhat irritating but that was the hardest thing he really graded within the class. He was very easy to get in contact with and is very understanding. Would definitely take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: It was cool to learn about algorithms. He is very nice. There are lots of readings but you do not need to do a heavy read on all of them and they are covered in class. You submit reading responses that are graded easily and then there are a bunch of group projects that he gives clear grading criteria and steps on.

Professor Shapiro is honestly just the best. 12/10 recommend taking one of his classes if you get the chance to. He's incredibly caring and does so much to make the material accessible and interesting to students, particularly in the range of class materials he assigns (podcasts, videos, films, etc). Truly one of the best profs I've had at UNC!

Papers and attendance are the bulk of the grades, originally had 3 papers and a final paper but he cut it down to 2 papers, the 2nd paper being the final. Understanding and accessible, chance to get extra credit with a 3rd paper. Lectures can get dry with little participation, and readings are a bit long, 40-75 pages, but it is interesting stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Shapiro was my favorite professor this semester. EXTREMELY understanding: he pushed back a paper, offered extra credit, and even allowed you to make up absences. His lectures were extremely interesting and he gave the option of if you wanted to attend in person or through zoom. Definitely take his course. Definitely take his class.
Awesome professor with interesting classes! 10/10 recommend

Aaron was a delight this semester. He was my first 400 COMM class and his class was not difficult at all. The workload includes writing reflections for readings every week, a sound-related exercise every week, a Soundscape project (got 100 for going out and recording sounds), and a 10-page final (find an interesting topic, it will help). 10/10 Prof

This was a sound studies course- special topics. Not a hard course. He's very understanding and chill. You do need to read for the course, but there aren't any textbooks you need to purchase. He provided everything. The assignments are not hard at all, it's very easy to pass this course.

Amazing lecturer and explained concepts really well. You can tell he really cares about his students and teaching. Very test heavy however but not too difficult of a course as long as you go to class. Really accessible outside of class and posts his notes right before the midterms/final. Not hard but you'll have to put in some effort for an A

Andy is a great and caring person who answered every single question with much consideration and patience. My only issue with the course is the structure of the class (2 exams, final replaces lowest midterm, homework grades). Very little resources to help students properly prepare for exams and a bad exam can tank your grade. Great guy though.
WOW, andy is one of the best teachers I've had at UNC, he is the sweetest guy who cares about his students. He is very open to meeting outside of class and tests are very similar to practice problems
Eh ok I guess

Fantastic lecturer, always energetic and engaging. You can tell he is truly passionate about the material and teaching it to his students. He cares about each of his students on an academic and personal level. His class was genuinely interesting and the material was important. I know many other STAN majors who are interested in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was the hardest course I ever took, but Andy is a FANTASTIC teacher. He truly loves the material & is very enthusiastic. You'll be writing R code to analyze complicated stats, so knowing calc helps. I understood very little of what was said in lecture just because I didn't know math. Overall, a rewarding class if you're willing to put in work!

Andy genuinely cares about his students. His grading criteria is clear but if any questions arise, he is quick to clarify and communicate. His aim is clearly for the students in his class to actually learn, grow, interact with each other and the material, and come away with a stronger understanding of both statistics and ethical considerations.

Andy is the best instructor I have had at UNC Chapel Hill. He is extremely accessible and cares for his students, having great availability outside of class. Andy's passion for teaching is inspiring and his class is applicable to all aspects of life, making it well worth it. I continue to build off what I learned in lecture, I highly recommend!

i am of the belief that actions speak louder than words and it felt that often this professor was focused more on sounding like they had good intentions than actually acting as someone who truly had good intentions towards their students. to clarify on this, i often felt that the bare minimum effort was put in covered up by enthusiastic lectures

If Andy has managed to keep me, a graduating senior in an 8AM class, then you know he's done something right. His enthusiasm in each lecture makes the most boring topics engaging. He encourages students to participate, from discussions on ethics to math principles. He is accessible via email or OH and goes above and beyond to support his students.

Unclear grading criteria and a bit argumentative at times in class. I don't think that he takes diversity into account much when creating his syllabus or discussing outcomes of thought experiments which myself and a few others students in the course felt was ironic given this special topics course focus on morality and ethics.
Overvalues participation being that many topics can be self taught but is an interesting lecturer to listen to.

Grading expectations are made clear on syllabus however exams count for majority of your grade. If you aren't a good test taker, he makes the exams heavily conceptual and does not provide many resources outside of class. Office hours are limited and he/TA would not provide feedback on any of the exams, so you'd have to meet with them personally

Great professor, what a wonderful guy. Super caring, and will answer every single question you throw out at him, and is great for office hours. Beware, he doesn't record lectures, and only writes on chalkboard, other than that, I loved the guy, but his class is a little harder than every other professor. I would take him again for sure.
Really good professor for Statistics. If you're taking STOR 155, this is the guy you want. Explains things very clearly and the class never feels like it's going too fast.

STOR455: Andy has by far been my favorite professor at UNC. Andy went above and beyond to care for and ensure that every student understood the material. the most caring, sweetest, knowledgeable, respectful, and overall amazing professors I have ever had the opportunity of learning from. I will definitely be taking more classes with him.
Review for Stor 113. Great guy! Genuinely wants students to succeed and is always willing to explain concepts. Lets you replace your lowest midterm with your final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You get a cheat sheet on your exams & drops the lowest midterm if your final is higher! Overall, he's great and genuinely wants you to succeed. He's very accessible and a good teacher, even though math isn't my strong suit. All lectures are on a chalkboard w/ no recordings, so if you miss content, you'll have to ask a friend for notes. Recommend :)

Super cool chill guy and good lecturer, very passionate about his job and statistics. 2 or 3 easy homeworks a week, drops lowest midterm(if final is higher) can overexplain things but sometimes that is appreciated. Best Stor 155 professor based on those I know who have had different ones. Straightforward and approachable. Take his class!

The goat. Awesome guy who loves to teach. He genuinely cares for his students, their well-being, and their performance in class. He talks to the students often and wants to know them well. He's super chill and loves to help also. 5/5 Great guy and would so take his class again!

Excellent professor, super passionate, and very caring. Though, exams are difficult and tested a lot on statistical concepts. He was generous in providing practice exam problems, but ultimately we had no good way to practice for concepts. Too much to bank on when exams are weighted so heavily. No stats exam should have a true or false section.

Super chill and cool guy, very personable. I believe he taught the class well, some people complain that the course was quite difficult, and that's going to come with any sort of statistics class. Overall, I thought he was great and it was very cool that he made an effort to get to know students.

Pretty cool guy. Chill, easy to reach, and always super helpful! Though would teach things a very specific way and then would throw curveballs on exams. No matter how confident I was in the material, exams were super stressful, even with a cheat sheet. Had plenty of conceptual questions on exams that didn't make sense for an intro level course!

Very available outside of class which is great however he is not very accommodating for extenuating circumstances. Tests are extremely conceptual based and conceptual-based material is barely brushed on in lectures making the exams quite hard. Class was done completely on a chalkboard and refused to post notes until a few days before the exam
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Andy is really good. Many office hours and very kind. THe only thing is that he did not give practice exams. You may need more time outside the classroom.

Great teacher, genuinely cares about stats and explains the material thoroughly. But the exams he makes are really hard compared to the classwork and homework. Even if you really know the material, exams are still bound to be challenging. Would not take again just to save my gpa but overall super nice and funny guy.

Andy was a good lecturer and funny. He was passionate about his teaching, explained concepts well in class, and was ready to help students. However, he was a bit stringent with deadlines so don't expect extensions. The course should involve more hands-on coding instead of just looking at code in lectures as I had to revise old lectures repeatedly.

Andy is one of the best teachers I've had in 4 years at UNC, and easily the best Statistics teacher. He genuinely cares about his students and is always available to answer questions. I had a bad experience with the group project, but Andy was very sympathetic and accommodating when I talked with him. Take him if you get the chance, I promise.
Nice guy, nice lectures, easy homework and labs. HOWEVER, GROUP PROJECT GRADINGS WERE EXTREMELY TOUGH SO BE AWARE OF THAT.

Best professor I have had in the statistics department. Actually cares about teaching and for his students. The kind of teacher you actually want to be friends with. I had a family emergency and he was super accommodating. Whenever I asked questions during office hours or over email, he was extremely helpful. Would give him a 10/5 if I could.

Andrew seems to care about his students, but it isn't always apparent in his actions. He has highly stringent deadlines that have sharp grade cut-offs for even being just a few hours late, (sometimes even a 0%). Lab TAs lack any semblance of motivation or urgency to help students. Andy seems nice but he doesn't really care.

Andy is one of the best professors I have had at UNC. He genuinely cares about each of his students and wants you to succeed. His lectures were interesting and easy to understand (and I am not a math person). Expectations for exams are clear and he prepares you well for them. Take Andy if you have the chance!

Andy was the best instructor I've had at UNC thus far. He was kind, patient, and cares about his students. He actually made math fun. I took Stor 113 and 155 with him and it's not an easy A but if you put in the work you will get good results. Definitely choose Andy as your instructor he is great!
The best, super cool guy, for sure take with him.

Andy was really great. Expectations on tests are made clear with review sessions and he's very cool and approachable. His explanations of concepts were great. While we worked out problems he walked around & asked everyone how they were doing (alleviates question-asking anxiety). If you're gonna take STOR 155, take it with Andy.

Lectures are somewhat stream-of-consciousness, interesting to listen to but sometimes feels unguided. About 4-5 graded assignments make up your grade, but she's a relatively easy grader. Incredibly caring and willing to speak with you during office hours, but the course would've benefitted from slightly better structuring.

Wellesley - ANTH 101 Really kind prof! Very accessible and inspiring/global with her viewpoint. Wants everyone to succeed and provides the means to do so. If you get the chance, take a class with her!
She's teaching at Wellesley now and I took her class last semester. Learned so much in her class, best professor I couldve ever ask for in college. I'd be thankful in my life to have Dr. Sadruddin.

The class I had her for was a seminar class about disability but the drop down didn't have the class I took under her. I absolutely loved her class. I definitely recommend her. whatever was confusing she made it easy to understand. she answered emails fast. gave a lot of feedback on papers which helped when writing the next paper assigned

She is really an amazing teacher and wants all of her students to succeed- I came out of this class with not only a catalog of amazing content but also someone I know I can go to for further advisement in my studies. Sadruddin is really great at lecturing and integrating concepts in very unique ways. I highly recommend her course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of favorite profs ever! Dr. Sadruddin is such a kind person and really cares about her students. She wants you to do well in her course. Graded mainly on papers but they were not too hard.

Dr. Sadruddin is the BEST! The course structure is weekly readings and an easy-going class discussion about them. There are several writing assignments, but she grades fairly and provides amazing feedback. She WANTS you to succeed and to love med anth as much as she does. She is energetic and passionate. There is not a class I would recommend more.

Sadruddin is an absolute gem. The class is on the anthropology of care and it was a wonderful experience understanding its complexities, both good and bad, especially how evident it is today. As long as you do the reading and participate, your assignment and class grades are fine. She is very sweet and calls our class the "care circle". Love her!

Best and clearest lecture slides in the COMP department. Labs were only hard because the sensors were not reliable but tests were pretty easy. Content is very interesting and I learned a lot. Would definitely recommend taking this class. But remember, there is a lot of unpredictability and a lot of uncertainty in robotics...

There wasn't too much homework, but there is a group project where you build a robot and design it for the given lab days. The labs get progressively harder and make up the bulk of the class grade, and took my group anywhere from 5 - 10 hours a week outside of class to prepare. The assignments/exams were fairly challenging (mostly trigonometry).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took COMP 89 with professor Alterovitz. SUPER easy class. 3 assignments and 2 projects for the entire semester, no homework. Class can be boring sometimes but Professor Alterovitz is super passionate about what he researches and studies. He does not take attendance. I highly recommend taking this class for a FC and easy freshman launch.

He's very passionate about tech., only talked about robots, AI, & internet instead of many topics. Grade based on a few assignments and 2 presentations (7 & 15 minutes). Attendance policy is unclear but as far as I know, he did not record attendance (syllabus said he would take it 3 random days). Lectures are somewhat boring but the class is easy

This class was poorly organized. He never gave us enough time to do assignments. His lectures were long and often not comprehensive. Refused to go over practice questions or homework. Never reviewed coding even though there were two massive assignments that were entirely coding.

He is clearly very knowledgeable about robotics but this class was bogged down by the way it was organized. We should've had more time to do the coding assignments and more example problems that are like the exams. He tended not to go over many problems and never coding. But he was considerate about grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: A super sweet guy and gives opportunities to make up for low grades (i.e., drops lowest lab grade and extra credit for participating). The robotics labs were pretty tricky and took up a lot of time, but otherwise, the class was relatively fair (I imagine most will get a B at the end of the semester). Super nice guy and a super interesting class!

Altervitz knows what he's talking about but is kind of boring and class was long. PowerPoint slides were very helpful as notesfor studying. Programming assignments were very hard and took a lot of effort to complete. Tests were hard but if you studied hard you could get a good grade on them.

We didn't follow the syllabus at all for this course, but it was fine. One lab assignment every 2 weeks ish (total 8) and a final project/presentation, with very lenient grading. Wouldn't take if I wasn't a geog major tho

Holy disorganization. Syllabus was completely unreflective of the course, he skipped half the content because of how much he rambles, quiz/paper due dates were given out randomly, etc. Thankfully, the content is super easy, papers are graded easily, and two quiz grades can be replaced. Easy A as long as you're ready to deal with the chaos.

I have to agree with others on Dr. Moody. He's very intelligent, but I don't think he's meant to teach; he's very unorganized, and the lectures make me want to fall asleep. His PowerPoints look like they were made in 2009. I only took this class because it's required for the Geography major, but if you're not GEOG, I do not recommend this course.

Dr. Moody is a wonderful person, but lacks the organization and preparation of a professor. Originally took this course for an easy allied science, ended up P/F due to the lack of information for assignments and course information in general. Class slides were often never uploaded and students are expected to understand material from diagrams only.

Dr. Moody is a great person, but do not take this class unless you genuinely care about the topic. I took this as an "easy" allied science and ended up having to P/F it because there were only a few quizzes, 2 papers, and 2 exams & the info on the quizzes and exams is nowhere to be found on Canvas bc he jumps around the ppt and doesn't upload them.

idk y ppl be savying he's unorganized. a little quirky, sure. it's one of those classes if you care, it will seem organized. but lowkey why are you taking a 390 class if you don't care tbh. loved dr. moody would take any class he taught ever again
Dr. Moody is so kind and compassionate. He is a little disorganized, but makes up for it with his humor and attentiveness. He's flexible and smart, but in a way that you have to keep up with.

Prof Moody was very nice and the TA was wonderful, but this class was insanely disorganized. The syllabus was completely optional and it seemed as though he came to class each day not knowing what he wanted to cover. No students ever had a clue what was going on either.

He's a bit of an eccentric guy and a dry lecturer but he knows the subject very thoroughly and explains things well. Assignments could be a lot but he often let us work on them in class and walked around helping people out. Midterm was very straightforward and was take-home, which was nice. I would take him if you are interested and self-motivated

Professor Moody is a sweet guy and is ALWAYS available to help you with homeworks and labs outside of class which is super nice. The syllabus is nothing like the actual class, but he often cancels assignments and pushes due dates back which means less work for the students. Great professor, but maybe don't take if you need a lot of structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Moody's lectures can get quite boring, but he is a nice person who is engaged in the material he is teaching. He wants to see his students do well, and shifted the syllabus to be more accommodating and gave lots of extra credit opportunities. The TA graded pretty strictly on papers and some grading felt inconsistent.

Unless you are truly fascinated with the intricacies of the subject matter, he is an extremely dry monotone lecturer. It was not a difficult class, but he goes on tangents that are generally underwhelming as someone who is uninterested in the subject matter.

Not sure why Professor Moody's rating is so low on here. He speaks about the subject matter clearly and intelligently and has always been available outside of class for questions. Opportunities for extra credit.  If you need a lot of personal attention and in-class activities, this is not the teacher for you, but I don't regret taking his class.

Do not take a class with him unless it is absolutely required. He is so unorganized and unprofessional. It was a living nightmare of a class could not stress it enough do not take a class with this man.
Boring class and teacher

Honestly the most boring, yet easiest class, I've ever taken in my life. Professor Moody lectures in a very monotonous way, and you spend way too much time drawing dirt. With that being said, this class is a great option for its respective gen-ed credit, so I would highly recommend it.

Dr. Moody is a nice man, but if you need someone with structure I would not recommend. Lab instructions are misleading and are not concise. Never really goes by the syllabus and assigns whatever whenever. Doesn't post grades. Claims to receive your emails but NEVER answers them and is sometimes late to office hours which is discourteous.

There was only one paper, but it was 20 pages minimum. Wasn't bad though since you can use photos and graphs to supplement. Dr. Moody is nice, I think, but really not interactive with the class at all. I found that there was honestly ALOT of material and it is straight memorization. Personally, I like something a little more interactive.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Moody is a fine teacher. His class is entirely based on lectures and a few online homework assignments, which can take some time but there were only 4 the whole semester. Very long final paper, 20 pages turned in through two 10 page papers. His study guides are almost the exact same as the tests. Easy, but very boring.
Seriously the easiest class I have ever taken. We watched movies and had two assignments the whole time.

For a first year seminar class, Professor Moody was a good choice as he is very laid back and we never even got to most of the assignments on the syllabus. Pretty much if you show up occasionally and do well on the stuff he gives you, it's an easy A.

Dr. Moody is a terribly ineffectual professor; this is the only class in my three years of college where I thoroughly prepared for the first exam, yet still failed it. His expectations for quizzes and exams were dreadfully unclear, and I never expected a 100-level course to be so unnecessarily difficult. DO NOT TAKE GEOG110 WITH THIS PROFESSOR!

DO NOT TAKE GEOG 110 WITH MOODY UNLESS YOU ABSOLUTELY NEED TO. Objectives of the class are unclear, syllabus dates were incorrect (had Good Friday listed as April 13 when it was in March), was unprepared for lectures most days, and did not answer questions clearly. I took this class as a gen ed and it was a terrible decision.
The class was a little disorganized but not hard to follow at all. Professor moody is really chill which made the class super easy. As long as you show up and pay attention, you will do fine.
Really passionate about his subject

GEOG 110 was the hardest class I've ever taken because there was no clear syllabus  we just jumped around and focused on whatever he decided to talk about. Lectures were completely out-of-touch with powerpoints and textbook readings. Professor Moody is chill but not the best at answering questions, either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I found his class to be very unorganized.... No textbook and lectures do not go in any clear order. No real syllabus, and TA took forever to get grades back (have yet to receive most of them still)  Difficult to know what to study and where to find information for exams
He never answered emails, didn't really stick with the syllabus. He wasn't very helpful even when contacted multiple times.
He was the most disorganized and least helpful professor I have had at UNC so far.

I recommend this class to everyone as it's relevant to everyone. It was a fairly depressing class--global warming and all--but I learned a lot. It was definitely not easy. I busted by tail for a B+, but I enjoyed it. He's laid back w/ a California accent, sitting cross-legged on the desk, cracking jokes. And he's really interested in the material.
Dr. Moody is interesting, funny, and knows what he's talking about. If you're interested in environmental science, definately take this course.
Dr. Moody is really engaging - his classes are a hoot! He may not always be organized but he always interesting material to present. Plus, he is a total hottie!!!

This class was a total waste of time.  no organization in his teaching.  no use of books assigned, thus lecture is always mandatory, yet you never know what will be included on the tests.  he goes off on tangents and tests you on them.  Do Not Take One Of His Classes!

Professor Harcus was a great lecturer, and I really learned a lot from this course! Class is fairly easy consisting of attendance, reading/listening responses, a listening exam, and final project which are all graded easily.

Reads directly off slides, but somewhat interesting class if you're SUPER interested in music. Attendance was literally just a number given at the beginning of each class. Graded by 6 pass/fail assignments and a final project (10-page paper or 20-25 min recorded presentation) and a final listening exam. It's an athlete class, so it's an easy A.
Great professor, very passionate about what he does. Highly recommend it if you want an easy class that is decently enjoyable.

Great man for a easy class, just show up to class and do the assignments as you are graded just for participation and short assignments. If you can't pass this class this easy, might be time to transfer out. Unbelievably easy trust me.

Professor Harcus is amazing, he is now one of my favorite Professor here at UNC! I would 100% take his class again! He is very understanding and the assignments were spaced out so it was very doable and I also enjoyed his lectures too!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Harcus is AMAZING!!! I loved his class sm and it was very enjoyable! I would def recommend taking his class here at UNC.

Professor Harcus truly cares about music so much, and he is so interested in all of his students' opinions on the music we all enjoy. He's super chill and very kind. I. At the end of the class, we got to create our final project on any album and explain why it's significant. Even if this was time consuming, it was a really fun project to complete.

Aaron went over every genre of black music, and also gave us historical context on how the genres came about and how a new music style was built off the previous popular music style. Assignments consisted of 3 listening assignments and 3 reading summaries. The final was a 10-page essay on any topic of your choice. I learned a lot in this class!

I was really looking forward to this class but it was not good. It was not hard, just a waste of time. Lectures were boring and the entire class just does work for other classes on computers (I do not get how he talks to a room where no one even looks at him). ChatGPT short essays and then a low-key hard final project but nothing crazy.

Prof. Harcus is one of the best professors I've ever had. His class consists of mostly lectures and reading assignments for homework. The lectures are very useful when writing your Reading Responses, but the readings can be long. Although these readings are long, Prof. Harcus does an amazing job of explaining them before making you analyze them.

Prof Harcus is incredibly understanding and kind. He also works really hard to make sure everyone fully understands a new concept- he never made anyone feel bad about needing further explanations. And you could tell that he was doing his best to transition the class to an online format that suited all the students' needs.

Aaron is one of the most genuine professors that I've had at UNC. He a professor that is a: human-being. I say this meaning that despite how much work is required for this class and how time-consuming it is, he is so understanding (medical emergencies, COVID-related matters, work + school , etc). His passion makes his lectures incredibly meaningful

Sometimes tough concepts, but always explains them well. Very useful powerpoints and examples. Understanding of personal circumstances and takes student's thoughts into consideration. For example, he extended a deadline during a busy period. Accessible for office hrs. He always has a smile, and you can tell he loves the subject. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great, charismatic guy. Music 131 was a little difficult sometimes regarding content late in the semester but nonetheless Prof. Harcus always had a positive attitude. He was also very accommodating for a family emergency that I had and I appreciate him so much for that. Always had a smile on his face, too.

Quite a few assignments, and he was a tad disorganized (blame COVID-19 for that), but I really enjoyed his class. The assignments and tests aren't too hard as long as you really pay attention to the notes and actually do the work. He was really chill and caring, and he really made an effort to help you understand. I also got really great feedback.
Very compassionate and caring, made the class fun in extenuating circumstances

Professor Harcus was one of the most caring professors I have had at UNC. He was always flexible with due dates and would give extensions if students needed them. We only had about 6 assignments, one ten page paper and an exam and final but everything was super easy because grading was clear and his study guides were thorough with answers attached
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: NICE class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Ron is a gem! He genuinely cares for his students and is passionate about information science. He has a lot of experience, both in teaching and in the field, that makes his content interesting! His grading and work are extremely lenient and he just wants you to learn and engage with the material! I also took 161 with him and he is the best!

Definitely one of the most understanding professors and is always just so kind and willing to help students. He has a lot of experience that he draws on and tells stories to supplement his teaching. Sometimes assignments would feel daunting, but he'd always give positive and constructive feedback and grade lightly.
The lectures really weren't that important, as they had next to nothing to do with the homework and project assignments. Really easy class to take for even non-Info Science majors.
My third class under this goat, and never disappoints and always a new learning experience. Take him!
Class was so easy, you do pretty much everything in recitation so can skip the lectures at 8. You will learn as much as you put into this class but it's an easy a

Love Professor Bergquist. He genuinely cares about his students' learning and he makes all assignment expectations crystal clear. I took both 161 and 385 with him, both of which were a cakewalk. Just to note 385 has group work and lectures focus a lot on military/historical concepts. He also gives great feedback

Bergquist is such an accomplished individual, and it definitely shows through in his class. Very useful content, but with a focus on military contexts rather than corporate America. If you don't mind that, I'd definitely recommend. Couple papers, optional attendance, group presentations that are recorded, and super light grading overall.
Take every information science class you can with him! He is great, very understanding, and is passionate about what he is teaching. 10/10!
One of the best professor ever! Very patient and have appropriate teaching pace, and you are always welcomed to pull up to office hours to ask any question related to this class or area

Prof. Bergquist is hands-down one of the best teachers at the school. He's been here forever and everyone loves him. The class itself is super easy and the website walks you through everything. Easy A, great teacher.
Very easy class with a professor who emphasizes learning without the stress of test-taking. Learn by a learn-by-doing approach for the assignments.

Professor Bergquist is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. He really cares for his students and wants to see them succeed. He is a professor who truly cares that you learn rather than causing students stress to do good on an exam. Has a lot of fun life stories and I think you can learn a lot from him. He's great!
Amazing professor. Truly cares for his students!

Initially was confused about this class but was able to learn very much thanks to Professor Bergquist. Great teacher overall however some of the grading and assignments could have been better implemented. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bergquist was awesome for an introduction into the information science major. The lectures were pretty interesting and the only grades in the class are discussion boards and four projects. The projects involve working with HTML, Word, Excel, and Powerpoint. It was pretty easy but the information was very useful. Great professor.

Sweet is a word that truly describes him. He is kind, approachable. Based past positive reviews, it's clear his class is easy. However, I strongly urge anyone reading this not to just attend class and then get distracted by your computers. Please take the time to listen to his lectures and his content is genuinely enlightening and inspiring.

Dr. Bergquist is one of the best professors at UNC. He is super kind towards the students and wants to see you succeed. His has very obtainable office hours and lets you easily schedule zooms with him. All of the answers are easily findable in his lecture slides. If he has open seats in his class, take the class even if it's just for an elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ron is wonderful. He is very knowledgeable about the topics he talks about. He is really sweet and will make the class as easy as possible, literally all the assignments are so easy.

Prof Bergquist is just the sweetest man! It is very easy to fall behind in this class and skip (given the lecture and most recitations are either 8 or 9AM), but it is just as easy to catch up, and he is extremely flexible with deadlines and regrading things if you communicate with him. This was a very valuable class, would reccomend!

Dr. Bergquist is truly an amazingly understandable professor. His class was an interesting way to expand on some of the skills we thought we previously knew. He's really flexible with deadlines and overall a really kind person. He follows the rubric strictly and if you can't get something to work, meet with him in office hours and you'll be fine.

Dr. Bergquist is a great professor. Lots of practice by doing rather than big, long lectures. Covers practical skills in common MS Office programs (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), as well as touching on UNIX and web dev. Always willing to help and go over topics again, but you have to be loud and proud so he can hear :)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Would definitely take again. Explains things well, and his grading standard are clear and comprehensive. Also very understanding.
Great professor, if you have a chance to take him, DO! Easy grader, likes it when students participate. No exams, all project-based -  and the projects are usually done in the recitation.

Prof. Ron is really nice; I would definitely take him again. This class has only 4 projects, and they are pretty straightforward. He uses a distinct teaching style from most UNC professors and is pretty lenient with assignments as long as you submit them before the semester ends.

Probably the nicest human being I've ever met. He's such a great person and so accommodating. His lecture was at 8 AM so by the third week nobody showed up and he still taught with the same care and precision he always does. Also, you can do this class in literally three days. I waited until the last day of class to do all the projects and got an A

The professor and class were great. Dr. Bergquist is so nice and caring and explains concepts well. You do the homework in recitations together. Everything I learned from this class is so helpful and applicable to the real world.

Ron is the best. He really cares about his students and wants us to learn. INLS 385 is no exception he says no one should be upset over their grade. He just wants us to read articles, write a little, present, and overall listen to his lectures. They can be a little boring but overall the class is super easy.

He is a caring professor and you can tell he wants his students to succeed and actually learn something in the class. I recommend taking him as a professor, he's great and I learned useful things from him.

Prof Bergquist is great - he explains concepts very well and his assignments are related to his lectures. He goes over every assignment in recitations, so I recommend having him as your recitation leader and that you attend every recitation. You will learn a lot in this class - I have nothing bad to say about the class or the professor.
Great professor! He was very chill, I would take this course again.

Prof Bergquist is one of the most chill profs I've had here. One of the few classes where I feel like I can relax. He is super understanding and tries to make his class as manageable and low stress as possible. Most of your assignments will involve working in the same group all semester. Final is a presentation about a book but it's pretty simple.

He is amazing. Super caring and wants students to do well and learn. Just go to recitations and you will be good. Lets you turn in assignments late and redo them. Such a nice guy all professors should be like him.

Professor Bergquist is a very kind and understanding professor. His class invokes thought-provoking conversations and creates an amicable atmosphere. It is easy to succeed in this class if you keep up with the forums and group assignments.

Professor Bergquist is the nicest guy ever. He is really knowledgeable about the material, and you learn very useful skills that apply to any field these days. He really just cares that students learn the material, so due dates are very flexible and gives great, specific feedback on assignments. Wish all professors were like him!

This class is both very easy and teaches a lot of useful things about information tools. Lectures/recitations are recorded, and recitations basically go over how to do the assignments step by step. Professor Bergquist is very nice and gives great feedback on assignments. 10/10 class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you are an environmental science major, I would def recommend taking this for the major. An easy class if you show up to lecture/recitation, basically assignment is given step-by-step instructions, very easy to get 100s. No penalty for turning in assignments late. This class made me consider applying for the INLS minor! Lots of useful info.

I showed up to lecture one time and still made an A because I did all of the assignments. I really only talked to Dr. Bergquist during the final, but he gave me great feedback on my presentation and I really feel like I learned something!

Ronald was great, it was a tough class for me not having any tech experience but Ronald lets you resubmit for points back and no late dates. Grading scale is a bit odd, an A is 95+ and everything less is an A- and so on, but resubmissions make this somewhat manageable. Nice and approachable and great responder to email. Attendance not required
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Lectures that were sometimes really boring, not really relevant to the assignments. Recitation was most valuable because it went over assignments. Doable course but will need to pay attention to understand if you have no prior experience.

Okay tbh it's really easy to get behind in this class because the professor is a bit lenient with us turning in late work and attendance is kinda optional (doesn't get taken). you also get to resubmit stuff and he gives specific feedback so you know exactly what to improve. He also grades stuff pretty quick which i respect.

The class lectures were given at 8AM and were boring most of the time. Definitely recommend attending on Zoom since most of the content was common sense. Pay attention to recitation because it is helpful for your assignments. Overall the course was super easy and doable.

Dr. Bergquist is one of the best professors I have ever had at UNC. He goes beyond what is required of him by posting all the PowerPoint slides and lectures on Sakai. Sometimes he does forget things. (Who does not forget things? We all are humans.) However, he is willing to help students outside of class and responds to emails right away.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Bergquist is a decent professor and an overall nice guy. The class itself is very easy and set up in a way to make you succeed. The lectures, while he says you should go them, are not necessary to get and A in the class because all of the projects are taught during recitation. The projects while maybe a little tedious and boring, are very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Recitations are not posted on Sakai. If you fall behind in recitation then you are limited to the course website for tasks that make up a huge part of your grade. It does not provide near as detailed instructions for projects and tends to be very vague. He goes fast in recitation, so if you can't keep up with him you're toast. Time consuming class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All the assignments have a clear rubric, and he allows you to resubmit work to make up for any lost points. You can get an A without showing up to class, but his lectures are pretty interesting.

This class is super easy, it was great to balance out my other harder classes. The lectures aren't mandatory, and honestly not needed for this class. All we had to do was follow instructions for a couple small projects with Excel, Word, HTML, & PowerPoint. It's totally possible to get a literal 100, take it if you want an easy A!

I took this class online and it's been my ideal version of a virtual class. Essentially asynchronous, with no papers or tests. Just a bunch of small projects that have loose due dates, tutorials and very clear grading criteria. Take this class with either Professor Bergquist or Jones, both are great!
He is probably my favorite Prof at unc so far. Super caring and gives lots of one on one opportunities if you are confused. Pretty easy to get a good grade and he accepts late work.

Super easy class. His website literally tells you exactly what to do to get a 100 on the assignments. He's a goofy guy, but no one ever goes to lectures cuz you don't need to. No hard deadlines in the class is a huge plus. One of the easiest As at Carolina for sure. Could not recommend him and this class more

Professor Bergquist is one of the kindest and most caring professors I have had at UNC. He wants to see his students succeed and is always available to give help. He is very knowledgeable and is very passionate about his class. He always gives room for improvement and helps you fix your mistakes. He is amazing!

One of the easiest classes I've ever taken. The assignments are graded by the TAs but my TA (Mr. Jones) was very accomdating and understanding with grades. I never went to lecture and only went to recitations and they were extremely helpful because it's basically a step by step tutorial to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Bergquist is kind and not necessarily a bad professor, but his assignments are grueling and excessive. They are not hard, but they are mundane and redundant to the point that no learning occurs. Making endless changes to format a word document or excel spreadsheet teaches nothing. Not hard to succeed at cost of doing tedious work

Dr. Bergquist is a great professor with a very interesting backstory. The course was well-structured and straightforward. The assignments aren't difficult, and he gives you a lot of guidance and feedback. Plus, the stuff you learn is pretty useful. While attendance wasn't a huge factor, he made the lectures enjoyable. Highly recommend!

This class is kind of a joke. I never showed up to the lectures because they never contained anything useful. Everything he teaches us is mostly stuff that we already know and the other stuff is covered in recitation. As long as you go to recitation and keep up with the easy assignments, the class is an extremely easy A.

Dr. Bergquist is a great professor, he's inspirational and extremely helpful. He as an interesting background of being a Colonel in the US Military but don't be afraid because he is a kind man. No textbooks so that's a plus. The courses can be a difficult but the instructions are typically clear and he is there to assist if you need it. Neat guy.

Dr. Bergquist is an incredibly caring and knowledgeable professor. Success in his class means maintaining a certain level of engagement and a willingness to speak up. The work load is incredibly reasonable.
i love bergquist so much. highly recommend a class with him. he's got good stories he incorporates into class. assignments rather than tests. talk and he'll love you!!

Not the most fun class to take at 8 am but there were no tests and he let you redo your work for a higher work. I really liked building my own website and he shows you how to do everything for the assignments the class before. There are also in-class work days so not too much work outside of class. Don't forget to post on the class blog

Bergquist is one of my favorite professors at Carolina! Had him for both 161 and 385 and had a fantastic experience in both! He really cares for his students and is understanding if you have any sort of issue. No tests in either class(grades based on assignments) Need to show up to class and participate to be successful. I definitely recommend him!

Bergquist is a nice guy and knows what he's teaching. The lectures can be boring especially at 8 AM. However, I learned a lot of practical and cool things in the class. Super easy assignments, no midterms, and the final is a presentation. The only thing is that he takes forever to give back grades. I highly recommend this class and professor!
Bergquist is a nice guy who does his best to make the material interesting. The class was boring, and the tasks were time consuming, but no midterms or final makes up for that I think.
Easy class with non-mandatory attendance. 25% of the grade is based on how much you add to your classmates' understanding of the class.

Bergquist is the man. I've never seen anybody own a class like he owns 161, but it makes sense since he's taught it 46 times. Lectures teach you how to use tools, and the only assignments are projects in which you have to use the tools. Overall a very caring professor, who is easily accessible and makes it clear what you need to do to succeed.

So this man is super nice, but he goes pretty fast during lecture. The class is organized & easy, but you're better off using his website to teach yourself than going to lecture. I had an 8 AM with him, and the morning after we won the national championship, he came in, said nothing about it and taught the 8 students that showed from 8-9:15 AM.

Professor Bergquist is one of those professors that will remind you of your grandpa. He knows a ton about the subject and has little anecdotes for every lecture that can sometimes be very interesting. The lectures did seem to be extremely long however as a lot of the material can be extremely dry. If you can stay awake, you'll do fine.
Great teacher, who cares about the students.
TA for calc spoke very quickly and seemed disorganized at times, making it hard to follow.
Lots of accesability from office hours

If you could summarize I prepared my lecture 5 mins before class into a person. Dude was all over the place and would frequently say he made the lecture slides at 3am the night before so to give him a break. Overall a not so good professor who talked in circles
Was a really nice professor in terms of offering extra flexibility, but he was not very clear with teaching. Made it more confusing

During class is lectures are pretty confusing. He moves fast and some of his examples just over-complicate concepts. In his office hours he was more helpful and pretty funny. We almost never had time to review in class before tests when many other 110 classes did, but he tried to host extra reviews outside of class. Tests were not curved.
Not very good at teaching and always procrastinates
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: VERY NICE TEACHER, the class is awful. It is very very test heavy, if you fail the test then you fail the class. I would take his class again but MATH110 is a nightmare. The absolute sweetest teacher but I did hate the class, he never makes you feel dumb.

He is a good person & cares about his students. But he can be very hard to follow, unorganized & very fast (not all his fault). He makes lots of mistakes in his lectures. The final exam is much harder than his other midterms because he doesn't write the final himself. Brought my grade from an A- to a C. Go ahead and get a tutor if you want to pass.

He just wasn't a very good professor. Nothing against  but he would spend 10 minutes teaching a problem then the ta woudk tell him he messed something up so he would go back and change signs, you would think this would be a one off nope, this was every class. Also he speaks very fast and skips around

Overall hes really nice. The class is not that entertaining but he does his best. If you know how to study, you will do good. 3 midterms and 1 final that is cumulative. This course could be easier and less confusing.

He is a nice guy but he always messes up in his own lectures and is confusing. His voice and lectures are boring. He is annoying abt curves and won't curve even though the other math department  for 110 do. Overall I wouldn't take this class w him because it's already difficult and he doenst make it easier. He's nice but not a great teacher.

As a person, he's nice and generally helpful. As a teacher, he's boring, talks too fast, and overcomplicates things.
