He gives partial credit for correct work on exams, and offers corrections when needed, but homework is infuriating and he gets scattered/confused during his own lectures. Some of it isn't his fault, but this class is a huge headache.

He walks around the room and laughs when students say something wrong. He keeps saying "I'm your professor, and you are my student." like he is getting off on the power dynamic. He gives very overly jargonized readings, look up "Sesquipedalian" " He spent 40 minutes having people guess what "belief" meant, only to say it "refers to truth."
I took Phil 210 with Aaron online and he's great! He genuinely cares about the students and class topics. Be ready to have a reading due every class but it is not that bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Thieme was an all-around great professor. I took PHIL134 with him and learned a great deal. He's incredibly knowledgeable and doesn't leave students with incomplete answers. He's available consistently in office hours. As well, I thought he was a fair grader. Super welcoming personality and does well engaging with students.

This class is quite difficult, but the professor is just so charismatic that it's impossible to dislike him. He is accessible outside of class, is never condescending, and wants the students to succeed. Perhaps the material could've been taught more effectively; this is certainly one of the more difficult classes I've taken.

I'm a bit late, but I also had Aaron for 301 and 455. He was an amazing educator inside and out: exceptionally clear, organized, and always available to explain concepts, problems, or provide a listening ear as a mentor. He listened to student feedback, made his classes both safe and engaging, and his passion was contagious. I wish him the best!

Was lucky enough to have Aaron as my professor for both COMP 301 and COMP 455, which really redeemed my experience with UNC CS. I have had some... less than amazing professors in this department but AARON is a shining star. What all professors should strive to be. He makes material accessible, assignments straightforward, and lectures a treat.
A legend, rip 2022

Besides Kris Jordan, Aaron Smith is the best Comp professor I've had so far. He gives great lectures and gives time for questions. The hardest part of the class was the frequency of the homework assignments and hand writing code on tests. However, office hours were very helpful and he is always available to help you pass.

Overall, a great professor! I would say it was one of my best experiences in a class. He is very easy to reach out to and ask questions in class or after class, and is very good at covering concepts from many approaches to ensure everyone understands. Very caring and very passionate professor, in other words, he actually likes his job and it shows.

Aaron is a legend! The class itself is not too bad, albeit the programming assignments can be quite consuming. This class does cover a lot of fundamentals in OOP so it is super helpful if you want to do internship/job in software development.
Great lectures and useful class. Assignments and tests are pretty easy, although it is annoying to write code on paper. Minimal work honestly.
Made content easy to understand and interesting. Super easy assignments, worksheets are a bit of work. Tests are pretty fair, just need to be familiar with main concepts.

This man is a diamond in the rough in the comp sci department. After taking 210, I really questioned choosing comp sci, but his lectures were very engaging, well structured and overall enjoyable. If you are taking comp classes and see his name pop up TAKE THE CLASS. The exams are fair and projects are fun. I learned so much from this class. Thank u

Aaron & 301 are amazing! His lectures are so organized and the slides were so aesthetically pleasing, which really helped me learn, & he ALWAYS encouraged questions & truly valued our thoughts. The 3 tests were fair and the 9 assignments were enjoyable. I learned so much and genuinely wish I could keep taking this class!

I love Aaron! He is so kind, respects his students, and makes the coding assignments themed. You will learn a lot, and he teaches it very clearly. Tests can be a little tricky, but most of the grade is based on the assignments. You get to create a game at the end of the semester, which is difficult but very rewarding. Thanks Aaron!

Probably the best prof at UNC CS. 301 is not an easy class, to be honest, but Aaron makes it much easier. He really encourages everyone to ask questions during lectures and answer all of them patiently. HWs are intense though, one programming HW each week, but as long as you listen carefully and start early, it will be fine. Will take him again!

Aaron Smith is probably the best professor I've had in college. He goes out of his way to answer questions and ensure you understand all the material. His lectures and slide decks are outstanding (and recorded to Panopto), which makes studying for exams very straightforward. 3 Java programming assignments, 5 worksheets, 2 midterms, and a final.
Nicest CS professor at UNC! I hope he can teach more classes before my graduation

I adore Aaron! So kind, very interactive lectures, really wants you to ask questions and learn, explains things so clearly - an overall 10/10. IMO he's right under Kris Jordan as best CS professors here. 301 is a great class because of him. He has so many fun catch phrases you could make a bingo.
Definitely his class!
Best professor ever. Definitely take his class. Easy A.

Definitely the BEST prof in the CS department. Aaron held excellent lectures explaining everything clearly, HW design is great as well. He encourages everyone to participate and answer every question with respect. The course is not easy but Aaron makes it wonderful, I got a good grade and learn a lot from it. Will take his course again for sure!

Professor Smith is a terrific lecturer, he makes difficult concepts very easy to understand and left me feeling well-prepared for exams. The programming assignments require you to think but are not too difficult. Would definitely recommend taking Comp 301 with Aaron!

Aaron is great. For 301 he emphasized a lot more "vocabulary" type stuff as opposed to practical, "show that you can make this work" on exams. IDK if that's the course or his perogative, but it wasn't my cup of tea. Other than that small quibble with regards to the curriculum, he was awesome, and I would definitely take one of his classes again.

COMP 455 is a really easy class. Most of the questions on the exams are similar to those covered in the slides and the homework. The 3 programming projects are not too bad either and can be completed in less than an hour. This class does not heavily depend on COMP 283/MATH 381 so that's also a plus.

SUCH an amazing professor and even more awesome person. UNC comp sci does not deserve Aaron Smith. He makes everyone feel welcome, encourages questions, and is super understanding. Lectures are fun and super easy to follow, assignments are fun... I cannot emphasize how great of a professor and person Aaron is. Would 100/10 take this again.

Professor Smith's lectures are organized and clear. There are 9 programming assignments in total, and they are worth 50% of your grade. If you go to office hours often and start them early, they should not be very hard. I got a 70 on the first exam but still almost end up with an A.

Aaron is probably the best professor I have had in the comp sci department here, if not all of UNC. From an academic standpoint, his lectures are crystal clear and super well designed. Aside from that, he is also a great person in general. You can really tell he cares about his students and wants them to succeed.

Aaron is a very nice person and a good lecturer who makes the content easy to comprehend. However, like someone else said, he is a bit insensitive with giving assignments over breaks. The assignments themselves can be hard but, are for the most part, manageable with office hours.

This class isn't difficult, but he is pretty insensitive with giving assignments over breaks. He gave us an assignment over fall break and the final project over Thanksgiving Break with limited office hours and a lack of help on Piazza. Also, we had a few "quizzes" over the semester that were more like exams, so beware.

Unnecessarily particular and impractical sometimes. Grades on dumb conventions sometimes. Otherwise the labs are cool and he teaches well. The "quizzes" are not an informal thing, they're very hard 10% assignments.

Zoom uni was Pain but I actually enjoyed this class. Aaron's teaching is so clear and efficient, and he's very empathetical towards students, always pausing his lecture to answer questions. That polleverywhere and watching a certain dance video was the highlight of my zoom life for sure. I'm gonna miss this class. Take him!!!

Seriously, GET AARON IF YOU CAN. He's definitely one of the best CS professors I have had; his caring demeanor and attitude toward teaching is definitely something I wish others would emulate in their own lectures. Quizzes in 301 can be tricky and difficult, but the class itself is rewarding. (See you in 455 Aaron!!! :) )

He's so amazing!! The best instructor I've ever had so far. He is understanding, accommodating, hilarious, and his lectures are very clear and the TA's are also amazing! I've learned so much from this course and he makes me feel better about myself.

April 19, 2021. 2:31 PM. Student: "We should make the PollEv answers 25% each." Aaron: "Let's do it." *Class proceeds to be the most epic thing in any lecture from the CS department ever for the next ten minutes. Highs, Lows, near Perfection, Custom Ink T-shirt designs. The whole enchilada.* This is the perfect description of 301. :)

Aaron is hands down the best instructor i've had at UNC. He breaks down complicated concepts into extremely engaging lectures. He would always ask us for feedback and making sure we understood the concepts being discussed, and would change lecture structures to go over a topic in more detail if needed. I would take ANY class he teaches.

Aaron was definitely one of the best professors I've ever had at UNC. Especially within the comp sci department. we need more professors like him at UNC for real. His lectures were very useful and organized, and he always always made sure that we understood concepts before moving on. His quizzes were also very fair
Good professor, easy material.

Aaron is arguably one of the best instructors that I ever had at UNC. He does amazing job explaining difficult material in simple terms. Aaron always responds to the questions during the lecture and you can clearly see how much he cares about the class and wants to make sure that the class is understanding the material. I highly recommend Aaro
Aaron is the sweetest guy and he is a fantastic teacher! He was really good at explaining concepts and the assignments were not very hard. Everyone in the class loved him.

Best professor I've ever had. Teaches super in depth, super flexible on assignments, super friendly and kind, very helpful, engaging classes. I wish I could take classes with him for the rest of college.
Professor Aaron is not very understanding or kind. She made this class much more difficult than it needed to be. She was very strict with speaking in class, especially if it wasn't Spanish.

I was nervous because of previous reviews, but the class was great! Dr. Aaron is one of the nicest profs I've had. She takes time to answer questions and will slow her speaking/adapt her explanation to ensure everyone understands. It is not the easiest(some of the translations are tough), but she is willing to help. Use her office hours and email
Professor Aaron was good at teaching Spanish in an understandable way, but she could be a little strict with grading sometimes. Still, I would recommend this class.

Profesora Aaron was a great instructor. She made learning Spanish fun and easy. Her grading is a little strict but the class is passable. Participation is a grade, she does a lot of partner work, and 90% of time only allows you to speak Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Aaron is a very sweet person! She explains things well, and her accent is easy to understand. She could be a little more tough in grading compared to other spanish professors, but if you prepare early, you should be in better shape!

Profesora Aaron was such a kind soul and her classes were always structured the same, which was nice. She is a tough grader, so if you are not confident in speaking up in class often maybe don't take her. Overall she is a sweet southern teacher who would slow her speech to make sure every student understood and offered multiple office hours.

Going into the final in a few weeks with her.  This semester has been VERY frustrating.  She speaks clear Spanish but expects ridiculous expectations from her students.  She can be fairly condescending in her tone.  Most frustrating is her tough grading.  No student gets over a 95 on participation, per her statements.  She always picks off points.

Not very helpful. Makes students feel bad about not knowing Spanish like they have done something wrong. She calls on students at will and still gives out low participation grades when you still answer multiple questions a class. Don’t t take this class as she is a tough grader and the class will not actually help you learn Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Aaron is a very sweet southern woman but is definitely a difficult grader. Specifically the 10 minute oral interview was graded MUCH harder than other 203 professors. If you are confident in speaking Spanish she is a good choice but I took AP Spanish and 100% never was graded this harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved taking Spanish with Prof. Aaron. She is super sweet and I feel like her Spanish is fairly easy to understand. It is important to pay attention in her class because she goes through the material very quickly and will call on you for participation points. Also, study as you work through the chapters, instead of right before exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is nice, but she teaches SO fast. She gives no time to do the in class practices and has high expectation for her students. She is overall very nice and helpful. Also, her pronunciation is super easy to understand which is helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Aaron is sweet and I really enjoyed having her! I'm not great at Spanish and she always speaked clearly and would slow down or restate when the class clearly didn't understand. She was really kind to us and made a point to learn about our personal lives. She's definitely a by-the-book grader but it pushes you to work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: By far the worst professor Ive had at UNC. It seemed like she took her own stress out on her students. The content discussed in class was random and structured poorly. I felt like I didnt truly learn anything useful or applicable throughout the entire semester.

Hands down the worst professor I've had at UNC. Prof Aaron is insanely unorganized and legit cannot teach (and her Spanish isn't that great either). I learned absolutely nothing and spent the whole semester stressing because expectations and deadlines were never clear. Grading wasn't tough but she took FOREVER to grade anything. DON'T take her

The class is fairly standardized. Professor Aaron did an okay job at following the rubrics with grading, but I really felt she graded with the expectation that we are native speaker (hello! non native learner here!) That being said she graded tougher than I thought was necessary. As a person, she is very kind and willing to have fun sometimes.

Here's the deal folks. Professor Aaron is the WORST, and I mean the WORST professor I have ever had at Carolina. We are in the middle of a pandemic, and this woman does not read the class and see that nobody does the HW, she is unclear and does not teach anything. She is not accommodating and refuses to help in office hours whatsoever.

She is unhelpful and unreasonable. I was struggling in her class at the beginning of the tri and I emailed her asking for help and she said it was too late to help me at all despite having almost half the tri left. She gave me an 85 in participation even though I always raised my hand and made an effort in class. Also mixed up my name CONSTANTLY
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: She is a very kind person. She is a good professor, but not a great one.

I was excited to take this course despite the not so good reviews of Aaron. This course stressed stressed me out. It thought it would be fun to do my own translation & learn general translation info. I learned nothing & had a terrible experience with the project because she didn't follow the rubric & it wasn't right if it wasn't how she would do it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She is a nice person, but she grades so so so so so much harder than all the other 203 professors. She shows no mercy for anything. I spoke during class every single day multiple times and she gave me an 85 for participation, which was very unfair. Also, I went to office hours regularly for help and she was not very helpful. I do NOT recommend her.
Extremely condescending. Not a very kind person and makes me feel like the fact that I don't know Spanish is a flaw. The fact that I have a question does not mean that I did not do my homework.

Professor Aaron is super sweet and southern! She has a fun easy going personality, but when it comes down to the actual work, she cuts no slack. she is strict to the rules and will only give you what you deserve, nothing more or less. She's  a little on the tough side, but a challenge worth taking if you want to improve your spanish.

If you are going to take SPAN 265, I highly recommend someone other than her.  She is a nice lady but doesn't teach.  Relies on class conversation for you to learn.  Then, the tests are extremely hard.  If you could get anyone else, I would highly suggest you to do so.

AWESOME TEACHER! she's so nice and genuine and really teaches with enthusiasm and passion.  She gave us gifts sometime, BUT she cuts no slack with grading. I always seemed to get 1 point away from an A -___- Other than her strictness to the rules, she's great!

Aaron was a strict teacher, but honestly that made me love Spanish and learn it a lot faster than I would with one not so strict. Sometimes she could come off as rude, but she really was one of the best professors I've had.
Great professor! She is very funny.

I don't know how she has bad reviews. she was one of my favorites. she is very nice and enthusiastic about teaching. she is very helpful and tries to clarify when people are confused. i've always been good at spanish, but I still worked hard for my grade. i think i will get a B or A in the class. overall she is a great teacher. i recommend her.

Despite all the bad reviews, I thought Dr. Aaron was very kind, enthusiastic, and helpful, if a little bit odd. Her style of teaching and obsession with the Honor Code are hard to get used to, but once you show some interest and talk to her outside of class, she is very helpful and really cares about her students.
All I have to say is that I have no idea how there are so many favorable reviews of this woman because I had a terrible experience. Her assignments and tests are nit-picky and ridiculous.

Definitely the worst professor I have had at UNC. A picky grader that does not teach you a concept, then grades you on something she has not told you how to do. For example, in my midterm she wanted me to use an example, but but that was nowhere in the instructions. She took off points for it.

The fact that this woman is a professor for upper level Spanish is an embarrassment to UNC. She does not speak Spanish fluently, her tests/quizzes/assignments are unrealistically difficult, and she doesn't tell you what the assignments are until 2 days before they're due. She is also condescending and is terrible at answering questions.

I have a 4.0 in my spanish major and got an A in professor Aaron's class despite the lack of clarity on material we would be tested on.  She is completely condescending and constantly paranoid about being taken advantage of and students cheating.  Punished the whole class for one student's complaint that test-prep info was incorrect.

Prof. Aaron is by far one of the very best professors at UNC. She is approachable and helpful, but expects your absolute best. She does not tolerate attitudes from students. She grades fairly and will go out of her way to investigate answers to questions she doesn't know off-hand. Amazing professor!
Amazing! She is very useful and makes you feel comfortable. Best language course I've taken at UNC
not approachable, condescending, horrible.

Professor Aaron teaches as if her students were in the kindergarten. She's condescending & power-hungry. She accuses students of cheating and is unforgiving of tardiness. She assigns an unreasonable amount of work and makes impossible tests. One of the worst teachers at UNC.(SPAN 369)

I took SPAN 101 at another university over the summer, and I had to make a HUGE leap into her class. I still feel like I am behind. She definitely favors the students that speak better spanish and loves students to suck up to her. When I ask for help, I feel like she is condescending and makes me feel dumb for not knowing something. NOT RECOMMEND

Aaron is an extremely enthusiastic teacher who clearly enjoys teaching. However, she can be condescending and sometimes expects more from her students than she does from herself. She's inflexible about student's homework but then takes her time getting back any grades. If you want to learn Spanish, take her. But don't expect much otherwise...
If you have a choice do not take it from her. Felt like I was a kindergardener and she does very little to answer your questions. Unapproachable.
She was awesome, really knows the material, very helpful and kept me laughing the entire time.  I would recommend her to every spanish student!
Extremely friendly, knowledgeable, approachable, and helpful.  Definitely one of my best profs so far.

Dr. Aaron was by far the best spanish professor that I have had at UNC thus far and I have taken upwards of 7 courses over the past 3 years.  I would definitely take a course being taught by Grace again!
great professor!
It's a hard class but she cares about how you do and will do anything to help.  She makes the class interesting and involves everyone, but you'll have to work hard to get the grade.
bad teacher. Don't take the class
GREAT teacher! very clear and very involved, shows obvious concern for every student and makes herself available for any student.
Nice lady, made class interesting, first Spanish class at Carolina during which I did not spend the entire time staring at the clock. Worked incredibly hard for my A, though!
Really great professor and very accesible outside of class!  But don't be expecting an easy A, even if you speak spanish well.  This is definitely a class on literature analysis!
College Thriving is an extremely annoying class to have to take. However, I thought Mr. Harris did a good job with what he was provided with.

College thriving sucks. He made it suck slightly less, pretty nice guy! He's super easy and laid back, we spent most classes discussing the required slideshow content and he'd let us leave early sometimes. Just show up to class and complete the occasional assignments (they take 10mins max) and you'll get an A.
Listen. College Thriving is a really annoying class. However, he really did his best with the material provided to him.

I genuinely enjoyed coming to class. The way he taught was so engaging and I liked how he didn't take anything about the course too seriously. He also was very helpful with registration and major questions. He genuinely cares about students. He did cancel class last minute 2 or 3 times but otherwise no complaints.

I feel that some of the negative reviews of Prof. Addo are exaggerated. She is one of the most caring and supportive professors I've had at UNC. She truly wants her students to succeed, is approachable outside of class, and takes the time to explain material when you're confused. If you put in the effort, she will absolutely meet you halfway.

Very nice person and is willing to help you outside of class, but isn't always good at answering questions. We had three midterm exams and one final exam with 5 policy assignments throughout the semester, which felt like a lot, but if you study the lecture content well you're fine. She reads straight off the slides which isn't helpful.

Professor Addo cares a lot and is knowledgable but her lectures were verbatim off the slides. She was not great at answering student questions in lecture either. 4 exams throughout the semester which was a lot but if you study the guide she gives then you should do well on them. Easy class and interesting content but unhelpful lectures.

When she lectures she often does not answer student questions well, or at all. The course was very disorganzied but easy. The TA's are lenient with the grading of the decontructed policy brief. Overall if you go to class and are willing to do some of the readings you are fine.

Dr. Addo seems like a very nice person, but she has very poor lecturing skills. No one in the class listened because she was reading the slides verbatim. This class was also so disorganized. I wouldn't take her if there is another professor avaliable. Her class was still easy, it was the last of my concerns and I did well.

Dr. Addo is a wonderful person and you can tell she has a lot of passion for her field. However, lectures were rather dry and I do not feel I gained a whole lot from the class. Still, assignments weren't too hard, nor were exams. Attendance is technically required but often not enforced.

lectures were boring and pointless since she mostly reads off the slides, the content is also boring, tests are more about memorization with a little application, I didn't pay attention but got >95 on every test and assignment

This class was extremely repetitive with the same content in every single module. Prof. Addo does NOT know how to lecture in any way shape or form. She needs to take a workshop on lecturing. The class itself was boring, tests were fine, just study the review that she posts. Application based. Our assignments were easy 100's. I skipped class a lot.

She is clearly smart but such a bad lecturer. She gets confused by her own slides, mostly just reads off them anyway, and struggles to answer student questions. She also weirdly giggles so much and it makes me so angry. Exams weren't too hard though and out of class assignments were easy 100s

I found her class frustrating. She is condescending and fails to answer questions beyond the content of her lecture slides. The content is manageable, but lectures are poorly organized. My biggest issue with her class was the volume of tests. A policy innovation and analysis course should focus on research and writing, not multiple choice exams.

These reviews over-exaggerate what Dr. Addo's class is like. While she is not an engaging lecturer (she mostly reads off her slides), she is clearly knowledgeable in her field. If you do the few readings assigned and put in a decent amount of effort on the problem sets, you'll be just fine. This class was my last priority and I ended with an A.

I don't think I learned a lot from this class and I found Professor Addo confusing in general (how she explained things), but I didn't feel that this affected my ability to succeed in the course. She was very helpful outside of class and seemed to care a lot about students. Grading didn't feel nitpicky and the workload was relatively light.

Professor Addo is a really nice person, but I think that they need to work on their lecture skills. It is really hard to pay attention. Majority of the time I had no idea what was going on. Available outside of class and just so nice, but the class needs to be restructured and they need to go to a lecture/public speaking workshop.

There were multiple occasions where the teacher or TA could not answer a question posed by a student in the class. Not gonna lie, I didn't even know if the teacher knew what was being taught. The tests aren't terribly hard but they grade hard for no reason. If you could pick another professor for 210 probably would do that. Gonna end with a B.

Probably one of the worst classes I have taken at UNC. The professor and TA's grade super hard for no reason and give no feedback. They don't even seem to understand the material themselves and just take off points randomly. They give you 8th grade level exams and then grade them super harshly for no reason. I might get a B in this class.
She's a robot reading slides and exams are poorly designed and graded. Don't take her if you can avoid it.

She does nothing to engage students while lecturing. While she seems to know a lot about the subject, she does not teach it well at all and you many leave lectures more confused than when you entered. She talks in circles and does not give straight answers. Impossible to reach outside of class and you're better off asking a TA.

Grading is fairly unclear with only very brief notes given, and the rubrics provided are inconsistent.Although she's very kind her lectures are unfocused and she tends to repeat herself or talk around clearly explaining something. It is also fairly difficult to review and follow the slides as they are mostly just terms without explanation.

Do not take her class unless you absolutely need to. She is a very unclear grader and when she explains your grade, she does nothing to explain it well. She is the worst professor I've had at UNC so far. I only gave her 1/5 because I couldn't give 0...

Dr. Addo is a really sweet lady who I believe genuinely does care about her students. However, she is quite simply not a good teacher. Her lectures are quite unclear and unfocused. She communicates quite poorly in general and it's very difficult to learn much from her class.

Funny, smart, charismatic guy. This was one of my favorite classes at UNC. You read a short story before every class, then discuss it in class. You have a 10-15 page short fiction story (basically about anything you want) due at a certain point in the semester, where it gets workshopped in class. Chill A, cool subject, if you're taking 130 take him

Adam was an amazing professor and his class was very straight forward. You have small readings with short writing assignments before each class and then one final long story that you get to create. Show up to class, participate every now and then, and listen to feedback from your draft and you will get an easy A.

Adam was a super nice teacher and made the class feel very open for constructive criticism. My only complaint with him was his "Do Not" list for writing, but with the way he structured the class it never became an issue. He was flexible as well.

Adam is a super awesome guy, and he is funny and very passionate about his craft. The class itself is easy, but there is a lot of busy work. I really enjoyed the first few weeks, but it started to feel a little bit repetitive. You have to read a short story, write a paragraph, and later write discussion posts. Sounds super light, but gets tedious.

I enjoyed having Adam as the instructor a lot. I thought he was very knowledgeable on the subjective of creative writing and was incredibly passionate. The class itself is easy, particularly weighted on your submission of your own 10 page short story. He's very sarcastic, but I find him to be hilarious. I recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved this class! Adam is funny, chill, and gives great writing advice!! Prompt and short story to read before each class. Final project is a short story. Shy people, FYI you have to share your story with class for a workshop - but everyone is nice and it is fun! It is an easy A if you show up and complete the assignments.

I've had Adam for three different creative writing classes in my UNC career, and he's been fantastic for all of them. He has a very different perspective and taste in literature than I do, which is actually super helpful in critique. He's respectful of everyone and genuinely wants students to write the best work they can. Also his twitter is great.

Adam is a very chill professor who wants to make sure you learn but is lenient on grading. Charasmatic and excited to be in the classroom. Just make sure you show up to class and do your assignments and you should be fine.

Adam was awesome -- super sarcastic sense of humor, so if you don't like sarcasm, don't take him. I thought he was hilarious. Makes everyone feel comfortable participating and class discussions are fun. We read "The Big Sleep" a murder mystery, so a fun read. Learned a lot as well! Gave most people a 19.2/20 on all assignments w/o feedback tho...

Adam was absolutely phenomenal this semester, and his class was without a doubt my favorite. He is hilarious and I feel like my writing has improved tremendously with his guidance. I had a few attendance conflicts, but he was very understanding with my situation. I can't say enough good things! Take his class if you can.

I liked this class. He didn't grade on quality of writing, but on participation. The "main" project was 10-20 pgs. you posted for critique. Homework: reading, prompts, critiques. I didn't deserve an A because I didn't do work on time (outside stuff), but I guess he appreciated me getting stuff in no matter how late it was. Super cool guy.

I would highly recommend Prof. Price's intro to creative writing class. The class is not graded on how well you can write, just on how much you participate and try to improve. Weekly readings and writings pushed me to become a better writer and critic. The workshops are super helpful too, and Prof. Price is an all-around great and chill professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was more work than I thought it would be but it is all very easy. Weekly writing workshop for short stories and no tests! I enjoyed that the class gave me motivation to write but I will say that this creative writing class does not let you do genre writing and expects you to focus on literary fiction which I was disappointed by.

I loved Adam's class. He's smart about writing and he's smart about the way he teaches it--everything feels important. He manages workshops so that they're always as constructive as they should be. Plus he's just a funny, interesting guy who clearly wants to see students succeed. Highly recommend!!

Professor Price's class is super easy to get an A in. The daily readings, workshop submissions, and daily assignments are not graded based on accuracy but on participation. Participation matters and keeping up with assignments are important in this course. It is a super fun class and easy to take.

Our textbook was a New Yorker subscription, and it was very cool to read contemporary stories while writing. His twitter is really funny, and he doesn't take himself too seriously which is really admirable. He cares about good writing, and he helps you hone a few great skills to prepare for Advanced fiction. I loved the assignments!

Adam was a cool prof. He's super chill and his class is easy if you put in effort & do the work. The class is composed of 3 papers, participation, and "feeder" assignments which are small outlines for the essays (so you don't procrastinate). The class can be boring at times, but that's also because it's a beginner English class. 10/10 recommend!!

Adam is a really nice guy, and this class is stupid easy to get an A in, but I didn't feel like I learned a single thing. As long as you complete the writing prompts and do your weekly writing pages, you'll get a good grade. The class was pretty small so it was noticeable if you skipped, but you really don't miss much.

Professor Price was my best professor this semester. On the first day, he said that he didn't want this class to be anything to stress over, and that he wanted to prioritize our mental health over everything. He followed through on those promises. I never felt stressed out, but I was also able to learn everything I needed to know. Awesome guy.
great teacher and very caring

Professor Price was a great professor and a really caring guy. He was super nice during the pandemic and could tell when we were stressed and offered us more relaxed classes on those days. To be honest, every class was relaxed though, it was mostly just peer reviews. A tip: Before writing the essay, discuss the idea with him over email/hours

Professor Price is very funny and chill. if you need to fulfill your 105 credit, definitely do it with Price! He's very helpful in improving your writing and helping you come up with ideas. He's always there to help too. Never a dull class, I loved it! Just 3 main assignments throughout the course that are pretty easy to do.

Best professor ever! Throughout this course you will write a decent bit but most of it is not really looked at in class. You have your one workshop where people will read your short story, but other than that you submit pages and review other classmates' work and it is an easy A. The final is just seeing if you made edits to your short story.

Adam Price is a genius. He's an excellent writer and a really effective creative writing teacher. Really down to earth and hilarious. Be ready to read the New Yorker. Super chill class vibe. LOOKS JUST LIKE FRANK GALLAGHER. 100% would recommend taking a course with him.

Adam is a great guy! I really liked how he split our 3 projects up into smaller parts to prevent procrastination and get feedback along the way. He really wants his students to do well and is willing to help however he can!! Take his class!!
He is a great guy who makes English fun.
An easy A and very fun class to attend.

Adam is by far one of the best professors I've had at UNC! Extremely laid back but also SO caring and passionate about the class! There were no exams; the only work was reading short stories (both from the textbook and classmates), reviewing them, and writing our own for review. Everyone had so much fun reading we forgot it was a class. Take him!

Professor Price was the best literature professor I ever had. He gives clear feedback and is consistent with his grading criteria. There's not too much work for a literature class either, which is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Adam is a super great guy. He doesn't take the subject matter too seriously like some English professors and the assignments he gives are generous in the amount of work they require. He gives meaningful homework and shows that he cares about the growth of his students. He was one of the best professors of my 1st year, so I highly recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A lot of the times, class was kind of pointless and we did mostly peer edits. He didn't really give a ton of feedback on assignment, but gives you plenty of time to complete them. If you work hard and participate, you'll surely get a good grade. I learned a lot about writing that my high school teachers never even touched on.

Adam Price was a really good professor for a class I had initially low expectation for. He doesn't give you unnecessary work, facilitates good conversations, and clearly states what is due when. A friend of mine also had him and highly recommended him too.

English 105I was amazing with Professor Lang. 1 individual project, 2 group projects, no midterm nor final. All the projects were writing wikipedia pages on topics you choose. You can only miss two classes, but he's very understanding if you explain absences. Super easy grader, and a B is the lowest you can get if you complete all the work.
He's very chill and super kind. Just make sure to turn in the homework on time and you'll get an A. Also, go to his office hours, he is very knowledgeable on classics (lowkey cool)!

An amazing teacher and my favorite professor this semester. Every assignment we did was marked based on completion. I loved how his areas of expertise (I believe it was Latin or Roman linguistics) seeped into the way he taught class. What you learn and get out of this class is based on what you put into it. There was one group project.

Prof. Lang is a great choice for ENGL 105I (Natural Sciences). The writing assignments were all interesting and relevant. They're caring and will work with you on deadlines if you communicate. You'll have homework each class, but as long as you show effort and turn everything in you'll get an A. Make sure to have some scientific topic in mind.

Prof. Lang was caring, kind, well-organized, and overall a really great teacher. Assignments were fairly easy but engaging and had lots of room for creative touches. Good incorporation of individual and personal work. Engaging lectures. Grade was mostly completion and attendance. Would highly recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved english 105 with this professor. The class was extremely well-organized and setup, and was not hard at all to get an A. This professor grades off of a 'completion' grading scale, so as long as you do all the work for the class, you are guaranteed a B. If I could take another class under this professor I would.

Professor Lang taught Medical Terminology in a concise and interesting way for Summer Session II. I appreciated his lecture style to be interactive and interesting. He is very knowledgeable in the subject of Latin and the coursework was straightforward and fair. He is a positive person and if you keep up with the work you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great teacher. He loves the language and the culture surrounding it. His recall of Roman/Greek history was helpful in class for context surrounding our readings. Was really fair in grading and super attentive to his students. I hope I get to take the second Latin course with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This was the one class I dreaded. Adam made the class much more difficult than expected. The martial arts section on Monday's led to a lot of trouble and I had to take it to higher ups. The Wednesday classes are all discussion after A LOT of reading. He is a tough grader on the few papers for no reason (he'll say it's great then take off points).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took DRAM284 with Versenyi, and didn't know how intensive the martial arts portion would be. It's a lot of work in and outside of class, requiring a significant amount of reading. Generous grader with participation, harsh with papers (take points off for no reason). Getting an A is doable but requires a lot of work
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Took Drama 486* (wasn't an option on here) with him & he was lovely! There's a lot of reading, but it's manageable. The class was interesting and he's an expert in the field, so we read a lot of his translations of the plays. It's a 400 level so there's a 10-15 pg. term paper. Hadn't previously taken a drama class & will prob end up with a A-.
Adam's class was alright overall. A lot of readings, but that didn't make it too hard to get a good grade. Strap in for the final project, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very tough grader. He is a good and supportive professor but his final paper was unreasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So much reading, but it's all plays and very interesting. Class is essentially a big discussion on that week's readings. A fair grader, super nice, and is very helpful and accommodating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Versenyi is a great instructor. His discussions are interesting and sometimes he even sings. He is very understanding and accommodating of students. However, there is a lot of reading and he can be a pretty tough grader on play review papers (I always get A's on writing assignments, but I can't get higher than a B+ with him).

Adam Versenyi is very good at illuminating the meanings of the most obscure dramatic texts, however, he can be a bit boring at times. I have also never gotten bellow or above an A- on anything yet (this is my second course with him). He is very nice, and quite helpful. No extra credit, 2 papers and a final exam which is also a paper.

I appreciated the clear grading criteria and overall clear communication. There are quizzes with corrections for half points back. I did alright on the quizzes, but the corrections were so helpful for material comprehension. Overall, I felt like Dr. Adkins was a very organized and fair professor.

The best professor to take 205 with. This class is so difficult but professor adkins made it easier to understand. She offers quiz corrections which saved my grade. Very caring and has multiple officer hours that you should go to. Cannot stress enough how much I enjoyed having her as a professor coming from someone who didn't do good in physics 1.

Dr. Adkins is a great professor. She's funny and very generous with grades (students can get half points back on midterms with corrections). She also does a great job of keeping the class relatively low-stress while still helping students learn a lot. I would absolutely take another class with her in the future.

Pretty average professor, statics isn't an easy class but is doable with Prof Adkins and a good bit of effort. She allows you to do test corrections for 50% points back on tests which is super helpful gradewise and for understanding the concepts. Downsides are she tends to read off slides and can brush over huge concepts pretty quick.

Class is actually taught as BMME 160 over the summer, but covers the same info as 205. Dr. Adkins was very fair in her assignments and allows test corrections to make up for the fact that the quizzes and exams are pretty hard and have a tough time limit.

Dr. Adkins was a great introduction to the BME program. She's very open to questions during lecture or lab and answers them well. She's also funny and makes the material especially engaging. She also offers test corrections for points back. I feel well-prepared for future BME courses after taking this class.

Dr. Adkins is a phenomenal professor for an intro engineering course. The format of her exams allowed for test corrections which was incredibly helpful when learning the difficult content. I cannot say enough good things about the organization of this course and its format, it was really easy to follow new material and get help from the textbook.

The class is a bit hard but that's the nature of the material. Dr. Adkins was always willing to answers questions at any time and also held office hours for a good duration, which were also useful for quiz corrections. The quizzes themselves were kind of hard, I guess I could have studied more. Final was pretty good, reflected class material.
Great prof.  Very fun class. 10/10 would take again.
David's lecutres were all over the place and made learning the material very difficult. His office was also a mess, so I can see why he never responded to his emails.

Lectures were very disorganized and he procrastinated until a couple days before finals to post notes. Just understanding the concepts is not enough. The online HW is no help but the HW worksheets and in-class worksheets should be studied for exams. The third exam was easy but everything else was a mess. Did not give partial credit on the final.

The class is very test heavy (80%) and test difficulty varies a lot (but questions are pretty consistent with HW and worksheet content). Lessons are quite hard to follow and participation worksheets are part of the grade. May still be a easier class than other MATH347 professors due to less weightage on proofs and a pretty easy grading scale/curve.

David is a really sweet guy, and wants his students to succeed. However, his lectures are incomprehensible, and slides are hard to follow. It's possible to self-teach, since it's mostly computation. ULAs/TAs are helpful, especially for hw--tricky hw problems often were tested. Most proofs were pulled from slides. Check grading--often has errors.

Easily the worst instructor in the school. Attendance mandatory but lectures are incoherent. He never responds to emails, and exams (80% of grade) test random proofs from lecture slides written in hieroglyphics. He talks about Julia (a random software) like it's his wife. Attendance mandatory too. Still got an A, so IDGAF. Philippians 4:13 innit.

Hands down the worst professor at UNC, but i got an A so IDGAF. Didn't learn a thing from him in class, exams were next to impossible to be finished in time, and no amount of studying can save you. At the end of the day some people aint cut out for ts like me and Simeon. But If I can do it then why can't you? Get up and make it Work!

Linear isn't hard material, but this class was nearly impossible. Only grading criteria shared was the floor for an A, so no way to anticipate your grade. Exam scores are consistently lower than he expects, but he blames students and will not curve. Very arbitrary grading on exams and unclear instructions. Unreachable via email.

Chill class. Tests were straight forward and very similar to HWs and were graded fairly. Proofs were from slides/HW. Besides the questionable lectures, I think this class was decent. People complaining about it just don't put in the time to study and think their 60 on the midterm/final is the professor's fault.

70% of your grade is tests. Lectures are convoluted and confusing; you'd be better off self-studying but attendance is required. Unreachable via email even with in class follow-ups. Material isn't too hard, the teaching and expectations are what make this class so difficult. David is very sweet, just not a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take 347 with him unless you're already confident you'll get an A. Tangents during lectures and graded questions and homeworks that are much harder than what's discussed in class. Proofs and examples are confusing, and exams are difficult and account for 80% of your grade. Stay away if you can.

DO NOT TAKE THIS GUY. There are others who offer MATH 347, just take theirs later if you have to or join a waitlist. THIS GUY IS THE WORST PROFESSOR AT UNC. he genuinely doesn't ever respond to emails and when confronted in person he "wrote my name down" and told me to email him AGAIN after 15+ emails with no response ALL SEMESTER. learn from me.

David makes the class so much harder than it needs to be with useless proofs and derivations while simultaneously making no sense and not explaining anything. A little bit on Youtube taught me more than him the entire semester. His slides are like a stream of consciousness that makes no sense to anybody but him. Just don't take him.

This has been the hardest class I have ever taken at UNC. He wants you to fail. There is no study guide only past tests and there is no answer sheet so you better hope you're doing it right. He expects you to just memorize all "short" proofs from the slide. Good luck even interpreting his slides. I would avoid this class at all costs.
Worst class I've taken at UNC. Made me question my sanity. If I could afford therapy I'd go because of him. Don't take, idc how much you think you can handle it. Listen to the reviews. Run! RUN!

Super fun class…if you're a masochist. Brutal class all around made worse by ambiguous teaching and prof's insistence on making you memorize useless proofs. Avoid at literally all costs, I'd rather get curb stomped than take this class again.

Very very bad experience. He doesn't post any answers to any of the assignments/midterms (despite saying he will) and this makes it soo hard to study especially when the slides he posts and uses in lecture don't make any sense. Very hard class made way harder by poor teaching and zero recourses.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful, awful class. Unorganized, unhelpful, uninteresting. Stay away at all costs, he makes it needlessly complex and it's brutal. Studying for this final will kill me.

So, so bad. So bad. Prof doesn't respond to emails, uses outdated/ambiguous slides to teach, and generally is very confusing. Take with someone else, this class isn't easy and he makes it way harder than need be.
Not a good prof, and an even worse class. Don't take with him if you can help it

Studying for exams right now and ready to just...be done with this class. A really, really painful class to take. Couple that with subpar instruction from David and it's a recipe for disaster. Please take with someone else if you value your sanity and are not a math prodigy. Thankful for the TAs/ULAs who helped me not get 0's on every test.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took this class for Econ BS thinking it couldn't be that bad, and it has been even worse. This is by far the worst taught class I've ever been in...the class is unorganized, lecture notes are incomprehensible, and homework is long, tedious, and constant. I would strongly recommend against this class, and if you HAVE to take, take with someone else.

Contrary to other reviews, professor isn't terrible. Lectures feel a bit disorganized, but homework is straightforward and tests mimic the homework. All proofs on the tests can be found on the lecture slides.

Probably not the best 347 instructor, but very fair and not as bad as reviews would say. Just put in time outside of class to things.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Would not recommend taking this class...David is a great guy but his lectures are confusing and his teaching style is frustrating. Tests are 80% of your grade in this class and for some odd reason he loves to throw in questions that look nothing like the work you do in class/homework. Take someone else and save yourself the stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just an awful class...David doesn't explain anything in an understandable manner, so you WILL be teaching yourself everything. Sitting in class for 2.5 hours every week just being talked at gets exhausting quick, and he makes zero effort to either help you understand or make class even remotely entertaining. Take with someone else, bc I hated this.
Very nice guy. He has an extremely cute dog named Mia, and he explains things pretty clearly.
he teaches it pretty confusingly, tests are incredibly accurate to homeworks and practice, is available for office hours, willing to answer questions but not the best at doing so.

If you have the option, find someone else. His lectures really don't make sense and his attendance policy is brain-dead. Won't curve prior to the end of class, and midterm averages hover around a 60. His tests always take longer than the allotted amount of time, and it is your fault for not being a professional in the sector.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely awful professor. His lectures are outdated, incorrect, and incomprehensible. He is unhelpful, boring, and just when you think you understand the material, he confuses you at the last second. Homework is tedious/unhelpful. Class averages for exams hover around 60, and he curves nothing. Take another teacher and save yourself the stress.

Everyone complaining just did not put the time into learning the material lol. His lectures can definitely be confusing if you sit in silence and don't ask questions, but he is always willing to re explain things. He also does make mistakes but quickly corrects himself. If you put the time and actually participate in class you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: don't waste time going to class, get someone else to do the in class assignments for you. one of the worst teachers at the school and literally impossible to learn from. the first and third midterms are easy if you have old ones. don't take this teacher if you can avoid it but it's not the end of world if you do

This class is a nightmare... he is hilariously bad at lecturing. Material is overwhelming, undigestible, and you had better be prepared to teach yourself everything. UNC Math department needs an overhaul, I have not taken a single good class with them yet.
Very nice and intelligent professor but completely incomprehensible lectures, which would be fine if attendance was not mandatory but it was.

Unlike many reviews here, I found the class itself to be good. There's a practical approach to various problems, and if you follow the content well, you should be able to take the exam with only a little self-study. However, there are many errors in his grading, so check it carefully.

Yes, maybe David is not that good at talking about abstract concepts, but I found it extremely helpful in his office hours. A lot of examples similar to the ones in final were presented, and he explained what you should know. You need to figure out something yourself, that's part of college. It's helpful if you bring questions to him. Nice guy.

Professor Adalsteinsson's lectures are pretty confusing but the midterms are easy. There is a good bit of homework every week (which is similar to the test questions) and a worksheet every class (which I think was graded for completion). The final was hard and very calc heavy, but the grading of it was chill and it was easy to get partial credit.

Dr. Adalsteinsson is a really nice dude but an awful lecturer, he spent the majority of the class scrawling barely legible proofs/definitions and would switch slides so fast it was impossible to both pay attention to what he was doing, and write all of it down. Grading criteria was unclear and made it impossible to know your grade in the class.

Linear is a hard class no matter what, but his lectures are horrible and impossible to follow. You have to teach everything to yourself. You have a worksheet you have to turn it every class and it's very difficult to understand how to do it by the end of. Homeworks take a long time to complete and require hours of learning.

David is very smart but doesn't know how to communicate abstract thoughts, which is unfortunate since linear algebra is a pretty abstract class. I spent most lectures figuring stuff out by watching youtube videos or using GPT. He also went outside the scope of the required content while making it an important part of the final.

Class structure with the worksheets, edfinity and gradescope helped solidify understanding but the lectures weren't the greatest. midterms are 40% final is another 40%. midterms are fairly straightforward and reflect what we learn. adalsteinsson is a cool guy just not the greatest lecturer. grading criteria is also a little confusing
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most lectures were written minutes before the class. The syllabus contained multiple errors and very odd grading criteria. Some of the lectures we're extremely confusing, but only because of unnecessary proofs. The final grade was given in connect carolina with no clear criteria or announcement on canvas. Only giving a 2 is because he's a nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely terrible. Lectures were illogical, unprepared, and he didn't even know what he was talking about. One of the worst of all the math classes I've ever taken (others not even close). Frequent mistakes. Eventually a final grade is given straight away without announcing the grade or grading scale. I don't even know how my grade was composed.

Absolutely terrible. Lectures were illogical, unprepared, and he didn't even know what he was talking about himself. One of the worst of all the math classes I've ever taken. Frequent mistakes. Eventually a final grade is given straight away without announcing the grade or grading scale. I don't even know how my grade was composed.

Absolutely terrible. Lectures were illogical, unprepared, and he didn't even know what he was talking about himself. One of the worst of all the math classes I've ever taken. Frequent mistakes. Eventually a final grade is given without announcing the grade or grading scale. I don't even know how my grade was composed.
he doesn't explain concepts well and lectures are a mess. he's a strict grader and doesn't curve in the slightest. please do not take him.

This class ruined my 4.0. Linear is such an easy subject but you cannot self study this class because of all the little things he makes you do his way on the exam. Final was 40%, midterms were another 40%. Honestly I've learned from this class not to take the insanely lower rated professors. I thought I'd give him the benefit of a doubt but rip.

Setup of the class forces you to participate. Do not plan on skipping a class. Content is easy for math oriented people but the way he explains it makes it seem harder than it is. The only way you could fail this class is if you try too hard to understand what he's saying. Exams resemble homework and both are typical style for a math class.

Lectures are SO confusing, I don't think he even knows what he's talking about. Homework was helpful, but expect to spend a lot of time learning on your own. Exams are not bad, just understanding of the basics but so different from lectures.

I stopped attending lectures after the first month because they were honestly confusing and unhelpful—it felt like the professor didn't fully understand the material himself. The midterms were manageable, but the final literally destroyed me. Thanks to him, I am going to say goodbye to my 4.0 GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Never again. NEVER explained what was covered on the final exam, the lectures were awful- so basically, teach yourself. I am a math major and David made several errors during most of his lectures- showing incompetence. Take someone who has respect for his students too, he denied my accommodations for an exam.

High rating bc he deserves a higher average imo. Other comments nailed it. The textbook he assigned was the best teaching he has done. I crammed the nights before and got A on every midterm (60% of grade). Textbook and online video walkthroughs are your best bet. Brings up confusing stuff in lec but only really tests whats on worksheets.

The lectures were useless. He doesn't respond to emails. Fortunately, the class is pretty easy. You're best off going to class, grabbing the in-class assignment, then leaving class and studying for a few minutes a day rather than wasting your time. It's a shame he's a bad professor, because I actually kind of like him on a personal level.

As everyone else said, the lectures are awful but still consider taking David due to the fact that he drops a midterm, the tests are pretty fair, and he's generally a lot nice and approachable than a lot of your other options in the math dept. Basically, trade-off between nicer grading vs having to teach yourself. Be ready to self study EVERYTHING

Do not. While admittedly this has been a tough semester for me due to some other outside circumstances, this guy did NOT help at all. Lectures are plainly incomprehensible -- not even because of the accent, he just says things and expects you to understand. Doesn't go through problem solving in class. Assigns an ungodly amount of homework.

Despite attending the lectures, I found it very difficult to do the worksheet given to us to have completed by the end of lecture. I found myself learning most of the content outside of class and my emails to the professor sent with no reply. It was difficult to get a straight answer out of the professor as he would ramble about unrelated topics.

This class is atrocious to say the least. I have learned ZILCH from the lectures—and trust me, I've been to all of them. If you want a chance at passing the exams, I would read the textbook and review the worksheets. The homework problems sometimes include topics we haven't even covered in class yet, but he keeps them on their for some reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Adalsteinsson cares deeply about his students, and attending his office hours is very helpful.

Dr. Adalsteinsson's lectures are extremely difficult to understand especially the posted slides themselves. Gives way too much homework every week with a P-set and Edfinity. Midterm 1 and 3 were pretty easy but midterm 2 was a PAIN with the amount of computation. Content is easier to learn compared to other math courses but extremely error-prone.

Anyone giving him more than a 1 is generous. Save yourself and DONT. His lectures are incomprehensible, and you'll have to teach yourself everything—no exaggeration. I thought his lectures couldn't be as bad as reviews said—trust me, they are. Exams are okay, but he as a professor is truly abominable and the worst ever. The homework is ridiculous.
Do not take this guy. He has no idea how to teach and does not care about the students. Tests are 80% of the grade and are inconsistently graded. Does not even tell you what will be on the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Make sure to have taken MATH381 or some proofs class before this. His lectures are mainly theoretical. However exams were mainly computation with about 10-15% being about proofs, except for the 2nd midterm. The computational aren't difficult but heavily error proned. Re-read lecture notes and go over proofs he discussed as some will be on exams.

Passionate professor, but the lectures are like hieroglyphics—extremely hard to understand and follow. The professor's focus on theory with little practical examples in class made it very challenging to grasp the concepts. I had to self-study everything. No answers or solutions were provided for homework assignments or lecture sheets.

His lectures are like a pizza with so many unnecessary toppings that it's hard to digest. He spent like four lectures talking about SVD but sprinkles in random side topics (like ODEs, exponential matrices, image space, Fibonacci numbers, permutations) that just make it overwhelming. He posts lecture slides but sometimes there's so much jargon.

He has extremely disorganized lectures and his explanations are REALLY bad. Homework is never posted when it is supposed to be, and tests make up 80% of the final grade. He is a nice man and you can see he enjoys teaching, but he is not a great instructor, at all.

He is a very passionate and smart prof, but hard to follow in lecture. He does not make the material intuitive and goes off on crazy tangents. Take the free A on the first midterm, because material gets harder after that. Hammer computational stuff, so you can afford to struggle with the proofs. Second midterm is brutal. TAs were useless.

Dr. A does not give any care to his students and expects us to treat Linear Algebra like its our passion. Extremely disorganized lectures, notes, and resources. He rarely gave solutions to work and even if he did they could be wrong. Don't take this class.

He is very disorganized in class structure. He tries to teach students not only application but also the reason behind, but is not doing it very well. He rushes through complicated proofs and thinks these scattering shots are enough. If any professor wants to give a hint on analysis in an application class that is not how they should do it.

You can tell he knows a lot and there are many ways to approach this subject that he doesn't fully flesh out thoughts, making lecture confusing at times. There are daily attendance worksheets that I recommend taking your notes on to stay organized. You can tell he wants you to learn and gets excited when people ask questions, but expect self-study.
Awful professor, extremely bad lectures and very strict and unfair grading. Requires you to do things “his way” and goes down a rabbit hole every time he teaches something

This dude's lectures are mysterious. Don't try to decipher his slides. Watch some linear algebra on Youtube to save yourself (linear algebra in this class is pretty self-studyable). Gave him a 2 because at least he is a nice guy. Exams are 80% of your final grade so beware of that.

Don't read any other review. This one is the only one you need. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. Students in class audibly laugh when this guy tries to explain the material. He's a nice guy, but he's the worst instructor of any sort I have ever seen. You will leave class more and more confused than from where you start. Avoid him please.

If you walked in on one of his lectures and looked around, half the people would be on their phones/laptops watching something, and the other half would be staring blankly in confusion. He ALWAYS went over on time and his lectures were extremely hard to follow. Use TA's and ULA office hours, and avoid his. He will take up hours of your time
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy and clearly very smart and knowledgeable. However, I often left lectures more confused on the material than when I started. Grading scheme/curve was never revealed, nor were our grades on the final exam. Despite being the applications class, there were very few applications mentioned, and there were proofs on multiple of our exams.

Professor Adalsteinsson's lectures are definitely hard to comprehend. He doesn't explain the material well and sometimes he will dive into what seems like random topics. Overall, he is a really nice guy, just not a great professor. His tests are not hard, with them being mostly computational, they feel like hw questions with different numbers.

David is not a good lecturer. Confusing, hard to follow, and difficult to contact. Office hours are a big help if you can manage to corral him into actually helping and staying directly on topic. David dropped our course grade in Connect Carolina with no message, no access to our final grades, no grade breakdown, no regrades, no curve description.

The class is not taught well. The upsides of the class is that there isn't much homework and that he is lenient with the curve at the end. 3 midterms and 1 final exam are worth 80% of your grade, so be careful of that. The first and third midterms were easy, but the second one was extremely difficult.

Very poor time management during lectures; you will have to learn a lot on your own. Said that we did too well on the first midterm, so he made the next one much harder (the median score for one of the questions was a 0). Made us learn Julia but we weren't allowed to use it on exams. Would avoid this professor if possible.

Great guy. Lectures can be confusing, but that's just how linear algebra is. If you study the worksheets and homeworks that he gives, you'll do well on the midterms and final because it's basically just doing the same techniques with different numbers. Personally, I don't think the reviews on here are an acccuarete representation of professor Adal.
W prof

genuinely the worst professor ive ever had at unc. he always talks about things for 30 mins of our 50 min class that are completely irrelevant to the worksheets or homeworks or exams that we are given and then im left trying to figure it out for myself before turning in the 3 assignments we have due every friday. run. do not take.
Lectures are very, very hard to understand. The material isn't too bad so you can definitely teach yourself if you need to, but I would avoid this professor if you can. Super nice guy, though.
fluent in yappanese....

His exams are easy that most students get 100 on the first, 40% on the third. The second one might be bad but he "curved." I do recommend math majors taking his class, since the proofs he covered will increase your mathematical maturity. I don't think he recommended Strang's lecture in class so I guess people below are just finding excuses...

Prof Adalsteinsson is probably the worst professor I've ever had at UNC. He is super nice and obviously super smart, but his lectures are terrible. Lectures are confusing, scattered and read off his own poorly handwritten notes. He doesn't provide solutions for classwork and actually RECOMMENDS you watch other professors' lectures online.

David doesn't reveal his grading scheme ahead of final grades being posted so beware. Also, he tends to teach the class in a much more abstract manner than any of the other linear algebra professors. With that being said, he has done some interesting research and work in the field so talk to him about it if you get the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: this guy blows, don't take him

Here I am thinking I won't have a worse professor than the past ones I've had here. Then comes this dude. My GOD is he confusing and hard to follow. It's useless to come to lectures because he never explains anything and instead recommends WATCHING OTHER PROFESSOR'S LECTURES. The entire semester I had to self-teach EVERYTHING. DO NOT TAKE HIM EVER

Nice guy, horrible teacher. I have never felt more confused in my life than after leaving one of his lectures. Gives no context to the content you are learning, goes at a rapid pace, does not explain content, and just does problems on the board in a confusing way. Terrible slides that dont help at all

Again, super smart dude, abysmal professor.

Professor Adalsteinsson is a fair grader who has great lectures. he explains concepts very well and the tests are a good reflection of what we go over in class and practice. He also drops the lowest exam which definitely helps.

A lot of people do not say good things about professor adalsteinsson, but he is not bad at all. You just need to come to class and he is great at explaining concepts. Tests are fair and I would definitely take this class with him again.

David's lectures are all over the place and he is not responsive to emails/messages outside of class. Even when asking for solutions to practice he's given us, he doesn't provide any because he says he doesn't have them written up. This semester was incredibly difficult due to his unreliability and confusing lectures -- I had to teach myself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's better than his rating suggests, although sometimes it can be hard to follow when he proves things in lectures. The homework is also a bit tedious sometimes, but the homework and textbook prepare you well for tests. There's not a huge curve, but the tests are just practicing each of the techniques from the course.

Had him for MATH 347, but couldn't select it. The best part of the way Adalsteinsson teaches linear is following along with worksheets, so it's not just a complicated lecture that you have to practice on homework. Sometimes lectures became a bit too complicated to follow, but he was friendly and did a lot to make sure you followed.

He was not the best lecturer by any means, and I definitely found myself having to do a lot of teaching myself outside of class. Attendance was mandatory due to the worksheets we had every class which ended up being the only resources we had to study. The tests were fair though and mimicked closely the worksheets from class.
Confusing lectures but easy tests. But you still can't miss classes bc he takes attendences. If you like to watch MIT open courses and teach yourself, then you're good to go.

Professor Adalsteinsson's lectures can become befuddling when he starts discussing theoretical aspects of topics we cover. But other than that, his exams are fair. As long as you make sure you are crystal clear on how to do the worksheets he gives each lecture, you will be fine.

He's a decent guy but not a good lecturer at all. His notes are hard to follow along with and lecture is very fast. Be prepared to have to teach yourself a lot of what he goes over in class through online videos and the textbook. The good news is the content is not hard on its own. He's just bad at teaching.

I was in the same section that he subbed for a single day (emphasis on a single day). Here is my review. 1. Adalsteinsson inspired me to play CoC during lecture 2. Adalsteinsson is hilarious because he may be the only lecturer at UNC who prefers a blackboard. Keepin it old school 3. Adalsteinsson is caring because he cares about proofs and diagrams

He substituted for my professor in one meeting of MATH 347. He prepared the lecture and examples with efforts, and goes in more depth than my original professor, which helped me a lot but wasn't appreciated by most other students in my session. He is a great guy. It is shocking to see that he receives such a low score here.

Programming assignment instructions are not clear from the start, but he was available outside of class to clarify what he wanted. The material is pretty standard, and his presentation is alright. See Stoer's book for rigorous proofs and details which were not covered.
Dr. Adalsteinsson's lecture notes are normally excellent. He could've done a little better in instructions for programming projects. The instructions should have been more detailed.

While I like Dr. Adalsteinsson as a person and he has been readily accessible almost every day, my main problem with this course was that it was unclear almost the entire time what the grading criteria would be. He changed the makeup of the syllabus on the last day of classes and before that we had no clue what determined our grade. I still don't.

David was absolutely the worst professor I have ever experienced in my entire life. Its impossible to know how youre doing in the course, and the final grade seems to be a lottery for how hes doing when he makes the curve. Please dont make the same mistake I did. Do not take Linear Algebra with David Adalsteinsson.
