reviews.comment: His explanations aren't anything special, but I guess I've had worse. His grading is rather unfair and he makes exams too long for the time constraints for the purpose of "distinguishing" students who know material just as well as others but are faster, letting him maintain a clean Gaussian curve for grades. Not impressed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Bohlman clearly has a passion and interest in her lectures. She looks forward to participation, reading over the short assignments, and gives great feedback on the midterm. She takes students' workloads into account when scheduling her big deadlines/midterm, clearly showing empathy for her students.

Prof. Bohlman's passion for music is evident taking this class and she really just wants students to find their musical passions. The two papers require a lot of thought, though the final project I felt was easier than these papers. This course will challenge you to think abstractly and let go of your preconceived notions about music.

Andrea is very knowledgeable in her subject areas. That being said, I had no interest in basically all of what she had to teach about (which is maybe more the music department's fault than hers), but it felt like a high school class where it was just fluff that had no impact on what I am going to be doing in my professional career.

I beg the UNC Music department to do away with this new curriculum. Dr. Bohlman was fantastic and clear but the material she was given to work with was nearly nonexistent. This course caused multiple people to DROP the music major because they have decided to stop teaching anything useful. The dumbing down of the music major at UNC is sad to see.

The main issue with this course was the course itself, not the professor. Bohlman is a zealous, involved professor who will help you with anything-- academic or personal. That said, I didn't learn a lot in this course. The lectures tended to be all over the place and slightly unrelated to each other. Homework is not required, tho assigned.

Andrea is alright; no more, no less. Similar to my experience with her MUSC 120, we learned absolute nonsense the whole semester. We basically studied music through unguided interpretation. Andrea has a knack for calling on students but not really caring for their responses & for giving unclear essay criteria, but overall this class is an easy A.

Andrea is fantastic. I would happily take another class with her. I would also give her a 5 if this class wasn't pure fluff. This is more beneficial than music history? The curriculum is disjointed nonsense and the final project was a show and tell of everyone's musical interests. I think music conservatories would laugh if they observed MUSC270.

Andrea is great, I've loved her in every class I've taken with her. Unsure about the other review for 270 -- this class was totally fair and each assignment's instructions took you through baby steps to complete. Lectures were diverse and required critical thinking. Being the first semester of this course, some bumps in the road were to be expected

Course was very badly structured and not well taught. Assignments lacked guidelines and grading was tough considering how vague the instructions were. Lectures were incredibly tedious on topics that were totally unrelated. Bohlman was completely useless when you asked for help, and gave feedback that resulted in bad grades. Do not take.

Music 120 was an interesting class to be sure, it would be hard for me to summarize exactly what we learned as it was a bit all over the place. Lacking in structure. HOWEVER Professor Bohlman was fantastic. She took the time to be personable, tried to get to know each of her students and was open to differing opinions.

MUSC 120 was a frustratingly disorganized class but this was much more due to the curriculum than the instructor-- Bohlman did her best to teach us useful material and some classes were very enjoyable. Participate & put some time into bigger assignments and you can get an A. Take advantage of her office hours to get to know her outside of class!
This class was so easy. I took it for my VP credit. As long as you did the participation assignments & the unit assignments, you'll do well in the class. Definitely recommend :)

Literally SOOO easy. If you submit the assignments you'll get an A; I'm not exaggerating. And, the class is super interesting; you get to learn about gender topics, drag, and sexualities, while listening to music. We even got to bring in Polish students studying gender studies, which was super interesting. Take this class.
Very nice and sweet and probably the easiest class I've taken at Carolina. Literally all you have to do is turn in the assignments and you'll get a 100 in the class

My favorite professor at UNC. Uses discussion-based class to engage everyone in the class. Very welcoming and understanding. Took me out of my comfort zone in a good way. Had her for 291 as well, which had a different class structure, but still great lectures. Incredibly caring, and challenged my perception of music as a violinist. Highly recommend
Dr. Bohlman is a good professor. However, her quizzes are near-impossible to do well on. If you don't have any experience in music theory, it makes it even harder.
literally just turn in ur work and you'll get an A

The easiest class I've taken at UNC. Never did a single reading and could sit through lectures and do other work if I needed to. One class we literally listened to ocean sounds and she laid on the floor. So chill and easy, a few essays that I could crank in a few hours. She's super caring and extended quizzes for me. Take this for your VP gen-ed!
This is definitely not an Easy A/ GPA booster class. Lectures were unprepared and unorganized
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's really chill and nice. I didn't find the class too interesting and actually wish she would lecture more (crazy to say I know but you'll understand what I mean). She's clearly really smart, it's just the classes can get boring since there's such a lack of structure.

Prof Bohlman is genuinely a good person. She cares about her students and is there to support you if you need. 355 is one of those classes where you can hear a bunch of different opinions and widen your perspectives even if the material is a bit out-there sometimes. Definitely a great way to get capstone credit class for a music major.

Andrea is a good professor, but the material is often disengaging. MUSC 291 is easy but boringthere's not much material to discuss. There are several rather difficult quizzes throughout the class, but she mitigates them with extra credit opportunities. There's no midterm and an insignificant final.

Andrea was a really nice teacher and the class was super chill. Only had a few papers and blog assignments but was graded based on effort. By far one of the laid back classes I've taken but really fun!

Genuinely the best professor I've taken at UNC. Her lectures are entertaining, and she's very passionate and knowledgeable about the content. She's also extremely accessible outside of class, through both email and her office hours. She had one midterm and the final; it was an extremely manageable course load. Can't recommend her classes enough

reviews.comment: Really good professor who cares deeply about her students!

LOVED her class. easy to follow, interesting and she is very nice. definitely an easy A as long as you do the homework and follow the study guides for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

I recommend taking Dr. Septer if you need an easy class!

reviews.comment: One of my favorite bio professors! Dr. Septer really cared about the success of her students, providing us with the BEST study guides and making herself available outside of class! I would definitely take a class with her again!

Professor was disorganized and unavailable.

Professor changed up on her word ALL THE TIME

listen to her lectures over and over again. she tests on what she says. lowk i dont think there are great options for biol 240 at unc so she might be your only option. i didnt buy the textbook, it was $$ and not super useful.

She is so sweet and quirky and a knowledgable but her class and exams are so unpredictable and unorganized. I would give her some grace because it's her first semester at UNC. absolute WORST professor for BIOL103. does not know how to get anything done technology-wise, always behind on lectures, and randomly sets unit quizzes so they are due at noon instead of 11:59 without ANY notice whatsoever. avoid at all costs unless you want a semester long migraine

nice person but not good lectures. goes on random tangents, adds in unnecessary info, and is condescending. feel like we barely made progress on content in class. frequent amount of work, and test question phrasing can be confusing/riddle-like. she ends up rushing content close to midterms, so need to cram in last-minute content close to exams.

great lady, bad professor. course content is pretty easy, but her lectures make it super confusing. understood the content better when i taught it to myself outside of class. we also rarely finished the lectures and fell behind often. dr. rea is a nice person and is willing to help you, but honestly just avoid her class.

Her lectures are terrible to follow. At this point, I don't even know what to study. reviews.comment: Genuinely the WORST bio professor at UNC. Avoid at all costs. Her exams are written like riddles and she is horrifically unorganized. Dr. Gillmore is a lovely person, and largely very fair. The assignments did have some confusing guidelines, because the class is taught by multiple professors with countering philosophies. She doesn't communicate with her TAs at all. They say my design is fine, then she claims it doesn't meet expectations. No clear grading criteria, completely inconsistent. RUN
took stor 415 with him, this professor CANNOT teach

Currently taking for STOR415 (not listed on ratemyprofessor). Took him a while ago. He was not an understanding professor and could not teach the material well. Would get hung up on seating assignments during quizzes, so much so that he would single kids out to move around the classroom as if we were playing musical chairs until it was to his liking.

got 100 for both 2midterms but for final only 86…Really hard!!
Quiz is based on homework but with slight change, homework is long and weekly, lecture is good but his handwriting is hard to distinguish
Hard class Hard professor...RUN

Very difficult professor that didn't understand the needs of the class. I found it difficult to study for the course due to the lack of guidance on what would be tested. There are slight bonus points on the midterms and no curve or bonus points on the final. I would not recommend.

Worst professor I've had so far at UNC. When the class expressed concerns over a lack of time for the midterm, he dismissed us and made the next midterm longer. Professor was not understanding of my circumstances. It's not the most interesting subject. Pretty easy class, as the grading is just very generous. Whether that's on homeworks, quizzes, or tests, they always give heavy partial credit. Professor Ali is a great lecturer and teaches concepts really clearly and well. His homeworks are straightforward and relates well to the lecture content and exams. Lenient grader on quizzes and exams. Gives extra credit questions on exams as well.

reviews.comment: You can expect discrete to be hard no matter who you take it with but Prof. Nezhad made it as easy as it can get. Fantastic lecturer, but exams are difficult.

She definitely focuses on lectures, participation is important. You can get away without reading EVERYTHING but you should read. She's not too tough on grading so just be present.

Dr. Monroe is a really sweet lady; you can tell she is passionate about what she teaches. reviews.comment: Dr. Monroe have lots of dense readings that werent really necessary unless there was a quiz (which were all scheduled on the syllabus). Often, her lectures were repetitive of what had already been taught. She is a pretty fair grader overall.

There's a lot of readings, though she gives you plenty of time to take quizzes and exams. Really interesting class, but if you're looking for an easy elective, choose something else
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Half way through the semester I'm having a great time in her class. The class is discussion heavy and participation is required. The upside is there aren't many assignments/quizzes but there are lots of readings. You can get away with not doing the readings but you should attend lecture so you at least understand things.

We did not have many grades in this course but Professor Monroe was fair. She does not provide clear rubrics and is VERY vague when discussing expectations in work. There was a reading for every class period but texts were free or inexpensive. She is very knowledgeable but not always the best at teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Monroe is very knowledgable about her studies, but can come off as intimidating. She really tries her best to get to know her students. Grading was often harsh and oddly specific, she expects her students to think like "historians." Reading was every class and long. No technology in class. Was an ok class but had to work hard for good grade
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Monroe is brilliant, no denying that. She is a master of her content. Grading can very between assignments. Some assignments are graded very leniently, some very harshly. Can be intimidating. There is also a *lot* of reading in class, no computers allowed, and you have to print readings out, which was a pain. But it's a fine class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: went to office hours for help, she implied she thought I wasn't trying or simply was not smart- offered no help to improve my understanding. I left feeling discouraged, the opposite of the purpose of office hours. She gave me a low participation grade even though I spoke 2-3+ times in every class, missing only 2 (both excused). absolutely absurd.

Don't be fooled by her kindness or her sarcasm. Tries to be funny but makes Spanish harder than it is. Participation is RNG, exams are 50%, and all papers and speaking is subjective to her harsh grading. Does not answer questions properly in class. Had to self study and learn to pass with a decent grade in the class. Take any other 203 professor.

Don't listen to the good reviews that say she is helpful, can teach, and is caring. She doesn't answer questions properly (literally said "I think that is the correct answer because it just is"), grades very harshly (points off for grammar), participation is biased and 10% of grade and not a free A. Take literally any other professor for 203.
Very nice and funny professor. Tries her best to make class interesting and engaging. Spanish 203 is not easy but I recommend her!!

Really great! I liked her a lot, she was super easy to talk to and was very excited about us learning! So sweet and make class very engaging and fun, we did a lot of great culture stuff too. Not difficult if you try and give it your best, just stay on top of the dates and you'll be a-okay!

Professor Alexander is super laid back and does not have heavy expectations. She doesn't expect you to be fluent in Spanish, and reviews a lot of key concepts. She grades very leniently, and she's very transparent about exam content. We spend most of class just working in groups; it's very low stakes, and casual. I would take her if you can!

Martha does come off as short or passive-aggressive to her students at times, but she does try to make class engaging and wants to see an engaging class having a lot of conversation during class. She's an understanding professor if you talk to her outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: While she has received good ratings for lower level Spanish classes, I would avoid taking her class for anything higher than 204. She struggles to teach more complex gramatical structures and does not know any of the curriculum that the rest of the 261 students are being taught.
I love Señora Alexander. If you have to take 203, this is the most painless way to finish the language requirement. Be sure to participate and do the readings but she is funny and fair.

Spanish-only course but Prof. Alexander is easy to understand and kind! Easy grader overall, but make sure you participate in class because that's graded (not a free A). HW due before every class at 7:59AM. In my opinion course content is kind of all over the place, but that's common to all sections and Prof. Alexander tries to make it engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I entered SPAN203 with zero confidence in my ability since it had been 3 years since I had last taken Spanish. She did a great job cultivating a comfortable environment so it was easy to participate. She is a kind grader and you can definitely get a good grade as long as you prepare for the exams, and she gives you the resources you need to succeed

Prof. Alexander is extermely nice. Class is taught fully in Spanish and feels more like a conversation than a lecture. Encourages a lot of participation from class. Great professor for understanding of the language.

I loved taking Professor Alexander. I enjoyed her lectures and she was always available after. I went from knowing virtually no Spanish grammar to bring conversational. She got frustrated when no one responded to her questions or did not engage so be conversational and if you're confused or don't understand something, just tell her (English is ok).

Hard class, tons of homework, but she is a really understanding teacher and genuinely caring person! Loved her attitude in class every day and she made going to Spanish 3 times a week much more bearable than it would have been otherwise. AMAZING!!!!!

Professor Alexander was defiantly my favorite teacher this semester and she made my days much better. She is a great teacher and gives very useful tips and is very funny. She made everyone in the class actually want to learn and engage with each other. Take her class if you can!

I honestly was afraid to take SPAN204 after a year of not taking Spanish, but Prof. Alexander made it a lot better! because I actually had a desire to learn! Super caring in my opinion and will try her best to cater to the class! She's an amazing option for SPAN204.

I really enjoyed taking SPAN203 with her. She was really great at teaching the material; she had good lecture slides, gave useful tips, and so on. She was also funny and nice. Also, she doesn't have a difficult-to-understand accent or anything like that, and the interview she gave that was part of the class was low-stress as well

Profe Alexander was definitely my favorite teacher this semester. She is so funny and cares a lot about her students. She is a fairly easy grader and pretty much as long as you participate in class and try on your assignments you will do well. If you're taking 204, try to have her. She is the best.

Professor Alexander is amazing. She teaches in a good manner and lets you participate in class. Participation is important in her class. She gives a lot of examples that can help you with quizzes, midterms, and the final. She cares about her students and helps them with anything you need. If you need to take a Spanish class she is the one to go to.

Dr. Alexander was a completely different professor in this class. Graded very harshly and without rubrics on papers. Made several comments about too many good grades making her look bad. Unhelpful and rude when asking clarifying questions. Everyone was shocked! I ended with a good grade, but it was difficult and took lots of effort outside class.

The grading guidelines were not clear, as were the expectations. Somehow there wasn't a clear breakdown as to what makes an a, b,c, etc. Made comments about now giving too many a`s? I don't feel as though I got better at spanish at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Alexander was very tough. She made the topic interesting but was very strict on grading. She even so much as said one time that she "didn't want grades to be too high because that would make her look bad." Homeworks and papers were graded very harshly, and the tests were even worse. Do not take this class if you're looking for an easy A.

Best 203 professor, no doubt. Class is difficult, but everything is standardized by the department across all sections. She does her best to make the content fun and engaging, and really cares about helping every student learn as much as they can. Would recommend every student try to take her if you can. If you put in the effort, you will be fine.
Martha is a GOAT.

Professor Alexander was hands-down the best Spanish professor I have ever had. She is extremely understanding and takes time to review things some students may not understand when she taught it the first time. Highly recommend her!

If you have a choice, definitely take her for 203. The content/tests and stuff are decided by the department, but she is great at explaining the concepts and keeping the class environment fun. She's super nice and friendly, but I should mention that you have to participate (it's part of your grade) and she does cold call every so often.

Prof Alexander is really nice and funny and I think she cares about how much we enjoy the class. There were times, though, that I missed assignments and her attitude was kind of like - theres nothing I can do, and that would end in 0s for the assignment. But overall, my grade in the class (B-) was mainly my fault. DO YOUR HOMEWORK every night

I LOVE PROFESORA ALEXANDER! She's super sweet, and she wants everyone to do well. She's a fair grader, and made the class fairly easy. She teaches material well. Whenever we were bored or finished material early, we would read our horoscopes in Spanish, which was fun. 10/10 recommend. I took 203 with her, and I'm also taking 204 with her.

Profesora Alexander is one of the best choices for SPAN 203. She really cares about her students learning Spanish rather than nitpicking small mistakes. If you speak up and try your best, she'll meet you the rest of the way. Take her if you can!!

Profesora Alexander made an early morning class feel like the middle of the day with her charisma and energy. Like many have said, SPAN203 is going to be hard, regardless of the professor, due to the department's curriculum. With that being said, your best chance to learn and succeed is with Profesora Alexander!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is a great class/professor if you want to get better at speaking Spanish. The Cengage Assignments (mostly review for me) and the fact that she's not very flexible with students unless there's a written reason from the school was annoying but other than that she's a passionate and helpful professor. All in all I enjoyed the class and professor

Professor Alexander was by far the best Spanish professor I've had at UNC and I've had to take three levels. She was always very considerate of the trials and tribulations of being in an online environment. If you want to truly learn the concepts I definitely recommend taking her. Professor Alexander is also hilarious and extremely enthusiastic.

Dra. Alexander was so kind and caring, and she literally made my semester with her kindness and fun teaching style. I took 255 with her, and she was mostly concerned with us speaking and ensuring we used our Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher, so understanding and fun class. Cover very interesting topics that are fun to discuss.

Professor Alexander is a solid choice for 203. It's not an easy A due to the way the general Spanish curriculum I set up but she is one of the best options. She was responded to emails quickly and often offered to help. She also spoke English when telling us really important info which was very helpful.

Professor Alexander was super nice! She does call on each person at least once per class but she releases the power point an hour or so before the class so you can prepare! We also did a lot of work in breakout rooms during class. Spanish was difficult for me but she was super helpful and did her best to make class exciting!

Be ready to be called on because she calls on every student to participate at least twice during class. Tests are super hard but she doesn't make them so it isn't her fault. MSL isn't difficult there are about 5 to do a night. You must read the textbook!!! I hope to never take another spanish class but she made it fine.

Words can't describe how incredible Dr. Alexander is. I got the flu and missed the midterm, then my partner left the class before a group project was due, but Dr. Alexander worked very closely with me to make sure that my grades didn't suffer. She is compassionate, hilarious, and will never decline to answer a question if it will help you learn.

Profesora Alexander is an awesome professor! She is clearly enthusiastic about spanish and teaching. She always makes an effort to make class activities fun, and she gives good feedback on all the graded items. She is very energetic and funny, and I can't recommend her highly enough.

I adore Dr. Alexander. She is probably the best Spanish professor I have had so far! She is so enthusiastic, funny, and kind. She gives useful feedback in class and on writing assignments. I appreciate her fairness and encouragement! Highly recommend her class.

professor alexander is a solid span255 choice. she's nice enough and teaches a pretty chill class but can get on you for small things. pretty easy to get an A and pretty low stress level, except for the voicethread everyone has to do at the end. overall would recommend

She is a wonderful professor who is dedicated to seeing all students understand and learn. SPAN 203 is a difficult course in and of itself, but she outlines the material very well, and her teaching style is very effective.

I love Professor Alexander! She's extremely caring and helpful both in class, as well as during office hours. She's also easy to understand and has a sense of humor that makes the class more enjoyable. Her quizzes are fairly easy, and projects and exams have clear grading expectations. Participate at least once a class and you'll be fine.

Really excellent Spanish professor. I had her for 203. She is very kind and made class enjoyable. Would definitely take again. The exams are weirdly culture heavy compared to 105 but very manageable. Great experience overall.
Fair amount of homework, but doable. Pretty quiz-heavy, but study the vocab and you should be fine. Not the best spanish teacher I've ever had, but she's very nice and I would take her class again.

Professor Alexander is a wonderful choice for Spanish! She is a fair grader, very nice, but you will also be expected to participate in class. Also, Spanish is her second language, so her accent is much easier to understand than many other teachers.

She is the NICEST teacher I've ever had and really helped me a long way in overcoming my fear of speaking Spanish. She really just wants her students to succeed - absolutely try to get her as a professor for 255 if you can.
Martha was SUPER organized and always fair.  I really enjoyed her 203 class and would definitely recommend

Sra. Alexander is phenomenal! She really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Homework is limited and if you prepare for tests, you'll do great. She's always there to help you and with her help the class isn't too difficult.

She is a super nice professor and she will help you if you don't understand things. Workload was fairly light- the hw isn't always helpful but its always super easy. helpful to use chat to break it down when its confusing. Quizzes and exams were superrrrrr easy- she gives you a refrence guide telling you exactly what to know- so just know that!!

She's a great professor who genuinely cares about her students. There's alot of homework and the exams are tough, but she's always willing to help and makes sure you understand the material. When I needed accommodations after an accident, she was very supportive. She is very friendly, approachable, and fair—just be ready to participate and keep up.
The class is not easy but she makes sure everyone understands the material. Participation is important. She is a great professor but there is daily homework's
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: not a very friendly teacher, other friends in classes would get small cards to help them on quizzes and other exams like oral quizzes. Good teacher, but another teacher would definetely be better
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very fun class even if you don't enjoy Spanish. She makes sure everyone knows the material in class and is attentive to students needs. Homework is informative and good (but not fun) practice.
Everyone knows she's the best! COMP 455 is known to be hard, but she explained the concepts in a way that they stick with you forever.
Comp 455 can be conceptually tough, but the way Alyssa taught it made it really easy to understand. The slides and lesson were perfectly clear. Tests were very fair too.

Pass/failed. Didn't post recordings, which for material that has meticulous steps and reasons for them makes it incredibly hard to review a concept more than just seeing the end result. Tests made up 90% of the grade, and were taken entirely from homework questions. Rewarded cramming over really understanding the material imo. Still a nice person.

Dr. Lytle is super nice and a great professor! I've never taken a comp sci class before, but she made it really easy to understand and is gracious with quiz grading. Office hours are super helpful if you're ever stuck, and the class is mostly smaller assignments that you can redo until you get 100%.

As someone who had no background of computer science, I was scared to take this class but it ended up being one of my favorites this semester! Go to lectures, submit homework early (you get extra credit), and take advantage of office hours! The quizzes are super similar to the practice questions provided on the class site. Would recommend!

No required attendance and slideshows posted so you can get by without going to class. Quizzes and final fairly straight forward and many question were taken from the practice questions she posted, which were often actually harder than the exam itself. Overall, she is very nice and would recommend taking the calls with her.

Maybe she's only really good at teaching 110, because the 455 lectures were overall the most confusing lectures I've ever attended. She didn't know what she was talking about and neither did we. At least the quiz questions were all off the homeworks, but like just know in advance that 90% of your grade will be exams.

Not sure how the high ratings happened. Lectures were often confused, turnout dropped fast, and many who stayed left frustrated. I left the course disappointed in the quality of instruction. Would recommend another professor if you want solid understanding.

Easy class and she's super generous with grading, you get bonus points for submitting things early and your lowest quiz gets replaced with your grade on the final if it's higher. Quizzes are also super simple and similar, if not easir, than hw/practice.

i was terrified of comp bc i've never coded in my life, but comp110 with dr. byrnes was super helpful with the basics of python. we do a lot of in-class practice/walkthroughs and the TAs are also really helpful. the quizzes are straight from the homework and the memory diagrams get easier with practice! 110 is nothing to be worried about.

This was my first time coding, and Dr. Byrnes was amazing! She explained things clearly and was very nice. It was fairly easy to pick up the material. EC is given if you turn in exercises early. Quiz practice questions are harder than the quiz questions. Practice memory diagrams, go to office hours, go to quiz review sessions, and you will be set!

Definitely the best professor to take COMP 110 with. As someone who had never touched a line of code before in my life, lectures were extremely interesting and the content never felt like too much. Assignments were dispersed throughout the semester and never felt like too much. Just practice memory diagrams before each exam and you'll do great.

Alyssa is great, and so are the COMP110 TAs. Coming from someone with ZERO prior coding experience, I won't lie, this class is NOT easy. Seek help from the TAs early and often!!! Content isn't super hard, it's just a plain grind. Lock in, DON'T USE AI, ask for help, and you'll succeed. Good class to meet bio major supplemental math credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am really bad at COMP110 and would not recommend taking it if you can avoid it, but it is required for many majors so if you're gonna take it, Byrnes is a great professor. She knows her stuff and is very kind. Class is hard but that's lowkey just me, if you lock in from the beginning (AVOID RELYING ON AI) it will be fine.
Professor Byrnes is the best! She is a great professor, especially for a class like COMP 455. Extra credit is given for solving homework and quizzes are very manageable with study.

I took COMP 110 with Prof. Byrnes in Fall 2024 having no prior coding experience. The COMP 110 team is amazing! Byrnes had maternity leave and was replaced by Kris Jordan for the second half of the semester; thanks to her, the transition was nearly seamless. I thought she was a solid teacher on her own.

Took this class with 0 experience in coding, and easily got an A. The lectures are great, the assignments are pretty easy, and the exercises are very doable if you spend a good amount of time. The pre-quiz practice questions are harder than the actual quizzes which is really nice.

Course design is ok, since her TAs are very helpful. Did not see herself with students much though. 
110 is really just a plain grind. You'll do well if you give it decent work for a 3-credit course.

Made a gateway course in comp 110 difficult to understand for students with no comp background. Took the material and quizzes from Kris Jorden but fails to teach this material. Overall she was very kind but did not teach the basics of comp well thus resulting in many students getting bad grades on assignments and quizzes.

I think your COMP110 experience depends on the group of professors that design the course material more than your lecturer, but Professor Byrnes made the class both interesting and engaging. The content in late October - early November gets difficult quickly, seek help from the TAs.

Prof. Byrnes is a great professor who cares about students learning the material. I stopped going to class besides the quizzes but I felt all the assignments were fair and didn't take me long at all. She is a great choice to take COMP 110 with.

Alyssa was very caring and made Python less daunting for everyone. The one time she was late to class, she explained she'd rescued a kitten and then made up for being late by showing us adorable pictures. Her lectures were always well spoken. She and the COMP110 team are the kindest educators I've had at UNC, and I'd recommend this class to anyone!

I am rating the class as a whole not Professor Byrnes. I always found it difficult to get help outside of class because of how many people were at tutoring sessions and office hours. Also, my emails usually took more than 2 days to get a response. Professor Byrnes was a kind person, but the COMP 110 team as a whole did not do a great job.

I have 0 coding experience but love math & problem-solving. Easy and fun class with knowledgeable TAs, office hours, and forums for virtual tech support. Start the EXs early because they can be tricky. Don't be afraid of this class, the comp110 team makes it fun and approachable!
I had Alyssa for around half the semester before she went on leave. She was such a fun, thoughtful professor. She explained everything so well and always reassured her students. Loved this class.

Dr. Lytle is great if you need COMP 110 but aren't a computer science-oriented student, like me. She explained challenging concepts really well, and was flexible regarding late penalties. The assignments are annoying, but prepare you for the quizzes and final, which are easy.

Most accommodating and clear professor I've EVER taken a class with here. Alyssa really wants to see her students succeed and explains the material in way that makes sense w 0 coding background. I'd recommend taking her a million times over. If you pay attention, you'll do well in this class, and there's lots of extra help (office hours, tutoring)

Had Dr. Byrnes before she left on maternity leave and was super sad to see her go! She is excellent at teaching to those with no experience and scaffolding material in a way that makes sense. I had 0 experience coming into 110 and I thoroughly enjoyed the class. The final is only 10% of your grade, very nice to have a low stakes final!

Had her for half a semester until Dr. Jordan took over. She was amazing, and her lectures were very clear and easy to follow. I didn't have much coding experience and felt that she explained all the concepts in thorough, yet concise ways that made sense to me.

If you don't want to be disappointed by other professors for the next however many more years your in college, don't take Alyssa. All my years of school, I have never had a better teacher. Shes incredible and so sweet. Absolute let down when Kris took over even though he is regarded as one of the "best". He sucked. I hope she is well! Alyssa >>>

Incredible professor, my first time taking any sort of comp sci class and I love it now. Explains things very well and has a very clear and forgiving grading system. Very easy A if you show up to class and do the assignments on time, don't be scared by the "12-15 hrs/wk" they talk about I studied a couple hours for each quiz and ended with a 97.
Super sweet and a great prof! She explained things in a very comprehensible way and the quizzes never had any surprises and were generally pretty easy and simple.

I had a bad Python experience before and was terrified for 110, but Alyssa made it so easy to understand. Lectures were really good and paced evenly. She is really good at explaining things. I appreciated all the opportunities to practice what we learned. Very unfortunate that Kris took over, but I hope she is doing well

Dr. Byrnes is an amazing professor!! I had zero previous coding experience and have done well! She is a great lecturer and is very funny! Multiple short quizzes throughout the semester help to balance the weight of the final. The majority of your grade comes from coding assignments, which are both fun and not too difficult. Highly recommend!!

If you have prior experience with coding (e.g. online courses or AP in HS), her COMP 110 will be a breeze for you. Her multiple-choice questions on quizzes are often just reused questions from homework. On the other hand, people with no coding experience will have to conquer a major learning curve, but that's natural with programming in general.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I came into this class with no prior coding experience, and I have really enjoyed it. Alyssa moves through her powerpoint quickly, but she explains concepts well. If you understand the practice problems for quizzes, they aren't difficult. Coding exercises have clear instructions especially at first. Lectures are posted so attendance isn't required!

This class is structured greatly and the TA's are all super knowledgeable. Office hours/tutoring are amazing resources and lectures are recorded. Alyssa is a great professor and explains everything clearly. The exercises are challenging, but quizzes are very straightforward. Practice questions are posted for every unit and are extremely helpful!

Not bad but not great. She's super nice but format of the class could be improved. A great deal of the grade on quizzes and tests comes from an understanding of memory diagrams, a conceptual idea, rather than actual coding and programming skills. As someone who'd never taken a coding class before, not hard to get a good grade but must put in work.
Amazing Professor. Had genuine fun with the assignments given and could tell there was a clear passion for teaching. Would 100% take again.

COMP110 was the most well-structured class I've taken at UNC. I took this course for SS1 with 0 prior coding experience and came into it intimidated. Although the material was difficult, Alyssa and the TAs were extremely kind and helpful. I found all homework to have a purpose, and I'd 100% recommend doing the study guides for every quiz.

As someone with no coding experience, did not think class was structured well. Lectures got very confusing and hard to follow. Lectures recorded, but notes posted after class are incoherent and hard to understand. Wish things were spelled out more clearly in class. Office hours very helpful for exercises and they are worth a lot so definitely go.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great and funny! Love her and made comp 110 easy and fun.

This class has so many opportunities to do well in the class. There is extra credit you can recieve from turning in your exercises early so, DO IT. Even if you do mediocre on the quizzes and final, you can walk away from the class with an A. However, I will say that the exercises can be frustrating but is very helpful with understanding the class.

As an experienced coder, 110 was easy with 1-2 hrs of work per week. Attendance wasn't required (except for 5 quizzes which were easy if you did the practice problems), and the weekly assignments were easy. But, if you don't know how to code, this course will def be challenging (maybe 4-5 hrs/wk), but manageable. This sem's avg was an A-.

I really love Alyssa as a professor. Genuinely I don't think she even knows my name but she is so sweet and cute and bubbly and helpful. My main advice is to make comp 110 your hardest class if you have never taken a cs course before (don't take with calc 2). Please go to office hours and do not slack on exercises and you will be great :)

I loved this class! Lots of assignments but they weren't hard and you get extra credit for turning them in early. Easy to do well if you put in some work. I've heard that the other 110 profs are a lot harder, so take it with her if you can!

Took this for PSYC degree requirement. Don't take in full semester. Assignments take a long time and are tedious. Professor is very good at explaining new concepts, but doesn't take the time to elaborate on harder concepts that are necessary for assignments. Overall, good experience for not coding before and not liking it very much.

If you have experience in Python, this class will be a breeze. Attendance is not required, and all the content is posted online, so missing lectures is not a big deal. For new coders, it's a great class if you are genuinely interested in learning the basics of coding, and Alyssa is a great professor for it. The class does have quite a bit of work.

Class was well designed through the site. Difficult if you have zero coding experience but that's expected in this course. Office hours will be your messiah with the coding assignments. You can essentially spend 3ish hours there and be done with the coding assignment for the week (this was me with 0 coding experience). Wonderful and caring prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Alyssas was generally a very nice person and cared about the success of all her students. I will say that the class is pretty hard for beginners with no experience as the class makes you spend a lot of time alone learning by yourself. Nevertheless, she was amazing and gave us many extensions and the grading policy was very fair.

Professor Byrnes was very kind and warm in the lecture. I never had a day where I dragged my feet getting to her class. I believe that with a small amount of programming experience, the class will be fairly straightforward but I know a lot of people without any experience getting overwhelmed. If this is you, go to office hours whenever you can.

As someone with no coding experience, the class was challenging. Lectures only introduced you to the exercises (homework) and then a lot of it was on your own IF you did not use all the resources. Tutoring is helpful so utilize it. The difficulty of the exercises set you up well for the final exam. She is considerate of her grade weightage.

Amazing teacher! Genuinely wants everyone to succeed. All materials are easily accessible, including recorded lectures. TA office hours are very helpful and offered at a wide range of times. I had previous CS experience so I didn't find the material very challenging, but new coders also didn't seem to struggle too much.

Solid professor. Mainly graded on exercises and quizzes. The office hours and help sessions are easy to access. Exercises often take a while, so get started ahead of time. Memory diagrams are also a heavy concept. Practice problems are available.

Alyssa was a solid professor for COMP 110. Nice grade drops and the quizzes/final weren't bad if you understood the review material and lecture slides. HW exercises were much more difficult then lecture/quizzes and I often required assistance on those. Coming from someone with little/no coding experience. Nice that she posted all class lectures.

I didn't have any coding experience coming in and this class was great. I learned a lot and Alyssa made Python feel easy. The quizzes weren't bad as long as you did the practice problems and exercises, but the exercises were a little confusing sometimes. However, the TAs were pretty helpful and there are tons of resources to help you.

She made this class feel like a breeze and was so caring and made it easy for students to ask lots of questions. The tests and final weren't that bad but the exercises could be difficult. Love that she recorded her lectures so that we could watch them if we couldn't make it to class!

Loved her COMP110 class! She is an awesome professor and is super understanding that some people may not understand the material at all to begin with, so she has many opportunities for extra credit and extra help outside of class to help people. The quizzes and final were not difficult, very similar to the practice questions! Take this class!

Alyssa was a good professor overall, I personally really liked her and I think COMP110 with her was a good intro for me (I had no prior coding experience). I will say I wish we were able to get access to reviews earlier on. I feel like we got access to quiz reviews last minute, but other than that I had a great experience.

Alyssa is a sweetheart. While she was a decent teacher, I feel like this class was easier for people with coding experience(I didn't have any prior coding experience). Figure out how to do memory diagrams early on. The exercises don't coincide with her lessons. Focus on what you learn in class; that's what will be on the quizzes.

Alyssa really did her best with such huge classes and was really accommodating with campus/life events. I didn't get the feeling she was particularly caring one-to-one though, and she and the TAs didn't pay much attention to issues with the live-streamed lecture. Practice super hard with memory diagrams and function writing, and you got the tests!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Met in person on Tuesdays and async on Thursdays. At the beginning of the semester Byrnes made sure to tell everyone that this class can be a 15 hour/week commitment which is definitely overkill. If you pay attention in lectures and do the homework at the beginning of the week you can get everything done and get office hour help if needed.

Alyssa is such a sweet professor! I had no absolutely no coding experience prior to taking this class and I did fine. Definitely go to office hours if you need help on exercises and attend review sessions before the quizzes/final!

This was a great class. Alyssa is so kind and accommodating to your needs. Definitely need to pay attention at the beginning of this course to be able to succeed. It is difficult to understand if you have no coding experience but she simplifies things. Make sure you go to class!
Would take again good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I knew nothing about computer science going into this class, but it's very easy to learn with the assignments. I would suggest going to class and starting the assignments early so you have time to go to office hours. The quizzes are very similar to what you learn in class. Overall not a class meant to trick you.

Alyssa was a wonderful professor: caring and helpful with any questions we had. She did fine explaining most concepts, but I still recommend doing some self study if you don't have prior experience. My only gripe was memories diagrams which don't pertain to actual programming. Overall, the class is very forgiving and it's quite easy to do well in.

With no programming experience I really enjoyed her class! She seemed really passionate. I had to spend some time on the exercises, but I really enjoyed doing it. I would happily take a class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: i had NO programming experience before this class. honestly one of the easiest classes ever. make sure you understand the core logic of this class and exams are a piece of cake. i mean the average for the final was literally an A!!! prof byrnes is so nice and attendance isn't even required. such a great class i totally recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I would recommend this class with Alyssa to anyone. She is great at explaining the material, but there can be a lot of work at times. If you do the homework and the practice during lectures, the quizzes are very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her lectures are pretty good at teaching the material and she is really sweet. The course content is not very difficult but the exercises/hw can take up a lot of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I didn't have programming experience and found the class manageable. It was not easy, but she's very good at explaining things and does her best to prepare you for quizzes. There's no trick questions on quizzes so you always know what to expect. You can only reach her through EdStem and she's a bit sassy sometimes, but I still enjoyed her course!

Alyssa is super sweet and a great prof! I had no prior programming experience, but she put things into terms that were easy to understand. While 110 can be pretty time-consuming (especially for those new to programming), it's not necessarily a difficult class. If you're willing to put in sufficient time and effort, your grade will reflect it.

I will say, I love the teacher. Very sweet and all the TA's and her are accessible via edstem. However, I dont know why everyone thinks this class is so easy. If you have no comp experience, I personally found that the class takes A. LOT. of time. u dont have to study much for quizzes, bc the exercises prepare u but its def a time consuming class

I thought this class was fine, but the professor was extremely difficult to reach out of class. You have to message her on EdStem and then she wants to setup a Zoom meeting when the question can be answered through email. She also has a snarky attitude so be prepared to be humiliated at times.
I thought this class was okay, exercises were very time consuming and more difficult than class. Make sure you understand memory diagrams.
She has very helpful lectures and a lot of TA time slots. This was my first time taking a coding course and it was pretty easy.

As someone with no prior experience coding, I found this class slightly difficult. Exercises were not similar to the lecture material, and can often be time consuming. Exams were easy as long as you pay attention to lecture. Everything is accessible online, even the lectures (no attendance). I never went to office hours but got an A lol. good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Alyssa was a great professor. I will say that what we learn in class is different from assignments and exams. However, her exams are very fair, and each exam (this semester there were 4) was only 10%. The class is effort-based, so as long as you try, you'll do just fine. I think she is also very nice, and overall a class I recommend.

Anyone saying she is easy to access outside of class is incredibly wrong. She does not respond to emails, must message through edstem. Half the responses to questions on edstem are rude. Office hours are basically impossible. Lectures are VERY different from assignments. Tests are full of trick questions. I wish I had this course with someone else.

She is a good professor, but I have never touched coding before in my life, and I was lost. The exercises are a huge jump away from the material we learn in class, but achievable and understandable. Expect to be in office hours a LOT! (recommend 7-11 hours to dedicate a week to this course). Her tests are fair and she is super sweet
Can be somewhat rude and unapproachable at times, but no need to approach her or the TAs much because COMP110 is one of the easiest courses at UNC. Zero excuse to not get an A

Amazing prof. I came in with a small background in CS which could have made the class easier for me (some of my friends are struggling in the class), but I felt Alyssa did a great job explaining the concepts in her lectures and she is very fair with her grading. Allows you to resubmit basically until you get a 100 on your HW. Easy quizzes also.

She is very approachable and very nice. If you think comp110 is very easy you can simply don't show up in class and she public every detail you need on a website. She responses lots of question online and she is very caring. The only down side of her class is probably the fact that it's so popular that the registration is difficult.
Did not explain content well at all and have very inaccesible TA and office hours. Also does not know how to explain content and blasts through content without explain concepts clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Alyssa is so understanding and was quick to help with any issues I had throughout the course. I have had literally zero programming experience and kinda despised CS before her, but I love it now. If you spend time on the work and actually pay attention, you will have no problem, no matter your experience level! Her course is structured to support u
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Alyssa is AMAZING! I was scared to take compsci,never having experience with it, and it seeming too hard to understand as I like to know the reasoning of doing things and understanding how the computer understands code but she prioritizes teaches this and much more, making everything so clear! I might even want to be a CS major because of her.

I had a great time in COMP110 with Alyssa. If you have no coding experience, don't worry, she's great! Also asynchronous Thursdays are the best. Class was easy and clear expectations were laid out with honestly very little work during the week, I always worked way ahead and you actually get extra credit for that too! Can't recommend this more.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had an amazing experience with Alyssa in COMP110! She was always so understanding and was quick to help with any issues I had throughout the course. I have had literally zero programming experience prior to this course, and I did amazing thanks to her and the TAs help!

Alyssa Byrnes was great and very accessible if you had any questions. Comp110/her class is very structured and you get a lot of extra credit opportunities. Definitely use TA office hours to your advantage (esp if stuck on an assignment)! Quizzes were pretty easy if you did the practice available before quiz day. Overall 110 is an easy effort A.

I didn't find her lectures that helpful but her online videos were great and gave you what you needed for the most part to succeed on assignments. Attendance isn't mandatory and everything is recorded.

I had no coding experience and was worried for this class, but it was so great! The class is extremely structured, and if you put in the work, it's easy to do well. Go to office hours, check CampusWire, and put in the time. Exams are not designed to trick, grading criteria is clear, and Dr. Byrnes really cares about her students!

I heard COMP 110 was supposed to be easy but it wasn't what I expected. I think that's also because it's her first time teaching the course. However, the quizzes and final were a little difficult, and you do need to get a good amount of studying if you don't attend the lectures.

i was so scared to take this and felt that there wasn't enough of a transition into learning concepts but it does get sm easier toward the end. worst part was office hours weekly, but it helps. quizzes are ok, final not so much. go to lecture and you'll be ok tbh, alyssa is v sweet, CHECK CAMPUSWIRE IF NOTHING ELSE PLS (extra cred/extensions)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It was slightly annoying how she would do the easiest examples in class and then the tests would be something completely different or way harder and she was just overall unhelpful and didn't really do much.

Alyssa overall was good for Comp 110. I had no coding experience and the course moved slow enough to where I felt it was an easy A. As long as you did the work you would do fine and the tests were on the easier side. I feel I'm rating the course more than the professor because Comp110 will be the same no matter who you have.

At the beginning of the course, she tells us that you don't need any experience with coding to be successful in this class. However, I pity anyone who actually knows nothing about computers or coding because very little teaching is done. Per week, I have spent roughly 10 hours outside of class working on the coding exercises. Thank you Chat GPT.
Good professor, as someone with 0 computer science history she made it easy and accessible to do good. Would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I had no coding experience before this course. I loved everything about this course and professor. Exercises and exams (except the final, which was more tricky) were clear and fair, resources were constantly available, and the structure of the course was great. I really learned so much and I am already set to take another class with her.

I never coded before this class (except a bit over break because I was scared of this class) however, it ended up being VERY manageable. If you're not a fan of exams, this is a forgiving setup where the final ends up being only 10% of the grade. The attention to detail on accessibility and resources is also shocking to see in a stem class.

Comp 110 is an okay class, but there are many major issues with it that make it unpleasant to take. For one, exercises often have nothing to do with what is on exams. The final exam also tested around 10% of all the course material, and was not at all representative of the semester of learning. Overall, a frustrating class-dont take unless required

She's nice and & flexible with the grading rubric as far as giving extra points for turning it in early etc. as everyone else said, but tbh this is not a beginner-friendly class for coding, despite being advertised as that. So if you're not required to take this  class, then don't; exercises take a long time and overall the stress isn't worth it.

She's super nice and wants you to do well. Everythings easy to find and has clear grading criteria. If you turn in work early, you get bonus points. If the overall grade for something is low, she gives extra points to bump it up. I really enjoyed having her, too bad im not good at comp lol.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Byrnes was amazing, this was my first coding class and she made it very accessible. There's lots of TAs and office hour help consistently. The exercises are long but there are unlimited submissions so you have opportunities to do well. The quizzes are not super difficult as long as you do the practice problems and watch the videos.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Good professor, don't learn much in in person lectures but her online videos are very clutch.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This was my first coding class and I absolutely loved it. Professor Byrnes is amazing and the most precious human. You can tell she is passionate about teaching and genuinely wants students to enjoy the class while also learning. I would 100% take her class again. Assignments were time consuming but not bad if you use office hrs!
This class was one of my favorites for my biology major. 99% individual learning, unlimited submissions on exercises, and quiz reviews mirrored the exam structure.

Alyssa was a great lecturer, but comp 110 is very focused on the individual. You do all assignments on your own and see TAs for help in office hours, and videos of lectures are accessible online. Can guarantee your grade with the autograder. Quizzes are just like the quiz reviews. Easy A for someone with 0 coding experience.

Comp110 was such a fun class. Dr. Byrnes was always on top of answering questions/concerns on CampusWire when students asked, and was very flexible with grading based on whether or not everyone understood the content. Gave clear lectures, office hours were super accessible and helpful, cared a lot about her students!

COMP283 is a really tough class but Alyssa did her best in teaching it. She's super nice and wants you to succeed. The textbook isnt mandatory but can help if you get lost with some concepts. Office hours with the TA's will help, and it will be helpfull if you really try to understand the concepts and how to apply them

I absolutely loved Alyssa. She was super sweet and caring. The textbook wasnt required and I dont regret not reading it. Discrete math is obviously a hard subject and you have to put in the work. Alyssa was very fair with grading, gave points back, and wanted everyone to pass the class. Def the best instructor you could take this class with!

If you have to take COMP 283 take it with Alyssa. She is far better than the other options and her class is pretty easy. Just do the work and pay attention in class and you should be good. A lot of work is participation based so just turn it in. Exams are same difficulty as homework too if not easier.

If you have to take COMP 283/MATH 381, take COMP 283 with Alyssa Byrnes. She's young, new, and nervous, and sometimes confuses herself when explaining concepts, but she's so sweet and patient (and very intelligent when it comes down to it). It's definitely not an easy class, but hers is the best option for the credit/material.

She's very participation heavy, which makes sense with an introductory language course. She's always happy to help and offer office hours, extra practice, and support when students ask for it. She's very patient and encouraging, the class is a very welcoming environment.
She was really nice and really made sure the students understood the material. I slacked off pretty bad and failed the first 2 test but she worked with me and I ended up doing ok. Don't fall behind.

I absolutely adore Professor Chambless. She is a fantastic professor. In-class time is typically spent practicing skills, so I would recommend taking time to read/take notes on the assigned textbook pages so the content doesn't sneak up on you for the test. Grades fairly and generously, and always gives clear feedback. Take ITAL 101 with her!

I highly recommend Dr.Chambless for Ital 101 and 102; she is an amazing lecturer and has a lot of empathy towards her students. She grades fairly and provides plenty of feedback, as well as resources, to help you improve your Italian. She is very knowledgeable about the textbook content and is always available to meet with students.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is very friendly and encouraging! Classes have a lot of fun activities to encourage constant learning.  There are short quizzes (vocab or the grammar concept you are learning), but they are easy and only count for 5% of your overall grade. There are also assignments w/each unit to record a conversation about a certain topic with a partner.
Highly recommend Dr. Chambless for any italian course at unc! Great lecturer, very friendly, and very caring

She is very well-organized and supplies a lot of resources to help you practice and understand the material. She also is a very fair grader and truly cares about her students. Participation is a super important part of the class but you definitely don't have to be perfect at the grammar construction or the pronunciation.

This was ITAL 300 not 203, but Professor Chambless is simply an amazing professor. Super kind and accommodating. There were 4 tests, a group project, and a final along with homework and participation. Definitely take Italian at any level with her if you can

Professor Chambless is an outstanding Italian professor. She makes learning a language fun and engaging! You focus on speaking and listening in class, and reading and writing on the homework.Your expereince in the class is very dependent on your partner (who you sit beside in the class). If you pick a good partner, you'll have a blast in her class!
The sweetest woman ever.
Genuinely just the sweetest, cutest woman ever. Such a great teacher! Adore her.

Amy is a wonderful teacher! She is so kind and caring. Something I love about UNC language classes is that the teachers just really want you to love the language as much as they do. I can say that by the end of this semester, I learned a lot and have more motivation to learn more about Italian culture and language.

Professor Chambless is genuinely so kind and patient with students. She's super flexible and understanding when it comes to grading and due dates. She's very encouraging and uplifting. I would recommend her for everyone but especially people who feel like they struggle in language classes. Love her!

Professor Chambless is amazing! Super nice and accessible outside of class, grading criteria is clear, and provides tons of useful resources to study for tests. Classes are mostly spent practicing in groups, so attendance is mandatory. Read the textbook and study and you'll ace her class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amy is such a good prof! She was super helpful and easily accessible for office hours or after class. She would quite literally tell us what would be on the exams, which was very helpful. The class itself is similar to 101 and 102, but she focuses more on culture than exam prep in class. Overall I would recommend and would take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Gives good feedback--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Sometimes professors have it out for you, that was my case. I will never take a class she teaches ever again. She gave lots of ways to learn though. I had a lot of test anxiety, I told her with each test I would have to leave and use the restroom (yay IBS) and I guess this made her so suspicious that she never treated me fairly again

Prof. Chambless is so nice! She is completely understanding that we are obviously not going to be near fluent in a beginners class (which isn't as common as you would think) and encourages you to just do the best you can. You get so many grades in this class that even if you bomb a test you still have a good chance of getting an A. 10/10 recommend

I absolutely love Professor Chambless! She makes learning a language so much easier and has so much knowledge that she wants to share with her students. She gives back lots of feedback on assignments so you know what you did right and wrong, but is not a harsh grader. I would take a class with her if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Chambless continues to be one of, if not my favorite professor at UNC. She's literally a dream professor. She's fair in her grading, and creates a great and respectful learning environment, which is important in a subject such as learning a new language. Could not recommend her more!!

Amy Chambless is an amazing professor and one of the best I've ever had! She is extremely approachable and very friendly. Her ability to teach students language is excellent and is no doubt derived from the above qualities. She really cares about her students success and gives ample opportunity to excel. Simply eccezionale!

Prof. Chambless is very helpful and encouraging in class. She is super nice and cares about her students. In my experience, quizzes are always easier than I expect them to be and the midterm was fairly easy as well. There are a reasonable amount of homework grades (including 3 oral grades) and you are graded on participation.
She's a great teacher, taught the material very well and she's a very nice lady. Would recommend her 10000x over.

She is extremely clear during lectures and has no problem with helping you on an individual basis during office hours or after class. She encourages everyone to participate during class. She pretty much tells you what will be on your tests and quizzes, and is very clear in what she expects for an writing done. Would definitely take again.

I don't do well with languages, but she is incredibly supportive and works to help you. She clearly explains the material and provides enough work to solidify it. Her lectures are very clear, and she is a honest but forgiving grader. There was a lot of group interaction. She even graded my final after I finished it so she could go over it with me.

Took the class in Fall of 2025. Class was TA-graded, but Dr. Cooper structures it well and doesn't set expectations terribly high. Show up, follow along, and you're in a solid spot to get a good grade. Course was mainly surface-level, though definitely more covered than your typical person would know. Lectures weren't boring or overly interesting.
Take her class! She's amazing and so chill. Dr. Cooper genuinely cares about her studnets, and it's so refreshing.

Lectures are a little boring. 3 essays and 2 exams (also essays) are graded by TA generously. Can learn a lot about academic writing from this course. Dr. Cooper is helpful with essays and arranges the course carefully (in Canvas). Only issue: she's from Duke
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper is an amazing lecturer! Though some lecture topics were not as interesting as others, overall, her style of teaching is really nice. Only drawback was the TA grading which was pretty harsh (at least for my TA). Felt they were too difficult considering it was just a gen-ed class. Otherwise, I'd recommend!

Mandy Cooper was an excellent professor. While some of her lectures were a miss, most were interesting. Everything was good, except for the TA, who graded every essay pretty harshly, in my opinion. There were multiple readings, but they were interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cooper is super nice and caring. Lectures were very hit or miss imo; some were super interesting, and others felt like a chore. Lots of writing but graded pretty easily (may have been specific to my TA). No tests at all and offers a ton of extra credit; pretty easy A overall, but there are definitely more interesting gen-ed history classes.

As a person, Professor Cooper is amazing. She truly cares about us as students, even in a large class. The way she set up the midterm and final was great. However, my TA who graded all my essays was unfair and difficult in grading considering it's a gen-ed. The lectures also weren't the most engaging although she is very passionate about her work.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved this class and it was pretty interesting most of the time. Dr. Cooper is very passionate about what she teaches, making the class great. There were a few essays, which I found to be a little harshly graded by my TA, but overall I enjoyed the class and totally recommend!

This class is great easy gen-ed to take. 5 essays throughout the semester that make up most of the grade, which are graded by the same TA. Gives opportunities for extra credit and different opportunities to earn your participation grade. Dr. Cooper was passionate, knowledgeable, and very willing to work with students.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class! As someone who loves history her lectures were very engaging and she often kept things light and easy to understand. Assignments weren't bad at all and she offers a lot of extra credit. Great Professor.

The lectures could get a little long, esp if you're familiar with US history already, but Dr. Cooper was super cool and knowledgable, regardless. Her assignments are very clear, but you are being graded by a TA who can be inconsistent and give little feedback due to the volume of papers. office hours and the writing center can help you do well!

Professor Cooper is a great instructor, and the class is very manageable. Most assignments are papers, and she gives plenty of time to complete them. Your grade can depend on your grader, since some are stricter than others. Still, her lectures are engaging, and you learn a lot in the course.

Dr. Cooper is very knowledgable! She is passionate about what she teaches and is easy to talk to and encourages group discussions. Your TA will be grading everything so I would say to make sure to go to both their office hours as well as Dr.Cooper's if you feel like you should have had higher scoring/asking how to improve for future assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Love her, great lecturer and very knowledgable of class material. HOWEVER, your grade will entirely rely on who your TA is. I am averaging a B in this class, while my friends with other TAs are getting As. Don't be afraid to go speak to her about problems you are having, very kind, very understanding. W
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper is knowledgeable and very passionate about the material she teaches. Do the reading and participate in lectures, and you will do great in the class. I have been to her office hours and she is very approachable and always willing to work with students. I wish I could take more classes with her, she is amazing!

Super fun guy with interesting lectures. You get 3 unexcused absences and my notes were just the slides copied down. didnt read the textbook and did fine. make sure to study for quizzes because if you bomb one you have to do really well on the midterm/final. He curves well though. Try to speak at least once every class as participation matters.

Attendance required, note taking required to do well, slides are posted tho, curved midterm and final (generous 10ish points) so that one person just did really bad, just talk in class and study, its a easy and interesting class

I really liked Professor Gebremichael's lectures and the group discussions! If you aren't comfortable speaking in front of the class, you may not score well in participation though. The material is very interesting and he often incorporated current politics into class. The exams were difficult but curved very generously (15% curve on the midterm).

Prof Gebremichael is extremely strict in attendance and participation, which altogether count as 25% of the total grades. He is also really strict in marking, not giving curves, and is not really helpful when you ask him about how to participate more in class. Would not recommend taking his course at all.

Professor Gebremichael was awesome. I had him for my African American Economics and Inequality FYS, and he had great content, excellent and funny lectures, and was an overall great professor. His grading is stricter for the final presentation and paper, but he gives you more than enough notice to complete them well in advance.

I enjoyed Prof. AG's sense of humor and how much he cared about our individual opinions in class discussions. Compared to other poli prof.'s, he is definitely more difficult. The class is graded on 3 five questions quizzes, a midterm, and the final. If you don't do well on all of the quizzes, it'll be very difficult to get your grade up. He curves!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Gebremichael is down to earth and engaging during his lectures. We had very interesting discussions and his quizzes were super easy. Don't underestimate the tests though, they are pretty hard and have a detailed written portion. The exams were based on the lectures, so I never did the reading and did just fine. Definitely take this class!

Angela is one of the best Spanish professors that I have ever had. She is an extremely fair grader but also provides good feedback. She made each class fun and not boring, even when using slides to teach. She is hilarious and always made class feel like a welcoming place, and she gives you lots of practice to prepare you for the tests and final.
