Said it was her first semester teaching and it kinf of showed. Good class overall and really learned a lot but it was a bit disorganized at times. Gave a lot of time in class to work on projects. It was online so not my most memorable but Val made UX easy and seems like shed have good connections if you want to go into that field.

Dr. Kalleberg is the goat. He is an expert in his field, very laid back, and a very caring guy. Absolutely take his class if you can. Do what he asks, which is not overwhelming, and you will succeed. 5/5 class and 5/5 prof.

Dr. Kalleberg is the goat. He is a caring guy and is very knowledgeable in sociology. He is an expert in the field and very well respected around campus and nationwide. If you can take a class with him, jump on it. Do what is asked, which is not much, and you will make an A. 5/5 class.
Legendary professor, readings were very short and content was pretty slight. Lectures were fun and interesting and overall just a cool guy.

I LOVE ARNE. Would regularly drag myself out of bed only to see him. Love his cutie NY accent, made me feel like I was back home. Content was easy. Lectures were not super heavy. He's just a sweetheart and I love him.

Was a decent lecturer. Course content was pretty simple and easy to understand. Multiple short readings, but not too much to handle. Laughed when a student asked about extra credit... but overall was alright.

Professor Kalleberg is wonderful! The lectures are entertaining and are also engaging. No tests or quizzes, just short papers weekly/biweekly in which you must recall the required readings (which were short). No final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Class was interesting and engaging, and super easy. If you're not doing well you're not trying. He mostly stands out for how he is as a person! He really cares about his students and makes an effort to know everyone. He's not the most tech savvy, so we spent a lot of classes with him on the phone with its, but we laughed it off! HIGHLY recommend
Dr. Kallegberg is the funniest professor on campus, and he makes class entertaining! As long as you do the work you will get an A!

I took Dr. Kalleberg's FYS about happiness, and it was a great experience! He's a funny guy and he cares about his students. Also, the class wasn't difficult - as long as you're a decent writer and you do all the assignments, his class will be fun and fairly easy!

Love ashu!! Very willing to help outside of class, lots of jokes throughout lecture to keep us engaged, and lots of step by step help to make sure we are really following what we are doing! TAs were great as well. Loved the treats ashu brought in (though wish we got to try his brownie recipe). If you can take a Class with ashu, do it!
TA Laraib Kamal has anger issues.

Professor Ashu is an amazing. He's incredibly engaging, bakes cookies for his students, is clearly passionate about the material, and makes his expectations/what we need to know for exams very clear. If you attend the lectures, utilize your recitation TA's and their office hours, and take good notes you won't have a problem in this class!

Ashu is super nice—he brought us cookies/cupcakes and even gifts when he traveled for research. The class itself isn't super hard, and the curves were also really generous. As long as you come to the class, do the problem sets, and attend review sessions, you will do fine. Favorite class & professor—definitely + highly recommended!!!

Professor Ashu is a really caring professor (he baked us treats often and got us gifts when he travelled)! He doesn't provide powerpoints for his class, so attending his classes would be really helpful. And the exams are hard and he's tough grader, but his exam grades and the overall grades are curved generously, so it's not too bad.

Ashu is one of my favorite profs I've ever had at UNC. He is so funny even when he isn't trying to be and that makes lectures fun even if the material isn't always. He's a great teacher and always willing to meet for office hours. 100% take any class you can find with him. I think he's also a secret genius

Ashu is the best and most hilarious Statistics professor you could possibly have, and he is very good at explaining complex concepts. He goes out of his way to help with the problem sets and gives us answers to pop quizzes. The tests are hard, but his curve helps. If you have to take PLCY 460, Ashu is your best bet.

Ashu is such a great professor, if you have to take PLCY460 I would only recommend taking it with him! He jokes around in class and makes it super casual. Also walks you through almost every homework assignment. The class content itself is difficult but you get plenty of support and the exam curves are generous.

I was dreading this class for 2 years, and finally took it and it was the only class I enjoyed going to, thanks to Ashu. Most of class time was spent talking about food or other random things. He gives you the answers for the quizzes and problem sets.

Okay, Ashu is truly one of my favorite professors I've ever had. He is hilarious and makes the class feel so welcoming and open, but he's also extremely good at explaining the material, which can be challenging. It's not a lot of math but the concepts are a bit complex. He moves at a good speed and answers questions well. HIGHLY recommend.

Ashton Rooney encourages students to participate in Spanish, and he grew my confidence. He doesn't care if you aren't proficient, as long as you try. He is lenient with grading, even though he does have to follow the Span 203 grading guidelines. His class is engaging, fun, and educational. If you are nervous to take Span 203, definitely take his.

I came into this class super scared because I hadn't taken Spanish since my freshman year of high school. However, Ashton made it such a supportive and fun environment, and I ended up doing great on all the exams, essays, etc., because he focused on building our confidence.

One of the best profs I've had. He genuinely cares and doesn't expect perfection, just effort. I hadn't taken Spanish in four years, but Ashton helped us learn and stay engaged. He doesn't control the class structure, but he makes the most of it. The tests are tough. Prep and do VHL early. I am not the best at Spanish and still managed an A-.

Professor Arbuckle is super nice and approachable. The class is very interesting and the homework is minimal. Attendance isn't required, but it'll be helpful to have someone to explain the slides to you. Fun and easy class!

Amazing class!! Professor Arbuckle is so nice and caring. He is accessible at all times of the day and often answers emails very quickly. He answers any and all questions. Professor Arbuckle's lectures are very interesting and sometimes showed images about his archaeology experience which was incredible to see first hand.

Minimal feedback given throughout the class, didn't grade any assignment until the day before grades were due. Very unclear final essay rubric and if you don't write in the exact style he is looking for, you will not do well. But you wouldn't know what that style is, because he doesn't grade anything or give feedback throughout the class.

Best class ever! There were no midterms or finals. One 5 page paper in the middle of the semester, but not difficult if you don't leave it to the last minute. Professor Arbuckle is understanding and kind. While his lectures were not required, they were very interesting and worth your time to attend. Would 100% take a class with Arbuckle again.

kind, very interesting, understanding prof. easy A. 1 paper due in the middle of the year making it possible to actually be interested in the content. you get downgraded if you use AI but are given the (optional) chance to revise the paper at the end of the sem. this was good incentive to be more ambitious with the work resulting in an A.
One of the best professors I have had here. He is so kind and knowledgeable about archeology. He is so passionate in his lectures that they are absorbing.

Joke of a class. Took online during maymester. Got the 2 weeks of work done very quickly and very ahead of time. Never knew what grade I got on the final paper, but I got a 100 in absolutely everything else, and finished with an A. Watch the lectures on 2x speed, if you even decide to watch them. Super easy quizzes and super low stress final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far one of the best professors I've ever had. He's extremely knowledgeable about the subject matter and a great lecturer. He also wants us to learn and engage rather than stress about grades.
One of the best teachers I've ever had, he's understanding, an interesting lecturer, and actually wanted us to learn and engage rather than stress over grades.

Professor Arbuckle's class was very interesting! There were two short, easy assignments each week and no readings. There was one fascinating paper that counted as both the midterm and final. I enjoyed the lectures and personal stories Professor Arbuckle shared from his archaeological finds. Great class, highly recommend!
love this man. great professor. very knowledgeable. wants all of his students to succeed and really values what students can/want to contribute to discussions. highly recommend.

Love this class/prof! Very aware that students generally hate abstract theory classes and makes the material as approachable as possible. Lectures like its standup - very easy to pay attention. Lots of assignments that feel like busy work, but I probably wouldn't do the readings otherwise so that might be a good thing. Highly recommend this class!

Prof Arbuckle is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. He is incredibly flexible and genuinely loves the material he teaches. He is fantastic and you need to take him at least once during your time at Carolina. This was a study abroad course so we had assignments every day but they were engaging and not too bad.

Dr. Arbuckle is a gem in UNC's anthropology department. He is kind, caring, and so passionate about the material. We covered a lot in this class, but he effectively broke the material down into easily digestible pieces. Professor Arbuckle worked very hard to make our classroom a safe, positive space and he 100% achieved this. Highly recommend!!!

I am taking this class during the Maymester. The class is online but professor Arbuckle is very engaging. I was nervous of the intensity of a Maymester, but it has been great. He is the best lecturer ever and has very detailed powerpoints so you are never bored. He is the most hilarious and caring professor ever + he is a Swiftie. Highly recommend!
I absolutely loved this class!!! Benjamin Arbuckle is amazing. Very clear guidelines and assignments so it's very attainable to get an A in the class. I literally recommend this to every person ever!

His lectures were funny and interesting. Assignments were simple, weekly quizzes or activities you could easily complete as long as you came to class and did the readings. Slides available online. Final project was a research paper and lightning presentation on a discovery of your choosing, which was super fun. Highly recommend him.
Absolutely spectacular. He is very personable and kind, and his lectures and readings are very informative and interesting. Best professor of my undergradate at UNC.
One of the best professors I have ever had. Super caring and energetic, really passionate about the subject. Definitely recommend.

One of the kindest people I've ever met. Grades were largely based off of regular homework assignments (reading plus written response). You can tell he really loves the content and wants his students to succeed. No tests! He does get rambley and runs out of time in his lectures, but he's a really sympathetic guy and very nice grader. I'd recommend.

Prof Arbuckle is very entertaining. His lectures were very immersive. Weekly quiz on content for the week and a written assignment covering the topic for the week. 1 paper on your choice of topic. Very doable load to handle. Great guy, great class. What are you still thinking about? Take it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Arbuckle is wonderful at teaching theory in an approachable and engaging way! There are no papers except for a 5pg final + presentation. Short assignments throughout the semester. Kinda seminar style. Very manageable workload and great delivery of the content. Relatively easy A but you learn a lot.

I've never written a review for a prof before, but felt inclined to for professor arbuckle. He's awesome, super knowledgable on the topics and really understanding and helpful when students come to him with things. Def take a class with him if you get the chance.

I enjoyed this class a lot. Dr. Arbuckle is very passionate about the class and the discoveries, which makes the class more interesting. Took the class for a gen ed but I would take it again. Highly recommend.

Professor Arbuckle is a very understanding and caring professor. He makes topics that would be otherwise dull rather interesting. There are few assignments and no formal final exam, but rather a final recorded presentation. I would highly recommend you take a class with him if you get the opportunity!

Cannot recommend this class enough. Easy weekly quizzes and assignments that maybe take 10 minutes combined. There is a 3-5 page paper and an online presentation but the topics were really interesting and super easy to write about. 12/10 take this class

ANTH 149 is the easiest WB credit at UNC. Grades are determined by a 4-page paper, 5-minute online presentations, participation as well as an assignment and short quiz each week. Dr. Arbuckle is a great guy whose very knowledgeable about the topics and researches frequently. His lectures are interesting and funny, can't recommend him enough!
Extremely nice. 1 assignment and 1 five question ONLINE quiz per week but both took almost no time and could finish both in 10 mins. He is nice and accommodating.

Arbuckle was probably my kindest teacher this semester at UNC, and this class was definitely helpful when I was struggling with my others. He is super communicative if you are having any mental health issues and is usually happy to excuse absences or extend deadlines. Most assignments are also pretty straightforward and easy to receive full credit.

Arbuckle is so funny! He genuinely cares about his students and loves when students make the material exciting. He is quirky and a little awkward but it makes him relatable and fun. He is also very understanding. He turned what could have been dull and uninteresting material into a fun and lively class. I would absolutely take him again.

Arbuckle is my favorite professor in my 3rd semester at UNC. He cares about us understanding the course content and hes really funny and down to earth in the process. Hes been super accommodating during this covid semester and its been such an anxiety relief for me. HIGHLY recommend
Dr. Arbuckle is a nice guy, but his class is not very interesting. I think if you want an easy class, not-challenging, sign up for Arbuckle.

This class relies on a lot of reading and writing, but Arbuckle is super helpful and passionate about the subject, which makes it easier. He also doesnt expect you to have any prior knowledge and encourages different interpretations and questions. The most flexible and understanding professor during covid - love this guy!

For a 200 level anthropology course it required too much. If you enjoy writing and are good at it then you'll do great! But he grades pretty harshly on the big assignments. You can revise the essays but sometimes this means fixing all/half your paper. Also, he's pretty disorganized. Great person though, very sweet. Just not the best professor

I don't know how to rate this class because Ben is very caring/accommodating especially if you need some extra time on an assignment, but he's a bit scatter-brained and the class feels disorganized. He grades harshly so you do revisions but this essentially doubles your workload. He's a funny, lively person, but not my favorite professor.
Literally the easiest class I have taken at UNC. As a STEM major, I had no background in this but I enjoyed his lectures. He is an easy grader as well. Definitely recommend.

Professor Arbuckle is an amazing prof. His exams are 99% from the lecture slides that he posts. Just show up to class, somewhat listen, & you're already half-way done studying for the exam (which are non-cumulative, at least when he taught our class). One very minor problem is that he talks a bit much to the point it may seem overwhelming.
He's a real chill guy. I would just hate how much he'd talk in lecture because then you feel like you missed a whole 1000 years of archaeology in 5 minutes. But it's not a difficult class.

I LOVED Professor Arbuckle. I had him for a FYS, so the class wasn't too demanding which was nice, but I still learned a lot. The class had a summary paper due almost every class and each class we discussed the articles in a very fun way. My favorite class my first year! I plan on taking another one of his classes. :)

He is amazing!!! I took this class because I wanted an FYS, and this one seemed pretty interesting and I had read good reviews about him. He is my favorite professor so far. Every class we just had opinionated discussions (participation matters) about the readings from the night before. No exams or tests. He is very willing to change the syllabus.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Arbuckle is the man! His lectures are more like story-time, and he usually throws in humor now and then to spice things up. Exams are based solely off his lectures and are very straight-forward. A super easy A, just show up, be entertained, and do the study guide.

Sitting in on Arbuckle's lectures is like story time for the class.  His enthusiasm and excitement for teaching the material rubs off on you, and this is being written by a science major & minor student.  Exams are easy to study for as long as you put in effort the night before or so & listen to the lectures generally.  GREAT class for gened reqs!

Dr. Arbuckle has been my favorite professor so far at UNC. He was accessible outside of class, caring, and gave great feedback on my writing. The readings and one page summaries due every class were a pain but you get used to them. We had some great discussions about the weirdest animal topics and even life which always kept the class interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: My favorite professor as a freshman at UNC. Arbuckle cares about his students and always is open to opinions about his class and things in general. Class is interesting, summaries from readings due each class which isn't the best but definitely manageable. Very friendly, funny and flexible with deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Arbuckle is a super genuine guy and his class is definitely worth taking. Other than short readings and a one page summary due every class, it is really easy and discussions can be really fun. I'm a chem major but his class helped me have a great transition into Chapel Hill.

Funny, nice guy. Gives clear lectures and does not over-complicate things. Five assignments based on relatively short readings. One midterm and a final. Tests are entirely based on what he says in lecture. Although archaeology is not my area of study, I found this class to be relevant and interesting. Worth your time if you need an ANTH credit.

I love Professor Arbuckle! He's so much fun and makes the class really interesting. He's dedicated to the subject matter and often talks about research he has done. I don't think I went a single class without laughing at something he did or said. You have to read articles and write 1-page summaries on them but its not too bad! Love this guy!

Benjamin is a baller. He is so good at archaeology and makes his lectures super easy to understand. The class is stupid easy, but it's so interesting that you WANT to pay attention. The tests are ridiculously easy, and he's just a really cool guy. 10/10 would recommend to anyone to meet this guy and take this class.

Professor Arbuckle is very straightforward with his class policies and expectations. As long as you go to class, do the minimal amount of homework, and study for the tests it should be an easy A.  He is very passionate about archaeology and makes little jokes to make lecture more interesting. Would always recommend this class!

This guy is my favorite teacher.  He's really funny, helpful, and clearly passionate about the subject.  You have to write one page summaries for every class but they're not that bad and he is very fair.  10/10 would take again.

A solid choice for 521. Final was hard but he curved it and has a generous grading scale. Soft spoken lecturer but his lectures are organized and his handwriting is really clear for a math prof. Read the textbook and prepare to study.
Very nice. Not a great professor to teach lower level math, he expects a lot from you and does not explain clearly. You'll need to learn a lot on your own.
He does not reply to email. He will tell you he will respond within 24 hours on Piazza but he doesn't. Does not submit grades on time.

Prof Assani cares about his students. His lectures make 521 like learning a new way of thinking. Go to office hours and ask for help, he wants you to succeed, so he will help. My sole complaint was the disparity in difficulty between this year's final and the material we had seen all semester/last year's final, but he does challenge you to think.
GOAT of a professor. Super awesome guy and really cares about the material and about his students. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! He will help you. Super great guy, really recommend.

I would like to preface this by saying I am a math major, so hopefully this review strikes your perspective more than the negativity I've seen for Assani. Assani is genuinely one of the best math professors: he's funny, very helpful in office hours, and makes sure you understand the concepts that are going on- all you have to do is ask for help.

While professor seems knowledgeable, accent creates understanding challenges. Classroom experience feels scattered, making learning difficult. Tests feel overwhelming compared to material covered. Tech problems slow us down. May want to explore other section options.

Communication barriers due to accent significantly impact lecture comprehension. Course lacks structured organization and clear learning objectives. Assessment difficulty exceeds course level. Recurring technical difficulties with course materials affect learning experience. Alternative instructor recommended.

AVOID! Professor's heavy accent makes lectures incomprehensible. Teaching style is completely chaotic with zero organization. Exams are impossibly difficult and seem designed for failure. Can't handle basic technology - constant issues with uploads and course materials. Save your GPA and sanity - pick another professor!

Dr. Assani was a good professor. The material is obviously not straightforward but his exams generally were right out of class. I felt I learned a lot and was not too overwhelmed so I recommend Dr. Assani.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I could not understand him or/and the course material for the life of me.

Prof. Assani is definitely one of the best professors I've ever had. His philosophy is that learning MATH 521 is like learning a new language, so he really cares about you learning the material well. He answers questions thoroughly and patiently, and lectures are super engaging. 521 is difficult but you absolutely should take it with Assani.

Don't be afraid of Assani, he is nicer than you think. Attendance isn't mandatory but good luck keeping up if you don't attend. Homework was due weekly on friday and group quizzes on Saturday - timing sucks but often nicer than in the middle of the week. Start HW early and attend office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Math 521 is hard no matter what professor you get. Assani is nice, his office hours are helpful, and his TA graded super fast. Exams were fair, homework was due every friday, and group quizzes were due on Saturdays. Definitely start homeworks early. Overall good class.

Assani was one of the best professors I've ever had. He was hilarious and kind and I looked forward to going to class every day. His lectures are a little bit hard to follow sometimes, but he answers every question very patiently and never makes you feel stupid for not understanding. I felt like he wanted me to learn and understand the material.

Assani was one of the best professors I've ever had. He was hilarious and kind and I looked forward to going to class every day. His lectures are a little bit hard to follow sometimes, but he answers every question very patiently and never makes you feel stupid for not understanding. I felt like he wanted me to learn and understand the material.

Couldn't understand a word he said. He has a fairly heavy accent but that was not even the problem. He was practically whispering and no one is the class could hear him. When asked to speak up he straight up said no. I dropped the class and switched to a diff prof for 521 and am so glad. From the days I was there his teaching was all over the place

The most lovely man, extremely intelligent, like the smartest person I've ever met (and probably will ever meet). 521 is a super hard class that I struggled a lot in but he was so kind and really did everything to help me understand during office hours.

521 is a very hard class in general, but Assani does his best to make it better. Weekly group quizzes that he offers a lot of help on, and exams are hard but manageable. The smartest person you'll ever meet, and answers every question superbly, but has a french accent so it may be hard to understand. Overall, the best prof. for 521 (15 pt. grading)

Dr. Assani is a truly caring professor. Truly. Unfortunately he's also very hard to understand and very bad with technology. very. When he forgot to share his screen in say a Monday class with the students on zoom, he would simply give the exact same lecture again on Wednesday instead of re-recording outside of class. A bit of a waste of time.

Dr. Assani is a good person and linear algebra shouldn't be a hard class, but yet he makes it difficult by flying through lectures while just reading the guided notes, saying "you guys understand this" when we don't. He also made us do homework on content that we didn't cover in class while not providing clear explanations. Tests weren't hard.

Assani is the worst professor I have ever seen. He never replies to your emails. You can never understand what he is talking about. Taking his class means that you will spend your whole time on YouTube channels, or you will learn nothing. His course syllabus is unclear that you have no idea what your grade will be until the last second.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Please take Calc 3 with any other professor.
Worst teacher I've had at UNC
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Assani's lectures were a bit hard to follow but doable if you pay attention. You really need to read the textbook beforehand to get much from the lectures. His 3 tests were fairly straightforward - just testing for understanding, and plus, he gives partial credit if you set up the problem correctly. A decent professor for calc 3.

Dr. Assan is difficult to understand, and his lectures are even harder to follow. I learned almost all the material through youtube videos or through recitation sessions which were extremely helpful. However the worst part of the class are the exams. Take another instructor if you want a less stressful time while learning more.

Dr. Assani was a very caring professor who makes analysis approachable. His lectures are some of the best I have experienced in the math department, focusing on intuition and applications rather than the minute details of proofs. His exams are very fair; if you do the homeworks and know the definitions and theorems, you will have no problems.

Professor Assani is the most funny and caring math professor that I've had at UNC. He really loves to see progress, and his grading policy reflects that. As long as you pay attention during lecture, read the textbook, and carefully do the homework, it's not too hard to get a good grade. My favorite part was getting carried on the group quizzes.

Getting a good grade with Assani is straightforward, since there's no curve. But, you have to work hard; he demands rigor, and brainless memorization isn't going to cut it. 521 is heavy on tests, but if you pay attention at class and come to office hours when necessary, he will set you up for success. Also, he really cares about his students!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a really nice guy who wants you to succeed. He's my favorite math professor I've had at UNC so far. Analysis is a hard subject no matter who you do it with, but Assani made it pretty approachable. One thing that is annoying are group quizzes because most likely 1 person will end up doing all the work because the other people are useless.

Dr. Assani is honestly a very good choice for this class. By nature, you will need to read the textbook and do practice problems around 5 hours a week to do well on the exams. For example studying, focus your practice on the quiz and homework problems first, then supplement a lot with problems from the book. Good luck! (The class is hard)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Probably the most difficult and frustrating material I have ever come across, but if you need 521 take Assani. He understands most of his students are required to be in the class and he can be quite entertaining during lectures. His handwriting is sub-par, but that is a small price to pay for a prof like him. I'd take many more classes with him.

One of the most caring and accessible teachers in the department! Super funny and nice, loves answering questions in a way that makes you think, and always listened to my frustrations. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS, even if you don't have questions he often goes over problems in a way that helps with quizzes and homework. Knew my name since day 1!

I LOVE THIS MAN. The class is definitely the hardest I have ever had to work, but he genuinely cares so much about his students (and he can be quite funny). Online classes aren't ideal, but if you need to take 521 or need a professor to follow take Assani you won't regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Math 521 is a hard course and Assani knows it is mandatory for most students. That's why he structures his exams so if you come to class and do the hw you will pass. He makes you work for an A but a B is achievable if you do the work. Online was rough but go to office hours. He wants to help you do as well as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His exams are okay and pretty straight forward and he gives group quizzes. Maybe not the best online teacher; he has a bit of a French accent and his handwriting is hard to read. A little unresponsive on email/difficult to get a hold of and forgets things frequently. He does care that you do well. Don't skip class.

Dr. Assani is without a doubt the kindest professor Ive ever had. He really cares about you. The tests are hard but not too hard. One thing, dont expect a big curve. I thought itd be curved heavily but it really wasnt, only like 3-5 points on the final grade. Either way, a good choice for analysis.

Professor Assani is very funny and a great lecturer, certainly more engaging than a lot of other members of the mathematics faculty. However, Math 521 is a hard class, no matter who you take it with, and you certainly have to work very hard to get an A. If you work kinda hard, as in, do all the homeworks well but don't study much, you'll get a B-.

Very intelligent, but sometimes gets too engaged in his lectures and makes him impossible to follow along with. Nice guy, but isn't the best help with questions. 75 percent of the grade is midterms/final, so if you don't test well I wouldn't recommend him. Would do a quiz a week in groups based off each weeks material, whether we knew it or not.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Everyone agrees that Prof Assani is well-respected, engaging, and a great lecturer. However, unlike most math professors, his style is actually better for those who are NOT naturals at math. For those who understand math easily and prefer to apply concepts creatively, be warned that he rewards memorization of theorems and problems from class.

Dr. Assani is an amazing professor. His lectures in Math 231H were always engaging and entertaining, albeit quite difficult. His midterm exams vary in difficulty, from being very straightforward to so difficult that nobody in the class can solve more than half the questions. The final course grade shocked many students and were lower than estimates

Dr. Assani, without a doubt, gives the best and most engaging Mathematics lectures I have attended at this school. He knows his stuff and it is evident in his answers to questions. This class can be tough, but Assani comes recommended if you need to take 521. Very fair grader. If you work hard you will get an A.
Nice guy. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Assani was a good teacher because to be a good teacher you not only have to teach the material in an absorbable and organized way but you have to make your students believe in themselves. He did both. This class however is not for the faint of heart. If you are not ready to review your notes after every class, then don't take it.
He's a great teacher, and expects you to put a lot of work into his class. ThE PyRaMiD iS sTrOnG with this one
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Assani is cool he draws pictures for us. Take him if you like descriptive pictures of uniform convergence.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor and math advisor.  Teaches hard classes, but a clear lecturer.

Beware, Assani will not answer questions, claiming that there is not enough time left in class. He will also ask if anyone has questions before the weekly group quiz, and instead of answering the question he will put it on the quiz that is graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Expect to put a lot of outside effort in for this class. Lectures are rushed through on Tuesday and quizzes on recently learned material are given on Thursday. Have a question? Don't expect a good explanation. It's also difficult knowing what to expect on exams, hit or miss. I'd recommend you take another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Assani is incredibly intelligent. You'll understand that after hearing his first lecture. But not all intelligent people are great professors. Professor Assani rushes through tons of materials in one lecture each week, leaving the other day purely for quizzes. You'll more than likely be relying on online resources to learn the material.

This course was HARD with Assani. He definitely made you work for any grade above a C. I think had I worked harder, I would have done better, but just to get an A- on an exam required 20+ hours of studying on my part. I love math, but this class was no joke. If you work VERY hard, you should be ok.
Hard to understand his lectures and he goes way too fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Dr. Assani is brilliant and made time for me when I really sought him out. He definitely kicked our butts by putting really hard versions of concepts on the exams. However, on our standardized final, I did really well because he made me work hard. I am definitely prepared for Math 233 next semester, but I did suffer a lot of mental stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Assani has, in my opinion, an unjustified bad rap. He does move through lectures quickly and he does sometimes get lost in the weeds of being technical. Honestly if you do the work/reading for this class and don't just expect him to somehow magically transfer his knowledge into your brain you will be fine. Exams are essentially out of the book.

Do not take math 232 with Professor Assani. His tuesday lectures fly over material and his thursday lectures are just a group quiz, on material we learned earlier in the week... if your lucky. We've had some quizzes that were on material he "taught" us earlier that same class. It is a GPA killer. Avoid if you want to learn and care about GPA.

He spends Tuesday lectures flying over a couple of sections and doesn't answer questions/tells you to look in the textbook.  Thursdays are essentially a group quiz that lasts the whole period.  With Assani you will have to teach yourself the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Avoid at all cost! GPA killer.

I got A's in all math classes before I got a D in this class. Lectures are very confusing and he gives pop group quiz which is ridiculous. That is 10% of your grade. His exams are very unfair because the questions are very different than the ones we did in class and homework, and he did not curve at all. Take another professor if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I won't take another class with professor again.  You can do poorly in his class even if you understand the material. Exams are extremely hard and unpredictable, and he refuses to curve. His lectures are theory-heavy and therefore very confusing. Not helpful in office hours.

He is a very smart guy but he has trouble explaining concepts in an understandable way. He is not very helpful and does not reply to emails. Exams are extremely hard and they are graded arbitrarily. No partial credit. Take another professor if you can.

He lets you ask questions then won't answer them. He'll say just look it up in the book so he doesn't have to teach you. Poorly taught us the material and then gave us a quiz on it in the same 75 minute class. Rushes through stuff even when people don't understand. No way in hell I will ever take his class again.

Assani spent the majority of the semester he taught my class in Africa opening 40 universities - which is great, don't get me wrong. However, we did not have access to him. He was gone for two of the exams and the entire week prior to the exams, so we could not meet with him to go over the stuff we did not understand...

We had group quizzes very often, but the questions are usually out of the textbook with odd answers in the back. He would explain the process, do a couple practice problems, then move on. We had homework regularly as practice. Test questions were usually straight out of the book, so I suggest doing the review problems to study. Want to take again.

Assani's 521 class was definitely one of the hardest classes I've ever taken, but Assani was able to make it much more manageable than I would have expected. He is a somewhat lenient grader with a great final curve, which helped make sure I didn't actually fail the class. I'd definitely recommend him to anyone looking to learn a class.

This class is like any advanced math class; it's hard. Prof. Assani really knows what he is talking about, but can breeze pass difficult topics. Tests are TOUGH. Don't get discouraged if you completely bomb one. I got a 37% on my first midterm, but studied HARD for the other tests and did fine. No initial curve; there's a final curve at the end.

Dr. Assani is by far my favorite math professor I've had at UNC. His lectures  move quickly, but he explains everything very logically so that if you keep up with the reading, its easy to make sense of all the concepts. The hardest part is applying these concepts on his exams, but theyre almost all like the textbookin class problems.

Professor Assani did not answer any student emails to see him outside of his office hours. He hired a T.A. who did not show up to recitation. He would ask for questions and then not wait for any questions. What is worse, he would ignore and even get annoyed with students who really did not understand the material. Overall, he was not helpful.

Dr. Assani is amazing.  He is way more concerned about his students than the average professor -- he will go out of his way to help you and has a strong interest in the success of his undergraduate students.  Totally my favorite teacher of all time.

I had Assani for Linear Algebra (not Calculus, as some of the other reviewers have).  He was great in my class.  He did go a little fast, but he was excellent in conveying "the big picture".  He (rightly) expected you to work, but graded fairly and *did* give partial credit.  Not a perfect teacher (those are rare) but I would still recommend him.
Exams are extremely hard and unpredictable. I recommend doing all problems in the textbook for each section because he chooses random ones to be on the exam.

Before taking this class I loved calculus. It was so frustrating taking his tests because they were nothing like the homework assignments or the problems in the book. That isn't even the worst of it. He doesn't give partial credit although he says he does. You could spend 20 minutes working one test problem and make a small mistake towards the end

After every class, I'd feel that I've gotten a very thorough lesson and that it was worth my time - quite substantial. He certainly doesn't waste time in class. He teaches on a slightly quick and advanced pace. He is fair with tests. He is my favorite math teacher here and I highly recommend him to others.

Ashok was a very kind and considerate professor however was not the best lecturer. The lectures were mainly watching professors code and follow along without a lot of explanation as to why things were done. This course would be much easier if you have an understanding of programming beforehand, however is not impossible without any.

Ashok and Stan were very kind and understanding to the COVID situation and were more than happy to adjust deadlines, but I feel like I didn't learn from their lectures. I found myself using google and youtube to teach myself rather than the lectures (even though I never skipped class). I needed the class for my major and I still don't get why.

Professor Krishnamurthy taught this class with Professor Ahalt, and it was a really good class. The material is not super difficult as long as you put in the effort, and both professors are very understanding people. Lectures could be unorganized sometimes due to technical difficulties, but nothing too bad.

Amazing teacher! I really enjoyed the structure of the class. They recorded the lectures and held them in zoom and in person. In some classes, they just went over interesting concepts that wouldn't be on the tests so the students got a brain break. Very caring and compassionate teacher.

Dr. Krishnamurthy and Dr. Ahalt are great. Even though the concept is sometimes hard to understand and you basically need to learn on your own, they are excellent in terms of understanding students who are stressing out over school and have mental health issues. Overall, I love these guys!!

Ashok is a very kind, caring professor and I would definitely recommend taking a difficult course, such as computer science, with him. I feel that there are some things to improve on in this course, as sometimes they would come with codes unfinished and it would take a large chunk out of class, but overall a great professor that I would recommend!

Professor Krishnamurthy taught this class with Professor Ahalt, and I loved it. For me, the workload in this class was very manageable. Both professors were extremely understanding of students struggling with mental health and other issues that kept them from completing work. I would highly, highly recommend this course.
Class overall isnt very interesting. Concepts covered arent explained clearly. Grading policy is nice. The class could be better.

Dr. Krishnamurthy taught this class with Dr. Ahalt and it was awesome! Very easy format and not difficult to get an A, but you also learn a lot about data science and get a good introduction to Python. I would highly recommend taking this class with both of these guys!

Took Ashok & Stan's COMP 116 class this Fall of the pandemic and they were absolute dolls. They're so caring, well-versed on the material, and really listen to their students. This'll be one of your best classes at UNC
Best comp teacher

One of the most highly respected professors. Works extremely hard to ensure that students understand the material. Is always available for outside help and presents many opportunities for students. Would definitely take another course with this professor.

Ashok is a very caring professor and absolutely listens to his students concerns. The semester I took him, he modified the previously difficult grading policies significantly in order to facilitate the course and reduce stress on students.

COMP 116 is tough no matter what but Ashok is by far the best option. He's funny and a patient lecturer. His extra-credit/take-home policy for midterms are way fairer than Majikes' and honestly saved my grade. He also offers a ton of options for extra-credit integrated into the assignments/worksheets and he doesn't take attendance. Really cool dude
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Ashok is such an amazing professor. Though I'm not sure why he is teaching, because he is a research professor and that's his main focus. Regardless, he is very caring and will curve exams based on the class average He also lets you fix your midterms, and your correction is 70% of the midterm's final grade. Overall, and easy class and a great prof

He can answer little to none of your questions on demand. When asking questions after class, he's googled answers and told me he's got a meeting to attend and left. He isn't accessible over Piazza or email. Spends 40-45 min of lecture doing useless announcements. Doesn't teach useful information for exams, end up learning everything on your own.

This class is definitely a bit different than most other classes in that learning is HIGHLY dependent on you doing the assignments and understanding the mechanism behind it. That being said, the class is pretty chill and Dr. Krishnamurthy definitely goes over a lot of useful, fun, and interesting material in the class. It's manageable.

I know some foreign professors are bad, this one is NOT. He just came from Ohio and taught this semester's 116 kind of tag-team with Dr. Ahalt. Both were extremely helpful and practical. Assignments were well-designed and they were flexible on dates. Lectures were good, not required. I highly recommend Dr. Krishnamurthy for any level class!

I loved Dr P's class so much I decided to minor in philosophy. She seems cold at first but she's just like that. If you reach out to her she's super nice and the course itself is super interesting. If you have a chance to take her classes definitely do, it's rewarding but not crazy hard.

Professor Passinksy is really intelligent and she puts a lot of effort into her classes and gives her students opportunities to actually talk to the philosophers we discuss in class. She is a tough grader but she is available in office hours to talk about your paper before submitting. If you're not a good writer, skip this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I've heard Philosophy at UNC is pretty tough, but Prof. Passinsky made the class as interesting as she could and she brought in philosophers to talk with us. The daily amount of work is not actually that bad, but the papers are crucial. She doesn't give specific criteria but if you make your paper topic specific and overly clear you'll be fine.

Since this is a philosophy class, your grade will heavily depend on participation and papers. If you are not a good writer, I would NOT recommend taking this class because one bad grade on a paper can cause you to fail. It would have been extremely helpful if the professor looked over rough drafts since two papers were over half our grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: no one cares that she went to Stanford and Harvard. this is a 100-level class. she's unaccommodating: i had to take weekly quizzes while hospitalized. grading feels TA-dependent, As are rare (94 = A, no rounding). i was docked for recitation participation despite university excused absences. not an easy A, and she acts like it's your only class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson is a wonderful lecturer. It is very apparent in class that she is extremely knowledgeable. The class requires a lot of reading, which is important for exams and papers. The grading is very TA-dependent. It is difficult to receive an A unless you do super well on the papers, which again is TA-dependent.

She is an amazing lecturer, passionate about explaining political science. Readings complement her lectures, which cover core concepts effectively. The readings provide essential real-world examples, crucial for excelling on papers and midterms. The two papers are graded slightly harshly. Overall, a great class!

Ashley clearly knows a lot about the subject and cares about what she is teaching. Lectures were easy to follow but mostly conceptual so most of the examples you'll need for the exam essay come from the readings. She's kind of disorganized so be prepared for the syllabus to change. She also does not round grades so do the extra credit!!

Super interesting lecture and class material. Anderson is incredibly knowledgeable. None of the assignments are very difficult; however, almost impossible to get an A, given 80% of your grade comes from just 4 assignments (2 papers and a written midterm and final / have to really crush the papers) + extra credit assignments were really dumb imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course was her just stating the blatantly obvious and she didn't really seem to portray her resume. This class being an honors class taught by an Ivy-Alum made me lose faith in Poli Sci and I dropped the major. Was geared towards how much surface level stuff you could learn as opposed to stimulating thought and depth into the Middle East.

I took POLI 130 with her, and she was pretty great! Informative lectures, clearly knows her subject matter, and encourages class participation. Readings are the main homework, and are necessary to know for the midterm and final. Additionally, I would recommend checking the lecture handouts for the key terms, because those will also be on the tests.

Very little homework for this class, just weekly quizzes that were online. She is a great teacher, very humble and real with her students. The most difficult part of the course is prepping for exams as there is such a large amount of information covered. Would definitely recommend for an intro poli class.

She's a little weird but all professors are. She talks very fast and makes really weird caricatures of different heads of state. I was doing well in her class until the final. The final bent me over and took everything. Study Study Study (I spent so many hours in Davis and it still wasn't enough).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are interesting, and the group project is fun, but the midterms are graded like English papers, not political science, which is hard with only 30 minutes. I didn't learn much comparative politics, did learn some more about the Middle East, and the class didn't feel like true comp politics.

Professor Anderson is disgustingly and dangerously educated. She makes lectures engaging and is very knowledgeable in pretty much everything she talks about. Attendance is required. There's weekly quizzes with five questions and two papers, along with the midterm and final that make up your grade. She challenges you, but an A is possible!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Loved her. Very intelligent, good prof. Fun class. Silly person! Made class enjoyable. Difficult assignments, but I learned from all of them and they all helped me improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great class and professor overall, but didn't love the communication between professor and I. She's very nice but unavailable. I showed up to her office hours once, waited an hour and a half just to find out that she was in Europe and didn't notify her students. This was a week before finals. But everything other than that about the class was fine.
Incredibly knowledgable, caring, and well spoken professor. The class is huge but she manages to make it feel very personal. I'd take POLI 130 with her again in a heartbeat. (Also, great TAs)

Anderson is a very knowledgeable professor and makes the lectures more interesting than they probably should be. The essays and exams are more easy than they appear. Only drawback is that the Professor Anderson is not very accessible and the TAs will be your primary source of advice and communication.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really informative course. Dr. Anderson's lectures were captivating and all the material was really interesting. You aren't graded on many things, which isn't ideal, but it isn't too hard to do well on her exams as long as you use relevant examples of what you learned in class in your essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super interesting class. I had a great TA (Marcos) -- become their friend! Don't skip recitation, review the course material a lot for midterms and finals, and utilize the writing center for your papers. Most exams/papers are graded by the TA's. The exam format is also distinct from most exams, so determine a study style/plan for them early on

Super interesting class. Lectures were super interesting and kept your attention even with large class size. I had a great TA (Spencer) utilize them as much as possible. I got 100 on last paper and that helped me a lot. STUDY A LOT FOR MIDTERM AND FINAL. You don't need to really do the readings just pay attention in lecture and go to recitation!

my favorite class so far as a polisci major. lectures were genuinely interesting and prof anderson was clearly passionate abt the subject. sayman was my ta- super nice grader and gave helpful feedback. prof anderson is brilliant- def take this class i loved it!

poli130 with professor anderson was my favorite. she's so respectable- weekly quizzes can have tough questions but overall very doable. 1 midterm and 1 final both the same format. memorized ~118 terms by the final but learned so much. my ta was sayman- also amazing. super nice grader and gave helpful feedback. definitely take this class!

Do well on the quizzes they are worth a lot and should be an easy A. There is a lot of reading but I never did a single one and got an -A. Make sure you know a lot about random examples for exams. Professor Anderson is so cool and the lectures are really interesting. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Anderson is awesome. She is very knowledgeable and helpful to her students. The exams were very fair because of being able to choose what questions you wanted to answer. Also the TAs don't grade too harshly. There are a lot of readings, but you don't have to understand all of the info to get a good grade..
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson's POLI 130 had very informative lectures and she is a nice person, although very difficult to find outside of class and somewhat condescending. Tough class to get an A in (94% with no rounding), but the TA you get makes or breaks your grade as they score your work on exams and papers. Long reading assignments daily.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A wonderful professor: passionate, well-informed, good lecturer. Lecture attendance is mandatory but there are lots of skips. She posts lecture slides and recordings. Class experience is dependent on your TA. Take S. Corp! Grades= 2 papers, midterm/final (no MCQ) participation, weekly easy quizzes. Reading=optional imo, DO pay attention in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you take good notes on lectures and know how to write, you'll have very little trouble with midterms and papers. Pay attention and go to TA office hours (especially for help on the two essays), and this will be an easy class. It helps that Anderson is a great lecturer and very well organized. There's also a small extra credit opportunity.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Uncaring for life circumstances and ambiguous grading criteria. Wouldn't take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course is made up of 2 papers, weekly 5 question quizzes, midterm and cumulative final and recitation grade. Overall the class was great if you are interested in comparative international politics. The first half is a lot about nations and nation-building, whereas the second half is about the types of government (parliament). Do the readings!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Anderson is a very smart and kind woman. Her lectures are easy to understand, but it is crucial for you to listen. Only a few grades in the class including a midterm, final, two papers, and weekly quizzes. Most of the TAs are good, but as long as you put in median effort you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class with Dr. Anderson was definitely challenging, but if you put in the work you'll do fine. Recommend doing the readings because you'll have to cite stuff for papers. Midterm was stressful, but there are only 2 exams including the final and two papers. Attendance is mandatory, though, and she uses the check-in app.

great lectures, DO THE READING, and pay attention. I saw a lot of ppl not paying attention during lectures, and they didn't do that well, so don't do that. I felt like the essays were made out to be more complicated than they seemed, which was intimidating. Midterm and final were stressful, but a lot of studying should pay off
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Incredible professor. Not a hard class in general considering the median is A-. Her lectures are engaging and she genuinely cares about her students though sometimes inaccessible with her emails. As long as you memorize the concept you will be fine.

This class was pretty difficult in my opinion (lots of reading and material), but Dr. Anderson made it an enjoyable experience. She is caring, funny, and obviously passionate about political science. The only thing is there is a LOT of reading and little opportunity for extra credit.
This class isn't that hard if you go to the lectures and try on the quizzes. But she is a good professor and makes the class interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Ashley Anderson is an incredible professor. She is very knowledgeable about the topics discussed in class and readily answers all questions in detail. She has clear grading criteria and I always felt prepared for exams. The weekly quizzes were a great grade boost.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ashley Anderson is one of the most intelligent professors I've ever had. She is very clear in her lectures and so good at explaining otherwise hard topics. There are weekly (open-book) reading quizzes and other than that the only grades are 2 papers, mid-term, and final. Make sure to do the burger or song of the day at least once for extra credit!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's clearly passionate about politics and her lectures are fairly detailed. TA really matters on if u have a good experience (mine is great - Bella Randle). She isn't very clear on some key terms tho and exams are way too hard. We have 50 mins and it's handwritten including an essay. She is also very clearly biased and puts that in her lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was not accessible outside of class and acted very superior to students, was not a fan of her as a person but her teaching style was mid. The weekly quizzes are full of trick questions, do not expect to do that well. Work with your TAs on the papers it WILL define your grade, they are super available. Also, do the song of the day.

She is incredibly passionate and knowledgeable about political science and comparative politics. Her lectures are engaging and easy to follow. She has a "song of the day" for each lecture, and students can submit a song related to the reading for extra credit. The extra credit can be beneficial at the end of the semester, so it's worth doing it.

Ashley is clearly passionate about the subject. She is extremely nice and helpful, but isn't very accessible outside of class. Your grade is dependent on two papers, a midterm, and a final. The papers totally depend on your TA, some are very generous, some are very strict. Take Eric Parajon if he is still TA'ing, such a nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Graded by very few things making it hard to do very well in the class. She lectures every single class all class long which gets pretty boring, and she does expect you to participate. Have to write two 5-7 page research papers which are awful. Can miss 2 classes total, and in class, you can easily work on other things while she talks.

This class was harder than I expected, but if you put the work in it isn't bad. 2 papers, midterm, final, and weekly quizzes make up most of the grade. There's a lot of reading as well, but you don't really need to read it in depth. Anderson is a good professor, gives good feedback and gives pretty in-depth lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer and makes content interesting. Grades papers harshly. A lot of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Anderson was pretty good for POLI-130. I thought it was a difficult course, especially for an intro level poli course. Papers were graded harshly (based on your TA). Lectures were very interesting and Dr. Anderson allowed for 5 class skips and 2 recitation skips. Lots of reading, but I didn't do any of them and did just fine in the class.

She had strict grading criteria, but would dissect papers you submit and still give you a reasonable grade. She had us write an essay as part of a test. She's lenient with her grading criteria. However, it's significantly harder than any of the TAs in the larger section will ever grade a paper. The class environment is extremely uncomfortable.

Sneaky hard class. 2 papers, weekly take-home quizzes, midterm, and final. Matters what TA you get for your papers. I thought prof Anderson was a very strange professor. She offered 2 extra credit opportunities, but they were a random competition for a song, and if the class could guess the race of celebs (wtf??) MC sections were vague & confusing
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She was good. 130 is very theory based, but I'm pretty sure she is the only professor you can take it with. Despite this, that is okay, she does a good job engaging the class with content, and you can tell she is passionate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson's lectures are entertaining and her TAs grade everything pretty easy.

You can tell Professor Anderson is passionate about her lectures. Readings for each class vary in length but are sometimes long. You can kind of skim them and be fine. Papers are based on lectures/readings so its important to take notes. Midterm and final were manageable if you took notes/review lecture slides. Overall a great class.

Anderson is an amazing prof who is super knowledgeable and passionate about her field. That being said, her class was a lot of work (readings for homework, papers, group projects). I think getting a good grade is attainable for anyone who puts in the work. Her lectures are effective. End project was a podcast which was so much work.

Professor Anderson is a great lecturer and is clearly very interested in the subject matter she teaches. If you are a political science major, I would highly recommend taking poli 130 with her. There is a lot of reading for the course, but you can skim through most of it and be fine. Pay attention in lectures, as essay prompts come from lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Attendance is taken but you get 5 skips. Lots of this class depends on your TA. Try and get Ezio Wang if he's still TA'ing. If you get a good TA essays are easy. Exams can be pretty tough.
Anderson was pretty cool. Very understanding with deadlines and emergency extensions and the like.

Honestly one of the best professors I've had so far. Her lectures are very interesting and the class is very fair grading-wise. She is deeply knowledgable and passionate about what she lectures about and she is very relatable. There is a decent amount of readings which I would recommend to do if you want to do well on the quizzes and essays.

Great teacher with lots of passion for her field. She's a little hard to access outside of class but the TA's are very easy to get into contact with. Her lectures are available on canvas and are very in depth. She also includes lecture summaries which was very helpful. The exams are hard but nothing impossible especially if you attend class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors! She is incredibly engaging in lectures, very easy to pay attention and retain information. The papers are not hard if you don't wait till the last minute to do them. Weekly quizzes, but they aren't hard if you do the readings and go to lecturers. She also drops the lowest quiz grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson is a very nice teacher and you can tell she loves what she teaches. I struggled in this class just because poli is not my strong suit, I would say only take this class if you are pursuing a career related to poli sci. We had 2 papers which were time-consuming, but the TAs were really nice when it came to grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson was a really good teacher. You could tell that she was genuinely passionate about what she was teaching and did her best to keep the large classes engaged. There is a lot of reading and hard papers, but the exams aren't awful if you pay attention and do the readings. TAs aren't always the best with grading/feedback though.

It is not difficult to get an A in this class if you put in the effort. I got a B+ because I didn't put in any effort into this class. If you do the all of the readings, it'll be easy. It's just a lot. Two papers, weekly quizzes, and recitation participation/attendance is a big part. She also uses UNC check-in for all lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It is not too difficult to get an A in this class.  The quizzes are hard, but the lowest 2 are dropped and the papers/exams are not bad.  There are 100+ pages of reading per week, but I didn't read any past spring brk and still got an A.  Manageable if you commit time.  Anderson is nice and tries to make lecture interesting.  Take Ranko as your TA!

Notot a ton of homework but there are two 5-7 page papers, a midterm, and a final. These assignments seem very difficult at face value but it is quite easy to get a good grade. Class felt a little formulaic but other then that it was good. It was my first and probably my only poli-sci class I will ever take. Subject material is a bit uninspired.

Anderson is an engaging lecturer and is passionate and knowledgeable about her subject. The attendance policy was generous, and so was the grading. Exam preparation was time consuming because there were so many terms to study and only four on the exam, but the exams themselves were manageable. Overall, I learned a lot and would recommend Anderson!

Multiple readings every week, but I never read them and ended with a B+. Tons of terms you need to know for exams because the exams are free responses, but I studied like a day before and did fine. TAs grade everything so your grade really just depends on if you get an easy one or not. Weekly quizzes, lowest two grades get dropped. Takes attendence

Solid class. Never did readings but studied hard for exams. Probably shouldve gotten an A, but got lazy on second paper. Exams are graded kinda weird but overall the grading was fair. Class made me consider poli sci as a major
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Anderson's lectures. She is very knowledgable in the content and has a likeable personality. The class consisted of weekly online quizzes, two essays, a midterm, and a final. If you pay attention to her lectures and do the readings, you'll be fine. I would absolutely recommend taking a comparative politics class with her!

very organized, and interesting lecture. easy to pay attention in class and many examples were given. there were a lot of readings but not super necessary. there were also weekly quizzes which boosted my grade

Prof Anderson herself is an engaging lecturer. Taught us the content via real-world examples. She is clearly so passionate about this subject, extremely intelligent, and funny. I want to be her friend. All grading done by TAs. Two 5-7 page papers, a midterm, a final. Exams were a few robust term definitions + an essay. Will do well if you study.

Very cool, young, and relatable professor. Very knowledgable about what she teaches and explains it well. However, there are weekly quizzes that are very difficult and multiple essays. Lots of reading if you want an A.

Lectures are amazing and informational, but with tons of information to sort through. There is also a crazy amount of reading, which you are expected to remember for the midterms and final. Papers are graded pretty harshly, and midterm is essentially all writing and identifying terms. Great class, but not an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The best lecturer I've had at UNC. Lectures are structured and connect the concepts of the class to real examples. Great intro to Polisci but is not an easy class. Lots of reading and keep up with notes. Midterm and final were very long and required you to know terms and authors, and papers were not graded easily.

I never really talked to Professor Anderson one-on-one, but she was a very effective lecturer. The class is mainly guided by TA's so she is really just there to maintain the stability of the course. She is very intelligent and you will learn a lot in her class.

Weekly quizzes, 2 papers, midterm, and final. Exams are both ID's (term definitions) and papers. Not hard at all if you put some effort in. Papers aren't bad either. TAs grade and were pretty easy. Quizzes were hard, but not big % of grade and 2 lowest were dropped. Prof was very knowledgable, interesting lectures and topics. Would recommend.

lots of readings for each week but you don't have to do them to pass the class. 2 papers and weekly quizzes which are not difficult and TA's don't grade papers harshly. Professor Anderson is very knowledgeable and this class was just interesting overall
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: This class was both one of the most challenging I've taken and one of the most interesting. The lectures are super fast and the quizzes are tough, but the paper topics are interesting. The midterm and final were hard, but doable if you studied well. She is willing to make adjustments for students as needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson is not very accessible to get help, but TA's do a good job. On the other hand, she is brilliant in this subject and knows what she is talking about. I would take this class, but be prepared to read a lot for every lecture. She records lectures but if attendance is low she will stop so show up to class.

I found Professor Anderson's lectures to be engaging and easy to follow. I didn't love how she was not very accessible via email, and she took forever to grade course assignments (2 papers, group presentation, final podcast) and the midterm. Nonetheless, she is passionate about what she teaches and the class was very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Anderson is an amazing lecturer and the content is so interesting. The class is made up of two papers, easy online quizzes, a midterm, and a final. The midterm and final really aren't difficult and the class average on each one was around an 89, so very manageable. Your grade depends on your TA, but not terribly hard. Very fun class.

I personally really enjoyed the content of the class. The lectures were engaging and I could tell Dr. Anderson really knew her material. The midterm and the final were ridiculously hard. I enjoyed my TA and she was easy to contact.

This class is very content heavy for an introductory course. The class is comprised of weekly quizzes, 2 papers, 1 midterm, and a final. The time limit for the midterm is very short for a handwritten essay and 10 terms with 3 parts each. The papers are graded fairly but the prompts are complicated.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy papers, but tough exams with a cumulative final of like 150 terms and 2 essays. She is super passive aggressive and shows zero to no compassion for her students. If you take notes and do the readings you should be fine but you have to stay on top of things or else you will get behind in the class. Personally, did not like her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No participation whatsoever, so there's no reason to go to class. Weekly quizzes aren't even about the concepts learned. Too much reading. Tests are unnecessarily specific and time limit forces students to rush. Try and find a different professor for 130 if you're a poli sci major. The grading is relatively fair however.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dull class and little was done to seek student engagement. Quizzes were unnecessary, overcomplicated, and did not add to the learning. Lecture recordings were taken away as "punishment" for people who didn't show. As someone who made it a point never to miss a lecture, this wasn't kind. All and all, not an enjoyable experience I'm happy it's over.

The class is lecture and reading-heavy, and you must keep up with the course material to stay on track. Also, her quizzes included nuanced questions and weird wording. The essay prompt(s) and potential ID terms for her exams are not provided beforehand, and there is a strict time limit for the midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Anderson was pretty good! Interesting lectures with helpful study materials and LOTS of reading though not totally unmanageable. Group projects were abysmal, but I think I just had a spectacularly bad group (they were assigned, the same ppl. all semester). Minus the projects, it was fun. Would take this class again.

Ashley Anderson is great. The class had plenty of opportunities for grades and nothing was too difficult. The course does have lots of readings that you are expected to know, but you can get by with just skimming them and going to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson was an amazing lecturer but she did assign a lot of readings. There were three group projects in the recitation which I didn't really like but they weren't difficult. The class was overall pretty easy with weekly quizzes, one paper, a midterm, group projects, and the final. Prof Anderson was super cool so take her if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson is the coolest professor I've had. I mean do you know another professor that lectures in high heels everyday? because I sure don't. The material of the class is also super interesting and combines different ways of learning for your final grade.

Weekly quizzes but I got by without reading the all the readings. Group work in recitation. Im not super interested in this topic, but I still managed to get through her lectures. Definitely go to class cause she says a lot of information that isn't written on the slides. Happy to be done with the class, but worth it for the credits.
