The final was worth 35% of the grade and it was out of 50 points, 18 points was a 9 question multiple choice and the remaining 32 was an essay. That means that if you get 1 question wrong on the multiple choice youre already getting 96%.

This class was fine. There were a decent amount of plays to read and weekly quizzes, but nothing that took more than an hour to grind out. Keep up with the readings and show up to synchronous class once a week and you're fine. Sometimes directions were confusing but just took extra communication for clarity. Participate to help yourself stand out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She always held herself higher than others and that air came off of her whether she was being rude or not. The only problem I have with the class is how disorganized it is- the syllabus says one thing and then she does another and doesn't bother changing the syllabus either. Her final project was also extremely confusing to understand.

The UNC Chem department cares more about their students than Prof. Snowden, and that's saying something. She beats up students when they ask for clarification, harshly critiques student work in front of the class, and seems to feel the need to be above everyone else. She offloads most of project grading to her poor TAs too. Just take someone else.

Professor Snowden is completely uncaring about her students and situations that might arise given now everything is online. Communication is difficult as she doesn't always respond to emails. Her lectures are boring and the expectations for the class are unclear. If you can, avoid taking this class at all costs; it is stress that no one needs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: She's very condescending and makes it seem as though everybody owes something to her. Type of person to be rude to her students for no reason. NEVER responds to emails, you have to email her many times to get a single response. Wouldn't recommend as a prof, even though the class itself was pretty easy to do well in. Just overall very annoying class

Professor Snowden is rude and uncaring. She was often late to lecture and legitimately just reads off the slides. There were several pop quizzes on the readings that had such specific questions it was inevitable few would get them right. She called out students and often came off as annoyed. The class was boring too. Take something else!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is being very disrespected by a lot of these ratings. She is an easy teacher and her class is not too hard. There's a lot of reading, but you can Google a summary and ace every test. The lectures can be dry but this class opened my eyes up to theater. I loved watching the plays and would have never had watch them if this class wasn't a GenEd
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Snowden believes that everyone in DRAM 116 should be as passionate about the theater as she is. As such, she gets visibly annoyed with students talk out in her class or don't know the answers to assignments. Not extremely hard, just a very tedious teacher. Be prepared to go to multiple plays throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Sometimes wasn't the most clear on her lectures and the final group project can be a real pain if you don't get put with good group members. Study guides for exams weren't very specific, but overall, if you come to class and don't miss attendance and do well on the quizzes and see the plays, it's a fairly easy class.

I like theater, but I hated this class. The readings were long and frequent, the textbook was pretentious and had numerous spelling and grammar errors. The icing on the cake was having a group project in an intro class full of uninterested students. She also wasted my time calling out talking students in class instead of just continuing her lecture

I was worried about this class based off what the previous students said, but it was not even close to as bad. We fortunately didn't have pop quizzes and the final wasn't cumulative so it covered only the easier end to the semester info. Plentiful extra credit that you should do! But I can agree with the people below that she can be rude at times.

this class was pretty awful. So boring and the midterm and final exam are unnecessarily hard. She just kind of runs through the powerpoints; there is no "teaching" involved. I think she tries to blame it on everyone for not paying attention/engaging, but the reading is stupid long (for no reason) and she doesn't even attempt to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class was a terrible experience. A large percentage of the class grade is based on "participation" of what she said would be a daily poll everywhere question but instead it was based on two pop quizzes taken in the last two weeks of class. She claims the study guides contain the exam material but it was completely different.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've had at UNC. She does not make any of her powerpoints or tests and does not show up on test day. Students are given lengthy reading assignments and quizzes weekly. She gives unnecessary pop quizzes on extremely specific things that hurt the majority of the students. She's often rude to students and doesn't care about our success
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Snowden is one of the worst professors I've had at UNC. She just straight up reads from powerpoints that she didn't even make. You could skip lecture if not for the pop quizzes. The group project completely screwed me. The group project had no clear criteria and I got assigned the worst partners. Honestly take a different class for your gen ed.

Attendance is not required although there were a few pop quizzes. Homework was to read about a play a week and take a quiz online as well as to see three plays. Grades are from quizzes, a play review, midterm, group project, and final. Midterm and final were very very tough, lectures were not interesting but short. Ample extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Only homework was read the plays and take an easy 10 question quiz, usually once a week or so. One midterm and the final, which were multiple choice/true-false/matching. Basically show up and pass. Also have to attend 2 or 3 plays at Playmakers. We got out of class 15ish minutes early every day.

Not as easy as you'd think. Lecture is just her speeding through powerpoint she hasn't made, but she does post them after class. Random participation quizzes on the reading assigned. Her study guides do not help at all with the midterm and final. Take advantage of the extra credit she assigns, it's easy and you can do as much as you want.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The lectures are not relevant to the midterm or final exam at all. Snowden doesn't make the powerpoints herself and doesn't seem to know what she's lecturing. The exams were straight from quizlet but also random. The one project is assigned into random groups and you are graded as a group. No curves. Don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: For a drama teacher, her presentational skills are lacking. No stage presence, its almost as if shes acting like a teacher, and acting poorly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: In class Professor Snowden often seems unprepared (she doesn't create the PowerPoints she teaches from) and can be hard to work with. She based our 10% participation grade off of a few pop quizzes that most people did poorly on. Members for the group project are randomly assigned, so you there's a good chance you'll get stuck with a horrible group.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Prof Avery is one of the best professors in the history of the college.   12 years later I still think about his courses.   Thorough knowledge of subject matter but always accessible, Avery defines what a scholar and professor should strive for. He's the best.  Willing to help you understand the material but pushes you to be your be best.   A+++
Nice guy, and the class isn't bad if you pay attention and take notes. Very helpful if you need it, though he does seem to play favorites sometimes.
Nice guy. Clear, knowledgable, definately old school.
No Comments

I didn't like her as much as other reviews. What made me mad is nothing was assigned in Canvas with specific dates so it was easy to forget due dates. Attendance is mandatory and you have to participate everyday.

Ellen is an amazing professor who makes it easy for students to succeed. She makes expectations clear with rubrics and grading criteria, and is a very fair grader. She leaves great feedback and resources for students to learn and improve. The exams were pretty easy and projects and in-class activities were fun and engaging. Overall great class!

Not sure how anyone could rate Professor Atterbury low, she is great! The class is pretty standardized for projects/tests but Atterbury prepares you well and encourages in-class group discussion which is super helpful if you actually want to learn the language. Midterms and final were easy if you just study a couple days before.
She was really amazing, we always know the expectations. She makes the class fun and educational!!

(Spanish 204) This class is pretty standardized for quizzes/tests and assignments but Professor Atterbury was super understanding all semester long and gave helpful feedback on assignments without being overly harsh. Make sure to talk in class and do your readings and you'll be fine!
She is a caring and lenient professor; does not listen to the 2-star review. SHE IS GOATED!!!
Miserable class to be frank. Type-A & overly strict grader. Super inexperienced in teaching. Be ready to devote all of your time to this class if you even want a B+ lol.

Great Professor overall, took her in the 2024 winter term, and her lectures were truly engaging. There's something admirable about her, from the way she speaks so eloquently, to how she engages with the class by eliciting introspection into our consciousness. And she also situates her lectures in real-life contexts for better understanding. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Atiya knows how to be engaging with her students and gives many examples to ensure that you understand a topic. She made complicated theories seem like elementary school with ease. She is always calm, cool, and confident. Highly recommend

Atiya is a great teacher and her lectures are very interesting. She does a great job of relaying the material in a clear way. There are 3 take home tests, each worth 20%, and an in-class final also worth 20%. She gives pop quizzes on the reading almost every class, but they trickled out at the end. The readings are all online, no textbook required!

David Attewell was my favorite professor during my first semester at UNC! His lectures were engaging, he values class participation, and he truly makes an effort to get to know his students. You have a few assignments throughout the semester but his grading criteria is clear. He is absolutely brilliant and I could not recommend him more strongly!

Professor Attewell is very knowledgable in his field and lectures with confidence. His lectures and powerpoint slides make politics easy to learn and he has made learning super accessible to non-political students. Highly recommend, be sure to take notes of his slides and read the case studies.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: David is one of my favorite professors at UNC. He's young which makes his lectures more interesting because he thinks about current events and relates to his students. He's a lenient grader and SUPER caring about his students and the quality of his teaching. Just make sure you are participating in class and doing the readings. 10/10 recommend.

He's the sweetest guy, always asking for feedback on where he can improve as a professor. Lectures are interesting and the grading system is extremely fair, consisting of a presentation, two 5-page papers, a final, participation and 3 pop quizzes. Very open to giving feedback during office hours and encourages class discussions on relevant matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I absolutely love David! He is so knowledgable, approachable, and caring . He explains concept well, but lectures can be dry. Fair grader on papers and no midterms! There are 3 pop quizzes (easy) but just on the readings so if you read you'll do good. I would do everything I could to take Attewell's class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: David is my favorite professor I have ever had! The lectures are interesting and very relevant. He is so helpful in office hours and will read full paper drafts. I promise if you take this class you won't regret it. This class inspired me to major in political science.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: David is a laid back, caring professor. He really made Poli 130 interesting! As long as you come to class and really keep up with the readings, youll do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Discrete is a tough class regardless but Jeff made it manageable. He was accessible outside of class and was as helpful as possible.

Considering this is an advanced math class, Jeff made the class as painless as possible. Even though we meet only twice a week, Jeff does his best to teach all the material in lectures to avoid outside reading (you will most likely be reading anyway). It's bittersweet that he is graduating this December, as he will no longer be teaching.

fantastic teacher/lecturer, has review sessions and tons of practice posted before the midterms/final. super helpful during office hours. discrete is a hard class, the first midterm is often misleading and the course piles up by the end. only concern id say is that you don't know grading scale until end of semester.

I would highly recommend taking his course. Lectures are greatly planned and his expression is super clear. His office hour is really useful. Two mid-terms in total and one final exam. I didn't do well on the course, but it's totally on me. I think he is definitely the best option for Math 381.

Jeff's lectures were very well planned, with the content he went over in class being accessible online for anyone who couldn't make the lecture. His tests were challenging, but with fair warning. He made himself available for 1-on-1 office hours every week, and was very open to helping students individually understand content. I would take again.

Jeff is amazing. Passionate, flexible, and great at making difficult concepts somewhat digestible. I enjoyed this class a lot, but he's a tough grader for sure, for both homework and exams. The final definitely sucked even with the curve. Still, if I could retake this class I'd try to get him again.

Ayers was amazing! He curved the tests that the majority of the class did bad on (20 points usually). He provided us with exam reviews before every exam which were extremely helpful. He is an amazing prof that wants us to succeed. However, the final was HARD. I had a B+ going into the final and ended up with a B- in the class even after the curve.

This class was okay but the final was very hard. Professor gives the option of turning in all the homework at the end of the semester but this can help or hurt you. Make sure to stay on top of the homework or your test grades will suffer. Ayers was always available during office hours and also would accommodate if you couldn't make office hours.

I've never had a better math instructor. Ayers' review sessions before the exams are super helpful and his lectures are great. He curves exams that the majority have failed on and seems like he genuinely wants the students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Ayers is great. Very generous with curving the exams if the average is failing.

He's a grad student, so there's not much I can really say other than he's just okay at teaching. First half of the class is MATH 110 review, but the second half is rough, and I don't think he was prepared. I'd take him again, but only if I had to.

Prof Aydin is a GREAT professor. He is so passionate about what he teaches and is very caring. Class is pretty lecture heavy and there is a lot of reading, but material is super interesting and he is a very fair grader with reasonable expectations. I highly recommend.
Cemil is a good lecturer and he cares about his students, I took a class I had little to no background in and he made it incredibly interesting. Would highly recommend taking if you are into history.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Aydin was the most understanding professor out of both semesters of online classes. He's very passionate about his work which focuses around decolonization and every class was fun to attend. 10/10 would recommend taking a class with him!

There is weekly assignments averaging around 400 words and lengthy readings with them. The TA grades most of your work and at times can be very particular on what his is looking for. Unless you want to learn about the Ottoman empire, I would not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Weekly writing assignments that are around 400 words, but the readings with it are very long and dense. Decent lecturer but goes on a few tangents. Gives out points for discussion and attendance, so show up or communicate (he was pretty flexible if you told him why you were out). Midterm was an essay, final was a take home exam and in person essay
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class was easy. I don't think his lectures were very engaging but you will do will in his classes.

Had a really good time in this class. Prof was very kind funny and entertaining, he is very knowledgable and is always going into interesting tangents he picked up from his years of research that tie into the class. Not a harsh grader at all and is very understanding. I took him for History 538 The Middle East and the West learned a lot Recommend!

Simple class, you do a 250-350 word forum per week but they can be tough to read the readings. Lots of extra credit avaliable and two essays. Not a hard course for a gen ed but it does require moderate effort. Ended with an 100 as someone who dislikes history so that was nice.
Dr. Aydin is one of the best lecturers I've had at UNC. He's super sweet and helpful, and this class is really informative. Just took this class for a gen ed, but I loved it. Would recommend.

Dr. Aydin was absolutely amazing, and this was my favorite class this semester. He is incredibly knowledgeable and offers an important and different perspective on many historical events. This course ties in with many current-day events, wars, and disputes. Note: there is a lot of reading, but 50% of your grade is recitation, highly recommend it!

We were graded on 10 forum posts, 1 a week, 150-250 words max. Also there were 2 papers, each 4-5 pages long. You can skim through readings for both. The only thing was his lectures were a little boring and hard to take notes on, so you don't really need to go to class. TA's grade everything so hope you get a good one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i absolutely love Professor Aydin! He's very knowledgeable and funny. His lectures are entertaining and informative. Very easygoing professor, great gen ed to take. Make sure to go to recitation and do the forum posts, that's half of the grade. Other than that, easy class and beneficial.

This class is by all means an easy A if you put in even a slight amount of effort. Professor Aydin isn't the best lecturer by any means, but you don't really need to attend his lectures. Make sure you prepare for recitations and write your forum posts, as attendance to those is 50% of your grade. Highly recommend taking for an easy gen ed.
Goat.

This class is really chill but also super boring. His lectures aren't that useful but every week you have some readings and a forum post that you will talk about in recitation. There are a couple papers throughout the semester but for the most part it's a pretty simple and easy class.

TAKE THIS CLASS FOR A GEN ED. Super nice and approachable. PPTs summarize his lectures well. Mandatory recitation attendance. Easy forum post every week. Easy A. -- recitation attendance (20%), essay (20%), forum posts (30%), final essay (20%), final exam (6%) --

Professor Aydin was an amazing professor. He always kept the class engaged and was very confident in his material and lectures. Attending class and participating was fun. There's weekly recitations and forum posts, and a midterm and final paper. Class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: class was ok, knows his stuff but got the feeling I wasn't allowed to disagree. kind of disrespectful of differing opinions, biased, etc. was super excited for this course but very let down. seems like an ok guy, but not very approachable, didn't have office hours from what I could see. easy A, especially with the right TA
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cemil Aydin is a solid professor. Hist 140 in particular was a very easy course, take it with him if you need the credit. The quizzes, recitation assignments, and midterm & final essays were easy. Aydin is not the best professor ever, but his content can be interesting and he does not make anything harder than it needs to be

Amazing prof, you will learn a lot but still an easy A. Initially seems like a lot of reading but you really don't need to do any of it. Guaranteed A if you just go to class and pay attention. Very nice guy, really interesting lectures and you can tell he is extremely intelligent and knowledgeable. Would definitely recommend.
I love Professor Aydin! Super nice to all his students and not many homework for a history course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Aydin should have his jersey hung in the rafters in the headquarters of the History department. My guy is a goat and the class is very well taught.

Dr. Aydin is easily one of the best professors I have ever had at UNC. By far the best choice for History 140. His lectures were engaging and on an interesting topic. Moreover, although your paper is graded by your TA, he is extremely forgiving and offers replacement quizzes if you miss any questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lots of reading! But overall simple and straightforward class. Lectures can be boring but Dr. Aydin's passion for history makes it a little easier to listen. Graded on one forum post a week, an occasional quiz, and two papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Aydin. He's such a knowledgeable, kind, and interesting professor. You can tell he loves his profession and the topics he teaches. I learned so much this class and the readings he chooses (while there are a lot) are super interesting. The class was mainly graded by forum posts, participation, and two papers. I definitely recommend him!

This course was fascinating. Dr. Aydin was super flexible with the pandemic and was also very knowledgeable on the course content. Course-wise, it is relatively straightforward. Although sometimes, expectations were a bit unclear. Nonetheless, Dr. Aydin was always available for help or clarification. He answers his emails very quickly.

Professor Aydin was really flexible with us over the semester and was a really easy grader!There is a semester long paper so don't procrastinate on that!The other assignments were simple and Prof would open up extra credit opportunities along the way!I wish it was more structured, a lot of expectations were unclear but professor was approachable!

Professor Aydin is a great professor, but be prepared to read! Also, lecture material can be dull at times, but Professor Aydin did a great job of keeping it informative. Would def recommend to knock out a good amount of gen-eds!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Aydin is very intelligent and is a good lecturer. Grading consists of forum posts , 5 quizzes, participation, take home midterm, and a take home final. This is a great class to knock out several Gen-Eds. I highly recommend taking this class with Aydin.
Professor Aydin is a great professor and is very understanding when it comes to students. I'm done with my history credits but I would definitely take Aydin again given the opportunity!

Professor Aydin is amazing and really passionate about what he's teaching. He's very caring and wants you to just understand the material, so it isn't hard to do well on assignments. He uploads all the readings and the course book as well to make it easier.

This was the most engaging and easy class I have ever taken. Aydin's lectures are amazing, and I never wanted to miss one. All you had to do was talk during recitation to make a decent grade. Easily one of the best classes of my college career.

Worst professor I've ever had. Presents an extremely slanted view of history filled with his own opinions and only assigns readings written by himself. Class is called history after 1945 but we spent the entire year on things WWII or before. Never explains any historical events, just talks about broad themes and expects you to know the rest. Awful.
Prof Aydin's awesome, take 140 with him!
Amazing Prof. I got an A in his class. And I hate history. His teaching method enabled me to enjoy history.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the easiest classes that you can take at UNC. Cemil himself isn't very involved in the grading; the grades you receive are completely down to the TA (mine was pretty nice). You seriously don't need to show up for class though and there isn't much homework.

Aydin himself is a really nice professor who is clearly passionate about history. I enjoyed having him as a professor. The only reason I did not like this class was because he is not the one grading anything that you turn in, it's all on how your TA grades, so if you get a hard TA, well it's hard to make an A. Participation is huge part of grade.

Dr. Aydin is very insightful and engaging with Ottoman history.  The only drawback of this class was the amount of writing.  Granted they were the only assignments, his class required roughly 32 pages of writing throughout the semester.  I found it manageable, but it was tough to keep up with at times.  Only drawback of an otherwise good class.

Professor Aydin is the best.  I've taken several classes with him and made A's in all of them.  He truly cares about his students learning and expanding their worldview.  There are no tests or quizzes, only papers.  He lectures with no set organization, but he grades very nicely and is very encouraging in class.  Everyone should take his class!

Professor Aydin is a funny, interesting, and very intelligent man. His class seems hard at first but he is a very easy grader (I got 100 on every paper) because he cares more about you showing you learned something than actual grading. He assigns a lot of reading but you can get through it by skimming. There were no tests or quizzes.

Prof Ayling has been one of my favorite professors at UNC so far. Very knowledgable about the subject area and makes the topic interesting for students. SO SO caring and accessible outside of class-- she really wants students to succeed. Would absolutely take another class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable about the subject matter, very kind and understanding, and overall great prof. Readings are pretty dense though.
She's a wonderful teacher and would absolutely take a class from her again.

Shes awesome. Show up to class and youll do very well in the class. She genuinely cares how youre doing and was willing to move assignments around based around how we were doing. Tests will push you for time, but getting 90% on them padded with all the homeworks will give you a pretty easy A

Dr. Younge is super nice, upbeat, and willing to help. The class material for Busi405 is commonly seen as common sense, but she finds a way to make it interesting through class activities and games. The tests are a little long and will push you to work a little more quickly than normal, but the classes tend to performs well. Homework is minimal.
Super nice professor. Always had interesting exercises and brought lots of energy to class. The tests were insanely long and difficult for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: ABY was one of the nicest professors I've had. She speaks very fast but she has a true passion for teaching french and ensuring that we understand everything. I would definitely take another class with her.
SHE IS THE BEST! Was so encouraging and always so helpful. take her for 105!!

Azza is such a light spirit who makes learning french enjoyable. She has a sense of humor which is refreshing in a classroom environment and she grades very fairly if anything she tries to give you as much credit as she can within reason. The course covers a lot of material, but she makes sure to go over specifically what we will be tested on.

She is such a kind, supportive, and funny instructor. She treats each student with respect despite different levels. She also explains cultural and relevant background info. She is just funny and seems to really enjoy teaching. Make sure you do the pre work. She is a fair grader. Participation matters and will help you succeed.

Azza is the best professor I have ever had. She encourages everyone to speak in French each class and I can testify that this has improved my French so much. She is very graceful correcting us when we make mistakes so we learn but are not afraid to mess up. She wants everyone to learn and succeed and knows how to help us do so!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is really funny and is very understanding of students and respect their time. The class was taught solely in French which really helped me develop my conversation skills. She can be a little intimidating but she is a really nice person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. ABY is excellent! She speaks almost exclusively in French (as expected in 204) but will kindly answer vocab and grammar questions at any point. Not a harsh grader but definitely values hard work and participation. Compassionate, encouraging, and accommodating. Take class from her if you have the chance!

Professor Youssef is by far the better of the two french professors I have had at UNC. She is much easier in grading and is sassy which I think is super funny. She is also super accommodating with grading (I forgot to submit half of a HW assignment and she gave me full credit for it). Overall, her class was the best french class I have taken.

I loved Professor Youssef! She is by far my favorite french instructor I have had at UNC. The french department in general is difficult but Youssef made it much more manageable. She was much less strict when it came to grading and tried to award as many points as she could on exams.

She grades a little harshly but not too bad. The homework is required for all FREN105 classes and usually takes about an hour. All papers are turned in twice and she gives a higher grade on the second. Participation is important and she will be nice when correcting you but mistakes show on your participation grade.

Native French speaker - she gives great feedback plus the curriculum is structured to give a good basis of the language compared to simply memorizing a load of vocabulary. 20% 4 tests, 10% in class participation, 15% 3 single page papers, 10% midterm, 15% Homework, 10% 5-10 interview (all in French), 20% Final
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Amanda was a good professor. Her lectures were very informative and she cared a lot about students' well-being. However, her criteria weren't always clear when it came to grading papers. I often got feedback that I didn't follow the prompt when I would address everything in the prompt. The class was easy, but don't expect to ace the papers.

Amazing professor and person! She cares about her students mental, physical health and wellbeing. I learned so much about myself and about how groups function within society in her class. I would highly recommend her.

Amanda said at the beginning of the semester that she wanted this to be a class that you could put on a temporary back burner in times of stress or difficulty. She values her students' physical and mental wellbeing above all else, which is clear in her easily approachable demeanor and ability to accommodate each student in their unique situation.
Amanda is such a wonderful professor who really cares about her students. The class was an easy A but was super interesting. Her lectures were very insightful
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amanda is one of the best instructors I have met at UNC. She tried to make everything easier and more convenient to her students. She could explain some confusing concepts very well. She is always very patient and very responsive to emails. The short answer format of the midterm and final is not easy, but overall I enjoyed taking the course.

Amanda is very nice and caring. If you ever need assistance or leniency, she is eager to help. She is a decent lecturer with a passion and competency in her subject. Pretty easy instructor too. I recommend.

I loved POLI 215 with Prof Aziz! She is always available via emails or at her online office hours. Although the course was async and there were lectures 3x a week, she kept them pretty short (25-30min) and always asked us for ways to make class better. She was very accommodating and she's a great person! 10/10 would recommend
Best EXSS class I have taken. Take this class if you can.

Best EXSS class I have taken at UNC! Exams are very similar to the study guides, and we were given the prompts to the final exam question a week before. Loved her lectures as they were interesting and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Professor Baez the first year she offered EXSS 581, I loved the assignments, and she was clear about what she wanted. The content was interesting and if you have a psychology background, it's cool to see topics and how they play a role in sports injuries.

Please do not take this class if you are looking for an easy gen ed. I worked so incredibly hard for the B+ that I go. Professor Bauer is kind, but her lectures are incredibly disorganized and the amount of material included on midterms is insane. Get ready to study and memorize your heart out if you take this class.

Very difficult considering it is an introductory level class. Her lectures go incredibly fast and are very disorganized to the point where I had to reorganize all my notes after every lecture. Midterms and exams are written only and require very dense knowledge about the structures covered and memorization of terms, dates, and architects.
This is a great professor and a great course to take some time here at UNC. Made learning more about the art styles in movies very entertaining and had good commentary on the aspects of movies.

This class was a lot of fun! I think this class is one that you can take regardless of your level of interest in film, because the movies were all very good and the lectures were extremely interesting! Just get ready to write a few papers, but overall the work is very manageable and the professor is so nice and accommodating!

JJ is one of the best professors I've had at UNC so far. This was a rough semester, but JJ's class was a bright spot. I'm not an art major and have never been the creative type, but the material in the lectures was pretty interesting and she is good at grasping students' attention. Great class and great prof

I am not an artsy person but was invested in Dr. Bauer's classes because of how she presented these buildings. She tells you about architecture as if she was there when every building was built, and it is genuinely so engaging. The paper prompts were unclear in parts, so work closely with your TA on how they will be grading essay formatting.

Amazing class! Every subject was not only interesting, but my favorite part is that Dr. JJ Bauer wears shirts every lecture that coincides with what you were supposed to watch before that class. Overall, it is a writing-heavy class, but nothing not manageable. Her pacing is perfect and recitations are interesting as well. Highly recommend.

I took this class for a VP credit and it was honestly pretty interesting. Im not an art person but I enjoyed Prof Bauers lectures and connections to history. The tests are relatively easy and she made them open note, but her lectures move really fast, so it's difficult to keep up. There are also 3 3-4 page papers but they're pretty simple
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: paper and assignment criteria is usually v unclear, usually its outdated. there are not 1 but 2 midterms in her classes. yeah, 2. on top of the 2 midterms, theres like 3 papers & a final, & post to a forum for 5 of the weeks. usually a recitation on fridays & made us write a 6pg paper in the span of 3 days only knowing the prompt on the 1st day.

Bauer is a sweet lady who is born to be into art history. She is extremely insightful into decorative arts of all aspects. We were required to finish a 10-page paper throughout the semester but once you have your topic in your mind or finish it partly, you can receive some of the grades. She always has good ideas to help you do your research.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Far too much work given the circumstances. Not interested in student feedback on onerous paper grades for a fundamental-level film course. When she assigns you a paper, be prepared to forget about the rest of your day.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: *taken remotely* -- Guidelines were unclear for the final project- given an example outline for an entirely different project than initially described and then criticized when we asked for clarification. Exams consist of lengthy papers but they are mostly graded lightly! However, a fun course if you love movies and want to learn more about them.

This class was really fun, but don't expect to breeze through, it's a lot of work, Dr. Bauer has you there to really learn about film techniques. She's fun in lecture though, it's all worth it. I was going through a tough time in my life and she was so caring. Very fun VP credit! You'll never watch movies the same way again, you'll love it
Not bad Just do the work and you will be fine.

this class was a gen ed for me but i loved this class. prof and TA are awesome and i learned a lot. not a lot of hw for the class, probably an 1-2 each week but readings are required and they do notebook checks. exams were easy and theres xtra assignments to pad out ur grade. overall a super nice guy who wants to see students succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: I LOVED this class and the teacher. He is a great lecturer and I was never bored in his class. He is very clear on his assignments and exams. If you put in the work, this is a very easy class to get an A in. he gives and adequate amount of work. There is a lot of readings but they are enjoyable. He also made us food for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Lots of reading to do with the required book. Honestly, most of it can be overlooked by the lecture and recitation. Very knowledgable about the content and created a light hearted atmosphere.

This was my favorite course so far at Carolina. It made me reflect on my own faith and consider ways we could be doing better. Professor Bayne is super knowledgeable about both Christianity and Native history. Sometimes it was tough to confront so many difficult moments, but he always gave us helpful context and led creative group discussions.

Dr. Bayne and Carla were amazing this semester. The classroom environment is very engaging and interesting, and both are very caring. As long as you pay attention and study the exam guides, an A is nearly guaranteed. The best professor and TA duo I have had at UNC so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of reading and lecture notes, if you pay attention and show up you should be ok. Tests can be challenging if you dont show up but you create a study guide together so no reason to do bad. Overall interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Bayne is amazing! He is very passionate about what he's talking about and is very nice! definitely not overwhelming! LOVE Carla(TA), although I believe she will be leaving next semester, so hopefully the next one will be good too! Def recommend!

Dr. Bayne is a great professor who knows so much about what he talks about. This course was very discussion based but it was very enjoyable and easy to take part in if you did the readings. It involved also going to plays of UNC arts performances and all assignments were given plenty of notice ahead of time. Overall a great course, would recommend

Dr. Bayne is super nice and really knowledgeable! All of the projects and assignments we did helped me think more deeply about the topics we were discussing and helped me explore lots of arts forms I had never been interested in before. I really enjoyed the class and would definitely recommend to someone looking for FC-AESTH credit.

Bayne and his TA were very nice and incredibly understanding. The class has a lot of work, but the work itself is pretty easy. The readings are very long and boring but you can get around doing them except for when it comes to discussion posts. Make sure to attend class and take notes, as the slides are very vague and mostly consist of pictures.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Prof. Bayne's class this semester. There is a lot of reading and you need to be prepared to discuss it at length in class. The work wasn't too bad though - discussion posts and responses, 2 quizzes, 1 paper, and a final project (no exam!) He wasn't good at keeping up with grading though. Overall very nice guy who wants you to succeed.

The class itself wasn't that much work: 10 discussion posts and replies, 2 quizzes, 1 midterm paper and a final project. But Bayne had no rubrics, barely any guidelines for assignments, and grading was random and subjective. He also didn't grade the majority of our assignments until the last week of class which was stressful and frustrating.

Disscussion posts were graded easily, but the readings are such a drab, and some are quite long. He started out quite nice, but became super jaded as the semster went on. Lectures are helpful for the essay portion of the exam, but referring to the slides to study is useless, there is nothing helpful on them.

This class is just made up of discussion posts throughout the semester, book review paper, 1 midterm and 1 final. Super easy. Caring teachers, and a nice environment. Would recommend to take for a gen end. Easy A.
Great guy, very organized. Made his midterm very fair and explained exactly what students needed to do. Material could be dry at some times.

I really enjoyed taking IDST128 with professor Bayne. He made the lectures interesting and the use of Jonathan Haidt's book was very informative and compelling. IDST128 is overall a great class when choosing a triple I.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The topic of the course was supposed to be about how to discuss hard topics (race, religion, and politics) in a respectful manner, but I feel like Dr. Bayne didn't teach us how to talk about religion. Instead, he mainly focused on colonization and moral philosophy. He's a nice guy, but his content didn't allign with my expectations for the course.

This whole class felt messy. He was fine but really boring and often went off on tangents that did not relate to the topic. We were supposed to learn about religious nuances in conversation and spent 3 weeks looking at a map of the conquistadors...yeah. Quiz wasn't super hard but he had the hardest of the three professors. Lots of vocab.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Seems decently well-informed, but did not adapt very well to the needs of the Triple-I class format. Lectures were dull and often focused on the same topics over and over. Relatively easy to score well, just do the homework and study vocab terms for his quiz. He is much better suited for a small class.

While the general course is fairly disorganized, I do not attribute much of that to Professor Bayne, though, his lectures only really focused on one topic despite the course being supposed to delve into multiple. He clearly is passionate about his research and is caring, but his teaching was not consistent with what was expected from the class.

Overall the problem wasn't as much him as it was the chaotic organization that is Triple I courses at UNC. Though his lectures kind of drifted from the topic, he still clearly is a smart guy who knows what he is talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bayne is a legend. This course taught me so much I never imagined and his care for both the subject and us shined through. He genuinely gets to know his students and adapts to  your struggles. Sometimes the reading was pretty high level and he focuses on small group discussions, but they were well organized and I learned a lot.

Most of class time is spent in class/group discussions and activities. Seems poor at time management, we almost never did everything in class he said we would. He tends to be unclear about specific rubrics/instructions and due dates, and rarely answers emails, but he is also lenient in return. Wouldn't dread taking him again but would rather not.

Professor Bayne's enthusiasm for his class is truly infectious. There is some reading and long videos up to an hour but if you take 2-3 hours out of your day you're able to complete your response quickly. The articles and documents provided increased my fascination for religion in America. The e-book was my favorite part of the class. Was very fun.

I would certainly recommend RELI 151 with professor Bayne to anyone considering taking it. The class is interesting and taught me a lot while not being overly demanding. There is one book you need to buy for class (for a book review near the end of the semester). Professor Bayne and his TA were both very kind and cared for their students.

Overall, his class was easy. His exams are very straight forward, only one midterm and a final, and before each one he lets the class come together and come up with terms you based on the reading and lectures you may need to study, and then that list acts as a word bank for the exam. Exams are based on the vocab, and then 1-2 essays. Easy professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took this as a gen ed and loved it. The TA is caring. Starts each class asking you to check in with your peers. He let the class come up with the midterm and final topics, let me make up the midterm when I missed it. There are readings but I never read any of them. Just do the work, show up for class, and pay attention and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bayne's okay, his lectures are dry at best but the material is fairly engaging. There's a fair amount of reading, but you don't really have to do it unless you have a forum post for the day. He can be slightly insensitive about the material (white man teaching Latin American religion), but overall an alright professor. Loved the TA for the course.

Beginning of the semester, the TA's make the class a lot harder than it needs to be and often take off points for no reason or with vague directions on things like what "have analysis" is. Bayne is a nice guy, however, and definitely do the extra credit he offers. There are also pop quizzes which can be annoying. Most of the class got an A or A-.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I feel like I took a different class than the others who posted this semester. Assignments were easy enough and my TA answered my emails quickly. I met with Dr. Bayne in office hours and he was very friendly and even remembered my name from lecture. There's one paper and an E-book final. I learned a lot about different religions, which was cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class was pretty solid overall with the exception of questionable grades from the TAs. You must go to class everyday and take notes because there are pop quizzes.  Lectures were informational but could be pretty boring. There are is a large paper and an E-book throughout the course and Ta's just look for something to take points off for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class for geneds and assumed it would be easy from reviews. However, you don't receive helpful feedback on graded assignments and the TA would take off random points for no real reason. Bayne was not very involved besides showing up for the lectures. Overall, I did not enjoy this class and the TA's have a huge impact on your grade.

I took this class to fulfill geneds and thought it would be somewhat not difficult through what I researched about the class. Grading in this class is questionable with the TA's, I found my TA taking off points just to do it and not really providing great feedback. Overall, simple class but TA's matter throughout this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class isn't terrible but the grading policy doesn't make sense. You can be in class every day but miss one day, and if there's a pop quiz that day, there's no way for you to make it up and it's going to hurt your grade. The grading policies for forums and assignments overall are unclear. It was probably better online but this semester is rough
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Really interesting class and thought provoking. However, it was so much reading, more than I've ever had in other higher level histories. He makes the readings accessible, but they're often long and repetitive. Graded on forum posts, one paper, two quizzes, and a final paper or project. Rubrics for these are often unclear. An awesome guy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bayne has been one of the best professors I've had at UNC. His grading is very clear and reasonable. With the transition to online, he couldn't have done anything better. He truly cares about his student's well-being and their education He and his wonderful TAs fostered an environment that made me want to learn.

Professor Bayne is awesome. His lectures are very interesting. He always gives good feedback and interesting ideas to help you with your papers. Go to his office hours and he will help. He is extremely humane and caring, understands that circumstances can impact your performance, and is willing to give an extension on a deadline if needed.
Amazing teacher! So kind, funny, and really gets to know his students. Lectures a lot but is super passionate about his topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: His lectures are engaging, and he takes time to answer students' questions. You don't have to read, as he goes over everything you need to know in lecture, and he tells you the specific readings that will be discussed in reciation. There are pop quizzes but they are open notes and easy. There are two essays and a final, which are graded liberally.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Bayne is a true gem in the reli departmeny. He is brilliant, motivational and fun; you wont regret sitting in his lectures for a semester. Beware though, 2-3 pop quizzes! Also, the TAs do all the grading, so hopefully you have a nice one. Overall, I would love to take another one of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Reli 140 with Bayne was easy and interesting! The TA's grade pretty easily which is nice. If you just do the bare minimum you'll be fine. Just go to lecture and recitation for the info on the 3 pop quizzes (which are easy too). Although lecture can be boring sometimes, Prof Bayne is a great guy and a good lecturer. Good class to fulfill a gen ed.

I love Bayne!!! He's the best. He's really passionate and knowledgeable. He also makes a genuine effort to get to know his students. I could not recommend him enough. I'm not a reli major but I loved this class. I learned so much and really enjoyed it.

Professor Blayne is a fantastic lecturer and definitely knows what he's talking about. He tries to engage with students and keep it as entertaining as possible. Beware of pop quizzes (it's how he takes attendance) and you HAVE to do the reading otherwise you will be VERY lost. Occasionally he does speak/go through slides very fast making it difficult to take notes but that's my only complaint
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I LOVED professor Bayne, but the workload of this class was just too much. There are on average 4 readings you must complete before each lecture in order to keep up. There are no tests, but 2 long papers, which are either graded harshly or nicely depending on your TA. And pop quizzes make you regret that ONE reading you didn't do the night before.
I loved Professor Bayne! His lectures were interesting and he was easy to listen to and approachable.  Your TA is key because they do all of your grading so it is important to show them you care.

Dr. Bayne's class has been one of my favorites so far at UNC. He is a great lecturer and you can tell he loves what he does. Class is very substance heavy but he does a good job of peppering them with videos and jokes.  I would definitely take this class again.
Professor Bayne is one superb professor!  His lectures are well organized, well presented, and fascinating.  His TA's are his  team members and everyone is on message.  Professor Bayne is a star!

Bayne's Class was great! It was extremely enjoyable and made me want to take another religion class at UNC. The TAs do grade harshly, so be careful on your papers. I never did any of the readings, but still managed to pull a decent grade in the class. Only one exam (the final) so just make sure you study for it. He basically gives you the answers.

Professor Bayne is awesome! The lectures are boring and there's a lot of reading, but the class was pretty easy for satisfying 3 Gen Eds. Just come to class and put in the effort and its an easy A. The TAs are really harsh graders so make sure you see them outside of class for your papers and you'll be fine. Would definitely take this again!

Bayne is a very good professor and has a great understanding of the material.  However, although the TA's are nice, they are harsh graders and the directions on most assignments are very bleakunclear.  Also, attending class is a must, and there is a lot of reading for each class.  Only take the class if you are truly interesting in the course.
Awesome professor! He actually cares about learning everyone's names and getting their opinions on the readings.  He's approachable and the material is interesting.  Definitely recommend.

I had Bayne for RELI140, Religion in America. This was by far, the most interesting class I had at Carolina and Bayne made it that way. The grading is very fair and the TA's are all awesome. Bayne puts in so much time into the class, learning people's names in a 150 person class, and shares his passion for this subject with everyone.

The only positive thing I have to say is that she was generous with curves & EC. However, she is very petty, extremely hard to follow during lectures, creates ridiculously long exams, and gives very few practice problems that I did not think looked anything like the exam. I only did well because I am comfortable with stats and put in a ton of time.
Erin Baker graded almost solely based on midterm exam scores, and didn't assign much homework to practice lecture material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She did change the grading scheme because of issues with AI which was unfortunate, but although the exams became weighted higher, I have never seen a professor give such generous curves on exams as her (even if average = 70s). She does problems slowly and in detail, and super open to questions. Exams are long but every 241 professor has long exams

very poor lecturer. was extremely difficult to follow along - expect to spend tons of time outside of class teaching yourself the content. 

tests weren't difficult but very long, so there was never enough time to check over work. 

but, if you are math-minded, you will find this class easier than other 241 sections because of its focus on stats.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Makes ARS absence accommodated students do a problem you didn't learn how to do (only blank slides provided) and submit it by 5pm the same day for credit. Admitted to people outside of the class that she made exams extra difficult on purpose after the AI issue. Punished class for some people's wrongs to be "fair." Taught unnecessary extra stats.

Different content from other 241s. Tests are based on lecture content (not textbook). Teaches extra math that won't be tested on, but she lets you know what will/won't appear on a test. Tests are long and seem hard, but curves are generous +EC. Didn't post slides afterwards & only wrote on chalkboard.

Overhated for AI imo - we were not faultless.

Dr. Baker seems sweet but the AI incident definitely left a bad taste in her mouth (She changed the syllabus to be 85% exams right after). Exams were long but she curved them all. The final was fair. I would take the other 241 sections over her's because she mostly teaches statistics, only the last 1/3 of class was actual chemistry.

I ended up getting an A after a near perfect score on exam 3 and replacing the lowest midterm grade with the final grade, however, her class was hard and not really reflective of what other 241 classes teach. Her lectures were confusing to follow, and my success at the end of the course came from reading the textbook, not from her. Kind of petty.

Covered half of what other CHEM241 sections did, which is unhelpful for the lab/MCAT. Said that the final would be a certain format, then changed it without informing students. Overcomplicates the simplest concepts and doesn't upload her slides/work half the time. The rare extra credit doesn't compensate for the stress you'll feel from this class.

Dr. Baker is rly nice and clearly cares about her students. That being said, this class was really math/stats heavy (big content difference from other classes or the lab) and the explanations weren't always the easiest to follow. Tests were really long but not terrible for UNC chem imo. Unnecessary hate.

I had only positive interactions with Dr. Baker. However, I found the most challenging part of this class to be that she wrote on the blackboard only and I struggled to read it a lot. I did appreciate the practice questions she provided and they were always very similar to exam questions. Once I understood her expectations, the course got better.

Go ahead and take her if you want extra premature balding. I genuinely did not comprehend a single thing this woman taught all semester, and trust me, I normally enjoy chem. I appreciate the extra credit but never have I seen such terrible grades as I had to dig thru everyone's exams to find mine. and don't even get me started on the AI situation

Acted like a child the entire semester. Held a grudge and retaliated against the ENTIRE class for ONE assignment that had nothing to do with the core curriculum. Was condescending and sent nasty email replies, if she ever responded at all. Told us she purposely releases exams after class, because she doesn't want to have to answer our emails…
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Baker handled this semester's 241 class with complete immaturity and lack of professionalism. She doesn't know how to teach to save her life, her lectures are all over the place, she made her own crazy curriculum, and changed the syllabus and grading system in the middle of the semester. Her midterms were 40 questions long, longer than finals.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her exams are extremely long, and the class is disorganized, but I feel she deserves some credit for how she tried to make up for the first half of the semester. Generous curves, extra 3 points on exam grades just for coming to the next class, and a very fair final exam. It is frustrating to have such a different experience from other classes.

Other reviews are unnecessarily harsh. She was an okay lecturer and her exams were very hard, but she was pretty clear about what was going to be on them. She posted review sheets beforehand and graded generously. Honestly if you can do the practice exams you'll be fine. Most stats heavy than the other professors, so avoid if not your thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While Dr. Baker is a brilliant researcher and kind person, she is not a very effective instructor. She struggled to convey even the simplest of topics, resulting in students needing to learn the majority of the material on their own.

While Dr. Baker isn't the best lecturer and doesn't cover some of the content that the other 241 sections do (which makes 241L more difficult), the other reviews are a bit harsh. She makes it very clear what will be on exams and she curves them + additional bonus points. She definitely has her faults, but the generous grading makes up for it.

Dr. Baker writes all her notes on a blackboard and doesn't post notes that you can go back to. Half the time she has to look at her paper to see the work she did before continuing on the board. The way she does problems is more complicated than it has to be. She is so strict about sig figs but messes them up on answer keys and lacks consistency.

Dr. Baker made CHEM 241 a terrible experience. She is incredibly immature and lacks professionalism. While some students used AI on an assignment, instead of punishing those who did, she punished the whole class. She did the same thing on participation grades. She is condescending and acts like she got her feelings hurt and needed to retaliate.

Nice lady, terrible prof. Do you want to succeed at UNC Chem 241 - don't take Baker. That's a fact.  Why would a professor have to curve and give extra credit for each exam?? Because most students did bad!!! It's a sad story; people fought to get into this class, just to be played in the end. This is the Carolina STEM experience.

Syllabus change, lack of partial credit, long exams, and limited practice. BUT she curved, gave extra credit for attendance so you could get >100 on exams, and is so kind and personable when you go to OH. Final exam almost all directly came from past exams or in-class slides. She's also famous but you'd never know just from class. Would recommend!!

Though this class was incredibly frustrating, I think Baker also had many saving graces in the class. Extra credit during certain class periods, curved every exam, and the very straighforward final after you make it through the class. Did I enjoy the class? No. Absolutely not. Very disorganized. But she makes it possible to get a good grade.

Extremely exam-heavy(85%)and unforgiving grading. Changed the grading scale weeks into the course. Penalized the entire class for "AI use" with no evidence. Rarely responds to emails. If you want a fair, transparent, or supportive instructor, avoid this class. Change your schedule around if you must, do not settle for Dr. Baker, you deserve better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yes, she teaches a different course than other analytical profs, and yes, she's not AMAZING at teaching. Keep in mind that half our class DID use AI to shortcut an easy paper, so take all you see here w/ a grain of salt. The content doesn't always feel like chem, but it's really not hard. Go to class, do the work, and go to office hrs. She cares.

Her exams aren't conceptually difficult but are very heavy on memorization. The course often felt more like stats than chemistry, but she didn't clearly explain either aspect. She seems friendly but her communication can come across as passive-aggressive at times, which made the class environment less comfortable.

Honestly, this was one of the worst classes I've taken. Partway through the semester she changed the grading scheme so that exams suddenly became 85% of the grade. On top of that, she barely taught actual chemistry and spent most of the time on statistics, which other 241 sections didn't even do.
just dont take her class or you will be played like a dog

Trash, absolutely trash. worst i have ever had. she changed the grading scheme in half of the term and made tests 85 percent of the whole grade. she canceled all attendance grade and a project grade which were easy for students to get grade on. she didnt even teach chem. instead she just teach you bunch of stats which the other 241 class does not.

Very passive aggressive. She goes on 30 minute tangents explaining the math behind something just to tell you right after that you don't need to know it. She accused the class of cheating and instead of reaching out to those students, she penalized everyone in class and made exams weigh more. She also took away in class participation a month in.

Very spiteful and immature. Obviously the AI thing (several students cheated on a participation grade using AI) was bad but instead of punishing the students who used AI, she made exams much heavier. Not only that, but there is very limited practice for her exams which are designed to be lengthy and tricky. No dedicated final exam review. Avoid her

Dr. Baker is one of the most condescending professors I've had at UNC, and I tend to like professors even with a bad rep. Her exams are insanely long (she had to extend time 30 minutes on all three midterms) and her lectures are super confusing. She messes up simple concepts while teaching them and makes them way more complicated than needed.

A few students cheated on an assignment and instead of giving those people 0's she took 12% of the whole class grade coming from attendance/easy assignment and added it to exams. Literally bad at teaching during lectures, unnecessarily long exams/not enough time, entire grade is exams. Not much HW. Stubborn + mean, not willing to help students out.

Take everything you read with a grain of salt, the AI thing was bad, but the ratings she gets are not deserved. If you show up to class and pay attention it is very manageable. She is clear about what we will be on exams, and they are fair(plus a curve to around a C+ average for each exam.

Wouldn't take at all. Her lectures are disorganized and often seems like she doesn't know what she's doing or how to solve problems. Very different curriculum from other CHEM 241 classes and seems to do things the ULAs don't even know. Does apply a curve but that's because the tests are difficult and lengthy (almost 40 questions long). Avoid.

I 100% agree with her response to students using AI to cheat but I want to focus on something else: her class is incredibly disorganized, but everything from the test comes from lectures that make little sense. Slides/textbook don't correspond with her lesson. She is generous with curves but it does not make up for her inability to convey content.

Her exams are extremely unfair. Both times she has made them 36 questions, with some being multipart and has had to let everyone stay at least 10 min more + barely anyone finishes. She also basically creates almost an entirely new course. Compared to the other analytical classes we learn things they've never heard of.

No annotated slides posted and lectures fall flat relating to math examples. This class relies more on self teaching than other UNC chem courses. While I understand her response to the AI situation to some degree, it also served to punish students that actually did put in the work. Removing attendance buffer was just further retaliation IMO.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE, like actually one of the worst profs at UNC, said half the class cheated on an assignment so replaced 10% of the grade into the exam category, making the class 85% exam weight? Then doesn't record lectures, doesn't drop any assignments or exams, no flexibility at all. Doesn't even fill in slides to post online. Lectures are scattered.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The material we are supposed to know isn't really explained to fullest extent that it can be. Often explains problems in the most complex way possible. Exams material isn't the hardest, but the sheer amount of questions given is too much. Lecture was mostly full even after extra time was provided. Keeps brining up the ai situation.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take analytical with Dr. Baker - if you work hard enough you can get through it but it will be miles easier with any other professor. Her slides are disorganized and she is not the best lecturer either. She does not explain concepts clearly and will often go on material tangents and then say that we don't actually need to know any of it.

It's actually true that more than half our class DID cheat using A.I. That in itself is problematic. But the cringe reviews complaining about the fact that Dr. Baker actually did something to address the cheating? They really devalue the UNC brand. The school seems to admit a lot of cheaters, who retaliate when caught because they resent working.

please just dont. its october and we've barely even touched actually chemistry. shes obsessed with math so we've literally been learning statistics since the start of the semester. so unfair to give such a different experience than the other classes. her slides make no sense and her test questions are obscure (and first test was legit 36 questions)

Much easier than any other chemistry professor at UNC. While accusing students of using AI and changing the grading scale to weight exams higher was unfortunate, it shouldn't really change anyone's grade in the long run if they're coming to class and putting in the work. You can tell she truly loves the subject she teaches and curves exams to help!

Avoid Erin Baker at all costs. Right before the first exam, she accused half the class of using AI, despite having no proof, and proceeded to change the entire grading scale to make exams weigh more. She has been nothing but spiteful since then, using obscure test questions from unrelated topics in class and being condescending in emails.

Take take take! She is miles easier than any CHEM241 prof with extra credit and curves to meet 85% test averages. Super caring and sweet. Although beware she has her own syllabus that will not match with lab - you will have to learn most of that content on your own.

I highly recommend Dr. Baker! She keeps exam averages around 85% and gives extra credit if they're lower. Her exams are very fair and she only tests on what she gets through in lecture. Her grading isn't very exam based for a chem class (only 70% of grade comes from exams). Also very accessible outside of class, friendly, and a very lenient grader!

Extremely caring and passionate professor! Tests are long and quite challenging but review questions are very similar. Didn't cover all topics that regular 241 sections got to but she writes her own exams so it's whatever. Recommend!
Very sweet and fair grader. The subject is interesting and she leaves space in the syllabus to discuss whatever the class wants to.
Lots of required readings but her exams were always clear and easy to study for. Fair grader she was very open to feedback!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Bella is an amazing professor! Poli-130 was by far my favorite class this semester. She made the class engaging, but there are readings due every class, with weekly quizzes. Some of the readings are pretty long and our final project was fairly difficult. Not an easy A, but Bella makes up for it with her awesome lectures and love for the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: i absolutely adored poli130 with her! she's a very good teacher and her lectures are very engaging and she definitely knows what she's talking about. not an easy a and there's reading due for every class with quizzes but the reading helps and if you do it you won't struggle.

Definitely have to put in effort to get good results. Good lecturer and engaging. Does a great job of keeping up with the syllabus and all readings are available on Canvas so nothing to buy. Lots of quizzes but always straightforward w/ no trick questions. Kind and approachable. Loved Bella!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Bella is very friendly and clearly knowledgeable and passionate about political science! She grades fairly and gives good feedback on papers. Definitely recommend her as a TA!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Bella was my TA for POLI 130 and she was wonderful. She was very understanding and caring and encouraged participation even if no one knew the answer. I would definitely recommend having her as a TA.

She was my TA for Professor Anderson's POLI 130 course. She was helpful going over information and condensing the material to help students better understand the readings. There were 2 absences available for the recitation. Overall great TA/Professor and person. She is really understanding and nice!
She's the best TA, and does a phenomenal job of explaining the concepts of the class. She has clear criteria for how she grades your things, so no excuse not to do well.

Bella is an amazing TA! She made an overwhelming class a lot easier to digest. The course material is hard, but she is always available for office hours and answering questions. You can tell she is passionate about the subject and cares about her students' success.

A very solid TA for POLI 130! I looked forward to going to her recitation every week. I felt like the way she explained lecture concepts made them easier to understand. I really recommend going to office hours to discuss papers!

these reviews are way too harsh... there are professors genuinely so much worse than her, and they still have a better rating. it seemed like she struggled a lot with anxiety and felt disorganized often times, but she was passionate and tried her best. her exams were very hard, as the other comments suggest, but it was not anything impossible.
Does not curve. Final exam was extremely hard.

GOOD PROFESSOR. She's good at teaching. I understood everything. Don't skip class and pay attention. You will be fine. Tests were pretty light, similar to practice tests. She's really kind. Don't be scared to take her class. Just study and review. There's too much hate on Bergland.

Pros: passionate, partial credit on exams (68% of course grade), final replaces lowest exam, exam format fair (potential +4% bonuses), active on Piazza, awesome in office hours, encourages participation
Cons: very slow to return grades, homework is super lengthy, seeks pity from students, assigns unnecessary group work, not a confident lecturer

Dr. Bergland is genuinely passionate about Statistics, and she knows her stuff. However, her lectures were not very engaging (had to self-teach outside of class) and practice questions were not effectively integrated into the class. She is available and helpful via office hours. Need to be VERY self-motivated. Definitely sit up front (no mic.)

DO NOT TAKE STOR 155 WITH HER. The midterms were way too hard and the questions cannot be completed in the allotted exam time. Even after students gave her feedback on the midterms, she still made the final insanely long and tough. She also refused to curve the final exam or our final grades when most of the class was in the 50-60% range.

Worst professor i've ever had at UNC. She literally walked into exams with them messed up everytime. She takes forever to grade. Isn't good at teaching the material to students.
