Didn't keep her word on credit with exams either. I understand it was her first year teaching but even a TA could have done better with the class. Nice lady but  wow.

Rated her 2 (not 1) bc she does genuinely have a passion and it shows in her good lectures. HOWEVER, she is not meant to be a professor. Harsh/rigid grading and closed-note tests aren't sensible for a coding class, and tests (that she made) not graded for 1-2 months. She tries to do too much then penalizes the students when she finds out she can't.

She is nice and extremely accessible. However, she often made topics more complicated than they were, failed to explain them in class (better explanations in office hours), and graded extremely slowly. We didn't have an accurate final grade until a few days ago. The 2 midterms did have revisions and homework is 28% of your grade.
Final was taken a week ago and we are still missing a homework grade from October and the final exam grade. So frustrating.

These reviews are wayyy too harsh. Most students who did not understand the material likely did not read the textbook or had not coded before. Logistically, the course was not designed well with 4 midterms, but she gave us bonus questions on exams, was very active on piazza, and had 2 office hours each week for 3 hours, and was very nice.

The course material itself wasn't difficult, but the professor made everything more difficult than it should've been. The homework and the practice exams did not reflect the exams. She was also an extremely slow grader. She did give revisions and re-tests though.

Dr. Bergland is really not an evil monster -- she is clearly new & trying but just doesn't hit the mark. Slow grader & made tests/grading more stressful than necessary. She gave test revisions and tried to fix problems she caused (albeit in convoluted ways) but ultimately was a bit condescending and needs to listen to students more.

Her first semester teaching at UNC and it shows. She took too long to get exam grades back and made the two midterms too long to finish in the time given. Nevertheless, she provided detailed notes on all the course concepts, so learning the material wasn't bad. If you have any prior stats or college math experience, the class is a manageable A.

She is a new professor, but the issues extended FAR beyond that. Takes FOREVER to grade (1 mo for midterms, over a week for final), practice exams do not reflect class exams, confusing lectures, always rushed content, no practice qs, and she raised her voice at students for asking genuine questions. I hope she gets her act together.

Nice Lady, worst professor I've ever had in my life. Going to class and listening to lectures made me more confused on the different topics. I was better off playing Clash Royale during class and watching YouTube videos outside of class to learn topics. I did better on second mid-term all while sitting there in class getting my trophies up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: GREAT PROFESSOR other reviews are too harsh. yes, studying requires effort, but what did people expect? it's a large lecture class, so you're in charge of keeping up with notes, etc. she is super kind in office hours, lectures are clear with blank fill-in notes provided. uses slides and chalk. 100% would take again, fav class this sem

Understand she's a first-year prof so she may improve, but nonetheless incompetent. Took ages to get grades back, practice nothing like exams, generally unhelpful - never made clear cut expectations for exam material and what to study. Hopefully she gets better, New York Jets level performance from her this semester.

SHE IS A GOOD TEACHER. People need to chill on her because she is genuinely good at her job, but she teaches a hard class so people are bound to get bad grades. She does her best, and while it takes her a long time to grade, she is very generous with extra credit. You are going to struggle in this class if you dont like STATS, but she does her best

As others have said, her exams are quite long.  However, she has recognized that the exams weren't completely fair and offered revisions worth half credit back.  Her lectures are pretty good and she's very accessible via office hours.  Homework is pretty light.  She's not perfect but def way better than some  of the other stor profs here.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: she has taken months to grade things, did not return our midterm scores until days before the final and never returned our grades for a retest of a midterm problem. has now taken over a week to return final grades while trying to guilt trip us for having expectations of timeliness. always trying to make you pity her

People are being unnecessarily harsh i feel like intro level classes are always super fast paced. She's really accessible and helpful. Considering it's her first semester teaching at unc, she did a good job. If you listen and go to her with questions, you will be fine. Some of these reviews r ac insanely unwarranted

Her class is about what I expected. idk why she has so many horrible ratings but she's lovely! Her lectures were good and her grading policy was reasonable. HW was 28% of the grade. 2 midterms and a final (all very similar to the practice tests). She improved a lot from her previous ratings so don't be scared to take her class.

Teressa Bergland has high expectations for everyone in the class and you can tell by how she holds herself and the exams. I have learned so much in this class because of the harsh grading and difficult exams but feedback was very delayed for midterms and homework, the exams covered too much content with no curve and harsh grading.

I hope she gives students less work in the future, and finds assignments better tailored towards understanding the content. Exams were confusingly worded, difficult MCQ's & required very in depth understanding. I feel she didn't want to give marks we deserved, petty at times. Would be nice if she narrowed the content, there's too much to remember.

This class was way too fast paced for the amount of depth it entailed. Midterms almost biweekly when assignments hadn't been returned (no feedback). Lots and Lots of content, covered to a shallow level through inadequate slides (consisted mainly R output with no descriptions). The final exam was way too comprehensive, I think she expected too much.

Teaching wise she's not as bad as these reviews make it seem. However, her structure's terrible, 4 midterms which took ages to be marked, weekly assignments taking minimum 4/5 hours to do not indicative of exams and just repetitive and superfluous in a nonpedagogical manner. Mostly self learnt with ChatGPT, and attending lecture's didn't help much.

She is understanding in office hours, but is hard to understand during lectures. She is very academic, so it makes it hard for her to teach an introductory course. She gave revisions for the midterms, but they are very difficult and not similar to her practice tests. This is her first year at UNC, so she may be better next semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
“400-level should be hard” collapses instantly once you realize 455 has intro-level prereqs (155/120), while lower-numbered classes like 435 and 445 require heavy probability theory and are famous for their difficulty.
If course number were meaningful, 445 would be easier than 455-  and anyone who believes that has clearly never touched either.

By the “400-level = harder” logic, STOR 455 is apparently more advanced than STOR 445 and STOR 435! If someone truly thinks 455 is supposed to be harder than 445 simply because the number is bigger, I honestly don't know what to tell them except:
please stop pretending the STOR numbering system is a difficulty ranking. It's embarrassing.

Any tiny question gets interpreted as a personal attack, and her responses are often defensive and unnecessarily rude. Meanwhile, the class has been suffering through unclear lectures, mismatched exams, and painfully slow grading for weeks. She acts like she's the one being “mistreated,” when students are the ones genuinely stressed and struggling.

I honestly don't know why people care so much about receiving grades fast—you can't change anything that happened in the past. She definitely has room for improvement, but always keep in mind all the reviews here are pretty subjective.

I wish people were kinder. While this semester was difficult, it was a 400-level statistics course, and it was meant to be challenging. I agree that Professor Bergland has room for improvement, as do all professors. It was clear she was trying her best and I felt that the tests were reasonable, especially since we were given studying materials.

Dr. B is not a good professor, but she is not a monster by any means. She's nice and you can talk to her, but I just don't think this job is the best for her. She has poor time management and panders for pity, which gets old quick. Her inefficiency when it comes to grading is extremely frustrating and the course content is DIFFICULT. Don't take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I do not understand other reviews. Is she the best professor? No, but she's a fine one. It's clear that she's adjusting to teaching here, but, her exams were quite fair. You'll struggle if you don't show up to class/study, but you'll do fine if you pay attention. Not an easy A, but you'll get a good grade if you show up and put in a little effort.

This professor is awful. The exam questions are very vague and uses weird wording to explain concepts (i.e. she said to "fudge" the proportions). She is super disorganized and wants you to feel bad for her by saying "I'm trying my best. I just haven't gotten sleep!" I felt bad the first time she said that but then she kept using it as an excuse.
did she not think when she got the job as a professor that it would entail grading assignments and helping student learn? like girl what did you expect
Still haven't gotten our grades for a midterm we took the week after halloween. Nothing is graded, nothing is organized, cannot recommend this class less.
Hanged, drawn, and quartered would be too light a punishment.
Did she vote for Trump?

Wow, 400 level class shouldn't be easy. The I guess you must feel 445 is MUCH EASIER than 455 because the course number is lower! Why didn't you go to MIT but end up here? Who remembers the prereq is 155/120?

A “teaching” assistant professor who does not have any idea how to teach. If she really wants to show off her knowledge, why didn't she get a research position? Maybe torturing students makes her pathetic little ego feel better.
i never looked both ways when i crossed the street going to this class, lost any will to live and my 4.0. STAY AWAY

She talks to students like we're wasting her time. Every question is met with a condescending or dismissive tone. Instead of helping, she seems annoyed that you don't magically already know everything. Easily the most unprofessional attitude I've seen from a professor.

This professor gives off the vibe that she doesn't want anyone to succeed. Exams are impossible, expectations are unrealistic, and she seems proud when students are overwhelmed. If you need support, clarity, or basic respect, you won't get it here. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class made me feel like the professor actually enjoys watching students drown. Everything is intentionally confusing, exams don't match lectures, and she is dismissive when you ask for help. It honestly feels like she's proud when the class is stressed or miserable. I've never had a class that felt so actively hostile to student success.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bergland means well, but she is so focused on explaining everything in the most detailed, "statistically correct" way possible, that she can end up making an easy topic sound hard. I wouldn't take another class with her, and there are many things she needs to improve on as a teacher, but some of these reviews are way too harsh.

These reviews are crazy. People were mad because she didn't have the extra credit project graded before it was literally possible (predicting point differential and steals from NBA games) because the games hadn't even finished yet!! She takes a while to grade the tests but the exams were fair, it's a 400 level class it isn't supposed to be easy.

There's only so much incompetence you can attribute to being new. 455 is not known to be difficult, but I can see many new STOR majors being discouraged after taking it with her. Slow and harsh grader with an incredible victim mentality. Just take it with any other professor.
The final is in 3 hours and we have not received homework grades from October. Grading is overly detailed and harsh with too many petty points taken off

Her exams were okay (but def not easy) but there wasn't enough time.  She's disorganized but her notes were helpful even though you still need to study on your own. I have no idea what my final grade is because she stopped updating our grade back in October. She offered revisions and re tests but never graded them.
Terrible slides, and that is all she teaches from. She expects you to understand material on a 10x deeper level than what is ever taught. Don't take 455 with her, every other 455 professor is easier.

455 is the easiest of the STOR required classes. She makes it so it's not. She makes you know every minor detail for a test, and her homework does not prep you for the exams at all. She is very harsh on a curve, and I know absolutely nobody who is doing well. She wants you to pity her with her "silly me" act, but she is the worst. Stay away.

I'm a senior and she's the worst professor. In most stor courses, professors who give hard tests will offer many extra credits or curve. Those who do not offer curves usually give fair exams. But she did neither. Only one point ec for doing a whole project. She will take points off for missing a really tiny thing, while your whole answer is correct

The worst, least flexible professor I've ever had. Her responses to reasonable questions are incredibly rude and unprofessional - for example, "Give it a minute to breathe!" in response to a question about the extra credit project. She makes everything all about herself. The content really isn't too bad - it's the professor!
So bad, even worse than awful. Mandatory participation, really comfusing group project, heavy homework but useless for exams, heavy tests with all tiny details and really HARSH grader.

Don't take she can't teach. I'd rather climb Mt. Everest with no oxygen tank. It is 3 days after the exam and the most recent grade we have in is from October. She is delusional and believes that we are all the problem and refuses to accept she could have messed up. No one I know is doing well in this class and she should probably find a new job.
Unclear expectations on exams (which were extremely difficult). Disorganized content and untimely grading. Very harsh and inflexible professor.

She seems like a nice person and is passionate but is completely disorganized and inexperienced. Her office hours aren't helpful, don't bother. If you take her you will have to do extra work and self study to get a good grade. Having to pay for her hw software sucks too. Midterm 2 and the final were a disaster, not enough time and too hard.

I did not imagine the other reviews will be so harsh on her. She is a quite new professor and might not be very experienced at explaining in the most concise and clear way, but she is definitely not awful. She is very kind and fun. She has extra credit opportunity and one exam dropped. The course structure is very clear. Exams to me seem fair
Even 1 is too much
Test are much longer and harder than other professors, and she graded harshly and slowly. Do not take any course with her
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her test structure is difficult. Not enough time to complete exams.
Some things aren't for everybody. She should choose a new profession.

The content itself shouldn't be this difficult but she makes it feel like it is. The actual exams are absolutely nothing like the practice exams, and she doesn't provide enough time for how insanely long she writes them. She also takes extremely long to get grades back (1 month per exam) which makes it difficult to gauge progress in the course.

You need the textbook to survive this class bc she will just read off slides in the most boring manner. She is nice, but that is different from good. She is poorly organized and is constantly going "woe is me!" bc of how poorly she plans and manages her time. Haven't gotten multiple assignments graded (from months ago) and the final is in two days.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is her first year teaching and you can tell she is very smart but just awful at teaching. Take any other professor. Midterm 2 and the final was nothing like the practice she gave us. Made the exams too long; so many people ran out of time. Just reads off slides and never gives any examples.

She is very off putting and harsh when she lectures. It's her first semester teaching and it shows. Takes forever to grade, makes exams way too long for time given, always has to move deadlines because of disorganization, and over complicates material. Also was 15 mins late for the final because she printed the exams in a different language.

you need a background in statistics to do well in this class, from high school or a previous course. the notes posted after class are kind of helpful but it was mostly self teaching for me and the midterms are pretty hard with barely enough time. going to class feels useless but attendance is mandatory

The other reviews are quite harsh, especially considering this is her first semester at UNC. This is a hard course, and while the extended time needed to return grades is frustrating, it's clear to me that she's trying her best. My one comment is I wish she were more open to 'helpers' such as a curve, a larger cheat sheet, etc.

I don't like this woman. She's a poor instructor - just reads from slides (with information taken straight from the textbook) and live codes. Nothing makes sense, and she is HARSH. Exams are unfairly graded, not to mention returned to months after the exam date bc she manages her time so poorly. No curve and vehemently against any grade drops.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: A lot of the difficulties with this class will probably get better as she gets more experience teaching. The main thing was the SUPER slow grading that was overly detailed. The tests themselves are written in a vague, overcomplicated way. If you have experience in R and go to class you will be fine.
Prof Bergland is a goat. clear expectations, lectures, and HW. super reachable outside of class and honestly pretty funny

She is not a good teacher. She does not know how to teach. I think if you let me watch Khan Academy all year I would do 100x better in this class. Her midterms are unbelievably hard and long so much so that no one finished on time for both. DO NOT TAKE DO NOT LISTEN TO THE GOOD REVIEWS. I'd rather do anything else she is the worst.

First year prof, very evident. Exams far too long, struggles to convey lecture material in a sensible way. Very knowledgeable, just poor at teaching it to students. Practice exams don't align with midterms, hard to know what to study. Doesn't seem to truly care for her students' success. Highly recommend another professor - fries in the bag Teressa

Do not take with her please spare yourself the pain. Only offered test corrections after the entire class did terrible on the exam. She does not lecture well and just expects us to understand everything...it's an introductory course. Worst teacher I have ever had. I am doing better in a physics class than this class I'm an Econ major btw.

people are too harsh. Dr. Bergland is incredibly caring (go to office hours!) and accessible. clear lectures, take notes and you will do well. allows corrections for exams, and minimal HW.  plenty of online resources provided. one of my favorite professors i've had at UNC.

I disagree with most other reviews. Dr. Bergland follows consistent structure with her lectures and provides clear notes on canvas if you miss a lecture. Super caring, incredibly kind in office hours. Offers test corrections. Overall great prof, would take again, and the class had very minimal HW.
Terrible!!! So unorganized. Lectures are not only confusing but completely irrelevant to how she does exams.

I have never pass/failed a class until this one, and so glad I did. She is BRUTAL! So unfriendly and unfair, always trying to make you feel bad for her. Her practice (which she frequently forgot to provide) were nothing like the exams, and on the final we only get a 3x5 index card. It is possible to survive her class and learn in it but it's awful.

She is knowledgeable but the worst professor I've ever had (and I'm a senior). Tests are 73% of total grade, requiring memorization of every tiny detail. Slowest grader ever and unfair when she finally got around to it. Constantly complaining, rude and condescending, no regard for students wellbeing. Would've enjoyed the class if not for her.

She is clearly is knowledgeable about stats, but is not good at explaining it for an intro stats course. She does not write fair exams, and our second midterm was so bad she let us do a retake. That being said, she does offer revision for exams and is nice in office hours.
She never explains anything unless you ask, she just writes everything and expect you to know

She definitely is new to teaching but she will improve with feedback. She offers test corrections on both exams along with a full credit retest on a difficult exam question. The class content can get a bit difficult but overall she seems knowledgable and does give many chances for questions. Not much homework. Exams are long but fair.

She definitely has her quirks but very passionate and not bad. I took AP stats in high school which made it a little easier to succeed but I think the exams are fair. So far, they have been quite long but I think she will improve with that as she keeps teaching. Don't let the other reviews scare you. Pay attention in class and follow the examples
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst Professor I've ever had. She is so incredibly unorganized and her lectures are practically irrelevant to her Exams. Good luck going to her for office hours....she'll just respond to your question with another question. I have no idea how UNC took her on as a professor.

It's Prof Bergland's first year teaching, and it shows. She is clearly very knowledgeable in her field but is not good at conveying content. Both exams were ridiculously difficult and far longer than the practice exams. Test corrections for partial points back are allowed but it hardly matters when over half the class failed the exam anyway.

Do not take it with her. I understand that she is a new professor, but it is ridiculous that she can get away with what she has. Her exams are so long that no one finished, and she took months to get our grades back. We got our second midterm grades back the week before LDOC. Her lectures are also very hard to follow. Also kind of standoffish.

She was very condescending when confronted about her policies and truly feels like she does not care for her students. Very knowledgable woman, but struggles conveying information to students and her class policies are very cut and dry even when majority of the class failed the second midterm. Would not recommend at all.

She gives FOUR hand-written midterms without cheatsheet. The exams were confusingly worded. Forced group assignments were pointless and just made students pick up the slack for others. When people asked for help or changes, she responded in a condescending way that made it clear she didn't care. One of the most discouraging classes I've taken.

She gives you 4 midterms that are all way more difficult and longer than the practice material or homework. Her expectations are unclear, and she is generally unpleasant. She gives group homework assignments that are really annoying to complete. Overall, the course was not managed well and was too difficult for what it should have been.

She takes forever to grade everything. Throughout the semester I have had no idea how I am doing in the class. The homework has nothing to do with the midterms. She changed the format of the final exam a week before we have to take it.

Terrible class. Lectures unclear, practice exams nothing like the real ones. Four midterms and a final where you only get a 3×5 card. Exams are confusing and way too hard for the prereqs. She's condescending and not supportive. Worst professor I've had in the STOR department. If you can avoid taking a course with her, please do yourself a favor.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors in STOR. Contents are pretty easy but she made the test extremely long and hard, compared to other professor's (She provided as practice). There are four midterms and she gets grades back extremely slow. There're 4 midterms and a final, she only allows a toilet paper size cheat sheet (3x5) for the cumulative final. AVOID

Nicest professor I've ever had at UNC. She literally let us do test corrections and the practice exams were exactly like the exams, which never happens. Bitter freshman on here don't know how good she made it for us. Lectures are giving you exactly what you need to succeed, but she uses chalk board with slides.

Exams are unnecessarily hard in comparison to other sections of the class. Not one person finished the second midterm, and grades are not returned until over a month after the exams. She is very knowledgable on the topic, but her lectures are hard to follow and she is not a very approachable professor. Overall would not recommend.

Lectures are odd and don't teach material well. Exams have been terrible, she makes them different from practice exams and makes them too long. She is a new professor so tried to give her a break but its gone too far. Took the midterm a month ago and do not have full grades.

Her exams are excessively long and often feel unnecessarily difficult. While she considers feedback, many policies stay unchanged despite ongoing concerns. Her lectures can be vague and difficult to follow, particularly for students who are new to the subject. It's clear that she is knowledgeable, but struggles to communicate concepts clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams were miles too long and grades never came back in under a month. I also felt that they were too difficult as did many other students. Her lectures were long and tedious and she is not especially approachable. She tried to implement student feedback but was not super successful. I think her heart is in the right place but her teaching is not.

I took the honors section of chem430 and loved it. We did a capstone project and got to present our work at the Undergraduate Research Symposium. I was able to learn new how to work with data and even apply some of what I did to my own research! It was hard at first but I learned a lot about myself and team science. This was my fav class at UNC.

Dr. Brunk is kind and clearly cares about her students. She is very busy, as most research faculty are but she answers questions when you bring them to lecture. The flipped classroom can be an adjustment, but it reflects med school style learning. Biochem is challenging (DUH). Homework load is heavy-it helps and can be a grade saver for exams

This class was really hard but really good. It changed my view of medicine and it changed what I want to do with my life. I love the real world applications and learning how to work with data. I loved the lectures on precision medicine and things that are really happening in science.

Took Brunk because Hogan's section was full - worst mistake ever. My friends in Hogan's section had a walk in the park compared to what Brunk put our class through. Prone to mistakes in videos/lecture, very confusing explanations when asked for clarification (which I had to ask at office hours bc she never responded to my emails!), tricky exams.

She is rarely available and actively makes it harder for you to find help. She doesn't let you email her so you can only get help from the TAs. I had to have my final exam rescheduled and she refused to help me out. Keep in mind it was an EXTREMELY easy fix. Don't expect any notes or videos to be posted, and her modules don't match with the exams.

Dr Brunk is very nice, but not a great lecturer. There were mistakes on nearly every assignment including concept check quizzes and exams. The lectures were quite confusing at times. I couldn't get answers for the exam problems I got wrong because she doesn't release keys to us OR the TAs, and I could never make her office hours.

Dr. Brunk has a unique style of teaching for her class that some like and others do not. In order to do well in this course I would suggest preparing to understand the concepts on your own outside of class.  Dr. Brunk is good at teaching but it just seemed like her style of teaching was out of date. Also took long times to return tests.

Genuinely don't know why she provides us with an email to send questions to. Also, you'd think having only video lectures would result in clarity and infrequent speech errors, but that's why you're the student and not the professor.

Professor is hard to reach, takes a few follow ups for a response, even with the designated email. Final exam date was told after having “TBD” in the syllabus up until almost two weeks before the final. Flipped classroom, 0/10. Tests included small details from DEs, practice exams unhelpful. Grading scale somewhat curved to help though.

This is why research faculty shouldn't teach classes. It seemed like Brunk didn't have time to teach the class and didn't care about the students in it. Very disorganized: never released answer keys for exams, incorrect answers on CCQs, lecture content often contradicted videos but barely able to get ahold of her through email to ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible class. The content itself shouldn't be bad, but Brunk is incredibly inefficient in lecture while also not teaching anything. She was extremely difficult to get in contact with and to communicate with. The coding for this class had almost no guidance and Brunk was very unhelpful. 0/10.

Brunk teaches biochem fine... the class had its own issues. Quizzes had wrong answers that wouldnt get fixed. Exam content wasn't weighed well: class emphasized big on topics just for there to be 1-3 exam questions on it. Wouldnt drop a quiz during the snow storm. Coding projects (DEs) were annoying. I didnt learn any Python I could practically use
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Data exploration assignments are accompanied by a quiz, where the questions are incoherent. They refer to the wrong section of the DE, they have demonstrably multiple correct answers for questions that are choose 1, and multiple answer choice is on for questions that specifically ask for 1. Canvas quizzes are frustrating beyond content difficulty.

Interesting method with adding coding into the material. Biochem is a bit tough but the layout is manageable. If you come to class and ask questions about the material from the lectures you will be fine. Lots of opportunities outside the exams to get your grade up.
Flipped classroom is confusing and no one likes it. Weird assignments, like python coding but its more like reading about how the code is made than learning coding.

Flipped classroom, meaning watch an 60+ min of lecture video before class and lectures are practice questions, they go incredibly slow because, well, she didn't actually teach the material. Writes small on whiteboard?? for some reason in a GSB classroom. No attendance. Believes in the flipped class too much, unorganized/a little incoherent in class

Dr. B, is incredibly sweet, caring, and fair. They create a supportive learning environment, encourage participation, and provide clear, engaging lectures. Their grading is fair with helpful feedback, and they're always available to assist students. An exceptional professor overall!

Dr. Brunk uses innovative technology in her teaching, which can feel challenging at first, but she provides all the resources needed to succeed. Her lectures are well-organized, and she explains complex concepts clearly. She also dedicates class time to discussions, giving students the chance to ask questions and deepen their understanding.

Dr. Brunk is not a great lecturer, but she cares about the class and tries to engage the students as much as possible. The course content is interesting, but the flipped classroom model really did not work for me and it was hard to motivate myself when we would just do a few practice problems after a 30-60 minute lecture video the night before
take the class with any one else. would take weeks to get exams back when she had less than a 50 person class. so so so boring. hated the flipped classroom and felt like I learned nothing

Exams were straightforward as long as you studied the lectures and did the homeworks. Textbook reading is not required at all. Pre-lecture quizzes are a hassle, but manageable. Also, class isn't as test heavy as usual due to a decent portion of the grade dedicated to protein modeling in Python, which was a grade boost and gave breaks btw content.

The class isn't based off readings which is nice, but the research assignments are difficult even though they were interesting. Overall, if you put in the work you should be fine. Just prepare to be frustrated if you need her help. Hard to reach, lots of question mistakes that she would end up docking you points for, gets worse as semester goes on

These other reviews are really harsh. This class is a walk in the park compared to Orgo. almost every stem class at UNC is flipped classroom and you can't be in a 400 level chem class if you're not willing to do work outside of class. She's clearly very smart, just not the best teacher in the world. I will say she was disorganized and hard to reach
I truly have no words to fully explain how disastrous taking CHEM 430 with Brunk was. Just read the other reviews and let that speak for itself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Horrible communication. Late to office hours. No exam question answer key or practice exams. PowerPoints don't have explanations on them when uploaded. Vague lectures with difficult quizzes/exams. New material last week of class with final 2 days after. More focus on programming than teaching biochem. Barely any partial credit. DO NOT TAKE!

- ARS students did not receive feedback on their second nor third midterm before the final
- non ARS students only received feedback on the third midterm the DAY before the final
- Regularly shows up late to office hours
- 5 quizzes and 3 assignments due the week of LDOC. New material on LDOC. Final exam is 75 questions and is 2 days after LDOC.

Its a flipped classroom that will have you watching mostly 45 minute lecture videos before each class. Dr. Brunks questions on her quizzes are typically extremely vague, have typos, and make you even more confused about the concepts. She also never responded to any of my emails, so I would avoid her at all costs if possible. Seriously, avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Tough grader--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible. I had to take Brunk because Hogan's class was full. Her exams have stuff we cover in class for like 2 minutes & are incredibly confusing & made to fail students. Like one exam was completely select-all questions with no partial credit which was ridiculous. She is not accessible outside of class & is careless with students' time.

She implements flipped classroom (so you are teaching yourself). Her quizzes and test are very confusing, and she words everything very weirdly. Her grading policy is also ridiculous, the class has no TAs, peer mentors ETC. She is NOT accessible outside of class, so do not expect your emails to have a response. Her office hours don't help :(

Nah. She can't teach, she's not very accessible, and she puts stuff on exams that we didn't cover in class or the lecture videos. Speaking of lecture videos, she often uploads them, and their corresponding quizzes, very late (one time she uploaded a quiz at 11PM and expected us to do it by 2:30 the next day). If I could give her 0 stars, I would.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class was mainly focused on Dr. Butler going through slideshows and discussing readings in groups. It's not the most organized, but as long as you somewhat pay attention, the class wasn't hard. If you commit some time to the readings or oral histories, getting an A is very doable. That said, you could get away with skimming the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: If you're looking for an easy or filler class, do not take this course. It is graded on around six different components, making it more demanding than expected. Dr. Butler is a good person, but the lectures and assignment details were very unorganized. The exams were also poorly structured and much longer than they should have been.
Do not take this course if you're just looking for an easy filler. Dr. Butler is very kind, but the lectures are often unorganized and the exams are much longer than they need to be.
Really great professor. Very accessible. LOTS of work. You will discuss the readings in class, so you have to actually do them. Learned a lot though.
I love Dr. Butler. She's amazing, grade very lightly and super understanding.

There are a decent amount of readings. There is a group interview, and a final paper along with a 10min presentation. There are only 2-3 homework assignments, and there were about 3-4 tests, all being online, including the final. The class was decently heavy on participation but it was always fun and usually was discussing the reading with someone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Definitely in the top 2 STEM professors I've had at UNC. STOR 435 is very hard material but he is hilarious and great at explaining the material, and there are many office hours every week.
Great class. Teaches very well. Only issue was loads of homework.

Shankar is incredible! STOR 435 is a very hard class, but he explains things so well and makes the course as straightforward and clear as possible, and the exams are very fair. Lots of homework, but they are very helpful. He is also hilarious.

Highly recommend taking him for 435! Very fair exams and grading, and he allowed us to use a cheat sheet on the final. The hws take a while, but the exams were all variations of hw or practice exam problems. He's also very accessible outside of class and explains difficult concepts in 435 well. Definitely would have done much worse if not for him.
Amazing guy. Super funny and knowledgeable. If you have to take 435 with anyone make sure it's him.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bhamidi is an excellent professor and cares deeply about the success of his students. On multiple occasions I was able to meet with him outside of his scheduled office hours because I had class during his office hours. He curved the grades at end of semester. Also a funny lecturing that makes a hard class more enjoyable.
I had Dr. Bhamidi for 435H. He's a super nice guy, and class is very manageable if you put in some work. Take Probability with him if you can!!

Shankar was great. He explains the course material very clearly, grades very fairly, and the tests are written very clearly despite the difficult course material. His self-deprecating sense of humor was amazing and kept the class alive. Somehow got an A, thanks in large part to Shankar's clear teaching. My only wish is that he recorded lectures.

Prof. Bhamidi was great this semester! He made calc 3 seem super easy, and although there were a lot of HWs, quizzes, and labs each week (apart from worksheets in class to track attendance), the workload didn't seem unbearable. Be prepared to go to class since he uses the blackboard a lot, and uploads empty slide decks. Stay on track and it's easy!

Shankar made calc 3 very easy to understand by showing us how it is used in the real world. There are weekly homework's, quizzes, and labs. You need to go to class because he works out the problems on the board, and he tends to show super long proofs that may cause you to zone out, but a great professor overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, there are a bunch of assignments for this class that help to balance out your grade and it helps you understand the material well. Explains the material really well during the lectures and is very accessible outside of class. All around great professor.

One of my favorite professors! Coming into the class, I was really intimidated by the topics on the syllabus due to previously struggling a lot with calc. Luckily, Shankar is an excellent lecturer and explains complicated concepts in a digestible way. No surprises on exams; they reflected the difficulty of HW/quizzes. Super nice guy. Def recommend!

Shankar is one of my favorite professors at UNC. The exams were fair and always questions we had seen before in homework or class. You have lots of grade buffers to boost your grade. The final was harder than our other exams, but not unmanageable. If you don't go to class, you will do poorly. His lectures are very important to do well.

Probability is a hard subject, but Shankar's explanations are thorough and his exams are very fair. The class is accessible to people without much statistics background. The exam questions are easier, multiple choice versions of the homework questions. If you stay on top of the homework, it is not too difficult to do well in Shankar's class.

The content is very hard, but Bhamidi is a good professor. It is really easy to get behind. Please pay attention in class and stay up to date because it is so easy to get off track and never get back on.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: GOAT. He was a very clear lecturer and explainer and was very nice to the class. He wants you to learn the material but understands the content is hard. His tests aren't too hard (most of my misses were bc reading errors). There is a lot of stuff to do and learn, but he makes it as easy as possible while still teaching you everything. Seek him out!

An absolutely amazing professor. It is very important that you go to lectures as I didn't halfway through and my grade suffered because of it. Regardless though, it was an amazing class and he makes a really difficult subject super accessible. Best STOR 435 professor out there.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Bhamidi is a great lecturer, the reality is just that this is a really hard class and it is very easy to get behind. There is a homework and a quiz each week, and he allows a note sheet for the final (but not the midterms). Go to lecture and pay attention because he doesn't post notes, just slides.

Shankar gives you everything you need to succeed in this class. Homeworks are lengthy and can get difficult, but he is super accessible during office hours and explains problems very well. The lectures were good, and in case you miss lectures there are scribed notes for every class. Awesome teacher and awesome person with a great sense of humour.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Shankar was a great professor. It's easy to pass with some effort, and not impossible to get an A in. He is accessible outside of class and makes it very clear he cares about students and their performance. Homework and quizzes are open-note which really helped. No midterms, just quizzes.

I was extremely scared to take this class but Shankar makes it easy to get a good grade if you put in the effort. Homeworks got harder and harder as the semester progressed but he is really accessible during office hours, letting you stay to listen to other students questions (it was on zoom) while working. Quizzes were easy if you were prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Bhamidi is definitely your best choice for STOR 435. The class is tough and he knows it but he accommodates for that. Super approachable during office hours. We had weekly open note quizzes along with lengthy homeworks due every week. Final was 30% but not terrible if you study. Overall a positive experience and Dr. Bhamidi is hilarious.

I also took STOR435 with him and my opinion remained the same. He is without a doubt one of the most intelligent, thoughtful, and accessible professors I have had as a computer science and statistics major at UNC. Do not miss an opportunity to take a class with him!

Dr. Bhamidi is a great instructor with clear expectations and grading criteria. Lectures are well-organized but focus a bit too much on perhaps unnecessary mathematical proofs. Assignments take a VERY long time and contained a computational and mathematical portion. The end-of-semester group project is great for building real-world ML experience.

He gives lots of homework BUT if you go to office hours and pay attention in lecture (which isn't hard to do because he makes them very interesting), you'll be fine. His STOR 435 class is very thorough, organized, clear, and overall amazing. Also, very kind and helpful person!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Bhamidi is funny and teaches the class well enough, but I think he just moves too quickly in lecture. He assumes you know exactly what is going on and most of the time I did not. Also, assigns homeworks that are due EVERY class that are hard and take a decent amount of time to do. I think the difficulty of the class was what got me

The best professor I have had at UNC so far. He is inspiring, intelligent (and great at explaining), clear with what he expects on homework and exams, and is readily available to respond to questions. Also has a good sense of humor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. B is a fantastic professor! Though the material is difficult he does a great job communicating it in a clear way. If you utilize his helpful office hours and make sure to actually engage the material (homework, practice exams etc.) you should be fine in the class despite the difficulty. He tests on understanding not memorization of the material
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Friendly and casual professor. Class is pretty easy; a couple of group presentations, a one-page paper, and a final project (research paper and presentation). Lectures are a bit dry despite the fascinating subject matter and he posts the slides; you do not have to pay rapt attention. Not math-intensive. A reasonable choice for a first-year seminar.

Bhamidi has a great personality which helped me decide to go to class for each lecture and actually listen to what he had to say, no matter how boring the subject material. He made every lecture more fun and was also pretty clear-cut and super helpful. He cares about his students and the class itself was not too hard to pass. Highly recommend.

Shankar is awesome! Best professor I've had so far. He's so helpful and cares so much about his students. He's super organized and clear and the class is really interesting. He goes so far to engage students in super interesting lectures and is also hilarious. Best dude ever seriously take him if you can

Really nice guy who knows your stuff. The class was challenging at times, but I think that's more a product of the material and not his teaching. He assigns homework every class, but it was never too long and you got feedback on it. I'd recommend him.
One of the best professors I've ever had. Very good teacher and eager to help. Exams are a clear test of knowledge.

He's really friendly and makes jokes during class.  The class wasn't the easiest A, but that was due to the inherently difficult material, not his teaching style.  He explained things simply and concisely.  If you had trouble understanding a concept the way he explained it, he was happy to explain it another way.
Very clear in his expectations, and transparent on what's on exams, etc. Not the easiest A, but fair for sure.

His class is similar to a high school class where you have homework to turn in every class. The book is not what he teaches in class, the tests seem easy but then you fail and wonder why. They are just tricky. Its such a boring class and he tests you on excel so take a teacher who is not that nit picky and who doesn't test you on stupid things.

Friendly teacher who recognizes how boring the class is. He shows a definite interest in both statistics and teaching. The class starts out easy and gets much harder after the first midterm, but he holds review sessions and office hours regularly so it shouldn't be a problem.

He is a pretty good teacher. He's pretty funny and not intimidating or mean so people aren't shy to ask him questions. The first midterm was on 1 chapter, which made him make the 2nd midterm a little too hard, and the final was bearable (he let you use 1 page of notes). Just do the homework and go to his office hours for help and you'll get an A!

INLS 490 is one of the most valuable classes that makes me feel more prepared for the job market.  Despite the fact that I am not a technical person, Professor Bhattacharya went out of her way to encourage me. You truly get what you put into it. The final project was creating a training; although we had to self-learn the software, it was worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: INLS 490 - Reema was accessible outside of class, however, I feel like she did not care for us at all. Her instructions were so confusing and she would contradict things she said. She would also change up her idea of projects after I had already submitted them. She is just all over the place. Overall, I can't say I learned much but it was easy

*This review is for INLS 490* Reema was really accessible. She always made it known that she was available for you to ask questions, and she gave great feedback. Assignments were mostly straightforward, but Reema was always more than happy to clear up anything and provide help.

taking inls 490, the learning design class. she gives off this superiority attitude where she feels like she's better than everyone else. her feedback are short and not helpful. she doesn't seem to care about her students. her modules are full of spelling errors, which show how little effort she put in and she don't care. 

avoid this class

Prof accused me of plagiarizing the final despite having no evidence and threatened to fail me if I didn't respond in a day (during finals). Obviously I didn't cheat and was able to prove it. Make sure to keep a record of all of your work. If you are looking to spend hours on assignments just to be accused of cheating, then this class is for you.

The class structure and course site were convoluted. The course is simply a laundry list of links to articles and videos with little "teaching". For this professor's section of the course, there were eight assignments, a midterm, and a final. None of which helped me learn substantially. Recommend avoiding.
Wish she could stay at UNC longer! Loved her classes. Always used to look forward to see her in class!

I love Prof. Bhalla for reason that she focuses on learning real stuff than just grades. How can one not be fascinated to attend a class where a professor shows stand up comedies to facilitate language learning! She's super cool, I could approach her like a friend, she talks to students in their language by giving reference to Instagram memes, etc.

One of the best professors I have taken classes with so far. She is really understanding and tries to make students comfortable with the teaching materials. I would love to take class with her again and have enrolled with her course in the next semester. I am super excited!

Kanikaji is an alright professor but there have been many times where she does not show grace to her students. She is not extremely forgiving and the way that she grades is rather harmful -- in the sense that she takes points off like nobody's business. She is fair in class but expects a lot of participation -- talking once a class is not enough.

The grading scale is difficult, but it's not impossible to get an A. There are 8 quizzes; two are dropped. You essentially need near-perfect scores on the remaining six, but she tells you what the questions will be in advance. The best advice for this class is to go to office hours for your papers to talk about them well in advance of the deadline.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Approaches philosophical materials in a strange way, mixing high school-level Engl, Philosophy, Polisci, and Classics but lacks depth in any. Extremely tough grader, focusing on trivial details. Avoid 270 if you dislike being disciplined - only by rewriting papers to her exact suggestions will you earn a decent grade. Tokens make little sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's awesome, the only thing that sucks is her grading scale. It's almost impossible to get an A. She is so caring, engaging, etc. I thought I was going to hate everything about this class and I didn't, I actually kind of loved it. Seriously my ONLY issue is the grading scale, you have to get a perfect grade on almost everything to get an A.

She reduces grades when your interpretation is different than hers, even if you provide textual evidence. The class itself is insightful, though I don't think it reaches a philosophical level. The class material is philosophical but how we approach them is not. Grading is too tough and reading&writing is too much for a 200-level class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Such a sweet and caring professor. Lots of writing in this class, and more centered on philosophy rather than politics, but was great overall. Assignments were well spaced out with lots of notice in advance. Some tough prompts for assignments but her feedback and office hours were helpful.

Professor Bickford is kind and knowledgable but her class is TOUGH. She's a very harsh grader and expects expert knowledge from her students. The amount of work that you have to do is not comparable to the grade you will get - it is next to impossible to get an A. If your GPA is important to you, take another political philosophy class for credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Bickford is an amazing educator and you will realize that if you engage and put in the effort like she asks you to. She is a tough grader but there are opportunities to improve your grade via "tokens." She stresses attendance and you won't do well if you are absent and don't do the readings. Readings are manageable and worth your time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Ugh, love her! Very respectful towards students. The class is mostly a philosophy seminar (see: participation!) with lots of assigned readings & quite a bit of writing assignments. That being said, she is very flexible & considerate. The final was a self designed project so we got to be a bit creative and dive in deeper to what we wanted to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took her POLI276H class and I will be taking as many of her classes as my schedule will allow. I love classes, but it does have a bit of reading. Amazing discussions, very respectful, and always able to talk. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: If you don't have experience with political philosophy this class will not be easy. Dr. Bickford is a tough grader, but she gives a lot of feedback. She is a very kind and approachable person and is genuinely passionate about teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Embodies everything I used to hate about English classes in HS, encourages individual interpretation but says your interpretation is wrong. Only gives decent grades to those that think like her. Lowest paper grade at UNC was a 92 before this class, yet she said my writing quality concerned her that I had a learning disability.

Professor Bickford clearly cares about the material quite a bit, and you can tell that it's important to her that she doesn't just tell you about it, but that you learn it. She also gives very informative feedback on the papers, all of which are very short besides the final. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: By far the best professor I've had at Carolina. She is engaging and really cares about her students. The readings are tough, and she's a hard grader but if you're willing to work for it this class is a must!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Bickford is one of the most genuine Professors at UNC. She truly cares about her students and strives to treat everyone with respect. I'm not going to lie- she's a tough grader, but she gives awesome feedback and will most definitely help you to become a better writer. This class reading and writing heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The content itself is interesting and so is class discussion, but the grading process is convoluted. It is extremely different to improve grades on writing assignments because the process it nit-picky and no rubric is given. Little feedback given and she doesn't specify where you lose points. Take a different political thought class for poli major.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Bickford is one of the most brilliant and kindest people you'll meet. She's not just a good professor, but a phenomenal teacher as well. I appreciate her dedication to class. Her courses are well-organized and cover a good variety of topics. The type of writing she expects is likely different from what you're used to. A's are uncommon.

Dr. Bickford is a great professor in that she's incredibly knowledgeable and cares about the subject and her students. In this class, you have to read a lot for each period and write papers often. She's definitely a tough paper grader and you do have to talk a lot consistently to get a decent participation grade. Not an easy A, but rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Bickford is a wonderful teacher and facilitator in class. Get ready to read--a lot! Some familiarity with reading philosophy papers will help you a lot in this class. She really cares about you as both a student and a human being, and is so helpful in and out of class! Highly recommend taking this class, even though an A is unlikely.

Professor Bickford is incredible!!! Definitely one of the tougher graders at UNC, but I have learned so much from her class! Readings are a lot and often v dense, but if you genuinely want to learn and improve as a student, you should take a course form her! Also so willing to help students if they need it!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Bickford is amazing! A tough grader, but genuinely wants to help improve your writing and critical thinking. I have improved as a writer from taking this course. Lots of reading, very discussion based and small group work. Lots of writing but all of the material is incredibly interesting and she does an amazing job leading discussions!

The material is super interesting and Professor Bickford clearly cares about it. Classes are structured around participation, which makes it all extremely engaging and enjoyable. Professor Bickford is helpful and very supportive.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is a harsh grader- does not like giving out anything higher than a B-. It should be a good discussion based class, but she makes it so difficult that no one ends up learning because they're so worried about their grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is an AWESOME professor. However, she runs the class almost like a graduate seminar- there is an incredible amount of reading, and you have to print out everything. For our class, this was about 400 pages per person. RIP to my CCI Printing money. She is a tough grader, almost unneccessarily so, but she cares about how you do in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Excellent class. It's not an easy course for anyone just to slack and get a good grade, but if you work for it, it's surely worth it. Professor is super helpful, friendly, and inspiring. Class discussion is always in a great atmosphere. professor smiles when you talk to her, and she gets so excited when someone come up with good thoughts!

Professor Bickford is a great professor. The first year seminar I took with her is one of my favorite courses I have ever taken at UNC. If you're taking it because you expect an easy A, you probably won't get it. But the class discussions are incredibly interesting, and you will improve your writing and analytical thinking skills.

Great prof!  Really let's everybody tell what they think about the questions at hand.  Also, she's very serious about participation so don't think that you can join her class and not talk or do the readings, which can get dull at times.  However, the great discussions make it all worth it.
I had her for Feminism in Political Theory, great teacher, SO passionate about this topic, but you definitely have to do the readings, which are usually quite long and sometimes really difficult

Jackson picked some really interesting papers for us to discuss this year! I learned a great deal about ongoing issues surrounding AI, as well as more general Philosophy topics! He was pretty strict on the papers, but it was worth it in the end with an easy final exam. Jackson is a fun, young professor and I enjoyed taking his class!

Jackson is an AMAZING professor. He explains concepts clearly and obviously wants his students to learn and succeed. Very accessible and helpful office hours. Mandatory in-person group discussion posts every class, but basically graded for correctness. 4x papers that were super fun to write. Very lenient grader, just not many points to lose.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Down to earth and offers extensions. Reading before class, and then the next 2 classes, you spend time discussing and analyzing the argument presented. In each class, you turn in answers for participation credit. There are 4 papers and a final exam. In each paper, you argue against one philosopher in the unit. He gives amazing, detailed feedback!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved Beaver for orgo 2, genuinely wants his students to succeed and get the most out of his class. Orgo 2 is a hard subject theres no workaround, but if you put in the effort it is very doable. Listen to his suggestions on how to study. Attend GPSS and do the ULA worksheets. Sit in the front, ask and answer questions in class.

man he's a good prof but unless you're confident you know the material he's not worth it. his exams are the hardest out of the entire department and the stress is unreal. i got out with an A but then my physical health genuinely declined due to the stress solely from that class. unless you want your entire life to be chem, dont take him.

Beaver is a great guy and probably knows the course content he's teaching better than anyone. Yes the midterms are very challenging but the final is much more fair in my opinion. If you got through orgo 1 with a decent grade, you know what to expect with Beaver. Study hard for the midterms and practice practice practice and you will succeed.

Dr. Beaver is one of my favorite chemistry professors at UNC. He genuinely cares, will listen to student feedback, and is amazing at breaking down difficult concepts. His GPSS is super helpful and his class is very engaging. I highly recommend taking 262 with him.

Dr. Beaver is really nice and truly wants you to succeed. Explains content well during lecture and provides a lot of resources to succeed, but the exams are HARD. You need to do all of the practice material he offers and understand everything fully, but that's probably true regardless of the professor for organic chemistry.

His lectures are great and he's incredibly knowledgeable about the material. He expects lot from students, but also cares about learning if you want to learn. I'd recommend if you truly want an understanding of organic chemistry, take it with him, but if you want the best letter grade you can get, take it with someone else.

I enjoyed 262 with Dr. Beaver. His lectures make sure you will know the content. There's just a lot. Exams always have a few trippy questions, but fair overall. Did amazing on the first 3 and poorly on the final due to other stuff. An A is certainly possible if you spend 1-2 hours a day practicing. He gave some extra credit too so can't complain.

Orgo is just a hard class, and it takes a lot of time to understand and memorize it. Beaver was a good lecturer and 100% cared, but he made his exams SO HARD. You aren't screwed when you take him, you just need to know 110% of the content to do at least OKAY on the exams. It isn't like you can know 80% and make an 70 on the exam, you need 100%.

Dr. Beaver definitely knows his chemistry and is good at teaching it. He just creates next level difficult exams that are hard to do well on unless you 100% understand everything in the class. My highest score on any exam was a 66% and I would study about a week in advance.... I did much better in Zurcher's 261 and found her exams to be more fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Organic chemistry is just such a hard and content filled class. Dr. Beaver was a nice guy and lectures seemed to be helpful but his exams were next level hard. He is not the worst professor but if there Is an easier option, go with that one. Office hours were only held in 8 minute increments and sometimes answered questions a little backhanded.

Man, first stem class I took at unc as a transfer student and it makes me want to switch my major. Required iClicker in class, weekly quizzes online, no required practice but you're screwed if you don't do the recommended. Hard exams, I thought I could study but it just got worse as the semester went forward. Probably will retake w/ someone else.

I took CHEM262 with Dr. Beaver over the summer, and I can confidently say it was one of the best classes I have taken. Orgo is a dense subject, but with how lectures are given, the support outside of the classroom, and with enough practice problems, an A is possible. I plan to take intermediate organic chemistry with him! Do recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Literally the least accessible person on the planet. Ignores every email ever and didnt respond to any office hour requests. Went to one problem sesh and he made me feel stupid. Mid teaching style. Lectures weren't horrible, but him ignoring me made them horrible. Overall, came in with high expectations, left with a low GPA and anger in my veins.

Like other reviews are saying, Beaver is a good guy but his exams are awful. I did much better in orgo 1 with Zurcher and also prefer her teaching style. Beaver does want you to succeed and is nice in lecture. Can be oddly passive in office hours/1 on 1 interactions. Again though, his exams are SO hard so be warned

I took Orgo 1 with Zurcher and much preferred it to Beaver's Orgo 2. He has a tad bit of weirdness to him; gets very easily offended (became very passive aggressive the lecture after our second exam because students were less engaged and pissed at the exam difficulty). He wants you to learn, but its beaver method or death. Exams are hard .

Great lecturer, but was VERY standoffish 1-on-1 sometimes. Make sure he knows your name. Exams were EVIL & if you didn't know 100% of content exams will get you. I never got > a 90 on any exam but ended with an A thanks to Rogue Chem and solving every textbook problem. He was fair with points back and cared for his students-you WILL learn orgo 2.
Beaver wanted to see us succeed as shown by the 4 final EC points he provided. Be warned that he always tests the hardest parts of each concept and the "exceptions to the rule"

Orgo is difficult, but Beaver's engaging lectures and clear expectations make the class manageable and even enjoyable at times. He is tough, but honest and tries to connect with students and help them succeed. He knows it's hard and pushes you to get help EARLY. Keep up with your rxn cards, practice DAILY, and consider rogue chem for the final!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Please take any Orgo class you can with Zurcher. Beaver is not a horrible teacher; he is just condescending at times and creates the most diabolical exams you can imagine. 3 midterms (70 or below was the median on all) and just took the 70-question final. Class is hard but doable.
Dr. Beaver is an exceptional lecturer who really cares about his students.

Dr. Beaver does an amazing job working with the lecture hall, making the large lecture hall feel like a small classroom. You could tell he cares about what he's teaching and who he's teaching it to. His tests are supposed to be the hardest out of all the orgo professors, though. Also, his voice is very easy to listen to lol.
Dr. Beaver is great but the class itself is challenging. The material is difficult, but he makes an effort to give students the resources they need to succeed.

Dr. Beaver is truly a beacon of light in the UNC Chem department. While the class is difficult, Dr. Beaver made the material very accessible and was always down to help us out with material. He is a very effective and engaging lecturer. Sometimes he is a little sassy, but never condescending or mean. He also tries to be reassuring, which is nice.

Professor Beaver is a really great orgo instructor. The content is just really difficult. He is very accessible outside of class and makes an effort to learn your name and truly wants to see you succeed. I am satisfied with the grades I got in this course and feel that they were fair given I crammed before every exam.

Chem261 is a tough class, but Dr. Beaver was an incredible teacher. If you're considering taking orgo with him, do it. He's incredibly understanding and caring. He learned the names of everybody who participated in class and would say hi while walking around campus. Attend ULA sessions, don't be distracted during class, and STUDY! You'll do great!
It's a no from me dawg.

Liked beaver in 261/262, not as much in 460. 460 was v difficult & structured poorly imo. You must be VERY confident with orgo 1/2 content, esp orgo 2, even if you took it years ago. Majority of class did poorly esp on exam 1. Added 15 pt curve to exam 1, 10 pt curve to exam 2, & a curve at the end, which was v nice and unheard of in UNC chem dept

The class is definitely a lot of work, but Dr. Beaver's a good professor. He's very caring and explains the material well. Exams were also fair. Just make sure to keep up with the workbook problems and rxn flashcards.

Beaver's got good lectures and very accessible via OH so don't be intimidated. His LAs were just awesome! They single-handedly saved me in the class with super clear explanations. Study hard for the thermo exam, that by far is the hardest exam in the course. You've got this!

This class was so informative and engaging. Exams were hard but extra credit opportunities were given, and the final also had a take-home portion. Group presentations were a good grade boost and also enlightened us on modern orgo research. Dr. Beaver was also very helpful during 1-on-1 office hours.

CHEM 101 was horrible for me, so going into CHEM 102 I was terrified, but Dr. Beaver was a great lecturer and made the class interactive and easier to understand. The lecture was a launch so the class was only about 35 people. Dr. Beaver was respectful and his LAs were great too. The tests were difficult. Go to the LA review sessions!
this class was unnecessarily difficult with him. beaver is rude and condescending at times, and sometimes appears to have an ego issue. take with literally anyone else.

Chem 460 review. Lots of prerequisite knowledge required, make sure to brush up on orgo 2 before taking. Lots of pre-class reading, and exams were extremely difficult (be he did give a generous curve). The class has a large presentation component, which is fine, but just be aware.

This review is for 102. Dr. Beaver is a great professor. He made learning chem easier and made sure students understood as much as he could. Chem 102 at UNC is hard, and the exams are ridiculous. But Beaver is definitely the best professor I've had in the chem department and is passionate about what he does. I would definitely recommend him.

Verily, this course is no mere pursuit, but an odyssey of torment where only the steadfast glimpse enlightenment. The lecturer bestows knowledge in fire and fury, yet we, mere mortals, are left scorched, grasping at fleeting truths. My soul writhes beneath this incantation of madness! And yet, is not true wisdom born from suffering?

Dr. Beaver was awesome. Set the best foundation for Organic Chemistry and his lectures were very informative. He is very smart and forces you to think through the course material. His lectures are also engaging and I would definitely take him again. The only slight is his exams are difficult, but I learned so much in this course.

I was pleasantly surprised by this course. Joshua Beaver was extremely professional and knowledgeable. He always came prepared and stuck to schedule, never falling behind on the course material. He was genuinely compassionate with his students as well, encouraging participation and making a point to remember people's names.

Great course overall. Orgo here is hard but getting a good grade is definitely doable. Beaver is a very caring and engaging professor. I can see how he may come off as condescending sometimes but he's very empathetic and receptive in office hours. Don't take Orgo with too many other hard classes. That was my mistake and I didn't lock in enough.

It's UNC orgo, it's going to be a lot of content. I bombed the first test before learning how to prepare for this class. Skim the readings before class, don't spend too long on them, there's a lot of unnecessary info. Keep up with the workbook, it's the key to the midterms. Go to the ULA session and at least one problem solving session a week.

I love Beaver. He was amazing, and the class is very manageable if you stay on top of it. He has q&A sessions and office hours to help and genueinly wants to see you succeed. Many people said he seemed condescending, which at first he kinda did, but as soon as I talked to him a couple times he is the best prof ever.

It's definitely possible to succeed by doing workbook +textbook problems, ULA worksheets, going to q&a sessions -- uncommon most students with other hard classes. Midterms are pretty fair, but Beaver is not super accessible; condescending and judgy -- gatekeeps info at his q&as, so go to those if possible (or todd). Has a buffer for graded work.

Prof. Beaver was a nice guy and could be pretty engaging during class. However, lecture slides were often vague. Midterms were significantly harder than the final exam, and final grades experienced a slight curve. When in doubt about whether you should have received credit for an answer on a midterm, submit a regrade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Beaver is a wonderful lecturer and instructor.  Organic Chemistry is hard, and requires lots of practice and attention to detail; Dr. Beaver emphasizes these things daily in class, and puts a ton of effort into helping people correct their misconceptions.  Easily approachable, spent a lot of time making the class digestible. Curved final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Beaver cares about his students but I do not think he is a good lecturer. The slides are a bit confusing and his explanations were vague so we could "teach ourself". The review sessions only helped if you knew what you were doing and had a few questions. Orgo is one of those subjects that requires consistent studying so don't fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Orgo is fairly challenging and requires a lot of practice. Attention to detail is key in the course. As for Dr. Beaver, I don't have much positive to say. You ask him a question, he will not only not answer your question, but he will make u feel like a fool for even asking. I got more clear answers on EdStem, the TAs do better than he does.

I quickly came to the realization that some people are good at orgo and others just aren't. I did the preclass, ULA sessions, the GPSS, workbook, and slides every week and still did bad in the class.
