I would not say this course is easy because sometimes you do need to do something comparatively tricky, like write the correct citation format and blend three articles into one. However, she is very nice and caring, which does make studying much easier. She is about to graduate; cherish and take your final chance to study with her!

The BEST professor at UNC. Bjelland is the sweetest human I have ever met and heavily reminds me of Ms. Honey from Matilda. The assignments are straightforward and easy to succeed on. As someone who isn't the best at English, I got great grades in the class and found the material super interesting and helpful for the real world.

I had my ENGL 105 class in the evening so it was hard to come to class sometimes but Professor Bjelland made it such a good class. She is one of the sweetest people and is very understanding. Her class was very enjoyable and I liked all the work she assigned. Each assignment was clear and had a purpose. This was a relaxing and stress-free class.
very understanding and also overall such a nice and sweet person. the class is insanely easy and if you turn in work you will be fine!!

She made English very enjoyable and it felt more like a summer camp than an actual class. It was very stress-free and the rubric tells u exactly what she expects. She is super friendly and always had a smile on her face.  I would strongly recommend Professor B for ENGL 105!
Caring, friendly, and cute professor. Her classes in summer sessions are pretty relaxing, and we have enough time to do our assignments. Also, there're lots of group activities on class.
Super nice and helpful.

Just follow the rubric and submit the assignments on time and you'll be fine. Pretty sure she didn't dock people more than two or three points on a fifteen point assignment. She's also very understanding about mental health and being sick.
very sweet and accomodating! the class is pretty easy as well

Take home exams- as long as you go to office hours, he will help you get an A on all of them. As long as you participate in class every so often, you will do fine. Definitely a bias grader, helps if he likes you and you seem interested. Going to office hours is enough to get an A in the class.
Absolutely horrible. Worst class I've taken at UNC

reviews.comment: Do not take this class with this professor, whatever you do do not take this class. Exams are hard and are overly graded. This class is worse than Orgo.

Though the seminar itself is hard (advanced biology, genetics) the class is very manageable. Grades mostly come from take home exams and participation. Attend class, come to his office hours with exam questions and you'll be just fine. He just wants people to be interested in what he's so passionate about.

The MTs and finals are open note, collaborative, and Prof Bloom will help you out if you go to office hours. His main thing is that you show up to class (he doesn't take attendance, but he notices who is there), ask questions, and pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Bloom for Biol59 - A FYS about Genetics. It was unnecessarily hard, we barely had any information on how to do well on the exams and were graded so harshly on topics meant for advanced molecular biology students. I learned a lot from this class, but if you're looking for an easy seminar without background knowledge, STAY AWAY!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kerry is a very passionate teacher and knows so much about what he teaches. The class grade is very heavily weighted toward the take-home exams, but he is very willing to help you out if you go to office hours or work in groups. He does pay attention to who is in class, so participation is pretty important.

Professor Bloom is truly incredible and his passion for science is clear in the classroom. Throughout the semester the class requires students to lead to presentations. Your grade is composed of very few things but exams are all take home and collaborative. Professor Bloom is also accessible for exam questions during office hours!

It is a genuinely interesting FYS to take. Dr Bloom maintains a good balance between lecturing and student participating in his classes. 3 take home exams and participation were the only things which were graded for. The exams were questions which you could discuss and encourage you to think and apply knowledge. Would recommend.

The expectations for assignments are never clear and it felt like we were expected to read his mind. He was unable to explain things in terms that we could understand. The syllabus was a  lie and Dr. Bloom was incredibly disorganized.  Unless you have prior knowledge of molecular biology, I would not recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this class if you have no pre-existing knowledge of biology. Dr. Bloom is incredibly unorganized and he is very unclear about what is graded in the class. There are very few things graded and the syllabus he provided is complete lies. If you want a challenge take this class you will learn a lot but be ready for some BS.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bloom was a very understanding and caring professor. It is very apparent that he cares about the material and his students, wanting them to learn and be able to think on what was learned. Exams were collaborative and critical thinking about real world circumstances was facilitated. I hold him in high regards.

Dr. Bloom is genuinely one of the kindest souls at UNC. The midterms were take home and consisted of 4 challenge questions. He encouraged students to go to his office hours and consult each other. He curated such a collaborative learning environment that challenged students to think critically about the implications and applications of genetics.

Dr. Bloom is a very nice person and you can tell he is genuinely interested in what he teaches. However, the class is very poorly structured and you are unsure of what you are being graded on or how you are being graded (we were never given any rubric for any of the assignments). The two midterms had very difficult questions with tricky wording.

How this class is developed is wonderful, love the format. Dr.Bloom is friendly.
Grading criteria are very vague, don't know how we were being curved, I promise you this is the hardest FYS to get A

Dr. Bloom cares A LOT about genetics, but is a very disorganized lecturer. There are no notes/PPs, only what he writes (quickly) on the board, and his content is ambiguous sometimes. First test was take home and pretty fair. Sometimes you can follow his lectures in the book. He's excited about genetics and teaches cool things, just is disorganized

Dr. Bloom is a brilliant professor. His teaching style is different from any other professor I've had before, but after a couple weeks it was awesome. He cares about the subject and his students. I would totally recommend Dr. Bloom for 202.

Bloom loves his subject and this comes across in the lectures.  He does tend to get on tangents but is overall a great professor.  I always enjoyed his lectures, although they do switch professors half way through the semester for this class which was kind of annoying.

VERY passionate about his subject, and he knows his stuff. I'm not going to lie, he does go on tangents and it's a little fuzzy until he gets to his main point. However, he's very knowledgeable and makes an 8 am genetics class worth it. He's bad about answering emails though... and his second exam was a lot tougher than the first. Very nice man!
Hard class. Make sure you get the assigned readings done and pay attention to details he not only makes his exams from lecture but a lot of it comes from the readings. Hard exams.

He was obviously very knowledgeable but not able to communicate ideas to the class.  He jumped from subject to subject during lecture so it was hard to follow and take notes.  His tests were hard, but if you paid attention in class, read the textbook, and reviewed masteringgenetics, they were fair.

He liked what he taught but was very disorganized. He's one of those professors that's definitely a great researcher, but NOT a good at teaching. He assumes that you know about a LOT of things beforehand. The exams were extremely ambiguous and hard, especially the 1st one. Also, he never showed up to class on the days we had exams. NEVER.

He is a nice guy and means well and is very passionate about what he teaches. That being said he is very tangential in his lectures and kind of disorganized, so it ends up being quite confusing. Exams are crazy hard, i know many classmates that thought they had a firm grasp on the material that ended up nearly failing the tests.

He introduces an idea, goes to something else, then comes back to finish his point; the end result is sometimes confusing. Not very personable and his test questions are left fielders (even for me and I had a solid A), be ready for curve balls! But, he knows his stuff big time. Minus a couple of nasty test questions, exams are actually very fair.

Dr. Bloom is disorganized, does not explain concepts well, bounces to another concept without thoroughly explaining the first one.  He writes confusing tests and does not clearly express how he would like the questions to be answered.  Biology is a culture and he doesn't do a very good job in helping students integrate into that culture. Avoid him!

Bloom is not a good teacher. He rambles, and refuses to use any kind of technology to teach except Lego blocks (yeah, you read correctly!) and an overhead projector--he seems quite proud of this, too. Tests are somewhat hard, especially the first one. Do yourself a favor and take the other section of this clas.

I enjoyed Dr. Bloom's lectures much better than Dr. Dangl's.  Bloom went slowly through the more complicated material, which was very helpful.  I wouldn't recommend taking this class because as a pair, Bloom and Dangl make this class very difficult to understand

I'm a double science major and Bloom's class was by far my easiest science class at UNC.  He teaches the complicated parts patiently and the practice tests he gives are very helpful.  Do the practice tests and go to review sessions and this class is no problem.
The material isn't easy, but he's very approchable for questions after class.
I did not think either Kerry Bloom or Jeff Dangl were effective teachers. This class contains difficult material and I would advise taking it with someone else.

Somewhat scatterbrained, but generally a good teacher. Stops frequently for questions and goes slowly through difficult material, very much unlike his colleague (and co-professor) Jeff Dangl. Average-difficulty or difficult tests. Likes what he does, so learning from him is a bit easier.

If you just want an easy grade, yeah, he's not the prof for you. Go take some pushover. But if you want to actually learn how to speak or write, he's helpful. He's very generous with his time outside of class, sometimes talking for over an hour if you need it.

reviews.comment: Terrific Prof! Yes his class for 170 was challenging but in the best way. He really goes through the material well with intentionality and passion. Go see him during office hours! He sat down with me multiple times to go through my papers and questions from the materials. The quizzes helped me keep up with the material and were easy if I read. :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Blake Faulkner is a terrible instructor and grader. He expects you to automatically understand aspects of rhetoric when it's a challenging concept. In addition, he gives tricky weekly quizzes that are not helpful, just more confusing. Do not take him for comm 170 do not.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I love Ms. Blanton. She is so kind and really cares about her students. I was afraid I would not learn much since it was an online class but Ms. Blanton made the zooms very interactive and easy to learn from. I learned a lot and I definitely recommend.

Professor Blanton is sweet and very helpful. I enjoyed her class even though I didn't know it was all online originally. Most of the work is done in the Alcanza textbook, while classes were spent reviewing and practicing the material. Would definitely take a class with her again!

Professor Blanton is a great instructor who truly cares about her students. The class was challenging for me since languages aren't my strength, but if you already know some Spanish, it should feel manageable. The assignments are easy, but the exams are tougher, so regular studying is helpful.

professor blanton was so knowledgable and passionate about spanish and clearly cared about helping her students succeed! she gave great feedback and was always kind when redirecting students during class and on assignments! the workload was completely manageable and she was a very fair grader! i would recommend her to anyone taking spanish!!

I would definitely take Span 100 with her again—she was so kind and the perfect teacher for learning a new language. Even if I made mistakes during my speaking exams, she was generous with grading as long as I stayed in Spanish.
Incredibly sweet and considerate. Really wants her students to succeed; participation is super important. You can tell she really cares about her language, too. Definitely take with her!

Profe Blanton was a phenomenal professor for SPAN 203 and I would recommend her to anyone who needs to take the class. Tests were a bit hard, but they are standard across all sections of the course. Blanton's homework assignments were not difficult and plenty of time was given to complete them.

Sarah ran our class with a lot of enthusiasm and humor which I appreciated. I missed quite a lot of classes and still pulled an 87% in participation, which is much higher than I deserved. SPAN 203 is a tough class, but I would recommend taking it with Sarah.

She's tough on her participation grading and I had her at 8am, so it was tough to do well on that. But she's a really good teacher and will always work with you if you need help with something. She wants her students to do well. Super nice and I'd take her class again at 8am rather than someone else's later in the day.

I really dreaded taking spanish and had to take the class for credit but Blanton was really enthusiastic and funny. She always welcomed mistakes and loves to talk to students. Participation really matters and I was bummed I ended with an A- but you will not regret taking her... one of my favorite profs.

Listen, taking Span for me has been difficult. But given the choice, I would gladly take 203 again if it is with Prof.Blanton. She made this class worth it and made learning Spanish enjoyable for me! It was tough (for me) but she clearly cares bout her students and is one of the kindest profs I know. Super approachable too. Please take her!

Prof Blanton was an absolute joy to have as a spanish 203 teacher. She made me want to go to class everyday, continuously brightening my day, welcomed mistakes, often let us out early, and made sure each of us felt valued in class. She always teaches with a smile, her energy is unmatched. Take 203 with her, you won't regret it.

Profe Blanton is insanely passionate about her job and creates a welcoming classroom environment similar to a high school Spanish course. She welcomes mistakes in our in-class discussions and genuinely wants to help every student improve throughout the semester. She's also a pretty chill grader, def take her for 203
Professor Blanton was wonderful this past semester. 261 is a really challenging course and she takes the time to really help each of us learn and succeed.

Profe Blanton is very caring and enthusiastic about Spanish. Always very outgoing and fun at 8 am. Always accessible and willing to help. Participation definitely matters. Makes you feel comfortable speaking Spanish even when riddled with errors.
Profé Blanton is a gem among Spanish teachers. She really cares about her students and gives great feedback. Participation helps you succeed in this class. I highly recommend taking Profé's class!
Profe Blanton was very kind and understanding during a very stressful online semester. It is clear she really cares about her students.

Profe. Blanton is extremely warm, kind, and passionate about Spanish. She loves getting to know her students and truly makes everyone feel cared for. She does a great job conveying the material and you will learn a lot from her. That being said, she is a tough grader, but her kindness and teaching ability make up for it.

Very nice professor who really cares. Class is pretty much the same as any spanish class but she checks in with students and really tries to make sure that everyone is getting what they need to succeed.

Super nice guy and good class overall. He made lots or resources available and taught helpful foundational writing skills. My one complaint is that he takes a while to grade. He clearly cares a lot about teaching and puts a lot of effort into the class to make it engaging. I highly recommend his class for English 105!

I love Professor Paul! He is so sweet, and you can tell he is a genuinely good human being. The only things I would comment on are that he takes a very long time to grade, and his lectures are also boring at times. However, his expectations are clear, and he tries to be as engaging as possible. Take him if possible!!
Super nice guy, lectures are long, but important information if you lack foundational writing skills.

He's a solid professor and a decent person. While nobody loves ENGL105, his section is good. You learn how to write. I'll leave it up to y'all whether you think it's appropriate for a student at an elite school like UNC to complain about being required to attend class and do simple assignments. To me, this is anti-intellectual and very dumb.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is a kind person but his class is attendance and homework heavy. The course load was easy but it felt more like busywork. Also the worst grader I have encounter, time wise.

Cares about his students and will understand if you ever need an extension. However, missing one class reduces your grade by a point, and if you come in late, he'll give you a .75/1. There are a lot of extra credit opportunities to fix that, though. A discussion post is due before every class, and he assigns both a final project and an exam.

Every single day you have a homework assignment. So if its a M/W/F class you have to read something for each of those day and post a discussion post (three to four questions to answer). All of those readings will also be on the final. SO be ready to read. Also he is a very slow grader. Although caring about his students I would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Super nice and clearly passionate about his work! I love his classes, and I think his readings are really good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: The class itself was very easy and I know we did much less than other ENGL 105 classes. However, he would ramble for half the class about what we did the prior class. I hated listening to him. Attendance is your whole grade, so you must go. Overall, it was VERY boring but super easy A if you showed up and just did the work.
Paul is a very fair and caring prof. English 105 is easy as long as you put in effort and do your work on time. Highly recommend taking his class for english 105.

Mr. Blom is one of the best the university has to offer. He is a very kind and caring when it comes to the learning of his students. This class is very manageable to get an A in as long as you do the work and do it according to the rubrics that Mr. Blom provides. He also gives excellent feedback on assignments and really makes you a better writer.
I loved Paul! He didn't grade harshly but I still felt like I learned a lot in his class and he gave good feedback.
The course itself is structured very well as there is little homework per each class and he emphasizes improving your writing.
Professor Blom is a wonderful professor who truly cares about his students' success. He gives extremely clear outlines and is always available to help, would recommend!

Paul is an incredible professor! It is clear he cares deeply about his students. He is very accessible outside of class and a passionate instructor who wants his students to succeed. The projects are manageable and interesting and Paul provides good feedback. Grading was slow, but I didn't find it to be a major issue. Highly recommend Paul for 105!

Blom was super personable and I loved the content for writing in Health and medicine. His class is slightly disorganized with an excess of sakai files and grading is super slow. I barely had any grades all semester, but because of this he graded easily. He is very funny and I overall enjoyed the class. Very accessible outside of class too.
Great content and a funny teacher, however, the grading was very slow. We still have not received our last unit project grades and those are due tomorrow.

I did learn a good bit when it comes to writing in health and medicine, however, the grading was slow. Professor Blom did acknowledge it and try his best to get on top of this. Overall he is a good professor who cares about his students and their success.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: SUCH A FIRE PROFESSOR!! If you get the chance, definitely take Engl. 105 with him! He is a great person and his class is interesting and he cares a lot about teaching. There is still work, but not an absurd amount and his grading is super clear and not too harsh. I really enjoyed his class and would recommend it to anyone. 10/10!
Paul is great professor who cares for his students. My one critique is his delay on returning feedback.

Blom is a great instructor who cares about his students' learning and feedback. He is a very fair and understanding grader and is available for help during office hours and emails. Takes a while to get grades back but overall a great instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Paul Blom is a great instructor who cares about his students' learning and feedback. He can take a while to get his grades back to you but he is a very understanding and fair grader. He breaks up large projects with smaller feeder assignments which makes the workload feel less intimidating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Paul Blom is a great instructor at UNC. Blom was always willing to send feedback via email or outside of class and he helped me revise an essay unrelated to the course. Overall, Blom is an easy grader, passionate for what he teaches, and will go above and beyond for his students.

Paul was an amazing professor for health and medicine, he cares about his students and it SHOWS! He's passionate, personable, and easy to access outside of class. He also gives good feedback. The projects done in class are time consuming but diverse and help you broaden your horizons when it comes to writing in health and medicine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I hate writing classes, but this instructor made it as painless as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Paul is a great English teacher and helps his students much as he possibly can. He is also accessible outside of class and also gives a clear grading rubric for assignments and provides insightful and helpful constructive feedback for his students. I would highly recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Paul is a solid choice for ENGL 105. While he does require his students to do a bit more work than most other ENGL 105 teachers, he is a super light grader while also giving great feedback. He is also super invested into his students and their projects, so he is more than willing to help during office hours. ENGL 105 was very bearable with Paul.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Paul is an amazing teacher and person. He truly cares for his students success. He gives great feedback and fair grading. Paul answers his emails so fast it's concerning. My only advice would be don't take an 8am with him if you do not intend to be on time everyday. Being present and on time is very important to Paul.

Blom is not only a great instructor but a great person. He's highly organized and very easy to contact outside of class. His feedback on assignments is helpful and encourages students to succeed. He made an 8 am class less of a pain.

Made my first 8AM more bearable. Super nice and chill, gave great feedback and was super accessible outside of class. Responds to emails concerningly fast. Will remove 25% of your participation grade if you show up a min late, however. Passionate about writing and teaching and it shows. Would definitely take him again if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: An amazing teacher who really cares about his students. You can tell he puts a lot of time/effort into creating his course materials and that he wants you to succeed. The projects are time consuming but easy to do well on if you put forth the effort. The class helped me view health outside of a purely biomedical perspective -definitely recommend!
very reasonable, comfortable environment, great teacher, gives feedback on feeders, caring teacher that really cares about what you're remembering and actually learning.

Prof. Blom is a wonderful professor. His class isn't very difficult, yet it is productive, He is a super caring and flexible guy who gives great feedback on your work. He also is extremely organized, so you know exactly when everything is due and where to find certain resources. Amazing professor

Paul has handled online teaching far better than my other teachers. He is one of the nicest and most caring teachers that I have ever had. The feedback he gives on our rough and final drafts are detailed and have greatly improved my writing. Take Paul for your ENGL 105 class!!!!

I absolutely love Paul- he is not only insanely smart, but also kind- he has a true talent when it comes to teaching! My favorite professor and class at UNC BY FAR. He gives great feedback on papers and would even help with those for other classes when it was allowed. Many thanks to him!

He's an excellent instructor and a great guy as far as I know. He's a bit nitpicky when grading little things and really strict with attendance and submitting things on time. As long as you don't miss any deadlines, you'll be ok. Great instructor to have if you never ever ever mess up with deadlines and actually into writing. Not an easy section.
Paul is really great for ENGL 105! He sucks at grading things in a timely manner but as long as you do the work and turn everything in on time, you will get an A.

Paul is a great choice for ENGL 105. He is knowledgeable, experienced, and accessible. He makes the first year transition even better. Just be aware, because it is ENGL 105, there is a lot of writing involved. You also have to revise this writing and improve your writing skills. Paul tries to make writing fun, just do the work and you'll get an A!

Paul was a great professor. This was one of my first classes taken at Carolina. With that being said, he made the transition into college very easy. I would highly recommend taking English 105 with him. Be prepared to write and revise, but do the work and it is an easy A.

Paul is a great teacher for english 105. He makes you do revisions due the midnight after the class occasionally which isn't very fun. He often makes you partner up for revisions and there is a mini presentation (1 min) during the semester. To succeed in this class write and revise and you are golden. Do the work and it is an easy A

If you're taking this for a Gen-ed, I recommend! She was very nice and the class was pretty easy. Lectures could be kinda boring and readings were long, but she went over them. She gives a clear study guide over the midterm, 3 essays with clear rubrics, and weekly reading quizzes. Just wish the TA gave more feedback on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super caring professor! Easy class, just don't be rude and occasionally add something to conversations. The tests were pretty easy, essay-style but she gives you some possible prompt beforehand so you can prepare. Recitations were basically just a rant sesh about the current state of feminism and women so honestly super fun class
Professor Bloesch is a great professor who clearly cares about her students and their success. I would take another class with her.

great intro to the wgst dept!! very very lovely prof, very well spoken, extremely kind. class itself has many readings but she goes over important info from them in class. very easy gen-ed and very enjoyable. only holds lecture once a week too.

I enjoyed this class Professor Bloesch is great and very knowledgeable. She prepares you very well for all the assignments she expects of you. There is a lot of reading but you can get away without doing it because she goes over it during class. There is a recitation which is mandatory but not too much work overall.

Attendance in class isn't mandatory but recitations are. They were pretty interesting though. Bloesch is a good professor and her lectures pretty much some up the readings. Although, if you do the readings there's not much to pay attention to in class. Exams were easy too as long as you did the readings.

She was very kind, accommodating, and interesting. There were 2 short papers, a midterm, a final (multiple choice), and weekly ten-question reading quizzes (take-home, open note). In addition attendance and participation in recitation were taken.

Professor Sarah Bloesch is an outstanding educator! Her Sexuality and Salvation class in Women and Gender Studies was engaging, thought-provoking, and eye-opening. She fosters an inclusive environment and encourages deep discussions on complex topics. Her teaching style is clear, passionate, and approachable. One of the best professors I've had!

She is an incredibly understanding and flexible professor. The only mandatory attendance was for recitation. She only had lecture once a week as well. I only did the readings for the exams and for the recitations and did fine, there were no time limits on the weekly chapter quizzes.

She's a great professor and teaches very well. Attendance is only mandatory for recitation and she ends up dropping the Thursday class. Midterm and final were easy if you studied well and the essay project was pretty easy too. I had Jacob as my TA and he was great too. This class is a great GPA booster and pretty interesting too.

Overall, good class and professor. She seems to care a lot about her students and this class. In my opinion, the lectures were nothing crazy or extremely helpful, she basically reads off the slides. There is a good amount of reading. Attendance is mandatory, but only for recitation; she also dropped the Thursday class, which was great.

Dr. Bloesch is INCREDIBLE! All lectures were engaging, and she was always willing to answer questions and have conversations. Participation matters, but is self graded . Bloesch did a great job breaking readings down and helping us understand the concepts. My class was almost in tears when it was over, the course, and Dr. Bloesch were excellent!

The class was pretty straight forward and discussion heavy. No tests/ quizzes which is nice, instead you're graded on a semester long research paper split into 7-8 ish different parts. Splitting it up is helpful because you get feedback before you move on, feedback never came outrageously late. I never did the readings but I never had an issue.

Professor Bloesch was caring but was terrible with time management. The class is one long essay with each step needed to be graded to do the next but she never graded quickly, making the class fall behind really quickly. The work wasn't terribly difficult but her lack of organization made a class that had the potential to be intersting miserable.

I loved Dr. Bloesch. She is so passionate about the subject and very open to everything students have to say. The readings were long, but they were easy to skim and honestly really interesting. Class conversations were always interesting. Would highly recommend this class.

There were 2 papers and a few small assignments. Dr. Bloesch is an amazing professor!! I wish I could take all my classes with her. The only thing is that she doesn't give above a 97 on anything, so you're "100" is a 97. If you're a perfectionist it can be discouraging. We read a LOT, but the readings were engaging and fairly straight to the point.

Amazing prof who cares about her students. Readings are required for class if you want to grasp the material but most readings are relatively short. Took this to fill a FC requirement and have no knowledge of WGST and did pretty good. Class involves a lot of group analysis and discussion and participation is part of your grade. No exams either

This class felt like a massive waste of time and I wouldn't have gone if I hadn't been required to for the major. I really don't feel like the teacher actually shared any true knowledge and also, we didn't read or discuss any of the foundational feminist thought readings?

The class is one drawn own essay that feels drawn out for no good reason. The rubric was incredibly unclear, and I had no idea what I was supposed to be writing, and the instructions we did have made my work worse. She was incredibly nitpicky and just overall hard to talk to when I did discuss my frustration.

I'm really surprised by the ratings for this teacher. I hated WGST 202. It felt incredibly basic and I learned absolutely nothing in the course. It was all discussion and the questions were so bad that I couldn't even really learn things from my knowledgeable peers.

Prof Bloesch is an amazing prof! The class is fun and interesting and if you do the (semi-difficult) readings and pay attention the papers aren't too hard or frequent so its very manageable. She'll also grant extensions if you ask and push back deadlines for the whole class if needed. No in-person final either.

I loved Dr. Bloesch! Her lectures are awesome and understandable even when discussing tough psychoanalytic concepts. As someone who has never taken a gender class, her style helped me thoroughly understand the material. She was easy to talk to, but encouraged us to work hard and participate. She made class enjoyable yet very informative!

Very knowledgeable but lectures tended to be very abstract. Her rubrics and grading were sometimes unclear, but she gave excellent and timely feedback on every assignment. The seminar was based around one research paper, but I enjoyed the freedom she allotted to us to pick what we wanted to write about.

Professor Bloesch is a great lecturer and very knowledgable. This seminar was devoted to a final paper and her directions can be a bit unclear. It is also very difficult to get an A because she only grades up to a 95 (with a 94 being an A). The class is also HEAVY on religious studies and lacks the gender studies component. Should be RELI 67H.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Prof. Bloesch. Gender studies can seem a bit abstract to many but she explains theory in such a way that makes it digestible to students. She is extremely well respected and everyone I have spoken to wants to take more classes w/ her. 3 papers and some film notes, all of which are pretty do-able. This class is amazing!
She is lovely, fun, and incredibly knowledgable. Our seminar was devoted to creating a long paper. Her directions can be a little difficult to follow but she is such an engaging lecturer.

Dr Bloesch is the best WGST professor I have had so far and in my top 5 favorite professors at UNC. Extremely caring and willing to work with you if you make an effort. The readings are hard but Dr Bloesch guides you to understanding even the most dense stuff. Gave extensions as needed and has been so accommodating. Cannot recommend her enough!

Professor Bloesch is a fantastic professor who knows her stuff! Her lectures are always super engaging and go in-depth into the material at hand! She is super accommodating but also doesn't allow for slacking off in class. Her grading system is difficult, and she makes you work for the grade you get and fairly rewards the work you submit. Take her!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: While I like Professor Bloesch, her grading criteria makes it very difficult to make an A in the class. The readings were really dense but interesting. Her grading system sucks, but I enjoyed the discussions and setup of the class. She doesn't give above a 98 for the "inability to be perfect," which I think is ineffective in this setting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bloesch is amazing! She really cares about her students, gave us many days off from class to complete assignments, and extensions. There are readings and a handful of short papers that are combined to be your final paper. This made the weekly homework a bit much but the final paper was super easy. (and you don't really NEED to do the readings)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Bloesch truly cares about her students. 202 was great with her. The course is reading heavy as to be expected. The structure of class is discussion based, with a few written assignments and final concept paper that you work on in bits and pieces throughout the semester. I highly suggest taking a course with her if you can.

I love professor Bloesch. She is so knowledgeable and caring, she really wants you as a student to succeed. Beware of her grading system, she does not give out anything above a 98 but typically gives a 95 as an "A." She doesn't make it impossible to make an A in the class, but she makes you really work for and earn it. Discussions are always great!

Sexuality & Salvation

PROS: Very caring/funny/encouraging. Readings/films were interesting. Adjusted class to lessen our workload when needed. Very clear rubrics for papers (We had 3-4). She'll give you an extension on papers 99% of the time. Self-graded participation.

CONS: Doesn't give 100% on anything (max is ~95), but it's not a big deal.

Bloesh is extremely knowledgeable in her field and very passionate about her teaching, which makes the learning in-depth and insightful. She is a tough grader and my seminar grade was based off of just a few papers, but I learned a lot in this class and she is one of the most respectful and engaging teachers I've had. Recommend if you're into WGST!

I cannot applaud Prof. Bloesch enough. Truly one of the greatest professors I've ever had. She cares so deeply about her students and about the material, she's so accessible and listens to feedback from students constantly. Gender and Spirituality was fun, engaging, and pretty easy, save for some long (but interesting) reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: We would discuss the theorist, watch the movie in class, then be assigned the paper. Class followed this same structure for every theorist and movie with the addition of two papers and two movies of our choice. Class was not too difficult, but your papers are your entire grade because all you do is analyze the film theorists. Overall enjoyed class.

Professor Bloesch was amazing for gender and spirituality! She really listened to everyone's perspectives and provided insight into the material. There was reading before every class, but not excessive. Overall, Professor Bloesch was super kind and made the course enjoyable.

Prof. Bloesch is great! We met once a week and had discussion based on the reading/videos assigned for that week. There are a few group papers but theyre easy to put together as long as everyone does their part. There are also a few individual papers shes a pretty fair grader overall. I really enjoyed this class and our discussions, take it!

Dr. Bloesch was SO nice!!! I was nervous for her class, but she was literally so sweet & helpful. You could tell she wants her students to succeed, and she was willing to be so accommodating to any circumstances in the pandemic. Class was discussion-based with a reading each week and some small group projects, but all the material was interesting.
super tough grader. Did extra credit papers and still got a bad grade because all he counts is the finals. Assigns way too much reading.
The Professor is a very intelligent man. His lecture style does leave much to be desired however. If you don't like reading do not take this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Blair is a brilliant man. He doesn't take attendance and rarely quizzes on readings, but it'd be a huge loss to neglect either. He's also glad to help his students professionally, his tips and reference letter being immensely valuable as a former admiral, DNI, and a talented professor. So make an effort, learn a lot, and ask for advice!

Not many chances to learn from a practitioner like the Admiral. He clearly puts a lot of time into his syllabus and lectures, and you won't hear stories like his from just any PWAD/POLI prof. Practical final paper, loves to support his students (rec letters, connections, etc.), and incredibly knowledgable. If you read & participate, you're all set.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I feel lucky to have had Taylor for 187. She brought real-world experience from her career into class and was accessible whenever we had questions. Her grading criteria are clear, she's funny, and she made web design seem less scary. The JavaScript section kicked my butt, but if you show you tried you'll be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Taylor is such a caring and kind human, but she isn't the best teacher. A lot of times when asking questions and being confused, she would seem equally as confused and almost act as if you should know the answer. If you take this course, Google and ChatGPT will probably be your best friend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed my time in this class. This was her second semester teaching this course, but she really values her students. Coming into class every day was a joy as she often makes funny comments throughout her lectures. I highly recommend taking 187 with her!

The other prof for this class is easier, but this class was my favorite for the semester. Blackburn is an amazing lecturer, he is genuinely interested in making sure you understand the material and is down for any questions. He moved a test because it was on the same day as an anatomy exam too, he wants to give everyone the best shot they have.

The class is only lectures that weren't very detailed and very hard to learn from. You have to listen to his lecturing to understand the content, so if you miss a class or don't take notes for a class, you're going to be very lost. The class is also only made up of tests and quizzes, so if you flunk one, your grade is done for.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was alright. I wish there were more assignments other than the tests and quizzes because they make up your whole grade. Never communicates via Canvas or Outlook and never updated the syllabus (which was crazy because he changed the dates of almost all the tests). He's very nice but if there is ever another section take it with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I did not enjoy this class, even as someone interested in physiology and neuroscience. Blackburn was incredibly lecture heavy, a big departure from other professors I've had in EXSS. Your grade is 3 tests (90%) and 3 quizzes (10%). I got A's on the MC parts of exams and quizzes and failed the short answer because of how vague the questions were.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a really nice guy. He's willing to work with you and in class he gives great examples to help you understand. Hes funny. Looks like a Doogie Howser and Ryan Secrest love-child, but in a cute way. Go to class and pay attention and you will be fine. Ask questions if you got to, he's willing to help!

He's a really nice guy. He's willing to work with you and in class he gives great examples to help you understand. Hes funny. Looks like a Doogie Howser and Ryan Secrest love-child, but in a cute way. Go to class and pay attention and you will be fine. Ask questions if you got to, he's willing to help!

Tanner is genuinely my king. Do whatever is humanly possible to have him as your professor. He's super nice and funny and he makes class very engaging. Participation matters and he rarely gives out 100s, but he really wants his students to succeed so he's super lenient with deadlines and partial credit.
Amazing professor would definitely recommend!

Very passionate about languages and teaching! Makes class fun and is a chill grader. Slow grader for bigger assignments, but will always give you an extension to make up for it. Participate in class and turn in textbook homework on time and you'll be fine.

Take this man if you get him, honestly probably for whatever course he is teaching. Super caring and chill. Was very lenient when it came to turning things in a little late and honestly just there to see you succeed. Just participate in class! I hadn't taken a whole lot of spanish before but I felt fine and learned a lot in the end

(I was in SPAN261)

Tanner is a very easy professor. He's friendly, hilarious, and gives great feedback on your assignments. He is a bit harsh on grading and likes to give out 90s a lot, so your grade can drop to a B easily. In class, there's homework assignments pretty much every night, but they aren't too hard. He does grade participation.
Tanner (who may go by Joseph on Connect Carolina if you're confused) is the BEST. Take his class. I don't have a bad thing to say about him.

I LOVED Tanner! He made lectures exciting and funny, which made learning feel so much more engaging. He was always willing to help and would ask if we wanted to redirect the class to areas we struggled with to make sure we did well on quizzes and exams. I genuinely felt supported throughout the course. Highly recommend! Office hours are great too.

I loved French 102 with Mr Bourne, super funny and class went by so fast with jokes and made everything super interesting. Loved learning with him! 4 quizzes, final exam, and oral exam with some papers, more work than 102 but enjoyable.

Great teacher! Tanner is so energetic and passionate about languages, it makes coming to class much more enjoyable. He's very encouraging and will continue to explain things in different ways until the class understands it. Absolutely take this class with him if you get the chance!!

100% recommend! SO funny, caring, easy grader, and personable. The class is fully spoken in Spanish, but he truly does make it so easy to pick up on. Doesnt care if you mess up, just wants you to try. 3 exams graded easy, 1 oral interview (chill), and 1 composition + revisions. Fabulous teaching method. Approachable and caring. Take 203 with him!

Easy class for me just because I did most of the content already in HS. Amazing professor who made the lectures more fun and interesting. One of the best professors during my first year. Would 100% take his class if you could.

Tanner is energetic, funny, and clearly cares about his students. He showed up to class everyday ready to teach spanish and created a carefree class environment that made it easy to ask questions and mess up. Otherwise, the course load was minimal and the tests and quizzes were not bad. If your'e going to take 203 you want it to be with Tanner.

I had Tanner for SPAN203 and I would definitely take this class over again. Tanner is always energetic even at 9am and he made the lessons very engaging. He is very accessible outside of class and willing to work with you. Tanner is one of my favorite professors I've had so far. Definitely take his class.

Great guy and good professor; made things easy to understand. Only subbed for my Spanish class for about 6 weeks, but I would definitely take with him again. My only complaint was that he was practically impossible to reach by email.

If I could repeat this course again, I wouldn't even think twice about it. This class definitely made my semester as Tanner is absolutely hilarious and caring towards all his students. As long as you put the work in Tanner is more than happy to help you succeed.

I took Tanner for SPAN 203, and he deserves all this praise. I have taken Spanish for over six years; this was the first time I wanted to engage in class. He is hilarious and makes Spanish a concept that everyone can understand. Literally, show up, participate, complete the work, and you will be fine.

Take Tanner for Span 203!!! He is absolutely hilarious, and is one of the kindest people I've met. He makes the class as easy as he can, and uses fun activities to help teach the concepts. Homework is very manageable, and classes were always fun. Tanner is incredibly kind and down-to-earth, and is overall a fantastic professor!

I had Tanner for SPAN203 and it was the best decision! He is fun, caring, and not at all difficult. He understands that its a hard class (especially if you haven't taken spanish since high school like me). He helps out so that everyone does well! As long as you entertain him and get your point across you'll do great! Take Tanner's class!!!

I have tanner for 203 and he is one of the funniest people I have ever met, although its hard because every spanish 203 class is hard he makes it more enjoyable to go to class because he has good lectures. every spanish teacher has to make 5 quizzes for thier class and all of ours so far have been take home and very easy.

The sweetest professor ever! Made sure everyone actually understoof the concepts. Played fun grammar/vocab games. Focused heaivly on partner/group work so it creates a nice oppurtunity to make friends in the class. Overall, take spanish with Tanner. He is a blessing and I cannot emphasis that enough.

Tanner is such an enthusiastic professor who really wants you to learn. He actively engages you in the material through songs and interactive games. He genuinely cares about you and is extremely understanding. There are daily homework assignments and weekly chapter reviews but the class is manageable if you put in the work.
Really, really enjoyed taking Tanner's class. He is very knowledgable of the topics covered in class & is very willing to help you. Definitely would recommend this class!!

Tanner is very flexible and understanding. He's super sweet and very energetic, even at 8 am. The class has lots of work, but he sets you up for success. He's willing to meet outside class for anything and is accessible through email. He makes boring grammar and lectures into fun games. Take SPAN105 with Tanner, he's the best teacher for it!

The most disorganized professor I've ever had. Already have had multiple assignments with due dates that weren't properly communicated or adjusted, even though she said they'd be moved. She's super entertaining, caring, and a fun person, but for someone teaching business communications, you'd think she would communicate more.

I honestly did not know how to rate Dr. Boyer; she's an incredible person who deeply cares for her students and is extremely reasonable. However, she is disorganized and often very behind in getting back grades to students, and in this particular class, grades are very harshly-like all other 401 professors. I would recommend taking it with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's funny and makes classes engaging. Hard to get an A, her grading criteria is very unclear at times and the feedback is not great either - sometimes even contradictory. 401 kinda sucks in general, so among the options I think she's one of the best to at least have a fun time. Just accept you will prob get an A- even if you try really hard.

Despite her slightly disorganized nature, this is the second course I have taken with Dr. Boyer. Her grading criteria is unclear and assignment deadlines and metrics often are changed, but she is truly hilarious and a caring professor. If you are looking for a laugh and a genuine connection, and are willing to work with her, take the class!

Boyer's cool and a great lecturer who made class engaging. That being said, she is so nitpicky when it comes to grading. You can clearly do everything on the rubric but she'll take off ten points for no reason. I guess that's just 401. Also all her assignments are written/graded by AI which is pretty annoying since it leads to unclear guidelines.

Difficult to get an A, A- didn't require much effort, but that's honestly just BUSI 401. Discussion based class with lots of small group work and in-class activities that aren't graded. Assignments were applicable and didn't take too long. They're graded harshly, but again that's just 401. Interesting lecturer, and I actually enjoyed going to class

Fun class but disorganized and expectations are unclear. Assignment guidelines would change right before they were due which caused a lot of time to be wasted. Finished the mod a couple weeks ago and still haven't gotten any grades back. Seems like one of the easier electives though in terms of workload.
Impossible to get an A, also incredibly unresponsive to emails or feedback
SUPER hard grader, impossible to get an A in this class. Seems to be the same with all professors though. She was funny and each class was interesting. She did not provide clear rubrics or criteria.

She's really nice, but wow is she a harsh grader. This is an email writing and presentation class, and she will nitpick you on the smallest things. Honestly though, no 401 professor will hand out A's, so go ahead and take her.

Lori has a super over the top personality. She makes class fun and engaging. She does grade things tough but all the assignments were super easy so if you put a little bit of effort in you are guaranteed a B. Be prepared for class to be a big group discussion every day.

Professor Boyer is a very engaging and funny lecturer but as other people have said her grading is needlessly harsh. Her harsh grading made this class more stressful and difficult than it needed to be when looking at the actual subject matter. Good person, bad pedagogy.

This is the first teacher throughout my time at UNC I would 100% not recommend to any student. I'm certain Professor Boyer is a wonderful woman outside of academics, but I can't appreciate her grading. It takes weeks for her to give feedback and when I tried speaking with her about the criteria, she was always unwilling or unresponsive.

Dr. Boyer was hard to reach outside of class, but she was a very easy grader and the material was interesting. She cold calls a lot to facilitate discussion in the beginning of the semester. One discussion post, 2 presentations, a midterm, and an easy final assignment.

Professor Boyer is super nice and caring and can be really fun in class, but she is the absolute worst about grading criteria and giving back grades. The grades seem arbitrary with little feedback and they aren't given back for months. I didn't know my grade for this class until over 2 weeks after the class ended, and we didn't even have a final.

Grading is awful. She assigns so much busy work and then grades harshly. Takes forever to give feedback on assignments and will find the tiniest issues even if you followed the rubric closely. On projects she gave everyone the same grade. At times it felt like she had unrealistic expectations while simultaneously treating us like children.

You will breeze through this class all semester until the end. She gives everyone the same grade on everything until after evaluations are due. She went through and changed all my grades. I thought I was chilling, but then found out I was not. Harsh grader and unforgiving for mistakes. Seems like a cool person but will screw you over for no reason
Professor Boyer is a nice person, but she is unforgiving and a harsh grader. I would recommend taking BUSI 401 with someone else if you want a good grade.

Professor Boyer's only weakness is her lack of communication which is odd given that this is a communications class. He class is fun, and there is usually no homework but she will grade you harshly for things she never taught you.
She extremely energetic and fun loving, only downside is that she is a tough grader. But 401 has a bunch of filler assignments which helps you get a good grade. Would definitely take her.

Professor Boyer is really sweet, but a deceivingly hard grader for no reason. I think that BUSI401 should be pretty easy, but she takes off for the smallest of things and turns an easy class into a hard on for no needed reason. I would try taking another teacher for 401 to get a better grade
Attendance is graded; just come and listen. Only 1 essay is graded at the end of the course. Gives you directions for every paragraph that needs to be on there.

Dr. Greg is great, I heavily recommend this class for anyone even slightly interested in public health! We just met once a week briefly on zoom with mandatory attendance, but Dr. Greg is very understanding and offers alternative options if something comes up for you. The only grade is the final paper and he wasn't a tough grader at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: super chill class. once a week class online and attendance was mandatory. had to have camera on. only assignment was a 800 word paper. learned a lot about how to get a health career.
Love Dr. Greg! Great class if you're pre-med or pre-nutrition. Mandatory attendance on Zoom once a week and class ends spring break. One 1000 word paper is the only assignment.
Dr. Greg is a really cool guy and this class with him was both extremely easy and enjoyable
Had a great time listening to all the lecturers come in and talk about their studies!

Your grade in the course consists of attendance and a final paper. The class is what you make it: if you are passionate about public health and interact with a guest speakers, you will probably get more out of the class. It's pretty easy to get an A, just show up and write a paper.
Greg is awesome, classes are super interesting, easy A and very informative if you're interested in behavioral health or public health in general.

I have no interest in Public Health but took this class because I needed one more hour to graduate. It ended up being really interesting! You do have to attend class with your camera on, but the lectures are engaging. I would recommend it (especially if you are actually interested in Public Health).

Dr. Greg is AWESOME! He really took his time with researching and reaching out to the guest lecturers, as they were super interesting. He's always willing to answer questions and genuinely makes an effort with his students. Wishing I could've taken this class in-person, but I appreciate the gesture of offering it online for more people to take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bocchino did a great job with SPHG 101! The guest lecturers and the different degrees he highlighted were a wonderful introduction to the world of pubilc health. This is interesting pass/fail, 1 credit course, so I would definitely recommend it for pre-med/pre-health students. You do one final paper at the end.
Greg really cares about helping his students. The guest lecturers have a lot to share. You can learn a lot from this class if you pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Bocchino was definitely the best professor I've had at UNC this far. His class is very chill as your whole grade is made up of attendance and your final paper. Very interesting content wise and you learn a lot from the guest speakers. I would definitely recommend this class

This class that introduces you to every public health field out there. It is a pass/fail class with only one essay due at the end of the semester. The guest speakers would each come one per week to talk about their specialty and answer any burning questions you have on career choices. Dr. Bocchino is a great resource for future Grad level planning.
I initially took this class to fill a focus capacity, but it ended up being my favorite course of the semester. I loved learning and writing about comics at a university level!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ben is such a chill dude. he literally says he tries to get everyone an A. there were maybe two assignments the whole semester that i thought were hard, but the rest were so calm cuz he gives rly detailed instructions and expectations. also i learned a lot! highly recommend if you have any interest at all in law.

Take the comics class when it's offered with Professor Bolling! I didn't know anything about comics before this semester. He clearly loves the material and it's infectious. Do the reading and you'll be fine.

Dr. Bolling was the best professor I had during my first semester and helped me transition to UNC. There's a lot of work in this class but he gives really detailed feedback and is always able for office hours.

I had Dr. Ben for 105 and learned a lot about writing from him so decided to take his comics class. Highly recommend. Made the material interest even though I didn't know much about comics going in. Always willing to make time to talk about projects during office hours.
I thought visual and graphic narrative was a film class but decided to stick with it because this guy was so funny. Knows the material like nobody else. Chill and kind.

Just straight up mean and condescending, easily offended. Took a student outside mid-class and I could hear him yelling. unclear assignments & class is a lot of work. assignments build on ones before which wouldn't be so bad if he could actually grade anything so u knew what was going on. when he does grade comments come back clearly ai generated.

Ben was so supportive and offered wonderful feedback. It was a go go go class, starting a project right after another, but it was manageable. I love Ben. I learned so much in this class and recommend him so much!! Very very funny.

Truly the best professor here at UNC!! He's so funny, caring, and easy to talk to. All his assignments were difficult, but they were also time-consuming. However, he provides samples for every assignment and is extremely helpful. He was such an amazing professor, I've decided to take another one of his classes next semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ben is an amazing professor and an amazing person. I thoroughly enjoyed taking Writing in Law and I learned so much from him. A couple group projects and every unit was structured. Definitely more difficult than a regular 105, but so worth it if you are considering law (also worth it if you aren't). Prepare for a busy schedule but a great class!

Professor Bolling is someone who genuinely cares about their students and their success. He provides really good feedback on assignments that typically involve analyzing constitutional cases and writing/presenting about them. The class was super interesting and I really enjoyed it.

Great professor. Grades come in somewhat slowly, but he's a very easy grader. Assuming you try and put effort in, you'll do well. Great class if you are interested in law. It is a very consistent workload and can be tough at times, but grading is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Ben is super funny and clearly cares a lot about his students and the material. Sometimes felt like a lot of work for a 100-level class, but no assignments were that hard. The textbook reading is boring, but Ben makes the concepts interesting. Highly recommend.

Take ENGL 155 with Dr. Bolling! A few reading quizzes, one paper, and a project. The midterm was easy and he's a pretty easy grader. Gives very detailed feedback. Clearly passionate about the material and makes you appreciate comics in a new way.
Was super engaging and I loved class discussion. The texts were fun and Professor Bolling is so chill.
This class was amazing. The class is mostly based on readings, quizzes, papers, and projects, but they are not made to be too difficult. Read the required readings each week, and you will be fine.

Super fun and interesting class! I learned a lot and enjoyed all of the material. Very manageable work level and lenient grading. Professor Bolling is focused on making sure students get the most out of his class and the material and you can tell!

(Writing in Law) Super easy grader with rubrics to follow. Available for questions. Manageable/concise assignments, a few group projects, open note quizzes. Extremely thorough feedback. Nearly everything he says is funny. Slightly slow grading but many opportunities for revision. Not prelaw but no regrets on taking this course.

Class content can be kinda difficult and there's a lot of work but Ben is an extremely caring and funny teacher. Really cares about the subject and is a pretty lenient grader. Only complaint is that he's a slow grader.

Professor Ben's class was more than I expected. My friends in regular 105s complained all the time about the basic work they had to do. I'm not really interested in legal writing, but I appreciate what I learned in this class. I didn't enjoy all of the work we had to do in groups, but it wasn't as much as some other 105s.

Dr. Bolling is the best! His class requires a lot of work, but I learned a lot about the law and writing, in general. He was always willing to make extra time during office hours when I had questions about class or about school, in general. He's a real one

I didn't expect to enjoy ENGL 105, but Ben made it worth my time. Especially if you're interested in legal writing, he is knowledgeable and gives really good feedback. This is not a basic 105 and I'm glad I actually learned something in this class.

Dr. Bolling is a great professor who is extremely willing to work with students, field questions, and provide clear rubrics and guidelines for course material. His Writing in Law class is great at teaching students about the importance of consistency and brevity in writing, and I found the course material manageable to keep up with.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: None of this is accurate because he admits to constantly reading his own reviews on here and flagging stuff he doesn't agree with. steer clear

Ben is a very engaging teacher and gives helpful and detailed feedback on every assignment. He's also a pretty easy grader. He took a long time to grade on some assignments, but it was understandable due to various uncontrollable complications throughout the semester. By far my favorite professor this semester. Don't listen to the review bombers.
My entire group opened the transfer portal at least once a week
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Look, if you are interested in writing in the law, this class's content is valuable. However, beware of his inconsistent and sometimes even demeaning teaching styles. He claims to promote asking for help and feedback, but can be condescending when you try to do so. Each project builds off of each other, but he lays out expectations unclearly.

It is end of October, I have ONE of six big assignments thus far graded. Super inconsiderate and petty when it comes to grading - normally wouldn't complain about this, but each project literally builds on what you wrote before, and you have no idea how you're doing. A big project every week, a lot of work. I do well and the class is interesting.

Ben was such a chill but engaging prof. We did a bunch of projects in Adobe's CC and it was fun and useful to learn. Workload not heavy but you do have to put in a decent amount of effort. We read/discussed comics which was cool, good amount of reading at times though. Very easy grader
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Genuinely the best professor I've had at UNC. I wasn't looking forward to 105, but he made the gen ed practical and useful. He was easy to talk to outside of class and seemed to really care about helping his students.
the worst professor for engl 105, and possibly the worst professor at UNC overall.

I never thought 105 would be the most useful class I took first semester, but Ben made it worth it. He's funny and kind and always makes time for you if you need to meet outside of class. The work load is harder than other 105s, but you will learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ben was the best professor I had during my freshman year. He clearly cared about everyone not just as students but as people outside of class. He says he doesn't think his class is hard, which is mostly true. It's a lot of work, but if you show up to class and put in effort on the assignments, this is not a hard class.

DO NOT TAKE. There is a ton of work in this course. Regularly, I would have been fine with the work load if he made the learning and class room environment enjoyable. Spoiler: he did not. He is super nitpicky about writing and basically polices your writing. He says to "ask him for help if needed" and then is the opposite of helpful.

Ben is the GOAT. He is a amazing and hilarious lecturer, and I genuinely looked forward to class every day. Most of the assignments were fun and reasonable, but they often took a ton of time to complete. The only small issue was that he would take a long time to get us grades and feedback. He is very kind and understanding.

Overall, Professor Bolling was a good teacher and taught me some things about grammar that I didn't know. His class at some times was a little more work than other English 105 classes, but he is an easy grader. Attendance is required and class can sometimes be boring as he lectures a lot but overall it's an easy class so I would do it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is hilarious and I genuinely enjoyed coming to class. There is kind of a lot of work due and it does take awhile to get feedback back, but that being said he is a very nice and understanding professor/grader

Professor Bolling is one of the best professors I've ever had. It's evident that he's passionate about what he's lecturing and that he has the experiences and skillsets to back up his lessons. If you are even vaguely interested in whatever class he's teaching, I highly recommend taking it (he's a really nice grader too).

Ben was so amazing. The course is well designed, and I learned so much. He is very passionate and clearly wants his students to succeed. This course teaches you Creative Cloud, which is so valuable. Definitely take a class with Ben if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Seems fine in the beginning and the work isnt hard (just a ton of it), but he can be condesending and rude at times. Also unprofessional and cusses a lot. I just took this class to get my engl 105 credit over with.

Ben Bolling was the best professor I could have had during my first year at Carolina. He very approachable and helpful, giving genuine and thoughtful feedback on every assignment. Not harsh on grading, he only really cared if you were learning something useful. If I could recommend only one professor, it would be him.

Ben is awesome. He is very kind, funny, and wants the best for his students. He is very open that he intentionally makes it easy to get an A/tries his hardest to keep your grade high so long as you put in a baseline level of effort. 100% recommend.

I love Ben so much!! He was the best professor I had in my first semester at UNC. He was super funny and loved the assignments he had us do. He and his niece even made us cereal bars one day! Ben wants the best for his students and always tries to make time to give students feedback.

Really amazing, caring, and down-to-earth professor. The class is a bit fast-paced, so be sure to be on top of the deadlines. It's also mainly group projects, but getting an A was not difficult. I took the Writing in Law, and it was a great first exposure to the legal industry. I would definitely recommend this class to aspiring lawyers.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Bolling is genuinely the most awesome person I have met at UNC. Such an amazing professor, such an awesome class, grading was super fair and lenient and yet I learned so much. He's such a cool guy and made super dense topics accessible, but also treated students like equals. 10/10. Everyone should take his classes.

Dr. Bolling is an amazing, caring, and lively professor. He just returned to teaching at UNC and I feel so grateful he came back this year! I got to work on case briefs, law articles, etc. in Eng105i for Law. He is not a super fast grader, but grades very leniently so I wouldn't be too concerned. Fair amount of writing but so helpful and worth it.

Ben is a great professor. He is very funny and personable. Not too much work outside of class. A couple of the books chosen were a little boring, but most of them were pretty good, and this is coming from a STEM major. If I needed to have taken another English class, I certainly would have taken him again. Take any class he offers!

Ben is the best professor I have had at UNC. From the first day of class, I felt comfortable participating in class and scheduling appointments outside of class to get more feedback. He gives you a chance to revise each assignment, which makes English 105 super easy. Could not recommend someone better.

Ben is SUCH a gem, and I'm sad that he is leaving UNC! Our class was usually a liberal echo-chamber, but I did enjoy the material and I felt like I learned a lot. Ben was great at fostering discussions, too!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great professor. He cares about students and you'll care about him too. The workload is standard for a lit class- a lot of novels and a few papers- but he makes it really flexible and manageable. Occasionally he seems to promote his own ideas a little too much, but I'd chalk that up to enthusiasm. Would definitely take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Great class, great feedback given for practical assignments. Definitely take this class if you get a chance, you won't regret it.

This guy is amazing.  Show up to class and give effort; that's all he wants. He is helpful in answering your questions and gives honest and insightful feedback.  He's hilarious, and he makes the course assignments fun. And go to his office hours. He baked cookies for our last class meeting - if that tells you anything about how cool this guy is.

Ben Bolling is the BEST professor I've ever had. He's hilarious, he really cares about his students and gave me the most useful feedback and tips I've ever received concerning my writing. The class wasn't easy, but you will come out a better writer. He's seriously great.

The guy is seriously great.  He takes the time to analyze the arguments in your papers and reflections and offers suggestions.  Grading is fair and generally positive, all you have to do is put the effort into the course.  Show up to class and hold on tight.  He's hilarious and insightful--a bit opinionated--but damned if I didn't have fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Ben was definitely my favorite professor at UNC. He genuinely cares about his students and took the time to get to know each of us. He's an extremely fair grader and if you put an effort in, you'll get the grade you want. I highly recommend taking this course with Ben.

Funny professor, is very interested in what you have to say, and although he may have an idea in his mind, he always asks for comment. The books that we have read were interesting. In Eng 128, as long as you read the book, you will succeed in the class because all he wants is effort and is interested in what you have to say.

Undoubtedly my favorite professor my first semester. He knew his stuff and was open to new ideas. Reasonable grader. The work you put is the grade you will get out. He cares about the well-being of his students and is down to earth.

He was my favorite professor first semester as he really cares about his students. He was always checking in on the well-being of students which as a fist-year is nice to have in a professor. They're a lot assignments but most are pretty manageable and he is an extremely fair grader. He was quite funny and keeps your attention very well.

Professor Bolling quickly forms opinions about his students in the beginning of class. There is a lot of work for an English 105 class. His style of lecturing can be condescending at times. Overall, not a bad class, but not a great teacher.
Great teacher, interesting class  and readings. Discussions were great.
Prof. Bolling was very, very helpful. It wasn't the easiest class I have ever taken but it was easy to stay focused. As long as you do the readings and go to class, you'll be fine.
Interesting lectures, good class, tough grading but worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Boittin's lectures are bone-dry, rambling, random, and occasionally border on offensive.
