had him for gender, and he was okay. my least fav prof. but he was still nice. gender seems widely hated but I highly recommend the class, I enjoyed it. his lectures are boring but you have to take notes on the art pieces because he only shows the paintings, which makes it hard to study for his portion of the class if you don't take good notes.

Professor Levine is great. His lectures were interesting and he really cares about the material. People who complain clearly don't want to learn because he's a really good teacher and cares about students understanding.

Prof. Levine gave me a newfound appreciation for art. Out of the 3 gender teachers, I find him the most entertaining and pretty knowledgeable. He tries to interact with students, but sometimes comes off as a bit passive aggressive. Overall, he picks interesting content and you can tell he's passionate about his lectures.

Some of these reviews are from students who just don't want to work. If you are on your phone while he is lecturing, he might tell you to put it away, but that's disrespect on the student's part too. If you don't like art history, this part of Gender will obviously not be great to you but if you pay attention and do the readings, it is not hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very nice and understanding guy, and really wants students to be involved. Lecture based with readings due each week, but easy. Grades aren't posted until end of semester, but midterms and exams fairly easy if you go to class and pay attention. Easy to zone out during lectures but participation counts, so be wary. Enjoyed this class.
Levine is amazing. I live the class and hope to take more from him.

Not my favorite. He's rude to some students and his part of this class is kind of unstructured. I think sometimes he's trying to be funny but it just comes across as mean and insensitive. I absolutely hate this class though, so my review might be biased. Just don't take gender and all these problems will be avoided.
Professor Levine is really great. Lectures are super interesting. I never appreciated art before.

The way he talks about women in art is creepy and objectifying, and he teaches this class like the concepts about gender are revolutionary when in fact they are common sense. Grading depends on your TA except for the midterm and final which honestly aren't too bad if you pay attention and briefly review material. Be prepared to memorize paintings
Great class
I really enjoyed the class
I really think he's a top professor. It's tough to fit all the material in to his portion, but he did so in a really interesting way. The art he covers is not easy, but it makes you think

Professor Levine is one of the best at UNC. This class was an inspiration to me, covering so much complicated art and in a really fascinating way. He's a gifted teacher who is caring but also pushes you to think hard. One of the best classes I have taken
This was a good as can be expected. The art covered by Professor Levine was so interesting, and his teaching style is casual but smart. Highly recommend this triple I or any other class he teaches
Loved him and his part
Really great. Highly recommend Prof Levine

if you are taking a tripe I don't take gender. The exams are hard and the reading check-ins are almost impossible. much harder than any other Tripe I. For his exams you have to memorize many paintings and he is such a boring lecturer.
He said he was going to give us extra credit the day before Thanksgiving break, but then he said he was just kidding. The other 2 profs from this class were great though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't listen to these whiny freshmen who don't have any interest in Art History and are too lazy to memorize 20 paintings for an exam. Most of them are too immature to handle looking at a nude painting in a gender class. In reality, Prof Levine is a great teacher who really made me appreciate art, looking forward to taking another class of his.

Prof Levine is really great, and this class is too. I learned so much, and the art history part was fascinating. He is a great lecturer, fun and entertaining while also packed with important info. I would definitely take him again.

Gender was an unnecessarily difficult Triple-I. The content was interesting enough, but Professor Levine's art history portion was the same concepts on repeat. Lots of memorization was necessary for exams and the in-class quizzes were also unnecessarily difficult. I would not take this class or one of Professor Levine's classes again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Gender was the worst class I've ever taken, especially because of the Art History section that Cary Levine taught. He would yap for a whole hour and the only thing I learned from his lectures was that women felt oppressed.The exam FORCES you to memorize artist names and dates for no logical reason in which you will forget about the next week.

Honestly, this class is super weird, especially the art history section. He pretty much only showed us art work of naked women or of genitalia which was pretty weird and annoying. In general, if you like art history, then this part of the course might not bother you too much but otherwise its pretty boring and at times highly condescending feeling.

Gender is the worst Triple I. Of the three profs, Levine was the worst as well. Had no content in his slides except pictures and his readings and lectures were pointless. Nothing he said or made us read had any significance or relation to the midterm/final. Just avoid it/him in general
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Levine is awesome. His lectures can be dense, and you look at a lot of art, but by paying attention in class, taking notes, and reviewing art for exams, you will be just fine. Very funny and cares about you as a student. Definitely a polarizing figure but he means well and is knowledgeable about art.

I found Levine's section to be the most interesting of the three because of his lectures. The professors have tweaked some of the subject matters from the past to make to more relevant to gender. The biggest struggle in this class was the reading check-ins but as long as you put in the effort, the class shouldn't be too bad.
Gender is the worst Triple I, do not take it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This prof. is going to say something like art is neither good or bad nor neutral. You'll learn nothing other than women is being objectified. Other parts of this class are way better. His portion only includes much memorization of art works that do not relate to gender.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Levine's part of this course was by far one of the most boring classes I had. Not only did he go into excruciating detail in his lessons, the readings were difficult to fully understand. He was also very rude to students when they asked questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Compared to the other Triple Is, this one is definitely hard. You have to memorize so much information for exams and especially for art history, a lot of it comes straight from the lecture itself. Classes are tedious and there's a good amount of work.

Lectures are so dry so it was often hard to pay attention no matter how much I tried. Slides are unhelpful because they only show pictures of the art he talks about in class but doesn't offer a description of them. Tests were difficult to study for because it was heavy on memorization and it was hard to know what he wanted us to focus on.

Cary is someone who loves to ramble with dry humor and even drier lectures. Many of the readings and art pieces he brought up were quite interesting, but the commentary that followed from him was less interesting. "Ok" is the best way to describe him.

Prof. Levine likes to ramble. A lot. His lectures are dry. The majority of the work we looked at was made by cis women from 1960s-1990s. The class mainly focuses on the gender experience of cis people and only briefly discussed non-cis people. Pretty disappointing for a class called "gender". The work he assigns isn't hard, but can be dense.

Dr. Levine is a polarizing professor. His sense of humor is dry and he may seem condescending, but I don't think that he is. The art history readings were fairly long and academic and there was a midterm question asking you to recall a specific piece's artist. Regardless, his lectures are interesting and he will explain the important takeaways.
Some of the content is very interesting but I never felt comfortable asking questions because I found him to be pretty condescending and rude.

Terrible lecturer he goes and just talks about paintings the entire class and most of them are irrelevant to the midterm or final. He picks one out of 15-20 you analyze over the semester on the midterm and makes you recount several things about the painting. Most pieces of art are also highly insensitive, and he rarely gives respect to them.
Professor Levine is fantastic. I look forward to taking more classes with him.

While he does go over the material, it seems as though he is just spending so much time on a particular topic that he then does not end up asking about in the midterm. The lectures are long-winded and sometimes difficult to comprehend

Professor Levine is a good instructor, but he can be rude to his students and make them feel bad for asking questions. Other than that, he has a lot of knowledge of Art History and explains the concepts well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Levine is really great. Lectures are interesting and he really cares about his students. Highly recommend.

Professor Levine is an okay professor, but not for Gender Triple-I. This class has potential if organized and done well, but if you think this is an easy class, do not take it. There are about 9 papers that you do and the midterm and final are hard. He does care if you can't take an exam on a day and will find another day for you.

Professor Levine has bad ratings for a reason. I found the content to be very interesting, but his approach was seriously upsetting sometimes, and honestly I frequently felt that he was very condescending and rude towards the students. If you have the misfortune of having a class with him, go to class because he lectures and doesn't post the slides

Prof. Levine is a great teacher. Lectures were interesting and concise. The work load was pretty light, with the exception of two end-of-semester papers that were graded easily. If you participate and show interest, he's a really engaging professor. I'm taking his 588 class this semester!

Professor Levine is overall a decent teacher, but he can come across condescending and insensitive at times. The class itself was interesting but there were a lot of readings and essays. Sometimes he would show triggering art images without any trigger or content warnings, the only warning being at the beginning of the semester.
This was an amazing course all around. Part lecture part discussing. Prof Levine is really passionate and makes this challenging art come alive. Highly recommend

The coursework was a nice balance to harder courses, however, there were two papers due at the end of the term that was extremely vague, and graded by an TA you will never meet. The midterm and finals were not bad only a having a time constraint that caused anxiety. He sometimes contradicts himself when giving feedback, so double check!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Such a good class and intro to college. Profs are smart and caring and Levine was the best of them. Interesting lectures, made art fun and relevant

Don't listen to the bad reviews, they're all whiny freshmen who make the class seem a lot worse than it is. Levine's lectures are organized and thought-provoking, and he's hilariously cynical. The readings are long, and it's a decent amount of work (nine short papers), but it's not that difficult. Looking back, I'm really happy I took this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This is such a good class. Professor Levine makes art interesting and so relevant. I recommend this triple I.

Interesting material but lectures tended to be repetitive/oversimplified. Assignment descriptions were vague and the second paper is unnecessarily due on LDOC. All grading is outsourced to a TA who never attends class and whom you will never meet. Her grading is fair, but pretty harsh. The final was hard. Take the class if you're ok with an A-/B+.

Honestly, this course sucked and I'm sorry the professors are getting bad reviews but it was mostly from the TAs. There was NO clear grading criteria, pretty much graded however they wanted to grade. NO FEEDBACK, and the few feedback they gave, when you would correct it, they would take points off and contradict their last feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: IDST-116 (gender) is not a bad class, and I feel that I've learned a lot (I actually enjoy the lectures very much).  However, the midterm and final (which cumulate to 45% of your final grade) test your ability to memorize hundreds of terms rather than requiring any real depth of knowledge, it's ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class with Dr. Levine. He challenged me to think in new ways about the world around me. Every work and reading he chose was intentional and he was a really well spoken and interesting lecturer. My only problem was that he asks leading questions that are posed as open ended but have a right answer. It is not discussion based.

Professor Levine is definitely not as bad as everyone makes him out to be. He made the class quite entertaining at times, and I learned a lot from his lectures, though there was a lot of content, especially for the midterm, but you are sure to do well if you put in the effort.
Really good class and professor. Will try to take him again.

Levine is a great professor-- anyone who says otherwise needs to grow up and learn that memorizing a few term is not some great injustice. His lectures were very funny + engaging and he was always available to meet with students. Great class would take again.

Loved this class, Levine is clearly super passionate about his topic and is great at teaching it! Grades can be a bit hard to follow since there aren't a whole lot of graded assignments in class, but would absolutely retake this again and take another class with him. Super interesting!

Professor Levine is the worst professor out of the three in the gender triple-I. This course is terrible and I dreaded going to class M,W,F. Levine's lectures are boring and offensive to women. Almost every image of artwork shown to us had a naked woman in it. He is rude to students and likes to pick people out from 300, and humiliate them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Really good professor. He kept things a little light but also really interesting. Highly recommend.

He wasn't horrible, but I definitely did not enjoy having him as a prof. He tried to be funny but it was always just awkward, and his lectures were either insanely boring or insanely weird. He always wanted us to know more about the authors of the readings rather than the actual meanings of them.
Very caring and passionate professor. Really cares about students. I had an issue and met with him and he was very sensitive.

This class is a lot of work. He is not very understanding and not a kind person at all. While it's not the most impossible class, it is hard and it's a lot of boring memorization of art pieces and their artists. You'll learn something for sure. Up 2 u whether it's worth the stress of memorizing 60+ art pieces, their artists, and their significance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good class good professor. A little hard with 3 subjects but all triple is are like that. Professor Levine makes it interesting and fun.
Yes what these last ones said is right. Class is not so hard and professor Levine is great. The rest are just complaining about having to actually do their work and be in college.

if you think this class is hard, you should not attend university. sir levine is my idol and i will take any one of his classes that i can. the TAs grade fairly easily. its a lot of readiing but its not necessary because the midterm is short and the class is mostly common knowledge.

In a class full of ultra-sensitive losers, you'll see various reviews on here that are simply a spiteful attempt to hinder Professor Levine's reputation. In actuality, he is a fabulous lecturer in a class that is possibly easier than any I took in high school. Any rating below a three on here is the result of an ego hit to low-achieving students.

Anyone who thinks this class is hard has no idea what a hard class is. His lectures are very interesting and entertaining, and he is clearly extremely passionate about the subject matter. Makes lectures fun and interactive, I look forward to coming to this class.

Cary was a terrible gender professor. He did nothing but continuously repeat different words for the female genitalia. He is very problematic and out of touch with reality. gross never take this class again/

Do not listen to other people's ratings of the gender triple-i. The class really isn't that hard. You can get by just skimming the readings, and the papers are pretty easy. The professors are friendly and genuinely want you to succeed. Everyone giving this class bad reviews plays games the whole lecture and expects not to have to actually learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Levine was clearly dedicated to gender representation in art history. However, his lectures were very monotonous and at times vague, with very little guidance on what exactly we should be taking away. If you enjoy art history, you'll most likely enjoy him, but if not, good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is a really good class and Professor Levine is the best of the three. Really made me appreciate art in a different way.  I would def take him again.

DO NOT listen to any other reviews. The people posting are mad that they had to pay attention to do well on the midterm and blame him for their incompetence. I didn't always pay attention either but that's not his fault! He's very funny and knowledgeable about art, and his portion of the class was pretty easy, albeit weird. Pick this triple-I!

He makes it fun and interesting. Yes, he's a little sarcastic and doesn't take bs from students. But you shouldn't sleep in class anyway. I never thought I would like art history, but Professor Levine makes it really interesting and relevant.
I would defintely recommend this class and Levine. All around good class and prof

Gender is a great class and Levine is the best of the three. I don't know what the neg reviewers are talking about. Levine is clear and passionate and caring about students. Most of the negativity is bc he doesn't let you off easy. Your in college, grow up! Levine is excellent as is this class!

Prof Levine is the worst professor out of the 3 professors in the Gender Triple-I. He literally screamed at the class to "shut up" and humiliates students who are sleeping/on phone in a 300+ lecture class. Showed fake s*x scenes and then never discussed it?? Class graded on impossible midterm/finals that are worth 45% of your grade. DO NOT TAKE!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: literally horrid. IDST 116 (Gender) is a fine class EXCEPT for Levine's portion. He expects a class full of freshman that were automatically enrolled in this Triple-I to memorize 50 art pieces, their artists, history, significance (in his pov), that we've maybe talked about once, if even at all. Class is horribly unstructured.

reviews.comment: awful. so much reading for no reason. midterm and final take up 45% of grade and isnt even what we discussed in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take gender (IDST116) The material is boring, class is not structured well, way more work than any other Triple-I. LONG, boring readings 3 times a week, 3 difficult quizzes on those readings. did NOT prepare us at all for the midterm. I'll be happy if I get a 70 on the midterm because this class is so dreary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take gender as your triple-I. The class overall has very little structure, and the professors do nothing to help. Levine is very condescending and expects everyone to think art history is the most important thing in the world. This class is definitely harder than it needs to be, and the teachers DO NOT CARE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible professor with no common sense. Did not have a clear syllabus, plan, or anything regarding how the course works.

Levine might be a good professor for art, but for Gender, try to steer clear of him. He went the whole semester telling us we only had to "interpret" art subjectively, and then 2 classes before the midterm, he told us we had to memorize a bunch of art that we covered, their creators, and their history. Highly disappointing, do not take him.
so annoying. the worst person to listen to ever. not understanding. toxic.
they don't even know what they are talking about. They are giving tremendous amounts of readings, and quizzes for every class, and never give practice for midterms.

Prof Levine was funny and pretty approachable. Lectures were were pretty interesting and if you take good notes you'll easily get good grades on the midterm and final. There were two essays for this class but they were easy and only had to be 2-3 pages. Overall, I'd recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof. Levine is a real art world guy. I gained a lot of base-level knowledge from this class, and found the lectures interesting and easy to follow. However, they could have gone a bit more in depth -- a lot of it was repetitive. If you attend lectures, take good notes, and do the readings (which are pretty easy/short for ARTH), you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Levine's 285H is a pretty good class. He is funny and approachable. The discussions weren't as interesting as you might expect them to be considering the material. The papers weren't too hard. We had to meet in groups periodically outside of class to discuss the readings, so he essentially added an unofficial recitation to the course.

Fairly vapid course full of base-level knowledge of artists and artworks. All the information/material provided to us felt like it was gleaned off the Wikipedia page of each artist before class, nothing very insightful or interesting. Assignments were vague, with no true rubrics ever being created. Not accepting of critiques he doesn't agree with.

He clearly cares about his students. Unfortunately, class assignments were vague and the discussion was as bland and conceited as you might expect from an honors class about contemporary art history. I'm not sure he graded any of the assignments himself, but grades were harsh without much explanation.

IDST 190 (gender) is a really easy and interesting course. Highly recommend for first years trying to check off some gen eds. The class is really easy and straightforward. If you just go to class and do the homework, it's really easy to succeed. The only exams are the midterm and the final, and both are really manageable.

This is not an easy class. But if you want to begin to understand contemporary art (emphasis and begin), then you will not do any better anywhere else in the world within an academic setting. He fits the perfect NYC art critic description. And he knows his stuff. He is literally writing the history of contemporary art. He will challenge you.

Prof Levine is an acquired taste. He's pretty savage, which is funny until you get caught in the crossfire. In and out of class, he will be brutally honest. He can do a little better with providing feedback and clarity for assignments, but he's a great professor overall. Really makes you think.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy, the class isn't too hard (just make sure you participate in discussion and show up to class bc attendance counts). Every two weeks-ish you have to ready about 40 pages and that can be kind of hard, but that's the only assignment besides the mid-term and final. Would recommend this class to non-art majors looking for a VP credit
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: took BIOL 490!

Dr. Mitchell, my glorious king. I barely had to put any effort into the class because it was heavily discussion based but still learnt so much from it. Very accommodating if things come up for you. Attendance policy was pretty chill. Please take this class.

This class was easy and discussion-based—few lectures, just student-led conversations on the readings. He was clear, responsive to emails, and very understanding if issues came up. The discussion format was super valuable, and I learned a lot in this class. We could ask questions about anything—bio, research, even current events. Highly recommend!

Dr. Mitchell is one of the kindest professors I have had - seminar style class with students rotating leading. Come to class, read a section of the textbook/article, and ask questions. He wants to see that you learned something new, and is very flexible and gives a lot of grace with grading/presentation topics/leading discussions. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Discussion-based class. 2-3 readings, come in and talk about it. Very kind and understanding professor, very fun class. Understands not everyone has a strong background in the content and is open to questions. Highly recommend.

Dr. Mitchell is one of the most genuine professors at UNC. The class is a little lecture heavy, but it *is* an upper level course, so it's not terrible. He truly cares about his students and makes sure his powerpoints are detailed and well thought out

Mitchell is a decent professor.  He just reads off the powerpoint slides (which he posts online) and doesn't add any more information.  Only tests on what he goes over in class, though the test was a lot harder than expected.  Decent for 201 though.
amazing professor and lecturer, plus hes pretty cute and has a nice accent

Absolutely incredible teacher with clear guidelines, a student-centered grading policy, and great accessibility outside class. Clearly understands what he's doing and works to make sure you do as well.

He is extremely smart, but kind of goes beyond the course material to explain what can be done in further math classes (which is great for math majors, just not my thing). 2 midterms and a final, final can replace the lowest midterm. A bunch of homework sheets that are way harder than the exam questions. Super nice guy with plenty of office hours.

I love Tom. Amazing lectures that really made the content make sense. Posted notes were neat as a pin. Second midterm and final were hard, but totally worth it to have him as a lecturer. Highly recommend for math majors
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chandler's a super well-organized prof with amazing lectures, and the content isn't too hard. He's definitely passionate about the class and wants everyone to learn/pass. Homeworks and practice exams aren't too difficult and prepare you well for exams. Strongly recommend taking 383 with him, it'd be a mistake not to. Also take linear algebra first!

British, lively, and efficient at explaining concepts and clearing up confusion. He shares his lecture notes, and practice sets mirror his brief, straightforward exams. Graded by weekly HW, two midterms, and a HARD non-cumulative final that replaces your lowest midterm.
Really enthusiastic and passionate about what he was teaching, made class super interesting and enjoyable. Only graded by weekly problem sets, two midterms and HARD final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best math class I've ever taken! Classes are extremely structured to really make you understand the concepts, beyond just knowing the right equations/methods. Very smart guy, but explains it clearly. Office hours are extremely helpful. Weekly homeworks and midterms are only 4 questions, very similar to the practice. Definitely take him if you can!

Super engaging professor. I would only recommend you take him if you are a math major. He dives very deep into theory and as a non-math major myself I found it hard to follow. Exams are just four questions and the second one is a lot harder than the first. Very application based as well, which I enjoyed.
I love this maf man!

Great lecturer, I was very engaged even in a longer T/TH block. He expects you to read but he also covers important topics from the readings during lecture. 2 group presentations (can't pick group); some had issue with lack of detail in his rubrics/instructions. He gives off the impression that he wants us to succeed. Sometimes takes roll.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Lentz in spring 25. Coursework was light but I would not take this to fulfill a focus capacity. He had no grading criteria or rubrics, so that allowed TAs to grade arbitrarily. When I asked for specific feedback and which criteria I had points docked from, my TA gave vague answers and was adamant that her grading was correct.
Doctor Lentz

Professor Lentz was a good professor and was available to help with course content. The material was fairly easy, but expectations for the quiz, midterm, and final were unclear, and his advice focused on big-picture themes, while the tests asked about specific details. The papers lacked rubrics, which can impact your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very few assignments but feedback was delayed. Course content is not difficult. Lectures could sometimes be dull, but not unbearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Content isn't hard, but grading is vague and based on just a few assignments with no real guidance. Despite full participation and strong work, I got a B+. Prof disappears for multiple lectures (trips to Singapore, etc.), returns feedback too late, and doesn't put in any grades until they are finalized (likely to avoid receiving complaints).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only had 5 graded assignments for semester. TAs did most the grading.  Lectures were boring.  He was approachable.   Left halfway through semester to go to Singapore for 2 weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Lentz is probably one of the best professors I have had at UNC. As someone whose major is not geography, his lectures are beyond fascinating. There are two papers, one quiz, and one midterm. There are also readings to do before each class, but he covers the important parts of these readings in class lectures.

Professor Lentz is easily one of the best profs I've ever had at UNC. He is a natural teacher. Very knowledgeable/passionate about SE Asia, genuinely cares, and keeps class fresh with field trips, museum exhibits, and group work. Two short papers + two quizzes; readings are hefty but fascinating. You'll stay engaged and actually learn a lot.

Dr. Lentz is truly a gem. He is so passionate about teaching and incredibly accessible outside of class. Ask him about his research! Get to know him outside of class! Highly recommend for any course of his.

One of the most informative classes I've taken! The quiz, midterm, and final are all multiple choice, papers are graded very leniently. Attendance is not mandatory and if you go, you get extra credit for EVERY time you attend. Uses slides for terms, but most of the information is given orally. You can do very well if you put in a little effort.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Lentz is very knowledgeable about Southeast Asia and very passionate about teaching it. I found this class very engaging and fascinating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed the content of Professor Lentz's class, and always found him incredibly helpful outside of class. Go to class and take notes, the lecture content is what he will test you on. The class grade is based on attendance, 2 quizzes, 2 papers, and a final. There is NO 'busy work' which is GREAT!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: graded by 2 quizzes short ppr final ppr participation final exam. NEVER uploaded quizzes participation final exam grades.Entered total grades w/o letting us know our exam grade. Rude over email& dismissed my concerns about grades not being entered properly. NOT student-friendly. DONT TAKE. inappropriately calculated grades Not a person of integrity
Don't know your grade until the end of the semester, and is graded by too less things.

This class was very reading based, but if u go to class n pay attention you'll do good. I was reluctant to take this class but it turned out to be so interesting and I actually enjoyed going. Professor Lentz is great and really inspiring, its cool bc u learn and think differently about food and the world around you. 10/10 class. recommend.
You won't know your grade until the end of the semester when they are submitted to ConnectCarolina and unclear grading criteria. not a bad class but not an easy A.
Rude and condescending. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Blind-sided all students by changing how participation was graded. Syllabus said he would take attendance regularly and never did, so randomly did one day and then bumped everyone down an ENTIRE letter grade that did not go THAT day. When asked about it this is what he sent students: you can't email me til fall 2022 and ur grade might go down MORE.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He was a nice guy and so were the TA's, but the syllabus is sorta misleading. I got a 60 on the first quiz and although there were supposed to be multiple quizzes, my one 60 accounted for 10% of my grade. Also, he is not very clear on participation and what it means in the class, so stay safe and just go to the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class is very lecture heavy and kinda hard to get into at first. Prof. Lentz is very helpful and caring to support students. The grading might be a little harsh for papers but the quiz/exams are not bad.

Prof Lentz is a passionate professor who cares about the topic. However, the grading was confusing and did not match what was on the syllabus. We didn't get grades for the papers until right before the final exam. The class was interesting, but if you're looking for just a gen-ed, this wouldn't be the class I'd recommend.

Prof Lentz is an awesome professor that really cares about the subject material. He takes care to break down and explain complex concepts in geography while also relating them to real-world examples. This class is graded primarily by 2 five page papers and a final, but none of them are particularly difficult. Wonderful experience with Prof Lentz!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Lentz is a very passionate and kind professor. The class consisted of going to lectures where he would talk about a topic and we would take notes and sometimes discuss it or discuss readings we did before class. The only homework, aside from 2 papers, was doing readings. The readings are a lot, but a good portion of them are interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Lentz is a very sweet and understanding person. He really cares about his students and asks for feedback on how to make the class better. There are a lot of readings for the class, but a lot of them were really interesting. He grades hard on papers, but there are only two of them in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: THE BEST CLASS IVE TAKEN AT UNC. you will learn about all aspects of the food system in a survey manner. Proff Lentz is knowledgeable in all topics, funny, has a huge vocabulary and is super open to feedback. There are 2 easy MC tests, and 2 papers. All the readings are engaging and you can write about whatever you fancy. MUST TAKE

Dr. Lentz is an extremely knowledgeable and dedicated professor. The lectures were engaging (but it was hard to make myself pay attention over zoom). The class makes you think deeply and learn. The reading is interesting and not overwhelming. The papers were graded a bit harshly for a pandemic tho but I think that was our TA not Lentz.

I love Prof Lentz as a person; he is interesting and passionate about what he teaches. However, I zoned out every single class period with it being online. The material is pretty interesting but the readings were sooooooo long, so if you're not into humanities this will not be an easy gen ed. Group projects were super fun and not too hard, tho.
Dr. Lentz was very engaging and made the class material interesting. He welcomed student feedback and was extremely flexible with extensions/mental health/making students feel comfortable!

do not take this class if you're trying to get a gen ed out of the way!! I was actually really excited about this material and professor lentz is extremely knowledgeable, but his lectures are dense and so hard to listen to over zoom. The are only a couple papers that are graded surprisingly difficult. Not an easy A

Extremely knowledgable and very approachable professor! Exams are easy, but papers are graded harshly, so watch out! Doing bare minimum and merely following instructions instead thinking outside the box will get you no higher than a C on them! If you really want to learn something though, this class is great and Prof. Lentz is a real gem!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super smart guy who is really passionate about what he teaches will definitely take more classes with him in the future.

Dr. Lentz sometimes gets off topic during classes, and uses ambiguous phrases/terminology which makes it difficult to stay attentive and take notes. He also doesn't have powerpoint slides, but nonetheless gives insightful lectures. An easy A as long as you show up to take notes and are good at writing essays.

Prof. Lentz was one of the best I've had at UNC! He's clearly passionate about the subject and that was reflected in how engaging his lectures were. Papers weren't too long or difficult, and he kept the midterm/final very simple. I learned a lot from this course and would absolutely take another class with him in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Definitely my favorite class at UNC! Dr. Lentz provided students with an impressive and comprehensive explanation of food justice worldwide, and I really enjoyed his lectures! The papers were a lot of fun to write, and the grading criteria was relatively easy. He also handled COVID-19 extremely well, and I overall appreciated his flexibility!!!

Great lecturer. Prof. Lentz really is an information haven on everything related to food sciences. The class is mostly article readings and discussions. The papers were not difficult at all and give students flexibility to write about the topic of their choice. Definitely would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lentz is a good guy and smart prof, but perhaps a bit strange. I highly doubt that he has ever uttered a curse word in his life. He and his TA Michelle were very accommodating, provided solid feedback, and the assignments were kindly graded. Very lecture oriented so while I can stay focused in a 50 min class, wouldn't suggest for TuTh classes.

120 and 392 were fine. All lectures, no powerpoints. Nice videos in 120. Lentz is kind but tends to overcomplicate things. Not sure how this hasn't been mentioned, but he uses "okay" like a valley girl uses "like" - as much as 4x per sentence. Kept count for a while and he said ok over 135 times in each 50 min class. Drove me a little nuts.

Professor Lentz is amazing. He will force you to think critically and go beyond the basics. There are 2 quizzes (pretty easy) and 3 papers. Professor Lentz, in my opinion, is a fair grader, but some people found him to be difficult when grading papers. Work hard and you will succeed. You don't need the textbooks. I highly recommend GEOG 64!

Honestly one of the best professors I've had while at UNC. Lentz seems to genuinely care about the growth of his students and puts every bit of effort he can into make it happen. Bit of a tough grader on papers but always gives very constructive feedback to explaining shortcomings and making recommendations for improvement.
Great lectures, very engaging but grades tough on papers for nitpicky things. Honestly a pretty tough first year seminar but if you're really interested in Vietnamese history, you'll learn a lot

Professor Lentz knows everything there is to know about Vietnam and its history. Grade consists of 2 quizzes and 3 papers. Tough grader at first but gives good feedback and will work with you as much as needed outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Lentz is a very engaging teacher. The lectures are all oral, but he engages with the class and is engaging when lecturing. The workload is not much, with textbook reading which is helpful for context but not necessary, and only a few papers and quizzes throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Lentz is one of those pprofessors who lectures for the entire class with NO PowerPoint. He does not give you any access to lecture notes what so ever. He rambles and jumps from topic to topic and makes no sense during lecture. His lectures dont follow any of the text book readings. NO test prep for midterm or final. HE DOESNT ROUND!! 89.99B+
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It was a little hard to get used to his teaching style, he doesn't use slides and often goes off on tangents. However, once you settle in the class is really interesting and the tests were straight forward, mult choice. None of the textbooks are really needed but they help when writing essays. If you show up and listen, no outside work is needed.

Mr. Lentz is a great lecturer, but the topic was pretty boring. Somehow he made learning about seeds halfway interesting. There were readings to be completed before every class, but I never did the readings. I went to class and learned everything from the lectures. There is two papers and a midterm, so there is rarely homework unless you read.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Lentz was an amazing professor, all lectures were given orally without powerpoints so you must go to class to know the material. He assigns pre-class readings for every class and discusses them at some length during lecture, so it helps to know what he's talking about as he attempts to engage the class in discussion. One of the best here.

Professor Lentz is smart, too smart. His lectures can be a little much sometimes due to his complex vocabulary. The class is relatively easy and quite interesting. It challenged my ideas concerning he way in which I view the world. If you go to class and do your readings you will have no problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Lentz is an amazing professor. His lectures are very clear and make you think about everyday things in a completely different way. His class is well-structured. There are three short papers (2-3 pages), one midterm, one short quiz, and the final. He assigns readings for every class but you don't necessarily need to read them. Easy class.

I am obsessed with him & will take more classes with him. He is brilliant & his lectures will often make you think about things in a way you never have before. He is very helpful & truly cares about his students. He has made geography so interesting to me that I'm considering minoring, and I never would've thought I would ever say that. He rocks.

Professor Lentz is very knowledgeable and very helpful. He will answer any questions that you have. There are no tests, a few quizzes, and a few papers. He is pretty strict when grading the paper. He assigned short readings before each class and participation is required. Overall it was a great class and I would take it again.

Professor Lentz makes class enjoyable and really encourages class participation. There are no tests, and very few quizzes, so the majority of your grade comes from papers. If you are a superb writer, then you will be fine, but otherwise, he is a very strict grader and isn't all too  clear on what exactly makes a paper a great paper in his eyes.

If you are relatively strong at Spanish you will not find this course challenging. However, there are some weeks with a lot of condensed work. Prof is extremely caring and kind and is not a harsh grader. I just suck at Spanish.

I loved her!  She is super sweet and a very understanding professor usually willing to take things late as long as you contact her and explain. She never called on anyone or forced them to answer. She brought us candy and food for our end of semester presentations which was not required of her. She is very approachable and just a sweet prof.

I loved Professor Arango-Sosa!  She was super sweet and understanding.  Assignments were easy, and tests were fine.  You just have to study and make sure you understand the material. She was a very fair grader on papers and presentations.  Remember to keep up with MSL and participate in class!

I loved Prof Sosa! She's a really lenient grader and is so sweet and understanding. You definitely have to participate in class, but as long as you do, you'll get a good participation grade. It's a flipped classroom, but the exams were pretty easy if you've taken Spanish in the past (plus they tell you what's on the exam). Try to get her for 203!

I had missed out on two years of Spanish and was still able to keep up well enough, especially considering how little previous Spanish teachers had taught me. Every time I had to make up quizzes due to medical reasons, she was very understanding and accommodated for me. She was also pretty lenient with grading at some points. I highly recommend.

I have never enjoyed Spanish and this class proved it. Professor Arango-Sosa was amazing and was always willing to meet with me when I had questions. No matter how hard I studied, the exams killed me. A huge portion of your grade is participation. She doesn't care if you're grammatically correct, as long as you speak in Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is nice and a mostly lenient grader. She is not perfect, but if you need to take Span 203, try to take her. She does not make anything harder than it has to be in terms of workload. Make sure you participate in class, and you should be good.

She is nice, and has a pretty defined structure for the class. Occasionally, she struggled with the technology aspects of online teaching and she pretty much reads from the textbook, but she explains it well. Probably not the best SPAN 105 professor, but she is definitely better than a solid amount of them.

Such a sweet woman. Very fair and reasonable with grading. Clearly wants you to learn Spanish more than she out to get you grading wise (would rather you branch out and get it wrong, then stick to simple structures, and rewards you grade wise for trying). Would have loved to haver for 203.

Prof Arango-Sosa is really nice and a very very lenient grader. She encourages everyone to participate but doesnt call anyone out. Theres a lot of partner work and homework after every class but it doesnt take more than 30 minutes.

Massi is a great teacher as well as a person. While he is strict, he is also funny. He makes learning another language cool and fun. His positivity and encouragement he gives to students make them want to learn more. Because Spanish classes at KU fill up crazy fast, this language is a good alternate. Italian is closely related to Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Massi is awesome! He cares so much about his students and puts in a lot of effort towards class. You have to do work outside of the class- as with any language- but it is easy if you stay on top of your stuff. He makes the class fun and everyone is involved during it. Attendance is key
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Honestly, I didn't put in much effort and only took the class because it was a requirement. However, Professor Massi made it fun. He is an easy going guy, and the overall atmosphere of the class is relaxed.
truly caring and amazing professor

I had Professor Cilizoglu at St. Olaf College, where she taught Intro to International Relations. It was a relatively laid-back class, but paying attention, doing the readings, and participating in class certainly helped. She's passionate about the subject matter and entertains student questions. However, her class isn't very engaging so beware.
Never taking again, will waste your time. Very unorganized.
Worst Professor Ever.

Love Professor Cilizoglu, fantastic professor who is well qualified. She does a great job at making class interesting while combining wit and humor. Test's were pretty tough but would take anything by her again.

Menevis teaches POLI150 for a small class (30-40 students) and it makes it super interesting because she always tries to engage in a debate. Her course is clear and easy to understand, and she is always available if you have further questions out of class. The multiple choice part of her tests are easy, the short questions are harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The only hard part about this class is trying to pay attention and take notes for 75 minutes straight, other than that, the material that would be on the test was extremely straightforward and the tests were exactly what was in the notes/ power points. The textbooks aren't really necessary and they are really expensive I wouldn't recommend buying.

There is a ridiculous amount of reading for this class. Also, lectures are packed with a large amount of information that will not be on the tests. Note-taking here will give you a headache. Study hard if you still want to take this class, but for a 100-level course, I was struggling.

Cicek did not make lectures very engaging and interesting, so it was very hard to pay attention. Her power points were vague. My friends and I absolutely dreaded going to this class. The tests are very hard, she expects you to know all the drawn plans of each city. This course could have been better if taught by someone else.

Worst class I have taken at UNC by far. The lectures are long and boring, there is a ridiculous amount of material to cover for tests and exams, and there is a participation component in the class. Definitely find another class to get the WB credit.

This class wasn't too amazing, but it is a WB gen ed. It wasn't awful but the papers are tough and the tests are worse. Cicek was a pretty entertaining lecturer for the material but it wasn't enough, especially to keep my attention for an hour and a half. If you like ancient history, then go for it, otherwise you may want to look elsewhere.
She did not make the material clear at all especially the material for the midterm. She did not engage the class and her lectures were extremely boring.
I enjoyed listening to Cicek, however, Ancient Cities was hard to capture my attention at times. Her points however, are pretty clear and if you pay attention you should get out with at least a B.

Currently enrolled in the class, was told it was an easy way to fulfill a gen ed. Not true.  Class requires a lot of work, exams require so much preparation and it often isn't enough. The papers are graded with remorse for the ridiculous exams, but it still isn't enough to have a lift your grade.

I took this class having been told it was an easy A with a different teacher. This teacher in conjunction with Matt Schueller present long and extremely dense powerpoints on overwhelmingly mundane history. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Working hard for a B-/B. With that being said, Beeby is more interesting than the other lecturer and teaches better .

You can tell she knows exactly what she's talking about and she's very passionate about the material, but be ready for long lectures and the tests are almost impossible after *15 hours* of studying. Would NOT take again

Do NOT take this class. Material was extremely boring, and the midterm was full of ridiculously minute details that nobody could be expected to remember. She is a nice person but not a good teacher, gives unclear instruction regularly and is difficult to understand. I would recommend avoiding this class at all costs.
Math 232 is a HARD class.  I have always loved math until I took this class.  He is a nice teacher but easily confuses students

Worst math teacher I've ever had. Always gets lost in the problems, can't use technology, made us all buy books that he wanted to use not the ones the book store sells. Unorganized. You never know what section you're learning anthe examples he gives have nothing to do with the homework and neither has anything todo with the tests. Enjoy

He grades hard and takes off points for trivial errors. Gets confused about his own problems, so he confuses the class. Has assigned nonexistant homework problems and has repeated homework problems. He seems nice enough, but don't take his classes if you don't already know the material or if you want a good grade.

He holds consistent office hours but his communication skills are so poor that it's pointless. He'd start on one topic and forget what he was doing midsentence and move on to a different example. He didn't know how to do half of the problems and mainly read frm the book. We had one test all year and ambiguous grading. Worst teacher I have ever had.

One of the worst math professors I have ever had!  This class is known to be hard, but his absent-mindedness and unrecognizable scribbles on the board did NOT help.  Had to drop this class.  He's crazy smart and has good stories, and he's nice (he pulled a box of kleenex out of his desk drawer during office hours one day) but he cannot teach!

The limit as x approaches a passing grade in this class basically doesn't exist. He has cool classical music playing in his office during office hours though, so take advantage of them. You're better off getting the cafeteria workers to teach you calculus than this guy.

HE IS THE MOST HORRIBLE TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD. and i have had some bad ones. i really hope he reads this so he will retire and acknowledge that he CAN'T TEACH. he should retire anyway, he makes so many mistakes because of his age. please don't make the same mistake i did. DROP THIS CLASS

I frankly thought that he was the most horrible teacher there is!  I mean I didn't understand a word he was talking about.  You should only take that class if you are willing to teach yourself, which defeats the purpose of having an instructor, right?!  Anyways, never take his class...taking his class will mess up your gpa.
Professor Cima is impossible to follow while teaching and does hardly anything to help the students that are struggling.

This guy was a dinosaur when I had his class (about 8 years ago).  Loved to use the overhead, and we could barely read his scribble.  Assigned homework, forgot about it, then collected it 2 weeks after it was due, so you usually didn't have it on you!!  Tests were a nightmare.  Took Assani's class the following semester, easily made a B+ AVOID CIMA
Attempted to schedule a test the day after Halloween, but might be talked out of it.  Rather confusing at times, expect to teach yourself from the book.

This is the old Math 128.  The material is pretty easy, but it's easy to mess up on the quizes.  There was no mandatory HW, but you should do the HW he suggests.  It's very possible to do well in the class, but it's made more difficult because he is disorganized and often confusing.
He seems like a nice guy, but I didn't like the way he taught.  It seems like he spent most of the time going over problems that we had already done for homework.  I didn't understand why...
He should be fired. Too old to still be teaching. He's mean, too.

Very difficult class.  Even after going to office hours and getting a tutor I was still amazed to pass the class.  I never felt like we did sample problems in class that were similar to the homework.  A lot of times it was hard to follow what he was doing in class.
Teaching style is to write equations on the board, boring.

dont bother buying or reading the textbook. Memorizing the videos and vocab are what you need to succeed for the final and midterm. Group projects are a headache so get started early. Putting in decent effort into projects will get you at least an 85.

Get ready to be graded on random, arbitrary things often unrelated to marketing. I'm surprised some comments call her their second mom; she is pretty scary to me. It's going to be way harder than necessary for you to get a good grade in this class. Take a different prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Malhotra is very knowledgable about marketing, and it makes lectures great. The flipped format is helpful for learning, and I find her, and her directions clear. My complaint would be the group cases, as I spent more time fixing others work and formatting rather than actually using marketing strategies. Grading is subjective and unclear.

Claudia is an incredible professor who clearly cares about her teachers and is very passionate about marketing. She always brought energy to the class and it was never boring. The class does have a lot of work and the case assignments can be tedious. The midterm I thought wasn't bad and final was harder. Both very heavy on memorization.

Amazing professor, cares so much about both her students and the material. Her passion and fun in class activities made this one of my favorite classes at UNC. Cases were a lot of work but graded fairly (loved new rubric system). Midterm/final surprisingly hard, definitely study and practice term definitions. Highly recommend, learned a lot!

30% of grade is 3 case studies she grades very tough and also includes an unrealistic page limit. For exams it's literally just hundreds of definitions, which is fine but she creates really niche arbitrary questions that I don't think trust ones true knowledge of Marketing. Very tough but also very nice at the same time. Would never take her again

Claudia is someone that was meant to be a teacher & it is so evident. She is so caring and understanding of her students & I genuinely appreciate her as a human being sooo much. Honestly, I won't say this class is easy, because I didn't find that to be the case. But taking her class was worth it because she is so knowledgable, passionate, & kind.

Claudia is so kind! There are a lot of chapters to get through but she does her best to cover them. I kind of did bad on the midterm & final, but looking back, there was def a way to do better. I recommend rewatching the lectures and using the sharpen app/website to help with vocab. The MC isn't bad, the written portion on exam is where it matters

Claudia is very passionate and knowledgable about marketing. She cares about her students' success inside and beyond the classroom. Group projects are pretty grueling - try and choose a good partner or group if possible. Exams are straightforward and fair. Lectures are lively, interactive, and include engaging in-class activities and guest speakers

Claudia is THE marketing professor. She is knowledgable, spirited, and kind. That being said this class is not an easy A. She lets you somewhat pick your own groups which was helpful and imo the cases weren't too bad. Exams are tough but fair, just study the vocab from the textbook. If you want a career in marketing take 406 with her.

F teacher. If you can apply the key terms (at the end of each chapter in the book), you will do well on exams. Meets once a week (watch all the pre-recordings done b4 class).Very dependent on Case Studies. Try to find hard-working people. You can do well if you do the work and meet with your team b4 the case studies are due.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Claudia is like your mom. She cares about you, your career and has very engaging lectures.

Claudia herself is amazing, but the 406 experience is tarnished by the risk of getting a group of incompetents to be stuck with through the course whose team work and evaluations will account towards at least 35% of your course grade. You can probably tell what sort of group I got. Great class besides that. Don't BS the class & you will have fun.

Claudia is a very kind professor. However, this class stripped me of any interest of marketing. Strangely difficult exams coupled with terrible group projects made this class a drag. Take this class with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Claudia clearly cares about her students and will do a lot to accommodate them. She genuinely is passionate about marketing and tries to make it as engaging is possible. The exams are extremely difficult and her grading regarding the case assignments is pretty inconsistent. I wish there was more room for growth in class.
This class is harder than you think it will be but she is very kind and good at teaching

Don't listen to the negative reviews! She is passionate about marketing and her students and makes every class fun. Watch the online videos and go through the in-class PowerPoint, you will be fine. Make her given corrections to each report (3 total) and study for the final!( had an A all semester, didn't study bc of easy midterm, ended with a B+).
Take with someone else

Heard a lot of negative things going into this class and heavily considered switching to another professor. Ended up staying in the class and really enjoyed it. Would highly recommend taking it. Claudia teaches the other professors so you might as well take it with her. Exams are challenging but fair, group cases require thinking outside the box.

Prof. Claudia was great! She lets you pick your team for the cases, but her feedback didn't really help us improve. Her exams were much harder than they were supposed to be, and she always tried to trick us on the multiple choice questions. You HAVE to read the textbook for the exams, and it's well over a 1000 pages long so get started early!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Claudia doesn't give clear instructions for group cases and isn't helpful in prepping for exams. She grades super tough and the exams are so much harder than they need to be. She can be condescending when students ask questions or answer something wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Claudia is super understanding. I thought her grading on the team assignments was a bit harsh, but not bad enough to severely impact your final grade. The midterms were pretty hard and you definitely need to study a lot. She doesn't give grade cutoffs at the beginning, so you never really know your final grade until the end. Pay attention in class!

Claudia was a great professor, very nice, and easily accessible. The class is pretty tough. There were three group projects that she graded harshly, so try to find people who you want to work with. The midterm and final weren't that bad in my opinion, but you should read the textbook chapters if you want to do well on them.

class itself is easy: just watching vids/taking notes on textbook for hw. Group cases: choose a good one since she grades these harshly when you only have 2 pgs of space to write with minimal instruction on what she wants. Tests unreasonably hard w/ MC having synonyms in the answers. Low test avgs. Can't review past test and unhelpful office hrs.

Claudia is really knowledgeable about marketing and gives off great energy during lectures.  Your grade's dependent on participation, midterm, final and 3 case analysis group projects.  The tests are hard and she's a strict grader for the cases.  On the plus side, class is only one day a week and the asynchronous component wasn't difficult.

Not really sure how anyone could like her. My least favorite class of all the BUSI core requirements I have had to take. I thought marketing would be fun/interesting but she took all fun out of the class. The groups projects are very annoying but you do get to sort of pick your groups.

Claudia is extremely knowledge about the material, and even more accessible outside the class. The midterm exam is fair, and the final exam is NOT cumulative. A large part of your grade is three group cases, so make sure you are with good people (you more or less get to choose your team members). Don't love marketing, but she made it interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Don't really know anyone that likes Claudia or the class. Average on midterm was about a 78 and she never released average for final, but there is no curve in the class. Incredibly boring and uninteresting class. Unfortunately, you gotta take it because its a core class and normally she teaches most sections.

Since this is a core class it's really not too difficult. Claudia is a great person and really easy to communicate with, and she really really cares about her students. The material is hard if you can't stand marketing BUT she makes her supporting videos really well and the exams are mostly from that content.

She's really sweet and checked in on our mental health frequently. Grade was made up mainly of short 3 team case write ups, a midterm, final, and participation. Midterm/final's weren't too bad if you take notes during the video lectures. Try and speak up in class. (textbook readings weren't essential imo)

Claudia is nice, but she made marketing very stressful and not enjoyable for me. Her tests are annoyingly specific and not really indicative of what's learned in class. She never really helps prepare you for anything, and her classes are always cluttered with work that you have to finish after class. Wouldn't highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Claudia is very passionate about marketing and knows what she's talking about. She's also pretty understanding of the situation we are under, so if you reach out she will be pretty flexible. Nevertheless, she has high expectations, and sometimes it's unclear how we are expected to do certain things. To succeed, be prepared to give your max.

Im frustrated with Claudias communication with myself and other students. She comes off condescending and disrespectf, and rather than offering insightful feedback we were called juvenile and high schoolish in a private meeting after one assignment. Ive had dozens of bosses and profs in my life & never experienced such unprofessional behavior

She really cares about students, is a sweet lady and cares about the topic- however, she grades hard, the exams are hard and you do not have much time to complete them. Marketing was not as enjoyable as I expected.

Class isn't hard material wise but Claudia grades very hard. Her criteria for the many projects aren't too clear and the feedback she gives doesn't really help. She is still a great teacher and is very passionate. You will have to do some serious work to get better than a B because the projects are extensive.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Claudia is fantastic. I took this class at 8 a.m. and she still was able to bring amazing energy to keep us engaged. Claudia is so passionate about marketing and her top priority is the students' learning of the material. She is super helpful outside of class and is such a caring professor. Would recommend Claudia to anyone in a heartbeat!!

Professor Roark is great! I've had him for both 420 & 425. He is generous with curves, accessible, and provides PLENTY of test prep. There are weekly assignments, but he will sometimes extend deadlines. Had an injury I was out for a month for, so he met with me via zoom to keep up. Hard content, but if you do hw will do fine. Take with Roark!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I like this better than 420, and he's genuinely a really nice guy which makes it a lot better. It isn't super easy content, but my complaint is really just that he makes the homework sometimes unnecessarily hard. One question will be completely fine, easy even, and then the next has math so convoluted that a TI-84 can't process it. Just annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I generally liked Roark. The structure of the class was logical, and content built so by the end I still remembered early stuff for the final. It's not a super easy class, but I preferred it to 410 and thought it was a little more intuitive. Lots of graphs, and some math like derivatives and iffy algebra. I did feel like it got harder throughout.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I did not enjoy 420 with Dr. Roark. Lectures are quite boring and there are plenty of mistakes on his slides. We also did't solve a lot of practice questions and mostly focused on theories. Midterms 1 and 2 were fine, but the final exam was extremely difficult and tanked my grade. Homework grading is quite harsh as well.

Roark is a caring professor and the goat grading-wise, but I'm not sure I love his teaching style. He's clearly a macro expert. However, during lectures he often skipped math steps or implicit assumptions about the concepts he was teaching, which made it difficult to follow. I had to become an EconAid warrior and teach myself some concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Roark is a great person; he cares about his students, and it shows throughout his class. However, his lectures are heavily based on the theory of Macro, and he does not explain much of the math behind the theory. The exams are difficult, but his grading scale makes the class easy to pass. Be prepared to teach yourself some of the concepts.

Roark is an expert in this field and I enjoyed this more than 420! I'm in QFE so I'll be taking 525 with him next semester too. Exams are hard and there is only one midterm. He drops one problem set and the last one is graded for completion. Group investment project which is a grade booster but also annoying to deal with if you have bad groupmates.
Slides, problem wording, and grading criteria were super confusing.

Roark is a super nice guy and very helpful. Only gripe is that he spent a lot of time on topics which weren't tested at times which meant some important concepts (like fed policy) were rushed. 

Overall the exams are difficult but doable. You have to be proactive and address uncertainties early or you will fall behind.

This guy is a total beast. Very generous with curves and willing to answer any question. Very available to students and honestly just an expert at macro. Don't know why I got on the final but very easy to do well if you put in some effort

Prof. Roark can be a little bit disorganized and confusing at times, but he is a super nice guy whose humor is often misunderstood. If you are engaged in this class and ask questions when things become unclear you will succeed. Definitely not an easy class, but there is no reason to avoid Roark when signing up. Making friends in class will help.
The only people who liked this class are the ones who do not care about their grades. I actually had a stroke trying to understand all the contradictory points in the materials.
he does a good job of making a bad class ok. he wants everyone to succeed and came to our office hours despite being sick.

IM WRITING THIS AS IM STUDYING FOR MY FINAL EXAM. PLS DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE WITH HIM. Chris is a chill person and hes funny but his lectures are SO UNORGANIZED. I actually studied so hard for the midterm but the materials he gave were super confusing and I got a B. Compared to Chris Handy and MSA, this class was x100000 more unorganized.

Very disorganized class, no clear grading expectations, and very passive aggresive with students. Thinks he's funny (he's not). The class itself is an amalgamation of idiosyncratic economic teaching that is not found anywhere but his lecture hall, so good luck studying outside of class. However, curve is forgiving. Overall just a "meh" class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Many self-contradictory points on the slides...
Was a sleeper class. Not that much work, just study problem sets before exams.

Dr. Roark is a fun professor and an overall good guy. Highly recommend going to office hours regularly (Roark or TA/ULA) to discuss homework questions and exam review material, as 420 can be unintuitive sometimes. Class is curved generously so that the median is a B+. Biweekly assignments + textbook readings not required ⇒ relatively light workload

Professor Roark is the best! He really cares about his students' learning and success– don't be afraid of this class if you take it with him. It's also curved so much and he posts a lot of practice tests and past exams. Super funny.

Dr. Roark's lectures are a little messy and hard to follow and his multiple choice grading is frustrating. But macro is just not intuitive, and I think that's why 420 is so challenging. His curve is generous though, and he is accessible outside of class in office hours and on CampusWire. He answers questions well in class.

Would give 0/5 if I could. Bad lectures, confusing MC questions with the worst grading system for them ever, passive-aggressive, unhelpful TAs and office hours, need I say more? If you have any reason to take this class, take it with another prof if possible. You will save both your GPA and your life.

He is a super personable professor. Really cares about student learning and wants us to succeed. The curve (already in the syllabus) is really generous. Its a hard class but the practice exams he gave were super similar to the actual exams, a lot of it is a matter of reasoning through a problem which was fun

I think some of these reviews, while containing valid criticisms, are a bit harsh. Yeah, he does make a decent amount of mistakes, but he's pretty flexible with deadlines and shifts them around to account for errors on his end. The curve is pretty generous as well, and I personally didn't find this course as taxing as 410. Also a personable dude.
Ngl I think people give him 1 just because they screwed up their exams. Overall a nice and approachable guy with some humor. Helps are available on campuswire and Econ aid center.
It is a difficult class, but Roark and the ULAs and TAs want to help you pass and do well. Just use the practice material, and you will do fine.

grading scale isn't terrible like some other Econ courses, decent guy just comes across as odd sometimes. never went to office hours but am currently passing with an ok grade so not the worst class just do the practice exams he gives they're almost identical to the actual ones. also relearn algebra tricks because its heavy on the exams sometimes.

Funny how as soon as a 1/5 rating appears, it's followed by at least two 5/5s to inflate the overall rating. If it's not obvious enough, those 5/5s are from trolls, or the few people who actually liked this class. 

Pros: Responds to CampusWire questions quickly
Cons: Arrogant, terrible grading system, near useless lectures, mistakes EVERYWHERE

Really hard class, but not impossible. Roark cares about his students, he can get frustrated when people are not understanding concepts, but this is fair since his office hours are usually pretty empty...if you are struggling go get help!!! The econ aid center almost always has someone to help with 420.
This class is not as difficult as people make it seem. It is a lot of work, but it is manageable, and tests are curved if people struggle.
Really kind, cares about his job and his students. It is a hard class, as all econ classes at UNC are, but Roark does a great job being available for students and is always patient and respectful.
AVOID AT ALL COSTS! If you need to take this class, take it over the summer with literally anyone else.

Didn't curve any tests when I had him. Awful wording on HW and test questions. MC system is the worst I have ever seen. Very passive aggressive and will not hesistate to humiliate you in front of the whole class for things you didn't even do.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things
