reviews.comment: didnt like his teaching methods, his "multiple choice" grading is the worst I've ever seen and the lectures and slideshows don't help that much without added notes and teachings on top of it. didn't enjoy the class at all but I managed to pass it, will not retake with roark ever again.

I loved this class and I love Chris, had him for 420 as well and that was much harder for me since it was a lot less intuitive. Graded by 6 homeworks (1dropped, 1 for completion), a midterm, final, and an easy prospectus project.

Roark is a chill guy, he's pretty understanding and fair when it comes to grading, this course is just hard to perform well in for a lot of students. Make sure to do practice problem sets/exams before tests and you should be fine. Go to office hours and go to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I think he gets way too much hate tbh. Had him for 420, and I think the content in that class is just not intuitive hence the ratings... but he was awesome for 425! Super active on CampusWire and made a 3:30 class bearable. While he does make a lot of /mistakes, he's pretty chill about correcting them and willing to help clarify anything confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Difficult exams with a final worth 35% of your grade. The slides are incomprehensible sometimes and Roark would often make mistakes whether it be the answer keys, slide information, or hw question wording. He seems to know what he's talking about but has difficulty relaying the info. He can be extremely passive aggressive when answering questions.

Roark really cares about students engaging with and learning the material. He is very accessible and wants to help. The investment project is super fun and a grade booster. The tests are as to be expected, but if you can do the problem sets then you will be fine, utilize the practice sets. Don't get the textbook it wasn't necessary.
I loved this class! Learned a lot and he really cares about students. Lenient with deadlines and just wanted us to participate. Not easy exams, but to be expected in upper level Econ.

Roark got upset with our lecture for not being enthusiastic enough (mind you - it was during a semester when many students' families were suffering in W. North Carolina). Tests were pretty hard and it took months for homework grades to be returned so you couldn't really use those to study. He lets you drop a couple hw grades though

Don't really get the other reviews. I sat on my phone pretty much every day and learned through the slides and homework. Wound up with mid 90s on just about everything.

I thought he was entertaining and was able to communicate well. His slides and other resources (i.e. previous hws) were everything I needed. Generally don't do well in econ either.

Overall lectures are confusing, problem sets only minimally help solidify concepts taught in lectures, and his responses to questions on campuswire are often vague. Chill guy but not great at helping to understand material which is already difficult. Takes up time trying to be funny at least once every lecture but speeds through difficult concepts.

Very nice and funny guy but something about his teaching style just didn't click with me. I often left class feeling even more confused. Answers questions but, again, answers just didn't usually click, which is dangerous in a class like 420 where the material is hard to wrap your head around. EconAid Center was also unhelpful, unfortunately.
Get ready for Mr. Grumpy.-and by that the most entertaining and quirky professor you'll ever have. Can't believe this guy is so polarizing, his lectures are straight comedy.
I kid you not I've had to copy-paste his slides into ChatGPT with the prompt "Reword to be more clear and easier to understand" at least a hundred times.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Good guy and it's obvious he tries, but his lecture slides are genuinely the worst slides I have ever seen in my entire life. They are border-line indecipherable and are rarely helpful for studying. If you're unlucky enough to miss a lecture, you might as well just not try to understand the material you missed because the slides won't help at all.
Genuinely the worst professor I have ever had. And not a good person either

He has to curve the class by 10-20 points at the end of the semester because everyone performs so poorly. Homeworks are insanely hard and lectures are comprised of bullet point slides that are extremely hard to follow. I recommend just ignoring anything in lecture and teaching yourself. The overall quality of this class is horrendous.

I'm a micro person, so class was kinda hard but not too bad. Lectures weren't helpful, too fast, not recorded, didn't really explain things well. STILL don't know half of my HW grades. Roark was kinda condescending and tried to be relatable but it was just a bit weird. Seems like a fine guy, but teaching style didn't work for me

Roark is an awesome guy, hard to get close to him in a 200 person class, but he's super easy to talk to and is funny/down to earth. Tests aren't too difficult compared to content, averages were in the B range. ECON aid center is super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are really bad. The slides aren't easy to follow on your own, he moves way too fast, and then will randomly ramble about nothing for 5 minutes. It's honestly easier to just not pay attention in class and try to figure out the homework on your own, vs trying to use what you learned from his lectures to do the homework.

Chris is a great guy, really cares about all his students and their success. Macro was very tough for me, not as easy to conceptualize as micro. I made a 42 on the first exam and finished with a B-. If you put in the work, you can easily make an A.

Dr. Roark is my favorite professor in the econ department. He is super accessible outside of class, curves generously, and his exams reflect the in-class practice problems and homework sets. It is also clear he really cares about his students, and I found him to be generally pretty funny. He made class engaging and worthwhile.

Professor Roark is great. I was really struggling in this course and was failing for first 12 weeks, ended up finishing with a C+. Roark assured me that as long as I did my best, I would pass the class. Very nice professor who wants the best for his students!

Prof Roark does a decent job of explaining things but could be a lot more concise and clear in his explanations. Problem sets were easy enough and tests were very fair and closely resembled problem sets and practice exams.

Roark genuinely cares about his students and wants to see them succeed, he gives helpful and quick responses on Campuswire, all of his exam questions pull from concepts you will have seen on a real/practice problem set, which have useful answers and grading criteria. TA's also give helpful feedback for psets, go to office hours and ask questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super smart guy, not the best professor. Can be rude sometimes when you ask questions but he still likes when people engage in lecture. If you are afraid of taking this class like I was, don't be. Dr. Roark curves GENEROUSLY on exams. My best advice would be to complete entire problem sets in TA/ULA office hours!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I found this class to be comparable to 410, its a lot of material that econ majors need to know to succeed. Roark does his best to give lectures and problem sets designed to teach more than we will be tested on so we have the best chance of success. Roark is funny, engaging, and intelligent, I enjoyed his lectures, and found office hours useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I've taken 3 courses with Roark (420, 425, 525/493) and he's a good professor. He gives engaging lectures, though sometimes confusing, and he's very personable. He designed a good curriculum for this class that reinforced concepts from 425 and built new skills, such as research and programming. Overall, this is an interesting and useful course.

I don't know if he personally understand what he was talking about. Going to office hour will just make you more confused. He was inconsistent with what he said, which is the key why so many people though this class was hard.

Overall he is a great professor, but sometimes the way he explained was really confusing. I have 17 credits this semester but i spent nearly all my free time with this course. it's hard to get an A, but A- is easy because you got it when overall grade was 86

Professor Roark is a solid professor who I think has gotten a lot better considering the reviews for him the past few semesters. He is a bit all over the place at times and his problem sets can be very tricky and graded a bit harshly. However he makes up for it with the midterms being a lot easier and straightforward (which he himself admits).

He's a definitely qualified professor as in he knows what he's talking about conceptually, but the way he formats and words his slides can give you a massive headache. You'll also have to read through some grammatical errors that can sometimes make learning the material more frustrating.
So far best pf in econ department

Dr. Roark is a little scatterbrained and his lectures move quickly. Yet, he's a great person who cares about his teaching. Homeworks are difficult, yet the tests are relatively easy (he even admits that). He's accessible at office hours which helps. Just work in groups on assignments and he gives a lot of practice problems that help for exams.

Roark is a great guy and a great professor. 420 is hard, but it's clear that he really wants all of his students to succeed. He's super funny and accessible. Just make sure you study a lot for exams and do as many practice problems as you can. You don't really need the textbook because his powerpoints are pretty comprehensive.

Roark cares a lot about his students and has been restructuring his class to make it as fair and manageable as possible. His exams are hard and you will have to study a LOT, but if you have this expectation going into it, you will be okay. Definitely utilize campuswire and your ULA's. Don't fall behind and ask him questions, he wants to help.

Prof. Roark genuinely wants you to do good. He assigns weekly problem sets + there are 2 midterms and a final. You need a very holistic understanding of the material to do good on his exams. If you utilize practice questions, past papers and attend class, you'll do fine. He also answers every Campuswire question he gets, and curves generously.

The second half of this semester is more difficult than the first half, but still doable. I unfortunately was sick for three weeks and fell behind in all my classes. There are plenty of practice resources. He tries his best to help you but the class is just too big for only one professor. The ULAs are your best resources.

I second the wholesome sentiment and enjoyed generous curves, but too many mistakes on in-class examples and problem sets for me to feel Roark is an authority. Just teach yourself the content from more thorough sources and hope the content transfers. Encouraging "game theory" on multiple choice is also goofy.

Roark is nice, but class is Hard with a capital H. Go to office hours to compare PS and USE CAMPUSWIRE! He answers so fast basically texting him. Multiple choice grading system SUCKSSSS. Never got above a 33% on an MC section. 54 on first midterm, and ~70% on the others, still ended with a B. Big overall curve. Good luck econ majors stay strong.

For Econ 420 you should review the slides and all relevant practice problems (he gives past problem sets and exams for review prior to each test). Additionally the textbook is helpful if you are confused on a topic and need a more in depth explanation, however he does not completely follow the textbook and to excel in the course it is not required.

He's a caring prof and explains things pretty clearly. The material can be challenging and confusing, but he's always willing to help. The exams can be difficult, and sometimes there are problems that feel unfairly difficult (i.e. we never did such difficult problems in homework), but if everyone does poorly, he curves, so don't stress.

He's a great professor who clearly knows his stuff. He's very funny, very accessible, and kind to everyone. The class is by no means easy, but he offers a generous curve. The workload is relatively light, but it is in your best interest to study throughout the semester.

Roark is the saving grace of UNCs econ department and one of few professor I look forward to taking again. He is good at explaining concepts although he can sometimes make things more complex than they need to be. He is extremely helpful and responsive via email/office hours/campus wire and genuinely wants students to do well. Also pretty funny.

Roark is a genuinely nice guy and cares a lot. I'll be honest though, his natural teaching abilities are pretty horrid. He has extreme difficulties explaining simple concepts, and most of the time comes off as condescending/sarcastic when he isn't even trying to. He makes this class more difficult than it needs to be but that's the whole department

Nice Guy. That being said, on test reviews and during tests there is stuff that wasn't really in the lecture. He tests for a complete understanding of the material. But, homework is not like this. He doesn't teach the understanding of the concepts well. Tests are harder than the reviews and problem sets by a good margin which is hard to study for.

Good guy. Course Material is tough and he was a fairly new professor when I took the class. You can tell he continues to grow and learn the more he teaches the material. ULAs were helpful. Was accommodating and held office hours for assignments. Generous curve at the end of the semester, so don't panic.

Roark is a good professor, and he really does care about his students. Very reasonable grading policies and problem sets, but the class is really hard (especially if you have no experience with the stock market/finance industry). Great guy, difficult class.

This classes' topics build on each other throughout the semester. If you get lost in the first units then the remainder will be more difficult to grasp. Roark cares about seeing you succeed, the class is just difficult for most people. Make sure that if you don't understand something that you take the time to get help or figure it out.

Excellent professor, knowledgeable and caring. The class is simply the hardest I have ever taken. Roark does his best to bring the material to the students. He is funny and wants to cut everyone a break, but at the end of the day it is still Intermediate Macro.

Makes the class way harder than it needs to be. Homeworks are overly complicated and take hours to complete. Constantly makes mistakes in lectures and on answer keys. Can be hard to follow at times during lectures. Also will round some students grades up and not others. Nice guy besides all that though.

The course itself has difficult concepts but as a professor, he is really great and understanding. He always wants to make sure we understand the material which is nice. His HW was harder than the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly, the material itself isn't that hard, but they he teaches it makes it much harder. There were moments where the same info was presented differently during the semester, which seriously confused me on the final. Prof Roark is a decent lecturer, however, I would recommend looking for alternatives for this credit if you want a good grade.

Great guy, one of my favorite professors in the econ department. The content in 425 is interesting although sometimes lectures can get boring and seem overcomplicated. Really straight forward grader though, and the work load is super manageable. Only downside is how long it takes for things to be graded. Overall loved Roark though, nicest guy.

Genuinely the best econ prof. I've ever had, I cannot write a review that does him justice. He's insanely nice, funny, and accessible, and is the first prof. I've had that has actually made sense regarding the material. 8 problem sets (2 lowest are dropped), 2 midterms, and a final. I would literally take every class with him if I could!

You can tell that Chris genuinely cares about the success of his students and I haven't felt this seen by a professor before but I really WISH he would change his multiple choice rule. Some MC questions have multiple answers but you can't get half credit if you get one right and one wrong and it is so absurd

Professor Roark is a very nice and funny guy who has the bad fortune of teaching a very difficult class. Though I feel that he occasionally struggled to explain concepts in class, he is accessible outside of class and easy to ask for help. Above all, I feel that he wants his students to succeed.

Chill dude but moves a bit fast and skips steps in examples, though outside of class he's super accessible and gives great explanations. Main concern was that most of his MC questions have 2 right answers and you have to get both for full credit, and one answer is usually far more convoluted than the other. He's the only prof I've seen do this.

Roark is a good professor and a very reasonable person. He uses Campuswire extensively and will answer messages and questions very quickly online, which is helpful when completing the (very difficult) homeworks or studying for the exams. The lectures can move fast, but you can always ask clarifying questions later.
just took the final and oh my god. Last semester reviews were right that the final will kill you. His personality is the only reason I'm giving him a nice review because that final was not very nice.

Chris genuinely cares about us and he's the most accessible prof I've had so far at UNC. His personality makes even macro bearable to learn
He's a really good prof but the material is still pretty hard you have to spend a fair amount of time out of class to get a good understanding 
My one complaint is the exams are DAMN hard. Very painful. Very.

Chris is the man. The content is hard and sometimes I blame him for making it overcomplicated, but overall hes such a genuinely good guy with a great sense of humor. I'll miss his presence in the classroom. 
Also he makes up for the difficulty of the class with a great curve so I have no complaints.

This class by no means easy. Our first exam was given a 15-point curve this semester, but the second exam was given a 4-point curve because of how the C. Breezy likes to curve the mean of the exams (or sometimes the median) to a 75. The grading scale makes the class passable, but the exams are tough, and the homeworks collaboration.

Roark is a very nice guy and has been one of the most accessible professors outside of class I've ever had. The material is tough, but if you attend every lecture and take notes on what he says instead of copying the slides it's not that bad. Homeworks are tough but you can collaborate and he answers questions on campuswire. Gives curves on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
His explanation of concepts and the lecture slides are difficult to follow and on occasion do not fully elaborate topics being covered. His tests occasionally, without warning, involve more complex math than he teaches.

Granted, he makes an effort to answer questions and presents in a friendly and engaging way.

Gotta self study to pass 420.

This class is just really tough. As someone who got As in Econ 410 and 400 without working that hard, this class really pushed my limits. Roark is overall doing his best with a massive class and hard material. He does really care about wanting all of his students to do well. Go to office hours, get ready to study, and you will be okay. Curves a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I've never had a professor so accessible while at UNC so points for that!! I wont bs this is a really hard class lol but it could be a lot harder...dr Roark does a great job at simplifying concepts during lectures and is always ready to answer questions/listen to feedback to adapt how he's teaching the concept. Don't be scared to take the class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I sometimes laugh during class because he can be funny but I often cry outside of class because of his lectures and assignments and exams.

He's better than some of the other econ professors and I think he is still finding his footing at UNC but I wish he would be better about returning grades and releasing assignments on a timely manner/sticking to dates he gives himself. Class is much harder than expected and some lectures overcomplicate textbook subjects, but unfortunately it's life
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was a nice guy, but his teaching was not the best. The material of the class is challenging but it is stuff that you will actually use in the future. Lecture slides are not super descriptive so you have to pay attention in the class. Tests and homeworks are lengthy and challenging.

I took 425 with him and Roark is one of the better Econ professors I've had at UNC. His lectures are long and often not too engaging so it is easy to tune him out but the structure of the class is fair and the content is interesting. His exams are fair and the homework takes a really long time and are tough but really prepare you for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I'm a neuroscience and econ double major and this is the hardest class I've taken at UNC. Prof is awful. Seems to make the class impossibly hard for no reason. One time Roark quoted "I make the home works and exams super hard so you have to struggle through them which helps you learn." Not a super nice guy either; passive aggressive, snarky, etc.

Roark was an all around terrible professor.  Lecture material was impossibly hard and on top of that he was awful at conveying the information. Homeworks took 8+ hours to complete and know one I knew ever got better than a 70 on them. Kind of class that makes you want to switch majors. Seriously, take class at a community college to avoid Roark

He's a really nice guy, but ECON 420 is just ridiculously hard. It is by far the most difficult course I've taken at UNC. It makes ECON 410 look easy. The test are extremely hard and almost impossible to study for, but they are curved significantly and the final grades are curved in addition to that.
Really nice guy but the class is hard af. I didn't really study much and still got a B because of the massive curve. (Failed the final and one of the midterms and still got a B.

If it's not obvious the 5 star reviews are trolls, this is the hardest class I've taken at UNC by far. Roark is a nice guy but he seemed to make a lot of mistakes in his lectures and just overall didn't prepare us very well for the exams; I ended up teaching myself everything and scored well only because of his very generous curves.

Roark wanted people to do well in his class but he just wasn't a good professor. He often made errors in class and on answer keys for homework and practice problems. Be prepared to spend hours working on homework assignments and studying for exams. The only good thing about this class is that he curves the exams because everyone does so poorly.

All the good reviews on here have to be from the VERY few ppl (i'm talking like at most 6 ppl) that enjoyed his class and MAYBE got higher than a B on the exams. Being completely honest- from someone who has taken all the notoriously hard classes here at UNC and passed with A's, the structure/grading/prof of this class is astonishingly ridiculous.

Def thought 410 and 101 were difficult but not NEARLY as difficult as this class. He was bound to have mistakes on every single thing he put out to the class and the whole "MCQ can have multiple answers but if you choose one wrong, then the entire question is wrong" was BS. I respect all my professors, but the ULAs were the backbone to this class.

Dr. Roark is clearly very smart & kind, but he struggled with lectures and often made mistakes that he didn't correct. The ULAs were the ones who taught a ton of us. 101 and 410 were a breeze for me, but I never knew what was going on in this class. Avg. curved exam grades were in the 70s, so raw scores were often failing. The final was a disaster.
Just show up and you'll be fine. Can't imagine anyone getting below an B+ in this class.  One of the easiest courses taught in Econ/UNC in general

*ECON 425* Nice guy, very knowledgeable but sometimes to the extent he makes things seem more complicated than they are. The problem sets are difficult and lengthy, but very helpful in reviewing for the midterm and final. He did curve the midterm and final course averages. Though the class was challenging, I learned a lot and would take it again.

Pros: Nice guy, test curves were big. Cons: Homeworks took incredibly long to complete, tests were long and very difficult, lectures were fast with lots of information, used weird, confusing notation, he made numerous mistakes during lectures and practice problems. Got an A, but the class was by no means easy as I've seen other reviews indicate.

One time Roark got mad for people talking and said "I can throw this on the hw/exam without teaching it" and a student said "you already do that" and I've never heard something more accurate. Always had an attitude and the teaching was not there. Hw took HOURS and exams were rlly hard and long. He did curve the class (bc ppl did bad bc no teaching)

Dr. Roark is great! Lectures fast-paced (don't take notes on slides b/c they're posted). Office hours essential to understand PS content. Exams are a time crunch. Most intimidating aspect was complicated notation and derivatives he threw at us initially, but we were his first group at UNC and he had a misconception of our calculus fundamentals.

Roark is simply the man. He always pulled up to class in the dopest fits and made every lecture exciting. I honestly don't get all of the negativity on this page, the class isn't that bad and C-Breezy (yes we are on a nickname basis) is always there to answer questions outside of class.

Chris is without a doubt the most intelligent person I have ever met, every time I spoke to him it felt like I was being injected with knowledge. Content wasn't too bad, studied for a couple hours before the tests and managed to get an A. Definitely an easy A if you go to class.

I learned from this class by rewatching his lectures. His lectures and homework are full of mistakes. It's the kind of mistake that confuse students. He also said the wrong things in class multiple times. For example, "Demand curve moves leftward...I mean rightward." MULTIPLE TIMES. It was a very frustrating experience.

*425* Dr. Roark is very nice, but damn this class was brutal. Each lecture is 30 slides of dense material so if you don't understand something initially, it's almost impossible to catch back up. Homeworks took hours to finish and ended up being nothing like the tests, which were somehow even more difficult. My hardest class at UNC by far.

The hardest class I've taken in my five semesters at Carolina. The other reviews say it... lectures are so incredibly dense. Exam averages are awful, but they get a handsome curve. Roark has another ECON class that I will likely be taking, but I wouldn't strongly suggest him. The MC grading system is bad, often multiple answers w/o him stating it.

Prof. Roark is a really cool guy and extremely knowledgable. The content for this course is intense. Part of it is heavy on the math and the other is very dense conceptual work. Simple mistakes are easy to make and he makes plenty. Lecture slides, homework questions, and answer keys always have something wrong. He desperately needs an iPad.

*FOR 425*

Roark is very knowledgeable and has passion. That said, this class was the hardest Ive taken at unc. Psets take hours (get ready for confusing questions), lectures are so dense, and tests are very challenging. He is a tough grader that doesnt award a lot of partial credit. Final was insane and nothing like the homeworks. Good luck.

If you struggled with 410 and are hoping to have a better time with Macro, you're in for a rude awakening. This class makes Econ 410 seem like 6th grade algebra. It's do-able with a VERY significant amount of time and effort but expect it to be the hardest class you've taken in your life. Roark is ok but sometimes hard to follow and a harsh grader
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Roark is a decent professor and is very knowledgable about economics. He also actually cares about the class and will get back to you if you reach out with concerns. In the flip side, his lectures are extremely dense and sometimes unclear. The tests are very hard with the un-curved average being around a D-.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: prof def knows a lot and is a very smart guy but his lectures are extremely dense, with slides often filled with mistakes, making the content just so dull and hard to engage in without extreme focus. material is conceptually hard but if you sit down with it you can grasp it. hard class no matter what. has high expectations.

He really cares about his students and gives us a lot of resources (ULAs, TAs, practice exams, etc), but he goes over SO much content during class and honestly it was much easier to rely on the internet or khan academy to study rather than go through the lecture slides. I usually have no idea how to do the homework. extremely hard class.

He's fr a genuinely great, great person. His lectures are super dense so it's easy to fall behind. If you just rewatch every lecture, you'll understand the material (I got an 80 from doing this and reviewing HW). He doesn't have practice problems which makes teaching yourself super difficult. HWs are hard, but dont let the other reviews scare you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are basically useless. He uses the strangest notation and uses complex terminology to explain stuff. The material is hard and he just makes it harder. HW takes a long time to complete. Midterms are so long
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: "I just kept flipping, and the test just kept going." _ my classmate after the last midterm
Roark is a great prof but hold on for dear life cause if you get lost in this class it's very hard to catch up.

Got a B+ in 410; didn't enjoy it but it was fine. This class is 5x harder than 410. 420 with Roark is an L any way you look at it. He is a brilliant and super nice professor but he explains everything in the most complex ways possible. Lecture is not helpful. Exams are insanely long and hard. Each mc q has multiple answers and he gives no partial c

This class is not it. He knows the material well but isn't the best at explaining it if you don't immediately understand it. He also does not do any example problems in class so the first time you do practice is one the problem sets and puts lots of information in one lecture to the point you can't keep up.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clay was an absolute joy the entire semester. Deadlines and grading criteria are super clear, and you have an automatic two-day grace period for every assignment. Not sure what he's teaching now, but whatever it is, take it!

considering his first time teaching, did a not bad job! do expect assignments to kind of hit at the same time, but they aren't hard to complete and there are options to rework for a better grade. definitely got to take away a decent amount of skills!

Clay is so awesome! He is super funny, kind, and a great professor! He really wants to help his students succeed and creates a very easygoing, fun learning environment in the classroom! The work is straightforward, and it's extremely likely you will get an A! Would take his class over and over again if I could!

Professor Williams is honestly one of the best professors I have had. There are quite a lot of assignments in the course, but I always felt prepared. Clay gives incredible feedback and cares so much about your success. I truly feel like I'm a better creative person because of this class.
Take 121 with Clay if you can!!! He's super chill, funny, and wants everyone to succeed. His feedback on assignments is super detailed and helpful. Absolutely loved this class

Clay is one of the best professors I've had. He is super charismatic, cares about his students, and super accessible outside of class. The feedback given on assignments is so valuable. The class moves fast with assignments almost every week, but it's very manageable. I would hands down take another class with him in a heartbeat!
Nice guy and seemed to know the material. However, lectures were hard to follow and exams were harsh and long. Everyone in the class struggled and I have never studied harder for a final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Josh is new and has room to grow, but the class improved a lot throughout the semester. The midterm was tough but he took accountability and allowed test corrections and provided extra practice materials. Allowed us to submit a draft paper for feedback, and exams had EC. Keep up with the readings and participate and you'll be fine. Nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Josh seems nice and could be a good professor, but he made PLCY 581 way harder than normal. We had two harshly-graded papers and a hard midterm. Josh did give chances for corrections on midterm, but paper grades were unnecessarily nitpicky and unclear. This class ended my 4.0, and I never really felt like I had a real chance of getting an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Trying to succeed in his class felt truly Sisyphean. You can go to office hours, read the textbook, pages and pages of the readings he assigned, and still not feel confident for his assignments. He was such a discouraging instructor. His syllabus said that effort does not mean success and boy was that true. Take anyone else for 581.

I think with more experience he could be really good professor because he knows the material well, was accommodating, and quick to answer emails and questions. However, I know from working in pairs with different people throughout the semesters that most people found his lectures hard to follow, which was the main issue.

You should immediately consider taking anyone else. His grading was unfair, harsh, & inconsistent. He also offers no actual assistance be it office hours or online. He made the notoriously manageable core PLCY class absolute hell, and ever other section had it much easier which was really unfair and disheartening. Not kind, capable, or helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easily the best professor I've had at UNC! He is fair and non-judgmental, and he turned around my entire perspective on Spanish. He's a talented professor, and a cool guy all around.
Absolute baller

Prof. Clemente is the best ever. Super caring and kind guy who recognizes the common pitfalls and works to help you avoid them. He is Spanish himself and likes to share fun phrases or stories about Spain. He cares about you as a person and you learning Spanish. He is just awesome!!

This professor was one of the nicest and most understanding professors I have ever had. He always helped with any homework, test, or general questions I had and did whatever he could to make sure students understood what he was teaching. He always made everyone laugh and wanted everyone to succeed.

very cool man that definitely is passionate about teaching. gives clear feedback with homework. participation in class is very important for your grade. his powerpoints are useful. it has a textbook but you honestly DONT need to buy it

Sr. Clemente Rodriguez is a professor who demonstrates ample passion for the Spanish language. He always ensures students feel comfortable to participate and get out of their shell to converse in Spanish without pressure. You will love Spanish more if you take 204 with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class was so much fun! Profesor was kind, funny, and helpful.  He gives good feedback on homework, and he's a chill grader.  Make sure to study for exams as they make up a good portion of grade! As long as you study, the exams will be fine.  He provides practice exams that mimic the actual exam.  Also make sure to participate regularly!

If you can take any class with Prof Cristobal, take it! He has 100% been the kindest, most helpful, and most genuine professor at UNC. He cares about his students and is very accessible outside of class. If you show him you care, he will work with you above and beyond

Professor Clemente was incredibly kind and funny. He also understood that many students in 203 are still learning some of the basics of Spanish and teaches accordingly. I hadn't taken Spanish for 3 years when I took his class and still did well. Would highly recommend.

The best thing about Prof. Clemente is that he really understands that we aren't fluent in Spanish. He comes prepared to class every day and tells us about his own life and experiences, which is really interesting. He makes class fun by encouraging participation and discussion, which is a must for Spanish. He is also hilarious. Highly recommend!

Professor Clemente is great! He definitely challenges his students to participate, but I feel like we all improved our Spanish skills so much during the class. Fair grader and obviously cares a lot about his students. I would recommend taking a class with him to anyone!
Favorite teacher at UNC. Take him if you can. He is so kind and understanding and a great teacher.

Profe Clemente is amazing!! He brings his own experience into lectures, and rather than just going through a powerpoint, he takes time to explain concepts and make sure each student understands the material. If you are taking Spanish, take it with Profe Clemente!

Mr. Clemente is a great professor. He understands that his students are beginners in a foreign language and really works with them to assure they are understanding the material he is teaching. He is not a super harsh grader and is a chill, funny, and personable guy all around. I would definitely take a foreign language course with him again.

Chris is very chill and a very easy grader. He really cares about his students and wants us to learn. He understands we are spanish beginners and is very accommodating. I would 10/10 recommend. It's an easy A. He's a great guy, funny, and very understanding.

Such a nice professor and really cares that you understand rather than pushing you to memorize. He was so caring and understanding. I actually learned a lot and he wasn't a harsh grader. Don't forget your online homework and make sure you actually try and you'll get an A. Love him!!!!

Cris Clemente is by far the best professor at UNC. He shows how much he cares about his students and how he wants them to succeed. He is the nicest guy ever. If you have the opportunity to take Professor Clemente, please do it! The class is a lot of work, but it is also 4 credit hours. Study and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class! Clemente is a really nice professor and cares a lot about his student. I struggle with Spanish but I went to office hours, participated a lot in class, and studied for the quizzes and exams. As long as you come to class and try then you will be fine!

I LOVE THIS PROFESSOR! He is super helpful both inside and outside of class. The actual class is filled with a bunch of participation but he makes it fun and doesn't judge if you say something wrong. Span105 starts off easy but starts getting tough around the midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is a great professor. He is very knowledgable and is willing to help out of the class. The content of 105 is not the easiest, and learning through the book is tough. Do well on the midterm and study for all of the quizzes and you should get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is the best professor at UNC. He really cares about your grade and loves it if you go to office hours. you can make an A if you study, he is a fair grader, and he usually tells you what to study for quizzes and tests if you ask him. He doesn't tell you when assignments are coming so make sure you look at the syllabus. Take him for sure. 10/10.

I love Professor Clemente! He's so adorable and always wears really cool shirts/pins. He is super reasonable, is always there and willing to help, and really cares that you learn the material. You have to keep up with the syllabus because he doesn't usually mention upcoming quizzes or due dates. Also, you have to participate, but it's not too bad.

He is a great guy and really cares about his students. He's super nice. The class is difficult but if you study, you'll be fine! Lots of homework and this is a self-taught type of class. You learn the material online through Pearson before class and then review the information in class. The quizzes can be difficult. Study!

Cristobal is the best Spanish teacher. He really cares about his students and wants everyone to do well. He is also super funny and just so nice. It's a difficult class but he is 10/10 the best. I wish he taught 203 as well. Take him take him take him

The best Spanish teacher I have ever had hands down. Not only does he know everything about Spanish (native), he also tells you what is important and what is necessary to know to be an actual fluent speaker. Readily available to talk about topics outside of SPAN, he is constantly teaching our class the culture and history of spain. Take him!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Hand down the best Span 105 teacher at UNC. Very sad he doesnt teach 203. There's a lot of HW from the textbook, but it's not too hard

Spanish 105 is a very work intensive class, but Prof. Clemente makes it a lot more exciting and he is a GREAT teacher and is very passionate about his job. I wish he would teach the next levels of spanish. The class is difficult but he is a great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Clark has been one of my favorite professors during my time at UNC! He is very engaging in lectures, is a fair grader, and is easy to reach if needed. Cannot recommend taking one of his classes enough.

Prof Clark is one of the most caring professors I've had at UNC. Although his classes are lecture-heavy, he throws in lots of engaging material (campaign ads, speeches, etc.) and plenty of jokes. Take a class with him if you can!!!

Amazing guy and very personable. Very easy A but as a southerner, I was really disappointed with the substance of the class. It was kind of structured as an orientalist view of the south through a northern microscope of awe which lowered my respect for the course. A southerner who understands southern culture and experience should teach the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor, but lowkey not the easy A I thought it would be. Exam questions come from study guides. Essays were a time crunch since he tended to delay releasing prompts, but they were not too difficult. He has funny tangents in class. Great guy, make a lasting connection with him! Grades: 3 essays, 2 exams, participation (attendance)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is a professor who will make you want to come to class on a snow day. From his vast knowledge of political theory to his desire to hear all students' opinions, he is extremely respected and beloved in the POLI department. He doesn't take himself too seriously and always has a fun anecdote-do yourself a service and take one of his classes.

Dr.Clark is a great professor! He is very passionate about the topics he discusses and it's obvious he cares for his students. A bit of a slow grader but he doesn't grade harshly. Would definitely recommend this course.
Great guy - super caring and an awesome personality. His lectures were entertaining and the midterm was not insanely difficult because of the resources he provided.

Clark is one of my favorite professors I have had at UNC. He is energetic, funny, and super engaging. He uses different media forms to teach like slides, ads, and discussion, and really cares about what students have to say. Papers and exams were straightforward and super easy if you review notes and ask for help when needed.  Take him if you can!

Dr. Clark was alright for IDST 128. He was the last professor so he was kind of in a time crunch. The pre-class materials were literally his papers he wrote so that was kind of weird. Didn't really teach enough about politics, more surrounding race which was odd. Easy class though, would take if you want an A!

The Triple-I format at UNC is undoubtedly poorly organized, and I think Dr. Clark would've been better in a smaller class format. That being said, his lectures had the tendency to be long-winded, and he tended to be slightly patronizing. Easy enough to do well, though.

He was the best professor in my triple-I. He is the only professor who could get all 300 students to speak. He knows what he is talking about and made me more interested in the topic. He shows fun videos that break up the length of the class. Discussion posts were a huge part of this class and there was no final- only a "hard conversation."

Professor Clark was one of the most entertaining and passionate professors I've had. He was so funny and welcomed student input a lot. It took some time to figure out how he wanted you to write, but overall he was a fair grader and inspirationally excited to teach what he did.

Professor Clark was overall really great this semester. He has an amazing personality and is certainly a funny guy. Class is very lecture heavy and readings are not required. Sometimes it was a bit unorganized, but I definitely learned a lot. Grade is based on participation, two papers, and two exams. Didn't find any of them too challenging.
One of my favorite professors ever. Dr. Clark knows his stuff and teaches with a passion.

Overall, I really enjoyed the class and topics. He is an amazing lecturer. I struggled getting responses via email during this semester. Additionally, I found the exam grading to be a bit picky about details when compared to the instructions. Just be sure to ask questions.

Dr. Clark was a great professor, he genuinely cares about what he teaches and for the well being of his students. Two papers, a midterm, and a final, and random attendance throughout the semester. You get a study guide for both exams covering everything that would be on them so it's an easy A. Readings not required, went over main points in class.

The class was rather straightforward. One midterm was easy with an hour of studying, two papers, a question, and a final group project. Not that much work. There was nightly reading but it was not mandatory and you can get away without reading it as long as you pay attention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor! He was really engaging, encouraged good class discussions, and was open to all students' ideas. Poli 204 was pretty easy when I took it - he gave us study guides for the exams and you can probably get by without doing all of the reading. Class attendance matters, so if you skip you're grade will be impacted.

Dr. Clark is one of my favorite professors at UNC. He is clearly extremely interested in politics and, will often go on tangents in class. A lot of his tangents are really entertaining, though, which make his lectures really easy to pay attention to, with him encouraging lots of participation. His lecture slides are easy to reproduce and useful.

Take classes with Dr. Clark! He is clearly passionate about the topic and encourages class discussion, which is super interesting. As of fall 2022, there are a lot of readings in this class and your grade is based off of a few assignments, but it is manageable. Not sure if that'll be changed up in the future. Nonetheless, great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved Dr. Clark! Lectures are interesting and engaging. Lots of class discussion. Only downsides are that he sometimes rambles and that the class is graded off 2 essays and 2 tests. However, you will learn a lot from the class and the classroom is very engaging and respectful. I would totally take him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS CLASS!

Your grade consists of a midterm, 2 papers, a group presentation, and participation. Prof. Clark is a fair grader for all of those assignments, and is always clear with his expectations. He's clearly invested in what he teaches, which always makes his lectures interesting to listen to. Take this FYS if you have the chance!

Dr. Clark is definitely one of my favorite professors at UNC. He is very passionate about what he teaches and encourages students to participate. His class consisted of readings, 2 papers, a midterm and a final group project. If you are interested in learning about the topics he teaches I would definitely recommend taking a class from him.

Professor Clark has been my favorite professor so far at UNC. His lectures are engaging and he clearly cares about what he teaches. If you are passionate about the topic of the class then you will surely enjoy taking his classes. He goes out of his way to create an inclusive class environment for all students.

I would 100% take Dr. Clark again. He was able to distill difficult information to us in manageable terms. His tests were not too difficult if you watched the lectures. You do not need to read the textbook to get a good grade either.

This was my second class with him, and I loved it! I learned a lot of useful information about Southern politics, and you can tell he loves what he does. He is an engaging lecturer, gives good feedback on papers, and his exams are straightforward. Definitely take him if you have the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super awesome guy and extremely knowledgeable, but he was slow to grade and we never got lectures on time, which was stressful for the COVID semester. Still a king tho and I would definitely recommend if the class is in person
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is kind and cares about what he teaches, but this class was not enjoyable online. Class was asynchronous, and he sent out lectures SEVERAL days after the day we should have had them. The 2 papers were difficult but the midterm and final were easy! This class was not a lot of work, but I'm not sure if I'd take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is a solid professor! I learned a lot from him and you can tell he is really passionate about the material. He is easily distracted which means his lectures can be a bit convoluted, but I didn't really mind. His class is definitely not an "easy A" because the exams are pretty tough, but the papers and projects help make up for that.

Clark is so enthusiastic abt his subject and is great at explaining the material even in the asynchronic format. There's A LOT of reading for POLI76 so be prepared but tbh u can skim and as long as u watch lecture u'll get the main points. Not a super harsh grader and there are few assignments other than reading/lecture. 2 papers and 1 group proj.

Great professor. His clear enthusiasm and interest in the topic made me really want to learn. Do your readings, take notes in class, and spend time thinking about the issues and topics this class discusses: you'll do well. Funny guy as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Loved having him as a professor this semester! I definitely plan on taking a class with him again. This class isn't necessarily an easy A, as the second midterm and final are pretty difficult. Attendance is taken occasionally, but info directly from lectures is on tests. He is very passionate and makes boring subjects more relevant an interesting!

Dr. Clark shows that a class doesnt need to be insanely hard for you to learn a lot from it. The tests are very consistent with the lectures/readings, and you get to spend a lot of time on discussions and current events. It can get a little dry/awkward if no one is participating, but hes very enthusiastic and knowledgeable about what he teaches.
Dr. Clark is awesome! One of my favorite professors at UNC. He is hilarious and genuinely cares about his students and is passionate about the class material. He also makes lectures interesting.

Clark is one of my favorite professors i've had at UNC. His exams come straight from lecture material so I recommend going to class. Also takes attendance once in a while. A fair grader & made lectures enjoyable! can tell he is passionate about politics & a super nice guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: My favorite professor at UNC. Absolutely incredible lecturer. I had Dr. Clark for 101 and 204, and thoroughly enjoyed both of them. The grades I received in both classes were not ideal, but that was not necessarily because of him. He's a fair grader and knows how to explain what he's thinking. He's so funny and I never felt nervous in class.

Dr. Clark is an amazing professor. This first year seminar was easy and very interesting. He is so encouraging when students share their thoughts and I always enjoyed going to lectures. Grading was based off pop quizzes, 2 papers, a group project and a midterm.

Dr. Clark is one of the best lecturers herehe's entertaining, animated, and passionate about the subject. He supplements lectures with videos (sometimes SNL) and class discussion. The overall class difficulty was about average for Political Science. Class always got out 2-5 min early too.

I loved Prof Clark! He made a lot of sports metaphors which I enjoyed. The tests are multiple choice but they are a lot harder than they seem. The class average on both midterms were in the 70s so don't expect an easy ride. You will need to read the textbook alot! Come to class because some questions will say "according to lecture" so beware!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Clark is amazing! Truly one of UNC's best. POLI 101 was an enjoyable class-- but beware, you MUST study. Multiple choice exams seem easy, but could easily bite you! Didn't particularly like the 2 midterm papers, but I loved Clark's lectures. He's funny and wants you to succeed (both as a student and as a person). Take his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Clark is a great guy, but the class overall was only okay. Some(not all)TA's grade papers and recitation participation strictly. The tests are really hard and are more based off the textbook than lecture. Really scrutinize the textbook, because many questions are about minor details. Careful because one bad test grade can quickly limit your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Clark is a great lecturer. Class is very lecture heavy but not monotonous. He is funny & approachable. I don't know why people have said the tests and papers are hard, tests are all multiple choice w/ a study guide and papers aren't graded harshly. You don't really have to come to class a lot and it's very manageable.

If you could take this class without the TAs affecting your grade maybe this wouldn't be the worst class ever. The test are made by the TAs and unbelievably hard. They also grade papers very harshly and without rubrics or logic. Clark tends to ramble in his lectures which makes it impossible to learn. Clark is a nice guy but I would avoid.

Dr. Clark is an excellent professor. He is so enthusiastic about the material that his lectures are pretty engaging even though the material can be theoretical and about specific journal articles. He asks a lot of reading but he goes over the points in class so the reading is not 100% mandatory. The paper is huge though, so start on it early.

Professor Clark seems very funny/considerate, and his lectures are nice but not mandatory. Tests are needlessly difficult, even if you read the textbook inside and out. The class is graded by few things (2 papers, 3 tests, and your recitation (which is only 15% of your grade!)). TA's were incredibly unfair for this class, so choose a decent one.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark loves to talk and will ramble during class. Class grade really depends on your TA. Tests are easy if you memorize vocab from both lecture and the textbook. Paper prompts can be very vague so definitely go to office hours. Probably the easiest poli class I've taken

He's a pretty cool professor and loves to tell jokes and anecdotes, but your grade depends mostly on the midterms and papers. Be sure to read the textbook and pay attention to lecture in order to even think about getting a decent grade on exams. TAs grade papers and mine is pretty strict.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took this class as a requirement for my major. Political science is not my strong suit, so I took this class thinking I would gain a lot of learning experience out of it. We have three weeks left in the semester and I'm doomed to fail, despite all the hard work I've put into this ridiculously hard class. Avoid if possible.

This wasn't a bad class but not my favorite. Dr. Clark is personable and if you go see him during office hours he is really nice, but your grade is more dependent on your TAs because they write the test questions and grade your papers. The lectures were fairly interesting but he gets off topic sometimes. Tests were also very nitpicky.

I really enjoyed this class. Dr. Clark is very passionate about what he teaches and wants students to succeed. He is also funny and personable - I'd recommend taking a class with him if you ever get the chance! He provides study guides for exams so you know what to study.

He is a nice person, he gets off track a lot. The class had a lot of open discussions which was nice. There was two papers, a midterm, and a final. So everything was weighted pretty high. He grades pretty hard, and even though this says intro to southern politics, it didn't wasn't an intro level class. Don't let this be the first poli class you tak
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you are interested in the Political Science major at UNC, I highly recommend taking one of Dr. Clark's classes. It is obvious that he is highly invested in the material for the class and is a very kind, respectful professor who listens to what his students have to say. Exams can be difficult, but Dr. Clark made sure that everyone was prepared.
He's the best. Genuinely cares about his students and his curriculum. Highly recommend him one of my favorite profs at UNC. Also, he is funny and open to class discussions.

He posts his slides on Sakai, so you can miss a few and still do fine as long as you study effectively. The (multiple choice) exams include information from the slides and the textbook with no curveballs, which is really nice. He likes to tell some anecdotes while he lectures. At 9 am, it's nice to get an occasional pause in notes during lecture.
Dr. Clark is awesome and super passionate. You will do just fine in the class if you go and listen and do well in your recitation.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Love his lectures and enthusiasm for the class. His slides are organized, and lectures are eloquent and easy to follow, and exams are reflective of what you've done in class. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you need to go and also read the book to do well. TAs are in-charge of 35% of your grade, so make sure they like you in recitation.

He's a great guy and cares about his students and the material. Southern Politics just wasn't interesting to me. All the homework is reading, and his lectures essentially break down the readings. There were two papers, and he is very clear about what he expects. He makes study guides for his midterm and final. He also enjoys class discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I love this man!! He is one of my favorite professors at UNC and makes class so interesting. The exams aren't hard and he seems to be an easy grader.
Chris Clark is great!! He takes attendance occasionally, but he tells good stories. He makes an effort to make the class engaging.

Dr. Clark has a great personality and really cares about his students! He can get a little off topic, but attend class to get a better understanding of the material. 3 exams, 2 papers, and recitation. The exams weren't bad (not cumulative) if you study the PowerPoints AND read the textbook. TAs grade the papers so they have a big say in your grade.

Dr. Clark is a great guy. Only a few grades, and half of them are graded by your TA. Having a good TA can make or break your grade. The exams are a mix of very easy questions, and difficult questions. All questions come from the textbook. Attendance isn't mandatory.

Clark himself is amazing and lectures aren't mandatory (he puts slides up) but he's easy to listen to and funny. However the grade for Poli101 is entirely based on about 6 grades, three of which are graded by the TA. Exams are fair and easy but you do need to study. But the papers and the rec grades can literally flunk you if you get a bad TA...

Clark is actually amazing and really funny. The lectures can get boring but you should still go to class to know the material. However the tests are for some reason quite hard even with studying. Also your grade in the class entirely depends on your TA's. The class has about 5 grades too (3 tests, 2 papers) which can really hurt you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is Minority Representation. There are 3 exams (none of them are cumulative) and he gives you a study guide a few days before each exam. There is one research paper towards the end of the class. Really interesting and fairly easy class. He goes over the readings in his lectures
I love Professor Clark to death.  He can ramble sometimes, but he means well and facilitates good class discussion.  Professor Clark took attendance occasionally, but you'll want to come to class.
Professor Clark is awesome. Focuses on the significance of the material, not facts. His tests are reasonable and he is an interesting lecturer.
had weekly quizzes, really nice guy, would definitely take it again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Extremely picky about grading papers/labs and would take off points for the tiniest things. Also had extremely specific weekly quizzes that were closed note and based off of multiple readings that were laughably long. Kind of nice, sometimes? Kind of also passive agressive.
Pretty straightforward class, interesting (but lengthy) readings and complicated quizzes. Grading was pretty inconsistent, but fair ins ome cases. He did not  fw me but was pretty chill to others.

Do not take this class if you are not good at weekly quizzes on lengthy papers. The quizzes are hyper specific and they are not open note making them quite tricky as they are a large part of your grade. The work wasn't necessarily bad, but Dr. Gray is not accommodating or flexible on any assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Love Professor Gray as a teacher. However, if you are not good at weekly quizzes, DO NOT TAKE. You will regret it and be very sad.

I love Clark! He's so sweet and teaches the class material in a very easy-to-understand way. Lectures were straightforward and you had weekly quizzes (they're easy if you did the readings/or paid attention to ppl presenting the week's readings) and a super quick and easy final presentation. I learned a good amount! Very nice gen ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super chill guy, really liked him. The setup of the class was a little weird- basically every semester he has students write their own variation of the exact same research paper and you work on this all semester. We used Stata but didn't actually write any code. I like how the work was spaced out though, nothing ever piled up or stressed me out.
Geog450/451 was super easy and manageable! you could easily get ahead on the papers and then vibe for the rest of the semester

I'm pretty sure this class is GEOG 451, not 450, but I loved this class! Dr. Gray is a great professor and definitely cares about the material and his students. There are lots of hefty journal articles that we were quizzed on, but if you pay attention to the class presentations on them you get the picture. Easy assignments and open notes quizzes!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is the most caring professor I've had! I struggled getting labs turned in and he reached out to make sure everything was OK and allowed me to turn them in with limited late penalties. Quizzes were hard but don't majorly affect your grade. Final is a paper which he has you turn in sections throughout the semester. All around just a great guy!
Great class and great professor! Grading criteria is very clear and fair. Always willing to work with you if you have questions and is great at explaining material.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Grading was clear and fair. Weekly quizzes were hard but he dropped low grades. I was in his office hours every week and emailed him constantly and he was always super helpful and caring. 437 was one of my fav research classes. Really smart, good lectures, kind of matter-of-fact when talking about heavy topics. Great hands-on research experience!

Do not take him for GEOG120. He is lazy when making notes for class and his tests are way too specific. Unless you plan on dedicating a large amount of time to studying for this class, do not take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor. He's very lively & kept me awake despite my tendency to fall asleep in just about all of my classes multiple times a week. Weekly quizzes are harder than they need to be, wish he would've allowed us to get one of the 5 questions wrong without hurting our grade. Lots of reading, but skimming works fine. Tests/papers are easy enough.
Professor Gray is a pretty good teacher.  He certainly knows his lectures well and has a real passion for geography.   If you put in the effort this class is a highly enjoyable one to take.

Lectures were absolutely unendurable. I resorted to playing games on my computer and taking vague notes about the powerpoints he gave (although that's not even necessary, since he posts all the lectures). He is mildly amusing if you get his nonsensical remarks. Reading from the textbook is the best way to get an A, though each chapter is very long.

Dr.Yang is great and super caring for students! 
Def needs a lot of practice to make lessons smooth, and it matters a lot whether you've worked on the things taught in the previous lessons. 
Piano is never easy but Dr.Yang makes it inspirational.
One of my favorites at UNC. Just one of the kindest and most intelligent people on campus. I love this woman.

Took Piano Lit with Professor Yang. Great teacher. Really wants to see all her students succeed. She is very accommodating of students and, as long as you let her know ahead of time, you can miss class occasionally. Her lectures were clear and captivating. All in all, a great teacher, passionate about the subject material.

Dr. Yang is one of the best pianists and professors I have ever had the pleasure of meeting. She always finds ways to improve your skills as a musician and is there to help you achieve any musical feat you desire. I have seen so much progress  and development in myself as an individual since taking lessons with her.

Dr. B was truly a great professor. He completely cares about his students and is really invested in the material. He sometimes goes over lecture time, but not too much. We didn't entirely stick to the syllabus, but he ended up giving points back for free essentially. He offers extra credit; I would totally take this again!

Dr. B is the best professor to take 376. He is so passionate about the material and keeps you engaged in an 8am class. This is a tough class with a lot of material, but the exams were pretty straightforward and he always wanted his students to succeed. He is so understanding of circumstances, but you need to put in effort to do well in the class.

I took LFIT 113 (Weight Training) with Dr. B. I was nervous to take this class because I have no previous weight training experience, but Dr. B was an amazing teacher! He is so friendly, patient, and caring. He was very understanding of our individual needs and helped us create our own personalized fitness plans. I highly recommend LFIT with Dr. B!

Dr. B is the best. He is caring and super enthusiastic about the material which makes it easy to pay attention, he is hilarious and uses his expertise to help give real life examples. His tests are focused on the material he repeatedly mentioned and the very few homework assignments were easy. Pay attention in class and you will do great.

just had him 409 (wasn't and option) not 410. The class is super chill and geared to exposing students to different clinical population and how exercise can be used to aid in their disease treatement. Your grade is composed of a semester long group project and article reviews. Dr. B is super enthusiastic and approachable!
Super nice guy, and his lectures are easy to pay attention to. The tests are straightforward. He truly wants his students to do well. A great human being.
Dr. B is AWESOME. He is extremely energetic and makes his lectures fun and easy to follow as well. He is passionate and explains course content well.

Dr. B was fun but a little boring. I felt like his lectures also tended to lean to the side of self-aggrandizing. Also at one point he chucked a foam brain at the lecture hall pretty hard. Not out of anger or anything, just pure excitement I think, but it was still noteworthy. Anyway, he seems nice, but not my favorite.

FUNNIEST GUY IV'E EVER MET. Genuinely cares about his students, and gives great lectures (sometimes he is a little had to understand because of his accent). Course content is super interesting and easy to understand. LOVE DR BATTAGLINI.

Dr. B was my favorite out the three professors for my IDST 115. He made his unit in the corse very interesting and fun to pay attention to despite it being an early corse. He is very insightful in his field, has a nice tone to everyone, and creates a safe safe in the room for anyone to ask a question. I recommend!!
Really cool professor, makes lectures fun and interesting! Content for his portion of the Triple I wasn't too difficult.
Dr Battaglini was so much fun for lectures and so caring outside of class. Even if you're not in sports and exercise science I would highly recommend taking a class with him.

Dr. B is the best! Favorite EXSS professor Ive taken so far. The labs were annoying but easy. Study the slides well and youll be fine for exams. He offered test corrections on the first exam, and threw out any commonly missed questions. No cumulative final. The most caring prof ever! If you have the chance to take this class with him, do it!

Dr. B is hands down the greatest professor I have had at UNC. He brings an incredible amount of energy alongside his lectures and sincerely cares about his students and the material he teaches. If you are looking for a professor to take 376 with, you MUST take it with him. You won't regret it!!
This was a special topics one credit class so not sure how DR. B is teaching EXSS but in terms of character, Dr. B's amazing! Very lively and willing to help everyone out.

IDST 290 was a pass/fail class. Dr. Battaglini is so caring and wants students to come to him and talk. He wants to help you any way possible (even after you finish the class). I really appreciate the advice that he has given me and I hope to keep in touch with him.

Great prof, if you get the chance to take 376 with him, do it. I was nervous taking this class in the summer but Dr. B really explains the material well and the exams are not hard if you study well before. He will gladly answer any questions and is quick to respond by email too. Not the easiest class, but Dr. B made it great. 5/5 would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. B is by far my favorite professor I have had in my entire UNC experience. He really is passionate about this material and has lots of knowledge! He gives real-life examples to make sure the concept is clear to students and even uses his own experiences, which are very interesting as he was an Olympic coach/trainer. I love Dr. B and so will you!
not helpful248

Dr. B is by far my favorite professor I've ever had at UNC. He draws on his past experiences to provide real world examples and is very hands-on. He truly wants his students to succeed. If you ever have the chance to take a course taught by Dr. B, I would highly recommend doing so.

Excellent professor. Very enjoyable lectures. Dr B draws on his practical experience to make lecture topics more interesting by relating anecdotes, training tips, etc. One of the best classes I've taken in my (very long) college career.
Dr. B is one of the best professors I have had at UNC!
Dr. B is awesome

Wonderful professor, and very helpful! Class is enjoyable and Dr. B provides excellent examples that keeps the subject matter even more interesting. Tests are not too difficult if you put in the time studying. Making A is definitely possible!! He wants his students so succeed.

Professor Compton was a great teacher! He really cares about students and whether they understand the material. Calc is test-heavy, but he always offered at least one freebie on each exam (apart from the final). The final was hard, but the entire department made that final. Overall, a great teacher, and arguably the best one for Calc at UNC.
