reviews.comment: Had a very hard time taking this class. Did not end well
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Really hard class in comparison to other sections. Only if you really want a big challenge
His test are way harder than the level he teaches.
There HAS to be better teachers to take this class with...

Professor Compton was able to make us laugh and make good connections while teaching. He recognizes which students attend every class. He's very clear in his explanations and tries to provide help outside of class. His exams are difficult but he also tries to give extra credit. No matter the professor, calc 3 is going to be hard.
Great in office hours but lectures felt a little fast and kind of jumpy at times.

Good at explaining content in class but the homework is completely different and challenging. Be prepared to go to office hours if you want to understand it. Even though lecture is not required, not everything he talks about is on the posted notes so I would recommend attending most.
Way harder than other teachers…

He is a silly and entertaining professor. His lectures were very clear and understandable. The tests were difficult, but expected with this class. He did randomly call on students, which was terrifying. Also, I had university-approved absences, and he took points off for them.
He is super funny and made learning fun, but has a bit of an ego. Made tests super hard for no reason and just graded harshly
Just not a great person to take any class with. Hard class to begin with, tests are hard and unfair
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is super accessible and presents the information in a way that is easy to understand. He is a very nice guy, and enjoys teaching. However, the tests were really hard and we didn't have many resources outside of homework and recitations to study for them. Lowest midterm is replaced with the final, making the final theoretically 48% of your grade.
I really enjoyed the class and his lectures were very informative. He is a very hard grader so it's hard to justify taking any class with him

He is able to teach the material well, but everything is so much more difficult than what is learned in class. Definitely pay attention to what you did on the homework and if you don't understand something ask in office hours because test questions are often similar to homeworks. Look at book practice problems, they are sometimes on tests too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He is a nice professor and is clearly passionate about the subject, but his exams are incredibly difficult with no review material or practice exams given. I took Calc 2 with him and liked his teaching style, so I took 381 with him. But compared to the other sections of this course, Compton makes it unnecessarily difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Joe is a solid option for 233. He's caring towards students and encourages you to come to office hours. Lectures are clear, but some topics are only covered in recitation so make sure your recitation TA is good. His exams are no walk in the park, but they prepare you very well for the department-created final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: great lecturer and very funny! unfortunately his exams are insanely hard, and he provides zero study materials.  he pulls from recitation, HW and lecture notes, so to prepare for the exams you need to practice everything. I still suggest him if you actually plan on learning calc 3, because i doubt youll find a better or kinder teacher then him
He is so funny. Overall really great person to take a class with. The only issue is that he will destroy you with his grading...
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He seems like a nice guy, but his lectures were pointless. He spent half of every class trying to develop analogies that were unhelpful and sometimes inappropriate. Once we got to the actual material he would breeze through it. Tests were fair though and the class itself isn't too hard if you put in the work to study and do practice problems.
Would rec that you consider other options. Good teacher incredibly hard grading for no reason espescialy for first semester of college.

Dr.Compton is a great professor if you attend lectures. I found him to be very accessible outside of class and helpful. However, I found his exams to be quite difficult they are nothing compared to recitation or lecture. He does drop lowest homework and replaces one test with final. P.S. This was my first semester at UNC
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Half the class did horribly other did fine. He didn't seem to be too upset about how poorly some of us were doing.

Lectures don't match the difficulty of exams/hw. Midterms and final exam decide your grade, and the 5% project is hours of work with strict grading. No practice tests or guides, and Edfinity isn't aligned. Many with strong calc backgrounds struggled (class stats shared only on first midterm, and it was a 67%). ONLY take if you can FULLY commit.
Very good lecturer and a very nice prof. Also very helpful in office hours. The class and tests are tough, but if you are willing to put in lots of effort it is possible to do well
Don't take if there are other options.

Difficult and time consuming homework, no practice exams or study guide, not clear on what he puts on midterms. Grading was harsh and unfair. Very harsh grader. Terrifying.

reviews.comment: I'm not sure why he has good ratings on here... He is very condescending, which is not a productive enviornment for learning difficult subjects like math. He doesn't give any practice for exams. Also, you can do great and understand all the topics on midterms, but then do slightly bad on the final and it will tank your grade.

Took him for Calc 2 and really liked him, so decided to take for discrete and regretted it. I know discrete is supposed to be hard, but not this hard. Homework is impossible to do with going to office hours and/or using AI/internet (and even then still incredibly hard). Test questions are also unnecessarily difficult. Don't recommend taking him.

reviews.comment: Great lecturer. Tests were so hard I had to start therapy.

reviews.comment: Great teacher. Do not rec taking unless you are very strong at math. Think deeply before taking this class.

I loved dr. Compton's lectures, he really teaches the concepts in a way which makes them easy to understand. My one big problem with this class is the tests.From what I saw with friends in other sections, our tests were more difficult and had way less study materials.

I love Dr. Compton! He's a great lecturer and truly cares about his students. I'd def recommend showing up to lecture and doing your homework w/out ai. Also go to office hours! He is super accessible and helpful in smaller group settings. For exams I go over his worksheets and I use my friends' old exams for practice. Exams are fair imo.

Super nice guy and definitely a good teacher. The only thing is the exams are nothing like any of the practice you do in class, homework or recitation and he refuses to give practice tests. Also can be unorganized as multiple times we have had homework for topics we need to know on a test due weeks after the test.

Dr. Compton is an amazing lecturer and strives to ensure that his students truly understand the content. If you don't show up to class, you're cooked, but if you do an actively take notes, you'll be fine. Make sure to study before midterms though! Midterms are a hefty portion of the grade, but he replaces your lowest midterm with the final.

Great lecturer and super funny but the exams are very hard and it's kind of hard to determine what you need to know for these exams. He will make questions based on things outside of lecture that you practiced in recitation or on the homework. Wish he was more clear on exam topics and expectations

I took this class with him over the summer after not doing so well on Calc 3 the semester before. He made the concepts easier to understand, and would help so much during office hours, and was very approachable. For this class, it seemed like the class had a structure, and the guided notes were very helpful in following along.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Haven't finished the course yet, but I am a big fan of Dr. Joe. He comes from teaching high school and it's very obvious. He goes very slowly in class and explicitly outlines instructions and the mathematical intuition that is very hard to teach. However, examples in class r nothing like the exam. prepare to do a lil self study.

Really great professor. I took this class during summer, so I don't know if a smaller class size makes a difference, but Joseph made sure to try to keep every student engaged. He also had prepared notes that you filled out in class, so it made it easy to follow along.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class pacing was poor (his first time teaching the course), but the content was quite easy. Some homework questions were deeper topics than what we learned in class which sucked. I thought he was funny. People say he was condescending: he was sassy when you asked a question 10 minutes after he asked if the class had questions about that topic.. lol

He was an alright teacher and was very nice. Homework took a while but nothing insane. Midterms were very hard and did not give study material. I do not feel like he prepared us well for the final. A lot of it was just the class, it was by far my least favorite class. Midterms + Final were 75% of the grade, and no drops which others teach's offered

Curved 2 midterms, then told us we were “cooked” right before starting the final, then dropped the curve entirely. No grading scale, no clear policy, and final scores hidden until grades were locked. Some secret points added to the final after complaints. Grading felt arbitrary, dismissive, and shady. If you value fairness, avoid this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was very full of himself and often skipped steps that seemed "easy" to him. The first few units weren't terrible but the semester went down. He favors power series and put them on every exam where as other sections only had 1 exam on them. Class structure is super random and not linear. He has a great attitude tho!

It was the attitude that got me. He's a fine professor and the class wasn't too hard if you showed up. He said that he used to be a high school teacher and would bring those methods which could've been helpful without the condescending tone. Not hard but I definitely wouldn't take a class with him again.

Chill professor overall. not sure if this is a him thing but grading for this course was super unclear and people often didn't know where they stood. he grades homework unnecessarily hard too, but his lecture style is pretty good. don't like how hard his exams are especially compared to other sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm not very good at math, and the first unit was honestly incredibly easy. Everything went downhill from there. Pacing was awful, lots of homework, no curves, no extra credit, 3 midterms, a 3-part final research project, and a cumulative final exam. One of the worst 100 level classes I've taken. Compton is rude, condescending, and hard to talk to.

Not a horrible class to take, but he spent so much time on the first unit that we didn't get enough time for the other units and it screwed us over during midterms. He got a bit rude to us and would ask us to ask questions but then gave attitude if we did. I would still give him a chance though!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very tough class compared to other 100-level classes. No extra credit, no make-up exams, no curve. Lots of homework. And he is not very nice to change the grades when you forgot to sign up during class.   And there is no review session before the exams. Time for preparing the exam is limited.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very condescending and not great when you have to ask questions or for help. Often times the homework was not things he taught us, and he tries to shove a lot of information into a unit test that should've been spread out across a few units. Four units, 14 homework assignments, final was a project and a cumulative exam.

Compton was a great lecturer and made himself available during office hours. 232 is a difficult course but the tests were made fairly based on the problems seen in class. I would recommend reviewing in-class notes if you have him before the exam, those are the kinds of questions you will be tested on, not whatever is on Edfinity.

he chill imo
does a good job explaining stuff in class and during office hours
Very hard grader, take a grad student

Overall, I really enjoyed taking Math 232 with Joe this semester, and I would totally take another class with him in the future. I'm not a big fan of calculus, but I really like Joe's personality and he is super approachable outside of class! You definitely can't go wrong with him for 232.
Professor Compton is excellent at explaining concepts, and his classes are great!

Compton is a great professor. His lectures are easy to understand, and he always stops before and after class to answer any questions that people have. His tests are fair, and he hosts office hours that are very helpful to figuring out the homework and studying for exams. If you need to take math at UNC I highly recommend!

I would highly recommend Dr. Compton for any math class, especially 110. He does a great job simplifying topics and making sure everyone understands the class concepts. He is kind, funny, and genuinely wants his students to succeed. Algebra should not be a difficult class, and Dr. Compton makes sure of it.

Dr. Compton was my favorite teacher so far at UNC. He was so helpful and easily accessible when having trouble in class. Lectures went through how to do everything we needed to learn and was open to answering questions. He also hosted review sessions before exams. I 100% recommend him.

Dr. Joe is an amazing lecturer. He taught high school previously, and I found he was really able to connect with the students in a more down-to-earth and approachable manor. Tests were manageable, however, homework didn't always align with what was taught in class. If you pay attention in class and do the study guides you will get a good grade.

As most math courses, this was very heavily weighted on midterms and the final. Tests were difficult and long for the amount of time we got. Despite the difficulty of the class, Compton made the content as clear as possible. He was very accessible and good at answering questions. I highly recommend!

Dr. Compton is an excellent teacher. He is friendly, funny, accessible, and has a knack for breaking down tricky concepts very well. Midterms were not easy, and class averages tended to reflect that (~70%), but Calc 2 is hard in and of itself. Irregardless, I highly recommend Dr. Compton.

Prof Compton is easily the best math teacher I've had. He explains content thoroughly and makes the lectures rly engaging. The homework can be difficult but if you can understand it then midterms shouldn't be too bad. Although the timing of the midterms wasn't ideal, he curved the final, which boosted my grade from an A- to an A. Def recommend!
Overall really good professor, homework was tough at times and not always related to test materials, exams were all fair, replaces lowest midterm grade with final.

Given how difficult Calc 2 is, Compton made it seem very straightforward and easy to understand. He explained concepts so in-depth, and his lectures were super easy to follow. He was also very funny and caring towards his students. Calc 2 is hard af no matter who you have but he was great.

I've heard a rumor that math 232 is the most failed class at the school (no idea if that's actually true) but Dr. Compton is peak. Exams make up almost 80% of your grade but he replaces your lowest midterm with your final. Tests are fair and homework is hard. Dr. Compton is overall a cool guy and checked all of the boxes and more. Engaging lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Compton is an amazing person! The class was tough but he did his best to help us on the midterms and the final! He drops a few homework assignments, which were online and more difficult than the exams, and also replaced our lowest midterm with the final. Overall, great professor just get ready to study a lot!

If you have to take a math class at UNC, take it with Dr. Compton. He made harder concepts easily understandable and really took the time to slow down if needed. He was very reachable outside of class and there were a few extra credit opportunities. Truly one of the best professors at UNC.

Notes during class presents the new topic with easy-to-do examples. Homework is quite a bit more difficult so the notes don't prepare you all too well. Midterms and final make up most your grade and the averages are in the low 70s. Tricky to prepare for the tests well since resources are scarce. Final was difficult.

Lectures are very clear, but the pace of the class makes it hard to keep up at times. The midterms created by him were much harder than the final, but the class never felt horribly unfair. The only unfair feeling part of the class was the midterms and final being worth 78% of your grade in total. Pay attention and you should be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Joe is the math prof i've ever had. takes a hard class and makes it enjoyable. knows most of his students by name.   lectures are so good and he posts all completed notes. midterms are hard and worth a lot of your grade, but if you pay attention in class and go to office hours you'll be fine. homework way harder than the test but good practice.

I really like Professor Compton because he is very caring and shows so much passion for teaching math. However, this class was the most difficult class I have ever taken and the exams were extremely hard. The class averages were never too great for these exams, but you genuinely learn a lot in this class. Also, make sure to go to class.

Great professor!! I had Dr. Compton for college algebra b/c of have no foundational math skills haha. He was a phenomenal teacher and introduced a conversational style in his lectures, as he used to be a high school teacher. He does a great job explaining concepts and always takes questions. I purposefully signed up to take math 130 w him next sem!

I loved him I had him for math 110!!!! So funny and caring!! He is so sweet attendance was mandatory sometimes (we did in-class assignments). I would so take his class again. after hearing what other math 110 teachers are like I think he is one of the better ones.
Hard class, but a good teacher. He wants to help you. Clear information.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love Calc 232 with Dr. Compton! He is readily available, wants us to succeed, and funny in class. Clearly explains information and his teaching style is very explicative. Very very good teacher!

He is very good at communicating information and helping you understand how to utilize the theoretical knowledge taught in class on questions. Exam questions are very straightforward and reasonable. The final was pretty challenging and you can lose significant points for small mistakes on the homework. Overall, he is a very good professor to have.

Joe is the best. I've heard of much easier 381 teachers, but Joe is an amazing teacher even if his exams can be difficult. He explained everything very well and is super accessible, and we learned a lot more than other sections. He encourages participation, attending office hours, and working in groups all of which made the class great

Great class! He wrote me recs for some summer programs which I really appreciated. He teaches almost directly by the textbook (which you could find online), so reading outside of class isn't really necessary but it can help if you don't understand something from in class.

IMO one of the better choices for 381. Hard grader, but he curved the grade scale based on all sections' grade distributions (a 50 was a B on the final). Super helpful in office hours and over email, and genuinely seemed like he cared. Explained things super well in lectures. Mildly concerned about his work/life balance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are very clear and fun. Explain concepts well and provide specific examples. Frequently hold office hours. Homework are not too bad, take about one or two hours if use LaTex. The homework of lowest grade gets dropped. Three midterms each worth 15% and final worth 35%.

381 is a hard class, but I really appreciated the way Joe taught it. His lectures were straight from the textbook, but I liked that because I could check the book later if I missed something in class. Weekly homework was also problems from the textbook, and it usually took me 2-3 hours. The final was worth 35%, but it also had a massive curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very caring and approachable (frequent office hours). Lectures are organized and follow the textbook. I personally feel his style/pace fits those who enjoy taking notes in class. Notes are important. Exams can be tricky. HW grading is not his fault so reach out to him during OH. (and don't use latex for hw. It's great but exam is with pen)

So it is a very difficult class and that is obvious but Joe is quite possibly the most accessible professor I have ever had. Would almost certainly take the class with him again and he is one of the best professors I have had at UNC and he is only a graduate student I hope he continues to teach at UNC after his PhD.

Joe is a wonderful professor. While his tests and midterms were a little more theoretical and complicated than the homework and examples in class, he's does only test on what's covered in class and is super available during office hours. He's also very kind and understands that it's a hard class so he's always a great person to go to and talk with.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pretty good professor, first year teaching discrete so I bet he would get better
Worst class taken here if you need this class don't take it with him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Such a hard class, teacher expects you to know everything.

His first semester teaching discrete but he basically just read out the textbook and wrote it on the board. He also wasn't super clear on what his expectations were on hw and tests and then would grade very strictly and had low test averages. If you're ready to put in the extra studying time you'll be fine but its not an easy class w/anyone...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Compton is a very clear lecturer who does an excellent job explaining mathematical topics. He clearly wanted the whole class to succeed. He was always accessible for questions and gave quick and helpful answers. No test question was ever not representative of what was done on homework and in class. You can't go wrong if you choose his class.

Haven't finished the class yet but Dr. Johnson is by far my favorite Biology professor that I have had so far. He is really funny and very willing to help you if you are having trouble understanding a concept. Explains content clearly. Responds to email way faster than the average STEM professor. Class isn't easy but is doable with some studying.

This class can be very difficult if you don't make it a point to study the Anki in between every class session. If you do use the Anki and go to open labs, the exams aren't too difficult but are definitely still challenging. There is a lot to memorize in this class, but it is definitely doable!

Dr Johnson is really caring and very knowledgeable. He is easy to reach outside of class and is super accommodating to all of his students. His exams aren't super difficult if you go to class and study the material, as well as the only work outside of exams is a Mastering due before each class period. Would highly recommend!
I absolutely loved Dr. Johnson; he was a great teacher and had very fair exams. Would definitely take again.

Should not be a 1 credit class. It's hard but not impossible. DO THE ANKI and practice provided and you'll be pretty prepared. Is all memorization with some application -- the application depends on what you memorize. Review sessions, open labs, and LAs are excellent resources. Hope for a good TA they can make or break the class and your graded

The GOAT. Material is straight forward from lectures. He records all lectures, and attendance is lenient. Talk to him in office hours, he is so very understanding. Would not have taken this course with no one else.
Absolute beast. The most straight-forward UNC STEM class. I learned a lot too.

Dr. Johnson is awesome! He is an incredibly effective lecturer and funny. His attendance and homework policies were extremely lenient, leaving room to miss class and turn in homework up to a week late. His exams are extremely fair and consistent. Take 252 with Dr. Johnson, you won't regret it!!!

The best STEM professor I've ever had. I wouldn't say the content is easy but his exams are very clear and very reflective of what you learn in class. He definitely wants students to succeed and gives every resource possible to do well for exams.

my fav prof of all time without doubt. genuinely has the students in tears of laughter multiple times a lecture, and WANTS us to succeed. the course content is hard, but i find it so easy to understand with how his lectures are set up and the jokes he makes. i have a 97 in the class rn and the final should be a breeze. def take him for a&p!!
Corey J is THE GOAT. A simple guy who doesn't make his mission to make his students miserable. Not a ton of grades but exams are relatively easy if you study. Best Bio class at UNC. He is hilarious

Dr. Johnson is THE BEST professor I have ever had. The course material can be hard, but he teaches in a way that makes everything so easy to understand. The only assignments are GRQs through Pearson that you have unlimited attempts for. He also provides practice exams to prepare you for each exam. Could not recommend him enough!
So much memorization. Worse than the actual anatomy class.

Dr. Johnson is truly one of the best professors I've had at UNC! He is very kind, understanding, and easily approachable. He genuinely wants you to succeed! With that said, the class is tough, but it is fair. Put in the work and it pays off!

Take Johnson!!!!!! Best anatomy professor here. Made me actually enjoy the content, and gave fair exams. He is a Hilarious guy who keeps you laughing throughout the lecture, and you can tell he has a true joy for the teacher. Give him a raise!!!!

Most of the class is the TA; but overall this class was really easy. Start studying the Anki about a week or two out from each exam, do the labeling exercises, online exercises, and take GRQs/PLQs seriously and you'll get an easy A. The exams were some of the easiest exams I've taken at UNC, I didnt take more than 45 minutes on any of them

Professor Johnson is ABSOLUTELY the professor you want to take Biol 252/253 with 100%. He is a great lecturer and gives exams that are solely multiple choice. Provides practice exams and tries his best to teach at a pace that gives you time to process and understand concepts. Attendance is just PollEvs. I would 1000% take a class with him again.

Professor Johnson is by far my favorite professor I've had at UNC. In both 252 & 253, he breaks down difficult concepts & makes them feel clear and approachable. It's obvious that he truly cares about his students' success and puts in the effort to help us do well. He makes lectures genuinely enjoyable - I always look forward to going to his class!

Had him for 252, and I'm so glad I have him again for 253. His lectures are super well organized, he's great at explaining tough concepts, and I feel the exams are very fair. You can tell he really cares about his students and implements their feedback for the class. Plus he's a really funny guy.

I cannot express just how amazing Dr. Johnson is! By far my absolute favorite professor. He takes time to get to know his students, ensures you know the material, engages students in lecture, and genuinely loves what he does. I like his group office hours, where he has spent both group and one-on-one time with students. Take his class if you can!

BIOL252L is a tough class, but with the right study approach, you can definitely succeed. Consistent memorization and using resources like Unstuckstudy alongside the lectures and textbook make all the difference. The exams are challenging, but the TAs provide great support.

I cannot speakly highly enough of Professor Johnson. He's understanding, encouraging, and a delight for any student. He does not allow cheat sheets but his tests are noticeably easier than other professors who do permit cheat sheets. Professor Johnson is an incredibly lecturer, and just a good person in general.

Dr. Johnson is the best bio prof. I have had so far at UNC. He actually teaches the material. He also provides practice exams before each exam that are extremely comparable to the actual exams. The textbook and homework are helpful. If you attend class and study you will do well. He's also super funny.

Corey Johnson was a great professor who genuinely cared about his students. Although the lecture sizes were large, he made the class interesting. I think the tests in his class were extremely fair, which is one of the reasons I liked this class so much. Would definitely recommend taking his class over any of the other anatomy professors!
He was very understanding and helpful with grading!

Best STEM Professor I have EVER HAD at UNC. Dr. Johnson is the best; he is very understanding, and his lectures are fantastic. He always takes his time to make sure everyone understands the material. His exams are practically based on the information he discusses in the lectures. Rewatch his lectures before each exam, and study your notes!

Johnson was an amazing professor! I was scared for this course, but Johnson eased my fears. His lectures are great and he is funny, inserting jokes whenever he can. His tests are very fair, ranging from straightforward to application questions; he only tested on what he taught. Take him if you're able. I heavily recommend him for this course!

Best professor. Easy to follow and entertaining lectures are recorded, class structure is clear, homework light, tests are all multiple choice and easy. Very accessible outside of class and seems to care a lot about student success. Anatomy isn't an easy subject by nature, but he makes it really approachable.

Dr. Johnson is a great professor and would highly recommend taking a class with him! His lectures are easy to follow, and he injects a lot of humor and excitement into them. He clearly cares about his students and is fair in his expectations for class and grading. The exams are all multiple choice and are very manageable if you do the assigned HW.
He is a great professor and lecturer. You can tell he enjoyed the subject he teaches. In my opinion, he is the best professor for the anatomy and physiology course.

Dr. Johnson is a great professor and is so funny during lecture. In my opinion his tests are significantly easier than the other anatomy professors. They are super straight forward and are straight from the reading and lecture

This class really depends on your TA but Johnson gives you lots of materials to be successful. There is so much practice provided and the lectures are pretty thorough. Overall just be ready to memorize new things and you'll be fine. It's hardly the horror it's made out to be.
Dr Johnson is an entertaining lecturer and his tests are super fair. He gives lots of opportunities for practice and is easy to reach outside of class. My fav BIOL professor so far!
The goat. 253 is more focused on physiology which was nice. Exams are difficult but you can do well if you prepare. 253L was MUCH easier than 252L.

Dr. Johnson was great; I don't know why so many people complain about 252L. Yes it's hard, but you have to lock in and spend hours studying and you'll get an A because it's just memorization based. The GRQs and quizzes are all graded for completion, and the exams are super easy. It's the TAs that do most of the instruction though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course can be very time consuming because it requires a lot of memorization. However, there are plenty of resources that you can use to study for exams. This course is also very lecture-dependent and it's helpful if you get a TA that explains the content well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Johnson was one of my favorite professors at UNC! The content is difficult, but he is a great lecturer and explains things well. He provides a practice exam before each exam, which is really helpful. This class is mostly physiology rather than anatomy, which was very nice. Definitely take him if you can.

Exams were taken on paper, open response, pure memorization, and the photos of the models were so poor in quality. The last 2 exams were on paper, and it was harder to see the picture than it was to recall what it actually was.

There is just SO MUCH content. Each lecture is a flood of material that you are expected to memorize. To make it worse, 50% of the questions on the exams are random application questions that are most times not even mentioned in lectures. The format of this class is lazy, making the students do all the work, an unrealistic amount of memorization.

I spent more time on this than on the actual BIOL 252 course. This is unforgiving, relentless, and extremely poorly designed for it to be a 1 credit lab. Honestly, it wouldn't be much of a problem if it didn't have the RANDOM application questions that makeup 50 questions on each exam. No teaching is done, this is purely a test of your memorization

Each exam is worth 20%, there are 2 non-cumulative exams. They consist of 50 identification open-response questions (no word bank) and 50 application questions (random and open-response). By each exam date, you should have memorized roughly 150 terms, this class only consists of memorization. The final is cumulative and 30% of your grade.

I aboslutely love Corey Johnson as a professor, I wish he taught more classes. Don't let the no cheat sheets scare you, he knows his stuff and can properly answer any question you have. Also, the exams are much easier than you'd think because of the lack of cheat sheet. Best professor I've had by far.

He is good at making things clear and posts the lectures so you can go back. The only reason I wouldn't take him again is because for both 252 & 253 the other profs allow cheat sheets and he doesn't.  Not really fair when students are all applying to med/pa/nursing school and some students had to study twice as hard without a cheat sheet
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: it felt like a bulldozer was crushing us each week. class was doable but at the cost of students leaving the room crying. so I guess pick your own battles.

Clear lecturer, easy exams, and provided practice exams that had questions from the real exams on them.  There were warmups and readings due before class, but it's no issue to skip the readings, as all the information on the exams comes from the lectures.  Also one of the best dressing STEM professors I've had if you care about that kind of thing

Lecture is very TA dependent, but you can learn everything on your own because exams are based off the lab manual. There are A TON of things to memorize, but there are a lot of resources they provide, like an Anki deck and practice questions, so it is doable. Nothing is really difficult to understand, just takes a long time to memorize it all.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Johnson is amazing, and I learned SO MUCH. But I feel like his section of the class was harder than the other profs. Other sections were allowed cheat sheets on exams and had a non-cumulative final, which was not the case for us. Exams were fair though. Worth the trade-off though because this was one of my favorite classes!

This is definitely a difficult class and Johnson does a good job at explaining things and doesn't mind if he needs to reexplain. Weren't many things to grade in this course. Exams are a large percentage of the grade. Attending group reviews and office hours help. Provides practice exams. He seems like a nice guy that wants to do his job well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I honestly really enjoyed this class with Dr. Johnson. He was super accessible and friendly and his tests were super fair. As long as you put in the effort in this class you'll do fine since the textbook isn't super complicated and his tests don't include anything he doesn't talk about in class, definitely recommend Dr. Johnson's class!

Anatomy is a hard class at UNC, but if you have to take it, take it with Johnson. He was so nice and caring. His tests don't allow a cheat sheet, but I preferred that because the questions were easier.

This class is DIFFICULT but has nothing to do with Dr. Johnson. He is very knowledgeable on the content and is good at explaining. The test questions are all pulled from lecture content and are either application, basic knowledge, or a super specific detail. Taking notes during lecture is necessary because he does not annotate slides but records.

If you're taking this class, be prepared to study regularly throughout the semester. It's all memorization, so do whatever is best for you to memorize things. They give an anki set which is semi-useful for identifying different parts, so use that. You do not need to spend 10 hours a week studying... just use anki early on and read the lab manual
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take BIOL 252 with him if you can! Any anatomy class is going to be hard, but at least he made it fun, and interesting, and the test questions were straightforward for the most part. The final was a lot harder than I expected and it ended up pulling me down a letter grade, but overall at least I learned a lot in the course.

Dr. Johnson is the way to go for BIOL252. His class wasn't 'easy' but it wasn't hard. The exams were fair and represented what we had learned in class. Read the textbook beforehand (don't take that many notes) and go to the lecture and you'll be good. He was also funny af and was nice to everyone. Take him!!!

Anatomy lab is really hard. You have to commit at least 10+ hours a week if you really want a good grade. All memorization and you'll get 0 points if you use one wrong letter. They put stuff on exams that isn't in the slides and can only be found in the lab manual. Also don't rely on study resources because there are mistakes and spelling errors

I LOVE COREY JOHNSON. He is the absolute best and the only way to go for physiology. He makes the content very understandable, I never read the textbook, only went to class and have gotten A's on all 3 midterms. His tests are so fair and he records lectures. I'm sad I wont have his class next semester. Best professor everrrrrrrr!

By far, he is one of the best professors at UNC. I would highly recommend that if you is teaching 252 or 253, to take it with him. He actually cares about you as a student and wants to see you succeed! His tests are straightforward and he tests directly on what he says within his lectures (re-watching lectures is honestly the most useful tool).

Dr. Johnson is one of the best professors I've had. The exams are very fair, include material straight from all the lectures. Nothing he doesn't lecture about is on the exams. Lectures are interesting and he's pretty funny and overall a really nice guy.

Everyone seems to love his teaching style but I don't. This class is worlds harder than any class I've taken at UNC, harder than chem 101/102 for me. Lab surprisingly is way better than the lecture. I leave class more confused and the tests are ridiculous

Amazing. He is a great professor and genuinely cares about his students. He makes lots of dad jokes, it's funny to hear during lecture. His tests are very fair and if you study for the exam you'll do good because he really is just testing to see your knowledge and not to trick you like other professors. Definitely recommend!

Material is very similar to BIOL 252. Exams are fair and based entirely in what is covered in the slides. Go to office hours if possible; Dr. Johnson is super accessible and kind so if you aren't understanding something or need help, talk to him directly.

Lab was VERY hard for exams; even if you understand the material you have to be extremely specific or you will get no credit. Even if you have the correct term but are not specific enough then you will not get credit. He will be accommodating when warranted though which is helpful. Be ready to study for hours

Corey Johnson is a great professor and his material is fair. This lab is only as hard as you make it. All the materials you need for the tests are clearly given to you. There are numerous study resources and people (TAs/LAs) who are there to help you! This class is a lot of memorization. Start studying well before exams and the tests will be easy.

Dr. Johnson was accessible outside of class and seemed like a very nice person through his emails. However, the level of difficulty in this class was ridiculous. Easily the hardest lab I've ever taken. The difficulty of material and amount of time I had to spend outside of class was equivalent to a 4 credit class.

Professor Johnson is awesome! Not a huge amount of work, and the tests were very fair. You'll definitely need to study and read through the textbook, but they're comparable to the tests I've taken in 201, 202, and 205 (maybe slightly easier). Also, the lecture exams were on different weeks from my other stem exams, which was very nice.

Take Dr. Johnson's class! His lectures include everything that will be on the exams, and he is very open to student questions in office hours. This class reminded me of how I've heard professional school classes will be - fair but comprehensive presentation of the material. He explained the material very well, and made learning easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is an amazing Anatomy professor. His test are hard but definitely fair. You do have to put in the work but it's fair and he has a option for exam grade replacement via essay
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The anatomy lab is a tough course that requires a lot of time outside of lab to put in the effort to memorize the material. That being said, Dr. Johnson is extremely caring and accessible outside of lab. I had some personal issues going on that affected my test scores and Dr. Johnson helped me get past those scores and I ended up doing well.

Whoever said this stem is easy is either a memorizing wizard or already had prior knowledge. A lot of pre-meds have an advantage in this class so I suffered through. Grading was so ridiculous, no partial credit even if 95% of the answer was correct. TAs gave misleading info so much and acted like stuff was not important. TAs sent rude emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tough tough class. It's a lot of material but an A is achievable. Be ready to commit at least ~10 hours (4hr per reading+notes, 2hr of looking over notes) of your week to the conceptualization of topics. You really have to be on top of your game.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: THE GOAT. Material is rough and dense, but he made it as bearable as possible. He TRULY and GENUINELY cares for his students. My all-time favorite STEM professor since being here at UNC.

Pretty solid choice for a professor. I heard this class is harder than normal A&P, but Johnson himself was pretty laid back and understanding. If u hate papers tho, u do have to write 1 or 2 for this class

I learned a lot of interesting stuff in this class, it was super fun! If you are taking the class, take it with Corey Johnson. He gives really good lectures, provides resources to ensure you are able to succeed, and is accessible outside of class. He also wants you to succeed, and will help you if you put in the effort. Great class and great prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you are taking BIOL252, TAKE IT WITH DR. JOHNSON. He is the professor for the lab too, and it made talking too him about the lab much easier, and less nerve wracking, since he knew who I was. Dr. Johnson is easily one of the most caring and understanding professors at UNC, and is more than willing to work with his students. Highly recommend.

One of the easiest STEM classes you will take at UNC, but it requires a lot of time and effort. There's a lot of info and details you need to know but Dr. Johnson/the TAs do a good job of telling you what to expect. Highly recommend using lab time/open labs to look at models even though they're optional since that's what you'll be tested on.

Do not take anatomy lab at unc unless you absolutely need to. The class is not set up in a way that encourages learning, you go to one class a week and go through a PowerPoint with maybe 15 out of the 50ish terms then you play with plastic models. Tests are extremely hard and you have 90 sec at each station, which is anxiety-inducing enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very clear lectures. Prepared you well for tests, no surprises! Very relaxed class setup, easy to follow along. Fresh of air from other STEM classes at UNC. you will do great!

Professor Johnson was the most understanding professors I've had. The honors course is difficult straight from Bio 101. Great lecturer and also posts online recordings. Best way to study for the class is rewatching lecture videos over anything else. We had opportunities to improve our grades which was awesome. Go to his office hours for questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The three exams are worth about 90% of your grade. The textbook is super dense and it's all about memorization. Prof Johnson did understand how coming back to in-person classes after over a year of online classes heavily impacted the overall exam grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would definitely recommend this class. It does require a lot of memorization but other than that, there really isnt a lot of work. We had 3 quizzes and and a number of GRQs that counted towards our grade and that was it. Professor Johnson was really understanding this semester and gave curves when needed.

Professor Johnson was extremely understanding this semester, considering the difficulty of the course and the tough adjustment to having in-person classes. The questions on exams were straightforward but require a lot of memorizing (the hardest part, in my opinion) and spelling is very important. Would take him again!

Dr. Johnson was amazing during the transition back to in person. He understood that it would be very difficult to come back to in person (especially in a course with so much to memorize). He was sure to curve appropriately and was very understanding of students going through difficult times. The course is HARD, lots to memorize. Stay on top of it!

A breath of fresh air from other UNC STEM courses. Exam questions are straight from the lab manual and really easy. What makes this course difficult is the amount of memorization, but that's true for any anatomy lab. Just space out your studying, use flashcards, and don't wait until the last minute to label your model diagrams and you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The way BIOL 252L is set up is bad. Like another review said, it's literally based on how well you memorize things. Exams are 80% of your grade and the way they grade is very specific and nit-picky, so good luck. I don't think this lab helps students learn or succeed.
If you can avoid taking this class, please do. It's so hard for no reason. You basically get graded for your ability to memorize
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I never leave reviews for professors, but Prof. Johnson is a real gem in the Bio department. He is super kind and you can tell how much effort he puts into his Powerpoints. He is a great professor and very knowledgeable about what he teaches. I would definitely recommend this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Johnson is a great professor. His only downfall is that his lectures can be boring and mundane. He explains things very well and his tests are fair. Would recommend!

SOMEONE GIVE THIS MAN A RAISE!! Unlike the majority of biology professors, he explains things amazingly well, posts his lectures for reviewing at home, and TESTS FAIRLY!!! If you study, you can do well and he makes difficult concepts so clear through examples. Also hes really funny and always makes himself available to talk to students.

Had him for comparative vertebrate anatomy ("evolution of vertebrate life"). IMO, the clearest explainer I've seen in the department. His powerpoints are also hilarious. The grade was based on four exams, which seemed intimidating at first, but if you start studying as soon as possible, they are extremely reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the best professors at UNC. Makes the class fun and keeps you engaged for the most part. The exams DO require you to study in order to pass; but if you do study, you'll be perfectly fine. Tells a lot of jokes during his lecture. I'd recommend going to class, but he does record lectures and post the PowerPoints. Highly recommend him.

Dr. Johnson is my favorite science professor at UNC. He makes fair tests unlike many other professors do, so if you study and put in the work you can do well. Re-listen to the lectures! That's a huge key to success in his class. Grade is made up of 90% tests and that scared me but it ended up being okay.

Dr. Johnson has been one of the best professors that I've had at UNC thus far. The class is interesting and he makes them even more interesting with his sense of humor. Re-listening to lectures is a must but, if you can do that you can pass the class. Also, the lab is super enjoyable and nowhere near as difficult as the 252 lab.

Dr. Johnson is the best professor I've had at UNC! He explains the complex material in a way that is easy to understand, and he truly cares about his students' success. His sense of humor really makes the class enjoyable. The exams take preparation, but he records the lectures which makes studying easier. I highly recommend taking his class!

BEST professor I've had at UNC!! He's hilarious and makes lectures interesting with his sense of humor. He's also very knowledgable and great at explaining concepts. He records the lecturs with audio AND video, which I recommend rewatching all lectures in preparation for exams. There are 3 exams which make up 90% of the grade, so study for those!

Dr. Johnson is by far the most genuine professor I have had at UNC! He is very willing to work with students, and just wants to see you succeed. His tests make up a lot of your grade, however he gives you more than enough tools to prepare for them (definitely recommend rewatching lectures). Overall, Dr. Johnson is very incredible- highly recommend!

One of my favorite professors at UNC. Excellent at explaining difficult anatomical concepts, and always has time to address questions. He posts lectures online, and his tests are basically straight off the lectures. Very do-able class, in my opinion.

Dr. Johnson is great! He's very laid back and approachable, knowledgeable of the course material, and makes lectures enjoyable. He records his lectures, which is nice; I definitely rewatch the lectures in preparation for exams. His exams are fair, but only 45 questions and compose 88% of your grade, so make sure you are confident going into them.

I did not have Dr. Johnson for BIOL 252, but I had him this semester for the second semester Human A&P (BIOL 253). He is a great teacher who really cares about the students learning the material. He seems to implement that same teaching style as 252 (recorded lectures, using online HW platform, tests are not too difficult).

Dr. Johnson is an absolutely incredible professor. The best lecturer I have ever had at Carolina. He is so clear and so easy to understand. He makes Physiology seem so simple. Exams are not easy, but fair. Lab is just hell- there is so much to memorize and it will take the majority of your time.

One of the most humorous prof at UNC. Give amazing lectures where he crams in a lot of information without it ever feeling rushed or overwhelming. Attendance not mandatory but highly recommend. HW is easy but time-consuming. 252  understanding, 252L  an overwhelming amount of memorization. Not recommended to be taken simultaneously as MCAT prep
I am amazed at how Dr. Johnson can explain so much in one lecture without it ever becoming overwhelming
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is an amazing professor and lecturer.  You have a lot of reading and the material is not easy to understand but he is very willing to work with you in office hours or if you have any questions.  He is also such a nice person and makes a lot of jokes that make the class enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Definitely one of the best professors I've ever had at UNC. The material's tricky but he made it easy to follow along. His lectures were always fantastic and I actually looked forward to going because I knew that it was going to be entertaining. His tests were fair and long enough that a misstep or two wouldn't be devastating. Take his class!!!

Amazing professor. Truly cares about his students. If you do the work and don't get behind on the readings, it's easy to do well. Also, his lectures are hilariousssss! and when I came a few minutes late to an exam one day and there were no more seats, he let me sit in the front so I'll have a desk. You can tell he truly cares about his students.

Fantastic lecturer. Anatomy is a lot of dense material but he explains it clearly. Also, Johnson records his lectures which is clutch af when studying. Be sure to get the poll everywhere question right! Correct answers give an extra bonus point. The tests are tough but they are completely fair and straight forward. TAKE HIM

Challenging class.  Soooooo much material, but you'll thank him later. Really great lectures.  There's some of the talk-to-your-neighbor BS like other bio classes but not too much.  This course helped me learn to READ, and I'm thankful for it.
Good lecturer

I would recommend him to anyone who is taking Anatomy and Physiology. It is definitely not a class you can easily pass by studying the day before. His exams are difficult but fair. Most of the exam questions are straight forward and some are tricky. Lab is a hard, so be careful and study a lot. He's such a cute and nice person.

Great lecturer.  The bio dept. needs more like him.  Tests were tricky, but very fair.  Purchase the bigger textbook.  The condensed one does not cover some of his lecture material.  That way, if you miss something from lecture, you can get it from the book.  Super approachable and caring; never felt rushed out the door in office hours.

Class uses both textbook and his lectures. There is a ton of information to learn but he does his best to make it fair albeit difficult. The first test was the easiest so don't slack especially on tests 2 and 3. He is engaging and committed to the class.

A pretty clear lecturer but boring. He's monotone and will throw around some jokes, but I honestly couldn't pay attention in class. Watch out cause his tests are tricky. Sometimes he takes more questions from the book info and sometimes more from his lectures/ppts. Nice guy and if you argue back for test points, he'll most likely give you one.

Awesome professor. As he says "Just know everything and you will be fine". Biol 252 is a had class, but if I would have to take it all over again, I would take it with him. I would take any possible class with him, loved him. He is a great teacher!

Professor Johnson is the best professor I have ever had. Take any and all courses you can with him. Heck, if he was teaching Intro to Women's Studies or History of Medieval Europe I would take that class. The subject matter is difficult for A&P, but he makes it interesting. The assignments are easy. The multiple-choice exams are not. Study a lot.

ONE OF MY FAVORITE PROFESSORS! Anatomy and Physiology is a lot of work! but his powerpoints are great! He always seems to cover everything you need to know without rushing. you have to do your part (study his ppts), but you can't claim your failure on him.

Love Dr. Johnson (so cute), but this class is hard. My advice - write down every single thing he says in class and study like crazy. Tests are fair but hard. He is great with email so def email him with questions (I did all the time). Lab is a pain b/c he writes the exams now, not the TAs, so lab is not as easy. Book is not really needed.
GREAT TEACHER!  Take him for A&P if you have the opportunity!!
I love Dr. Johnson! Probably the best professor I had at UNC.

By far the best professor I've had. Tells you exactly what will be on the exam (what's on the outlines). The book he chose is very good. Only tests you on material you go over in class although you need to know more details on those topics. Also very nice person who will be glad to help you with any problems.

Dr. Johnson is a sweet man & a good professor. He e-mails back very fast & is willing to meet with you/hold exam study sessions. BIOL in general is hard but straightforward so if you don't do well it's not his fault. His tests are completely reasonable & he makes little jokes in class. He also sometimes mentions his new daughter which is adorable.

Dr. Johnson is the best! He is readily available for office hours and his lecture notes are clear and concise. While I recommend that you read the textbook (it's helpful), you don't have to, since he only tests things that he covered in class. Plus, he is incredibly cute and fun to listen to!

I love Dr. Johnson!! :) Amazing professor. The class was at 8am but definitely worth coming to. Exams weren't too bad pretty straight forward but theres a ****ton of material, but thats for any class. Would definitely take him again for other bio classes.

Very nice guy. Extremely helpful and cares a lot about his student. Not an easy class...lots of memorizations but you bust you butt and you'll do well ;) Plus he gives you a chance to make up for you lowest grade if you improve well enough.

Great Professor. Unlike most bio profs he cares about his students. Funny, helpful, and makes class enjoyable. Outline notes are posted before lecture, which helps when the lecture material gets dull. Tests are fill in the blank & T/F, but he makes it clear what will and will not be on the test.

Great professor. Vertebrate class was easy. Powerpoints and outline lecture notes are posted on BB. You can get thru the class w/o using much of the book. Studying his notes very thoroughly are enough to pass his tests (even make an A). Test questions are usually straight forward questions. He answers questions, is fair, and has a nice humor.

Funny guy. Teaches clearly, but his tests are not that easy. Since Lab makes 25% of the grade(for Bio 252) if you do WELL in the lab, you might get an A. And BTW, the course is really interesting since it teaches you the human anatomy. (MED, DENT students have to take)

Good professor. He seems somewhat shy and hesitant at times, but he presents material in an enjoyable, easy to comprehend manner. He's far, far better than Bynum, no doubt. Take him if at all possible.

Timid at first, but warms up to class quickly. Entertaining and helpful. Always willing to answer questions in class. Does very good job of keeping pace with lab. Use blackboard notes and ppt presentations. ALWAYS read the chapter.
Very good teacher! Very helpful and clear at gettin his point across to the students!!!

It may only be the beginning of the semester but so far this prof. is awesome compared to the other prof. that "teaches" this course.  He actually answers questions, takes the time to explain things and makes use of our $200, extremely well written textbook.  Super improvement over the Anatomy class I attempted to take last semester!

Took Cervantes class with Dr. Collins - reading heavy, obviously, but we took Don Quixote piece by piece and she knows so much about the book, so lectures were interesting, even at 8AM. Did not provide super clear feedback about grading criteria, but wasn't harsh, either. Take notes in class and you'll be prepared for the minimal essays + exams
Such a great professor. Homework is just reading. Good books ngl and i dont even like reading. Participate and you will do fine. Everything is super chill too
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. You read a lot of books but she covers them thoroughly, so as long as you take notes you're fine! Few tests (Midterm, 1 paper, 1 group project and final). Gives comprehensive feedback and she's the sweetest teacher. Take notes and you'll be grand. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is the second class I have taken with her and it was the same format. There is one group presentation, a research paper, and two exams. She is very kind, but class can get kind of boring. It is all discussion and presentations. She grades fairly easy and I would likely take another class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's very passionate, but she teaches in a confusing way. Classes were discussion based and exams were based on stuff mentioned by students in lectures. No rubrics were given for anything. You never know what she's looking for, and she mentions out of the box connections in your assignments and takes off points if you didn't make the connections.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is discussion based and she chimes in to make sure the conversation is continuing. There is a group oral presentation that is fairly easy with pretty open guidelines. There is also one 12-15 pg research paper, but there was little instruction on what to do. No rubric provided either so really no idea what she was looking for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Collins is hands-down my favorite professor at UNC. She is passionate about her work and truly values hearing the interpretations and thoughts of her students. She would guide the overall structure of the lectures but for the most part she let us provide our opinions, point to places in the text, and ask questions. TAKE HER CLASSES!

She is passionate about her lessons and tries to be as engaging as possible. It's nice that most of the material is discussion-based rather than lecture style. She isn't a tough grader but gives helpful feedback and communicates well via email. 10/10 recommend :)

A great choice for a 300-level ENGL course. There's a 12-15 pg paper and a lot of reading but you could get away without doing the readings because they're discussed in class. Beloved is an amazing book though and I would recommend reading it. The midterm was an open-note essay during class and the final wasn't bad either. Attendance is required.

Professor Collins has been one of my favorite professors I've had at UNC!! She is amazing, and truly cares about each of her students. The class has a fair number of readings, but if you keep up with them, and pay attention to lectures, you will do fine on the limited amount of assignments Professor Collins assigns.

She is the nicest professors I have had! She is constantly smiling & cares a lot about her students. You do have a 10pg paper at the end of the course but you pick your own topic. Theres a lot of reading, but as a person who usually doesnt like reading, I enjoyed reading for this class. She is very insightful about curiosity and makes learning fun!

Prof Collins is so kind, and super accessible via email/office hours/appointment. For 300s level classes, she usually has a midterm, a group project, a final, and a 10-page paper. She's a very lenient grader--as long as you put in the effort, she will reward your hard work. She also took our class to Ackland a couple of times for a change of pace.

Professor Collins is a gem! She is very eloquent in how she describes curiosity and the imagination and is so intelligent. On top of it all, she is one of the sweetest people I have ever met! If you have the opportunity, take a class with her. Although there is plenty of reading(I don't like to read), I thoroughly enjoyed the class and lectures.

One of my FAVORITE professors at UNC! I have taken two of her comparative literature classes (Romancing the World and Don Quixote) and plan to take more if possible. There is a lot to read but her lectures are always so interesting and insightful.

One of my favorite professors so far at UNC. As long as you come to class and do the readings, you will pass. Some of the readings were boring, but others were great and interesting (about half and half). Professor Collins truly cares about each student and what they learn from her. I would take this again.
She is the sweetest teacher. Her tests are very hard/specific, but she grades papers fairly. Lots of reading per class, but I would definitely recommend her!

I was delighted to have my senior seminar with Dr. Collins. For starters, she is SUCH a sweet, ebullient lady. She chose interesting texts, kept class discussions lively, and was reasonable with expectations/feedback. Also super knowledgeable in Renaissance lit and Cervantes.  If I hadn't graduated I'd be in her classes all the time!

I enjoyed this class because I love literature but I have a friend in the class who does not and she thought it was miserably boring. Overall, very easy if you read the books and attend lecture every now and then.

I took CMPL 390 - Don Quixote with Prof Collins and LOVED it. Stay on top of the readings, attend class and participate occasionally and you'll make an A. The tests weren't difficult if you did the reading and paid attention. Prof Collins is incredibly intelligent and very helpful! Definitely take her class!
Collins' lectures are very boring, she reads them directly from a piece of paper and they tend to be pretty unnecessary. You don't have to attend lecture very often to get a good grade in the class.

Dr. Collins is sooooo nice and very helpful. She really knows the material very well, and she is encouraging to all students. I learned so much from her. My only comment is that it would be better if she taught classes all in Spanish instead of English.

Dr. Collins is the best professor! She is very helpful, kind and patient, and she really knows her stuff. She works with both Golden Age and Twentieth Century Spanish lit and is well-versed in both. Her classes are not easy, but they are worth taking, and if you work hard you will do well.

Funny, passionate, and very helpful with consistent office hours. Took time to explain things when asked. Weekly homework and pop quizzes were challenging, weighed really heavily and hurt the most. I declared pass/fail and low-passed :(

Considering the fact that Math381 is one of the hardest freshman year classes, Crawford made it extremely easy to follow, understand, and do well. First Midterm: 101, Second Midterm, 95. Bonus questions on midterms were understandable and the "pop" quizzes we had were mainly easy 100's. Could not be more happy with Crawford's Math381 course.

Matt is awesome. I think he's one of the harder professors for 381 but not completely sure, however he made the lectures super engaging and encouraged us to think critically. Made himself available outside of the classroom as well and is a hilarious and smart guy. Would recommend, course is incredibly hard though. I pass/failed.

Matt was respectful, understanding, and enthusiastic. He was very charismatic in his approach to lecturing, and his office hours greatly helped on the difficult topics. This was by far the most difficult course I've ever taken, and the learning curve was tremendous. However, Matt made the material genuinely intriguing and I'd recommend him for 381.

Very nice/open to questions. Was his first year teaching though, so pace lagged behind 2 days and a few lectures had to teach self rest of content. Midterm 1 average: 72%, midterm 2 average: 70%, historical final average: 65%. Not easy, but among other options (especially Snoeyink if CS major) is a good choice. Study hard though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Matt did an amazing job of being enthusiastic and helping us to the best of his ability. I disliked mainly things outside of his control about the Math 130 class. The class is designed as a flipped classroom, and the grading is insanely test-heavy, so it was harder to understand and achieve, but I felt that he did everything he could to help!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Crawford is enthusiastic, caring and genuinely wants his students to succeed. He went above and beyond to help his students understand difficult concepts. He was easily accessible before/after class and by email. As someone who was taking this class as a prereq, this was the best professor I could've taken this class with.
His dad jokes make the math seem less bad.

Professor Crawford was O.U.T.S.T.A.N.D.I.N.G. By far the best math professor ever. He is only a graduate student, too! In his class he is animate, enthusiastic, and very encouraging. He truly cares for the success of his students. Timely email responses and very enjoyable classes. If you aren't taking Matthew Crawford, WHAT ARE YOU DOING!!!??

Genuinely do not listen to any of the good ratings. This class is actually impossible. She is hilarious and I can tell she is passionate but she is the worst lecturer ever. She jumps from topic to topic, making her impossible to follow. Her slides have no information, just pictures. No matter how much I study it doesn't pay off.

content was disorganized and could have been given to students in a way that actually makes sense. Also exams are worth basically everything, so all the other assignments you do don't even matter. Cramer also likes to talk/yell at us during exams, which really messed with me. Overall, not the best class i've taken here.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She can be difficult to understand: jumps from topic to topic without care, difficult to follow, hits the ground running, everything said, looked at, and even lightly covered is important. DO THE ORGANISMS FROM DAY 1. DO ANKI. Look over everything everyday and make sure you understand it. Everything builds and she SUCKS at answering questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is the worst professor at UNC. She is derogatory and does not care to see you genuinely succeed. Very awful, unclear, and unhelpful woman, she knows she is the only professor for this course and therefore does not care to help you even if you meet with her several times. I firmly believe UNC should fire this woman and replace her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was one of the best classes I have taken at UNC. Dr. Cramer is hilarious and the tests were also easy if you studied and did everything she advised to do. There was a lot of work sometimes but if you review the Anki Cards, Organism Cards, and Lecture Notes, you should be able to do well on the exams. She curves too!

Dr. Cramer is amazing if you put in the effort she asks you to. Do the Anki every day, rewatch the lecture videos, and do the organisms cards. You will get an A if you do this, and she gives extra credit on every exam. My favorite STEM professor I have had at UNC, and don't be scared, she is very nice in person.

I was scared of this class because of the reviews too. But genuinely Dr. Cramer is super caring and yes her lecture can feel disorganized sometimes but she heavily emphasizes what will be tested. The topics were super interesting! Her exams were straightforward with no tricks. If you space out studying and memorize early on, you will be fine!

Don't take this class. The grade is based almost entirely on exams,required to write blog 3 page every week he exams require memorizing lectures, the textbook, and Anki material. No study guides.the teaching style made the course overwhelming and hard to understand. I would not recommend this class.

I love Dr. Cramer! Her lectures are engaging, there is a lot to remember, but she gives all the resources needed to do well and curves exams. Micro is just a hard class but it is super interesting and she is very passionate about it. She can come off as intimidating but she just really wants her students to learn and succeed. Best class I've taken!

Overall very nice and does want you to succeed. Biggest tip is rewatch all the lecture videos and put basically everything she says into an anki card. It sucks but it helps. Definitely easier than chem in my opinion. Exams are straightforward, there's just a lot to know which makes them difficult. Putting what she says into anki helps with this

On the first day of class, she told us her RMP ratings were inaccurate, and she wasn't a bad professor. This is a lie. She's a messy lecturer, bouncing around topics and mixing things up. In addition to this, she often shames the class on how awful the test scores are instead of taking accountability. So, prepare yourself for a 60% class average!
The content is super dense and the workload is heavy but it was interesting. She's very tough love but is a good lecturer (go back and rewatch lectures tho). DO THE ANKI AND STUDY!!

I don't mean to scare you because I know she is the only professor for this course, but she sucks. There were classes after an exam where all she would do was shame those who did not get a perfect score. She scribbles all over the slides and only uses them to help herself remember what to say. If you are going to survive this course, use the Anki!

The content is dense, as UNC requires her to condense three semesters of micro into one. The workload is a lot, but manageable: I learned a ton from the work she assigned. She's very upfront, which is nice when you need some tough love and motivation. You can tell she mostly teaches at the medical school, lol. Overall, a hilarious, awesome person.

Dr. Cramer is hilarious, which makes lectures fun to attend. She is very passionate about the material, which makes it easier to learn. This class is only really hard because of the insane amount of writing you have to do, and the sheer amount of information. Micro is a dense subject regardless of who teaches it, so the class is simply difficult.

I know you don't have a choice to take anyone but Cramer for MCRO251, so just prepare yourself mentally. Her exams are really hard and she's rude - called us stupid after our class got a low exam average. There's a lot of reading and she talks fast in lectures, which are very information heavy but still on your exam. I'd take the class elsewhere.

Don't take this class! I HATED IT! Grade is JUST exams, but you still have to write a 2-3 page paper every week for literally no reason. Unless you somehow can memorize everything she says (she speaks insanely fast), the textbook, and the Anki, don't take this class. She is very nice and approachable but too smart for me to know what she's saying.

I really enjoyed this class! It is a hard class and you have to study all the material she gives you, but she is passionate and the lectures are super interesting. As long as you make time for the class you'll do well, the lab is fun. Exams are tricky but everything she asks can be found in recorded lectures or the anki.

Mcro is challenging but doable. The homework for this class was a lot, especially having to read the textbook, doing GLQ, doing the anki, doing the blogs, and doing lab work. She is lovely, but OMG, how she will talk ( announcements) through exams was annoying and made me struggle. Consider an ARS accommodation before you take one of her exams.

MCRO is a difficult class, you need to listen to lectures and study to do well but I believe I was given more than enough resources to be successful. I personally found the lectures super interesting which helped. I also found the content to be pretty basic - there is just A LOT of it. Do not be afraid of Dr. Cramer! She was awesome!

Don't listen to the bad reviews! Dr. Cramer is by far the best stem professor at UNC. Yes, this class is challenging, has a lot of information, and requires an insane amount of studying. But if you put in the work, study, and go to her office hours, you will be fine! You can tell she cares about her students and wants them to do well!

I'm not gonna lie this class is really as difficult as you make it. Requires HEAVY studying in anki cards and paying attention in lecture for very specific nidbits.
