reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I audited this class, so grain of salt, but Dr. Curtain is kind and extremely knowledgeable about horror movies. He isn't afraid to call on people out of the blue and challenge their answers, but he's also funny and encourages discussion. Really enjoyed this class.
Very weird about missing assignments. Definitely insecure about teaching a horror class haha.
Really chill class. Just watch movies and talk about stuff. Curtain is a chill dude who knows everything anyone ever needs to do about horror in general. Great dude with a great personality.

Genuinely a great class. Professor Curtain really makes you think about the films you watch, I have a whole new perspective of sci-fi film now. All you do is talk about the films/books in class, make sure to watch/read everything because he will cold call. All films except 2 books during the whole semester but easy reads. 1 midterm and 1 final.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Curtain is very good at what he teaches and is good at getting you to think more deeply about you ideas on the material. You are graded on participation in class, a midterm, and final but they are fairly straightforward if you keep up with the films needed for class.

This is a great class! I was worried throughout the semester as your final grade consists of participation, one midterm, and a final and you never know your grade for any of them. The material is interesting and attendance is never taken. Ended up with an A.

Overall, I enjoyed this course. It's pretty much entirely discussion based where you talk about films and books. Participation is really important, and you're expected to be active in discussions. My only issues is his viewpoint can be narrow at times and grading is very unclear (there's no canvas site). Easy filler course if you need one.

Hilarious guy and so nice. Our in class convos were thought provoking and deep. There's a midterm and final as our only graded assignments (they're straight up memorization). Homework is watching movies and reading 3 books that we discuss in class. Exams ask for titles, director, and release year of each work we cover. Awesome class and easy A.

We had two assignments and one final that was a breeze. Grades weren't posted until after finals though, which was frustrating. He also refused to acknowledge points of view that contradicted his own, which was rather disappointing, because I wanted to engage in the material. After I gave up trying, the class was fine.

Professor Curtain was very relaxed, so there weren't many assignments or feedback in general which was stressful at times. I ended with an A in the class but got no feedback whatsoever throughout the semester. This was a great class though, your grade is based mostly on participation in class discussion.

Professor Curtain is fun, if not a little unstructured. This class had a 1/2 page syllabus and about 10 books to read. Attendance was not mandatory, but he would assign items in class for the following week and not post on Canvas or notify students, so you had to keep your head on a swivel! His classes were fun, but he would cold call sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Midway the semester, as we were discussing a film by James Cameron, I pointed out the racial stereotypes. As I did this, I also voiced how I could not finish the movie due to the movies racist nature. Professor Curtain stated that my viewpoint, as a POC woman, was incorrect. He also said that I needed to learn how to be uncomfortable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: As long as you watched the movie before the class and were prepared to talk, this class was a breeze. The only assignments we had were a midterm and final, and a final project sequence, which were all very easy. If you do the work, you pretty much get an A. Good easy filler class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class consisted of watching around 30 movies and reading 3 books. The classes were just discussions of the content. There was a midterm and a final, along with a group short film project. Really fun class, just show up and pay attention and talk every once in a while and you will get an easy A. Great professor, great content, take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I have had the honor of having Professor Curtain for two classes during my time at UNC. He is a really great person, and I enjoy his lecture style. He keeps you thinking and encourages participation. Watching movies as homework is a great escape from the heavier assignments from other classes, and the films are all worth it. Take a class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took Prof. Curtain's horror movie class expecting a typical english class, but was pleasantly surprised. The class just consisted of discussing movies we watched before class. The only assignments in class were a midterm, final, and short horror movie group project. Exams were easy and the project was fun. Easy and interesting class!
Amazing professor. Very wise man. Take the class if you can. Start reading early and enjoy the books.

Tyler is an amazing professor! He is so interested in what he teaches that it makes class such a pleasure. The class consists of watching movies/reading books and discussing them. He is a super laid back professor and I enjoyed his class thoroughly.

This semester was really chill. The reading/watch list consists of contemporary things. I'm very shy to talk in class, but this class made me feel welcomed and safe to talk about issues whether it be the news or controversial topics in the movies/books. Take this prof if you get the chance! We had a paper as our midterm, and no graded final.

This class was interesting and definitely an easy A class. If you don't have time to read the books or watch the movies you can just read summaries so you have something to talk about. Got off-topic a lot and talked about some controversial political topics so if those conversations can be triggering for you then I would not reccmonmmend.
Prof Curtain is one of the most caring and accomodating professors I've ever had. Class is very discussion-based, so as long as you know the material you'll be fine.

Prof Curtain has a great story and is very accommodating and welcoming to his students. Half the class is watching and discussing sci-fi/fantasy movies, the other was reading fantasy novels. Some of the books are tough to read in the time allotted before a class discussion, but overall the class was a breeze and I really enjoyed myself in there.

Prof Curtain helped me understand the meaning within sci-fi & fantasy films & books, rather than just the "wow" aspects in them. Each class consists of a group discussion based on the film or book you viewed/read outside of class (which can take a lot of time). He provides a lot of insight and makes class intriguing! Grading criteria isn't clear.

This has definitely been one of my favorite classes in college so far. Professor Curtain facilitates interesting discussions, and I always looked forward to coming to his class. I look at horror movies in a completely different way now. I highly recommend taking a class with him.

I'm a huge horror movie fan and this course was a perfect way to understand the history and really analyze classic horror movies. If you watch the movies and go to class, you'll do well. Class consists of talking through what we all think of each of the movies and its meaning. Professor Curtain is great and really wants to hear what you think.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Loved this class! It was an interesting topic and we got to watch a lot of movies and read interesting books! I hope to take another class with him.

I have a fear of public speaking so participating in group discussions can be hard for me. However, Professor Curtain was super understanding and give me great advices on how to slowly start participating more. The class is also super interesting so it made it easier for me to start participating. Definitely recommend this class to everyone!

I LOVE Tyler Curtain. In class we alternated between reading books and watching moves (we got to watch the Captain America trilogy!). So interesting, so funny, so caring. Would highly recommend this teacher!

I loved Professor Curtain. This class was all about horror and we just watched three movies a week and read three novels (that you didn't actually have to read). There is a midterm, a final and two short films. Literally just talk in class and you'll get an A. Tyler is such a great guy and super funny. Highly recommend any class with him.

Tyler is a really great person and teacher. You will not only talk about the genre of horror, but hold a discussion on a different movie each class. Just try and say something during the class period at least once and you will be in good position for the A. He took over a month to return our midterms to us, but it was ok because the tests were easy
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The grades were a midterm, a final, and creating two short films. He's a really great guy, guides the Socratic style class to question important topics. Most of the lecture time is analyzing the film as a class, discussing what worked and what didn't. Sometimes he brings cool prop duplicates from films. You may watch 2-3 films on your own per week.

Professor Curtain is absolutely incredible. He is a Socratic teacher, so how well you do in the class will be dependent on how much you participate in the class. The exams are very easy as long as you have participated and he just wants to see that you learned from the class, not that you can recite alot of facts and numbers. 10/10 would reccomend

Professor Curtain is an amazing and very knowledgable guy. The class was a lot of fun but we had to read a book(could be short story or a book like Dune) and watch a movie for classes every week. Fun discussions and no real essay-writing (he lets you rewrite them if you get <70). Final had us list all works read/watched and discuss general themes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Curtain is amazing! He's very intelligent and I can guarantee that he will challenge your way of thinking. For the class, all you need to do is read & watch the course material! The class is discussion based but don't be afraid, the class only gets better when everyone is involved. We had a paper and the final exam was pretty clear cut.

Professor Curtain had really profound insights in genre literature. You can explore the heavy social contexts of horror genre, together with its amazing charm. This is definitely a class that can give you something you cannot achieve outside this classroom. The class materials are very representative, and you can pass if you follow lectures well.

Mr. Curtain was an amazing professor and human being. He was one of my first professors coming into Carolina and made the transition much more bearable for me. This class is very interesting if you enjoy horror movies or film in general. It makes you think outside of the box, and Mr. Curtain highly values each student and their opinions.

A great guy, truly amazing. His class was Socratic, but he was always okay to just let you listen. If he knows you well, he'll call on you out of the blue, but just because he values your insight. Lots of reading, but really worth it; the discussion is mind-blowing most days. Hands down my favorite class. If you ever get a chance to take him, do.

Professor Curtain is a really great professor. He makes the seminar interesting, it's 99% discussion based and he directs the conversation in really interesting ways and is very responsive. He assigns a lot of readings/movies, I wouldn't recommend buying them because it would cost a lot and a majority of them you can find either online or in audio.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The class is more about group discussion, Tyler acts as a sort of mediator and explains context behind the movies that came out before our time. Interesting movies and discussions. From day 1 you're put in a group you'll have all semester to make various video projects. The final is a 5 min horror movie. Have fun!

Professor Curtain was awesome. He listened to what we had to say and added his own thoughts when necessary. The only downfall to this class was that I had $70 worth of novels we didn't even read. I'd buy the books he wants you to buy when he actually assigns the readings, if possible.

Professor Curtain is a great professor who truly cares about the classes he teaches. He uses a socratic style of teaching and really engages with discussion. He makes his students think, while also giving them the opportunity to voice their thoughts. I will say that the class I specifically took had a lot of novels and we did not read them all.

Tyler Curtain was probably the most respectable professor I have had at UNC so far.  He is a great lecturer which tons of knowledge!  Make sure to show up to class because participation does matter for a good grade.

Banned Books was the best class I took my freshmen year. Be sure to attend class, since it was almost entirely discussion based, and your level of participation determines your grade. I hope that I can fit another class with Professor Curtain into my schedule during my time at Carolina.

I respected Dr. Curtain as both a professor and a mentor. He is incredibly intelligent, kind, and pushes students to think in new and challenging ways all through a Socratic style teaching. Definitely try to get into one of his classes!
Finally a professor that cares more about what you learn and not about testing your memorization skills. This class was so much more than I ever thought it could be. AWESOME

Professor Curtain is one of my favorite professors at UNC. You don't get grades throughout the semester which is kind of annoying, but it really doesn't matter because if you participate & care you will be fine. He truly cares about you learning and I have never had a professor with so many examples on hand at all times. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this banned books first year seminar! The in class discussions were very thorough & I learned a lot of little things about English, politics, & history. My only complaint might be that we didn't get any grades throughout the semester, so I was unsure of how I was doing in the class. Would definitely recommend this class though!

Professor Curtain is fantastic. His banned books class was truly one of the most enticing courses I've taken at UNC. As long as you participate in class, you are almost guaranteed an A. I would highly recommend him for any FYS.

I took Sci Fi, Fantasy, and Utopia with Curtain and the class was GREAT! All we did was basically watch movies outside of class and a little bit of reading (we also had about 3 assignments for the whole semester that were papers) and all we had to basically do was show up to class and talk about the movie or reading. IT WAS SUPER EASY! TAKE IT!
You can tell he comes up with lectures on the drive to campus. Just sit near the front and participate a lot. easy A

this was a very chill class. he would assign us horror movies to watch and we would talk about it the next class. very interesting class discussions. tyler is the most intelligent and inspirational professors i have had at unc. i learned so much about the subject and what it means in the world and our everyday lives. highly recommended.

He values Interesting discussions and topics. There really is no structure to his class  it's a laid back and an easy going class to have in the middle of a rough schedule. We had no tests and only 2 papers, participation is HUGE.

If you like structure and organization, don't take Dr. Curtain. He is a knowledgeable, approachable and understanding man, but he was almost too nonchalant. If you want laid back and don't care about organization, you will probably get more out of the class than I could. Keep in mind that you might not ever know your progress until the end.

He was really smart and laid back, and values analytical thinking through discussions. He assigned almost no work and we didn't have tests, just a final project, which made it a very easy class as long as you participate.

I love Dr. Culbertson. He's frank, witty, philosophical, and a lot of fun to talk to. I'm a STEM major, and it made me genuinely sad when I realized I probably wouldn't be taking another class of his.
Goated teacher

Graham is v passionate & the BEST! I didn't know what to expect, but this quickly became my fav class. You read weekly, play board games in class, & write discussion posts. The final is playing a board game that u create. Graham truly cares ab his students & uses a low-pressure grading style that makes u rly want to put in effort. HIGHLY recommend

Great class that provides a broad history of action films in a low-stress environment. Daily film viewing + discussion posts, plus three papers. For all assignments, if you meet the word count, you get an 100. The short video lessons were really informative, and Culbertson gives good feedback on papers. Really fun class, definitely recommend.
took it online over the summer. he is so chill and gives great feedback. he also does contracts based grading which is super nice. you can tell he is passionate about film and i learned a lot!!

Professor Graham was an amazing teacher! We had different units which were all very unique. Definitely not a traditional teacher in his grading contract-- but his system of 100 or fail made it a lot less stressful and allowed us to explore the content more! Provides a worldly view and always opened the class up for group discussion! TAKE HIM!!

The easiest professor I've had at UNC! Doesn't believe in making students stress about grades, so you either get a 100 or a 70 on assignments/projects/papers, no in between! I believe everyone in my class ended with a 100% in the class. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!! Group final project was so fun, you literally played a video game. Love Graham!
I love Graham!
Graham is an extremely caring professor who runs a great learning environment. He encourages discussion and individual thinking. I would highly recommend for ENGL 113.

Graham is probably the best professor you could ask for if you're taking English 105. He uses contract grading, where an honest effort is essentially all you need to get an A on every assignment. Roundtable discussions take up pretty much the entire class period, but they're honestly very fun and thought-provoking. Very chill guy. TAKE IF YOU CAN!

This class was fun! We watched Star Wars and Asian cinema.  Class consisted of daily discussion posts, 2 short papers, and a final paper.  All essays were divided into chunks.  Class used specifications grading.  Just meet all the requirements for assignments and you'll get full credit.  Graham gave good feedback on papers too.

A good professor and I would recommend to any freshman taking 105 who wants to broaden their horizons. The class is EXTREMELY discussion heavy, not for you if you're shy. He has interesting perspectives but is maybe a little overly critical about a lot, and the class's scope can sometimes be too much. Contract grading is a big plus.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was interesting! We read different commencement addresses and other classice pieces. The class used contract grading. Complete all the work, and you get a B.  If you do very well on one of the major assignments, you can get a higher grade.  Dr. C grades very easy, so it is very easy to get an A. Dr. C is also kind and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you're not super passionate about video games for the love of everything do not take this class. Graham and his TAs were frustrating to listen to (made everything more complicated than it needed to be) and I was not a fan of the subject material. Still an easy a, but one that was excruciating for me to get through.

Overall I found this class to be pretty enjoyable and I love Graham as a professor. The class was a little too focused on philosophy rather than individual video games but Graham said he plans to fix this in the future. Overall a pretty easy general education class that I would highly recommend! The work isn't bad at all and recitations are fun.

Easy professor, nice guy. I found his overly cheery personality a bit grating, but most others seemed to enjoy him.Class was technically about video games but we talked way more about philosophy... Just be aware that it's all about the critical study of games and not so much about the individual games themselves, so it's not as fun as it sounds.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Graham is a great professor, anarchist, and a wonderful human overall. He let the class pick the units (after the first one) which made the required writing more enjoyable. Don't be afraid to ask for help, he'll tell you what you need to do to get the grade that you want. Long story short, Graham was always on time but Bus 7 was always late!
I have nothing to say except that Graham Culbertson is an incredible, chaotic, kind anarchist and that I recommend him to anyone taking ENGL 105.
If you're looking for a chaotic anarchist who cares a lot about his students and video games, you're in the right place. Trust me when I say I doubt there's a better English 105...

Graham is a very unconventional teacher and a self-declared anarchist, he has very interesting takes on things and challenged us to think deeply about topics that were not remotely related to our class. It's contract grading and you only produce two pieces of work, an essay and a podcast.
An unusual class, but it went really well. Readings are interesting, and the contract grading is different, though it works out.

In ENGL 105, he only makes you write 3 papers and 1 group podcast. He was very understanding and typically gave extensions when you asked. We had a decent amount of class discussions but they were not graded, so if you are shy you do not have to worry. Great class! Would recommend taking it with him!
I love discussions and we had many of them so I loved this class. I also felt that I learned a lot about life so just great professor.
He is super nice and grading is fair. I would definitely take one of his classes again!

He is really easy to work with.
As someone who is shy and doesnt really like to speak up/be put on the spot, I found this class quite fitting. 
You dont have to speak up if you dont want to.
Its contract graded as well.
So as long as you do the work by the deadline, you're guaranteed a B!

Graham is great! He uses contract grading for this class, so as long as you turn in your work on time and come to class, you're guaranteed a B. He makes sure to engage the class and leads lots of thoughtful discussions. There's only a handful of major assignments and he does allow some class time to work on them.

This class managed to be "easy" but also challenging/ mind-expanding. As long as you turn everything in you're guaranteed a B, but you will get a lot out of this class, because Graham inspires his students to do their best, and facilitates their growth as students/ people with thought provoking assignments.
He is a great guy, super friendly, super accessible, and overall super caring. Is very understandable if you're sick or stuff like that. Work is thought-provoking and very doable.

Graham was great! He uses contract grading but expected work to be completed and your best work. He gives great feedback on papers and plenty of in class time to work on individual and group assignments. I never felt rushed to complete anything and he was aware of our other responsibilities. I was challenged as a writer but learned so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Graham was a very caring professor throughout this semester. He is very laid back while also clearly caring about teaching and his students. This class wasn't stressful but was still engaging and Graham was accommodating whenever students were ill or could not attend class. I would recommend his as an English 105 professor.

Graham is so lovely! He's kind and caring and you can tell that he's passionate about teaching. He tries to make the class interesting for students and he would ask us for feedback. The class was broken up into 3 projects but he didn't traditionally grade them, as long as you attended classes and did your assignments on time you were promised a B.

I loved this professor! He was funny, highly interested in his subject (American Authors is what I took with him), and created great discussions without pressuring people to talk. His insights are great. If you're looking for a class just for fun or to fill a gen. ed., I highly recommend Graham.
Helpful guy with a real passion for his subject. Top Lad, would discuss sci-fi with.

Graham (that's what he likes to be called) is one of the most laid-back yet challenging professors I've had. He's engaging and funny, and is great at getting students to participate in discussions. He's a tough but fair grader and always gave helpful suggestions for improvement. For English 105 used contract grading. I would definitely recommend!
A great professor. The classroom discussions Graham leads make challenging material easier to understand. He also uses contract grading, which is another plus.

Great teacher for ENGL 105i Humanities. He used contract grading, so as long as you tried and did all of the assignments, you were guaranteed a B. He gave helpful feedback on papers and guided us in workshopping each others papers. In class, he led really interesting discussions, but also encouraged us to contribute our own thoughts and ideas.

Cuadros was an awesome professor! The class was very consistent in work, which was a good schedule to follow, but also not overwhelming in work. Cuadros is very considerate with extended help and is very open to questions. I really enjoyed this as a fun journalism course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Continually brought in bias in class, he was by no means impartial to anyone who went against his grain of thinking and you paid the price with a poor grade. It was either submit to his ideals, thinking or fail the class. No dissent, independent or critical thinking was allowed.
Truly one of the most caring professors I've had at UNC. An accessible, friendly, and genuinely good human.

As the other reviews goes, he does assign a story every week, usually around 600 words but he has a set limit! He is very helpful though and understanding because he wants you to succeed in the class. Would 10/10 take another class again with him.

Professor Cuadros is a gem in the J school, and if you aspire to be a journalist or reporter, you have to take a class with him. You have an article due every week but this class teaches you so much and Cuadros is super accommodating, caring & gives excellent feedback. He is a great person to know and he deeply cares about his students doing well.

An amazing, seasoned reporter with a love for teaching and developing his students' crafts. Tough work (one article a week, 3+ interviews, conducted remotely), but accomodating with people not getting back to you and granting extensions. Grading is based both on AP style and how he thinks it reads, so there can sometimes be "hidden traps."

Professor Cuadros is a real gem in the j-school. It's very clear he knows his stuff. He cares deeply for his students and was very flexible with turning in assignments amidst a global pandemic. His grading is a little inconsistent, but nothing concerning. I would absolutely take another class with him. Highly recommend!

Professor Cuadros is my absolute favorite professor at UNC. He is such a role model for anyone hoping to pursue journalism as a career. He is incredibly knowledgeable and you will learn a lot about good reporting from him. He expects a lot from students, but is very clear about what he wants and very understanding if things go wrong.
Paul Cuadros is a tough grader and expects you to turn in quality work, however, he is extremely caring and sees potential in all of his students.

JOMC 253 is a class where you write a report every week based on the beat you select at the beginning of the semester. Cuadros is really clear on what he wants, is nice and personable, and sympathetic when "life" happens. The class is a significant amount of work no matter who you take it with, but Cuadros made it enjoyable.

One of the best professors at UNC—this was my second class with Dr. Curtin, and I'd take a third! Lectures are engaging, and grading is fair if you put in the effort. The class focuses on understanding and thoughtful discussion over regurgitating forgettable facts. Highly recommend Gender & Sexuality and Bodies Under Capitalism (390 courses).

Dr. Curtin is the best. As someone who has never taken anything in Gender Studies, I am amazed by her teaching method, which makes this subject as engaging as possible. She is very approachable in her OHs and is always willing to share her thoughts for any concerns you might have. I really had a great time, so HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!

I've taken Gender and Sexuality and Fitness Culture with her. Her lectures are heavily discussion based, so as long as you read what's due, the class goes by relatively fast. She has the tendency to go off topic, but she's interested in listening to her students opinions. You have to do ten reading responses a few papers depending on the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class not only broadened my perspective but also challenged me and my peers to think critically about societal norms. Dr. Curtin is an exceptional professor who wants you to do well. She breaks down complex and abstract topics into simple, thought-provoking ideas. Her lectures are engaging and insightful—I would recommend any class with her.

very much discussion based class. Almost every class is just about talking about the readings which are not very hard + interesting. you only have to make a discussion post for 10 readings. One easy essay writing about art from the museum and a group project making a documentary about a revolution. Participation is graded and discusson can b boring
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable- all readings are on canvas or accessible through UNC. Gender, sexuality, and health is lecture based with student led discussions some weeks. attendance required but 2 absences no questions asked allowed. HIGHLY recommend to any med anth major/minor or anyone interested in the topic!

Climate Change and Health was an incredible class and while topics can be quite heavy, they are relevant and easily applicable to life outside university. Dr. Curtin is very approachable and her knowledge of various fields makes her a great lecturer. 390 is heavily based around discussion. Do the reading + participate and you'll do well.

I cannot recommend professor Curtin enough! I took anth of fitness culture with her and it was so fun! lectures are discussion based and very entertaining. You complete a research project of your choosing during the semester, and the workload is split up well throughout the semester. she is very supportive and wants you to succeed.

Dr. Curtin is so easy to talk to during class and office hours. She is slow to grade things, but most of the assignments are really straightforward, easy, and completion. Those that are not are not worth a huge percentage of the grade

Dr. Curtin is definitely a favorite of mine at UNC. Her classes are only conversational, so participation is important, but the conversations are pretty fun! There isn't too much homework, just readings and occasional papers. There's only 5 reading responses for the entire semester and two papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's the best. My favorite professor this semester!

Cyrus was an amazing teacher. Unfortunately it looks like he won't be back next semester but he made the class so engaging and enjoyable. Everyone I talked to also loved the course. If you ever have an opportunity to take a class with him do it!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Quite literally the goat. Super interesting class, and very chill.
Sweetest guy ever, and a ridiculously easy class. Think I will get a 102 as my final grade. Take it
so chill, hes the goat,

Cyrus is absolutely the best professor I've ever had! He cares so much about his students and it's clear that he truly loves what he does. I especially like how he takes the time to get to know students and goes above and beyond to make the course relevant and interesting for everyone. Additionally, if you pay attention in class, you'll do well!
Easy class, take it if you need the credit

Nicest professor ever. Cares so much about his students and their success and is very passionate about the topics he teaches. Not a lot of work assigned, 1 assignment and reading reflection per week and only 1 midterm and final which you can use a one pager on each. Would recommend him to anyone. Take his class!!

Cyrus is the absolute goat. He is willing to work with you on extensions, late work, anything you need. the man would probably donate a kidney if I needed a transplant. homework is extremely light since my class voted to move half the assignments to be optional. extremely easy tests: 1-pagers allowed, hard questions dropped, you can get points back
I haven't finished the class yet, but i dont need to. It was that easy. I already got an A+ and its September.
Made the class as easy as possible. Never studied a single bit, too bad he's leaving

Cyrus's lectures were easy to understand and very informative. Expectations for exams were clear and grading was pretty straightforward. He allows one-pagers on exams and as long as you pay attention to lectures/participate in the class activities you'll get a good grade. Class activities were helpful in understanding the course material.

Cyrus is an awesome professor. He is very knowledgeable and has many anecdotes and stories from his past experiences that make the class engaging. Very accommodating and understanding if you communicate with him about any questions or need help. I learned a lot from this class. We did focus more on sub-Saharan Africa than on other regions, though.
Very respectable and understanding professor. Very clear expectations if you want to succeed in this course. Would highly recommend IMO. Interesting material too.

Professor Current clearly cares about her students but the way this class was run confused me. I think it's supposed to be discussion based, but not much discussion ever happened. Also, she would often ask questions that were either way to specific or way to vague and it always seemed that she had a specific answer in mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very relaxing class if you are comfortable participating. Readings can be overwhelming (~50 pages per class), but they are very worthwhile. Essays were not given any criteria or rubrics, but were graded fairly as long as you put in a good effort. Also, she sometimes gave pop quizzes/reading responses, so come to class prepared every time.

Dr. Current is super nice and the class is not too hard if you're doing the readings. Class participation is super important, but if you have anxiety about public speaking you can talk to them because they're very understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Current always gave me good feedback on my writing, and I believe I improved as a writer by taking this course. I never had any problems with her but some of my classmates, from what I've heard, would disagree. A lot of class time is spent listening to her explain assignments, but sometimes we would get off topic. Overall, pretty good class.

I appreciated their personal care for each student- immediately remembered our names and passions, will even go out of her way to email articles she feels will benefit you in their class or future profession. Make sure to call her Dr. Current, not Mrs!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took the class online during the summer, and she was delightful. She gives you a 100 as long as you follow the rubric and apply previous criticisms.

Worst professor I have had in all my time at UNC. Beyond unorganized, fails to lay out clear and succinct expectations for assignments and grades like you are supposed to know exactly what she wants when she doesn't tell you. Doesn't bother updating assignment information from previous semesters. Avoid! Find a professor who has their act together.
Very unorganized and confusing system of giving assignments and describing student tasks/responsibilities. Never specified exactly what she wanted and then left negative comments on all assignments.

She is very lecture heavy, and a pretty tough grader. She kinda purposively makes sure your papers are below 88% so you have to do revisions, but I was able to bring my grade up to an A after them. I thought the books very interesting to read. However, as much as I enjoyed her, this is not a class to take as a GPA booster.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Current is a great professor. If you take this class you will definitely improve as a writer. They are really caring and guide you through the assignments. Also if you get a bad grade on something she lets you resubmit for a total new grade. Everyone rating them a 3 or lower probably just didn't put in the effort.

I was personally not a fan of the very lecture heavy classes. Professor Current frequently spent a lot of class giving her personal analysis. While this was valuable, I would have preferred more open discussion with other students and developing our own analyses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Current is very passionate about what she teaches. If you are looking to improve your scientific writing, take her class. If you want an easy A in engl 105I, take one of the classes taught by grad students. Dr. Current is very kind and cares about her students, she just sometimes goes on tangents for entire class periods.

I thought Dr. Current was very passionate on what she taught and how the course material was intertwined. I wish the final exam was not as big a part of our grade considering we also had a final paper. I particularly enjoyed the discussions that were had each day about what we read as they challenged me to think more critically.

Dr Current cares abt the material, but the classroom discussions tend to be rly repetitive (asking what we thought of a book/chapter, and writing down bullet points). It's a lot of reading and there isn't much instruction given on papers (each of which were 8-10 pages) and the final. You can do revisions on the midterm paper which is nice
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Current is at best an arbitrary grader. Her syllabus has a specification stating if a student gets under an 88 on the midterm they can do revisions for a regrade, but it seems she will go out of her way to nitpick so a student is below that point. Be ready to read and basically go to a book club as a class. Can't tell you one thing I learned.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She was an amazing teacher.

Taking ENGL105 over the summer before college was the best thing ever. Dr. Current gives examples of what work should look like and posts rubrics for assignments so expectations for earning A's are clear. She is always willing to read over your work before you submit it, too, so you know what she thinks before she ever grades it. Just do the work!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Current's class was incredible. I strongly recommend ENGL105i to anyone planning on a medicine/research career. I learned how to read research and understand it well even if the words were big. Plus, we got an in depth lesson on how to make an academic research poster which is super great. Office hours are super helpful so be sure to attend.

I loved Dr. Current! She's fun and kind and great to talk to outside of class. She will give feedback that may sound harsh, but it's all to help you get better. She also allows resubmissions if you get a bad grade. You get out what you put into her class, and if you plan on going into medicine, she gives a great introduction to medical writing.
Super sweet and caring, and gave me an extra opportunity to revise one of my papers, but also a bit tough if you don't REALLY try.

Dr. Current is spectacular and I can  say with confidence to disregard any harsh reviews pertaining to them. She is very caring and forgiving, offering extensions and full revisions for the midterm paper should you get an unsatisfying grade (my grade for that paper went up from a low B- to an A+). The readings are interesting, too. Take them! :)

Dr. Current without a doubt deserves her 5/5 rating. She is an incredible professor who deeply cares about her students. She will give you precise feedback in a timely manner and opportunities to improve your work. Her 105i class genuinely prepares you to read and write works in health and medicine.

Very interesting class, but I admit it was harder than I was expecting it to be and required a decent amount of work. Dr. Current is very nice and knows a lot about the material. I learned a lot, but it was a ton of reading. I would take her again though!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Probably the most overrated professor in the English department. She cannot lecture anything to save her life. Lecture is always all over the place and does not have a firm grasp on the structure of the class. Her grading scale is awful and has never been fair and logical. Avoid her class in general.
Absolutely the best professor I have had!! Great at giving feedback and explaining exactly what needs to be done. I like the project based system over written exams.

I loved Dr. Current! She was very clear about her expectations and very accessible outside of class. You can tell that she genuinely cares about the well-being of her students. Dr. Current gives you a lot of autonomy in what topics you choose to write about in her class, which definitely makes a difference. I will say she is a tough grader!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I fully recommend taking ENGL 105 with Professor Current. I had it online over the summer and was abroad for half of it but Professor Current was very accommodating and understanding. If you make an effort and communicate with her you will do well in this class, truss.

I really enjoyed this class! Dr. Current was very passionate about literature and it shined through in their lectures and classes. I definitely recommend taking this class to anyone who enjoys reading or who wants to explore analyzing new genres!

Not a lot of reading compared to other English classes, and most of your grade comes from two papers. Dr. Current is a tough grader, but she gives great feedback on papers, and there is an option to rewrite one for a higher grade. I loved this class, but stay clear if you're looking for a gpa booster!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Current was great for the medicine Engl105i. We had 3 large unit projects and a few feeders that did require a lot of thought but she was always there if I had any questions. She helped me with topic selection and gave me ideas on what I should focus on. She is very intelligent and caring and offers equal opportunity to everyone in her class!

The ENGL105i class that Dr. Current teaches was one of the best classes I have taken at UNC. If you are considering a health profession, this class is incredibly valuable to you. Classes are often held online or asynchronous to work on projects, and she is super reachable if you need help. Take this class if you are able to.
Professor Current clearly shows how fervent she is in the research field for the health sciences. The research skills she teaches are all utilitarian and invaluable for any STEM major in my opinion.

Independent research course structured to take you thru 4 modes of sci communication: literature review, academic poster, podcast, + project proposal. Definitely learned a lot. Lectures always flesh out exactly what she expects from our projects. Her feedback is excellent and has definitely helped me become a better writer. Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Love Dr Current! I took writing in health and medicine. She's very caring and nice and her class is very manageable, but you still learn a lot.
they are very nice but really harsh when it comes to participation and attendance. Does not care if you had strep, were in ER, nothing

I took her summer session course and really enjoyed it. Dr. Current really pushes you to think deeply about the text. She is a really fair grader, offers feedback on papers, and lists out clear grading criteria. Writing papers for her aren't stressful as long as you reference her Hints for Writing guide.

I took this class simply as a GPA booster. If this is you, do NOT take this class. The content and materials were interesting, however who has enough time to prioritize reading 6 novels throughout the semester on top of the major papers she has us write. Unless you're an ENGL major/minor, this class was way more work then it was worth.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She clearly outlines what you're getting into, and the expectations/workload for this class are quite reasonable. She's always willing to help out if you're stuck, and makes 105I a very informative and fairly stress-free class.

I loved Dr. Current's class. You can tell she cares about her students and wants to make them better writers. She gave an original grade on papers and then provided feedback and an opportunity to edit your submission and raise your grade. She requires a lot of preparation for papers, but teaches her students how to approach and write great papers.

Take 105 with a different professor. I cannot stress enough how passive aggressive and awful Dr. Current is. She will send you nasty emails ridiculing you if you miss a class or an assignment. She was non-understanding and rude even when I was mentally struggling and when I had COVID. She also rants about her opinions often instead of teaching.

Arbitrary grader. It is clear from her condescending emails/feedback that she thinks extremely highly of herself. She spends most of class on a rant about something random. She is very serious about attendance/doesn't regularly offer zoom. She does give extensions if needed. No one got less than a B, but ENGL 105 is supposed to be an easy A.

Professor Current is lovely in and out of class. Her class did not require a ton of work aside from readings. She loves to hang out after class and talk further about the readings. I've never had a professor so invested in the well-being of their students. She's accessible, easy to talk to, and so passionate about the narratives she teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Current for ENGL105 during Summer Enrollment. I LOVED this class! Dr. Current gives clear expectations of each assignment, offers examples of the expectations, and provides so much feedback. We can pick whatever topic that matches our interests for our assignments. She is extremely encouraging and wants everyone in the class to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super nice and chill. Just wants what is best for students. The books were interesting and I enjoyed class most of the time. Forums are slight if you just meet word count and make an argument. Two papers are hard to get an A+ on but also hard to get below a mid B on.

Dr. Current was fantastic! I learned a lot from her, even though I wasn't a huge fan of the ENGL 105 curriculum. She really made us work for the class, but gave great feedback and was a great help in learning writing styles we'll need to know. I hope I can take a class with her again, because she's truly passionate about writing and teaching!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof. Current is very nice and it is clear she loves talking about literature. However, she loves to go on rambles and keep talking about her personal life. Workload is not too bad for an English course, just 2 papers, reading, and forum posts. Her essay grading style is not very clear... its either her way (and her "course policy) or the highway

Professor Current really cares about her students, especially during the pandemic, which she makes clear. For ENGL105i, she made it very structured with semester-long projects/topics we can put on our resumes. This class was very helpful for future STEM classes and careers. She is a clear grader, but sometimes the lectures felt unnecessary.

Professor Current made online class enjoyable. She is super helpful and is passionate about helping you grow as a student. Her class was set up discussion style, which I really enjoyed. You definitely should read all of the books in order to participate in class. 10/10 awesome teacher and so kind, would recommend (also go to office hours)!

Took ENGL146 in COVID times: Dr. Current was a great professor. Her passion for the material shows and she can help students deeply understand key points of the texts. Prepare for plenty of reading, though most of it is pretty interesting. Theres a text for everyone in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: COVID edition: Responsive in/out of class, "by the book" but understanding, excellent feedback, knowledgeable, assigns many written assignments, but the workshops and feedback make it worth it and not that difficult as long as you don't procrastinate, I developed and enjoyed myself most in this class out of my whole COVID semester.

Dr. Current was the best English professor Ive ever had. She also cares deeply about her students. ENGL 105i is a tough course but she helped each and every student succeed. I have turned into such a better writer myself thanks to Dr. Currents guidance. If you show her youve improved by the end of the class, youre bound to get an A.

Dr. Current is extremely nice and clearly cares about her students. She makes sure that first year students are ready for their career at UNC. ENGL 105 is a writing-intensive class, so there will be a lot of papers to write, but they're pretty interesting if you pick the right topic. She's great!
Dr. Current is so intelligent and she'll push you to expand your analytical skills beyond belief. It's not easy, but it's worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Current is a great professor and I would love to have class with her again. ENG 123 is discussion-based and students should be prepared to speak up. The books we read are interesting. We have 2 papers and do forum posts- papers can be challenging but we learn a lot in the process. Dr. Current is so intelligent and kind!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Only hw is reading books and some writing. You can get by with reading summaries online, but if you do that, pay attention in class for final. Class is pretty easy, she doesn't grade terribly hard on essays, and is pretty forgiving if she sees effort. Workload: 2 big essays (can revise/rewrite one) and 1 paragraph response each week based on novel.

Her class is sooo much harder than normal ENGL 105 classes. She really makes you work for it but your writing will likely improve. If you want an easy A, choose a different professor. Good feedback but no rubric so impossible to know where she gets the numbers from Also talks a lot about random things
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She gives good feedback on our papers but she has no rubric so it can be frustrating to try and understand why you got the exact grade you did. She goes off on tangents fairly often and class time isn't terribly productive but the writing assignments are useful enough and your writing will likely improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Current is an excellent english 105i teacher. She gives very detailed feedback and really cares about her students. She grades in a timely manner, and really wants to see her students improve and succeed. She does not give busy work, and explains the reasoning behind every assignment.
She can seem tough at first, but she really does care about her students. She is a truly kind person and always provided insightful feedback to help you improve your writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Wonderful personality. Her grading can be a little jarring at first, but it really does improve your writing coming into college. Tough, but not overly so. Tries to make the best use out of this class without either being too strict or blowing it off completely.

Dr. Current is a great teacher and will help improve anyone's writing no matter what level you start off at. She even took time to talk with us one on one for each of the three major papers in the class. Although this is not Dr. Current's fault, the UNC curriculum for ENGL 105 leans to the left politically, which moderates may find unpleasing.

Get ready to do completely unnecessary work for the class! We had to do the most ridiculous assignments (make a webpage about events that had absolutely nothing to do with what we were working on). Be prepared to listen to her as she talks about absolutely nothing of importance for the entire class time because she loves to hear her own voice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: For how terribly organized English 105i in general, Dr. Current did a very good job. She cared so much about her students and still remembers my name when I see her around campus. We had a lot more freedom in our topics and the class was easy to pass if you did the work.

Dr. Current really cares about the material she teaches and the students in her class. We read 8 books during the semester, but she makes it manageable. If you reading or do not want to show up to class, do not take this class. Otherwise, I would recommend it to someone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Current genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed. The class consists of a handful of assignments, most of which are pretty time consuming. However, they really help you explore potential research areas and introduce you to a career in science.

I can not stress enough how caring she is. Draft workshops are really nice and she has mandatory office hours during each unit so you get 2 days of no class but get to meet with her individually and it is actually super helpful. If you like medicine/science this class will be interesting enough that you won't notice how much work it is
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Current is a really good professor. My writing skills were weak going into her class, but they definitely improved due to the amount of papers and tough feedback that she gave. I appreciate the difficulty of her class and the way that my skills improved, however this class is not an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Took this class my first semester of college, she was so mean that I immediately regretted it. She disrespected me and other students in front of everyone. Doesn't even teach class, talks about random stuff for an hour then does class for fifteen minutes but you're still responsible for the material. Don't take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable and thorough professor who really cares about improving her students as writers. Grading can be a bit tough, but you'll end up getting the grade you deserve if you really work on revising your drafts. Don't take this class just to get the requirement out of the way, but to really develop your skills and knowledge on chosen topic
Amazing professor. Knowledgeable and understanding, I love her class. She made me a better writer. Hard to reach during office hours, you'll have to make an appointment.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Highly recommend her for the 105 requirement. She's reasonable in her expectations and genuinely cares about her students. Take the time to go to her office hours, and if they interfere with your schedule she will work with you to meet. She's a great professor and a wonderful human!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Took Dr. Current for intro to fiction. She talks a lot in class but picks interesting books. Essays aren't too difficult and she provides feedback and the chance for a rewrite. Office hours were very helpful. Would take her again without a doubt.

I love Dr. Current. She's professional and really knows her stuff. I've taken multiple  classes with her. She really cares about you if you respect her and put in some effort. Don't take a class with her if you won't be able to dedicate a decent amount of time to it.

Dr. Current's class was almost unnecessarily difficult. She seemed like a nice person but she was very narrow-minded with how she wanted things to be written. When reading through comments on my papers, it felt as if she was marking them simply to have marked them. She rambles in lectures and is very hard on attendance. I don't recommend her class.

I really enjoyed this class. You have to schedule office hour time. The first two units require a lot of work, but are informative for those interested in health science. The last science fiction unit, however, was completely irrelevant. This class requires a lot of writing, but if you have a good foundation it'll be an easy A.

Loved this class. I was almost always behind in the reading so I didn't participate in discussion as much as I would have liked but Professor Current is one of the coolest professors I've ever had. Tons of respect for her.

Easy and fun. There is reading, but the books are actually interesting/entertaining. Try not to get too behind on reading, because it can be difficult to catch up. You can miss 3 classes, before it hurts you. Current is awesome! She encourages open discussion about many of the tough issues brought up in the books you'll read. Loved it!

Prof. Current is a great teacher and very accessible and helpful. She doesn't ask for much in terms of homework and you can pretty much BS your way around this class and get an A, if you really want to. She's a great teacher, very much interested in what she teachers and instills that interest in her students. She tries to help as much as possible.
Most helpful teacher I ever had. She was extremely helpful during office hours and shows real care for her students. But she is a tough grader and strictly adheres to attendance.

Very helpful and open to different viewpoints (she's liberal, I'm conservative, we're friends). Really wants to get to know her students. Gives fair grades and expects people to improve and participate. Lectures can ramble a bit, but it's not too bad. Lots of emphasis on the actual writing. Expectations are clear.

Current is really passionate about her teaching. She taught a variety of works in the class, from short stories to novels to movies. Class discussion was encouraged and was easy to follow. Assignments were hard and Current was very helpful with essays. She even had an option extra credit assignments for kids who wanted to improve in their writing.

Do not take a class with Professor Radding. She expects far more prior knowledge than should be expected of a 200-level requirement. The course is lecture heavy but with no slides, she pretty much just reads facts of a paper. She is not communicative with students and does not understand technology at all. Don't take it!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took Introduction to Mexico but I really should have read the ratings first. She can't lecture for anything. She reads off of a paper the whole time, and her PPTs are so text-heavy yet contain separate info than what she's lecturing on. Papers every week. This is not an "introduction"--it is from before the Mayans to 2021, and we sped 100%
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Do yourself a favor and dont take any course with Radding!! She reads off of her lecture notes and is rude to you outside of class if you dont understand something! Seems easy on paper but extremely inflexible and harsh grader. Had to work to get a B despite getting A+ on tests!! Youve been warned...
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Biggest regret was taking this class. Lecture was boring and she doesnt excuse absences. A LOT of writing and assigned more papers at the last minute. Grading criteria wasnt clear and no one got full marks on a paper. Midterm was fine but you could get high As on the midterm/final and STILL get a C in the course. Avoid at all cost
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do no take Radding!!!! I regret taking this class with her soooo much. Definitely not worth it. All she does is read off a piece of paper the entire class. Extremely boring... She also added essays to the syllabus, but would not tell us until 5 days before they were due and you would have to read a ton for it
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Her lectures are super hard to follow she usually just talks without stopping and has powerpoints with like 4 words per slide so if you dont get it when she says it, you will not get it ever. The good thing is that she gives you everything that's going to be on the test so if you study it you can get a solid grade. She is a very sweet lady
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Every class for the entire class, she is talking at us, many times reading directly from a paper she had wrote on the topic in preparation for the class. Thankful for the powerpoint. The lectures were extremely boring. I learned more from doing the readings than from going to class. I would not take this professor again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very very boring class. The material is extremely interesting but the lectures are very dry and just not fun to go to. They are mandatory and the recitation section is better but still like pulling teeth. The exams are in a nice format and if you study you will do well. Do not know if it is worth it though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Required course for LTAM majors. Most of the class agree seems she just leaves us to teach. Discussion based on reading, be sure to give specific examples from text ( what was said on page __, etc). Only grades are attendance/participation, group project, & 20 page final. Very tough grader & dry. Uncomfortable silences. But is for student success.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is a good class if you show up most of the time and take notes. You can download the power points and use them to study along with the study guides that she gives for the midterm and final, which are not too hard and graded very fairly. She wants you to do well and isvery flexible, even let me re-take the midterm so I could get a better grade.

Lectures are long and read from papers she holds during class, it's as if she's reading prose to the class. Not sure what it is about this method, but it makes the lectures dry despite being on interesting material. I've asked for help once from a TA and he was extremely responsive. An extra-credit paper was offered for this section, not everytime

This class was very dry, the lectures were boring, and the readings were long. That being said, Professor Radding really wants her students to succeed. Getting an A or B in this class is not out of the question if you are willing to go to office hours.
No Comments

Horrible professor--stay far away.  Has no idea how to teach undergraduates or how to use powerpoint in a lecture.  She tries to be friendly but actually has a very alpha-type, bulldog-ish, unapproachable personality that makes her defensive and even hostile.  I cannot imagine why UNC hired her.
Radding's class is sooooo boring!!!  I had her for a 3-hr seminar and the whole class was bored to tears.  Way to make a seminar full of bright students seem extremely dull.  DON'T TAKE HER CLASS!

She changed the course from what it used to be, now with more weight on tests instead of building the actual compiler (assignments). Her lectures are super boring and her slides are poorly written and will sometimes contain wrong information for something that will be on an exam. Assignments are very unbalanced, unclear and don't guide you at all.

I took this class in 2024 and loved it. The labs are tricky, but manageable with OH. The professor is very engaging in lectures and super passionate about security. I loved to learn from her! This class is on a uni-level standard. Definitely challenging, but in the best way possible. Don't let other reviewers fool you, take this class!

Sturton's 590 (formal methods for security) is a great research-focused CS elective. No programming; homework is reading research papers. Grades are from ~10 very doable quizzes and a group research project. She takes a while to grade but is exceptionally kind and helpful in OH. Recommend if you liked COMP 455 or prefer discussion-based classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 0 detail of slides. Practice tests? Oh u mean polleverywhere, yes pollev questions r highly related to tests, do that. Labs are busy work with screenshot, I hope they can come up with some actual original up-to-date labs that teach u stuff. Exam grading is like Teemo, annoying, u would get points off for somethign stoopid. Professor is chill, tho.
I really liked this course and I thought she was very kind and knowledgeable. One thing though is that there is a LOT of material for the exams. Other than that, solid course.

Please do not take this class with her. Every time I step into this class, I fear something terrible might happen. Her lecture slides have less detailing and poor formatting, and it's a matter of whether you know the content or not. The labs are sometimes lengthy; only OH can save you on that. Other than that, please refrain yourself from this.

Great crash course for cybersecurity! Professor Sturton is a caring professor who you can tell loves to teach the material. If you attend class, take notes, and read the textbook you will be okay! Labs were not really a stretch from the material, but did require outside research at times. 5 FREE late days given for the labs & drops lowest lab!

A good lecturer. Interesting class. But lectures arent recorded, and I could not remember information from class, so I dropped in fear of knowing that I cant do well on the exam if I cant remember infromation from class. Slides arent that detailed either.

The most boring and useless class I have ever taken. The professor has a terrible lecture format with slides that contain very little information by themselves. It's not even that hard a class, the professor was just so atrocious I didn't want to do the work and wasn't interested. It's a shame, because I though computer security would be cool.
Would avoid classes with her. Content is interesting however her teaching style effects the experience negatively.
it's the way i'm feeling i just can't deny. you need to remember a lot of useless information for the exam.

Cynthia seems like a nice person but is a terrible prof. The way she ran this class was disrespectful and unacceptable imo. She wouldn't accept any late work but would routinely release lecture videos and grades late. The labs (40% of grade) were also such a stretch from the class content and were the bane of my existence. Do not take this class :(
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: OK lecture and assignments but bad logistics. We had to wait so looooong before we received any feedbacks on our midterms, labs, and finals. The prof posted the course grade 10 days after the deadline set by the school policy. I was graduating this semester and seeing an NR on my CC was not a good experience at all!

I actually found the material to be really cool which is the only reason I didnt loathe the class. One time I went to OH for **conceptual** help (literally asking to clarify something in lecture) and an LA told me he couldnt help me bc Cynthia doesnt let us ??? That being said, Sturton is a genius and nice person even if a bad prof.

Smart in the subject, but incompetent as a professor. She did not communicate well with students, did not accept late work but gave us assignments late, took months to grade, and the labs had nothing to do with what she learned in class. She was lazy to the core, and this class was a waste of time and money.

This class is not hard but for some reason she likes to grade it like it is. Flipped lecture was fine and same with pollev questions. I don't think two midterms + final project + final (an essay) was necessary though. A lot of unneeded work for a class that lacks substance. Tries to cover too much, so topics lack any real world application.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For the LOG, if you value your grade or mental health do not take this class. Everything about this class is incredibly frustrating. Every time I show up to class I want to stick a screwdriver through my ear and swirl it around. The class isn't too bad, but everything is graded randomly and after 2 months.

Definitely not the hardest CS class I've taken. I think Dr. Sturton is the most engaging lecturer I've had in the comp department (by far) but there are definitely improvements that can be made. I don't think anyone is a fan of the flipped classroom and labs are challenging and time consuming but manageable once you get used to them.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Horrible labs, does not allow student collaboration, not accessible, flipped classroom with lectures uploaded midnight the day of. All around smart person, but dismal teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Idk what happened to this class but it is absolutely terrible. Irrelevant, harshly graded, and very difficult lab assignments. Everything in this class is graded insanely, including something as small as a project outline. Sturton is disorganized. Seriously don't take this class. My grade is sitting around a B and I've put way too much work in.

This review is more about the class than Sturton personally. Idk what happened to this class but it's not as easy as people previously said. Labs are insane and you get little to no guidance. There's a problem when around half the class begs for an extension and gets no response. Test 1 average was around a high 70. Lab 1 average was less than 80.

This is the worst COMP Class I have taken to date. Lectures are irrelevant to the LABS and there is little direction and guidance given. LABS are released late and then she doesn't accept late work. The reverse classroom is lazy teaching, Youtube teaches better than this professor. Be prepared to pay the school to teach yourself in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: New labs are extremely difficult, time-consuming and the lectures are not very helpful. Sturton is not accommodating: when 50 people requested extension on a lab it wasn't provided. Mandatory videos, which are 40-80 mins long, are uploaded late in evening and you need to know the material for the quiz next morning. This is very bad class, avoid it
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: the material was taught *exclusively* on the blackboard for a class of 200+ students. no resources were available (no lecture notes, no slides, no reading guide, no study materials for exams, etc.). the assignments were piss easy, but werent related to the course. she literally stopped showing up after the midterm (which took 1.5 months to grade)

Unclear schedule and poor turnaround on grading (our sole midterm took 1.5 months to be graded). No accompanying lectures slides, would often designate lectures to other people such as her TAs. High grade cutoffs (A was cutoff at 94.5). Tests were the first time many concepts were applied.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Didn't learn much from this class, the professor doesn't give out any study guides or show much intent to teach. It's not hard to do well in her cybersecurity class but it's boring and lacks structure.

Decent course, lectures and HW could have dived a bit deeper though. This is NOT the course you should take if you want to get into security, its basically a conceptual primer. Not a bad prof but could tell the course suffered from the growing pains of too many students and needed to scale assignments for ease of grading. Exams  fair; HW  easy

The tags rmp provides isn't enough to describe how bad this class is. When you take the exam it's like a hit or miss on each question because it's your first time applying the info. The professor just gives you definitions, no study material, no assignments related to the class. If your looking into a cs elective this isn't the one

Horrible professor. Half-assed this class, doesn't provide any materials at all. Assignments, though easy, provide no learning material whatsoever and are barely related to the class. Would have preferred a more challenging class that actually provides learning.

No lecture slides or study material provided. Large amount of concepts taught in class with no resource to check what will be on exams. Hardly any practice problems ever done in class so exams are first application of many concepts. Had guest lectures after midterm and she barely showed up to class. HWs are easy but class organization is terrible
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The concepts that this class covers aren't difficult in itself but the professor gives you absolutely nothing to study with. Assignments are irrelevant to the test and worst of all you are forced to take hand written notes as she does lectures on the whiteboard. She writes so fast and unclear you cant even get the info you need to learn. Take 535
She is so unprepared for everything and grades harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Schauer is not an effective lecturer. Your TAs are your best resource for information. Recitations for this class consist of students working on other classwork or websurfing while Schauer talks in circles. There are poll everywhere questions every lecture, otherwise everyone would skip. Students and TAs alike think she is very disorganized.

The first two weeks a class she spent the whole class period trying to figure out how the projector worked, no lie. Bad at explaining things, textbook is useless, other than the useless textbook assigned questions, no other study material is provided. Clicker questions are nothing like the test. Practice exam is way shorter than the real exam.
Poor at explaining concepts and often tongue-tied. Book is not helpful. Tests are too long for the allotted time. Generally bad class.

Worst teacher I've taken in the chem department. Awful, point blank. Takes forever on the easy concepts and can't explain the more difficult ones. Tests are stupid and it's often unclear what the question is asking. Very unfortunate that they don't find a replacement for her.

She explains material in a nice simple holistic fashion in class, but then expects you memorize every single diagram and obscure calculation she ever mentioned for the test. The tests are too long, and though curved they are just too hard compared to the rest of the course material.

I really think that Dr. Schauer is a smart woman, but she just has trouble explaining what's going on in her head. She gets tongue-twisted easily and ends up circling everything on the notes, so you really don't know what's important. Tests are too long for the time allotted. Her accent can be pretty amusing - she pronounces anions "EAN-iens."

She is hard to understand. Reviews here are accurate: material seems easy, but isn't. And she sucks at explaining it. If you can't teach yourself in this class, you are screwed. Online quizzes are extremely rough as well.
