The information seems easy, but you really do need to study all the information. The test are LONG and just barely enough time to finish them. The book was NOT helpful at all, all notes.
No Comments
Junior Transfer Seminar is a pretty easy A. There is a presentation and 10 page paper at the end of the semester, but it really is not difficult. She is easy to get in contact with and REALLY nice.
Cynthia is a wonderful professor. I took her junior transfer seminar course and enjoyed it.
Amazing person.

Among the best teachers I've had. Her style is remarkable. She's able to efficiently guide discussions, keep students interested, and she is clear in her instruction and expectations. She tests and grades fairly as well. I highly recommend her.

She is amazing. By far the very best teacher I have ever had. He style of teaching is remarkable. She's clear in everything she says, upbeat, funny, and motivating. Inclusive of all students. Just the absolute best. I highly recommend her.
Great teacher, lots of readings to do though

Overall a good professor, however theres a lot of readings and participation is necessary. We talked about topics that were kind of controversial and she would sometimes challenge peoples ideas if they were different from her own which lowkey made me very uncomfortable.

Dr. Riger is a very intelligent and authentic professor, I recommend any of her courses. You will be required to do a lot of reading and participating, but I personally think learning is facilitated well in this course.

One of my favorite professors I have taken a class with. She is not only so funny and caring, but so knowledgable. Best teacher ever. Lectures are so fun and she is such a funny person.
Overall just a nice human who is very knowledgeable
Great overall! Lots of extra credit and overall really clear lessons, guidelines, and expectations.

Dr. Riger's lectures were very clear and easy to understand. She was also extremely kind and understanding when you had a question. The assignments weren't too much and the grace periods were life-savers. Also plenty of opportunities for extra credit.
Awesome professor! She is extremely knowledgeable and truly cares for her students and their ability to succeed. There is two exams but both online and then one in person final exam! Overall amazing!

It's clear that Dr. Riger really cares about each and every one of her students. Dana is by far my favorite professor I've had at UNC for the past three years. She is extremely intelligent and cares about her students. If you can take one of her classes I highly encourage it! She gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit and makes lectures fun and engaging.

Professor Riger is great!!! I loved this course. Class was very interesting and the workload was manageable. She offers extra credit at the end of her course and was very accessible. Attendance is mandatory.

Riger is such a great professor. She makes lectures interesting and engaging, and will genuinely make you laugh. She cares about all of her students. Provides clear expectations of the class and will have you fully prepared for any exams. She is awesome!!

This class was by far my favorite class I have taken so far at UNC. Dana was the coolest, most understanding, and passionate professor I have had and this class was super interesting. Professor Riger is super approachable. She tries to make the lectures as engaging as possible during Zoom meetings. Not a rigorous course and doesn't have a heavy workload. Riger is AMAZING!! She is so understanding and genuinely cares about her students. Great at explaining material and v engaging in class even on zoom. EDUC181 is super easy but still interesting and the workload is v manageable. The 3 main assignments throughout the semester can be fun if u care. 1000% would recommend her and the class.

Prof Riger is Amazing!! I only took this class for the education credit, but it taught me so much about myself and culture surrounding sexuality/identity. I LOVED PROFESSOR RIGER! She is by far my favorite professor I have had at UNC thus far and EDUC375 has been my favorite class! Never wanted to miss a class. Professor Riger is AWESOME! I took her EDUC181 class at UNC and loved her enthusiasm and genuine care for her students that I ended up taking EDUc375 with her even though I'm not an HDFS major. Professor Day is one of the best instructors I've had. He combines high standards with genuine support and clarity.
Great guy, funny, and cares about his students. Highly recommend as a MAC student or anyone using excel.

Great class - Professor Day makes things super accessible and assignments are clear. Content was very well organized and there was a lot of transparency surrounding expectations and grading. Professor Travis is an amazing professor and person, he made learning new things in excel fun and interesting. Really a good class to get an edge on excel modelling.
Practical course, good sense of humor, solid teaching and presentation skills, definitely recommend.

Very strict and tedious but the course is useful.

Travis is the GOAT. Easily the most useful class I've taken so far at UNC. Assignments take awhile, but at the end of the day they teach you how to be an excel demon. Took on top of a super heavy course-load–wouldn't recommend but definitely doable and still learn a lot.
Travis is an exceptionally knowledgeable and professional teacher. I've learned a tremendous amount in this class—thank you!

Professor Day has mastered teaching Excel. His explanations are clear, he covers the important stuff, and his instructions for assignments are detailed and clear. Awesome teacher! Very clear instructions and grading. I wish all my professors were such great communicators!

Professor Day is by far one of the best professors I've ever had at UNC. TAKE AT YOUR OWN RISK.

reviews.comment: Prob the most useful class to take in the B-school, will help out with internships and anything that uses excel. Assignment every week that takes 3-5 hours. Final is worth 50% so that could ruin ur grade. But, Travis is the Goat of excel and teaching it.

One of the most useful courses I have ever taken! Amazing instructor! I learned so much and truly appreciate the amount of detail, effort, and clarity provided in the async videos and during class. He provides impeccable notes to match the modules. He is very passionate about teaching and genuinely cares about the quality of work    he expects!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A little heavy on the "dad jokes" but I didn't mind. Professor Day knows his materials backward and forward. He's also willing to help you with Excel and Microsoft problems unrelated to coursework. Even as a well-seasoned, Excel user, I found his course useful to improve my skills. Highly recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's an amazing teacher who's always there to help and easy to reach. His classes are super interesting and fun. He's very detailed about homework, but you'll learn a lot from his class.

The only thing I did not like about Professor Day's class is the fact it went from 10 PM to midnight.  Still, he is a very engaging professor, so it was not hard to stay awake during his lectures.  The class is really useful and Professor Day does a great job teaching Excel's important tools.

Prof. Day is incredibly knowledgeable about Excel. He's very accessible to all students, even in the online format. He is also clear and objective about grading because he cares about accuracy and quality of work. I learned a lot from him and sincerely appreciated the way he runs his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The class is very applicable to professional life regardless of industry. I learned a ton and will carry these skills with me going forward. The teaching style is mostly lecture, but the notes are extremely valuable and very thorough. I would recommend this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Most useful class at UNC. Usually 90+ minutes of videos each week, just watch on 2x or 1.5x speed to help go faster. Assignments are easy as long as you watch weekly videos. Very time consuming class but also very rewarding. Only bad thing is assignments are due 8am on Sunday, so don't procrastinate! Watch the videos each week. Highly recommend!!!

Professor Day loves what he does and is passionate about excel. This class was one of the most helpful classes  I have ever taken! I learned a lot about excel and I know it will greatly help me in the future. However, the assignments took me about 3 hours a week to complete. It was a lot of work but definitely worth it!

The BEST class I have ever taken in my time at UNC! Everyone talks about how hard the class is, and I was scared going in, but it really is not that bad. Travis is such a good teacher and you will learn SO MUCH useful Excel stuff in this class. The assignments are long, but start early in the week & you'll be fine. TAKE THIS CLASS!

This class is useful but be prepared. I didn't find lectures to be valuable so you just teach yourself as you work through the hw (which took 4-6 hrs on avg). They're pretty tedious but it's not too hard to get good grades for them. The final exam was 50% of the grade which I found a little dramatic, so that dropped my grade from a 96 average lol.

MAC 707 is the most thoughtfully planned online course I have ever taken. His instruction is crystal clear and in total alignment with the notes he provides. Live sessions are a review of the week's lectures and notes. Homework is time consuming but every task is straight from the notes. He is very caring and responds to questions quickly.

Professor Day is really good about being available at all times to meet with students. If you put in the work, you will do well. BUSI 520 is an extremely valuable class, as most top tier banks look for students who have extremely good excel skills. If you have the chance to take it, definitely do as it helps you a ton after college.

Travis is one of the best professors I have ever met. His class materials are most valuable and practical. Travis is very good at making difficult parts of the course easier for us. He made lots of tips and explanations for course materials and homework assignments. He knows which part could be a problem for students.  I am so impressed.

Prof. Day is extremely talented and knowledgeable. The course structure of MAC 707 is well-planned and paced and the lectures were in-depth. It was a pleasure to attend his classes and I'd like to thank him for his continued efforts to make his courses relevant and palatable for students coming from different backgrounds.

Overall, Travis's teaching style is comprehensive. He really wants you to learn Excel. At first, I was a little overwhelmed by his vast notes files, but ultimately I came to view them for what they are: extremely useful resources that explain and demonstrate the functions and features he wants you to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class was awesome!

I say very difficult because I'd been out of school for years and only used Excel for basic data entry. Professor Day's enthusiasm is infectious, and he wants you to succeed. Yes, he has high expectations, but this is a master's level course. Lots of homework, but you'll only learn Excel by using it. This class greatly improved my Excel skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable and makes excel easy to understand for beginners while also teaching new skills/tricks to students with lots of excel experience. I came into this class with no excel skills and left feeling very comfortable with using excel.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you view the professor as a resource he will be. If you ask for help it will be given thoroughly! If you want to sit quietly and breeze by, this will not work as well.

Overall this class was very useful to learn the basics of excel. My main issue with the course is the unrealistic expectations set by professor Day. HW assignments that take 3-6 hours every week, a 2 hour zoom lecture, and often 4+ hours of weekly videos. It is too much given that we have other classes. Grading depends on your TA, and final is 50%.
Professor Day is definitely knowledgeable about Excel. The class itself was alright. Assignments took a while so be prepared to dedicate some time for those. The final is 50% so be prepared to study.

I enjoyed this class - you can get a reasonable grade without going to class and you get out what you put in with your Excel skills. Travis replies quickly and genuinely wants students to learn from the class. Assignments take 2-5 hours a week and grading can be picky. The final is worth 50% of your grade but curved so A/B range is doable.

Professor Day definitely cares about the material, but the class is tough. Assignments take 2-5 hours and are due on Sunday mornings. The final exam is 50% of the grade and it's pretty tough as well. The class is once a week, but it's 2 hours and not the easiest to follow along with. I will say that the actual material is useful.

Extremely tough to please with ridiculously detailed assignments, which can take up to 6 hours to complete
Will convince you to buy a windows laptop, even though a mac works perfectly fine
Needs things to be done ONLY in his way

Professor Day is a super understanding professor who clearly cares about the development of his students. Busi 520 is a great course that I would recommend. From a work load perspective, it is very manageable. There are thorough notes and pre recorded videos (essentially in place of lectures) that are helpful, even after you finish the course

Travis Day is the worst professor I've ever had. I don't know if I can even consider him a professor as he doesn't lecture, assign peer or group work, or is really there for his students. Theres 1 session per week (doesn't teach), and so you use prerecorded lessons to teach yourself. Weekends are ruined, bc 4-5 hr assignments are due 8:00 Sunday.

Great class to take. Homeworks are laid out well and the notes he gives are super useful to help walk through the assignment. Not a huge fan of the grading structure and his grading scale is harder than a normal one (95 to get an A). He did curve our grades at the end and was very helpful over email for any questions. A tedious but necessary class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Super useful class. Weekly excel projcts that take like 3-6 hours each. You can easily get an A on the projects (55%) because you can work with others. You don't have to go to class. 45% of grade is the final exam which is tough. If you take this class be ready to grind before exam. You don't have to go to class at all. I never went.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible instructor. Course materials are minimal, perhaps to prevent redistribution. Ridiculous to pay tuition just to be told what to learn and then have to search the internet for answers. Live sessions are just lame summaries of pre-recorded videos. Zero feedback on assignments; questions were dodged both during and outside of class. Shameful.

The class was almost entirely online. He gives you reading and powerpoint slides but you have to teach yourself the entire course. He does know it front and back and can help over the phone if you need it. The material is super helpful and in depth so that makes it worth it. Tough grader and final is 50%.

If you are an undergrad and not great at computers.. BEWARE. Homework assignments take about 4-8hours each and are graded extremely hard. Also, homework is 45%, quizzes are 5%, and the final is 50% of your grade. I had a 90 avg before the final and it brought me down to a C+ overall. Try to take another elective if possible. Yes-useful.. but hard!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Your final grade is determined by homework and the final exam. Homeworks are graded incredibly hard with point deductions for so much as not CC'ing your own email.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: David is kind, funny, and passionate in his work and teachings. He is EXTREMELY fair in terms of recognizing fault; he eased up on our second exam after understanding what students didn't like from the first exam and offered extra credit. He's also very helpful outside of lecture to thoroughly explain topics that I didn't understand well in class.

Dr. Pfennig is an amazing professor. The class was amazing and very discussion based. The structure of the course was amazing for learning the material deeply. There was one presentation, a grant proposal, and a few weekly assignments. All were amazing and things I looked forward to completing. 100% recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great teacher and great class! graded by 4 things (HW, which is a 100, participation, a grant proposal, and a presentation you work on with a group). He gives you great feedback but also grades leniently. Highly reccommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great professor who made lectures incredibly enjoyable to attend. He is passionate about the topic and transfers that feeling to the class. Lecture slides contain the exact content you will be tested on. Only difficulty is the tests can be a time crunch, so you have to know your stuff.

Dr. Pfennig was fantastic, and the relaxed nature of this course really worked for me. There was a lot of reading, and everyone had to do multiple group presentations as well as a significant amount of individual/group writing, so the workload is somewhat high, but it seemed like the work was very applicable to what would be done as a scientist.
He is a chill guy but grades everything so harsh.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Engaging + enjoyable class and Prof. Sands is knowledgeable and impressive. The content was very interesting and useful beyond class. Biggest issue was unclear grading which caused unnecessary stress. Workload felt very heavy for a MOD class, but maybe that's not bad. He's new though so it may improve.

Professor Sands is a very chill professor and a fair grader. Class wasnt filled with busy work or unnecessary assignments. It was graded off a few things, mainly final presentation and report. No final exam either. Would definitely recommend to take 411 with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hands down the best professor at UNC! He is kind, thoughtful, compassionate, and an exceptional mentor who cares about your perspective and success. As a senior now, who took this class as a freshman, Dr. Gitterman is the best professor I've ever had. His classes are engaging, preparing you for the real world in politics, policy, or life itself.
Easy A class and great professor!
Absolutely Amazing

Gitterman's a nice, funny guy and a good professor. There are only a few assignments, and they're not graded hard at all. He tells you word for word what's going to be on the exams, and all the answers are straight from the readings.
Gitterman is a great prof, very in touch with students and knowledgeable. Class if difficult but also getting an A is attainable.

Lowkey all grades will depend on your TA, but I know Gitterman gives them specific answers for the midterm and final. He assigns readings, but as long as you stay in class and skim the readings for examples: you will do fine on the midterm & final. Your other main grade is your policy brief, which is long but very simple. Easiest 101 class.

The goat. Really cared about his students as people. I had a disagreement with him about the way he broached a difficult topic and he took the time to meet with me and hear about my perspective. Absolutely loved the class. Super easy but valuable nonetheless.

This was a great class, and Professor Gitterman genuinely cares about his students! Class was based on a few papers, attendance, a midterm, and a final. The assignments had a clear grading criteria and were designed to build toward the final paper. The midterm and final were both based off a top 10 list he provided so it was clear what to study.
He is the goat. I loved coming to the lectures, he was very lax and communicated well.

Take this class if you're interested in Policy or need a focus capacity. Gitterman is super chill, and all of the TAs are chill as well. There's a policy brief, midterm, and final, and they're all fairly simple. Gitterman gives clear directions too. Class is actually interesting as well so that's a plus.

Professor Gitterman is very passionate about the content and lectures are always interesting. He is so sweet, brought in donuts to class and even the Cleffhangers one day. Gman rocks. The class is not hard at all and he gives you a study guide for midterm/final telling exactly what will be on the exams. 1000000/10 recommend he is the best
Professor Gitterman is super knowledgable and experienced with policy and you can tell how much he cares! Genuinely loved his lectures.
Super easy A and hes genuinely an awesome person

Really just depends on your TA, as they grade everything (which is only about 4/5 things for an entire semester). Very clear outline for the midterm and final exams. Lectures get a little dry, but he's a very understanding guy outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: would HIGHLY recommend taking PLCY 101 with Gitterman in the fall. He is funny and caring and wants his students to succeed and have a good time with the class. There is a lot of reading, but if you pay attention in lectures you can get away with not doing it. The mid-term and final are based off a list of topics he the lecture before the test day.

Professor Gitterman is the best, he genuinely cares about his students and lectures were really enjoyable to go to. Policy brief was biggest component of grade and midterm/final were given a study guide that was close to exam. Take him at UNC he's awesome!
Professor Gitterman has been my favorite professor so far at UNC. He's funny, knowledgeable, and very accommodating. Take a class with Gman if you can!!
genuinely made going to class interesting and his lectures were never boring.

I loved Dr. Gitterman and couldn't recommend him enough! He has such a kind heart and genuinely cares about the well-being of each of his students. Class was also very versatile: "game-show" style activities, watching short films, hearing from guest speakers, etc. He even brought in the Clefhangers one class. So awesome.
He is an amazing professor that cares about his students. A few assignments and a midterm and final exam but as long as you take notes during lectures you will be fine.

Amazing class, great professor. Incredibly knowledgeable about policy and cares that you learn. Used UNC Check-In for attendance, and would be engaging with PollEverywhere. Readings were manageable but you could go without doing them (but needed for midterm/final). Only real grades are midterm, SWA2, policy brief, presentation and final.
Love Gitterman. You can tell he is very devoted to teaching and cares about making an impact on the students. If you put in the work you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. Really funny and very helpful if you get to know him. Would highly recommend office hours. He is a great professor overall.

Gitterman is honestly so funny and chill. He's just hilarious and he also knows what he's talking about. His lectures are easy to understand and it's clear that he just wants you to succeed. He genuinely wants everyone in his class to get A's. We only had like 5 assignments graded but it's not difficult at all. He's amazing like truly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Gitterman is an awesome professor who provided a great seminar experience. His assignments and readings were super interesting and engaging, and he consistently aimed to provide us with unique opportunities and insights. This class was incredibly inspiring and made me think differently about various avenues of policy and entrepreneurship.

Very funny, engaging, and chill. You can tell he cares a lot about what he is teaching. Gives a midterm and final exam study guide which are very applicable to the test. Not much work besides 2 small writing assignment and the final policy brief.

Gitterman is a funny and engaging lecturer who makes class go by quickly. The grade is based on a midterm, final, and a policy brief, but he spreads everything out over the semester so it never feels overwhelming. Attendance does matter, but the class itself is very easy as long as you show up and put in a little effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Gitterman was the best! Lectures are amazing and he is hilarious. You have a big policy brief due, but he does it in chunks so it is doable and not overwhelming.

His lectures are extremely engaging and he genuinely cares about all his students. Only homework is readings, which you don't have to do if you just take notes. He tells you what will be on the exams so study that material and you will be fine. TAs determine grades but all of them are great. Policy brief is also straightforward.

His lectures are very enjoyable, especially as someone who usually gets bored easily. Very respected in his field, and it shows with his expertise. Very little homework other than the readings. The midterm is completely based on his top 10 list. Take this class.
What a lovely guy who really cares about what he teaches

Absolutely loved this course, super interesting if you like sustainable business, etc. Great connection to have at UNC. A couple essays and final presentation. Got us Purple Bowl at the end of the semester. Met so many cool people.

Dr. G was an extremely funny lecturer, and he made rather dense content enjoyable. The midterm and final are extremely fair, and completely based off of his top 10 list. TA's will probably make or break your grade though, but Anna B. was mine and she was very helpful and not a tough grader at all. Definitely recommend this class to freshmen.

I loved this class and Professor Gitterman! As a policy major, this was a great introduction to a wide range of US policy topics. Attendance is mandatory as he uses the UNC check-in app. The main assignment is the policy brief, due near the end of the class, but he breaks the writing process down nicely to help students block time to write.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AMAZING PROFESSOR!! Super accommodating, understanding, friendly, funny, and brilliant! He really just cares about teaching you things you need to know for the real world, and his content is super useful. The class really is not hard, just be prepared to study before a midterm and final exam, but that's really the only stress of the entire class.
Super clear grading, but TA's make the grades! I had no problem getting an A. The recitations well prepare you for the midterm and final exam. Dr. Gitterman had hilarious lectures!

Hilarious guy, caring, and knowledgable professor. PLCY101 was a great class with him and very enjoyable, but the content felt quite easy and barebones (to be expected of a 101 class). Grading was clear, he is VERY accessible on Calendly, and was overall a good experience! Highly recommend.

Gitterman cares more about each student's success than anything else. Gives take-home midterm & final, just be sure to cite literature given as he was adamant about using it. Instructions were not clear for assignments but easy to figure out. Didn't think the class was too hard, but he has a bold personality that can take some time to get used to

Daniel Gitterman was an amazing professor! He made the lectures fun and engaging. It's important to go to class, but I promise he will make it worthwhile. It has interesting content but does not go too in-depth because this is an intro-level course. I definitely want to take a class with him again!

Amazing TAs! He was funny and although there was only a few graded assignments they were graded fairly and the feedback was great. The office hours were very helpful! There are lots of reading but you only need to skim them in preparation for class. Favorite professor at UNC so far!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is fine. Projects are fun and you learn a lot. Good chunks of reading but he tells you to skim. Caring professor wants you to succeed. Gets in your face a lot. Calls people out in the middle of class. HEAVY participation. Takes off points for project grades with no explanation. Overall decent professor. Kind heart but a little aggressive IMO.
Great professor with engaging lectures. Often put on music and led dances towards the end of the semester. Not many assignments so an overall really easy class you just have to show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Gitterman is amazing. Lectures are engaging, organized, and relevant to the exam material. More importantly, you can tell that he really does care. I would highly suggest taking the "no multitasking" agreement seriously – just try it for a semester! This class is incredibly rewarding when you are consistent, present, and attentive.

Dr. Gitterman is a great professor. The class was super interesting and engaging. He will provide you with a list of questions to review for during the midterm and final, but those were easy. So, as long as you come to class, participate, take notes, you will do fine.

There is one midterm (20%) and one final (25%); he gives you a "top 10" list before each exam and he literally pulls questions directly from that list. Your other grades are from attendance (20%) and a paper (35%) that you write and present on in recitation. My only gripe is that he doesn't post the slides. The class is pretty easy overall though.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Gitterman is a very good lecturer and does hos best to make sure the class is interesting. The semester long project is meant to serve as an introduction to policy overall, which is nice. Recitation is also pretty fun if you are comfortable discussing politics with your classmates.

Dr. Gitterman is a wonderful professor and person. He cares deeply about his students and has a wealth of knowledge and experience to share from his time in the public policy field. I learned a lot from his class and didn't mind the readings as they were interesting and applicable. I would highly recommend taking a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Gitterman is engaging and cares about his students. The class is lecture-heavy, but the practical projects are worthwhile. I found unstuck study and the free textbook very helpful for studying.

Gman is alot of fun to have as a Professor. I think his class really does prepare you for the real world and encourages you to think about the things that matter most to you! He is not really on email, but is accessible via office hours. His feedback can at first be confusing, but always meet with him. He will push you to think critically. No BS!

If there is any course or professor that I would recommend, Dr. Gitterman is at the top of my list. He is understanding, funny, and really passionate about the material. Work is not very heavy and he can accommodate you, if you communicate. Attendance and participation does matter. I think you will really enjoy this course and it will help you!

Professor Gitterman is awesome. He is fun and engaging and makes class interesting. He understands that we're taking other classes and does what he can to make our lives easier while also being in his class. He makes the content he teaches easy to understand. I highly recommend taking his class.

Dr. Gitterman is the most caring professor I have ever had. From my first year seminar to my senior year, he has been so willing to support me. His subject material is super interesting and he is so passionate, it helps you learn and connect with the courses well! He also really encourages students to share their thoughts! His classes are amazing!

For the DC semester, he had great connections and was intelligent on policy. He was also often vindictive, unforgiving of small mistakes, and targeting select students in a way that made for an uncomfortable class environment. Efforts to connect with students, particularly those struggling, were minimal, and his tone was perpetually self-important.
There is not much more I can say about Professor Gitterman that has not already been said. He is hilarious, incredibly smart, and you 100% need to take one of his classes if you are a policy major.

I highly recommend taking a class with Professor Gitterman. His perspective is very interesting and he is also really funny. It is nice to have a professor that cares about you even after you take their class. He has so many connections! (Also to comment on his wokeness, it would be concerning if a PLCY prof wasn't "woke"... just saying.)
Awesome professor, you will learn a lot in this class and can apply the skills you learn to any area of your personal life. I definitely recommend taking this class, you won't regret it.
W professor. Would definitely recommend.
He aint woke, hes just funny

Dr. Gitterman truly cares about his students, but at first he comes off as "woke". If you can move past this you'll see he means well. He hates that students are super focused on grades, and at times it felt like he picked a random grade to give(always within A or B range). He is head of the public policy department and is a good connection to have
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Gitterman really cares about his students and wants to make their learning environment as strong as possible. This class is definitely lecture heavy and projects dominate the workload. If you put in effort, you should get an A (although it is difficult to follow your grade).

Prof Gitterman is great! The class is a bit boring but it is very practical. He is so caring and understanding. The class consists of a take home midterm and final (he is very specific about citations - use APA). There is also a letter of intent (3 pages) and a grant proposal (8 pages). It is not as much work as it sounds. I would recommend it!

Dr. Gitterman rocks. 61H was not a super difficult class but you really do learn a lot. He cares so much about his students and wants to make sure each of us is successful both inside and outside of his classroom. Take time to get to know him and you can form a really valuable professor-student relationship.

Dr. Gitterman is my favorite professor I've had at UNC. He is incredibly passionate about his policy and especially knowledgable about the topics covered in this seminar. He keeps class interesting and engaging. Class is fairly repetitive, but that's because he really believes in what he is teaching and wants to make the world a better place.

Professor Gitterman very clearly cares about his students. He always offers to meet with them to make sure youre getting the most out of the class. He also gives really good feedback on papers. The class required a fair amount of reading that was pretty dry but he condensed the info in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Gitterman is a staple of the UNC public policy dept. I respect him so much, and he is clearly passionate about the material. However, I didn't really know my grade in the class until the last week of class (only got two grades back before then). Still, he's a great prof who cares A LOT about his students. Def recommend him.

Professor Gitterman is amazing! Even during the rough semester, he kept our class engaged and went out of his way to show us he cared (donut party, split class in half, etc). Grade was comprised of a take-home short answer midterm exam based on readings, two 5/10 page papers, and participation. Easy course if you think creatively/discuss in class

Dr. Gitterman is a good lecturer and very knowledgeable in his subject. Class is entertaining. He is a fair person and tries to be there for his students, even in large classes. It won't be an "Easy A", but if you go to class and do the reading, you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Gitterman for PLCY101! Despite it being a big class he still encourages you to interact and is a very entertaining lecturer. The study guides are EXACTLY like the exams and the assignments are straightforward. Only con is you must show up to lectures and recitation for attendance credit but this class should be an easy A/B
Good class good professor - truly the gem of the public policy department. Assigns a lot of reading but you'll be fine if you skim.

Gitterman seemed to be a really great guy and showed a deep care for Public Policy as well as Carolina Students. He is extremely sarcastic and has a unique sense of humor (I loved it). The tests are extremely fair and lectures are engaging. I am not a PLCY major, but still enjoyed this class.

I took this class during my first semester at Carolina. I would definitely reccomend this to new students. The lectures were really amazing and hilarious, and even though I didn't get an A, I am glad I took this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I have never had a more fair professor. He clearly cares about his students and the material and gives "Top Ten" lists for his exams. I'm sure the exams would be hard if you don't study or listen because he doesn't post slides; however, he gives you every tool necessary to succeed. Homework is minimal. Just pay attention. (easy bc he is HILARIOUS)

Dr. Gitterman is the best! The class always felt like it flew by because it was never boring. He is very straightforward about what will be on exams. However, I will say, attendance is very important. If you do happen to miss a class, don't do the Poll Everywhere from wherever you are, he will probably catch you. The slides also won't be on Sakai.
Best professor I had this semester. Cares about students, fair with grades, upfront about tests. One of my favorites.

This man is THE BEST. Easily my favorite professor at UNC. His lectures are engaging and interesting, but be prepared to attend always. He's well-respected and serious about attendance. Put in the work and you'll get great results. Can't say enough good things.

Dr. Gitterman is super passionate about the content. He sometimes gets a bit off topic but he knows a lot and cares about student learning and wellbeing. There's also a lot of room to work on things you're interested in.

I love Dr. Gitterman! His class was extremely enjoyable and informative and made me realize that I 100% want to do Public Policy as my major, so thanks for that! I wish I recorded his lectures bc I would love to hear his information and life lessons again. The TA I had graded really harshly though, which was disappointing as I put in a lot of work

I love Dr. Gitterman! He made class interesting and educational. His priority is the students; I appreciate the way he makes things work for each individual. He is very accessible outside of class. He also has a great sense of humor. The exams are very straight forward and there are plenty of extra credit opportunities. I 100% recommend this class!

Professor Gitterman is easily one of the most caring professors I have ever had - he clearly looks out for all of his students (even in a 300 person lecture class). Furthermore, even though I was not very interested in public policy, I looked forward to every single lecture because he made class fun and interesting. Would 100% recommend his class!!

Gitterman is the best professor I have had at UNC. His lectures are engaging, I loved it so much I changed my major. He makes somewhat boring topics(if you do not like history) fun and he tells funny stories. If you just pay attention and study you will be perfectly fine. There are 2 papers(one 2 page and another 10 page), but you have all semester

I loved Gitterman and Policy 101. Professor Gitterman makes the material interesting and constantly welcomes students to come and chat with him. He clearly cares about his students and the material. After taking the course with Gitterman, I've decided to add public policy as my second major. Needless to say-- take his class!

Gitterman was by far my favorite professor. He has a real passion for public policy and he really cares about his students. There is a 10 page paper, but you work on it throughout the semester in different parts. His tests are clearly outlined. There are extra credit opportunities but if you study for the tests they are just extra.
Good professor generally. He didn't want to teach this class, though, and that was pretty clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. G is an energetic, passionate, and involved educator. He's well respected in the UNC community, and his class was fair in terms of assignments, expectations, and grading. However, personal issues, calling out students, and what he did for the final (unreasonably hard) was unfair to overall effort by the students and, frankly, very petty.

Professor G really cares about the material he is teaching, and has clear expectations for assignments, presentations, and tests. It's worth putting in some extra effort outside of class to understand the material and projects, and def go to office hours for feedback or to chat

On a personal level, I think Prof Gitterman is a passionate department chair. He truly cares for UNC students, especially Public Policy majors. Go to his office hours. Chat with him. Explore what the UNC Public Policy Department has to offer. However, do not waste your time with the class. You will learn nothing about policy. Only life lessons.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Gitterman is a great professor who really cares about UNC and its students! His material is very straightforward, and if you go just go to the lectures and pay attention you'll have everything you need to know for his tests. He does take it to heart if you are late/don't pay attention, but he is also the department chair and just wants respect.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Gitterman was awesome. You could tell he really cares about his students and the subject. His midterm and final were straightforward and he doesn't try to trick you or get you on small details.

I throughly enjoyed this class! Although I am in the major, I feel that this class would be interesting even to students who just interested in learning more about policy. Prof. Gitterman is a nice guy despite what some of these other posts say. Go to class, put forth effort on the brief, and take notes on the reading and lecture and you'll be good
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I'm really glad I took this class. Gitterman does a wonderful job making the material understandable, and very clearly cares about his students. If you come to this class willing to put in work, you can get an A. He's really funny, I enjoyed every lecture. BUT, do NOT go on Facebook, he'll call you out in front of everyone in the 375 person class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS AS HONORS. Literally don't! Honors classes are supposed to mean a smaller class size and more in-depth material, that is not what I receive from this class. The grading for honors was 10x harsher than normal, for NO reason. Not to mention this class taught me nothing more than a google search could. Gitterman is cool tho.

Awesome professor!! He made lectures interesting and made me want to have a possible double major in public policy. The midterm and the policy brief wasn't bad, but the final was nearly impossible, even if you did do the readings.

I usually don't post on here but since Gitterman reads it religiously I might as well. Theres not much work involved and it's an easy B+/A- if you show up to lectures and write a decent policy brief. He was too concerned with people being off task that it affected his teaching. He shows passion for the class, but the final was a bit uncalled for.

The class was great until the final. After reading a Rate My Professor review that said that reading was optional, he made the final difficult and based on the readings, some of which were 80 pages long and not talked about in class. Loved his lectures but the final was too much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Gitterman is an amazing professor. He makes a broad, introductory course feel interesting and relevant. He also really cares about his students; he's really invested in his classroom and department. His level of passion does, in fact, extend to reading RMP, and understandably resulted in some frustration. Still loved his class and would take again.

To whoever put on here you don't have to read for exams I hate you. He read your comment and now is making it so you will fail the final exam if you have not read. Other than that Dr. G is the best. I love that man. Honestly my favorite professor. Just complaining cause I'm about to fail this final. woo!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Thinks a Google Doc is a violation of the Honor Code. Really?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Gitterman is a great professor. He makes lecture super interesting even though the topics can sometimes be a little dry. Attendance is mandatory, but his lectures are interesting enough that you want to go. Also, he goes over everything that's on the midterm and final in lecture. Readings aren't necessary unless you don't go to the lecture.

I love Dr. Gitterman! I was in his Policy 101 class during the (painful) election of 2016. He made a wonderful effort to talk about the necessity for unity and moderacy. His lectures are hilarious, but he isn't above public humiliation. Just be respectful and you can have a great time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Gitterman is your stereotypical zany professor. In addition to being funny, he was passionate about the subject. He obviously cares about his students, even when there are 300-400 in a lecture. Just beware: he takes the no multi-tasking agreement very seriously. He will not hesitate to call you out for being on your phone/sleeping during class.
Professor Gitterman is awesome! Such a cool dude and a fun class. Want to take something he teaches again.

He's the most respected professor in the Public Policy department, yet he teaches PLCY101, and does so extremely well. He makes lectures super laid back and funny, yet still informative. His top ten list is a gem, and he definitely cares about his students. Offers extra credit for going to forums! Overall, definitely a great professor.

Dr. G is a good professor. He knows what he's talking about, and really tries to make a boring class seem interesting. My only complaint is that participating is difficult, he can be condescending and twist your words to make fun of you. If you're right leaning/conservative like myself, be ready to face some opposition from him and the TAs.
He's the reason I decided to major in Public Policy. Best professor I've had yet. His lectures were very informational and hilarious. Great man.
Great lecturer fun class.

An awesome professor. Public policy - particularly the readings - can get a little cumbersome and boring sometimes, but he does an excellent job of making it as interesting as possible while having to graze over an insane amount of topics in a short period of time. A large class, so it's hard to get to know him, but he's super helpful when you ask.

Dr. G is a knowledgable professor teaching a very vague class. Plcy 101 has a lot of material, but he touches it all and keeps you interested by being interactive and using multimedia. You must read the assigned policy briefs to pass the final. Would I call Dr. G one of the best profs at UNC? Probably not, but he's a really good guy nonetheless.

One of the best professors I've had. Makes every class interesting and really cares about his students. It is well worth your time to come to class because he clarifies difficult points in the readings and makes the ideas from the textbook (READ IT TO SUCCEED IN CLASS!) more applicable. Wish I could take the class again or another course by him.

Dr. Gitterman is absolutely great! His lectures are very clear and quite interesting considering the material can sometimes get a little boring. He does a great job of making you appreciate public policy. There are few assignments throughout the semester, and you absolutely have to attend class. It's not hard, his lectures will make you want to go!

Don't listen to the salty kids-- one of the best professors at UNC. He does hold you accountable, but makes class worth coming to with lectures and videos that keep you engaged and interested in the material. He wants to be fair and he wants you to learn, which is refreshing in a professor.

An amazing professor! He really cared about the students and stressed learning and becoming interested in the material rather than making his class difficult to pass. My TA (McHale) was great; just as engaging as he was and really helpful with any questions I had. The work was easy and little. Great start to UNC! (PS: do NOT buy ANYTHING for PLCY)

Great professor and really tries to connect with the students by showing videos and telling short anecdotal stories to keep you interested.  Make sure to go to class, because although the topics may not be super exciting are very informational and on his tests.  A must have teacher a one point in your Carolina career. If motivated easy A.

Awesome prof!  You have to go to class, but his lectures are really interesting and entertaining and make you want to go.  He really cares about the students and will help you with anything you want.  He's more interested in making sure you learn than making the class difficult.  Everything is graded very fairly.  Best prof I've had at UNC!

I loved this professor. I would recommend my friends and other take his class. It's not easy, but it's not supposed to be. I loved learning about everything in policy and enjoyed his enthusiasm and love for the subject. his lectures are interesting and keep you entertained.

ATTEND CLASS. It may seem like you don't have to, but his TA's monitor the PollEverywhere and they will catch you skipping. Readings are not necessary, and he gives helpful study guides for the exams. One big paper, but outside of that its not a lot of work. He's super entertaining in class, and he shows a lot of videos, which make you want to go

Awesome professor. He kept the class entertaining and gave realistic examples of Public Policy in action. You do need to attend class to do the Poll Everywhere questions and his lectures are the most helpful when it comes to studying for the exams.

This was by far one of my favorites classes. He makes class so interesting and you actually WANT to come to class. Has a little bit of a fowl mouth so if you are sensitive to that beware. Overall, his TA's grade very fairly and are always able to help!

Not as easy as everyone says.  Not particularly work intensive, but not an easy A. The work you do have to do is usually hard to ace.  Midterm and final I got a solid B, pretty much everything was a solid B for me. Gitterman is cool and funny. Not very interesting class, didn't learn much. Readings aren't necessary even for the final.
Excellent professor. Really cares about his students, engaging, and informative. Even if you aren't interested in policy, I recommend a class with Dr. Gitterman.

Took PLCY101 for maymester and loved it. Best professor I've had so far. His lectures were interesting and made the 3 hours fly by. The work was very manageable. He cares a lot about his students and what he teaches and it shows. Highly recommended.

Best professor I've had yet. Personable and hilarious. Extremely fair tests and assignments - no curve balls. He really wants you to succeed, and he will help you with ANYTHING if you just ask. My recitation was a little unnecessary, but it was probably just my TA. Everyone should take this class - it gave me the final push to become a PLCY major.

Gitterman is an excellent professor. He is friendly, helpful, knowledgeable, and accessible. He definitely has the best handle on how to engage a 250+ person lecture of any professor I've ever had. Also, he is VERY clear about what he wants in assignments and is fair in grading. There are no curve balls.
Agree with almost all of the previous sentiments on Dr. G.

I took the maymester last year with Gitterman and LOVED it.  The class was a little intense because of how fast you have to move with the time constraints, but he was so entertaining and made a long class time go by fast.  I highly recommend taking his maymester!

Professor Gitterman is an extremely nice man who knows all about his class subject. He's willing to meet with students and he seems to genuinely care about their well-being. While I do agree the final was a little surprising, we had the readings assigned for a long time prior. Overall my best class this semester and if you can, definitely take it.

I had Gitterman for 101 and he is an amazing teacher. His lectures are engaging and he actually cares about his students and what they get out of his class. I only took it as a gen ed requirement and i might be a public policy major now. i highly recommend this class.

Gitterman was an engaging professor for teaching a intro course of 240. His powerpoints are easy to follow and he makes the class interesting through videos and outbursts of enthusiasm. As for the final, he made it reading-based because on two occasions the overwhelming majority of the class admitted to not reading! We deserved it. He's a good prof

Professor Gitterman is one of the best professors at UNC. He makes 300+ student lecture class interactive and extremely interesting. Going into this course I had no real interest in public policy but now I am really going to miss it. Learned a lot that will be applied in everyday life. Take this class and you will not be disappointed.

Gitterman is one of the greatest professors.  The "reading based" final was hard but he also announced that in lecture.  And my TA was awesome.  If you show them you genuinely care about your grade and the material, they will genuinely care about it too.  A lot of what I learned is useful in life.

He always keeps the class interested in lectures, using youtube videos and polling questions. Minimal work, good lectures, good teacher. Everyone please stop whining about the exam, he told us like four times what would be on it and how to study for it.

Made this class as interesting as possible. Obviously loves what he does and cares about the topic. I actually like lectures and he made them genuinely entertaining. By far one of the best professors at UNC.

I took PLCY 101 last semester and thoroughly enjoyed the course. Dr. Gitterman does a great job at giving an overview of American policy making and prepping students for further policy work (exactly what the course is designed to do). If the professor threw you for a loop on the final, well, welcome to college...

This class is really engaging and Gitterman makes lectures interesting and fun. He's one hell of a professor. For students who attend his lectures, they recieve heads ups on what is going to be on the exams and finals. The final exam was a little rough, but he did give us a warning before hand that the final will be based on readings. Overall, good

Amazing professor! Really cares about his students. Put in the work and you will do well. Strict no-technology policy but he makes his lectures very entertaining and engaging to compensate. Very straightforward about exam material and offered extensions for both papers. Best class I've taken at UNC!

For those who complain about the readings being too much because they have a life, Policy 101 (and likely school in general) was just not a priority for them. Considering we were given a heads up about the final being reading-based, I think the amount of lecture material on it was very generous. Gitterman is a great professor and I learned a lot!!!

I really liked this class. I don't think this page should be dedicated to the final, but since we were all emailed about it I can say I didn't think it would be totally based off the readings. But that's completely understandable. He's a great man, and has contributed lots to society already, and wants us to do the same!

Professor Gitterman is a fantastic professor and was very fair in his tests.  He let his students know exactly what was going to be on the test with a very specific study guide. I'm appalled at these comments from people who took Gitterman for granted.  As someone who didn't do any of the readings whatever I receive on this final is what I deserve.

Gitterman was always concerned with students actual well being and frequently extended due dates solely to reduce student stress.  As far as his final; he explained what it consisted of and that it was based on the readings many times.  If one attended class and did the readings, there wouldn't have been a single problem.  Excellent professor.

Good person and professor. The final was hard for those of us that actually have lives/other classes that are also reading based. More work than I would have liked for a 101. I didn't feel the final accurately represented the material covered. for all of you who said "just do the readings," some were 10 pages long and very dense. not an easy A.

Prof. Gitterman was completely fair in giving out a reading-based test. From day one we were assigned readings and this was always expected from us. Studying will make exams much smoother, as it should. Loved this professor and hope you all take a class with him. I always looked forward to his class.

I loved this class. Professor Gitterman is an extremely enthusiastic lecturer who adds videos and examples to make class interesting. He seems to genuinely care about students and that they truly learn and apply what they learn to the real world. The final was reading based, yes, but he gave fair warning and if you read through them it was fine.

For everyone who is complaining about the final ... he told us to make sure and do the readings.  None of my other classes with supplemental reading go over the readings in class.  For any future students: the mid-term is totally different than the final so just be prepared!

Though this is my 1st semester at Carolina, Gitterman is one of the best professors I've had so far. Didn't really get the chance to talk to him, but he keeps the class entertained with stories and outbursts of excitement. The final wasn't bad at all, TAs were great, and to those who complain, he told us that the final would be READING BASED.

A great class. The professor cares about us as students and is very funny. The final was not easy but for anyone who studied and had at least a basic knowledge of the readings it shouldn't have been too difficult. Even after the final I still highly recommend this class. Ps. Just do the readings.

I would ignore most of the criticism about Gitterman.  He is easily one of the most funny, interesting, and entertaining teachers you will have at Carolina. PLCY 101 is definitely a class worthwhile taking.  He always takes in consideration wht students are going through.  The final can be as easy as you make it.  Do the readings and its quite easy

I'm a little ashamed of my classmates at the moment. The class was interesting and engaging and the final's difficulty was determined only by the work you put into the class. When a teacher assigns work, it is fair game for it to be on the exam,and this is coming from someone who probably did quite poorly on the final.

Great class and teacher. Not sure why people are complaining about the final - went out the night before and still thought it was extremely fair. Very representative of his powerpoints and lectures throughout the year if you reviewed them for any time at all - Would recommend to anyone with an interest as Gman really is a top notch prof
Gitterman is the greatest professor at UNC. His lectures are extremely interesting! I had no interest in policy before I took this class but now I am planning to minor in public policy. TAKE HIM!!!!!
I'm sad Policy 101 is over--Professor Gitterman is awesome!  Take his class, its great for anyone who is even remotely interested in policy.  :)

It was a blessing and a privilege to have a professor as dedicated and caring as Professor Gitterman. He has a good heart and invests a lot of time and effort in making his lectures both engaging and informative. Professor Gitterman is someone who makes  Carolina the great school that it is! I loved his course, and you will too!

This guy is the bomb dot com.  He cares about his students and makes it almost impossible to not do well in the class. He puts in a great deal of work into the class, so he does expect you not to multitask (facebook, twitter, etc), but that's reasonable.  He's an understanding person whom we can all relate to. The class itself is also very engaging

Professor Gitterman is the man. He is engaging, funny, and there is never a dull moment. He gives his class a good grasp of policy issues and you will learn a lot. Not the easiest class to be sure, but informative and worth taking. On a side note, don't multitask. He makes you sign an agreement and if you break it, well, its painful to watch.

He is one of the nicest professors I have ever met. He is a really charming guy and has a big heart. During my midterm, my computer had glitches, but he was completely understanding about it. He keeps lectures entertaining, although you learn a lot from them. As long as you put in an effort to do the readings and study his notes, you can get an A.
extremely funny
He's a great guy! So funny, too. He'll keep you active in class-even if there are 300 students.
Really great class. Keeps it interesting and entertaining. Good to take if you just want a broad scope of public policy.
His class honestly flies by. It's a really interactive class and he will keep you entertained. I definately recommend.
When my parents and friends ask about my classes and professors I talk about Gitterman. If you go to UNC, take this class.

Easily my favorite professor at Carolina so far. His class is very interactive, and many (not all) of the students seem to have informed opinions. He assigns readings and then goes over the main points (which you will be tested on) during lectures. Going to class is extremely beneficial because it is interesting and will help you do well on exams.
Gitterman is possibly the best professor at UNC. His class is very interesting and not extremely difficult.

Gitterman is an excellent professor. EVERY DAY his lectures are interesting, and even if you aren't particularly into politics and policymaking in the beginning by the time you take the midterm you will be! Definitely one of my favorite classes at UNC.
Fun class...lots of youtube videos that relate well to the material...out of class readings not helpful
Fun class.  The TA's rock too.
Great professor, fun class!
Really funny professor. You will really enjoy his lectures!
freaks out about facebook and email but he's hilarious and engaging, and knows what hes talking about

Just had him for Maymester. You would think that a class 3 1/2 hours long every day for three weeks would be horrible, and it has been a lot of work, but Professor Gitterman has been absolutely awesome. He genuinely cares about what hes teaching about, has great credentials considering his past work experience, and went to great schools. Awesome!!!

Gitterman is a cool guy.  Good lecturer, funny at times and uses youtube clips to integrate current events to discussion topics.  only downside is he requires attendance which really isn't necessary.  It's a good class and I would definitely recommend.  You might find you have an interest in public policy!

Went into class only knowing what I'd read about Gitterman on this page. Have an open mind about him. I found him to be funny, a clear lecturer, and maybe a little embarrassing to students at times, but never horrible. Only class I didn't surf the web in, since the TA's watch. I think it's good that he is serious about it, and not a pushover.

This class is a general overview of lots of different aspects of American Public Policy.  It's really not helpful if you already follow the news and are aware of the current political structure.  Class attendance is required, which is silly since lectures don'aren't instructive, and debates are ineffective because the class is so huge.

Really great teacher and willing to help. Picks pretty interesting topics and tries to engage students by using youtube and discussion. People say he attacks your ideas if you don't agree with him, but I'm not even sure what he believes--He doesn't really give his opinion in class, he just presents the facts.

Easy class and shows himself to be a nice, understanding guy in a big lecture. If you go to him during office hours he's very hard to talk to and doesn't seem very approachable, almost standoff-ish. If you're having trouble, the TAs are usually most helpful, but the class itself is pretty easy if you've taken Poli 100 or Econ 101.

This class is meant to be a general introduction to Public Policy in America. If you read the assigned readings and debates you will get just that. If you don't, you won't. Put garbage in, get garbage out. Dr. Gitterman is great. He wants respect in the classroom, and if you give that to him, you'll have no reason to dislike the guy.

If you have interest (doesn't matter how much) in policy and looking for an amazing professor who made the course material interesting enough: then this is the class. He always tied his material to topics that influence you. People writing neg. stuff prolly didn't pay attention and failed. Jst go to class all the time do your work: you will get A!

Good class - sometimes really boring sometimes very engaging. He is a menschlekeit guy, and I've told him this, who overall wants an active class and engaged student population. He really helped to make sure I could stay engaged with the class under difficult circumstances. The textbook does leave a lot to be desired. He wants students to do well!

Gitterbug is an effective prof.  He wasn't really available this semester, but I think he was just busy advising the Governor, which is pretty cool.  Most of the poor reviews come from egotistical freshmen who expect a mirror image of their perfect selves.  Prof is a sociologist with serious hopes for democratic cooperation in public policy.
Great class!

Such a nice guy!  Does really use class time all that effectively (goes on tangents, personal stories, etc.) but he really cares about his students.  If you're concerned about your grade he is willing talk during office hours and usually he'll give you a few points back on a midterm if you have a problem with question.

TAs grade the tests and policy briefs, which can be a drag, but his class is fairly interesting, especially when he uses YouTube clips to show different sides of an issue or just to have fun.  I've decided on becoming a public policy major after this class. Highly recommended!

nice guy, goes on tangents a lot with personal stories and video clips, connects PP to real world issues for clarity, a lot of reading for the class but you don't really have to do it, study the power points from lectures and its a piece of cake
funny, cares about students, applies to real world life experiences, gets whole class involved in discussion even though its a big lecture class
Awesome teacher, hilarious, really knows how to hold students' attention during lecture
AWESOME GUY!
I took Hist 153, but it wasn't an option! it was a very interesting class, but there was just too much reading. nearly impossible to read before every class

I took HIST 153 with Professor Czendze, however, that was not an option to select. He is one of the most genuine professors and often brought candy to class for us :) There is a midterm early in the semester, a final, and a 1-2 page paper due roughly every other week. Take notes, pay attention to lectures, and do the readings - you'll be fine!

I took hist 153 with him but that wasn't an option to select -- great teacher, very knowledgeable and I really learned a lot. Definitely a lot of readings but its easy to get by with just skimming right before class. Pay attention in lecture too. One midterm, final paper, final exam, and ~6 mini papers throughout the semester based on readings.

Prof. Czendze is a very thoughtful and kind professor. I took "Holocaust Remembrance" with him which was fascinating. He encouraged lots of student participation while still guiding the discussion. The readings WERE a bit heavy at times, but they were genuinely interesting. If you at least skim and think about them, you'll be alright.

MEJO341 is a boring class but Lightning made it so much fun! There's no homework, and quizzes and exams are fairly easy, just be prepared to read. Only downside is it's an 8 AM but it lowkey doesn't feel like that sometimes (+ attendance technically isn't mandatory, he does give extra credits if you come though).

Lightning is the best! Goes out of the way to be accessible during office hours and help with assignments as much as you need. Gives great lectures as well and is very engaging. I wish I could take more classes with him, he's one of the best Hussman professors I've had.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER! Media Law is not the easiest class, but Lightning makes it so much better. Three exams + five quizzes + participation. As long as you do your readings, you'll be fine. He also curves the grade and offers extra credit, so don't worry if you didn't do well initially.

I had the pleasure of taking Lightning for Mejo-341. He made law material understandable and digestible for someone who has no background knowledge of it. He had great communication, was open to questions, and quickly gave us our grades back. You can tell when someone is meant to be a professor---and Lightning is one of those gems!

MEJO341 is no joke, so do yourself a favor and take it with Lightening. Grades consisted of four quizzes, three exams, and some extra credit. Awesome person - super smart, caring, and engaging. Brings dog to class!

I've never rated a professor on here but I MUST rate Lightning. IF I COULD TAKE EVERY CLASS WITH HIM I WOULD. He makes the information so digestible, holds exam review sessions before each exam that basically tell you what to study and genuinely cares about the success of his students so. much. his dog Bert is adorable and he brings him to class.

I loveeee Lightning!!! HANDS DOWN BEST professor at the j school. He let us color in class, got us all starbucks gift cards and always brought his dog to class ALL WHILE teaching us the material in the most knowledgable and engaging way. I LOVE YOU LIGHTNING!!

If you have the opportunity to take this Maymester course in South Korea with Lightning, don't miss it! He is hilarious and organizes fascinating industry visits to a wide array of Korean companies. Getting credit while traveling with such a fun professor makes this the best class in the Hussman School.

AMAZING PROFESSOR!! 10000% recommend. Not only are the lectures engaging, but Professor Czabovsky really cares about his students and puts in the effort to get to know each of them. We only had two papers the whole semester; they took a lot of time and detail, but they were so worth it in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lightening was awesome. I will for sure take another class of his. He is super caring and makes things interesting. He really cares about his students.
I could write an essay on how incredible he is. I LOVE YOU LIGHTNING

Lightning is one of the kindest most compassionate professors in the entire world. He cares SO MUCH about his students and wants the best for everyone. He gives extra credit all the time and brings snacks and has pizza parties. So qualified and smart, I adore him more than anything ever. Not a hard grader

Joe is one of the best professor at Hussman school who really cares about his students. He devotes himself in office hours with any kind of concerns or helps that students have. He grades fairly and has a clear criteria on grading. So don't worry so much about your grade and just try to have fun and learn something from his classes.

Joe is incredible. Cares about his students in and out of the classroom! Makes himself available for questions and is so helpful with feedback on assignments. Wants to help you succeed! Bonus points for humor.
A lovely man who wants everyone to do well. I recommend him and the class in general

Joe is a great professor! His exams are straight-forward and he is very accessible outside of class. I'm taking MEJO 340 over the summer with him and he has made the course load manageable. There is required reading (~25 pages per night) but he expands on/explains the readings in class. I would definitely recommend him for MEJO 340.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Joe is the best. If you do not take a class with him then you are making a mistake. This class focused on media in Asia and it was so interesting. I learned so much about another part of the world. The work is not too difficult but you need to stay on top of it. Best professor at UNC.

Joe is so amazing and one of my favorite professors! He is so caring and knowledgeable about all things PR. I learned so much in his class and always felt comfortable participating and asking for help. He truly wants the best for his students and even gave us Starbucks gift cards during finals. I would for sure take another class with him!

JOE IS A KING. One of the best professors, by far, I have ever had. He encourages participation but gets that we all got things going on. Fair grader and SO nice. He also split the work in half b/c of COVID stress and got our class coffee (sent gift cards) AND did social distancing at maple view. cannot recommend this guy enough.

THE. BEST. If you are a UNC media and journalism major, do not graduate without taking one of his classes. The most caring professor at Carolina and an awesome teacher in general. Wish I could take classes with him every semester.

Joe is an absolute gem! He gives great feedback and is an awesome lecturer. He is so kind and caring and truly wants his students to succeed. Make sure you actually buy the right version of the textbook because having access to the cases is super important for class discussion, midterm, and final! 10/10 would recommend Joe for MEJO 531!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hands-down the best professor at Carolina. Cabowksy is literally incredible. Lectures are so much fun if you participate and you learn so many valuable professional skills. If you put in the time and effort, you will get a good grade. You're missing out if you don't take 531 with Cabowsky.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Joe is the man, you understand? His classes involve a lot of participation but it definitely benefits the class and for your assignments as well. The feedback that is provided during his office hours is CRUCIAL for success. He is extremely accessible outside of class for any help that is needed. Overall, one of the best professors at UNC!

Joe is SO sweet. I wish this class hadn't been moved online last semester because I could tell I was really going to enjoy learning from him. He is such a kindhearted human & he truly cares about his students. He assigns interesting homework & likes to "shake things up" from a typical class. He isn't easy, but he is fair, and I would recommend him!

Joe is one of the best professors I've had. He is really knowledgeable about all sorts of areas of PR and I learned a lot from his class. He really cares about his students and actually makes you want to show up and learn. 12/10 loved his class and love him.

The most caring and accomodating professor I have had, he is really invested in student success and wellbeing and leads a very interesting and interactive class that I really enjoyed attending. Lots of good career advice as well.
LOVE Joe!!! One of my favorite teachers at UNC. He's very knowledgeable and makes lectures interesting by bringing in cool examples and case studies. Definitively take his class.

Really nice prof. The lectures are really boring, but he really knows his stuff. Exams are trickier than you would think. I pulled out a B on the first one after starting studying the night before. There's a big group project and you're randomly assigned to groups, so as long as everyone does stuff you will be ok. Offers extra credit.
Gives extra credit which is nice, really boring lectures he just talks the whole time, strict attendance requirement, and just so much busy work
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DeFreese's voice is the most monotone, boring voice ever. The content in this class is organized a little bit oddly and could be done better. It is just about a bunch of different theories you need to memorize. This class is one of worst classes I've taken at unc. Also, there is a big group project that is so busy work.
exams are trick questions and you must memorize every slide. average was a 65 for exam 1. he makes the class harder than it needs to be. dont take
