JD is a really good professor. He's very understanding and responds quickly to emails. He also grades really quickly. Our exam grades were released the afternoon after we took the test. Class can be challenging and instructions aren't always the clearest for the big group project. Exams are fair but not the easiest.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Defreese is so kind and a great professor! He is a quick grader and gives you feedback to improve on future assignments. Class was group project heavy, but if you get a good group you are fine and he is not too harsh on the group papers or presentation. Tests straightforward. Groups made doing class assignments easier. Take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of the best professors in the department IMO. Definitely recommend!

I love Dr. DeFreese and would take another class with him. He is very understanding of students! Despite having a pretty tough attendance requirement, he really cares about the material he teaches and makes class engaging.
I really enjoyed his class. And he's just a nice guy.

Defreese is definitely one of the dryest lecturers I've had, but he knows what he's talking about. I just sometimes find it difficult to stay engaged. The class is broken into groups which honestly is helpful and I enjoyed talking to them. The semester long project is a bit of a pain, but not too hard, nor graded too harshly.

Quizzes are straightforward, with the answers coming from the textbook. The group project can be daunting but very manageable. The groups are randomly assigned. Exams are fair. For exams, make sure you understand the models discussed in the lecture well. Extra credit is offered. Dr.DeFreese is very understanding and patient, so reach out.

I liked 181, but be prepared to read the textbook and turn in an assignment before each class. There's also a semester long group project, which was frustrating at times. All exams given were fair in my opinion. He is an understanding individual and is willing to work with you to accommodate your needs outside of class or his office hours!

I loved Dr. Defreese, his lectures were straightforward and exams matched the material presented in them. Lots of low-stakes assignments that you pretty much will get credit for if completed. There is a big group project that is considerable for grades but if you have a good group (assigned) you'll be fine. Take with Defreese if you can!

Recommend taking this class with the other professor. If you are not a good test taker don't take this class. Test were made hard for no reason. I made a 100% on every quiz and most assignments outside of class besides a few and receive partial credit with no feedback. If you get a bad group for the semester long group project then good luck.

Such a great professor! He gives extra credit, which I wish I had taken advantage of earlier. Quizzes are easy, straight from the textbook. Most assignments are group work (assignment groups). Just make sure to put effort into having good communication within the group. Overall wonderful class!

Overall, Dr. DeFreese is a good professor. He gives a lot of examples to understand the material. He is a fast talker so be ready for that. The tests are mainly based on memorization and being able to apply the material to "real life situations". This class I group work heavy also. Overall, other than exams this class is easy its not really to much

Dr. DeFreese was an OK lecturer, if I could do it again I would take this class with Ling Beisecker. She did a guest lecture for our class and she was much more engaging and interesting. The class is based around group work (groups are chosen for you), which was sometimes difficult but overall fun. The exams were worded poorly and were difficult.

Everything was pretty easy except for the tests. Even though I studied a few days in advance, the tests were heavily memorization-based, which I struggled with. My test average was in the mid 80's and it brought me from an A to an A-. There is a group lab project and partners are random and it is relatively time-consuming. Overall an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Defresse is a great choice for 181. The class is lecture and terminology heavy, but it's not conceptually difficult, just a lot of memorization. Not a huge fan of the group project, but it's manageable and graded easily. He seems super serious but he does care about his students. Do the extra credit! Mandatory attendance (you can miss 3 classes).

Dr. DeFreese is a great professor, although his lectures can be a little boring. There is a group project which takes most of the semester and a presentation. Two exams and a final, which is cumulative. I would take a class by him again, just really did not like the group project.

One of the easiest classes I've taken. All exams come from in class slides. I got a B+ cause I never studied but if you put in like 3 days to prepare for each exam it's an easy A. A lot of your grade is a group project. 
Homeworks take like 2 seconds. Genuinely enjoyed this class. Dr. Defreese is a nice, interesting professor

Dr. Defreese's class is a little lecture heavy, but the material is interesting and easy to understand. Tests and quizzes aren't bad if you are paying attention and doing your work! Definitely recommend him for 181.

Defreese is really kind and caring and his class is pretty easy but also, interesting! There is one group project which is difficult over Zoom. He takes attendance every day so be sure to go to class but all powerpoints are posted and tests/quizzes are straight from the powerpoints.

Prof JD is super chill... class is so easy. Attendance is taken, so go to class and you will do fine on the exam. Very sports psych and super interesting. A lot is common sense just elaborated upon. Genuinely enjoyed this class. SUPER EASY AND INTERESTING!!
The class was easy, but the group projects were annoying, especially if you don't have good group members because you all get graded for their poor work.

DeFreese genuinely loves what he does and this is conveyed through his lectures. His exams are not hard as long as you study the material and read the textbook. He's willing to work with you to make sure you understand the concepts and get the best experience out of his class.

Dr. DeFreese is a kind man and is very knowledgable in the subject. Despite COVID-19, he was still easily accessible via email and answered questions to the best of his knowledge. There is a lot of group work, but I had a good group. Quizzes/tests are straightforward from his lectures. Attendance is important and there are EC opportunities.

I feel like its probably unfair to rate a professor under these circumstances with COVID and everything being virtual. However, In this particular course I thought it was very odd the amount of group work we were made do. I have never done so much group work in a normal classroom much less in a virtual one. This made things very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He gives lots of group work & projects but they're not hard. His quizzes are from textbook but exams are from slides, questions are always direct, he doesn't try to trick you. Dr. Defreese really cares about his students and the material is interesting, he gives so many opportunities for extra credit, overall a great guy!

Dr. DeFreese really cares about his subject and his students! He is very personable and understanding. The test questions come form the slides and he does not try to trick you. The quizzes are very simple but you will need the textbook. The group work/papers are not graded incredibly hard, either. He also gives out EC throughout the semester!

a pretty easy class. The exams were straight from the power points, and a lot of the class material is common sense. There are a lot of opportunities for extra credit. If you go to class, pay attention in lecture, and study a little you should do fine. The group projects are annoying, but they aren't graded too hard.

The class is mostly common sense. Simply go to class and pay attention and you will succeed. The textbook is used for weekly quizzes (not hard). He is not the most exciting man and a lot of the material is redundant. There is a lot of group work interaction but they again are very easy assignments.

The content makes a lot of sense but it is the terminology and theories that make it hard. I got a 76 on a test and still got an A so one thing doesn't define you. If you get a good group that makes all the difference. He grades the papers pretty easily, the tests are harder, but they're all MC. need to read/skim well the textbook for the quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Defreese is a fine teacher. He will lecture all class which yes can be boring, but the content is simple and easy to understand. You WILL have to read the book, but if you do a chapter a week you'll be fine. This class has a heavy emphasis on group work. While it can suck if you have an unmotivated group, it can also make things a ton easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: At the beginning of the semester you're put into groups that you will write two papers and do one presentation with throughout the semester along with other small in-class assignments. Test are relatively easy and straightforward as long as you pay attention in class. Very approachable & nice professor who clearly cares about his students.

The class is very group work heavy, but the assignments are basically just busy work (not difficult). The tests are very fair, based mostly off class material, all MC, and honestly very easy if you just review the slides and have a clear understanding of definitions. DeFreese is easy to talk to and gives many opportunities for extra credit. 10/10

This is perhaps one of the most boring classes I have ever taken. All of the information seems super redundant and most of the information is very general and common sense. However, JD makes the exams very specific to counteract the "common sense" material. Most of the class is doing pointless group work since he doesn't have a ton to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Such a boring lecturer. Also the class information is boring and kind of a joke. Sport psychology isn't a real subject and shouldn't be included in the major. Avoid this class if you can.

He's a good professor and was accessible. Lectures were kind of boring but the material was interesting so it was fine. A ton of group work and group projects but overall it helped my grade. Exams were kind of hard just because it was a lot of material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: One of the worst classes I've taken at UNC. Probably the most boring professor. Focuses too much on useless group work when the room isn't even set up to work in groups. Makes the tests extra hard for no reason. This class is the reason I'm dropping the EXSS major

He is the only one that teaches EXSS 181. DO NOT, I repeat, DO NOT take this class for granted. I went in thinking this class was easy, when it definitely is not. Tests are hard and I did worse than I thought I would in this class. He is a good lecturer and makes for a lot of group projects. There are peer evals, so make sure you contribute.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The original computa. Derek can do whatever you put your mind to. Congrats bud, you've been Derek'd
He "touched" me
Every class he encouraged us to get "snug" with our classmates. He would then pretend to be a classmate.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Wow, Derek!!!!!
Derek is just a stand up man. His lectures are VERY "hands-on" and I find you learn a lot that way. Highly recommend, but be prepared to "break a sweat" to get good grades in this class.
He really cooked my goose with his stiff grading system. However, his stiff grading system opened my eyes to the world of "responsible" "research".
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Desire is a great professor and also a joy to talk to. He made econometrics enjoyable to learn and his problem sets, although somewhat challenging, are great review material. I would highly recommend you study and understand the problem sets and attend each class since he goes through important math proofs.
The exams felt very long and math/proof and he does not curve
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ECON 470 is very difficult, no matter who you take it with. Kedagni was a really nice guy, but resources were super limited outside of class. Thankfully, I passed/failed this course because the average on the final was a 70 with no curving whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I didn't like Econ 400, but Kedagni made me love econometrics! You have to go to class, since he takes attendance for a grade and includes concepts from lectures on exams. He's a chalkboard lecturer, which isn't everyone's cup of tea. My one gripe is that the midterms are way too long. However, their content isn't difficult. You just have to study.

Desire is a good lecturer and kind to students. Easy to follow along with, and he doesn't expect you to do any complicated proofs. His exams can be (very) long, but are almost exactly like practice problems, and all exams are graded out of 100 points but have at least 10 bonus points on them. Good option for a class as notorious as 470.

The average on the final was a 72. He refuses to curve anything in the class. His actual teaching style was not terrible, and a lot of the exams reused questions from the problem sets, but the fact that he did not curve a single test with the justification of "if 4-5 people get an A, the grades work" was terrible. The average class grade was a C+.
I took ECON 470 in fall 2023 and this course covers everything you need to know about linear regression. The pace of the class is very reasonable and Professor Kedagni's notes are easy to understand.
Probably the easiest 470 professor. The concepts in the class are not that complicated, he just grades the exams really strictly. Really nice guy to talk to in office hours.

Kedagni never made you feel bad if you asked to go over a topic again. Exams were p long but many problems were repeated from problem sets. So just study those solutions you'll be perfectly fine. He also works through problem sets in office hours. Attendance is taken but also there's not many resources outside of class anyway so don't skip!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Kédagni's lectures -- he's very enthusiastic about the material, making lectures very engaging. The problem sets are good practice for the exams, as the questions on the exams tend to resemble the homework questions. He also sometimes pulls questions from the textbook, so looking at some textbook problems is helpful too.

ECON 470 is hard no matter the professor, Kedagni has some issues with pacing/understanding our prior exposure but has the right idea. Attendance is mandatory and the lectures are helpful for actually applying what you learn, but working through textbook problems will help on the exams. Sometimes gives bonus points for answering questions in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Highly recommend taking 470 with a different professor. The class was disorganized and we didn't get through much of the material, which was super frustrating. The exams were really similar to the homework which was nice, but the lectures were really dull and overall left me with little new knowledge about the topic.

Must unorganized professor I have had. Was supposed to cover 6 chapters of material but only got through 4. Required to learn the other 1/3 of class material for the final independently during the last week of the course. Would not recommend this course for anyone, just wait and take 470 with different professor.

I took the first version of his FYS, so some disorganization could be expected. His lectures are intriguing, however, and the course taught me a lot even though I am not a language major. He is caring and not a tough grader as long as you participate and make an effort to stay engaged in class.

*PORT 203*
I had Pedro for both 102 and 203, and both semesters he helped a lot with learning. He is very passionate about us learning the language, and grades fairly if you at least attempt to speak and write in  portuguese. He relies a lot on participation in class, but will still take the time to explain confusing concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Was surprised at the one 3-star review. All languages classes are flipped at UNC, and you are not going to find a calmer-paced learning schedule than any of UNC's Portuguese classes.

Pedro is an excellent prof. You NEED to look at the vocab before each class, but it's a very reasonable amount of content. Lots of participation which truly helps.

pedro relies heavily on the flipped format for learning, so if you struggle with learning on your own with the textbook, be sure to visit office hours for questions! however, he is available during class times for you to ask questions, he regularly asks if there are concepts you don't understand, and takes the time to explain in depth.

Participation heavy. Readings are due each class, they tend to get a little long. Deadlines shift around often which may seem good at first glance, but it does get frustrating if you have a job and are calling out for important dates (presentations and such). Set up meetings in advance because office hours fill up!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class has readings, an essay, and presentation projects. Katie clearly cares about making the class interesting and informative. Grading is quite fair but the class still requires work and office hours are helpful. A lot of the work for the class comes later in the semester, so be prepared for the workload at the end.

You can tell she's very passionate about what she teaches and only wants you to succeed. If you put in the work and listen in class then you'll be fine. I will say that it is homework heavy, so a good amount of readings that can be quite difficult to understand.
amazing, would take.

I really enjoyed her teaching honestly, very enjoyable and the way that she would make the content was engaging. I would say that there was a lot of reading at times even though she tried to get the readings as short as possible. She's very engaged and passionate about the material and wants us to do the best we can in the class.

This is for 102 but there wasn't an option. Katie is very kind, accessible, and fun in class. Heavy emphasis on classroom discussion and participation. Easy to get B+/A-, not an easy A due to lots of reading and high expectations for understanding. I really loved this class and feel like I learned a lot about philosophy and good communication!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Deavon is genuinely one of my favorite prof! She is so caring/accommodating to everyone's needs. She'll work w/ you if you talk to her. She has a clear outline of what she expects. There are 1-3 readings each week (some are dense some not), video diaries, no exams, a final presentation, 3 big papers, + student facilitations. TAKE HER CLASS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Katie clearly cares about her students and classes. While sometimes a little disorganized, she does not hesitate to adjust class or grades around it. Very generous with deadlines and assignments. Clearly loves philosophy and wants her students to learn. She really just wants people to participate, discuss, and ask questions. Would highly recommend!

I really enjoyed bioethics, not just the content of the course but also the materials Katie used to teach.  I loved the class was hands on and discussion based. I felt like I got what I brought in. I worked hard and got a grade that reflected that work. She is a fair grader, but it is def not a class you can coast through.

Katie genuinely cares about your learning. She focuses a ton on small group discussions and truly values every idea brought forward in class. When discussions weren't flowing she always adapts and gets people involved, super engaging and genuinely cares about her classroom environment and student success.

Topics in this class were a bit confusing, and her explanations were super long but I felt like I never gained much insight. Our first paper went well, but it was confusing when it came to the final paper draft as we got the rubric 4 hours before the deadline. While unorganized, she was understanding and fun in lecture.

Katie offers an inspiring list of topics and approaches them in a contagiously enthusiastic manner. Sometimes her lectures are overly "improvised" as she attempts to respond to whatever question someone raises. She may appear a bit disorganized, but at the end of the day she's a very charitable grader and the course overall was pretty low-stake.

Great person, Awful professor. Katie is terribly disorganized, doesn't tell her students what is expected of them, then proceeds to grade harshly. She doesn't do a good job providing advice and feedback on the papers, which make up most of the grade, and rarely has time to meet before big assignments are due. Would not recommend this experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment:
absolutely goated. class is very discussion and small group heavy, and she cares a lot about students' learning. no midterm and the final is just a presentation. class was pretty disorganized, but this was her first sem at unc, so i doubt it'd be an issue in the future.
idk why people are wining about her grading; it's pretty average in difficulty
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Katie is a little disorganized and grades go in late. There are lots of readings in this class (PHIL 143). There is also a lot of writing and your grade is determined by this. The final exam was extremely easy (a really short presentation). As long as you stay on top of the work and put effort into your papers, you should succeed in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: There is no grading criteria so you will never know what she wants. So, so disorganized. It almost feels like she has never taught before, everything is so unclear in this class. Do NOT take it. I have no idea what my grade is in the class because she's graded like 1 assignment total. Avoid at all costs. Class consists of random tangents.

He does not seem to care for our success. We do much of the learning ourselves so he is essentially the placeholder that contributes relatively little to our understanding. The actual learning is done during the 3-hour lab sessions. Would not recommend the class but there is a very limited selection of instructors here who teach this, so no choice.

Dr. Deardorff was a bad explainer so I mainly had to learn through Studio labs, my peers, or Dr. Hansen. Practice exams and exam prep sessions are the most helpful when studying. Exams were quite long compared to the 50 min we had, so making a mistake could cost you time.

First time taking physics, but it was manageable with freshman courseload. Gives multiple homeworks/warmups a week. Office hours and the online vectorious worksheets helped me most to prepare for exams. Exams were hard, but Dr. Deardorff offers extra credit for improved performance. Studio takes a lot of time. Final was the easiest exam for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He was ok. I preferred the other professor (Dr. Hansen). Participation is SUPER important so go to all the labs/lectures. Labs were hard. I failed every exam, but I was able to get a 70 at the end with help from CramBetter and practice problems. If you're not doing well, it's ok just try to get as many points as possible.

Exams are only 50% of your grade so studio (25%) really helps bring your grade up. Partial credit is generous, but the class is very self-taught. Manageable as a freshman. 70% of the class got a B or higher, ~75% class average on exams. Utilise practice exams, Vectorious problems, and Friday exam prep sessions.

The exams are graded well (lots partial), so it is possible to get an A. However, Deardorf is one of the most condescending and rude professors I have ever had. Would not be kind to students when they answered incorrectly in class. When 9% of the class got a question right on an exam he told us we needed to study more...
He was fair. The class is hard and he understands that, he wants you to succeed but you have to put in the work for that to happen.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good professor, sometimes has a bit of an attitude but overall the exams were very fair. Hw was harder than exams and the practice exams he gives out are very similar to the actual midterms so just focus on those. Use exam preps and Vectorious as well. Would recommend to time yourself taking practice exams to get urself used to that 50 min limit:)

Lectures aren't helpful, definitely a self learn class. If you work hard in studying/keeping up with content the test questions are pretty fair, but the 50 minute time limit isn't nearly enough to finish. No curves nor rounding grades, the class is fast paced but very organized. Duane is nice and responsive to emails! I was super close to an A- :(

I didn't go to class so can't say much abt the professor. The class was hard but not impossible. Attend vectorious review sessions consistently, do the homework, and do well on studio assignments (they really cushion your grade). Attendance matters but we could also sign an attendance sheet at the end of class, so I just did that the entire sem.

Very smart professor but it hinders his lecturing ability in that he expects you to understand everything at the same level as he does. The class is challenging but navigable if you're willing to devote the time to it; the units build on each other to an extent. Studio and Vectorious sessions are super helpful, just find a group you work well with.

If you do not have a background in physics the class will be tough. I also advise against taking this course with a stem heavy semester, you will have to teach YOURSELF ALL of the material. You don't learn in class, in fact he says that. Instead, you learn in lab how to do the problems and if your group mates aren't willing to help you learn, GG's.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Deardorff is not a good lecturer, but he genuinely wants you to succeed in his class. But the class is extremely organized, and he is extremely responsive via email concerning absences and excusing missed work/class. The exams were a little unfair but doable. I was super scared of taking physics at UNC, but it wasn't bad with Deardorff!

Dead serious this guy is the worst professor Ive ever had. I would not take him if again if my life depended on it. This guy is horrible at teaching. I learned absolutely nothing in his lectures and had to basically use ChatGPT to teach me everything. He makes friday exam prep session mandatory but they just make everyone in the class feel stupid

Writing this as I actively crash out abt how unprepared I am for the final. The lectures don't go into the depth that you are asked to apply the material on the homeworks and exams. Thankfully the midterms are only 10% each, otherwise I'd be failing. Wouldn't recommend taking this class at all if you have no prior knowledge bc you'll get no help.

This dude stinks. I was in the ER with a university-authorized absence, and I couldn't make up the missed attendance and lab. Lectures are not helpful; you can tell he is very intelligent, but his ability to teach students is nonexistent. You will be fine in this class with a strong math/physics background (take calc first, you premeds!).
Awful lecturer, mean to students, rushes through lectures, and never shows up in Studio. His co-lecturer, John Hansen, was much better.
He is the worst lecturer to ever exist. He reads exactly what is on the slide, shows no work for any questions, and moves on. You have to teach yourself the entire class.

Not too bad but his atitude and approach to teaching a physics class rubbed many people the wrong way. Seems like Dr. Hansen put more effort and actually cared about teaching the material where as most of the time I felt Dr. Deardorff just read from the slides and briefly explained some things. Study the material/ do practice exams and you're good.

duane would be a great professional juggler. he is not a good professional professor. extremely condenscending in both emails and lectures and manages to make simple concepts confusing. had a different lecturer for two months and the class did better than previous semesters on the second exam.

I think Dr. Deardorff is a lovely person, and he seems very sweet outside of the context of PHYS-114. He is very condescending and snappy in lecture, and is not the most effective at teaching the material. Most of his class is self-taught with the help of TA office hours because the TAs seem very sympathetic about how the class is run.

Deardorff does not explain the material at all and is very condescending. He acts like the material is all common sense and expects us to solve problems in seconds and answer them in class (where the majority of the class then answers wrong). He seems like a decent person but is truly a terrible professor.

Get ready to self-study the whole class. The content itself isn't hard but he cannot teach, and then gets mad when we don't do well on exam prep sessions. Only surviving because I have prior physics experience. Only positive is that the style of questions on the practice exams are similar to the midterms.

I've never felt a need to rate a professor before until taking this class. Professor Deardorff is extremely condescending and passive agressive in lecture and emails. He speeds through slides without any explanation and expects us to know the answer and gets mad when we are not doing well on poll everywhere or the Friday exam prep sessions.
Don't take this guy. Very condescending
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Deardorff didn't actually teach, so this is just about 114 in general. The course has a lot of content, and it's important to stay up to date. However, if you can manage to do all the assignments, readings, and studios, the course is actually relatively easy. The hardest part is just staying on top of things. Be disciplined and you got it!

Professor Deardorff doesn't actually teach; he is just the coordinator. That being said, he is still responsive to emails and kind enough to help you if you need it. However, this class can be quite difficult if you don't have physics knowledge upfront. It is fairly difficult, but I appreciate the little bits of EC provided.

Professor Deardorff is one of the most caring professors I've ever had. He truly wants his students to succeed, and goes the extra mile to help. He's super flexible and willing to meet with you outside of class, and also offers extra credit opportunities. About half of your grade is based on assignments, which takes some stress off of exams.
Professor Deardorff is pretty good at teaching physics to beginners in the subject, but he can be a little condescending, especially if you don't answer lecture poll questions.
Tests were generally fair and partial credit was generous. Duane's lectures were bad. I only went to lecture for attendance. The homeworks and studios is where you'll do all the learning.

Not a bad professor, but not a great professor either. This may be due to the fact that it is a large lecture. He essentially would read off of the slides and that was that. Dr. Deardorff is a lovely person though. Very kind and accommodating, but personally I would have liked more engaging lectures.
Tests were fair but lectures were confusing and did not help me learn content. You learn most from figuring out problems on your own in studio.
He is alright.

I put in hours studying for an exam and ended up with a stellar 39%. The cherry on top? A grueling fourteen-page practice test covered concepts that played hooky on the actual exam. In class, the instructor's "Only twenty percent got it right" prompts are met with crickets. It's like a silent comedy show, starring us as clueless characters!

Professor Dolan really teaches this class, and she is very difficult to understand as she just reads straight from the lecture slides! Note: Physics is probably a very difficult class not matter where you take it. The exam grades are not curved, your raw score is what will enter the grade book. Try to avoid taking this class at UNC if possible.

Dr. Deardorff did not directly give lectures. He was more of a coordinator, but he was very responsive to email even with a large class size. I don't think you have any other professor choices when it comes to introductory physics at UNC, but this class' difficulty is reasonable that any hardworking student can get an A in.
He is one of the meanest professors I have ever had, and he didn't even teach the class. He did the behind the scenes work, such as responding to emails, and he was so rude. AVOID!

Not bad, though he only lectured for the first (syllabus) lecture. He seems like a good guy the four times I have interacted with him. The class is difficult but if you pay attention to the slides, homework's, practice exams, and Vectorious, you should be good! Also, don't forget to do the warm ups, they are easy to miss.
Take it at CCCC, Dolan and Deardorff are the absolute worst. Insane homework due everyday, studios are intense and exams murder hopes and dreams.

Exams are quite unfair. This is one of those classes that makes you wonder why you chose UNC. Professors appear more concerned with making their department seem competitive than you learning introductory physics. Exam 2 class average was 52 and median was 50. They did curve, but those raw scores are absolutely insane for an intro class. Avoid.

exams are extremely difficult and often so unlike anything we have seen or are given that studying becomes futile at a point. says it is to better challenge us to understand the content conceptually but if that were true our other assignments like HW and studio would reflect it. does curve slightly. also rarely lectures, it was usually Dimitri
Do not take this professor. Professor does is not very helpful, not really good at explaining. Take this class with someone else please.

When I took this course, this man did not do anything to help students. He simply sent out email reminders about suggestions to improve your grade and inputted grades into the system. He is also very insensitive and is a culturally incompetent person. I would not waste your time to meet with him or anyone in this department. Take physics elsewhere

Duane doesn't seem to care about his students. The phys 114 instruction team was rude and condescending. When I asked questions I was met with "well this is easy" rather than an explanation. Studio is really the only place you learn, lecture is useless other than participation points.

PHYS 510 is a one credit hour teaching seminar, so different from the classes he usually teaches, but he did a fantastic job at explaining concepts, getting us involved, and I really felt my teaching improve tremendously over the course of the semester. There's kind of a lot of work for 1 credit hour, but still less than a 3 credit class.

Actually the worst. The entire class does poorly on exams due to bad questions he 'admits' it by saying we should've done better but have 2 points extra (a TA told me this is his way of admitting when an exam is poorly written). Try and find someone else or take it over the summer if you can. A majority of the class got 0-50 on every midterm.
Physics is definitely a hard topic to teach, but Dr. Deardorff does a very engaging job. He obviously cares greatly about his students, and he is very understanding if something comes up.

Dr. Deardorff is a nice person but his lectures weren't very helpful. The practice questions we had during lecture didn't reflect the difficulty of the exams. The final exam was absolutely BRUTAL and it was much harder than the midterm exams. This is a challenging class and I started off fine, but mental/physical health concerns damaged my grade.

I only had positive experiences with him but I know other people complained about interacting with him through email. He was amicable in studio and was willing to patiently explain concepts repeatedly. Lectures were easy to follow but midterms were fairly difficult, and studio could be awful if you have a bad group.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Deardorff can be extremely rude through email and condescending in person. The idea is that a lecture teaches the material on the exam. You would think, that splitting the content into 3 lecturers, that they would be able to find a way to teach the material well and within a lecture time frame. If not, that says it needs to be taught longer.
Dr. Deardorff is the rudest professor I've ever had. He only started being nice after he realized I wasn't an idiot.

He's a decent lecturer and I personally have not experienced him being rude, he just is very dry and can come across as blunt. He responds quickly to emails (like within hours usually). But, he grades SO nitpicky and you can lose points from using an extra significant figure. You won't follow the lectures well if you don't do the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: pretty much the opposite of everything I selected:)

Physics at UNC is horrible. However, this professor is even worse. I did not think that I would have a worst physics teacher than my physics 1, but boy was I wrong. He is rude and not understanding. Take my advice and dont take any physics at UNC. many people in my class were afraid to email him just because of how rude and disrespectful he is.

Dr. Deardorff is so much different than some of these reviews describe him to be. I always take RMP reviews with a grain of salt. He is so caring about his students and goes out of his way to help them. During class, he pays a lot of attention to what his students need, and outside of class, you can expect to hear back from him very quickly.

Dr Deardoff was never clear with his answers in the QnA sessions we had. The exams for the course were also ridiculous, so much so that 2-3 students would score well out of 300 and that is a source of pride for the phys115 professor team this semester. Very disappointed.

Did everything possible to screw up students during an already screwed over semester. Obviously smart but does not know how to teach or explain basic concepts to students not familiar with this type of subject matter. Take it with someone else

I really liked Dr. Deardorff and always found him to be approachable outside of the classroom. The exams definitely required some preparation, but were fair and never insanely hard. Overall, I would recommend Dr. Deardorff and had a good experience in his class

Deardorff is unnecessarily rude, condescending, and demonstrates little to no empathy or compassion for his students. His emails are always laced with sarcasm and hostility, making students scared to communicate with him. Students with the most dire situations have reached out to him, and they're just slapped in the face with his inflexibility.

Unnecessarily hard tests and it is surprising how upper level 400 STEM classes are easier than this introductory level 2 physics class. The physics department itself is bad at UNC and Dr. Deardorff is rude at some times despite the pandemic. We also got points off for not putting our name down on our tests which is very stingy of them. Dont take.

If you are not majoring in physics or if you are not required to take this class, don't take it because it is useless. This class gave me anxiety and fear throughout my entire semester. I worked so hard and I spent all of my time completing about 124 papers(assignment, quizzes, exams, warm-up questions, lab work...) and I ended up with a C-.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: I thought I liked Dr. Deardorff, he's a good lecturer & made physics about as simple it could be. Yet at the end, after frequenting his OH through the semester, I asked if he could write me a rec letter & he said "you got a B+, it's not like I could write anything good", the rest of the convo was condescending and uncomfortable. A bad day? Idk
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Deardorff clearly knows his stuff, but sometimes it seems he forgets this is an intro, non-major course. He goes quickly through material, even when it's clear we don't understand it. I appreciate how much he cares, but his half of the lectures were much less clear. Studios can be long but they're productive, and tests are challenging but fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is probably an unpopular opinion but I actually like 115 better than 114. Deardorff is very caring for your success. Studios were helpful but are super long and seated exams are based on what you learn in studio and some similar to the homework. I would have never thought that I would enjoy physics!

Dr. Deardorff is a solid prof for PHYS 115. His lectures were pretty good, although I thought he went too fast at times. The class is structured fairly with a bit of extra credit built in, which is really nice. Overall not a terrible class if you put in some work, although I found the concepts harder than 114

I think Dr. Deardorff gets a bad rap. I found his lectures clear & engaging, and he was always so kind and helpful. Exams are very generous with points. Studios are tough but designed to make you actually engage with the material and learn. Dr. Deardorff will spend as much time with you as you need to understand the material (esp in studio)
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: PHYS 118 is incredibly hard if you don't have a physics background, but it's doable if you do all the homework, try in your studio, and get help when you need it.

His lectures are very vague, and then the tests are in depth questions that you might have seen maybe once in a homework that you did three weeks ago. The wording on his exams is meant to trip you up. He is a bit condescending when the class does overall very bad on the exam, saying "the exam was very easy," and will not really work with you.

If you don't have to take this class, don't. Surface level lecture for intense in-depth exams. Rarely shows calculations (during lecture, where it honestly matters more) and talks instead. When he does show calculations (in studios), they're over the top and almost never show up on the exams. Get some physics background if you must take him.
wasnt helpful, you have to teach yourself. He didnt finish lecture bc he ran out of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Solid professor: reasonable grading standards, and one of the better that I've had. Very caring. He writes thought-provoking test questions which require critical thinking; this was my favorite part of the class. His explanations and lectures were long-winded at times. But overall, good pick.

Its obvious that Professor Deardorff means well and is a nice guy, but he is not good at explaining things and answering questions. I'm guessing that the time pressure of the summer session must have made him spend less time explaining things than normal, so I would not recommend taking him over the summer. He is also condescending at times

Dr. Deardorff's lectures left a bit to be desired. His explanations were okay but he was bad at answering questions. He definitely seemed to want his students to learn, but was simply not the best at conveying the information sometimes. This class will be hard no matter who you take it with though, so Deardorff is overall not a bad choice.
Good guy who really cares, just ask questions!
The way he explains things isn't always clear, but he cares and is approachable. Class is made more difficult than it should be - seems they are always inventing new problems to trip you up.

He is a very caring and enthusiastic professor. He makes a pretty confusing class enjoyable for all of the students. You can tell he truly loves what he does. Read the material to get a better understanding of the topics because it will help the concepts stick better to your brain. Study the practice exams and you should be good.

Deardorff is actually a great professor. He does a really good job to help you understand physics, and in a fun and engaging way. Go to his office hours, and he will really help you understand the material much better. Do not be afraid to ask questions in his lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr D is a gem for studio and gives subtle hints at test questions all the time. He likes to spurt some fun in when he can, he answers questions pretty transparently, but expects good work. I'd take his class again, no doubt.

He is a great lecturer, and he explains topics pretty well. He has fun anecdotes and cheesy demos, but he helped structure this class in a way that optimizes learning. This is still a very hard class with difficult material--if you don't put in the work outside of class you will not do well. Good professor for an 8AM class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very passionate which is great but poor lecturer. Over complicates things and relies too heavily on his toys. It keeps you awake in class but I don't care if he can juggle or not, he needs to explain the concepts better. He gets his directions messed up and confuses himself and us.

Solid choice for a physics teacher. Class is co-taught and is reversed classroom so he only taught 2 weeks a month and didn't lecture that much. Can be kind of rude in a funny way but he can juggle so class was entertaining.

Professor Deardorff is hilarious and tried to be as helpful as he could in class. Nevertheless, PHYS118 is just a hard course of especially first-year students and needs a lot effort to get a good score in test. Professor Deardorff also had good grasp in juggling balls to demonstrate gravitational acceleration. Make sure you search him on youtube!

Dr. Deardorff was a great introduction to college physics. He was funny and lighthearted (and a little nerdy) but really wanted students to understand the material. It's a tough course, so taking advantage of office hours and TA time in studios is important. He was very organize. Tests were fair and predictable, but still challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Disappointed. Professor claims to have a degree in Physics Ed but gives unclear lectures. Makes errors frequently.

Very passionate about his field, but his tests are tough. I've taken advanced courses in the other sciences, but it was nothing like this. Physics everyday is a drain, and there's so much homework that is only moderately helpful. Studio is long and tedious but good for your grade if you do well.
I do not like him. He expects us to have this wide array of knowledge of the world and then gets disappointed when we dont know some random fact. Third test was absolutely impossible.

Great Lecturer and really tries to help you learn the material. Took the scale up version which is definitely better than the normal lecture. Inconsistent grading but it's not his fault that the TA's suck.

Extremely helpful outside of class; would recommend. You get out of it what you put into it. Took the SCALE-UP version, which I considered extremely helpful compared to normal lectures. SCALE-UP makes it easy to ask questions and to receive help from one of the two professors or two TAs (all in class at the same time).

Avoid the scale up classes for your own good.  Basically nothing is taught in these classes and you are responsible for not only teaching yourself all of the material outside of class, but also a maddening amount of short and long lab reports and homework assignments.  Class attendance is mandatory for some reason, despite being completely useless.

Awesome professor!  Has a wonderful way of taking difficult physics concepts and making them understandable.... very committed and dedicated to teaching and is one of the best physics professors I've encountered. Makes physics quite interesting and even fun.  Very willing to work with students and answer questions. Really cares about students.

Duane is an amazing teacher for those who want to do well. He is always willing to work through confusion with you. Homework is intense and intro physics is not a class during the summer, considering we conver a chapter a day. Deardorff is, however, a passionate instructor who lives for learning. for the record, I'm no genius, I did well, not great

VERY boring and a major dork.  A lot of work comes along with this class, like multiple homework assignments a week. tests are hard and multiple choice because he doesn't word them right, or sometimes doesn't put the correct answer as a choice.

I don't have any issue with heavy accents but on top of that her PowerPoints don't outline anything. They have just questions without answers, and you have to try to decipher what she is saying with no visual aid. I am a visual learner, and not having the notes in writing on the PowerPoints in class made this class pretty much impossible.

Worst professor I've had. The class is easy, but she is very rude to students. Interrupted student presentations and was passive aggressive when the class expressed concerns about an unfair exam. You can do just fine in the class, but if there are other options for 581, I would absolutely avoid her. She's new to teaching so hopefully she improves.

Worst class I've taken in PLCY dept. Completely unclear grading criteria, awful instructions: 1 Q on midterm was only answered correctly by 1 person in the whole class and she said she "taught it well enough." Very rude, does not treat students with respect. Sure, I did learn something useful, but the environment was not supportive whatsoever.

Don't take this class. Bathia would contradict her own syllabus and get mad when students were confused. Harshest grading I've experienced in the PLCY department; the midterm average was in the 60s. She does not respond well to student questions or feedback. Overall, it's not a very welcoming learning environment.

Definitely the worst professor I have had at UNC. She seems aggravated when students ask questions or give answers (whether their answers are right or wrong). Her instructions for assignments are confusing, with no rubrics and inconsistent deadlines. The exams are graded very harshly and she takes points off even if you are correct.

I think Professor Kelly was great; however, the class had like a million readings for every class and we learned a lot of the content through readings which were supplemented by lectures, rather than the other way around. There is a lot of grade padding and she was very reasonable (and generous) with curves. So many readings though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I'm pretty sure people expected an easy course (as it used to be). The curriculum has been redesigned, so maybe thats why some assignments were graded a bit nit-picky at first. Later, they made efforts to improve our grades with extra credit and making the tests essay-based rather than MCQ. 2 exams, 1 final, mandatory attendance, in-class quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Not the most engaging professors - but the information is honestly common sense and just explained further. Graded by participation/attendance, quizzes, homework, two midterms, and a final. Honestly really easy class, quizzes were just on the reading and for the homeworks just don't LLM them and you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class itself isn't bad, but the professor's grading is excessively strict. Exams aren't hard, but they are short response and there are weekly reading quizzes, so stay on top of the readings.

She was so boring, but also so easy. I went to every single class, but was locked for maybe 20 minutes all semester. As long as you look at the slides the day before the test you are fine. This is such an easy class, but she is nitpicky about some of the homeworks which may be the reason for the bad reviews. The tests are the easiest things ever.
Really nitpicky grading from the professor. The class is relatively easy; it's just that the professor will point out every little thing "wrong" in your work and grade extremely subjectively.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class was only difficult because of the professor. The information taught is genuinely interesting, but the way the professor is so hard on clarity/punctuation when forcing students to write in a time crunch is asinine. Would only take if interested in the INLS major/minor. Really hope she changes how she approaches this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Diane is honestly such a good professors, the learning environment is fun and interactive which is helpful because the course is a little difficult but she makes it easy to do. Exams are open notes from your previous readings, attendance is mandatory and you will get extra credit. I would honestly take her again, she loves what she does
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Worst class i have ever taken at UNC., This woman single-handedly made me hate Information Science. INLS 201 was a nitpicky, terrible and useless course, She refuses to accommodate students, and seems to pride herself all the time. DO NOT TAKE!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The exams are based on really nitpicky concepts. Her lectures are boring. I hate the quizzes that start in the first 5 mins and just close, plus you never know when you will have a quiz. Lots of reading and just too much work

It was incredibly frustrating. I've never encountered such a ruthless professor at UNC. You can't get a good grade even though u put efforts already. She spent so much time on formalism that I felt like I wasn't learning anything useful. This class is incredibly difficult for an prerequisite, totally disaster
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Kelly is very kind and knows her stuff. Not a very interesting lecturer, but has all the answers and really cares about her students. Loves it when you participate. Lots of readings, but if you study hard for the tests then it's not hard to get a good grade.

Good teacher who is very straight forward with the information she is going to test you on. The lectures are not terribly interesting but she's very educated in the material and is always willing to stop and discuss in-depth any questions anyone has. She's not the most gripping/interesting professor but she's kind and explains the material well.

She was really chill, the class consisted of watching films and two people coming in with discussions questions about the movie for us to discuss. Shewouldstart of withlecture and thenwe wouldgo into discussion, butshewouldn't force peopleto participate although she did encourage it. Youcouldbring an indexcardfor everyquizandcheatsheet forthefinal.

This class is fairly easy, as there are not many assignments. The majority of the class is group projects, which make it more fun and interesting. Although class drags on and we often go off topic, Toni gives us everything we need to succeed in the class. I would definitely take this class for the english requirement.

Toni is a great and accommodating person, and cares for the wellbeing of us as students.  English 105i in the social sciences wasn't the most interesting for me as a STEM major, but Toni's class is very easy to follow along with regardless of your major.  I highly recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Toni just speaks at you in class with language complexity that many students can't understand. She is chill but her class drags on and is just to get the requirement done. As a stem major, I couldn't recommend it less. Maybe if you're business you would enjoy it more. Or if you know about Lord of the Rings, as that's all she talks about.

We covered all of the ENGL-105 curricula in the first month and spent the rest of the semester putting together conference papers. Toni gave us a lot of freedom, so I ended up having a great time researching a subject I had been interested in, but never had time to research before! If you have to take ENGL-105, take it with Toni!

They were not a great teacher to have first thing in the morning. Their lectures seemed to drag on and did not feel relevant to the PIT paper at all. But overall the class was easy, you do the assignment you'll get full credit. There is one big paper and you have to present it with a slideshow.

I loved Toni's class! She provides great feedback and was always super lenient with extraneous circumstances affecting assignments. I really felt like she cared about my success in and out of the classroom. The most caring professor I've had thus far at UNC. Also, the opportunity for the PIT conference in ENGL105 is one I wouldn't pass up.
GOAT

Very clear with instructions and gave really good advice. 3 main projects for the whole semester and was very accommodating. Considered the mental health and well being of students which was appreciated.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! You can tell he really cares about his students and is willing to accommodate. The class is very discussion based but if you don't feel comfortable speaking up in class he gives multiple opportunities to get those points. He also gives multiple extra credit opportunities and helps students prepare for exams!

Dr. DiSalvo is a super cool guy and really knows American history and judicial history. Very informative class but could be a little dry in lectures. He clearly cared about his students and was easy to talk to and ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor DiSalvo is awesome! The only reason I didn't rate him as a 5 is because I am personally not the biggest fan of the structure of the class. However, I know it could work very well for many others. Essentially, you read historical documents and take notes (not graded) outside of class and then spend the whole time in class discussing them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class wasn't hard but him and Professor Havice weren't the greatest instructors in my opinion. I appreciated their passion for Geography but a lot of time they were both borderline rude and made the class kinda uncomfortable sometimes when they'd call out students publicly or make snarky comments.

This class was so unbearable. Everybody was taking this as either a focus capacity or to fulfill their data science minor. They wanted us to be so dedicated to the topic so bad but no one cared. Such a boring class and attendance matters. Started picking on me for no reason towards the end of the semester in a 200 person class. Don't recommend.

Seems like a chill guy, but lots of condescending comments. Blamed wifi. Expect you to devote your life to geography in a 100 level class for data science majors. THE WORLD DOESNT REVOLVE AROUND GEOGRAPHY. Expect you to come to class having done the readings but not doing that. So i just didn't go a lot of times. easy class though

Honestly I dreaded going to this class. Professor was passive agressive and randomly called on us. The lectures were a bit boring to me. Definitely requires some studying for the exams as the material is pretty dense, but making a good grade in the class overall isn't too difficult. Most exams were very similar to the practice ones he posted.

Dr. Riveros-Iregui is so friendly and a very engaging professor. You can tell he wants his students to succeed in class and he'd specify on slides where they would be important in an exam. He gets upset when students don't focus in class or are distracted on their devices, and you get more out of class when you pay attention in lectures.

Big class (~150), but this professor makes a boring subject interesting with his genuine passion and animated lectures. He asks lots of questions, so stay alert or he'll call you out. Tons of material, but his energy and lively teaching make it manageable. He's one of two instructors, and he clearly loves what he teaches. Great engaging instructor

For a 100 level class the coursework was way too involved. For multiple assessments we were split up into small groups with randomly assigned people in a 200 person class, which ofc turned into chaos where nobody could get any work done. Profs were very stubborn to get any real feedback and scolded multiple people during lecture for not listening.
back handed comments, blamed students for the wifi problem, honestly felt like i was in middle school again.

Diego is one of the real gems of Carolina. If you aren't interested in his class topics, I'm sure it may seem boring. But, if you are interested in environmental science (particularly the kind of hands-on science the ENEC department brushes over in favor of more conceptual/political environmental education) you will love geography.

He is a kind person but for a first year seminar I think he was disappointed in the lack of initial interest in geography. He does not do much to spark interest in the topic. Project grading criteria is often unclear. He may be better in a higher level class.

He likes what he teaches, but he's very passive aggressive. The class is a bunch of seniors and it's been clear they don't really care about what they're learning. If he doesn't get an answer to a question, he will call on someone random and saying "I don't know" isn't an option. Exams are all multiple choice and a couple essays every so often.

this class kinda felt like a waste of time, and other students would agree as the attendance of the class dropped so much to the point that they had to do random attendance checks. other than that, the lectures were super boring and felt pointless. class was graded by few things and graded by the ta and was super lenient with grading.

I did not like this class. I felt like the assignments were unnecessarily time consuming and required readings were often long and not posted until the night before class. Grading, however, was extremely generous.

Dr. Riveros-Iregui is a nice person who had great experience and insights into physical geography issues that he shared with students through lectures. However, he did not give off a friendly vibe, and was condescending to students when giving directions or answering their questions.
A lot better than Havice. He did cold call in a 200 person class though. Easy A and was more tolerable

His lectures were harder to learn from as it's mainly graphs, not info. Also tended to cold call more in class which was always stressful. Seems like a nice guy, and the content wasn't awful, but it was hard to retain with the structure. Class is just ok, honestly hated it more because of Dr. Havice, who teaches it with him. Be cautious lol
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought Prof. Diego was a great teacher! His class may be a little boring but he seems to really enjoy what he teaches which is great. The assignments were pretty easy but this is just an intro class and I am a junior. There were 3 exams, in-class participation, and 3 essays. Overall, I would take him again for sure!

Overall, I really wanted to like this class and like Professor Riveros-Iregui. He's a very nice guy, but his lectures make little sense and his slides are full of confusing graphs. For this class, Professor Havice's lectures are great but I always dread his lectures. Overall, this class is boring and confusingly structured but has potential.

Diego seems nice and that he cares, however, he is not the best lecturer. I got bored a lot in this class and found it hard to pay attention. They also altered the class structure so its more difficult now for no reason. I don't enjoy the class much, don't know anyone that really does.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I literally never showed up and got an A. Really nice guy and passionate about the material. this can be a throwaway class if you want it to be, or a really good class if you're a GEOG major. 3 essays based on articles (not class material) and online exams. TA's were responsible for grading the essays but mine were really easy graders.

This class was literally so easy and is a great gen ed if you need a science without lab. I wish I cared about the subject because Professor Riveros-Iregui is so passionate and knowledgeable. Lecture heavy but attendance not required.

This class was a very easy A. I hardly attended classes because it felt as if I was wasting time. The assignments were either exactly what happened in class or not at all. There were only a few assignments that made up your grade. Additionally, he was very easy to reach via email unlike the other prof for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Riveros Iregui gave more interesting lectures of the two profs, however this class was still highly boring and came across useless. Most of what we were taught we were not tested on, and the assessments seemed like wastes of time. Very VERY easy A however.
for the most part Geog 141 is easy to the point of being boring. Then it randomly picks up and there's an assignment or two where you have to grind.  Overall it's an easy A though.

Dr. Riveros-Iregui is a good professor. He explains concepts well in class. He is also very caring and understanding of your situation. The class is also very easy. There aren't a lot of things determining your grade, but the TAs grade very easily. The class is also interesting.

This is an excellent class if you're interested in geography, with a great professor who is highly knowledgeable and enthusiastic about his field. The coursework includes weekly participation assignments, three 4-page essays spread across the semester, a midterm, and the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super enthusiastic about the course content. Every class is just a lecture so if u aren't super interested it can be boring. don't buy the textbook, you'll never use it. go to class cause all you have to do is sit and listen. start the papers like a week before cause u usually have to read a dense article for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very excited to teach, but since this was a for gen ed class I wasn't interested, which made the lectures boring. He was very kind and is easy to contact though. Great professor just not my style.

This class was definitely manageable for a research capstone during the pandemic. Dr. Riveros-Iregui is kind and helpful. There was a lot of flexibility and personal projects (due to the nature of the class) but I still felt like I had some sense of direction.

This prof is great! He's understanding and makes class enjoyable. However, I didn't learn as much as I had hoped. Our only homework involved weekly articles, one book, and a few presentations. The work is easy and we never had any lectures. Participation is important and he is not afraid to call on people randomly. Do your work and you'll be fine!
Was the better professor out of the course and gave good responses to emails about questions. Did take awhile to get grades back though, and it was probably only an easy class because it was online.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class online and it wasn't bad at all. Most of the time the lectures were prerecorded. We'd have a forum every week and after 4 weeks we do an assignment that wouldn't be hard just time consuming. No papers or textbook. Tests were application, answering short answer questions based off articles given during test.
Diego is very enthusiastic and laid back! Writing assignments are very clear and midterms are all multiple choice.

I took this class just because I needed more hours and after finishing this class I'm so close to declaring a geography major. Diego makes this class so easy to succeed and I feel like I learned useful info about climate change too. Exams were all multiple choice that were pretty easy and the essays were graded fairly. Easy A if you put in time.

Prof Riveros obviously cares deeply about the subject and his enthusiasm shows. To add on top of that, the course isn't particularly difficult. The TAs graded the papers fairly leniently, and as long as you studied the slides you'll do well on the exams. I would consider taking this class even as a gen-ed, it's interesting and an easy A.

Diego is so sweet and obviously loves the subject. He gives 5 points of extra credit (on your overall grade) as long as you do the participation activities. The class itself is pretty boring, but he tries his hardest to make it interesting. The papers were easy and the exams were straightforward but not always as simple.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Riveros enjoys geography and gives good lectures. Only 2 exams and 3 papers throughout the semester. The textbook is not needed, just read the powerpoints to help prepare for exams. Very easy essay rubrics and all exams are multiple choice.

Super nice and caring professor. Cracks jokes, but will call you out if you look like you're not paying attention. Class consisted of reading one book and talking about it, in-class activities where you read articles and discuss what you liked about them, two presentations, and a final paper. Fun FYS and would definitely take him again!

A great and dedicated teacher. he has that knack for making the a pretty dry subject matter relatively interesting. The overall course was three papers, three tests (including the final) and a ton of extra credit.

Go Diego Go! The lectures are fine depending on the topic. He is very passionate about Geography and will talk about his field work. He's super nice and please answer questions! You will have a better experience if you participate! The three assigned papers take some time but are manageable. You'll learn a lot for sure!
i love him

Diego is a great professor. While many students in the class are not geog majors, he still tries his best to be engaging. The content can be a little boring at times, but the exams and papers are very easy. On the exams, he only includes topics covered in class, so the textbook is not entirely necessary. Very easy A if studying is done!

Graded by: 3 papers, in-class assignments on Sakai, two mid-terms, one final. Easy class, show up to get the in-class assignments, but don't really need to pay attention. Professor is enthusiastic about subject matter, the subject matter is just boring in and of itself. He's nice though, but will put you on the spot for one of his questions.

Professor Riveros-Iregui is a very nice and understanding professor. He assigns weekly readings which have discussions in class. The class is discussion heavy and most of your grade is participation. I enjoyed having him as a professor and it was a good class that made me consider things I wouldn't usually think of. Only downside is boring lectures

Geog50 is more of an intro to environmental research class than a geography class. that said, he is super excited about his students and the content, and his chill but happy attitude is really contagious. Can be absentminded at times, on the whole a great dude. Inspired me to want to do my own research!
He is a lovable guy!! He is so nice & has a great time during class! He really cares for his students & is knowledgeable about many topics!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Diego is great! The only grades were three papers (3-4 pages each), two tests, and a final. The class is very lecture heavy and he tends to read off the slides, making it easy to lose focus. However, he has a very charismatic personality and he is very passionate about the subject, so if you ask any questions he is always willing to help.

Great professor who is knowledgeable about his field of study. Passionate and cares about his students. There are frequent group projects but they aren't for a grade. There are 3-4 page papers about once a month. Tests are all multiple choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Really nice guy who is passionate about his field. goes through slides fast so make sure he posts then on sakai. group projects are dumb but they arent for a grade
Martina is my favorite UNC professor. I changed my schedule to take ITAL 204 with her because she's that great. I learned so much from her and loved her class!! I can't recommend her enough!!

I have taken Martina for ITAL 101, 102, and 204 because she is THAT amazing. She is a caring instructor and makes class so much fun. She is so funny and really cares about you succeeding in the class. She is always making sure we are comfortable with the material and comfortable in her class. Can't recommend her more!

Martina is amazing and definitely one of the best professors you could get for any italian classes. The course is set up the same as 101 and 102 with homeworks due before each class, 4 tests, a small group project before each test, and two very easy quizzes in each unit. Would definitely recommend Martina to anyone taking italian!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is so sweet! Never judgmental of your ability level & meets you where you are. If I could I would have taken her for all 3 levels.

Martina made learning a new language enjoyable and easy! I took 101 as a gen-ed but am seriously considering an Italian minor after taking her class. She goes out of her way to help comprehension and uses hilarious real world examples. Take Italian with Martina!!

The best teacher!! So kind and caring! Class was fun and engaging, and I learned SO much. Not hard to get an A. She is so knowledgeable on the topics and wants to talk to you about them! Go see her outside of class, you won't regret it! weekly online quizzes, a couple of projects, and a collaborative final.

I felt kind of patronized throughout this class, we were treated like children. Pretty project heavy,  but graded easily. Attendance was super important to your grade, felt like she thought her class was the only one that mattered.The class felt unorganized and had confusing instructions. She's a nice person, but not great for a college professor.

Dr. Diliberto is such a sweet and knowledgeable professor, but the class material often feels repetitive and grating. Class is pretty project and quiz-based. Quizzes are very specific. Projects have slightly unclear instructions. The professor is great to talk to outside of class. Overall, not a bad class, but not the most engaging.

Sweetest Professor ever! She clearly wants all of us to learn and gives encouraging, constructive feedback. This async class was very reasonable and very interesting. You do have 5 discussion zoom calls with other students, so just be aware of that going in if you're expecting a fully async class. Great class and I learned a lot!
Dr. Diliberto is an amazing professor. She truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed. This class is easy but you will learn! Take a class with her!

Dr. Diliberto is really nice, clearly cares about her students. Automatically gives three grace days on all assignments, no questions asked. The textbook SUCKS though. Reading quizzes aren't great either and are much harder than they need to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took for EDUC 689 she cares about her students with built-in grace deadlines and she is very understanding. Some of the material was hard to stay engaged with if the chapters were pretty long. But overall enjoyed what I learned and wish there was more feedback given on points lost.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Diliberto is so sweet and cares about her students! She was good about asking for feedback twice throughout the semester to see what she should change. Lots of fun group discussions but never forced to participate in front of the whole class. She encourages you to think outside of the box but sometimes can be vague, but easy grader regardless.

Diliberto was kind and cares about students, however, this class was the most confusing class I've ever taken. Assignments changed it felt like almost daily, assignment deadlines were so confusing, and projects popped up throughout the semester with 0 warning. She was so disorganized that it made me really dislike a course I was really excited for

I LOVE Dr. Diliberto!!! Because of this class, I have decided to go into special education.
