I took Nobels freshman seminar class, STOR 89. it was pretty easy especially because there are no exams! there was some homework, but overall the workload is very minimal. therefore even if you think it is difficult it doesnt really matter because you will never be tested on the material. Nobel is very quirky and loves what he does! nice guy.

Professor Pease made math 130 much harder than it should've been. The class is graded majority from midterms and the finals. I recommend not taking this class with a heavy course load and getting a tutor asap.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bad professor. Clearly thinks he's too good to be teaching precalc since he teaches it in a complex/ confusing manner. You'd be better off learning from YouTube

10/10 would not recommend. TAs were SO unhelpful and the professor overcomplicates simple topics. I definitely could have done better but l think the way he teaches is directed for higher level math and not pre-calc. He is a very stylistic and funny person and very accessible outside of class with his office hours.

I took MATH 130 with him. He is a cool and stylish person, but not a good teacher at all. He deserves to be teaching higher level maths and not pre-calc because he overcomplicates simple concepts making it very hard to follow along. I strongly advise not taking this class with him if you are taking a lot of other STEM courses.

I took math 130 with professor pease, it was terrible. The class itself is not too hard, but the way he explained concepts got very confusing very fast. You have to spend a lot of time outside of class learning the concepts before you can get to actually studying them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible at explaining “basic” mathematical concepts. If you want a straight explanation, you're not going to get one.
Andrew is very sweet but explains things horribly. He makes everything sound more complicated than it actually is. Learn things on your own and you will do well.

Objectively a really bad professor- made MATH130 feel like rocket science. If you are in his math 130 class, i HIGHLY recommend getting a tutor or use outside resources. The tests feel nothing like what we go over in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class itself was not too difficult, but I went to office hours and he was really short with me. I never went back again.

I took Andrew for MATH110. This class was supposed to be way easier than Andrew made it. His teaching style was very interesting, he goes way too fast, and is just kinda bad at teaching. I ended up just not going to the lectures anymore and teaching myself. He is a very nice and caring person though, and always made the class laugh.
The class was okay, and he was super friendly outside of class. The way he explained concepts was another story….

I took math 130 with Andrew and he is the most sweetest/ caring person ever! however, his teaching style and the way he explains things is absolutely ass. Other than that he never makes you feel dumb for not knowing things that should be "simple"!

He's so nice, caring, and accessible outside of class. Great person, but his teaching style was so confusing and he made simple concepts seem SO complicated. I've taken algebra 1 and many maths higher than this in hs before, but his teaching made the info feel 100x harder than it is.

I had Andrew for MATH110, one of the easiest math classes at UNC. But, at no point throughout the course did Andrew make us feel "lesser-than" or stupid. He never gave us an overwhelming amount of work and heard our frustrations when we had them. Held office hours constantly and was always warm and inviting when you attended them!

Andrew was my TA for calculus and our class would not have survived without him. He basically taught us the course and always helped us work through our homework. He is also a very generous grader and so hilarious. Shout out to Andrew!

He cares about his students and does not take any shortcuts in helping them succeed in the class. He adapted the pacing of the class based on student feedback and gave students sufficient opportunities to ask questions and connect in office hours. Pay attention to lectures and do the practice exams, and you will know everything you need.

Having had difficulty in math my entire college career, andrew was by far the most impactful professor I've had in this field. He cares a lot and provides plenty of outside help to allow his students to succeed. He's a lil goofy but a great explainer. DO THE HANDOUTS AND PRACTICE EXAMS FROM OFFICE HOURS!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: STOR 113.The class was fine. The content wasn't bad. The first midterm was kinda awful but the rest were fine. My main issue was how passive aggressive this dude is. Literally could not ask a question without getting a weird remark. Went to his office hours once and never again. He kinda chilled out after a while but yikes, did not wanna be there.

The first test was hard, but after we gave feedback he totally adapted his lectures for us. Even though this was a lecture based class he went above and beyond to make weekly lecture notes, problem sets, and practice exams. Overall, couldn't ask for a more dedicated and flexible teacher who wants students to succeed without handing it to them.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Stor 113. Class content itself is not terrible, but Andrew truly is not meant to be a teacher. Constanly getting annoyed and showing absolutely 0 will to teach. Gives practice material the day before exams and doesn't even announce it. Sometimes only gives practice papers to student who show up to office hours. Avoid if you can.

Pretty vague on what my grade was until it was finalized, but a chill dude who is clearly very passionate and respected in his field. Very niche topics but you don't have to memorize as much as other ARTH electives I've taken (only like 20-30 things per exam) and attendance didn't matter.

Prof Turner was a great, he was understanding and didn't mind absences (don't abuse this). He graded papers for completion and the 'term paper' on accuracy. His exams aren't bad but you must memorize a lot (took me 2-3 hr w/flashcards). I rec if you have a busy schedule bc he has no homework, but exams are weighed heavily but graded forgivingly.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures can be boring, but overall it is a chill class with interesting content and teacher. What started off as a filler class eventually became a fav. He doesn't grade harshly, and focuses more on conceptualization than gpa. He said before the final. “I'm not here to tank your gpa.” Not much work outside of the classroom, few assignments.

Prof Turner is very knowledgeable and passionate about his work and that shows in his lectures. The content is quite interesting, but the lectures themselves can drag on and feel boring at times. Final grade is determined by 3 assignments and 2 exams which kind of sucks, but he is a pretty forgiving grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: While some do say his voice is a little monotone, he's clearly passionate about the subject and really cares. He revamped the curriculum this semester a lot to make it more accessible and interesting to students, and his willingness to change and tinker stuff shows he's super caring of students. Exams are open note and online, albeit a little hard.

Prof. Boysen is clearly very knowledgable about the world of corporate strategy. I really enjoyed the assigned cases and the in-class exercises - they really helped me grasp the course concepts. Prof. Boysen was also always willing to meet with students (even outside of his scheduled office hours). He has been one of my favorite proffesors at KF!
Professor Boysen was one of the kindest professors ever. He makes the class super manageable and I would 100% take another class with him. Definitely take him for BUSI 412!

I think 412 is overall j a boring class in general. But prof boysen is very respectful and knowledgeable in this field of study. He is also SOOO kind and often would bring small treats and gifts to class (which honestly makes my day)! Overall, choose a good project group, and you'll be fine

Professor Boysen is a kind and caring person who repeatedly emphasizes we prioritize our mental health before all else. His attendance policy is relaxed, and he is encouraging of us to schedule office hours for extra help. Reading-heavy with lots of cases and a discussion-based class. I enjoy his sense of dry humor. He loves his daughter! )

Such a good guy and understanding but extremely boring. All the quizzes and exams are online. There's a group project that is relatively easy but a big portion of the grade so choose your group wisely.

Boysen is such a great guy and wants everyone to succeed. The lectures are extremely boring though which is a bummer because it makes it hard to pay attention and learn. Choose a good group for the group project, my group screwed me over :/
Not a good teacher and is in the wrong line of work. Not sure who gave him this job or how he passed an interview to teach at KF. Take 412 with someone else.

The content was difficult to understand, but Prof Boysen is accessible outside of class and wants you to succeed. The weekly quizzes are difficult, but if you go to office hours, he will help you out. If you put forth any effort in the class, you will do fine. He is also funny and breaks up lecture with group activities/Pollev's version of Kahoot.
insanely boring but not hard to get an A if you try

He's definitely passionate and very knowledgeable about corporate strategy but its extremely difficult to understand his course material. His teaching style incorporates a lot of in-class group discussion, but often times the other people in the class were just as lost so it made it harder to learn this way.

Prof. Boysen is very knowledgeable about corporate strategy. However, he has trouble explaining these concepts to undergraduate students, and it boils down to students using his buzzwords without knowing what they actually mean. I believe he is better suited for research as other ratings say, but maybe he will improve in future semesters.

Dr. Boysen is extremely knowledgeable and knows a ton about corporate strategy and management. Classes are reading and case-based and the format is straightforward. Lectures can be long, but breakout groups split up lecture time and he is very supportive. He is really accessible outside of class for office hours and overall is an awesome professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Boysen does a great job of making himself available outside of class. You can tell how much he cares about his students and spends a lot of time going over feedback to make his lectures better. He is a little bit shy at first, but is definitely one of my favorite UNC professors!

Professor Boysen really cares about his students and makes a deliberate effort to be available for office hours and take students' feedback to make his class better. He definitely is monotone/the material is somewhat boring, but he really does his best to make the class as engaging as possible (PollEv activities, group breakouts).

Horrible class. Its almost like he didnt even try to design it from the perspective of a student. Make him do research instead of teaching undergrads. Im sure hes probably brilliant at that, but he is very out of touch with the average college student. If everyone fails your exam, you are a bad teacheryour students are not bad

DUDE CANNOT TEACH FOR HIS LIFE, avoid at literally all costs. Take this class with Wilson and save yourself the agony. 5 minutes into your first class with him and you'll see what I'm talking about. he teaches in the same voice you'd expect to hear a lullaby, maybe softer. Showing any sort of enthusiasm might make this guy explode. U've been warned

The most boring and unhelpful professor at KF. Let's start with the fact that this guy never posts his deadlines for stuff until like a week before. The quizzes are actually challenging, especially once he found out the answers were online. WORST PART, THIS DUDE CANNOT TEACH. He thinks he's talking to PHDs and doesn't know how to teach undergrads.

Took him during Covid Pandemic. Quizzes after every class that are not too bad. One group project where you can choose groups and isn't too difficult at all. Final exam worth most of the grade. Class material is dry, but Boysen is super nice and accommodating. If class is hard he will give you a break or let you turn in stuff late, just talk to him
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. D is awesome! The class is easy if you do the readings and go to lecture. The essays/writing assignments are chill and have clear instructions. The TA's were very nice!

Very funny, respectful, and intelligent. His lectures were really interesting, engaging (many people participated), and he used a lot of cool media as examples (music videos, artifacts, literally like Little Women and SpongeBob too). Gives good feedback and grades well if you try. Class became kinda optional towards the end. Fav prof at unc so far

Dr. Dooling has been one of the best professors that I have had. The class has reading checks every week which were pretty easy and 3 papers. There were no tests and if you ask for feedback before assignments are due he will give you it.

Dr. Dooling is a wonderful professor that is truly passionate about his work and studies. His lectures are entertaining and fun. He is a tough grader, especially with the bigger papers, but not unreasonable and he is willing to talk about it. I would take his class again any day!

If you can take any insightful and phenomenal class at UNC, take Comm 224 with Dr. Dooling. He is amazing, hilarious, caring, etc! The class is genuinely enjoyable and incredibly thought-provoking. Dr. Dooling is a fair grader but expects passion and effort. Take this class or any of his classes!

Loved taking 325 with him! He is very down-to-earth and always makes the content fun/engaging. Lot's of group collaboration, so prepare to talk. Class is so much better when you do the readings, btw. They aren't just busy work. Exams are open-note/textbook, but not too easy. Very relevant content!

Dr. Dooling is my favorite professor I have had at UNC. His lectures are super engaging, he uses pop culture examples to help students understand concepts, and he truly cares about his students. He is also very helpful in office hours. I would recommend him and this course to anyone!

I love Dr. Dooling! He is super engaging and is very passionate about the course content. I would reccomend this class to anyone! Graded by a few essays and some reading responses; a great choice for those who do not love the typical exam format in most classes.

Dr. Dooling has been a great professor and has a clear passion for his area of work. The readings are relevant to the class, and his lecture style is engaging. Minimal busy work, reasonable grading, relevant insights- all of that. 10/10!

Lectures are in-depth and engaging. Homework is a huge portion of your grade, so do not procrastinate doing it. Paying attention in lecture is important because the posted slides do not have the same level of depth or insight that you will need to do well on the final. Group project is quite a bit of work too, just make sure to start on time.
Class wasn't too difficult, but it was hard to understand what we actually needed to know and what was just extra, which a lot of people ended up struggling with when came the final.

His rmp rating scared me before taking the class but as someone who doesn't go to UNC I thought he was a really good prof and gave all the resources to succeed compared to the profs I've had for my other pre-med classes. Just grind the practice exams and make sure you understand how to do the homework questions + studios and you're golden.

Dr. Drut was a fantastic professor. I've heard some people didn't enjoy his teaching style for PHYS 115, but for Numerical II I couldn't disagree more. He is genuinely the best physics professor I've had here at UNC by a wide margin. He's a clear lecturer and realistic about what we will and won't need in our careers, and encourages questions.

Terrible lecturer. Everything he tried to explain was explained in the worst way possible, where i thought it was hard until i watched youtube videos and realized it was pretty simple. Almost never finished all the slides from lecture as he went on lots of tangents. Tests problems were always confusingly worded or had things he didnt teach us.

SS2 didn't tell us hw due b4 class starting but graded it.talked about stuff not on exams for 20/50min class & leave 10+slides for you to learn on own, say "oops out of time" hold us over when we had studio after class! exams had material that we didn't learn bc he was too lazy to make a new exam based on course.didn't release final exam grades

SS2, 2025: this prof. is one of a kind. he comes across as a friend, but acts as a foe. every single exam had questions from content he explicitly said would not be on the exam. its like he didnt check what the exam was before he gave it to us... assignments due b4 FDOC and after LDOC.

SS2. office hours were 20 min before our 9am class. lazy professor who didn't want to change the grading of a question because he messed it up. we had an assignment due the day before class started. changes exam questions mid exams. doesnt follow posted schedule/syllabus. confusing syllabus. said attendance isnt graded but syllabus said it is

Was able to effectively dumb down physics concepts for freshmen in a humanities class. Lectures were occasionally excellent, sometimes okay. Not his fault imo but overall the class is horrible. Think of a bad attribute a class could have and it probably has it. I would rather rip off each of my toe nails one by one than take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Drut was a good professor overall. I'm not a physics person and never will be, but I thought he explained the concepts well enough. I would not take IDST 122 again because we were graded on so few things that were each weighed heavily, but I did feel like I learned from the course. As long as you pay attention and take notes, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Drut was really nice but his lectures were all over the place and a bit complex for a Triple-I. I wouldn't recommend taking IDST 122 for your Triple-I. It's an interesting enough course, but you're only graded on the midterms, paper, and final, and the expectations they have seem unrealistic for people fresh out of high school.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Decent professor. Not a physics guy, so by far the most confusing of the three for me, but by no means is he bad or trying to trip anyone up with his lecturing. I'm sure he's fine solo in an actual physics course. IDST122 is a useless course, however. Don't take it.

I thought Professor Drut was very kind and passionate about his subject. However, I found the concepts hard to grasp as someone who had never taken physics before, and I didn't feel like Drut explained things in a thorough way at times. Overall, IDSt 122 was a very interesting and engaging class but definitely one of the hardest triple-Is.
he explains topics of astrophysics pretty well and answers all questions as well as he can,

Prof.Drut is a kind man, but his classes are not the most clear, especially if you are not into physics. He wants you to succeed though, and if you go to oh he will explain things until you feel satisfied. Overall he is a good professor, but this format does not allow for him to be at his best, and reading material/ testings are heavy, so be ready.

Professor Drut is a funny guy who knows how to apply difficult topics to real life situations. If you're in HATC, you seriously don't need to know the formulas or the fine details of physics. Have fun, do the readings, ask questions in his office hours, let yourself be confused from time to time.

Professor Drut is an excellent professor! He's passionate about his content and very easy to talk to. One of the problems that you'll often find with highly intelligent professors is that they are somewhat incomprehensible: this is NOT the case with Dr. Drut. He's a genius in his fields and also very personable, especially in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice guy and passionate about his field, but HOC was a trainwreck. His lectures were disorganized, and he doesn't know how to explain physics to non-majors. His lectures were also painfully boring, and I gave up taking notes. You might survive in a class taught just by him if you're a physics major, but avoid Humans and the Cosmos at all costs.

Gave very engaging lectures, if sometimes difficult to follow. Very few grades overall so take the HW and project seriously. Was always friendly to the class, and cares about his students. Big ups as well to Tyler Britt if you can get him as your TA for anything, super cool guy and gave great explanations for the HW concepts.

I took this course over summer session 2 and can confidently say this was the WORST CLASS I have ever taken in college. Dr. Drut cares more about his ego than his students and can not teach for the life of him. His tests were far too difficult given the time constraint, and he did nothing about rampant cheating and incompetent TAs and assignments.

Took this class over SS2. Professor Drut knows his stuff and is very knowledgeable. However, this does not quite translate to being a good lecturer/teacher. Although this class is over the summer and the content is sped up, Professor Drut rarely slows down on the complex topics. The exams were fairly difficult and did not correlate with HW at all.
ABSOLUTELY AVOID FOR PHYS 114/115!!!!!! Drut does not care about students' feelings and his course structure was horrible. I hated every second of this class and Drut made it worse.

Dr. Drut is an awful professor. His lectures are barely understandable because he talks too fast and he gives you like 5 seconds to do the hardest problems. He is determined to weed you out and ruin your career.

Dr. Drut is probably the best professor I've had at UNC. Unlike many phys professors, he's able to read the room and tell when students are generally lost and makes changes to accommodate the students. He is respectful and his lectures are clear. He answers your questions very clearly. I had very little coding experience before this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Drut was attuned to students' feelings and very lenient with regrade requests. Additionally, he curved our first midterm despite the median not being that bad by UNC standards. Sadly, I had to watch COVID era videos on YouTube because his lectures were not great. The studios were tedious but exam questions may be drawn from them so beware.

Drut is a great professor in 331. He has clear and informative lectures (attendance is not required, but I encourage it), and the homework sets are long but legitimately helpful and interesting. The concepts in class are abstract, but he connects them with subjects you may see in other physics classes. Tests are very fair and he grades leniently.

Drut was my favorite out of the professors (Trop a close second) for Humans & Cosmos. Really interesting content and a great teacher of it. I had to go to him multiple times due to my TA for the class being an absolute hater towards me, and he really heard me out and attempted to help. This class was a waste of time overall, but he's a great prof.
Dr. Drut does a decent job of explaining complex physics topics to humans and the cosmos but ultimately it is a very difficult task. He is very nice prof though, Vamos Argentina

Dr. Drut teaches physics well but as someone who does not previous knowledge on physics it was hard to understand. This class was the worst class I've ever taken in terms of rigorousness and excessive reading. The professors expected a lot out of freshman students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Drut taught the complex physics concepts very well in this class, but it was still difficult to follow especially for it being a first year triple-i for any major. The lectures were very packed, and you have to pay close attention in order to grasp the full concepts.

He does an excellent job at teaching extremely complex physics concepts in a way that someone who doesn't have any prior physics knowledge (like myself) can understand. Gives detailed answers to questions and is very friendly.

Out of the three instructors, Professor Drut was my favorite even though I found it a bit hard to understand the physics section of the class. He explains physics at a high level, probably a little too advanced for first year students in a class mostly about philosophy. Don't take Humans and the Cosmos though, it's just not a good experience.

Professor Drut seems very nice and passionate about physics, but it is just difficult to follow. While I like Professor Drut, I do not recommend Humans and the Cosmos because it is just way too difficult for a first year course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Humans & The Cosmos is extremely interesting but prepare to READ. Too much reading for a first-year requirement in my opinion. Assignments were manageable: 1 weekly reading response, 2 papers, 1 midterm, and the final. Everything is graded by TAs.  Prof. Drut is passionate about the material and it translates through his lectures -- enthralling.

He seems to know his information and is very smart but when paired with humans and the cosmos it makes no sense. Trying to teach and dumb down heavy and strong ideas of physics is hard to do and it does not work out. Most of his lectures make no sense and there is no connection to the course. Outside in a physics class it might be interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Drut is great. He really recognizes students who are putting in effort in the class and is very understanding about workload and the test are crafted very fairly.

As much as I enjoyed Professor Drut, I feel like he did not do a very good job explaining physics to a group of non-physics students. It was clear he knew what he was talking about, but I was frequently in the complicated lectures about particle physics or thermodynamics. However, I am sure that taking a pure physics class with him would be great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Drut was very good at explaining very complex physics concepts in a way that non-physics students can understand. He is very nice and loves to take and answer questions from curious students. He is a great professor, very approachable, and very kind.

took the triple I class, didn't really understand any of the content he lectured about but I always felt smart after his class (you didn't really need to understand the specifics for that class). very interesting and i'd like to listen to his lectures again, but if I had to actually do the physics work it would probably be tough

I had Prof Drut as part of the triple I course, which was very interesting. Prof Drut's lectures were very dense and equation heavy, which made it hard to understand at first and would require extra work outside of class. Overall, the class was very interesting and I highly recommend Prof Drut for another class as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I didnt enjoy the Humans and the Cosmos class overall because subject matter between him and the other professors seemed disconnected, but Prof Drut is clearly a good teacher. He is very willing to help students understand, good at explaining, and attractive too

Drut is a literal genius. It seriously freaks me out. He is insanely good at explaining challenging concepts. I usually walk into his class completely lost from our readings but then somehow leave understanding everything. I would definitely recommend taking a class from him.

Drut is a very amazing professor. He is very interested in his topic and tries to answer every question people may ask. The attendance was not mandatory but they may change this. He is willing to help his students and can explain very complex subjects in simple, understandable ways. Reading heavy and complex.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Prof Drut is an amazing teacher. He taught alongside 2 other professors for this class but was easily the best one. He is so passionate about physics and it's clear from his lectures he is extremely intelligent. He cares about his students, is funny, and has engaging lectures where you learn a lot. Highly recommend!

Professor Drut is easily one of the best I've had in the physics department. Take a coding class and/or linear algebra before 331 if you want to do well otherwise the homework will be impossible, but Drut is always available to help and offers great solutions. Emails back very quickly and is overall just a kind and incredibly helpful professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Drut is a very caring and funny guy. He will go out of his way to help you and will work with you in any way you need. The linear algebra in this class is taught well enough that you don't have to take the math class prior to this course. Take a coding class before this one, bc the homework is insanely difficult if you don't have prior experience.

Dr Drut is a wonderful professor. Phys331 is VERY challenging, and if you have no prior experience with linear algebra or coding you will have to work even harder, but Dr Drut will do to ANYTHING to help you succeed. If you reach out, he will drop everything to help you. I learned a lot, and I owe it all to him. I wish more profs were like him.

I feel like my previous comment was unfair for Professor Drut. After I struggled a little more, I talked to Professor Drut and he really showed care for my situation. He expressed understanding and also encouraged me to not be held back by the difficulties in the course. I'll probably still get a B to B+ in the course, but I don't regret taking it.

I'm not a physics major and was taking this class for interest. Had all the prereqs but they are definitely not enough for the course. Dr. Drut is a really nice guy, hilarious too at times, but not the clearest in lectures. If you are a physics major I'd recommend you take it with him, but if you are like me then just stay away from the course!
What a guy. Has an espresso machine in his office. Great hair. Actually knows python. You can't beat em.
Very approachable and willing to talk to you about the class and your problems. If you have trouble understanding something he will be able to help you.

Great professor, really cares about his students and their learning. Willing to go the extra mile to make sure his students get the most out of his classes, and genuinely cares. Amazing professor, and would take again!
He was not the best of teachers. He did an OK job
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Duan is very accessible but was not the most understanding. Assigns a LOT of work, one of my heaviest workloads I have ever had at UNC, and a lot of it is not productive work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Duan is amazing, I had no poetry experience before and she had such a welcoming class for all levels. You do have to go to class and attend all workshops, there is no test/exam and the final was reading our completed poems and she brought drinks and food. I recommend this class to everyone I know!

Incredible! absolutely amazing professor who cares about every individual student. I feel like my writing improved so much over the course of the semester. This class was never a source of stress, but you can get so much out of it because of the poetry workshops, and Carlina's constructive comments on every poem you write.
Professor Duan is an angel on earth, truly. She is incredible, caring, and kind, and fosters the safest space. Her knowledge is vast and her acceptance is unwavering.

Professor Duarte was an extremely caring and passionate professor. I found him funny and tried to make a boring class more interesting through real world examples. With that said, the class is very difficult. I could not follow along in lectures easily and it took me time outside of class to grasp the topics. Tests are very hard, but have big curve

Duarte is great. 445 is a math-heavy continuation of Micro with a lot of game theory involved. He keeps lectures interesting with real-life legal examples. Exams are hard but the curve is very generous. If you're decent at math, you'll be fine for an A-.

Class is insanely hard. That being said Marco works with you to ensure you don't fail. He has numerous extra credit opportunities, hw is graded for completion, and exams are curved extensively (30=C, 40=B, etc.). While this class is not by any means a guarranteed A I found it easy to obtain a B with pretty average effort. Just go to class.

Arbitrary grader. The topics are interesting, but he speedruns through them, and lectures have little to do with his horribly difficult math-heavy exams. Gets easily frustrated and mad when the class doesn't understand his teaching methods. I threw up one question into midterm 2, and he wouldn't let me retake it. Don't take this course, trust me!!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class will have super challenging midterms where you just speedrun solve everything you know, but the curve will SAVE YOU from getting below a B unless you skip class/put in 0 effort. Legit got a 14 on a midterm curved to C- LOL. Content is super interesting, pricing strategy/game theory, you actually learn something meaningful in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would avoid this at all costs unless you have to have it for credit. As far as a general 400 level econ elective this is a horrible choice. Class is ridiculously difficult, averages on exams are in the 40s. 80% of the class is graded on exams. There is curve on exams where a 30 is a C and 60 is an A. Overall just a miserable experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this class unless you need the credit. Exams are nearly impossible to finish, and lecture notes lack depth or relevance to the math-heavy tests. Lectures are dull and hard to follow. The professor is brilliant but assumes everyone can keep up, making this one of the toughest and least rewarding econ classes offered.

Material is challenging enough that going to lectures is important even if not required. Problem sets graded on completion, which offsets extremely difficult tests with averages below 50%. All exams are curved extensively. Marco knows his stuff and applies class topics to real world issues. A must-have class for those interested in consulting

His lectures are fun, tho sometimes a bit hard to follow. However, his lecture notes explain everything. He is very accessible for help, and responds to emails quickly. If you keep up with class, you should get an A- at least. I unfortunately missed the deadline of a problem set and fell behind in class after being sick for 3 weeks.

Overall Marco is a great guy and can be very personable. His information that he teaches you in class isn't too hard and pretty interesting but the test were quite intuitive and takes further knowledge from outside of what he teaches you. Everyone would fail the test but would curve a lot to match older section grading scales, a 30 would be a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Marco is a nice guy, but this class is just not worth it. The material presented should not have been that difficult to learn, but there was an utter lack of resources, and each homework and test question had layers of intuition stacked on it. Midterm averages were right around 50%. With 20's curving to C's. Homeworks are graded for completion.

Prof. Duvall was amazing! My favorite teacher during my first semester, definitely take ENG105 with her. Class was 3 projects, each with drafting assignments that prepare you fully for the final submission. She gave incredible feedback as well! Did not stress at all with this class.

super chill and easy class. Basically everything is completion if u put in a bit of effort. Attendance is not rly required either, she's pretty lenient with missing class as long as u email her beforehand, and it won't even affect ur grade. TAKE THIS PROF FOR ENGLISH
Easy course, but I don't feel like I actually learned anything.
If you can take a class with her next term you MUST.

Genuinely such an amazing professor and person. Class was not hard at all, and she made it clear she didn't want this class to be a stressor. Class consisted of some small assignments and 3 projects. Plenty of time was given, and she was very understanding on attendance (probably missed 5/6 classes from sickness). Great professor!

Emma made a class I thought I would hate one of my most enjoyable. She genuinely cares about all of the people in her classes. There are no exams, just 2-3 feeder assignments and a culminating project in each of the 3 units. She gives clear rubrics and feedback to help each student thrive in the course. If she teaches another section, take it.
Easy A for 105. Amazing professor who really cares and is invested in you. No tests just three projects for three units. No final as well. 10/10

Emma is an amazing professor! She is extremely caring and kind, and absolutely wants the best for her students. The assignments are very straightforward, and she is an understanding grader. I loved this class. If you are able take ENGL 105 with Emma, do it!

Emma was my TA for CMPL 120. Recitations were fun and really helpful for understanding the course, Emma was super knowledgeable on the course material. Emma was kind and caring, always super accommodating and willing to answer questions. Can't recommend her enough, she's awesome!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Lots and lots of readings in the semester, very fast paced. 3 essays that are all 1500+ words, plus a (really hard and strictly graded) midterm, with a final at the end. Tons of work for a class that's only a 100 level class, wouldn't take this at all if you're not a CMPL major or whatever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Emma is an absolute sweetie. Most of her classes are discussion based, so it is easy to participate if you can get 1 comment in each class. There are 4 papers and she will review them before you turn them in as many times as you want. You can tell she wants you to succeed always. There isn't much prep that goes in and even if you don't it's fine.

Emma gave me a completely new understanding of poetry in the best way. Lectures were interesting and engaging, and she really made an effort to get to know each student. She is one of the most genuinely caring professors I've had so far. She was also very flexible with deadlines. The class workload was very manageable.
Emma is fantastic. Really interesting lectures and readings. Super accommodating and flexible when it comes to assignment due dates.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures and homework were directly geared towards assignments. She's very nice, meeting with her will help if you need it for papers. Not a lot of work though, just a few projects. Just do your work and you'll do well, it's an easy class.

Emma was a great TA for CMPL 120. She is genuinely one of the most caring instructors I have met at UNC. She is very accessible outside of class to answer questions about essays. Her recitations were a great addition to the main lecture, having us perform close readings of passages or art pieces.
Definitely should choose her as your 105 teacher if it's possible!

Quick chase for those of you who just want it: 100% awesome professor. Finished with a 99%. Super respected. Very nice. Kind.
I found this class to be one of the greatest introductory classes, especially online, though the units move quickly, the class goes by fast, despite being 90 minutes, 5 days a week. 
Grades "easy" but you have to try!

Take her for your 105!! I would've never expected to enjoy ENGL. I didn't even mind going at 8am. She is so kind and uplifting and gives you an A for just attempting to improve from your draft. The units are all different so it's not just paper writing. 1-2 assignments per week, most of which took me 10 minutes.

She is very kind and accomadating for circumstances! ENGL 105 coursework relatively easy and she gives great feedback for your rough drafts so that you can do well on final projects. No midterm or final. Very sweet and respected by all of the classmates. Love her!

Take eng105 with her if u can (even if its early its worth it)!! She is so nice and understanding. Very reachable outside of class. Give u extension if u ask. Easy grader as well. Some say lecture is boring but thats not on her all eng105 lecture r boring its an intro class what do u expect. She will make ur life easier trust me.

This was the easiest A I will get in college. Really, don't bother buying the book because you won't use it and probably already know the material. Emma is a sweet teacher and approachable but a boring lecturer and the class is such common sense but she taught it so in-depth. Just do the work and you get credit. I attended over zoom to save myself.
Emma is a wonderful teacher that is so flexible with everything in her class. Her class was very fun and nothing was particularly hard. She was one of the best teachers I had freshman year at UNC.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you're taking ENGL 105 I definitely recommend Emma. She was the kindest and most understanding professor I had this spring. She was very flexible on assignments and gave very useful templates for each. Her class was structured very well and I can tell that she genuinely cares about her students. It is not difficult at all to get a good grade.

YOU WANT HER FOR ENGL 105. Her class is the easiest I've ever taken bc she always pushes back deadlines and wants to help you. I still learned the material but was never stressed. She's sooo sweet and gives clear feedback and is a very lenient grader. And if you're shy she lets you do the one presentation for her individually.

Emma Duvall is truly a nice person. She is considerate and the perfect supporter in an otherwise very stressful college environment. I had her for English 105. The workload is extremely manageable, and she often gives time in class to work on assignments. She is an easy grader, but still gives great and helpful feedback for the assignments.

Really enjoyed this class, favorite of the semester. I found Prof. Sebell's discussions engaging, even if they often trailed off a bit or lagged behind the readings. Don't take if you don't want to read or don't like engaging in in-class discussions. I found what brought me success was just staying engaged in class & actively participating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Really interesting class. Attendance is mandatory but as long as you show up and do the readings it's an easy A. Pop quizzes here and there but short and not difficult. Participation encouraged but not required. 1 midterm, 2 papers, 1 final. Nice professor and fun class as long as you complete the readings and put some effort into the essays!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He lectured the entire class and was extremely disorganized, making it difficult to study my (paper) notes— no devices allowed. Lots of pop quizzes that make up a good bit of your grade (and were often given a whileee after the reading it was based on). Not a great environment to ask questions during class or ask peers for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Some of the topics were interesting but I feel like half the time the class was sidetracked so bad by some random kid saying something so irreverent. And then Sebell entertains it and before you know it the class is over and you're sitting there wondering what you even learned. The levels of disorganization in this class should be studied in a lab.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tough class because it's the same thing every single day (reading books/writings and analyzing them). Gave pop quizzes so make sure you do the readings. He also gives extra credit opportunities by going to events, having perfect attendance, and participating class. Can be hard to participate and understand the key points sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a bad professor, just a boring class. But I am also not interested in the class topic at all. Beware of pop quizzes because lots of reading, and class consist one 1 exam, 2 papers, and a final. A reasonable grader, and easy to reach out to. I would recommend this class if you are interested in philosophy, but if not, I wouldn't take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class wasn't awful but it was just so boring. Every day in class it was just us listening to him talk about the dense reading we were assigned. There are random pop quizzes throughout the semester. I just wish the class was more organized as the syllabus is a joke for staying on track. There were times Sebell didn't even know when break was
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked Professor Sebell - he brings up very interesting points about justice and how justice is defined (the class is listed as SCLL 103). I really don't understand the hate against him, especially considering how our class average is probably around the A/B range. Great lecturer, lots of discussions in class, and very quick with emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst professor experience I have had at UNC. Horrible, unorganized lectures and awful grading system. Absolutely no positives from taking his class, and I dreaded every day that I had his class. Painfully long and boring lectures. DO NOT take any of his classes by any means.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures the whole class, line by line through dense readings. No participation, just him talking. Pure suffering - everyone hated it and struggled to stay awake, except that one reviewer. You haven't seen lifeless students until you've watched Sebell's class walk out at 10:45, and he noticed and didn't care at all.

In class, Prof. Sebell delivered incredible lectures on the basics of modern political theory. He is very knowledgable on the topics he teaches on, however his fatal flaw, funny enough, is that his lectures are often very long, because of his love for the material, so we did not get through all the expected readings. Overall, phenomenal professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course is one of the more doable chem courses at UNC. I would recommend taking it with Tiani.

His exams were fair. Lectures and practice sheets were helpful. However, he can be a little derogatory and overall unhelpful when you ask him a 1-on-1 question about a concept or question. ULAs were very helpful. He gives lots of resources to help you succeed. Easiest chem prof/class at UNC so far.

I took CHEM 241 as a first semester freshmen so my difficulty rating may be a bit high. Dr. Tiani gave clear lectures and the LAs would answer questions promptly. The only downside is that when drawing on the slides, his handwriting can be very hard to read at times.

Tiani really cares about students and is a very fair professor. Exams are challenging but expected based on what was covered in class and the practice problems. ULA sessions are VERY helpful. His practice sessions are also super helpful as well.

Good professor, good lectures, grades pretty fast. Actually teaches the material. CHEM241 is a lot of math and conceptual questions. Was nervous for the class but heard Tiani was the best, and he delivered! Make sure to read the textbook, stay on top of homework and pre class assignments. Review for at least a week before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The material is super dry but I really liked Tiani. Most of the exam questions were pretty straightforward, but some questions are very niche. Go to review sessions, especially Tiani's. If you skip class, make sure you have someone you can ask for notes. His handwriting is so bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Analytical chemistry is not the most exciting of classes, but I did really like Dr. Tiani. He is quite helpful during office hours and his exams were challenging, but fair. Unlike other professors in the chem department, I believe Dr. Tiani truly cares about student well-being and success. Would overall recommend him!

Tiani is very understanding of academic pressure and wants his students to succeed. If you want to do well in his class make sure to do all of the ULA practice problems before tests and go to or do the worksheet from his twice weekly review session. Sometimes he uses problems from these sessions on the exam.

this chem lab is not taught by him but he did write the final which was impossible and caused my grade to go from an A to a B+. however, this is just standard of all UNC chem lab finals, where they are impossible to do well on and unrelated to the actual course materials.

tiani is the best chem professor i have had at UNC. his lectures are extremely helpful and to the point. he goes over exactly what you need for the exam and his exams are extremely fair. they were all problems i had seen before, whether it was on homework or from his problem sessions. however, his handwriting is impossible to read on the slides.

I can't say too much because this lab isn't exactly taught by him, but I will say I was shocked as he was extremely gracious and understanding when I got violently sick mid chem exam week; he let me take the lab final the next week. Overall seems very understanding in terms of student well-being (although I can't speak on his teaching capabilities)
His handwriting is quite literally indecipherable. If you miss one class be prepared to be lost for the remainder of the entire unit.

very lecture heavy, yet the exams almost always have content that was barely touched on. I never once skipped his class, took notes, and studied with plenty of time, and i found it super difficult. he is very knowledgable about analytical chemistry but also kind of rude when students don't understand a concept. discouraging a little.

Dr. Tiani clearly knows analytical pretty well but his class is very lecture/textbook heavy. He seems caring in class but 1-on-1 he can be super rude and unwilling to explain difficult concepts. The material is extremely boring but he doesn't ask any trick questions on exams.

Dr. Tiani sounds like a professor who knows the information that he is teaching, but this is another case where his exams don't match what he teaches sometimes. Theory questions on exams are easy, but math can be ok to very niche and crazy sometimes, rarely in stuff he gives. He is very helpful in his office hours, would recommend him overall.

not a bad teacher at all, but very tough. my main issue with prof. tiani is that about halfway through the semester he would get mad at students asking questions in the lecture/just answering a question he asked wrong. it kinda discouraged engagement a bit. also for exams, study the content that doesn't get reviewed often. it WILL be on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Tiani is really good at teaching. I enjoyed his class and it came out well. He is really a nice person, and it's helpful to go to his office hour.

Dr. Tiani was one of the best professors I've had under UNC's chemistry department. I was personally a big fan of his lecture style, as he'd often go over the exact content that you needed to know to do well on his exams. The lectures are somewhat rapid paced, but if you set aside some time a day to work/review practice problems, you'll do great!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Tiani is an amazing professor. He is always eager to help you and answer the questions and hold multiple help session for students to grasp the content. He's a very caring toward the success of his students. The only challenge was the final, which was a lot harder than the midterms imo. Would 100% take again.

I took Dr. Tiani for Summer 241 class. Overall he's a very nice teacher and always happy to help you whether it is discussing study strategies or helping clear up concepts. His exam questions are similar to problem session and poll ev in class questions so make sure to attend his sessions whenever you can.
One of the fairest STEM profs I've had at UNC. Great lecturer, fair exams, and super accessible outside class. 100% recommend taking 241 with him!
tiani is awesome.

Glad I took 241 w/ Tiani! Easy to understand lectures & tests were very fair (+ part of your final can replace your lowest test grade). 241 (content) may be the easiest chem at UNC. Tiani is very straightforward which can come off as condescending but imo he just tells it like it is. Take notes in class - handwriting is impossible to decipher.

Analytical is already a weird class since it doesn't go along with other chemistry courses, but Tiani made this way more unbearable. His handwriting was impossible to read, and I spent more time trying to decipher it than learn the material. I couldn't follow his lectures and ended up teaching myself the entire class online in order to get an A.

Tiani's lectures were helpful to explain the readings. However, extra practice and GPSS are definitely necessary to get a good grade in the class. Do not go to his GPSS or office hours. He is very condescending, especially in small groups and one on one. He talks over you, does not answer your question, and rambles. Makes you feel dumb.

If you go out of your way to get to know Dr. Tiani, he is extremely nice and willing to help however he can.  Tests are hard but cover material closely to what is taught, although some questions will catch you off guard.  Go to problem sessions, ask questions, practice, take it seriously, and you will be fine.  Long final, bring a snack with you.

Chem is challenging no matter what. Tiani's handwriting is hard to read, but I got used to it with time. I found him to be very kind and whenever I approached him he was super welcoming. Remember to get iclicker responses in before he closes the window. The app will show that you submitted answers after the window closes, but they won't count.

Dr. Tiani is very passionate about his job and cares a lot about the success of his students. I think his tests were similar to his PowerPoints, PollEv questions, HW questions, and Tiani review sessions. Tons of resources available, so if you use them and practice you'll do well. Some of chemical methods are more abstract but it is interesting!

Despite not having a great grade, Dr.Tiani is such a good professor for Analytical Chem. His tests are pretty straightforward, he teaches in a way that is applicable outside of class, and he's funny. He is very helpful both in and outside of class. Further, he ensures that students understand the material and know they aren't defined by a grade.
Chem 102 is hard in general but Tiani is a great teacher. no complaints besides his handwriting which is pretty atrocious but other than that great guy.

You can tell that Dr. Tiani enjoys teaching this class and is very knowledgeable about the subject. However, this means that sometimes he goes off on tangents unrelated to the tested topics. Additionally, his class is very test heavy but the tests are fair. Finally, the only negative thing about his lectures is his handwriting.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is truly a great professor to have for 241 and is good at teaching the material. He is organized and it was a pleasure to be in his class. Doing a lot of practice problems and understanding the concepts is the best way to succeed in this class. Go to LA sessions as well.

Tiani is a great professor and his exams were fair. I went to his problem solving sessions and he wasn't too condescending. He just wants to make sure you understand the material and wants to get the best out of you. He is very nice and I enjoyed his class. Sometimes it was hard to read his handwriting on the lecture slides. Do lots of practice.

I was soo nervous to take 241 w/ Tiani but I think he's the best choice! His exams are fair, only tests you on class material, and he grades generously with lots of partial credit. If you study, you'll be fine. He is also accessible and willing to help during office hrs. A lot of people said he was condescending, but I didn't get that from him.
His handwriting is terrible but he's a pretty good professor. Lectures are good.

He's fine, I honestly learned more from going to Bliem's GPSS sessions whenever I had questions though. Since Chem is standardized, it doesn't really matter who you have, you just need to learn the concepts

Tiani had incredibly fair midterms and finals and gave a lot of things to prepare for each one. His slides are helpful, although his handwriting can be hard to read. Best analytical professor. I can see how he could come off as condensing like some reviews say but his intentions are kind and he always wants to help. Always accessible.

He seems really nice but has the most unengaging lectures. I don't think I learned a single thing from his lectures they were so all over the place. The exams were easy enough that I could cram the night before and do well. Also... his handwriting

He is smart to the point where he doesn't know how to "dumb" things down. He is honestly so caring and really tried to help when I went to him about concerns about my grade. However, if you need an organized professor to learn DO NOT TAKE HIM. His handwriting is literally impossible to read, and he can be hard to understand during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tiani's class is manageable if you keep up with the readings and stay engaged. The exams are fair, but he can be blunt in office hours. Unstuck ai was helpful for practice problems - a great resource alongside the textbook.

He is a very good lecturer and wants his students to succeed. He cares about the subject and explains better than most of the other chem professors I've had. Definitely recommend taking his class, but if you go to office hours beware he will yap forever.
Great professor with fair exams. Exam heavy class, but lots of resources to succeed. Very nice guy and wants his students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Tiani's slides aren't very organized, which was really difficult to study. Tiani doesn't test solely on lecture content, so you have to be sure that you understand supplemental material like the homework problems. I appreciated that he was accessible outside of class, but he can be condescending/rude in office hours, so just be aware of that!

Great professor!
Nice and accessible, offers plenty of office hours and extra credit. Is knowledgable and will answer your questions. Clear about everything- doesn't offer practice exams but lectures and reading materials are very direct and everything is easily accessible and organized.

I was nervous to take Tiani but didn't find anything wrong with him. ULAs were helpful & his exams are fair. Tho the book is dense and indirect so rely mainly on his annotated slides and ULA practice. His exams are not very long so don't make silly mistakes (like I did lol). And he does reuse questions, so study with friends' old exams if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Tiani is a great lecturer whose slides and course schedule are very organized and well-planned. Read the textbook, take notes of everything during lecture, and attend ULA sessions and you'll do well. Exams are very fair and the homework is easy if you do the reading!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good lecturer, makes it clear what is expected of you on tests. Good about providing reminders for due dates. I thought the class was structured well and the slides showed important material from the textbook. No practice exams so use PM sessions as that. There is a textbook but you'll be fine with slides and practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Your grade for 241L is dependent on your TA, but Dr. Tiani made a well-organized plan for this course. Everything they are looking for in reports is stated, and there are sheets with information about what to do when writing. He was also accessible and adaptable to changes in the semester.

Dr. Tiani is a good lecturer. If you want to do well on the tests, study all of the slides, complete his problem sets, work through the LA slides, and redo the graded homework. Studying for the tests is very time-consuming, so don't procrastinate! He's very condescending in office hours, so be prepared to get insulted even though he will help you.

This class was very doable and the easiest chem class I've taken at UNC. I was able to sneak through while doing basically the bare minimum and am still set to do decently overall. Tests were fair for the most part - but the final was way too long. Dr. Tiani was an okay lecturer, but I agree with the other reviews that say he can be condescending.

As my first Chem class at UNC, this certainly was not a bad one. However, I can say that Dr. Tiani can be often rude and condescending when you ask questions. The exams were fair and his presentations and participation questions helped me prepare for them. You also get one midterm replacement with the final exam, which is nice.

Analytical is not a difficult class as far as UNC chem goes, but Dr. Tiani makes it impossible to ask for help at problem-solving sessions without feeling humiliated. It says a lot that his TAs/grad students are scared of him, and I frankly feel bad for them.
Very present as a lab instructor. He does not determine grading of lab reports; however, is able to get changes out very quickly through messages. No real complaints.

Genuinely one of the meanest, most condescending people on planet earth. He will make you feel absolutely terrible when you ask a question. Constantly told students to walk themselves back to gen chem. Also he always has an ugly/cruel/mean smirk. Least favorite professor in the chem department... that's saying a lot.

The overall course wasn't too bad, the easiest chem course I've taken at UNC. Tiani is friendly but tends to ramble when you ask him questions. I depended on peer mentors for explanations. He is nice, especially if you sit in the front and participate in class and are attentive. The tests are fair and mainly cover what are on his power points.

I'm in Tiani's summer session. Lectures and his online site are very disorganized and hard to follow. He is often rude when people ask questions, saying they would know if they did the reading. He hardly does practice problems in class and only gives conceptual explanations for complicated math problems. Have to teach myself how to do all the math
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, I loved Dr. Tiani. I had him for the honors section. Chem102 is difficult, but he makes it a priority to help students. For the honors section, we had a few random assignments, and he graded them pretty difficult, but overall it was a grade boost. The exams were hard but manageable, just stay on top of your work and ask questions.

Tiani was a good lecturer. My only issue with his teaching is that when you'd ask a question, he'd interrupt you to answer the question, but he wouldn't even fully answer the question. However, he does still explain concepts well in lecture. I have also heard from other people in my class that he's condescending, but he was nothing but nice to me.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tiani is a good lecturer, but dry. He gives a pretty clear outline of what concepts to focus on in the pre-class reading which is helpful for preparing. You definitely need to do the readings thought to succeed in the class. His exams are pretty fair, and he also reuses problems from past exams a lot which is nice.

I def enjoyed this class and the material much more than gen chem, and thought Dr. Tiani explained everything well. If I ever had any questions, the peer mentor review sessions helped A TON. He was also very communicative with the class, which I really appreciated!
Exams are pretty straightforward (no trick questions) and Tiani is straightforward as well. Expectations were made clear and this class was a much better experience than gen chem at UNC.

Dr. Tiani was very straightforward (which could sometimes come off as being rude), but in my experience he's been very nice and pretty humorous. I found the class to be very fair; we didn't really find things on the exam that we didn't cover. The peer mentor sessions helped me a lot! I found this class better than general chemistry classes.

CHEM-241 was definitely straightforward if you read/skimmed the textbook and did multiple practice problems a day. The material is different from the usual stuff you learn in chemistry but can be interesting once you understand it. The lectures for 241 were dry, but as long as you can teach yourself some of the curriculum, you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are probably more boring than listening to stories about your grandmother's Hummel collection, but as long as you somewhat understand what is going on you'll be fine. He says a bunch of extra stuff in the lectures that will never appear on tests. The tests are fair but provide very little room for error and limited partial credit.

He's a decent prof. He is not always the nicest; I'd feel weird going to him with questions. His handwriting is also awful which can make understanding lectures challenging. Basically, he isn't fantastic but he gets the job done (241 won't be great no matter who you take it with). If you take his course, the peer mentors are your best resource!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked Dr. Tiani. I took his course as a First Year Launch. He was very interested in teaching the course, but also in guiding us as students at UNC, and provided helpful advice and was flexible. You do have a flipped classroom model of sorts, but his lectures go over the content, and he includes practice problems in them. Exams are fair.

Overall, Tiani isn't a bad professor. The material itself is hard and lectures can be rambly at times, but his tests are very straightforward if you do the end of chapter problems and attend a few review sessions. Not an easy A but not a bad choice for 241 if you're able to teach yourself some of the material
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were clear, but he is rude sometimes, so I would be afraid to ask him questions. I relied mostly on peer mentors for help. Tests questions are often unclear, and he will not provide clarification during exams. Pay attention to small details on slides because they often came up on exams. The class requires a lot of time and effort.

Definitely the best chem professor so far. A good teacher, but test questions can be unclear or overly complicated. He also has a tendency to come off rude so don't take it personally. Make sure you always check the Sakai, syllabus, and email before you ask a question because he WILL try to tell you he already answered it there (even if he didn't).

One of the rudest profs that I have ever had. Despite the fact that the class material isn't that hard, and he lectures very well, he does not treat students with respect AT ALL. Very condescending, and often blames the class for things that are his fault. Make sure to pay attention WELL in lecture. Overall, good professor, but not a good person.

Dr. Tiani can be condescending towards students, but he wants them to succeed. He actually teaches the material in class and offers many helpful peer mentor sessions outside of class. The class takes a lot of time and effort to understand the material, but the tests were very reasonable and fair.

This course needs to be structured better so that failing or getting a C is not the expected outcome. IT should not be this hard to succeed in a class. 
Tiani often had a condescending attitude towards students. Class material was heavy and complicated and often not well explained in lecture.

Tiani is great. I was a little worried based on some of these reviews, however, he really values you getting to an answer yourself and similarly not giving you the answer if its a simple question that you already know which may come off as condescending. He is by far the best lecturer I have had at UNC and one of the most approachable profs here.

Tiani is genuinely the worst professor I have ever had. He laughed at the class when talking about midterm grades and said he knows we have been taught the content and that it was our fault for not learning it. He will regularly laugh at you when you ask questions. Tests are insanely hard and totally out of left field. Do NOT take his classes.

Tiani is a good lecturer and give fair tests. He has a personality that can come off as rude sometimes, but he just wants you to think and means wells. The tests reflected what was went over in lecture and were not that bad, though it did make up 89% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is so condescending and honestly makes me not even want to try. I studied so hard and was continually told how inferior I was. He interrupts students constantly. Clickers in class are graded (80%+ right = 100%). The class isn't impossible, but don't even try to get help outside of class. I relied on peer tutors.

Dr. Tiani wants you to actually learn so he won't give straight answers, but he will always go over everything in lecture, so its fair. You can expect your grade to reflect the amount of effort you put in. Nothing too horrible but the subject can be dry at times. Do your readings, attend lectures, and go to problem solving sessions to get your A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class was fair but very difficult, lectures can be boring as well and he was unapproachable most of the time. Honestly I only felt comfortable asking the peer mentor questions and going to his review sessions to get my questions answered. Not a necessarily bad professor but try to avoid if you can

Dr. Tiani was a fair professor. If you go to office hours, do your research beforehand (in lecture slides and the textbook). Attend peer mentor sessions, refer back to lecture slides, re-do iClicker problems, and you'll find the exams to be very fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I have mixed feelings about Tiani. As someone who is subpar at chemistry, I cant blame him for me not doing as well as I wanted, but his class is just a lecture the whole time which can be really hard to pay attention to. He can be a bit condescending but always means well, if you put in a ton of time into his class you can succeed.

Second time taking Tiani- had him a couple of years ago for CHEM 102. One of the better choices for 241, he replaces your low midterm scores if you do better on the final, so just study for the final and you're set. Pay attention in lecture and expect about 2-5 hours of work outside class per week.

Look--it's a chemistry class at UNC so it isn't going to be easy or fun, but Tiani made this class about as good as it could be. It's a very dry subject, but he made it somewhat interesting. Tests were very fair and mirrored provided resources exactly. He gave students bonus participation points so missing class wouldn't affect your grade.

Ah yes, good old "Demonic" Tiani. I've had this guy twice; for CHEM 102 the first time and then for 241. He's by no means the worst chemistry professor at UNC, his lectures are clear and exams are generally fair yet difficult. Middle of the road, not the best choice but not the worst either.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: On the whole, Prof. Tiani is decent. Very personable during lecture but less so outside of class. For a level 200 class, it's unusually content-heavy. Exams are medium-hard, and grading is on the more stringent, nitpicky side. If you're one of the few people who likes challenges, take it with him. Otherwise, look into other options.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: TBH he has never come off as rude to me when answering questions, but I've only ever interacted with him during class time. Dr. Tiani is a solid choice for 241 in my opinion.

Tiani seemed like a solid professor, but made the class a bit difficult with the amount of reading that we had to do. Lectures can get a bit boring and the material of the class is tough. He definitely makes you put in the effort to pass the exams. Consider taking another professor if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Just a rude professor in general and his problem sessions aren't helpful because he takes 30 minutes to explain one problem . He has clear lectures and his tests aren't easy but nothing surprising but just so rude
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I swear to god if this man mispronounces solute again I will lose it.

Tiani is a tough professor and can be insulting when you dont know an answer but I can say hes earned my respect because he made me try really hard to get through this class. I think he just tries to use a scare tactic in order to get his students to try harder. Make sure to read chapters before class and come prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is 89% test heavy, 35% is the final and the rest are 3 midterms (18% each). Mentor review sessions, working through end of chapter problems, and doing the practice sets are the best way to succeed. Be prepared to study and ask questions to Dr. Tiani or the mentors.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ignore everything that has been said in the other reviews. He is a real gem, he cares for you to learn the material and his exams are not tricky. They are difficult, but not failure level. Him being condescending is only to those who ask questions when he has clearly said that answer.. don't be that person. You will do great. He is my fav professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tiani is way better than his reputation makes him seem. He's not super friendly; I think his personality rubs some people the wrong way. But he is a good teacher. I really learned the material, and the exams are very fair. And he does do exam replacement for your lowest midterm which is nice. Overall, he's a solid choice and deserves more credit.

Overall this was an ok class. He's a fair grader as some people say. I wouldn't say I loved or even liked going to his office hours that much. If you want to succeed, definitely go to mentor sessions (they know what they're doing) and do practice problems. As said before he's a fair grader and doesn't give too many trick questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: good lectures, pretty test heavy. Don't go to office hour without having read the concepts and tried to understand the topics. Tests are pretty difficult, especially the final, so work lots of practice problems before them. Mastering the material is a must, not just understanding concepts
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tiani is by far the worst professor I have ever had. He was condescending towards students and would criticize students who asked questions he deemed not the 'right' question or not smart enough (the question), but he gets upset the no one asks anything. Beware of the final exam, it comes out of left field. Avoid his class as much as you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Tiani's exams were very straightforward. You have to read the textbook a lot to do well, which can be super boring. There aren't too many assignments. This is definitely not the hardest chem class.

He gave us fair tests throughout the semester , until the final which totally blindsided most of the class by being the hardest test of the semester.
