He is not curving saying that people earn their grades, but for one test that brought people 2 letter grades down, it is extremely unfair. Was on a steady track to get an A, now sitting at a low B
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Is extremely unprofessional. Was completely rude to students who were just trying to ask questions about the topic, discouraging students from speaking up in class. Just don't take him if you want a nice prof who is willing to help you get through this course.

I think he's very knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches. As others have said, however, he does often come off as pretty condescending if you don't understand everything right away. Consistently doing the problems at the back of the textbook and redoing problems from lecture slides is your best bet to succeed in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Tiani was incredibly condescending towards students who asked questions during class and would get easily irritated whenever someone would ask a question because he assumed that we would be experts at the material after one lecture. He was a good lecturer but I mainly relied on the textbooks and peer mentor sessions to make it through.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Tiani was a great professor, and he is very knowledgeable on the material. The exams were very fair as he was not trying to trick you, but make sure to do the end of chapter problems in book. His lectures are normal, but the material can get complex so had to spend a lot of time reading book to grasp it. Only downfall is he lacks patience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ok so Tiani does not at all respect his students and makes anyone who asks questions feel stupid and ridiculed. However, he is a great teacher, especially compared to the other 241 teachers. His tests and grading are fair and pretty consistent with what he teaches. You will just have to go to mentors or someone else for one on one help.

I did well in this class, but because I worked hard. I refused to go to office hours and ask for help because he is very condescending and mean, but I was able to understand all the concepts by reading the textbook and doing textbook and pollev problems again and again. This class is a lot of work to get an A, it should be more than 2 credits.

I liked Tiani, his lectures made sense and gave a lot of opportunities for practice. If you know how to study (do his practice problems and pm sessions!) you'll be fine. We got grades for participation and daily hw, but it was mostly made up of exams. Opportunity to replace lowest midterm w final, but final was v hard.

Honestly, Dr. Tiani is rude and unaccessible. He asks for questions only to roast anyone who asks a question he sees as unnecessary. He was by far my worst professor when adjusting to the COVID-19 pandemic and he made my situation much more difficult than it needed to be. He does care about his students, but he does not know how to relate to them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's truly just a rude man. Even online he somehow found a way to be condescending and mean. His class isn't the worst so if you need the credit it will be ok but try another teacher at all costs. He really is just not great at conveying information.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Tiani's lectures were pretty clear and easy to understand. He does a good job of explaining the information from the textbook and he frequently posts videos to help. However, he is extremely condescending and is very difficult to ask questions. He would threaten harder tests or to grade participation on accuracy if we didn't answer immediately.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The textbook for this class is horrible. Tiani is very condescending to his students and will shame you for not knowing things. Class is 3 times a week for a 2 credit course but easily dominates your schedule. Do not take.

Dr. Tiani is knowledgable and a decent lecturer, but if you ask questions he is VERY condescending. I was afraid to ask questions because he treated students like they were dumb. Overall, I felt like I learned a lot and the exams were fair. The textbook sucks, but Tiani posts videos that are helpful. Graded homeworks were similar to the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is my third class with Tiani and by the end of every semester I realize why he is one of my least favorite professors at UNC. While the class might not be that bad, not only are the lectures BORING, the class somewhat follows a flipped classroom setup. Even though the textbook is horrible, I learn more from that than the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Not an easy teacher, but if you put in the work, he will recognize that.
Tiani was a decent lecturer - he definitely knew the material. But he was consistently rude and condescending to students who asked questions in class. The textbook is a complete joke.

I think Dr. Tiani is actually a really good professor and good at explaining things - he's a master of metaphor. I do think that the textbook for this class isn't great and should be replaced. This class is hard and Tiani expects a lot, asking challenging questions on tests, so it can be hard to get a good grade, but I learned a lot in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really disliked Dr Tiani. Lectures were SO dry - hard to focus in class. He seemed to discourage questions from students and was unapproachable. Exams were 80% of our grade and graded harshly. The textbook was more confusing than other textbooks used in the chem dept. Lab was such an extreme amount of work for a measley grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Doctor Tiani obviously understands his material, however if you dont got to class there is no way you will know what is going on because his power points dont convey what he says in class. No mater how much work you do outside class it will never be enough for him and his answers to questions are condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Overall I found Dr. Tiani to be a pretty good 241 prof. He can def be condescending during class but he was a clear lecturer. You definitely have to study a lot to do well, but the final grade replacement can help a lot. The tests were fair and grading wasn't too harsh compared to some others. Not a bad choice at all for analytical
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Tiani is the worst teacher I've ever had in my life. He sends a million emails even on weekends. He speaks to us lie we are not worth his time. He is not considerate towards the difficulties we face in the COVID19 epidemic. I really regret taking his class, avoid at all costs. Lab was trash, imagine spending 20 hrs on a report for a D!!

Tiani is absolutely terrible. He has is condescending towards his students, he is not willing to help at all. He sends massive emails that could've been 4 lines long; he just loves wasting your time. He is not considerate at all about circumstances such as the COVID-19 pandemic. Taking lab with him was the worst experience I've had at UNC.
Gave him one star just because I couldn't give him zero.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I have never held such little respect for a professor before. He's rude, unhelpful, and passive aggressive. When students ask for help he will tell you it was in your reading. Chemistry is a hard class, and relying on a poorly written textbook to teach materials is childish. If you must take 241 with him make sure to read the text book and GL
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tiani does not deserve all the bad reviews on here. Took him for Chem 241 and 241L and he was great!!! He made analytical chemistry better than gen chem by far, was easy to understand, and had really fair tests. If you do the practice problems at the end of the textbook and take good notes in class you will be fine!!

I found lectures confusing and boring. He often goes off on long rambling tangents. Exams are hard and graded hard. Lectures did not help my understanding at all. In fact, the only way you'll understand anything from this class with Tiani is if you are taking lab too.

I won't lie and say professor tiani was nice, but he definitely knows how to teach chemistry. I would come in knowing nothing and be incredibly confused by the textbook and he would explain everything in an easy way that was relatable. I loved his class! He is very clear about what is expected and his tests are never unpredictable.

I have had the man for Chem102 and Chem241 and truth to be told he is a good lecturer. He's def scary, but he gives you enough resources in order for you to succeed. Just like most classes, the more work your put in the better your grade will be. Tests are fair. The man is condescending for sure, but he has the knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Worst professor you'll ever take. The guy hates his students and grades way too harshly. Lectures are boring and dry, and if you have him for 241L it is even worse -- so much work, graded way too hard. I spent 10+ hours on a lab report only to get a 50. Do not take his class!

Dr. Tiani makes lectures extremely boring and really hard for students who barely have a grasp on the material. You are expected to master topics just from the readings. Not very accessible outside of class and really only likes you if you know the material and ask good questions. Would not recommend for a introduction chemistry course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Tiani is naturally condescending, but you can tell he wants students to understand and to apply chemical concepts in 102. I don't suggest going to office hours since they never helped me personally, but the peer mentor sessions are definitely helpful depending on the mentor. Also, do the recommended practice problems. The class is test heavy!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A great lecturer. He is very fluid and easy to follow. As a person, he can be a little condescending but it never bothered me. He makes you work for an A, but if you have a good work ethic then you'll be fine. I am taking another chem class with him. Don't be intimidated by the comments, he isn't that bad. Chem is just a hard subject at UNC.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tiani is a really great lecturer. General chemistry is really content-heavy so I assume it is pretty difficult to teach, but his lectures are clear and precise. He gives you a lot of extra practice and encourages all of his students to go to either his or the mentors' problem sessions. (Go. They are helpful!) I am taking his class again!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Tiani is a good lecturer and easy to follow in class. His exams are pretty straightforward if you paid attention in class and studied well. However, he is pretty condescending and does not seem to really care about his students. All in all he is a good professor who knows his stuff, he just is not the nicest human
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. He always takes time to make sure we understand the material, clear, and grades fairly. If you understand the material and do well on the homework, you should ace the exams. Good choice for CHEM 102.

Professor Tiani is a solid choice for chem 102. He is fairly straightforward and his expectations are clear. He definitely knows how to demand the respect of the room. There are daily quizzes with the clickers, a good amount of homework and readings everyday. There are graded homework assignments every weekend. I am taking another course by him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Tiani explained the course material well and didn't overcomplicate anything. It's chemistry so it's not supposed to be easy but he did the best he could. Other reviews make him sound condescending but as a woman, I have not experienced that at all. He's a solid choice and I chose him again for my next chem class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you took AP Chem in high school and did well in it, this class shouldn't be too hard for you. He's a good lecturer, clearly knows his stuff and easy enough to follow. I will say that he is a harder grader than the other professors though. But other than that, it's definitely not the end of the world if you're stuck with him for 102.

It's important to keep in mind that CHEM102 is meant to weed people out and reduce the number of chem majors early on, the difficulty on the tests are to be expected regardless. That being said, Tiani is a pretty solid lecturer who gives good explanations and teaches well. His downside is that he is not a very receptive person in and out of class.
He wads so condescending and rude when I went to him for help, and was not at all understanding of extenuating circumstances. Literally the rudest professor I've had in college.
really condescending and mean
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: tiani is a great lecturer and his exams are very fair. He can be a bit intimidating one on one, but overall very helpful professor.

Great lectures but difficult exams. Slightly unclear what you are expected to know for exams, and it is very easy to lose points. Not a very personable guy either, but definitely knows his chemistry and can convey it well.

Dr. Tiani's course was a flipped classroom style which I don't enjoy. I find the concepts of CHEM102 difficult to learn from a textbook. His lectures were not very helpful and he can be condescending at times. Overall, try to pick someone else for chemistry, but if you have to take it with Tiani utilize outside resources for help like peer mentors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Chem102 is a flipped classroom which I hated. He expected you to have mastered complex math concepts from explanations in a mediocre textbook that would have been better taught face to face. Tiani would be pretty kind sometimes and all of a sudden be vicious towards a student. Overall a pretty solid prof if you pick up things really quickly.

Literally you can go to class and completely comprehend the material but Tiani will find a way to make you fail the test. Honestly he knows his material but he has such an inadequate way of teaching the class that you just cant ace the tests. I enjoy chemistry in general and love analytical but this was such a pointless hoop to have to jump through
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: CHEM102 is always hard; it's not up to individual professors to decide tests/homework. Tiani tries to get us to understand material instead of memorizing, which is good since that's what you need to do on tests. However I've been to office hours often and he's condescending, unhelpful, and has yelled at me instead of listening to me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The teacher was fun and he brought in a few physical examples of topics. One bad side is that he occasionally laughs in that way like "this is so easy" and then gets serious when he sees that we haven't got it yet and looks like he is judging us.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Tiani is an excellent teacher! The material IS hard, but he provides everything in timely manner, ensuring students can work as efficiently as possible. Everything he does in a classroom directly prepares students for exams and beyond. Most importantly, Dr. Tiani is a kind, good-hearted man who truly cares about students reaching their goals!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: worst professor. extremely rude and condescending. expects you to remember everything after only reading it once. unrealistic expectations of what students are able to understand after one lecture.

It is very obvious that he understands chemistry, but sometimes he expects his students to fully understand the concepts that are currently being taught. He does want his students to perform well, but appears condescending when a student asks a question, resulting in students shying away from asking questions.

Professor Tiani made gen chem way harder than it needed to be. The class average of Fall 2017 was a 74 (C average). His class acts more like a flip classroom, very learning catalytics (LC) heavy. He would go over the LC questions everyone got right, but then the ones that had a 30% correct he would skip....
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He's a really great lecture however the midterms rarely add up to the difficulty of the graded homework. A lot of times the midterms combine topics in ways that you have never seen before making it extremely difficult. Would recommend going to office hours and problem solving sessions in order to pass the class.

He is going to be tough, no sugarcoating. But it's because he wants his students to learn more than just memorizing equations. The concepts will be essential for pre-med, chem majors, etc. He won't accept questions that has him hand the answer to you. Study, try, and show him that you are trying. He'll respect you if you try your hardest.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I feel like I wasted a whole semester going to his lecture because he just reads what is on his slides. He will work out some problems and clicker questions were the only reason I went to class. He is a poor lecturer: I never went to office hours because I heard he was condescending and I passed. I went to chempossible and that really helped.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class was tough. Tiani is an okay lecturer at best. My real issue was office hours. I would ask him questions in office hours and he was very condescending and seemed generally bothered by my presence. If you take his class, go somewhere else for help. His office hours were honestly a waste of my time.

TAs do all the work/grading for this course, but Tiani organizes everything and makes the exams and rubrics. Grading is much better than 101/102L since your TA grades all your lab reports. Final exam was kind of tricky, but each course section gets curved at the end, so overall not bad. Definitely take advantage of TA office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He is a pretty good lecturer and he explains the material really well. However, when I asked him about an exam question to see whether it should've been regraded, he completely passed me off and would be even let me finish asking my question before he interrupted me. He has a little bit off a testy personality and is tough to deal with sometimes.

Yes his office hours are awful and you will feel like the dumbest person on the planet but it'll help you understand the concepts. He's a great lecturer and genuinely cares for how well his class does and explains concepts fairly well. If you have a background from AP Chem, you'll be fine.

Tiani is an amazing professor if you are interested in science. If you are taking his class for the credit, you won't like him. He makes lectures fun and interesting and understands his students' needs. Many people say he is rude and condescending but I don't see it. Mandatory reading quizzes (easy) every day so don't show up late
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Wow Tiani is actually really bad and the worst. Chem Lab in itself is brutal but the fact that we have him as a coordinator makes the whole process a lot worse. Very disorganized, rude, impatient, and just an overall negative quality. -1000/10 dont reccomend. But lol hes the only lab instructor tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very organized and very unhelpful. Dr. Tiani is extremely unwilling to help students with anything that he deems not worth his time. Instead of trying to understand student's needs, Tiani tends to ignore them in order to keep the classes running smoothly. The classes are very organized, just hope that you never have to deal with the man in charge.
Not the nicest person but he knows his stuff. would not take this class if i didn't need it. pay attention and don't skip. also go to peer mentors
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I struggled with this class. Going to lecture is SO important and reading about what he's going to talk about BEFORE lecture is so important, or you won't understand a word he says. The tests are really tough, and you have to know how to solve chem problems fast or you won't make it through them. Found HW questions from the book to be a bit useless
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: A truly condescending man. You can do something like ask a question and he will treat it like the end of the world. The course itself was not hard but dealing with Prof. Tiani was one of the lowest things at UNC.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Really not that bad. Was a very good lecturer; you could tell he knows his stuff. He can seem a little offensive when responding to questions- but if you use the peer mentors more, you can still get answers. You can drop one exam, and he also gave us some extra points at the end for hw. Gives you a ton of extra material, the more you do the better.

Just please don't take his class. I love chemistry and taking his class was just a pain. He is unapproachable; he stresses how he wants to help students but will just belittle you if you give an answer wrong or ask a simple question. Also, I feel pretty unprepared for the common exams when just looking over the lecture notes/practice problems.

Dr. Tiani is a gifted lecturer. Compared to many professors who ramble/ stutter, his lectures are extremely organized and coherent. Offers many opportunities to get help outside of class. Exams are hard, but fair (similar to difficult HW problems). Rumored to make people cry, but in reality doesn't seem to be all that bad if you show up prepared.

Dr. Tiani is a great lecturer. His tests (hard) are written on specifically what he talks about in class; the more math heavy questions are from the homework. You really have to "understand the chemistry" when taking this class with him. Be strong and study hard; he can be hard on you if you let him-don't let him. He wants you to learn. Final hard

Great professor.  He expects his students to be mature and accountable for their own learning.  Do exactly what he recommends to prepare for tests.  Do the practice problems and come to class.  If you do these things you will find that his tests are very fair.  He really wants everyone to do well.  He is the professor to take for analytical chem.
One of the most difficult courses I've taken at UNC. Extremely tough grader, can be kind of rude to students, made me cry once in office hours.
He explains concepts clearly and is upfront with what he expects of the class. Do your work and you'll be fine.

Great lecturer presents topics very clearly and efficiently. He doesn't mess around in class which was good for someone like me. He gives lots of required homework and some optional problems. If you do all the problems he gives you you should be fine. he is a little unapproachable

To give him credit, Professor Tiani knows gen Chem topics and is solid at teaching them in lectures. Besides that, he is an abysmal professor. Completely unapproachable and rude. Every time he talks to the student its like he's getting in a the ring with them, trying to knock them down with insults and ruin their day.

Everyone told me I would hate Tiani and to switch out but honestly I loved being in his class. His lectures are amazing and yes his personality is a little rough around the edges but he does care for students and cracks a few jokes every now and then. This class isn't for everyone but I do recommend him as a professor.
I really hated this class. He made the concepts sound easy in lecture but then tested us on incredibly difficult problems. I would not recommend him at all.
He is not easily to approach but really does want you to do well. He just makes you work for it more then others.

I had to switch to regular 241 not bc material was hard but bc of his condescending attitude. Also he's needlessly strict about certain things that are a waste of time. For ex, my calculator solves quadratics. He said on an exam Id have to do it by hand to get credit, implying anything else was lazy. Nvm, doing it by hand leads to more errors.
Definitely a hard class but he gives you a lot of opportunity for help. Very condescending, but helpful nonetheless. Tests are hard but doable if you read and do practice problems.
He can be mean sometimes. Make sure not to ask stupid questions. The lab was really tiring. He uses clickers for the lecture quizzes.

He has way too high expectations for a general chemistry class. You have to put in a lot of work to read and do all the online homework. But he's a great lecturer, and I really understood the material just by attending class. I would only recommend him if you want to put in the work to really understand chemistry. If not, then stay away!
Tests weren't too bad for me.
Went in for help and he literally gave me a lecture on how I shouldn't be in his class.

Dr. Tiani is a pretty good lecturer teacher, but beware of office hours.  He is super condescending when you ask questions and makes you feel pretty stupid, even though in lectures he encourages students to stop by. There are also way too many online assignments.  Overall though, if you go to lectures and do the work, you should be fine.

Here's the truth: Tiani is a great lecturer, but everything he teaches can be learned from all of the online homework he gives you. The tests are simple (not easy) but tricky. There's more work than is necessary, and he can be condescending during office hours. Don't take him if you don't have to, but don't lament if you do. It won't be too bad.
HE'S SUCH AN JERK. NEVER ASK HIM A QUESTION. GOD. HE REALLY NEEDS TO RELAX AND BE LESS RUDE TO STUDENTS.

Lecture was interesting, tests were tricky and not easy. If you ask for help, he'll rant about how he already talked about it in class, berate you, and then go over everything. All in all, if you like criticism and subpar grades, then I recommend this class for you.
Tiani is the best lecturer I've had at Carolina. He is incredibly organized, explains concepts clearly, and lets everyone know exactly what will be covered on each test. I highly recommend him.

Tiani is very condescending and not helpful what so ever. If you are taking this class with him be prepared to give 90% of your semester attention on this class. You will have to read the book. He also gives online homework questions 4 times a semester that are designed to trick you and are full of mistakes and typos.

Tiani is a GREAT lecturer. However, If you do not like chemistry/aren't good at chemistry, don't take his class. It's tough & you have to be willing to work hard. If you do the practice & read, and are decent at chemistry, you'll be fine. He doesn't really answer questions, but if you go to office hours prepared, they are somewhat helpful.

This man has made this semester a living hell. I'm in no way good at chemistry but I've worked really hard in this class and still might not pass. The man is really smart but not a good teacher, he's rude in office hours and his tests are VERY difficult. Do yourself a favor and take it with someone else. I told myself I'd be ok and boy was I wrong!
Had CHEM 241 with him. Very hard class, especially the acid-base part. Make sure to do most of the homework.

Professor Tiani is one of the best professors I've had. He is a gifted lecturer and knows how to teach. He led an extremely organized class and is  highly responsible to his work and students. He also provides a lot of resources and help sessions. One word to summarize his class is: Wow!

This is the worst Chem teacher to get at UNC. There is a graded quiz question every day in class.  His tests do not focus on the general concepts and instead focus only on specific details. His lectures are ok. If you ask him a question he rambles on about what an idiot you are for asking before giving you an answer. DO NOT TAKE HIM!!

I do not doubt Dr. Tiani's intelligence. However, he is in no way good at teaching what he knows to general chemistry students. Going to Q&A sessions and office hours usually winds up with him asking you "Why don't you know this?" or saying "I've already covered this material." Smart, but condescending and quite unapproachable.

Tiani is a great lecturer but his tests are practically impossible.  Expect to be tested on Chem I material in Chem II tests.  He does not give study guides or old tests to look over. Tests are a million times harder than the practice questions in the book.  I highly recommend you take this course with any other teacher if possible.

Tiani is an EXCELLENT lecturer. You can learn a lot in this class if you attend class regularly and read your textbook...and reading your textbook is pretty much mandatory if you want to do well. His tests and graded homework assignments are difficult though, so you'll have to be prepared. Start off as strong as you can, don't leave room for slack!

Tiani is a good lecturer. He is very clear and explains the material well. If you speak with him one-on-one, though, he is pretty condescending and unhelpful. The class averages for the tests were '50', '63.7', and '59'. He applies a small curve (less than 4 points). He grades on a scale so that the vast majority of people with receive 'C's
If you can take this class with another professor, I'd highly recommend that course of action.
This class is hell and Tiani is Satan.

Teaching style very dull and unhelpful. The tests seemed to be purposefully made very hard. Many concepts would be wrapped into one long question, so going in knowing 90 percent of the stuff really well will never get you a 90. Unless you like overstudying for a 2hr class, avoid. I agree the teacher comes off as a snob. The textbook sucks too.

A nice person but sort of terrifying: don't be afraid to go see him but make sure you have specific questions because he doesn't want to baby anyone through the class.  Do as many problems as you can and don't put off ANYTHING. The material is hard to begin with and he can help you but not without helping yourself.

He's a little awkward but he tries to help out as much as possible. He kinda treats you like you're 5 though when he speaks to you. Nevertheless, he knows what he's talking about. THere are worse teachers out there. He's REALLY hard though.

Tiani is a great instructor who really wants you to learn the material. He's tough, but who isn't? Taking his class helps you improve your study skills and really prepares you for advanced Chem classes. Can't go wrong taking Tiani.

Tiani was a really nice guy and really enjoys lecturing.  His class is hard and you need to study and understand not only the math but also the concepts so reading the book is very important.  If your not a fast test taker, his test may also be difficult.  However, he prepares you for it.  Show your work or he will take off points!

Dr. Tiani is by far one of the best teachers I've had.  He really knows his stuff and he works his schedule around the students.  His class is a tough class, but for me it was a class that taught me how to study a lot better.  Definitely get this man, because he's a boss!
He is not helpful. He thinks just because things make sense to him they make sense to everyone. He really should just quit teaching.

a self-centered, egotistical **** who should be fired from UNC because of his arrogant cocky I?m better than you attitude towards all of the undergrad.  this jackoff thinks and carries himself like he is the baddest teacher in the department. if he?s so brilliant why is he working a 50k a year job and mopping up the general chem labs everyday

Must be a smart guy behind closed doors because I did not find his efficacy in the necessary intro chems and analytical chem. Any questions he receives in lecture are an excuse to sprint through explanations to demonstrate his brilliance without addressing underlying concerns/misunderstanding. not a people person unless you are a cute co-ed.

Dr. Tiani is the best chemistry professor I have ever had. His lectures are relatively interesting and as long as you know your stuff, he is pretty easy to follow along with. His class is very regimented in a detailed manner. He provides all the resources you need to succeed in his class including skeleton notes. So just study and you'll be fine.

Either you get him or you don't.  I don't.  He's incomprehensible and yammers on in the way that only a man who's defined by his PhD can.  Some people have this inborn Tiani decoder that lets them decipher the over-inflated gibberish in the lecture notes.  If you don't, drop the class  because it only gets worse.
He's a good teacher-- he's very clear with the material and the tests are not too tricky if you study a lot. However, he's pretty rude on a one on one basis.
He's a nice guy, but can be weird on a personal level. His assignments and often have errors that he has corrects later via e-mail, which can get confusing.

Dr. Tiani genuinely desires for his class to do well and learn the material.  He gives you all the resources you need to succeed.  The class is hard and requires a lot of work, but all tests and grading are totally fair.  His lectures are interesting and easy to follow - I find myself actually /interested/ in chemistry!

Tiani is not intimidating at all, he actually sent out an email one time apologizing for being too mean in class, when he wasn't being mean at all.  And he brought in his daughter's blocks for a visual one time and one was purple with a penguin on it. Extremely helpful, uses blackboard and the text a ton.  Do the work and you will have no problems.

Dr. Tiani can be fairly intimidating in class but a very personable professor if you ever need academic advising or a recommendation outside of class.  His class is very regimented, and he sets you up with every resource you need to succeed.  Also, if you simply do the assigned book problems then it's almost impossible to do poorly in his class.

Dr. Tiani was the best teacher i think i have ever had.  he provides detailed answers to the questions in the textbook.  he obviously does this for a reason, so if you just do the problems, go to class, and get over the fact that he is intimidating you will get a lot out of the material.  he has this class down to an art,  his lecturing is flawless

Although he is organized & posts skeleton notes online, Tiani does not teach, he simply talks AT you in every lecture. It's like he expects you to already know the info. Doesn't give examples that will be on exams (which are very difficult)& your exams are your Entire! grade. HE IS FULL OF HIMSELF AND MAKES THE CLASS WAY HARDER THAN IT SHOULD BE!
Worst professor and very snobbish. Does not like student and frequently make you feel as a complete idiot. Test are impossible. Rude and intimidating person. Avoid him!

Tiani is a great teacher. He is cocky and NOT a good person to ask questions but he is nonetheless brilliant and disciplined. I would take him for any chem class he taught. ESPECIALLLY OVER TODD AUSTELL

He's fun, but it's difficult sometimes. You need to stay on top of the material if you want to do well - trying to cram for analytical is not advised. Do the practice problems too - alot of his test questions are really similar.

Tiani is kind of tough to get used to - he's very strict in his ways and it's not very often that he'll go out of his way to accomodate you. However, he's a pretty good lecturer and his tests are challenging. Don't take him if you're looking for a good grade, bt you'll get a good understanding of the material.
very knowledgeable about topic. some what too confident and cocky. but great teacher nonetheless. as long as you study, you will do fine in his class. the subject isnt too hard to understand.

Chem 241 is not easy but I will give Tiani credit for being a good teacher.  I may not like him as a person, but his explanations are pretty clear.  You learn a lot in his class even if his exams are pretty hard.  It's not awful if you have him for 241.

Chem 241 is a hard, but having him as a professor greatly clarifies things.  He is great at explaining things and gives plently of examples.  He gives you an opportunity to redeem yourself if you messed up on a test with his one exam replacement for the final.  The class is challenging, but there were always people who made a 100 on every test.
Tiani is a GREAT teacher.....when he's not talking about organic or analytical chem.  The Man is full of himself and the tests are HARD.

Tiani is clear and organized.  His teaching method is very coherent and you should attend classes to maximize your learning.  While he is a good teacher, he may snap at students during class or in office hours.  Tests are fair, but points off for careless mistakes are common; class test average around 70.  I think he curved for improvement.
I now love chemistry

The material is challenging, but Tiani's teaching style is much easier to follow than most Chem instructors I've had. Assigns problems (not to turn in) and gives detailed solutions for them on blackboard which are very helpful. Tests are fair but require quick thinking. Can be condescending at times, but you'll learn the material.

This man is a complete ass, even though his lectures are very good and organized.  He is *incredibly* pretentious and unhelpful if you don't understand something he said.  Attend all lectures and write down anything he writes on the board because he doesn't post the most important parts of the lectures online.

Dr Tiani is a wonderful professor. He is extremely clear in what you need to know on every test. He provides a study guide and equation sheet well before the test date. The tests are meant to challenge you but if you follow along in the book and do the problems, you should do well. He is always open to answer questions and willing to help during of
He is very clear and explains concepts well.  Tiani moves at a moderate pace, making time to ensure that concepts are grasped before moving on with the next topic.  He uses lots of examples

Tiani was very interested in his students' understanding of the material. However, the tests were extremely difficult to do in the time given. The problems were complex and like the hardest examples from the book. Tiani is hard to approach because he is quite intimidating. He explains the material well and provides ample resources for the lectures.
the tests are hard
sucks

He explained the topics well and provided skeleton notes.  However, if you ever asked a question he was very condescending and not very helpful.  You only have 3 tests (no HW to turn in) so get good grades on all of them!

Tiani is a good teacher, but is patronizing, full of himself and is unfortunately bad at answering questions in a friendly way. He is very honest about what students must do to succeed, to the extent that he babies everyone. Probably does not realize he comes off as a jerk, because he does seem genuinely invested in his teaching.

boo hoo hoo.  lots of complaining from people who probably failed his class.  Dr. Tiani is AWESOME!  he holds tons of office hours, is respectful of students needs, and offers group help sessions every week.  If you can't pass chem21 with him you need to think about transferring.

While I found Dr. Tiani's Chem class challenging, what made the difference was his utterly horrible attitude towards his students.  He was consistently condescending and degrading to the individuals and the class at large.  Attending office hours or study groups bought brownie points though he continued the verbal abuse there.  Avoid at all costs!

If you want to learn something and then the test be something totally different then what you learned then this is the teacher for you.  He taught on one thing and then tested on another.  The first test we had almost no one finished b/c it was 26 questions long and the average was below 50 with no curve.
He is very hard.  I would only take him if you are majoring in Chemistry.  He is nice though.
No Comments

Very difficult; it helps to attend the discussion session and stop by during his office hours.  His tests are definitely harder than what he goes over in class.  The more problems you do from the textbook, the better off you'll be.
No Comments
He is very hard, but he is a very good professor and very helpful!!!!

This man is a robot. He talks about little except Chemistry. He seemed very distant and cold when i went to his office hours. His tests have nothing to do with what he teaches in class. Hardest class and worst teacher ever.

He didn't make Analytical Chem any easier. His Teaching techniques are good considering  how many people were in the class. He could give some feedback other than just tests (like webassign or something). Some people just CANT go to office hours. Overall a good instructor but a terribly hard class.
He is a good teacher, but that does not make up for the fact that his tests are very hard.  Unless you are prepared to study very hard, you will find this material very difficult.

He is the meanest professor I've ever had.  He makes you feel really stupid whenever you ask a question and acts like he's better than you because he has a PhD.  I hated him and I will continue to do so.  His tests are VERY difficult and he's kind of strict for a college professor.  Bad professor.
i liked him alot :D his tests were not horrible at all.

One of the worst professors that I have taken at UNC.  His tests are horrible, the first exam no one in the class finished it because it was so long and difficult.  He doesn't curve and you are told to study one thing and tested on something totally different.
Domti is a beast.
Probably the worst professor I have ever had in my entire life.  Tests are ridiculous, the workload is incredible for a 2 hour class.  Take another professor if at all possible!!

Too much work for a 2 hour class.  Doing the homework/problem sets before the test is exquisitely helpful.  Tiani will email you or answer questions in office hours/review sessions, but this doesn't always make up for the fact that he teaches at one level and tests at another.
Not effective at teaching the material (especially separations) in an understanable way--that's the reason this class was hard. Anyone who can add, multiply and divide will be fine with the math.

Tiani is the best teacher you can ever ask for He teaches well and ask you to come to his office hours, but make sure you have a knowledge of the question you want to ask him. He uses easy examples in class but give you the hard ones in his tests. He does not curve. Think twice before you take him.
No Comments
Really hard class.  Make sure you are prepared to do a lot of work before taking it.  Tiani is a good teacher though and will provide you with a lot of help if you are willing to seek it out.
He's pretty hard, his tests are long, but he's a fair guy-he'll give you days off during the semester to recuperate from workloads. Kinda cute too, in a chemistry way
Expects a lot from you.  If you're not serious about a career that needs chemistry, don't take his class.  He generally teaches well, though, and offers his time for help.
He is a good teacher and very approachable to students. However, the work load is tough (esp. if you're taking 41L too) and the tests are hard.

Professor Duncan is a great professor. Just do the work (which is minimal and not difficult at all), participate, and you'll easily get an A. He does take attendance, but communicate with him and he's super understanding, and class was often asynchronous. I will say he is a tad bit strict, but overall, great instructor.

Professor Duncan was great! He gives great feedback and wants you to do well in the class. He is willing to work with you and is incredibly helpful, just make sure you actually go to class. I took this class as a major requirement but I really enjoyed it.

Minimal work outside of class and easy to get an A. He's also very caring for his students and offers lots of flexibility. English isn't always the most fun class, but he finds ways to make it engaging. He is very thorough with instruction and gives feeders leading up to the projects, which makes it so projects don't burden us with work to do.

Prof. Duncan makes taking eng 105 more bearable. He gives you time in class to work on assignments so that you do not have homework. He also is very understanding if you cannot make it to class or have a question about one of the assignments. Each assignment can be resubmitted to get back points. I recommend!!

While Prof. Duncan can be a little serious and the class isn't super exciting, it is exactly what I needed as a first-year requirement. We had no homework and time in class to work on assignments. You will get an automatic A if you show up to class and turn in your assignments on time. You get to do a mock interview, which is super helpful.

Professor Duncan is simply too serious about ENGL 105 which should be an easy pass first-year english class, but the assignments have to be submitted on time, he gets passive aggressive about attendance, and honestly expects too much out of us when we are just trying to do class to get the credit and get it over with.
Best Prof ever! Great person, great lecture, great project!

Professor Duncan was my favorite professor this year. If you do the work on time you get an automatic A. He did his best to do the HW in class so you didn't have to do it out of class. He was super understanding about physical and mental health if you missed the class and was good about responding to emails! I would 100% recommend taking his class.

Matthew was an amazing professor. All the assignments he gave during class were super useful and he gave extremely valuable feedback every time. He wants every student to succeed and understands that we're all first year students so most if not all assignments are relevant to each student and is super open to helping both inside and outside class.

Matt is a very easygoing professor. He likes to work with students to find solutions to issues. If you communicate your needs for an extension or anything else he is usually more than happy to work with you. He gives good feedback to improve our writing and presentation skills.
Professor Duncan was great for ENG-105. He took time to make sure how every student was doing, and assignments were not difficult as long as you complete them. I 10/10 recommend him!

Mr. Duncan made ENGL105 a lot more enjoyable then I was expecting. He is very clear about what he wants in every assignment and you will get an A if you put in the bare minimum. Grade is made up of 6 short assignments and 3 projects, but theyre not difficult. Highly recommend him for this class.

He does a really great job with understanding the stressors students have in school and how to get efficient work done while still making sure we are not overwhelmed or lost. His class schedules are always well laid out and he makes sure we are well aware of due dates but is willing to change them when he sees that the class needs it.

This was the second class I've taken with Professor Duncan and much like the first, I found it to be easy and pretty good. The entire class consists of three papers, which sounds daunting but he's an easy grader. He doesn't want any of his students doing poorly, and would be happy to see everyone get an A in the class.

Professor Duncan was a great professor and was so caring. He would sit with students after class and answer any questions they had no matter what. He truly wanted to make sure they had it down. 3 big projects: a paper, a zoom presentation, and a posterboard. Very lenient and understanding of situations regarding online school as well.

Professor Duncan is a pretty solid English professor. He gave lots of extra credit opportunities and graded fairly easily. At the beginning of each class, he would show us a meme that related to what we'd be working on. The last project was about memes, but I found it far more complicated than it needed to be, which really sucked the fun out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof Duncan is amazing! He is so caring and is always available for his students. He did an amazing job teaching online and was always clear on rubrics and projects. He made ENGL105 fun and insightful at the same time, I learned so much! The projects do require a lot of work to be put in, but he is a fair grader. Overall the best!

Easiest english105 prof ever! You do an entire project on memes and spend time making them in class. He is super caring and willing to help students outside of class. His rubrics are clear and he grades fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Matthew was always available outside of class for help. Grading was fair and even gave leeway through forum posts that were basically free points. He was good at introducing us to the three main schools of writing and this class was a fairly easy English 105 class.

Ended up with an A-, but don't take ENGL105 with Duncan if you want the easy A as ENGL105 usually is. He takes the class too seriously for English 105 and you will be more than annoyed when you are putting in loads of effort while your friends with other teachers don't do anything all year. Oh and they'll have better grades too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Duxbury is incredibly kind and makes the homework very straightforward. I came in with no coding experience, and he makes everything doable. He's passionate, always willing to help, and his office hours are amazing. Plus, there's a ton of extra credit available.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Duxbury is such an amazing human being and lecturer. He's clearly knowledgeable and enjoys teaching. He introduced me to data science and motivated to pursue it as a major. Overall, take this class with him if you can! :)

i think you'd have to try to do bad in this class. Scott is a great prof - v caring, accessible, knowledgable, gives great feedback. i loved this class; it was genuinely interesting, and learned a lot w/out ever being stressed abt it. no exams, just reading quizzes (open note) and ~5 hw and a final project - all v doable w/out R/coding experience
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Scott was an amazing professor. If you had any problems he was always available and throughout the course of the semester we would slowly chip away at our final. He gives great feedback and makes all the hw/quizzes very manageable. If you show up and do the work you will do fantastic. Highly recommend

Dr. Duxbury was amazing. This class was super interesting and very manageable. He was very accommodating to those of us without any coding experience. He gave really good feedback and was available outside of class to get help. Can definitely get an A if you show up and do all the work. Highly recommend!

Scott is one of the best professors I've had at unc! He is so kind and is always available to answer your questions outside of class. Class went by so fast because the discussions were always really interesting and inspirational. He is such a smart and funny professor. Take this class if you can, you wont regret it!

I loved this class so much! It was super interesting and not too hard. We had weekly quizzes and biweekly writing assignments, but most of the grade was the midterm and final, which were both open note. I would definitely recommend this class!

I took SOCI 318 (not 123) with Professor Duxbury and it was my favorite class I have taken at UNC so far. Professor Duxbury is very understanding and makes content extremely interesting, 10/10 would recommend this class and Professor Duxbury for students within every major!

I had Scott in Fall 2021, and he's an excellent professor. He's a criminologist so he really knows the subject matter. He's always approachable and very flexible. It would be pretty difficult to get less than an A in his class; just pay attention, do the short assigned writing, and follow the study guide for the midterm/final. Great teacher!

Scott was the greatest Prof I had last semester. He really cared about his students and has a super simple grading scheme. If you show up to class and take the quizzes + exams which are open note then youll be fine. He assigns reading but you can get by without doing them. Definitely a GPA boosting class
Probably the best professor I've had at UNC. The class covers some difficult material, but Scott is great at making it easy to understand. As long as you show up and do your best, you'll get an A.
Scott made lectures interesting and always stopped to answer questions and have spontaneous class discussions. All assignments or quizzes/tests were simple and open-note. Class flew by.

Very clear expectations, good amount of graded items, no one type of assignment (quizzes, papers, participation, exams) was weighted too heavily. He's always willing to explain and discuss topics. Readings only mattered for the weekly quizzes, not exams. Midterm and finals were direct from study guide.

Professor Duxbury is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is so intelligent and explains concepts clearly. I've learned so much in his class. He is also caring and will work with you if things come up. He is clearly more interested that we learn in his class rather than being a tough grader. Highly recommend taking his classes!

Duxbury made this class very enjoyable. He is very transparent about caring for his students and wanting them to learn and does not intend to overload them with homework or give bad grades. The content covered in the course is interesting, and Duxbury does a good job of teaching some difficult machine learning processes. Highly recommend!

This man has my favorite type of teaching style -- informative but not bulky presentation slides, clear and concise when explaining the material, and encourages engagement from the class. Not to mention he's a very understanding professor. SOCI290 is not hard if you've done stats/R classes, the reading is cool and the HW/quiz aren't hard.
Loved this class! Super easy A--short & easy weekly quizzes, 1-page reflections every other week, an easy midterm & final. Classes were interesting, would definitely recommend.

Computational Sociology is a really interesting class. Although a very complex topic, Scott makes it seem clear through his lectures. The work is hard, but he walks you through the R and is very helpful if you need it. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Duxbury gives great lectures that are easy to follow. His tests are very similar to his lectures and are very straightforward and simple. Duxbury is very understanding about late work and the workload is not too heavy. The main grades are from discussion posts, weekly quizzes, and small writing assignments.

Best professor I've had in the 4 years I've been at UNC! He provides the reading material, exams & quizzes were super reasonable, lecture slides are available on Sakai, he explains topics well, has optional zoom meetings during class time, and is super helpful! He's very accommodating to students' needs and is super chill/friendly!
Probably my favorite professor I've ever had at UNC. The class was a super easy A as well, definitely recommend!

Nothing but good things to say about Dwight, I learned so much from taking this class and if I had to opportunity to take another class from him I would. His assignments force you to learn the topics while actually being interesting. Without a doubt one of the best professors I've ever had.
Great guy
Very great teacher, easy to follow assignments, very flexible with due dates, gives a lot of good feedback every week, and he's really easy to talk to if you need help.
My favorite class, even if it was just a gen ed. He made it enjoyable and I got a lot out of it!

Tanners a great guy, and really cares about helping you learn how to be a better writer. By far my best class last semester, if you can take him you should. show up to class, and when he assigns a reading you do it, because he will talk about it in class and youll feel stupid. Gives great feedback on papers, just make sure you do them on time.

Prof Tanner is lovely! He chose interesting material for the course and he's extremely knowledgeable about all of it. Lectures are pretty interesting and the assignments/essays are actually fun. Do the readings, show up to class consistently, and you'll do great
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great professor. Favorite of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely my favorite professor at app so far. Takes the time to learn his students names and genuinely cares about improving your writing. He is respectful and creates a safe space in his classroom
Great professor and by far my favorite class. Very smart and opens your thinking into avenues you never thought about before. True gem. You get as much out of the class as you want to as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I have him at Appalachian State University, and he has been awesome! He is very hip and relatable unlike a lot of other professors, and he is very caring about his students and their capability. When I had COVID, he was the best at reaching out to me outside of class and I really appreciated it. He is very inspiring and makes writing interesting.

I took his class my first year at UNC as a transfer student and I don't think I ever thanked him for helping me with my writing. He really took the time to look at my papers and critique them. I took his class on a whim but I am so glad I did. He loves to 'unpack' the literature and relate it to current times. He's an amazing professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dwight is young and hip, and he is able to convey stuff in an exciting and engaging way. He is always funny and relaxed, totally approachable, and most importantly, he gave great feedback on writing assignments. There wasn't that much work and everything we did do was really interesting and allowed for a lot of creativity. 10/10 would recommend

Dwight is probably one of the best professors I'll ever have. He's awesome at lecturing, always willing to help (by email or office hours), and clearly cares about all of his students. Abide by his pet peeves, follow his super clear grading criteria, and you'll have a great semester with a great guy.
Taking ENGL 105 was relatively stress-free. There aren't too many assignments and gives good and fair feedback. If you are relatively good at writing, getting an A/A- isn't too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class is a lot easier when you read the required texts and participate somewhat in the group discussions. Two papers and a relatively easy final make this class an easy A as long as you're a decent writer. Read the books!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dwight is literally the coolest professor I've ever had. He's super chill, very caring, and all around a pretty cool guy. The class required a lot of books, but they all were pretty good, and as long as you didn't procrastinate till the last day it's really doable. Definitely my favorite professor, would highly recommend taking one of his courses!

Dwight is the coolest! This was my favorite class this semester. He's super passionate about the material, explains topics really well, and gives great feedback on assignments. There's a lot of reading but most of the books are pretty interesting and the rest of the class definitely isn't too heavy of a work load. 11/10, would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Younger professor but super interested about his subject. Always very invested in class discussion and always willing to talk about papers or in class assignments outside of class. Not too easy but definitely not too hard as long as you go to class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: COMP550: Sridhar is a really great person who definitely cares about his students. However his lectures are pretty unorganized. Instead of slides, he projects his handwritten notes that are almost illegible. His exams are worded ambiguously and can be difficult, but his homeworks are perfect. Curve was generous and ensured no one got less than a C+

I'm not sure why the ratings are low. I found that he was a pretty good professor and was really kind. I think a lot of people rating low just didn't show up to classes regularly or office hours. Attendance isn't mandatory, but basically is if you want to do well, since it is a harder class. His handwriting can be difficult to understand at times.

Really cool dude, he's one of my favorite comp sci professors. I also thought he was a good teacher. It is tough material, probable should have went to office hours and would have probably done better.

Very knowledgeable, not mean, gives extensions, gives extra credit, but teaching was just not great. Difficult to follow handwriting and lectures. I don't think I really absorbed anything. Maybe the material is just extremely difficult, but the homework and exams felt impossible. You don't know your grade until the end, and it's too late by then.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you wanna take any class with this guy, think thrice. That's the worst professor I've ever had—unclear grading, low-quality teaching, and tough exams. It'd have been okay to make exams tough if his teaching were good. Please, for your own good, if it's your last semester, postpone graduation and take 455 with someone else.

OMG what an awful journey it was. I lost 10 pounds and some hair on my head bc of the stress in this class. His lectures were useless; hw are extremely difficult; horrible exams. I can go on with the negatives bc i don't have any positives to say about him. He's funny? Yeah, creepy funny.

His grading is very unclear and unfair. I don't know where he was educated but his style of teaching doesn't fit into the standards of American College Education. He is such a bad lecturer—his exams and hw were so difficult as if we're in India and we have to take JEE to get into the best college in India to survive. ZERO points to Duggi.
I have no idea where the los

I swear all the positive reviews are just Duggirala trying to save his average. no way anybody actually thinks he is a good professor. funnyish guy, which is why he gets a 2, but worst professor I think I've ever taken. yes, the curve is legendary, but the real challenge is surviving his incoherent lectures long enough to complete the course.

ok yeah he sucks at teaching and the hw is hard but if u put in the time (as u should for a class at this level), u will do well and pass. the curves are HUGE, and he has dumb extra credit like making memes. he also really does try to be funny/engaging, just kinda fails at it. but srsly if ur complaining, just take some time to like...practice?try?
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Homeworks were insanely difficult. Midterms were also very difficult (not as difficult as HW's but still absurdly more difficult than needed). Practice Exam answers were incomplete or hard to understand!

Sridhar is an amazing professor with clear grading who gives us more curve than we deserve. So curved that you could probably get a 70 and still finish with an A. Homeworks are very difficult, but relevant and helpful. His handwriting is truly scary, but otherwise lectures are fun and abstract. Taking 550 with him next semester, would recommend!

I've finally finished the course yesterday. This was a tough and awful journey. Hopefully no other CS professor would be that horrible in terms of exams, hw, grading, and relaying information during lectures. Didn't attend the class bc I thought his lectures were just useless. TAs helped a lot but the way they graded hw was vicious.

Class is not well-organized. We missed a few lectures bc of the weather and bc prof decided to cancel one of the lectures. He covers the material very quickly with his bad handwriting. He'll be teaching 550 next sem so expect not to understand anything from his lectures. It's unfortunate that Kevin didn't teach 455 this sem.
just very bad. have no clue how

OK prof but his exams and hw are extremely tough so don't take 455 with him if u can. Midterms were very difficult and long. Good thing is that he doesn't typically fail students because of the curving. I got 60%s on both midterms and it was curved up close to 70%s. Otherwise just a horrible teaching and extra credit is hard to get.

The assignments were challenging, requiring several hours to finish. Rather than focusing on basic understanding with simpler problems, all the homework questions were difficult. Exams were also challenging; the lectures didn't provide adequate support. While the course could be structured for better learning, the current design feels unmanageable.

Very knowledgeable guy who's not the best at teaching. Bad handwriting and lectures are difficult to follow, but maybe because the material is just difficult. Homework and exams are very challenging and time consuming. He's not mean or anything and I'm sure he's trying his best. Overall, lots of room for improvement and would recommend another prof

Homework was graded strictly, likely due to TAs, while exams were more lenient. Prof. Duggirala was very helpful during office hours. Many complaints stem from students avoiding responsibility. Go to an Ivy and you'll see teaching isn't perfect there either—welcome to academia.
Didn't show to class bc duggi was p useless, but the class content is not hard and midterms/hw were generally chill. idk why we take this class

The worst CS professor out there. Thanks God I'm taking COMP 550 with Kevin Sun next semester, not with Duggirala. This guy might be a good researcher, but he's a horrible prof. Hope he will stop teaching bc I don't want other students to go through this hell.
Avoid at all cost. His slides, homework, and exam grading are horrible. The whole semester was just full of stress.

While he is clearly very knowledgeable about the topics, he is not a good professor. Midterms and exams are more like IQ tests rather than testing to see if you actually learned something, and they are way too long. He has messy handwriting and lectures are completely useless. HW's take forever to complete and don't really help with understanding.

He's a nice person, but his teaching isn't effective, so think carefully before enrolling in COMP455 with him. The lectures aren't helpful, assignments take an excessive amount of time, and exams are so challenging they're hard to finish within the time limit. However, the TAs are excellent and do most of the actual teaching and explanation.

Just a bad professor. Not tough, not strict, just bad. He's clearly a genius in his field, but teaching is not his strong suit. Hardly elaborates on topics, interrupts students' questions, gives little to no explanation on practice midterm solutions (just writes "trivial" or tells us to read the textbook). Curve is legendary, but 455 is still hell.

This class is so tough -- I can't imagine how it's possible to succeed in his class. Not many people show up to his lectures because his slides are useless, so you should do a lot of self-studying. His exams are so tough that I can't even finish answering all questions on time. In general, I'm having horrible experience with this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It doesn't make sense how this guy was hired as an instructor, he's terrible at relaying information and teaching. Not only that but his handwriting sucks and he's hard to understand. The TA's save this course, as all learning is done during their office hours where you try to string together the Prof's incoherent lectures. I enjoyed class content.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take 455 with him. He makes the class unnecessarily difficult. Other sections with different profs had easier time with this course. Duggirala's 455 is illegally hard. One of friends even attempted s…. while taking this class.
horrible. avoid at all cost or burn. i hope one day karma will catch with Duggirala for making me depressed and mentally unstable for the whole semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: When the huge portion of the grade are exams, you know that Prof doesn't know how to design a class.

This class made me think of self-harm at least thrice. As a student with perfect attendance, the discrepancy in difficulty between his lectures and homework is genuinely unfathomable. Staring into his homework is like staring into the abyss - try to comprehend it and you'll go insane. Don't do this to yourself. Take this class with someone else.

The other reviews are accurate: this is probably one of the harder CS professors out there.  But he gives so many opportunities and resources to learn the material, and OH are invaluable.  If you put your nose to the grindstone he you will certainly do good

Professor Duggirala's class is extremely proof-heavy and harder than other sections, but he makes up for it with curves and plenty of extra credit. I received a 54, 67, and 62 on the midterms and final and still ended up with a B+ in the class. The material is VERY VERY hard but if you put the time in on your homework you will get an A or a B.

Oh boy this class was not it. He really cares about his students but the material was impossible to understand. You have to spend hours in OH to solve the HWs, and although he had extra credit on his exams they were impossible to finish. Never gave proper solutions to his practice problems - just wrote "TRIVIAL". How are we even supposed to learn?!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures were confusing so get ready to learn all the material outside of class. He is a funny guy though. Curve came in clutch. But take someone else for COMP 455 if you can.

Sridhar is nice but god this class was the worst. Tests are difficult and long. The final was 20 pages long. Homeworks were hard but exams were harder for the amount of time you had. Always wanted participation in class but spoke over people with the right answer and created never ending circular debates. Don't bother w/ this class or prof

Sridhar wants students to succeed, but he wasn't always timely or thorough in giving feedback (solutions for practice problems called "Trivial" with no more explanation).  Exams and HW were difficult.  Curved final, extra credit on HW and for improving test to test.  Decent lectures with bad handwriting.

I somewhat disagree with the ratings of previous students. The exams and homeworks were difficult and the professor took too long to grade, yes. However, it's evident to me that he only wishes to motivate and help students, and significantly curved the final exam. Plus he does his best to explain concepts in class and ensures understanding.

This class is insanely difficult for an introductory class to theoretical computer science. Exams are extremely difficult and make up a significant portion of your grade. His explanations aren't clear usually, slides aren't detailed at all and his handwriting is hard to follow. Be ready to spend hours outside of class trying to understand anything.

Could understand more from random YT channels than him, he refuses to upload key for the practice midterm the day before the midterm, exams were horribly hard and difficult, super PROOF HEAVY compared to other teachers, was thinking to drop out or withdraw after the first midterm, disturbs students during exam with changing seats w/o prior notice.

Dr. Duggirala is a passionate, caring, and funny teacher, and will take the time to help you understand on a deeper level if you ask, but he expects you to spend a LOT of time in office hours every week trying to get the homework done and understand it.

This professor refuses to release answer keys for the midterm. He's unclear during lecture. The class is all math proofs and the homeworks are incredibly difficult. The doesn't hold office hours and is unwilling to do the bare minimum to help students. It has been a horrifying experience. The concepts are beyond what should be reasonably expected.

WORST TEACHER EVER. Doesn't explain answers to any question or procedures for solving proofs. Completely illegible handwriting makes lectures impossible to follow. TAs can't understand his answer keys due to how poorly he writes them. Unfair, extremely difficult HW problems. Proof heavy (other 455 teacher has no proofs in the curriculum). AVOID HIM
Such an awesome teacher! Class is pretty easy as long as you study. One of my favorite classes I've ever taken.

The homework was so hard and the exams were extremely difficult. Although he's a nice professor, he really makes you work for the answers during office hours and does not give coherent lectures. The material was hard and confusing and I had to mostly learn the material myself. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's not for you if you just want to program video games, as his version of COMP455 is more difficult and more proof heavy, but don't let that fool you into thinking Prof. Duggirala isn't a good lecturer or doesn't care about his students. He may not have the best handwriting, but he's helpful, he'll make you laugh, and you'll learn a lot from him.

Encourages students to give wrong answers to encourage participation during lectures. Thinking through the problems during lectures (how to approach the proofs, how to design an automata) helped in solving the assignments and exams.

Course is difficult but would have been worse if the practice problems were given during the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is made much more difficult than necessary with Professor Duggirala. The class is very lecture heavy and most of the time difficult to understand and review due to his poor slides and sloppy annotations. His HWs are very difficult and time-consuming and his tests are even more difficult with content that has not been thoroughly explained

Struggled to grasp the concepts from the very first class due to his unclear and fast paced teaching style. The homework assignements were often confusing and unrelated to lecture material and the tests and exams were even harder. Would strongly encourage people not to take this class.

Lots of difficult homework and difficult tests make this class pretty brutal. Duggirala isn't the greatest teacher and his slides are average at best. Very little, and not super helpful, office hours (3 hrs a week between him and a TA). If you take 455 with Duggirala I'd highly recommend supplementing his lessons with the textbook/online videos.

He's a nice guy and is very open for questions during lecture. Lectures were pretty confusing,and he didn't do the best job of conveying his expertise in the subject. Even if you understood the material in lecture, the homeworks were still pretty confusing, a lot of them I had absolutely no idea what to do. Would not take another elective with him

if you want to actually become a better writer, take his 153. i have also now started to enjoy writing again and he gives helpful feedback, fair grading and always gives room for you to improve/make up assignments you didn't do well on!
Take Belichick's $50 million and give it to this guy.
BEST PROFESSOR EVER PLS TAKE HIM! Kindest teacher and genuinely cares about you and your learning. Gives thorough feedback and is so understanding. I love going to his class!
Professor Howlett is so good. If he has other classes I'll definite take it with him. Interesting lectures and meaningful assignments. Clear feedback too. Love him.

I can not recommend someone better or more kind than Prof Howlett. He is truly such a caring and personable guy. 

He always checks up on his students, provides great feedback on assignments, and keeps class interesting. I have never felt that my time in his class was wasted. Take him for MEJO 153. Even if it is in the evening. Take him.
He is genuinely the best professor I had at UNC. He really cares for his students and wants everyone to do well. He is always there to help and listen. I learned a lot from his class.
Prof. Howlett is so amazing I cannot even attempt to write it all here. Whatever you do, take this class with him.
